issues.title: windows: child processes (npm plugin install/load) spawn visible console windows
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, opencode spawns child processes (npm plugin install/resolve, cmd wrappers) **without hiding the console window**. Every plugin (re)load — which happens on each config hot-reload, for every connected project directory — briefly opens one or more black `cmd.exe` windows in the foreground. With a plugin configured, editing a watched file can pop 3+ windows in a row, which is very disruptive on the desktop and cannot be avoided from user config.

Two related problems:

1. Spawning `npm`/`cmd`/console children lacks `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `windowsHide` on Windows.
2. Plugin installs are not reused: **every config hot-reload reinstalls the plugin into a fresh timestamped cache directory** even when the pinned version is unchanged, so the npm spawn happens far more often than necessary.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.6 (OpenCode Desktop, bundled `opencode-cli.exe 2.2.6-x64`)
- OS: Windows 10 (19045, win32 x64)
- Terminal: OpenCode Desktop app
- Shell: PowerShell 7 (user), cmd.exe used by opencode for spawns
- Install/channel: OpenCode Desktop latest
- Active plugins: `@codemem/opencode-plugin@0.48.0` (npm), `context-mode`, `oh-my-openagent`, `superpowers` (git)

## Reproduction

1. Configure an npm plugin, e.g. `"plugin": ["@codemem/opencode-plugin@0.48.0"]` in `opencode.jsonc`.
2. Connect sessions in two or more directories (they share the background service).
3. Touch any watched config/skill file (edit `opencode.jsonc` or a file under `~/.config/opencode/skills/`).
4. For each connected directory, one or two visible `cmd.exe` windows flash in the foreground, e.g.:

```
npm exec node C:\Users\<me>\.cache\opencode\npm\@codemem\opencode-plugin@0.48.0\1794019618465\node_modules\@codeme...
```

A nested bare `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe` window also appears inside it.

Server log confirms a fresh install + load per directory on each reload:

```
timestamp=2026-11-07T02:47:00.799Z msg="loading plugin" id=@codemem/opencode-plugin@0.48.0 entrypoint=file:///...@
codemem/opencode-plugin@0.48.0/1794019618465/node_modules/...
timestamp=2026-11-07T02:47:02.837Z msg="loading plugin" id=@codemem/opencode-plugin@0.48.0 ...
```

The timestamped cache dir name (`1794019618465` = epoch ms 2026-11-07T02:46:58Z) is created anew on each reload even though the version is pinned and a full copy already exists from the previous reload.

## Expected Behavior

Child processes spawned by opencode on Windows should not create visible console windows (`windowsHide: true` / `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), and plugin installations should be reused across reloads when the resolved version is unchanged.

## Actual Behavior

Visible console windows flash (sometimes 2 nested ones) on every plugin install/load cycle; with hot-reload and multiple directories this repeats rapidly and steals desktop focus.

## Additional Context

- Search of the repository source for `windowsHide` / `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` returns no results (grep-based code search), so this appears unhandled rather than a broken implementation.
- Frequency observed: ~18 plugin loads over 5 minutes while sessions churned across 3 directories; every subsequent config/skill edit reproducibly triggers the same burst.
- Workaround attempts: pinning the plugin version does **not** prevent the reinstall-on-reload (cache dir is still recreated); no user-side setting hides the spawn.
- Related but separate note: shortcutting the reinstall when the version is unchanged would also reduce desktop churn on all platforms.

issues.title: cli: run hangs before creating a session when the initial SSE event is buffered
issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode run` can hang indefinitely before creating a session when the client's connection buffers the initial server-sent event on `GET /api/event`. The CLI opens the event stream, never receives `server.connected`, and sends no subsequent request (no session creation, no prompt). It exits only when the caller times out or aborts; there is no diagnostic output.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.6 (client and server)
- OS (server): Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS)
- OS (client): Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64), cloud VM
- Terminal: non-interactive / no TTY (scripted invocation)
- Shell: /bin/bash (GNU bash 5.2.21)
- Install/channel: server via Homebrew (latest); client via the official v2 installer (https://opencode.ai/v2/install), npm package `@opencode/cli-linux-x64` installed to `~/.opencode/bin`
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. On a server, run `opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096` with `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` set.
2. From a client host whose egress path buffers SSE responses (in this case a cloud VM behind a Tailscale tunnel proxy), set `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` and run `opencode run --auto --server http://<server>:4096 "say pong"` from a working directory that exists on the server.
3. Observe the CLI: no output, no session created, until the command is killed.

## Expected Behavior

`opencode run` should either complete the turn, or fail with a clear error or timeout that identifies the stalled event subscription.

## Actual Behavior

The CLI hangs indefinitely. No session is created on the server, and the only request recorded server-side is the event stream subscription:

```
GET /api/event 200 span=14283   (14.3s)
GET /api/event 200 span=45137   (45.1s)
GET /api/event 200 span=93069   (93.1s, matches a 90s caller timeout)
GET /api/event 200 span=59537   (59.5s)
```

`--auto` does not change the behavior, so this is not a wait on a permission prompt.

## Additional Context

- The server sends an initial event immediately on subscribe (96 bytes): `data: {"type":"server.connected", ...}` followed by `: heartbeat`.
- Through the buffering proxy, an idle subscription received only response headers (~352 bytes in 12s) and no event data; events arrived only once another session produced traffic (~4.2KB in 18s).
- Against the same server from a client on the same host, `opencode run` completes in ~1.6s, and the `/api/event` request lives exactly that long.
- `opencode models` and session listing work when the client cwd exists on the server, so name resolution, authentication (Basic `opencode:<password>`), and model fetching are all fine.
- Workaround: create the session and submit the prompt through `POST /api/session/<id>/prompt` and poll the session instead of using `opencode run`.
- Suggestion: log the startup phase (server resolved, subscribing to events, session created) at debug level, and add a timeout for the initial `server.connected` event.

issues.title: Loss of select ability (copy/paste) shortly after it was working - VSCode
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When running OpenCode inside the VS Code integrated terminal (over SSH), OpenCode text selection works normally at first. However, after performing a few copy-paste operations, the terminal completely loses the ability to select text. The mouse events get captured/locked by the TUI, forcing the user to either manually type reset or permanently disable mouse mode.

The whole reason I use VSCode terminal is primarily because it supports native copy actions, [unlike MacOS terminal  over SSH, which effectively also rules out pain free copy/paste](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47165). 

**Expected behaviour**
Native terminal text selection should remain stable and usable for sustained sessions without desynchronising or requiring a terminal reset.

**Root Cause Analysis**
The issue stems from an aggressive mouse capture hook within the text input framework. After a few paste operations, the interface drops focus anchors and fails to send the proper disable mouse tracking (\e[?1000l / \e[?1003l) ANSI sequences back to VS Code. This leaves the terminal permanently stuck in application mouse tracking mode, requiring the user to close and start a new session to restore the ability to even select text.

opencode v2.2.6

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Launch OpenCode inside the VS Code integrated terminal with mouse mode enabled.
2. Select and copy code blocks a few times using OpenCode mouse capture native copying
3. Paste elsewhere.
4. Attempt to select text again using standard click-and-drag.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: expose subagent execution identity and timing to clients
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Expose supported identity and timing data for each native subagent execution so clients can distinguish successive runs of the same child session.

OpenChamber needs this for [openchamber/openchamber#6358](https://github.com/openchamber/openchamber/issues/6358). A resumed subagent should appear at its new invocation while earlier results and durations stay unchanged.

In the v2.2.5 source, the background completion message carries `source`, `childID`, `agent` and `state`. The parent tool's progress/result metadata carries `sessionID` and `status`. Neither identifies the execution generation or carries its authoritative start and finish. A delayed report from an older run cannot safely be matched to a newer call using the child ID or delivery time.

Could core expose an opaque execution token and known start/finish timestamps through its existing tool progress, session/event records and completion metadata? The token should survive restart and remain consistent when callers join a running child. Each parent tool invocation still needs its own association; several callers can share one execution.

This should preserve the reporting lifecycle in [#61833](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61833). Its held reporting cycle can span busy periods, so execution identity and report identity must remain distinct. This request does not change notification preferences, background defaults or spawning behavior. Old records without timing should remain readable with unknown duration.

Related: [#36349](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36349) covers preserving parent completion across restart. This request is about the supported client-facing identity/timing contract.

The limitation above was checked in source; an isolated live end-to-end reproduction will be included with the implementation evidence.

issues.body:
## Summary

When `--server` points at a remote server and the client's cwd does not exist on that server, `opencode models` and session listing hang with no output instead of returning an error. Aligning the client cwd with an existing path on the server makes both commands respond immediately.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.6 (client and server)
- OS (server): Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS)
- OS (client): Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64), cloud VM
- Terminal: non-interactive / no TTY (scripted invocation)
- Shell: /bin/bash (GNU bash 5.2.21)
- Install/channel: server via Homebrew (latest); client via the official v2 installer (https://opencode.ai/v2/install), npm package `@opencode/cli-linux-x64` installed to `~/.opencode/bin`
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Start `opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096` on the server.
2. On the client, run `opencode --server http://<server>:4096 models` from a directory path that does not exist on the server.
3. Observe: no output, no error, indefinite hang.
4. Run the same command from a path that exists on the server (for example `/Users/<user>/project`); it returns immediately.

## Expected Behavior

A clear error such as "location/directory does not exist on the server", or a fallback to a valid directory.

## Actual Behavior

Indefinite hang with no output and no error.

## Additional Context

- The client's cwd is sent as the session `location.directory`; the server cannot resolve it and the request never completes.
- Workaround: `cd` to a path that exists on the server, or pass an explicit directory where supported.
- Suggestion: validate the location on the server and fail fast.

prs.title: fix(core): keep Code Mode catalog updates small and stable
prs.body:
### Problem

- **Noisy updates.** The catalog shared one 2k budget across all servers, filled cheapest-first. A server connecting or leaving reshuffled which tools the others showed, so most updates restated the whole catalog (~2.2k tokens each), and every restatement stays in history.
- **Wasted work.** Picking the cheapest tools meant rendering every tool's signature on every rebuild.

### Change

Same format and 2k cap as today. What changes is which tools are shown, and what updates say.

- **Which tools show:** pinned tools first, then the groups take turns showing their next tool, alphabetically, while it fits. Space one group can't use goes to the others. Only the shown signatures are rendered (plus one per group, to check that it still fits).
- **Updates (capped at ~1k tokens):**
  - a new group: its first tools that fit, plus a count;
  - new tools in a known group: `New:` with their signatures, then "N more; search for them";
  - a shown signature that changed: `Changed:`;
  - removed tools: one line; a removed group: one line.
- **No update** when a group shows more or fewer tools because another group came or went, or when a tool is pinned or unpinned. What the model saw is still true.
- The full catalog is restated only around an empty catalog, or when that is shorter than the update.
- The stored catalog keeps each group's tool names, so an update can tell a new tool from one that just wasn't shown.

```text
The Code Mode tool catalog has changed.

New:
  - tools.github.actions_cancel({ owner: string, repo: string, run_id: number }): Promise<unknown> // Cancel a workflow run

Changed:
  - tools.github.actions_get({ … }): Promise<unknown> // Get details about GitHub Actions resources

No longer available: tools.github.actions_list
The `slack` tools are no longer available and must not be used.
```

### Results

**Updates** over a replayed session (GitHub, Playwright, Context7, Filesystem; a late server, the browser attaching and detaching twice, GitHub gaining a tool):

| | `dev` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Starting catalog | 2,218 tokens | 2,322 |
| Late server connects | 2,235 (full restatement) | 24 |
| Browser attaches (×2) | 2,254 (full restatement) | 802 |
| Browser detaches (×2) | 2,235 (full restatement) | 27 |
| GitHub gains a tool | 42 | 236 |
| **All updates** | **11,255** | **1,918 (−83%)** |

**Rebuild time**, only when tools change: 2–12 ms typical, ~70 ms with Cloudflare's 3,767 tools.

**Evals**, `dev` vs this PR (\* beyond noise):

| | `dev` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Unseen tools (`codemode-novel`, 480 trials): pass rate | 0.97 | 0.98 |
| Unseen tools: steps | 4.43 | 3.34 * |
| Unseen tools: input tokens | 34.7k | 23.3k * |
| Unseen tools: seconds | 11.4 | 6.3 * |
| Known tools (`codemode-catalog`, 256 trials): pass rate | 0.86 | 0.84 |
| Known tools: seconds | 13.8 | 10.1 * |
| Known tools: input tokens | 53.3k | 57.1k |

**Real servers** (`codemode-real`: GitHub's MCP server read-only, and Playwright on real pages, 11 tasks), plus the fully fake tracker suite. 9 models, 2 repetitions:

| | `dev` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Real servers: pass rate, 8 models without `gpt-5-nano` | 0.98 | 0.97 |
| Real servers: steps | 4.1 | 3.9 |
| Real servers: input tokens | 42.3k | 41.3k |
| Fake tracker: pass rate | 0.88 | 0.89 |
| Fake tracker: steps | 5.2 | 4.6 |

The one regression is `gpt-5-nano` on real servers (7 of 22 passed vs 2 of 22). It tried a plain web request instead of the tools, then gave up, once saying the GitHub tools had no issue lookup because the catalog showed only the first GitHub tools alphabetically. Stronger models searched.

Evals: anomalyco/evals#21. The older `codemode-catalog` suite mixed real tool lists with fake responses and was replaced by `codemode-real` and `codemode-tracker`.

### Known limits

- In a group too big to show in full, the shown tools are the alphabetically first ones, not the most useful. `search` covers the rest.
- Sessions from before the upgrade restate the catalog once.
- Weak models may conclude a tool doesn't exist instead of searching for it (see `gpt-5-nano` above).

### Verification

- `packages/core`: `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, and the full suite. On this machine 29 shell, plugin and image tests time out on `dev` too, plus the known `isolates global home and XDG roots` failure.
- `packages/codemode` suite, root `bun run check`.
- Unit tests: turn-taking and spare space, pinned tools past the budget, rendering only what is shown, every update shape and the 1k cap, and no update when only the shown tools move.
- End-to-end: new and removed groups, a new tool, compaction, fork, revert, and a large group never crowding out a small one.

prs.title: feat(core): present a configured client certificate on model requests
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Some company model gateways require mutual TLS: the client must present its own certificate. OpenCode couldn't, so those gateways rejected every request at the TLS handshake.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds `network.client_certificate`:

```jsonc
{
  "network": {
    "client_certificate": {
      "cert": "/etc/company/client.pem",          // path: absolute, ~/, or relative to this config file (project dir for inline config)
      "key": "/etc/company/client.key",            // optional: defaults to cert, for a PEM holding both
      "passphrase": "{env:CLIENT_KEY_PASSPHRASE}" // optional, same as apiKey: literal, {env:} or {file:}
    }
  }
}
```

Where it hooks in:

```diff
 LayerNodePlatform.requestExecutor        (model requests only)
   RequestExecutor.layer
     withoutBunTimeout                     RequestInit { timeout: false }
+    withClientCertificate                 RequestInit { tls: { cert, key, passphrase }, redirect: "error" }
   httpClient                              webfetch, MCP, plugin installs: unchanged
```

Per request:

```text
model request
  not https:                         → unchanged
  Location config has no client_certificate → unchanged
  otherwise
    read cert + key files            (per request, so a rotated cert works without a restart)
    unreadable → "Could not read the configured client certificate: ..."
    fetch with tls + redirect: "error"   (the cert can't follow a redirect to another host)
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant OC as OpenCode (model request)
    participant GW as company gateway
    OC->>GW: TLS ClientHello
    GW->>OC: server cert + CertificateRequest
    OC->>GW: client.pem + proof of client.key
    GW-->>OC: handshake ok → model response
```

The TLS handshake only sends the certificate to servers that ask for one, so public providers never see it.

Config layering is normal: the last document that sets it wins, so project config can set it and managed config (MDM, `/etc/opencode`) overrides both.

Implementation note: the base HTTP client pins its own `fetch` per request, so swapping `FetchHttpClient.Fetch` does nothing. The TLS options go through `FetchHttpClient.RequestInit`, merged with the existing `timeout: false`.

Not covered (by design, for now): remote MCP, webfetch, plugin installs; certificates held in the macOS keychain or Windows certificate store (needs OS-side signing).

### How did you verify your code works?

`opencode run --standalone` against a local OpenAI-compatible gateway that requires a client certificate (`requestCert` + `rejectUnauthorized`), with an encrypted key:

| Config | Result |
| --- | --- |
| no `network` | handshake rejected |
| relative paths + `{env:}` passphrase | model reply |
| `~/` paths | model reply |
| wrong passphrase | request fails |
| missing cert file | "Could not read the configured client certificate: NotFound ..." |
| one combined PEM, no `key` | model reply |
| `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` with relative paths | model reply |

Re-run after rebasing on current `dev`. `bun typecheck` (core, schema), core config tests and `verify:package` (packed workerd SDK) pass.

prs.title: fix(core): clearer shell exit and timeout status, pass unmatched zsh globs through
prs.body:
**Shell results now word their status as `Exit code: N`, a timeout says how long it waited and how the process exited, and zsh passes an unmatched glob through instead of failing on it.**

The layout stays the same as today: the output comes first and the status is a separate piece after it, only on failure. Successful commands are unchanged (just the output). Background "running" results are unchanged.

### Shell status

Failing command:
```diff
  <build log>
- Exited with code 1
+ Exit code: 1
```

Timeout (the old text was mixed into the output, then a second notice):
```diff
  server starting
- Command exceeded timeout of 120000 ms. Retry with a larger timeout if the command is expected to take longer.
- Timed out before completion
+ Command timed out after 120 seconds. If it needs longer and isn't waiting for input, rerun with a larger timeout.
+ Exit code: 143 (SIGTERM)
```

The retry hint stays because models otherwise don't raise the timeout on their own (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/4197), and it now also says not to bother when the command is waiting for input.

Killed by a signal, reported the usual shell way, 128 + the signal number, followed by the signal name:
```diff
- Killed by SIGTERM
+ Exit code: 143 (SIGTERM)
```

A timed-out shell now also records how the killed process exited (exit code or signal). Before, the timeout was recorded first and the real exit got dropped, so there was nothing to report. The background completion notification and the notification for user-run shell commands use the same wording. Structured output keeps the raw log in `output` and the status in `exit` / `signal` / `timeout`, with no timeout prose mixed into the log.

### zsh unmatched globs

In a week of local sessions, about 5,400 distinct commands hit zsh's `no matches found`. Over half were unquoted grep flags like `--include=*.rs`, not globs at all. zsh aborts the whole command line before grep even runs, and `cd pkg && ls dist/*.map && bun build` stops the whole chain.

```diff
- zsh -c <command>
+ zsh +o nomatch -c <command>
```

Now an unmatched glob passes through literally, like bash: grep gets its `--include` flag, and a missing path gets the program's own "No such file".

### Truncation note

When output is cut, the note now matches what's actually shown, and the cut no longer splits a UTF-8 character (which showed up as `�` at the start).

Long lines, where the cut lands in the middle of line 6:
```diff
- [showing lines 6-10 of 10; full output saved to FILE]   (but line 6 was only half there)
+ [showing lines 7-10 of 10; full output saved to FILE]   (the partial line is dropped)
```

One huge line, like a 200 KB JSON blob:
```diff
- [showing lines 2-2 of 2; full output saved to FILE]
+ [showing the last 50 KB of line 2 (200 KB); full output saved to FILE]
```

### Read

- `packages/core/src/shell/result.ts`: `notice()` builds the status piece.
- `packages/core/src/shell.ts`: keeps the exit code or signal after a timeout kill, and builds the truncation note.
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts`: passes the final timeout through so the status can say how long it was.
- `packages/core/src/shell/select.ts`: the zsh flag.

### Checks

- `bun test test/tool-shell.test.ts test/shell.test.ts test/session-shell.test.ts` (packages/core): all pass except two `conditional substitutions` tests, which fail the same way on `dev`
- `bun test test/mini/tool.test.ts` (packages/tui) and `bun test src/tools/run-machine.test.ts` (packages/session-ui): pass, no UI changes
- `bun typecheck` in packages/core, packages/tui, packages/session-ui, packages/util: clean

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an Android (Termux) page to the V2 docs and links it from the CLI install section.

The Linux ARM64 build is a glibc ELF and Termux is Bionic, so it does not run as shipped. The page documents the setup I verified on aarch64: install glibc and `patchelf`, point the ELF interpreter at Termux's loader, and wrap the binary in a launcher that clears `LD_PRELOAD`.

Two details are worth calling out because they are easy to get wrong:

- Only the interpreter should be patched. `--set-rpath` (what `grun -c` does) rewrites the executable and corrupts its bundled payload, which shows up as `SIGSEGV` or `libc.so: invalid ELF header`. Termux's loader already searches `$PREFIX/glibc/lib`.
- Running through `grun` or `ld.so` makes `/proc/self/exe` the loader, so the background service's re-exec fails with `serve: error while loading shared libraries: serve`. Running the patched binary directly avoids it.

The page is marked community-maintained, so it does not claim official Android support.

### How did you verify your code works?

On Termux aarch64 with Android 15 and `@opencode/cli-linux-arm64`:

- `opencode --version` prints the release version
- `opencode service status` returns the background service URL
- The TUI starts and connects to the background service
- The launcher works while the parent shell still has Termux's `LD_PRELOAD` set

I also checked that the standalone `opencode-linux-arm64.tar.gz` from the update API requests `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`, so the same patch applies to the download path the page uses.

prs.title: fix(tui): retry a state write that loses its rename to a Windows lock
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61119

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`packages/tui/src/util/persistence.ts` replaces state through a temp-plus-rename write. On Windows NTFS that rename fails with `EPERM` or `EBUSY` while any other handle holds the destination open: an antivirus scan, the search indexer, a backup agent, or a second TUI writing the same state file. The lock is transient, so `renameWithRetry` retries the rename alone, first attempt then one retry per delay in `renameRetries = [50, 150, 450]`, and rethrows the last error after the schedule. Anything else, including `EACCES`, throws on the first attempt, so waiting is never spent on failures it cannot fix. A rename either landed or did not, so a write that gives up leaves the previous file intact; the staging file is removed once the write is abandoned. The shape follows the desktop settings helper proposed in PR #54530 (issue #51470). Note that #54530 is still open: its `packages/desktop/src/main/storage/atomic-write.ts` is not on `dev`.

`packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx` saved pinned sessions fire-and-forget with `void writeJsonAtomic(...)`, so a save that outlived the retries would surface as an unhandled rejection. The new `writeJsonAtomicDetached(filePath, value, report)` attaches the failure handler at creation, the same `console.error` shape the other state saves use (`packages/tui/src/app.tsx:551`, `packages/tui/src/context/session-tabs.tsx:114`, `packages/tui/src/prompt/directory-recents.ts:28`), and no longer loses the error. `writeJsonAtomic` still rejects for the callers that await it (`packages/tui/src/context/storage.tsx:79`, `packages/tui/src/model-preference.ts:120`).

Because a save can now spend up to 650ms in retries, saves no longer overlap. `save()` keeps one write in flight; saves that arrive while it runs collapse into a single follow-up flush of the newest `sessionStore.pinned`, so the most recent list always lands last. This mirrors how the file's other writers already serialize: `storage.tsx` writes under `Flock.withLock`, `model-preference.ts` runs a pending chain.

`rename` and `wait` are optional seams, not production defaults: `node:fs` opens every handle share-mode aware, so two such handles never contend and a POSIX test cannot produce this lock. Production always runs the real `fs/promises` rename and a real timer.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/tui/test/prompt/persistence-lock.test.ts` and `packages/tui/test/prompt/persistence.test.ts`, run from `packages/tui` on Linux (bun 1.4.4), current revision:

- `bun test test/prompt/persistence-lock.test.ts test/prompt/persistence.test.ts --timeout 30000 --only-failures` → exit 0, 7 pass / 1 skip (the Windows-only case) / 0 fail in 438ms. Same files with `--rerun-each 5` → exit 0, 35 pass / 5 skip / 0 fail.
- `bun test test/context/storage.test.ts test/model-preference.test.ts test/cli/tui/dialog-session-list.test.tsx test/plugin-model.test.tsx --timeout 30000 --only-failures` → exit 0, 6 pass / 0 fail. These cover both awaiting callers of `writeJsonAtomic` and the renderer tests that mount `LocalProvider`, the changed call site.
- `bunx oxlint` on the three files → exit 0, 0 warnings and 0 errors. `bunx prettier --check` on the three files → exit 0. `bunx tsc -b` in `packages/tui` → exit 0.
- The originally pushed revision was validated on Windows 11 (bun 1.4.4): the same focused files exited 0 with the real-lock case included, and a junit run confirmed the Windows case at 25.6ms, the injected `wait` keeping the retry schedule out of real time.

The detached-write test is deterministic: it awaits the promise the helper returns. `report` consumed the rejection, so awaiting it is the exact gate; the case asserts `report` received the error and the promise carries no value. The first revision's `Bun.sleep` polling, `setImmediate` turns and `unhandledRejection` observer are gone.

The suite's cases: the rename lands on the second attempt after waiting 50ms; the last lock error is rethrown after the first attempt plus 50, 150 and 450ms retries with the old value intact and no `.tmp` left; a rename failing with another code gets a single attempt and rethrows; the Windows-only case (`test.skipIf(process.platform !== "win32")`) holds the destination through `bun:ffi` → `kernel32!CreateFileW` with `FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE`, the way a scanner does, and drives the real rename through the whole schedule; and the detached case above.

The net change of this revision is +20/−21 lines; no comment text was added.

prs.title: feat(core): present client certificates for mutual TLS
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR Builds on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60259 by @adamdotdevin (that branch doesn't allow maintainer edits). His 4 commits are unchanged, with one fix on top. ### Type of change - [x] New feature ### What does this PR do? Some company gateways require mutual TLS: the client has to present its own certificate, not just check the server's. This lets OpenCode do that. ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc, /etc/opencode, or MDM managed preferences { "network": { "client_certificates": [ { "hosts": ["llm.company.example"], "cert": "/etc/company/client.pem", "key": "/etc/company/client.key", "passphrase_file": "/etc/company/client.pass" } ] } } ``` Rules work like `permissions`: an ordered list, `*`/`?` wildcards, and the **last** matching rule wins, so put broad patterns first and specific hosts after: ```text [ { hosts: ["*.company.example"], cert: general.pem }, { hosts: ["llm.company.example"], cert: special.pem } ] llm.company.example → both match, last wins → special.pem api.company.example → first only → general.pem ``` Which requests present it: ```mermaid flowchart LR R[outgoing request] --> M{model request?} M -- "no: webfetch, skills, MCP" --> P[plain fetch] M -- yes --> H{https and host in a rule?} H -- no --> P H -- yes --> X{https:// proxy applies?} X -- yes --> F[fail: cert would reach the proxy] X -- no --> T["read cert, key, passphrase
fetch with tls, redirect: error"] ``` Where it can be set (highest wins, the whole list is replaced): ```text managed preferences (MDM) ✓ system dir (/etc/opencode) ✓ global config ✓ project opencode.json ✗ a repo can't pick the machine's identity OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT ✗ ``` The fix on top. Reading the files with `Bun.file` put `Bun.file` into the packed workerd SDK bundle and failed `verify:package`. They're now read through `FSUtil`, still on every request so a rotated cert works without a restart: ```diff + const tls = yield* Effect.all({ + cert: fs.readFileString(rule.cert), + key: fs.readFileString(rule.key), + passphrase: rule.passphraseFile ? fs.readFileString(rule.passphraseFile) : Effect.succeed(undefined), + }) // unreadable file -> "Could not read the client certificate for " fetch(input, { ...init, - tls: { ...init?.tls, cert: Bun.file(rule.cert), key: Bun.file(rule.key), passphrase: ... }, + tls: { ...init?.tls, ...tls }, ``` Not covered yet: remote MCP servers, the WebSocket transport, and AI SDK providers that aren't native. ### How did you verify your code works? `bun run verify:package` in `packages/sdk` passes. `client-certificate.test.ts` passes (real mTLS handshake with an encrypted key and passphrase file). `bun typecheck` and `typecheck:tsc` pass in `packages/core`. ### Visual ```svg ``` ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #40111 Public API: adds the `network.client_certificates` config key and `Config.Network` schemas (backwards compatible)

prs.title: fix(opencode): cap images re-sent from history (backport #39929)
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Backport of #39929 (and the follow-up #56983) to the 1.x release line. No separate issue.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

1.x keeps every image in a session's history and re-sends all of them as base64 on every request. Auto-compaction only counts tokens, and images cost almost none, so on 1M-context models (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) request bodies reach 100–200 MB before compaction kicks in. On 2026-11-05, 1.x clients sent 23.4k of the 29.4k requests over 64 MB that reached the OpenCode gateway; 2.x sent 232. Those bodies run gateway isolates out of memory and get 413/400s from providers.

**Image cap (ported from 2.x `boundImages`).** At the end of `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect`, once inline images in the converted history pass 25 MiB, the oldest are replaced with the same placeholder text 2.x uses until 15 MiB remain. It uses the stable-cut version from #56983: the cut only moves each time another 10 MiB of images arrives, so the replaced prefix and the provider prompt cache stay the same between cuts. It counts user image/file parts, tool-result `media`/`image-data`/`file-data` items, and the synthetic user message that carries tool-result images for providers that can't take them in tool results (OpenAI-compatible and others). Remote URLs don't count.

Differences from 2.x:
- It runs on AI SDK `ModelMessage[]`, since 1.x has no `LLMRequest`. It's applied in `toModelMessagesEffect`, which feeds both the AI SDK and native runtimes, title generation and the compaction size estimate, rather than in `ProviderTransform.message` (which receives the AI SDK's provider-level prompt shape on one path and `ModelMessage` on the other).
- There's no `unsupportedParts` composition. 1.x handles unsupported media separately in `ProviderTransform.message`, which runs after this.

**Overflow classification.** `Request body too large` and `multimodal data size is too large` now count as context overflow in `@opencode-ai/llm`'s `isContextOverflow`, so 1.x compacts and retries instead of failing the turn, the same way it already handles HTTP 413 and `context_length_exceeded`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Ported the four `boundImages` tests from 2.x (below the trigger, oldest-first replacement with identity kept for untouched messages, stable cut across new images, images nested in tool results), plus one end-to-end `toModelMessages` test for the OpenAI-compatible synthetic user message path. Added both new error strings to the existing overflow tests in `packages/llm` and `message-v2.test.ts`.
- Red proof: with the cut disabled and the two patterns removed, every cap test except the below-trigger one (4 of 5) fails, and both overflow tests fail. With the change, they pass.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/opencode` and `packages/llm`. `bun test test/session test/provider` in `packages/opencode` (1166 pass, 0 fail). `bun test` in `packages/llm` (298 pass, 0 fail).

@rekram1-node: this is your #39929 on the v1 branch. Could you take a look?

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(data): per-page Open Graph cards for model and lab pages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Model and lab pages on OpenCode Data now unfurl with their own card instead of the generic "DATA" banner. The card shows the model name, its lab with logo, last week's rank and tokens over the last 2 months. A lab card shows the lab, its tokens and its model count. This came up after a launch tweet linked `/data/thinkingmachines/inkling-2-small` and showed the generic banner.

- `/data/[lab]/og.png` and `/data/[lab]/[model]/og.png` render a 1200×630 PNG with satori (`satori/standalone`) and resvg-wasm, in the site's OpenTUI Mono.
- Rendering runs in a small private Worker, `StatsOg`, with no URL or route. The Stats Worker reaches it through an `OG_WORKER` Service Binding (`infra/stats.ts`). It has to be its own Worker for two reasons: Workers can't compile Wasm from bytes at runtime, and SST uploads the Stats Worker as a single file, so the Wasm and font modules can't ship there. Under `bun dev:stats` and in tests, the same renderer runs in-process (`#resource` in `package.json` picks the implementation).
- `og:image` points at `/og.png?v=<hash of what the card shows>`, which changes at most once a UTC day. Only the current `v` is rendered and cached for days in `caches.default`, keyed by the request's origin, so dev and production keep separate entries. A stale or made-up `v` gets today's card with the pages' short cache and creates no new entry.
- If a page doesn't exist or a card fails to render, the route returns the existing `banner.png`, cached for 60 seconds.
- satori 0.63 compiles its inlined HarfBuzz Wasm at runtime. The OG Worker build extracts those bytes as a Wasm module, and `src/og/worker.ts` hands that module to satori's one runtime compile call. satori is pinned, and the build fails loudly if the bytes move.
- Refactor: one shared `providerIconId` replaces six copies, and the public model names moved to `lib/model-name.ts`.

Labs without an icon in `@opencode/ui`, such as Thinking Machines (it publishes no icon mark), get no avatar on the card. Compare pages still use the banner.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/stats/app` typecheck (`bun check` and `tsc`), all 36 stats tests, the Vite build and `build:og` all pass on a Linux VM. The production server bundle contains none of the in-process render code.
- `test/og.test.ts` (18 tests) covers card data, the version hash, the cache rules (current, stale and random `v`, per-origin keys, the fallback after a failed render) and a real OG Worker build. Each test was broken on purpose and went red.
- The built OG Worker ran under Miniflare and returned a 200 `image/png`, 1200×630, byte-identical to the local render.
- Through the dev server's real route, with the database unreachable: the banner fallback, HEAD, the alias 301 (`/data/zai/glm-5.3-flash/og.png` → `/data/zhipuai/glm-5-3-flash/og.png`) and no locale redirect for image paths. A forced card renders with the long cache.
- I compared cards rendered from live opencode.ai numbers (Inkling 2 Small, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B, Thinking Machines) against the approved design.
- The systems review's findings are applied: the read-only `contentSha256` removed from `WorkerVersion`, cache keys per stage, failed renders cached briefly, and `build:og` running in CI via the stats tests.

Not verified yet, to check on the first dev deploy:
- the page meta tags with real data (`bun dev:stats` needs AWS credentials I didn't have);
- the Service Binding and `caches.default` on Cloudflare: the first request returns a card rather than the banner, and a repeat is served from cache.

In dark mode, opencode.ai shows links, menu accents and focus rings in `#6b8fff`. Data and the shared nav menus used three other blues: `#4f8bff`, `#3b5cf6` and `#8190ff`. Now every dark-mode link, active accent and focus ring in this repo uses `#6b8fff`. Light mode stays `#3b5cf6`, which already matched.

This comes from David's neutral colour audit. @adamdotdevin, the Console and status page change is the companion PR, anomalyco/opencode-console#6208.

### What changes

- `packages/nav-menus`: the dark fallback for `--link` and both focus rings changes from `#4f8bff` to `#6b8fff`. The site passes its own `--nav-menu-link`, so this only changes the surfaces that use the fallback: Data, the Console pages and Status.
- Data (`packages/stats/app`): in both dark blocks (the `data-theme` attribute and the system media query), `--stats-accent` and `--stats-accent-text` are now `#6b8fff`. `--stats-accent` was not set in dark, so focus rings, active bars and markers showed the light `#3b5cf6` (3.5:1 on `#161616`). The accent text was `#8190ff`. The active chart bars (`--lab-usage-active`, `--model-trend-active`) get the same dark value.
- Site: three places still had the old `#4f8bff`: the arcade's link and focus rings, the docs' highlighted-line bar (`--code-mark`), and the DevTools console API's dark link. `--link-dark: #4f8bff` in `site.css` stays the same. It is the "4f8bff" option of Settings › Dark blue, and the shipped default (`6b8fff`) already overrides it.

Only colour values change. There are no non-blue colours, other audit items or flags.

| --- | --- |

prs.title: fix(site): pin the Like letters? bar so Safari's toolbar turns blue with it
prs.body:
Fixes how the "Like letters?" bar opens in iOS Safari. The bar appears at the end of the page once the footer wordmark's letters are dragged into a new order.

### What Safari did
When the bar started to open, the page's bottom took the bar's blue at once, so Safari's bottom toolbar turned blue in that frame. The bar itself was still growing from zero height, so a band of page colour sat between the blue toolbar and the thin blue bar until the opening finished.

### The fix
- While the tint is on (`data-letters-end`), the bar's link is pinned to the bottom edge at full height (`position: fixed`), so the whole bar is blue in the same frame as Safari's toolbar.
- The bar's room in the page grows behind it, and the page and the label slide up with it. Once open, the bar sits exactly where the page puts it.
- The tint holds while the bar opens. The page catching up with the bar's growth can leave it a frame short of the end, which used to drop the tint. Once the bar closes, the tint holds until the bar has finished closing. Under reduced motion the bar has no transition.

Only `services/site/src/component/site/site.css` and `site.tsx` change.

### Tested
In the iOS 26.3 simulator (Safari), light and dark, with the bar sliding open and appearing at once (the dev-only `?letters-bar=instant`). These stills come from the 4× slow-motion recordings, at the first frame where the blue appears:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8118254-1775-4037-ae0f-e0b9f59fb521) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1069bef7-52e9-45a0-b0e8-9d3c0e6dd777) |

**Gap:** the simulator reports a bottom safe area of 0, so the `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` part of the bar's height is untested. On a device with a home indicator, the pinned bar and its room in the page both include it.

### Checks
- `services/site`: `bun typecheck` and `typecheck:tsc`, and `bun test` (196 pass).
- Production build: the server-bundle guard, `check-css-output` (14 stylesheets keep native `light-dark()`, none lowered) and the docs budgets pass.
- `bun run check` (root).
- Smoke on the dev server: no 5xx in en, ja and ar. `/font`, `?letters-bar=instant` and `?letters-bar=slide` all return 200.

No feature flag: a visual fix to the footer bar.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

At startup the desktop main process reads the user's login shell environment (`$SHELL -il -c "env -0"`) so the background service inherits their PATH and exported variables. It used `spawnSync`, so a slow `.zshrc` (nvm, oh-my-zsh, ...) froze the main thread for up to 5 s before IPC was registered, which kept the window on the splash screen.

The probe now runs with async `spawn` (same 5 s timeout, child killed on timeout) and is applied to `process.env` when it finishes. Only the things that start processes wait for it:

- `BackgroundService.ensure` waits only when no compatible service is already running. Reusing a running service reads the registration file, which needs nothing from the shell (the early sidecar probe already does this before the env is loaded).
- The CLI installer, `which` in app detection, and "Open in" also wait for it.

The result is held in memory for the process, the same approach VS Code takes (`src/vs/platform/shell/node/shellEnv.ts`). Nothing is cached to disk, since the env usually contains API keys.

### How did you verify your code works?

Recorded production renderer builds (`electron-vite build` + `preview`) under Xvfb, with `$SHELL` set to a wrapper that sleeps 3 s to stand in for a slow rc file:

| No service yet: `app starting` → service ready | 5.17 s | 4.81 s (service spawn still waits for the env) |

prs.body:
<!-- Title: feat(core): cap images per request with a per-model limit.images -->

### Issue for this PR

Closes #59794

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Some backends reject any request with more images than they allow, e.g. vLLM with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4}'`, often behind LiteLLM. OpenCode sends every image in the session history again on each request, so once a session goes over the cap, every later request fails, even plain text prompts. `boundImages` only limits image bytes, not count.

This adds an optional per-model `limit.images`, next to the token limits. If a request would carry more images than that, `boundImages` replaces the oldest ones with the placeholder the byte budget already uses and keeps the newest N. Leaving it unset changes nothing.

```jsonc
"models": {
  "qwen3-vl": {
    "capabilities": { "input": ["text", "image"] },
    "limit": { "context": 131072, "output": 8192, "images": 4 },
  },
}
```

- Config layers merge `limit.images` the same way as the other `limit` fields.
- GitHub Copilot models get it automatically from the `max_prompt_images` value in Copilot's model list.
- Compaction's prompt estimates apply the same cap, so they match what is actually sent.
- Docs: a note on the models page and a row in the attachments limits table. Client types are regenerated.

Related PRs:

- #59303 adds a fixed cap of 30, so a backend that allows 4 still fails. The two fit together: the effective cap would be the smaller of `limit.images` and 30.
- #61563 adds one global `media.image.max_images`. I made it per model because the cap belongs to the backend serving each model. One config often mixes a 4-image vLLM model with hosted models that accept far more, and a global 4 would strip images from all of them. The token limits already live in `limit`, and the per-model field gives catalog sources such as Copilot somewhere to put the value they report.

Trade-off: the byte budget cuts in steps so the prompt cache survives. The count cap can't do that, because the backend rejects even one image over the limit. Once a session is past the cap, each new image moves the cut by one, and the prompt cache misses from the first replaced image onward.

No feature flag: the setting does nothing unless configured. The only models that get a value automatically are Copilot's, from the cap Copilot itself reports.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/session-model-request.test.ts`: with six images and `limit.images: 4`, the oldest two are replaced and the newest four are sent unchanged. With a limit of 6, the messages come back unchanged.
- `test/github-copilot/models.test.ts`: `limit.images` is read from `max_prompt_images`, and stays unset for models that report no vision limits.
- `test/config/provider.test.ts`: `limit.images` survives layered config merges.
- `bun test` in core (session request, compaction, runner, Copilot, config provider), schema and protocol: all pass.

prs.title: fix(ai): recover DeepSeek DSML tool calls leaked into message text
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #50206

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

DeepSeek serving lanes describe tool calls with DSML markup. When a lane's text→tool-call conversion fails or isn't configured (seen on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, OpenRouter and DeepInfra lanes), the markup streams inside `delta.content` instead of structured `tool_calls`. Nothing runs, the turn ends with no error, and the leaked markup makes the model repeat the leak on later turns.

The fix is a recovery filter in the OpenAI Chat protocol parser, so every lane that reuses it benefits:

- Complete invokes inside a DSML block become real tool calls, so the tool executes and the session continues. Handles the V3.2/V4 (`function_calls`/`tool_calls`) and V4.1 (`<｜DSML｜ calls>`) dialects, `string="true|false"` parameters, omitted `string` attributes, direct-JSON values, and bare JSON invoke bodies.
- A standalone invoke whose wrapper opener never arrived, and complete invokes inside a block cut off by the output limit, still recover.
- Stray markup (orphan closers, bare parameter tags) is stripped from the text so stored history stops teaching the model to repeat the leak. Truncated calls are dropped.
- Calls with undecodable arguments emit a tool-input-error, which flows through the existing malformed-input path so the model can re-issue.
- Recovered calls upgrade a `stop` finish to `tool-calls`, including calls that only surface at end-of-stream flush.

Recovery turns on for DeepSeek families while tools are declared; other lanes opt in with `compatibility.dsmlRecovery`. When it's off, content passes through unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Fixture tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/dsml-recovery.test.ts` cover each shape above, markers split across chunk boundaries, the finish-reason upgrade from both mid-stream and end-of-stream recovery, call-id uniqueness across responses, withheld text at stream end, and byte-for-byte passthrough when disabled or when no tools are declared.
- `bun test` in `packages/ai`: 2034 pass, 0 fail. `bun typecheck` clean on both configs.
- Manually replayed the leak shapes reported in the issue thread (missing opener, orphan closers, truncated block, space-delimited V4.1 block).

prs.title: fix(ai): prevent Gemini continuation retry on content-filter blocks
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #62619

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When Gemini emits a `continuationToken` checkpoint on an earlier SSE chunk and then terminates the stream with a policy block in `promptFeedback.blockReason` (such as `PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `SAFETY`, `BLOCKLIST`, `SPII`, `RECITATION`, or `MODEL_ARMOR`, matched via `GeminiGenerateContent.contentFiltered`) without a `candidates` array on the final chunk:

1. `GeminiCheckpoint` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/gemini.ts` previously only decoded `candidates[0].finishReason`. As a result, `candidateFinishReason` was `undefined` on the blocking chunk, leaving `token` set and `finishReason === undefined`.
2. `transport` then treated the blocked response as an unfinished continuation (`token !== undefined && finishReason === undefined`) and emitted `new NextRequest()`, which cleared `state.promptFeedback` and sent an unnecessary follow-up continuation request.
3. This change decodes `promptFeedback.blockReason` in `GeminiCheckpoint` and treats policy block reasons (`GeminiGenerateContent.contentFiltered(blockReason)`) as terminal in `transport` so `token` is cleared and the stream finishes immediately with `{ normalized: "content-filter", raw: blockReason }` and `providerMetadata.google.promptFeedback` preserved, while keeping non-policy `promptFeedback` reasons such as `"OTHER"` resumable from checkpoints.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added a regression test in `packages/ai/test/provider/gemini.test.ts` (`does not continue when blocked by a policy promptFeedback reason after a checkpoint token`) and verified that existing checkpoint continuation tests (including `forgets a block once the resumed request finishes` with `blockReason: "OTHER"`) remain intact.

prs.title: fix(core): make build metadata a required service so flags can't silently fall back to release defaults
prs.body:
## Problem & Root Cause

Core feature flags (`packages/core/src/flag.ts`) resolve in precedence order:
1. `OPENCODE_FLAGS` (`Flag.Overrides`, defaulting to `process.env.OPENCODE_FLAGS`)
2. `experimental.<key>` from the location's `Config`
3. `experimental.all_flags`
4. Build-channel default: enabled for `local` and `dev` builds, disabled for release/other channels

Previously, build metadata lived in `App.Metadata` (`packages/core/src/app.ts`), a `Context.Reference` defaulting to `{ channel: "unknown" }`, and `Flag.all` fell back to empty config entries via `Effect.serviceOption(Config.Service)`.

The server installed `App.node.replace(App.configured(options.app))`, but `LayerNode` keeps node dependencies private to each node's construction and `App.node` was in neither `Instance.nodes` nor `applicationServiceNodes`. As a result, session code running under `instances.provide(session)` had no `App.Metadata` in its Effect context and silently resolved the channel as `"unknown"`:
- **`codemode_vm`** (`packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts`): `execute` and schedule `check` calls always ran on the legacy interpreter in `dev`/`local` builds.
- **`media_blob`** (`packages/core/src/session/blob.ts`): `SessionBlob.enabled` on live prompt-admission (`session/inbox.ts`) and projector (`session/projector.ts`) paths under `instances.provide(session)` was silently off in `dev`/`local` builds (`enabledFor` previously worked around this for fork, import, and reads by manually providing `App.Metadata`).

## Design

1. **`App.Service` as a required `Context.Service`:**
   - Replaced `App.Metadata` (`Context.Reference`) with `App.Service` (`Context.Service<Service, Info>()("@opencode/App")`) with no default value, so reading `App.Service` without providing it is a compile-time type error in Effect/LayerNode graphs.
   - Added `App.node` to `Instance.nodes` and `applicationServiceNodes` (`packages/server/src/routes.ts`) so both location contexts and server contexts carry the configured `App.Service`.
   - **`App.node` default choice:** Kept `App.node = configured()` (matching `Database.node`, `Bus.node`, `Config.node`, and `ModelsDev.node`) so focused `AppNodeBuilder.build` / `LayerNode.compile` tests wire `App.node` automatically without boilerplate across ~35 test files, while `LayerNode`'s `CheckDependencies` still statically rejects any node that uses `App.Service` without listing `App.node` in `deps`. Added an assertion in `packages/server/test/flag-channel.test.ts` verifying that the server path replaces `App.node` and exposes `options.app` in both server and location contexts.
2. **Location-scoped `Flag.Service`:**
   - Added `Flag.Service` (`packages/core/src/flag.ts`) built from `App.Service`, `Config.Service`, and `Flag.Overrides` as a location node (`deps: [App.node, Config.node]`) in `Instance.nodes`.
   - Exposes `resolve(entries)`, `all`, and `enabled(key)`. `all` reads `config.entries()` on every call so flags stay live across config reloads.
   - Removed the `Effect.serviceOption(Config.Service)` fallback to `[]`, and made `Flag.enabled(key)` and `Flag.all` require `Flag.Service` in the Effect context.
3. **Callers migrated:**
   - **Code Mode (`Tool.node` / `CodeModeTool`):** `Tool.node` depends on `Flag.node` and passes `Flag.Interface` into `CodeModeTool.create` and `CodeModeTool.check`, reading `codemode_vm` per call.
   - **`SessionBlob`:** Reads `media_blob` through `Flag.Service`; dropped the manual `App.Metadata` parameter and provision from `SessionBlob.enabledFor`.
   - **Schedules, Artifacts, Compaction, and internal tool plugins:** Migrated from `Flag.resolver` to `Flag.Service` (and exposed `Flag.Service` / `Flag.node` in `PluginInternal`).

## Behavior Change

- **`dev` and `local` builds:** Feature flags (`codemode_vm`, `media_blob` on live prompt admission and tool output projection, etc.) now genuinely default to **on** when not overridden by `OPENCODE_FLAGS` or config.
- **Release builds (`latest`, `beta`, etc.):** Unchanged — all flags remain **off** by default unless explicitly enabled via `experimental.<key>`, `experimental.all_flags`, or `OPENCODE_FLAGS`.

## Tests

- `packages/server/test/flag-channel.test.ts`: End-to-end test booting `createEmbeddedRoutes` with `app.channel: "dev"` vs `"latest"` (no flag config, no `OPENCODE_FLAGS`), running a session prompt with an image attachment and a step calling Code Mode `execute`, and asserting VM + blob storage on `dev` and legacy + inline storage on `latest` (fails on `origin/dev`, passes with the fix).
- `packages/core/test/flag.test.ts`: Added `@ts-expect-error` type guards verifying `Flag.enabled("todo")` and `Flag.all` cannot be assigned to `Effect<..., never, never>` and `makeLocationNode` using `App.Service` without `deps: [App.node]` fails typechecking, plus live config reload coverage.
- Shared `Flag.testLayer` and `toolNodeReplacements` helpers for unit tests.

## Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core & Server Typecheck | `bun run typecheck:tsc` (`core`, `server`, `cli`, `sdk`, `schema`, `util`) | Pass |
| End-to-End Server Flag Channel Test | `bun test test/flag-channel.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` (`packages/server`) | Pass (10/10) |
| Core Flag & CodeMode Execute Tests | `bun run script/test.ts test/flag.test.ts test/tool-execute.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` (`packages/core`) | Pass (370/370) |
| Core Domain Suites (`codemode`, `session*`, `schedule*`, `artifact*`, `config`, `plugin`, `tool*`, `mcp*`) | `bun run script/test.ts ...` (`packages/core`) | Pass |
| Full Server Test Suite | `bun test` (`packages/server`) | Pass (126 pass, 0 fail) |

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #6279
Closes #17084

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

MCP servers currently have no way to know which opencode session called them. This adds two things:

1. **Built-in session context**: opencode now always includes `_meta: { sessionID }` in every `callTool()` request. MCP servers receive the caller's session ID automatically via the standard MCP `_meta` field.

2. **Plugin-extensible `_meta`**: the `tool.execute.before` hook output now includes an optional `_meta` field. Plugins can add custom metadata (correlation IDs, trace context, etc.) that gets forwarded to downstream MCP servers alongside the built-in sessionID.

When no plugin sets `_meta`, MCP servers still receive `{ sessionID }`. When a plugin adds fields, they merge with the built-in ones.

**Files changed (3):**
- `packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts` — read `_meta` from execute opts, forward to `client.callTool()`
- `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` — seed `_meta` with `{ sessionID }`, pass through hook and into execute
- `packages/plugin/src/index.ts` — add `_meta` to `tool.execute.before` hook output type

### How did you verify your code works?

- All 236 session tests pass (0 fail, 624 assertions)
- Typecheck: zero new errors (existing `llm.ts` errors are from upstream #19955, present on bare `dev`)

prs.title: fix(core): commit a staged revert before a goal command queues work
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62138

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After `/undo`, a revert stays staged on the session. `Session.prompt` commits a staged revert before admitting new work, but a goal command sent after an undo — such as `/goal <objective>` — queued its kickoff behind the staged revert. The kickoff goes through `session.synthetic`, which stays held in the inbox while a revert is staged, so the goal showed as active but never ran. Committing after the command would be too late: the commit deletes inbox items after the revert point, including the kickoff itself.

The first version of this PR committed in `SessionCommand.execute`, which was too broad: it dropped the revert for every command, including ones that queue no work (`/goal pause`, `/goal clear`, `/goal` with no text, unknown commands, failing commands), permanently deleting the undone messages and redo history for nothing. This version moves the commit into the goal plugin, on the only two paths that actually queue work: the `resume` continuation and a new goal's synthetic kickoff. The attached-files path still goes through `Session.prompt`, which commits once preparation succeeds.

Committing inside `Session.synthetic` was considered and rejected: synthetic messages are deliberately parked while a revert is staged (#55394), and its background senders — subagent completions, shell results, the goal's own idle continuations — must not silently commit a revert the user is still deciding on.

To let the plugin do this, `session.revert` (stage/clear/commit — the existing stable `SessionApi` operations) is now part of the plugin session API (`SessionDomain` in both the Effect and Promise SDKs), wired through the plugin host. No new endpoint, no new flag: this fixes existing behavior.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/plugin/goal.test.ts`: "runs a goal commanded after an undo staged a revert" — two prompts finish, a revert is staged at the first prompt, then the `goal` command runs. Before this change the revert was still staged after the command and the goal never ran; after it, the revert is committed, the reviewer is asked once, and the goal completes.
- New tests pin the review feedback: `/goal` with no text, `/goal pause`, `/goal clear`, and an unknown command all leave a staged revert untouched; pausing an active goal leaves it untouched; resuming a paused goal commits it and the continuation runs to completion. Restoring the old unconditional commit makes the no-work test fail.

prs.title: feat(server): include message times in session list
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62655

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds the last stored user and assistant message times to session lists, avoiding per-session message requests.

### Experimental

Return `experimental.time.lastUserMessage` and `lastAssistantMessage` by default in session lists. Each is a creation timestamp in milliseconds, or `null` when absent. No flag or client opt-in is required. The fields are specific to list items; the shared `Session.Info` and import schemas are unchanged.

### Database performance

The existing list query selects the page first, then performs two indexed lookups per session in the same SQL statement. It does not read message content or require a migration. The trade-off is extra indexed work for session-list requests; internal store operations that do not need the timestamps avoid it.

### Pagination

Ordering and cursors remain based on `time.updated` and session ID. This avoids changing existing behavior, but metadata changes can still affect ordering and concurrent updates can shift pages. Message-activity ordering is a separate follow-up discussed in the feature request.

### Semantics

“Last” follows stored timeline order. Assistant timestamps include tool-only steps and are not necessarily the last visible chat reply. The two separate fields let clients choose how to interpret activity without fetching message content.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check`; focused server and Effect-client tests.
- Isolated live HTTP test with synthetic sessions, pagination, and a server restart.

### Issue for this PR

Related to #43758, but does not implement session-scoped terminals or terminal context. This change addresses Mini's terminal/tmux-owned scrollback.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Emit OSC 133 C/D boundaries around each live Mini turn, including the echoed prompt and optional agent/model/duration summary. Historical replay is not marked. This is automatic, with no configuration option, visible UI change, A/B shell-prompt markers, or claimed exit status.

Use `renderer.writeScrollbackSequence()` to order markers with scrollback snapshots, replacing Mini's private FFI access and DECSC/CUP/DECRC workaround. Close each shell operation independently rather than waiting for the whole prompt queue to drain.

**Dependency:** anomalyco/opentui#1944. This PR is blocked on a published OpenTUI release containing that API; the dependency bump is intentionally deferred until that version exists. The current published dependency does not provide the new method. Local integration uses the built OpenTUI patch.

### How did you verify your code works?

The original revision passed Mini tests, TUI typechecking, formatting/linting, and a v2.2.0 demo PTY run. Review then exposed incorrect end-marker row placement and missing per-shell completion, which those checks did not catch.

With the built OpenTUI dependency: Mini suite 426 passed, 2 skipped; TUI typecheck and targeted Prettier/oxlint passed. New Mini tests interpret captured output with an embedded terminal and assert D is on the summary row at cursor seed rows 1, 21, and 24. Separate regressions cover per-shell completion and C/D/C/D output without summaries.

OpenTUI's split-renderer/ABI tests cover native ordering, small scrolling panes, a full-width line, close-time draining, and bounded payload admission. Its packed-distribution regression passes on Bun 1.4.4 and Node 26.4.0.

Built and installed v2.2.0 using a compatibility backport to OpenTUI 0.7.0, without upgrading the installed renderer. Its Mini suite passed (425 passed, 2 skipped), as did TUI typechecking. Interpreting the captured stream confirms D lands on each actual final row, not the previous output row.

prs.title: fix(core): size compaction output limit to room left by shortened requests
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62185

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes an issue where automatic conversation compaction throttles the summary request's output token limit to the compaction trigger buffer (e.g. 13,107 tokens on a 256k window with a 5% buffer) even when older exchanges were omitted or shortened into a small transcript leaving hundreds of thousands of tokens of free context room. When the summary output reaches that artificial ceiling, compaction fails with `Compaction summary reached the output token limit` (#62185).

1. `prepare` sizes the initial request options leaving room for `budget` (the trigger ceiling, e.g. `window - buffer`). When the unchanged transcript fits, `requests[0].maxTokens` correctly reflects that ceiling.
2. However, when the transcript exceeds the ceiling, `flattenAndDropOldest` shortens the transcript by dropping older exchanges and flattening history to text, or `shrink.history` drops the retained tail. Previously, the shortened request retained `prepared.request.maxTokens` (the trigger buffer size, e.g. 13,107).
3. `fitOutput` then took `Math.min(request.maxTokens, ...)`, which locked `maxTokens` at 13,107 and prevented it from expanding to the model's actual allowed output limit, despite hundreds of thousands of tokens of headroom left by the shortened prompt.
4. Sized the output limit on shortened requests (`flattenAndDropOldest` and `shrink.history`) to `SessionModelRequest.outputLimit(context.model.limit)` so `fitOutput` dynamically scales `maxTokens` to the actual remaining context window headroom up to the model's catalog output limit.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added `compaction sizes output limit to room left by a shortened request` in `packages/core/test/session-compaction.test.ts`. Verified that without this fix, the test reproduces the issue with `Expected: 32000, Received: 13107`, and with this fix it passes cleanly.
- Verified all 40 tests in `packages/core/test/session-compaction.test.ts` pass (40 pass, 0 fail).
- Verified adjacent compaction suites (`test/session-native-compaction.test.ts`, `test/session-compaction-transport.test.ts`, `test/session-compact.test.ts`, `test/config/compaction.test.ts`).
- Verified clean types with `bun typecheck` (2,012 files across 2 projects clean) and `tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json`.

prs.title: fix(site): stop server functions failing on the dev server behind a proxy
prs.body:
The site's server functions no longer 500 on the local dev server when the page is opened through an HTTPS proxy.

**Before:** `sanitizeServerActionRequest` copied the request with `new Request(request)` whenever a `/_server` call had a missing or cross-origin referer. On the Node dev server the request isn't Node's own `Request` class, so the copy threw `TypeError: Failed to parse URL from [object Request]` and every server function returned 500. Opening the dev site through a proxy (for example `https://dev-box.example.ts.net` in front of `http://127.0.0.1:3001`) hits this on every call, because the referer's origin never matches.

**After:** the request is rebuilt from its parts (url, method, headers, body, signal), with the referer replaced as before. A GET or HEAD drops its body, since Workers can hand those over with one and a new `Request` refuses it.

```diff
- const sanitized = new Request(request)
- sanitized.headers.set("referer", requestUrl.origin)
+ const headers = new Headers(request.headers)
+ headers.set("referer", requestUrl.origin)
+ return new Request(request.url, { method, headers, body /* null for GET/HEAD */, signal, duplex })
```

Read `services/site/src/lib/server-action.ts`. Tested with the existing referer tests plus two new ones (method and body kept; GET body dropped), and by hand: a cross-origin `/_server` POST on the dev server now reaches the server-function handler instead of failing in the middleware. Bun's `Request` accepts the dev server's request either way, so the Node-only failure itself isn't reproduced in `bun test`.

prs.title: feat(app): load configured GUI plugins in the web app
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related to #60976. Draft for review.

### What does this PR do?

The web app loads configured GUI plugins from the server that served the page. It does not load code from other servers added to the app. Existing `./gui-experimental` CommonJS bundles work without a rebuild; desktop still uses its own bridge. The web CSP stays unchanged: no `unsafe-eval` or `blob:` script source.

**Flag:** `experimental.web_plugin_gui` (`OPENCODE_FLAGS=web_plugin_gui`). Off by default in release builds. Only enable it for plugins you trust to run in the page; this is not a plugin sandbox.

- The authenticated client lists GUI entries from the server's startup directory. Each gets a single-use ticket valid for 60 seconds, scoped to its ID and revision. The browser imports a same-origin module that wraps that bundle as a factory and uses the host SDK instances. No password or pairing token goes into the URL.
- An update fetch that fails leaves the running revision in place. The next plugin update or reconnect can retry. Removing the plugin from the inventory unloads it.
- Only the window setup runs. OS exclusions apply to setup after evaluating declarations; they do not sandbox bundle top-level code. Desktop main, IPC and desktop's per-plugin controls are not provided on the web.

### Verification

- Built the web app and served it through the real CLI web handler with an isolated password-protected server and a GUI-only fixture plugin. In three fresh Chromium contexts, entered a password, opened a pairing link directly, and pasted a pairing link into the sign-in form. In all three, the plugin command appeared and ran when clicked; `main` did not run. The password case had **no session cookie** on the successful module request.
- Verified the unchanged CSP, anonymous rejection, wrong-target rejection and ticket replay rejection. With the flag off, the server returned an empty inventory. A failed module fetch during hot reload kept the previous command usable; the next revision loaded successfully.
- Added a server regression for both auth methods and ticket scope/replay, and a CLI CSP assertion. Server process, CLI web UI, plugin host/bundler, GUI machine, ticket and experimental route identifier tests passed. Regenerated OpenAPI and clients. `bun run check` and the normal pre-push hook passed.

prs.title: fix(site): stop the page dimming when a product card opens
prs.body:
**Opening a product card on the site no longer dims the whole page for a moment.**
When a card grows into its product page, the rest of the page crossfades. The sidebar, logo and GitHub link are the same on both pages, but they briefly dimmed with everything else. The card growing into the hero is unchanged.

❌ **Before**
1. The old page faded out in about 130 ms, starting at once.
2. The new page faded in over 200 ms, starting 40 ms later.
3. Partway through, both were half see-through, so the dark background showed through and everything, including the unchanged sidebar, dropped to about 77% brightness ❌

✅ **After**
1. The old page stays fully visible underneath.
2. The new page fades in on top of it.
3. Anything that is the same on both pages never changes brightness.

```diff
- old page: fade out (0.6 × fade)      new page: fade in (fade, after delay)
+ old page: stay solid                 new page: fade in (fade, after delay)
```

📊 **Proof**: Chromium, animations slowed 10×, home page → Mobile card

| Brightest pixel, every frame | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar text (steady value 143) | dips to 111 ❌ | 143 throughout ✅ |
| Logo (steady value 238) | dips to 182 ❌ | 238 throughout ✅ |

prs.title: feat(core): wake sessions on Console event watches
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None; OpenCode Console feature (event watches).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Lets a session wake when a Slack thread or GitHub PR, commit or Actions run it's watching through OpenCode Console gets a reply or status change, instead of polling. It's only in the built-in Console plugin (`opencode.ts` plus a new `opencode-watches.ts`), using plugin APIs.

- Dormant unless Console's `/api/v2/config` response carries `x-opencode-event-watches`. No probe requests and no tools otherwise, so cloud agent sessions and other workspaces see nothing.
- One connection per Console workspace across locations. It uses a WebSocket, reconnects at once when Console's ~10-minute lease closes it (4401), and falls back to long-polling with an opaque cursor when the upgrade fails.
- Wakes with `ctx.session.synthetic` (`delivery: "steer"`, `resume: true`). Teammates' text is fenced and framed as not from the user. Only the member's own human-typed replies read as theirs. Labels and statuses are flattened to one line so nothing escapes the fence.
- Acks only events for sessions on this machine. After 5 watch wakes in a row with no person's prompt, it stops resuming.
- Adds `console_watch` tools (`watch`, `unwatch`, `watches`), auto-watches after `gh pr create` and `git push` in the shell tool, and cancels a session's watches on `session.deleted`.

The Console side is in review in opencode-console. This change does nothing until Console sends the header.

### How did you verify your code works?

19 tests in `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-opencode-watches.test.ts` against an in-process fake Console. They cover dormancy, the shared socket, snapshot paging, lease reconnect, the polling fallback, framing and injection, the streak cap, lost-ack replays and cleanup. Each was checked to fail when the behavior it covers is broken. The core typecheck and `packages/core/test/plugin` (582 tests) pass. Not yet run against a deployed Console.

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): reuse Console config across startup activations
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Regression from #53775. Follow-up to #53813.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Since #53775, startup with a connected OpenCode Console fetches the Console config (`GET /api/v2/config`) twice, one after the other, before plugin activation finishes. Models, `/connect` and anything else behind `Plugin.awaitActivation` wait for both.

Cause: the supervisor first activates the guarded plugins on their own, then activates the full plugin list. `Plugin.activate` keeps a running plugin only if it is in the unchanged prefix of the new list. In the full list, `OpencodePlugin` comes after `models.dev`, Azure and other plugins, so the plugin from the early pass is torn down and set up again, and its initial `load()` fetches the Console config a second time. Each fetch took ~0.9–1.25s here.

Fix: the plugin saves each successful Console config fetch with the connection key and the time it was fetched. On plugin startup only, a fetch for the same connection from the last 30s is reused instead of fetched again. The saved value is keyed by the `ManagedPolicy` service instance, so it is shared within a server process and does not leak between tests.

What stays the same:
- Credential switches, the one-minute refresh, and the 401/403 re-checks still always fetch.
- Failed fetches are not saved, so if the early pass fails, the full pass retries.

I kept the plugin order unchanged. Moving `OpencodePlugin` earlier would avoid the restart, but its provider transform reads catalog providers that `models.dev` registers first.
