prs.title: fix(web-shell): reload an e2e boot aborted by host network churn
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Web Shell smoke suite now recovers a boot that a transient request abort killed, instead of leaving the page on the boot watchdog's "failed to load" panel. When the app's module graph fails to load because a module request was aborted, the harness reloads the page after the load event — at most twice per tab, and only when the boot itself failed. A page that finishes loading hands the budget back, and a boot that keeps failing stops after two reloads, so the watchdog panel with its real error text remains what a test fails on. Two regression tests arm that behaviour: one aborts the entry module once and proves the shell still mounts, the other aborts it on every attempt and proves the run stops at three attempts with the panel in place. The retry is installed from the mock-daemon installer that app specs and the visuals harness already call before navigating, so no spec body changed.

## Why it's needed

The lane's dominant failure on the shared runner pool is not a product regression. A dev-server boot is a few hundred module requests, and Chromium aborts every in-flight request with `net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` when its network-change notifier fires. On a busy pool host that happens every minute or two, so a boot that spans one of those events never completes: the watchdog paints "failed to load", every assertion on the shell times out, and the shard goes red on a diff the PR never touched.

Evidence from the run in the report (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/42440846137): shards 1 and 4 of that head wrote 98 per-test failure folders and 51 of them carry that panel (12 on shard 1, 39 on shard 4); of the failure contexts that captured a page state, all 12 on shard 1 and all 39 on shard 4 show it, including first attempts that cleared on a later retry. Shard 4's trace network logs show 14 to ~300 requests aborted at each of fourteen separate instants across its 18-minute run, and shard 2 of the same head was green. That is why the shard result looked like a wholesale regression rather than a host event.

Playwright's own retries do not fit this failure: each retry spends a fresh test body and its multi-second visibility timeouts before it gives up, while one reload costs about a second and keeps the test's fixtures and page state.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the two boot-retry tests in the chromium project (from `packages/web-shell`: `npx playwright test --project=chromium -g "stranding the boot|reload budget"`). Both should pass in roughly 18 seconds: the first arms a single abort of the entry module and still ends on the mounted shell, the second aborts it on every attempt and ends on the watchdog panel after exactly three attempts.

To watch them pin the change, comment out the installer call in the mock-daemon helper and re-run: the first test then fails with the watchdog panel visible in its error context, and the second records a single entry request instead of three. Restoring the call makes both green again.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — this is test infrastructure; there is no user-visible surface.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Playwright Chromium against the `packages/web-shell` dev server. WebKit was downloaded but this host is missing its system libraries (`libenchant-2`, `libhyphen`, `libwoff2dec`, `libGLESv2`, `libx264`), so the mobile-webkit project was not exercised locally; CI installs it with those dependencies.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the retry could hide a boot a spec deliberately broke. No spec does that today, and the two-reload budget keeps a genuine breakage visible on the watchdog panel instead of looping.
- Not validated / out of scope: WebKit locally; harness-only specs that boot a page without installing a mock daemon keep no retry; a document request aborted before any module loads still fails at navigation and is left to Playwright's test retries.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Web Shell 的 smoke 套件现在能恢复「被瞬时请求中断掐死的启动」，而不是把页面留在 boot watchdog 的「加载失败」面板上。当应用模块图因为某个模块请求被中断而加载不完时，测试基座会在 load 事件之后重载页面——每个标签页最多两次，而且只在这次启动确实失败时才重载。启动成功的页面会把额度还回去，一直失败的启动在两次重载后停下，因此 watchdog 面板连同它记录的真实错误仍然是测试失败时看到的东西。两个回归用例钉住这个行为：一个只中断入口模块一次，证明 shell 仍能挂载；另一个每次都中断，证明三次尝试后停下且面板在位。重试由 mock daemon 安装函数装载——应用类 spec 与视觉套件在导航前本来就会调用它，因此没有改动任何 spec 主体。

## 为什么需要

这条通道在共享 runner 池上的主要红灯不是产品回归。dev 模式的一次启动是几百条模块请求，而 Chromium 在网络变化通知触发时会把所有在飞请求以 `net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` 掐断。繁忙的池宿主上这件事每一两分钟就发生一次，于是正好跨过该事件的启动永远加载不完：watchdog 画出「加载失败」，所有针对 shell 的断言超时，分片就在与 PR 毫无关系的 diff 上变红。

证据来自报告里的那次 run（https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/42440846137）：该 head 的分片 1 与分片 4 共写出 98 个单测失败目录，其中 51 个带着这块面板（分片 1 是 12 个，分片 4 是 39 个）；在捕获到页面状态的失败上下文里，分片 1 的 12 个与分片 4 的 39 个全部是它，其中包含重试后才通过用例的首次尝试。分片 4 的 trace 网络记录显示，在其 18 分钟的运行里共 14 个独立瞬间、每次有 14 到约 300 条请求被中断；同一 head 的分片 2 是绿的。所以分片结论看起来像整片回归，而不像一次宿主事件。

Playwright 自带的重试不适合这种失败：每次重试都要重新跑一遍用例主体并耗掉数秒级的可见性超时，而一次重载大约一秒，并且保留用例的夹具与页面状态。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 chromium项目里跑那两条 boot-retry 用例（在 `packages/web-shell` 下：`npx playwright test --project=chromium -g "stranding the boot|reload budget"`）。两条应在约 18 秒内通过：第一条只中断入口模块一次，最终仍落在挂载好的 shell 上；第二条每次都中断，最终在恰好三次尝试后落在 watchdog 面板上。

要观察它们如何钉住改动，把 mock daemon 辅助函数里的安装调用注释掉再跑：第一条会以「错误上下文里可见 watchdog 面板」的方式失败，第二条记录的入口请求次数会是一次而不是三次；恢复调用后两条重新变绿。

### 证据（修改前后）

不适用——这是测试基础设施，没有用户可见表面。

### 测试环境

本机 Playwright Chromium 对着 `packages/web-shell` 的 dev server。WebKit 下载完成但本机缺它的系统库（`libenchant-2`、`libhyphen`、`libwoff2dec`、`libGLESv2`、`libx264`），因此没有在本地跑 mobile-webkit 项目；CI 会连同这些依赖一起安装。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：重试可能掩盖某个 spec 故意弄坏的启动。目前没有这样的 spec，而且两次重载的额度让真正的损坏仍然显示在 watchdog 面板上，不会无限循环。
- 未验证／范围外：本机 WebKit；不安装 mock daemon 就启动页面的 harness 类 spec 没有这层重试；在任何模块加载前就被中断的文档请求仍会在导航阶段失败，交由 Playwright 的用例级重试处理。
- 破坏性变更／迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): add Skills and MCP self-service
prs.body:
## What this PR does Managed-only users can prepare Skill ZIP/tar.gz archives and authored stdio, Streamable HTTP or SSE MCP connections without a daemon or Session placement. A normalized preview leads to one-confirmation publication, optional encrypted Workspace settings, and explicit application to the current eligible Session through the existing immutable package and configuration-install lifecycle. Receipt lookup and frozen operation identities support interrupted installs; other Sessions retain their selected versions. Explicit Runtime Skill import scans only the selected Workspace's project roots and snapshots through its original ready owner. Personal HTTP MCP OAuth adds encrypted actor-owned grants, PKCE authorization, generation-fenced refresh/revocation, per-request token delivery, versioned Session bindings and execution-identity checks. Self-service publication, Runtime import and personal OAuth have separate default-off switches. The public/WebShell contracts, generated types, Java SDK and specialized management UI are updated together. ## Why it's needed The existing package lifecycle already supports resources and versioned configuration, but Managed-only users lack a way to author/import those inputs. Workspace service credentials also cannot represent a private user grant safely. This reuses the current package registry and recovery authority while making installation explicit, reproducible and limited to the selected Session; personal authorization restricts who can drive execution while retaining Workspace read permissions for results. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify 1. On a deployment with self-service enabled, review and install a Skill archive containing a resource/script and each MCP transport without a local daemon. Preparation must not open a Session, request placement, connect MCP, execute a Hook/setup script or initialize a model. Credential values must remain outside uploaded packages and browser storage. 2. Keep two Sessions on different package revisions, update only one, and restore older content as a new configuration revision. Unrelated packages, independent MCP selections and base Hooks must remain intact. Busy Sessions, stale revisions, file-only profiles and read-only children must reject application without implicit upgrades. 3. Interrupt publication, settings and apply responses and retry the original operation identities. Saved content must remain distinguishable from active installation; an unknown post-commit outcome must retain the admission barrier until the original operation is reconciled. 4. Import a project Skill through the selected Runtime and replace/change its source or owner during the flow. Only that Workspace may be read; changed sources and stale/unready owners must fail without fallback or provisioning. 5. Personal OAuth must stay unsupported until provider configuration and cross-actor process/channel isolation are qualified. On a qualified deployment, verify actor/nonce/state/resource binding, refresh/revoke races, revocation during commit-to-ACK, explicit recovery, and refusal of another actor's prompt/approval/resume or unattended delegation. Disabling OAuth must block new authorization/token delivery while retaining query, revocation and binding removal. ### Evidence (Before & After) Before: Managed configuration depended on published MCP definitions or daemon-assisted package preparation; there was no Managed-only standalone Skill/MCP authoring, Runtime Skill snapshot import or actor-owned HTTP OAuth flow. The installed global CLI did not recognize the Hosted profile, so no running global-binary HTTP baseline was measured. After: 44 real authenticated packaged-Hosted HTTP checks passed without Session/turn creation. Chromium exercised the actual installer at 1280px and 390px with scoped styles/portals, preserved unrelated pins and kept secrets out of package/pending storage; publication/settings/apply in that browser fixture were mocked. A separate check sent the exact browser-generated MCP bytes to the real packaged Hosted preview and received HTTP 200. These results do not establish the complete Java/SQL/Runtime installation path. A separate PR comment records the detailed verification report and remaining gates. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested | | 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested | ### Environment (optional) macOS 26.7.1, Node.js 26.12.1, pnpm 11.24.0, JDK 21 and Maven 3.9.14. Local browser coverage used Chromium and fixture-only credentials. Java used an isolated Maven repository; no real MySQL, production model or qualified personal-OAuth execution profile was exercised. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: configuration recovery, execution-actor admission and token delivery cross TypeScript/Java boundaries. All new deployment switches default off; personal OAuth additionally requires an explicitly qualified isolated profile and registered provider. Java admission/token handling is kept outside the existing size-capped facades without increasing their limits. - Not validated / out of scope: acceptance remains pending. The last local Managed server selection had 24 passes and 28 errors across 52 cases: 27 Spring context errors from missing OAuth Properties registration and one H2 SQL type error. The causes and subsequent recovery fixes were changed after the shared ten-minute local Java budget expired, so final Java compilation, `ManagedAgentApiContractTest`, `SurfaceRegistryGateTest`, full MySQL/Hosted crash recovery and end-to-end OAuth still require CI. Git/npm acquisition, daemon token import, personal stdio credentials, watchers and a new isolation platform are outside this change. - Breaking changes / migration notes: update the shared V1 schema baseline and recreate disposable development catalogs; no V2 migration is introduced. Legacy non-OAuth packages remain version 1, but an old apply request cannot overwrite version-2 personal bindings. OAuth packages are installed through authorization plus versioned apply after Session creation. Compatible Harness/worker capabilities are required, and pool capabilities must be homogeneous. Design decisions, constraints and acceptance criteria are synchronized in the [English design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/824db8ddffabc4be1e8c5709aee84fae5dac1b47/docs/design/2026-11-07-managed-skills-mcp-self-service.md) and [Chinese design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/824db8ddffabc4be1e8c5709aee84fae5dac1b47/docs/design/2026-11-07-managed-skills-mcp-self-service.zh-CN.md). ## Linked Issues None.

prs.title: refactor(core): share the main-route predicate between the send layer and the compression service
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extracts the shared main-route check that #16473 asked for. The same three-part condition — resolved model matches the main model, a spelled authType matches the main one, and the `\0` endpoint pin matches the main base URL — was sitting in two places: the send layer's resolution early return and the compression service's cache-sharing gate. #15318 kept both copies on purpose so its diff stayed frozen; now that it's merged, there's one exported predicate next to the model/base-URL splitter, and both call sites use it.

The one real difference between the two copies — what happens when a selector can't be resolved — stays at the call sites, as the issue proposed: the send layer still falls back to the main generator, the compression side still treats it as a cold route. Both are noted on the shared function. The old comment citing the send layer by line number is gone too; it would have drifted on the next edit anyway.

## Why it's needed

Two copies of one condition never stay in sync for free. If someone later touches only one side — say, the base-URL comparison starts normalizing trailing slashes — the compression gate and the send layer quietly disagree about what counts as the main route, and that difference now feeds the window guard, the reactive ceiling, the budget window, and cache sharing with its skip reason. One predicate, no drift.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The interesting property is the one #16473 set as acceptance: break the shared predicate and both suites must notice. Flip the endpoint-pin clause to always-true — both go red (the send layer's "does not reuse the main generator when the requested baseUrl differs" case, and the compression matrix's pinned-elsewhere cell). Flip the authType clause instead — both go red again. Untouched, the two suites pass together (284 tests). I ran both experiments before pushing; typecheck, lint and formatting are clean.

## Risk & Scope

Net 30 lines across the two files that already owned the copies. Core module, so the two-tier gate applies — the equivalence argument is above and the mutation check is the evidence. No behavior change on either side.

## Linked Issues

Closes #16473. Follow-up to #15318.

<details><summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

按 #16473 的要求把主路由判定收敛为一份。同样的三条件（解析后模型是主模型、显式 authType 是主 authType、`\0` 端点 pin 匹配主 base URL）此前在发送层的解析早返回和压缩服务的缓存共享门里各有一份；#15318 为了冻结 diff 有意保留两份，如今已合入，提取为 splitter 旁的一个导出谓词，两处共用。未解析选择器的处理差异保留在各自调用点（发送层回退主生成器、压缩侧走冷路径），共享函数上有注明。

## 为什么需要

两份副本不会免费保持一致。将来只改一侧（比如 base URL 比较开始归一化尾斜杠），压缩门与发送层就会对"什么算主路由"悄悄分歧，而这个判定现在供血窗口守卫、响应式上限、预算窗口和缓存共享四个决策。一份谓词，没有漂移。

## 审查验证

把 pin 子句置真——两套测试同红；换 authType 子句置真——同样两套同红；还原后 284 个测试全绿。typecheck / lint / 格式干净。

## 风险与范围

净 30 行，只动本来持有副本的两个文件。两侧均无行为变化。

</details>

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): prove A3 rewritten command recovery without Hook rerun
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Completes the remaining A3 rewritten-input / Hook-no-rerun half of the G3 Step 3 recovery matrix. It proves that a command input rewritten by a Hook is treated as a new, independently approved step rather than inheriting the previous step's Allow; that completed Hook occurrences and completed command steps replay durable results after restart without physical re-execution; and that an outer skill expanding into two command steps survives a crash between the steps while preserving the second Action's identity and deadline. It adds a packaged failover arm, durable evidence collection, focused regression witnesses, and synchronized English/Chinese design documentation.

## Why it's needed

Issue #14481 tracks recovery gaps where restart could reuse an approval for a different final command input, rerun already-completed Hooks or command effects, or lose the identity of a later command step. These behaviors are safety- and correctness-critical for managed command execution: a rewritten input must not ride on a stale Allow, and durable receipts must be the source of truth for replay. This change closes the A3 gap with real packaged evidence rather than only unit-level assertions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the new packaged command-rewrite failover arm in the managed-agent harness. The expected observation is a three-generation sequence: generation 1 waits for the first command approval; generation 2 allows the first step, completes it and its PostToolUse occurrence, then crashes when the second approval is requested; generation 3 replays the first step and completed Hook occurrences from durable results without physical rerun, preserves the second Action's ID, creation time, expiry, and input reference, and requires a separate Allow for the second step. The final evidence must show two distinct Actions, one physical execution for each command stage and each completed Hook occurrence, settled command receipts, recorded model traffic, a completed relief Turn, terminal count 2, and reliable close. A focused TypeScript regression can be run with `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-command-step-hook-recovery.test.ts`. The merged branch passes local TypeScript build/typecheck and contract/meta suites; full Java and Hosted CI gates are pending on this PR.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI recovery and evidence changes. A separate PR comment contains the packaged run report, evidence hashes, local gate results, and CI-pending caveats.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS TypeScript tests, build, and typecheck; real packaged managed-agent harness on Linux with Temurin 21, MySQL 8.4, registered storage, and delegated cgroup. Acceptance remains pending until the required CI gates pass on the merged revision.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Recovery now distinguishes extension-owned Hook/command replay from native approval continuation; incorrect gating could either re-execute durable effects or block legitimate recovery. The added packaged arm and regression witnesses pin both sides.
- Not validated / out of scope: Full post-merge Java/Hosted CI suites are not yet green. Local full ESLint was OOM-limited on this host, so lint was run partitioned with generated build outputs ignored. R2 remains out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No public API migration. Action ID validation now accepts the command-step Action grammar alongside the legacy tool approval grammar; stored development catalogs should follow the module's baseline schema policy.

Design documentation: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and follow-up work.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14481 (G3 Step 3 A3 rewritten-input / Hook-no-rerun recovery). This PR does not auto-close the tracker.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

完成 G3 Step 3 恢复矩阵中剩余的 A3「改写输入 / Hook 不重跑」半边。它证明：被 Hook 改写后的命令输入会作为新的、需要独立批准的步骤处理，而不是继承上一步的 Allow；已完成的 Hook occurrence 和已完成的命令步骤在重启后通过持久化结果重放，不会物理重跑；外层 skill 展开成两个命令步骤时，在两步之间崩溃仍能保留第二个 Action 的身份和截止时间。它新增了一个打包故障支路、持久化证据采集、聚焦回归见证，以及同步的英文/中文设计文档。

## 为什么需要它

Issue #14481 跟踪了一些恢复缺口：重启后可能把批准复用于不同的最终命令输入、重跑已经完成的 Hook 或命令副作用，或者丢失后续命令步骤的身份。这些行为对受管命令执行的安全性和正确性至关重要：改写后的输入不能搭上旧的 Allow，持久化回执必须作为重放的唯一事实来源。这个变更用真实打包证据关闭 A3 缺口，而不仅依赖单元级断言。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 managed-agent harness 中运行新增的打包 command-rewrite 故障支路。预期观察到三代序列：第 1 代等待第一个命令批准；第 2 代允许第一步，完成第一步及其 PostToolUse occurrence，然后在请求第二个批准时崩溃；第 3 代从持久化结果重放第一步和已完成 Hook occurrence，不物理重跑，保留第二个 Action 的 ID、创建时间、过期时间和输入引用，并要求对第二步单独 Allow。最终证据必须显示两个不同 Action、每个命令阶段和每个已完成 Hook occurrence 各一次物理执行、已落定的命令回执、记录的模型流量、完成的 relief Turn、terminal count 2，以及可靠 close。聚焦 TypeScript 回归可通过 `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-command-step-hook-recovery.test.ts` 运行。合并后的分支已通过本地 TypeScript build/typecheck 和契约/元测试套件；完整 Java 和 Hosted CI 门禁仍待本 PR 触发。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A — 非 UI 的恢复与证据变更。单独的 PR 评论包含打包运行报告、证据哈希、本地门禁结果和 CI 待通过说明。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地 macOS TypeScript 测试、构建和类型检查；Linux 上的真实打包 managed-agent harness，使用 Temurin 21、MySQL 8.4、注册存储和委托 cgroup。在所需 CI 门禁于合并修订上通过之前，验收仍为 pending。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：恢复逻辑现在区分扩展拥有的 Hook/命令重放与原生批准 continuation；错误门控可能导致重跑持久化副作用，或阻塞合法恢复。新增打包支路和回归见证钉住了两侧。

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(managed-agent): prove A3 rewritten command recovery without Hook rerun (#16116)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(managed-agent): prove A3 rewritten command recovery without Hook rerun

Add the packaged command-rewrite arm and a focused three-generation witness
for two approval-bound extension command steps. Recovery keeps each rewritten
input on its own command Action and original deadline, replays settled
Hook/tool-stage results without physical rerun, and still accepts a relief
Turn and reliable close.

The real MySQL/Linux counterexample exposed small lifecycle gaps that are
fixed here: command_approval_* Action ID grammar, extension recovery resource
closure, commandStep load routing and Hook owner construction, a fast Shell
close race, and command receipt acknowledgement before Runtime retirement.

* fix(managed-agent): refuse Hook broker swap while the mount is held

delegateBrokerToMcp(broker) replaced the broker without reconciling the acquired/mount-claim state, so a config-revision enable that swapped owners after a Hook turn had acquired the mount would orphan the old claim and leave acquired pointing at the previous broker. Refuse the swap while the mount is held (the no-argument handover keeps the same broker and stays valid); a fresh load binds the new owner at construction. Adds a red/green regression plus free-swap ownership and shared-disown pins.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(managed-agent): capture extension Shell output before an already-closed handoff

The already-closed Shell adoption resolved closure before any data listener was installed, so a command that wrote stdout/stderr and exited during owners.start()'s membership wait was persisted as a successful empty result (silent data loss) instead of the base's explicit unknown-outcome failure. start() now optionally buffers stdout/stderr synchronously from spawn (prereadOutput), and the Shell detaches, replays those bytes through its capture, and installs live listeners in one synchronous step, so no output window is lost. hook/stdio callers do not opt in and keep their fail-safe behavior. Adds a deterministic pre-handoff replay regression (red before, green after) and a real-owner spawn-buffering regression.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(managed-agent): release preread capture on failed extension Shell startup

A failed start() never handed detachPreread to a caller and the catch left the early stdout/stderr listeners attached; since stopOwner keeps the child in the owner map, child -> listener -> buffer retained every preread byte for the instance lifetime (reproduced at 8 MiB per failed start). The catch now detaches the listeners and clears the buffers. Adds a red/green regression that injects a post-spawn journal failure and asserts the retained child has no data listeners. Also strengthens the mount-held swap guard test to construct mountWorkUnproven()=false with the mount held so the new clause itself is pinned (whole-guard removal now reds it), and adds a Linux-runnable real-spawn preread test (cgroup unit mocked) so the spawn-time attach is covered on the OS CI uses.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(managed-agent): use ChildProcess type for the preread test cleanup handle

The Linux preread regression typed its cleanup handle as { kill: (signal?: string) => void }, whose kill parameter is wider than ChildProcess.kill(number | NodeJS.Signals). Under strictFunctionTypes the assignment of started.child is TS2322, and the test file is part of the CLI tsc --build regardless of it.skipIf, so clean builds failed on every platform. Use a type-only ChildProcess import. Verified the exact rule with an isolated strictFunctionTypes probe (old annotation TS2322, ChildProcess clean) and a full CLI tsc --noEmit (rc 0); the host OOMs on the full reference-graph tsc --build, so the bundle build is left to CI.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(managed-agent): pin failed-start preread cleanup on Linux

verify-pr round 2 F7: the failed-start preread detach/clear was pinned only by a darwin-only test, and the macOS CI lane never runs on pull_request, so removing the cleanup (M9) stayed green on Linux. Add a linux-cgroup failure regression (cgroup unit mocked, real child) that rejects the post-spawn saveOwner after a short delay so sentinels are captured, then asserts the retained child has zero data listeners; removing the detach reds it on the platform CI runs. Mirrors the reviewer's Linux probe.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(managed-agent): address A3 review R1 findings

R1-1: replace the broker-swap guard with close-and-rebuild so a config revision bump that keeps the Hook catalog no longer parks a mount-held apply at recovery_required; revert the delegate overload. R1-2: cap the spawn-time preread at the shell 1 MiB budget with an overflow flag folded into outputCaptureLimitExceeded. R1-3: add a tool_stage domain-refusal load test. R1-4: batch the package-config retention walk (BFS + IN(...) + delta insert) with a delta witness. R1-5: precompile the Action-id Pattern at four sites. R1-6/7/8: anchor the crash/final evidence matrices and the package hook-command contract. R1-9: drop the inert admission-failure acknowledge. R1-10: read back both command-action decisions in the A3 arm. Verified by red/green regressions, CLI typecheck, the affected suites, and packaged arm owner-r46 on real MySQL 8.4/cgroup v2.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(managed-agent): pin A3 owner rebuild, preread overflow fold, broker disown

verify-pr round 3 found three test-evidence gaps where the R1 mechanism
was fixed but the regression pinned only half of it. Strengthen the tests
so each named mutation reds:
- N1: fire a second Hook after the revision bump and assert the executing
  broker owner moves ownerFor(1)->ownerFor(2); kills M-close (no-arg
  handover) and M-close2 (close without rebuild).
- N2: assert preread.overflow folds into outputCaptureLimitExceeded and
  [Output truncated]; kills deleting the fold line.
- N3: assert close() does not release the shared broker after disown;
  kills removing ownsBroker=false (double release).

Test-only; production byte-identical to 6d15829e52.

* fix(managed-agent): narrow A3 load-gate takeover and degrade pre-edge snapshots

Round-4 review (bot R2/R3 + maintainer) raised two behavioural Criticals:
- R2-1: the resume-approval gate's extensions arm lost its takeover
  conjunct, so a bare/lifecycle load of an extensions Session could set
  resume, skip the only 409 and drive a parked Turn. Require
  takeoverFlags && !lifecycle (dropping only !session.hooks so a Hook
  catalog still reaches the arm). Harness suite 693 green.
- R3-1: the bundle->contributions closure edge was enforced
  unconditionally on read, so a snapshot committed before the edge
  shipped read as corrupt. Mirror the page-envelope precedent and drop
  an absent contributions child in both the inspection walk and the
  native read; add a read-side fixture proven red/green.

Also address two Suggestions with red/green witnesses:
- R2-3: lift the A3 decision read-back into assertCommandRewriteDecision
  so the contract suite drives it; add disagreeing-revision/option cases.
- R2-6: pin that a lost durable receipt write leaves the native entry
  unacknowledged; moving acknowledge above the write reds the case.

* ci(managed-agent): cap the rewritten-command cgroup delegation step

The failover job's rewritten-command cgroup delegation was the only arm
step without timeout-minutes, so a wedged smoke could spend the whole job
ceiling uncapped. Cap it at 10 like its sibling arms and re-derive the
hosted-failover-e2e ceiling (280->290 summed, 295->305 job, allowance 15)
in both the workflow and the hosted-process-ci meta-test that pins it.

* test(managed-agent): pin the projection dedupe so lost retention reds

R2-8/R2-5: the delta-growth test could not red if the retained seed was
lost, because re-walking an already-projected level left row counts and
gmt_create unchanged. Assert the projection holds every recovery resource
exactly once across the preparing->prepared revisions; emptying the
retained seed now reds it with duplicate resource ids, proving projection
growth is bounded by the delta rather than the revision count.

* fix(managed-agent): repair merge column residue, size ratchet, native tolerance scope

Round-4 review (bot 5757389507) caught three issues introduced by the
round-4 merge / cgroup / native-tolerance changes:
- R4-1: the merge rename missed SUM(terminal) in the plain-arm durable-event
  audit; ma_public_event only declares is_terminal, so MySQL 1054 aborted the
  arm before its verdict. Restore SUM(is_terminal) and add a contract test
  reconciling every single-table ma_public_event column the runner names
  against the V1 schema (reds on terminal, passes on is_terminal).
- R4-2: the rewritten-command arm plus its capped cgroup delegation grew
  sdk-java.yml past its size ratchet; bump .size-baseline 150332->155957 the
  growth is real and the Lint & Static size gate reds without it.
- R4-3/R4-6: scope the native-snapshot contributions tolerance to transitive
  refs collected from resource bodies; a directly declared contributions ref
  stays on the strict isDeepStrictEqual path, matching the inspection walk's
  direct-reference guard instead of silently accepting a missing dependency.

* fix(managed-agent): correct the column guard tokenizer and legacy MCP retention

Round-5 review on the round-4 fixes:
- R5-1: the ma_public_event column guard was wrong in both directions — a
  quoted value (LIKE 'agent.%') posed as a column and red valid SQL, while
  ${sessionFilter} was blanked so a column typo inside it passed unseen.
  Extract a maPublicEventColumns helper that strips quoted literals and
  expands interpolated SQL fragments, with a two-direction witness.
- R2-5: the retention read-then-insert form was applied unconditionally, so
  the legacy MCP-settings path stopped releasing the projection row it
  supersedes and accumulated one row per revision for the Session's life.
  Keep the accumulate form only on the package-config branch; the legacy
  branch replaces its row. Witness: two legacy revisions leave exactly one
  SESSION_RECORD row (reds if the else branch keeps accumulating).

* fix(managed-agent): tolerate a legacy bundle's absent contributions child on commit

R6-1 (Critical, fails-closed regression): isReferenceContainer gained the
extension bundle/contributions kinds, so the commit-side closure walk descends
into a persisted legacy bundle's contributions child. That child was never
staged, so the read 404s and aborts the commit permanently — a legacy Session
loads via the read-side tolerance but can never be reconfigured. Add the
commit-side counterpart of that tolerance: drop only an absent contributions
child from the closure; a present or conflicting one stays fatal. Witness: a
commit whose closure reaches a persisted bundle whose contributions child was
never staged resolves and keeps the bundle in the census; removing the skip
reds it with 'Resource not found.'.

* fix(managed-agent): structural legacy-closure tolerance + command-step takeover arm

Round-7 review, two Criticals on the earlier tolerance/takeover fixes:
- R7-1: the legacy-snapshot tolerance was enumerated site-by-site and
  kind-by-kind, missing a dangling contributions part and a staged bundle
  whose contributions child was never uploaded. Hoist the tolerated kinds
  into one module constant (contributions + contributions-part) and apply it
  uniformly in all four walks (inspection, native page, commit persisted,
  commit staged); the staged arm gains the same async has-tolerance. Direct
  refs and present-but-conflicting children stay fatal. Two witnesses: an
  absent manifest part inspects cleanly, and a staged bundle with a 404
  contributions child commits with the bundle in the census; emptying the
  constant reds both.
- R7-2: the extensions takeover arm admitted every approval continuation, so
  an extensions+Hook Session's native approval reached resumeSavedNativeBatch's
  no-hooks refusal and 503'd the load. Scope the arm to a command-step plan;
  native approvals stay on the no-hooks arm.

* fix(managed-agent): share the extensions command-step takeover with the settle exemption

R8-1 (Critical, fails-closed): an extensions Session that also carries a Hook
catalog never satisfies `takeover` (hooks set), so the file-history settle probe
took canSettleHostedFileHistory and refused on the await_action phase alone. A
batch that owes file history while a command step parks at await_action was 409'd
on every load before the extensions resume arm was ever consulted, leaving the
parked round recoverable only by an out-of-band cancel. Compute
extensionsCommandStepTakeover once and use it in both the settle exemption and
the resume arm, so the parked command-step batch is resumed instead of demanding
a settle a parked approval can never produce. The R7-2 command-step scoping is
unchanged.

* fix(managed-agent): key both cold-load answer guards on one command-step predicate

R9-1 (Critical, regression): the second answerResumedTurnCalls suppression keyed
on resumeApproval, which is only assigned inside the takeover arm and is therefore
undefined on a bare load — so the guard was true exactly on the cold-load path it
was added to protect. A cold load answered the parked command-step round, writing
an irreversible tool_result for the plan's own skill call and permanently
destroying the continuation (or 503'ing via the uncaught hook-recovery throw).
Derive one commandStepPark predicate keyed on the unconditionally-computed
pendingCommandApproval (plus resumeApproval) and use it at both answer guards;
hoist the resumeApproval declaration above it. extensionsCommandStepTakeover is
unchanged (still requires takeoverFlags) — only the two answer guards change.

* refactor(managed-agent): extract MCP settings projection to honor the class-size ratchet

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(cli): keep the deterministic Hook owner re-acquirable across detach

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(cli): keep deterministic owners re-acquirable on every non-delete close

Move the terminal-release rule onto the owner instead of a single call site:
Hook and MCP close default to non-terminal and only DELETE opts into the
terminal release, so the shared MCP broker, the v2 lifecycle close and the
enable() owner swap no longer tombstone the id a same-revision reload
recomputes. A non-terminal close hands the mount back via releaseMount and
keeps the owner READY; the MCP drain stays ahead of the handback and skips
markReleased so the reload still derives the same owner id.

Translate the documented release-mount refusals (busy/conflict/writer-unproven)
into recovery-required on both owners instead of letting a raw rejection escape
as a close failure, and drain held Runtimes before the v1 owner close asks for
the mount back.

* fix(cli): re-initialize drained MCP configs on reload and complete the owner close fence

A non-terminal close left every mcp_configuration at 'drained', a resting state
the journal cannot reopen and nothing else consumes, so a same-revision reload
could never re-initialize MCP and stayed recovery-blocked. Advance the drained
row to released (its one legal exit) and reinstall a fresh configuration under
the same runtimeSessionId, so the server restarts, no drained row lingers, and
the deterministic owner id the reload derives does not move.

Add the documented 503 runtime_reconciliation_required release-mount refusal to
the handback fence so a Broker restart beside the Harness is named
recovery-required instead of escaping as a raw rejection that breaks the close.

Let a DELETE terminally release the deterministic owner even on a reloaded,
never-acquired Hook instance, keying the terminal arm off the terminal intent
rather than the transient mount hold, so load->detach->reload->delete no longer
orphans the owner.

* fix(cli): reinitialize released MCP configs and clear superseded drained rows on reload

The drained->released advance stranded the deterministic extension record: the
next reload resolved the same deterministic id back to the released row and
aborted. Treat a released predecessor like a drained one and reinstall a fresh
row under the same runtimeSessionId, picking a revision past every existing row.

A non-terminal close drains every row but only the latest per server is
reinstalled, so superseded same-owner drained siblings held recoveryBlocked (and
mountHandback) forever; advance them to released once the replacing active row is
committed.

The non-terminal discard sites left drained rows under a superseded owner that a
later apply's new owner made the reload reject (owners.size>1). Rather than make
the discard terminal — which would strand an apply that fails and keeps the
previous revision active — release superseded-owner drained rows at cold load,
sparing the active owner's own rows so a failed apply is never stranded.

Also sync ChildWorkspaceServiceTest's busy-storage assertion with the #16369
message reword that landed on main.

* fix(managed-agent): close the MCP/Hook owner lifecycle release gaps

Round-19 review raised three Criticals in the deterministic-owner release
path; all three are fixed:
- R15-3: the live enable callback constructed HostedMcpSession without the
  superseded-drained sweep the cold load already runs, so an off/on/off/on
  extension toggle accumulated owners.size>1 and threw recovery_required.
  Call releaseSupersededDrained before constructing on the live path too.
- R17-1: a DELETE of a never-acquired deterministic Hook owner let the
  Broker 404 (and post-restart 503 reconciliation) escape close(), wedging
  the session undeletable. Absorb both for an un-acquired owner and book it
  released, as releaseOwner does; the un-acquired terminal release itself is
  kept (R15-4). Two regression witnesses proven red/green.
- R17-2: releaseMount refused runtime_session_busy without the drain sweep
  the drain release runs, so a background Shell run outliving its turn wedged
  every detach. Sweep the unproven background rows before the busy check
  (mount handback, owner stays re-acquirable, R13-1).

hook/mcp suites 203 green; cli tsc 0; runtime-broker compiles; bundle builds.
MySQL fault-gate IT verification deferred to the CI full tier.

* fix(managed-agent): keep the mount handback observe-and-hold over live background writers

Round-20 R18-1: the R17-2 releaseMount sweep drained background rows and
then excluded exactly those rows from the busy check with no un-excluded
re-read, so a background process the sweep could not prove stopped stayed
excluded and the mount was handed back over a running writer. drain=true
also stopped legitimate background runs on the two observe-and-hold
handback routes (#13800).

Restore the contract: an observe-only sweep (drain=false) settles provable
exits and stops nothing, the excluded check clears only what settled, and
an un-excluded re-read refuses runtime_session_busy for any row still live
or unproven — the same guard the pre-R17-2 busy check already had. The
method javadoc is rewritten to match.

Witness: mountReleaseStaysBusyBehindASettledExecutionWhoseBackgroundProcessStillRuns
is green with the fix; removing the re-check reds it ("Expected
CompletionException ... nothing was thrown", releaseMount proceeds and
releaseMountCalls flips to 1). RuntimeBrokerServiceTest 199 green;
checkstyle 0 violations; spotbugs 0. MySQL fault-gate IT verification
deferred to the CI full tier.

* refactor(managed-agent): keep RuntimeBrokerService under its size ratchet

Round-21 R19-1: the R17-2/R18-1 releaseMount additions grew
RuntimeBrokerService.java to 4252 lines, past both its ratchet pin and
GLOBAL_MAX_LINES (4216), so ClassSizeRatchetTest failed and the SDK Java
lane went red. The ceilings only ratchet down, so raising them is forbidden.

Move the guarded second half of the mount handback (claim re-check, excluded
busy check, un-excluded background re-read, unproven-capture refusal, then
the transport handback) into RuntimeExecutionRecovery.releaseMountAfterSweep,
beside the observe-only sweep it follows. The facade drops to 4212 lines;
the recovery collaborator is 442 (< 800, so it needs no pin of its own). No
behaviour changes: the sweep stays drain=false, the un-excluded re-read still
refuses, and the claim re-check still runs under the lock.

Witness: ClassSizeRatchetTest reproduced the two 4252-line violations and is
green at 4212; RuntimeBrokerServiceTest 199 green; removing the re-check in
its new home reds the pinned mount test ("Expected CompletionException ...
nothing was thrown"), then restored. checkstyle 0 violations; spotbugs 0.
MySQL fault-gate IT verification deferred to the CI full tier.

* fix(cli): name a raced mount-handback admission_closed as recovery-required

Round-23 R15-2: fencedMountHandback's doc comment says its codes are the
documented release-mount refusals, and the design doc names 409
runtime_admission_closed for the close/archive/delete window
(workspace-execution-mount-recovery-block-release.md). releaseMount's
requireLifecycleRelease throws exactly that conflict when a v2 lifecycle
fence row exists and the harness is not yet draining, but the fence omitted
the code, so a non-terminal detach racing a close/archive/delete rethrew the
raw rejection out of close() and the route answered a generic
managed_session_close_failed instead of the declared recovery-required.

Add runtime_admission_closed to the 409 fence group (additive — no existing
member weakened): the lifecycle operation's own drain frees the mount, so the
detach backs off attached/retryable. Both callers (Hook close, MCP
closeResources) share the fence. Keep 404 runtime_session_not_found out (the
terminal arm books it) and do not fold in 501 workspace_mount_release_unsupported
(a permanent misconfiguration, not a retry-once-it-settles fence).

Witness: add the code to the Hook recovery-required it.each and a MCP
closeResources twin; with the fix both green (hook/mcp 208). Removing the
member reds both new cases with the raw HostedWorkspaceBrokerRejection
("Runtime Broker returned HTTP 409") instead of HostedHook/McpRecoveryRequiredError,
while the unrelated terminal-acquire admission_closed case stays green; restored.
cli tsc --noEmit 0 errors.

* fix(cli): drain held Runtimes before the v2 non-terminal Hook mount handback

Round-24 R22-1: the lifecycle-v2 settle_resources branch issued the owner
close — which for a deterministic owner on a non-terminal close hands the
Workspace mount back — before the branch's only Runtime drain. A
Hook-configured turn shares that Runtime and leaves a live background Shell
(its finish() skips the release), so the release-mount guard refused
runtime_session_busy, the fence named it recovery-required, and the route
answered 503 workspace_lifecycle_resources_unsettled on every retry while the
process lived. The drain that would have stopped the run was never reached.
The v1 close already keeps the opposite order (moved there for R14-2); the v2
branch never got the same treatment when the cleanup-debt drain landed.

Move the drain ahead of the owner close, mirroring v1. This also puts it ahead
of the publisher close, so the drain's stops land their finalize through a
still-open publisher. The owed file-history marker is already retired earlier
in the same route, so the drain's file-history guard is unaffected. DELETE is
unchanged (terminal short-circuits the handback arm), and the handback stays
non-terminal for detach with the deterministic owner id intact.

Witness: a route-level v2 settle_resources close of a session holding a
deterministic Hook owner and cleanup debt, with releaseMount refusing busy
until the descriptor drain runs — 200 with the fix, and reverting the reorder
reds it with `expected 200 "OK", got 503 "Service Unavailable"`. The first
draft of the witness was vacuous (an unrelated lease drain cleared the flag);
only the descriptor-carrying drain now counts. Full harness suite 712 green;
cli tsc --noEmit 0 errors.

* style(cli): apply Prettier to the R22-1 handback-order witness

The Lint & Static lane failed on Run Prettier: the releaseMount spy added with
the R22-1 witness exceeded the print width. Formatting only, no behaviour
change; prettier --check now passes on every file this branch touched.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(cli): drain the held Runtime a Hook turn leaves on a v2 close

R22-1 moved the v2 drain ahead of the Hook mount handback, but the drain it
moved only acts on cleanup debt, and a Hook-configured turn writes none: it
acquires through hooks.acquire(), while oweHostedTurnCleanup and cleanupOwed
both sit in the else branch. What that turn leaves is a held Runtime recorded
client-side, and the only drain of that set was the v1 close. So the handback
still went out over a live background run, the guard refused
runtime_session_busy, and the detach parked on 503 for as long as the process
lived — the wedge R22-1 was raised for.

Drain heldRuntimeTurns in the v2 block too, mirroring v1, after the debt drain
and before hooks.close so the R22-1 order holds. Tolerate only 404
runtime_session_not_found; v1's 503 reconciliation tolerance is deliberately
not carried over because the releaseMount that follows would refuse with that
same 503 anyway, so tolerating it would only claim an unproven stop. Every
other refusal throws and the route parks honestly, as before.

The R22-1 witness was vacuous for this shape: it called f.owe() to manufacture
a descriptor the Hook path never writes. The new witness asserts there is no
cleanup debt, seeds heldRuntimeTurns instead, and keys the busy guard to the
held turn's own Runtime — the lease drain also issues {drain:true} with no
descriptor, so an opts-only check would let it clear the flag.

Red before: expected 200 "OK", got 503 "Service Unavailable". Green after.
hosted-harness-session 716/716 (full file, run alone), hook+mcp 208, build rc0,
Prettier clean.

* fix(cli): tolerate an unprovable held-Runtime drain on a v2 close

R24-1's drain tolerated only 404. The reasoning for leaving out v1's 503
tolerance was that the releaseMount right after it would refuse with the same
503 anyway, so tolerating could not unwedge the close. That premise is false:
HostedHookSession.close() guards the handback with
`ownsBroker && (mountHeld || (terminal && deterministicOwner))`, and a reload
builds a fresh instance whose mountHeld stays false until a Hook turn acquires.
After a Harness restart a non-terminal detach therefore never calls
releaseMount at all — the close would have succeeded, and the throw was the
only thing blocking it. Because the entry is deleted only on success or 404,
every retry re-seeded the same id and failed identically, leaving the mount
claimed, the lease pinned and the publishers open indefinitely.

Carry both v1 tolerances now, with the compensation that makes them honest:
503 runtime_reconciliation_required deletes the entry and marks the drain
unproven, and the two v2 monitor-loop stops settle runtime_lost rather than
stop_requested when it is. Other refusals still throw; there is no cascade to
hand those to.

Witness: a v2 settle_resources close whose held-Runtime release rejects 503
must answer 200, delete the entry, and stop the loop with runtime_lost.
Red before (expected 200, got 503), green after. Forcing stopSettle back to
stop_requested kills the test on the runtime_lost assertion, so the
compensation is pinned and not merely present.

hosted-harness-session 717/717 (full file, run alone), hook+mcp 208, build rc0
with no type errors, Prettier clean.

* fix(cli): settle a blocked v2 Session on the runtime_lost line

The v2 stopSettle added for R25-1 keyed only off heldDrainUnproven while its
comment claimed it matched the v1 close, which also folds in session.blocked.
A Session whose own settlement already failed never proved to the Runtime that
anything stopped, so certifying stop_requested there writes a terminal run
state that rebuildFromRuntimeLost refuses to recover, and reports a cancelled
task's writer as settled.

The blocked-Session half of this gap predates R25-1 — v2 hardcoded
stop_requested before it — but the parity claim in the comment did not, and
the term belongs here either way. v2 has no heldDrainFailed variable because
that arm throws instead, so the expression is session.blocked ||
heldDrainUnproven.

Witness: a v2 settle_resources close with blocked=true, no held Runtime (so
the drain is trivially proven) and an injected monitor loop must stop the loop
with runtime_lost. Red before on exactly that assertion, green after; the loop
assertion cannot pass vacuously because a failed injection fails the spy check.

* docs(cli): scope the v2 held-Runtime drain to the shapes that reach it

The R24-1 drain reads session.heldRuntimeTurns, and its comment claimed it
covered a Hook-configured turn's background run. No producer registers that
obligation for a Hook turn: finish() calls broker.release() only under
!mcp && !hooks && !cleanupOwed, runtimeHeld is assigned only in that release's
409 runtime_session_held catch, cleanup() returns early on hooks, and every
add() site keys on runtimeHeld or a cleanup hold. So the loop is empty for
that shape and the close still parks on recovery-required.

Comment-only in production. State the reachable scope (a wake turn's held
aftermath, a cleanup hold), say plainly that the Hook shape is not covered,
and record why the load restore keeps its v2 gate: a restored id can be a
deterministic Hook owner, and this drain releases terminally, which would
tombstone the id a reload recomputes.

Pin the producer fact so the drain is not mistaken for a fix of that shape:
with the same fixture and the same 409 mock, the no-hooks turn ends with
runtimeHeld true while the Hook turn never calls release and ends false.
Retitle the R24-1 case to stop claiming the Hook shape; it seeds the
obligation the way the reachable producers do.

Lifting the gap needs a keep-READY drain, deferred to a follow-up: the
terminal release used here cannot stop a deterministic owner's background
run without tombstoning it (R13-1/R14-1).

Tool-turn suite 573/573, the three v2 witnesses green, build rc0 with no type
errors, Prettier clean.

---------

prs.title: refactor(serve): move the restore's worktree reconciliation into a helper
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Part of PR A of the daemon PR state transitions design (`docs/design/2026-11-04-daemon-pr-state-transitions.md`, §4 "Dormant sessions"; earlier steps are #16523, #16530 and #16543). The PR-state watch will restore dormant sessions through the same restore as `POST /session/:id/load` and `/resume`, so that restore has to come out of the route handler. The handler is about 940 lines, so the extraction goes in steps; this is the first, and it changes no behaviour.

The handler's last stage, after the bridge restore and before the response, reconciles the restored session with its worktree sidecar: a legacy sidecar is re-attached best-effort, and a sidecar that records its workspace must prove ownership or the session is released and the restore fails. That stage (about 300 lines) moves verbatim into a module-level function in the same file, `reconcileRestoredSessionWorktree`, which takes everything it used from the handler's closure as explicit inputs. The handler calls it at the same point, under the same live-conversation guard.

- The function's code is the old block statement for statement; the only differences are the indentation, the trailing commas prettier drops when it joins lines, and two in-body comments reworded for the new location.
- Its JSDoc states what a future in-process caller must hold, as the handler does: the worktree ownership lock (taken from the handler's own sidecar read before the bridge restore), the order of a deferred restore question (fired only after this call, discarded on cleanup), and that live-conversation runtimes skip it.
- It stays in `session.ts` on purpose: a new file must import core by submodule, while `server.test.ts` mocks the worktree helpers at core's package root, so a new module would run the real helpers under those tests.

## Why it's needed

The design has the daemon wake a dormant bound session through the same restore the channel accessor uses, so the route and the refresh must share one restore. Moving the worktree stage first, on its own, keeps each step reviewable as a pure move and gives the later extraction a smaller handler to work on.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-worktree-reset.test.ts`: 1,477 passed. These include the load/resume and worktree-classification tests that drive every branch of the moved code (legacy restore, monorepo subdirectory, foreign marker, missing marker, interrupted reset, superseded redirect, corrupt sidecar, relocation rejected or returning another path, active sessions inside and outside the worktree, the deferred Channel question, runtime closing during the sidecar read, and the ownership lock against an in-flight reset).
- Negative control: with the call to `reconcileRestoredSessionWorktree` disabled, more than 30 of those tests fail.
- `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts src/serve/multi-workspace-sessions.test.ts src/serve/routes/`: 3,875 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed — `workspace-channel-management.test.ts` "reports a failure instead of an empty journal when the scope is unreadable", which uses `chmod 000` and fails only because the run was as root.
- Token comparison: the old block and the new function body are identical once whitespace, comments and the trailing commas before a closing parenthesis are removed, and so is the rest of the file apart from the call and one type import.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (refactor; no behaviour change).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node 22.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: low; the move is verbatim and the function is awaited at the same point inside the same `try`, so errors reach the same response mapping and the `finally` still releases the reservation and the lock.
- Not validated / out of scope: the rest of the restore extraction, the in-process caller and its resume hook (later PR A steps). The JSDoc records a pre-existing gap rather than fixing it: the handler decides whether to take the ownership lock from its own sidecar read before the bridge restore, and this stage re-reads the sidecar without checking that it still names the locked checkout, so a sidecar that was missing, legacy or invalid at that earlier read is validated without the lock. Closing it changes behaviour; #16593 does that, and whichever of the two merges second carries the change across (and updates this JSDoc paragraph).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Part of the work designed in #16246 / #16487; follows #16523, #16530 and #16543.

## 本 PR 做了什么

属于 daemon PR 状态转换设计（`docs/design/2026-11-04-daemon-pr-state-transitions.md`，§4「Dormant sessions」）中 PR A 的一部分，前几步是 #16523、#16530 和 #16543。PR 状态监视将通过与 `POST /session/:id/load`、`/resume` 相同的 restore 唤醒休眠会话，所以这段 restore 必须从路由 handler 里拿出来。handler 约 940 行，提取分几步做；这是第一步，不改变任何行为。

- 负向对照：禁用对 `reconcileRestoredSessionWorktree` 的调用后，上述测试有 30 多个失败。
- `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server.test.ts src/serve/multi-workspace-sessions.test.ts src/serve/routes/`：3,875 个通过，1 个跳过，1 个失败。失败的是 `workspace-channel-management.test.ts`「reports a failure instead of an empty journal when the scope is unreadable」，它用 `chmod 000`，只因以 root 运行而失败。

- 主要风险或取舍：低。搬移是原样的，函数在同一个 `try` 内的同一位置被 await，错误走同样的响应映射，`finally` 照常释放预留和锁。

prs.title: fix(ci): report main CI runs a job timeout cancelled
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The main-CI failure tracker now also reports a run GitHub concluded `cancelled`, after separating a job-timeout cancellation from a concurrency supersede by the job annotation. A timed-out run gets rerun whole instead of one-for-one, and the report names the cancelled job and step and says why the run ended.

## Why it's needed

The gate in `main-ci-failure-issue.yml` only admitted `conclusion == 'failure'`. A job that hits its `timeout-minutes` cap caps the whole run as cancelled with no failing job anywhere in it, so that class of breakage produced no report at all — which is how the E2E `sandbox:docker` shard sat red for weeks (#16214). Roughly half of that day's main E2E runs ended cancelled and only the failure-conclusion ones were ever looked at.

The two ways a run ends cancelled need opposite treatment. A concurrency supersede is replaced by the run that cancelled it and owns nothing, so reporting it would file an issue per supersede. A timeout is a real breakage whose only trace is this event.

A timed-out run is only rerun and filed where there is a destination that files: a `main` push, a nightly schedule, or a merged PR. A `workflow_dispatch` whose head resolves to an open PR, a closed-unmerged PR, or no PR at all is neither rerun nor filed, because filing would record a regression for an unmerged head and the rerun would spend `actions: write` for a destination that writes nothing. Such a run is still reported as a comment when it resolves to a PR; when it resolves to no PR there is nowhere to report it and only the step warning remains. The job annotation tells them apart: only a timeout carries "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time". Reads fail open like every other one in that step, and the repeating dedupe marker bounds a misclassified supersede to one comment.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the two touched suites:

```
npx vitest run scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js
node --test .github/scripts/ci/main-failure-signature.test.mjs
```

Then confirm the classification against a run that actually timed out. Run 41743539611 is the one this issue was split from: its `E2E Test (Linux) - sandbox:docker - shard 1/1` job was cancelled at 01:14 after the full 60 minutes.

```
gh api "repos/QwenLM/qwen-code/check-runs/<id>/annotations" --jq '.[].message'
```

Expected: `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1h0m0s`, which is what `cancellation_kind=timeout` selects on. A cancelled run without that annotation (a supersede) selects `superseded=true` and reports nothing.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI workflow change, not user-visible.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only; no workflow run was executed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the annotation read is one API call per cancelled job, bounded by the cancelled jobs in that run. A cancelled run whose annotations cannot be read is reported rather than dropped — a misclassified supersede costs one comment, a dropped timeout costs the regression, which is the direction the existing fail-open reads already take. A timed-out run's whole-run rerun counts as attempt 2 and the next repeat as attempt 3, so an occurrence spends two full matrix reruns before the first report files; that is deliberate, and it is what lets a lane that died on a transient stall clear itself without a human.
- Not validated / out of scope: the workflow itself was not executed end to end. The annotation classification was verified against real cancelled runs through the same commands the step runs, but the rerun, dispatch gates and issue rendering were exercised only by the suite's stubs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16272

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

主 CI 失败追踪现在也会上报 GitHub 结论为 `cancelled` 的运行，并通过 job annotation 区分「超时取消」与「并发取消」。超时的运行改为整轮重跑而不是只重跑失败 job；报告会写明被取消的 job 和步骤，并说明运行为什么结束。

## 为什么需要

`main-ci-failure-issue.yml` 的门条件只接受 `conclusion == 'failure'`。job 撞到 `timeout-minutes` 上限时，整个运行会被标记为 cancelled，而其中没有任何失败的 job，于是这一类故障完全不会产生报告——E2E 的 `sandbox:docker` shard 就是这样红了数周（#16214）。当天 main 上的 E2E 运行约有一半以 cancelled 结束，而只有结论为 failure 的那些被看过。

两种 cancelled 需要相反的处理方式。并发取消会被取消它的那次运行取代、本身不拥有结果，上报它等于每取消一次就开一个 issue；超时则是真实故障，这个事件是它唯一的痕迹。两者的区别在 job annotation 上：只有超时带有 "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time"。读取失败时按开放处理，与该步骤其它读取一致；重复的 dedupe marker 会把误判为超时的并发取消收敛到一条评论。

## 审阅者验证方式

跑两个受影响的测试套件：

```
npx vitest run scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js
node --test .github/scripts/ci/main-ci-failure-signature.test.mjs
```

再用真实超时的运行确认分类。run 41743539611 就是这个 issue 拆分来源：它的 `E2E Test (Linux) - sandbox:docker - shard 1/1` 跑满 60 分钟后于 01:14 被取消。

```
gh api "repos/QwenLM/qwen-code/check-runs/<id>/annotations" --jq '.[].message'
```

预期输出 `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1h0m0s`，这正是 `cancellation_kind=timeout` 的判据。不带该 annotation 的 cancelled 运行（并发取消）会得到 `superseded=true`，不上报。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— CI workflow 改动，非用户可见。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 仅单元测试，未实际执行 workflow。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：annotation 读取按被取消的 job 数量增加 API 调用，上限由该运行的 cancelled job 数决定。读不到 annotation 的 cancelled 运行会选择上报而不是丢弃——误判的并发取消只多一条评论，漏掉的超时则丢掉整个回归，这与此处既有读取的 fail-open 方向一致。超时运行的整轮重跑算作新的运行，因此重复超时会转而 filing 而不是无限重跑，这是有意为之。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：workflow 未端到端执行。annotation 分类用与步骤相同的命令对真实 cancelled 运行验证过，但重跑、调度门和 issue 渲染只由测试套件的桩覆盖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #16272

</details>

prs.title: fix(web-shell): gate the automatic recap on general.showSessionRecap
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Web Shell's automatic session recap now reads the two `general` settings that describe it. It fires only when `general.showSessionRecap` is on, and it waits out the number of minutes set in `general.sessionRecapAwayThresholdMinutes` instead of a hardcoded 3. The manual `/recap` command is unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Both settings already render in the companion's settings panel, so flipping either one wrote a value nothing read. The result was a panel that described a feature it could not control: a user who turned session recap off still got an automatic model call on every return to the tab, and a raised away threshold did nothing. `docs/design/session-recap/session-recap-design.md` gates the automatic trigger on `general.showSessionRecap`, default off, specifically so an ambient model call is never started without the user opting in.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open the Web Shell with the daemon serving a session that has at least four transcript blocks.
2. In Settings, leave "Show Session Recap" off. Switch away from the tab for more than the threshold (default 5 minutes, or whatever `general.sessionRecapAwayThresholdMinutes` is set to) and come back: no `Recap: …` line is appended.
3. Turn the setting on and repeat: the recap appears on the next return, and a return before the threshold appends nothing.
4. From the running tab, change the threshold in Settings and confirm the next away period uses the new value without a reload.

Automated coverage: `npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t 'ecap|falls back to 5 minutes'` — 22 passed (the whole file is 1442); `-t "recap"` is case-sensitive and selects only the 19 pre-existing cases. The new case mounts with the setting off, turns it on through a re-render, and asserts the next return fires; removing `showSessionRecap` from the effect's dependency array turns it red.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Not captured. This is a user-visible behaviour change and the section should hold a before/after recording of the two states described above; it is empty because the run that produced the current head only had a unit-test environment. Treat the automated cases as the evidence until a recording is added — a maintainer deciding from this section is deciding from nothing.

### Tested on

|            OS             | Status |
| :-----------------------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS                 |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows                |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux                 |   ⚠️   |

Only macOS was run locally. CI covers the rest.

### Environment (optional)

`npm run dev` in `packages/web-shell` against a mock daemon, plus the package's Vitest suite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the trigger now also requires a new block count of at least 4 and an idle session, which is unchanged, so the only behaviour change is the gate and the threshold. A user who had recap working now gets no recap until they turn the setting on — that is the intent, but it is a visible change for anyone who relied on the untracked default.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full `App.test.tsx` suite was not run to completion; only the `recap` filter (19 tests) and the new case were. `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports 110 errors on `main` and the same 110 with this diff, so the change adds none, but the typecheck is not clean and was not made clean here. Windows and Linux were not run locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Both settings already existed; this makes them effective.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13911

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Web Shell 的自动会话回顾现在会读取描述它的两个 `general` 设置：只有 `general.showSessionRecap` 打开时才触发，并且等待 `general.sessionRecapAwayThresholdMinutes` 配置的分钟数，而不是写死的 3 分钟。手动的 `/recap` 命令不变。

## 为什么需要

这两个设置本来就会渲染在配套网页的设置面板里，所以改动它们的值写进去却没有任何代码读取。结果是一个描述了自己无法控制的功能的面板：关掉会话回顾的用户，每次切回标签页仍会触发一次自动模型调用；调高离开阈值的用户也没有任何效果。`docs/design/session-recap/session-recap-design.md` 要求自动触发必须由 `general.showSessionRecap`（默认关闭）门控，正是为了在用户没有明确选择加入时绝不发起环境性的模型调用。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 打开 Web Shell，让守护进程提供一个至少包含四条转录块的会话。
2. 在设置里保持「显示会话回顾」关闭。切走超过阈值（默认 5 分钟，或 `general.sessionRecapAwayThresholdMinutes` 设置的值）再切回：不会追加 `Recap: …` 行。
3. 打开该设置后重复：下一次返回会出现回顾，未达阈值的返回不会追加任何内容。
4. 在已打开的标签页里修改阈值，确认下一次离开按新值生效，且不需要刷新。

自动化覆盖：`npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t 'ecap|falls back to 5 minutes'` —— 22 项通过（整个文件 1442 项）；`-t "recap"` 区分大小写，只选中原有的 19 项。新增用例在设置关闭状态下挂载，通过一次重渲染打开设置，并断言下一次返回会触发；把 `showSessionRecap` 从 effect 的依赖数组里删掉后该用例变红。

### 证据（改前 / 改后）

未提供。这是用户可见的行为变更，本节应放上面两种状态的改前/改后录屏；目前为空，是因为产出当前 head 的那次运行只有单元测试环境。在补上录屏之前，请把自动化用例当作证据 —— 单凭这一节做判断的维护者实际上没有可判断的内容。

### 测试平台

|      操作系统      | 状态 |
| :---------------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS         |  ✅  |

prs.title: fix(core): skip managed auto-memory extraction when every write tool is denied
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Managed auto-memory extraction now checks whether both write tools are denied before it forks the extractor agent, and records a `writes_denied` skip instead of running a fork that is guaranteed to save nothing. The check treats only bare tool-name rules as a blanket deny; a rule with a path specifier (`edit(src/**)`) constrains one path and is left to the scoped agent, which re-decides each write.

## Why it's needed

In non-interactive runs the CLI adds `write_file` and `edit` to the deny list for `default` and `auto` approval, because there is no UI to answer a prompt. The managed memory agents are forked from a Config that inherits that deny list, and the scoped memory permission manager merges the base verdict in with `mergePermissionDecision`, where `deny` outranks the scoped `allow`. So the extractor is forked, reads the transcript, spends its token budget, and then has every save refused.

Reported in #15597: 19 of 19 memory writes denied over six runs, 143K–234K extractor tokens per run, and an empty project `MEMORY.md`. The run is slow and pure cost with no possible durable result, so the fix is to not start it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reproduce on `main`: run `qwen --approval-mode auto --output-format json -p "For this project, always use pnpm instead of npm, and run tests with vitest. Please remember that. Reply with OK."` and inspect `stats.tools.byName.write_file` — every call is denied and `memory/MEMORY.md` stays empty. With this branch the same run reports the extraction as skipped for `writes_denied` and never forks the extractor.

A reviewer can confirm the two halves directly:
- `packages/core/src/memory/write-access.test.ts` pins the rule classifier: aliases (`Write`, `Edit`, `WriteFileTool`, `replace`) count, specifier rules and MCP names do not, and both tools must be denied.
- `packages/core/src/memory/extract.test.ts` pins the effect: with `['run_shell_command', 'write_file', 'edit']` the extractor is never called and the cursor is untouched; with only `write_file` denied extraction still runs.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible output changes, only whether a background agent is forked.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, run from `packages/core`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the gate is deliberately conservative — it only fires when a bare rule denies *both* write tools. A deny list that leaves one write tool usable still runs extraction, so the only behavior change is the case that could never have saved anything. The cursor is not advanced on the skip, so turns stay owed and are picked up if the caller later allows writes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the two other memory agents (remember, dream) share the same inherited deny list and have the same failure mode; this PR covers extraction, which is the one that runs on every turn and was the reported cost. Widening to the remaining agents is a follow-up, not a change in this diff.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `writes_denied` is an additive member of the existing skip-reason union and the matching telemetry enum.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15597

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

托管自动记忆的抽取（extraction）在 fork 出抽取 agent 之前，先检查两个写工具是否都被整体拒绝；如果是，就记录一个 `writes_denied` 的跳过，而不是启动一次注定什么都存不下来的 fork。这个检查只把「裸工具名」规则当作整体拒绝；带路径 specifier 的规则（如 `edit(src/**)`）只约束某一个路径，仍然交由 scoped agent 在每次写入时自行判定。

## 为什么需要

在非交互模式下，`default` 和 `auto` 审批会把 `write_file` 和 `edit` 加入拒绝列表，因为没有 UI 可以回答授权提示。托管记忆 agent 由继承了这份拒绝列表的 Config fork 出来，而 scoped memory 的权限管理器在 `mergePermissionDecision` 里合并基础判定时，`deny` 的优先级高于 scoped 的 `allow`。结果是抽取器被 fork 出来、读了 transcript、花掉了 token，然后每一次写入都被拒绝。

#15597 里记录的现象：六次运行中 19 次记忆写入全部被拒，每次运行抽取器消耗 143K–234K token，项目 `MEMORY.md` 始终为空。这类运行既慢又是纯成本，不可能产生任何可持久化的结果，所以正确的做法是干脆不启动它。

### 如何验证

在 `main` 上复现：运行 `qwen --approval-mode auto --output-format json -p "For this project, always use pnpm instead of npm, and run tests with vitest. Please remember that. Reply with OK."`，然后查看 `stats.tools.byName.write_file`——每次调用都被拒绝，`memory/MEMORY.md` 保持为空。在这个分支上，同样的运行会把抽取记为因 `writes_denied` 跳过，并且不会再 fork 抽取器。

评审可以直接确认两部分：
- `packages/core/src/memory/write-access.test.ts` 钉住规则分类：别名（`Write`、`Edit`、`WriteFileTool`、`replace`）算，带 specifier 的规则和 MCP 名称不算，且必须两个工具都被拒绝。
- `packages/core/src/memory/extract.test.ts` 钉住实际效果：拒绝列表为 `['run_shell_command', 'write_file', 'edit']` 时抽取器完全不会被调用且 cursor 不变；只有 `write_file` 被拒时抽取照常运行。

### 证据（改前 / 改后）

不适用——没有用户可见输出变化，只是后台 agent 是否会启动。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

只跑了单元测试，在 `packages/core` 目录下。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：这个门禁刻意保守——只有一条裸规则同时拒绝两个写工具时才会触发。只要还留下一个可用的写工具，抽取就照常运行，所以唯一的行为变化是那种本来就不可能存下任何东西的情况。跳过时不会推进 cursor，因此这些轮次仍然「欠着」，如果调用方之后允许写入会被重新处理。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：另外两个记忆 agent（remember、dream）共用同一份继承来的拒绝列表，存在同样的失效模式；本 PR 只覆盖 extraction，因为它是每轮都会跑、也是被报告的那部分成本。推广到其余 agent 属于后续工作，不在本 diff 内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。`writes_denied` 是既有 skip-reason 联合类型和对应 telemetry 枚举的新增成员。

## 关联 issue

Refs #15597

</details>

prs.title: feat(channels): add Microsoft Teams extension and host ingress
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Microsoft Teams channel extension for personal conversations, explicit group mentions, channel-thread isolation and ordered final-text replies. It supports standalone operation and an application host using the same protocol code.

Hosts can call `createTeamsIngress(name, credentials, acceptInbound)` without constructing a bridge, router, channel or listener. It returns only `handleWebhook`; the Microsoft SDK authenticates and normalizes each Activity, and success waits for acceptance. TeamsChannel delegates to the same verification path. Execution and send hooks remain separate from HTTP ingress.

## Why it's needed

Teams users lack a native channel provider. Application hosts need durable acceptance and ownership checks without copying Teams protocol logic or modifying inference core.

## Reviewer Test Plan

- Verify private messages and trusted bot mentions execute; ordinary group text, wrong bot/tenant, bad serviceUrl, and invalid signature/audience/issuer/expiry do not.
- Set another bot's `Connections__*` environment registry: explicit Teams credentials must remain authoritative, including audience and issuer validation.
- Block or reject the acceptance callback. HTTP success must wait, and persistence failure must be retryable. Original actor/thread/target must survive concurrent requests.
- Verify exact-event cancellation and revocation suppress output, including empty/oversized completed results. These results become bounded notices through the ordinary ChannelBase cancellation and send path.
- Base 0.23.0 supports hosted operation only; 0.26.1 supports standalone and hosted operation. One physical host-provided base instance is required.
- Run the actual release script for a new version, pack/install the manifests together, and confirm the current exact base peer follows the release while the tested legacy peer remains supported.

### Evidence

Focused package tests, repository build/typecheck/bundle, release-script tests and independent compiled SDK/Fastify verification are reported in the verification comment for the current source revision. Independent checks cover the new ingress on both supported base versions, existing channel behavior, completed-result/cancellation races, and an actual release consumer installation.

JWT tests use temporary RSA keys and local JWKS lookup through the real SDK verifier. Connector/UserToken clients are controlled recorders. This demonstrates protocol and host behavior, not live tenant delivery.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| macOS | Local build, package, SDK/host and release-consumer verification |
| Windows | Local verification not performed |
| Linux | CI results are recorded separately |

Node 22.23.1, Microsoft Agents SDK 1.9.1, Fastify 5.11.3.

## Risk & Scope

- Standalone scheduling/dedup is in memory. Durable acceptance, execution recovery and delivery retry policy belong to the host. The standalone ingress itself neither queues nor deduplicates.
- No changes to inference core, ChannelBase or built-in provider registration. Publication and registry inclusion remain maintainer decisions. Untested base versions are not declared compatible.
- Not validated: real tenant app installation, Microsoft JWKS/Connector network, actual agent tools, and end-to-end CLI extension loading. The global CLI baseline was unavailable; built CLI smoke is tracked separately. National clouds, attachments, Graph history, cards and scheduled delivery are outside this proposal.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/teams-channel/docs/design/teams-channel.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/teams-channel/docs/design/teams-channel.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Refs #15618. This remains a draft proposal; it is not merged or published.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

通用 Teams 扩展支持私聊、群显式 @、帖子隔离和顺序文本回复。新增独立 `createTeamsIngress`，无需临时 Bridge/Router/Channel，也不启动监听器；同一 SDK 验签路径等待宿主接收完成再 ACK。显式认证连接隔离宿主环境配置，空白/超长确定结果沿正常取消与发送保护处理，发版脚本同步当前 base peer 并保留已验证 legacy peer。

持久化、恢复与重试策略归宿主；插件不绑定特定应用或数据库。未改推理核心、ChannelBase 或内置注册表。合成 SDK/Fastify、取消竞态和实际包安装证据与真实 Teams 租户验收分别记录；维护者接受、合并和正式发布仍待完成。

</details>
