prs.title: feat(cli): support operator-pending find and line motions in vim mode
prs.body:
## What this PR does

In vim normal mode, the delete, change and yank operators now compose with the find motions (`t`, `f`, `T`, `F`) and with the line-boundary motions (`$`, `0`, `^`), and the resulting edits repeat with dot. Before this change those key sequences silently cancelled the pending operator and only moved the cursor, so `d` followed by any of them was a no-op edit. `d$` and `c$` delete what the already-working `D` and `C` delete and end in the same mode, `y$` yanks to the end of the line, and a change lands in insert mode with the cursor where the deleted text started.

## Why it's needed

These are some of the most frequently used edits in vim, and the failure mode is the worst kind: the editor accepts the keystrokes, moves the cursor, and deletes nothing, which reads as success. Users have to discover by trial and error that a whole family of edits is missing. The engine already composed operators with word motions, the doubled line forms and the uppercase end-of-line forms, so this fills in the remaining motions that share that same machinery rather than adding a new subsystem — including dot-repeat, which now replays them from the current cursor position.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Enable vim mode with `/vim`, then on a line such as `hello world, again` with the cursor on `w`:

- `dt,` deletes up to but not including the comma, leaving `hello w, again`; `df,` deletes through the comma, leaving `hello w again`. `c` behaves the same and ends in insert mode; `T`/`F` do the same backwards, excluding and including the found character respectively.
- `d$` from mid-line deletes exactly what `D` deletes, and lands on the last remaining character. `d0` deletes back to the start of the line. `d^` deletes back to the first non-blank, and when the cursor is inside the indentation it deletes just the indentation.
- `y$` followed by `p` duplicates the rest of the line, and the yank leaves the cursor where it was.
- `.` repeats the last one of these from wherever the cursor now is.
- A motion that finds nothing — `dtz` on a line without a `z` — deletes nothing and does not replace what `.` will replay afterwards. It also leaves the yank register and the system clipboard untouched, so pressing `d$` twice at end of line does not wipe what you copied.
- Repeating a find with a count works (`d2tc` deletes to the second `c`), and a count that cannot be satisfied deletes nothing rather than stopping early.
- Pressing Escape after `dt` but before the target character cancels cleanly.
- A delete that consumes the end of the line leaves the cursor on the last remaining character, so the next edit stays on that line.

On the released build every one of these only moves the cursor.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for screenshots — I had no way to drive and capture the interactive UI on this machine. What I do have: 35 new unit tests that drive the key handler keystroke by keystroke against a buffer that really applies the edits, so they assert on the resulting text and cursor position rather than on which helper was called. With the source change reverted, 27 of those 35 fail and no pre-existing test fails. A final test drives the buffer reducer directly to pin where the cursor lands after the range deletions. I also built the CLI from source and used it by hand.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

The change is key handling and range arithmetic over the existing buffer primitives, with no platform-specific code; the unit tests run in CI on all three.

### Environment

Local build from source (`npm run build && npm run bundle`, and `npm run dev` while iterating).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: an operator now survives the keypress that starts a find, waiting for the target character. Sequences that previously cancelled the operator (`d` then `f`) now wait and then edit. That is the fix, but it is the behaviour change to look at hardest. Backward deletes are exclusive of the cursor and forward finds follow vim's inclusive/exclusive split, which is where any disagreement will show up.
- Not validated / out of scope: visual mode; text objects such as `di"` and `ci(`; `;` and `,` after an operator plus find; the same empty-motion guard on the doubled line forms, which has always overwritten the register when it deleted nothing; and a count before a bare find motion, where the existing motion path applies its adjustment inside the count loop and so ignores the count — meaning `2tc` and `d2tc` do not agree today. Converging those two loops is a separate change that fixes a pre-existing bug. Three behaviours that were already like this before the change are left alone: a count with `$` (`3d$` deletes only the current line's tail, exactly as `3D` already does), a count before `d0` (since `0` doubles as a count digit), and find targets outside the basic multilingual plane such as emoji, which also affects the existing find and replace-character commands.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No settings, no new keybindings, and no change to any sequence that already did something useful.

## Linked Issues

Related, not closed by this change: #844 concerns dot-repeat in this same editor, and #2779 asks for visual mode.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

**本 PR 做了什么**

在 vim 普通模式下，delete、change、yank 三个操作符现在可以与查找移动（`t`、`f`、`T`、`F`）以及行边界移动（`$`、`0`、`^`）组合使用，并且这些编辑可以用 `.` 重复。此前这些按键序列会静默取消待定操作符、只移动光标，因此 `d` 后接这些键等于一次空操作。`d$` 与 `c$` 删除的内容与已经可用的 `D`、`C` 一致并结束在相同模式；`y$` 复制到行尾；change 会进入插入模式，光标停在被删文本的起始位置。

**为什么需要**

这些是 vim 中最常用的编辑之一，而它的失败方式最糟：编辑器接受按键、移动光标、却什么都不删，看起来像成功了。用户只能靠反复试错才发现这一整类编辑是缺失的。引擎本已支持操作符与词移动、重复的行级形式、以及大写的行尾形式组合，因此本 PR 是补全共用同一套机制的其余移动，而不是新增一个子系统——包括 `.` 重复，它会从当前光标位置重放这些编辑。

**如何验证**

用 `/vim` 开启 vim 模式，在 `hello world, again` 这样一行上把光标放在 `w`：`dt,` 删除到逗号之前但不含逗号，得到 `hello w, again`；`df,` 连逗号一起删，得到 `hello w again`。`c` 同理并在插入模式结束；`T`/`F` 向后同理，分别排除与包含找到的字符。行中间的 `d$` 删除的内容与 `D` 完全相同，光标停在剩下的最后一个字符上；`d0` 删到行首；`d^` 删到第一个非空白字符，且当光标位于缩进内时只删除缩进。`y$` 后接 `p` 会复制行内剩余部分，且 yank 不移动光标。`.` 从当前位置重放上一次同类编辑。找不到目标字符的移动（例如行内没有 `z` 时的 `dtz`）什么都不删，也不会改变 `.` 将要重放的内容；同时不会改动 yank 寄存器与系统剪贴板，因此在行尾连按两次 `d$` 不会清掉你复制的内容。带 count 的重复查找有效（`d2tc` 删到第二个 `c`），而无法满足的 count 什么都不删而不会提前停下。在 `dt` 之后、目标字符之前按 Escape 可干净取消。删除吃掉行尾时，光标停在剩下的最后一个字符上，下一次编辑仍留在该行。在上述已发布版本中，这些操作都只移动光标。

**证据**：没有截图——本机无法驱动并录制交互式界面。有的是 35 个新增单元测试，逐键驱动按键处理器，并使用会真正应用编辑的 buffer，因此断言的是结果文本与光标位置，而不是调用了哪个 helper。回退源码改动后，35 个中有 27 个失败，且没有任何既有测试失败。另有一个测试直接驱动 buffer reducer，钉住范围删除后光标的落点。我还从源码构建并手工使用了 CLI。

**风险与范围**

主要权衡：操作符现在会跨过发起查找的那次按键而保留，等待目标字符。此前会取消操作符的序列（先 `d` 再 `f`）现在会等待并随后编辑——这正是修复本身，但也是最需要审视的行为变化。向后删除不含光标所在字符，向前查找遵循 vim 的 inclusive/exclusive 划分，分歧最可能出现在这里。

未验证或超出范围：visual mode；`di"`、`ci(` 等文本对象；操作符加查找之后的 `;` 与 `,`；重复行级形式上的同一空移动保护（它在删除为空时一直都会覆写寄存器）；以及裸查找移动前的 count——既有移动路径在 count 循环内部施加调整，因而忽略 count，这意味着 `2tc` 与 `d2tc` 目前并不一致；把这两个循环收敛是另一个修复既有 bug 的改动。另有三项在变更前就如此、本次不改动：带 count 的 `$`（`3d$` 只删当前行的行尾，与既有 `3D` 相同）、`d0` 前的 count（因为 `0` 同时是 count 数字）、以及基本多文种平面之外的查找目标（如 emoji），这同样影响既有的查找与单字符替换命令。

破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有新增设置，没有新增键位，也不会改变任何原本已有效用的按键序列。

</details>

## What this PR does

Pins background activity separately from held work at the third snapshot and registers cleanup for two prototype spies. The first spy previously retained later call records.

## Why it's needed

The bridge reports running background tasks independently from its busy state. Regressions in that distinction and retained spy call records need direct coverage.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. With background tasks running and no holds, confirm the snapshot reports running tasks, no active prompt, an idle session state and an idle aggregate.
2. Confirm the admission spy is restored before the next test.

At `07f9f6b` on Windows, all 16 focused tests pass, and the snapshot test passes in eight separate processes. Three production mutations trigger their expected assertions; deleting the aggregate assertion lets its corresponding mutation pass. A temporary cleanup witness passes with the first spy's hook and fails without it. All temporary changes were restored.

The ACP bridge and its dependencies build successfully. Bridge type checking, targeted ESLint and Prettier checks pass. The complete test file has 1,021 passing tests and one failure at symbolic link creation (`EPERM`), also reproduced by a plain Node filesystem probe.

N/A — changes are confined to tests.

Windows; Node 24.19.0; pnpm 11.24.0; package Vitest configuration.

prs.title: feat(desktop): post macOS turn notifications from the desktop host
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On the packaged macOS desktop, the Web Shell now delivers turn notifications as native system notifications posted by the desktop host itself: when it detects the macOS desktop shell and that Web Notifications are not granted, it triggers the new `show_turn_notification` Tauri command, and the Rust host posts the notification through `UNUserNotificationCenter`. Host notification authorization is requested once at app launch. The Task notifications toggle and status now reflect the host preference in the macOS desktop shell, because the Web Notification permission can never be granted there. Plain browsers and non-macOS desktop shells keep the standard Web Notification path unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Task notifications could not be enabled in Qwen Code Desktop on macOS (#15109). WKWebView never grants Web Notification permission to the embedded web shell, and no host API can make it grant one: this was verified against macOS 26.6.2 / WebKit 624.2.5 — the `WKWebsiteInfoStore`/website-access APIs referenced by web-notification write-ups do not exist in the runtime, and `Notification.requestPermission()` still resolves to `denied` even with host `UNUserNotificationCenter` authorization granted and WebKit's internal notification settings enabled. As a result, the Task notifications panel showed "Notifications are blocked" with a permanently disabled Allow button, and the toggle could not stick on.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Build and launch the desktop app on macOS from this branch (the existing `packages/desktop` Tauri build flow; the app posts host notifications on first launch and shows the OS authorization prompt once).
2. Before this PR, hovering the bell (Task notifications) control shows "Notifications are blocked. Allow them in your browser site settings." with a disabled Allow button; after this PR, clicking Allow turns the setting on and keeps it on, and the status shows enabled.
3. Unfocus the app (or switch to another tab), send a prompt, and let the turn finish. Expected: a native macOS notification with the app icon, a title like "<App> · <session title>", and a body with the turn status plus prompt/reply excerpts. Observed: as expected (screenshot below).
4. Negative checks: no notification is posted while the app is focused; turning the toggle off stops notifications; in a plain browser (or a non-macOS desktop shell) the standard Web Notification behavior is unchanged.
5. Unit tests cover the new paths: `browser-turn-notifications.test.tsx` (macOS desktop shell keeps the toggle on when WebKit denies and delivers through the host; non-macOS desktop shell keeps the standard path; granted permission prefers Web Notifications over the host) and `BrowserNotificationControl.test.tsx` (enabled status in the macOS desktop shell when Web Notifications are denied).

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (macOS Desktop, 0.26.x): the Task notifications panel reports the permission as blocked and the Allow button is disabled, because WKWebView never grants the permission.

![Before: Task notifications panel with "Notifications are blocked" and a disabled Allow button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/fa395904d209deccfa22e8ec4043ca3c0e041ce4/01-before-blocked-panel.png)

After (this PR): the toggle stays on and the desktop host posts the native system notification for a finished turn.

![After: native macOS notification posted by the desktop host](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4ekuct25/qwen-code/fa395904d209deccfa22e8ec4043ca3c0e041ce4/02-after-host-toast.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ |

### Environment

macOS 26.6.2, packaged desktop (Tauri) built on the merged upstream/main with the web shell served by the bundled daemon; the web-shell unit/type/lint gates were verified in Docker (node:22-bookworm).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: desktop-shell platform detection uses the WebKit user agent (`macintosh`/`mac os x`); a future WebKit UA change could hide the macOS host path, in which case the app degrades to today's behavior (no notifications) rather than failing. The Rust command is macOS-gated (`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`) and a no-op on other platforms.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Windows/WebView2 half of #15109 (the host command is a no-op there and the Web Shell keeps the standard Web Notification path); Linux host notifications; click-to-focus on host-posted notifications is not wired.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15109

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在打包的 macOS 桌面应用中，Web Shell 现在通过桌面宿主自行发布的原生系统通知来传递回合通知：当它检测到 macOS 桌面壳且 Web Notifications 未获授权时，会触发新的 `show_turn_notification` Tauri 命令，由 Rust 宿主通过 `UNUserNotificationCenter` 发布通知。应用启动时请求一次宿主通知授权。由于 Web Notification 权限在 macOS 桌面壳中永远无法被授予，Task notifications 开关和状态现在直接反映宿主设置。普通浏览器和非 macOS 桌面壳保持标准的 Web Notification 路径不变。

## 为什么需要

在 macOS 上，Qwen Code Desktop 的 Task notifications 无法开启（#15109）。WKWebView 永远不会向内嵌 web shell 授予 Web Notification 权限，也不存在任何宿主 API 能让它授予：这一点已在 macOS 26.6.2 / WebKit 624.2.5 上验证——网络资料中提到的 `WKWebsiteInfoStore`/网站访问 API 在运行时中并不存在；即使宿主已获得 `UNUserNotificationCenter` 授权且 WebKit 内部通知设置已启用，`Notification.requestPermission()` 仍解析为 `denied`。因此 Task notifications 面板显示 "Notifications are blocked"，Allow 按钮一直被禁用，开关也无法保持开启。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在本分支上构建并在 macOS 上启动桌面应用（使用现有的 `packages/desktop` Tauri 构建流程；应用启动时会请求宿主通知授权，并首次弹出系统授权提示）。
2. 本 PR 之前，将鼠标悬停在铃铛（Task notifications）控件上会显示 "Notifications are blocked. Allow them in your browser site settings."，且 Allow 按钮被禁用；本 PR 之后，点击 Allow 会开启设置并保持开启，状态显示已启用。
3. 取消应用聚焦（或切换到其他标签页），发送一条提示并等待回合完成。预期：出现带应用图标的原生 macOS 通知，标题形如 "<应用> · <会话标题>"，正文包含回合状态以及提示/回复摘录。实际：与预期一致（见下图）。
4. 反向检查：应用聚焦时不发布通知；关闭开关后通知停止；在普通浏览器（或非 macOS 桌面壳）中，标准 Web Notification 行为不变。
5. 单元测试覆盖新路径：`browser-turn-notifications.test.tsx`（macOS 桌面壳中 WebKit 拒绝时开关保持开启并经宿主投递；非 macOS 桌面壳保持标准路径；已授权时优先 Web Notifications 而非宿主）和 `BrowserNotificationControl.test.tsx`（macOS 桌面壳中 Web Notifications 被拒时的启用状态）。

### 证据（前后对比）

之前（macOS Desktop，0.26.x）：Task notifications 面板报告权限被阻止，Allow 按钮被禁用，因为 WKWebView 永远不会授予该权限。

（见上方 Before 截图）

之后（本 PR）：开关保持开启，桌面宿主为已完成的回合发布原生系统通知。

（见上方 After 截图）

### 测试平台

|     操作系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ |

### 环境

macOS 26.6.2，基于合并后的 upstream/main 构建的打包桌面（Tauri），web shell 由内置 daemon 提供；web-shell 单测/类型/lint 门禁在 Docker（node:22-bookworm）中验证。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：桌面壳平台检测使用 WebKit 用户代理（`macintosh`/`mac os x`）；未来 WebKit UA 变化可能隐藏 macOS 宿主路径，届时应用回退到当前行为（无通知）而不是出错。Rust 命令带 macOS 门控（`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`），在其他平台上是空操作。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：#15109 的 Windows/WebView2 部分（宿主命令在那里是空操作，Web Shell 保持标准 Web Notification 路径）；Linux 宿主通知；宿主发布通知的点击聚焦未接入。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15109

</details>

prs.title: fix(memory): back off after a failed auto dream
prs.body:
## What this PR does When an automatic project dream fails, it now records the failure time in the project's memory metadata. The scheduler reads that marker and backs off from relaunching the dream for one hour after a failure, mirroring the existing backoff used for user-scoped dreams. A user-cancelled dream is treated as a cancellation, not a failure, so it does not trigger the backoff. ## Why it's needed Refs #15018: a failed automatic dream left no trace in the project's metadata, so the very next turn saw the same stale state and launched another dream. The issue reports this repeating on every later turn. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify Trigger an automatic project dream that fails (for example, by having the dream agent throw, or by hitting its turn cap), then take another action in the same project within an hour. Before this change, the next turn relaunches the dream immediately. After this change, it is skipped with reason `failure_backoff` until an hour has passed since the failed attempt, after which a new dream can run again. Cancelling an in-flight dream instead of letting it fail should not trigger this backoff. ### Evidence (Before & After) N/A — no user-facing UI change. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ✅ | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ | | 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ | ### Environment (optional) Unit tests only (Vitest), no interactive runtime needed. Ran `npx vitest run packages/core/src/memory/manager.test.ts`: all 159 tests pass, including a new regression test that schedules a dream, fails it 70 minutes later, confirms a retry 30 minutes after the failure is skipped with `failure_backoff`, and confirms a retry after the backoff window runs again. Also ran the new test alone against the pre-fix code to confirm it fails there (RED), then confirmed it passes on this branch (GREEN). A separate existing test already checks that a user-cancelled dream still ends with status `cancelled`; it now also asserts the cancellation leaves no failure marker in the metadata. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: the one-hour backoff window is a fixed value, matching the existing user-dream backoff; a future tuning pass could make it configurable. - Not validated / out of scope: the issue's other two asks (a deterministic coverage cursor for consolidation, and reporting when a run hits the turn cap) are separate follow-up work, not covered by this PR. - Breaking changes / migration notes: none. This only adds a new optional metadata field and a new skip reason. ## Linked Issues Refs #15018
中文说明 当自动项目回忆（dream）失败时，现在会在项目的记忆元数据中记录失败时间。调度器会读取这个标记，并在失败后的一小时内不再重新启动该回忆，这与现有的用户级回忆的退避机制保持一致。用户主动取消的回忆被视为取消，而不是失败，因此不会触发这个退避。 Refs #15018：一次失败的自动回忆没有在项目元数据中留下任何痕迹，导致紧接着的下一轮对话看到的还是同样的旧状态，于是又触发了一次回忆。issue 报告称这会在之后的每一轮重复发生。 **如何验证**：触发一次失败的自动项目回忆（例如让回忆代理抛出异常，或达到其轮次上限），然后在一小时内对同一项目执行其他操作。修改前，下一轮会立即重新启动回忆。修改后，会以 `failure_backoff` 原因跳过，直到失败后过了一小时，之后才能再次启动新的回忆。如果是主动取消而不是失败，则不应触发这个退避。 **测试**：运行 `npx vitest run packages/core/src/memory/manager.test.ts`，全部 159 个测试通过，其中包含一个新的回归测试：调度一次回忆，70 分钟后使其失败，确认失败后 30 分钟内的重试会以 `failure_backoff` 被跳过，并确认退避窗口过后的重试可以正常运行。同时在修复前的代码上单独运行了这个新测试以确认它会失败（RED），再确认它在本分支上通过（GREEN）。另有一个已有测试检查用户取消的回忆仍以 `cancelled` 状态结束，现在还额外断言取消不会在元数据中留下失败标记。 **范围之外**：issue 中提到的另外两点（为整理过程增加确定性的覆盖游标，以及在达到轮次上限时报告该状态）属于后续工作，不在本 PR 范围内。

prs.title: fix(core): replay the persisted startup prelude on resume
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A resumed session now replays the exact startup prelude it originally sent instead of rebuilding it from the current date, directory tree, git snapshot, MCP instructions, skills, and deferred-tool list. The prelude is persisted as a system record when a session starts or rebuilds it, recovery keeps the latest record and places it as the first API-history entry, and a session that already has the saved prelude no longer builds a second one.

This keeps the first user message byte-identical across resume, so an implicit prefix cache can reuse the conversation history instead of stopping at the system prompt.

## Why it's needed

When a session is resumed, the client rebuilds the startup prelude in front of the saved turns. The rebuilt prelude contains fresh workspace data, so the first user message differs from the one the previous process sent. With vLLM-style implicit prefix caching, the reusable prefix ends at that first difference.

A reported 417k-token conversation reused only about 14k tokens of KV cache and recomputed about 186k tokens, producing a 126-second time to first token. The stored transcript's first user record is the real prompt; it has no startup prelude, so a resumed process had nothing to replay.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused regression tests; all should pass on the branch:

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/core/environmentContext.test.ts -t "reuses a stored startup prelude"
npx vitest run src/services/session-api-history.test.ts -t "startup context replay"
npx vitest run src/core/client.test.ts -t "records a generated startup prelude"
```

To see the regression, temporarily remove the saved-prelude reuse and the startup-context recovery branch (or stash the implementation) and rerun the same tests. Before the fix, the first test rebuilds a fresh prelude in front of the saved turns and the second drops the saved prelude entirely; both fail.

For a real session, start a new conversation with the branch and `--openai-logging`, complete a few turns, exit, and resume. The first request's `messages[0]` should be identical to the pre-resume request's first message, and the provider's cached-token count should include the conversation history rather than only the system prompt.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — this is a core session-recovery change with unit-level evidence.

Before the fix, the two focused tests failed:

```
environmentContext: reuses a stored startup prelude -> 1 failed
session-api-history: startup context replay -> 1 failed
```

After the fix, they pass. Full local runs:

```
client.test.ts                      624 passed
environmentContext.test.ts          116 passed
session-api-history.test.ts          63 passed
chatRecordingService.test.ts        191 passed
session-transcript-reader.test.ts   152 passed
transcript-records validation        48 passed
ACP targeted test                     1 passed
```

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | ⚠️ not tested |
| Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| Linux | ✅ tested (Node 26.8.1, packages/core vitest) |

### Environment

Local Node 26.8.1 with `npx vitest` from `packages/core`; core `tsc --noEmit`, Prettier, and ESLint pass. The full CLI build and a live vLLM prefix-cache run were not executed in this environment.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the saved prelude keeps the original date and git/MCP/skills snapshot. Date freshness still comes from the existing history-derived tail reminder. The git snapshot is intentionally frozen at session start; the model can run `git status` for current state.
- Not validated / out of scope: full CLI build and live vLLM E2E; divergence caused by changes in the system prompt or tool declarations is a separate part of the broader context-immutability issue. Managed-session journals that cannot carry the new record fall back to rebuilding the prelude.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: sessions recorded before this change have no saved prelude. Their first resume rebuilds once and records the new prelude; later resumes can reuse it. No configuration or migration is required.

## Linked Issues

Part of #14215. Related: #8277, #14246, #16362.

## Design docs

- [English design](https://github.com/MikeWang0316tw/qwen-code/blob/fix/resume-startup-prelude-cache/docs/design/2026-11-06-resume-startup-prelude-cache.md)
- [Chinese design](https://github.com/MikeWang0316tw/qwen-code/blob/fix/resume-startup-prelude-cache/docs/design/2026-11-06-resume-startup-prelude-cache.zh-CN.md)

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

resume 后的 session 现在会重播它当初送出的同一份 startup prelude，而不是用当下的日期、目录树、git snapshot、MCP instructions、skills 与 deferred-tool 清单重新建一份。session 开始或重建 prelude 时会把它写成 system record；还原时保留最新的一笔，放到 API history 的第一个 entry；已经有存档 prelude 的 session 不会再建第二份。

这让 resume 后的第一个 user message 与原本 request 完全一致，implicit prefix cache 才能重用整段对话历史，而不是只重用到 system prompt。

## 为什么需要

session resume 时，client 会在存档 turns 前面重建 startup prelude。重建的 prelude 带有最新的 workspace 信息，所以第一个 user message 与前一个 process 送出的不同。对 vLLM 这类 implicit prefix cache，可重用前缀就停在第一个差异。

实际回报的 417k-token 对话只重用了约 14k tokens 的 KV cache，其余约 186k tokens 重算，TTFT 126 秒。存下来的 transcript 第一笔 user record 是真正的 prompt，没有 startup prelude，所以 resume 的 process 无从重播。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

跑三个 focused regression tests；在 branch 上都应通过：

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/core/environmentContext.test.ts -t "reuses a stored startup prelude"
npx vitest run src/services/session-api-history.test.ts -t "startup context replay"
npx vitest run src/core/client.test.ts -t "records a generated startup prelude"
```

要重现 regression，暂时移除「重用存档 prelude」与「startup-context recovery」的逻辑（或 stash 实现）后重跑同一组测试。修正前，第一个测试会在存档 turns 前重建一份新 prelude，第二个测试会完全丢掉存档 prelude；两者都失败。

用真实 session 验证时，用这个 branch 开一个新对话并加上 `--openai-logging`，完成几轮后离开再 resume。第一个 request 的 `messages[0]` 应与 resume 前的第一个 message 完全相同，provider 的 cached-token 数量应包含对话历史，而不是只有 system prompt。

### 证据（修正前后）

N/A — 这是 core session-recovery 变更，以 unit-level 证据为主。

修正前，两个 focused tests 失败：

```
environmentContext: reuses a stored startup prelude -> 1 failed
session-api-history: startup context replay -> 1 failed
```

修正后通过。完整本地测试：

```
client.test.ts                      624 passed
environmentContext.test.ts          116 passed
session-api-history.test.ts          63 passed
chatRecordingService.test.ts        191 passed
session-transcript-reader.test.ts   152 passed
transcript-records validation        48 passed
ACP targeted test                     1 passed
```

### 测试环境

| OS | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| Linux | ✅ 已测试（Node 26.8.1，packages/core vitest） |

### 环境

本地 Node 26.8.1，从 `packages/core` 跑 `npx vitest`；core 的 `tsc --noEmit`、Prettier、ESLint 都通过。此环境没有跑完整 CLI build 与 live vLLM prefix-cache 测试。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险／取舍：存下来的 prelude 会保留原始的日期与 git/MCP/skills 快照。日期新鲜度仍由既有的 history-derived tail reminder 负责；git snapshot 刻意冻结在 session 开始时，模型可自行跑 `git status` 取得目前状态。
- 尚未验证／超出范围：完整 CLI build 与 live vLLM E2E；若 divergence 来自 system prompt 或 tool declarations，属于更大的 context-immutability 问题，不在这个 PR。Managed session 的 journal 若无法携带新 record，会退回重建 prelude。
- Breaking changes／migration：在此变更之前建立的 session 没有存档 prelude。它们第一次 resume 会重建一次并记录新的 prelude，之后的 resume 才可重用。不需要设置或 migration。

## 关联 Issue

Part of #14215。Related: #8277、#14246、#16362。

## 设计文件

- [English design](https://github.com/MikeWang0316tw/qwen-code/blob/fix/resume-startup-prelude-cache/docs/design/2026-11-06-resume-startup-prelude-cache.md)
- [Chinese design](https://github.com/MikeWang0316tw/qwen-code/blob/fix/resume-startup-prelude-cache/docs/design/2026-11-06-resume-startup-prelude-cache.zh-CN.md)

</details>

prs.title: Feat/i18n add indonesian locale
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a new built-in Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia) locale to the CLI i18n system. All existing UI strings — extension management, command descriptions, MCP server dialogs, approval mode prompts, model selection, permission dialogs, and every other user-facing text — have been translated to Indonesian. The language registry is updated so that "Bahasa Indonesia (Indonesian)" appears in the language settings dropdown alongside the existing nine locales.

## Why it's needed

Indonesian speakers currently have no built-in locale option and fall back to English for all UI text. This PR gives them a fully translated experience without requiring custom language packs.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npm run check-i18n` — all checks pass with zero errors. The Indonesian locale shows 1757/1891 keys translated (92.9%), with all required (must-translate) keys fully covered. Then start the CLI with `--lang id` or set `QWEN_CODE_LANG=id` and confirm that the UI renders in Indonesian.

### Evidence (Before & After)

`npm run check-i18n` output:
- Before: 5 required keys fell back to English ("Set up Qwen Code's status line UI", "Cache Hit Rate", "Tool Success", "streak", "In/Out")
- After: All checks passed, 0 errors

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | N/A |
| 🪟 Windows |  ✅ tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | N/A |

### Environment

Windows 11, Node.js 24.17.0, `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: None. This is a purely additive change — a new locale file and two lines in the registry. No existing behavior is modified.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Linux not tested (locale is platform-independent). Unit tests not run (only `check-i18n` which covers key parity, must-translate coverage, and placeholder integrity).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None.

## Linked Issues

N/A

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

为 CLI 国际化系统添加了新的内置印尼语（Bahasa Indonesia）locale。所有现有的 UI 字符串——扩展管理、命令描述、MCP 服务器对话框、审批模式提示、模型选择、权限对话框以及所有其他面向用户的文本——均已翻译为印尼语。语言注册表已更新，因此"Bahasa Indonesia (Indonesian)"将与其他九个现有 locale 一起出现在语言设置下拉菜单中。

## 为什么需要

印尼语用户目前没有内置的 locale 选项，所有 UI 文本都回退为英文。此 PR 为他们提供完全翻译的体验，无需自定义语言包。

## 审核者测试计划

### 如何验证

运行 `npm run check-i18n` — 所有检查零错误通过。印尼语 locale 显示 1757/1891 个键已翻译（92.9%），所有必须翻译的键完全覆盖。然后使用 `--lang id` 启动 CLI 或设置 `QWEN_CODE_LANG=id`，确认 UI 以印尼语渲染。

### 证据（之前和之后）

- 之后：所有检查通过，0 错误

### 测试环境

| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | 不适用 |
| 🪟 Windows |  ✅ 已测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | 不适用 |

### 环境

Windows 11, Node.js 24.17.0, `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：无。这是纯增量更改 — 一个新 locale 文件和注册表中两行。不修改任何现有行为。

releases.name: Release v0.27.0
releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

- Managed-agent sessions can hold multiple child questions at once, answer them in any order, and keep drafts and errors separated per child. ([#16484](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16484))
- Web Shell adds a task Q&A heatmap and an Ask for details side task that explains pending Ask User Question options without answering. ([#16037](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16037), [#16458](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16458))
- GitHub channel editor adds Repository Filter allowlists and blocklists, while bound PR delivery and plain comment delivery become more reliable. ([#16493](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16493), [#16502](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16502), [#16416](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16416))
- Shell tool edits now handle CRLF and Unicode safely in sed substitutions, and cancelled commands report as interrupted while keeping partial output. ([#15701](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15701), [#15836](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15836))
- Managed-agent runtime is faster and less prone to deadlocks, with safer session rename, snapshot publication, storage admission, and lock handling. ([#16480](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16480), [#16478](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16478), [#16376](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16376), [#16489](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16489), [#16447](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16447))
- Upgrade refusals and Advisor startup errors no longer expose embedded credentials, and empty Harness user info is rejected during start and verify. ([#16352](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16352), [#16083](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16083))

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- Added FileChanged hooks for local non-managed sessions, reporting add, change, and unlink events for watched files and directories. ([#13969](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13969)) by @samuelhsin
- CI Failure Patrol now posts visible bilingual notices when it reruns flaky failures or cannot classify them, improving PR feedback. ([#16459](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16459)) by @wenshao
- feat(cli): align managed agent basic tools with daemon ([#16445](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16445)) by @doudouOUC
- Moves Web Shell session search into the sidebar top row beside View activity and improves narrow-layout behavior. ([#16467](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16467)) by @wenshao
- Improves CI triage security by isolating triage agent credentials and routing all triage runs to ECS. ([#16468](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16468)) by @wenshao
- Managed-agent sessions can now keep multiple child questions pending, answer child questions in any order, and keep drafts and errors separated per child. ([#16484](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16484)) by @doudouOUC
- With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop enabled, Ink TUI turns send the continuation round after tool batches and handle queued input and retries. ([#16428](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16428)) by @qqqys
- Web Shell composer now offers a task Q&A activity heatmap; clicking a day scrolls the transcript to that day's first Q&A and highlights it. ([#16037](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16037)) by @samuelhsin
- Adds a Repository Filter to the GitHub channel editor with allowlist and blocklist modes, URL-friendly entries, and skipped-notification timeline rows. ([#16493](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16493)) by @wenshao
- Adds an Ask for details action to pending Ask User Question panels in Web Shell, opening a side task that explains options without answering. ([#16458](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16458)) by @wenshao
- Reclaims idle channel sessions in serve so cached channel routes no longer exhaust the maxSessions budget. ([#16532](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16532)) by @wenshao
- Adds a single-pull-request view by URL for daemon PR-state watch, returning state, mergeability, and head SHA. ([#16530](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16530)) by @wenshao
- feat(ci): add disposable external PR runners ([#16513](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16513)) by @yiliang114
- feat(web-shell): show tool arguments and result in expanded cards ([#15435](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15435)) by @BigDaddy1337

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed Managed Agent session rename failures by waiting for an in-flight title delivery to settle instead of returning a 503 error. ([#16447](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16447)) by @yiliang114
- Fixed release blocking by moving audio capture prebuilds to macOS 15 while still producing Apple Silicon and Intel Mac artifacts. ([#16464](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16464)) by @liuxuely0626
- Improved Web Shell Skill suggestions by showing the Skill name as the title and the owning Extension on a separate line. ([#16451](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16451)) by @callmeYe
- Fixes CI failures on older PR checkouts by refreshing OpenTUI host assets after unpacking shared builds. ([#16476](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16476)) by @yiliang114
- Fixes Web Shell sidebar layout so session search appears to the right of View activity. ([#16481](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16481)) by @wenshao
- fix(channels): deliver plain conversation comments to PR-bound sessions ([#16416](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16416)) by @wenshao
- Managed agent storage admission now locks rows through alias keys so concurrent storage requests queue instead of deadlocking. ([#16376](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16376)) by @wenshao
- Local Managed journal reads now accept a grown journal prefix even when file timestamps do not change, preventing unnecessary read failures. ([#16483](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16483)) by @wenshao
- The shell tool's sed simulation now handles CRLF files and Unicode characters correctly in substitution patterns, preventing failed edits and corruption. ([#15701](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15701)) by @2SinceJuly
- CI Maven cache handling now preserves suite results and reports failures clearly when cache setup or write-back fails. ([#15274](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15274)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- After Esc or Ctrl+C, cancelled shell commands are reported as interrupted instead of completed, preserving partial output. ([#15836](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15836)) by @2SinceJuly
- Managed agent snapshot publication now waits for an in-progress claim, reducing failed publications caused by deadlocks. ([#16489](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16489)) by @wenshao
- VS Code companion now writes only the selected model name and baseUrl, preserving other settings.model values when configuring providers. ([#15829](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15829)) by @2SinceJuly
- Web Shell session view now names tool blocks using lifecycle toolName when no other tool name is present, preventing unknown Tool labels. ([#16306](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16306)) by @yiliang114
- Interactive TUI now prompts for background workflow agent tool approvals by opening background-task details, preventing stalled runs. ([#16432](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16432)) by @yiliang114
- Non-interactive, ACP, and channel runs now warn when a prompt stacks more than five skills, delivering the notice without disrupting model replies. ([#16404](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16404)) by @yiliang114
- fix(serve): treat a payload-invalid start reply as a definite refusal ([#16460](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16460)) by @yiliang114
- Startup errors for unavailable Advisor models now sanitize aux-model selectors, hiding embedded credentials and NUL bytes while keeping routing unchanged. ([#16083](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16083)) by @yiliang114
- Ctrl+B promoted commands that create the first commit in an unborn repository now register it for Auto-mode amend exemption. ([#16081](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16081)) by @yiliang114
- The publish-triage CI job now recreates Git metadata before checkout, preventing leftover workspace hooks or config from running in credential-bearing steps. ([#16494](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16494)) by @wenshao
- fix(core): keep follow-up suggestions in Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar ([#16341](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16341)) by @spped2000
- Enables sandbox image builds on mainland release hosts by detecting the managed egress proxy and using it only when Docker Hub is reachable. ([#16281](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16281)) by @yiliang114
- Keeps the user's instruction as the last content in fresh-turn model requests by moving injected context ahead of it. ([#16274](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16274)) by @yiliang114
- Masks passwords in upgrade command refusal messages and rejects empty Harness user info during start and verify. ([#16352](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16352)) by @wenshao
- Fixes managed-host Web Shell issues so shell panes, host status updates, session measurement, and owner navigation behave reliably. ([#16203](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16203)) by @yiliang114
- Keeps channel turns completed when the answer was delivered but the follow-up notice fails, and fails turns only when nothing was delivered. ([#16512](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16512)) by @yiliang114
- Makes GitHub channel bound PR delivery reliable by watching all open bound PRs and continuing polling during public turns. ([#16502](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16502)) by @wenshao
- Web Shell now respects optional transport capabilities and keeps local prompt timing correct while waiting for an authoritative user echo. ([#16536](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16536)) by @chiga0
- Web Shell no longer crashes when a UI language lacks relay copy and now falls back to English text. ([#15474](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15474)) by @4ekuct25
- Cursor saves now succeed on filesystems that refuse temporary-file permission changes instead of failing before publishing. ([#16257](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16257)) by @wenshao
- fix(ci): route the review/resolve permission gate to the ECS pool ([#16482](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16482)) by @wenshao
- fix(cli): restore OpenTUI dialog editing controls ([#15908](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15908)) by @chiga0
- fix(managed-agent): restore two runtime-broker classes to their size ratchet ([#16542](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16542)) by @wenshao
- fix(serve): serialize overlapping cleanup retries ([#15482](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15482)) by @jabrailkhalil
- fix(memory): match reader advice to the binding index budget ([#15368](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15368)) by @jabrailkhalil
- fix(release): derive the next patch when the preview baseline lags latest ([#16470](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16470)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- fix(web-shell): include channel sessions in release dialog ([#16537](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16537)) by @wenshao
- Show Anthropic refusal details in finish messages instead of the generic SAFETY notice, while keeping refusal handling fatal. ([#16079](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16079)) by @yiliang114

### Performance

- Improves managed-agent performance by reducing tenant guard locking for ordinary session runtime binding control. ([#16480](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16480)) by @doudouOUC
- Improves managed-agent tool execution performance by removing tenant placement locking from ordinary session admission. ([#16478](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16478)) by @doudouOUC
- MySQL pools now cache parsed statements by default with cachePrepStmts=true, prepStmtCacheSize=512, and prepStmtCacheSqlLimit=8192 unless already set. ([#16414](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16414)) by @wenshao
- Reduces memory use when reading large growing local journals by comparing grown prefixes in 64 KiB chunks. ([#16507](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16507)) by @wenshao

### Documentation

- docs(design): correct the daemon PR state transitions design ([#16487](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16487)) by @wenshao

### Internal Changes

- Improved interactive foreground-shell test reliability by waiting for composer draft and approval footer to appear before asserting. ([#16455](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16455)) by @yiliang114
- Updated managed-agent lifecycle tests and snapshot publication retries to reduce false failures from deadlocks and lane changes. ([#16446](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16446)) by @yiliang114
- test(serve): cover the workspace_runtime_stop boot-time conjunction ([#16469](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16469)) by @yiliang114
- Adds an internal unit test for Web Shell /settings development route rewriting. ([#16456](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16456)) by @yiliang114
- Managed-agent storage alias key generation and digest handling are now consolidated without changing user-visible behavior. ([#16485](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16485)) by @doudouOUC
- Consolidated managed-agent JDBC statement preparation and JSON mapper reuse without changing timeout behavior. ([#16486](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16486)) by @doudouOUC
- Internal refactor consolidates CSI statement timeout handling with no user-facing behavior change. ([#16503](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16503)) by @doudouOUC
- Internal runtime modules replace inline fully qualified type names with imports, improving readability without changing behavior. ([#16504](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16504)) by @doudouOUC
- Makes typecheck projects compile cleanly under the TypeScript 7 native compiler while keeping the existing tsc 5.8 build unchanged. ([#16463](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16463)) by @sorrycc

issues.title: proposal(workflow): verified candidate evaluation for experimental search (review-only)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

issues.body:
## Summary

Codewhale already has a useful candidate-generation path: `workflows/operate_best_of_n.workflow.js` supports `strategy: "search"` with independent worktrees and a read-only reviewer. However, the result is currently **generation/review evidence, not runtime-verified evidence**. Worker-reported commands and `self_verdict` are not trusted gate results.

I propose landing the **smallest real evaluator-host slice**, integrated with the existing Workflow search caller, **before** exploring multi-generation/evolutionary search. This is intended as a bounded contributor PR, not a new scheduler or an autonomous self-improvement system.

## Existing design and constraints

- [Workflow experimental search](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/WORKFLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_SEARCH.md) explicitly calls for a frozen baseline/evaluator, independent clean-baseline replay, runtime-owned gates, durable receipts, and review-only selection.
- [Workflow authoring](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md) describes the current `strategy: "search"` recipe as generation/review only.
- [Best-of-N skill](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/crates/skills/assets/skills/best-of-n/SKILL.md) already requires treating self-verdicts as untrusted.
- [#6517](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6517) removed the unused `WorkflowSearchSpec` prototype. Any replacement must have a **real production caller in the same PR**, rather than another stand-alone framework.

## Proposed first PR: verified candidate evaluation

Reuse the existing Workflow, Fleet, Runtime and worktree mechanisms. The smallest acceptable vertical slice would:

1. **Freeze** the baseline commit, candidate contract, evaluator identity/hash, allowed write paths, test commands, and budget **before** candidates run. Explicitly report what was frozen.
2. Preserve each candidate's patch/diff and immutable artifact reference. Candidate self-reports remain *untrusted*.
3. After candidate work completes, evaluate against a **clean checkout of the frozen baseline**, using host-owned commands/permissions, not the candidate's claim that tests passed.
4. **Fail closed** on out-of-scope writes, modified protected tests/evaluator files, patch conflicts, failed commands, or unverifiable evidence. Never let the candidate edit or select its own evaluator.
5. Record real commands, exit codes, baseline SHA, patch hash, evaluator hash, failures, and available provider/usage/cost receipts (mark unknown fields as unknown rather than inventing numbers).
6. Rank **only verified candidates**; return `NONE` when all fail. No automatic apply, merge, push, config promotion, or permission expansion.
7. Re-run a provisional winner from the frozen baseline and produce an independent read-only review/verification record before returning it for explicit user review.
8. Integrate this with **one existing Workflow search entry point** and focused regression tests; do not add an unused public API, second agent loop, or new product mode.

### Focused acceptance tests

- Candidate claims `PASS` but host command fails → rejected.
- Candidate edits protected tests or evaluator → rejected without evaluating modified tests.
- All candidates fail or a patch cannot apply cleanly → `NONE`, parent checkout unchanged.
- A candidate tries to escape its declared write scope → rejected; no authority escalation.
- Repeated evaluation from the same frozen inputs reports stable gate results and traceable artifact hashes.
- Integration test proves the existing search entry point actually invokes the evaluator host.

## Follow-up experiment (separate PR; not part of the initial claim)

Only after the first slice is usable: a strictly opt-in **two-generation, failure-guided candidate search** using verified test failures to propose the next generation, with explicit lineage and no online policy mutation.

Compare against **equal-budget** independent Best-of-N on a held-out coding task set, keeping model route, permissions, evaluator, and task distribution fixed. Primary metric: verified task success. Also report cost per successful task, elapsed time, regressions and `NONE` rate. Negative or inconclusive results are acceptable.

This is inspired by experiments with offline orchestration-policy mutation and trace-based scoring in [TomorrowEdge](https://github.com/axobase001/tomorrowedge) and feedback/receipt loops in [Skuld](https://github.com/axobase001/skuld). Critically, counterfactual trace scores **do not establish real task improvement**: only independent execution/evaluation can.

## Non-goals

No automatic skill rewriting, silent profile evolution, learned router, new scheduler, autonomous deployment, hidden permission escalation, or claims of performance improvement before actual trials. No model-provider-specific implementation requirement.

## Maintainer feedback requested

Does the **existing Workflow search caller → runtime-owned clean-baseline evaluator → review-only receipt** path fit the intended boundary? If so, I can start with a narrowly scoped PR covering one real caller, one evaluator gate, and focused tests. I would prefer to align the insertion point with the current runtime owners before touching a large surface.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Use status:awaiting-release for source fixes that are landed but still need final verification and shipment; do not close them merely because main contains the fix.

Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。 Related (closed): #7042, #5036.

### What happened? 发生了什么？

New TUI sessions in one workspace show this on every sub-agent sidebar refresh:

```
Warn Failed to clean up sub-agents: Runtime coordination was opened without its writer lock; stop and restart this Runtime process after the other session exits
```

Restarting does not help. Every new session's TUI log shows why:

```
WARN subagent: delegated store admission failed; writable state remains refused error=another Codewhale process (pid 69066) owns delegated coordination for <workspace>: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
WARN subagent: this session cannot append to the shared coordination ledger error=Runtime coordination was opened without its writer lock; stop and restart this Runtime process after the other session exits
```

- **The named holder is wrong.** PID 69066 does not exist. No acquirer writes its PID into `subagents.v1.lock`. The file's content dates from August, so the diagnostic names a dead process.
- **The real holder** was a `codew` started six days earlier and suspended since then (`STAT T`, no TTY, parent launchd). It held two fds on `<workspace>/.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.lock`.
- **Why it blocks everything:** the workspace still had a legacy `subagents.v1.json` file and no `subagents.v3.json`. So every new session attempts the v1→v3 cutover, and the cutover requires the lock **exclusively**. One forgotten process blocks the cutover indefinitely, and every new session in the folder runs with sub-agent state read-only.

Expected: one stale process does not degrade every other session in the folder. If something does block, the message names the actual blocker and says what to do, once.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Use a workspace that still has `.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.json` and no `subagents.v3.json`. Start any Codewhale session there and leave it running or suspended (Ctrl+Z).
2. Start a current-build session in the same workspace.
3. Open the sub-agent sidebar. The warning repeats on each refresh where cleanup is due. The log names whatever PID is in the lock file, not the holder.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 0.10.3 (d214a969012f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

macOS

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Built from a git checkout

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-flash (does not matter)

### Terminal and shell 终端

_No response_

### codewhale doctor (optional)

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

**Mechanism** (on `main` at `d214a9690`):

1. `ensure_subagent_store_cutover` (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:13710`) calls `CoordinationProcessLock::acquire(root, true)` (exclusive) whenever the v1 tombstone is missing. Any other live session fails it, even one holding the lock shared or sitting suspended.
2. On that failure, `with_state_path` and `require_coordination_process_lock` (`mod.rs:6070-6105`) set `coordination_snapshot_read_only = true` for the life of the process. Nothing retries when the holder leaves. `ensure_coordination_process_lock` (`mod.rs:6110`) then returns the "restart" error forever.
3. `Op::ListSubAgents` (`crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs:4110-4135`) runs cleanup on each refresh where cleanup is due and sends a user-visible error every time. The result is repeated warnings that never name the blocker.
4. The holder PID is read from the lock file's content (`mod.rs:4037-4050`), which no acquirer writes.

**Proposal: remove the workspace-wide process flock.**

The v3 store already handles its own concurrency:

- a bounded, per-operation `subagents.v3.transaction.lock` (`acquire_store_transaction`, `mod.rs:13638`);
- per-writer boot leases, `subagents.v3.writer.<boot>.lock` (`mod.rs:13910`).

`docs/architecture/delegated-coordination.md` (§ "Legacy cutover and recovery") already says two things: the retained `subagents.v1.json` directory is what stops an old publisher from overwriting state, and concurrent old binaries are not a supported coordination domain. So:

- Run the v1→v3 cutover under the transaction lock only.
- Delete `CoordinationProcessLock`, `coordination_process_lock[_required]`, `coordination_exclusive` and `coordination_snapshot_read_only`. They have 66 references in `subagent/mod.rs` and 40 in `subagent/tests.rs`.
- Decide whether the single-host policy of `codewhale serve` and the runtime API (#7042's exclusive constructor) still needs anything the store leases do not cover. Keep it only if it does, and state why.
- Keep working: #5036 (isolated worktree builders) and #7042 (several resumed sessions in one folder). Update the architecture doc in the same change.

If full removal is rejected, the minimum fix is:

- Retry store admission once the holder exits, instead of staying read-only for the life of the process.
- Report a cleanup or admission failure once, naming the real holder and the remedy, rather than on every sidebar refresh.
- Write the PID on acquire, or stop claiming to know it.

**Workaround:** end the stale process (`kill -CONT <pid>; kill <pid>` for a suspended one), then start a new session.

issues.body:
## What happened?

`redact_proxy_userinfo` in `crates/net/src/proxy.rs` returns its input unchanged when the string has no `://`. One caller passes a raw environment value rather than a parsed `Url`, so when the configured proxy is malformed and carries credentials, the password is written to the log file in clear text.

The branch is the malformed-`HTTP(S)_PROXY` warning in `configured_mcp_proxy`:

```rust
let Some(normalized) = normalized else {
    tracing::warn!(target: "mcp", proxy = %redact_proxy_userinfo(&proxy_url), "ignoring malformed HTTP(S)_PROXY URL");
    return Ok(None);
};
```

`proxy_url` is the raw `read_environment(key)` value, never parsed at that point. The other three call sites pass `reqwest::Url` values (`url.as_str()`, `target.configured`), which always carry a scheme, so they are fine.

`tracing::warn!` goes to `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-YYYY-MM-DD-PID.log` and is kept for the retention window, so the value persists on disk.

## Steps to reproduce

Feed the redaction function the strings that actually reach that branch (checked against `0.10.3`):

```text
input                                      Url::parse   http:// prefix   logged
http://user:pass@proxy.example:8080        ok           ok               -
user:pass@proxy.example:8080               fail         ok               -
user:pass@ho st:8080                       fail         fail             LEAKS
user:pass@proxy.example:port-not-a-number  fail         fail             LEAKS
user:pass@[::1:8080                        fail         fail             LEAKS
user:pass@                                 fail         fail             LEAKS
```

A row that fails both parses reaches the warning; `logged` is what the warning would write. The four rows marked `LEAKS` come through with the password intact, because none of them contains `://` and the function bails out before redacting.

End to end:

1. Export a malformed proxy carrying credentials, e.g. `HTTPS_PROXY='placeholder-user:placeholder-pass@proxy.example:not-a-port'`.
2. Start the TUI with an MCP server configured, so `configured_mcp_proxy` runs.
3. Search the current `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log` for `placeholder-pass`.

It appears in clear text.

## Expected

Either redact the value or drop it from the message. "Ignoring a malformed HTTP(S)_PROXY URL" already identifies the problem, and the operator knows what they exported.

A fix that keeps the diagnostic: when there is no `://`, locate the last `@` before any `/`, `?` or `#` and replace everything before it with `***@`, mirroring the schemed branch. The existing table in `proxy::tests::redact_proxy_userinfo_strips_password` can take the four unschemed inputs above as regression cases.

## Version and configuration

`0.10.3` source. The early return predates the loopback-proxy work in #7231; that PR tightened the function's doc comment to say unschemed input is not redacted, but did not change this branch's behaviour.

## Where did it happen?

MCP — the warning fires from `configured_mcp_proxy`, which the MCP HTTP client calls per request.

## A note on classification

I am filing this as a bug rather than a private advisory on purpose, and I would rather be explicit than quiet about it: there is no attacker and no remote path here. It needs the user to put a plaintext password in `HTTPS_PROXY` *and* malform the URL, and that password is already readable by same-user processes through the environment. What changes is that it lands in a file that people paste into issues. One step short of what `SECURITY.md` calls a credential leak.

I could not open a private advisory either — creating one needs `admin` on the repository, and outside contributors do not have it (`permissions.admin == false`). If you read this as a security report rather than a bug, close this and I will follow whatever channel you prefer.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

error: ChatGPT token signature or identity claims failed verification

issues.body: > This feature request article is manually drafted by me and rewritten by Deepseek for more-organized content textflow and more-authentic English. ### Before you start - [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. Related work I found: #6540 / #6544 (compaction summary cache miss), #6541 (cost-based compaction trigger, closed as not planned), #6969 (prompt-cache economics), #6721 (emergency compaction), #6504 (sub-agent compaction). None proposes the incremental fold layout; #6541 is the closest, but it changes when compaction fires, not how the replacement history is laid out. ### What problem does this solve? Long coding sessions on 1M-token routes hit a late, one-shot compaction: at ~80% of the window, Codewhale summarizes the older span (including previous checkpoints) and rewrites the prefix. That is a good overflow guardrail, but it has three structural costs: - the model runs at a very large context before anything happens; - replacing the prefix invalidates provider prefix-cache reuse for the next request; - re-summarizing prior checkpoints makes early detail decay, and tool-heavy history is reduced to one summary plus a short tail. #6540 / #6544 fixed a specific summary-cache bug (reasoning tier), and #6541 proposed an earlier cost-based trigger; #6541 was closed as not planned. The replacement layout itself is unchanged, so the cache/retention problem remains for long sessions. ### What should Codewhale do? Add an **opt-in** `fold` strategy inspired by [billion-context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context): - trigger at ~45% of the effective window **and** after ~50K tokens of new growth; keep the existing 80% path as the emergency fallback; - keep a stable prefix (system/tools + existing summary blocks), append one new summary block for the consumed increment, and keep a recent verbatim workspace (~50K, all message types); compress only the consumed increment and never rewrite earlier blocks; - reuse the existing summarizer, archive, and survival contract in the first slice; add block IDs/provenance and reuse `context_archive_search` / `context_archive_get`; - add `[compaction] strategy = "legacy" | "fold"` (default `legacy`), with `fold_trigger_percent`, `fold_growth_tokens`, `recent_workspace_tokens`, and `summary_block_budget`; - add the matching audit fields and a 100+ turn long-session fixture; compare billed input, cache hit, p95 latency, recall probes, and survival-contract tests. Non-goals: no default behavior change; no proxy; no provider API change; no new required dependency; no wholesale port of billion-context; no weakening of the survival contract. Acceptance: fold is opt-in and legacy stays untouched; survival-contract, tool-pair, anchor, and current-user-instruction tests pass; measurable reduction in billed input and cache-miss tokens with no recall regression; failed folds preserve history; docs explain the knobs. This is a safety-critical engine change. I'd rather you or a core contributor own the Rust implementation than review a drive-by PR from someone unfamiliar with the engine. I can provide the detailed spec, fixture matrix, benchmark harness, and long-session testing. Detailed background, current behavior, prior art, and open questions are in the first comment below. ### Where? TUI (terminal interface); CLI command (codewhale exec, ...); Providers and models. ### Workarounds or other tools (optional) Today I can lower `auto_compact_threshold_percent` (more frequent one-shot rewrites, worse cache), raise `retained_user_message_tokens` (more verbatim user text, less compression), or run `/compact ` manually. An external billion-context proxy is possible but adds a process and cannot change Codewhale's engine-side checkpoint/archive semantics. #6541 proposed an earlier cost-based trigger; it was closed as not planned, and it does not address the fold layout. ### Contributing - [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this. I'd rather the maintainers own the engine change; I can help with the spec, fixture matrix, benchmark harness, and long-session testing.

issues.body:
## Summary

`POST /v1/threads/{id}/patch-undo` accepts the same `UndoTurnRequest` body as
`POST /v1/threads/{id}/undo`, including the `turn_id` field, but only reads
`depth`. When a request contains both fields, `/undo` removes the named turn
while `/patch-undo` removes `depth` turns from the tail and answers `201`.
The caller gets a different turn than requested, and the snapshot rollback is
applied to that different turn.

## Environment

- Codewhale v0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`), macOS arm64 release binary
- Finding target commit: `6391f4f307040851fca29d679d3c05a985828a54`
- Local runtime API: `codewhale app-server --http --insecure-no-auth`
- Workspace with two completed user turns in one thread

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the runtime API and create a thread:

   ```bash
   codewhale app-server --http --port 17878 --insecure-no-auth
   curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:17878/v1/threads \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"title":"undo-test","workspace":"/tmp/cw-workspace"}'
   ```

2. Add two user turns to that thread:

   ```
   POST /v1/threads/{id}/turns  {"prompt":"first turn"}
   POST /v1/threads/{id}/turns  {"prompt":"second turn"}
   ```

   Both turns complete. The thread now has:

   ```
   turn_22987612d61345a2912e36be2e973d6d  "first turn"
   turn_95e24ffb79a64cf6b35c82f15ac3e542  "second turn"
   ```

3. Send the same request body to both endpoints:

   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:17878/v1/threads/$THREAD/undo \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"depth":0,"turn_id":"turn_22987612d61345a2912e36be2e973d6d"}'

   curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:17878/v1/threads/$THREAD/patch-undo \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"depth":0,"turn_id":"turn_22987612d61345a2912e36be2e973d6d"}'
   ```

## Expected behavior

Both endpoints name the first user turn, so both should return
`original_user_text: "first turn"` and fork with both turns removed.
`patch-undo` should also roll back the files changed by those two turns.

## Actual behavior

`/undo` behaves as documented:

```
original_user_text = "first turn"
```

`/patch-undo` silently ignores `turn_id` and uses `depth: 0`:

```
original_user_text = "second turn"
patch_result = {
  "files_restored": false,
  "summary": "The undone turn(s) ran no tools, so they changed no workspace files; nothing to restore.",
  "snapshot_label": null
}
```

It forks with only the last turn removed and returns `201`. With turns that
changed files, the rollback would restore the second turn's snapshot rather
than the first turn's — the wrong files, with no warning.

## Root cause

`patch_undo_thread_turn` takes `Json(req): Json<UndoTurnRequest>` and starts:

```rust
let depth = req.depth.unwrap_or(0);
...
let prepared = state
    .runtime_threads
    .prepare_fork_at_user_message_in_sessions_dir(&id, depth, &state.sessions_dir)
    .await
```

It never reads `req.turn_id`.

The sibling handler added in the same change, `undo_thread_turn`, does read it:

```rust
match req.turn_id {
    Some(turn_id) => state
        .runtime_threads
        .fork_dropping_user_turn_in_sessions_dir(&id, &turn_id, &state.sessions_dir)
        .await,
    None => state
        .runtime_threads
        .fork_at_user_message_in_sessions_dir(&id, req.depth.unwrap_or(0), &state.sessions_dir)
        .await,
}
```

`UndoTurnRequest` documents the field as “The user turn to undo, with every turn
after it. Wins over `depth`.” `/patch-undo` accepts that body and silently
drops the winning field.

## Suggested fix

- Mirror `undo_thread_turn`: when `turn_id` is present, resolve it to the cut
  under the thread restore guard and use that cut for both the snapshot
  rollback and the fork; fall back to `depth` only when `turn_id` is absent.
- Or reject `turn_id` on `/patch-undo` with `400` instead of ignoring it, so a
  caller cannot silently undo a different turn.
- Add an endpoint test that sends both fields to `/patch-undo` and asserts the
  named turn, not the tail turn, is removed.

## Impact

Clients that send `turn_id` to `/patch-undo` (for example an editor undo that
must also restore files) remove the wrong conversation turn and roll back the
wrong snapshot, while the API answers `201`. The mistake is silent: the only
signal is `original_user_text` naming a turn the caller did not ask to remove.

issues.body:
## Problem

Tsubasa users currently need to define a custom provider instead of selecting a named preset. A small descriptor could supply the endpoint, dedicated key name, and public model aliases without adding another transport.

## Proposed solution

Requesting maintainer sign-off before an agent-assisted provider change, as required by CONTRIBUTING. Add one descriptor in `crates/config/assets/provider_descriptors.json`, consumed by `crates/config/src/descriptors.rs`, using the existing OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions path. Intended values: `tsubasa`, `https://api.tsubasa.sh/v1`, `TSUBASA_API_KEY`, default `tsubasa-pro`; alternative `tsubasa-fast`. Both aliases have a 32,768-token context. Use an 8,192-token generation default and text-only metadata; do not infer advanced capabilities, prices, release dates, or underlying model identities.

## Use case

A discoverable provider entry makes configuration less error-prone and keeps Tsubasa credentials separate from OpenAI credentials.

## Alternatives considered

The existing custom-provider block already covers manual setup. If maintainers prefer that route, a short named example in `docs/PROVIDERS.md` is sufficient; a new ProviderKind is unnecessary.

## Impact

This is a focused configuration improvement, not a request to change provider policy, authentication semantics, sandboxing, or ranking.

## Additional context

Research pin: `94130d91aed546de1ebfd7621603acf6fec6b6e2`. Proposed checks: descriptor loader/selection, actual Chat request and SSE decoding, dedicated-key isolation, 401 handling, and captured-request schema/context validation. A controlled endpoint can test those local boundaries; live inference remains unverified because the current public model-discovery request returned HTTP 404.

No implementation or maintainer approval is claimed. Codewhale's instruction against agent comments will be respected; there will be no automated follow-up/status comments.

prs.title: feat(tasks): pause the task wall clock for answerable human waits
prs.body:
## What and why

Upstream's turn layer already treats human waits as outside the budget — `crates/runtime/src/turn_budget.rs`: "the budget bounds what the agent spends on its own, not how long a person takes to answer." #6118 already suspends the task idle watchdog while an approval is pending. The durable task wall clock, however, still bounds a run parked on its own prompt — task_manager's #6118 note records that bound deliberately ("`0` waits indefinitely by configuration; the wall deadline still bounds the run"). For an automation run with no operator at the keyboard, that bound interrupts the run at the wall deadline, withdrawing the pending approval on the host's behalf (`ApprovalOutcome::Cancelled` — a withdrawal, not a denial) and discarding the run.

This pauses the durable task wall clock while a prompt on the run itself awaits a decision — deliberately relaxing that documented bound, and only where a decision surface can actually answer:

- `TaskManagerConfig::human_waits_answerable` (default **false** — TUI-managed tasks behave exactly as today). The app-server runtime API opts in: its tasks are answerable via `POST /v1/approvals/{id}` and `submit_user_input`.
- While a prompt is pending, the wall deadline moves with each closed window (preserving #5898's crossed-first attribution — a crossing before a window still terminalizes `WallTimeout` at the moved deadline). A 24h aggregate fail-safe cap (`human_wait_cap`, new `human_wait_timeout` terminal reason) bounds the exclusion across the whole task, and Cancel/Shutdown classification outranks a spent cap so a canceled task is never mislabeled.
- Parked decision polling backs off 200ms → 2s; a decision wakes it immediately.
- Idle handling composes with #6118 (unchanged): a window close restarts the idle budget fresh.

`[approval] timeout_seconds` is unchanged and remains the lever for bounding the wait on the human's side; this changes only the task supervisor's accounting. The feature row `thread-scheduled-turns` in docs/features.toml is updated (its `api` surface is where the opt-in lives).

## Issue

No-Issue: extends the documented turn-layer human-wait philosophy to the durable task layer; complements #6118 (unchanged).

## How I tested it

- Red-on-base evidence via mutation runs recorded in the commit (raw wall clock, cap hoisted above cancel/shutdown, aggregate arm removed, gate removed, server flag off — each flips a named test).
- Targeted suites: `human_wait`/`execution_guard` filters → 21 passed, 0 failed (two new ordering/attribution pins included: cancel outranks a spent **parked** cap; `WallTimeout` attribution at the moved deadline); task_manager module → 101 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; app-server `server_task` pins → 2 passed; `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` → 2 passed.
- Zero-regression pin: an unanswerable (default) surface still wall-times out through a prompt, asserting no window is armed.
- Honest limits: the `run_http_server` call-site hop is not test-pinned (pinning it requires booting the server); the two runtime_api pins cover the builder and executor-forward hops.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] User-facing feature: docs/RUNTIME_API.md updated and the `thread-scheduled-turns` row in docs/features.toml updated (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` passes)

## Environment and observation
OpenClaw 2026.10.5; macOS; Node 26.10.0; native bundled boot-md; SQLite session store. One observed occurrence on 2026-10-21 at 20:22 EDT. Reproducibility has not been tested with another restart.

## Steps observed
1. Enable only hooks.internal.entries.boot-md.enabled and perform one approved native Gateway restart.
2. BOOT.md uses native status, sends one startup message, and admits a main-session reconciliation turn.
3. Boot run finishes; native hook attempts to remove its temporary session.

Expected: startup work succeeds and the hook removes its temporary session.
Actual: startup notification and main pickup both succeeded, but cleanup failed and the finished temporary row remained. Hook logged startup task failed although useful work completed.

Sanitized error:
```text
boot: failed to clean up session: SQLite session entry changed before lifecycle removal for <temporary-boot-session>
hooks/boot-md: startup task failed; reason=session cleanup failed
```

## Impact / suspected area
Small cleanup/reporting defect: retained finished temporary session and misleading failure log. No observed lost startup message or duplicate execution. Installed boot handler finally calls applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation with expected session ID; exact-entry comparison in the SQLite projection rejects removal. The rejecting guard is located; the changing writer and root cause are not proven. Related finalization fallback appeared in the same run; causality is unknown and it is not a second blocker.

## Evidence and limits
The error excerpt above is sanitized from the observed Gateway log. Raw private transcripts, chat destinations, host names and user paths are not included. A maintainer can request a separately sanitized excerpt. No raw DB access, manual session deletion, installed patch, weakened guard or second restart was used.

issues.body:
## Summary
A client that authenticates only with its stored device token (no shared `gateway.auth.token`, e.g. a device paired with a setup code) is told `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH` after that token is revoked or the Gateway state is reset. `GatewayChannel` neither clears the stale stored token nor pauses automatic reconnect: every reconnect reloads the same token and is rejected again, until the Gateway's auth rate limiter trips. The surfaced problem is "Gateway token is out of date — Retry once", which names a shared token the client does not have.

## Steps
1. Pair a client via setup code only (`token: nil`, `includeDeviceIdentity: true`), connect once so a device token is stored.
2. On the Gateway: `openclaw devices revoke <id>` (or reset Gateway state).
3. Let the client reconnect.

## Expected
Either the stale stored token is cleared and the client falls back to pairing, or reconnect pauses with a problem that names the device token.

## Actual
Automatic reconnect loops (backoff capped at 30 s), the stored token stays in the device-auth store, problem kind is `.gatewayAuthTokenMismatch`.

## Why
`GatewayChannel.swift:741-746` sends the stored device token as `auth.token` when no explicit token exists. The Gateway reports the shared-token reason for that source (`auth-context.ts:270-277`) and sets `canRetryWithDeviceToken: true` (`handshake-auth-helpers.ts:267-271`). On the client (`:641-659`): `shouldRetryWithStoredDeviceToken` is false (no explicit token, `:1279`), the clear-token branch needs `authDeviceToken != nil` (false), `isNonRecoverable` is false, and the pause clause (`:1293-1295`) needs the retry budget to be used (never). So `scheduleReconnect()` runs with the same credential each time.

## Evidence
`L4_18 stale stored device token stops reconnecting or is cleared` — RED:
```
330 connect attempts in 0.7 s with the same stored token (still stored: true)
problem names the shared gateway token although the client has none: kind: .gatewayAuthTokenMismatch, title: "Gateway token is out of date", actionLabel: "Retry once"
```
(The test stubs out the backoff wait; in production the loop is paced by the ≤30 s backoff.)

Reviewed on `upstream/main` 8088fcd1f41 (2026-10-31). Repro test file: `Round4ReproTests.swift` (Swift Testing, `apps/macos` OpenClawIPCTests), run with `swift test --disable-sandbox --filter Round4`.
