issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

First-run onboarding with a valid Z.AI Coding-Plan-Global API key fails: the wizard's validation probe gets no usable reply from the always-reasoning GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash defaults, the wizard refuses the endpoint with "The model did not return a usable reply", drops the provider config, and loops back to the provider picker.

### Steps to reproduce

Clean Ubuntu 24.04.5 container, Node v24.21.0, `npm install -g openclaw` (2026.9.8):

1. `openclaw onboard --tui`
2. Accept the security notice, telemetry off, one agent named `main`, "Ask first" access mode, "Yes, take a look"
3. Model/auth provider → More… → Z.AI → auth method Coding-Plan-Global
4. Install Z.AI plugin → "Download from npm" (second pass: "Download from ClawHub"; identical outcome)
5. Paste a valid Coding-Plan-Global API key

The key is valid: direct POST /chat/completions calls to both `glm-5.3` and `glm-5.3-flash` on `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` return 200, and the wizard itself prints "Verified GLM-5.3 on coding-global endpoint." right before the failing check.

### Expected behavior

Onboarding completes: key and coding-global endpoint persisted, default model set, connection test passes.

### Actual behavior

Both install paths (npm plugin 2026.9.8, ClawHub plugin 2026.9.7) fail identically:

```
✗ zai-coding-global: The model did not return a usable reply.
Credentials saved; default unchanged. Unknown model: zai/glm-5.3. Found
agents.defaults.models["zai/glm-5.3"] bound to the "openclaw" agent runtime. Models
served by an agent runtime come from that runtime and its linked account, not from
models.providers["zai"].models[] — registering it there will not make it usable. Confirm
"glm-5.3" is still offered by the "openclaw" runtime and switch
agents.defaults.model.primary to a currently available model (run `openclaw models list
--refresh --provider zai` to list them). See
https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers. Choose the saved sign-in in Model
Setup to retry without signing in again.
```

What is left behind:

- The provider config is dropped. The saved `openclaw.json` keeps `plugins.entries.zai.enabled: true` and `agents.defaults.model.primary: "zai/glm-5.3-flash"`, but no `models.providers.zai` section is written at all.
- Retrying via the saved sign-in fails differently: `✗ Saved Z.AI API key sign-in: This AI route is not available right now. The saved connection settings are no longer valid. Choose the provider settings again.`
- With the gateway up, `openclaw gateway call models.probe --params '{"provider":"zai"}' --json` gives `zai/glm-5.3` → `"status": "ok"`, but `zai/glm-5.3-flash` → `"status": "unknown", "error": "The connection probe failed."` The gateway log shows both probe requests returning HTTP 200 with an event-stream body, so the probe dies after a successful HTTP response, not at the transport layer.
- GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash always emit reasoning tokens (Z.AI rejects disabling: "This model always engages in thinking and cannot be disabled; please use low, high, or max."). The failure signature matches a probe whose token budget is consumed by reasoning before any content is produced. Checked outside OpenClaw with a raw streaming call under probe-like conditions (`stream: true, max_tokens: 16, reasoning_effort: "low"`): HTTP 200, `finish_reason: "length"`, 16 reasoning deltas, zero content deltas.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (clean Docker container; same failure on a bare-metal install)

### Install method

npm global; Z.AI plugin installed from npm (@openclaw/zai-provider 2026.9.8) and separately from ClawHub (2026.9.7)

### Model

zai/glm-5.3 and zai/glm-5.3-flash

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → @openclaw/zai-provider (Coding-Plan-Global) → https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4

### Additional provider/model setup details

Config left behind by the failed wizard (gateway and unrelated sections omitted):

```json
"plugins": { "entries": { "zai": { "enabled": true } } },
"agents": { "defaults": { "model": { "primary": "zai/glm-5.3-flash" },
                            "models": { "zai/glm-5.3-flash": { "alias": "GLM" } } } }
```

No proxy or extra gateway between OpenClaw and the API. Wizard defaults otherwise.

### Logs

From the repro gateway (redacted):

```
13:14:09 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=zai api=openai-completions model=glm-5.3 status=200 elapsedMs=3097 contentType=text/event-stream
13:14:47 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=zai api=openai-completions model=glm-5.3-flash status=200 elapsedMs=1280 contentType=text/event-stream
```

The models.probe RPC completes on both; it reports ok for glm-5.3 and failed for glm-5.3-flash.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Full wizard transcripts from both install paths were captured; the failure block quoted above is verbatim from them. Happy to paste a fuller transcript if that helps.

### Impact and severity

Affected: new installs onboarding with a Z.AI Coding-Plan-Global key (GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash defaults). Severity: blocks workflow, first-run onboarding cannot complete at all. Frequency: always, on both plugin install paths, in a clean container and on a bare-metal install. Consequence: the user is stuck at the provider picker with two different error messages, neither pointing at the real cause; only manual config editing or a patched plugin gets past it.

### Additional information

The "Unknown model: zai/glm-5.3" text is misleading: the model resolves, the API accepts the key, and the HTTP layer returns 200. The thinking-flag and prefix-matching defects that contribute to this state are filed separately in #164328.

What fixed it locally: flooring max_tokens for always-reasoning models in the plugin's stream wrapper (I used 4096) makes the connection test pass and chat work. Core-side, either a token budget floor for always-reasoning models in validation probes, or treating a length-stopped turn with reasoning activity as a successful auth check, would cover the other entry points. On probe failure the wizard should also keep the validated provider config instead of dropping it, and surface the real cause instead of the "Unknown model" text.

issues.body:
**Version:** upstream main @ aa11c6c05c5 (post-2026.10.4), bundled @openclaw/muse 2026.10.4, muse 1.4.10

**Summary**
The meta provider's manifest and thinking profile support xhigh for muse-spark-1.3, but sessions routed to the native `muse` runtime can't select it. With an explicit `models.providers.meta` entry carrying `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` including xhigh, the Control UI picker lists xhigh, but setting it fails:
`thinkingLevel "xhigh" is not supported for meta/muse-spark-1.3 (use off|minimal|low|medium|high)`.
Without the entry, the picker stops at high.

**Repro**
1. Plugin `muse` enabled. `agents.defaults.models["meta/muse-spark-1.3"].agentRuntime.id = "muse"`. Muse login via the global Muse CLI store (no `MODEL_API_KEY`, no meta auth profile).
2. Open a session on Muse Spark 1.3. The picker shows off-high.
3. Add `models.providers.meta.models: [{ id: "muse-spark-1.3", reasoning: true, compat: { supportedReasoningEfforts: ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"] } }]`. The picker now lists xhigh; selecting it fails as above.

**Cause (from source)**
- `gateway/sessions-patch.ts:663-670` validates against `loadThinkingProfileForPatch`, which selects the catalog row for the session runtime (`selectModelCatalogRuntimeEntry`, runtime `muse`).
- `model-catalog-view.ts:50-75` drops rows without `nativeRuntime` for runtime `muse`, so the config row's compat is ignored, and the fallback row has none.
- The meta provider thinking profile (`extensions/meta/thinking.ts`, off-xhigh) isn't applied: the meta plugin is `activation.onStartup: false`, and the profile is only reached via a catalog row's prepared policy or the active registry (`provider-thinking.ts:77-100`).
- The picker doesn't apply the runtime filter, so picker and validator disagree.

**Expected**
xhigh selectable for meta/muse-spark-1.3 on the muse runtime, matching the meta manifest. At minimum, the picker shouldn't offer levels the validator will reject.

**Possible fixes**
Apply the meta thinking profile to native `muse` runtime rows, or let donor-row compat merge into native rows (`model-catalog-entry.ts:~110-135`).

issues.title: Does the small-model web tool fix (PR #169556) cover omlx/MLX providers?

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

issues.body:
## Problem

PR [#169556](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169556) fixes the small-model security block for web_search and web_fetch on native Ollama runs. The release notes for v2026.10.10 state:

> _"A native local Ollama agent can use permitted web search and fetch tools even without Tool Search configured."_

This fix was merged Oct 15, 2026 and closes issue [#145137](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/145137).

## Question

Does this fix also cover **omlx/MLX providers** configured with `api: "openai-completions"`?

I'm running OpenClaw v2026.9.2 with the following provider config:

```json
"omlx": {
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-4bit",
      "name": "Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-4bit",
      "reasoning": true
    }
  ]
}
```

My primary model is `omlx/Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-4bit`. Currently on v2026.9.2, web_search and web_fetch work fine.

The follow-up PR [#173280](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173280) extends the exception to memory_search/memory_get for "native local Ollama" — again mentioning Ollama specifically.

**Before I upgrade past v2026.9.2:** will my omlx/MLX local model retain web_search, web_fetch, and memory tools after upgrading to v2026.10.10 or later? Or does the fix only apply to native Ollama protocol, meaning omlx users might still hit the small-model block?

## Context

This matters because:
- omlx provides both chat models AND the nomic-embed-text-v1.5 embedding model for memory search
- If the fix doesn't cover omlx, upgrading could break web tools AND memory search for MLX users
- The security rationale (small model risk) applies equally to any local model, not just Ollama

issues.title: [Feature]: Support keyterm prompting in ElevenLabs batch transcription

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

issues.body:
### Summary

List NagaAI in the external provider catalog, so it appears in onboarding and installs on demand.

### Problem to solve

NagaAI users set it up as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider: base URL, model ids, context windows and prices by hand. The model list goes stale as NagaAI adds and retires models, and reasoning effort and image input are not declared.

### Proposed solution

A `nagaai` provider plugin built like Cerebras (defineSingleProviderPluginEntry with liveModelDiscovery), with no new core surface:
- onboarding choice `nagaai-api-key`, key in NAGA_API_KEY;
- `api: "openai-responses"` at https://api.naga.ac/v1, as ClawRouter does;
- live model discovery from the public GET https://api.naga.ac/v1/models (no credentials): models whose chat operation is served on Responses and accepts `tools`, each with its context window, image input, reasoning effort and per-token prices;
- a few seed models in the manifest for offline use;
- docs page docs/providers/nagaai.md and a provider icon.

Two ways to ship it, whichever you prefer:
1. In-tree as extensions/nagaai, published as @openclaw/nagaai-provider, like Cerebras.
2. Published and maintained by NagaAI as @naga-ai/openclaw-provider and listed with `source: external`, like @telnyx/openclaw-provider. The PR here would then add only the catalog entry, the docs page and the icon.

### Alternatives considered

A ClawHub plugin without a catalog entry. It works, but users find it only if they already know to search for it; onboarding lists catalog providers only.

### Impact

Affected: users who route OpenClaw through NagaAI.
Severity: annoying; manual setup and stale model lists.
Frequency: on every setup and whenever NagaAI adds or retires a model.
Consequence: hand-written model config, missing reasoning and image capabilities.

### Evidence/examples

Prior art: the Cerebras plugin (in-tree, live discovery), ClawRouter (`openai-responses` at a relay base URL) and @telnyx/openclaw-provider (vendor-published).
NagaAI API docs: https://docs.naga.ac
Model list format: https://docs.naga.ac/get-started/models
Public model list: https://api.naga.ac/v1/models

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Disclosure: I work on NagaAI and will maintain the plugin.

issues.body:
### Summary

On stable **2026.10.7**, background `exec` completion wakes still fail the way #168637 describes. #177063 fixed this on `main` on 2026-10-19, but the change isn't in `v2026.10.7` or `v2026.10.10-beta.3`. The installed `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication-state` still gates settings on any pending sharing publication: `readGenerationSettings: () => active && !pending(true) ? … : void 0`.

Two gaps also remain on `main` after #177063:

1. **A failed wake is never retried.** `session-event-handoff` only readmits a session event after a config-publication change (`MAX_CONFIG_READMISSION_ATTEMPTS = 2`). `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` says "retry after session storage is ready", but the handoff calls `ownership.cancel()`. The exec notifier then only logs `completion delivery failed`, so the completion notice is lost and the user sees a failed turn.
2. **Model fallback runs a candidate that can't succeed.** `prepareAgentRunAdmission` latches `sourceFailure`, so the fallback candidate fails in about 30 ms with "source execution authority is no longer active". The log reads like a model failure (`candidate_failed … next=opencode/…`) instead of a lifecycle or authority failure.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (npm global), Linux VPS, Gateway running as a systemd user service. Primary model `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, fallback `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Sessions come from the Control UI dashboard and Slack threads. `exec` runs with `notifyOnExit`.

### Observed (2026-10-26 UTC)

5 of about 20 event-triggered wakes failed in one day. Each one started a turn that died about 0.2 s into preparation, and the completion notice was dropped.

| Wake failed | Session | Previous turn in same session ended | Session-row write during preparation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:57:24.9 | dashboard | 4.5 min earlier | none logged (likely run-start bookkeeping) |
| 18:46:26.5 | dashboard | 1.4 s earlier | Control UI `sessions.patch` at 18:46:26.045 |
| 19:05:15.5 | Slack thread | 40 s earlier | Control UI `sessions.patch` at 19:05:15.177 |
| 19:47:31.3 | dashboard | 1.4 s earlier | Control UI `sessions.patch` at 19:47:30.759 |
| 21:35:19.5 | dashboard | 1.2 s earlier | none logged (turn-end bookkeeping; that turn followed a `prompt-tools` CLI session reset after config revision 40) |

Three of the five fired right after another turn in the same session settled. All five match #168637: a session-row publication lands inside the wake's preparation window.

```text
19:47:29.930 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=1705663
19:47:30.759 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.patch 87ms bytes=18779
19:47:31.300 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:dashboard:<id> durationMs=228 error="admitted run authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE"
19:47:31.322 [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=unknown next=opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash detail=admitted run authority is no longer active
19:47:31.454 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=24 error="source execution authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE" taskKind=turn
19:47:31.469 Embedded agent failed before reply: source execution authority is no longer active | …
19:47:31.480 [session-events] session event execution failed source=exec agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:<id> error="Session event execution failed"
19:47:31.481 [exec] completion delivery failed (Session event execution failed); inspect the process result.
```

### Repro conditions

- `claude-cli` runtime, background `exec` with `notifyOnExit`.
- The completion arrives while another turn in the same session is running or just settling, or while the Control UI has that session open and sends `sessions.patch`.
- The settled-foreground fixture in #168637 reproduces it on code without #177063.

### Ask

1. Backport #177063 to the stable 2026.10.x line.
2. Treat `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` as retryable in `session-event-handoff`: readmit with a bound once `prepareRead()` settles, as is already done for config changes. Or fall back to a passive system event so the next turn still sees the completion. Revoked or permission-restricted cases should keep failing closed.
3. Skip model fallback for latched admission or authority failures.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

While connected to a local Gateway and idle, the Linux desktop companion (`open-claw` 2026.9.4) starts three `openclaw` CLI commands on every watchdog round (`gateway status --json`, `nodes pending --json`, `devices list --json`); in two 60-second measurements, these short-lived processes and their children used 31% of one CPU core.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Ubuntu 26.04.1, run a local Gateway (OpenClaw 2026.9.4) and install the Linux companion `open-claw` 2026.9.4 (.deb).
2. Start the companion, let it connect to the local Gateway, and leave it idle.
3. For 60 seconds, read `usage_usec` from the companion's cgroup `cpu.stat` and list new PIDs in its `cgroup.procs` (or watch the companion's child processes in `ps`/`top`).

### Expected behavior

Reference: the macOS app had the same class of problem. It kept polling Devices and Automations after the status menu was closed (#136562). #136572 tied that refresh work to the menu's lifetime; its evidence table shows closed-menu `node.list` requests going from 8 to 0, with native CPU at about 2% of one core. The Linux companion is expected to behave comparably and not keep spawning CLI polls while idle.

### Actual behavior

- A new round starts about every 21 s: the 15 s `CONNECTED_WATCH_INTERVAL` sleep plus about 6 s while the commands run. In the log below, `gateway status --json` first appears at 16.6 s, 37.8 s and 59.0 s.
- In each round, the cgroup also showed `systemctl --user` and `ps` processes and three `sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js` processes between `gateway status --json` and `nodes pending --json`. `nodes pending --json` and `devices list --json` each also appeared as a second `node` process with `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning`.
- The companion's cgroup used 18,787 ms of CPU in a 60-second window (18,797 ms in an earlier run). Long-lived processes (the companion and WebKit) used 360 ms; the short-lived processes used 18,427 ms (31% of one core).
- The watchdog loop has no visibility condition. In v2026.9.4, `main.rs` L41 sets `CONNECTED_WATCH_INTERVAL` to 15 s, and `start_watchdog` (L905–L933) calls `gateway::status` and then `poll_pending_approvals` on every reachable tick. `gateway.rs` L128 runs `gateway status --json`; `pending_approvals.rs` L83 and L86 run `nodes pending --json` and `devices list --json`.
- The same loop is unchanged on `main` at `ca7c900`: `main.rs` L53 and `watch_local` L1829–L1853. `pending_approvals.rs` is identical to v2026.9.4.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d); companion package `open-claw` 2026.9.4

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, GNOME Shell 50.1, WebKitGTK 2.52.6)

### Install method

Companion: `open-claw` 2026.9.4 .deb. Its CLI calls run through `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` (shell launcher) with Node 24.19.0 under `~/.openclaw/tools`; an npm-global copy of the same version is also on `PATH`.

### Model

N/A (companion polling, not model-related)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# 60 s cgroup measurement, 2026-09-15 17:59-18:00 CEST
# <openclaw> = ~/.openclaw/tools/node-v24.19.0/lib/node_modules/openclaw
companion pid 4269, cgroup app-gnome-OpenClaw-4269.scope
processes in cgroup at start: openclaw-deskto, WebKitNetworkPr, WebKitWebProces, WebKitWebProces, openclaw, openclaw
measurer inside cgroup: False (expected False)
window: 60 s, sampling cgroup.procs every 0.1 s
```

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.4, an active WebChat conversation using the native Codex runtime and `steer` queue experienced accepted user prompts reaching the model transcript 8–62 minutes late, alongside failed completion handoff, unconfirmed steering consumption, and session-lane waits up to 75.8 minutes.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The documented `steer` behavior is to deliver at the next available model boundary, or defer until the active run ends when steering is unavailable. Acceptance alone is not consumption, and ambiguous inputs must not be replayed automatically. A failed continuation should not silently strand interactive inputs behind long-lived session ownership.

References: [Queue modes](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/queue), [Codex queue steering](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-harness-runtime/queue-and-feedback).

### Actual behavior

Observed during one long-running WebChat direct conversation with tool work and native child completions. Follow-up questions were answered much later, after intervening assistant output, making the conversation appear out of order and the assistant appear to ignore the user.

The local diagnostic compared preserved user submission timestamps against transcript append timestamps. Prompt text is omitted; each ID below denotes a separate submitted message. Times are 2026-09-13, UTC−04:00.

| Input | Submitted | Appended to model transcript | Delay |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 20:55:01 | 21:51:27 | 56.4 min |
| P2 | 21:00:06 | 22:02:07 | 62.0 min |
| P3 | 21:51:08 | 22:18:58 | 27.8 min |
| P4 | 22:00:50 | 22:20:17 | 19.4 min |
| P5 | 22:01:25 | 22:28:04 | 26.6 min |
| P6 | 22:02:34 | 22:31:19 | 28.8 min |
| P7 | 22:03:36 | 22:31:36 | 28.0 min |
| P8 | 22:23:55 | 22:31:59 | 8.1 min |

**Scope:** this establishes delayed transcript delivery/recording and stale follow-up handling. Sampled user-to-user order remained sequential; arbitrary inversion of two user messages is not proved. Permanent message loss, duplicate execution, and duplicate billing are not established.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (`3a9d69d`)

### Operating system

Omarchy 4.0.2 (Arch-based Linux), kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2, x86_64; Node v26.8.1.

### Install method

Global Node package; local Gateway service.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

WebChat direct → local OpenClaw Gateway → native Codex app-server runtime. Exact model/provider route for each failed turn was not established by this diagnostic.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Queue mode: `steer`. Native subagent completion announcements were present in the affected session. This is an incident report, not a deterministic reproduction or a claim that every native child triggers the failure.

### Logs

Sanitized excerpts from the Gateway file log. Same date/time offset as the table; identifiers omitted. The earlier failed completion wake and later announcement cleanup were correlated by the local trace.

```text
20:36:02.764
Active requester session could not be woken for subagent completion;

queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming gatewayHealth=live

21:51:27.255

21:51:33.731
failed to mirror codex app-server prompt at turn start
error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence"

21:51:49.686
queue message accepted without confirmation:
Codex accepted steering but did not confirm transcript consumption |
codex app-server steering queue aborted

21:51:49.893

21:51:53.716

error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence"
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The timestamp table and sanitized log excerpts above are the public evidence. No full transcripts, databases, private prompts, session/thread IDs, credentials, or diagnostics uploads are attached.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one observed WebChat direct session on 2026.9.4.
- Severity: blocks timely interaction and steering of ongoing work; repeated follow-ups receive stale answers tens of minutes later.
- Frequency: multiple delayed inputs in the same incident; frequency across other sessions is unknown.
- Gateway connectivity probe and configuration validation passed. No WebSocket disconnect/error churn was found in the bounded three-hour log inspection.

### Additional information

At 22:35:48 UTC−04:00, `diagnostics.lanes` showed all queue counts zero and only the diagnostic turn active. This session's pending-input records had no queued/interrupted inputs, only three older cancelled records. The backlog had drained, but no root fix was applied. No restart, queue-mode change, database edit, or input replay was performed.

The announcement/ownership stall, unconfirmed steering, and prompt-mirroring rejection are correlated; the full causal chain is **not established**. The annotation error is a redaction/provenance guard rejection, not evidence of SQLite corruption. Please preserve that guard and no-replay guarantees while investigating continuation ownership and consumption acknowledgement.

Related reports reviewed:

- #138723: native child completion wake/handoff stalls. Our logs overlap, but this report adds delayed ordinary WebChat inputs and unconfirmed steering on 2026.9.4; identical root cause is not proved.
- #143335: the same annotation redaction-guard error; its causal role here is unproved.
- #142813: delayed mid-turn channel messages on WhatsApp/2026.6.34, with a different delivery-loss signature.

Last known good / first introducing commit: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. Investigation and report preparation were AI-assisted; diagnostic evidence was read-only and sanitized before publication.

## Bug Report

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), macOS 26.4.1 arm64, node 26.9.0
**Runtime:** claude-cli agent runtime (model `claude-cli/claude-fable-5`), webchat channel (Control UI, single connected client)

**Describe the bug**
Since upgrading to 2026.9.6, assistant messages are intermittently delivered twice to webchat. The duplicate is not a UI rendering artifact: the same assistant message is recorded **twice in the session transcript**, ~293 ms apart, with the **identical idempotencyKey**, differing only in stopReason:

- record 1: timestamp `1790279252950`, `stopReason: "end_turn"`, `api: "cli"`, `provider: "claude-cli"`
- record 2: timestamp `1790279253243`, `stopReason: "stop"`
- both: `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:397f5a7e-274b-4b3d-815a-17e55bdc907b"`

So the CLI runtime double-emits the final assistant message (once on `end_turn`, once on `stop`) and idempotencyKey-based dedup does not collapse the pair; both records persist and both deliver to the channel.

**Frequency/pattern**
Intermittent within one evening session: 4 duplicated interim (pre-tool-call) assistant texts + at least 1 duplicated final message. Turns with tool calls seem overrepresented. Only one webchat client was connected (verified in gateway logs). Duplicates began immediately after the 2026.9.6 upgrade; the same session/agent had no duplicates before the upgrade.

**Context that may be relevant**
- The upgrade's first restart tripped a refused startup state migration (`codex:codex-app-server-orphaned-session-bindings`) and required `openclaw doctor --fix` before the gateway would start; duplicates appeared in the session that resumed afterwards.
- Several "OpenClaw resumed this CLI session after prompt content changed (changed=prompt-tools)" resumes occurred in the same session after config hot-reloads (plugin reinstall, per-agent subagents.allowAgents change).

**Expected behavior**
One assistant message per emit: either the runtime should not re-emit on `stop` after `end_turn`, or transcript/delivery dedup should collapse records sharing an idempotencyKey.

**Possibly related:** #125824 (idempotencyKey not honored as at-most-once delivery identity), #146472 (Control UI duplicated bubbles stream vs final — but in this report the duplicate exists in the transcript itself), #144918 (closed, UI duplicates).

## Problem

Authorized Discord reaction notifications currently remain passive system events; Signal reaction removals are ignored. Reactions therefore cannot reliably become conversational input with the original target context. Retried outbound reaction tool calls also lack a durable, transport-bound conversational receipt.

## Proposed scope

Keep the behavior in the existing Discord and Signal plugins: use their access/notification policies, native routing, ordinary room-event dispatch and existing durable ingress. Carry a small typed reaction context (actor, account/conversation, exact target, add/remove and transport occurrence). Reuse existing final-reaction conversational completion, adding a shared receipt operation over plugin-state worker stores for keyed sends.

A reaction must never accept a worker/task result, grant approval, clear a human gate or authorize destructive/production actions. Existing explicitly bound native approval controls remain a separate contract. No new manager, daemon, schema or configuration option is proposed.

## Evidence and limits

Deterministic tests exercise real SQLite ingress, actual channel handlers and ordinary dispatch with injected model/provider boundaries, plus outbound adapter receipt/replay/uncertainty cases. Live Discord, Signal and phone delivery and production activation are not claimed or requested by this source change.

issues.body:
## Summary

Matrix automatic progress, typing and reply callbacks can fail with `Matrix runtime not initialized` even though the account is connected and direct message sends work.

## Environment and reproduction

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4, Node 24.20, macOS, encrypted Matrix conversation with provider-plugin execution.
- Start a normal channel turn that emits partial replies or tool progress.
- The channel admits the turn, but the provider invokes the saved channel callback inside its own plugin invocation scope.
- The callback reads the channel runtime store from the provider instance and fails. Restarting and starting a new conversation did not resolve the reproduced failure.

Expected: automatic updates and replies use the runtime of the channel instance that admitted the turn.

Actual: automatic callbacks fail while independent direct sends and channel health probes continue to work.

## Root cause and evidence

The shared channel-turn delivery boundary passes delivery, dispatcher and reply-option callbacks into provider execution without retaining their admitting plugin instance. The per-instance runtime store correctly remains isolated; the callback is invoked under the wrong owner.

Four regressions through `runChannelTurn` reproduce the exact error for preview, typing, tool and final callbacks. Binding these callback records through the existing instance invocation owner repairs the cases while preserving payload/result identity and rejecting new calls after retirement. The same focused repair was deployed through the managed updater; a fresh real Matrix turn delivered automatic commentary, tool status and edited previews, and the operator independently confirmed visibility.

Related: #145804. That repair covers other shared callback boundaries; this report concerns channel-turn delivery. This is not a claim that every similarly named runtime-store failure has the same cause.

issues.body:
## What problem this solves

The official Perplexity plugin currently exposes only the `web_search` provider contract. Operators can use Perplexity's Search API for retrieval, but cannot opt into Agent API cited synthesis or deep research as a native plugin tool without separately configuring Perplexity as a model provider or installing an external MCP server.

## Proposed solution

Add one optional read-only tool to `@openclaw/perplexity-plugin`:

- `perplexity_research`
- required `query`
- optional explicit `effort`: `low | medium | high | xhigh`
- returns the synthesized answer plus normalized citations/search-result metadata
- reuses the plugin's existing Perplexity credential resolution
- is declared optional and hidden unless explicitly allowlisted

This leaves the existing `web_search` provider, Search API defaults, and OpenRouter compatibility unchanged. It also avoids encoding an opinionated automatic decision tree: the calling agent or operator chooses the effort level.

## Alternatives considered

- Four separate ask/reason/research tools: larger prompt and manifest surface for the same API.
- Change `web_search` to use Agent API: breaks the structured retrieval contract and existing users.
- Require Perplexity MCP: valid external option, but not equivalent to extending the official plugin users already installed.
- Native Router API support: premature while Router remains private preview.

## Evidence / prior art

- The plugin SDK supports mixed plugins with `webSearchProviders` plus optional tools.
- The bundled Tavily and Firecrawl plugins already combine provider and tool contracts.
- Perplexity Agent API exposes effort presets and cited search-backed output.
- #126889 documents Agent API/model-provider and MCP setup, but does not implement a native plugin tool.
- #152778 handles only the retiring synthesized `web_search` compatibility route and intentionally does not add new tool surface.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On the macOS Peekaboo provider, `get_window_state` passes a detection-only UUID to the owned-snapshot manager and fails with `Invalid snapshot reference ... expected ps1_ followed by 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits`, even though window enumeration, accessibility readback and input work.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run the OpenClaw macOS app based on 2026.9.3, with Computer Control enabled and Peekaboo selected. Accessibility and Screen Recording must be effectively granted.
2. Open a disposable TextEdit document. Use a gateway/session where the advertised V2 actions are exposed. If blocked at action-schema validation instead, that is the separate issue #148541.
3. Call `computer(action="list_windows", node="<paired-mac-node>")` and obtain the actual TextEdit `windowRef`.
4. Call `computer(action="get_window_state", node="<same-node>", windowRef="<returned-windowRef>")`.
5. Observe the snapshot-reference error below. The caller supplies a window reference, not the rejected snapshot UUID.

This is the observed live sequence, not a claimed clean-install or all-version reproduction.

### Expected behavior
Return the selected window observation using the provider's supported snapshot/reference lifecycle, as documented for the V2 window action family: [2026.9.3 computer-use contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.3/docs/nodes/computer-use.md).

### Actual behavior
```text
UNAVAILABLE: Invalid snapshot reference '<uppercase-hyphenated-UUID>'; expected ps1_ followed by 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits
```
The UUID above is redacted. It is generated inside the observation path.

In the same real session, `list_windows`, `get_accessibility_tree`, `bring_to_front`, click, typing into the identified disposable document and final accessibility readback succeeded. A separate observer verified the text. This is not a blanket permission or disconnected-node failure.

### OpenClaw version
Live failure: 2026.9.3 macOS app, based on tag commit `1391f7cd2d40ab5bbcf2f5f831d3a64f520e72d7`, with an unrelated local Apple Event permission-probe backport. The affected executor, Package.swift and Package.resolved are unchanged from the official tag. Built Peekaboo checkout is clean at the official pinned revision `44eff916c3330739108cc1d73683338d4250503a`.

The gateway also has a bounded V2 schema-exposure fix; the reported error occurs after successful dispatch inside the unchanged macOS executor, not in that schema layer.

Source-only follow-up found the same relevant consumer in v2026.9.5 with Peekaboo 4.4.0. No live 9.5 test was performed.

### Operating system
macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon Mac mini (M1).

### Install method
Signed macOS app, connected as a paired node to a Gateway.

### Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain
Gateway agent `computer` tool → paired macOS node `computer.act` → in-process Peekaboo provider.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
The source chain matching the live error is:

1. [OpenClaw getWindowState](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.3/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ComputerWindowActionExecutor.swift#L271) constructs `DesktopObservationRequest` without output options, then manually calls `snapshotManager.storeDetectionResult` using `elements.snapshotId`.
2. [Pinned request model](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/blob/44eff916c3330739108cc1d73683338d4250503a/Core/PeekabooAutomationKit/Sources/PeekabooAutomationKit/Services/Observation/DesktopObservationRequestModels.swift#L347) defaults to `saveSnapshot=false`, `snapshotID=nil`.
3. [ObservationOutputWriter](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/blob/44eff916c3330739108cc1d73683338d4250503a/Core/PeekabooAutomationKit/Sources/PeekabooAutomationKit/Services/Observation/ObservationOutputWriter.swift#L67) does not reserve an owned snapshot in that case.
4. [SnapshotPublicationBinding](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/blob/44eff916c3330739108cc1d73683338d4250503a/Core/PeekabooAutomationKit/Sources/PeekabooAutomationKit/Services/Support/SnapshotPublicationBinding.swift#L4) generates `UUID().uuidString` for a detection-only result with no explicit snapshot ID.
5. [InMemorySnapshotManager store](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/blob/44eff916c3330739108cc1d73683338d4250503a/Core/PeekabooAutomationKit/Sources/PeekabooAutomationKit/Services/Support/InMemorySnapshotManager%2BLifecycle.swift#L51) requires an existing owned entry; [ID validation](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/blob/44eff916c3330739108cc1d73683338d4250503a/Core/PeekabooAutomationKit/Sources/PeekabooAutomationKit/Services/Support/InMemorySnapshotManager.swift#L171) rejects this UUID before ownership checking.

The [v2026.9.5 executor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ComputerWindowActionExecutor.swift#L271) retains the omitted output options/manual store sequence. This is source inspection, not runtime confirmation on 9.5.

### Impact and severity
Affected: the tested macOS Peekaboo V2 window-observation path.
Severity: blocks full window-state retrieval and workflows depending on its returned references.
Frequency: observed in the bounded live acceptance attempt; population-wide frequency and first affected release are NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.
Consequence: the agent cannot use this window-state operation. Separate accessibility readback/input remained usable in the tested document. No data loss observed.

### Additional information
A repair should use the owned snapshot reservation/publication lifecycle, not merely reformat the UUID or weaken validation: ownership is required as well. A regression test should exercise the real observation-to-publication integration.

The standalone Peekaboo CLI is a distinct consumer; [v4.4.0 see](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/blob/v4.4.0/Apps/CLI/Sources/PeekabooCLI/Commands/AI/SeeCommand%2BObservationRequest.swift#L87-L113) explicitly requests `saveSnapshot: true`.

CUA was investigated as an alternative but did not reach Computer Control readiness on this installation. Its separate node-host-worker startup failure is not attributed to this snapshot defect and is intentionally not combined into this issue. Peekaboo was restored and real window enumeration verified afterward.

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), @openclaw/matrix 2026.10.9, Linux.

**Config:** `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["matrix:user:@alice:example.org"]`, the form listed in `docs/channels/matrix/accounts-and-homeservers.md` ("Users: `@user:server`, `user:@user:server`, or `matrix:user:@user:server`").

**What happens:** in a room, `@bot /acp doctor` and `@bot /acp spawn …` from `@alice:example.org` get no reply at all. Only the debug log shows:

```text
Ignoring /acp from unauthorized sender: @alice:example.org
```

**Why** (reading `dist/command-auth-*.mjs`): in `resolveOwnerAllowFromList` the check `/^[^:]+:user:[^:\s*]+$/` does not match because a Matrix user ID itself contains a colon, so the entry is kept as `user:@alice:example.org` and never equals the sender. Because an explicit owner list is configured, `isOwnerForCommands` is then false for every sender, access becomes `"reset-only"`, and even the public `/acp doctor` is refused.

**Works:** `matrix:@alice:example.org`.

**Expected:**
1. The documented `matrix:user:@user:server` form matches Matrix senders (or the docs list only the form that works for `ownerAllowFrom`).
2. An unauthorized `/acp` in a room gets a short refusal, as for other owner-only commands, instead of silence.

issues.body:
The containerized-gateway docs only describe host-centric behavior: they never explain how a gateway inside a container reaches model servers on the host (the host-gateway alias fails the SSRF guard under rootless Podman), never warn that `gateway.bind: "loopback"`/`"tailnet"` leave published ports unreachable inside a container, and lack troubleshooting entries for common rootless-Podman failure modes.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

- `docs/install/podman.md` — https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/podman
- `docs/install/docker/networking-and-storage.md` — https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/docker/networking-and-storage
- `docs/gateway/local-models.md` — https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/local-models

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Open `docs/install/podman.md` — there is no section on reaching host-local model servers. An operator who points a provider `baseUrl` at `host.docker.internal:<port>` (the standard container pattern) hits `Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address` with no documented cause or fix.
2. Search `docs/install/podman.md` and `docs/install/docker/networking-and-storage.md` for bind-mode guidance — nothing warns that `loopback` and `tailnet` are host-centric. Inside a container, both leave published ports unable to reach the gateway while startup logs report ready.
3. Check the troubleshooting list in `docs/install/podman.md` — no entries for:
   - `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process` when running config commands outside the gateway container
   - `failed to change selinux label: insufficient permissions` on root-owned bind mounts
   - EACCES from one-off `podman run` commands that touch gateway state without `--userns=keep-id`
4. Follow `docs/gateway/local-models.md` for scripted setup — non-interactive onboarding with a hosted `--auth-choice` silently ignores `--custom-*` flags, so there is no documented path to a hosted primary + local fallback.

### Expected docs behavior/content

- A "Reaching model servers on the host" section in the Podman doc: map the alias (`--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` for manual runs, `AddHost=` for Quadlets; `host.containers.internal` is automatic on recent Podman), and explain that under rootless Podman the alias resolves to a link-local address (`169.254.1.2`) which exact-origin SSRF trust excludes. Document both fixes: prefer the host LAN/tailnet IP as the provider `baseUrl`, or opt in per provider with `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork: true`.
- A bind-mode warning in both the Podman and Docker docs: inside a container, keep `lan` (the setup default) or use `custom` with `customBindHost: "0.0.0.0"`, and scope exposure through published ports.
- Troubleshooting entries for the ownership lock (run config-mutating commands through `openclaw --container <name>` or `podman exec`; wait about 90 seconds after stopping the gateway for the ownership heartbeat to expire), the SELinux relabel failure (plain `ro` mount for system directories you don't own; reserve `:Z` for state directories your user owns), and the keep-id requirement for one-off commands touching gateway state.
- A non-interactive hybrid setup recipe in `docs/gateway/local-models.md`: onboard with the hosted provider, patch the local provider into config (`openclaw config patch --file`), then `openclaw models fallbacks add` — running config-mutating steps through the container once the gateway is up.

### Actual docs behavior/content

- No host-model-server networking section; the alias/link-local SSRF interaction is undocumented for generic custom providers.
- Bind-mode docs describe host semantics only; no container-namespace caveat or published-ports guidance.
- Troubleshooting covers token generation, catatonit, host-path ownership EACCES, `gateway.mode`, image updates, and CLI targeting — but not the ownership lock, SELinux relabel, or keep-id mapping for one-off commands.
- No non-interactive recipe for combining a hosted provider with a local fallback provider.

### Impact

Operators running the gateway in Podman/Docker with local models (llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM) hit unexplained SSRF blocks, unreachable published ports, config-write rejections, or container-start failures, and must reverse-engineer causes from error strings. Scripted/headless setups have no documented path to hybrid hosted+local inference.

### Evidence

Behavior verified against the current source tree:

- Bind fallback: `src/gateway/net.ts` `resolveGatewayBindHost` — `loopback` → `127.0.0.1`; in a container `tailnet` finds no Tailscale interface and falls back to `127.0.0.1`; `lan` → `0.0.0.0`. The Quadlet template `scripts/podman/openclaw.container.in` ships `--bind lan` with `127.0.0.1`-published ports (18789/18790).
- Ownership lock: `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts` — error text `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process`; `GATEWAY_OWNER_HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS = 90_000`; its own remediation text says to run inside the Gateway container or a shared PID namespace.
- SSRF/link-local: `src/agents/provider-network-policy.ts` — exact-origin trust excludes link-local hostnames; `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts` — trusted-host resolved-address checks reject link-local DNS answers without the Podman-specific exemption; `allowPrivateNetwork: true` bypasses both.
- Onboarding: `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/` — when `--auth-choice` is set, custom flags are never read and no warning is emitted.
- Observed on a real rootless Quadlet deployment (Fedora, rootless Podman): all three troubleshooting failure modes reproduced; the alias `baseUrl` is rejected while a LAN-IP `baseUrl` works.

### Related issues

Earlier issues fixed the underlying code paths but left the documentation gap that operators still fall into:

- #68684 — Docker setup wizard now defaults local providers to `host.docker.internal`, but the rootless-Podman link-local SSRF behavior (and its fixes) remain undocumented.
- #79850 — SSRF guard vs. `*.internal` hostnames; resolved as "works with `allowPrivateNetwork: true`", yet that workaround was never documented — a later commenter in that thread was still hunting for it.
- #163315 — Ollama memory embeddings got a narrow link-local exemption (#172015, `host.containers.internal` only); generic custom providers on rootless Podman remain undocumented.

These confirm the behavior is correct and intended; what is missing is the documentation. A fix is prepared on a branch covering all four gaps; a PR referencing this issue will follow.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Session state / gateway performance (event-loop starvation)

### Summary

After the sqlite→jsonl session migration (`openclaw doctor` session-sqlite path), `session-sqlite-import-archive/` — the migration's **already-imported source archive** — is left inside every agent directory (`<state>/agents/<agentId>/session-sqlite-import-archive/`, created by `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts`). Session-state initialization and post-ready prewarm then walk/parse that archive **synchronously on the main thread**: with a large migrated store this blocks the Node event loop for **~6 minutes per load**, freezing the entire gateway — channel polling, healthcheck, even signal handling.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have an agent with a large sqlite-era session store; run the session-sqlite migration (or upgrade across it). Our `main` agent's archive ended up 575MB / 868 `.jsonl.imported-*` files; 15 agents totaled ~690MB.
2. Restart the gateway, or trigger any interaction that initializes session state on an affected agent (e.g. an inbound Telegram message → `reply.init_session_state`).
3. Observe the event loop pegged at ~100% of one core for the duration, with no log output.

### Expected behavior

Already-imported `*.imported-*` archive artifacts should be skipped by session enumeration/materialization, and any bulk parsing should happen off the main thread (worker) with a materialized cache. Boot and per-reply session init should stay in the sub-second range regardless of archive size.

### Actual behavior

Measured on 2026.9.3 with the archive present:

```
reply resolver timings ... reply.init_session_state:347506ms   (also 342205 / 343716 / 378058 / 385348 / 409839 ms across messages)
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization ... eventLoopDelayMaxMs=377420 eventLoopUtilization=1 cpuCoreRatio≈1.0 phase=post-ready.gateway-data.sessions.<agent>
[health] host timing gap detected: process was frozen ~335876ms
```

- Each affected interaction stalls ~6 min; consecutive loads chain into 20+ min of continuous 1-core saturation.
- The Docker healthcheck flips unhealthy mid-block.
- `SIGUSR1` (graceful in-process restart) **cannot be handled** while the loop is blocked — the signal queued for 8+ minutes behind the freezes.
- Inbound channel updates hit the ingress `handler-timeout` (~348s) and cycle through retry, so messages are effectively lost or delivered extremely late.

Moving the archives out of the agent dirs (nothing else changed) took post-restart CPU from 100%+ to 2% and inbound→reply latency from ~6 min to ~24s.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.3 (1391f7c), gateway docker image, node 24.19.0

### Operating system

Linux (docker); state dir on ext4, ~690MB archive total

### Install method

Docker (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.9.3 lineage)

### Model

zai glm-5.3 (irrelevant to the freeze — the block is pre-model)

### Provider / routing chain

n/a

### Logs

See "Actual behavior" (liveness/diagnostic excerpts). Can provide full logs on request.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

n/a (log-based)

### Impact and severity

**Severe for anyone with a large migrated session store.** Every reply on an affected agent stalls minutes; the whole gateway (all channels, crons, healthcheck) freezes with it; graceful restart is impossible until a block yields. Likely code paths: `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts` (`reply.init_session_state`) and `src/gateway/server-startup-handler-prewarm.ts` (`post-ready.gateway-data.${name}` loads). Suggested fixes: (1) skip `session-sqlite-import-archive/` and `*.imported-*` in session enumeration; (2) off-thread bulk materialization + cache; (3) regression test asserting init time stays bounded with a large archive present. Workaround (verified): move `session-sqlite-import-archive/` out of the agent directories.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An ambient heartbeat whose heartbeat file is intentionally empty/comments-only skips every interval by design, but each skip is recorded as a *failed* task in `openclaw tasks list --status failed`, even though the heartbeat event layer reports the run as ok-empty/silent with consecutiveErrors=0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Leave the agent's heartbeat file empty/comments-only (the stock template reads: "Keep this file empty (or with only comments) to skip heartbeat API calls").
2. Let the ambient heartbeat run for several hours (`agents.defaults.heartbeat = {"every":"30m"}`).
3. `openclaw cron get <heartbeat-id>` → `lastRunStatus:"skipped"`, `lastError:"heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file"`, `consecutiveSkipped` rising, `consecutiveErrors:0`.
4. `openclaw tasks list --status failed` → one row per interval (~48/day) for the heartbeat cron, reason `heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file`.

### Expected behavior

An intentional ok-empty skip should be recorded as *skipped* (or excluded from `--status failed`), consistent with `openclaw system heartbeat last` already reporting `status:"ok-empty"`, `silent:true`, `indicatorType:"ok"`. A designed no-op should not surface as a failed task.

### Actual behavior

Each intended skip is labeled *failed* in task accounting: `openclaw tasks list --status failed` accrues ~48 rows/day for the heartbeat cron, all with reason `heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file`, and `consecutiveSkipped` climbs unbounded (observed 330). Failed-task counts and any monitor/audit built on `--status failed` are inflated with false positives, despite `consecutiveErrors:0` and `openclaw system heartbeat last` reporting `ok-empty`/`silent`/`indicatorType:"ok"`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro (build 26200)

### Install method

npm global (openclaw); local gateway, login-item

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 (agent default; not exercised — the empty-file skip returns before any model call)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> local LiteLLM proxy -> anthropic (agent default; not exercised — skip returns before any provider request)

### Additional provider/model setup details

The failing path is model/provider-independent: `heartbeat-runner-*.js` calls `contentEffectivelyEmpty(heartbeatScratchContent)` and returns `skipReason:"empty-heartbeat-file"` before any model or provider request. Config: `agents.defaults.heartbeat = {"every":"30m"}`; `agents.entries.main.heartbeat` unset (inherits). Related theme: #83143.


_No response_

Affected: any agent whose heartbeat file is intentionally kept empty/comments-only (the documented way to skip heartbeat API calls).

issues.body:
## Summary
A required subagent completion can successfully send the final answer to a Slack DM thread through the message tool, return `NO_REPLY`, and still fail requester settlement with `visible_reply_missing`. The expected destination is `user:U000000001`, while the settled receipt identifies its actual DM conversation as `D000000001` (also observed in normalized `channel:d000000001` form).

These identifiers are synthetic. The defect is destination equivalence in delivery bookkeeping, not a failed Slack send or a request to accept unverified silence.

## Version and evidence scope
Reproduced against the unmodified 2026.9.2 delivery function and native delivery-evidence helpers with a controlled Gateway response. The relevant direct-delivery path was also inspected in published 2026.9.4 and current main at the pinned source below. This is not a claim of a live end-to-end run on main.

## Reproduction
1. Set up a required child completion with a user-facing requester, `requireVisibleReply: true`, Slack destination `user:U000000001`, account `default`, thread `1700000000.000001`.
2. Let the requester send its complete answer through the message tool to that user's verified DM conversation `D000000001`, in the same thread and account.
3. Return this synthetic successful requester result to `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly`:
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [{"text": "NO_REPLY"}],
    "meta": {"stopReason": "end_turn"},
    "didSendViaMessagingTool": true,
    "messagingToolSentTargets": [{
      "provider": "slack", "to": "D000000001", "accountId": "default",
      "threadId": "1700000000.000001", "text": "Complete report delivered",
      "sourceReplyFinal": true
    }]
  }
}
```
4. Observe `{delivered:false, reason:"visible_reply_missing", error:"completion agent did not produce a visible reply"}` despite the completed send.

Expected: credit the committed final receipt only after verifying that the DM conversation belongs to the expected user, with identical account and thread. Do not resend the answer.

## Mechanism and fix direction
`hasMessagingToolDeliveryToSource` relies on `sourceDeliveryTargetsMatch`; normalization alone cannot establish the relationship between a user ID and a DM conversation ID. [Current direct-delivery source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/520bf609efacf80918d84c9a196288b646076574/src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts).

An isolated candidate fix that resolves the receipt's conversation to the exact recipient and adds an equivalent destination to this attempt's delivery evidence changes the result to `{delivered:true, requesterVisibleFinalDelivered:true}`. It does not rewrite the outbound destination or bypass account/thread checks.

Regression coverage should include wrong recipient, different account, omitted account under a non-default account, wrong thread/provider, `final:false`, absent receipt, failed recipient lookup, abort, and requester ownership change during lookup. A focused native-function suite with those boundaries passes 24 cases against the candidate. Default-account omission must not become a wildcard for arbitrary accounts.

Related: #121187 (silent completion settlement), #142037 (different explicit-route bookkeeping defect involving top-level thread placement). Here the thread is identical; the mismatch is specifically user destination versus verified DM conversation.

3. It returns { base: "HEAD", baseRef: "HEAD" } without considering origin/trunk.

### Expected behavior

All changes should compare against the intended branch base or indicate that no reliable base is known. The resolver documents a branch-relative merge base; silently substituting HEAD loses that distinction.

### Actual behavior

For this ref layout, both all and uncommitted compare HEAD with the working tree. The scope remains all; only its comparison base falls back. This follows from source inspection, not a captured Gateway/UI response.

### OpenClaw version

Source inspected: 21eb84fbf795c0ab38c549f06a6fa44657a4de23 (merged #144246). Runtime version for this case: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Operating system

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Install method

Source inspection only; no installation modified.

### Model

N/A: Git base resolution

### Provider / routing chain

N/A: local Git diff collection

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

### Local-checkout flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["sessions.diff: scope=all"] --> B["loadSessionDiff forwards scope"]
  B --> C["loadCheckoutDiff resolves branchBase"]
  C --> D["origin/HEAD absent"]
  D --> E["main/master and origin/main/master absent"]
  E --> F["Return base=HEAD; origin/trunk not considered"]
  F --> G["all uses branchBase.base"]
  G --> H["HEAD to working tree"]
  I["uncommitted explicitly uses HEAD"] --> H
```

- [Merged resolver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/21eb84fbf795c0ab38c549f06a6fa44657a4de23/src/sessions/session-diff-revisions.ts#L13-L49): no scope parameter; its caller decides how to use the base.
- [Scope forwarding in the reported implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93b59c0dae/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-diff.ts#L75-L94).
- [Comparison selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a93b59c0dae/src/sessions/session-diff.ts#L440-L482): all uses branchBase; uncommitted uses HEAD. The scope is not renamed; the comparison points coincide.

Session-start filtering runs afterward and cannot recover committed changes omitted by the HEAD comparison.

### Impact and severity

Committed branch changes can be omitted from All changes. Repository data is unchanged. Runtime frequency and affected-user count: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information

### Related, not a duplicate

#144246 fixed #144205 by adding origin/main and origin/master fallbacks. This follow-up asks how to select a reliable base and expose an unknown base, not to add trunk to the list or undo that fix.

Design questions:
- Should an explicit review/PR base take precedence?
- Which remote should supply the base for forks?
- How should nonstandard branch/remote names be discovered?
- What should Review show when discovery fails?

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Two observed requests spent 66 and 151 seconds in the aggregate system-prompt preparation interval before their model calls; current diagnostics do not identify which awaited dependency or synchronous segment consumed that time.

## Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Expected behavior

Later observed requests on this deployment completed preparation in under four seconds. A private request with a short exact-response prompt should not spend over a minute preparing before inference, and preparation diagnostics should let operators distinguish the delayed operation.

## Actual behavior

The hosted request spent 65,985 ms in system-prompt preparation and 66,168 ms in total preparation, then successfully answered in a 6,850 ms model interval. A separate queued local-provider request spent 150,845 ms in system-prompt preparation, followed by a roughly 50 ms model attempt. Resource-loader work in those runs took 55 and 224 ms, respectively. The hosted request also waited about 44 seconds in the session queue, so an 85-second CLI wait expired before the successful final result was available.

## OpenClaw version

Observed release string: OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (2b26444). The deployment carries previously reviewed local changes. The new incident diagnostic patch has not been applied. These observations have not been reproduced on current upstream main.

## Operating system

macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon; gateway Node 24.21.0.

## Install method

Source checkout with a launchd-managed gateway and a versioned runtime build.

## Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash for the successful hosted check; configured local deepseek-v4.1-flash for the other measured preparation span.

## Provider / routing chain

Hosted check: OpenClaw -> official DeepSeek endpoint. Other measured preparation: OpenClaw -> operator-managed local OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint. The reported intervals precede inference.

## Additional provider/model setup details

Both timings come from the same preserved durable conversation after compaction. The successful hosted check requested a short exact response with delivery disabled.

## Logs

```text
hosted: totalMs=66168
bundle-tools completed @121ms
system-prompt:65985ms@66106ms
session-resource-loader:55ms
model interval: durationMs=6850
terminal result: successful, exact expected response

local: system-prompt:150845ms
session-resource-loader:224ms
model attempt: approximately 50ms
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source attribution: attempt-stage-timing.ts measures wall time since the preceding stage marker. attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts marks system-prompt only at its end, after runtime prompt lookup, docs/source resolution, memory-prompt plugin preparation, optional project-memory lookup, and synchronous prompt/report construction. Current evidence does not isolate the slow operation or prove a continuous synchronous event-loop block.

## Impact and severity

Two observed preparation delays in one conversation; the hosted diagnostic succeeded but its overall queue-plus-preparation latency exceeded the CLI wait. The last observed later replies were faster. Recurrence conditions remain unknown.

## Additional information

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148349 corrected attribution of tool preparation, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153432 addresses a separate interrupted-replay boundary. Neither establishes a fix for these observed system-prompt spans. This report is separate from the original 124-second session-preparation/channel stall. Required next diagnostic work: instrument individual awaits and synchronous assembly segments with privacy-safe owner identity and event-loop evidence before selecting a functional fix.


## Proposed follow-up and acceptance criteria

1. Instrument runtime-prompt lookup, docs/source resolution, memory-prompt plugins, optional project-memory lookup, and synchronous prompt assembly separately. Record bounded timings and privacy-safe owner identity, not prompt content. Correlate event-loop delay to distinguish waiting from blocking.
2. Establish which operation owns the observed delay, then reproduce that boundary in isolated state with a controlled delayed dependency or a representative safe fixture. Compare the inspected source against the exact active build before assuming identical boundaries.
3. Prefer an existing upstream change only if it covers that proven path. Otherwise submit a narrow fix that yields, caches, or bounds the identified operation without hiding failures or dropping required context.
4. Verify the identified operation is bounded or responsive under its reproducer, cancellation settles, unrelated gateway requests remain responsive, and fresh conversation replies complete with recorded preparation/model/queue times. Do not close solely because later turns happen to be fast.

Related candidate, not an established remedy: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148822 addresses synchronous pinned-skill Library reads. This has not been demonstrated to be the delayed operation here.

This is an AI-assisted report of two measured preparation spans. The cause and deterministic minimal reproduction remain outstanding.

## Related reports from this incident

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156229
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156230

These reports describe distinct observed phases; a shared root cause has not been established.
