### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

A Mattermost interactive button click is answered with HTTP 200 and then handled entirely from process RAM, so a gateway restart or crash after the 200 silently loses the click. Mattermost treats the 200 as final and does not redeliver, the click never reaches durable ingress, and `chat`-side post updates can even rewrite the buttons so the UI claims the click was handled.

In `createMattermostInteractionHandler` (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts`):

- `interactions.ts:629` enqueues the click into the in-memory system-event queue (`core.system.enqueueSystemEvent`), which is documented as intentionally non-persistent, capped at 20 entries, and cleared on restart.
- `interactions.ts:654` then responds `200` with `{}`.
- `interactions.ts:661` runs `dispatchButtonClick` only after the 200, inside a swallowed try/catch, so a thrown handler error also loses the click without any retry.

The Mattermost durable ingress (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-ingress.ts`) only admits `posted` WebSocket events, so interactions have no durable row at any point.

This is the Mattermost sibling of the Slack defect fixed in PR #132809 (Slack interactives were acked before durable admission). The Slack fix does not touch Mattermost because the seams differ: Slack had an existing durable receiver admission that interactions merely bypassed, while the Mattermost interaction HTTP endpoint sits outside its message-only ingress pipeline and its custom-handler branch must keep returning dynamic synchronous HTTP bodies. Distinct from #64545 (token forgeability, fixed) and from the heartbeat-injection reports #102380/#91888/#99544.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the Mattermost channel and have the agent post a message with interactive buttons (default-on when Mattermost is enabled, no extra flags).
2. Click a button; observe the provider receives HTTP 200.
3. Restart or kill the gateway before the next heartbeat consumes the in-memory system event.
4. The click never produces an agent turn and is not recoverable anywhere.

### Expected behavior

The HTTP 200 to Mattermost is sent only after the interaction is durably recorded, and a restart replays the click, matching the admit-then-ack contract the message paths (and now Slack interactions via PR #132809) follow.

### Actual behavior

The 200 is sent while the only copy of the click lives in the process-local system-event queue; restart or crash after the 200 discards it with no trace, and `dispatchButtonClick` failures after the 200 are swallowed.

### OpenClaw version

main f9b3bcccdba3dc159c6484c30f56974b90a6d938

### Operating system

macOS 15 (defect is platform-independent, verified from source)

### Install method

git clone (source checkout)

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

Mattermost channel plugin, interactive message action webhook path

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Runtime trace from driving the production `createMattermostInteractionHandler` against the real system-event queue with the HTTP response as the ack seam (network stubbed only at the Mattermost post GET/PUT):

```
mattermost HTTP status returned to provider: 200
mattermost HTTP body: {}
mattermost dispatchButtonClick ran after HTTP 200: true
mattermost owner-facing queue after 200, before restart: ["Mattermost button click: action=\"approve\" by alice in channel chan-1"]
mattermost owner-facing queue after restart: []
RESULT mattermost: http=200 queuedBeforeRestart=1 queuedAfterRestart=0 lost=true
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code references on main f9b3bcccdba3: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts:629` (RAM enqueue), `interactions.ts:654` (200 response), `interactions.ts:661` (post-200 swallowed dispatch); non-durable queue contract documented at the system-event queue definition in the plugin SDK system-event runtime.

### Impact and severity

P1 silent data loss on a default-on interactive surface: the user action and the agent turn it should produce disappear with no error, no record, and a UI that can indicate success.

issues.body:
### Summary

Replace the static progress label with the latest primary-model commentary when narration is unavailable, independently of whether commentary history is displayed.

### Problem to solve

In `streaming.mode: "progress"`, the draft begins with a generic label such as `Working`.

When narration is enabled, generated narration replaces that generic label with a meaningful description of the current activity. When narration is disabled or unavailable, the label remains permanently static even though the primary model may already be producing useful commentary.

The latest commentary could provide a meaningful current-status label without requiring a separate narration-model request.

### Proposed solution

When progress streaming is active and narration has not supplied a headline:

1. Show the configured progress label as the initial fallback.
2. When commentary becomes available, replace only that generic label with the latest commentary.
3. Update the label as the latest commentary streams.
4. Replace the label again when newer commentary arrives.
5. Preserve tool, plan, approval, and other progress lines unchanged.
6. Fall back to the configured label if no usable commentary is available.
7. Stop updating the draft when final-answer delivery begins.

The headline behavior must not depend on `streaming.progress.commentary`. That setting should continue to control whether commentary lines are displayed in the draft body, not whether commentary can be used as the current headline:

- `commentary: false`: do not display commentary timeline lines, but the latest commentary may still be used as the headline.
- `commentary: true`: display commentary timeline lines as before, while also using the latest commentary as the headline.
- Historical commentary must not be removed or collapsed when commentary display is enabled.

**Examples**

With commentary-line display disabled:

```text
Checking the current compositor behavior.

🔧 Exec: rg ...
```

With commentary-line display enabled:

```text
Testing the proposed behavior against existing semantics.

_Checking the current compositor behavior._
🔧 Exec: rg ...
_Testing the proposed behavior against existing semantics._
```

Before any commentary is available:

```text
Working

🔧 Exec: rg ...
```

**Expected behavior**

1. The first line represents the latest current status.
2. The configured label is only a fallback.
3. Commentary-line visibility remains controlled independently by `streaming.progress.commentary`.
4. Enabling commentary continues to preserve the complete commentary timeline.
5. Disabling commentary hides the timeline but does not prevent commentary from supplying the headline.
6. Deterministic progress lines retain their current behavior and ordering.
7. Existing sanitization, truncation, throttling, silent-text filtering, and final-delivery guards continue to apply.
8. Existing narration behavior retains precedence when narration supplies a headline.

**Benefits**

- Replaces the static `Working` label with meaningful current status.
- Reuses commentary already produced by the primary model.
- Requires no additional narration-model request.
- Keeps headline selection independent from commentary-history visibility.
- Preserves the complete commentary timeline when enabled.
- Preserves deterministic tool and progress telemetry.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Impact

Affected: users of many frontier models that provide "commentary" channel, who have enabled progress streaming and disabled narration
Severity: minor
Frequency: always for the given configuration
Consequences: more informative progress message without additional model calls

### Evidence/examples

_No response_

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary

Two related ways the model ends up with no conversation history even though the OpenClaw session transcript on disk is complete and appending correctly:

1. **`sessionMode: "none"` — structural.** Interactive Mattermost DM turns run as fresh CLI executions with no history in the prompt. Reproduced on 2026.6.11 and on a pinned 2026.7.1-2 install.
2. **`sessionMode: "always"` — intermittent.** A turn resumes a session id that has no matching transcript file on disk (a "phantom" resume). The turn logs `historyPrompt=present`, but the model demonstrably has no memory of the immediately preceding exchange. Observed on 2026.6.11; one turn had full context and a turn one minute later in the same thread had none.

In both cases `historyPrompt=present` is logged, so the failure is invisible from the journal.

## Observed (`none`, 2026.6.11 and 2026.7.1-2)

Gateway journal per user turn:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-4-6 promptChars=554 trigger=user useResume=false session=present resumeSession=none reuse=reusable historyPrompt=present
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session start: ... activeSessions=1
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session turn: ... durationMs=...
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session close: ... reason=restart
```

- `promptChars` ≈ 530-560 for every turn = current message only, despite `historyPrompt=present`.
- The live session is closed with `reason=restart` after every turn, so no in-process continuity either.
- Result: the model cannot see even its own immediately preceding answer (e.g. it answers "which PDF do you mean?" to a follow-up about a PDF list it produced 4 minutes earlier in the same DM). Reproduced across independent agents.
- The per-session `.jsonl` transcript on disk contains the full conversation; only delivery to the model is missing.

Reading the 2026.7.1-2 code (claude-live-session), this looks structural rather than a regression: when the backend is resume-capable and `useResume=false` (which is what `sessionMode: "none"` produces), the existing live session is deliberately closed at turn start, and the fresh CLI run is seeded only from compaction content — which is empty before the first compaction. `reseedFromRawTranscriptWhenUncompacted: true` does not cover ordinary turns either: raw reseed is gated on a reason allowlist (`missing-transcript, orphaned-tool-use, message-policy, system-prompt, cwd, mcp, session-expired`), i.e. binding invalidation and resets, not normal continuation turns. So none-mode has a structural amnesia window between session start and first compaction.

## Observed (`always`, 2026.6.11)

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: ... trigger=user useResume=true resumeSession=34d27d586241 historyPrompt=present promptChars=891
```

- No transcript file matching `34d27d586241` existed on disk (694 transcript files checked; the session store's own id also did not match).
- The turn produced an answer with zero knowledge of the conversation seconds earlier; the next turn in the same thread had full context again. Intermittent, not constant.
- Expectation would be that a resume pointing at a missing transcript triggers the `missing-transcript` reseed path; in this case it apparently did not.

## Expected

- With `sessionMode: "none"`: model context rebuilt from the OpenClaw session transcript each turn (as documented), bounded by compaction settings.
- With `sessionMode: "always"`: a resume against a non-existent CLI session should fall back to transcript reseed rather than silently running with an empty context.
- In both cases: if no history was actually delivered, the journal should say so (`historyPrompt=present` currently overstates).

## Environment

- openclaw 2026.6.11 (global install) and a pinned 2026.7.1-2 test install, @openclaw/mattermost 2026.6.11/2026.7.1, claude-cli backend, Linux (Ubuntu), one gateway per Linux user.
- `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"` (workspace bootstrap files inject fine; verified via systemPromptReport.injectedWorkspaceFiles).

Happy to provide more logs/repro details.

## Related

- #124991 (open) documents CLI session reseed being inert on SQLite session stores (`loadCliSessionEntries` reads the legacy JSONL path). The installs here use the per-session JSONL store — the transcripts exist and are complete — so this report is a different failure in the same area: with `sessionMode: "none"` history is structurally never delivered, and with `"always"` a resume can point at a transcript id that does not exist on disk.

issues.body:
# RFC: Surface plugin update availability in `plugins list` / `update status` / Control UI

## Status

- **Proposed** (2026-08-28)
- No prior RFC or issue asks for this. The gap is confirmed against current `main`
  (`src/cli/update-cli/status.ts`, `src/cli/plugins-update-selection.ts`,
  `src/cli/plugins-update-command.ts`).

## Summary

Today there is **no in-band signal** telling an OpenClaw user that a newer version
of an installed plugin exists. Plugin updates are purely pull-based and
user-initiated:

- `openclaw plugins list` renders installed versions only — no "latest available"
  column, no update hint.
- `openclaw update status` checks **core** update availability only; it does not
  load the plugin inventory (`src/cli/update-cli/status.ts` rows are `Install`,
  `Channel`, optional `Git`, `Update`).
- `plugins update <id> --dry-run` and `plugins update` only report availability
  when the user already decides to run an update command.
- The Control UI surfaces **core** update availability (sidebar card per #104041)
  but nothing for plugins.

Consequence: a user running a pinned or drifting plugin has no way to learn a
maintenance/bugfix release exists until they happen to run `plugins update`
(and even then, #100309 shows the updater can select a stale version).

## Motivation / concrete example

The OmniRoute provider plugin (`@openclaw/omniroute`) ships new model catalogs,
provider fallback fixes, and routing changes on its own cadence, independent of
the core OpenClaw release. Users who installed an older release have no signal
that a newer one is available — they keep running stale routing/provider config
until something visibly breaks.

## Proposed solution

Add plugin availability to the existing read surfaces, reusing the update
resolution already present in the npm/ClawHub update path. No new background
polling, no new notification channel — just make existing commands and the UI
show what a dry-run already computes.

1. **`openclaw plugins list --verbose`** — add a `Latest` column / `⬆ update
   available` hint per plugin, resolved from the recorded install source
   (registry or ClawHub), same resolver used by `plugins update`.

2. **`openclaw update status`** — fold a plugin availability section into the
   table (and JSON output), adjacent to but not a substitute for the candidate-core
   compatibility and migration-safety preflight tracked by #122019. Plugin
   availability must not imply that an update is safe.

3. **Control UI** — extend the core update-available surface (#104041) with a
   plugin-level indicator (e.g. "N plugin updates available" summary), clicking
   through to `plugins update`.

4. **`plugins update --all --dry-run`** — already computes targets; keep it as
   the actionable path.

### Non-goals

- No background version polling / push notifications in v1.
- No automatic updates.
- No change to the core-only semantics of `update status` beyond adding a
  plugin section.

## Prior art / related

- #122019 — `update status` omits configured-plugin availability (open, upgrade-safety).
- #104041 — Sidebar update card for **core** updates (closed). Model for the UI surface.
- #100309 — `plugins update` can downgrade/pin stale version; wants dry-run to report current/latest/proposed.
- #53228 — `openclaw notify` push-to-UI (only if we later want push-style delivery).

## Open questions

1. Should the `Latest` column resolve every plugin on every `list` (network cost)
   or be opt-in via `--verbose` / a flag? Default should be non-blocking and
   cached.
2. Should availability for **core** and **plugins** share one `update status`
   table or stay separate subcommands?
3. Should the Control UI indicator aggregate plugins or list each?
4. Do we gate network resolution behind a config flag (e.g. `updates.notify`,
   per #66118) for offline / containerized installs (#94279)?

issues.body:
## What problem this solves

OpenClaw's OpenAI-compatible provider transport never compresses request bodies, and there is no configuration surface to enable it. Against gateways that cap **uncompressed** request size, this turns large-but-legitimate requests into hard failures that a compressing client would serve fine.

Measured on OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), node v24.22.2, Linux/WSL2 aarch64, npm-global install, `systemd --user`:

| request | result |
|---|---|
| 1 MB body | 200 |
| 2 MB body | 200 |
| 3 MB body | 200 |
| 4 MB body | 200 |
| 5.1 MB body | **413** `FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` |
| same 5.1 MB body, gzipped (5,079 bytes on the wire) | **200** |

The upstream accepts gzip; the client never sends it. So the ceiling is purely client-side.

## Evidence

**1. The transport sends no `Content-Encoding`.** Pointed a provider at a local capture server that logs only headers and byte counts (no prompt content, no credentials):

```
{"path": "/v1/chat/completions", "content_length": 160,
 "content_encoding": null, "accept_encoding": "gzip, deflate",
 "user_agent": "OpenAI/JS 7.28.0"}
```

It advertises `Accept-Encoding` for responses but sends the request body as identity.

**2. There is no switch to turn on.** Checked all three plausible surfaces:

- `models.providers.*.models[].compat` — the schema exposes ~20 keys (`supportsStore`, `supportsPromptCacheKey`, `supportsUsageInStreaming`, `supportsTools`, …). **None** relate to request compression.
- Provider-level keys — `baseUrl`, `api`, `apiKey`, `headers`, `models`. No transport/compression option.
- Environment — no `OPENCLAW_*COMPRESS*` / `*GZIP*` variable exists in the bundle.

`Content-Encoding` appears zero times in the model-transport modules.

**3. The upstream side is not the blocker.** Same payload, same endpoint, only the header differs:

```
# identity
http=413 sent=5100101
Request Entity Too Large / FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE

# gzip
http=200 sent=5079
{"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"...","usage":{"prompt_tokens":637530,...}}
```

## Proposed change

An opt-in, per-model or per-provider flag, defaulting off so no existing behaviour changes:

```jsonc
{
  "models": {
    "providers": {
      "example": {
        "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1",
        "api": "openai-completions",
        "requestCompression": "gzip",   // or compat.supportsRequestCompression: true
        "models": [{ "id": "m1" }]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

When enabled, the transport would gzip the serialized body and set `Content-Encoding: gzip` (plus `Content-Length` of the compressed bytes). A size threshold (e.g. only compress above ~1 KB) avoids inflating small requests — gzip on a 99-byte body produced 115 bytes in testing.

## Why not a proxy

A local gzip proxy works, but it inserts a process on the critical path of every model call: if it dies, the agent loses its model. A transport-level flag has no such failure mode, and the compression is a property of the request the client already builds.

## Notes

- This is a feature gap, not a regression — no prior version compressed either, as far as I can tell.
- Related but distinct: #182699 (zstd for backup archives) and #162699 (Control UI translation-memory compression) are about on-disk/asset compression, not model request bodies.
- Happy to test a patch against the endpoint that produced the 413 above.

issues.body:
## Summary
Official Android OpenClaw app **Talk / live Talk** drops mid-session. First listen/send can work; after the agent starts tool work (or a long wait), playback goes silent and listening stops. Repro is consistent enough that Discord voice is used as the fallback.

## Environment
- App: official Android OpenClaw (Play), Talk / live Talk
- Device: Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
- Gateway: OpenClaw `2026.8.1-beta.3` on Windows, port 18789
- Talk path observed: listen → `chat.send` → wait → `talk.speak`
- TTS: xAI Eve voice (`summary=on`)

## Steps
1. Open official Android app Talk / live Talk against a paired gateway.
2. Speak a short message that requires tools or a longer model wait (not a one-line chit-chat).
3. Wait while the agent runs tools.

## Expected
Talk stays the live owner for the whole turn: one spoken answer plays, then listening resumes.

## Actual
- First native Talk send may work.
- If the agent speaks early, uses tools, or waits in the background, the **live response owner is dropped**.
- Later `talk.speak` / TTS has nothing to play into.
- Mic/listening stops. User has to leave Talk and come back (or switch to Discord voice).
- Same class as Talk dying after gateway disconnect / app background.

## Notes
- Workaround on the agent side: do not speak before tools; one spoken payload only. That does not fix the app dropping the Talk session.
- Gateway-side cannot patch Play Talk ownership.
- Related but not the same: #125371 (mic suppressed during playback), #46546 (duplicate Talk playback).

## Workaround
Use Discord voice (`stt-tts`) when the Android Talk session dies.

issues.body:
## Summary

**At least 28** failures on stable **2026.10.5**; child effects unproved; no fix.

```text
service child cleanup identity lost: Error: Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission
```

## Environment

- Ubuntu **24.04.5 LTS**, Linux x64 **6.8.0-147-generic**.
- Node.js **24.21.0**.
- Stock npm OpenClaw **2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)**, managed user Gateway service.
- Official `v2026.10.5` tag resolves to commit
  `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`.
- No locally patched core files were carried into this stable update.
- No deliberate concurrent schema mutation, forced workflow, restart,
  database repair, integrity bypass or child replay was used to reproduce it.
  The triggering operation was an already occurring ordinary scheduled turn.

## Actual Evidence And Timing

Original native event clocks, UTC:

| Evidence | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Host-exec request event | 2026-10-19T19:05:14.174Z |
| Native error result event | 2026-10-19T19:05:15.134Z; `isError:true` |
| Event-clock difference | 960 ms; not measured child runtime |
| Admitted helper stdout | None returned |
| Child start/exit/reap/cleanup receipt | None returned; lifecycle unknown |
| Repetition count | At least twenty-eight unique ordinary native-exec failures, including intervening successful ordinary turns |

Opaque SHA-256 digests of the retained canonical events (no event payloads
or identifiers are published):

```text
request event:
ae50b2c38b43da7eeaa4661d8c5a36ff8e4c58b2a0280c511be60b0775b6f345

error result event:
dcab76a3549ce54435f8b1245466fb17c4624f85b4c06ab4ef7d6a6b68e9a31b
```

### Subsequent Ordinary Observation: Did Not Recur

The next untouched normal turn exercised the same pure preparation path:

- Native request: 2026-10-19T19:34:48.783Z, event digest
  `71b87546c13fb672d52fa4a8351e939a5e38e7e59056a77b6f57ded597e6d488`.
- Admitted result: 2026-10-19T19:34:49.693Z, `isError:false`, `ok:true`,
  event digest
  `5f6fb687db628e2c9d9ccb80141195c0c5226716dd392155740503c9a63275b6`.
- The owning turn then genuinely persisted its question and source attempts,
  validated the written plan successfully, completed normal delivery/release
  and reached native terminal at 19:36:16.953Z. At 19:36:43Z the read-only
  handoff check found no matching runtime processes or active OAuth leases.

Intervening independent success required no core patch or restart; it neither repaired nor replayed the earlier unknown child outcome.

### Recurrence On A Different Local Read

A subsequent untouched ordinary turn returned the same full error on a
different local Python command that reads retained JSON research context:

- Request event: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.112Z, digest
  `e9b1da906778bf797fd8fc53bf117112a83053f26dc9aa253eb84005504cfa61`.
- Error result: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.751Z, `isError:true`, digest
  `70720e276fc1c900f1d3a01c94001c691ad8b1d89f045bde0c6b012965916bd5`.
- Event-clock difference: 639ms, not measured child runtime. Again, no helper
  stdout or child start/terminal receipt was admitted; actual child outcome
  remains unknown.

The turn continued using independent retained facts and fresh provider observations, without a same-reference retry, deliberate invalidation, core change, restart or forced workflow. That continuation does not prove the rejected child's outcome.

The local helper is a pure structural preparation operation: its relevant
branch imports no SQLite/OpenClaw state, Node runtime, claim or database
reader. A separate direct local structural invocation succeeds. That control
does **not** exercise native service-child admission and is not a repaired
native-exec result.

The owning workflow retained the failed preparation/persistence disposition;
it did not obtain completed question registration or attempt persistence
through this rejected call. The turn later completed its mandatory reporting
and bookkeeping. Those later technical flags do not prove the rejected exec
operation healthy, its persistence completed or any financial action cleared.

## Installed Source Boundary, Not A Captured Stack

Package-relative locations in this exact installed build:

- `dist/openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs:97`:
  `prepareOpenClawStateDirectReader` rejects if the integrity revision differs
  from its epoch, or an existing-schema context lacks integrity/proof.
- `dist/exec-approvals-store-B7WwLRrI.mjs:218`:
  `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead(context)` prepares this direct reader;
  its returned guard independently rechecks admission and reads current policy.
- `dist/plugin-node-host-YOtba4hi.mjs:102`:
  plugin-exec authorization captures the worker context and prepares that
  current-policy reader. The approvals store has another authorization
  settlement caller; this error alone does not select between them.
- `dist/child-DMrKblk4.mjs:702`:
  service-child `loseIdentity` wraps its message as
  `service child cleanup identity lost: ...`.

The retained tool error is **not a JavaScript stack**. It does not reveal the
exact caller branch, concurrent writer, integrity epoch/revision/proof values,
schema operation, or ordering relative to process spawn. The source matches
identify a boundary to investigate, not a proven root cause or proof that
Python itself accessed shared state.

Exact installed artifact SHA-256s:

```text
openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs
591be6e4250c8d18e3a788b98a578b0488ea6415e44df2dc549b7098c4e5aad7

exec-approvals-store-B7WwLRrI.mjs
5f57efa4ef09811e566d46f3c24b90930983ffc7fe32c5ab0bf7f201f2ddd4c7

plugin-node-host-YOtba4hi.mjs
44ec8e0167df30d308818637a70de85436604f8404a6bcd9b86b127135d84664

child-DMrKblk4.mjs
8065787d49ea90be0af69e2f45deaf003e11db127fbe6c8d3769a06bb246228e
```

## ClawSweeper Follow-Up

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6275795871)
requests an isolated failing native stable case, payload-free admission and
child-lifecycle diagnostics, and the same case on pinned main. **These behavioral
proof requests remain unfulfilled.** No repair PR or incident-matched fix is claimed.

Source inspection confirms that merged [PR #169584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169584),
commit `d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88`, replaces the
[stable direct-reader policy preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L148)
with a [worker-prepared current-policy owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L286).
The changed path is a relevant candidate, not proof it resolves this incident.
Its separately reported synthetic allow/revocation evidence is not this case.

Inspected suites, an inconclusive bounded attempt and successful native controls

issues.body:
## Summary

The silent token `NO_REPLY` is documented as "never delivered as user-visible text", but it is delivered verbatim whenever anything follows the token on the same reply. A heartbeat agent that writes `NO_REPLY <note-to-self>` leaks that entire string into the external channel.

Verified against `2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)` by importing the shipped dist modules and calling their exported functions directly.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd <openclaw>/dist
node repro-no-reply-leak.mjs   # script attached below
```

Output:

```
=== A) heartbeat path silent determination ===
  silent | isSilentReply=true  | token only (expected silent) | "NO_REPLY"
  LEAKED | isSilentReply=false | ASCII space + note         | "NO_REPLY note"
  LEAKED | isSilentReply=false | full-width punctuation     | "NO_REPLY、全角括号、"
  LEAKED | isSilentReply=false | trailing period            | "NO_REPLY.句点。"
  LEAKED | isSilentReply=false | newline + note             | "NO_REPLY\n「换行 note」"
  LEAKED | isSilentReply=false | real leaked payload        | "NO_REPLY （12:00 已投递，下次 15:00。）"
```

5/6 inputs leak. The single input that is correctly suppressed is the exact-token case.

This is not hypothetical. Six consecutive heartbeat polls leaked into a live Telegram channel before the behaviour was traced; the delivered payloads match the `real leaked payload` row above character for character.

## Defect A — heartbeat silent determination only matches an exact token

`heartbeat-runner-run-*.mjs`, lines 318-325:

```js
const isSilentReply = isSilentReplyPayloadText(textForStrip);   // 318
const stripped = stripHeartbeatToken(...);                      // 319
silent = notifyFalse.silent || isSilentReply;                   // 325
```

`isSilentReplyPayloadText` delegates to `isSilentReplyText` (`tokens-Ljy0DfNV.mjs`), whose exact regex is:

```js
const getSilentExactRegex = createTokenRegex((escaped) => new RegExp(`^\\s*${escaped}(?:\\s+${escaped})*\\s*$`, "i"));
```

That is a whole-string match. `NO_REPLY note` fails it, so `isSilentReply` is false, so `silent` is false, so the payload is delivered.

The two partial fallbacks do not cover the gap:

- `startsWithSilentToken` fires only when the token is glued to an alphanumeric (`NO_REPLYnote`) or followed by a newline.
- `stripSilentToken` only strips a *trailing* token via `getSilentTrailingRegex`.

A token followed by a space plus text, or by full-width punctuation, matches neither.

## Defect B — dispatcher fallback is skipped for heartbeat replies

`normalize-reply-BHa9FmoK.mjs` wraps its entire silent-filtering block in a metadata guard:

```js
if (!getReplyPayloadMetadata(payload)?.heartbeatReply) {
  const silentToken = opts.silentToken ?? "NO_REPLY";
  if (text && isSilentReplyPayloadText(text, silentToken)) { ... }
  if (text) { const stripped = stripMixedSilentReplyTokens(text, silentToken); ... }
  ...
}
```

The heartbeat path constructs its payload with exactly that marker set (`heartbeat-runner-run-*.mjs`, line 949):

```js
reply: setReplyPayloadMetadata(markReplyPayloadForSourceSuppressionDelivery(payload), { heartbeatReply: true })
```

So the dispatcher-level normalisation never runs for heartbeat replies. Demonstrated on the plain-token case:

```
"NO_REPLY"
   plain payload       -> suppress (silent)
   heartbeatReply=true -> deliver
```

Even a bare `NO_REPLY` is delivered when it carries heartbeat metadata. The two layers fail in opposite directions: the heartbeat check is too narrow, and the safety net beneath it is switched off.

## Documentation mismatch

`docs/concepts/messages.md:170` states:

> The silent token `NO_REPLY` (case-insensitive, so `no_reply` also matches) is reserved for sessions connected to external message channels and is never delivered as user-visible text.

The measured behaviour contradicts this. Either the filter should reject any reply whose *leading* content is the silent token, or the documented contract needs to be narrowed to "exact token only".

## Impact

Heartbeat polls fire every 30 minutes by default. Any agent that annotates its own silence turns that annotation into a channel message. The failure is silent from the operator's side: nothing in the logs marks the payload as mis-delivered.

Related, already open: #165025 (reasoning-prefixed variants), #143787 (heartbeat re-delivery), #170158 (partial token leakage).

## Suggested direction

Make the silence check leading-token based rather than exact-match based: if a reply begins with the silent token and the remainder carries no substantive content, suppress the whole payload. Keep `heartbeatReply` from bypassing the silent branch, or scope the guard to only skip the heartbeat-token stripping it was meant to guard.

I did not patch local `dist` files, since an update would overwrite the change.

issues.body:
## Summary

On four consecutive nights the gateway's cron scheduler stopped firing for **5.6–9.4 hours**, then **resumed on its own** with a catch-up pass. The process stayed `active` the whole time, never restarted, and remained responsive to I/O.

This is distinct from the existing permanent-stall reports (#102534, #73166, #43937), where the timer dies and stays dead until a restart or `cron run --force`. Here nothing is restarted and the scheduler recovers by itself — but only after multiple hours, so every job in the window is silently lost.

## Version

- OpenClaw **2026.7.2-beta.7 (dabe191)**
- Node **v24.15.0**, Linux 6.12.93 x64, systemd unit
- Gateway continuously up since **2026-08-17 22:54:30** (no restart at any point below)

## Evidence

Probe is the `heartbeat:*` cron jobs (`every 55m`, `everyMs: 3300000`). Measured interval between consecutive ticks on healthy nights is 55.0–56.2 min. Extracted from `journalctl -u openclaw` by `trigger=heartbeat`:

| Night | Gap | Last tick before gap | First tick after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 24 | **9.38 h** | 02:44:54 | 12:07:41 |
| Aug 25 | **8.01 h** | 02:59:51 | 11:00:11 |
| Aug 26 | **5.63 h** | 02:59:52 | 08:37:53 |
| Aug 27 | **6.00 h** | 02:46:39 | 08:46:40 |

Heartbeat ticks per day, against the expected 26/day:

```
Aug 23:  26   <- clean control night, full expected count
Aug 24:  19
Aug 25:  18
Aug 26:  20
Aug 27:  21
```

Aug 23 is a clean night on the **same process** as all four failures, so this is not an upgrade or config regression.

On resume the scheduler self-reports the lateness rather than silently skipping:

```
Aug 24 12:07:36 openclaw[200169]: [cron:60874166-...] skipping stale delivery
  scheduled at 2026-08-24T12:00:00.000Z, started 245m late, current age 248m
```

All timers stall together — `heartbeat:main`, `heartbeat:emma`, `heartbeat:group-bot` and unrelated jobs resume in the same burst — so it looks like the scheduler timer itself, not per-job state.

## Onset window

The last good tick clusters at **02:44–02:59 local (AST/UTC-4)**. Since the cadence is 55 min, the true onset is anywhere in the ~55 min following that tick, i.e. roughly **02:44–03:54**.

## What I ruled out

I checked each candidate against the **clean Aug 23 night**, and both plausible correlates failed:

- **WebSocket upgrade failures.** There is a `[ws] closed before connect ... code=1006 phase=ws_upgrade_started` burst at ~03:01 on Aug 25 and Aug 26, which looked like a blocked-event-loop signature. But it is **absent on Aug 24 and Aug 27**, which also froze. Not a discriminator.
- **Memory/dreaming pipeline at 03:00.** Log volume in the 02:30–03:30 window is comparable on the clean night (82 lines, 18 memory-related) and the frozen ones (76–123 lines, 19–35). Not a discriminator.
- **Restart / upgrade.** No restart in the window; package unchanged since Aug 15.
- **Host-level suspend or clock jump.** Independent host cron (`*/1 * * * *`) ran continuously throughout. During the 9.38h Aug 24 freeze it executed in **563 distinct minutes** — exactly the 563 minutes of the gap, with no missed minute — so the machine was awake and the system clock was advancing normally. Only the gateway's internal timers were stopped.

I have no root cause, and I'd rather report the symptom accurately than guess at one.

## Impact

Every scheduled job in the window is lost, silently. The gateway cannot witness its own outage: `openclaw status` is green throughout, because the process is healthy — it is only the timers that are dead. Detection requires an external observer.

## Notes

The recovery consistently coincides with external activity reaching the gateway, which is consistent with a wedged timer being kicked by unrelated event-loop work rather than by anything in the scheduler. I have deliberately **not** added an automatic restart on our side, so the natural behaviour stays observable — happy to run diagnostics on the next occurrence if there's something specific worth capturing (`cron status` / `nextWakeAtMs` at freeze time is the obvious one, and I'll grab it).

issues.body:
I run OpenClaw on the Codex harness with a few dozen long-lived sessions. Since May, none of them has been compacted automatically. They have been cleared instead, with no notice, and it took me two evenings to find out why. Each piece below is already filed as its own issue; this is the whole picture in one place.

### What happens on a Codex session today

1. The session grows. OpenClaw's preflight compaction runs each turn and skips it with `reason=codex_native_auto_compaction`. The code comment says Codex owns token pressure.
2. Codex's native thread reaches its token fuse, and `startup-binding.ts` runs `bindingStore.mutate({ kind: "clear" })`. The thread binding is dropped and an empty thread begins, with no summary carried over. The log line is `warn` level and names a token limit, not lost context.
3. Nothing reaches the channel. On Matrix or Signal the assistant forgets everything and keeps talking.

The native compaction request (`compact.ts`, `thread/compact/start`) works when I type `/compact`. For every automatic trigger it is refused with the reason "codex app-server owns automatic compaction". Each layer defers to the other, and the action that runs is a clear.

This came in with #85958 in May. Its premise, "Codex already owns automatic compaction inside the Codex runtime", does not hold in practice. My logs show three thread clears in three days and zero `thread/compact` requests in seven.

### The byte fuse has its own problems

The only automatic path to a real summary on a Codex session is `maxActiveTranscriptBytes`.

- It is unset by default, so the default behavior is the clear. (#115192 made Codex sessions honor it at all.)
- It measures bytes on disk, which compaction does not shrink, so a compacted session can re-trigger indefinitely (#126900). `/new` does not reset it (#119984).
- When it triggers, compaction issues eleven model calls totalling four times the transcript size (#115904). It then hits the 180s timeout, which `timeoutSeconds` can raise, and then the 600s reply-operation cap, which nothing can raise (#120162 is adjacent).
- When compaction fails, the turn retries with the full uncompacted history, 1.35M characters against a 272k window, and fails again.
- When a quota cooldown blocks it, that is not surfaced to the channel either (#130613).

The user-visible result, on a session of 183k tokens: "Context is too large and auto-compaction could not recover this turn", followed by "Compaction failed: Compaction timed out".

### What I changed locally

Removed the bypass in `agent-runner-memory.ts` and turned both `clear` sites in `startup-binding.ts` into log-and-keep. Set `models.providers.openai.contextTokens` below Codex's reported window so the threshold sits where the clear used to fire. Both test files updated. The two Codex tests whose assertions had to flip are named "skips ... for explicit Codex runtime overrides" and "leaves an under-limit SQLite Codex session to native token compaction"; they were asserting the clear as correct behavior.

That is 5 insertions and 24 deletions. A session at 347k tokens on a 350k window now compacts, which is the default behavior of every other harness I have used.

### What I am asking

Not for this patch to be merged as-is. It removes a boundary someone drew on purpose, and I do not know what that boundary protects. I am asking for a direct answer to one question:

**When a Codex-runtime session crosses a token threshold, what is supposed to compact it?**

If the answer is Codex, then automatic triggers need to be allowed to request native compaction, and the clear needs to become the fallback rather than the only action. If the answer is OpenClaw, the bypass needs to go. Either answer works. Today the answer is "nothing, and the user is not told."

I would also ask that the byte-size fuse stop being the only route to a summary. It is a proxy for a number Codex already reports and `startup-binding.ts` already reads at the clear site (`tokenCount`, `maxTokens`, `reserveTokens`). The 20,000-token reserve held there is sized for a compaction request; clearing a binding needs none of it.

Related: #131337 (the deferral loop), #130613 (quota failures never surfaced), #126900, #119984, #115904, #115192, #85958.

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.7 (`ace03a674af`), Node 24.15.0, Linux; Codex harness, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`; channels Matrix and Signal.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw 2026.8.1 beta 3 can send an overlength OpenAI Responses `call_id` during Codex settled turn finalization. The provider rejects the request before a final answer can be generated, leaving the channel session unable to respond until it is reset.

This appears to be a regression or an uncovered execution path related to #74665. That issue was closed after a replay identifier normalizer was added, but this failure occurred through the Codex harness finalization path.

## Reproduction steps

1. Use a channel bound Codex agent on an OpenAI Responses model with tools enabled.
2. Let a turn complete tool work without producing its final text response, causing settled turn finalization.
3. If finalization replays a historical tool call whose `call_id` is longer than 64 characters, observe the provider rejection.

## Expected behavior

Every OpenAI Responses request, including the Codex settled turn finalizer, should normalize or reject invalid historical tool identifiers before dispatch. Matching `function_call` and `function_call_output` identifiers must be rewritten together deterministically.

## Actual behavior

The Codex harness attempted isolated finalization and OpenAI rejected the outbound request:

```text
Invalid `input[3].call_id`: string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.
```

OpenClaw then recorded that settled turn finalization failed closed and surfaced a generic generation error to the channel. The affected session had to be deleted to recover.

## Context

1. OpenClaw: `2026.8.1-beta.3`
2. Node: `24.18.0`
3. Harness: `codex`
4. Provider and model: `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`
5. Failure phase: isolated settled turn finalization after tool work
6. The installed embedded Responses replay path includes `normalizeOpenAIResponsesToolCallIds`, but the observed request still reached OpenAI with an 83 character `call_id`. This suggests that Codex harness finalization bypasses that transform, or builds the final payload after it runs.

## Proposed fix

Apply the existing Responses replay identifier normalization to the Codex settled turn finalization path. Add a final request boundary guard for every OpenAI Responses dispatch that verifies all `call_id` fields are at most 64 characters and preserves the paired call and result mapping.

## Notes

The original identifier may have entered history during a provider switch, but that origin has not been proven. The demonstrated defect is that the Codex finalizer sent it to OpenAI unnormalized.

Related: #74665.

issues.body:
### What happened

Changing a restart-required config key (`openclaw config set gateway.controlUi.root <path>`) made the gateway schedule its own restart ("config change requires gateway restart, deferring until N operations complete"). When the in-flight runs finished, the deferred restart fired as an in-process SIGUSR1 restart and its shutdown did not complete cleanly. The HTTP server came back 10 s later, but the failed close wrote a stability bundle and dropped every connected client (the macOS app then went through its own recovery).

A full process restart a few minutes later (`SIGTERM` via the service supervisor, `openclaw gateway restart`) shut down cleanly in 240 ms, so the failure is specific to the in-process SIGUSR1 restart path.

### Log excerpt (gateway 2026.9.3, times UTC)

```
18:28:19.525 INFO  Updated gateway.controlUi.root. Restart the gateway to apply.
18:28:20.015 INFO  gateway/reload  config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.controlUi.root)
18:28:20.037 WARN  gateway/reload  config change requires gateway restart (gateway.controlUi.root) — deferring until 2 operation(s), 2 reply(ies), 2 embedded run(s), 2 gateway request(s) complete
... "restart still deferred after 270396ms" ...
18:33:02.194 INFO  agent/cli-backend  cli turn: provider=claude-cli ... durationMs=1817502
18:33:03.026 INFO  gateway/admission  admission closed: restart-signal fence
18:33:04.110 INFO  gateway/admission  admission closed: restart drain
18:33:04.110 INFO  gateway  received SIGUSR1; restarting
18:33:04.301 INFO  gmail-watcher  gmail watcher stopped
18:33:04.365 ERROR gateway  shutdown step failed (gateway close): Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state | service child cleanup identity lost: construction aborted
18:33:04.365 ERROR gateway  shutdown step failed (gateway server close): Gateway shutdown did not complete cleanly | shutdown step failed (gateway close): Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state | service child cleanup identity lost: construction aborted
18:33:04.370 WARN  gateway  wrote stability bundle: .../logs/stability/openclaw-stability-2026-09-10T18-33-04-366Z-793-gateway.restart_close_failed.json
18:33:08.020 INFO  gateway  loading configuration…
18:33:14.685 INFO  gateway  http server listening (19 plugins ...; 6.6s)
```

Clean comparison, same process tree, 12 minutes later:

```
18:45:32.937 INFO  gateway  received SIGTERM; restarting
18:45:33.204 INFO  gateway/shutdown  shutdown completed cleanly in 240ms
18:45:33.363 INFO  gateway  restart mode: full process restart (supervisor restart)
```

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (1391f7c), gateway run by a user LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.gateway`, `/bin/sh` env wrapper, node `dist/index.js gateway --port 18789`)
- Node 24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), macOS 26.6.2 arm64
- Gateway uptime before the restart: about 29.6 h (pid 793)
- 19 plugins loaded; a claude-cli agent turn had just completed (`durationMs=1817502`) when the deferred restart fired
- The stability bundle (1000 events, mostly diagnostic.heartbeat / model.call / session.state) is available on request; nothing in it precedes the shutdown errors except normal idle traffic.

### Expected

The deferred restart triggered by a config reload should close as cleanly as a supervisor restart, or fall back to the full process restart when the in-process close fails. Related reports that look like the same family of shutdown problems: #142394, #142701.

### Steps to reproduce (as observed)

1. Long-running gateway (hours) with active agent runs.
2. `openclaw config set gateway.controlUi.root /some/built/control-ui` (any restart-required key).
3. Let the runs finish so the deferred restart fires.
4. Observe the two `shutdown step failed` errors and the `gateway.restart_close_failed` stability bundle.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Memory-flush maintenance can fail repeatedly, and finally be abandoned for the compaction cycle, without producing any user-visible outcome or any recorded operator-facing reason beyond a verbose-only log line. The two callers of `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded` disagree about whether maintenance degradation is reportable, and neither of them delivers the visible payloads the maintenance code builds for exactly that purpose.

This is source-level analysis against current `main`. No live reproduction was attempted.

### Steps to reproduce

Source-level, against `main` at `30837ae7035b3027c06b790c38cf0b1c70654fbf`:

1. Let a memory-flush maintenance run fail (restricted write, plan resolution failure, target preparation failure, or an error payload returned by the maintenance run itself).
2. `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded` builds a bounded, sanitized `⚠️ …` payload with `isError: true` and hands it to `run.onVisibleErrorPayloads?.(…)`.
3. Observe where that payload goes:
   - On the auto-reply path the callback only writes a verbose log line and returns.
   - On the agent-command path no callback is supplied at all, so the optional call is a no-op.
4. Repeat until `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES` is reached. The exhaustion branch stamps `memoryFlush: { kind: "succeeded" }` to break the retry loop and emits another `⚠️` payload through the same discarded callback.
5. Observe that the only escalation path, `sendDirectCompactionNotice("memory_flush_degraded")`, exists on one caller only, fires only for `outcome === "exhausted"`, and is itself gated behind a config flag that is unset by default.

### Expected behavior

- A maintenance operation that fails, and especially one that is abandoned for the cycle, ends in either a visible outcome or a recorded, intentional non-outcome.
- Both callers of the same maintenance function agree on whether degradation is reportable.
- `outcome === "failed"` is consumed somewhere, or the state is removed.
- The user's answer is never replaced or truncated by maintenance failure (this part already holds and should stay).

### Actual behavior

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execute.ts:207-212` supplies `onVisibleErrorPayloads` whose entire body is a `logVerbose` call; the payloads are dropped.
- `src/agents/command/post-run.ts:339-354` supplies no `onVisibleErrorPayloads` at all and reads only `memoryFlushResult.sessionEntry` at `:355`, so both the payloads and the outcome are lost on that path.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execute.ts:245-249` is the only escalation, and only for `"exhausted"`.
- `shouldNotifyUserAboutCompaction` requires `cfg.agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser === true` (`src/auto-reply/reply/compaction-notice.ts:37-39`), declared as `z.boolean().optional()` with no default (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts:177`). Out of the box the escalation is off, so even `"exhausted"` is silent.
- `MemoryFlushResult.outcome === "failed"` is read nowhere in production.

### OpenClaw version

Current `main` at `30837ae7035b3027c06b790c38cf0b1c70654fbf`.

### Operating system

Source-level, platform independent.

### Install method

Not applicable.

### Model

Not applicable; the defect is in maintenance bookkeeping, not model routing.

### Provider / routing chain

Inbound turn -> memory flush maintenance -> (auto-reply path) reply delivery, or (agent-command path) post-run settlement.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The maintenance run is deliberately built without a delivery surface (`buildEmbeddedRunExecutionParams` in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.ts:317-350`, invoked with `silentExpected: true` and `trigger: "memory"`), so it cannot emit its own message. Reporting has to come from the caller, which is exactly the seam that is missing on one side.

### Logs

```shell
memory flush produced N visible maintenance error payload(s); continuing user reply
memory flush exhausted: skipping flush for this compaction cycle after N consecutive failures
```

Both are `logVerbose`, so they are absent at the default log level.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Producers of the discarded payloads:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts:1726-1731` — exhaustion notice.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts:1739-1742` — generic failure notice via `buildMemoryFlushErrorPayload` (`:296-312`).
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts:1632-1637` — a maintenance run that itself returned error payloads is converted into a recorded failure. Contained by the catch at `:1661-1663`; `recordMemoryFlushFailure` (`:1672-1744`) never rethrows, so the user's turn is correctly unaffected.

Consumers:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execute.ts:207-212` — discards the payloads.
- `src/agents/command/post-run.ts:339-354` — supplies no callback; `:355` reads only `sessionEntry`.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execute.ts:245-249` — the only escalation, `"exhausted"` only.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/compaction-notice.ts:19,37-39` — fixed notice text and the default-off gate.

Existing coverage:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts:1123,1170,1197,1219,1242,1276-1333,1462` assert the payload shapes and outcomes at the producer.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts:437-470` pins that the main reply survives and `onBlockReply` is not called.
- No test covers a failing flush on the `post-run.ts` call site, and no test covers `memory_flush_degraded` with `notifyUser` unset.

Related history: `75a3e753752` ("fix: preserve conversation after memory flush exhaustion", fixes #131957) removed the older, worse behavior where exhaustion reset the session. The remaining gap is reporting, not data loss.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any deployment where memory maintenance degrades. Default configuration receives no signal at all.
- Severity: medium. No data loss and no truncated answers, but a maintenance capability can silently stop working for a cycle, which is the repository's worst failure class applied to an operator-facing rather than user-facing surface.
- Consequence: operators cannot tell that memory maintenance stopped running, and the two call sites will keep drifting because only one of them reports anything.

### Additional information

Suggested shape, for discussion rather than as a decided design: give the maintenance result one owner-side reporting decision instead of two divergent caller-side ones, so `failed` and `exhausted` both end in a recorded fact that operators can read, and drop `outcome` values that nothing consumes.

Found while fixing #136560 (terminal error finals dropped at the WhatsApp delivery boundary). Same doctrine, different owner: that one lost payloads at the channel, this one loses them at the caller.

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

- Code Mode advertises string boolean literals for Gemini-routed tools while local validation requires booleans.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Code Mode for a Gemini-routed agent.
2. In `exec`, inspect `(await API.read("tools/read.d.ts")).content`.
3. Follow the generated `optional?: "true"` declaration: `await read({ path: "missing-optional.txt", optional: "true" })`.

### Expected behavior

- The declaration advertises `optional?: true`; the boolean value returns the structured `not_found` result for a missing optional file.

### Actual behavior

- The generated string value fails local validation with `optional: expected boolean`. Compact Tool Search hints advertise the same string literal.

### OpenClaw version

- 2026.11.1, d4ae77eae296fd8eb1f90f7a4ebb5d77fa2e6ad9

### Operating system

- macOS 26.6.2; Node 24.22.1

### Install method

- Source build; `pnpm build`, then `node openclaw.mjs agent --local`.

### Model

- `proof/gemini-schema-proof`, a deterministic loopback model fixture selecting Gemini schema normalization.

### Provider / routing chain

- Built CLI → OpenAI-compatible loopback SSE fixture → Code Mode → tool catalog → real read handler.

### Additional provider/model setup details

- `tools.codeMode: true`. The fixture sends an `exec` call that reads the generated declaration and chooses the advertised value.

### Logs

```text
HEAD d4ae77eae296fd8eb1f90f7a4ebb5d77fa2e6ad9
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (d4ae77e) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.
Error: Invalid arguments for tool "read": optional: expected boolean; received "true" (string); optional: must be equal to constant (allowed: true); received "true" (string). Expected input: { path: string; cursor?: number /* integer, >= 0 */; limit?: number; offset?: number /* integer, >= 1 */; optional?: true }.
    at openclaw-code-mode:user.js:5:22
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

### Impact and severity

### Additional information

- The read-schema widening in #192113 addresses `optional: false`; this defect concerns input guidance for projected schemas.

- Fix verified at `322b96118984793b847b40f2b70d024d95d5e32e`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On every Control UI reload, the accent palette is projected onto the document root three times with the same inputs, and each pass forces a full-document style recalculation. In the cold-load benchmark this costs about 105 ms of CPU time per reload (from CPU profiles) and delays the first route being ready.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `3fed691416b3`, run `pnpm install` and `pnpm ui:build`, and copy `dist/control-ui` to `/absolute/base/control-ui`.
2. Run the committed cold-load benchmark with CPU profiles on the chat route (built-in synthetic fixture, no environment or seam color configured):
   ```
   node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
     --gateway-http --bundle-dir /absolute/base/control-ui --runs 3 --cpu-profile
   ```
3. In the source-mapped profiles, look at `applyControlUiAccent` and `applyControlUiPresentation`.
4. Optional: run untraced with `--untraced --thread-cpu-time` (no `--cpu-profile`) and read `threadCpu.styleMs`.

Where the three passes come from on `3fed691416b3`:

- `ui/src/app/config.ts:229` applies the operator seam color, which runs `applyControlUiAccent`.
- `ui/src/app/bootstrap-theme.ts:76` applies the user accent, which runs `applyControlUiAccent` again.
- `ui/src/app/config.ts:92-98` imports `control-ui-environment-presentation.runtime.ts`, whose `applyControlUiPresentation` (`control-ui-environment-presentation.runtime.ts:19`) applies the seam color again. The import condition includes `root.style.getPropertyValue("--ring")` (`config.ts:96`), and `applyControlUiAccent` always writes `--ring` (`control-ui-presentation.ts:282`), so this pass runs on every reload even with no environment and no seam color.

Each pass removes about 18 root custom properties (`control-ui-presentation.ts:238`), calls `getComputedStyle(root)` (`control-ui-presentation.ts:245`), then mixes `setProperty` writes with `resolveThemeColor` reads, so each read after a write forces a recalculation.

### Expected behavior

A reload projects the accent once, because the inputs (accent or seam color, theme, mode, palette stylesheets) do not change between the three calls. The environment presentation pass only runs when there is an environment or a seam color to apply or clear. #193338 removed the same kind of unchanged reapply for profile appearance on reload.

### Actual behavior

CPU profiles (3 runs) show `applyControlUiAccent` at a median of 105.1 ms inclusive per reload, `resolveThemeColor` at 93.1 ms, and `applyControlUiPresentation` at 86.7 ms, with no environment or seam color configured. Untraced, the renderer spends a median of 180.9 ms on style CPU per reload, with 3 long tasks per reload.

### OpenClaw version

main @ 3fed691416b37f91b0db8dd77446f739e7bf92af (timings measured on d999f7b1b675; the only `ui/src` changes between the two are e2e test files)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple M3 Ultra), Google Chrome 156.0.8078.80

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm ui:build`, production bundle served through the Gateway HTTP handler by `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts`

### Model

Not applicable: Control UI boot only, no model request is involved.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: Control UI boot only, no provider request is involved.

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

```shell
CPU profile attribution, base, 3 runs, inclusive ms per reload [min, median, max]
  applyControlUiAccent             ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.ts            99.3  105.1  128.0
  applyControlUiOperatorSeamColor  ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.ts            86.9   91.4  106.3
  resolveThemeColor                ui/src/lib/theme-color.ts                        86.7   93.1  117.3
  applyControlUiPresentation       ui/src/app/control-ui-environment-presentation.runtime.ts  84.5  86.7  98.8
  syncControlUiSystemChrome        ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.ts             1.5    1.8    2.1

Untraced, 10 base runs (chat route), median [Q1, Q3] ms
  threadCpu.styleMs                180.9 [175.8, 183.7]
  threadCpu.taskMs                 842.5 [825.7, 861.8]
  firstRouteReadyMs                523.3 [511.1, 534.7]
  long tasks per reload            3 (range 3 to 4)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No visual symptom: the final colors are correct, the cost is CPU time during load. Evidence is the profile attribution and benchmark numbers above. A fix and before/after measurements are in the linked PR.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: every Control UI reload, for all users. It does not depend on an environment or seam color being configured.
- Severity: annoying (slower reload, no wrong output).
- Frequency: always (every profiled and untraced run).
- Consequence: about 105 ms of extra main-thread CPU per reload on the test machine, and a later first route ready.

### Additional information

Not a regression from a known version; the triple projection is how the current boot order works. Searches of open issues and PRs for "accent palette", "seam color", "applyControlUiAccent", "control-ui-presentation" and "accent reload" found no duplicate. #160399 (open) changes System theme handling in `bootstrap-theme.ts` and `theme.ts`, which is separate from this. A PR with a fix is linked.

issues.body:
### Summary

Interrupted/cancelled pending inputs are retained indefinitely with no TTL, no manual clear, and no context exclusion. Beyond UI clutter (#140243), they actively corrupt model behavior by injecting stale context into every turn.

### Problem to solve

## Problem

After context compaction, stale interrupted/cancelled pending inputs are injected into the model's context every turn. The model cannot distinguish these from current context, leading to **incorrect responses**.

## Evidence

### Reproduction Steps
1. Start a session, send message A ("What model are you?")
2. The run is interrupted (gateway restart or provider error)
3. Send a new message B ("Check this URL")
4. After context compaction, the model sees: compaction summary + stale pending input A + message B

### Observed Behavior
The model responds to **stale pending input A** instead of current message B. In our case, a7+ hour old interrupted input caused the model to respond with content from an old probe task, ignoring the user's actual current request.

### Why This Happens
- Pending inputs live in `session_pending_inputs`, scoped to `(session_key, session_id)`
- `/reset`, `/new`, and `sessions.reset` preserve the `sessionId`, so pending inputs survive
- The only deletion path is full session deletion (refused for main session)
- After compaction, pending inputs become a larger proportion of the reduced context, increasing confusion risk

## Proposed Solutions (any one suffices)

1. **TTL for interrupted/cancelled inputs**: Auto-expire after configurable duration (e.g.,24h)
2. **Manual clear**: `sessions.pendingInputs.discard` RPC or `openclaw sessions clear-pending` CLI
3. **Compaction cleanup**: Clear interrupted/cancelled inputs during compaction
4. **Context exclusion**: Don't inject stale pending inputs into model context (keep for UI inspection only)

## Environment
- OpenClaw2026.9.2 (3928bad)
- Windows NT10.0.26200 (x64)
- node v24.20.0
- Model: ollama local model (Qwen3.8-27B)
- Session: main session, duration2d+,7 compactions

## Related
- #140243 (closed as "Not planned") — same root cause, focused on UI clutter. This issue adds evidence of **model behavior corruption**, which is a more serious impact.

### Proposed solution

Add a TTL (e.g., 24h configurable) for interrupted/cancelled pending inputs, auto-expiring them from the queue. Alternatively, provide a manual clear path: sessions.pendingInputs.discard RPC limited to interrupted/cancelled states, or openclaw sessions clear-pending CLI. Both approaches preserve the current "retained for inspection" behavior while preventing indefinite accumulation.

### Alternatives considered

1. Session reset (/new) - loses all history, too destructive
2. Offline SQLite surgery - requires gateway stop, users should not hand-edit database
3. Compaction cleanup only - helps but doesn't address non-compacted sessions

### Impact

Affected: Main session (most common for interrupted inputs)
Severity: High (model gives wrong responses)
Frequency: Every context compaction cycle
Consequence: Model responds to stale pending inputs instead of current user messages, requiring manual re-sending

### Evidence/examples

Yes — see the Evidence section above; full session diagnostics (pending-input states, acceptedAt timestamps, compaction count) can be provided on request.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, I do not plan to open a PR for this.

### Additional information

Session history shows interrupted pending inputs persisting7+ hours after the run completed:

- pendingInputs.total:2 (both state: "interrupted")
- acceptedAt: timestamp from7+ hours ago
- Session last message: completed (stopReason: "stop")
- Model responded to stale input instead of current message after compaction

---

issues.body:
## Bug: `doctor --fix` deadlocks after removing one invalid Memory Core host event — legacy source already renamed to `.migrated`, leaving `plugin-doctor-state` step-refused with no supported recovery

### Summary

After upgrading OpenClaw **2026.10.4 → 2026.11.1** (npm, stable channel, Ubuntu Linux, Node 24.22.1), `openclaw doctor --fix` refuses at `plugin-doctor-state` with **"Skipped invalid Memory Core host event at [redacted-path]"**, blocking every later step (`sessions`, `acp-session-metadata`, `agent-dir`, `plugin-doctor-post-session-state` all show `blocked-by-prior-refusal`).

I traced the root cause to a **single stray record at line 2904** of `/home/ubuntu/memory/.dreams/events.jsonl` — a legacy classification record shaped `{"timestamp","query","tier","pipeline"}` with **no `type` field** and an embedded `→` character, which fails the Memory Core host-event schema (`discriminatedUnion("type", …)` in `event-store-*.mjs`).

Following the documented community workaround (issue **#160242** — identical situation), I made a byte-exact backup and removed only that one line, leaving 3177 valid typed events. **However**, by the time I removed it, a prior `doctor --fix` run had already renamed the legacy source `events.jsonl` → `events.jsonl.migrated` (at 10:02), and the migration's **import receipt was never written** because it had refused on line 2904.

Now every subsequent `doctor --fix` / `openclaw update repair` run is wedged: the legacy source the doctor expects is gone (renamed), and there is no supported command to reconcile the receipt with the post-edit source (mirroring the deadlock described in **#156016**).

### Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), npm install, stable channel
- **OS:** Ubuntu Linux 7.0.0-38-generic (x64)
- **Node:** 24.22.1
- **Upgrade origin:** 2026.10.4 → 2026.11.1 (manual `npm install -g openclaw@latest` + Node 24.21.0 → 24.22.1 for the eMudhra security patch)
- **Gateway:** systemd user service `openclaw-gateway.service`

### Exact failure

```
Failing check plugin-doctor-state (step-refused): Skipped invalid Memory Core host event at [redacted-path]
Failing check sessions (blocked-by-prior-refusal): Migration step "sessions" was not run because prior step "plugin-doctor-state" refused execution.
Failing check acp-session-metadata (blocked-by-prior-refusal): ...
Failing check agent-dir (blocked-by-prior-refusal): ...
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-prior-refusal): ...
```

Additional (separate, harmless) warnings:
```
Warning: /home/ubuntu/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json: [entry_invalid] Session entry is missing a valid sessionId.  (×2)
```
These two entries are the known benign ID-less cron stubs (per Peter Steinberger's note in #163668) — **not** the blocker.

### Key diagnostic facts

- `/home/ubuntu/memory/.dreams/events.jsonl` no longer exists — it was renamed to `events.jsonl.migrated` (5091182 bytes) by a prior doctor run.
- A byte-exact backup exists: `events.jsonl.bak-20261108-0958` (5091323 bytes, the pre-removal original).
- After removing line 2904, the file parses clean: 3177 records, all with a valid `type`.
- The doctor produces a fresh capture dir on every attempt (e.g. `doctor-eabe40b4-…`) with **"No repair outcome is recorded"** — confirming it never reaches a completed migration.

### What I tried (all run, Gateway stopped where required)

1. `openclaw doctor --fix` → step-refused (memory event)
2. `openclaw update repair` → blocked
3. `openclaw plugins registry --refresh` → "requires exclusive offline state ownership" (gateway keeps re-owning the lock; even with `sleep 8` the refresh runs after gateway restart)
4. Removed the single invalid line (line 2904) per #160242 → source is now clean, but the receipt/source mismatch (from the earlier `.migrated` rename) still blocks completion

### Impact

Gateway starts and runs normally (2026.11.1 serving, Telegram OK, all ports healthy) — **not an outage**. But `openclaw update` reports "Last update run failed (step-refused)" and the five plugin convergences (`brave`, `deepseek`, `memory-map`, `openclaw-honcho`, `opencode`) remain `pending`, so the installation is pinned with a permanently-failed update record.

### Requested fix

A supported escape from this state is needed — ideally one of:
1. A `doctor --session-sqlite rebaseline` / explicit re-baseline command that rewrites the migration receipt from the *current* verified source (as suggested in #156016), **or**
2. Re-validate the Memory Core source by content hash alone (not full inode/mtime identity) so the post-edit `events.jsonl.migrated` can be re-imported, **or**
3. Any documented procedure to reconcile a legacy Memory Core source that was renamed to `.migrated` before its import receipt was written.

Happy to provide sanitized failure JSON, migration-run reports, or the exact file/record details on request.

*No raw JSONL, config, credentials, session content, or local paths beyond what is necessary are included.*

labels.name: clawsweeper:source-repro

issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.11.5-beta.1, every turn in a session created with `deviceFolder` fails before the node does any work. The error is:

```
Session capability metadata requires worker preparation
query: {"storePath":"~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/sessions/sessions.json","agentId":"<agent>","sessionKey":"agent:<agent>:dashboard:<uuid>"}
```

Gateway-local sessions for the same agents work normally.

### Environment

- Gateway: macOS, 2026.11.5-beta.1. Reproduced on both a stock build and a locally patched build. `subagent-session-store-DCBvtZoV.mjs` and the session-row capability reader are byte-identical in both.
- Node hosts: two headless macOS node hosts on 2026.11.5-beta.1 (version matched to the gateway), enrolled with `openclaw devices join-code` + `openclaw connect --service --session-host`. Both use `nodeHost.workerRuns: { enabled: true, capacity: 2 }` with native isolation and a folder allowlist.
- Agents tried: two different agents, each with a model fallback chain (OpenAI primary, Anthropic and OpenAI fallbacks).

### Reproduction

1. `sessions.create {agentId, label, deviceFolder: {deviceId, path}}` with no initial message.
2. `sessions.dispatch {key, deviceId}` → `ok: true`, placement state `active`.
3. Wait 60 s.
4. `sessions.send {key, message}` → `status: started`.
5. `chat.history`: the response shows two "Model switched …" rows, then a `custom` row containing the error above.
6. A second `sessions.send` on the same session 60 s later fails the same way.

This reproduced on both nodes, for both agents, and on every turn. It is not a first-turn race.

### Observations

- Each attempt fails about 300 ms into the gateway-side embedded run. The log shows `embedded_run_agent_end isError: true, providerRuntimeFailureKind: unclassified`, then `lane task error … requires worker preparation`. The model fallback chain retries each candidate and gets the same error, so in the transcript it looks like model switching.
- The failing query is the session's own key with no field. It is not a parent or subagent lookup.
- Nothing appears in the node host log at the time of the failure.

### Analysis (from the shipped dist; exact caller not confirmed)

- The error is thrown by `readDurable` in `createSubagentSessionStore` (`subagent-session-store-*.mjs`) when a synchronous `.get(sessionKey)` runs and none of its sources have the entry:
  1. `sessionRowProjectionOwner.readCommittedEntry` (skipped when the prepared scope is `retain`)
  2. a prepared entry from `withPreparedSessionCapabilityRead` / `prepareSessionCapabilityRead`
  3. the legacy reader
- `createSessionRowCapabilityReader` (`session-row-projection-*.mjs`) returns `undefined` when `topologyDirty` is set or when `row.sharingEntry !== row.storedEntry`. When that happens, any unwrapped synchronous capability read throws.
- In gateway-local runs, path 1 usually succeeds, which hides unwrapped synchronous reads. For device-folder (placed) sessions, path 1 consistently misses, so some synchronous capability read in the gateway-side turn setup throws. The log serializer keeps only `message` and `query`, so we could not capture the stack.
- Synchronous readers we found that are not wrapped near their call sites: `resolveStoredSubagentCapabilities` → `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` (subagent-capabilities), `isInternalAnnounceRequesterSession` (subagent-announce-delivery), `resolveSpawnAdmission` (acp-spawn-policy). On the worker-turn path, `executeWorkerTurn` prepares `conversationCapabilityProfile`. However, `createOpenClawCodingToolsInternalAsync` runs the synchronous `assembleOpenClawCodingTools` outside a prepared scope.

### Expected

Turns in device-folder sessions either run, or fail with an actionable error. The capability metadata needed by synchronous policy code should be prepared for placed sessions as it is for local ones.

### Requests

- Include the error's stack (or the throwing caller) in `lane task error` logs. Today `SessionCapabilityReadRequired` serializes only `message` and `query`.
- Don't treat `SessionCapabilityReadRequired` as a reason to fall back to another model. It is deterministic, and the fallback chain currently hides it.

issues.body:
### Summary
After upgrading to `2026.8.1-beta.3` (5831b80), the Control UI left-hand session/conversation list is empty — no historical sessions are shown. The sessions list API returns 0 sessions for the main agent, and session search cannot find older content. The underlying transcript data is fully intact in the agent SQLite database; only the new session registry / search index appear to have been rebuilt without backfilling existing sessions.

### Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.8.1-beta.3 (5831b80), installed via npm global
- Schema: state=9, agent=17
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Node v24.15.0
- Upgrade path: from the earlier 8.x-beta line; a migrate/restore step ran at upgrade time (see Evidence)

### Expected behavior
- After upgrading, all pre-existing sessions remain visible in the Control UI left rail and searchable via session search.
- The migration should backfill the new session registry (and search index) from the existing agent database transcripts.

### Actual behavior
- Control UI left rail shows no historical conversations.
- `sessions_list` with agentId=main (or kinds=[main/group/cron/hook/node/channel/direct]) returns `{count: 0, sessions: []}`. Only an unfiltered call returns 3 unrelated `agent:claude:acp` sessions.
- `sessions_search` for terms that previously matched returns no results (tested with two terms that matched before the upgrade).
- The currently active session IS registered and appears in `session_windows`, so new activity works — only history is missing.

### Evidence (read-only SQLite inspection)
State DB `state/openclaw.sqlite` (~98.8 MB):
- `audit_events`: 99,697 rows (intact)
- Registry tables all empty: `session_state_heads` = 0, `session_groups` = 0, `sidebar_sections` = 0, `current_conversation_bindings` = 0

Agent DB `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` (~103.7 MB):
- `session_transcript_active_events`: 19,229 rows (all historical messages intact)
- `session_windows`: 134 rows (only sessions active since the upgrade)
- `session_transcript_fts`: 6,203 docs (search index rebuilt, only covers recent content; `session_transcript_index_state`: 127 rows)

Migration log at upgrade time shows it moved aside legacy files from a previous upgrade attempt on the same beta line:
- `openclaw.sqlite.corrupt-20260818-0942`
- `openclaw.sqlite.bak-20260818-8.1upgrade`
- `openclaw-agent.sqlite.schema17-20260818`
and copied both DBs to an external backup location before restarting the Gateway.

### Suspected cause
The schema migration (state 9 / agent 17) recreates the session registry and search index but does not backfill/register pre-existing sessions from `transcript_events`. UI and search APIs read from the new (empty) registry, so history disappears from the UI even though the data remains on disk.

### Suggested fix
During/after migration, backfill the session registry and rebuild the FTS index from existing `transcript_events` (or lazily re-register sessions on first access). A CLI command to rebuild the session index from the agent DB would be a useful workaround (e.g., `openclaw sessions rebuild` / `openclaw db reindex`).

### Impact
Users on the 8.0 beta line lose UI access to all historical conversations after upgrading (until sessions become active again). Data is not lost but is unreachable through the UI/search without direct DB access.

issues.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp channel does not implement reconcileUnknownSend, so sends interrupted at send_attempt_started are permanently unrecoverable (silent reply loss)

labels.name: P1

labels.name: clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr
