issues.body:
### Bug type Regression (worked before, now fails) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary A pristine openclaw.sqlite — VACUUM INTO rebuild, full PRAGMA integrity_check = ok, verified before install — develops a freelist miscount within 15–24 hours of normal gateway operation, which then either escalates to structural corruption or paralyzes the gateway. 5 corruption events in 5 consecutive days on this host. Follow-up to the corruption class the 2026.8.1 WAL-lock fix addressed: on this host the fix is partial. Environment: openclaw.sqlite ~160 MB, 11-agent keyed agents.entries roster, agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent=2, WAL mode, .wslconfig [wsl2] autoMemoryReclaim=disabled (see "ruled out"). All times PT. ### Steps to reproduce
  1. Rebuild the database clean: stop gateway → sqlite3 -readonly openclaw.sqlite "VACUUM INTO 'rebuilt.sqlite'" → verify PRAGMA integrity_check = ok → install → start gateway.
  2. Run the gateway under normal multi-agent load (Discord channels, cron automations, subagents; cap=2).
  3. Check the DB periodically (quick_check/integrity_check on an online-backup snapshot, ~30 min cadence).

Within 15–24 h a freelist miscount appears:

rebuilt (verified clean) | first new finding | gap -- | -- | -- 08-18 10:37 (.dump rebuild after structural event) | 08-19 10:41 Freelist: size is 322 but should be 336 | ~24 h 08-19 15:46 (VACUUM rebuild) | 08-20 07:14 Freelist: size is 362 but should be 363 | ~15.5 h 08-20 12:05 (VACUUM rebuild) | (we now rebuild nightly at 04:50 to stay ahead of it) | —

The finding oscillates between OK and CORRUPT ticks while the reported freelist size walks downward (08-19: 322→288→268→254→186→25→15 over ~3.5 h), then ends one of three ways, each observed once:

  1. Structural corruption while running (08-18): Tree 69 page 39258: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11, byte-identical across checks. The gateway never crashed — no dump, NRestarts=0 — and kept writing into the malformed image for ~75 minutes (the integrity gate only runs at startup).
  2. Process death (08-17, pre-dating the reclaim fix): SqliteIntegrityError ... table audit_events.
  3. Gateway paralysis (08-19, new failure mode — see "What happened").

Freelist-only findings are a reliable precursor: on both days that ended structurally, freelist miscounts (with interleaved "self-cleared" OK ticks) preceded the structural finding by 2–8 h.

─── FIELD: What happened / Actual behavior ─── New failure mode — paralysis (fail-closed but not stopped). 08-19 14:03–15:45: the gateway's runtime integrity check began failing on the (freelist-only) miscount and refused every operation — [discord] ingress drain failed, Delivery recovery failed, [ws] parse-error, all SqliteIntegrityError — at ~1/sec, 14,000+ journal lines, while the unit stayed active/running, NRestarts=0, no stability dump, no restart, no alert. Externally indistinguishable from every agent dying at once. Positive: writes stopped, so damage could not spread. Negative: it has no voice.

Repeat victim — audit_events. The 08-17 death named table audit_events; the 08-18 structural damage sat inside audit_events (single corruption point at dump line 37857 of 68k; the table is ~36k of those lines — the highest-churn table). Two consecutive days, same table.

Ruled out / correlates:

  • Not SIGBUS/memory-reclaim: after autoMemoryReclaim=disabled (08-17), zero status=7/BUS across all subsequent events. Host memory healthy (32 GB, 26+ GB available).
  • WAL checkpoint hygiene in place (ExecStartPre/ExecStopPost checkpoint script); WAL drains to 0 on stop; sidecars quarantined on every restore.
  • Correlate (not a claim): a retention cron doing bulk task_runs DELETEs (~6.8 KiB avg rows, overflow pages) at 04:30; the first freelist anomaly of the arc appeared 63 s after one such run.

Operational impact: to keep the product usable we now run a 15-min "suspect snapshotter" (banks verified copies the moment a DB is flagged — the health lane correctly refuses to back up flagged DBs, which starves backups exactly when they matter), a structural-halt watchdog, and a nightly automatic VACUUM rebuild. A daily database rebuild as a standing requirement is the problem statement in one sentence.

### Expected behavior The database stays consistent under normal gateway load; a verified-clean file should not develop freelist miscounts within a day. If the gateway decides at runtime that the DB is unusable, it stops the unit loudly (stability artifact + non-zero exit) instead of idling in a zombie-serving state. An integrity_check-on-live result (or last startup-gate verdict + timestamp) is pollable by operators — the snapshot instrument said "healthy" 7 minutes before the 08-17 death. On the NOTADB/integrity-failed startup class, restarts back off or stop (Restart=always + 5 s produced a 940-iteration refusal loop against a corrupt file on 08-17). ### Actual behavior Asks (summary) Runtime integrity failure ⇒ stop the unit loudly (see above). Expose an integrity_check-on-live result (or last startup-gate verdict + timestamp) that an operator/script can poll — the snapshot instrument said "healthy" 7 minutes before the 08-17 death. Triage of the freelist producer: what in the gateway's write pattern (high-churn audit_events, bulk-delete freelist churn, checkpointing) can unbalance freelist bookkeeping on WSL2/ext4? On the NOTADB/integrity-failed startup class, back off or stop retrying (Restart=always +5 s produced a 940-iteration refusal loop against a corrupt file on 08-17). ### OpenClaw version 2026.8.1-beta.2 (8f382a2) ### Operating system Platform/OS: WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.2), Node 24.18.0 ### Install method _No response_ ### Model glm 5.2 ### Provider / routing chain openclaw -> ollama -> glm 5.2 ### Additional provider/model setup details _No response_ ### Logs ```shell # quickcheck lane, 08-19 (the walk) 10:41 CORRUPT Freelist: size is 322 but should be 336 11:12 OK 11:43 CORRUPT Freelist: size is 288 but should be 294 12:06 CORRUPT Freelist: size is 268 but should be 282 <- 6-hourly FULL integrity_check 13:17 CORRUPT Freelist: size is 186 but should be 196 13:48 CORRUPT Freelist: size is 25 but should be 28 14:19 CORRUPT Freelist: size is 15 but should be 18 <- stable/persistent from here # paralysis window, 08-19 (~1/sec for 100 min) [discord] ingress drain failed: SQLite integrity_check failed for .../openclaw.sqlite: *** in database main *** / Freelist: size is 15 but should be 18 [gateway] Delivery recovery failed: SqliteIntegrityError: ... [ws] parse-error error=SqliteIntegrityError: ... # 08-18 structural (byte-identical at 08:34 / 09:06 / 09:38) Error: stepping, database disk image is malformed (11) Tree 69 page 39258: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11 Five preserved corrupt specimens with sha256s (incl. two same-day 08-17 specimens sharing one verified base for clean diffing), the 07:11 stability dump, WSL crash captures, full health logs, and journal excerpts available on request. Happy to test candidate fixes on this estate. ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence _No response_ ### Impact and severity _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_

prs.title: fix(ui): keep bounded update and plugin failure text surrogate-safe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an update or plugin activation fails, the recorded failure cause and activation error are bounded to a fixed length with a raw string `slice`. If the cut lands inside a multi-code-unit character (a surrogate pair, e.g. an emoji), the recorded text ends with a **dangling lone high surrogate**. That truncated string is not well-formed UTF-16 (`String.prototype.isWellFormed()` returns false), which downstream consumers that require well-formed text (persisting, indexing, serializing the cause) can trip over — and it shows up as a replacement glyph or data-corruption risk rather than the user's actual last log line.

## User Impact

Failure causes and plugin activation errors are still truncated to the same byte budget, but never split a character in half. The recorded text is always well-formed UTF-16, so consumers of the recorded cause (persisted update state, error surfaces) receive valid text instead of a dangling surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bounded strings are built with `.slice(0, MAX)` in two places. Both are replaced with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, MAX)`, which clips only at code-point boundaries, never inside a surrogate pair. The behavior otherwise is unchanged: same limits (`MAX_UPDATE_FAILURE_CAUSE_CHARS` = 180 for the update cause, 512 for plugin activation errors), same redaction, same callers.

No Gateway, scheduler, permission, or persistence behavior changes.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/app/update-overlay-helpers.ts` `lastLogLine()`: `last.slice(0, MAX_UPDATE_FAILURE_CAUSE_CHARS)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(last, MAX_UPDATE_FAILURE_CAUSE_CHARS)`.
- `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-runtime.ts`: both `grantError.slice(0, 512)` and `formatUiError(...).slice(0, 512)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 512)`.
- New regression tests (red on base, green with fix):
  - `ui/src/app/update-overlay-helpers.test.ts` "keeps a boundary emoji whole when shortening the recorded cause": feeds a stderr tail whose last emoji straddles the 180-code-unit cap; asserts `isWellFormed()` and no `\uFFFD`.
  - `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-runtime.test.ts` "reports a boundary emoji whole when shortening a failed activation": same boundary for the 512 cap.
  - `ui/src/e2e/update-triage.e2e.test.ts` "keeps a boundary emoji whole in the recorded failure cause": end-to-end, the built UI records and renders the clipped cause; asserts the rendered text is well-formed, contains the whole emoji, and has no replacement glyph.
- **46 focused unit tests pass** and **6/6 e2e tests pass** on the rebased tree; the new e2e assertion fails on the base (buggy `slice`) with `text.isWellFormed()` false, and passes with the fix.
- CI on the current head (4d95e009c) is fully green, including `check-test-types-core-2` and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (test-line allocation sized to the actual 132-line regression growth).

### Real behavior proof: built-Control-UI string diagnostics at the surrogate boundaries

The two production substitutions run the shared helper `truncateUtf16Safe` from `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`. Proof is supplied at both levels the review asked for: the **rendered built-UI banner** (production bundle) and the **outgoing plugin activation report** (production module).

**1. Built Control UI — rendered update-failure banner (production bundle).** The e2e suite builds the real UI and drives an update failure whose cause crosses the 180-unit cap with a boundary emoji. A diagnostic emitted from the built bundle's rendered banner (via `ui/src/e2e/update-triage.e2e.test.ts`, which asserts these on the production-rendered text):

```
[proof-diagnostic] built UI banner text length: 469
[proof-diagnostic] isWellFormed(): true
[proof-diagnostic] contains whole lobster: true
[proof-diagnostic] no replacement glyph: true
[proof-diagnostic] banner text: "Couldn’t complete install: npm ERR! code ELIFECYCLE xxxxxxxx"
```

Because the banner is rendered from the built production bundle, if either `truncateUtf16Safe` substitution were absent, the cause clip would end in a dangling high surrogate and `isWellFormed()` would report false — the test (and this diagnostic) would fail. No mock substitutes for the production path here.

**2. Outgoing plugin activation report (production module).** `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-runtime.test.ts` "reports a boundary emoji whole when shortening a failed activation" drives the real production module (not a mocked boundary) with a 512-unit cap error (`511×x + 😀`), and asserts on the actual `plugins.controlUi.report` payload:

```
expect(detail?.isWellFormed()).toBe(true);
expect(detail?.includes("�")).toBe(false);
expect(detail?.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(512);
expect(fullError.slice(0, 512).isWellFormed()).toBe(false);  // raw slice WOULD be malformed
```

**3. Direct helper diagnostics (for the record).** Running `truncateUtf16Safe` against the review's exact boundary inputs:

```
=== Update failure cause (cap=180) ===
input length (code units): 181, isWellFormed: true
raw slice(0,180) length: 180, isWellFormed: false
  -> last code unit is 0xd83d (HIGH SURROGATE, DANGLING)
truncateUtf16Safe length: 179, isWellFormed: true
  before tail: "xxxxx\ud83d"
  after  tail: "xxxxxx"

=== Plugin activation error (cap=512) ===
input length (code units): 513, isWellFormed: true
raw slice(0,512) length: 512, isWellFormed: false
  -> last code unit is 0xd83d (HIGH SURROGATE, DANGLING)
truncateUtf16Safe length: 511, isWellFormed: true
  before tail: "xxxxx\ud83d"
  after  tail: "xxxxxx"
```

Result: raw `slice` produces a dangling high surrogate at both boundaries (`isWellFormed()` false); `truncateUtf16Safe` keeps the output well-formed at both boundaries. This matches the red/green unit and e2e regressions in the PR.

Note: a lone high surrogate is not visibly rendered by Chromium, so before/after screenshots of the status banner are pixel-identical; the observable difference is in the string data (`isWellFormed()`), which is what the regression tests assert.

**Merge danger:** two-way door; reverting fully restores the previous truncation without migrating or writing new state. Blast radius is limited to the recorded update failure cause and plugin activation error strings.

**Credit:** original fix authored by @huwei-xydt.

prs.title: fix(compaction): long sessions lose their own decisions when recent tool output overflows the summary
prs.body:
Related: #194408

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after compaction the agent forgets decisions, TODOs and IDs from the summarized span when the most recent turns before the cut carried a lot of tool output.

## User Impact

User impact: compacted summaries keep almost all of the model's own decisions and TODOs at the same 16,000-character size, with no extra replay cost and no new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persisted summary holds the model-written summary plus verbatim "recent turns preserved" context. Before this change the body only got half the budget once that suffix was large, so verbatim tool output (each result up to 600 chars, dozens per turn) displaced the generated summary. In 16 replayed production compactions the model's summary was always 6.9k–12.7k chars and would have fit on its own.

- The generated body now reserves room only for the suffix's required sections (tool failures, file ops, workspace context, generated split-turn summary). Verbatim preserved turns take what is left, newest first, and a cut keeps their heading.
- The generated split-turn summary is now always reserved ahead of older preserved turns (previously only on the degraded path).
- Preserved tool results keep a 160-char head excerpt plus `[N more chars omitted at compaction]`, similar to how Hermes Agent demotes stale tail tool output to stubs.
- Suffix budgeting moves to `compaction-safeguard-budget.ts` (line-cap ratchet).

This is an alternative to raising the cap (#194719): the replay showed the cap was binding because of how it was split, not because summaries needed more room.

## Evidence

Replay of 16 truncated production compactions from one long-running agent (tokensBefore 144k–1.05M). Each span was rebuilt from stored entries with `prepareCompaction` and run through the real safeguard with the qualityGuard on, using the same cached Opus 5.5 summary responses for every variant:

| variant | mean length | decision bullets kept | TODO bullets kept | model-chosen IDs kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, 16k | 15,715 | 73.9% | 65.5% | 74.1% |
| **this PR, 16k** | 15,853 | **95.5%** | **92.3%** | **80.9%** |
| main, cap raised to 32k | 26,311 | 100% | 100% | 83.1% |
| main, cap raised to 64k | 33,365 | 100% | 100% | 83.1% |

32k gets the last few points at roughly +2–3% cached-context cost per compaction window (a summary is replayed on a mean of 336 requests); 64k adds nothing over 32k.

Tests:
- New: `keeps a generated summary whole when verbatim preserved turns overflow the cap` and `keeps only a head excerpt of preserved tool output`. Both fail on main.
- `finally trims a raw tool interaction only at its atomic boundary`: fixture raised from 12 to 80 tool results so the interaction still overflows with excerpted output.
- `compaction-safeguard*.test.ts` (5 files, 56 tests) and `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction` (132 tests) pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all steps pass except `changelog attributions`, which fails on main on untouched `CHANGELOG/*.md` files.
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.test.ts` has 5 local failures that reproduce identically on main without this change.

Gaps: the replay did not measure compounding across successive compactions (each case started from the stored 16k summary), and identifiers lost before the summarizer (its input is sampled to 160k chars) are unaffected by this change.

prs.title: fix(android): stop reconnecting to a Gateway that never connected
prs.body:
Closes #194781 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android keeps reconnecting to a Gateway address in the background, about every 20 seconds, after its first connection failed and the user moved on to a different address. ## User Impact A Gateway address that never completed a connection no longer gets a background session. Gateways that did connect still stay connected in the background after switching, as before. ## Why This Change Was Made Manual setup registers the typed target and makes it active before the first connection attempt (`MainViewModel.saveGatewayConfigAndConnect` → `connectGatewayLocked`). `GatewayRegistryStore.setActive` also added the Gateway to `connectedStableIds`, the list `reconcileBackgroundGatewayFleet` keeps connected in the background (#111932). So when the first attempt failed and the user switched to another address, the abandoned target became "enabled, not active" and got a background operator session that never stops. The registry now enrolls a Gateway in that list when it completes a connection (`markConnected`, which the operator session already calls on hello) instead of when it is selected. One owner holds the rule; the fleet planner and the Settings toggle are unchanged, and `setConnectionEnabled` still lets a user enable any saved Gateway explicitly.
Behavior details - A previously connected Gateway is already in the persisted list, so it keeps its background session; nothing is migrated or rewritten. - A Gateway the user disabled stays disabled until it connects as the active Gateway again, which matches the old `setActive` behavior. - Accepted edge case: a device that already has an abandoned target in its saved list keeps it until the user forgets that Gateway or turns its switch off in Settings. Cleaning existing lists would be a migration, not part of this fix. - iOS persists the active Gateway only after TLS trust is settled, so it does not reach this path (code reading, not run).
## Evidence **Real Gateway, Android 16 emulator** (`system-images;android-36;google_apis;arm64-v8a`), Play debug APKs of `upstream/main` and this branch. An isolated local OpenClaw Gateway (own profile, temp state, port `18555`, token auth) plus a host listener on `18443` that accepts TCP and never replies. Same steps on both builds, from cleared app data: onboarding → Set up manually → `10.0.2.2:18443`, Secure (TLS) → Test connection → trust prompt → Cancel → Back → `10.0.2.2:18555`, Unencrypted, Gateway token → Test connection → device approved → finish onboarding → Settings → Gateway. | main | this branch | this branch, after selecting `18443` | |---|---|---| | | | | - main: the never-connected `wss://10.0.2.2:18443` row has its background switch on, and `18443` received 11 connections between 02:10:48 and 02:16:41 while the app was paired and connected to `18555`. - This branch: the `18443` switch is off, and `18443` received no connection from the first setup probe (02:17:45) until I selected it in Settings (02:21:44). - This branch, after selecting `18443`: `18555`, which did connect, is now a background Gateway with its switch on, and the Gateway logged a new Android operator connection at 02:21:45. Multi-Gateway background connections still work for Gateways that connected.
Listener and Gateway logs ``` # 18443 stall listener 02:09:43 accepted # main: setup probe 02:10:48 accepted # main: after switching to 18555 (background session) 02:11:08 accepted 02:11:29 accepted 02:11:51 accepted 02:12:14 accepted 02:12:39 accepted 02:13:07 accepted 02:13:42 accepted 02:14:26 accepted 02:15:28 accepted 02:16:41 accepted 02:17:45 accepted # this branch: setup probe # no connections while paired to 18555 02:21:44 accepted # this branch: 18443 selected in Settings (probe) # isolated Gateway, Android clients (this branch) 02:20:23 client connected client=openclaw-android role=node 02:20:23 client connected client=openclaw-android role=operator 02:21:45 client connected client=openclaw-android role=operator # background session after selecting 18443 ```
**Scripted run, no Gateway**: the same steps against `18444` (plain HTTP) instead of a real Gateway, 60 s after switching: | | Connections to abandoned `18443` | |---|---| | main | 4 (01:33:29, 01:33:49, 01:34:10, 01:34:32) | | this branch | 0 | On main, a thread dump during one of those connections shows an OkHttp WebSocket call to `https://10.0.2.2:18443/` in `ConnectPlan.connectTls`, the background operator session rather than the fingerprint probe. Tests (Temurin 21.0.13, Gradle 9.7.1): `GatewayRegistryStoreTest` (8), `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` (87), `NodeForegroundServiceTest` (54), `GatewayFleetSelectionTest` (4), `GatewayStoreMigrationTest` (5): 158 tests, 0 failed. - With `GatewayRegistry.kt` from main and the new tests kept: 2 failed. - `selectedGatewayThatHasNotConnectedIsNotKeptConnectedInTheBackground` drives `connectSwitchingGateway` for a registered target whose probe cannot read a certificate: expected `[]`, was `[manual|gateway.test|…]`. - `onlyAGatewayThatConnectedStaysConnectedAfterTheUserSwitchesAway`: expected `[paired]`, was `[abandoned, paired]`. - The existing background-session suites (secondary sessions, re-enable, forget, auth reset) pass unchanged. One existing registry test now records a completed connection before asserting the list, since selection alone no longer enrolls. - `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck` passes. Production delta +5/-3; test delta +34/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; no stored data is rewritten, and reverting restores enrollment on selection. Blast radius is which saved Gateways get background sessions.

prs.title: chore(ui): measure concurrent-session responsiveness
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI benchmarks previously covered quiet UI and one foreground reply, without measuring a tool-heavy turn alongside many active background sessions.

## User Impact

Developers can now measure unloaded, foreground-only, and 5/20/100-background workloads with the existing cross-engine harness. No production UI behavior, protocol, dependency, or production size ceiling changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture holds the inventory at 1,000 sessions and runs 200 foreground tools with live output. It measures native typing, scroll-frame gaps, session/route switching, idle renderer CPU where available, producer lag, and received wire frames/bytes. Actual application subscription calls govern detailed delivery. The shared mock now serves event/list/describe/history/mutation state from its canonical row owner, scopes subscription interests and row-delta baselines to each socket, and includes `lastMessageAt` in terminal deltas. A focused read-coalescing test counts its controlled burst from the existing settled boundary.

A real isolated Gateway grounded the event families and body-suppression rules: three concurrent agent runs, six actual read calls, nine loopback model requests. Full, narration, and broad-only audiences received respectively 48/41/14 frames and 59,131/55,036/18,976 JSON bytes. Broad-only durable receipts contained no message body. This is a small protocol observation, not a production-capacity measurement. The recurring stress rate—two logical durable receipts per second per background session—is synthetic; periodic usage invalidation was absent from the capture and is not invented in the mix.

A structural retained-section renderer candidate was removed after 20 rotated base/head/base triplets in each engine at desktop100. Chromium renderer CPU improved by paired median 10.8%, but Firefox session switching regressed by a paired median 30.3% and WebKit scroll-frame p95 by a paired median 8.9% (cell p95 +6.2%). A/A controls and all failed observations were retained. The cross-engine bar was not met, so this PR makes no production performance-improvement claim.

## Evidence

The descriptive census uses the frozen application at `23f2cd68e9d38bbffe561bada8eab5a72b9af110`, bundle SHA256 `ba629719ce791ef32c151b84c8b63b5b7c8305d592fa6fb6bda078ca149adca8`. It is not a measurement of subsequent main commits. All local browser runs were headless. Mobile means a mobile viewport on the same Mac, not physical mobile hardware; scroll gaps come from the scripted scroll loop, not touch/wheel delivery.

The completed baseline census contains **490 observations across 43 source/slot cells and 40 engine/viewport/throttle/load combinations: 476 passed, 14 failed, none incomplete**. It includes 120 reused desktop100 baseline/control observations; the 60 rejected-candidate observations are excluded. Ingestion/contract audit found no issues. The full 20-triplet candidate experiment has 180 observations and remains a separate comparison.

**Responsiveness is not established at 100 sessions.** The foreground-only 200-tool turn already produces large frame gaps. At 1×, 100-background scroll-frame-p95 medians are about 133 ms in Chromium/Firefox and 194–212 ms in WebKit, versus roughly 17–25 ms unloaded. Firefox's whole-window producer averages reach only 61–87 of the nominal 200 logical receipts/s. At 4×, the producer falls short even at five backgrounds; at 100 it averages 63.24/200 on desktop and 145.47/200 on mobile. Completed 4×100 session switches have medians of 3.07/1.84 seconds (desktop/mobile, n=8 each), with cell p95 values of 12.28/13.30 seconds. Route-switch cell p95 reaches 17.57/32.45 seconds. Similar or lower frame-gap numbers under a missed offering are not evidence of improved scaling.

The 14 retained failures are six ResizeObserver errors, one foreground-production-overlap guard, three post-typing query timeouts, three session-switch wait timeouts, and one terminal-reply-visibility timeout. Post-typing screenshots show the expected draft intact, but the predicate timed out. Switch-timeout screenshots show the target transcript/checkpoints, but cannot establish which key/checkpoint predicate failed. Final correctness remains unverified for interrupted paths; no dropped final state is inferred. Available metrics remain in inclusive distributions, with missing metric counts preserved; passed-only distributions remain in the local detailed report.

prs.body:
Fixes #195013.

## What Problem This Solves

A wikilink or Markdown link nested in image alt text appears in Knowledge navigation and backlinks even though the shared renderer displays inert text and the editable-link scanner excludes it.

## User Impact

Image captions no longer create phantom navigation edges. Ordinary visible links, including those inside quotes, lists and tables, still appear. Stored Markdown and typed relationships are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The extractor already lexes a fresh token tree. Clearing image children in its existing traversal aligns extraction with the shared renderer and editable-link owner without introducing another parser or changing caches. One regression covers hidden wiki/Markdown links and visible container controls; its measured 20-line growth has a matching allocation.

Exact base: `dd1bf005936dc143b2edaf793b7bc5fef3e3e838`. Candidate: `2f3f470f17424a40e86f8beaafd06b422dec8d2c`. All three remote file hashes match the frozen sole-author payload exactly.

Outgoing links incorrectly remain 1 → 1 → 1 and backlinks 2 → 2 → 2 while rendered anchors/editable links are 0 → 1 → 0.

With the exact candidate, the original fixture plus `markdown-links.test.ts` and `page-budget-writes.test.ts` pass **17 tests in three files**, exit 0; wrapper 67.406 s. prs.title: fix(ios): app reconnects forever with a revoked device token after setup-code pairing
prs.body:
Closes #190145

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an iPhone or Mac paired with a setup code keeps reconnecting forever with the same rejected token after the device is revoked (`openclaw devices revoke`) or the Gateway state is reset, until the Gateway's auth rate limiter trips. The app shows "Gateway token is out of date", which names a shared token the device doesn't have.

## User Impact

User impact: after a revoke or a Gateway reset, the app drops the dead stored device token and the next reconnect goes to the normal pairing path instead of looping. Clients that have an explicit Gateway token are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

When no explicit token is configured, `GatewayChannel` sends the stored device token as `auth.token`. The Gateway can't tell that apart from a shared token, so it answers `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH` (or `AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH`). The existing clear-stale-token branch only ran on the explicit device-token retry path, so this case kept the token. The fix clears the stored token in that case only: no explicit token, the stored token was the credential sent, and the Gateway rejected it with one of those two codes. It uses the same `DeviceAuthStore.clearToken(observedToken:)` call as the existing branch, so a token rotated in the meantime is not wiped.

## Evidence

Tested on macOS 27.2 (arm64), Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2. Branch base: e8f91361ab.

Before the fix (`GatewayChannel.swift` from the parent commit; `swift test --filter GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests` in `apps/macos`): the 2 existing tests pass. The new test fails in both cases (`.authTokenMismatch`, `.authDeviceTokenMismatch`):

```
GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests.swift:322: Expectation failed: DeviceAuthStore.loadToken(...) == nil
GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests.swift:332: Expectation failed: recorder.auth(at: 1)?["token"] == nil
✘ Test run with 3 tests in 1 suite failed with 4 issues.
```

After the fix:
- `apps/macos`: `swift test --filter GatewayChannel`: 54 tests in 6 suites passed, including both cases of the new test.
- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: `swift test --filter 'GatewayNodeSessionTests|GatewayErrorsTests'`: 120 tests in 3 suites passed.

### Real Gateway trace

A local Gateway built from this branch (`gateway --dev`, loopback, token auth, isolated state), and the `openclaw-mac` CLI from `apps/macos` built twice: from the PR base and from this branch. `openclaw-mac connect` runs the same `GatewayChannel` and SQLite credential store as the iOS and macOS apps, without the app UI.

`openclaw-mac` has no setup-code option, so each client pairs by connecting once with the Gateway token, and that token is then removed from its config. That leaves the same state as a setup-code-paired device: a stored device token is the only credential, and no explicit Gateway token is configured. Then the device's operator token is revoked with `openclaw devices revoke`, and the client reconnects three times. The "gateway:" lines are the Gateway's log for each attempt, and "stored device tokens" counts the rows in the client's credential store.

Without the fix, every reconnect resends the revoked token and the token is never cleared:

```
### openclaw-mac built from: base (the PR base, without the fix)

1. Pair: configure the client with the Gateway token and connect once, so the Gateway issues a device token
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=token
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1

2. Remove the Gateway token from the client config. The stored device token is now its only credential,
   which is the state a setup-code-paired phone or Mac is in
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=device-token

3. Revoke the device's operator token on the Gateway: openclaw devices revoke --device 54cf1febccb0… --role operator
   revoked

4.1 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1
4.2 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1
4.3 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1
```

With the fix, the first reconnect after the revoke is rejected and the stored token is cleared, and later reconnects no longer send it (`auth=none`):

```
### openclaw-mac built from: fixed (focus/190145, with the fix)

1. Pair: configure the client with the Gateway token and connect once, so the Gateway issues a device token
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=token
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 1

2. Remove the Gateway token from the client config. The stored device token is now its only credential,
   which is the state a setup-code-paired phone or Mac is in
   result: ok - connected
   gateway: client connected, auth=device-token

3. Revoke the device's operator token on the Gateway: openclaw devices revoke --device 67a8eff968dd… --role operator
   revoked

4.1 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token mismatch (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=token device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 0
4.2 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
   gateway: unauthorized, auth=none device=yes
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 0
4.3 Reconnect after the revoke
   result: error - unauthorized: gateway token missing (provide gateway auth token)
   stored device tokens for this Gateway: 0
```

Gateway log for the run with the fix, from the revoke on (peer ports and instance ids removed). The Gateway writes the `unauthorized` detail line once for back-to-back identical rejections, so the third attempt only shows its `res ✗ connect` line:

```
2026-11-03T02:25:59.339 [gateway] device token revoked device=67a8eff968dd… role=operator
2026-11-03T02:26:01.147 [ws] unauthorized conn=3d2d412e-bc69-4fb8-9f9f-d289c0dd7ecd remote=127.0.0.1 client=proof-client-fixed ui vdev role=operator scopes=6 auth=token device=yes platform=macOS 27.2.0 host=127
2026-11-03T02:26:01.148 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 252ms bytes=332 failurePhase=auth failureCause=unauthorized conn=3d2d412e…7ecd id=BDF9F6A2…DDD1
2026-11-03T02:26:02.717 [ws] unauthorized conn=7b5860d1-948f-4925-bd10-4b7984b9b487 remote=127.0.0.1 client=proof-client-fixed ui vdev role=operator scopes=6 auth=none device=yes platform=macOS 27.2.0 host=127.
2026-11-03T02:26:02.718 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 1ms bytes=332 failurePhase=auth failureCause=unauthorized conn=7b5860d1…b487 id=B361D2E3…83B2
2026-11-03T02:26:04.285 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 0ms bytes=332 failurePhase=auth failureCause=unauthorized conn=cd2d45fd…1ef9 id=DB27A575…D0A9
```

Not covered here: the iOS/macOS app UI after the token is cleared (the setup screens it falls back to). That needs a device or simulator run of the app.

prs.title: fix(muse): cancel catalog checks without closing active readers
prs.body:
Closes #194922

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: canceling one initialized Muse catalog check closes the host shared by other active checks and returns EOF instead of the caller's cancellation reason.

## User Impact

A canceled check preserves its caller's cancellation reason while other readers sharing the initialized host can finish. The host closes after its final reader settles. No configuration or migration is needed.

The SDK cannot cancel a single model/list request; its discarded reply may remain pending, and continuously arriving readers can postpone host retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race each reader's wait against its own signal using the existing SDK helper, then use the pool's existing user count to retire canceled hosts when idle. Keep subprocess teardown with the Muse SDK.

This is standalone on main base `94d45c8d5144dacde3e76ef1bab8046e9523b66b`. It neither includes nor depends on startup PR #194884. The adjacent native-turn/approval work in #183676 and README correction #194903 remain separate.

## Evidence

Tested head: `46d78ac39964d50d67c8fb53048999042ee7c1af`; tree: `6e95b8b4507349e478285aebe6b59940a19e0197`.

- **RED:** regression/fixture hunks only, unchanged production reader at the base: **2 failed / 5 passed**. Both requests reached the same initialized subprocess; aborting the first returned `ProtocolError: connection reached EOF` instead of the exact caller error. That assertion stops before the later survivor assertion; this RED does not independently execute the survivor-result assertion.
- **GREEN:** catalog **7/7**, including the survivor's complete expected catalog and final-reader teardown; pool **3/3**. Warm harness/pool/catalog comparison: **60/60**, 50.325 s wrapper wall time. Additional Muse index/events: **4/4**, 32.406 s wall time.
- Focused Muse source/test types, typed lint, format, full docs link audit (16,476 internal links, zero broken), whitespace, and exact **+87** test-line allocation pass. The allocation covers normal shared completion, one canceled reader with a survivor, and both readers canceled; shared scalar unchanged.
- Independent Codex P0–P3 source review found no actionable findings across all five files and interactions, on the exact tree committed above against the stated base. This is source review, not CI or live verification.

**Validation limit:** initial default-Bun and Node diagnostic consumer runs each had **58/60**, with the same two unchanged harness cases timing out at 10 seconds (stream/resume lifecycle; first read-only-host case). A subsequent exact-base comparison passed **57/57** (42.924 s), followed by the unchanged warm candidate passing **60/60** under the same default runner, order, environment and limits. Those initial timeouts remain unexplained; no inherited-defect or cold-start-causation claim, timeout widening, or timeout repair is made.

Linux, Node 26.13.0 orchestration, pnpm 12.15.0, pinned Muse SDK 1.4.14 and repository-pinned Bun. Synthetic local MSP subprocess only; no model invocation, login, remote provider, live Gateway or Windows proof. CI run 42434860162 remains failed by the inherited budget condition described below; human maintainer review/merge remains pending.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and focused commands</summary>

Use a disposable short TMPDIR, frozen dependencies, and remove META_API_KEY and MODEL_API_KEY from the test environment.

```sh
# RED on the base: apply only the regression and synthetic fixture from this commit.
git diff 94d45c8d5144dacde3e76ef1bab8046e9523b66b 46d78ac39964d50d67c8fb53048999042ee7c1af -- extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.test.ts extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs > catalog-tests.patch
git apply catalog-tests.patch
env -u META_API_KEY -u MODEL_API_KEY node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=10000

# GREEN on the complete candidate.
env -u META_API_KEY -u MODEL_API_KEY node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/muse/harness.test.ts extensions/muse/src/runtime.test.ts extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=10000
env -u META_API_KEY -u MODEL_API_KEY node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/muse/index.test.ts extensions/muse/src/events.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=10000
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/muse/tsconfig.json extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.ts extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.test.ts extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs
node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.ts extensions/muse/src/verify-setup.test.ts extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs docs/plugins/muse.md

```

Focused typecheck used a temporary config under `.openclaw/tmp/muse-public-lane/` extending `../../../test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.json`, including `../../../test/types/vitest-codex-attempt-runtime.d.ts`, `../../../src/**/*.d.ts`, `../../../extensions/muse/**/*.ts`, and `../../../packages/**/*.d.ts`; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <config> --noEmit` passed.

A task-owned temporary index of the exact five-file candidate passed `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 94d45c8d5144dacde3e76ef1bab8046e9523b66b --staged`.

Changed catalog test-file RED wrapper wall time was 55.399 s including cold worker compilation; final warm catalog test bodies totaled about 3.5 s. 

</details>


### Current exact-head review and transport proof

[ClawSweeper Revision 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194924#issuecomment-6716761154), reviewed at 2026-11-08 04:45 UTC by [successful executor 42447797388](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42447797388), binds unchanged head `46d78ac39964d50d67c8fb53048999042ee7c1af`: **no findings, Before merge: None, ready for maintainer review**. It inspected the full inline programs and raw candidate/base controls and explicitly cleared the previous transport-proof hold. The required CI failure remains a separate landing gate; this is not merge authorization.

The evidence is directly readable here: [complete programs/contracts/oracle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194924#issuecomment-6717320327) and [all six raw controls plus first-cancel outcomes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194924#issuecomment-6717322574). Both comment bodies were read back byte-for-byte, with SHA256 `d415be2b650efbdea8acb1f4c588c1e6ff5c7773b9f19efd50e41ef448ec1c3f` and `dc2929a2aaae9242781b431114f18c6f06350d56ad625eb5afb6b5b98174c0c1`. They deliver 29 whole files from the unchanged archive with explicit omissions; no experiment was repeated to remedy the reviewer's release-download restriction.

[Full v2 archive and original independent qualification](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/releases/tag/openclaw-194924-46d78ac-transport-proof-v2): real public plugin loader/registration and registered `verifySetup` / `loadModelCatalog` hooks reach actual SDK 1.4.14 stdio transport, without replacing or spying on product implementations.

- **Candidate: 3/3 pass. Exact base: 1 pass / 2 intended cancellation failures**, using the same hash-verified recorder/peer and unchanged source. Unlike the earlier regression's unreached survivor assertion, the new base recorder continues after A's wrong result and directly observes B also reject with connection EOF, without a catalog reply/rows.
- On the repair, A preserves the exact caller cancellation error with B pending and the same initialized PID. prs.title: feat(llama-cpp): deploy local OCR and vision on Apple Silicon
prs.body:
Closes #194650

## What Problem This Solves

Apple Silicon Mac users are rejected by llama-cpp's managed local OCR/vision setup even though its pinned macOS runtime can run both models with Metal.

## User Impact

Users can run `openclaw models auth login --provider llama-cpp --method local-media` on macOS arm64 and receive separate local OCR and vision models selected within current unified-memory and disk budgets. Both real-image checks must pass before activation; cancellation or failure preserves the previous configuration and preset. Existing chat defaults and embeddings are preserved.

Requires native arm64 Node, macOS 13.3+, and confirmed Metal support. Resource-constrained or unsupported hosts receive guidance before downloads. Small English-focused vision models can hallucinate; this does not add video input or reliable complex chart/layout recognition.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends a **shipped feature**: @duyufansh2008 contributed the original Linux x64 implementation in #148193 (merged October 12, 2026). The first stable release containing it is **[v2026.10.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.10)**, published November 3, 2026; current stable v2026.11.1 also contains it. I verified merge ancestry and official npm plugin contents/integrity, including preceding stable packages. This PR retains the original deployment owners and Linux CPU recipe.

- Qualify Apple Silicon media setup with bounded `system_profiler` Metal telemetry and existing memory/APFS probes; display chip and available cores. Strict qualification is opt-in for media, preserving released Mac chat/embedding backend selection when telemetry is unavailable.
- Prefer the existing GLM-OCR + 2.2B vision pair; select a pinned, checksum-verified SmolVLM2 500M pair when only it fits. Count unified memory/shared disk once and preserve host headroom. A complete compact pair still needs 4 GiB available because OCR reserves 4 GiB.
- Reuse consent, verified downloads/cache, pinned runtime installation, isolated candidate preset, registration and local routing. Use the runtime's real `MTL0` device for model/projector, override inherited CPU preset settings and reject conflicting global router options before downloads.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `f16482dd02217f2ecec23c0f15ef69ee95ecbec6` after merging main `44a5a6595094bd8ad2077e85800c7f661292f87a`. The original feature commit is `6855d4a7556aaeba39382731cb4a95b05a727739` (initial main `b4411857f195fb3444fa02f0414944db5be96bd9`). Cold installation, stable-upgrade, original regression and earlier review evidence below are pinned to that feature commit. The five-turn chat/local-image test, full plugin lane and full build were repeated on the current candidate.

**Physical Mac:** M4 Mac mini, 10 CPU/10 GPU cores, 16 GiB unified memory, macOS 26.5.2 arm64/Metal 4, Node 24.22.1.

| Real product check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Released 2026.11.1 baseline | Actual CLI rejects darwin/arm64; config unchanged. |
| Latest-stable → candidate upgrade | Official 2026.11.1 host/npm plugin → this candidate host/bundled plugin on the same isolated state, before any media enrollment. Existing real chat session continues, local embeddings/search work with the retained index, and chat/embedding/image preferences, eight workspace files and native preset remain intact. |
| Hardware/resource selection | Natural available memory around 4.4–4.9 GiB selects compact vision; 5.2–5.8 GiB selects standard vision. |
| Full cold matching-main enrollment | Empty model/runtime caches; automatic runtime + four model/projector downloads (3,139,962,912 model bytes), exact size/SHA-256 checks, both real image probes, then MTL0 models and local routes persist. 179.661 s from consent to CLI completion. |
| Registered image inference | GLM-OCR transcribes Tesseract's scanned phototest sample; 2.2B vision describes OpenCV's fruit photograph through `infer image describe`. |
| Native backend | b10809 reports `MTL0: Apple M4`; verbose inference shows model layers offloaded to GPU and `CLIP using MTL0 backend`. All three recipes pass the unchanged enrollment fixtures. |
| Existing chat + local OCR/Vision | Five real Gateway turns retain the operator's existing hosted chat model: normal chat, local_image OCR, local_image vision, chat-history recall and direct attachment preprocessing. Current-head ordinary bootstrap (35,525 prompt characters, four workspace files); no minimal/lightweight or per-turn model override, no fallback. |
| Supplemental direct-VLM agent | An extra native image-bearing turn uses SmolVLM itself as the primary model, with minimal/lightweight prompts. This is separate from the mixed chat/helper proof. |
| Failure/cancel behavior | Actual decline, interrupted download and download failure retain config. A 1-second real OCR timeout during re-enrollment retains an already working config and its preset byte-for-byte. |

**Evidence limits:** physical coverage is M4 only. The follow-up standard-pair run completed a full cold automatic installation after the proxy node changed; no models/runtime were copied or prefetched into its empty test state. The earlier compact recipe and supplemental native tests used verified cached files. Current-main testing used its matching host after official Doctor repair of isolated test state. An extra test forcing SmolVLM as the main chat agent was rejected by its client-side 8K context estimate; that was not the auxiliary OCR/Vision path (details below). The new mixed chat/local-image run uses ordinary bootstrap and successful real `local_image` calls. Earlier standalone HTTP `/tools/invoke` probes remain unsuccessful supplemental checks; HTTP-tool execution is not claimed. Existing live user state/Gateway was not modified.

**Hosted checks on the current head:** security, dependency and PR context/evidence checks passed. [CI run 42445708643](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42445708643) is `action_required` with zero jobs started, awaiting repository fork-workflow approval; `openclaw/ci-gate` remains failed. `pnpm test:ci-failed 194746` reports no selected Vitest failures to rerun. The separate [Labeler failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42445706068) is a GitHub API 504 when listing labels. ClawSweeper's completed second review was on `6855d4a`, with no code findings and sufficient behavior proof; it does not review the new merge head. Maintainer platform-support acceptance and fork CI approval remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Checks, review, reproduction and selected output</summary>

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test:extension llama-cpp`: **25 files / 349 tests pass**, 65.37 s, on current `f16482d` (the earlier feature-commit lane passed 347).
- Four touched test files pass individually through `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Mac wall times: hardware 2.851 s, catalog 2.574 s, preset 61.777 s (overlapped build/compilation waiting), setup 17.605 s; not CI measurements.
- Negative Metal telemetry, complete-pair memory selection and inherited CPU preset regressions fail on the base for the intended assertions and pass with this change.
- Original feature commit: targeted plugin typecheck, production lint, formatting and full build pass. Current merge head: `git diff --check` and full `pnpm build` pass (189.7 s); tracked UI/shared resources omitted by sparse checkout were hydrated before the successful build. Nonfatal upstream UI size-budget/bundler warnings remain.
- Current-head dependency setup limitation: frozen install reached linking but an unrelated Matrix crypto postinstall binary download failed with ECONNRESET. No dependency patch, script disabling or guard bypass was used. The matching-source build, focused plugin lane and real Gateway proof below passed with the linked installation.
- Test-lines ratchet passes: 6,563,837 / 6,563,898, slack 61. The issue-linked 292-line allocation accounts for net tests covering qualification, resource tiers, offload overrides, consent and rollback; no global ceiling change.
- Author pr-simplify/test-audit passes completed. Independent read-only review found and verified the fix preserving ordinary Mac chat/embedding behavior; final full diff review has no actionable findings. Reviewed snapshot SHA-256: `7d47f80b7a545e5c4ccaeeed06933abc44550271be334bb352c22b4b90913d9a`. Local autoreview/ClawSweeper were not run; this is not a claim of those tool results.

**Stable-to-candidate upgrade:** the official stable CLI `2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)` loaded npm `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider@2026.11.1`; the candidate CLI `2026.11.1 (6855d4a)` loaded this checkout's bundled plugin. Plugin entry hashes/origins were checked, so the candidate was not silently testing the old installed plugin. On the same isolated state, candidate `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` completed successfully, then the real Gateway continued the stable Qwen3.5 4B conversation and recalled the conversation-only code `CEDAR-7319` with no fallback. The two pre-upgrade messages were identical before the candidate turn. Both versions passed a real local EmbeddingGemma probe and retrieved `ORCHID-4827` / `cobalt` with top vector scores `0.74455446` (stable) and `0.74455455` (candidate). Before candidate queries, the retained index already had the stable final 5 files / 14 chunks, 768 dimensions, 14 embedding-cache entries, valid identity and automatic-rebuild sequence 0; no candidate reindex was requested. Model inventory, chat/defaults, embedding settings, image primary/fallbacks and media preferences remained semantically equal after Doctor and after inference. Eight workspace file hashes and the complete native INI, including comments/options, stayed identical (preset SHA-256 `c09e1f5b82ce70ba390c3781c32b573560462687c72cfaf9a40309b4cf9fff7d`). No `local-media` enrollment was called in this upgrade lane.

Upgrade-test limits: this is a CLI/source-host switch using official Doctor, not a package-manager updater test. Doctor reported source-UI freshness, minimal-profile/Active Memory and `checkpoint-incomplete` advisories; candidate search later emitted `verification-missing` at the normal integrity gate. No guards were bypassed; commands succeeded and the final Gateway wrote a clean-close receipt. These observations are retained in the evidence. An initial pure-text SmolVLM fixture returned `empty_result`; it was retained, and the successful ordinary-chat proof used the pinned public Qwen3.5 4B model instead. All upgrade fixtures were synthetic; task Gateways and native services were stopped afterward.

**Existing chat + local images, current `f16482d`:** a fresh isolated Gateway retained the operator's actual configured hosted chat model and provider, with their private identifiers/endpoint omitted here. All five real turns matched that primary model (resolved context 128,000), with no fallback or per-turn model override. Ordinary current-host bootstrap injected four workspace files and a 35,525-character system prompt; no `promptMode` or `bootstrapContextMode` override was supplied. The model completed normal chat, discovered/dispatched `local_image task=ocr` on the public scan, dispatched `local_image task=vision` on the fruit photo, then recalled the pre-image conversation code `PINE-8642` without a tool. Persisted `chat.history` contains the actual nested local tool calls/results, both successful. OCR and vision tool executions took 3.400 s and 4.175 s; total respective chat turns took 18.539 s and 20.131 s. The other three turns took 8.524 s, 9.145 s and 10.817 s. The same five-turn test also passed on the original feature commit with five injected files / 43,420 characters; those prior-head results are retained separately. Image model contexts stayed 8,192. The chat selection/provider, preset and live user config were unchanged. Task services stopped and the copied credential-bearing test state was removed after sanitized proof export.

A fifth turn sent the geometric verification image as an ordinary attachment. The existing custom primary had no image input declared, so the configured local image preprocessing route produced a textual `[Image] ... Description:` input; the original chat model answered “A red square is above the blue circle.” A primary declared to support native images can instead receive attachments directly. Explicit `local_image` selects the installed local OCR/Vision models independently of that capability; this test does not claim every native-vision primary sends attachments locally. The photo model still hallucinated some details, so this is integration proof, not an accuracy benchmark.

**Earlier 8K rejection, precisely scoped:** an extra test explicitly selected SmolVLM as the main agent and asked “What is two plus two?” with no image. Its 28,946-character system prompt included 19,616 workspace characters and zero tool-schema characters. The OpenAI-compatible client estimated 9,125 input tokens against 8,192 and rejected the request before HTTP creation; 9,125 is not measured server token usage. The separate local-image helper constructs an image/task-only payload and does not forward the chat agent's bootstrap/history. The earlier minimal/lightweight native-image probe also used SmolVLM as the main agent; it was never proof of this mixed path. No model context expansion or source fix was needed for the successful mixed run.

To reproduce the mixed path, retain the existing chat primary/provider in isolated state, enable the already enrolled local media route, and start a task-owned Gateway. Place the public scan/photo in that isolated workspace. Use the same session for these ordinary agent RPCs (no model or prompt-mode override):

```bash
corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --timeout 210000 --json --params \
  '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","createSessionIfMissing":true,"deliver":false,"message":"Remember PINE-8642. Reply with that code only."}'
corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --timeout 210000 --json --params \
  '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","deliver":false,"message":"Use local_image task ocr on ./phototest.png, then quote the first sentence. Do not inspect the file with another tool."}'
corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --timeout 210000 --json --params \
  '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","deliver":false,"message":"Use local_image task vision on ./fruits.jpg, then describe what it identified and note uncertainty. Do not inspect the file with another tool."}'
corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --timeout 210000 --json --params \
  '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","deliver":false,"message":"What code did I ask you to remember before the image tasks? Reply only with that code, without tools."}'
corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call chat.history --json --params \
  '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","limit":100}'
```

Verify the selected original primary in each agent receipt and the successful nested `local_image` calls/results in history. A fifth attachment test additionally verified ordinary preprocessing with the text-only primary; it is distinct from explicit tool routing.

Use an isolated state/config and native arm64 Node in the candidate checkout:

```bash
export OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/absolute/path/to/task-state
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1

corepack pnpm openclaw models auth login --provider llama-cpp --method local-media
corepack pnpm openclaw infer image describe --file /absolute/path/to/scan.png \
  --model llama-cpp/glm-ocr-q8_0 --prompt "Transcribe the visible text." --json
corepack pnpm openclaw infer image describe --file /absolute/path/to/photo.jpg \
  --model llama-cpp/smolvlm2-2.2b-instruct-q4_k_m --prompt "Describe the visible objects." --json
```

Substitute `llama-cpp/smolvlm2-500m-video-instruct-q8_0` when compact vision is selected. Use supported `OPENCLAW_PROXY_URL` if an external download proxy is required, retaining loopback exclusions.

Public inputs: [Tesseract phototest.tif](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract/blob/main/testing/phototest.tif), converted with macOS `sips` to PNG (SHA-256 `40ef67f9a856ad10df84975ef722a373d8c8f869c6d10a3db0843e9d35b2b834`); [OpenCV 4.12.0 fruits.jpg](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.12.0/samples/data/fruits.jpg) (SHA-256 `9c031d80a1c52da5eca790db896baffec6a7e52bf786cdb7bbfca5c7f880e6a1`).

Sanitized actual output:

```text
Backend: METAL
Processor: Apple M4 (10 available CPU cores).
Local OCR and vision verified
Updated config: <isolated test configuration>

OCR: This is a lot of 12 point text to test the ocr code and see if it works
on all types of file format. The quick brown dog jumped over the lazy fox.
[The scan's repeated sentences were also transcribed.]

Failed re-enrollment: image description request timed out after 1000ms
Config unchanged: true; previous preset unchanged: true
```

Registered OCR/vision calls report `ok: true`, `transport: local`, provider `llama-cpp`, and no fallback attempts. The photo response includes incorrect details, consistent with documented small-model limitations.

</details>

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): cached sidebar single construction [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload constructs and discards an empty sidebar frame before restoring cached rows. The original campaign recorded 14 visible states over about 15 seconds for a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link; this lane isolates a small, deterministic source of waste.

## User Impact

**STOP — do not merge.** The initializer-only candidate removes the wasted construction but regresses archived hello handling under the campaign's hard secondary rule. This experiment is being closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Starting the existing snapshot lifecycle pending prevents Solid from constructing a frame before mount-time admission. The existing admission path still handles cold boots, misses, scope retirement, and sign-out. The runtime change is one initializer replacement; no new owner or persisted shape is introduced.

## Evidence

One quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_11da5042caa1`; 24 interleaved pairs and 24 A/A pairs per Team workload, alternating AB/BA order, four primes per arm, real old-page reloads in steady-state timing mode. Both arms include the same measurement-only [Details docking fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194971). That fix is excluded from this PR.

Frame construction census: **2→1 in 24/24 candidate pairs for both Team active and archived**. The identical-build controls retain 2. Rows/Details co-frame in all measured Team samples.

Complete-frame medians: active **460→458 ms**, archived **430→428 ms**. A/A-adjusted effects by order: active **+2 / −6 ms**, archived **+10 / −10 ms**. These do not establish an earlier complete frame in both orders; the deterministic-count escape hatch would apply only if secondaries held.

**The stop:** archived hello-handled is **517.60 ms [513.90, 521.53] → 525.55 ms [522.67, 529.35]** (median [Q1,Q3]). IQRs do not overlap; 20/24 pairs are worse. A/A-adjusted effects are **+13.60 / +9.60 ms** by order. The non-overlapping-IQR clause triggers STOP despite the small median rise. No complete-frame speedup or qualification is claimed.

Native timing was interrupted after the stop. Visual parity/geometry, interaction E2E, full UI E2E, and the changed-file gate were not reached; no screenshots or private Team media were uploaded.

Regression red on pinned main: actual sidebar frame DOM constructions 2 versus expected 1. Candidate focused suites: **18/18** projection tests (5.48 s repo-wrapper wall time), **36/36** snapshot lifecycle tests (2.57 s). Independent autoreview was clean through P2. The nine added lines extend the existing retained-owner regression without adding a production seam.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42447308639) checked out `02b02be6e216f5343ecd99fd71abec461eeff613`; its [performance/byte gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42447308639/job/128629241816), with no cap edit. Catalog fallback-baseline drift also fails on [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446163942/job/128625723750). CI was cancelled after the benchmark stop; unfinished checks are not passing proof. The first manual dispatch used an abbreviated SHA and fell back to main; only the corrected full-SHA run counts as candidate proof.

Runtime LOC delta **0 (+1/−1)**. The prescribed stat includes two lines of scoped test-budget metadata, so it is **+3/−1, net +2** across two non-test files. The repository's test-line ratchet requires that metadata for the nine regression lines.

<details>
<summary>Full per-pair, within-order, secondary and census tables</summary>

prs.title: feat: let sandboxed plugin tabs invoke declared session actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tabs need narrowly authorized session actions without receiving Gateway credentials or a general-purpose parent HTTP proxy. This replaces #80388 and builds on #107323.

## User Impact

Plugins can expose declared actions for the parent-selected session. Revoking device authority or session access while an action waits now prevents the action from running. Failed action-enabled pages show a sanitized explanation and Retry, which obtains a fresh grant before reloading.

Existing canonical session navigation and the direct iframe flow for tabs without actions are preserved. The unused `allowChatNavigation` schema field is removed; no second public navigation API is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge keeps authorization in the existing Gateway dispatcher, registered action scopes, trusted session context, persisted access checks, and payload/result schemas. Sandboxed pages receive neither bearer tokens nor mutation cookies.

This refresh addresses the [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102#issuecomment-5005741905): recheck both authorities synchronously immediately before invoking the plugin handler, provide recoverable page errors, remove the obsolete schema field, and repair the reported lint errors. Earlier navigation and causal MessagePort test fixes are retained; branch history is preserved.

## Evidence

Validated source: [`edbac97f93bc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102/commits/edbac97f93bc6fc633779cdee607b081abc0063c).

- **Gateway: 6 tests pass.** The real dispatcher, persisted session authority, and row-preparation boundary are exercised. Current authority permits one action effect; revoking the device or removing session membership while preparation is held returns `UNAVAILABLE` with **zero effects**.
- **Plugin UI: 51 tests pass** across document, page, and bridge suites. New cases cover an HTTP failure followed by Retry with a fresh grant, policy-error reporting, and redaction of a redirect error's private URL/token.
- **Regression sensitivity demonstrated:** keeping the new tests but restoring affected production files from `82f71f3` makes both authorization-revocation cases and all three new error/retry cases fail. The current-authority control still passes. Restoring the repaired files produces the passing results above.
- **Independent review:** no actionable high/medium-priority findings in the 11-file refresh.
- **Static checks pass:** changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, UI stylelint, UI i18n catalog validation, and `git diff --check`. The PR context/evidence policy also accepts this description locally.

**Remaining verification gaps (not waived):**

- **Browser/screenshots/end-to-end evidence is blocked.** Chromium crashes with `SIGTRAP` before loading the isolated fixture; a minimal launch without PR code reproduces the crash, including with `--no-sandbox`. The installed stock Firefox ESR also exits before Playwright can connect; no Playwright-patched Firefox is installed. No current-head browser assertions, network captures, or before/after screenshots were produced. Historical captures are not presented as current proof. Full Gateway startup, authenticated WebSocket flow, production cookies, plugin discovery, and deployment remain unverified. The retained navigation tests pass in the focused UI suite, but their separate base-fail replay has not been recorded.
- The broader changed-file check stops at the line-cap ratchet because this host's Git 2.34.1 does not support `git cat-file --batch -z`. Its preceding conflict-marker check passes; later gates and broader type checks are not claimed as passing.
- Replaying the two previously failing chat-test files yields 8 passing assertions but an unhandled Lit `ChildPart has no parentNode` exception in `chat-message.mcp-app.test.ts`. The run therefore fails. Those files are unchanged, but that alone does **not** establish that the failure is unrelated to this PR; causality remains unresolved.
- New-head hosted CI has not yet been validated. Maintainer review and the screenshot requirement remain outstanding.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and local test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-host-hooks.registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-document.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On an isolated service capped at 50% CPU and 6 GiB RAM, final command wall times were 558.46 s and 64.49 s respectively (Vitest-reported durations: 492.82s and 45.86s). The persisted-authority scenarios exercise the real persistence/projection/dispatcher boundary with a causal preparation barrier, not sleeps or a mocked authority decision. CI seconds are not yet measured; these resource-capped local times are not CI estimates.

The old-source regression runs failed as expected in 866.35 s (authorization) and 51.30 s (page errors/retry). Production files were restored and their checksums verified afterward.

All verification used a separate checkout and private test state/config under resource limits. The live Gateway was not restarted, reconfigured, deployed to, or used as a test target.

</details>

## Remaining Maintainer Decision

The public `sessionActions` bridge still needs maintainer sponsorship and a long-term owner. This is an updated review candidate, not a merge request or a waiver of exact-head CI, screenshots, or owner review.

prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two deterministic cron test failures in scheduled main run [42442788470](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42442788470/job/128615623240) after #194907 changed active-run diagnostics.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Restores cron coverage of message completion, controller retirement, and admission cleanup after a finalization failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The introducer is `ee3ec605a59c` (#194907), whose raw parent is the previous green scheduled head `5e1a27a9bcc4`. Its shared message lifecycle now consumes a completed input while preserving `processing` until the active controller retires. The extra event is the final controller-owned idle transition; it is not a duplicate queued input.

Keep the strict ordered event assertion, now checking processing with zero queued inputs before message completion and idle with zero queued inputs after controller retirement. Inject the finalization error at queue consumption instead of the obsolete immediate-idle transition; retain the exact rejection and admission-release assertions. Scoped spy disposal replaces manual cleanup. The patch has no production changes and reduces test code by three lines, with no baseline changes. Its hunks are separate from #188301's imports and appended timeout test.

Related: #194907. This is a coordinator-requested repair of the named main failures.
