prs.title: fix: allow retained repair after session rotations and native deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained repair preparation rejecting intact historical transcripts after repeated session rotations, or intentional removal recorded by the native agent-deletion owner.

## User Impact

Operators can prepare and continue a retained repair when existing runtime evidence explains the evolution since the original activation witness. Controller adoption still requires the complete reviewed, merged four-file closure; this PR performs no deployment.

Unexplained rewrites remain refused. Rewrite generations are random tokens with no predecessor receipt: a different token and newer timestamp alone cannot prove preservation. The original generation or its verified immutable archive is still required unless completed native agent deletion explains the loss. No schema, retention policy, runtime config, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical historical windows outlive the current entry's direct previous-session reference. Accept their exact physical store, window owner, and generation. Consume completed native deletion records in the existing shared-state read, binding agent, path, operation, journal time, phase, completion, and physical identity. All preparation and later lifecycle floors use the same owner.

Runtime code grows by 20 lines after simplifying the witness API to consume the existing original journal. The additional code accounts for deletion evidence; no cache or second shared-state scan is added. Rerunnable synthetic benchmark tooling is separately included. The 102-line regression allocation covers the new behavior and refusal controls without changing the shared test budget.

## Evidence

- Adopted baseline `57c015ff0331`: the three positive continuity regressions fail at the intended boundary; 12 negative controls pass.
- Candidate: 123/123 focused continuity, preparation, transaction, runtime, and startup tests pass, zero skips (111.811 seconds in the qualified Linux controller fixture).
- Codex autoreview through P2 is clean for the complete candidate against `43a197415643`, including the benchmark.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all checks pass except 20 existing changelog-attribution failures independently reproduced on exact parent `43a197415643`; introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364), retained as a main regression. Test-line ratchet passes with the exact 102-line allocation.
- Full controller suite: exact parent 846 tests / 457 pass / 388 fail / 1 skip; candidate 863 / 474 / 388 / 1. Complete failure-name and attribution-bucket sets match: zero new failures. Existing main regressions trace to #193647, #169752, and #187090; Python health/maintenance and Prometheus checks pass on both arms.
- The expanded changed-check run passed all typechecks, lint, and structural checks. Initial benchmark formatting failures were fixed and the exact format check passes; only the attributed changelog failures remain. Initial-head CI formatting failures are superseded by the corrected head.

Synthetic btrfs proof uses 35.04 GiB SQLite, 6,000 original and current witnesses, and 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.1 GB. Five serial interleaved timing samples per arm plus two separate V8 allocation samples provide A/A controls. Each sample starts with a fresh process/fixture; native witness capture warms metadata before measurement. Fixture preparation and allocation-instrumented durations are excluded from wall-time results.

| Flow | Base → candidate median wall | p95 wall | User+system CPU median | Sampled V8 allocation median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Repeated rotation | Refused at 48.4 ms → prepared in 1025.8 ms | 56.1 → 1038.0 ms | 0.04 → 1.04 s | 24.1 → 192.5 MB |
| Unchanged successful path | 1271.5 → 1030.4 ms | 1308.5 → 1042.0 ms | 1.27 → 1.04 s | 204.7 → 186.8 MB |

Rotation compares different outcomes, **not a speedup**. The unchanged path improves wall time 19.0%, CPU 18.1%, and sampled allocation 8.7%; its predeclared no-regression guard passes. Wall ranges: unchanged base 1263.5–1308.5 ms, candidate 1014.4–1042.0 ms. Allocation A/A: base 203.89/205.50 MB, candidate 187.46/186.23 MB. Allocation is V8 sampling at 64 KiB, not total native allocation. SQLite padding uses materialized compressible zero blobs; native service observations are synthetic. All disposable containers/storage were removed.

Rerun: `.agents/skills/update-team-server/controller/bench/retained-continuity/README.md`. Final benchmark-only correction and formatting also received clean Codex review through P2. Final-head CI passed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446915803 on `4c77b1158961b29de47a6cbabab03c7981e65577` (27 successful jobs, 30 skipped, no failures).

The production incident's read-only diagnostic is a separate operator handoff. This PR does not assert that an unarchived rewritten generation can be recovered from evidence the runtime never recorded.

prs.title: feat(ui): add saved gateway account switching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This repair closes the remaining Gateway-profile correctness and proof gaps:

- Active profile removal uses the returned survivor projection directly, so the deleted URL cannot be reintroduced by fallback loading.
- Query-aware migrated credentials are sent only to their owning exact endpoint at the outgoing WebSocket client boundary.
- Successful token-mode migration retires the old origin-scoped token; clearing an owned migrated profile retires both exact and legacy slots.
- Query-distinct profiles cannot recover a neighboring profile's credential.

Profiles remain local browser metadata. Credentials remain session-scoped; no server-side account or shared credential store was added.

## Evidence

- Pushed head: `9b7ed952e4a4d0fd5367c96074b62b93496f38cb`.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec vitest run ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-registry.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **117/117 passed** across 4 suites.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec oxfmt --check ui/src/app/settings.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/pages/connection/connection-page.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 tsgo:ui` — passed from an independently owned checkout install.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 ui:build` — passed: **3,401 modules**, **840 finalized sidecars**, startup JS gzip **345,895 B** under the **352,235 B** limit; startup CSS **44,978 B** under the **51,200 B** ceiling.

## Fresh headed-browser proof

Run on 2026-09-11 against exact-head build `8023b23`/the pushed repair checkout, using disposable token Gateways and temporary state:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:19889` with a synthetic redacted token label `personal`.
- `ws://127.0.0.1:19890?account=team` with a synthetic redacted token label `team`.
- Real headed Chromium opened `http://127.0.0.1:19889/settings/connection`; the UI reached the actual WebSocket Gateway handshake and displayed token-authenticated connected state for both endpoints.
- Browser flow added and switched to the query-bearing Team profile, then confirmed removal of the active Team profile. The page reconnected to the surviving `19889` profile and the removed row stayed absent.
- The outgoing-boundary regression captured the actual client constructor options: migrated exact URL plus its owned token; after token-mode hello, the exact token key existed and the legacy origin key was gone.
- The clear regression seeded an owned origin-migrated token, cleared it, and verified both that profile and a query-distinct neighbor loaded with an empty token; the legacy key was absent.
- Browser storage and console diagnostics were redacted: no token values were retained. Browser console reported 2 development/runtime errors from the session; no zero-console-error claim is made.

## Limitation

After the browser's first successful token handshake, the Gateway issued a device grant. Clearing the visible Gateway secret and clicking Connect therefore remained connected through device authentication; this does not claim that clearing revokes an existing device grant. The no-token-reuse claim is proven at the outgoing client boundary and by the storage regression, while the live browser proof confirms the real handshake, profile switching, survivor removal, and endpoint identity.

The final post-push exact-head startup check launched runtime `9b7ed95` but detected that the runtime build stamp was still from `8023b23` while the rebuilt UI was `9b7ed952`, and correctly returned HTTP 503 rather than serving a mixed build. The interactive headed-browser receipt therefore comes from the immediately preceding compatible runtime; the final-head changes are covered by the 117-test suite, exact-head UI build, and the outgoing-boundary regression.

No new ClawSweeper review was requested.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep authored agent order when saving config
prs.body:
Closes #165055

## What Problem This Solves

An unrelated macOS config save alphabetizes the agent roster and can change which agent the Gateway treats as first.

The first PR revision also refused saves for valid configurations whose Gateway intentionally returns `raw: null` to protect secrets. The prior follow-up restored those saves through the existing `config.patch` contract. This follow-up fixes a separately reproduced Unicode scanner defect that rejected existing quoted keys beginning with a literal combining mark.

## User Impact

Existing configurations retain authored object-key order across local-file and Gateway saves. Valid redacted Gateway configurations remain editable, and quoted Unicode keys survive unrelated full-document saves. No config option, migration, or change to secret redaction is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing `.sortedKeys` alone is insufficient because Swift dictionaries do not retain JSON source order. Both full-document save paths use one source-aware writer. Local saves read the existing file under their existing lock; Gateway saves retain the source with the loaded document's route lease and revision hash.

When the Gateway intentionally withholds source text, the app instead sends only the differences from the loaded structured baseline through `config.patch`. Unchanged agent entries and redacted credentials are omitted, so the Gateway-owned source retains their order and values. Explicit `replacePaths` preserves full-array edit intent for reorder, shrink, and subtree deletion instead of invoking ID-keyed upserts. Revision, route, fallback, and local credential-preservation guards remain in place.

The writer scans Unicode scalars so a literal combining mark cannot absorb an opening quote into a Swift grapheme cluster. Foundation still owns JSON5 validation and key decoding.

The full-document writer retains existing keys, omits deleted keys, appends new keys deterministically, and accepts JSON5 comments, quoted/unquoted keys, escapes, and trailing commas. Retained array values keep their object order when moved or when neighbors are inserted/deleted. Arbitrarily moved-and-modified array objects without stable identity receive deterministic order; comments and whitespace are normalized as before.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `ae4cd9bbcab468fbde71ef994386d2a1aa81e0b6`. Unicode follow-up parent: `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Base: `c3b2b7d3fc1a053d2f6907e55e1629c16fc53706`. macOS arm64, Swift 6.4.

### Unicode compatibility control and repaired behavior

At the published parent `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, Foundation accepts a strict JSON document whose quoted key and string value begin with literal U+0301 scalars. An unrelated browser edit fails in both production save owners:

```text
BEFORE local save refused; original fixture unchanged
BEFORE raw-present Gateway save throws DecodingError; no config.set request
AFTER three local saves succeeded; combining-mark key/value and authored order retained
AFTER three raw-present config.set saves succeeded; key/value/order and baseHash retained
```

The exact production `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict`, `ConfigStore.load/save`, and `ConfigJSONWriter` sources were compiled with synthetic transport/peripheral adapters and run using `sandbox-exec -f proof.sb unicode-before-proof before` and `unicode-after-proof after`. The sandbox denies operator files, network, preferences/Keychain services, and child processes. Only disposable fixtures were used; this is not installed-app/live-Gateway E2E.

The new parameterized Swift regression fails before for both double-quoted JSON and single-quoted JSON5, then passes with scalar scanning. It creates literal combining marks through Swift scalar escapes rather than JSON escape tokens and checks preservation across repeated unrelated edits, including strings containing delimiter/comment text.

### Valid raw-null compatibility control and repaired behavior

The exact published first revision `21fa0613ea2f389d6d1eeb998d85ccd3c1c03a12` refuses a valid raw-null save with ConfigStore error 4. At prior head `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, the repaired production `ConfigStore.load/save` owner succeeds against the same boundary.

A synthetic configuration deliberately gives its token the same value as an unrelated configuration field. The exact production `redactConfigSnapshot` owner therefore returns `raw: null` while retaining structured configuration. The proof then exercises five edits through the compiled production Swift save owner and applies the captured requests using the exact production `applyMergePatch` owner:

```text
browser off, browser on, browser off, provider-model reorder, provider-model shrink
5/5 saves succeeded through config.patch
Every request retained baseHash=synthetic-revision
Unchanged gateway/auth and agents were absent from every patch
Auth credential retained; agent roster remained zmain,alpha
Model reorder and shrink retained exact replacePaths and final array intent
```

The Swift owner ran in an OS sandbox against disposable fixtures. Gateway transport and peripheral app adapters were synthetic. This is direct save-owner plus production redaction/merge-contract proof, not an installed-app/live-Gateway end-to-end run. No operator configuration, installed app, or live Gateway was changed.

### Original ordering control

At the earlier first PR revision, compiled exact baseline and repaired local/Gateway serialization owners showed:

```text
Baseline: three unrelated local saves and three config.set encodings -> alpha,zmain
First PR revision: all six retained authored zmain,alpha
All three config.set requests retained baseHash
```

The full-document writer was unchanged by the prior raw-null compatibility follow-up; the scalar scanner correction above is new on this candidate. The earlier raw-null refusal is superseded by the repaired behavior above.

### Tests and checks

- Current exact-source pure serializer and merge-patch tests: **10 tests / 13 cases passed in 0.002s** in a separately linked, audited OS-sandboxed Swift Testing executable. This includes the failing-before literal Unicode regression, existing JSON5 comments/escaped keys/trailing commas, array movement/insertion/deletion, minimal patches, and array replacement/subtree deletion.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passed in **20.72s**.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed in **21.36s**. This is test-bundle compilation, not native suite execution.
- Strict pinned SwiftLint on both follow-up files passed with zero violations. Full macOS SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Touched tests now use required failable UTF-8 conversions.
- Broad macOS lint / `check:changed` still report only the unchanged, previously documented `QuickChatFocusedTextCapture.swift:232` multiple-trailing-closure violation. All other changed-check lanes passed; no unrelated production fix is included.
- Current independent P2 AutoReview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings. Reviewed source bytes match this candidate. Scope is this two-file Unicode follow-up versus the published parent. The inherited Codex auth attempt failed with HTTP401 and is not counted as a clean review.
- Earlier raw-null repair retains its five production-owner saves, nine pure tests/eleven cases, and clean compatibility review at `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Those are explicitly earlier-head measurements; the compatibility owner was not changed by this follow-up.

### Remaining checks and limits

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper reassessment are pending. Previous-head green CI is not current-head validation. Full native test execution requires disposable macOS CI/VM and was not run on the operator desktop. The separate generic JavaScript full-suite attempt was interrupted without an aggregate result and is not claimed as passed or as native proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes skill validation and packaging hanging indefinitely when `SKILL.md` is a FIFO (named pipe) with no writer.

## User Impact

Both commands now exit with `SKILL.md must be a regular file`, so authors can correct the input and retry. Ordinary skill files still validate and package normally; failed validation leaves an existing archive intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject non-regular entry files before reading them in the shared validator, which the packager already calls. This is two production lines with no new helper or dependency. The regression invokes both real CLI entry points against a real FIFO, with a timeout that kills and reaps a hung child.

Related categories recently merged from an external contributor: #194059 (FIFO input hangs, merged by obviyus on November 6) and #194635 (skill packaging filesystem errors, merged by obviyus on November 8).

## Evidence

- **Real CLI before/after**, in offline, non-root, secretless Linux Docker (Python 3.11.10, 256 MiB, 0.5 CPU). At base `9a5df3d60f12b6c303225c50abeaa4d17bd27108`, both `python3 -S skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py <skill>` and `package_skill.py <skill> <out>` hang on an actual FIFO named `SKILL.md`; the harness kills and reaps each after 2 s. At head `426f1e8e893f5440bf99a64cc510129fd9d3cea6`, both exit 1 in about 0.1 s with the regular-file diagnostic.
- Directory inputs also fail clearly. A regular-file control still validates and creates a ZIP containing the original `SKILL.md` bytes. Rejected inputs leave an existing output artifact byte-for-byte intact with no temporary output.
- **Committed regression red/green:** both CLI subcases hit `TimeoutExpired` on the base (3 s limit per child), then pass with the fix. All **13** owner/consumer tests pass with `python3 -S -m unittest discover -s skills/skill-creator/scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v`; Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` pass. The exact-head combined CLI/test/lint/format verification took **2.07 s**. Python tests are outside the repository test-line ratchet patterns; no allocation or shared budget changed.
- Simplification: one check at the existing owner, **+2 production lines**, and **+25/-1 test lines** for the two affected CLI consumers. No packager-side duplicate validation.
- Independent read-only review of the complete committed diff, both consumers, tests and proof harness: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Scope: stable filesystem input types in these standalone tools. No claim of protection against a concurrent file replacement, no live Gateway/model run, and no full local build/test suite. The exact-head [`skills-python` CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446942771/job/128628000381) passed in **50 s** including setup; remaining CI and automatic Security Review are pending.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
Related: #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate` and `withLease`, the insert and lease-admission paths. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error. Recovery is gated on the current host's required capabilities; a host that lacks them cannot run the sweep and keeps reject-new behavior.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (16 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact; and a real `resolveCodexSessionBinding` authority whose `previousSessionId` changes between observe and `compareAndApply(delete)` is rejected at final worker admission with one delete attempt and the disposable row preserved.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Before the final test-lint and format-only follow-ups, the full `extensions/codex` suite, `check-changed` lanes, and fresh `$autoreview` were clean with no actionable findings.
- At prior head `e721d349d2b6c9dca567e240c681829378c8fc45`, the registered-path test lint findings and the two overflow files' formatting were addressed without changing recovery behavior. PR CI at that head was green, including `check-test-types`. The xAI type failure seen at `f8d62fcb212d7adb73e5a51f89a3be618be7623f` was fixed upstream by #177830, and this PR does not change xAI.
- At current head `58efcd3c65f944499b2ff7454f05787e4ecadccc`, the final-delete negative control now starts revocation only after the unbound observation completes, limits rejection to caller-bound stores, and asserts exactly one `compareAndApply(delete)` attempt before rejection while preserving the disposable row. The strengthened assertion failed with zero attempts before the timing correction and passes with one after it. The low-value source-snippet inventory was removed; the registered production-path behavior test remains.
- Current head `acd84820f892ff2517adc6853e19cf6a9bb192e7`: `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` passed 16/16 and `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` passed 2/2 through `node scripts/test-projects.mts`; oxlint passed on the changed test file. `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passes after merging current `upstream/main`, and `test/scripts/pr-dependency-cache.test.ts` passes 41/41 locally, resolving the darwin workflow/source mismatch seen before that merge. Full extension-test typecheck passed with the already-landed #177830 xAI baseline fix temporarily overlaid and then restored. Without that overlay, the local branch reports only the known xAI baseline error, not an error in this PR's changed files.

Remaining evidence gaps: this head strengthens the final-delete negative control but does not supply a shipped Gateway fresh-session recovery trace with real session reset/reassignment lineage, a latest-stable upgrade run, or the maintainer's retention-policy decision. Those gates remain open and are not represented as complete here.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.title: fix(ui): scope agent session management and preserve owner filters
prs.body:
Depends on [#194755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194755); this branch is stacked on its `5adf1572` head. Scope changes are `4ab20e2e` and `56aed841`; current head `c82b75dc` integrates the exact upstream context used for validation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent session management mixing chats from different agents and hiding the selected agent’s own conversations behind an implicit personal-owner filter.

## User Impact

Authenticated agent management starts at **All owners**, showing the selected agent’s authorized conversations. Saved owner filters remain active and intersect with that agent, including when the result is empty. Restricted guests keep the **Involving me** default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the selected agent in every session-list query, including reads with an explicit owner. Preserve a saved owner choice when the current or bounded owner facet omits it, rather than silently replacing that choice. Agent switching, empty results, background refreshes, and reloads therefore retain the same intended query scope. The visible agent picker subscribes to the existing authorized roster inventory for unread badges and the latest conversation, then projects it through the selected agent and owner. This avoids depending on the sidebar cache that owner changes correctly retire; no cross-agent rows enter the sidebar.

This changes the initial presentation default, not the Gateway’s authorization: session membership still comes from the Gateway, and explicit owner selections remain supported.

## Evidence

- Synthetic baseline captures reproduce the problem: selecting Mentor A can show a Main conversation while omitting Mentor A’s student discussions.
- Final browser proof passed 5/5 (18.72 s wall): three selected-agent scenarios cover the default, an explicit human owner, and an explicit agent owner; two existing page-scope regressions also pass. Assertions cover query agent/owner intersection, switching to existing and empty agents, saved-owner retention, and reload without cross-agent rows.
- Owner/query/preference unit contracts passed 68/68 (1.12 s wall), including the guest-specific default. Scoped UI, E2E and component type checks, lint, formatting, and the test-line allocation check passed.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. These are source-branch tests with a mocked Gateway and synthetic data.

- Broader CI exposed eight expectations for the old cross-agent/default-self behavior. Owner-specific tests now explicitly select that owner. The retained resume/unread assertions also found and verify the independent picker inventory fix. The seven affected/sibling test files pass 150/150 on the exact merged head; the five browser cases and strict types also pass.
- Canonical performance against upstream `4cedec0f`: Chat boot 1,295,020 B (base 1,295,231 B; cap 1,295,248 B), New 802,413 B (base 802,603 B). Request counts remain 20/15; no budgets changed. Exact-head CI passed for `c82b75dc` (45 successful checks; 39 intentionally skipped checks).

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

### Actual compiled CLI behavior — October 21

Ten independent ordinary standalone invocations used credential-free synthetic private config/state, real loopback MCP transports and the compiled CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json \
  --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning
# Repeat each scenario with --severity-min error.
```

| Synthetic failure | Finding at warning threshold | Exit: warning threshold | Exit: error threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refused remote Streamable HTTP connection | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Initialized remote server delays `tools/list` beyond the real 10-second deadline | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Remote catalog repeats its pagination cursor | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Missing local executable | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Local stdio child exits during initialization | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |

Every invocation reported `checksRun: 1`. At error threshold, remote-only warnings were filtered out (`findings: []`, exit0). Representative sanitized output projection:

```json
{"scenario":"refused-http","threshold":"warning","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"warning","errorCode":"mcp-service-unavailable"}
{"scenario":"catalog-deadline","threshold":"error","code":0,"checksRun":1,"severity":"below-threshold","errorCode":null}
{"scenario":"closed-stdio","threshold":"error","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"error","errorCode":null}
```

**Build provenance/limit:** this CLI proof ran on [assembled fork commit dda926bb935](https://github.com/Grynn/openclaw/commit/dda926bb93528517d02666179d4478579af6e4a9), which contains this exact repair plus separately reviewed immutable-launcher/runtime fixes and other local units. All 13 files in this PR are byte-identical there to `92b501e7e5af68ad01b829ff005739fe69ed45b1`. Its full `pnpm build` passed with the live-service safeguard enabled. This is real compiled CLI evidence, **not an exact standalone PR-head build, a production deployment or a full installed-release Doctor certification**. No serving credentials, user state or model calls were used. The older blocked CLI attempt remains historical evidence, not a success claim.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `deepseek/deepseek-flash` is not recommended in model pickers and gets collapsed under "All models" because `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json` omits the canonical `deepseek-flash` key.

## User Impact

Users selecting DeepSeek models see `deepseek/deepseek-flash` directly as a recommended option in `/models` and model pickers without having to expand "All models".

## Why This Change Was Made

The DeepSeek provider manifest declares the canonical model id as `deepseek-flash` with display name `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash`. In `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json`, versioned aliases (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`) were present, but `deepseek-flash` was missing. prs.title: fix(release): recover plugin authorization after quota reset
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin npm publication stops before publishing when the shared GitHub installation quota is exhausted during final authorization. This blocked both 2026.11.2 publication attempts.

## User Impact

Release publication can recover from one measured quota reset without weakening authorization or retrying npm writes. No candidate/runtime changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Limit the publish matrix to four concurrent jobs. On the exact installation-quota HTTP 403, read the same credential’s quota reset and wait at most 3,700 seconds, then launch authorization once in a fresh process. Both routes run existing live publisher guards after any wait. Other errors and second failures remain terminal. Artifact consumption and npm publication are never retried here.

Four files (+220/-6), including a two-line allocation for the 134-line regression suite; no generalized retry framework or cache. Signed candidate and sealed validation unchanged.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(media): canonicalize missing media paths like their roots
prs.body:
Fixes #194406.

## Root cause

Local media containment compared two paths that were canonicalized differently:

- **Allowed roots:** `resolveCanonicalBoundaryPath` used `fs.realpath` with a lexical fallback; `local-roots.ts` uses existing-ancestor resolution.
- **Requested path:** `resolveLocalMediaPathForContainment` tried realpath on the file, then its parent, then fell back to `path.resolve`.

With a symlinked state dir (the reporter has `/data/.openclaw -> /data/stronghold-wm/wintermute`) and a missing folder in the requested path, the path keeps its alias spelling, fails `isPathInside` against the canonical root, and is reported as `path-not-allowed` instead of `not-found`.

The same mismatch existed in `media-reference.ts:102` (managed inbound detection) and the wildcard inbound anchor/matched-root pair.

## Fix

One function now spells every path in the containment comparison: roots, inbound anchors, requested paths, and `media-reference.ts`.

`realpathViaExistingPrefix` (`src/infra/path-existence.ts`) realpaths the longest existing prefix and appends the missing segments. Unlike `realpathExistingAncestor`, it:

- never folds `..` after a missing segment (that segment could later become a symlink), and
- refuses dangling, unreadable or looping link prefixes instead of guessing their target.

Paths with no canonical spelling fail closed with `path-not-allowed`.

**Kept:** host-read callbacks with staged, not-yet-written files still get the path (now also under symlinked roots); the open-time `opened.realPath` recheck still guards check-to-open symlink swaps; `not-found` is only reachable after containment passes, so it reveals nothing outside the roots.

**Wrong allow closed:** for assert-only callers (Control UI, webchat audio, managed image attachments, custom readers), a missing file under an in-root symlink to outside, or under a dangling symlink, used to resolve lexically inside the root and pass. It is now denied.

**Error text for the agent:**

- `Local media path is not under an allowed directory: <path>. Use a file inside the agent workspace or another allowed media folder.` (identical whether or not the target exists; tested)
- `Local media file not found: <path>. The path is in an allowed folder, but the file or one of its parent folders does not exist; check the path or create the file.`

## Evidence

**Matrix** (`src/media/local-media-access.test.ts`), real temp folders and symlinks, plain and symlinked prefix, through both `assertLocalMediaAllowed` and `readLocalMediaFile`: inside (file / parent / ancestor / nothing below a missing root / `..` through an existing folder), outside (file / parent / nothing), `..` escape after a missing folder, `..` after a missing folder that stays lexically inside, outward symlink (file / missing), dangling outward symlink, plus a no-existence-oracle check.

Also: staged host-read file under a symlinked root (`web-media.test.ts`), and an entry-point `view_image` test under a symlinked state dir (`openclaw-tools.media-workspace.test.ts`).

**Base vs fix on Linux** (`node:24-bookworm`, aarch64, `/data/.openclaw -> /data/stronghold-wm/wintermute`):

| file | base `d59f00281eb0` + new tests | fix |
|---|---|---|
| local-media-access.test.ts | 5 failed / 41 (4 matrix cells + updated message text) | 41 passed |
| web-media.test.ts | 1 failed (staged host-read) | 49 passed |
| openclaw-tools.media-workspace.test.ts | 1 failed (`view_image` got "not under an allowed directory") | 10 passed |
| local-roots.test.ts | passed | passed |

Base fails in both directions: wrong deny (symlinked prefix, only an ancestor exists) and wrong allow (outward/dangling symlink with a missing descendant).

**Replay of the issue's refusals** on Linux with the reporter's layout and roots from `getAgentScopedMediaLocalRoots({}, "main")`. Only `mouse.jpg` and `tmp-view/p-1.png` are real paths from the issue; the rest recreate the shapes it describes.

| case | base assert / load | fix assert / load | category |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tmp/td1031/mouse.jpg` (exists) | ok / ok | ok / ok | exists |
| `tmp-view/p-1.png` | path-not-allowed | ok / **not-found** | missing directory (bug) |
| 2× still-missing directory | path-not-allowed | ok / **not-found** | missing directory (bug) |
| created later, directory missing at call time | path-not-allowed; ok after create | ok / not-found; ok after create | not yet written (bug) |
| created later, only file missing | ok / not-found; ok after create | unchanged | not yet written |
| `tmp-media/x1.png`, directory missing | path-not-allowed | ok / **not-found** | missing directory (bug) |
| `tmp-media/x2.png`, only file missing | ok / not-found | unchanged | missing file |
| `tmp-media/x3.png`, exists | ok / ok | ok / ok | exists |
| `media/y1.png`, directory missing | path-not-allowed | ok / **not-found** | missing directory (bug) |
| control: outside, exists | path-not-allowed | path-not-allowed | denied |
| control: outside, missing | path-not-allowed | path-not-allowed | denied |
| control: `..` escape after missing folder | path-not-allowed | path-not-allowed | denied |

**Checks:** the three media test files on macOS and Linux; media/gateway/channel callers (`image-tool`, `pdf-tool`, `media-tool-shared`, `read-capability`, `media-reference*`, `path-existence`, `plugin-sdk/media-local-roots`, `chat-webchat-media`, `chat-reply-media`, `control-ui-assistant-media-*`, `server-http.control-ui`, `worker-turn-media.boundary`, `send`, `message-tool.source-reply`, msteams, discord, telegram, agentsapi) all pass. `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format and guards pass; the only failure is `changelog attributions` on existing `CHANGELOG/*` lines this PR doesn't touch. `git diff --check` clean.

## Other containment checks audited

- Fixed here: roots, wildcard inbound anchor/matched pair, `media-reference.ts`.
- Inherit the fix: `chat-webchat-media.ts`, `control-ui-assistant-media-read.ts` (missing webchat audio no longer reports path-not-allowed).
- Already consistent: `sandbox/fs-paths.ts`, `sandbox/host-paths.ts`, `assertSandboxPath`, `workspace-path-containment.ts`, `workspace-fs.ts`, `session-file-read.ts`.
- Follow-ups (deny-only): `read-capability.ts:73,177,263` remote-reader routing compares `path.resolve` spellings; `sandbox-paths.ts:391-393` `resolveAllowedTmpMediaPath` can refuse macOS `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp`.

## Not verified

- Nothing ran on the reporter's machine, and their 9 refusal logs aren't available; 7 of the replay rows are recreated shapes.
- Windows: new tests are `runIf(!win32)`; the helper splits on both separators but hasn't run on Windows.

prs.title: feat(backup): restore PostgreSQL stores into a staging database for restore drills
prs.body:
Closes #182772

**Decision needed: how `backup restore` picks a different PostgreSQL destination.**

- **Recommended (this PR):** one restore flag, `--postgres-connection-env <name>`. Every PostgreSQL import, and the cleanup after a failed import, uses the DSN in that environment variable. Nothing else changes: the archived family selections and `schemaPrefix` still apply, and the restored `openclaw.json` stays byte-identical to the archived one. The output names the variable and says to point the archived connection at the same server before activation. No new config keys, and the DSN never goes on the command line. The output deliberately names only the variable, not the server identity (host, database, user), so the DSN is never parsed or printed.
- **Alternative B:** also write the override into the restored `openclaw.json`. Activation would then follow the restore destination automatically, but restore would have to rewrite captured config, including `$include` files, so the restored config would no longer match the archive under test. This can be added later on top of this flag if maintainers want it.
- **Alternative C:** accept a full SecretRef (`file:`, `exec:`, JSON) instead of an env var name. This is more flexible but needs a new CLI SecretRef syntax. An env var already covers file and exec setups: the operator can export the staging DSN for one command.
- **Out of scope:** a restore-time schema prefix (`restore_<uuid>` naming). That is a separate decision, as the issue review noted.

## What Problem This Solves

Restore drills of a PostgreSQL archive write full copies of every store into the production database when the archived connection is a file or exec SecretRef, because `backup restore` can only import through the connection recorded in the archive.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can verify a production archive by restoring it into a staging database. Production rows and schemas are not touched, and neither is the production secret file:

```
openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir> --postgres-connection-env STAGING_PG_DSN
```

Restores without the flag behave as before. The flag is rejected when the variable is unset or the archive has no PostgreSQL stores, and nothing is extracted in that case.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore already validates the archived config in its own offline scope and resolves the import connection from it. The flag replaces only `database.postgres.connection` in that in-memory copy with an env SecretRef for the named variable. Imports, verification and failed-import cleanup all read the same scope, so they all go to the same destination. Cleanup going to the staging server follows from that shared scope; no test forces a failed import with the flag set. The restoring host's own state ownership check still uses the live config, so a staging DSN cannot be confused with the host's live database. `--from` restores forward the flag too.

Activation stays explicit. If the restored state is used with the archived connection still pointing at the original server, the anchors name a `restore_<uuid>` namespace that does not exist there. State ownership then refuses with the existing `Missing PostgreSQL metadata; use the matching OpenClaw version or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor.` error, and nothing is created on that server (checked in the CLI run below).

## Evidence

**Through the built CLI**, using the same base (`72b51fb6089`) with and without this change. The setup is one PostgreSQL 17 server with two fresh databases: A, the "production" database behind a **file SecretRef**, and B, the staging database, whose DSN is supplied only through the environment. Each run starts a scratch install on A (`doctor --non-interactive`), records three backup runs as sample rows, runs `backup create --verify`, then restores with the flag and again without it. The table comparisons count rows and hash the ordered row text of every table.

Before (base build):

```
$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-override --postgres-connection-env DRILL_STAGING_PG_DSN
OpenClaw does not recognize option "--postgres-connection-env".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-default
Backup archive restored to staging: <dir>/restored-default
[exit 0]
A: drill_state_eecebf80adfa4f79, restore_d1dca86a713f4d838205bf7f6f5610be   <- copy written into A
B: (empty)
```

After (this branch):

```
$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-override --postgres-connection-env DRILL_STAGING_PG_DSN
Backup archive restored to staging: <dir>/restored-override
Archive entries restored: 12
PostgreSQL stores imported through: $DRILL_STAGING_PG_DSN
The restored config keeps the archived PostgreSQL connection; point it at the same server before activation.
[exit 0]

A: drill_state_9fe85f6bc3464805                       (no new schema)
B: restore_9933cc84eb5542efbe14cdc0c19a7879
A source schema rows: unchanged (98 tables, row counts and content hashes identical)
B vs A at archive time: identical (97 tables, row counts and content hashes; openclaw_schema_meta compared below)
tables with rows: 4, total rows: 7
openclaw_schema_meta store/version/store_id: identical (state v39 9fe85f6b-c346-4805-b1e8-bd5628ff1fe5)
restored state anchor: postgres restore_9933cc84eb5542efbe14cdc0c19a7879
restored openclaw.json: byte-identical to the archived config

$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-default      (no flag)
[exit 0]
A: drill_state_9fe85f6bc3464805, restore_ba2db7e46b0a4a1a9c6c98d80664c269   <- unchanged default behavior

# copy of the staging-restored state used with its archived config (connection still on A)
$ openclaw backup record --status ok --target activation-probe
Warning: the backup outcome could not be recorded: Cannot admit backup.recordOutcome ... failed to acquire gateway state ownership | Missing PostgreSQL metadata; use the matching OpenClaw version or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor. | relation "openclaw_schema_meta" does not exist
A: drill_state_9fe85f6bc3464805, restore_ba2db7e46b0a4a1a9c6c98d80664c269   (nothing new)
```

`openclaw_schema_meta` is compared on store, version and store id because one of its hash columns depends on the schema name. A's own `backup_runs` table gains the archive's run record after capture, so B is compared with A as it was at archive time.

**Tests, red on the base and green with the change:**

- `src/infra/database-engine/archive-restore.postgres.test.ts`, new `override` scenario: the archived connection still resolves to the source database and the flag points at a separate recovery database. It checks every store's rows on the recovery server, that the source server gets no `restore_*` namespace, and that the restored config bytes match the archive. On the base, the import goes to the source database and the recovery-server check fails (`relation "restore_….user_profiles" does not exist`). With the change all 5 scenarios pass (the new one takes 7.6 s).
- `src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts`: the flag rejects an invalid name, an unset variable, and a SQLite-only archive before anything is extracted. Red on the base (the restore resolved), green with the change (20 passed).
- `src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts`: `--from` restores forward the flag. Red on the base (`unknown option`), green with the change (4 passed).

Also run: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `git diff --check`. Docs: `docs/cli/backup.md` and `docs/gateway/postgresql.md` describe the flag next to the existing "point that secret at the recovery server" guidance.

**Risk:** low. The flag is opt-in, and the code path without it is unchanged. The override uses the default env secret provider, so an archived config that redefines a provider named `default` with an allowlist would refuse the variable with the usual SecretRef error.

prs.title: perf(ui): reduce blocking while opening chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Chat can block the main thread while its initial visible transcript rows are constructed and measured, even after #194815 separated shell and pane startup. The remaining measurement ladder chains row commits through microtasks. This change lets only the initial multirow tail ladder yield between steps when the browser supports `scheduler.yield()`.

The existing commit lifecycle owns cancellation and completion. Saved-offset restoration, single-row snapshots, message navigation and ordinary geometry callbacks keep their previous microtask timing. The initial transcript remains hidden until complete Markdown and settled positioning are ready. No history, retention, scroll-anchor or sanitizer ownership changes.

A live history update during the new interval exposed a position-rail refresh inside a Solid render computation. Its plain interaction reset remains synchronous; its reactive refresh now waits for settlement. The existing overflow test exercises that owning boundary and was red with the exact CI error before this repair. No test expectations were weakened.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Source | `963de16b208f24f398172db276fba482af98277c` → `1bd78cdf101b462eaec04ec524ebe563410acb9c` |
| UI types, targeted lint/format, diff check | Passed |
| Changed rail + Talk tests | 20/20 passed; strengthened rail regression red before / green after |
| Independent Codex P0–P2 review | Scoped-clean on the complete four-file change |
| Production Knip and production build | Passed |
| Exact-head full CI | [42441225682](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42441225682): success; full UI units, seven E2E shards, both real-Gateway shards |
| Primary performance | 1,800 passing observations: 20 rotated base/head/A-A triplets in 30 cells |
| Fixed replication | 120 passing observations: 20 more triplets for mobile cold 1× and mobile large-open 4× |
| Rich first-visible/scroll proof | 8/8 base/head × desktop/mobile × Chromium/Firefox passed; final PNGs byte-identical to the inspected images below |
| WebKit rich-content probe | Standalone probe stalled before baseline history; no rich-content result claimed. Canonical WebKit performance matrix passed |
| Startup JS normalized gzip / CSS requests | 90,861 → 90,861 B / 1 → 1 |
| Chat JS normalized gzip / requests | 1,295,698 → 1,295,546 B / 20 → 20 |
| Raw Chat JS | 4,175,421 → 4,175,673 B (+252 B); gzip changes include mangling variance, not a byte-optimization claim |
| Strict paired size check | No new violations; no ceiling raised |
| Leases / live state | No Crabbox/Testbox lease; no live Gateway changes |

The two bare-browser cases still fail locally on the final head: appended end-row gap is 1014 px instead of zero; saved-reader placement times out. The same two cases fail on the pinned base, and both pass in exact-head full CI. This is an investigated local/CI discrepancy, not a claimed product repair.

The prior New Session recovery failure coincided with `HEAD /index.html` returning `net::ERR_ABORTED`; the application remained on its error/Retry surface. It was not classified as inherited, no New Session code changed, and the exact-head full CI run passed it. No separate repair is claimed.

## Performance and Targets

The committed `scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts` workload runs production bundles against its synthetic Gateway: 400-message cold/warm boot and a 2,000-message large open, desktop and mobile, serially with rotated base/head/base-control triplets. Chromium runs at 1×, 4× and 6×; WebKit/Firefox at 1×. Hardware: Apple M3 Ultra, 32 logical CPUs, 512 GiB RAM. Host-load samples and all cohorts are retained in the lane artifacts. No local E2E suite or live-provider latency claim.

Acceptance is at least a 5% target longest-task improvement with readiness inside the 5% band and no correctness/boot-CLS regression. Primary Chromium longest-task medians improve 11.1–33.2% across all 18 cells; their p95s also improve. WebKit/Firefox application readiness stays within the band; those engines do not expose equivalent Long Tasks/CPU metrics here. Long Tasks values below 50 ms are censored, never zero work.

The two predefined replications preserve the original cohorts. Mobile cold 1× readiness p95 was +5.10% in the primary cohort, +0.41% in replication, and +4.26% pooled. Mobile large-open 4× readiness improves in the replication and pooled sample. All primary boot CLS measurements are zero where supported. The rich probe's later programmatic mobile scroll records 0.0549179 CLS on both base/head, separately from zero boot CLS; this is not a claim of zero CLS in every interaction.

CPU is not an across-the-board win. Pooled mobile cold 1× script/task medians are +1.13%/+0.84%, while p95s are +6.66%/+5.99%. Pooled mobile large-open 4× script/task medians are +0.21%/−0.11%, while p95s are +7.28%/+5.30%. Neither p95 increase repeats beyond the band in the second cohort; its corresponding changes are +2.51%/+0.36% and −1.41%/+1.46%. The cold replication's paired A/A CPU variability is comparable to the head's, so these measurements do not establish a repeatable CPU regression. The campaign coordinator (automated agent) accepted this CPU-tail tradeoff: pooled p95 increases of 5.30–7.28% in the two mobile cells, approximately flat CPU medians, and fixed second cohorts that did not repeat an increase beyond the band. Acceptance is based on the 11.1–33.2% longest-task median improvement, readiness within the band, unchanged appearance and zero sampled boot CLS. This is coordinator acceptance, not acceptance by Peter. The claim is reduced uninterrupted blocking and preserved readiness, not universal CPU reduction.

| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |

## Alternatives and Limits

The current-main source/trace audit found all 400/2,000 sources normalized, grouped and indexed before the first complete viewport. Ordinary estimates scan 2,200/11,000 lines. Only six desktop/five mobile rows initially mount. In the alternating one-source-per-group fixture, 99.70%/99.75% of the 2,000 sources lie outside that initial range. These are source counts, not CPU percentages, and do not generalize to grouped tool/run rows.

| Order | Owner | Scaling and initial offscreen participation |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | History admission and `chat-thread-build` / `message-normalizer` | O(N + content bytes), all loaded sources; retained-tail reconciliation only when an earlier matching snapshot exists |
| 2 | `chat-thread-grouping` | All-history participant/run/reply attribution and grouping; source/segment caches apply on later updates |
| 3 | `chat-transcript-message-index` and gallery | All rows: identities, revisions, reply/rail/gallery membership and line estimates |
| 4 | Markdown parser/render and DOMPurify | Mounted text/tokens only before reveal; already viewport bounded |
| 5 | Virtualizer geometry | All-row metadata, but actual layout reads only connected active/preparing rows |
| 6 | Transcript mount | Initial visible range, measured one predecessor at a time; this patch splits that ladder inside the transcript owner |

Source-mapped 4× diagnostic samples show normalization 7.4→15.4 ms, grouping 40.8→94.7 ms and projection/index 29.8→57.8 ms when desktop history grows 400→2,000. Markdown 23.3→26.8 ms, sanitizer 43.0→39.8 ms and geometry 150.8→147.6 ms remain largely viewport-bound; transcript mount is 128.8→167.4 ms. These intersecting longest-task samples are diagnostics, not acceptance medians or CPU measurements. The source audit and both 1×/4× attribution tables are in the local lane report.

The independent estimate-deletion experiment improved large-open medians about 10% but left warm tails unresolved, so it does not ship. A standalone canonical normalization/Markdown worker lost end-to-end latency in 600 Chromium observations: 2,000-message normalization cold 11.50/12.10→18.50/19.90 ms; six-message Markdown 23.75/28.80→28.10/32.90 ms. At 100 ms asset delay, Markdown moved 227.15/229.40→333.20/334.00 ms. Token transfer expanded a 0.51 MB input to 4.58 MB and still left sanitization/DOM on main. No new worker ships; this does not rule out a prestarted worker or compact intermediate form.

Full compact-structural-facts plus lazy content preparation was source-audited, not implemented or measured. Blind tail slicing would lose participant attribution, duplicate keys, causal run/reply facts and rail/gallery membership. Actual offscreen DOM measurement was already avoided; the measured change is inside the remaining visible-row ladder.

The primary table reaches 50 ms only for desktop cold at 1× (at median); all 200/300 ms medians remain above target. The separate mobile-cold replication is below the 50 ms Long Tasks threshold, and pooled p95 is 53 ms. There is no proven hard browser floor, nor a demonstrated path to every target. Earlier candidate profiles shifted the peak to pane construction/Details/composer in three of four cold/large cells, with desktop large still grouping/indexing/transcript-bound. Those profiles are not final-head acceptance evidence. The next useful work is compact structural facts/lazy content and decomposition of pane/control construction, not another shell delay.

## Size and Scope

Production LOC: 1,961→1,989 (+38/−10, net +28); existing rail test 715→719. Renderer 433→460, virtualizer host 790→790, rail owner 738→739. The added lines keep the real yielded continuation inside the existing cancellation/settlement contract and preserve old timing for other callers. No dependencies, caches, config, public APIs or size ceilings were added.

Refactor census across touched production: `createEffect`, render effects, `untrack`, direct listeners, DOM queries and `flush` remain 0; owner API 1→1, `onCleanup` 1→1, signals 1→1, `onSettled` 4→5. The sole new settlement callback replaces the render-phase rail refresh. The retained owner API/lifecycle belong to the existing isolated transcript renderer.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): clean scratch databases after gzip output errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge source-manifest snapshots leak their owned scratch SQLite database when gzip output fails. An actual existing output directory ending in `.gz`, or a `.gz` symlink to Linux `/dev/full`, triggers an unhandled destination error and bypasses the caller's existing `finally` cleanup. Related #194615 fixed the distinct gzip input failure; this repairs gzip output.

The existing output owner now uses one awaited stream pipeline, so destination errors propagate back through the existing database-close/scratch-remove owner. It replaces manual pipe/write/finished bookkeeping without introducing a second cleanup path. Stdout is not ended. Manifest format, gzip settings, hash position, persistent schemas and deletion/retention policy are unchanged. This is not a transactional-output rollback feature.

Preserves @zhangguiping-xydt's contributor commit `a1d2eff0e80e0fa589fefbbb1f8fbf937761f661`. Current main was merged before proof. Reused existing snapshot fixtures for output cleanup, newest-observation precedence, and conservative partial-snapshot deletion; retained duplicate-ID and missing gzip-input checks. Removed the allocation file. Production **+17/-29 (net -12)**; tests **+26/-27 (net -1)**.

## Evidence

[Maintainer full built-artifact / filesystem receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194706#issuecomment-6717136735).

Baseline main: `43a197415643b7285989bbe9141ccc2c941a216f`. Secretless Linux Docker **Node 24.22.1**; both versions received frozen installs and full `pnpm build` (only declaration build skipped). Then packed with `npm pack --ignore-scripts` and executed the actual extracted `package/dist/extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/source-manifest.mjs` with Node.

Each real invocation had a dedicated TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP. No injected stream errors, mocked SQLite, forced process termination, or private-helper-only proof.

| Natural snapshot failure | Main, twice | Candidate, twice |
|---|---|---|
| Existing output directory ending `.gz` | exit 1 / EISDIR; leaks owned directory plus 8192-byte SQLite | exit 1 / EISDIR; scratch root empty |
| `.gz` symlink to `/dev/full` | exit 1 / ENOSPC; same leak | exit 1 / ENOSPC; scratch root empty |
| Equivalent plain-output controls | Original errors; scratch roots empty | Identical |

Successful plain, gzip and stdout artifacts are byte-identical across main/candidate, including independently assembled expected protocol bytes. SHA-256: plain/stdout `52599316a361cbd2195623d4fe6ab151a30d0e7f4844b5fb5317c36bc38989ca`; gzip artifact `10b583158676290b417558f195b8726b15030ee381b2990fb95d4f5b06d90782`. The real candidate planner reads candidate gzip against main plain and reports `changed: []`, `unchanged: ["a"]`. Existing destination directories/symlinks are preserved.

Focused suite **3/3 passes on native Node and pinned Bun**. Exact-main output-owner revert on native Node produces **1 failed / 2 passed**, specifically the leaked-scratch assertion. Scoped Oxlint (zero warnings/errors), Oxfmt and Node syntax checks passed. Hosted CI and fresh exact-head ClawSweeper are the final gates.

## Merge Risk / Blast Radius

Confined to Knowledge's standalone snapshot output stream lifecycle. Successful artifact bytes and planner compatibility are proven unchanged. No stored-data rewrite, new dependency, schema/auth/Doctor/update change, model-facing text, or Control UI asset changes. Only per-invocation owned scratch cleanup is restored; pre-existing user output targets are not deleted.

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude Code session limit notice skips rate-limit fallback
prs.body:
Related: #118793

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Claude Code (`claude-cli`) turn fails with the subscription-window notice as its error text, for example `You've hit your session limit · resets 2:50pm (America/New_York)` (also `You've hit your limit · resets 5pm` and `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm`), the failover classifier returns `unknown` instead of `rate_limit`, so an exhausted subscription window is handled like an unexplained failure. Where only the error text is classified, as described in #118793, the classifier returns `null`, the run decision becomes `surface_error`, and the configured fallback chain is never consulted.

## User Impact

User impact: when the notice is the error text, it now counts as a rate limit. The failover decision records `rate_limit` with status 429 instead of no reason, so everything that keys on the reason (the fallback step, auth-profile cooldown where an OpenClaw auth profile exists, reply copy) sees a known, retryable reason. Only the `hit your ... limit ... resets` forms change: `weekly limit` and `monthly limit` were already `rate_limit`, and `You've hit your monthly spend limit` stays `billing` because the billing check still runs first.

What this does not fix:

- Claude Code can also exit with code 1 and print the notice only on stderr. That run error stays `Claude Code process exited with code 1` with no reason, because OpenClaw attaches stderr to the error for display only and deliberately never classifies it (`src/infra/error-diagnostics.ts`). The runtime proof below shows that shape unchanged. Classifying stderr would change that design, so it is not part of this PR.
- The user-facing copy. No copy text changes here; which copy the user sees depends on the path. The known-failure reply (`buildKnownAgentRunFailureReplyPayload`) forwards the notice with its reset time, for example `⚠️ You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`. It forwards the whole CLI error text through the user-facing sanitizer, as it already does for `weekly limit` notices, so other lines that share stderr with the notice are forwarded too (token-like query values are masked). The external-run failure reply (`buildExternalRunFailureReply`) and the saved-history copy (`renderRecordedAssistantFailureCopy`) use the generic rate-limit template, `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.`, which drops the reset time and understates the wait for a multi-hour subscription window. A bounded, reset-aware formatter for these boundaries was suggested in review as a separate follow-up and is not part of this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE` in `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` only knew `daily|weekly|monthly ... limit`, and `ERROR_PATTERNS.rateLimit` knows `usage limit` but neither `session limit` nor the bare `hit your limit · resets` form. Claude Code names the window by its reset time, so the periodic pattern now also accepts `hit your <up to two words> limit ... reset(s)`. The new rows are tagged with provider `claude-cli` in the classification corpus, and the CLI exit-error tests cover both the plain text and the structured `result` record.

## Evidence

Runtime proof on the released CLI (isolated, local, redacted):

- Setup: the published `openclaw@2026.11.1` npm package, run as `openclaw agent --local` with a minimal environment and a fresh state and config directory (`OPENCLAW_PATH_BOOTSTRAPPED=1` keeps the CLI from moving `/usr/bin` ahead of the stand-in on `PATH`). Primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, configured fallback a loopback OpenAI-compatible stub model (`synthetic/fallback-model`). A stand-in `claude` executable answers `--version`, `auth status --json` and the stream-json `initialize` handshake, then fails the user turn with `You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`. No network beyond 127.0.0.1, no real credentials. `before` is the unmodified package; `after` is the same package with only this PR's matcher change applied to its bundled `message-patterns` chunk (diff below), because this host cannot run the full source build. Two turns per run, same results in both turns.
- Notice as the failed `result` record (the shape this PR fixes):
  - before: `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=unknown next=synthetic/fallback-model detail=You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`; structured fields `reason: "unknown"`, no `status`, `fallbackStepFromFailureReason: "unknown"`.
  - after: `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=rate_limit next=synthetic/fallback-model detail=You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`; structured fields `reason: "rate_limit"`, `status: 429`, `fallbackStepFromFailureReason: "rate_limit"`, then `decision=candidate_succeeded ... candidate=synthetic/fallback-model`, and the reply came from the fallback model.
- Notice on stderr with exit code 1 (not changed by this PR): before and after both log `cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli ... error=Claude Code process exited with code 1` followed by `stderr (process-wide; may include earlier turns): You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`, and `decision=candidate_failed ... detail=Claude Code process exited with code 1` with no reason, then the same fallback.

The native Claude login has no OpenClaw auth profile in this setup, so turn 2 tried Claude Code again in both variants and a profile cooldown is not observable here.
- Bundle change used for `after` (2026.11.1 predates the Chinese quota alternatives on main; the added alternative is identical):

  ```diff
  -const PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE = /\b(?:daily|weekly|monthly)(?:\/(?:daily|weekly|monthly))* (?:usage )?limit(?:s)?(?: (?:exhausted|reached|exceeded))?\b/i;
  +const PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE = /\bhit your (?:[\w-]+ ){0,2}limit\b[^\n]{0,40}\bresets?\b|\b(?:daily|weekly|monthly)(?:\/(?:daily|weekly|monthly))* (?:usage )?limit(?:s)?(?: (?:exhausted|reached|exceeded))?\b/i;
  ```

Field data from 2026.11.1 on one host (claude-cli runtime, real Claude Code at its session limit): `model_fallback_decision` events with `decision: "candidate_failed"`, `reason: "unknown"` and `errorPreview: "You've hit your session limit · resets 10:20pm (Europe/Berlin)"` (the result shape this PR fixes), next to `cli terminal failure ... error=Claude Code process exited with code 1` lines whose stderr carries the same notice (the stderr shape this PR does not change). An earlier version of this description presented those stderr lines as fixed by this change; the runtime proof shows they are not.

- Classification corpus (`src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts`), three new rows: without the pattern change `3 failed | 61 passed (64)`, with it `64 passed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/exit-error.test.ts`, two new tests through `createCliExitFailoverError`: without the change `2 failed | 5 passed (7)`, with it `7 passed`.

- `oxlint --type-aware` on the four TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt --check` clean, docs formatting clean, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` clean, line-cap and max-lines ratchets OK.
- User-facing copy on this branch (temporary local vitest probe, not committed; the plain text and the structured `result` record give the same results): `buildKnownAgentRunFailureReplyPayload` returns `⚠️ You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`; `buildExternalRunFailureReply` and `renderRecordedAssistantFailureCopy` return `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.` With an extra stderr line before or after the notice, the known-failure reply forwards that line as well (token value masked); a `weekly limit` notice on the same path behaves the same way.
