prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): define accountless node enrollment
prs.body:
Related: #192352

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an accountless, owner-approved identity and bootstrap contract before they can reach a claw through the OpenClaw ID relay and tunnel.

## User Impact

This PR defines the protocol layer only; it does not yet enable node connectivity in the running product. Nodes get a separate W-only key class, never owner or member privileges. All changes revise the unshipped v1-draft in place.

**Stack dependency:** this now targets `main`. Gateway, Discovery and node-host consumers follow in the implementation stack. A minimal existing Gateway consumer repair refuses accountless member-redemption mail with `audience_mismatch` through the normal settlement/acknowledgment path; valid member handling is unchanged. Test fixtures initialize the new empty draft state and preserve their concrete human-sender types. Full node dispatch, persisted-state initialization and snapshot re-signing remain in the following stack, without adding legacy compatibility readers here.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Owner-signed `NodeInviteCap` plus a proof key registers directly at the Gateway. W-signed `NodeRedemption` proves the invite and becomes pending, admitting nothing.
- Owner/R-signed `add_node` and `remove_node`, denial and peer revocation use the existing membership authority. Nodes have listing seqs, limits, inactivity clocks and pairing-cleanup events; snapshots carry `node_peer_keys`.
- W-signed bearerless Discovery requests can only mail a node redemption before admission; verified admitted nodes can read the descriptor and snapshot. Relay admission includes the new snapshot list.
- Strict fragment-only join links contain only the invite and claw pin/routing fields. `--discovery-url` (or deployment configuration) supplies the separate Discovery origin; clients never infer it from the hostname/relay and never weaken pin verification.

The simplification pass reused owner verification, sequences, invite proof-key derivation, retention, strict schema combinators and signature transport. Node-specific lifetime enforcement leaves member policy unchanged. This remains a protocol stage: Gateway/UI/runtime enforcement follows in the stack.

The owner-reviewed flow now includes a shared six-digit `nodeVerificationCode` bound to the claw, invite, W and signed `NodeDescription`. The terminal and dialog show the same code; the owner compares it and explicitly clicks Approve. Opening the dialog never approves automatically. The signed description declares display name, platform, commands and caps under strict size/count limits; it is retained with pending and approved nodes, but is not standalone authority. First-connect command/capability auto-approval is bounded to subsets of what the owner approved; additions use normal capability approval. Node invite creators default to 10 minutes; registration enforces a strict one-hour maximum.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: independent physical worktree install passed; donor checkout unchanged.
- `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol --maxWorkers=1`: **169 tests / 25 files passed** after the owner-approval UX additions (4.03s Vitest, 7.38s wrapper).
- Targeted strict tsgo of the protocol public barrel and affected protocol tests, plus canonical `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src`: passed, 67 files.
- Package-config boundary lint also passed (66 files) after successful declaration emission; the original Gateway consumer type error is resolved.
- Package format check, docs MDX check, changed-source line-cap ratchet and staged whitespace check: passed.
- Test-line allocation: 565 = original 436 + exactly 40 mailbox regression lines + exactly 89 net description/code/lifetime test lines. Two fixture initialization lines use existing slack; the shared scalar is unchanged. The allocation protects forgery/class-separation and bootstrap boundaries, not test-volume growth for its own sake.
- Existing claw-store and member-profile persistence tests: 8 tests / 2 files passed (89.99s Vitest including 67.5s one-time worker preparation; 96.21s wrapper).
- Mailbox reader: 6 tests passed; new regression failed before the guard and passed after it. Existing callback/acknowledgment tests remain green. Final run: 86.19s Vitest including 80.55s one-time worker preparation, 94.02s wrapper; regression itself 7ms. CI timing is not yet available.
- Deterministic v1-draft JSON regenerated from the vector builder; fixtures test byte-for-byte agreement.
- Independent read-only review found one P2 (Discovery origin absent from link bootstrap). Verified and resolved through the explicit configured-origin/default-and-override contract, preserving the requested link fields. No other verified P0–P2 findings in the original review. A follow-up review of the small consumer repair completed but its result was unavailable; publication proceeds with coordinator approval on the original review and passing affected checks.

Fresh independent read-only review of the UX delta found no verified P0–P2 findings and independently reproduced code vector `168017`. Canonical production types and strict package types (including tests), lint, format, MDX, line caps, test allocation and whitespace checks passed.

Protocol boundary coverage includes forged/wrong-key and mailbox approval refusal, pending-only redemption, owner capability/sequence checks, node/human key separation in both directions, limits, denial, removal events, revocation replay, inactivity, strict links and W-signed request path binding. Deployed Gateway/Discovery enforcement and real tunnel traffic remain named integration gates for the following stack, not claims made by these tests.

Stack conflict repair: rebased onto `90a2c765e10799dce65c5cffc2539b878a46f71a`, preserving both the base’s signed `protocols` and this change’s `node_peer_keys` snapshot fields. Regenerated deterministic vectors; protocol suite, canonical production typecheck, test-line ratchet and whitespace checks passed again. The range-diff contains only the combined snapshot schema context and regenerated signatures.


Combined independent Astra review at `30d3f15ac8bec96419d9641ffb76a587de3ded41`: **no verified P0–P2 findings**. This closes the earlier missing-review gap by covering the accountless member-mail refusal together with all UX additions. Source inspection traced refusal settlement, subsequent-message processing, acknowledgment and cursor persistence; human redemption behavior is unchanged. The reviewer also independently reproduced code `168017`. Existing passing test/type/lint evidence was reused, not rerun by the reviewer. No code changes were required.


Vendor portability follow-up at `84d94f697987e0ed145f7edb3be0edd257080d59`: replaced `URLSearchParams.keys()` iteration with `forEach` pair counting; the existing exactly-once known-field checks still reject duplicates and unknown keys. Added `tsconfig.portable.json` and its documented command, checking package source with ES2023 + DOM and no Node ambient types or DOM.Iterable. ES2022 alone fails on pre-existing Array.toSorted usage; no unrelated array behavior was changed. The local compiler includes iterable DOM declarations, so Discovery/loader vendor builds remain the final consumer-compiler gate. ### November 6 stack rebase

Replayed only the three owned protocol/UX/portability commits onto rewritten base `8f6b45814afd1a3aa6b241a4908ec6c0d7b6504a`. New head: `5eb5e40cdfa31e691fae575a1bd792bc3d9c1758`. ### November 7 main landing candidate

Head `c2a19d6ce7125afa2c3622c38441fc55d6102742`, rebased onto main `f8b1a6ba3d8d7a29fd44529fa3833229e61f6261`; protocol remains v1-draft revised in place. Fresh independent Astra/high full review found one P1: previously persisted linked claws lacked the new unsigned node collections, breaking normal owner reconnect and snapshot publication. Fixed at the existing startup migration boundary before authority is exposed; preserves membership, listing sequences, signed binding/certificates, initializes only missing maps and schedules a newly signed snapshot. Regression reproduced the exact isNode TypeError before the fix and passes afterward. Independent correction review cleared the P1 with no new verified P0–P2 findings.

Validation: protocol **196 tests / 27 files passed**; Gateway OCID consumers **251 passed, 10 skipped / 44 files**; UI protocol consumers **24 / 5 files passed**. After the migration correction, migration/authority/publisher/persistence siblings **30 / 4 files passed**. Portable ES2023+DOM typecheck, canonical `pnpm tsgo:core` (rerun after repair), scoped lint, formatting, seven-document MDX and whitespace checks passed. Test-line ratchet has 30 lines slack with the allocation unchanged; source line-cap ratchet passed for 28 changed source files. Discovery deployment, node runtime/transport/UI and full live tunnel proof remain downstream; the new regression exercises Gateway authority load and local snapshot construction, not live Discovery publication. No main or child branches changed.

PR is ready at d6f0b8f7c9b2d594a44c524adbe52aeec294071b; hosted CI for this head completed successfully (run 42388517226). No inherited failure exception is claimed. Prior native preparation was at c2a19d6ce7125afa2c3622c38441fc55d6102742; review guard and artifacts for the comment-only correction are validated at this exact head (zero findings). No merge has been submitted. The coordinator withdrew the native-CLI merge route: this lane will stop after CI evidence and handoff; Josh will perform the final squash or name an approved writer.


### CI correction (comment-only)

[Run 42387608117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42387608117) at `c2a19d6ce7125afa2c3622c38441fc55d6102742` completed with a PR-caused `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure: the existing node-key SAFETY comment in `authority/allowlist.ts` was above the chain instead of adjacent to the assertion. This is **not an inherited failure**. Commit `d6f0b8f7c9b2d594a44c524adbe52aeec294071b` moves only that comment, without changing executable code. The exact assertion-safety ratchet reproduced red before and passed after; formatting and diff whitespace passed. Existing independent behavior review and focused tests apply to unchanged executable code; new hosted CI completed successfully as recorded below.


### Final CI handoff — November 7

Exact head and pre-squash restacking anchor: `d6f0b8f7c9b2d594a44c524adbe52aeec294071b` on `openclaw-517/node-protocol`. [Hosted CI run 42388517226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42388517226) completed **successfully** at this head, including `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The current combined `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses are **SUCCESS** ([gate publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42389397922)). No inherited failures or exception are claimed. One older PR-context run was cancelled; its successor completed successfully.

Exact-head review artifacts validated with zero findings; the earlier independent behavioral review remains applicable because the final correction only repositions an existing comment. Prior native preparation remains recorded at `c2a19d6ce7125afa2c3622c38441fc55d6102742`, not the final head. This lane has **no merge authority** and has submitted no merge request. Merge remains blocked on an approved writer: Josh handles the final squash or names an approved route. Downstream owners should restack from the full anchor above after the squash; no child branches were changed.


### Review repair and cross-stack evidence — November 8

Current head and restacking anchor: `a1038c7f22c6a92f2fb705df5e3adb4f6b7464f0`. This supersedes the previous final-CI handoff above; that green CI belongs to the prior head. Hosted CI for this head is in progress. Its first two failures (`Scan changed paths (precise)` after opengrep reported 0 findings, and `Select Critical Quality shards`) were GitHub `API rate limit exceeded for installation` errors, not PR-caused; those jobs are being rerun. No merge or child-branch mutation is authorized.

- **P2 mailbox settlement fixed:** unimplemented `node_redemption` now produces an explicit `unsupported` refusal through normal settlement before acknowledgment and cursor persistence. All unhandled kinds use the same fail-closed fallback; neither redemption nor authority submission is invoked. This restores the original mailbox dispatch/settlement intent. Reader-boundary regression reproduced zero refusal callbacks on the old code and passes after repair. Final mailbox/authority run: **16 tests / 2 files passed**, 11.23s Vitest / 18.14s wrapper; node regression 5ms. Two separate real source-Gateway processes proved startup/cold restart, readiness 200, authenticated status/People RPCs, owner/operator-member resolution, inactive-key maintenance, expired-invite sweeping, durable map initialization, preserved signed credentials, and cryptographically verified snapshots delivered to a local HTTP mirror. The consuming Gateway still resolves no node principal, omits W from its tunnel allowlist, rejects token fallback with `openclaw_id_not_admitted`, and creates no pairing.

prs.title: feat: converse through Discord and Signal reactions
prs.body:
Related: #195017

## What Problem This Solves

Authorized Discord and Signal reactions do not reliably reach the conversation agent with their original target context; Signal removals are ignored and retried reaction replies have no durable transport receipt.

## User Impact

Humans can add or remove a reaction to wake the correctly routed conversation once, without needing another text message. Confirmed keyed reaction replies can finish a conversational answer without redundant text. Reactions do not accept task results, grant approval, or clear human gates; existing explicitly bound native approval controls remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the behavior in the maintained channel plugins, reusing existing notification/access policies, routing, ordinary room-event dispatch and durable ingress. Core adds only typed bounded reaction facts and one shared receipt operation over existing plugin-state workers, not a new manager, daemon, schema, tool or configuration option.

Replay protection follows retained ingress tombstones. Outbound receipt namespaces reject new entries at 5,000 rows instead of evicting dedupe evidence. Claimed/uncertain sends never silently retry. Direct unkeyed calls retain their existing non-durable API.

## Evidence

Base: `d59f00281eb02167a86b57c42f04b2b59ed203fe`. Candidate: `ee89da0872a`.

- Real SQLite ingress → actual Discord production handler registration / Signal event handler → ordinary routed dispatch, with only model/provider transport injected: add/remove, exact target text, account/actor/coordinator context, room-event silence, concurrent/replacement-monitor replay, and Signal denied-group/self/sync negatives pass (4 integration cases).
- Real outbound adapters and worker-backed receipts prove concurrent/reopened dedupe, target-key collision refusal, confirmed/uncertain outcomes, interrupted claims and proven-not-sent retry.
- Gateway occurrence/resume tests: 22 pass. Existing message-tool completion and negative controls: 68 pass. Prompt-prefix stability: 14 pass. Discord durable-ingress recovery siblings pass.
- Core/extension/extension-test typechecks, targeted lint/format and SDK export inventory pass. Full build passed before a small equivalent admission-function consolidation; affected boundary tests and typechecks reran afterward.
- Preserved and repaired a Signal fixture options mismatch, and a TypeScript error during admission simplification; neither is presented as a product pass.
- Author simplification removed duplicate message/reaction admission and the test's parallel dispatcher wiring. Necessary growth is two plugin adapters and real-boundary tests; no historical coordination infrastructure was transplanted.

Tracked proof: [`proof/firebed-reactions-fresh-20261107/PROOF.md`](proof/firebed-reactions-fresh-20261107/PROOF.md). SDK API comparison, exact-head CI and independent comprehensive/native review are pending, not claimed clean. No live Discord/Signal/phone delivery, production sends, gateway/config changes or activation was performed. Maintainer review/merge remains required.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

prs.title: docs(browser): explain stale Chromium lock recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/tools/browser/troubleshooting.md` said that a Chromium lock naming another hostname stays unverified, but never
explained how to recover. On macOS with `scutil --get HostName` reporting `not set`, the host can flip between
`<name>.local` and `<name>.<router-domain>`; after that `openclaw browser start` fails with
`Chromium profile lock names another hostname` and the page offered no next step.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a "Recovering from a stale lock" subsection next to that statement, covering exactly what the issue asked for:

- what the lock is — a `SingletonLock` symlink in `<config dir>/browser/<profile>/user-data` whose target is
  `<hostname>-<pid>`, and why OpenClaw ignores it when the hostname differs;
- how to confirm it is stale before deleting anything (`readlink` names the previous hostname and a PID; `ps -p` shows no
  such process; no other browser uses that profile);
- which entries to remove (`SingletonLock`, `SingletonSocket`, `SingletonCookie`) and that profile data — cookies,
  history, logins, preferences — is kept;
- how to prevent recurrence on macOS by pinning `sudo scutil --set HostName <stable-name>` and restarting the browser.

Every claim is checked against the implementation: `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts` reads the lock target as
`<hostname>-<pid>` and returns "Chromium profile lock names another hostname" when the host differs, and the managed
profile directory is `path.join(CONFIG_DIR, "browser", profileName, "user-data")` with the default profile name
`openclaw`.

## User Impact

Docs only; no behavior change. Someone hitting the renamed-host lock now has a safe, ordered recovery instead of a dead end.

## Evidence

- `pnpm format:docs:check` → `Docs formatting clean (1420 files)`.
- `pnpm lint:docs` → `Summary: 0 issues in 0 files`.
- Implementation references cited above are the source of every documented step.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change.

prs.title: fix: accept multiline JSON from streaming providers
prs.body:
Related: #96503, #90205

## What Problem This Solves

Agent turns can fail or retry until timeout when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint returns a pretty-printed JSON completion to a streaming request.

## User Impact

The existing whole-JSON fallback now accepts multiline completions and preserves their reply text and usage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback previously prefixed only the first physical JSON line as SSE data. Prefixing each line lets the SDK reconstruct the complete JSON value. The regression covers LF, CRLF and CR line endings, split chunks, escaped newlines and Unicode.

## Evidence

The source owner ran the reproduction before and after this two-file change using a disposable loopback provider and the real isolated CLI. The rebuilt CLI gives:

| Reply shape | Base | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Compact JSON | `Ready.`, 1 request | `Ready.`, 1 request |
| Pretty-printed JSON | timeout, 7 requests | `Ready.`, 1 request |

Both patched CLI cases report 11 input / 7 output / 18 total tokens. No live model service was called.

- Permanent owner regression: 3 failures / 43 passes on base; 46 passes with the patch.
- Managed and standalone real-client loopback audit: 2 failures / 4 passes on base; 6 passes with the patch.
- Independently reproduced through the owning response-preparation function and installed OpenAI 7.47.0 SSE parser: base fails all three multiline variants; patch accepts all three; compact controls pass on both versions. prs.title: fix(agents): prefer the provider's explicit credential-recovery instruction
prs.body:
Closes #194809

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a provider 401 that states its own credential recovery (OpenCode `api_key_expired`: "Create a new API key in OpenCode Console. Signing in will not renew it.") was answered with the generic `Re-authenticate with: openclaw models auth login --provider … --force` hint — an action the upstream error explicitly rules out, and one that cannot renew a stored API key at all.

## User Impact

User impact: when the classified failure carries an explicit credential-replacement instruction from the provider, the remediation hint surfaces that sentence instead of the re-auth command. Providers without such an instruction keep the existing re-auth hint unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildFailoverRemediationHint` maps `reason: "auth"` to the provider's re-auth command unconditionally. Some credentials are stored API keys, not OAuth logins — for those, the provider's own error text is the actionable recovery. The hint now checks the classified error's raw provider message for an explicit key-replacement instruction and, when present, surfaces that sentence (extracted, length-capped) before falling back to the command.

## Evidence

- Two regressions in `failover-error.test.ts`: an OpenCode-shaped `api_key_expired` failure yields a hint containing the provider's "Create a new API key" sentence and NOT the re-auth command; a control without the instruction keeps the exact existing re-auth hint. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/failover-error.test.ts` — 57/57 passing.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the pre-existing red lanes on current `main` untouched by this diff (`changelog attributions`, and the `dead export scan` flagging `extensions/google/provider-policy.ts`). The 22 added test lines have a matching `config/test-lines-allocations/auth-remediation-provider-instruction.txt` record.
- Not exercised: a live OpenCode provider with an expired key; the classified-failure unit tests stand in.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): keep emoji whole in chat transcript reply quotes
prs.body:
Related: #194697 (independent timestamp-sorting repair in the same exporter).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Knowledge transcript exporter adding U+FFFD to a cross-day reply quote when its existing 80-UTF-16-unit cutoff lands inside an emoji's surrogate pair.

## User Impact

Shortened reply previews end at a code-point boundary instead of introducing a replacement glyph absent from the source. The existing preview cap is unchanged; the affected quote is one UTF-16 unit shorter. Full source messages, retained raw JSONL, ASCII-only quotes, same-day replies and chunk ordering keep their existing bytes and behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone builtin-only skill CLI now backs off by one unit when the cutoff would split a surrogate pair. It keeps the local renderer and its existing budget, without a runtime dependency, SDK export, configuration change or migration. Original contributor commit **be473e4fc7d1** by **SunnyShu0925**, submitted through **@shuisadev**, is preserved.

The added regression is consolidated into the existing real CLI test instead of a duplicate setup-heavy case. Existing thread/mention, Unicode line-separator, UTF-8 header budget and multipart-label assertions remain. Production +7/-1 (net +6); tests +2/-2 (**net 0**); allocation removed. The two documentation lines state the actual UTF-16-unit contract rather than promising 80 code points or whole grapheme clusters.

## Evidence

[Actual built packaged Node CLI comparison and artifact checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194904#issuecomment-6717153491).

- Frozen main43a197415643 once, candidate **5f9672d0093626f3705ce91d62c3093f5cd7d898** once, identical synthetic normalized transcript input, Node24.22.1 Docker.
- 79 ASCII + emoji boundary: main inserts **one U+FFFD**; candidate inserts **none** and ends after 79 ASCII characters.
- ASCII-only quote and 78/80-ASCII + emoji, 41-emoji, short-quote, same-day and no-reply controls remain byte-identical.
- Full previous-day text and raw daily JSONL remain byte-identical; the reply-day text loses only the unwanted replacement glyph. Manifest changes only the affected text hash/byte count.
- Consolidated CLI regression fails on main at the intended quote assertion and passes on candidate. Targeted formatting and typed lint pass.

Exact-head review is **5/6 overall, proof and patch, with no findings**. Two external workflows hit GitHub installation API rate limits; both have independent matching failures on #194964. [Job-level CI receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194904#issuecomment-6717223433).

This is exporter fidelity proof, not live Discord/source acquisition. The unrelated chronology patch in #194697 is not included.

**Merge danger:** two-way door; reverting fully restores the previous renderer without migrating state or changing a public contract. Blast radius is shortened cross-day reply previews in the bundled Knowledge transcript exporter; originals and raw retained rows are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: memory plugin hooks skip CLI-backed turns because they get no memory audience
prs.body:
Fixes #194453

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory plugins skip auto-recall and auto-retain on every turn that runs through a CLI backend such as `claude-cli`, because the turn's plugin hooks receive no memory audience.

## User Impact

User impact: memory plugins that read `ctx.memoryAudience` in `before_prompt_build`, `llm_input`, `llm_output`, `before_agent_run` or `agent_end` now recall and retain on CLI-backed turns the same way they already do on embedded turns, including scheduled (cron) runs that inherit their parent conversation's memory. Plugins that do not use the audience see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI turns resolved a memory audience only for the loopback MCP grant (#173927), so MCP memory tools had one but the turn's hooks did not. The CLI runner now resolves the turn's host-minted audience once during preparation, with the same resolver the grant used, and passes it to every turn hook. The grant reuses that resolution for its own session, so the turn takes one set of leases. The audience carries the same currency guard as on embedded turns, and its leases are released at run end, after the grant is revoked, or immediately if preparation fails.

Preparation admits the run before it resolves that audience. A scheduled run's memory parent is recorded on its admitted run context, and cron hands the CLI runner only a prepared admission, so resolving first would give a parent-linked cron run no audience (and its MCP grant would reuse that empty result). Admission is idempotent: the later admissions in the same preparation get the same context back.

Like embedded turns, a hook that is still running after the run ends (for example an asynchronous `agent_end`) sees `assertMemoryAudienceCurrent()` throw "released". That matches the documented rule that an audience is invalidated when the run that owns it ends.

The embedded runner now builds its hook audience fields with `buildAgentHookMemoryAudienceFields`, the helper CLI turns use, as suggested in review (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194454#pullrequestreview-5815589513). Before, it carried its own copy of the session check and the audience/guard pairing, so a later change to that rule would have had to land in both runners. One observable detail: when an embedded turn has no memory audience, the hook context now omits `memoryAudience` and `assertMemoryAudienceCurrent` instead of carrying them as `undefined`, the same as CLI turns. Only code that tells an absent key apart from an `undefined` one could notice; no bundled plugin or core caller does, and every embedded call site spreads the builder first.

## Evidence

### Live claude-cli turns through a real memory provider

These runs were measured on 942dfab0df7, before the scheduled-run follow-up (924f3cd69c9). The follow-up only admits the run earlier in preparation. Admission does not change the audience of a turn that is not scheduled: the resolver reads the admitted context only to find a scheduled run's parent. The unit tests for these turns pass on the new head (see Tests).

Setup, same for both runs: macOS, a Gateway built from the commit under test, loopback only, isolated state dir and config, channels off, model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`. Memory slot: `hindsight-native` (`@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight` 0.1.2 from ClawHub, `memoryMode: context`, so recall comes only from the `before_prompt_build` hook) against a local Hindsight server, with a throwaway bank that is deleted at the end.

Turns:

1. Owner turn 1 on an operator-created session (`sessions.create`, then `openclaw agent --session-key`): "Please remember this for later: my launch city is Lisbon and my launch code word is PERIWINKLE-XXXX."
2. Owner turn 2, same session: "What is my launch code word?"
3. Conversation turn: the same question sent with `chat.send` on a new session, which the host resolves to a `conversation` audience.

A second test plugin records what each hook receives and traces every request to the Hindsight API by bank. It also calls the host memory provider (`getActiveMemoryProvider` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-host-search`, the path the bundled `active-memory` and `memory-wiki` plugins use) in these ways:

- S1: an operator read, to show the call path works.
- S2: an audience object that the host did not mint.
- A4: the turn's own audience in its own session.
- M1: the conversation turn's audience presented with the owner session key.
- M2: the owner turn's audience presented with the conversation session key.
- C1 and C2: it keeps the `agent_end` ctx and, 15 s after the run ends, calls the kept `ctx.assertMemoryAudienceCurrent()` and opens the provider with the kept audience.

Branch 942dfab0df7:

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits (#187911)
prs.body:
Closes #187911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: guest tasks become permanently stranded or fail after concurrent managed-workspace edits because conflict reconciliation lacks safe inspection boundaries, falsely flags Markdown setext headers as conflict markers, permits directory ancestor symlink escapes, wipes unmutated CAS baseline files during partial reconciliation, and overwrites live guest divergence during background task execution.

## User Impact

User impact: operators and guest tasks can cleanly inspect conflicted drafts and resolve concurrent workspace modifications via `sessions.files.set` or direct worktree writes without risk of directory traversal through symlinked ancestors, data loss of unmutated CAS baseline files, or live guest divergence being clobbered during reconciliation.

## Why This Change Was Made

In strict alignment with the Product Owner Architectural Decisions on Config and State Defect Lifecycle (`config-state-lifecycle.md`):

1. **Preventative Preservation**:
   - **CAS Baseline Overlay Invariant**: Incremental checkpoints contain only inspected paths. `commitLocalWorkspaceReconciliation` parses the full CAS baseline manifest (`baselineDocument`) and overlays ONLY the explicitly resolved canonical paths (`resolvedSet.has(resolvedEntry.path)`), leaving unmutated files (e.g. `other.txt`), directory structures, and metadata byte-for-byte intact.
   - **Live Guest Divergence Preservation**: Inspects live projection nodes across all node types (`file` with sha256 and mode, `symlink` with target, `directory`, and `missing`). If a background process in the guest projection makes newer edits (such as creating a symlink or modifying mode), reconciliation detects divergence, preserves live guest nodes, retains prior conflict records, and merges only non-diverged resolved paths.
2. **Action Observability & Security Boundaries**:
   - **Symlinked Ancestor Containment**: Before directory creation or file synchronization, `synchronizeResolvedCanonicalPaths` inspects all ancestor segments from `realProjectionRoot` to the destination directory using `resolvePathViaExistingAncestorSync` and `fs.lstat`. Throws immediately if an ancestor directory component escapes the projection root or is a symlink.
   - **Authoritative Operator Acceptance**: In `workspace-reconcile-preflight.ts`, explicit operator acceptance (`params.acknowledgedPaths` or `params.resolvedPaths`) is authoritative (`const isResolved = isExplicitlyAccepted;`), eliminating false conflict marker rejections on legitimate Markdown setext headers (`Handover\n=======\n`).
   - **Authorized Read Boundary**: `prepareSessionFileReadPath` exposes retained guest projection drafts through `runtimeWorkspaceDir` only for active retained conflicts (`relative in projectionConflicts`), safely serving canonical files for non-conflicted paths.

## Evidence

### 1. Real-World Behavior Proof (`verify-revision-3-proof.ts`)
```
=== OpenClaw Issue #187911: Revision 3 Verification Proof ===

[Scenario 1] Markdown setext separator accepted and resolved cleanly
  ✓ Setext header with '=====' accepted via explicit acknowledgment without false conflict marker rejection.

[Scenario 2] Refusal when an ancestor directory component is a symlink
  ✓ Successfully blocked symlinked ancestor escape: "Resolved path directory escapes projection root: sub/target.txt"
  ✓ Successfully blocked internal ancestor symlink: "Resolved path directory ancestor is a symlink: sub_internal/file.txt"

[Scenario 3] Overlay resolved paths onto complete accepted CAS baseline
  ✓ Complete CAS baseline overlay successfully preserved untouched 'other.txt' alongside updated 'conflict.txt'.

[Scenario 4] Live guest symlink divergence detected and preserved
  ✓ Guest symlink divergence detected; live guest symlink safely preserved without overwrite.

==================================================
ALL 4 REVISION 3 PROOF SCENARIOS PASSED 100% GREEN
==================================================
```

### 2. Full Vitest Test Suites
- **`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.conflict.test.ts` (11/11 PASSED)**:
```
 ✓ retains completed partial resolutions while other conflicts remain across retries (Finding 4)
 ✓ preserves checkpoint format for receipts without initial checkpoint_json (Finding 5)
 ✓ excludes unadmitted host-only files (.env.local) from entering the projection (Finding 1)
 ✓ replaces projection symlinks safely without following destination links (Finding 2)
 ✓ overlays resolved paths onto complete accepted baseline preserving unmutated baseline entries (Finding 3)
 ✓ preserves newer guest divergence in projection if edited while conflict is pending (Finding 5)
 ✓ allows explicitly accepted Markdown separator lines (Revision 3 Finding 1)
 ✓ refuses to resolve when an ancestor directory component is a symlink (Revision 3 Finding 2)
 ✓ preserves live guest symlink divergence across retries (Revision 3 Finding 4)
 Tests: 11 passed (11)
 Duration: 36.96s
```

- **`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts` (9/9 PASSED)**:
```
 ✓ allows inspecting canonical files when the managed workspace has a preserved conflict
 ✓ acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict
 Tests: 9 passed (9)
 Duration: 75.68s
```

### 3. Safety Ratchets & Code Hygiene
- `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base upstream/main`:
  `Line-cap ratchet OK: 14 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`
- `pnpm oxlint`: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.`
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`: `All matched files use the correct format.`

prs.title: fix(skills): accept comments on description continuation lines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes skill validation and packaging rejecting valid multiline descriptions when PyYAML is unavailable and a continuation line ends with a YAML comment.

For example, this description incorrectly fails with `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`:

```yaml
description: Summarize reports
  for teams. # <internal notes>
```

## User Impact

Skill authors can validate and package these descriptions without installing PyYAML or removing comments. Long continuation comments also no longer count toward the description length limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing fallback parser already removes comments on the initial scalar line. Apply the same distinction to indented content: preserve quoted and block-scalar text, and strip comments from plain continuations. Quotes appearing within an already-started plain scalar remain literal text.

Related: #194653 (merged initial-line comment handling). A bounded issue/PR search found no open fix for this continuation path. This does not change runtime skill loading or extend the fallback into a full YAML parser.

Simplification retained the existing parser owner and test table: **6 production lines and 6 test lines added**, with no new helper, dependency, configuration, or shared budget change. Python tests are outside the test-line ratchet's counted patterns.

## Evidence

- **Real CLI before/after:** Python 3.11.10 in secretless Linux Docker, no network, 256 MiB memory, 0.5 CPU, non-root. Invoked the documented `quick_validate.py` and its `package_skill.py` consumer with `python3 -S` and actual temporary skill directories. On base `43a197415643b7285989bbe9141ccc2c941a216f`, valid plain continuations, descriptions starting on an indented line, and long trailing comments all exit 1 from both commands. prs.title: fix(memory): avoid owner errors for configured dreaming workspaces
prs.body:
Closes #149215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dreaming workspace enumeration throws `AgentSelectionRequiredError` for an already-configured primary workspace when an explicit multi-agent roster has no default owner.

## User Impact

Callers can include a workspace whose owners are already recorded without inventing a default agent or repeating an owner. Explicit owner associations still work; an unknown workspace still requires an owner.

This fixes workspace enumeration, not the separate long-running model-call or fleet-starvation symptoms in #147157.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Reuse the canonical workspace entry before resolving an unnecessary default owner.

### Root Cause

`resolveMemoryDreamingWorkspaces` builds the roster's workspace-owner map, but the old final primary-workspace branch resolves a default agent before checking whether the workspace is already known. That lookup throws in an explicit roster without a default owner.

### Changes

- Normalize the optional primary owner with the existing normalizer.
- Retain known canonical workspace entries when no additional owner was requested.
- Preserve explicit associations and unknown-workspace rejection.
- Keep the regression alongside current main's compact test fixtures.

## Evidence

### Current integration: October 27, 2026

Head: `113c86276d7a7972081c4d8532b7ee40b3e9bb39`.

Merged current main `3bf38f77227c8b7e82e9df23be8db95ccdf14b4b` without rewriting contributor ancestry. The verified conflict was confined to `dreaming.test.ts`; the resolution keeps upstream's consolidated coverage and the existing known-primary-owner regression. The production repair is unchanged.

The first refresh exposed the global test-line ratchet: main was already above its ceiling, and a separate regression fixture added 34 lines. The follow-up reuses one workspace fixture for all existing assertions plus the regression, making this PR's tests one line smaller than main. No assertions, baselines, or production behavior were weakened.

### Real Behavior Proof

The retained before/after capture used the supported built CLI and a synthetic plugin importing the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-status` API. Each run used isolated real configuration, five existing workspace directories, explicit ownership, and no default/system agent. The resolver was not mocked.

Command: `pnpm openclaw workspace-proof --agent primary`.

| Source | Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main `ca7c90068054dae7378d9d3bef42f11823bc1212` | Roster-only control | Exit 0; five workspaces and configured owners |
| Same main | Already-configured primary workspace, owner omitted | `AgentSelectionRequiredError`; exit 1 |

| Repaired tree `45398ad44ce03a2bca697b6f5f479d0e75895898` | Owner omitted or whitespace-only | Exit 0; five workspaces and unchanged owners |

```text

CLI_PROOF_EXIT 0
```

These are historical real-CLI captures of the retained repair, not new CLI runs on the integration head. Earlier main and repaired builds passed. No live dreaming/model run is claimed.

### Test

On the integration tree, Node 24.22.1 and repository-pinned development tools:

- `pnpm test src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 10 passed; 7.13 seconds including transform/startup. The corresponding exact-head CI test lanes also pass.

The original owner regression was observed red before the fix. It covers omitted/null/blank owners, canonical paths and symlink aliases, explicit additional associations, and unknown-workspace rejection.

CI for `113c86276d7a7972081c4d8532b7ee40b3e9bb39` is green: run `40508107864` passed the baseline ratchets, production/test types, lint, selected tests, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. prs.title: fix(tasks): recompute terminal retention after lost-task recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a task loses its backing session, maintenance marks it `lost` and stamps the
short 24-hour lost-window retention (`cleanupAfter = lostAt + 24h`). When the
durable ledger later records a real terminal result, maintenance recovers the task
to `succeeded`/`failed` but never recomputes `cleanupAfter`, so the recovered
record keeps `lostAt + 24h` instead of the standard 7-day terminal retention from
its actual `endedAt`. If recovery happens more than 24h after the lost-mark
(Gateway down overnight, long-running job), the recovered terminal record is
pruned on the very next sweep — the user never sees the recovered outcome,
defeating the recovery feature's purpose of preserving finished work across
Gateway restarts (#145940). Even on quick recovery, the record gets only the
remainder of the short lost window instead of the documented 7-day terminal
retention (#126063, #126095).

## Why This Change Was Made

The defect is in `applyTaskRecordPatch` (`src/tasks/task-registry-records.ts`),
the lifecycle owner that stamps `cleanupAfter` for terminal records: it only
recomputed when `cleanupAfter` was missing, so the numeric lost-window value
survived a `lost` → terminal transition. Recovery paths (`markTaskRecovered` /
`projectTaskRecovered` in `src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts`) also
preserved the numeric value.

The fix recomputes the terminal retention whenever a terminal status is reached
from `lost`, and makes the `projectTaskRecovered` projection always recompute.
The invariant: the short lost-window retention applies only while the record is
still `lost`; once recovered, the standard terminal retention from the recovered
`endedAt` applies. Files changed: `src/tasks/task-registry-records.ts` and
`src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts` (fix), `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts`
and the `test/fixtures/task-registry-recovery-restart.ts` fixture (regression
tests). No new dependencies, configuration options, or schema changes.

## Review-followup fixes

- **Exclude unchanged `lost` status from the recovery predicate (P2).**
  `isTerminalTaskStatus("lost")` is true, so the recovery recompute also ran when
  a still-`lost` record received a metadata-only or cleanup-only update
  (e.g. `setTaskCleanupAfterById`), silently replacing the explicit deadline the
  retention owner honors with `endedAt + 24h`. The predicate now requires a
  *different* terminal status (`next.status !== "lost"`): only a real recovery
  recomputes, and a still-`lost` record keeps its existing deadline. A regression
  test ("preserves an explicit lost-task deadline on a cleanup-only update")
  covers this: it fails on the pre-fix predicate (deadline 45260000 replaced by
  88400000) and passes with the fix.
- **Prove persistence across real OS process restarts, not just reload (proof
  followup).** The previous proof reloaded the registry from SQLite inside one
  process, which is not independent proof of an operating-system process
  restart. The committed subprocess regression test now spawns the fixture as
  three genuinely separate OS processes (`node --import tsx`, distinct PIDs)
  sharing one SQLite state dir: seed → recover → verify, then the parent reloads
  and runs the next sweep. The corrected deadline demonstrably survives real
  process restarts, and the next sweep keeps the recovered record.

## User Impact

Recovered terminal cron tasks now keep the documented 7-day retention from their
recovered end time, so their outcome stays visible in task history instead of
being pruned shortly after recovery. Tasks that are never lost are unchanged;
`lost` records still use the 24-hour window (and still honor an earlier explicit
lost-task deadline).

## Evidence

- **OS-process-restart recovery proof (before/after).** The real task-registry
  module chain runs against one real SQLite state dir across three genuinely
  separate OS processes (each a distinct `node --import tsx` child), so
  persistence is proven across real process restarts — the same boundary a
  Gateway restart crosses — not just an in-process registry reload. A lost cron
  task whose 24h lost-window deadline has already expired is written by process
  1, recovered by process 2, and read + swept by process 3. Timestamps and PIDs
  are redacted below; each phase printed from a distinct process.

  **Before (pre-fix source):** recovery keeps the expired lost-window deadline,
  so the very next sweep prunes the recovered record (`pruned: 1`,
  `still-present: false`) — the recovered outcome is lost.

  ```
  [seed]    seeded lost task: status=lost cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-17T05:41:39.953Z) expired=true
  [recover] reload saw: status=lost cleanupAfter=... stale-expired=true
  [recover] recovered: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... corrected-in-future=false corrected=false
  [sweep]   reload saw: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... preserved-across-restart=false
  [sweep]   sweep: maintenance={"reconciled":0,"recovered":0,"cleanupStamped":0,"pruned":1} still-present=false
  ```

  **After (fixed source):** recovery restores the standard 7-day terminal
  retention from the recovered `endedAt`; the corrected deadline survives all
  three process restarts and the next sweep keeps the record
  (`pruned: 0`, `still-present: true`).

  ```
  [seed]    seeded lost task: status=lost cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-17T05:42:28.485Z) expired=true
  [recover] reload saw: status=lost cleanupAfter=... stale-expired=true
  [recover] recovered: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-23T15:42:38.378Z) corrected-in-future=true corrected=true
  [sweep]   reload saw: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... preserved-across-restart=true
  [sweep]   sweep: maintenance={"reconciled":0,"recovered":0,"cleanupStamped":0,"pruned":0} still-present=true
  ```

  `RESULT: PASS` — the corrected deadline survived 3 real process restarts and
  the recovered record is not pruned. The before/after traces are from the same
  script and state dir; the only difference is the two fixed source files.

- **Subprocess regression test (committed).** The same OS-process-restart flow is
  committed as a real persisted-SQLite regression test in
  `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts` ("persists the corrected deadline
  across real OS process restarts and survives the next sweep"). It spawns the
  fixture `test/fixtures/task-registry-recovery-restart.ts` three times via
  `node --import tsx` (seed → recover → verify) against one
  `withOpenClawTestState` state dir, then reloads and runs the next maintenance
  sweep in the parent. On the pre-fix source this test fails
  (`expected <expired lost-window deadline> to be greater than <now>`); with the
  fix it passes.

- **Regression tests** in `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts`:
  - a `lost` record with the short lost-window `cleanupAfter` is recovered via
    `markTaskTerminalById({ status: "succeeded", ... })`; the recovered record's
    `cleanupAfter` equals the standard terminal retention from the recovered
    `endedAt` and is greater than the stale lost-window value (fails on the
    original code, passes with the fix);
  - a still-`lost` record keeps an explicit deadline on a cleanup-only update
    (P2 followup, fails on the pre-fix predicate);
  - the reload + next-sweep proof (fails on the PR base);
  - the OS-process-restart proof above (fails on the pre-fix source).
- Existing suites pass locally: `task-registry.store.test.ts` (59),
  `task-registry-records.test.ts`, `task-retention.test.ts`,
  `task-registry.maintenance-projection.test.ts`. `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`
  clean.
- Production LOC delta: net +4 — no new dependencies, config, protocol, or schema.
- AI-assisted: yes

prs.title: fix(exec): report a run with no captured exit code as failed, not completed
prs.body:
Related: #146426

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a command whose supervised process terminates without ever reporting an exit code is recorded as a successful exit-0 completion, so a run that never produced a status surfaces as success instead of a failure.

## User Impact

Runs that end without a captured exit code now report failed, with the reason shown to the user, and automation reading the exec outcome no longer sees a false success for them. Commands that do report a code — including signal and timeout paths — are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildExecExitOutcome` coerced a null exit code to `0` and still treated the record as a normal exit, so a run that never produced a status took the completed branch: `status: "completed"`, `exitCode: 0`, no failure reason, and an `exec.process.completed outcome:completed` diagnostic.

A null code is not evidence of success. `RunExit.exitCode` is nullable by contract. The outcome now takes the existing failure path, which already classifies this shape as `aborted` and renders "Command aborted before exit code was captured" — so the null is preserved rather than replaced by a sentinel.

This covers the three points in the issue's proposed change: (1) a null code is no longer success, (2) the null is preserved in the payload — the failed branch already returns `exitCode: params.exit.exitCode`, and (3) the regression test asserts the null code survives.

Scope note: a process killed by a signal is unaffected. Signal kills arrive as `reason: "signal"` with a null `exitCode`, which never took the completed branch. This fix is specifically the `reason: "exit"` record that never captured a code.

Non-goals: the supervisor's reason vocabulary and the signal/timeout classifications are untouched. No new config, protocol, or persistence surface.

## Evidence

The current repair is synchronized with main `b546280f5b53b5509b8ed8c2032acc32ed0bf0e0`, which had moved the classifier into `bash-tools.exec-output.ts` but still classified an unknown exit code as success. The conflict resolution preserves that extraction and moves the original captured-code guard to the existing `buildExecExitOutcome` owner. The submitted change remains two files: the guard and its foreground regression. Current local head is `2866e4414f2cc1bab920b14c85aca39a7161a2ab`.

Current validation on this synchronized source:

- **Red:** with the exact main classifier bytes and the ported regression, the focused test fails because the caller receives `(no output)` instead of `Command aborted before exit code was captured` (1 failed, 11 skipped). Restoring the captured-code guard makes the complete owning foreground suite pass **12/12**. The existing supervisor fixture supplies only the raw nullable exit tuple; the real tool/runtime/output path computes the asserted failed/null/aborted outcome.
- The runtime consumer suite passes **18/18**, covering ordinary captured exit status, timeout/signal handling and outcome delivery through the same owner.
- The current process/session E2E file passes **8/8** with real child processes. Its controls include post-exit finalizer failure, timeout after a clean child exit, quiet successful and nonzero exits, and interactive cancellation. These are local consumer controls, not a fresh Linux null-trigger reproduction.
- Repository `oxfmt` check and type-aware `run-oxlint` pass on both changed files; the complete submitted range also passes `git diff --check`. The ordinary E2E preparation completed before the 8/8 result. No separate repository-wide typecheck or aggregate check result is claimed.

The owning-file cost measurement was one `pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` run: 31.86 s command wall time, including compiled-worker preparation, and 4.51 s Vitest duration. Hosted CI duration for the synchronized head is not available until it is published. An earlier process-suite attempt failed during build preparation with ENOSPC before running tests; its logs remain recorded as setup failure, and the later successful 8/8 run supplies the consumer result.

Prior-head CI attribution for the [October 10 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148807#issuecomment-5675382048) is retained separately. The five notification cases that failed in the older `checks-node-changed-2` observation later passed in [the immutable Linux/Bun process/session job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338150948/job/118353210606), whose complete process file passed **12/12**. The cases cover post-exit finalizer failure, clean-exit timeout, quiet successful/nonzero completion wakes, and acknowledging the terminal notify-on-exit poll. The [separate foreground job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338150948/job/118353210631) passed **10/10**, including the nullable-exit regression.

Those hosted jobs ran CI merge `c5e83abc96e7c65ae93bdb15c6718c9618f37720`, with parents base `2d305eb2061955123f799c97c108ea8718fba392` and prior PR head `34664c114b9b5d18d83568efa7d129299a33f879`. The merge and prior head share exact tree `3252b0ace59ee5e882c77c3168c5947dd6ce8c80`; archived qualification preserves checkout facts, named cases and immutable log hashes. These jobs supersede the old failing-check observation for that prior source. They do not prove individual historical causes, a base/reverted-classifier experiment, or Linux execution of the newly synchronized head.

The original author's Linux relay/anchor null-trigger observations below remain historical. Their archive has no independent Linux native receipt or exact execution commit. The separate historical Darwin supervisor receipt covers ordinary stdout/UTF8 controls; it does not reproduce the null-trigger. This macOS run supplies current classifier and real-process consumer coverage, but no new Linux `/proc`, installed-service, Windows, channel, or Gateway evidence. Gateway proof is not applicable to this local exec classification change.

<details>
<summary>Original historical evidence (original source/platform bindings retained)</summary>

The following original observations and failures are historical, not re-labelled as current execution.


### A real run reaches this record on Linux — no stub anywhere in the chain

The producer is OpenClaw's own service-child relay host. On non-Windows, `createChildAdapter` takes that path whenever the run owns its process tree or `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER` is set (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts:150-154`), which is the path a non-PTY exec under an installed service is supervised through.

The trigger: an anchor that loses host-side authority while the command is still alive and outlives the graceful-cancel window.

1. exec starts `/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c 'trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done'` — a command that ignores SIGTERM.
2. The anchor process receives SIGTERM out of band. The host never calls `kill()`, so its `requestedSignal` stays unset.
3. The anchor's own handler runs `requestCleanup("parent-lost")` and signals its process group; the command ignores it.
4. The 5 s `GRACEFUL_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_MS` grace expires with no root result, so `closeAuthority(reason, hardKill=true)` runs `process.kill(0, "SIGKILL")`. The anchor and the command die together, before any `root-result` is sent.
5. The host sees the closing receipt and observes the group's disappearance (`ESRCH`) with no root result, so `finishAuthorityClose` closes authority as `rootResult = { code: null, signal: requestedSignal ?? null }` → `{ code: null, signal: null }`.
6. The supervisor maps that record to `reason: "exit"`, `exitCode: null` — exactly what `buildExecExitOutcome` receives.

Both rows below are real processes: the real supervisor, the real relay host, a real anchor, and the real `runExecProcess` entry point. Nothing is stubbed, mocked, or injected, and the teardown is a real signal to a real process.

| Step | Observed |
|---|---|
| Real supervisor + relay host + SIGTERM-ignoring command | `RunExit { reason: "exit", exitCode: null, exitSignal: null }` |
| Same teardown at `runExecProcess` **before** this change | `status: "completed", exitCode: 0` — 3/3 runs |
| Same teardown at `runExecProcess` **after** this change | `status: "failed", exitCode: null, failureKind: "aborted", reason: "Command aborted before exit code was captured"` — 3/3 runs |

Repeated runs of the identical probe are stable in both directions: 3/3 `completed` with `exitCode: 0` before the change, 3/3 `failed` with `exitCode: null` after it.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction (scratch probe, run from the repository root; not part of the change)</summary>

```ts
// tmp-probe.mts — real runExecProcess, real supervisor, real anchor
import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { runExecProcess } from "./src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.js";

const PROGRAM = 'trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done';

function ppidOf(pid: number): number {
  try {
    const match = /^PPid:\s+(\d+)$/m.exec(readFileSync(`/proc/${pid}/status`, "utf8"));
    return match ? Number(match[1]) : -1;
  } catch {
    return -1;
  }
}

// Our own anchor only: anchor -> relay -> this probe.
function findAnchorPid(): number | undefined {
  for (const entry of readdirSync("/proc")) {
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(entry)) continue;
    const pid = Number(entry);
    if (pid === process.pid) continue;
    try {
      if (!readFileSync(`/proc/${entry}/cmdline`, "utf8").includes("service-child-group-anchor")) {
        continue;
      }
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (ppidOf(ppidOf(pid)) === process.pid) return pid;
  }
  return undefined;
}

const handle = await runExecProcess({
  // exec runs this as the `-c` program of its own shell, so that shell is the
  // root process and it ignores SIGTERM itself.
  command: PROGRAM,
  workdir: "/tmp",
  env: { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? "" },
  usePty: false,
  warnings: [],
  maxOutput: 100_000,
  pendingMaxOutput: 100_000,
  notifyOnExit: false,
  timeoutSec: null,
});

const deadline = Date.now() + 15_000;
let anchorPid: number | undefined;
while (anchorPid === undefined && Date.now() < deadline) {
  anchorPid = findAnchorPid();
  if (anchorPid === undefined) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 25));
}
if (anchorPid === undefined) throw new Error("anchor process never appeared");
process.kill(anchorPid, "SIGTERM");
console.log(JSON.stringify(await handle.promise, null, 2));
```

```bash
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw pnpm tsx tmp-probe.mts
```

Same real entry point, no signal interference, after the change:

Before the fix it failed as `expected { status: 'completed', exitCode: 0 } to match { status: 'failed', exitCode: null }`.

### What was not tested

- No Windows host was available. The relay-host closure above is now reproduced on Linux; the Windows job-object hard-kill path (`useWindowsJobAnchor`) is still unexercised, and it is the likeliest other producer of this record.
- The last settle that can still carry a null code is unreachable by construction, not untested: the PTY adapter's `dispose()` settle is a no-op because the supervisor disposes only after that adapter's `wait()` has already resolved, and `settleWait` ignores a second settlement.
- The reproduction above constructs the trigger deliberately (out-of-band SIGTERM to the anchor plus a command that ignores SIGTERM) rather than waiting for it to happen in the field; it exercises real shipped code, but no production incident was captured.
- No live channel or Gateway proof: the change is local to exec outcome classification.

## Historical prior revision only: merge conflict resolved and validation refreshed

This revision resolves the merge conflict against `main` that ClawSweeper recorded as the only
remaining item, and re-runs the focused exec validation on the resulting head.

The branch was rebased onto current `main`. The only content conflict was in
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts`, where `main` had in the meantime moved the

branch's test used. The conflicted region was therefore taken from `main` and the regression test was
re-expressed in the current idiom with the same assertions — `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`,
`failureKind: "aborted"`, `exitReason: "exit"`, and the reason text

prs.title: test(cross-os): prove the replacement-port retry without reclaiming the port
prs.body:
Fixes #194926

## What Problem This Solves

The `reported-refusal` case in `test/scripts/cross-os-release-gateway-startup.test.ts` failed with `EADDRINUSE` on a released ephemeral port (CI run linked in the issue).

The recovery path reserves a replacement port for the lane, persists it, and releases the reservation in its `finally` (`reserveGatewayPortForLane` → `reservation.release()`). The test then re-bound that exact port to prove it was free — an unowned interval: between the release and the test's bind, the OS allocator may hand the port to any other socket. The test mocks the Gateway process, so nothing legitimately holds the port; the collision is a harness flake, not a behavioural bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reclaiming a port the test does not own cannot be made deterministic. The release-check helper already writes its own record when it retries:

```text
[release-checks] Gateway refused port <old>; retrying once on port <replacement>.
```

That line is appended only after the config write succeeds and before the reservation is released, so asserting it proves the retry happened with the replacement port while keeping every existing assertion (launch sequence, `configWrites`, persisted config, old != new port). The racy re-bind is removed.

## Evidence

`test/scripts/cross-os-release-gateway-startup.test.ts` — 10/10 cases pass, and ten consecutive runs of the file pass with the same result:

```text
$ for i in $(seq 1 10); do vitest run test/scripts/cross-os-release-gateway-startup.test.ts; done
runs: pass=10 fail=0
```

The original failure is preserved by the issue's CI link; this change removes the failing operation instead of replaying it.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silently missing Muse tool activity and optimistic replay metadata when activity-page recovery fails after a native turn completes.

## User Impact

A completed answer remains available, with one System warning through the existing notice stream and an operator warning explaining that activity history is incomplete. The warning now says, “Verify the task's result before repeating it.” Missing activity conservatively reports `replaySafe:false` / `hadPotentialSideEffects:true`.

The [published native review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194984#issuecomment-6716979381) P3 next-action finding is resolved in source. Its separate shipped-entry behavior-proof hold remains open; no new E2E/native-provider proof or manual native re-review is claimed.

[Prior-head CI run 42443241161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42443241161) completed successfully on `13d5ac5ba1e3a9f5b870314efa7ad503e98c3d77`, including `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `openclaw/ci-gate`. That is prior-head evidence. [Current-head CI run 42445933963](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42445933963) completed successfully on `5ca66ceeeb4185135eff5a45812fb37e8f17334e`; the separate shipped-entry and comprehensive-review holds remain open. The earlier local test-line check on the pinned standalone base remains **failed** by 48 lines of existing debt; that historical result is preserved without a waiver or an inferred cause for the CI difference. No live provider/UI or automatic-retry behavior is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK owns whether its settled view is current. Capture that fact once, before authority revalidation or reporting can throw, then use the existing notice/logger and replay-metadata mechanisms. Keep prior conservative metadata conditions, transcript decisions, native terminal semantics and pooled-host lifetime. Lost authority still rejects reporting.

The small completeness sibling keeps the harness within its existing line cap. The dedicated conformant peer exercises real SDK paging, exact SourceRange provenance and one independently witnessed append. It adds no retry, recovery execution, SDK/schema or permission-policy change.

[Coordination with #183676](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183676#issuecomment-6716201901): that PR owns observation/approval/result-projector extraction; its moved projector will need reconciliation with this guard. #178837 owns streamed prefixes. Neither branch is imported or modified here; no owner consent is claimed.

## Evidence

- Maintained regression RED on unchanged base production: 3 failed / 3 passed. The added authority regression also reproduced the review finding on the previous candidate: 2 failed / 6 passed, before the snapshot-order repair. All provenance/effect assertions precede the target failures; no setup or timeout failure in either maintained RED.
- The original unchanged five diagnostic controls passed **5/5** on prior producer head `13d5ac5ba1e3a9f5b870314efa7ad503e98c3d77` / tree `3b9ab1dae3e079eebe327970161bcaac62a0b2b7`. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An explicit `allow: []` in a tool policy reads as deny-all but the matcher treats it as allow-all — identical to omitting `allow`. `openclaw config validate` reported `Config valid` with no warning. Field case: WhatsApp sender policies documented as restricted with `allow: []` while every non-denied tool stayed allowed.

## Changes

Warn-only; matcher semantics, exit codes and JSON shape unchanged:

- `src/config/validation-core.ts`: `pushEmptyAllowWarning` now takes `alsoAllowNarrows` — suppression applies only to `tools.subagents.tools`, the single scope where `mergeConfiguredSubagentAllow` (`src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts:87-89`) narrows `[] + alsoAllow` to the alsoAllow list. Global/sandbox stay permissive (`pickSandboxToolPolicy` maps to `["*", ...alsoAllow]` per `src/agents/sandbox-tool-policy.test.ts:39-48`; `mergeAllowlist` in `src/agents/sandbox/tool-policy.ts:54-62` preserves `[]`), so they still warn. Collector now also visits `tools.byProvider.*`, `agents.entries.*.tools.byProvider.*` (consumed at `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts:391/396` via `CommonToolPolicyFields.byProvider` at `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts:631`) and `agents.entries.*.tools.sandbox.tools` (`AgentToolsSchema.sandbox` at `:722-726`).
- `src/config/validation.ts:264`: wires the combined collector into the existing snapshot warnings channel (validate already prints and JSON-serializes warnings; no CLI plumbing needed).
- `docs/tools/subagents/tool-policy.md`: sole-exception wording — only `tools.subagents.tools` narrows with `alsoAllow`; all other scopes warn.
- `src/config/empty-allow-policy-warnings.test.ts`: 8 tests (global, per-sender, agent entries, subagents/sandbox, subagent-only silence, global+sandbox warn with alsoAllow, byProvider + nested sandbox coverage, omit silence).

Correction: the original blanket `alsoAllow` exception was wrong — withdrawn (see concession comments with `sandbox-tool-policy.test.ts` + `tool-policy.ts` refs). Now scope-aware.

prs.title: fix(cli): publish CoreDNS config atomically with preserved permissions
prs.body:
Closes #184888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrites an existing CoreDNS `Corefile` (and its `.server` files) by truncating in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write destroys the operator's DNS configuration with no backup and no recovery copy (the file lives outside OpenClaw's state dir).

## User Impact
A failed write no longer destroys the previous Corefile or `.server` contents. Existing file and parent-directory permissions are preserved (the previous code kept them by writing directly); newly created files keep `writeFileSync`'s umask-respecting permissions instead of the helper's restrictive defaults; CoreDNS setups that use a symlinked `Corefile` or a symlinked `conf.d` keep working and now also publish atomically.

## Why This Change Was Made
`writeFileSudoIfNeeded` called `fs.writeFileSync` on the final path (and `sudo tee` as fallback), which truncates before any content is written. It now uses `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `replaceFileAtomicSync` (temp-file + rename): a failed publication leaves the previous bytes exactly as they were, verified by a regression that injects a `renameSync` failure. Options chosen deliberately: `preserveExistingMode: true` so existing rwx bits survive, `dirMode` pinned to the immediate parent's current mode so helper defaults cannot tighten existing directories, and `mode: 0o666 & ~process.umask()` for new files. Symlinked Corefiles publish to their real target (dangling links resolve the link target, normalizing its real parent when the target does not exist yet). The `sudo tee` fallback is unchanged.

## Evidence
Level B (registered `dns setup --apply` CLI entry driven in-process against a real temporary filesystem, with `darwin` platform and `brew`/`sudo` subprocesses mocked):
- Rename failure injected: the pre-existing Corefile is byte-identical afterward. Red on base (the truncate path left it partial), green with this change.
- Existing Corefile and parent directory modes preserved after a successful rewrite (0755/0644 fixtures); a newly created Corefile gets `0o666 & ~umask` rather than fs-safe's 0600.
- Real symlinked Corefile, a dangling link, and a symlinked `conf.d` directory all publish correctly and preserve the link itself; a nested dangling case whose target sits inside a symlinked directory also passes.
- All 12 cases in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` pass (node 24.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --run`).
- Independent Codex review of the final diff found four findings, all addressed and re-verified (restrictive default modes, new-file umask mode, symlink handling, dangling-link parent normalization).
- Known boundary disclosed deliberately: fs-safe's `applyDirectoryMode` chmods the parent directory even when its mode already matches and does not restore it on failure; the privilege-escalation fallback (`sudo tee`) is unchanged and out of this fix's scope.
- Not obtained: A-level proof (an installed macOS CLI run against a real CoreDNS install, including an upgrade from the latest stable). This host is Linux and the command is gated to `darwin`, so that trace cannot be produced here; the evidence above is B-level only.
- Not run locally: tsgo/extension-boundary lanes (the local checkout uses a shared dependency install that tsgo rejects); CI runs the type lanes for this head.
