prs.title: fix(codex): private conversation recall misses indexed sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private conversation recall returning no relevant memory on the Codex harness when the source conversation is already indexed.

Related to #100140.

## User Impact

Codex-backed recall can search the intended private conversation corpus through the existing visibility checks. Ordinary memory search keeps its configured sources.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the trusted conversation recall context to the host tool factory, matching the embedded harness. The memory owner already selects the recall corpus and enforces the same-agent, private-anchor and sandbox boundaries.

The existing memory/auth context table moves to a sibling test file because the owner file has reached its line cap. Production grows by one line. Net test growth is 45 lines, covered by the required allocation record. The added cases protect absent, sessions and configured recall contexts.

## Evidence

- A synthetic direct-chat source was published by the normal producer. With memory-only search defaults and memory/session index sources, the native recall child issued memory_search without a corpus argument, received eight Memory-only hits and returned NONE. The same main turn found the expected answer using sessions_search and sessions_history. No external messages were delivered.
- Before the fix, the owner regression failed for both trusted recall contexts because the host factory received undefined. After the fix, all 82 owner tests passed. After the required extraction, the final four affected Codex/memory suites passed 140 tests across two shards in 135.60s. The new sibling's three tests took 1.254s, with compiler/import preparation dominating its 63.55s cold shard. Native CI passed on attempt 1 in approximately 408s wall time. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42413423590).
- Local autoreview covered the complete staged candidate against 037c8a6ed9009f2be7de0811efe4ca4e909a3b7b through P2 and reported no actionable findings. The review used the unchanged context producer, host-tool construction and memory visibility sources. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.
- Personally inspected native Codex dynamic-tool protocol at rust-v0.160.0, commit a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc. This context is owned by OpenClaw's host tool construction.
- The repaired source head passed a live-model normal-producer QA cell in 55.02s. The supplemental fixture used `qa/scenarios/memory/remember-across-conversations.yaml`, removed its forced `memory index` and Gateway restart steps, and selected the documented native Codex user-home auth route with Codex CLI 0.167.0. Separate private source and target conversations returned the exact synthetic preference. The recall helper called `memory_search`, included the private source transcript, excluded the group and target-anchor transcripts, and preserved `tools.sessions.visibility`. The live channel was the isolated `qa-channel`. The fixture's mock-only group-destination, pause and setting-off checks were outside this live cell.
- Initial test setup rejected an absolute output path. The first live cell then stopped before the source acknowledgement with HTTP 401 because its isolated agent home had no prepared credential. A separate run passed after selecting the documented existing native account route. The six synthetic native threads were archived and read back after teardown.
- Official distribution and Shannon's repaired-runtime automatic recall acceptance remain pending. The successful live cell is bound to this source checkout and its stated native Codex runtime.

The focused extension and extension-test typechecks, format, plugin boundaries, line-cap and test-line budget checks passed. Optional broad check:changed encountered existing changelog attribution violations in unchanged historical records. Its dead-export scan reported six unchanged exports in scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts and was stopped. Exact-head native PR CI completed successfully. The local broad-check findings remain documented above.


## Inspectable runtime and authority evidence

The following output is projected from completed runs on `3e01344f4079d6e4454d172f1e53a2692fe4adf5`. The live cells used native Codex 0.167.0 with the documented existing-user-account route. Both used the isolated `qa-channel` and ordinary inbound conversation production. All facts and requests below are synthetic.

```json
{
  "head": "3e01344f4079d6e4454d172f1e53a2692fe4adf5",
  "nativeCodex": "0.167.0",
  "providerLive": true,
  "channel": "isolated qa-channel",
  "privateRecall": {
    "passed": 1,
    "wallMs": 55020,
    "ordinaryProducer": true,
    "manualIndex": false,
    "restartAfterSeeding": false,
    "reply": "lemon pepper wings with blue cheese"
  },
  "groupDestination": {
    "passed": 1,
    "wallMs": 25989,
    "sourceAcknowledged": true,
    "helperCountBefore": 1,
    "helperCountAfter": 1,
    "nativeModelInputItems": 12,
    "nativeToolCalls": 0,
    "privateMarkerInNativeJournal": false,
    "reply": "QA-GROUP-NO-CONTEXT"
  },
  "authorityReturnBoundary": [
    {
      "proof": "recall-authority-return-boundary",
      "destination": "private",
      "candidateTranscriptHits": 1,
      "releasedTranscriptHits": 1,
      "partialTranscriptHits": 0,
      "persistedSessionOwner": "real SQLite session store",
      "retrievalBackend": "controlled deferred candidate"
    },
    {
      "proof": "recall-authority-return-boundary",
      "destination": "group",
      "candidateTranscriptHits": 1,
      "releasedTranscriptHits": 0,
      "partialTranscriptHits": 0,
      "persistedSessionOwner": "real SQLite session store",
      "retrievalBackend": "controlled deferred candidate"
    },
    {
      "proof": "recall-authority-return-boundary",
      "destination": "becomes-shared",
      "candidateTranscriptHits": 1,
      "releasedTranscriptHits": 0,
      "partialTranscriptHits": 0,
      "persistedSessionOwner": "real SQLite session store",
      "retrievalBackend": "controlled deferred candidate"
    }
  ],
  "unitTestFiles": 1,
  "unitTestsPassed": 3
}
```

### Native private-recall tool trace

The saved native recall thread contains this tool invocation, followed by the returned session hit and the final synthetic preference. The invocation omits `corpus`. The original QA assertions also verified exclusion of the group-source and target-anchor transcript IDs.

```json
{
  "toolCall": "const r = await tools.memory_search({query:\"what snack do I usually want for QA movie night\",minScore:0,maxResults:10});text(r);\n",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "sessions/qa/30b11b93-9cc5-48c8-aac8-97a7d8326216.jsonl",
      "source": "sessions",
      "startLine": 2,
      "endLine": 2,
      "snippet": "User: Stable QA movie night usual favorite snack preference: lemon pepper wings with blue cheese. Reply exactly: QA-REMEMBER-SOURCE-SEEDED\n\nSource: sessions/qa/30b11b93-9cc5-48c8-aac8-97a7d8326216.jsonl#L2"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Group destination before model output

A separate private conversation produced `QA_PRIVATE_GROUP_MARKER_194802_20261108`. A subsequent group request asked for the private code using the unique challenge `QA-GROUP-DESTINATION-PROBE-20261108-0404`. The group native thread was selected by its exact isolated workspace and that challenge. Its persisted model-input items and full native journal contained zero occurrences of the private marker. The private source journal supplied a positive control for the same extractor. The group produced `QA-GROUP-NO-CONTEXT`, with zero tool calls and no additional recall helper.

The group native journal SHA-256 was `5ac8696c90957d5be4da7e5969ade1d2e3c0f0268e37080ef26c8746c1b53285`. The QA summary SHA-256 was `8f8b7bc7092934926d166754d9fea3df75ec9996ddac0d7f2784ab0d03835bf3`. The three task-owned native threads were archived through the native API and read back after the runner removed its isolated state.

### Destination invalidation while retrieval waits

The supplemental owner test calls production `executeMemorySearchToolQuery`, including its production session-visibility filter, with the real SQLite session owner. Its retrieval backend deliberately holds one private transcript candidate at a deferred search boundary. The test persists a private-to-group change through `upsertSessionEntry` before releasing retrieval. The query returns zero transcript hits and publishes no partial transcript result. The already-group case also returns zero. The unchanged-private control returns the candidate.

This establishes the search-result boundary before a caller can supply the result to the model. The live group cell above separately exercises inbound routing, native model input and the completed reply. The retained source change remains the one-line adapter forwarding repair. The supplemental fixtures below were executed from the exact checkout and removed after their evidence was retained.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the real session-owner and deferred retrieval proof</summary>

Save this as `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-tool-query.recall-authority-proof.test.ts`, then run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-tool-query.recall-authority-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

```ts
import { createDeferred } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/extension-shared";
import type {
  MemorySearchManager,
  MemorySearchResult,
} from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-storage";
import { captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-config-snapshot";
import { upsertSessionEntry } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime";
import { withOpenClawTestState } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-state";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { executeMemorySearchToolQuery } from "./memory-search-tool-query.js";

it.each(["private", "group", "becomes-shared"] as const)(
  "withholds transcript content at the query return boundary for %s",
  async (destination) => {
    await withOpenClawTestState({ scenario: "minimal" }, async () => {
      await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()();
      const anchor = "agent:main:qa-channel:direct:dm:authority-target";
      const source = "agent:main:qa-channel:direct:dm:authority-source";
      const persistAnchor = (chatType: "direct" | "group") =>
        upsertSessionEntry({
          agentId: "main",
          sessionKey: anchor,
          entry: { sessionId: "authority-anchor", updatedAt: Date.now(), chatType },
        });
      await persistAnchor(destination === "group" ? "group" : "direct");
      await upsertSessionEntry({
        agentId: "main",
        sessionKey: source,
        entry: { sessionId: "authority-source", updatedAt: Date.now(), chatType: "direct" },
      });
      const hit: MemorySearchResult = {
        path: "sessions/main/authority-source.jsonl",
        source: "sessions",
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
        score: 1,
        snippet: "QA_PRIVATE_AUTHORITY_MARKER_194802",
      };
      const entered = createDeferred<void>();
      const release = createDeferred<void>();
      const partials: unknown[] = [];
      const manager: MemorySearchManager = {
        search: async (_query, options) => {
          options?.onPartialResults?.([hit]);
          entered.resolve();
          await release.promise;
          return [hit];
        },
        status: () => ({ backend: "builtin", provider: "fixture" }),
        readFile: async () => ({ status: "not_found", path: "", text: "" }),
        probeEmbeddingAvailability: async () => ({ ok: true }),
        probeVectorAvailability: async () => false,
      };
      const query = executeMemorySearchToolQuery({
        initialManager: { manager },
        query: {
          text: "private authority marker",
          resultLimit: 3,
          defaultSources: ["memory"],
          indexedSources: ["memory", "sessions"],
          sessionKey: `${anchor}:active-memory:123456abcdef`,
          conversationRecall: {
            anchorSessionKey: anchor,
            scope: "same-agent-private",
            corpus: "configured",
          },
        },
        visibility: {
          cfg: { agents: { entries: { main: {} } }, tools: { sessions: { visibility: "self" } } },
          agentId: "main",
          sandboxed: false,
        },
        signal: new AbortController().signal,
        onPartialResults: (result) => partials.push(result),
      });
      try {
        await entered.promise;
        expect(partials).toEqual([null]);
        if (destination === "becomes-shared") {
          await persistAnchor("group");
        }
      } finally {
        release.resolve();
      }
      const result = await query;
      expect(result.rawResults).toEqual(destination === "private" ? [hit] : []);
      expect(partials).toEqual([null]);
      console.log(JSON.stringify({
        proof: "recall-authority-return-boundary",
        destination,
        candidateTranscriptHits: 1,
        releasedTranscriptHits: result.rawResults.length,
        partialTranscriptHits: 0,
        persistedSessionOwner: "real SQLite session store",
        retrievalBackend: "controlled deferred candidate",
      }));
    });
  },
);

```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the additional live group-destination cell</summary>

Save this as `qa/scenarios/memory/codex-private-recall-group-proof.yaml`. Select an available live OpenAI model and run the official `qa suite` command with this scenario, `--provider-mode live-frontier`, `OPENCLAW_QA_FORCE_RUNTIME=codex`, and a relative output directory. The native CLI path and explicit native-home setting bind the existing test account.

```yaml
title: Codex private recall rejects group destinations

scenario:
  id: codex-private-recall-group-proof
  surface: session-memory
  risk: high
  objective: Keep a normally produced private fact out of a group destination.
  plugins:
    - active-memory
  gatewayConfigPatch:
    session:
      dmScope: per-channel-peer
    memory:
      search:
        rememberAcrossConversations: true
    plugins:
      entries:
        codex:
          enabled: true
          config:
            appServer:
              transport: stdio
              command: /opt/homebrew/bin/codex
              homeScope: user
        active-memory:
          enabled: true
          config:
            enabled: true
            mode: always
            agents: []
            toolsAllow:
              - memory_search
            logging: true
            persistTranscripts: true
            transcriptDir: qa-private-group-boundary
            queryMode: message
            maxSummaryChars: 220
  successCriteria:
    - The private source is produced by a completed ordinary conversation.
    - A group request starts no private recall helper.
    - The completed group reply contains no private fact.
  execution:
    kind: flow
    channel: qa-channel
    suiteIsolation: isolated
    isolationReason: Creates synthetic private and group conversations in isolated QA state.
    summary: Produce a private fact and verify the group destination boundary.
    config:
      requiredChannelDriver: qa-channel
      privateFact: QA_PRIVATE_GROUP_MARKER_194802_20261108
      sourceMarker: QA-PRIVATE-SOURCE-ACKNOWLEDGED
      challenge: QA-GROUP-DESTINATION-PROBE-20261108-0404

flow:
  steps:
    - name: group destination receives no private recall
      actions:
        - call: waitForGatewayHealthy
          args:
            - ref: env
            - 60000
        - call: waitForQaChannelReady
          args:
            - ref: env
            - 60000
        - resetTransport: true
        - set: transcriptRoot
          value:
            expr: "path.join(env.gateway.tempRoot, 'state', 'plugins', 'active-memory', 'transcripts', 'agents', 'qa', 'qa-private-group-boundary')"
        - sendInbound:
            conversation:
              id: private-authority-source
              kind: direct
            senderId: private-authority-source
            senderName: Private QA Source
            text:
              expr: "`My private QA code is ${config.privateFact}. Reply exactly ${config.sourceMarker}.`"
          saveAs: sourceInbound
        - call: waitForCompletedQaReply
          saveAs: sourceReply
          args:
            - ref: state
            - ref: sourceInbound
            - expr: liveTurnTimeoutMs(env, 60000)
        - assert:
            expr: sourceReply.text === config.sourceMarker
            message: ordinary private source did not complete
        - set: helpersBefore
          value:
            expr: "(await fs.readdir(transcriptRoot).catch(() => [])).filter((entry) => entry.endsWith('.jsonl')).length"
        - sendInbound:
            conversation:
              id: public-authority-target
              kind: channel
              title: Group QA Destination
            senderId: public-authority-member
            senderName: Group QA Member
            text:
              expr: "`@openclaw ${config.challenge}. What is my private QA code? Reply with the code if you know it. Otherwise reply exactly QA-GROUP-NO-CONTEXT.`"
          saveAs: groupInbound
        - call: waitForCompletedQaReply
          saveAs: groupReply
          args:
            - ref: state
            - ref: groupInbound
            - expr: liveTurnTimeoutMs(env, 60000)
        - set: helpersAfter
          value:
            expr: "(await fs.readdir(transcriptRoot).catch(() => [])).filter((entry) => entry.endsWith('.jsonl')).length"
        - assert:
            expr: helpersAfter === helpersBefore
            message: group destination unexpectedly started a private recall helper
        - assert:
            expr: "!groupReply.text.includes(config.privateFact)"
            message: private fact reached the group reply
        - call: waitForQaInboundCompletion
          args:
            - ref: state
            - ref: groupInbound
            - expr: liveTurnTimeoutMs(env, 60000)
```

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix: Incognito agent turns stall before execution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Incognito agent turns stalling before execution when Gateway admission enters the nested command and runner path.

## User Impact

Incognito turns can enter execution while retaining their selected in-memory session owner. Durable-session routing and existing authority, cancellation, and settlement checks keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Command preparation read the memory-owned session but returned the configured durable store path. Nested admission then used a different scope, and the runner could queue behind its own still-held Gateway operation. Return the already-selected memory owner's path, retaining the existing durable fallback.

The regression composes the real Gateway selector, command resolver, nested session admission, runner target, and lane-controller queue. It asserts actual execution and one identical operation across all stages; the existing fixture also rejects host-data SQL. Related: #194674 (merged; this is a separate follow-up).

## Evidence

Source: `13dc6d0f38a9ef65a99e584809deb796af48f09c`, based on fresh main `d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1`. Both affected baseline files match the original reproduced source byte for byte.

- **Red → green:** the regression fails on unchanged production at `runner queued behind its own Gateway owner`, then passes with this repair. Fresh-source focused coverage passes **28/28**: six Incognito cases, eight exact-target cases, and fourteen session-admission cases.
- Core types, changed agents-root test types, two-file type-aware lint/format, whitespace, and the canonical test-line checker pass. The readable regression adds 82 LF lines using existing fixtures; cheap queue mocks would hide the self-wait. The shared budget and allocations are unchanged.
- Measured full Incognito file: 40.88s including transform/import, new case 67ms; complete wrapper 160.1s under local contention and compiler preparation. Isolated CI cost for this regression has not been measured.
- Independent source review of the exact repair found no actionable defect. Comprehensive OpenClaw autoreview also reviewed `d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1..13dc6d0f38a9ef65a99e584809deb796af48f09c` through P3 and returned clean with zero findings. That reviewer reports supplied-diff scope without project execution; local runtime proof is separate.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42444836543) passes: 39 successful jobs and 31 skipped, including a successful `openclaw/ci-gate`. The `build-artifacts` job was skipped, so this is routed check/type evidence; runtime-build proof comes from the local exact-source build below.
- Supporting live comparison from a separate executor: the same model-only marker contract timed out after 35s before repair and returned the actual assistant marker in 6.658s with the identical repair in a combined diagnostic candidate. That candidate contains other changes, so this is supporting evidence rather than an exact public-head build or inference proof.

The native `pnpm build:runtime` profile passes on this exact public head in 175.04s, with a clean checkout afterward. Its UI budget report emitted six advisory overages while the build exited successfully; no baseline attribution or UI repair is claimed. Full release/package and global declaration builds are outside the claimed proof; this change does not alter package or public API boundaries.

The regression uses synthetic memory sessions and real admission boundaries without provider calls. Live X results, citations, and client end-to-end proof remain separate. No temporary diagnostics are included in this two-file PR.

<details>
<summary>Fresh-source focused commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime-recovery.incognito.test.ts --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/command/session.exact-target.test.ts src/sessions/session-controller.admission.test.ts --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/runtime-recovery.incognito.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1

node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/command/session.ts src/agents/runtime-recovery.incognito.test.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1

```

The red run used only the new test on that base, before applying the production hunk, and selected it with `-t 'borrows one Incognito owner'`.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): finish retirement after slow shutdown finalizers settle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown permanently skipping database retirement when accepted finalizers settle after the diagnostic grace windows.

## User Impact

Slow session, cron, hook, and harness finalizers can finish their accepted work and then release shared state normally. Databases remain available until those writes settle; the existing process watchdog still bounds process shutdown. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final cleanup-work join used the same five-second cutoff as optional close steps. Once it timed out, the close operation retained that failure and never resumed database retirement, even if the underlying work subsequently completed. The outer close also treated core Gateway cleanup as optional after ten seconds.

Keep the final owner join required at both boundaries. Earlier grace warnings remain diagnostic, and accepted persistence still owns database lifetime. Resume markers do not authorize abandoning pending transcript or cron outcome writes. Increasing grace periods would only move the failure threshold.

Production LOC: +6/-4 (net +2, from formatting the existing join). Tests/test support: +177/-150 (net +27); most churn moves the existing SQLite retention matrix into its existing retirement test registrar and removes an obsolete max-lines exemption. The two standalone performance/recovery scripts add 456 tooling lines.

## Evidence

- The fake-clock late-cron regression releases persistence at 12 seconds, beyond both grace windows: red on base `0e60b80cbd8d29d0fe6bca0ba46fe09449ce89fa` with `cleanup-work resources remain after grace`; green with the fix and shared state retired.
- Focused close + outer-shutdown suites: 50/50 passed. After the test-only extraction, close suite: 44/44 passed, including the five real-SQLite retention cases. Existing cron drain suite also passes.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 0e60b80cbd8d29d0fe6bca0ba46fe09449ce89fa`: typechecks, lint, formatting, SQL/database guards, and dead-export scans pass. The obsolete max-lines entry was removed; the final complete run passes every check except changelog attribution. Changelog attribution remains red with 20 violations reproduced using the exact base's changelog files and unchanged checker; the rule change in `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` (#194364) introduced that main regression. No aggregate-green claim.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview of the complete candidate including the workload: scoped-clean, no actionable P0/P1 findings.

## Loaded Gateway proof

Added standalone synthetic fixture and measurement scripts. On Linux btrfs (`compress=zstd:1`) in a network-disabled local container, each run used 5,000 stored sessions, a 35 GiB padded SQLite database, 62,000 workspace files / 1.1 GB, 16 active streaming chats, four cron runs mid-flight, and four parallel fio sync writers. Baseline is the exact parent runtime; candidate runtime is `61adf131b1175d64bd654421de8b2721a85a7f49`.

Five pairs ran in AB/BA/AB/BA/AB order plus A/A:

| Shutdown metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 1.414 s | 1.363 s |
| Range | 1.284–1.581 s | 1.301–2.146 s |
| Main-thread CPU median | 555.1 ms | 552.2 ms |
| Session-admissions median | 775.3 ms | 771.9 ms |
| Cron median | 3.5 ms | 3.4 ms |

All 12 primary runs exited code 0 with no signal under a 90-second stop budget. Every run recovered 16/16 markers and verified all 16 persisted recovered chat histories plus four persisted cron abort receipts. A/A was 1.400/1.651 s; paired candidate-minus-base median was +64 ms. These results do **not** establish a speedup. Fio p95 ranged 9.50–42.21 ms, maximum 190.86 ms, with no writer errors; these samples cover warmup plus shutdown, not traced Gateway fsyncs.

A final smoke of the committed script also passed: 2.302 s, exit 0, 16/16 recovered histories, four cron abort receipts, and 2,076 competitor fsyncs. This is separate from the frozen paired sample.

Four separate allocation controls also passed recovery. Sampled main-heap bytes were baseline 97,857,008 / 96,334,680 and candidate 95,084,768 / 96,298,152. Their wall times varied 1.621–3.629 s under profiler overhead; no allocation/CPU improvement claim.

The larger 128-chat/eight-cron trial failed readiness before pressure or measured shutdown: all chats but only seven cron streams reached the provider within the readiness window. Concurrent container memory pressure was logged; causality is unproven. No candidate stress result or stress shutdown claim.

The btrfs loopback is backed by a host filesystem, the 35 GiB padding is compressible synthetic data, and the provider is a local streaming fixture. This is real Gateway shutdown/restart readback, but it does not reproduce a production block device or systemd. CPU and sampled allocation cover the Gateway main thread/heap, excluding child processes.

Reproduce on a built Linux checkout with Node, pnpm and fio, with btrfs mounted at `/fixture`:

```sh
node scripts/perf/shutdown-loaded-fixture.mjs /fixture/seed
mkdir /fixture/tmp
TMPDIR=/fixture/tmp node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/shutdown-loaded-measure.ts \
  --fixture /fixture/seed --pressure-directory /fixture/pressure --output /fixture/result-1
```

Use a fresh output directory per run; `--allocation` enables sampled main-heap allocation. The larger `--sessions 128 --crons 8` workload did not qualify in the 12 GiB container. The caller owns fixture cleanup.

This fixes late retirement after finalizers settle. The long admissions stall remains unreproduced and unexplained; no unsafe abandonment change or merge is requested.

CI note: the seven failures observed at this head all have directly inspected installation API rate-limit errors: [Critical Quality scope selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446202622), five [CodeQL security shards](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446202565), and [OpenGrep SARIF upload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446202664). Other checks were still running. This is separate from the exact-base changelog regression above; no aggregate-green claim or merge.

prs.title: fix(agents): bound skill delivery and attribute lane admission waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automatically selected skills can exceed the worker's aggregate resource budget before inference, then repeat the same deterministic failure through model fallback. Startup diagnostics also label writer and placement admission as global lane waiting, hiding the blocking phase.

Oversized catalogs now produce a working turn within the existing 8 MiB decoded-resource bound. The existing delivery owner prioritizes prompted, explicit, and pinned skills, reserves bounded omission notices, and retains whole instructions where they fit. Otherwise it delivers an explicit unavailability notice. The model is told which supporting files are unavailable and how to continue. Instructions are never silently truncated. Typed delivery-limit errors stop model fallback immediately; publication and transport integrity limits remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission phase transitions update scalar facts on the existing controller admission record. The queue lends its existing entry to that record and retains the same entry for active-holder identity. The revision removes eager holder snapshots, extra task closures, string building, and diagnostic arrays from queue admission. No new timer or cache is introduced. Existing periodic stuck-session reporting and slow-send logging format the facts only when emitting a diagnostic.

Live stuck diagnostics name the lane/group capacity, enqueue position, and up to 64 current holders. Completed slow-send diagnostics retain enqueue counts and cumulative lane/writer/placement durations, including readmission and fallback attempts; they deliberately do not misrepresent current holders as historical blockers. The caller's predictive queue scan is removed. Task duration starts after lane admission, so it does not establish queue-wait duration. No capacity-release leak was found or claimed fixed.

## User Impact

A first turn that waits in writer or placement admission is now reported under its real phase instead of `global_lane:waiting`, deterministic skill-delivery-limit errors fail fast instead of retrying through model fallback, and oversized skill selections are delivered within the worker limit with a model-visible note instead of failing the turn.

## Evidence

### Measurement

Original main parent: `b97bc15cd7afd6eea35c68c6dfb0cc07706a8671`. Five A/A timing pairs followed by five AB/BA blocks (ten comparison samples per arm), with allocation measured separately using two A/A pairs and five AB/BA blocks. Identical harnesses run against the original owner source overlay and the revision. Allocation includes sampled collected objects, not merely retained heap. Wall/CPU numbers below come from unprofiled runs.

| Owner workload, median | Original base | Revision | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Saturated queue wall / 4,096 turns | 13.022 ms | 12.829 ms | -1.48% |
| Saturated queue CPU / 4,096 turns | 23.021 ms | 23.130 ms | +0.47% |
| Saturated queue sampled allocation | 34.794 MB | 35.060 MB | +0.77% |
| Ordinary skill preparation wall / call | 10.495 ms | 10.870 ms | +3.57% |
| Ordinary skill preparation CPU / call | 12.210 ms | 12.812 ms | +4.93% |
| Ordinary skill sampled allocation / call | 5.195 MB | 5.219 MB | +0.47% |

All median regressions are below 5% and within A/A variation. Queue A/A median halves: wall 12.835/13.076 ms, CPU 23.070/23.383 ms, allocation 34.910/34.783 MB. Queue A/A full ranges were wall 12.656–51.055 ms (one noisy outlier), CPU 21.999–30.243 ms, allocation 34.313–35.253 MB. Ordinary skill A/A median halves: wall 10.673/11.974 ms, CPU 12.004/13.815 ms; allocation range 5.153–5.235 MB. This is a shared-host local measurement, not a production latency claim.

The saturated fixture uses 4,096 synthetic session identities: 32 waves of 32 holders and 96 waiters. Every revision run settles all turns and exposes 3,072/3,072 queued admissions, with no remaining active/queued work. The 13-minute regression reproduces a saturated lane and verifies the real stuck-diagnostic and slow-send output. Ordinary preparation runs 50 calls per sample and preserves all 32 file reads and 1,302,894 payload bytes per call, with zero failures.

The earlier oversized fixture remains synthetic: 150 skills with 11,992,050 source bytes alongside 61,700 unrelated files containing 1,110,600,000 bytes. Its worker regression is rerun on this revision and completes with a clear note. Queue and resource owners do not read a session database or scan unrelated workspace files; no btrfs or 35 GiB database performance claim is made. No production access or data copying was used. Commands and limits are documented in `scripts/perf/README.md`.

### Validation and size

The original fallback, oversized-resource, worker-completion, and attribution regressions fail on the pre-fix owners. Focused queue/controller/watchdog, resources/worker, diagnostics, fallback, and prompt-prefix suites pass. The Control UI dependency is type-only; affected UI unit tests (2) and Chromium diagnostics E2E (1) pass. Codex autoreview of the full revision against the original base is scoped-clean at P0–P2; the reviewer examined source and proof but did not independently execute the project.

Production delta is **+153 lines** versus the original base, up from +104 in the first revision; test delta is +199. The resource owner simplification removes a redundant byte reduction and avoids decoding instructions that cannot be retained, but the total LOC reduction goal was not achieved. Growth supplies the explicit transition state, optional watchdog projection, bounded cold diagnostic reader, and cumulative attempt accounting. The hot queue/controller path is smaller; moving collection off that path requires those cold readers. No new configuration, cache, schema, protocol version, dependency, or cap increase.

`pnpm check:changed --staged --base 8a607d07aa275d48d87bd93d1f884da2545f34ce` was run for the revision. It completed with the two inherited gates below and two revision-owned TypeScript errors: a synthetic queue-entry fixture lacked its now-required lane, and the inferred wait array made the optional admission field required. The final change uses the canonical snapshot element type for that existing array, with no runtime behavior change. Core, scripts, and all core-test typecheck graphs pass after those corrections; the seven cancellation tests also pass. All other changed checks passed. The mechanical type annotation and one fixture field follow the clean autoreview; neither changes runtime behavior.

Two broad gates were already red on the exact main parent and remain unresolved main regressions:

- Changelog attribution: `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364 changed policy without reconciling archived credits; the exact base reproduces the same 20 rejected records.
- Dead exports: `5e1a27a9bcc4` / #194899 removed the last consumer of `readReleaseChangelogFiles`; `c339698bbd7e` / #194839 removed the last external consumer of `isSessionUnreadAckOnlyPatch`; `9151ac22e005` / #194721 exported the internally used `CommandPaletteOpenDetail`; `adca0b0844c7` / #194815 wrapped a Solid lazy import so Knip no longer recognizes the still-used `OpenClawShell`. An isolated archive of the exact base reproduced all four signatures with working root and UI dependencies.

### CI repair after c433cc0b

The previous revision introduced a real static import cycle: `command-queue.state.ts → command-queue.types.ts → command-queue.state.ts`. The runtime-only cycle guard excludes type edges, so its green result did not cover this defect. The callback and diagnostic timeline now consume `CommandQueueWait`, a four-field leaf contract in the existing types owner. Queue state implements that contract and still lends its existing entry. No barrel, lazy import, runtime object, or additional diagnostic work is introduced. Madge fails before this repair and both Madge and runtime import-cycle guards pass afterward.

The failed cron test injected its finalization error only when diagnostics reported `idle`. Main commit `ee3ec605a59c859ba0ad68efe9c199481c543b52` / #194907 correctly preserves `processing` while a controller lease is active, so that fixture stopped injecting its error. The test now targets the recorded completion fact (`consumeQueuedTurn`) and retains both its rejection and released-admission assertions. The unchanged test reproduces the identical CI failure on the exact main parent `b97bc15cd7afd6eea35c68c6dfb0cc07706a8671` (14 pass, 1 fail) as well as the previous PR head. This repairs an inherited main test regression; production cron lifecycle behavior is unchanged.

This follow-up adds two net production type/comment lines and zero net test lines. Previous performance measurements remain applicable to the unchanged queue and resource runtime. Full affected proof: 17 queue/controller/watchdog/diagnostic files pass (264 tests); all seven original CI cron files pass (39 tests), plus the three message-lifecycle tests. Core and all core-test typecheck graphs pass. Both cycle guards pass. Fresh Codex autoreview of this repair is scoped-clean at P0–P2; it reviewed source but did not independently execute tests or verify historical attribution. The exact-parent failure and introducing patch were verified separately. `pnpm check:changed --staged --base c433cc0b1c56d8969eac46cf9554557913654017` completed with every gate passing except the same previously proven inherited changelog-attribution and dead-export failures listed above. No new failure signature remains locally.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from the custody store (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` (tree `53363f7964f31a47109cf0575aa23f31eefa0338`), the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. It was reached by fast-forward on 2026-11-05. Every earlier presented head, including `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba`, remains an ancestor; no presented history was rewritten. ### Receipts bound to this exact head Each is a separate receipt in the preserved exact-head packet, [`PROOFS/a22bd9c05c…/`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb) (docs `main` at `9ba5518b`). | gate | ruling | scope | |---|---|---| | Recipient-authority row (`R-CD-RECIPIENT-AUTHORITY`) | PASS-candidate ([docs#620 comment 6651745479](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/pull/620#issuecomment-6651745479)) | the gate-3 fire only; the row stays `partial` until a corpus fold review | | Mode-B and the locally run cut shards | PASS-candidate ([karmaterminal/openclaw#1271 comment 6653747059](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6653747059)) | the candidate-owned regression gate; it doesn't claim Mode-B was green | | Fold source review of the `2907e656 → a22bd9c05c` delta | PASS-candidate ([#1271 comment 6655365352](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6655365352)) | source review only | **Mode-B** [`41927761314`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/41927761314) ran on product `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` with workflow `a768f04231bd0a6f94cc7b845aecaec28a4a4c9e`, from 2026-11-04 22:43Z to 2026-11-05 04:47Z. It finished terminally **non-green**: 91 jobs (53 succeeded, 27 failed, 3 cancelled, 8 skipped) and 218,033 tests passed / 220 failed. - Its receipts are valid, routed equals planned, and every hosted job ran on the project's own runner pool. - **Its 64 distinct failing tests are exactly the previous accepted head's set** (the same sorted-set sha256 `185b6dea…`), and none is new. - The four shards the workflow cuts at 90 minutes were run locally at this exact SHA, serially with one worker: - two were clean; - two carry only baseline or test-order failures, each classified in the receipt with counterfactual runs. **Packet status: preserved, NOT acceptance-complete, NOT terminal.** Of 37 required rows, **0 pass, 1 partial (the recipient-authority row above), and 36 missing**. No live row has fired at this SHA, because no deployment runs it yet: the deployed fleet is on a separate, older line. Running live rows here needs a deployment whose runtime has this SHA as an ancestor. That is a migrating cut (an agent-schema step), gated on its own timed restore rehearsal. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` does not point at this packet, and nothing here is a terminal rollup claim. ### Earlier evidence: provenance, not exact-target proof The live behavior observed on earlier heads, and the earlier corpora, are ancestry and materiality evidence for this head. They aren't exact-target execution, and no row is carried over from them as a pass: - Mode-B [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) at `3821eaef72`, 2026-09-18; - corpora [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) and [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393). The behaviors those corpora observed are the ones this feature exists for: - stale ambient backlog suppression; - typed and bracket `continue_work` wakes with granted provenance and Tempo model-call spans; - cost-cap rejection; - max-chain, scheduler, durable recovery and delegate surfaces. They are re-fired against this head's runtime once one is deployed. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. - [Exact-head packet for `a22bd9c05c`: README, status and limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md: identities and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md: how the packet was built](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/METHOD.md) - [Gate 4 receipt: Mode-B and the local cut shards](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/gates/GATE-4-MODE-B-AND-LOCAL-SHARDS.md) - Historical corpora (provenance only): [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567), [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - `139e3657…` packet files: [README](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) · [RESOLVED-SHA](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) · [METHOD](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) · [TRANSPOSED-FROM](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) · [manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) ### PROOFS METHOD Live rows use a Grafana k6 proof harness. Each packet's `METHOD.md` carries the exact reproducer commands. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers, because OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access. Structural completeness is not proof: a row counts only with an authoritative receipt at the exact SHA. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially host Cron plus / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A tool adapter over durable flow records is also not a lifecycle host, and upstream has since removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime (#159179) that such an adapter would have called. Marking a stored record as running neither reacquires a session lane nor invokes the model; continuation needs the turn machinery itself to own which session runs next, how child results return, and what survives finalization. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(workers): preserve missing-module startup errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a missing worker module can replace its useful startup error with `DataCloneError` and terminate the native worker supervisor.

## User Impact

Users receive the original module failure and the failed worker joins cleanly. Non-Error object-valued diagnostic causes become text; primitive causes and real Error metadata remain structured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native host objects in loader-error causes need not be structured-cloneable. The existing error encoder now renders non-Error objects, functions, and symbols as diagnostic text before transport. It owns the normalization, replacing raw-object forwarding without runtime checks. The extra work occurs only while encoding failures.

The tests reuse a shared/cyclic error fixture and the existing supervisor recovery scenario. They cover the missing-module failure, then prove a healthy sibling still exchanges messages and joins. Native error types, shared references, cycles, falsy suppressed values, and opaque diagnostic values remain covered. The final diff adds 16 production lines and removes 2 test lines; no test-budget increase remains.

## Evidence

- Removes OpenClaw's dependency on https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46711 for forwarding loader error causes.
- macOS arm64, stock Bun main `2596ac5d`: the real retained-worker missing-module path fails with `DataCloneError` before the change and preserves the original loader error plus native join after it. The final consolidated supervisor regression also fails on the base and passes after the fix.
- The same regression passes on the repository-pinned Bun fork `191755ec11` and Node `26.12.1`. Final focused coverage: 8/8 on each runtime.
- Final full owning files: pinned fork 17/17 passed; Node 17/17 passed. Stock: 16 passed, with one unchanged raw-Worker async-context fixture failing before the retained-worker path (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/42593).
