prs.title: fix(knowledge): order mixed-precision transcript timestamps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Knowledge transcript exporter sorts `occurred_at` as an unnormalized string. When normalized UTC rows mix second, millisecond and fractional-second precision, this can put `.000000001Z` before `Z`, or `.100000001Z` before `.1Z`. Raw day exports and readable transcripts consequently disagree with chronological order.

## What Changed

Preserve @zhangguiping-xydt's small owner fix: compare canonical timestamp keys with trailing fractional zero padding removed, without converting to millisecond-resolution Date values. Keep original timestamp strings in output and preserve the existing message-ID tie-break for equal instants.

Merged current main as requested. Removed the precision test allocation and consolidated its cases into the existing transcript owner test. It now exercises second/millisecond equality, fractional nanosecond ordering and exact raw timestamp preservation while retaining day/thread boundaries, cross-day replies, mention/line rendering, byte limits and part labels. JSONL serialization is shared by fixture input and expected raw output.

Whole-change deltas: production **+5** (`6 added / 1 removed`), tests **0** (`9 added / 9 removed`), docs +2. No defaults, format fields, validation policy, model-facing text or public API changes.

## Evidence

[Built CLI before/after proof and uniform-output control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194697#issuecomment-6717105760).

Built Node CLI before/after receipt linked below. Secretless `node:24.22.1`; independent frozen-main/candidate runtime builds; actual shipped `dist/extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/chat-transcript.mjs` entry point. Synthetic normalized JSONL input covers seconds, milliseconds, short fractions, trailing-zero equal instants and distinct nanoseconds with ID ordering that exposes precision loss.

Expected chronological IDs: `10,40,50,60,70,20,30,01,80,90`.

- Main: `50,10,60,70,20,01,30,80,40,90` (wrong).
- Candidate: expected order in both raw JSONL and readable text.
- Every message and its original timestamp survives; index endpoints, byte count and hash match actual output.
- Uniform-precision control: transcript, raw JSONL and chunks.json byte-identical across revisions.
- Focused regression red on main, green on candidate; scoped types, lint, syntax and format checked.

Boundary: standalone file-input export, not live Discord acquisition or downstream Gateway ingestion. Contributor commit/credit retained.

prs.title: fix(muse): correct README claim that auto never picks Muse
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #194886

## What Problem This Solves

- The Muse plugin README (`extensions/muse/README.md`) told users the harness is "opt-in only" and that `auto` never picks it. That contradicts the canonical Muse guide and current native-catalog routing, so users reading the package README could wrongly conclude that explicit runtime configuration is always required, or misunderstand why a discovered native Muse model is selected.
- **Related:** #194886 (reporter prepared a README-only correction); separate from startup-cancellation PR #194884, which does not touch the README. Labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** The README selection paragraph now matches the documented and implemented behavior: explicit selection via `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on a `meta/*` model or the `meta` provider, plus the existing implicit route where a model discovered by exactly one native runtime can use that runtime when no authored API binding or host credential takes precedence (an API catalog row alone is not an API credential). Explicit runtime choices and required cloud workers keep their existing runtime policy.
- **Out of scope:** No runtime policy or code change is requested or made; no changed links. The `extensions/copilot/README.md` wording is a different plugin and left untouched.
- **Highest-risk area:** None — docs-only, +6/−2 lines in one README.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Wording is taken verbatim in substance from the canonical guide (`docs/plugins/muse.md`) and verified against `implicitNativeRuntime` in `src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts` (definition at L142–151, implicit-policy use at L303–309).

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** The README no longer claims `auto` never picks Muse; readers of `extensions/muse/README.md` get the same selection rules as the canonical guide: explicit routing, the single-native-runtime implicit route, API binding/credential precedence, and unchanged policy for explicit runtime choices and required cloud workers.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `extensions/muse/README.md` Install section (the replaced paragraph) against `docs/plugins/muse.md` L92–99 and `src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts` `implicitNativeRuntime`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Repo source at `origin/main` (`a606a90b4bf`) in an isolated worktree; documentation/source claim only — per the issue and the clawsweeper review, no live Muse run is needed to establish the contradiction.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  git show origin/main:extensions/muse/README.md | grep -n "never picks"   # before
  sed -n '142,151p' src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts                       # implicitNativeRuntime
  sed -n '303,309p' src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts                       # implicit-policy use
  sed -n '92,97p' docs/plugins/muse.md                                     # canonical guide
  grep -n "never picks" extensions/muse/README.md                          # after
  git diff --stat origin/main -- extensions/muse/README.md
  ```
- **Rendered README preview (media proof, GitHub-rendered blob at the PR head):** The changed file is outside `docs/`, so per the ClawSweeper ask this attaches screenshots of GitHub's own rendered `extensions/muse/README.md` view showing the corrected Install paragraph and the retained guide link. Captured headlessly from `github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/<sha>/extensions/muse/README.md` at the pinned refs; no private details are present in the rendered page.
  - **After** (PR head `4dccb675be9` — corrected paragraph, "never picks" claim gone, guide link intact):

    ![Rendered extensions/muse/README.md at PR head 4dccb675be9 — Install section now documents explicit selection plus the single-native-runtime implicit route, and the Muse Code agent runtime guide link is preserved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LiuwqGit/pr-evidence/main/pr-194903/muse-readme-after-rendered.png)

  - **Before** (PR base `a606a90b4bf` — stale "`auto` never picks it" claim):

    ![Rendered extensions/muse/README.md at base a606a90b4bf — Install section still claims the harness is opt-in only and that auto never picks it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LiuwqGit/pr-evidence/main/pr-194903/muse-readme-before-rendered.png)

  - Capture-time rendered-text assertions (from the same headless session): after → `has-old-claim=false`, `has-new-para=true`, `has-guide-link=true`; before → `has-old-claim=true`, `has-new-para=false`, `has-guide-link=true`.
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  === BEFORE (origin/main extensions/muse/README.md L15-16) ===
  The harness is opt-in only: set `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on a `meta/*` model
  or on the `meta` provider; `auto` never picks it.

  === Source of truth: src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts L142-151 ===
      implicitNativeRuntime(entry: Pick<ModelCatalogEntry, "provider" | "id">) {
        // An API metadata donor is not evidence of API credentials. Host bindings
        // and credentials still take precedence in evaluateNative below.
        const runtimes = new Set(

  === Implicit-policy use: src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts L303-309 ===
        if (
          !policy.forcedByEnvironment &&

          policy.runtime === "auto"
        ) {
          policy = { ...policy, runtime: routes.implicitNativeRuntime(entry) ?? policy.runtime };
        }

  === AFTER (working tree extensions/muse/README.md L15-20) ===
  Select the harness explicitly by setting `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on a
  `meta/*` model or on the `meta` provider. Without explicit routing, a model
  discovered by exactly one native runtime can use that runtime when no authored
  API binding or host credential takes precedence; an API catalog row alone is
  not an API credential. Explicit runtime choices and required cloud workers

  (no match — false statement removed)

  === git diff --stat ===

   1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

- **Observed result after fix:** The README paragraph now states the same selection rules as `docs/plugins/muse.md` L92–99 and the `implicitNativeRuntime` implementation; the false "`auto` never picks it" claim is gone and no links changed.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** Before: README asserted `auto` never picks Muse while `model-catalog-view.ts` L303–309 replaces an implicit `auto` policy with the single native runtime (e.g. `muse`) when exactly one supplies the model. After: README documents both explicit selection and the implicit single-native-runtime route with API binding/credential precedence preserved.
- **What was not tested:** No live Muse run and no whole-Gateway run — the issue and the clawsweeper Codex review both scope this as a documentation/source claim established by reading the README against the guide, the selection implementation, and existing tests. prs.title: docs(cli): drop the unnecessary Gateway restart after enabling Workboard
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

## What Problem

`docs/cli/workboard.md` tells operators to run `openclaw gateway restart` after `openclaw plugins enable workboard` (lines 12-17). That contradicts the two pages that own plugin enablement:

- `docs/plugins/workboard.md` documents the same CLI workflow as `openclaw plugins enable workboard` then `openclaw dashboard`, followed by "Enablement applies to a running Gateway automatically. If it is offline, start it before opening the dashboard."
- `docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md` ("Apply changes and inspect") states that ordinary CLI install, enable, disable, and uninstall commands use the running local Gateway when available, and only apply at next startup when no Gateway is running.

An operator who follows the CLI reference performs an avoidable Gateway restart that interrupts live sessions and channels, and is left unsure whether enablement needs a restart at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the initial enablement example in `docs/cli/workboard.md` changes. The command block drops `openclaw gateway restart` and is followed by the same online/offline guidance the plugin pages already use, plus a note that `dispatch` needs a running Gateway and a link to the authoritative section in `manage-plugins.md`. The runtime behavior is not changed, and the page's separate "Dispatch says data-only" troubleshooting section (which legitimately starts or restarts the Gateway) is untouched.

Fix for #194414 (from ClawSweeper's recommended next step: correct the initial CLI example and verify the online/offline guidance against the existing plugin guides).

## User Impact

The Workboard CLI page and the Workboard plugin page now describe one enablement workflow. Operators no longer restart a healthy Gateway after enabling a bundled plugin, and operators with an offline Gateway know the change lands at the next start.

## Evidence

Diff:

```diff
 Enable the plugin before using the command:
 
 ```bash
 openclaw plugins enable workboard
-openclaw gateway restart
 ```
+
+Enablement applies to a running Gateway automatically; if the Gateway is offline,
+the change takes effect at its next start. `openclaw workboard dispatch` needs a
+running Gateway. See [Apply changes and inspect](/plugins/manage-plugins#apply-changes-and-inspect).
```

prs.title: improve(knowledge): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Knowledge copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The Knowledge plugin's Control UI had ~425 user-visible English strings hard-coded across its views, dialogs, session panel, settings, loading/failure frames, and record panels. They didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary (for example "chat"/"conversation" for the session container, "turn" for an agent reply) or style rules (contractions, curly quotes, sentence case, "Couldn’t …" errors with a next step), and the plugin had no translation catalog, so none of it could be localized.

## Solution

- Add plugin i18n on the existing plugin pattern (`extensions/nostr/browser/i18n`): `extensions/knowledge/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `extensions/knowledge/src` (from `openclaw.controlUi: ./src/control-ui.ts`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` discovers the catalog. `activate(host)` binds `host.locale` once; every view reads copy through `t()` when it renders, so the page, session panel, and dialogs all use the host locale.
- The English catalog is split into `en.ts` (shared/page/search copy) plus `en-records.ts`, `en-scribes.ts`, and `en-settings.ts`, merged under one `knowledge.*` key tree. The split keeps each file under the 700-line cap; key paths are unchanged. All keys live under `knowledge.*`, so none collide with shared core keys.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-facing string the lane owns (the 31 changed view modules). Text written for the model (Ask request drafts, the record reference, scribe prompts, scribe session names) is unchanged.
- Small cutovers that came with moving copy:
  - Scribe catalog presentation fields (`blurb`, `cadence`, `startLabel`, `dialogTitle`, `submitLabel`) moved out of `scribes-catalog.ts` into the catalog and were removed from `ScribeDefinition`.
  - `sourceDateNote` moved from the shared `temporal.ts` (also used server-side) into `record-view.ts`, its only caller, so server code doesn't import Control UI copy.
  - Recent activity save badges key on the change id (`created`/`updated`/`observed`) instead of their English label. The one CSS hook (`[data-change="New"]`) moved to `[data-change="created"]`.
  - The page's source-files rail moved to `record-sources.ts` to keep `record-view.ts` under the line cap. It's a straight move with no behavior change.
  - The evidence excerpt eyebrow is sentence case in the catalog. `text-transform: uppercase` keeps its look.
- Docs that quote changed labels: `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` (Session not found, Open session) and `docs/plugins/knowledge/control-ui.md` (Ask starts a new session).

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Starts a new chat with {agent}. … | Starts a new session with {agent}. … |
| Chat was not started. Your request is still here. | Couldn’t start the session. Your request is still here. |
| Chat was started but the request was not sent: {error} | Couldn’t send your request. The session started; open it to try again. {details} |
| Can’t reach the vault. … | Couldn’t reach the vault. … |
| Refresh unavailable / Search unavailable | Couldn’t refresh / Couldn’t search knowledge |
| This store couldn’t be opened | Couldn’t open this store (body now ends with “Retry, or check Stores & sharing.”) |
| The scribe was not started. {error} | Couldn’t start the scribe. Your choices and prompt are still here. {details} |
| The assignment was not changed. {error} / Access was not changed. {error} | Couldn’t change the assignment. Your choices are still here; try again. {details} / Couldn’t change access. Try again. {details} |
| The run did not start: the automation is paused | Couldn’t start the run because the automation is paused. Resume it, then try again. |
| In this conversation (session panel) | In this session |
| Open conversation · Conversation not found | Open session · Session not found |
| Which conversations · Active conversations · Conversations in your sidebar. | Which sessions · Active sessions · Sessions in your sidebar. |
| Knowledge will start a conversation called … | Knowledge will start a session called … |
| Each run is an agent turn over every unlinked claim … | Each run is one agent reply over every unlinked claim … |
| Conversation not recorded (claim source, Learned in) · Saved in conversation | Session not recorded · Saved in a session |
| … from owner-direct conversations | … from direct sessions with the owner |
| Group chats see only their own conversation’s knowledge. | Group conversations see only their own conversation’s knowledge. |
| No page is named exactly "x". · Search all text for "x" | No page is named exactly “x”. · Search all text for “x” |
| PREMISE · EXCERPT / EXCERPT | Premise · excerpt / Excerpt (still rendered uppercase) |
| cannot / is not / does not / could not / must not | can’t / isn’t / doesn’t / couldn’t / can’t |

Strings moved into the translation catalog: **823 English keys**. That's the ~425 source strings, plus one/other plural forms and conditional variants that used to be assembled in code.

## Impact

- English copy now follows the glossary and style rules. The layout and controls don't change.
- Knowledge copy can now be localized. The post-merge Control UI locale-refresh job owns foreign catalogs; this PR adds no foreign strings, `translated.json`, or `.i18n` memory.
- Raw technical details in errors (Gateway messages) stay inline after the next step. This surface has no shared host “Show details” disclosure, so I kept the detail visually secondary instead.
- Known gaps, intentional:
  - Scribe titles such as “Knowledge Consolidation” keep their current case. The title is the scribe session’s display name, which the Scribes tab uses to find a scribe’s session, and it also appears in scribe prompts and automation names. Renaming it would orphan existing scribe sessions.
  - There’s no `translated.json` yet, so `locales.ts` returns English for every locale. The translated catalog loader needs wiring once the locale refresh creates that file.
  - A locale change applies on the next render of each view, not instantly. Only English exists today.

## Evidence

- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=knowledge keys=823`)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/knowledge/src`: green
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/knowledge/src docs/plugins/knowledge`: green
- `git diff --check`: clean
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge`: 64 files passed. `scribes-view.test.ts` and `search-date-filters.test.ts` assertions were updated to the new English.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main` (d59f00281eb0216) on head bc913e8842dc236, max priority P1. Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that its empty sandbox couldn’t run a build.
- pr-simplify: the catalog fields, the shared `sourceDateNote`, and the English-label status hooks were removed, and the shared count/plural helpers were folded into the catalog. Remaining growth is the catalog itself plus one-time `t()` call sites.

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge. Before/after screenshots of Recent, Browse, a record page, Scribes (list, detail, start dialog), Settings (all four sections), and the session panel are still needed under the visual gate.

prs.body:
## Summary

- add a bounded scheduled/manual matrix for the npm `latest` and `extended-stable` release lines
- run current `main` tooling against each shipped line's source and bytes through the postpublish verifier, Plugin SDK renderer, and ClawHub dry-run packer
- let the existing plugin pretag checker separate the shipped source root from the trusted tooling root while preserving existing callers
- materialize shipped source as archive data only after trusted restore-only setup, without a dynamic checkout or shipped dependency install
- add workflow and packer contract coverage, including guards for the cache/execution boundary and SDK rendering of identical `main`/tag commits

## Why

RRI-587 identified three regressions that reached shipped releases because current publication tooling was never exercised against the last-shipped stable and extended-stable inputs. This lane keeps that compatibility proof on protected `main`, resolves immutable npm tags, uses read-only permissions, bounds each matrix job to six hours, and retains SDK evidence for 30 days.

## Scope decision

Moving the operator invocation of `release:candidate --skip-dispatch` is intentionally left as a release-controller follow-up. The current checklist already performs its early Plugin SDK review before waiting for Full Release Validation; changing when the controller invokes that checklist is separate orchestration policy and is not needed for this causal compatibility lane.

## Validation

- `pnpm test test/scripts/plugin-release-pretag-pack-check.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (5 passed)
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (201 passed)

`pnpm check:workflows` could not launch actionlint on this host because Python venv/pre-commit support is unavailable; the focused workflow parser/contract suite above passed.

## Review

Independent read-only review of the exact staged CodeQL repair found no P0/P1 issues. It confirmed one static checkout, restore-only cache setup before shipped materialization, no shipped dependency install, and retained postpublish, SDK diff, and ClawHub pack coverage.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): persist Details docking measured before connect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Draft — qualification stopped at the visual gate; do not merge.** The producer repair works and passes the revised complete-frame timing gate. However, active visual captures expose a newly observed intermediate state: populated sidebar beside a transcript skeleton in **3/4 candidate captures versus 0/4 main captures**. Native paired requalification and the final full UI suite remain incomplete.

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link can fail to persist Details docking measured before connection. The campaign's original evidence recorded 14 visible states over about 15 seconds, with dashboard content first at 11.75 seconds. This focused change repairs the missing warm-cache receipt; the synthetic measurements below are separate from that original recording.

## User Impact

Restores the existing cached Details/rows first-frame contract from #194142. Team-scale active and archived co-frame improves **0/12 → 12/12**. Complete frame is `max(rows ET, Details ET)`; its order-adjusted effect is **−34 ms active** and **−11 ms archived**, passing the revised ≤+17 ms gate in both orders.

**Rows alone are later because the co-frame contract is now active on Team:** +96 ms active and +83 ms archived after A/A adjustment. Preparing Details on the critical path also increases active LoAF blocking. The follow-up is **Details readiness**: make that existing preparation earlier/cheaper. This producer repair does not restructure imports or relax the co-frame wait.

No configuration, durable server record, permission, migration or cache-shape changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`captureChatDetailsSnapshot()` correctly refuses disconnected writes. The existing `surfacePresentation` memo did not observe connection state, so unchanged geometry rejected before hello was never republished when the connection admitted it. One dependency in that memo retries through the existing `position()` and snapshot writer. Every client, epoch, session-incarnation, cache-key, session-key, scope and locale guard stays intact. No new effect, store, wait or geometry-read call site.

Persisted docking enables desktop composition prewarming. The existing snapshot store waits for `detailsReady` before the chat pane becomes ready. That restores co-framing, but can expose the already-ready sidebar beside the held center skeleton. The visual STOP below is separate from the accepted rows-only tradeoff.

Production runtime delta is **+1 line**. The requested production-stat command reports **+3 lines across two files**, including the two-line test allocation. The missing dependency is necessary to restore the existing contract and makes no other machinery unnecessary. The rendered-owner regression adds 53 test lines, with an exact 53-line allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged. Simplification review found no redundant path to delete.

## Evidence

### Multi-reload reproduction and producer proof

Successive real old-page Team-scale reloads did not restore a frozen snapshot between samples. On pinned main, cold snapshots and the warm prime had no docking; all 12 active and 12 archived warm snapshots still lacked docking, co-frame 0/12. With the repair, the warm prime persisted docking and all 12 successive reloads retained it, co-frame 12/12 in each workload.

A separate main-only real resize (1720 → 1721 → 1720) produced an admitted receipt that survived the prime and three successive warm reloads in both Team workloads. The observed bug is missing publication; this does **not** establish deletion of a previously persisted receipt. The original native single-build control naturally persisted docking and co-framed, explaining how explicit fixture qualification can hide the producer defect.

Producer regression: red on pinned main (expected docking, actual undefined), green with the fix. Final-head browser file: **20/20**, **5.78 s wall**, **2.77 s Vitest duration**. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-browser.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Fresh isolated review is clean through P2.

Separate forced-layout diagnostics around hello (published−25 ms through handled+50 ms): active **2 → 0**, archived **0 → 0**; whole capture **85 → 85**, **42 → 41**. These are diagnostic counts, separate from observer-only timing.

### Inspected visual STOP

Four active captures per arm, supported single-build mode with a fixed bundle per browser, `--visual-proofs`, real old-page reloads. All eight complete visible-state overviews were inspected, with original full-resolution frames checked at the changed boundary. The first root-switching comparison attempt failed setup before capturing a reload and is excluded.

| Active capture | Main masked unique states | Candidate masked unique states | Main animation-normalized unique states | Candidate animation-normalized unique states | Candidate populated-sidebar/center-skeleton interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 71 | 68 | 71 | 67 | absent |
| 2 | 70 | 73 | 69 | 72 | approximately 319–502 ms |
| 3 | 68 | 72 | 67 | 71 | approximately 298–498 ms |
| 4 | 73 | 72 | 72 | 72 | approximately 270–470 ms |

These clocks are from instrumented visual captures, **not performance comparison results**. Pixel counts include late synthetic live updates and animation phases; they are reported without treating the heuristic as semantic proof. Main shows skeleton → rows without sidebar/Details → sidebar → populated Details. Candidate capture 1 removes the rows-without-Details stage. Captures 2–4 instead show skeleton → populated sidebar with center skeleton → rows and Details together. That newly observed intermediate ordering triggers the brief's visual STOP condition, even though co-framing improves.

L297 geometry remains stable in all eight captures: section top/height movement **0 px**, insertions/removals **0**, Environment **81 → 81 px**. The #193217 transcript probe records **0 px excess movement/backtracking** and no missing-anchor frames throughout. This does not waive the visible-state gate.

Inspected synthetic frames from active capture 2 follow. These are independent visual runs, not a side-by-side latency estimator. No private capture or real account/state was used.

Main first rows, approximately 351 ms: Details and sidebar still absent.

![Synthetic main first rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4eacd0ef-996b-477b-9ff1-f7b20670a4f3)

Candidate first rows, approximately 502 ms: transcript and populated Details together.

### Timing method and source identity

The lead explicitly requested reuse of the existing Team timing pairs under the revised gate; no Team timing rerun was made. Twelve alternating AB/BA pairs plus matching A/A, one quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, repository headless Chromium, 1720×1180, live-fast network, 2200 ms observer-only capture and one unmeasured warm prime. Deltas are candidate minus main. For each order, subtract the A/A median delta from the A/B median delta; the reported adjusted effect is the mean of those two effects. Raw better-pair counts and paired medians are diagnostics.

prs.title: fix: native Codex oauth/token without a host profile should still forward unlisted models
prs.body:
Fixes #194980

### What Problem This Solves

A native Codex login that has not selected a host auth profile reports `authProfileMode` as `oauth` or `token`. Doctor is not involved. `resolveCodexForwardCompatModel` forwards a model missing from the static patch table only when `authProfileMode` is absent. Those sessions therefore cannot forward an unlisted model id. Models already in the static table are unchanged.

### Why This Change Was Made

The unlisted branch now accepts `authProfileMode === undefined || authProfileMode === "oauth" || authProfileMode === "token"`. It still requires `authProfileId === undefined` and `providerConfig?.auth === undefined`. `api_key`, and `oauth` that already has an `authProfileId`, still return `undefined`.

The existing spark-routing test moved to `extensions/openai/openai-codex-spark-routing.test.ts` so the provider test file could take the new cases without growing past its line cap. That test's assertions are unchanged.

### User Impact

An operator signed in to native Codex without selecting a host profile can use a model id that is not yet in the static patch table. A selected host profile and API-key auth still do not receive that forward path.

### Evidence

Inspectable transcripts: https://gist.github.com/ericcaiwx-star/dd9f3325c07c785afceabb7fb25572db

Resolver, exact command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts -t "delegates an unlisted first-party model|does not extend native model forwarding" --maxWorkers=1`:

- Parent of `bd5140669e8`: exit 1. `oauth` and `token` return `undefined` for `gpt-future`. `undefined` still forwards. `api_key` with no profile, and `oauth` with `authProfileId` `openai:selected`, still return `undefined`. (`base-red.txt`)
- Head `bd5140669e8`: exit 0, 5 passed. `undefined`, `oauth`, and `token` forward. The two refusal cases stay `undefined`. (`head-green.txt`)

Profile-free native login on published OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (`4ffdd20`) with `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.1`, then the same isolated config on this source head:

prs.title: perf(ui): publish refreshed model auth before catalog completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fresh Models credential rows waiting for model discovery after an agent change, reconnect, or explicit refresh, even after current auth has arrived.

## User Impact

Users can read and search current credential rows while model discovery continues. Refresh stays visibly busy until the catalog settles. Provider usage retries can recover independently while that catalog is still pending. Background catalog publication retains its actionable warning while pending and clears it when recovery succeeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing core owner publishes current auth independently and adopts the already-started catalog behind its existing receipt. Unknown inventory stays visibly pending. Forced and credential refresh still wait for auth before starting refreshed catalog discovery, because auth publishes the runtime facts that discovery reads. The complete refresh promise still waits for catalog settlement.

Background publication already has usable rows. It keeps its combined completion boundary and retires the previous catalog receipt/error only when the current publication settles. The first CI run exposed this warning-lifecycle requirement; the repair preserves both pending feedback and successful recovery. A follow-up review caught usage retries still consulting the aggregate core busy flag: after incomplete or failed usage, the five-second retry could queue behind a catalog that never returned. Removing only that dependency lets the existing supplemental owner retry independently. Its settled-route, connection, current-data-client, and Gateway-epoch guards stay intact. This global usage read already runs during manual refresh; it does not depend on the credential snapshot. No cache, state owner, authentication, selected-agent identity, policy, or mutation-authority layer is added.

## Evidence

Original timing base: `156203ef9713fe8bea51109b129dbf860432d4bb`. Current retry-corrected candidate: `f88670fc6d2d084a3cf1cb2bb029b03a759400ff`, atop merged `b6ca3a5591726dcd6bce56865166d87fe3ffde2a` and integrating main `46f74089b595c0f63d2ed77cef787d0280f3cf24`. Normal/RTT and behavior measured `ce653c27d95e5e491e7034fef5a1f825055370d3`; delayed timing measured the earlier head identified below. The merge preserved the Models runtime and refresh scenario while retaining main’s independently landed Skills scenario. The subsequent usage correction removes the catalog-busy term only from automatic usage retry admission. Its exact-head build, strict-size comparison against the retained immutable main build, UI and UI-pages typechecks, and production Knip all pass. Historical timing evidence keeps its original head/base attribution; no old size numbers are presented as current-head measurements.

| Independent P0–P2 review | Whole change reviewed before CI; final publication correction reviewed scoped-clean after resolving its stale-error finding |
| Original rendered regressions | All 3 fail on the original base: agent/reconnect readiness and forced auth-before-catalog ordering |
| Publication recovery regression | Fails against the incomplete repair because the old warning survives successful publication; passes with completion reset |
| Final affected tests | 18 catalog + 5 core recovery tests pass from the prior correction. Fresh held-catalog usage regression: both refreshing/error cases fail before the one-term admission fix (2 reads instead of 3); all 5 readiness tests pass after it. UI types, UI-pages test types, and focused format/lint pass for this correction; no successful unit suite was repeated. |
| Static checks | Prior UI types, focused lint/format and UI-pages test type leaf pass. The canonical staged test-line check against exact integrated main `46f74089` passes: 6,572,198 total / 6,572,262 ceiling / 64 inherited slack. Core’s prior allocation was 207 own rendered readiness/order/recovery lines; the new two-case usage retry regression adds 63, taking its exact allocation to 270, with no inherited-debt credit. Fresh exact-base isolated P0–P2 review is scoped-clean; the usage-retry correction has an additional scoped-clean P0–P2 review against `b6ca3a55`. Scoped script typechecking for the merged benchmark passes after setting the scratch configuration’s repository root. |

Chat CSS 133,507→same B (3 requests), New CSS 99,202→same B (3 requests). Document 15,989→16,012 B (+23 B, within 64 B variance). Total JS gzip decreases 50 B; total CSS is unchanged. No ceiling changes. |
| Delayed catalog timing | 180/180 passed: 20 rotated base/head/A/A triplets per engine, on pre-publication-repair head `0d36f2b59b3266718a56a18d44a871cf5db29204` |

Their initial scratch configuration omitted the repository root and stopped with TS6059; the corrected scratch-only path passes without source edits or repeating either build. |

The publication repair inserts only a `reason === "publication"` branch; removing that branch reproduces the previous core owner byte for byte. The measured forced-refresh path is unchanged. The latest merge combines the separate Models and Skills scenario blocks without changing either block’s body; their distinct page IDs select them independently. Total JS raw increases 154 B; served JS gzip decreases 43 B and served Brotli increases 139 B. Fixed-cap warnings remain: document +2,119 B, total CSS gzip +469 B and raw +962 B. Readiness is measured in the application from the native Refresh click to visible fresh credentials plus an editable search input; it is not labeled full-refresh completion or CPU.

Acceptance weighs the delayed readiness gain against ordinary-use cost: require at least a 5% delayed improvement and reject a real normal-use median regression. Report near-band tails together with medians and A/A noise. The final matrix meets that rule. The delayed readiness improvement is 97.67–99.23%; under 100 ms RTT readiness improves 41.98–44.19% while full-action wall medians improve 2.49–4.94%. Normal-use readiness and wall medians are flat or improved. The near-band Firefox wall tail and small CPU movements below do not outweigh the delayed improvement. Normal WebKit/Firefox catalog-response medians move 17→20 ms. Chromium normal script CPU moves 13.56→14.06 ms (+0.50 ms, A/A +3.70%; its p95 improves); RTT script CPU moves 15.51→16.08 ms (+0.57 ms), task CPU 44.63→46.55 ms (+1.92 ms). These small costs are retained explicitly alongside the application-readiness win. No claim of CPU equivalence for WebKit or Firefox is made.

Touched production LOC: **1,161→1,173 (+12)**. Touched tests: **1,232→1,502 (+270)**, including the existing catalog file. Benchmark: **4,984→5,109 (+125)** against integrated main `46f74089`. Solid effects remain **2→2**; render effects, direct listeners, DOM queries, `untrack`, `flush`, owner APIs and component cleanup remain **0→0**.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep peer replies through target yields
prs.body:
Related: #173026

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a missing `sessions_send` peer result when the target yields to nested work and completes under a successor run.

## User Impact

The original requester retains its result obligation through the target's yield. The result is consumed once from the accepted successor, using main's existing peer return authorization and delivery policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit eligible native cross-session peers to the existing `SessionFollowupCompletion` owner, so the committed yield cohort can hand off result custody. This adapts the completion-custody approach in #173026 without its broader progress-card or required-visible-reply changes. ACP, steering, self-send and registered-child routing keep their existing paths. Ownership remains process-local; restart durability is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New admission regression fails on base `30db562cc539` because the ordinary peer has no completion owner, then passes with the fix. It exercises the real completion owner, committed cohort, successor and single consumer.
- 64 focused tests pass across peer admission, followup authorization, completion cohorts, send admission, A2A replies and requester-owner continuation.
- Core production types, focused type-aware lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet and test-line ratchet pass.
- Local Codex autoreview of this change against `30db562cc539`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The published source tree is identical to the reviewed tree.
- New regression: 16 ms test time in the first green run. Cold shared preparation plus the first green 16-test group took 138.90 s; CI timing is pending. The separate 145-line allocation covers this missing admission boundary, which the existing owner-only tests cannot detect.

A separately tested compatibility adaptation on an installed 2026.10.10 build verified an actual target yield, successor completion and one requester final delivered to the original channel topic. That older-build deployment also needed a return adapter. This current-main PR preserves main's newer return path; a fresh current-main model/channel run is not claimed. Hosted CI remains pending.

prs.title: perf(ui): reduce remaining first-visit request waves
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

First visits spend response intervals on small separately fetched helpers, and Skills loads detail and dialog renderers before they are opened. At 100 ms RTT, these assets compete for the browser's six HTTP/1.1 connections.

Related: #194745.

## User Impact

Skills details, its Markdown reader, and library editor/import content load on demand. Small controls, schemas, and catalog helpers travel with existing lazy chunks that already need them. Routes, tags, controls, and styles are preserved. The four lazy component boundaries keep existing owner state and mutation authority; their shared error boundary preserves Close locks and uses the existing guarded stale-chunk recovery.

Custodian keeps its original renderer. A transcript split was removed after repeated measurements found a localhost WebKit greeting regression without a useful 100 ms RTT content win. The stronger greeting benchmark remains: it requires actual rendered Markdown and an enabled composer, whereas the existing Custodian visit measures shell readiness.

This draft is pending final repeated performance acceptance. Auto-merge is not armed.

## Evidence

Baseline: `1ad3ec3d2081f3c7228b5bed8ae95e3821cd609f`. Candidate: `306a81a06118d2d6709a4260ce82b5926994d854`. Immutable bundles use identical fixed comparison metadata on the same machine. No dependency or size ceiling changes.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Refreshed baseline census | Completed: 54 scenarios across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox at 100 ms RTT; 324/324 paired census observations passed. |
| Final acceptance | Running: 20 rotated base/head/A/A triplets in all three engines at 100 ms RTT and localhost. Skills and Skill Settings first; Talk, MCP, Security, Plugins, Plugin Settings, Memory, Templates, and Custodian shell/greeting follow. |
| Strict differential size check | Passed. Startup JS 90,814 → 90,814 B gzip; one startup CSS request. New Session JS −61 B; Chat JS −64 B. CSS unchanged. |
| UI typecheck | Passed on final production source |
| Chunking unit tests | 9/9 passed on final production source |
| Skills view tests | 24/24 passed |
| Skills retry boundary tests | 2/2 passed |
| Census scenario tests | 9/9 passed; tooling test typecheck passed |
| Library upload tests | Initial 20/21; added the existing dialog polyfill for the newly lazy dialog and the failing case passed. |
| Production Knip | Passed on final production source |
| Scoped lint/format and test-line ratchet | Passed |
| Independent review | Complete candidate and subsequent deltas reviewed with Codex autoreview through P2. Final pruning review is clean; no unresolved actionable finding. |

The baseline already exceeds the document and total CSS caps. This change adds no bytes to those surfaces and passes differential enforcement without raising a ceiling.

Request counts are assets completed by browser-local readiness: an upper-bound ready-window measure, not a causal dependency count. `ceil(requests/6)` is a connection-capacity floor. The final table will also report observed request-start bursts and requests outside readiness. Custodian shell readiness is labeled separately from actual greeting readiness. WebKit timings use browser-local application readiness, not driver wall time.

Affected production LOC: 2,364 → 2,487 (+123). Tests: 1,524 → 1,786 (+262). Benchmark tooling: 2,699 → 2,748 (+49). Most source movement extracts existing Skills renderers. The shared boundary supplies loading/error/Close/Retry behavior for four real callers. Solid refactor counts: memos 36 → 36, lazy declarations 0 → 4; no added effects, writable state, DOM queries, listeners, or owner capture.

Final route timing/request/byte tables and inspected synthetic before/after screenshots will be added before marking ready. `ci:full` is set; broad CI starts when this draft becomes ready.

prs.title: fix(telegram): durable final deliveries skip the channel-final transcript mirror
prs.body:
Closes #194783

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: delivered Telegram final replies get no `channel-final` delivery mirror in the session transcript when live preview is off, for example when a plugin registers a modifying `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending` hook.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram finals record the same `channel-final` delivery receipt in the transcript whether they go out through preview finalization, the plain fallback, or core durable delivery. Control UI history and other tools that read the receipt now see it after preview is disabled. Delivery itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable `handled_visible` branch in the Telegram final sender returned before any mirror ran. Core durable delivery also reported the provider-visible `content` only on partial failure, so the channel had no confirmed text it could mirror. ClawSweeper's review pointed out that mirroring the original payload would record text that a message hook may have rewritten.

- **Core (`src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts`):** collects the post-hook text from each confirmed payload's `message_sent` event (`onMessageSentEvent`, already threaded through the durable send) and reports it as `content` on `handled_visible`. `ChannelDeliveryOutcome.content` is already documented as the "final provider-visible text … for this logical payload's terminal observation", so this fills a documented field on the success path instead of adding a new one.
- **Telegram (`bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`):** the `handled_visible` branch writes its channel-final mirror from that confirmed text. It uses the same `hasReplyPayloadFinalDeliveryCapture` guard (dispatcher-owned replies keep their own transcript owner) and the same idempotency sequence as the preview and fallback paths.

Ownership: core durable delivery owns the confirmed post-hook text, and Telegram keeps owning its channel-final receipt. The deprecated `sendBatch` `mirror` parameter is ignored, and automatic destination history deliberately skips the producing conversation, so neither could own this. Each final takes exactly one of the three paths, so it is mirrored once.

## Evidence

- New `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.delivery-transcript.test.ts` › "mirrors a durable final with the confirmed post-hook text": the durable send returns `handled_visible` with hook-rewritten content, and the test asserts exactly one `channel-final` mirror carrying that text. **Red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- New `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.test.ts` › "reports the confirmed post-hook text on a visible final": **red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- Related files, all green: Telegram `final-delivery-lifecycle` 12, `preview.telegram-http` 40, `recovery.telegram-http` 8, `reply-targets.telegram-http` 24, `fallback-topic-media` 4; core `durable-delivery.reload` 25, `run-channel-turn.delivery` 17, `run-channel-turn.finalize` 9, `run-channel-turn.settlement` 3, `delivery-result` 6.
- oxlint (type-aware, tsconfig), oxfmt check, the import-cycle check (0 cycles) and the whitespace diff check are clean.

Gaps: I did not run a live Telegram E2E (it needs bot and user credentials I don't have here), and I did not run a full local typecheck (CI covers it). Other channels' durable `handled_visible` results now also carry `content`. I found no consumer that treats its presence as a partial delivery, and the lifecycle's terminal observation already prefers `content` over `payload.text`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat(backup): omit Doctor migration originals from archives on request
prs.body:
Closes #183277

**Decision needed:** should `openclaw backup create` keep Doctor's retained pre-migration originals
(`<database>.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak` and `.scoped.bak`) in archives?

- **A. Keep them by default and add an opt-out flag (this PR, recommended).** Default archives do not change.
  Operators who already keep a separate pre-upgrade backup can pass `--exclude-migration-backups`.
- B. Omit them by default and add a flag to keep them. This gives smaller archives with no action, but a restored
  archive silently loses the rollback path that `repair-and-recovery.md` tells users to keep with their
  pre-upgrade backups.
- C. No code change, only a docs note on archive size.

I recommend A. It keeps today's recovery coverage, matches the ClawSweeper recommendation on the issue, and
follows the existing opt-in `--exclude-worktree-templates` flag (#190822). If you prefer B, the same matcher and
reporting work with the default flipped.

## What Problem This Solves

Full backup archives carry every retained Doctor original as raw bytes next to the live database snapshot.
That makes archives much larger and slower after each update, with no way to leave the originals out.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can run `openclaw backup create --exclude-migration-backups` to leave Doctor's retained
pre-migration originals out of an archive. Each omitted file is listed as `excluded`. Archives made without the
flag are unchanged.

A restored archive made with the flag cannot roll back the last migration with those originals. The docs say
so. The flag never deletes or changes the originals on disk; `openclaw update cleanup` still owns their
retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The flag matches only Doctor's exact producer names, `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak` and
  `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.scoped.bak`, beside the shared state database and each registered
  agent database. Look-alike names, other `.bak` files, `.postgres.bak` export directories and session-store
  recovery copies stay included.
- The exclusion goes through the backup resource plan, like `--exclude-worktree-templates`. Each omitted file
  appears in `skipped` (kind `migration backup`, reason `excluded`) in the dry-run plan, the text and JSON
  output, and the archive manifest. The reason is not `regenerable`, because these files are recovery
  artifacts.
- The name rule was inline in the migration manifest's restore check. It is now one exported predicate that
  the manifest and backup planning share, so backup cannot drift from what Doctor and update cleanup
  recognize.
- `docs/cli/backup.md` documents the flag and its rollback tradeoff. `repair-and-recovery.md` points to it.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI, real Doctor originals.** On an isolated state directory, OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (latest stable)
created two agents. Current main's `openclaw doctor --fix` then migrated the databases (agent schema 27 to 41,
state 22 to 39), which left three real originals: one agent `.bak`, one state `.bak` and one state `.scoped.bak`.
Each run below is `node openclaw.mjs backup create` from a `pnpm build` of that commit.

| Run | Members | Uncompressed bytes | Originals in archive | Compressed bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main, default `--verify` | 58 | 4,692,781 | 3 (2,158,592 bytes) | 159,413 |
| this PR, default `--verify` | 59 | 4,805,384 | 3 (2,158,592 bytes) | 176,928 |
| this PR, `--exclude-migration-backups --verify` | 56 | 2,647,516 | 0 | 134,042 |

- Main rejects the flag: `OpenClaw does not recognize option "--exclude-migration-backups"`.
- Default archives keep the same member names and sizes on main and on this PR. The one extra member on this PR,
  `state/openclaw.sqlite.seal`, is the state database's clean-close seal. It appeared on disk between the two
  runs and is unrelated to this change.
- On this PR, the default and flagged archives differ only by the three originals. The manifest grows by 724
  bytes for the three new `skipped` entries.
- Main and the default run each warn four times about SQLite files archived as opaque bytes, three of them for
  the originals. The flagged run keeps only the unrelated warning.
- `backup restore` of the flagged archive into a fresh target returns `ok: true` and
  `sqliteInventoryVerified: true`, and restores 56 entries with no `.pre-startup-migration` files. The restored
  agent and state databases pass `PRAGMA integrity_check` at `user_version` 41 and 39, the same as live.
- The three originals on disk have identical SHA-256 before and after all runs.

<details>
<summary>Text output with the flag</summary>

```
Skipped 7 paths:
- workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace (missing)
- agent: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent (covered by ~/.openclaw)
- plugin skills: ~/.openclaw/plugin-skills (regenerable)
- managed state: ~/.openclaw/tmp (regenerable)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-575fa006-78d6-861b-8b22-2d62c7a52f3c.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-575fa006-78d6-861b-8b22-2d62c7a52f3c.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-aa5e7499-c95e-4e0f-a82c-379b91b423d6.scoped.bak (excluded)
```

</details>

**Regression test** (`src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts`, "backup Doctor migration originals"): a
default archive contains full and scoped agent originals and a full state original. A flagged archive omits
exactly those, keeps look-alike names, lists each as `excluded` in the result and manifest, restores, and leaves
the originals on disk. It fails on main (`expected true to be false` on the first flagged archive member check)
and passes with this change. It builds two real archives with `--verify` and restores one: 7.5 s on a
quiet machine, 14.3 s under heavy load (`pnpm test src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:
15 passed).

**Checks run**

- `pnpm test src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed.
- Consumers of the changed plan, manifest predicate and CLI: `backup-resource-inventory`, `backup-shared`,
  `register.backup.product-path`, `register.backup.offsite`, `backup.create-verify`,
  `backup-verify-completeness`, `backup-create.worktrees`, `doctor-migration-backup`,
  `update-command-missing-originals`, `doctor-session-sqlite-recovery-inventory`, `doctor-session-entry-state`:
  all passed.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK. This PR adds an 83-line allocation for the regression, like the record
  for `--exclude-worktree-templates`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: formatting, core and test typechecks, lint, line caps, import cycles and the other guards
  pass. Two checks fail identically on main without this change: `changelog attributions`
  (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.6.8.md`) and the dead export scan (`parseDarwinProcessBirths` in
  `src/process/command-reservation-census.ts`, plus `scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts`). Neither file is
  touched by this PR.

Not covered: PostgreSQL-backed stores (Doctor writes `.postgres.bak` directories there, which this flag does
not touch) and Windows.

prs.title: fix(sessions): Telegram transcript echoes are not recorded on explicit multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #194829

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a gateway with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` and several agents, a delivered Telegram transcript echo (`tools.media.audio.echoTranscript`) is never added to the conversation history. Instead it logs `result was delivered but was not added to the conversation: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, even though the Telegram account is bound to one agent.

## User Impact

User impact: confirmed sends that have no producing turn, such as transcript echoes, are recorded once in the destination conversation of the agent the channel/account binding selects, as the [conversation transcript ownership](docs/refactor/conversation-transcript-ownership.md) rules require. The missing-owner warning goes away for bound destinations. Single-agent and unbound setups behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` (`src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts`) chose the history owner as `producer?.agentId ?? resolveDefaultAgentId(config)`. A preflight transcript echo has no producer, and explicit ownership has no default agent, so `AgentSelectionRequiredError` was thrown before destination lookup could consult the binding. The ownership doc says destination lookup does not need a producer: carried route, producer context, exact local binding, then plugin resolver.

Without a producer, the owner now comes from `resolveAgentRoute` for the destination's channel and account. That reuses the routing owner's binding tiers, and unbound destinations keep the old default-agent fallback, which is the same error when no default exists. Peer-level bindings are still enforced: the existing `belongsToAgent` check re-resolves the route with the destination peer and skips with the documented "belongs to a different agent" diagnostic.

The fix lives in the shared recorder, so other producer-less confirmed sends benefit as well; Telegram code is untouched. This does not overlap #194783, which covers the durable `sendPayload` final mirror.

Accepted edge: the owner is chosen from channel/account bindings before the peer is known. A destination covered only by a peer-specific binding to a different agent than the account binding is skipped with the cross-agent diagnostic, not recorded under the peer's agent.

## Evidence

- New regression `records a producer-less send under the agent its account binding selects (#194829)` in `confirmed-visible-message.integration.test.ts`. It uses explicit ownership, two agents, account bindings and no producer, and the echo lands in `beta`'s conversation.
- Red on `origin/main`: it fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner…`, the same text as the issue's warning. Green with the fix (11/11).
- Consumer suites green: `deliver` 86, `outbound-send-service` 24, `delivery-queue.transcript` 14, `deliver-confirmed-visible` 3, `outbound-send-service.accepted-outcomes` 2, `echo-transcript` 4, `echo-transcript.integration` 2, `audio-preflight` 5, `apply` 29, `media-understanding-runtime` 7, `subagent-announce-text-delivery` 5, `subagent-completion-mirror.integration` 1, `voice-call realtime-handler` 37.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Telegram voice-note round trip, which needs a bot account and an audio provider. The integration test drives the real recorder against real session storage.

prs.title: fix(skills): reject unreadable resource directories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes skill packaging reporting success while silently omitting unreadable resource directories. `Path.rglob` suppresses traversal errors, so an unreadable `assets/` can replace a complete `.skill` with a ZIP containing only `SKILL.md`.

## User Impact

Packaging fails visibly if required resources cannot be enumerated, preserving the existing archive or publishing none for a fresh destination. Restoring permissions permits normal packaging. Unreadable excluded directories remain skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `os.walk` with an error-raising callback at the existing traversal owner. Prune established excluded and staging directories before descent, retaining global archive-relative POSIX ordering and existing no-follow, containment and staged-publication/mode checks. No new permission or storage policy.

Retains @zhangguiping-xydt's original commit and integrates current main, including merged #194700's `strict_timestamps=False` and combined normalized-timestamp/source-preservation/linked-entry tests. Consolidated walk-failure coverage into existing present/absent ZIP-write failure rows without removing assertions. Whole PR tests **+15/-15, net 0**, no allocation; production **+17/-4**.

## Evidence

[New exact-head integration proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194635#issuecomment-6717021920) and [pinned main before/after permission and ZIP evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194635#issuecomment-6710650221).

The actual packaged CLI matrix was re-run once at `0cf674475cbcea6fdf85f41038696f4e45c7dd45`, as UID 1000 in secretless Linux Docker:

- Four unreadable-resource cases independently demonstrate EACCES listing failures; candidate refuses and preserves exact existing bytes or leaves fresh output absent.
- Permission restoration yields the same complete archive hashes and 0600/0644 modes. Unreadable exclusions, optional directory symlinks, internal output and no-debris controls pass.
- Main's recorded baseline reports success with SKILL.md-only archives. No new baseline run is claimed; ordinary in-range source dates and successful archive bytes remain matched.
- Integrated validator/packager suites: **12 passed in 0.04 s**, including epoch/2024/2108 and source-byte/mtime checks. Ruff lint passes. Packaged/source script hashes match.

Earlier review-service preparation failures are historical; the service is repaired and a fresh review of the integrated SHA is requested. This is interpreted packaged-script proof, not full application or Windows/root permission-enforcement certification.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores silently incomplete archives. Blast radius is the bundled packager's resource enumeration. No broader symlink admission, permission relaxation, stored-file cleanup, concurrent-writer coordination or new power-loss guarantee; completed-archive staging and normalized timestamp handling remain intact.

prs.title: improve(mcp-relay): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Connected apps copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The MCP relay **Connected apps** page (`extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.ts`) hard-coded all of its English in the view. The plugin had no translation catalog, so the post-merge locale refresh couldn't translate it. Some of the copy also broke the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: an all-caps eyebrow label, a passive "is required" sentence, "do not" instead of a contraction, and "embedded browser sessions" (which reuses the product noun *session* for a different concept). Errors showed the raw request message as the whole alert, with nothing saying what failed or what to do next.

## Solution

- Added the plugin's English source catalog at `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, at the path `control-ui-plugin-i18n-catalog.ts` derives from `openclaw.controlUi`. The view now reads every string through `translateControlUiMessage`.
- Added `src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts}` on the nostr/whatsapp pattern. This page is plain DOM, not Solid, so `locales.ts` keeps the translated catalog in module state and the page re-renders when it loads. The page also re-renders on host locale changes; date formatting follows the locale too.
- `src/i18n/locales/translated.json` is committed as `{}`. The brief said to leave it absent, but without the file the plugin's Control UI build fails: the unresolved dynamic import trips "Control UI builds must bundle their browser dependencies". The empty file holds no translation values; the locale refresh bot fills it after merge.
- Errors now follow "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The redacted raw message moves under a collapsed **Show details**. The Control UI SDK has no shared disclosure component for plugin pages, so this uses a native `<details>`.
- Static `innerHTML` templates are now `element()` builders, so translated text is only ever set as text content.
- Manifest config hints: `Default Agent` → `Default agent`, and the help text says "new sessions" instead of "new conversations". I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` to match (only the plugin baseline hash changed).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No read access | Read access is required to view connected apps. | You need read access to view connected apps. |
| Consent eyebrow | CONNECTION REQUEST / CONNECT ANOTHER GATEWAY | Connection request / Connect another Gateway (CSS `text-transform: uppercase` keeps the look) |
| Consent, no permission | …permissions do not allow connecting an app. | …permissions don’t allow connecting an app. |
| Revoke hint | Revoking an app ends its MCP access and embedded browser sessions. … | Revoking an app ends its MCP and embedded UI access. … (matches the existing revoke notice) |
| Load failure | *(raw message)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load connected apps. Try again. + Show details |
| Approve / deny failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t connect {app}. Reopen the app’s connection page. / Couldn’t deny {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Revoke failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t revoke {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Pairing failure | *(raw message)* / Pairing failed. Try again. | Couldn’t create a pairing code. Try again. + Show details |
| Invalid relay return | The relay returned an invalid return address. Reopen the app’s connection page. | The relay returned an invalid return address. (now the detail; the next step is in the summary) |
| Config hint label | Default Agent | Default agent |
| Config hint help | Optional agent for new conversations; … | Optional agent for new sessions; … |

Moved into the translation file: **53 keys** (`ui:i18n:verify`: `plugin=mcp-relay keys=53`). About 9 existing strings changed, 6 are new (5 error summaries and "Show details"), and 2 manifest hints changed. The rest moved unchanged.

Left as is on purpose:
- "Gateway owner": an owner principal, not a role name. See the open question below.
- "Full access, including administration": names an activity, not the role.
- `ui-tunnel*` transport errors.
- The model-facing `recommendedPrompts`.

## Impact

- The Connected apps page becomes translatable through the existing locale refresh. English rendering is unchanged except for the copy above.
- The error alert is now a `div` with the summary and a collapsed details element. It got small margin and details styles, so expect a slight visual change in error states.
- Known limit: the page label in the navigation is resolved once at activation (`registerPage` takes a static string), so it stays English until the next activation.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.test.ts`: 7/7 pass. Assertions follow the changed English. The refresh-failure case now checks the summary and that the collapsed (closed) details hold the raw message.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=mcp-relay keys=53 locales=0 unused_translations=0`).
- `pnpm check:changed` on the committed head: all lanes ok, including typecheck extensions and extension tests, lint extensions, format, the dead-export scan, the Control UI i18n catalog, the bundled channel config metadata and the config docs baseline. One check failed, `changelog attributions`, and it fails the same way on `origin/main` (existing `Thanks @steipete-oai` entries in `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` and `2026.7.1.md`). This PR doesn't touch those files.
- Plugin Control UI build (`scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/mcp-relay`): succeeds.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify pass: I removed an unused `Translator` type export that the dead-export scan flagged. There's no new state beyond the error-detail fields and the locale tracking the re-render needs.
- Local review: local ClawSweeper isn't installed on this host, so I used autoreview, the documented fallback (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, merge base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `2cd7495c4c6`, max priority P2). Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that unchanged SDK and build contracts weren't in its context; the build and verify runs above cover them.

Before/after screenshots are pending and will be added before landing (visual gate).

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(teams-meetings): accept newer Microsoft work meeting links
prs.body:
Closes #146824

## What Problem This Solves

The Teams meetings plugin rejects Microsoft's short work invitations and fails to recognize a work meeting after Teams redirects a classic invitation to teams.microsoft.com/light-meetings/launch?coords=.... The latter was reproduced with a private, zero-invitee synthetic meeting: the AI guest was admitted normally, but native status remained inCall=false and speechReady=false, and speak returned spoken=false because neither parser recognized the admitted page. No private invitation or participant data is included here.

## User Impact

Users can supply short work invitations to the existing workflow. Classic work invitations and their observed light-meeting redirect resolve to the same work-thread identity, allowing existing status, recovery, transcript, leave and audio guards to recognize the page without granting authority from a Leave button alone. Different short-link passcodes, work conversations and session owners remain separate.

**This is source/build proof, not a deployed voice fix.** Actual guest admission was observed on unmodified official 2026.10.9; native two-way audio on this candidate remains unqualified. Tenant admission, isolated participant routing, media readiness and trusted-official plugin provenance still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Microsoft documents the short work format [here](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/publicsectorblog/march-2025---microsoft-365-us-public-sector-roadmap-newsletter/4394967). A real admitted-page observation additionally exposed the work-host light-meeting route, which previously existed only for consumer coordinates.

Sanitized observed work coordinate shape:

    {"conversationId":"19:meeting_SYNTHETIC@thread.v2","tenantId":"synthetic","organizerId":"synthetic","messageId":"0"}

One self-contained decoder is called by the Node parser and serialized into the browser parser. It accepts a single bounded Base64 coordinate value containing a flat string-valued JSON object and a valid conversation thread. Duplicate query fields and JSON keys (including escaped key spellings), malformed coordinates and unsafe origins are rejected. Its thread must equal the session's expected classic work thread; it does not derive a work thread from a numeric short meeting ID. Existing consumer coordinates are unchanged. Session ownership and request-owned cleanup are not relaxed.

No dependency, permission, trust-policy, workflow, configuration, or production-installation change is included.

## Review Follow-up

Earlier actionable ClawSweeper findings remain addressed: login guidance follows ownership denial without granting login pages meeting controls; the caption-rerender fixture proves its observer was installed before detaching the old control. The restored short-link audio-capture ownership regression remains intact and is not removed by this follow-up.

## Evidence

- Candidate: 28d1c0659d6b6ec1ddaeb6946441694093c807c4. Follow-up base: f7b2da91097e6e575401cc9b5faef8ee63ea260d. That prior head's CI was green; it is not candidate CI.
- 57 focused tests pass (33 work-light regressions plus 24 URL tests), using the repository's Vitest runner with a local configuration projecting the SDK's pure page-script factory to its **actual source owner**. Generated status/leave/audio scripts and ownership logic are real, not stubbed. This bounded local run does not replace the normal extension CI suite.
- The restored short-link audio ownership test file is unchanged. Broader sibling suites could not collect locally under this bounded projection (they also require the wider SDK adapter factory); the normal CI harness has now run them successfully, as recorded below. Normal local extension config and guarded lint cannot load against the pre-existing dependency tree (missing proc-safe/Solid tooling and the required TypeScript fork). No dependencies were installed or altered to conceal that mismatch. These local environment gaps are now covered by the passing current-head CI jobs below; they are not relabeled as local passes.
- The new decoder passes strict TypeScript compilation with unchecked-index checking. Complete plugin source bundles successfully in ordinary and minified ESM builds with host SDK imports external. Formatting and diff whitespace checks pass. These are not release packaging or installation qualification.
- Tests exercise both parsers, actual status/leave/audio scripts, cross-host and malformed/duplicate fields, mismatched conversation/meeting identities, consumer controls, stale session owners and leave-pending rejection. The regression fails on the base.
- Independent review found a nested-shadow duplicate-key bypass in the initial local decoder. Raw flat-object grammar is now validated before token deduplication, with three real Node/browser regressions for shadowed object/array values. Independent read-only subagent review of the complete five-file change against f7b2da91097e6e575401cc9b5faef8ee63ea260d, followed by a focused security correction review, found no remaining blocking findings on this candidate. This is independent source review, not ClawSweeper or autoreview. The reviewer identified a pre-existing consumer-coordinate base64 Node/browser parity gap; consumer semantics are intentionally unchanged here and that hardening is follow-up scope. Exact-head CI has completed successfully; the separately requested hosted ClawSweeper review completed and requests real candidate authority-chain proof, not another source change.

## CI on the Current Head

[CI run 41193134299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193134299) completed **successfully** for `28d1c0659d6b6ec1ddaeb6946441694093c807c4`. The [normal changed-extension harness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193134299/job/124514087634) passed **186 tests across 7 Teams files** (178/6 plus 8/1): work-light, URL, short-link, platform-adapter, caption capture, caption ownership and runtime. This includes the restored short-link audio ownership regression and does not use the local SDK projection. Production types, test types and guarded lint all pass; `openclaw/ci-gate` is success. No workflow rerun was requested. This is selected repository CI, not every repository test or live deployment proof.

[Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146828#issuecomment-5651874677) completed for this exact head via [run 41193411634](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41193411634). prs.title: fix(muse): settle canceled startup without stopping other callers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cancellation waiting for Muse initialization, and prevents one canceled startup caller from stopping another caller sharing the same host.

## User Impact

Canceling a Muse attempt during startup settles without requiring a successful initialization. Other callers sharing the startup remain usable, and the last canceled waiter waits for host teardown. Already-leased warm hosts remain protected. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the attempt’s existing abort signal into the existing Muse pool. Keep cancellation ownership per waiting caller while retaining the SDK’s subprocess teardown owner. This does not change accepted-turn, busy-resume, permission, or reset policy and does not add an adapter.

Related work: #183676 covers busy-resume/approval observation/retention; this change avoids those implementation hunks. The README automatic-selection contradiction is a separate follow-up, not part of this PR.

## Evidence

- Public base: `ade7c07d4c70a08ea0b294de27ddc519120e817e`.
- Base: deliberately withheld initialization makes the harness cancellation test time out; canceling one of two startup callers kills the surviving caller’s peer. The existing verification cancellation control passes.
- Candidate: **59/59 tests passed** across Muse harness, runtime, and verification suites. Includes stopped-peer/no-dispatch/no-binding checks, a surviving startup caller completing a real model-list request, and the existing warm-host control.
- These are **synthetic owning-path tests** using production Muse code, the pinned SDK, and a disposable MSP subprocess, not live Muse or whole-Gateway proof. No credentials or provider calls used.
- Targeted source and package-boundary typechecks, focused lint/format, whitespace, and test-line ratchet passed. The +116 test-line allocation is exactly the two distinct boundary regressions; existing fixture/control coverage is reused.
- Independent native Auto Review on the complete local candidate against that base: **P0/P1 scoped-clean**, no findings. It did not independently execute tests or validate live behavior. The published head `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1` was fetched from the public PR and its Muse tree matches the reviewed/tested candidate exactly. The range from the stated base contains only the six intended files.

- Exact-head supplemental Auto Review: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no findings, commit `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1`. Static only; the initial preparation rejected symlinked SDK evidence. A tracked-evidence run completed without that SDK input and explicitly did not independently verify SDK teardown semantics or execute tests.
- The coordinator reports an independent read-only Codex review, `muse_exact_head_review`, **P0–P3 substantive coverage, no actionable findings**, on all six changed files and their pool/harness lifecycle, catalog caller, abort helper, fixture, and boundary contracts. Reviewed tree: `e783c1657b96233c41b8341b81f07592e2876009`, matched to the published head by full-tree and six-blob comparisons. This reviewer executed no code; this is not live Muse, whole-Gateway, Windows, CI, or hosted ClawSweeper proof.
- Publication parent `3c2fd048d9917e7d41dcd6aa4eba12cfcb9f7afc` has the same tree as reviewed base `ade7c07d4c70a08ea0b294de27ddc519120e817e`; it introduces no source drift.
- Additional finite-sweep coverage on the unchanged candidate: **29/29** existing tests passed (native-catalog precedence, Muse event finalization, registration cleanup), 62.23s wrapper. These supplement, rather than replace, the 59 startup/consumer tests.
- PR is non-draft at this head. [Product CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42429030746) completed successfully at `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1`: 25 successful jobs, 30 intentionally skipped, no failed or unfinished jobs; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. Successful automation/security-gate jobs are not presented as a substantive code review.
- [Published ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194884#issuecomment-6716788694) from [successful review run 42442999394](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42442999394), for exact head `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1` against captured base `d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1`: **no actionable findings**, **Before merge: None**, and **Ready for maintainer review**.
