prs.title: fix(test): reject malformed PID receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The test helper previously accepted PID receipt text with a valid numeric prefix, such as `42stale`, because `parseInt` stopped at the first non-decimal character.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the complete trimmed receipt as a positive safe decimal integer before returning it, while preserving the existing AbortSignal lifecycle.

## User Impact

Test and CI cleanup helpers no longer treat contaminated PID receipts as real process identifiers.

## Evidence

- Current head: `9b1d0b815a00887d49b0f40f27b56d61b755e0d4`.
- Baseline source reproduction: current `main` at `c0081c581549cdbed5b3111d70fc7d9a0a4f2c7d` still uses `Number.parseInt`, so `42stale` is accepted as PID 42.
- Claim-matched direct helper proof: a temporary-file harness accepted `4242` and rejected `42stale`, `42\njunk`, `4.2`, and `0x2a` with the abort diagnostic.

  ```text
  strict PID receipt proof passed
  ```

- Regression coverage includes trailing text, newline-separated junk, fractional, and hexadecimal receipts while preserving newline-terminated decimal receipts.
- Supporting checks: `oxfmt --check test/helpers/process-wait.ts test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Proof boundary: this proves complete PID receipt parsing in the shared test helper and regression fixture only; it makes no production runtime or platform-specific claim.

prs.title: fix(auth): stop automatic session accounts from vetoing strict CLI routes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A session's machine-chosen model-account binding (`authProfileOverrideSource: "auto"`) was fed into the CLI runtime auth evaluation as if the user had selected that account. `evaluateCliRuntimeModelAuthAvailability` collapsed both fields into one value:

```ts
const selectedProfileId = ref.pinnedProfileId?.trim() || ref.preferredProfileId?.trim();
```

and then, for a backend declaring `strictSelectedProfile` (`claude-cli`, `nativeAuthProfileIds: ["anthropic:claude-cli"]`), the non-pinned branch returned the untouched provider-only `evaluation`:

```ts
return ref.pinnedProfileId
  ? evaluateProviderAuth(provider, { modelId: ref.modelId, requiredProfileId: selectedProfileId })
  : evaluation;
```

For Anthropic through `claude-cli` that provider-only evaluation has no credential evidence, so every Anthropic row came back `available: false` / `unavailableReason: "missing-auth"` whenever the session's automatic account happened to belong to another provider (OpenAI in the report). The credential was never missing: the CLI's own login is prepared on the route (`preparedRuntimeAuthModes["claude-cli"]`), and the executor already agrees that an automatic preference is a preference, not a constraint — `resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId` deliberately ignores a selection whose `authProfileIdSource` is `"auto"` (`src/agents/cli-execution-auth.ts:60-92`).

Only an explicit pin is a selection now; an automatic preference falls through to the prepared native-runtime result for the route, which is the fact the UI needs to stop disabling every Claude row.

### Changes

- `src/agents/model-auth-availability.ts` — the `strictSelectedProfile` veto requires `ref.pinnedProfileId`, and the non-pinned fall-through that returned the provider-only evaluation is gone. Pinned-profile and `requiredProfileId` behavior is unchanged.
- `src/agents/model-auth-availability.test.ts` — regression coverage: an automatic account owned by another provider keeps the native CLI route `available: true` (`evidence: "runtime"`), while an explicit pin of that same account is still refused.

## Evidence

Pre-fix (base-commit implementation restored in the worktree), the new regression case fails with the reported verdict — the automatic preference vetoes the route and the provider-only evaluation comes back indeterminate:

      Tests  1 failed | 52 passed (53)

```

Adjacent suites that drive the same evaluator (session pins, native runtimes, reason classification, catalogue recovery, CLI runtime availability in `models.list`) all pass:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/model-auth-availability.session-pin.test.ts src/agents/model-auth-availability.native.test.ts src/agents/model-auth-availability.reasons.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
      Tests  67 passed (67)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models.catalog-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism

exit=0

Closes #142781

好的 runtime-auth 结果（`evidence:"runtime"`）→ 行可用。显式 pin 对照行为不变。

## 2. 证据层级：哪层真、哪层 stub

**真实（真跑，非 mock）**

prs.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): model discovery no longer hangs on repeated page tokens
prs.body:
No linked issue: found during a proactive source audit of provider discovery pagination.

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic Amazon Bedrock model discovery can loop indefinitely when `ListInferenceProfiles` returns a previously seen pagination token.

## Why This Change Was Made

The discovery owner tracks returned tokens and fails when one repeats, including multi-token cycles. The original nine-line production guard is preserved while resolving the current-main conflict. Tests cover strict failure, complete retry without a poisoned cache, and three advancing pages.

## User Impact

A cyclic response now reports a failed catalog refresh instead of hanging. Strict catalog acquisition remains all-or-nothing; successful pagination still collects every page. The public advisory failure behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `abf88cbc0a4484faeab8f80db4ce35200f6ff53e`; current head `9813e447c5ac6e84a05f90550427c286a91f772e` adapts the existing tests to the current SDK mock and keeps the token guard. Current-head CI is pending. All results below refer to the earlier commits identified there.

- Conflict repair based on main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `656559337ad7454e05a500206fe7ca783393f3fa`. Only two files changed: production +9 lines, tests +69 lines.
- Red-before on that main: both repeated-token and multi-token-cycle regressions fail; 33 other discovery tests, including the advancing-page control, pass.
- Green-after: `pnpm test:extension amazon-bedrock --maxWorkers=1` passed all 254 tests across 14 files in 44.9 seconds wall time (251 regular tests plus 3 temporary transport proofs). The added regression cases each took 3–4 ms. The temporary proof was removed after validation.
- Real AWS SDK transport proof used `BedrockClient` serialization, SigV4 signing, HTTP transport, and response deserialization against a controlled localhost peer. All requests carried AWS4 signatures with synthetic fixture credentials. No live AWS account or AWS endpoint was used. On current main, the repeated-token case made a third profile request and the three-token cycle made a fourth, reaching an HTTP-409 sentinel. The candidate stopped after two and three profile requests respectively with the expected pagination error.
- For both failing transport cases, the next call reacquired the complete foundation list and all three healthy profile pages; a subsequent successful call reused the cache. The independent advancing-page control also returned the complete four-model catalog on both revisions.
- Mutation control: deliberately retaining the rejected cache entry made both new recovery tests fail. The exact validated production source was restored afterward.
- Fresh isolated autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. Formatting, conflict-marker checks, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, assertion-safety ratchet, timeout-race ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- On the exact candidate commit, `pnpm test extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 35/35 tests in 35.55 seconds wall time (32.73 seconds Vitest duration, dominated by transformation).
- Targeted type-aware lint passed: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` (3m32s including the first plugin-SDK declaration build).
- [Fresh-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37097599385) passed for `656559337ad7454e05a500206fe7ca783393f3fa`. The [Bedrock CI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37097599385/job/111130806457) passed all 251 tests in 13 files: 33.96 seconds Vitest duration, 94 seconds job wall time. The new repeat, cycle, and advancing tests took 2 ms, 3 ms, and 2 ms respectively. Raw GitHub mergeability was clean after CI.
- Local validation was scoped as listed above; a separate full build, full-repository typecheck, and aggregate check were not run locally.

The earlier signed-transport proof on `c2f1c562000754490c9a22bd3017885aa92a1294` remains documented in the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145758#issuecomment-5644469536); the current-main proof above was rerun for this repair.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex was used for source review, implementation, and test authoring; all listed validation was run and inspected directly.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.

prs.title: fix: model catalog scan starves the gateway event loop on large catalogs
prs.body:
Closes #145675
Related: #138139

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with a large configured model catalog (hundreds of provider entries) would experience the Gateway becoming fully unresponsive to all concurrent traffic -- dashboard, chat channels, RPC -- for the duration of a catalog evaluation pass. Concurrent requests, including a plain HTTP request to `/healthz`, get no response at all until the scan finishes; from the outside this looks like the Gateway went offline.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createModelsListEntryEvaluator` scheduled every catalog entry as an independent `Promise.resolve().then(...)`, so a large catalog ran as one uninterrupted microtask batch with no point where control returned to the event loop between entries. The fix chains entries through a single tail promise and yields back to the event loop (via `setImmediate`) roughly every 8ms of wall-clock time spent evaluating, instead of letting every entry run in the same batch. No evaluation result, cache key, or ordering guarantee changes -- only *when* each result becomes available.

Separately, this also adds a smaller, always-correct improvement to `providerConfigMatchesRuntimeSnapshot` (called from within each entry's evaluation): a deep-equal shortcut before the two `hashRuntimeConfigValue` calls, for the common case of structurally-identical-but-not-reference-identical provider configs. This is related to #138139 but does not fully close it -- that issue's suggested identity-keyed memoization breaks an existing test that models in-place runtime-config mutation (`keeps distinct configurations current after runtime mutation and replacement`); details in [my comment on that issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138139#issuecomment-5644065185). This PR takes the safe subset (a fresh-every-call shortcut, never stale) rather than the full memoization. (Note: #138351 has since merged a separate, narrower shared-object shortcut for that same function; this PR's `isDeepStrictEqual` addition targets the different, still-uncovered case of distinct-but-equal objects.)

## User Impact

The Gateway keeps answering concurrent requests while a large model-catalog scan runs, instead of appearing to hang or go offline until the scan completes.

## Evidence

### Real production reproduction (2026.9.4, before the fix existed)

This defect was found by diagnosing a live incident, not by reading the source in the abstract. On the affected install, while a catalog scan was in flight:

```text
$ top -bn1 -H -p <gateway-pid>
  PID USER  PR  NI  VIRT   RES   SHR S  %CPU %MEM  TIME+  COMMAND
 <pid> ...  20   0  27.6g  1.0g  ...  R  93.9  1.6  7:42.90 MainThread

$ curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code} in %{time_total}s\n" http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz
HTTP 000 in 5.002484s

$ openclaw gateway health
gateway timeout after 10000ms
```

After applying this fix and restarting:

```text
$ openclaw gateway health
Gateway Health
OK (79ms)
Telegram: configured

$ openclaw gateway call health
{ "ok": true, "eventLoop": { "degraded": false, "reasons": [] }, ... }
```

### Controlled before/after measurement (isolated repro, this checkout)

To get a clean, repeatable A/B measurement (not just the live incident above), I wrote a small standalone script (not part of this diff) that:
- builds the same `createModelCatalogDecisions` owner used by the real Gateway, with a synthetic 500-entry catalog across two providers,
- starts a real local HTTP server sharing the process's event loop (the closest same-process analog to the Gateway's own `/healthz` handler),
- fires real concurrent HTTP requests against it every 5ms while `Promise.all(entries.map(owner.evaluateEntry))` runs,
- measures actual request latency, success/timeout counts, total scan time, and process RSS.

Ran 3 times each on `main` (unpatched) and on this branch (patched), Node v24.19.0:

| | Unpatched (`main`) | Patched (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrent requests attempted per run | ~18 | ~18 |
| Concurrent requests that **succeeded** | **1** (all 3 runs) | **17-18** (all 3 runs) |
| Concurrent requests that timed out | 0 (rest just never got a chance to run before the scan ended) | 0 |
| Median successful-request latency | 1653-1772ms (i.e. the one request that got through waited almost the entire scan) | 10ms |
| Scan wall time (500 entries) | 1627-1742ms | 1747-2519ms* |
| Process RSS delta during scan | +10MB | +10-21MB |

\* Slightly higher on the patched side -- expected, since the scan now periodically yields to the event loop instead of running flat-out; this is the traded-off cost of staying responsive, not a regression in per-entry work.

Raw output, patched run 1:
```json
{"entries":500,"scanElapsedMs":2519,"concurrentRequestsDuringScan":17,"concurrentRequestsSucceeded":17,"concurrentRequestsTimedOut":0,"maxRequestLatencyMs":2210,"medianRequestLatencyMs":10,"rssBeforeMb":627,"rssAfterMb":648}
```
Raw output, unpatched run 1:
```json
{"entries":500,"scanElapsedMs":1627,"concurrentRequestsDuringScan":1,"concurrentRequestsSucceeded":1,"concurrentRequestsTimedOut":0,"maxRequestLatencyMs":1653,"medianRequestLatencyMs":1653,"rssBeforeMb":630,"rssAfterMb":640}
```

Honest caveat: in every patched run, the very first concurrent request (only) landed before the first yield point and took longer than the steady-state 10ms median (up to ~2.2s) -- consistent with it racing the initial synchronous batch of promise-chain construction before any yield has occurred yet. Every subsequent request in every patched run was fast and none timed out; in the unpatched baseline, only that first request *ever* got serviced at all, and only once the whole scan had nearly finished.

### Test coverage

- Added a regression test (`yields to the event loop instead of monopolizing it across a large catalog scan`) that mocks `performance.now()` to force the yield threshold and asserts `setImmediate` is invoked. Verified it fails without the fix and passes with it (confirmed via `git stash`/`git checkout main --` before finalizing).
- Existing coverage for the deep-equal shortcut: `provider config structural comparison > matches a equivalent clone` in `model-auth.test.ts` already exercises the structurally-identical/different-reference case this shortcut targets, and still passes.
- Full targeted lane: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/model-auth.test.ts src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.test.ts` -- 110/110 passing.
- `pnpm tsgo` (core typecheck) clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on all three changed files.

prs.title: fix(ui): quiet pending steer states
prs.body:
## Problem

Pending steers from #193665 work well, but a few edges are rough:

- Messages that cannot be sent early show a warning-styled line under every waiting bubble (`Waiting for exec; cannot interrupt safely.`), using internal tool names.
- A refused **Send now** puts a sticky notice above the composer (`Sending a pending steer now requires session write access.` / `The conversation changed…`). It stays there after the user sends new messages, so it reads as if those failed.
- Several waiting messages each show their own row (**Send now** or a warning), which is redundant: waiting steers are delivered together.
- A pending bubble can show the delivered footer (sender, time, copy/comment/rewind) on hover or focus next to **Send now**, and pending bubbles sit at different spacing than delivered ones.
- Viewers without steer access see nothing under their pending message.

## Solution

Presentation-only changes in the Control UI. The Gateway, steering lifecycle and **Send now** interruption are unchanged.

- **One row for all waiting steers.** Waiting steers drain together at the next model boundary, so a single **Send now** sits under the newest steer that can interrupt. When none can (or the viewer cannot steer), the newest shows a muted **Steering…** label instead. Example: three rapid messages where only the first two can interrupt → **Send now** under the second, nothing else.
- **Plain copy.** **Steering…** has no spinner; the reason is on hover and is the accessible name: “Steering — sends when the current step finishes.” or “…on the next model turn.” No tool names.
- **Permission-aware.** **Send now** renders only when the viewer can steer (already gated by session access). Everyone else sees **Steering…**.
- **No composer notice for Send now.** A refused or failed **Send now** refreshes the pending list and the row shows its current state. Dismiss errors still use the notice.
- **Delivered spacing.** Steer rows use the same footer and action-row slots delivered messages use, so bubbles keep identical positions before and after delivery. Sender, timestamp and footer actions appear once the message is delivered.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui.md`, `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md`.

Accepted edge: if a viewer loses steer access while **Send now** is on screen, the click is refused quietly and the message stays queued.

## Screenshots

Before → after screenshots (mocked Gateway, synthetic content) are attached in comments below. The latest comment shows the four states with identical bubble positions.

## Evidence

- Component tests: `chat-message` (including row assignment across steers waiting together), group, markdown, queue/steer lifecycle, pending-inputs pagination, session-controls and transcript projection suites — 104 passed.
- Browser e2e `chat-flow.messaging` (10 passed): one **Send now** on the newest sendable steer; an earlier sendable steer carries it when the newest cannot interrupt; refused Send now shows no composer notice; blocked steers show one **Steering…**; Send now still delivers.
- Measured bubble positions in the mocked Control UI are identical for all-blocked, all-sendable, first-two-sendable and delivered states.
- Real Gateway proof `chat-steer-send-now.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` with `OPENCLAW_STEER_NOW_PROOF=fixed` passed on this revision.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on touched files, stylelint, format check, `git diff --check`; `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` on the first revision.
- Foreign locales show English for the changed strings until the locale refresh workflow runs.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(deep-research): keep the idle session header free of research chrome
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the bundled Deep Research plugin enabled, every Control UI conversation showed two research entry points: the
`header` action button and a full-width `session-header` bar. The bar was not reporting anything — with no research job it
fell back to the literal label `Deep research`, so idle conversations carried research chrome with no state behind it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/deep-research/browser/index.tsx` registers the accessory with `placement: "session-header"`, and its
component rendered a button unconditionally, substituting `"Deep research"` when `snapshot().job` was null. The accessory
now renders only when it has something to say — an active job (`Research · <phase>` plus source counts) or an offline
client — and renders nothing otherwise.

The `header` action stays untouched, so the single discoverable entry point, keyboard access to the panel, and access to
retained reports are unchanged; only the empty state loses the redundant bar.

## User Impact

An idle conversation no longer shows a research bar under the header. Once research runs, the bar appears with the same
phase/progress text as before, and an offline client still reports itself. Nothing changes for the panel, the reports, or
the header button.

## Evidence

New component test `extensions/deep-research/browser/accessory.test.tsx` (jsdom, real Solid render, stub client):

- idle snapshot (`{ offline: false, job: null }`) → the accessory renders **no** button and empty text;
- active job → button with `Research · searching · 2 sources`;
- offline client → `Research · offline`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: release backport discovery can present a conflict-free patch as a complete applicability verdict even when the candidate is outside the pinned main scan or its runtime caller and prerequisite contracts remain unverified.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible runtime change. Release operators receive provenance-bound, explicitly patch-only evidence and must complete caller-chain and prerequisite review before qualifying a backport.

## Why This Change Was Made

The probe now requires a pinned scan end, rejects candidates that are not ancestors of it, and separates patch status from the overall qualification, which remains contract-review-required. The release runbook names the runtime reachability, caller-chain, and prerequisite checks that remain manual.

This intentionally changes the internal CLI/API/TSV contract so old consumers fail closed instead of treating clean as a complete verdict. Repository callers and documentation are updated; no repository TSV parser exists.

RRI-606

- Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, test-lines ratchet, and git diff check pass.

prs.title: fix(ui): show elapsed time in main-chat subagent rows
prs.body:
Fixes #194737

## What Problem This Solves

The main-chat Subagents card omits per-child elapsed labels even though the same runs have timing in the Subagents panel. Its bounded collection projection drops the existing session timing, and its collection row has no elapsed renderer. Ordinary child-session rows already show their time.

## User Impact

Started collection rows now show elapsed time beside their names, using the same existing component and styling as ordinary rows. Queued rows stay blank; a completed child's label stops at its recorded end time. The separate Subagents panel is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry only the existing `startedAt`/`endedAt` fields through the bounded display receipt and render the shared `ElapsedTime` component in the collection row. Real browser proof confirmed that projection alone was insufficient, so both omissions are repaired. No new clock, formatter, layout rules, child hydration, routing or configuration. Reported by @tre1d.

## Evidence

Exact head `9687a384dcda6fe50b22bfbd903a91c6d28711f6`, compared with main `fe2b1a51b41b80941fe93cfb0dfbdc0def2401d1`.

[Observed real-run receipts, inspected side-by-side screenshots and measured gzip deltas](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194778#issuecomment-6712313561).

Built Gateway + built Control UI, real Linux Chromium, **main twice and candidate twice**. A real parent agent run executes five `sessions_spawn` calls in two waves (3+2), then collects all results with `agents_wait`. A deterministic local Responses fixture controls model output/completion timing; no live-provider or model-quality claim. An independent ordinary child-session run supplies the adjacent parity control.

Main shows no collection clocks; candidate shows all five after admission, advancing active clocks and a frozen terminal clock. Queued labels remain blank. Ordinary rows and the native Subagents panel keep their behavior. Inspected before/after screenshots include both the collection and ordinary row; actual served UI asset hashes and client build IDs identify the compared builds.

Paired official served-gzip measurement: startup **+27 B**, chat boot **−33 B**, combined **−6 B** (hash-normalized combined **+47 B**), within the 600 B limit. No latency/optimization claim. All **48 focused tests pass**; the timing projection and row-rendering regressions fail on main. Tests **net 0**, production **+14/−1**, no test-line allocation. The existing Details guide documents started/queued/finished labels.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous presentation. Receipt fields are already supported by the schema; no migration, preference or public API changes. Blast radius is compact collection-row timing in main-chat Details on desktop/mobile. The separate panel, ordinary-row clock and Gateway timing authority remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(matrix): answer an attachment and the text typed with it as one turn
prs.body:
Related: #161505

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent replies to a bare attachment and then separately to the user's question when a Matrix client without caption support (for example Element Web) sends the file and the typed text as two messages.

## User Impact

Operators can set `channels.matrix.mediaHoldMs` (or `accounts.<id>.mediaHoldMs`) so a captionless attachment waits briefly for the sender's next text and both are answered in one turn. Default `0` keeps today's behavior. When enabled, an attachment sent on its own is answered only after the wait (maximum 60 s). A held attachment keeps its place in the durable inbound queue, so a Gateway restart delivers it again instead of dropping it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hold sits between Matrix durable ingress (#176491) and the room message handler. A captionless attachment is buffered in the plugin SDK keyed inbound debouncer (keyed by room and thread); its delivery returns `deferred`, so the attachment keeps its own ingress claim while the room lane stays free for the text. The sender's next plain text joins it and becomes the attachment's caption, the same shape caption-capable clients already send, so existing caption handling produces one turn. The merged turn runs under `fanInChannelIngressLifecycles` of both claims: adoption, deferral, failure and abandonment settle both together, and a turn the handler drops before adoption still consumes both claims. Nothing is re-claimed and nothing is replayed. Any other message in the conversation (another sender, a second attachment, a poll, a location, a reaction), a control command, or the deadline dispatches the held attachment alone first; the debouncer holds the keyed lane until that turn is admitted, so a following `/stop` cannot overtake it. Control commands are recognised with the handler's own normalisation (route, mention patterns, display name) through one shared helper the handler now also uses. Voice messages and captioned attachments are never held. When the monitor closes, held claims are handed back (`onCancelled`) instead of starting turns, and a claim the drain aborts is dropped silently. The setting is Matrix-only, following the triage note that a global queue setting would widen the immediate-media policy to channels that don't need it.

Rebased onto main after #176491. Findings from the first review: the keyed lane is now held through admission (debouncer flush lifecycle); no synthetic replay claim exists any more (each event keeps its durable claim); command normalisation is shared with the handler; polls and locations flush the hold; encrypted double emission and cold-start history no longer reach the hold (ingress deduplicates by event id and skips historical rows before dispatch); the account-level override is bounded like the top-level field.

Second review round (Codex on `92913c1b5a`): an event the server already bundles a replacement for now bypasses the hold like redactions and edits (never folded, never held), and media without `filename` whose body is a single-line file name with an extension (pre-MSC2530 clients, for example `vacation photo.jpg`) is held as captionless; the handler's own caption heuristic is unchanged. Tests added for both. Third round: a reaction's thread is only known after its target is fetched, so a reaction now releases every attachment held in its room before it is dispatched, instead of being keyed at room level; test added. Fourth round: a text joins a held attachment only if its server timestamp is within the hold window of the attachment's (a replay after downtime drains old events back to back); the hold's command check reads the runtime's live config snapshot like normal ingress and uses the canonical `isControlCommandMessage` predicate, so bare abort triggers such as `stop` release the attachment first; tests added. Fifth round: a reaction also waits for attachments already on their way to a turn (flushed but not yet admitted) before it is dispatched, and a claim that cannot be reopened on close is logged rather than left as an unobserved rejection; tests added. Sixth round: the hold is measured from the attachment's server timestamp, so a replay after a restart keeps the original deadline (and an attachment already past it is not held at all) instead of starting a new window; a reaction releases held attachments only when the reaction handler could act on it (it targets one of the bot's own messages), never for a reaction to the held attachment itself or to another user's message; tests added. Seventh round: an attachment replayed after an outage longer than the hold still waits for the companion text that is already queued behind it in the lane (`readLaneBacklog`), so recovery stays one turn; when the reaction target lookup fails, ordering is preserved (the hold is released) rather than skipped; key-verification traffic bypasses the hold like the handler ignores it; the encrypted scenario also asserts no second reply; tests added. Eighth round: the hold reads reaction targets with the handler's own `extractMatrixReactionAnnotation` (a reaction without an explicit `rel_type` is recognised), and the expired-replay companion check applies the same ignored-event predicate as the classifier (edits, bundled replacements, verification traffic, the bot's own events never count as companions); tests added. Ninth round: the hold now uses the reaction handler's own preflight (`resolveMatrixReactionMayStartWork`: approval target, notification mode, target ownership, lookup failure preserves order), and the command check routes by the same effective thread as normal ingress (`resolveMatrixThreadRouting`); tests added.

Tenth round (ClawSweeper on `025c5c3d961`; the ninth-round commit above already covered its reaction-preflight and thread-routing findings): the two recovery cases the earlier body listed as known limits are now handled. (1) Encrypted companions: an expired replayed attachment decrypts queued companion ciphertext through the same local SDK path ingress uses for each delivery (`hydrateEvents`) before it judges it. Ciphertext that cannot be decrypted yet (late room key) still counts when its envelope fits (same sender, within the hold by server time, same thread relation, which stays in clear): the attachment then waits one hold window, and the text is checked again by the normal join rules when the lane delivers it decrypted, so a wrong guess costs at most that bounded wait. (2) Partly admitted catch-up batches: Matrix sync admission now shows each sync batch to the hold (`onSyncBatch`) until every event in it is durable, so an expired attachment that the drain delivers before the rest of its batch is admitted still finds the text that follows it. Nothing in the durable-ingress contract changes: no stored payload, ordering or claim behaviour differs, and nothing runs when `mediaHoldMs` is 0. Also fixed: the previous head's CI failure (`index.test.ts` runtime mock lacked `getOptionalMatrixRuntime`, which the shared reaction preflight's approval-reaction state reads). Tests added for each case, plus two live scenarios (below).

Rebuilt on current main (`ac13a7e0c13`, 2026-10-24) as one commit: main moved the Matrix config UI hints into `config-schema.ts` (the `mediaHoldMs` hint moved with them), inlined the reaction handler's notification mode (now one helper the handler and the hold share), and slimmed the QA scenario contract (`{ details }` executions, no actor cursor bookkeeping); the scenarios follow it.

Eleventh round: rebased on current main (`1f7035c15f3`, 2026-11-07) as one commit, `f31c19123c5`. Main now includes #192585 (`c2cb56c665e`), the core fix for #192522, which is the error the previous evidence recorded for `matrix-media-hold-command-ordering` (`ReplaySafeTranscriptConflictError` when a `/status` arrives while a turn on the same session is still preparing). Nothing in the hold changed since the tenth round. Other changes: the index test runtime mock passes the real module through (`importOriginal`) and overrides only `getMatrixRuntime` / `setMatrixRuntime`, so the mock-exports ratchet accepts it and its baseline entry is pruned; the total test-lines ratchet gets an allocation for the 1049 test lines this change adds (`config/test-lines-allocations/matrix-media-hold.txt`: `media-hold.test.ts`, the ingress sync-batch case, the runtime mock); generated config metadata and docs baseline are regenerated on this base. The command-ordering result on this base is in Evidence: it now passes most runs but still fails intermittently in core, with a different error.

The bound the setting advertises, no attachment waits longer than `mediaHoldMs` past its own server timestamp (or one window after a recovery replay), holds in every case.

Config surface: `channel` count 4003 -> 4005 for the two bounded `mediaHoldMs` fields (top-level and per-account).

## Evidence

Exact head `f31c19123c5`, on main `1f7035c15f3` (2026-11-07), run on a throwaway Linux x86 box.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-matrix.config.ts extensions/matrix`: 129 files, 1190 tests pass (includes `media-hold.test.ts`, 33 cases).
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ingress.test.ts`: 5/5.
- `vitest.extension-qa.config.ts` over the scenario catalog, coverage report, scenario selection, live scenario timeouts and the Matrix live-transport units: 53 files, 422 tests pass.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 1f7035c15f3`: all nine pass (max-lines, assertion-safety, database-dialect, timeout-race, mock-exports, test-lines, config-docs, plugin-inventory, database-worker). `pnpm config:channels:check` and `pnpm config:docs:check` clean; `pnpm build` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean; oxlint, oxfmt and `pnpm lint:docs` clean; the pre-commit hook ran and passed.
- Data model: nothing stored changes. No ingress payload, SQLite, session or migration change; the two `mediaHoldMs` keys are optional and additive; nothing new runs when `mediaHoldMs` is 0.
- **Live behaviour proof (QA Lab Matrix lane, real Tuwunel homeserver + real Gateway + the real Matrix plugin, `--provider-mode mock-openai`)**: `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --scenario …`, **7 of 7 pass** on the exact head in one run (report below). The mock provider answers the image prompt with the image's colours only when the image reached that turn, so a colour reply proves one turn.
  - `matrix-media-hold-attachment-then-text`, `-standalone-timeout`, `-restart-recovery`, `matrix-e2ee-media-hold`, `matrix-media-hold-outage-catch-up`, `matrix-e2ee-media-hold-outage-catch-up`: PASS.
  - `matrix-media-hold-command-ordering` (DM, hold 8 s): PASS in that run, but **not reliably**. Because the 10-24 failure was 3/3, I ran it ten times per tree on the same box (for this head, the run above plus nine runs of this scenario alone; three on the rebuilt 10-24 code):

    | Tree | Runs | Pass | Fail | Core error in the failed runs |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | this head `f31c19123c5` (main `1f7035c15f3`, includes #192585) | 10 | 9 | 1 | `SessionWorkStartChangedError: Persisted user turn changed before replay admission. Retry the turn.` |
    | this head with only #192585's production change reverted (20 lines in three files; local only) | 10 | 10 | 0 | none |
    | this head with `mediaHoldMs: 0` in the scenario (hold off; local only) | 10 | 10 | 0 | none |
    | the 10-24 code rebuilt on its 10-24 base `ac13a7e0c13` (local only; the 10-24 head is no longer fetchable) | 3 | 2 | 1 | `ReplaySafeTranscriptConflictError: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite` |

    Both failed runs show the sequence recorded on 10-24: the `/status` reply arrives, then the attachment's turn, which the hold dispatched before the command, dies before its reply, and the room gets "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request". The gateway lines from the failed run on this head:

    ```text
    [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=947 error="Persisted user turn changed before replay admission. Retry the turn." errorName=SessionWorkStartChangedError taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:qa:main
    [model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=local_runtime_coordination candidate=mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna errorName=SessionWorkStartChangedError
    Embedded agent failed before reply: Persisted user turn changed before replay admission. Retry the turn.
    ```

    My reading: #192585 fixed the 10-24 error (#192522) for `/status`, but the delivered `/status` exchange is still mirrored into the transcript through the shared command mirror (`mirrorDeliveredReplyToTranscript` -> `recordDeliveredCommandExchange`), and when that write lands between the attachment turn's replay preparation and its admission, admission refuses the turn. That is the mechanism #194303 (open) reports for `/stop`; #194451 (open) covers other directives on the older error. So the race is in core and not specific to Matrix, but the hold makes it likelier, because it dispatches the released attachment and the command back to back. With these counts I cannot say whether #192585 changed the rate for this flow. I have not changed the hold for it: the plugin has no signal for "this turn has passed replay admission" beyond adoption, which it already waits for. If maintainers prefer, the hold could keep the releasing command back until the attachment's turn has replied; that makes the command's reply slower, and a `/stop` sent while an attachment is held would then not stop that attachment's turn.
- Not run: a hand-driven Element Web session (the lane drives the same Matrix client API Element Web uses); the upgrade-survivor lane was not re-run this round (no stored data or migration changed since its 2026-10-19 pass).

prs.title: docs: containerized gateway networking, host model servers, and rootless Podman troubleshooting
prs.body:
Related: #194988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a containerized gateway cannot reach model servers running on the host, and nothing in the docs explains why published ports go unreachable, config edits get rejected, or container starts fail on SELinux hosts — operators reverse-engineer error strings like `Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address` and `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process`.

Affects anyone running the gateway in rootless Podman or Docker with local models (llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM) or scripting a hosted-primary + local-fallback setup.

## User Impact

Users can now: point a local provider at a host model server from inside a container (with the SSRF-guard caveat and both fixes explained), understand why `loopback`/`tailnet` binds strand published ports and what to use instead, script the non-interactive hybrid setup (hosted primary, local fallback), and self-recover from three rootless-Podman failure modes (config ownership lock, keep-id mismatch on one-off commands, SELinux relabel denial).

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented behavior is incomplete, not the code: bind modes, the config ownership lock, exact-origin SSRF trust, and onboarding flag handling all behave as designed, but the containerized-gateway docs describe host-centric semantics only. Each section documents observed behavior — verified against source and reproduced on a real rootless Quadlet deployment — rather than proposing changes.

## Evidence

- Source verification: bind fallback semantics in `src/gateway/net.ts`; ownership-lock error text and the 90-second heartbeat in `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts`; link-local exclusion from exact-origin trust in `src/agents/provider-network-policy.ts` and `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts`; `--custom-*` flags ignored beside a hosted `--auth-choice` in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/`.
- Real deployment: all three troubleshooting failure modes reproduced on Fedora rootless Podman with the Quadlet; the alias `baseUrl` is rejected while a LAN-IP `baseUrl` works.
- Docs checks: `pnpm docs:check-links` passes (16,476 links, 0 broken); `docs:check-links:anchors` shows only two pre-existing failures that reproduce unchanged on the unmodified upstream tip; `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` passes (the json5 patch fence validates); `oxfmt` clean on touched files.
- Issue: #194988 (with closed predecessors #68684, #79850, #163315 — code paths fixed, docs gap remained).

<details>
<summary>Commits in this PR</summary>

- `docs(podman): reach host model servers from a containerized gateway` — alias setup, link-local SSRF caveat, both fixes, cross-link from local-models
- `docs(local-models): add non-interactive hybrid setup recipe` — hosted-primary + local-fallback scripting sequence
- `docs: warn that container bind modes strand published ports` — Quadlet note, Docker networking note, troubleshooting entry
- `docs(podman): add rootless container troubleshooting` — ownership lock, SELinux relabel, keep-id entries

</details>

prs.title: fix(skills): package sources with normalized timestamps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The bundled skill packager rejects otherwise-valid source trees when filesystem timestamps fall outside ZIP's representable range, such as epoch-dated files extracted from a reproducible tar archive.

## User Impact

Standard-library `strict_timestamps=False` clamps only unsupported ZIP member dates, allowing those skills to package. Original source content and mtimes remain unchanged. In-range archives, member ordering, no-follow checks and staged publication retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing ZIP writer's supported option rather than adding a timestamp parser, source mutation or configuration. Original @zhangguiping-xydt commit preserved.

## Evidence

[Real GNU tar/touch metadata, packaged CLI captures and independent ZIP inspection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194614#issuecomment-6707771000) on `5be987a2f868becdb5dad5cbd5e3e93261b111d4`, compared with main `c3b92c2597b3039a537878f159c79989c49c187d`.

Secretless Linux Docker, real files and Python zipfile; no clock changes or mocked writer. Main fails on a GNU-tar epoch tree, epoch-only resource and 2108 resource. Candidate produces readable archives with supported minimum/maximum member dates. Every ZIP has exact expected inventory/bytes; source bytes/mtime/mode remain unchanged. Normal-2024 archives are byte-identical across refs. Symlink exclusion, destination-mode preservation and failure/staging behavior remain intact. No cross-platform or Nix deployment claim.

All 11 focused validator/packager tests pass after integrating main's required-entry protection. The combined timestamp/required-entry regression passes in UTC, America/Los_Angeles, Asia/Kolkata and Pacific/Kiritimati; epoch/2108 fail on main, and both fresh/existing-output symlink controls remain intact. Reused common archive-inventory setup without losing assertions: tests **+39/−41 = net −2**, production **+3/−1**, no allocation. Scripts run from npm tarballs with source-byte checks; no compilation/core build required. Existing usage documentation remains accurate and unchanged.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting fully restores strict timestamp handling. No source-file mutation or state/API migration; newly produced archives simply contain representable ZIP dates. Blast radius is timestamp metadata written by the bundled skill packager; contents, validation, permissions and archive publication retain their existing owners.

prs.title: fix(whisper): keep extensionless output beside its input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes default transcription output escaping its input directory when an extensionless audio filename has a dotted parent. For `audio.v1/voice`, the script currently writes `audio.txt` or `audio.json` in the parent directory, potentially overwriting an unrelated existing file, while reporting success.

Related: #194593, an external-contributor filename-boundary fix in the same script, merged by obviyus on November 7.

## User Impact

Extensionless inputs now produce `audio.v1/voice.txt` or `audio.v1/voice.json`. Existing extension-bearing filenames and explicit `--out` retain their behavior. No provider request, model, response format, credential handling or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only strip an extension when the final pathname component contains a dot. Previously Bash's `${in%.*}` could strip from a parent directory. The repair stays in the existing default-output owner: production +4/−1, net +3 lines, with no new parser or naming policy.

## Evidence

Actual Bash script, real curl multipart HTTP upload, Node response extraction and filesystem writes in secretless offline Linux Docker (256 MiB, 0.5 CPU), base `99f4ff69c621e6cb67b10514502fb1922deee547` versus head `1dfcbd03eab25317d4060710d2b531333e1bb79b`.

- Before: valid 1644-byte PCM WAV named `audio.v1/voice` returns exit 0 but overwrites an unrelated `audio.txt` or `audio.json`; the intended sibling output is absent.

prs.title: fix: unblock retained repair after repeated config replacements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained repair preparation refusing an operator-reviewed config after multiple native Gateway replacements since the retained journal.

## User Impact

Operators can prepare a retained repair when a complete native audit chain connects the journal's original config inode to the reviewed current config, including replacements across Gateway restarts. Missing or conflicting evidence still refuses preparation. This requires adopting the merged four-file controller closure; publication of this PR does not install or deploy it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit owner previously combined the journal's original inode with the latest backup's hash and required one row to connect directly to the current config. It now validates at most 64 contiguous replacements in native sequence order, binds every accepted row, and checks the backup against only the final link's preimage. Native read-only observations are skipped; observations that restored a backup are not. Every link retains native source/rename and file-metadata guards and checks the candidate-release Gateway process metadata. Current live-process authority remains separately checked. Ordinary startup additive reconciliation remains single-link.

The production change is confined to the existing audit function: **+16 net lines** for chain continuity, chronology, writer provenance and the bound. No schema, config, cache, or additional scan is introduced. Simplification removed a test-only save wrapper and repeated deletion. The 79-line test allocation covers the five-link regression, 64/65-link boundary and distinct refusal cases; it does not increase unrelated debt.

Related: #194605, #194949, #194955. The open #194573 touches different functions in the same library; its hunks do not overlap this change.

## Evidence

- Five-link regression fails on the unchanged adopted controller and exact main parent `d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1` with the reported native atomic-replacement-audit refusal. Final config suite: **25/25**, 31.27 seconds under concurrent proof load, including existing single-link behavior, five/64-link acceptance, gap/fork/source/scope/writer/non-rename/order/backup/time/metadata refusals and the 65-link limit. Fixtures use two historical PIDs, a newer live generation an identical-byte third replacement, and an interleaved native read observation. The test file uses real lock-bearing owner subprocesses to exercise refusal before durable preparation, which accounts for its runtime.
- Qualified Linux focused run: **62 passed, 29 inherited ordinary-startup fixture failures, one opt-in native test skipped**. The failures hit canonical FD9 admission before audit behavior; they are not passing startup proof.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all selected gates passed except 20 changelog-attribution violations reproduced on the exact parent, introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364. This is an existing main regression. Exact-parent test-line budget passes with 151 lines of headroom.
- Actual synthetic btrfs fixture: 35.04 GiB SQLite agent DB, 6,000 sessions, 62,000 files / 1.10 GB workspace content. A/A base refusals: 29.22/28.89 ms, 0.02/0.02 CPU seconds, 2.99/2.98 MB sampled V8 allocation. A/A successful preparation: 928.89/904.85 ms, 0.91/0.90 CPU seconds, 125.54/128.07 MB sampled V8 allocation. These are different outcomes, **not a speedup**; successful preparation includes witness capture and durable artifacts. Native service/process observations are synthetic; allocation uses separate V8 sampling runs. No production data or access was used.
- Ordinary successor adoption and exact replay were rehearsed under real systemd and FD9 with the unchanged adoption owner. The operator handoff requires a fresh post-merge packet, ordinary `prepare → apply → context`, and preserved prior evidence. No deployment occurred.

- Final Codex autoreview of the full local change against `d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1` is **scoped-clean through P2**. It found an interleaved-read regression in the first candidate; that was reproduced and repaired before the clean final pass.
- Exact-parent full controller suite: **438 pass / 388 fail / 1 skip**. All failures match prior qualified evidence and trace to #193647 (`3efe1deca653`: lock fixtures, drain mode and call order), #169752 (`aee12b63234c`: removed migration-stop helper) and #187090 (`a968dc19900d`: rollback instance). Python health/launcher and Prometheus checks pass. Final candidate full suite: **457 pass / 388 fail / 1 skip**, 642.71 seconds versus 688.31 seconds for the parent. Complete failing-name multisets match: **zero new failures**, with 19 added passing cases. Both Python suites and Prometheus also pass on the candidate.

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42444186722) **passed** for `adf74b18e041ee16bd2b74c5c4d6bc6fdb397e50`. No CI retries were needed.

This PR is intentionally not merged.

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route bound conversations when agent selection is ambiguous
prs.body:
Closes #159334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram conversation with an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` on a multi-agent install that has no channel-wide Telegram route, so its messages are never processed.

## User Impact

User impact: runtime-bound Telegram conversations reach their bound agent regardless of how many agents are configured. Conversations without a binding, or whose binding names no agent, keep today's behavior — including still requiring an explicit channel owner. A binding revoked or replaced while a message is being routed no longer leaves the former owner selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` asked ordinary agent selection for a route before looking at the binding, and ordinary selection refuses an ambiguous roster. It now selects the base route inside the SDK's `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync({ resolveRoute })` (and `inspectRuntimeConversationBindingRoute({ inspection, resolveRoute })` for route-owner inspection): the binding owner's canonically classified `boundAgentId` arrives before ordinary selection, and when it is set the base route is derived from session-only config with that agent as the default. This is the shared binding-owner selection Slack, Discord and iMessage use, so Telegram no longer re-implements the session-key/metadata classification. Topic overrides, configured bindings, and the runtime-binding step that follows are unchanged.

### Binding changes during resolution (review follow-up)

An earlier revision chose the agent from a synchronous binding read and then let `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync` read the binding again after an `await`, so a binding revoked in between could leave the former owner selected; that revision guarded it with a re-prepare/retry loop.

Since merging current `main` (`4ee4606`), agent selection runs inside the `resolveRoute` callback of the single awaited inspection, so the agent and the binding facts come from the same read. There is no second read to diverge from, and the retry loop is gone. The same applies to `prepareTelegramConversationRouteInspection` (new on `main`), whose `resolve(inspection)` now selects the agent from the inspection it is handed. `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` shares the inbound path with `touchBinding: false`.

## Evidence

New cases in `conversation-route-owner.test.ts`, all on a two-agent config with no route bindings:

- inbound `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` selects the bound agent and session, reports `runtime-bound`, and touches the binding once;
- `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` selects the bound agent without touching liveness;
- a sentinel `global` session with `metadata.agentId` selects that agent;
- a binding that names no agent still rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`;
- a binding revoked just before the awaited inspection rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` instead of routing to the former owner;
- a binding replaced just before the awaited inspection routes to the new owner and its new binding.

Negative controls: with `main`'s `conversation-route.ts` (`4ee4606`), 4 of these 6 fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (the bound-agent, inspection, sentinel-metadata and replacement cases); the no-agent and revocation cases pass there, as intended, since both assert that rejection.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts
19 passed (19)
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram
passed 63 Vitest shards
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
0 errors
```

Focused regression cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts` — 19 tests, 16.4 s Vitest duration / 20.8 s wall time locally. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the assertion SAFETY ratchet are clean on the changed files. The test fixture uses `agents.entries` (the authored shape since `agents.list` was retired on `main`).

**Live Telegram proof:** not included. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` harness needs Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have as an outside contributor. The evidence above is unit-level through the real binding-routing SDK with a test adapter.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the change and ran the tests and negative controls above locally.

prs.title: improve(ui): move Lobsterdex and lobster pet copy into lazy English catalogs
prs.body:
## Problem

The Lobsterdex page chrome (title, count, dates, Copy link, theme-hidden notice) already used translation keys, but the rest of its copy was still hard-coded English. That covers all 49 card lore pairs (`flavor`/`hint`) and the lobster pet's hover titles: honorifics, “Jr.”, “just moved in”, the elder and old-friend flavor, the bottle and its 14 fortunes, and the passer-by titles. In every non-English locale this text stayed in English, and some of it broke the approved Control UI style rules (lowercase standalone tooltips, missing contractions, sentences without periods).

## Solution

- Added lazy English registrar `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-lobsterdex.ts` (`lobsterdex.lore.<paletteId>.{flavor,hint}`), registered by the Lobsterdex page. `satisfies Record<LobsterPetPaletteId, …>` keeps the old compile-time guarantee that every palette has lore.
- Added lazy English registrar `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-lobster-pet.ts` (`lobsterPet.*`), registered by `lobster-pet-scene-view.tsx`, which is the only place these keys are read.
- Owners now hand over key ids instead of English text. `lobsterHonorific()` returns `elder | captain | sir`, the pet owner's `flavor` is `elder | oldFriend`, and `LOBSTER_BOTTLE_FORTUNES` is an ordered key list, so seeded fortune indexes keep their mapping. `PASSER_TITLES` and `THEME_CRITTER_TITLES` are gone. Plugin critters keep their artwork title, or fall back to their kind.
- Both registrars are wired into `scripts/lib/control-ui-i18n-catalog.ts`, appended at the end so existing translation-memory order doesn't change. I ran keyless `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`. The only baseline change is that the raw `"a message in a bottle"` title entry is gone.
- Palette and pet names (Blueberry, Clawnstantine, Pinchy, …) stay proper names in `lobster-pet-lore.ts`, per the brief.
- Removed the code comments that called lore, fortunes and pet titles an “English-only easter-egg / no i18n surface” channel. This PR reverses that earlier decision (see the reviewer note below).

prs.title: fix(ui): focus project search when opening the picker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The project picker can open with only a search icon, requiring another click before users can find a project. Even when search is visible, keyboard focus can remain on the picker trigger.

## User Impact

Opening the project picker shows and focuses search immediately, including empty and small catalogs. Reopening the picker restores focused search, even after explicitly collapsing it. Users can start typing without another click.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the catalog-size threshold for the initial search state and focus lazily mounted search inputs when autofocus is requested. Native popover autofocus handles retained inputs on reopening; no extra document listener is needed. Keep explicit collapse available within the current opening and reset it when the picker closes.

## Evidence

- Both responsive phone setup cases pass after following real focused-search dismissal: first Escape collapses search, second closes the picker. The test waits for completed hidden phase before keyboard reopening; no artificial focus change bypasses search.

- Project/GitHub search and folder drafting: all 15 Chromium E2E cases passed after main integration, including initially empty search, immediate typing, collapsed reopening and retained reopening.
- The replacement project-access flow passes for both writer and guest roles. Its old conditional toggle could race lazy mounting and close the already-open search; the flow now fills the initial input directly, preserving access assertions.
- The native autofocus contract passes Chromium and WebKit. It asserts retained query and focus before selecting and replacing text through the keyboard, allowing native caret placement on reopening.
- The original read-scoped test removed by #194830 stays removed; its replacement access coverage remains intact.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Local lint could not run because the declaration preparation owner rejects shared dependency links; exact-head CI owns remaining lint/type/broad validation.
- Independent review of the original runtime diff found no actionable P0-P2 issues. Runtime behavior is unchanged by integration; the only follow-up edits repair browser test assumptions.
- Test growth is 108 lines including the responsive Escape lifecycle repair. The existing allocation and shared cap are unchanged; the native ratchet passes with 44 lines of headroom.
- Current-head CI at `599ffe77dea8f9e3d52047890ff4e4bf533ca078`: all functional, browser, lint/type, and ratchet jobs passed, including the repaired responsive shard. Only the [performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42443736480/job/128618515838) failed: base largest JS is 564580 B, candidate 564660 B, allowed base plus variance 564644 B, leaving 16 B excess. The maintainer accepted this size excess, but native landing supports only inherited-failure or prior-success conflict exceptions; this incremental excess is not falsely classified as inherited. The old auto-merge was retired before publication and remains disabled.

### Before

![Before: project picker requires a click on the search icon](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fb7e61c-7e6f-49df-b134-11890a6946d6)

### After

![After: project picker opens directly in search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b7668b0-7e4f-4c02-88e1-8b2bb12bb6fb)

Both captures use the same synthetic empty-catalog scenario. Keyboard focus and immediate typing are asserted by the browser regression.

prs.title: fix(release): bound Linux selected-tag checkout
prs.body:
## Summary

- replace the Linux release validator's unbounded selected-tag checkout with the pinned CI Git owner
- retry exact tag acquisition three times with 120-second attempt deadlines and bounded backoff
- detach at the resolved tag commit and fail closed unless `HEAD` retains that exact commit

## Problem

During GitHub degradation, the selected-tag checkout in Linux App Release could stall or fail immediately. It had neither a bounded retry policy nor explicit exact-checkout verification.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts test/scripts/release-workflow-git-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --silent` — 228 passed
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` — passed
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ...` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint test/scripts/ci-git-owner.test-support.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts test/scripts/release-workflow-git-lifecycle.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed
- independent GPT-6.1 Sol review of `596c9d463e4c..7560ed2e1160` — no P0/P1 findings; narrative subagent route used because the local Codex CLI was unavailable

Focused behavioral contracts cover retry recovery, exhausted retries, exact-ref checkout, exact-commit mismatch rejection, process cleanup boundaries, and the static workflow contract.

## Risk

The new path uses the existing pinned CI Git owner and a literal public remote, so it does not persist checkout credentials. All network attempts and the detached checkout are bounded, and any unresolved tag, cleanup failure, checkout failure, or SHA mismatch stops the release validator.
