prs.title: improve(clawrouter): apply the Control UI glossary and style to ClawRouter copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The ClawRouter pool page (`extensions/clawrouter/src/control-ui.tsx`) hard-coded every English string inline. That made the copy untranslatable, and some of it didn't follow the approved Control UI style: no contractions, sentences ending fragments with periods, passive "is required" phrasing, a raw error message shown as the alert headline, two different names for the same "enabled state unknown" concept, and Gateway status messages pointing at a "Model Providers" page whose actual label is **Models**.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr/Workboard pattern: `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, `src/i18n/locales.ts`, and `src/i18n/index.ts`, using `translateControlUiMessage`. `browserRoot` is `src/` (the dirname of `openclaw.controlUi`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` picks the catalog up automatically.
- Move **70 strings** into `en.ts` (68 under `clawrouter.*`, plus the shared `common.refresh` and `common.refreshing`, which match core English exactly). Composed strings such as "Observed {date} · Policy {policy}", "{used} used / {limit} monthly limit", and "{count} subscriptions with headroom · {unknown} unknown" are now single templates instead of JSX fragments.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-visible string the lane owns, including the four Gateway pool status messages in `index.ts` that this page renders.
- Errors: the alert now reads "Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh." The redacted technical detail is still shown, but as a secondary hint line under the alert. Plugin views have no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main` (`ControlUiComponents` has none), so per the sweep brief the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- `locales.ts` serves English only. This plugin has no `translated.json` yet, and the sweep brief says to leave it absent. A static import of a missing JSON file would break the esbuild bundle, so the lazy loader isn't added yet (see the open question below).

The `ClawRouter` page title and nav label stay as literal product names.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Could not load the pool. Try refreshing. *(only for non-Error failures; otherwise the raw message was the alert)* | Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh. *(raw detail shown below as a hint)* |
| Read access is required to view the ClawRouter pool. | You need read access to view the ClawRouter pool. |
| Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value is not a subscription charge. | Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value isn’t a subscription charge. |
| Enabled state unknown *(grant badge)* | Enabled state not reported *(same as the extra-usage wording; one name per concept)* |
| Not reported. *(extra-usage fragment)* | Not reported |
| ClawRouter pool status is unavailable. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. | Couldn’t load ClawRouter pool status. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. |
| Configure a ClawRouter key in Model Providers, then try Refresh. | Configure a ClawRouter key in Models, then try Refresh. |
| The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Model Providers. | The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Models. |
| This ClawRouter deployment does not expose pool status. … | This ClawRouter deployment doesn’t expose pool status. … |

All other strings moved into the catalog with their English unchanged.

## Impact

- The English copy is the same apart from the rows above. Layout and markup are unchanged, except that a failed refresh now shows a fixed alert plus a secondary detail line.
- No docs quote the changed labels. `docs/providers/clawrouter.md` and the README reference **Refresh**, **Not reported**, and **ClawRouter**, which are unchanged.
- Foreign locales: none yet. The post-merge locale refresh owns parity. `ui:i18n:check` parity is non-strict on PRs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/clawrouter/browser/pool.test.ts extensions/clawrouter/pool-gateway.test.ts`: 3 + 12 passed. The browser test assertions are updated for the new alert headline, the detail line still being redacted, and the "You need read access" copy.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green, `plugin=clawrouter keys=70 locales=0`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>`: no problems.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>`: clean.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/clawrouter`: bundle builds.
- pr-simplify pass: removed duplicate keys (one "Observed {date}", one "Subscription") and collapsed repeated enabled/disabled ternaries into one helper. Production delta: +260/−126 across 6 files. Most of it is the new 90-line `en.ts` plus the line-wrapping of `t(...)` calls.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex engine, gpt-6.1-sol), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `14ab4736fa24`, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.9)", no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up on this host.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge** (the visual gate needs before/after screenshots of the pool page, including the refresh-failure state).

## Open question

Leaving `translated.json` absent means that after the locale refresh writes it, nothing loads it until a follow-up adds the Nostr-style `loadMessages` loader. The alternatives are to commit an empty `{}` `translated.json` with the loader now, or to add both in the first locale refresh.

## Problem

The **X replies** Control UI page hard-codes its English copy in `extensions/x/src/control-ui.tsx`. Several strings also break the approved Control UI glossary and style rules:

- "bot" where the copy means the agent
- "Administrator" as the role name
- "hidden helpers" for subagents
- fragment sentences that end in periods
- raw server error text shown as the only error message

The empty-state hint also put the internal config key `allowFrom` in normal copy.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr pattern: `extensions/x/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `src` because `openclaw.controlUi` points at `./src/control-ui.tsx`. **63 strings** moved into the catalog under the plugin-specific `xReplies.*` namespace, so no key collides with the shared core catalog.
- Translate the page, navigation label, and page label through `translateControlUiMessage`. The view tracks `host.locale` in its existing presentation store.
- Notices are now typed keys (`added`, `removed`, `guestsOn`, …) translated at render time instead of English strings held in state.
- Request failures are wrapped in a small `RequestFailure` that records which action failed. The alert now reads "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." and the redacted server message follows inline as secondary text (`<small>`, muted). The plugin SDK host components (`ControlUiComponents`) on main have no shared "Show details" disclosure, so as the sweep brief directs, the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- Copy that wraps inline elements (`<time>`, the repository link) uses a small `withSlots` helper. It splits the translated string at `{name}` placeholders, so translators control word order.
- `locales.ts` is English-only for now, and other locales fall back to English, which is today's behavior. `translated.json` isn't added, per the sweep brief. The Nostr-style lazy `translated.json` loader can't be wired until that file exists, because the bundler can't resolve a missing import.

### Notable copy changes

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| Choose whose mentions the bot can answer publicly. | Choose whose mentions the agent can answer publicly. |
| Administrator access is required to manage X replies. | You need admin access to manage X replies. |
| Bot account | Agent account |
| Applies to the selected bot account. Guests get repository answers with hidden helpers of the same agent. No writes, commands, visible work sessions, or other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. | Applies to the selected agent account. Guests get repository answers from this agent and its hidden subagents. They can’t write, run commands, open visible sessions, or use other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. |
| Per guest, per UTC day / `3 mentions` | Mentions per guest, per UTC day / `3` (no more "1 mentions") |
| Could not resolve on X: @a, @b. Check the declared profiles. | Couldn’t find @a, @b on X. Check the declared GitHub profiles. |
| No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or set `allowFrom` in config. | No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or in config. |
| *(raw server error)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load X replies. Try again. · Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. · Couldn’t remove this entry. Try again. · Couldn’t change guest mode. Try again. *(the redacted server detail follows as secondary text)* |
| No successful sync yet.Entries update… *(missing space)* | No successful sync yet. Entries update… |

prs.title: fix(feishu): let isolated topics process messages concurrently
prs.body:
Related: #72972, #89687, #96315

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unrelated Feishu topics waiting behind a long-running request in the same group when topic session isolation is enabled.

## User Impact

Different topics can run concurrently within the configured agent concurrency limit. Messages in one topic retain FIFO ordering. `group_topic_sender` also separates senders within each topic. Default group and direct-message scheduling remain unchanged.

Events without a reliable native `thread_id` still serialize ordinary messages within the group and bypass message batching. The existing five-minute queue timeout remains unchanged; timed-out handlers can continue running.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both durable ingress and ordinary dispatch now use the existing canonical topic session resolver. Fixing only the inner sequential queue was insufficient: a deferred input in topic A still held the durable group lane and blocked topic B.

Ordering reservations begin before debounce buffering. An unidentified-topic fallback waits for earlier ordinary messages and blocks later topic work through queue settlement. Topic batching uses the canonical queue identity and seals different-sender batches without merging sender identity. Retained pre-upgrade durable chat-lane rows remain recoverable.

The change adds no network lookup, configuration option, dependency, schema change, or migration. It preserves WebSocket acknowledgement timing, global concurrency, typing behavior, and the existing queue timeout.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

Please confirm that configured `group_topic` and `group_topic_sender` scopes should also enable topic-scoped inbound scheduling. This changes the previously intentional group-wide ordinary-message FIFO boundary. The proposed contract retains FIFO within each queue and conservative barriers for unidentified topics. Default `group` and `group_sender` scheduling remain unchanged. No new opt-in setting is proposed. Maintainer acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

### Real Feishu WebSocket and model proof

Tested commit: `0f01fa718fcedf99e9cfa1dbed82dcc50159dfbf`.

An operator-authorized controlled run used the built Gateway, real Feishu WebSocket events, real model calls, and real replies in two threads of one ordinary group configured with `groupSessionScope: "group_topic"`. The isolated instance used a separate state directory and loopback port, `maxConcurrent: 4`, and `debounceMs: 1000`. The model executed a bounded 45-second command in A1. The test then submitted same-topic A2 before different-topic B.

Sanitized terminal observations, November 7, 2026, America/Los_Angeles:

```text
19:13:54.384  topic A / A1  model started
19:14:09.223  topic A / A2  submitted
19:14:09.990  topic B       submitted
19:14:11.937  topic B       model started
19:14:16.486  topic B       dispatch completed; reply PR194688_V2_B_DONE
19:14:47.473  topic A / A1  dispatch completed; reply PR194688_V2_A1_DONE
19:14:48.027  topic A / A2  model started
19:14:51.585  topic A / A2  dispatch completed; reply PR194688_V2_A2_DONE
```

B completed about 31 seconds before A1. A2 started only after A1 completed. The exact reply markers were independently read back from Feishu. These are actual runtime observations, not synthetic-handler test results.

The initial live run on `c9fa618688b9ae5c2438a6111682a1aa1a25e3ab` failed: B started only after A1 completed because A2 occupied the durable group lane. That failure led to the durable-ingress repair in the tested commit. It is not counted as passing evidence.

### Missing-native-thread fallback

The same built head then ran its real authenticated/encrypted webhook endpoint with two locally signed event envelopes. The first event deliberately omitted native `thread_id`; the second supplied a known different native thread. Event IDs were synthetic, while Feishu message/thread references were real. This is a signed-envelope replay, not a claim that Feishu delivered a naturally missing-thread event during this run.

The first event used real Feishu message lookup and entered the native-thread session matching the API metadata. Both events reached real model calls and produced real Feishu replies.

```text
19:18:40.115  fallback F    authenticated webhook accepted (thread_id absent)
```

### Limits and operational scope

The real WebSocket run covers ordinary-group threads, not a newly provisioned native topic group. Configuration reload between durable admission and claim inspection remains untested. Production code and configuration were not replaced; the production receiver was temporarily paused to prevent competing WebSocket clients. The original production service was restarted, its recovery timer was canceled, and the isolated test Gateway was stopped after validation. No merge or permanent deployment is requested by this evidence update.

prs.title: fix(ui): local performance base comparison reports false plugin UI growth after a full build
prs.body:
Related: #194544

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `pnpm ui:check-performance:base <sha>` reports false Control UI growth on a no-op or dependency-only diff when the local checkout has a full `pnpm build`, which blocks local proof for every PR that runs it while main is already over its absolute caps.

## User Impact

Developers and agents get a trustworthy local performance comparison: a change that does not touch the Control UI now measures +0 B, and the report lists both sides' plugin UI inventories so any remaining difference is attributable. CI is unchanged (a fresh checkout packages only Settings presenters on both sides). Budgets, thresholds and the growth policy are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two causes stacked up, both only on the local path:

1. **Different plugin inventories.** The candidate's Control UI build consumes every plugin UI its checkout has packaged: all of them after a full build, Settings presenters only in a fresh checkout. The archived base only ever packaged Settings presenters, so the six extra plugin entries in the candidate's distribution inventory read as growth. The wrapper now reads the candidate's packaged inventory and asks the base's own builder (the existing `--prepare-settings` owner, which already runs the canonical build, asset-copy and metadata-copy steps) to package those plugins too. No new build list or step sequence lives in the wrapper.
2. **Silent no-op on macOS.** `os.tmpdir()` is a symlink (`/var` → `/private/var`). Node resolves the archived builder's `import.meta.url` to the realpath, so its direct-run guard never matched `argv` and base preparation silently did nothing; the base only got Settings presenters because its own Vite plugin re-prepared them. The wrapper now realpaths its temporary root. Linux CI's `/tmp` is not a symlink, which is why CI never saw this.

The base packages plugins with its archived builder on purpose, so builder changes stay visible in the comparison. Consequently bases that predate this change still package Settings presenters only; the new inventory line makes that visible. Once this lands, comparisons against current `main` pick it up.

Behavior change worth noting for CI: if a PR adds Settings views to an existing plugin UI, the base now packages that plugin too, so the comparison counts the added Settings entry rather than the whole plugin entry. That matches what full release builds ship.

## Evidence

Local, on a loaded shared Mac Studio (`nice`d), candidate checkout packaged with the canonical plugin asset build, asset copy and metadata copy for all ten plugin UIs (what a full build produces).

**Before** (current wrapper vs `origin/main` f6a8ce9a, no-op diff): FAILED

```
startup JS gzip vs base: 90782 B -> 90782 B (+0 B)
chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1295227 B -> 1295856 B (+629 B)   raw 4175975 -> 4178705 (+2730 B)
new boot JS gzip vs base:   802650 B ->  803279 B (+629 B)   raw 2614086 -> 2616816 (+2730 B)
violations: largest JS gzip 551.0 -> 551.7 KiB (cap 551.3), new boot JS gzip 783.8 -> 784.5 KiB (cap 784.4)
```

The +2,730 B raw delta matches the attribution from #194544 exactly.

**After** (this wrapper vs a base commit containing this change, candidate = that commit plus a comment-only UI edit to force a real base rebuild instead of input reuse): passed

```
Control UI plugin distributions: candidate clawrouter, deep-research, knowledge, mcp-relay, memory-core, nostr, openclaw-id-access, whatsapp, workboard, x; base <same ten>.
startup JS gzip vs base:   90782 B ->   90782 B (+0 B)
chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1295856 B -> 1295856 B (+0 B)
new boot JS gzip vs base:   803279 B ->  803279 B (+0 B)
```

An intermediate run with only the inventory fix still showed `base memory-core, nostr, whatsapp` and +629 B, which is how the macOS temp-root no-op surfaced.

**Regression tests** (red on the base, green with the fix):

- `test/scripts/control-ui-performance.test.ts` › "packages the candidate's plugin UI inventory into the base": candidate holds an extra packaged plugin UI; asserts both inventories match and identical inputs are reused at +0 B. The archived-comparison fixture now runs under a symlinked `TMPDIR` and its fake builder keeps the real direct-run guard; reverting the realpath fix fails with `base none`, reverting the request fails on mismatched inputs.
- `test/scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.test.ts`: the Settings builder packages a requested non-Settings plugin UI and leaves an unrequested one alone.

Also ran: both test files in full (54 passed), `run-oxlint` on changed files, tooling `tsgo` leaf, `check:script-erasability`, `oxfmt --check`.

prs.title: improve(workboard): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Workboard copy
prs.body:
## Problem

Workboard's Control UI copy didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules. It had straight apostrophes, a `...` placeholder, "could not" / "cannot" errors with no consistent form, "Board agent" capitalized mid-sentence, the British "Cancelled", and "board conversation" used for what is a session. Its errors also showed internal RPC text: `sessions.create returned no key` and `workboard response did not include a card`. About 19 user-visible English strings were still hard-coded in `extensions/workboard/browser/` instead of living in the plugin's translation source, so they could never be translated.

## Solution

- Rewrote the existing English in `browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the rules. Errors now read "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The copy uses contractions, curly apostrophes and the `…` character, sentence case, and **session** as the container noun.
- Moved the remaining hard-coded English in `browser/` (execution, loading, mutation and normalization errors; the stale-session fallback; the "Workboard is no longer active" message; widget registration labels; the board-kind suffix on duplicate sidebar names) into `en.ts` and called it through `t()`.
- `host.ts` calls `translateControlUiMessage` directly instead of `t()`, because `i18n/index.ts` imports `host.ts` and using `t()` there would create an import cycle.
- Two places that had the same stale-session fallback in different words (normalization and card alerts) now use one key.
- Updated `docs/plugins/workboard.md`, which quotes the sidebar suffix: **Planning (Cards)** / **Planning (Sessions)**.

Notable copy changes (old → new):

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page load failure | Workboard could not load. Check your connection and reload this page. | Couldn’t load Workboard. Check your connection and reload this page. |
| Delete without write access | Connect with write access to delete this board. | Couldn’t delete this board. Connect with write access and try again. |
| Bulk edit stopped | The operation stopped. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. | Couldn’t apply changes to every card. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. |
| Sessions board agent missing | The board conversation's agent is unavailable. Choose a configured agent or update the board's conversation. | Couldn’t open the board session. Its agent is unavailable; choose a configured agent or update the board’s session. |
| Sessions board create failed | The board conversation could not be created. Try again. | Couldn’t create the board session. Try again. |
| Rules help | The Board agent can edit column rules and session scope. | The board agent can edit column rules and session scope. |
| Note placeholder | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note... | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note… |
| Dispatch help | …this board's Ready cards… | …this board’s Ready cards… |
| Refresh status | Refresh failed | Couldn’t refresh |
| Session status | Cancelled | Canceled (American English, same as core approvals copy) |
| Widget card not loaded | This card is not loaded yet. | This card isn’t loaded yet. |
| Start, hard-coded | sessions.create returned no key | Couldn’t start a session for this card. Try again. |
| Card payload, hard-coded | workboard response did not include a card | Couldn’t read the updated card. Refresh the board and try again. |
| Gateway missing, hard-coded | Gateway client unavailable | Couldn’t refresh Workboard. Connect to the Gateway and try again. |
| Scheduled start, hard-coded | Scheduled cards cannot start before their scheduled time. | Couldn’t start this card. Scheduled cards can’t start before their scheduled time. |
| Already started, hard-coded | This card already has an execution. Refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link before starting another. | Couldn’t start this card. It already has a linked session; refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link. |
| Stop, hard-coded | Refresh this card's session details before stopping it, or use Edit to choose its session. | Couldn’t stop this card’s session. Refresh its session details, or use Edit to choose its session. |
| Changed card, hard-coded | This card changed. Refresh its details before starting or stopping it. | Couldn’t start or stop this card because it changed. Refresh its details and try again. |
| Stale fallback, hard-coded (×2) | Session has not reported… / Linked session has not reported recent activity. | Linked session hasn’t reported recent activity. |
| Inactive plugin, hard-coded | Workboard is no longer active. Reload the plugin to continue. | Workboard is no longer active. Reload this page to continue. |
| Unknown error, hard-coded | Unknown workboard error. | Unknown Workboard error. Refresh and try again. |
| Sidebar duplicate name | Planning (cards) | Planning (Cards) |

String count: 12 existing English values rewritten. 19 hard-coded literals moved into translation calls: 14 go to new `en.ts` keys and the rest reuse 3 existing keys (`widget.boardLabel`, `cardsBoard`, `sessionsBoard.kind`). No foreign locale, `translated.json`, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` or `*.meta.json` file was edited. The post-merge locale-refresh bot owns parity.

Raw Gateway error text still shows inline in the existing Workboard error toast. Workboard has no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main`, and the copy written here no longer includes internal names.

## Impact

Only copy and translation sources change; behavior doesn't. Two edge cases are accepted:
- Widget registration labels and the stale-reason fallback are resolved when they're created. A locale switch picks them up after the next refresh or reload; before this change they were always English.
- The session label `buildCardSessionLabel` writes for new card sessions, and agent-facing template drafts, stay as they are. They're stored data or model-facing text, not Control UI copy.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workboard/browser`: 34 files, 265 tests passed (assertions updated in `index.test.ts` and `widgets/runtime.test.ts`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=workboard keys=395 locales=22`).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `oxlint` on touched TS files: 0 warnings or errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is a copy move or rewrite. The only new code is the 4-line `inactiveMessage()` helper in `host.ts`, which avoids the import cycle. One duplicate stale fallback was merged into a shared key. Net production change is small: about +40/−30 lines, mostly `en.ts`.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol, medium), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head of this branch, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.82)", no findings. The reviewer couldn't see unchanged context, so key validity and import cycles rest on the `ui:i18n:verify` and madge runs above.

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge (visual gate).

## Problem

The Nostr profile panel and the Memory overview/search views had copy that didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: Title Case buttons and labels (`Hide Advanced`, `Import from Relays`, `Save & Publish`, `Public Key`, `Edit Profile`), straight quotes and `...`, "Could not" / "does not" with no contractions, lowercase "gateway", internal jargon ("host memory search runtime"), and error messages that didn't use the "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." pattern. Nostr also had one hard-coded English label (`NIP-05`) outside its catalog.

## Solution

- Rewrote the English source catalogs in `extensions/nostr/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the glossary and style rules.
- **Shared-key collision:** Nostr's `common.hideAdvanced`, `common.showAdvanced`, `common.importFromRelays`, `common.saveAndPublish` and `common.publicKey` share keys with the core catalog (`ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`), and `ui:i18n:verify` requires a plugin's English to match the core text for any shared key. These five now live under plugin-owned `channels.nostr.*` keys, so the core catalog stays untouched (it belongs to another lane).
- Moved the hard-coded `NIP-05` profile-fact label into the Nostr catalog (`channels.nostr.nip05`). The truncated public key now uses `…`.
- Nostr save/import failures now show `Couldn’t update/import the profile. Try again.` with the raw detail after it. Before, a failed request showed only the raw server message (e.g. `Invalid profile`). Both paths share one `failure()` helper in `controller.ts`, which also removed the duplicated prefix logic.
- Placeholders are unchanged on every key that keeps its name (`{prefix}`, `{error}`, `{message}`, `{engine}`), so existing translations still pass verification.
- **Raw error detail:** the Plugin SDK has no shared "Show details" disclosure for plugin settings views, so the raw detail stays inline after the sentence. This matches the existing core pattern (`Couldn’t load cloud device profiles. Try again. {error}`).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Surface | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nostr button | Edit Profile | Edit profile |

| Nostr button | Import from Relays | Import from relays |

| Nostr placeholder | Tell people about yourself... | Tell people about yourself… |
| Nostr error | Request timed out after 30 seconds; the server may still have applied the change — check the profile before retrying. | Couldn’t confirm the profile change within 30 seconds. It may still have applied, so check the profile before you try again. |
| Nostr error | Profile update failed: {error} | Couldn’t update the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile import failed: {error} | Couldn’t import the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile publish failed on all relays. | Couldn’t publish the profile to any relay. Try again. |
| Nostr public key | `abcd1234...wxyz5678` | `abcd1234…wxyz5678` |
| Memory search placeholder | Search this agent's memories | Search this agent’s memories |
| Memory search error | Memory search failed: {message} | Couldn’t search memories. Try again. {message} |
| Memory file error | Could not load this memory file: {message} | Couldn’t load this memory file. Close and reopen it to try again. {message} |
| Memory file | This memory file cannot be shown as text. | This memory file can’t be shown as text. |
| Memory notice | Update the gateway to search memories from the Control UI. | Update the Gateway to search memories from the Control UI. |

prs.title: fix(agents): keep bundle MCP access for turns woken by an exec completion
prs.body:
Closes #183589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a backgrounded host exec exits and `tools.exec.notifyOnExit` (default `true`) wakes the originating session, the woken turn has no bundle MCP tools although the run that started the exec had them (Code Mode telemetry `sources: {openclaw: 51, mcp: 0}`, `tools.effective` notice `mcp-not-yet-connected`), and any child spawned from that woken turn inherits the restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: a turn woken by an exec completion keeps exactly the MCP access of the run that started the exec, and children it spawns do too: an unrestricted run keeps every configured server, a run capped to `fixture__*` wakes a turn that can reach only the `fixture` server, an exact-name policy such as `fixture__read` keeps only that tool. Runs with no `mcp.servers`, or whose cap excludes bundle MCP tools, behave exactly as before, so a woken turn never gains access the producer run did not have. No config, schema, or wire change; `notifyOnExit` no longer has to be disabled to keep MCP in long-lived sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createOpenClawCodingTools` (`src/agents/agent-tools.ts`) builds each tool's Gateway caller with a default `sessionEventSourcePolicy` whose `toolsAllow` lists the finalized coding tools. Bundle MCP tools are materialized afterwards (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`), so no `server__tool` name or `bundle-mcp` marker is ever in that list. The exec tool records the policy as the completion event's `producerPolicy`; `captureSessionEventTarget` intersects the woken turn's `toolsAllow` with it; `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` then finds no bundle name and creates no MCP runtime for the woken turn or its children.

The fix captures the producer's final surface instead of predicting it (revision 5). `createOpenClawCodingTools` now fills a caller-owned array (`sessionEventToolsAllowRef`) with the coding tool names and hands that same array to every Gateway caller as `sessionEventSourcePolicy.toolsAllow`. The embedded attempt (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`) appends the bundled MCP/LSP tools that survived the attempt's runtime allowlist, `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`, and schema projection, by exact name, in the same place it already captures the cron creator cap and the spawn allowlist. The exec tool reads the policy when it records the completion, so the woken turn gets exactly the tools this run could call:

- sender-scoped denials (`tools.toolsBySender["id:alice"].deny: ["admin__*"]`) already removed `admin__reset` from the producer's final surface, so the senderless woken turn never sees it;
- intersected caps, partial globs (`fixture__read*` ∩ `fixture__*All`), and namespace-reaching globs (`fixture*`) are resolved by the existing runtime matcher on real tools, not approximated;
- a refresh replaces the previously appended bundled names, so a tool quarantined or filtered on refresh drops out;
- no marker or glob is ever added, so the continuation cannot widen past the producer.

The surface stays under the existing 512-name bound the target reader enforces (`SESSION_EVENT_TOOLS_ALLOW_LIMIT`, now exported from `session-event-target.ts`); past it, the attempt logs a warning and the woken turn keeps only the coding tools. Revision 5 deletes `agent-tools.session-event-policy.ts` and its tests (revisions 1–4 projected MCP access from allow patterns, which the review showed cannot preserve denials or every glob shape).

## Evidence

Regression in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts` (`session event tool surface`, 9 cases through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` with `fixture` and `admin` servers materializing `fixture__read`, `fixture__readAll`, `fixture__write`, `admin__reset`; each captured cap is then run through the woken turn's `intersectSessionEventToolsAllow` → `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` → `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`):

- unrestricted producer → all four MCP tools; `["exec", "fixture__*"]` and `["exec", "fixture*"]` → the three fixture tools; `["exec", "fixture__read"]` → `fixture__read`;
- intersected `[["exec", "fixture__read*"], ["exec", "fixture__*All"]]` → `fixture__readAll` (revision 4 returned nothing here);
- `["read", "exec"]` → no MCP tool and no bundle runtime in the woken turn;
- producer final policy drops `admin__reset` (the sender-scoped denial shape) → the woken turn never admits it;
- refresh after a projection drops `fixture__readAll` → the cap shrinks to `["exec", "fixture__read"]`;
- a coding surface at the bound → MCP names are not appended.

Red on `main`: the attempt never appends to the cap, so every case expecting an MCP tool fails, the reported loss.

Suites: `attempt-bundle-tools` 23/23; `bash-tools.exec-notify`, `tools/gateway-caller-context`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `attempt-tool-prepare.web-search`, `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-context`, `session-event-permissions` 115/115. Oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean.

### Live Gateway run (revision 5, head 18721460f1e, shipped entry point, scripted provider)

Built dist from this head (`build-all gatewayWatch` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, non-interactive onboarding with `--custom-no-auth` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible provider written for the proof. The provider scripts each step from the conversation and logs every request's offered `tools[].function.name`.
Two loopback streamable-http MCP servers, `fixture` (`echo`) and `admin` (`reset`), each log every JSON-RPC request. Config: `mcp.servers` for both, `tools.profile: full`, `tools.codeMode: false`, `tools.toolSearch: false`, `tools.exec.security: full`, `tools.exec.ask: off`, `tools.exec.notifyOnExit: true`; Gateway `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18399`.
Every scenario's producer turn runs `exec` with `background: true` and ends. Its woken turn then calls `fixture__echo`, `sessions_spawn` (child task: `fixture__echo`, then `admin__reset`) and `admin__reset`. The provider emits each call whether or not it was offered, so the Gateway has to refuse what the turn may not use.
Policy changes were applied with `node openclaw.mjs config patch --file …` while the Gateway was running (log: `config hot reload applied (…)`). Times are UTC; tool results come from the session transcript in the agent SQLite store.
No credentials, all loopback; the host was heavily loaded, which explains the minutes between exec exit and wake.

**S1: allowed completion-turn MCP call** (`tools.allow: ["read","exec","process","sessions_spawn","fixture__*"]`, session `agent:main:s3d`, dispatched with `node openclaw.mjs agent --agent main --session-key s3d --json`)

```text
18:40:53.533  provider  producer   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 5; echo PROOF_EXEC_DONE","background":true}
18:40:53.686  provider  producer   -> "started" (turn ends, exec still running)
18:56:00.145  provider  woken      last user msg "[OpenClaw exec completion] Exec completed (… code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
                                   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.155  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.158  toolResult fixture__echo  "fixture.echo ok: {\"text\":\"from-woken-turn\"}"
18:56:00.279  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: initialize / tools/list only, no tools/call
```

The turn woken by the exec exit got `fixture__echo` and its call reached the fixture server; `admin__reset`, outside the producer's cap, was not offered and was refused before any request left the Gateway.

**S2: sender-scoped admin denial preserved** (no `tools.allow`; `tools.toolsBySender: {"id:alice": {"deny": ["admin__*"]}}`). The producer message entered through the **qa-channel** plugin: the repo's qa-lab bus ran on loopback and `POST /v1/inbound/message` carried `{"conversation":{"id":"alice","kind":"direct"},"senderId":"alice"}`. The producer request shows `"sender":{"id":"alice","name":"Alice"}`.

```text
19:30:58.826  provider  producer (sender alice)  tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> exec background
19:31:06.503  provider  woken (senderless)       tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:06.598  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
19:31:06.995  toolResult sessions_spawn  accepted  childSessionKey=agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:07.206  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call
control, same config, CLI sender (not alice), session agent:main:s2ctl:
19:38:41.052  provider  producer  tools=71  admin__reset=yes
19:38:48.506  admin     tools/call reset {"reason":"from-woken-turn"}
```

The denial applied only to alice's run, and the senderless woken turn inherited it: `admin__reset` was absent from the woken turn's tools and its call was refused. The same config still gave `admin__reset` to a non-alice sender, so the denial is sender-scoped and not global.

**S3: inherited restrictions in a spawned child** (children spawned from the S1 and S2 woken turns)

```text
S1 child agent:main:subagent:0e4cffe3-…
18:56:00.479  provider  child  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
18:56:00.488  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
18:56:00.505  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
S2 child agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:10.113  provider  child  tools=51  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:10.254  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
19:31:10.536  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call in either run
```

A child spawned from a woken turn keeps that turn's MCP access (`fixture__echo` works) and its restrictions: the S1 global cap and alice's denial still exclude `admin__reset`.

**S4: revocation after capture, before the woken turn** (S1 config; session `agent:main:s4`; exec `sleep 240`)

```text
19:10:29.444  provider  producer  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 240; …","background":true}
19:10:30Z     producer turn returned (agent exit 0; exec still running, its completion target captured while fixture__echo was allowed)
19:11:52.750  gateway   config.patch write changedPaths=tools.deny            (tools.deny: ["fixture__echo"])
19:11:52.877  gateway   [reload] config hot reload applied (tools.deny)
19:29:59.180  transcript user "Exec completed (oceanic-, code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
19:30:02.327  provider  woken     offered=exec,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
19:30:02.575  toolResult fixture__echo  isError "Tool fixture__echo not found"
fixture server: last tools/call at 18:56:00.818 (S1), none after the revocation
```

The cap captured `fixture__echo`, but the woken turn applied its own current policy. After the hot-reloaded `tools.deny` the tool was not offered, and the call was rejected before any `tools/call` reached the fixture server.

Discovery (`initialize`/`tools/list`) still connects both configured servers during each run, as on `main`; policy filters tools, not discovery.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

prs.title: fix(compaction): finished turn re-summarized as split after bootstrap marker
prs.body:
Closes #194915

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: safeguard compaction summarizes the previous, already finished turn a second time as an unfinished "split turn" when the cut lands on a user message in a Gateway session.

## User Impact

User impact: in that case compaction now makes one summary request instead of two. The saved summary no longer carries a "Turn Context (split turn)" section that describes a finished turn as unfinished. Cuts that really land inside a turn behave as before.

No transcript messages were ever deleted. But the extra section competed for room in the capped summary (see #194408) and framed finished work as still in progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`findCutPoint` keeps metadata entries in front of the selected message, and that retention is unchanged. But it then asked the first retained entry, rather than the selected message, whether it starts a turn. The per-run `openclaw:bootstrap-context:full` marker sits right before every later user message, so the answer was "no", and the previous complete turn became a turn prefix. The split decision now comes from the selected message, taken before the metadata scan steps back.

## Evidence

**Regression tests** in `compaction-cut-point.test.ts`:

- **Metadata before the kept user message.** Fails on `c61a7c0cf` with `isSplitTurn: true` and `turnStartIndex: 0`. Passes with the fix.
- **Metadata before a genuine mid-turn cut.** A model snapshot sits inside the turn. This test passes on base and with the fix. It fails on an over-corrected variant that treats any metadata step as "no split", so a real split still reports as one.

The file runs 14 tests in about 1 second of test time, 3.3 seconds wall.

**Gateway:** an isolated source Gateway with throwaway state and a healthy loopback stub summarizer. It uses no real model and does not depend on #194813. The run seeds eight turns, then sends `/compact`, with default `contextInjection`. [Evidence and harness](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/tree/5e3365e00f5f771db9baf58d4f0ec884f8203f40/issue-194915-split-turn-gateway).

| Cut | Build | Summary requests | Split-turn section saved |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/muse/README.md` told readers that the Muse harness is "opt-in only" and that `auto` never picks it. That is
wrong: the canonical guide (`docs/plugins/muse.md`, "Set `agentRuntime.id` …") states that without explicit routing a
model discovered by exactly one native runtime can use that runtime when no authored API binding or host credential takes
precedence. A reader following the README would conclude Muse can never be chosen automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Install section now describes the same rule as the guide instead of asserting the opposite:

- explicit routing is still `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on a `meta/*` model or the `meta` provider;
- without it, automatic selection can still use Muse when it is the only native runtime for the model and nothing more
  specific wins;
- the existing link to the Muse guide stays, so the full rule has one owner in `docs/plugins/muse.md`.

## User Impact

Docs only. Behaviour, packaging, and plugin routing are unchanged; the README no longer contradicts the guide.

## Evidence

- Statement being corrected: `extensions/muse/README.md` (Install section).
- Rule being matched: `docs/plugins/muse.md`, the paragraph that starts "Set `agentRuntime.id` on one model entry …".
- `pnpm format:docs:check`: `Docs formatting clean (1420 files)`.

prs.title: feat(agents): make Tool Search control result character limit configurable
prs.body:
## Summary
- Adds `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` (`number | "auto"`) to configure the pre-wrapper character budget for network-sourced Tool Search control results (`renderToolSearchControlText` in `src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`).
- Preserves the existing `20,000`-character default (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) when `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` is unset.
- Supports `"auto"` to scale with the active model's live tool-result cap (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) minus the external-content wrapper overhead, and clamps explicit numeric limits at or under the active model's live tool-result budget so wrapped results are never cut mid-marker by the outer tool-result guard.
- Consciously raises the `core` config baseline count budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` by +1 (`2638` -> `2639`) and updates `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the new `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` setting requested in #194857.

## What Problem This Solves
Network-sourced Tool Search (`dispatch_action` / `call_tool` and Code Mode) control results were hardcoded to truncate at `20,000` characters (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) in `renderToolSearchControlText` (`src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`) before `wrapExternalContent`, even when the active model's context window and live tool-result budget (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) could safely accommodate larger structured responses (#194857). Operators and high-context agents had no configuration knob to raise or auto-scale that pre-wrapper character limit while preserving the `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT ...>>>` boundary against outer truncation.

## Evidence
- Verified schema, config resolution, and runtime truncation behavior with Vitest unit tests in:
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-gateway-tool.test.ts` (validates `maxResultChars: "auto"` and positive integers in `AgentToolSurfacePresentationSchema.properties.toolSearch`, rejecting `0`, negative, non-integer, and unknown string values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-config.test.ts` (verifies `resolveToolSearchConfig` omits `maxResultChars` when unset and retains `"auto"` or positive integer values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts` (`scales network control output with maxResultChars='auto' or clamps a fixed limit to the live budget`: verifies a `30,000`-char network payload is preserved un-truncated under `maxResultChars: "auto"` with a `200,000`-token context window, and that `maxResultChars: 50_000` on a `32,000`-token context window is clamped prior to wrapping so `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="...">>>` remains intact).
- Verified `pnpm config:docs:gen` baseline artifacts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`).

Fixes #194857

prs.title: fix(macos): key Agent Events rows by globally unique id
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

The macOS **Agent Events** window (`Debug → Open Agent Events…`) keys its rows by `ControlAgentEvent.seq`, a per-run counter the Gateway restarts at 1 for every run (`src/infra/agent-events.ts`). The window keeps up to 400 events, so `1, 2, 3…` repeats across runs and SwiftUI treats rows from different runs as the *same* element: earlier runs lose their rows or get them reused. The event type already carries a globally unique `id` (`"\(runId)-\(seq)"`).

Fixes #187608.

## The change

`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/AgentEventsWindow.swift:21` passes `id: \.id` instead of `id: \.seq`. `seq` still orders events inside a run; the store, the event shape and the Gateway's sequence allocation are untouched.

`AgentEventsWindowRowIdentityTests.swift` renders the shipped window (an `NSHostingView` around the real view and the real `AgentEventStore`): it starts `run-a` at `seq=1`, lets that row render, then starts `run-b` at `seq=1` while the window stays open and reads the rows back from the AppKit accessibility tree. On `main` the window ends with `["run-b"]`; with this change it holds both runs.

## User impact

Debug-only pane: no user flow, config, protocol or storage change. After more than one agent run the list keeps one row per run instead of dropping earlier ones.

## Evidence

**Both runs in one frame.** `dist/OpenClaw.app` (ad-hoc debug build from `scripts/package-mac-app.sh`) attached to a local Gateway running the `stub` model (`--attach-only`); the pane was opened from the menu through the accessibility API; two real CLI turns ran while the window stayed open (`events-a`, then `events-b`, each restarting `seq` at 1). The window is 1270×840 (the runner's default 1024×768 display clamps it to 822×619, so the harness first switches the virtual display to 1920×1080). One capture, no stitched screenshots ([run 42440664583](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/42440664583)):

![this PR: rows of both runs in one frame](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/v22/both-runs-head.png)

Vision OCR of that bitmap, at the boundary where the runs meet ([full text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/v22/both-runs-head.ocr.txt)):

```
LIFECYCLE run 879ee244-6104-47ef-9073-093c6d238586   <- events-b, started last
LIFECYCLE run ee0257cb-a7ed-4c32-a854-7f3441499b32   <- events-a, below it
```

The window's own accessibility tree lists 14 rows for that frame: 7 for `879ee244…` and 7 for `ee0257cb…` ([dump](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/v22/ax-head.txt)).

`main`, same two turns, same window, same capture path ([run 42440671079](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/42440671079)): the tree holds 7 rows, all `41db0568…` (the newer run), and scrolling to the end leaves nothing behind ([window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/v22/base-window.png), [after scrolling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/v22/base-scrolled.png), [scroll clip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/v22/scroll-main.mp4)).

| build | runs in the window | rows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` — `id: \.seq` | 1 | 7 |
| this PR — `id: \.id` | 2 | 7 + 7 |

Earlier passes on this runner reported "inconclusive" for a harness reason, not a product one: wheel events only reach the frontmost app there, so those runs scrolled a backgrounded window and captured identical frames. The harness now sets the process frontmost, verifies `AXFocused`/`AXMain`, and refuses to emit a verdict unless the capture changes (or the whole list already fits).

**Committed test, both ways**: `AgentEventsWindowRowIdentityTests` built and run against the same branch with the one line reverted ([run 41197202500](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41197202500)) and as shipped ([run 41197195509](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41197195509)):

```
base:  Expectation failed: (rows -> ["run-b"]) == ["run-a", "run-b"]
head:  test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed after 0.419 seconds
```

**In-process harness**: [before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/agent-events-before-seq-key.png) / [after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/agent-events-after-unique-id.png).

Upstream already encodes the per-run reset: `src/infra/agent-events.test.ts:144` expects `[1, 2, 1, 1]`.

prs.title: fix(codex): Codex turns fail when a plugin MCP server shares a configured server's name
prs.body:
Closes #194825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Codex-harness turn fails with `url is not supported for stdio in mcp_servers.<name>` when a plugin bundles an MCP server with the same name as a server in `mcp.servers`.

## User Impact

User impact: a configured MCP server now wins a name collision with a plugin's bundled server for Codex turns, as it already does for the merged static surface. Codex turns start, and fallback chains ending in a Codex model work again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex receives MCP servers from two projections: the bundle thread patch and the user-server (configured) projection. The bundle patch kept bundled names that an enabled configured server already owns, so Codex merged both into one `mcp_servers.<name>` table carrying the plugin's `command` and the configured `url`. That combination is rejected at `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:321` (`throw_if_set("stdio", "url", …)`) in the sibling `../codex` checkout.

The bundle patch now drops entries shadowed by an enabled configured server, using the same enabled/session-override rule as the user-server projection. This happens before plugin data dirs are prepared, so a shadowed plugin server no longer gets a data dir either.

Cutover: the bundle path projected durable "Allow Always" grants only for configured names (#136019). Those names can no longer appear in the bundle patch, and the user-server projection already projects their grants (`bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts`), so that dead filter and its test are removed. The optional `agentId` field stays on the exported `LoadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigParams` SDK type, because removing it would change a public contract.

Accepted edge: when a configured server is enabled but excluded for the agent by `isCodexMcpServerAllowedForAgent`, the bundled copy is still dropped. The operator configured that name, so it is not silently replaced by the plugin's server.

## Evidence

- New regression `leaves a same-named bundled server to the enabled configured server (#194825)` reproduces the issue's shape (bundled stdio `gbrain` plus configured HTTP `gbrain`). The patch now holds only `notes`, and `gbrain` is in `userStaticServerNames`.
- Updated `lets user config disable a same-named bundled server unless the session enables it`: a session override enables the configured server, which now owns the name rather than shipping the bundled copy alongside it.
- Red/green: both cases fail against `origin/main`'s `codex-mcp-config.ts` (2 failed / 5 passed) and pass with the fix (7/7).
- Sibling suites green: `bundle-mcp-codex.user-config` 12/12, `run-attempt.configured-mcp` 23/23, `thread-lifecycle.configured-mcp-ownership` 5/5, `attempt-startup*` (20, 9, 4, 3), `mcp-app-session-preparation` 4/4, `run-attempt-client-prewarm` 5/5.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Codex app-server turn. It needs a ChatGPT-authenticated codex-cli plus a plugin bundling a same-named stdio server. The reporter verified the equivalent local patch on 2026.11.1 with codex-cli 0.167.0.

prs.title: fix(ui): consume --session-row-actions-reserve so touch session rows stay clickable
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Session rows in the Control UI sidebar become silently unclickable when the touch-mode stylesheet block applies (`@media (hover: none), (pointer: coarse)` — headless browsers, remote-desktop sessions, and touch-primary Windows configurations report this even with a mouse attached).

Diagnosis + runtime repro: #194768 (comment with instrumented evidence).

### Why This Change Was Made

The touch block renders always-tappable 44×44 Pin/Archive/Menu buttons over each session row and assigns `--session-row-actions-reserve` (48/92/136px) so the row link stays clear of them. However the variable **is never consumed** — it is assigned in five places and read in zero. The link's hit area therefore extends under the buttons: clicks intended for the session land on the action buttons, and the navigation silently never happens (no pushState, no intent event, no RPC, no console error).

### User Impact

Before: clicking a session row (anywhere over the action-button zone) does nothing — the previously active session stays open, which reads as "session switching is broken".

After: the row link's hit area ends before the action buttons (`margin-inline-end: var(--session-row-actions-reserve, 0px)`), so row clicks always navigate and the buttons remain fully tappable.

### Evidence

Instrumented repro against 2026.11.1 (managed Chromium, gateway :18789):

- With the shipped CSS: `document.elementsFromPoint` at the row click zone returns `BUTTON.session-action--pin` as the top element; a scripted click produced **zero** `pushState`/intent events (navigation never attempted).
- With this rule injected at runtime: the link box narrowed by the reserved width, and the **same click** fired the navigation intent (`defaultPrevented: false`), pushed the target session route, and opened the session.

### Notes

- Touch behavior is unchanged: buttons stay always-visible/tappable; only the link's hit area is now actually reserved.
- `:has()`-based reserve values (48/92/136px) are untouched.
