prs.title: improve(cron): surface scheduled jobs blocked on a missing creator channel and guide recovery
prs.body:
Related: #162087

## What Problem This Solves

An automation can retain a named-account tool cap while losing its recorded creator channel. For a tool-runtime job whose creator origin is unknown and whose owner key supplies no group/channel reference, the account liveness guard cannot resolve the channel and rejects the run. The retained head/base reproduction used a synthetic `qa-channel` DM job whose origin became unknown after an operator CLI edit. It did not reproduce an original job from a release that predates origin recording; applicability to those older jobs is inferred from the shared [origin normalization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe17c08e16d9c00d7e645e25480c39493028a791/src/cron/scheduled-tool-policy.ts#L12) and guard path.

The authenticated same-cap re-save path already exists, as the reported head/base proof below demonstrates. On the base, the reproduced job's inventory does not flag this condition, and its run error suggests re-adding the account even though that synthetic account is configured and running.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now discover blocked jobs and recover them without demoting their authority. `openclaw automations status` reports a `reauthorizationRequired` count, each affected job's details and list entries flag `reauthorizationRequired: true`, and the run error names the real cause and the least-privilege recovery: re-save the job's tool cap from the creator's authenticated turn (which records a fresh origin via the existing reauthorization path), or recreate it from the intended account.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the guided-recovery side of the failure mode recommended by the security review on #162087 ("require guided reauthorization: keep the fail-closed boundary and add a clear operator or creator recovery flow"). It does not change the boundary: the liveness guard still fails closed; the change only detects the exact blocked class, surfaces it, and makes the error accurate. The trigger-path origin threading is already merged (#176158) and is not touched here. The [detector](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe17c08e16d9c00d7e645e25480c39493028a791/src/cron/tools-allow.ts#L73) checks named-account policy, unknown creator origin and an owner key without a group/channel reference. It excludes jobs that do not construct agent tools.

## Evidence

Source head: `fe17c08e16d9c00d7e645e25480c39493028a791`, which merges main `0d38c2dfcbfb`.

### Author-reported shipped Gateway proof, October 26

The execution results below are retained from the October 26 author report. This refresh independently inspected current source, review records and hosted check metadata; it did not inspect the original local execution receipts or rerun the Gateway proof. The current-head review accepted the report within the synthetic-channel and CLI-edited-origin limits stated below.

I built the head (tree `8132c05bdac84fa711ae03d9bf8fafd50ab82dd9`) and its main parent `0d38c2dfcbfbb1ae2bec19a0a26973640390a5a8` (tree `40c5902ba2f3ece22bf6461af8bfe93ad3b34398`) on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime`. Both exited 0. `dist/entry.js` SHA256 is `ae7797afd96e9a9fb60d6bf1ec8cb1a0ea9383307cf740a151ba0ac4015ad913` for the head and `a1454578a78ce6c7614a1113671823495c9ad187b78d4e161c0102e5046bc991` for main. Tracked source was unchanged before each run.

Each run used a fresh HOME, state and config and a loopback Gateway started with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`. The channel is the repository's `qa-channel` plugin on its local QA bus (`extensions/qa-lab`), with accounts `default` and a named `creatorbot`, `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"` and `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["alice"]`. The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` with scripted responses. Every operator step goes through the shipped CLI. The DM sender `alice` is synthetic; no Telegram or Discord account and no real provider were used.

The script:

1. `alice` DMs `creatorbot` and the scripted model calls `automations` `add` with `toolsAllow: ["read"]`. The Gateway stores cap `["read","skills_read"]`, account-mode policy, owner `agent:main:qa-channel:direct:dm:alice` on `creatorbot`, and creator origin `{"kind":"external","channel":"qa-channel"}`. The origin is store-private, so I read it from the job row with a read-only SQLite open rather than from a projection.
2. The operator reschedules the job from the CLI with `openclaw automations edit <id> --every 1m`. Remote management carries no creator source, so the stored origin becomes `{"kind":"unknown"}` while the cap, owner and account stay the same. The detector and the run guard normalize that to the same unknown origin as a job saved before origins were recorded. I did not reproduce an actual pre-origin row from an older release.
3. Discovery, rejection, same-cap re-save from an authenticated `alice` DM turn, then the next scheduled occurrence.

Head run, 18:03:55Z to 18:07:54Z, condensed from the run transcript (commands verbatim, JSON trimmed to the fields this PR changes, exit codes kept):

```text
18:04:45Z  qa-channel creatorbot -> dm:alice "PROOF-178677-CREATED"        (job bd23054f-4e32-4342-b0ed-412d95c95b8e)
           stored: toolsAllow ["read","skills_read"], mode account, accountId creatorbot, callerOrigin {"kind":"external","channel":"qa-channel"}
$ openclaw automations status                     "jobs": 2, "reauthorizationRequired": 0                      [exit 0]
$ openclaw automations edit <id> --every 1m       "everyMs": 60000, "reauthorizationRequired": true            [exit 0]
           stored: toolsAllow ["read","skills_read"], mode account, accountId creatorbot, callerOrigin {"kind":"unknown"}
$ openclaw automations status                     "jobs": 2, "reauthorizationRequired": 1                      [exit 0]
$ openclaw automations get <id>                   "reauthorizationRequired": true                              [exit 0]
$ openclaw automations list --json                proof check-in: true; Memory Dreaming Promotion: false        [exit 0]
$ openclaw gateway call cron.list --params '{"compact":true}' --json
                                                  proof check-in: true; Memory Dreaming Promotion: (absent)    [exit 0]
18:06:04.154Z  scheduled run: "status": "error", "error": "Scheduled account \"creatorbot\" is unavailable: the job has no
               recorded creator channel, so its scheduled authority cannot be resolved. Re-save the job's tool cap from the
               creator's authenticated turn to record it, or recreate the automation from the intended account."
$ openclaw automations run <id> --wait --wait-timeout 3m --poll-interval 2s
                                                  "completionStatus": "failed", same error (run 18:06:20.081Z) [exit 1]
18:06:35Z  qa-channel dm:alice -> creatorbot "Re-save my check-in automation's tools as read, same as before."
           scripted model calls automations update {"payload":{"kind":"agentTurn","toolsAllow":["read","skills_read"]}}
           stored: toolsAllow ["read","skills_read"], mode account, accountId creatorbot, callerOrigin {"kind":"external","channel":"qa-channel"}
$ openclaw automations status                     "jobs": 2, "reauthorizationRequired": 0                      [exit 0]
$ openclaw automations get <id>                   "reauthorizationRequired": false                             [exit 0]
$ openclaw automations list --json                proof check-in: false                                        [exit 0]
$ openclaw gateway call cron.list --params '{"compact":true}' --json
                                                  proof check-in: (absent)                                     [exit 0]
18:07:22.253Z  scheduled run: "status": "ok", "summary": "PROOF-178677-SCHEDULED-OK", "deliveryStatus": "delivered"
               qa-channel creatorbot -> dm:alice "PROOF-178677-SCHEDULED-OK"
```

The two rejected runs reached no model. The mock recorded 6 requests in the whole run: 2 for the create turn, 1 for the scheduler's existing owner-conversation repair brief after the second failure (Gateway run id `cron-failure-repair:8717eb54-...`), 2 for the re-save turn, and 1 for the recovered scheduled run. The Gateway log shows the two blocked runs ending in 686 ms and 56 ms with the error above.

Control on main `0d38c2dfcbfb`, same script, 18:08:11Z to 18:19:46Z:

```text
$ openclaw automations status                     "jobs": 2   (no reauthorizationRequired field)           [exit 0]
$ openclaw automations get / list --json / gateway call cron.list compact
                                                  no reauthorizationRequired field on any row, before or after the edit
18:12:52.947Z, 18:13:53.054Z  scheduled runs: "error": "Scheduled account \"creatorbot\" is unavailable. Re-add it to the
               channel configuration, or recreate this automation from the intended account."
$ openclaw automations run <id> --wait ...        "completionStatus": "failed", same error                      [exit 1]
           same-cap re-save from the alice DM -> callerOrigin {"kind":"external","channel":"qa-channel"}
18:19:21.268Z  scheduled run: "status": "ok", "summary": "PROOF-178677-SCHEDULED-OK", "deliveryStatus": "delivered"
```

On main the same job stays undiscoverable and its error tells the operator to re-add `creatorbot`, which was configured and running throughout: the Gateway logged `[qa-channel] [creatorbot] starting account` at startup, and every reply in the run, including the one sent during the blocked window, went out through `creatorbot`. The re-save path itself already existed on main and recovered there too, so this PR's change is the discovery surface and the accurate error, not the recovery mechanism.

Two earlier head attempts are excluded. In the first, `alice` was not a configured owner, so `automations` refused with "needs the owner's authority" and no job was created. The second re-saved `["read"]` instead of the stored `["read","skills_read"]`, which narrowed the cap, so it was not a same-cap re-save. Its status, get and list results, rejection, recovery and scheduled run otherwise matched the run above; it did not query the compact list.

### Author-reported base and head runs of the added tests

The PR's three changed test files, run with `pnpm test <files>` on October 26:

- Head `fe17c08e16d9`: `cron-tool.output-contract.test.ts` 5/5, `tools-allow.test.ts` 7/7, `agent-tools.policy.test.ts` 17/17.
- The same three files copied over main `0d38c2dfcbfb`: `accepts the reauthorization flags that Gateway projections emit` fails (1 failed, 4 passed); all 7 detector cases fail with `TypeError: cronJobNeedsCreatorReauthorization is not a function`; `names the missing creator channel when a DM-key scheduled account cannot resolve a channel` fails against the old message (1 failed, 16 passed).

### CI and review, refreshed November 1

Across all workflows attached to `fe17c08e16d9c00d7e645e25480c39493028a791`, all 160 check runs are terminal: 88 success, 71 skipped, one neutral; none failed. Those totals are the full head inventory, not the job count of a single workflow. [CI run 40255363226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40255363226) and its changed-test, typecheck and lint jobs passed. The test counts above are the previously reported head/base runs, not new execution in this refresh.

The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178677#issuecomment-6299241359) accepts the bounded synthetic Gateway proof and identifies no remaining source findings. Source inspection independently confirms that the [canonical job schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe17c08e16d9c00d7e645e25480c39493028a791/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts#L511) declares `reauthorizationRequired`; get, full list, add and update inherit it, while [compact list and status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe17c08e16d9c00d7e645e25480c39493028a791/src/agents/tools/cron-tool-output-schema.ts#L47) declare the flag and nonnegative count. The original schema finding is addressed in this head.

The separate [security-sensitive and combined commit statuses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40256618010) remain failed: "A maintainer must approve the current PR revision". The [guard notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178677#issuecomment-6298677887) names this exact head and `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts`. A qualified maintainer must review it and post the required approval command. No security approval or merge is claimed.

### Limits

- The channel is the repository's synthetic `qa-channel`, not Telegram or Discord. The authenticated turn and the scheduled delivery go through the same channel plugin boundary, but no real transport was exercised.
- The unknown origin came from an operator CLI edit, not from a job written by a release that predates origin recording.
- The human `openclaw automations show` view does not print the flag; the JSON surfaces above do. This PR does not change `show`.

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user ignores the question number in replies like "1. Deny"
prs.body:
Closes #190485
Related: #173760, #173845, #146646

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a multi-question `ask_user` answer is saved as `1. Deny`, lands on the wrong question, or is rejected when the user numbers each reply line the way the prompt numbers the questions.

## User Impact

User impact: replying `1. Deny` and `2. Approved` on separate lines answers question 1 with `Deny` and question 2 with `Approved`, in any line order. A reply that answers only some questions is still rejected and the question stays open. Multi-question prompts now label questions `Question 1: Deploy` and number each question's options from 1. On Telegram and Signal, the old `1. Deploy` header ran together with the option lines into one list (`4. Checks`), so answering by the displayed number picked the wrong question. Single-question cards rendered as Telegram messages or Teams cards now number their options to match "Reply with the number".

Compatibility: in a multi-question reply, a line starting with digits, a dot and whitespace (`2. Approved`) is read as an answer to that question number. `1.5`, `Node.js: 22` and `U.S. region: East` parse as before. A line matched to a question by number or id no longer also fills another question by position. On main, `2: Approved` alone completed question 1 with the text `2: Approved`; it is now rejected as incomplete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply parser only treated `:`, `=` and `-` as key separators. `1. Deny` stayed positional, so the agent received `1. Deny` as the answer, reordered lines landed on the wrong question, and questions with fixed options rejected the reply. Numbered lines are now a separate rule that requires whitespace after the dot, checked before the unchanged keyed syntax. The single-question card text now uses the same `1. Label - description` lines as the text prompt.

Multi-question prompts numbered each question (`1. Deploy`) directly above options that also start at `1.`. Telegram and Signal render markdown lists with their own numbering, so the header and the options became one list: `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`. Questions are now labelled `Question 1: Deploy`. That is not a list marker, so each question's options render from 1, and the question number is the one the `1. answer` rule binds.

The first revision of this PR also copied a single-line reply into every question. That was wrong: it invented answers the user never gave and broke the incomplete-answer contract from #146646. It is removed. The multi-question guidance wording is left to #173845, so this PR no longer touches that string.

The live replies in #190485 were each a single line for a two-question card, so they were incomplete and their rejection was correct. That issue is corrected.

## Evidence

- Regression table in `src/agents/harness/user-input-bridge.test.ts` (5 rows): 5/5 pass. With `user-input-bridge.ts` from main (`1b15b48e2f3`), 2 rows fail: `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"`, and a lone `2. Approved` fills question 1 with `"2. Approved"`. With the previous head (`303c244630d`), 4 rows fail: lone `2` answers both questions, `1.5\n2.5` becomes `5`/`5`, and `Node.js: 22` / `U.S. region: East` split at the dot.
- Consumers: 18 test files, 354 tests pass locally, including the 3 suites that failed in [run 41326074085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41326074085): `dispatch-from-config.question-custody` 17/17, `session-accessor.question-answer-transcript` 8/8, and `test/contracts/ask-user-msteams-presentation` 2/2 (updated to the numbered lines).
- New qa-lab scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` (mock-openai, real Gateway): `1. Production` alone gets "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer" and the question stays pending. Then `1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent` resolves it as `Production` / `E2E` / `Urgent`, and the waiting run resumes with those values. With main's parser, the same reply is stored as `1. Production` / `2. E2E` / `3. Urgent` and the scenario fails.
- Multi-question prompt through Telegram's markdown renderer: on `b2b86091a7f` the numbered lines are `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`, `5. Unit`, `6. E2E`, `7. Lint`. On this head they are `1. Staging`, `2. Production`, then `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, under `Question 1: Deploy` and `Question 2: Checks`. The new test in `test/telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` fails on `b2b86091a7f` and passes here. Signal's renderer showed the same merged list before and per-question lists after.
- Telegram plugin against a local Bot API stub (scripted model, not live): after an incomplete `1. Production` was rejected, the reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), as `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production`. On `b2b86091a7f` those four lines resumed the agent with Production / E2E / Urgent. On main `f5f27c3ef6e` the same four lines resumed it with `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E`. A three-line reply without the replay was not run on main.
- Card text from the real Telegram and Teams renderers for a single question with options: main shows `- Staging (Recommended): Safer default`; this branch shows `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`. Channels without a presentation renderer already received the numbered prompt text.
- `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean. 22 test files (474 tests) pass locally. Test-line growth is 94 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-numbered-reply-lines.txt`. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails because main is over its test-line ceiling before this PR's lines count: the 11-03 run reported `over by: 834; net delta: +59`. Replaying it on this head merged with `982f3b1ee2b` gives `over by: 49; net delta: +94`, and `982f3b1ee2b` alone is `over by: 49; net delta: 0`. An allocation cannot exceed the PR's own growth, so this clears once main is back under its ceiling.
- Not covered: no live Telegram run yet. The qa-lab scenario answers through `chat.send`, which reaches the same parser and `question.resolve` call as a Telegram reply but delivers the rejection notice another way. In the Telegram stub run the rejection notice did not arrive, on main as well: #193159, which this PR does not change.

prs.title: feat(ui): render LaTeX in Control UI markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Markdown displayed supported LaTeX literally. This renders bounded math while preserving code, escaped input, currency, URLs and sanitized output.

## User Impact

Math is lazy-loaded; ordinary messages request no KaTeX engine, styles or fonts. Equations stay readable as source until ready, and failures keep that fallback. Wide equations scroll inside the message and now show a fade where content continues. Math stays findable in transcript search and readable in paste excerpts and web source previews.

Original contribution by @jjjhenriksen; repair work requested by @RomneyDa. Contributor ancestry is preserved and Allow edits from maintainers remains enabled.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/clawtributor-review-pr-144324)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/41d889a9-23c8-4603-889b-a35ad86acfb6)

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing parser, generation-fenced leaf, shared lazy runtime, MathML and separate sanitizer. One 200-expression allowance covers stable streamed additions and the mutable tail. KaTeX **0.18.2** addresses GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 while retaining `trust: false`. Plain-text consumers of the shared parser (search, paste excerpts, source previews) read math tokens as their TeX source, so math stays searchable and readable outside the rendered view. Wide equations reuse the table fade convention rather than adding a new affordance.

This remains built-in math, not a plugin. The product-direction deferral in #125222 / #127859 is not claimed resolved; dense math retains real CPU cost.

## Evidence

- Published head: `65a255a2d8e00e681705abe5a8b8f5d2ee8f2c6a`; tree: `edc8b9ffc9e0fadbdd3fc467a074f43f19bf92ae`. Since the QA round: the named test-line allocation covers the new regressions (the PR was over the ceiling against current main), and web source previews now also keep display math (`$$…$$`) in titles and search excerpts, per hosted review. That fix's regression fails on the previous head and passes now; 64/64 affected tests, oxfmt, oxlint, typecheck and the test-line ratchet against main `e5253a3b05` passed. Signed fast-forwards preserve contributor ancestry; it merges cleanly with current main `802ddc70847`. #175507 and #144324 carry the same tree; these PRs are alternatives.
- **Latest round (re-review + visual QA):**
  - Hosted review P2 fixed: math was dropped from plain-text projections. Transcript search text, paste-chip excerpts and web source previews now keep the TeX source (`Solve $x^2$ today` → `Solve x^2 today`, not `Solve today`). Four regressions fail on the previous head for exactly that reason and pass now.
  - Visual QA fix: wide display equations scrolled inside the message with no visible cue on overlay-scrollbar platforms, so they looked truncated. They now fade their clipped edge(s) like Markdown tables do (CSS scroll-driven mask, no JavaScript). Equations that fit are never masked, keyboard focus drops the fade so the focus ring stays visible, and engines without scroll timelines keep their native scrollbar. The new browser test fails without the CSS and passes with it in **Chromium and WebKit (6/6 each)**.
  - 374 affected UI tests across 20 files (math, streaming, paste, source previews, chat-thread consumers), UI typecheck, lint, format, production build and `ui:check-performance` (zero violations) passed; test-line ratchet passed with no allocation change. Independent P0–P2 reviews of both changes were scoped-clean.
- **Earlier rounds (unchanged inputs, reused):** Node-safe math element registration with a real red/green Node regression; one 200-expression budget across a whole streamed message; KaTeX 0.18.2 (GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7); measured Chat boot allowance kept separate from upstream baselines (all 13 effective limits unchanged); finite-animation settlement in one native-menu geometry test. The previous head passed dependency review and the aggregate CI/security gate.

Not claimed: a real-model Gateway run, product-direction sign-off on built-in math, or a cause for one historical WebKit overlay-bounds flake (it passed on the matching-runtime replay and later heads). No merge or auto-merge is requested. Fresh hosted CI must evaluate this head.

### Visual QA (production UI build, synthetic conversation, mocked Gateway)

Wide equation after the fix: start (right edge fades), mid-scroll (both edges), end (left edge only):

![Wide equation at start](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e574f4b-d99f-465c-82d0-adca9e58a939)
![Wide equation mid-scroll](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aac7d626-2402-4b3e-ad9d-dca1f7713aa5)
![Wide equation at end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33ab7d56-a064-4f7e-a0b2-e2fe9f7e2355)

| | Before (previous head) | After (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| Light, 1600×1200 | ![Before light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec9ad42a-b271-4549-b5e5-2581df466cbf) | ![After light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5f6e2af-196e-4b55-9d68-0df4d556cf49) |

| Dark, 1600×1200 | Mobile, 390×844 |
|---|---|
| ![After dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fb4cad5-0c55-41c2-aa9d-3e5545141b0f) | ![After mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4123ab4-97ba-4172-b880-0c97613f7315) |

The only visible difference between before and after is the edge fade on the wide equation. Inline, display and table math, literal code, prices and dark contrast are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep reload explanation when toast assets retire
prs.body:
Fixes #194730

## What Problem This Solves

A retired toast asset hides the explanation when unsaved config correctly blocks reloading an outdated Control UI tab.

## User Impact

The save-or-discard explanation stays visible alongside Retry and Dismiss even when the rich toast renderer cannot load. Draft protection, reload admission, and ordinary loaded toast behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The eager import-error fallback now presents retained active notice messages and descriptions with the existing redactor. A read-only copy preserves Node/fragment content for a later successful Retry. The existing toast owner and lazy renderer keep their responsibilities; there is no new notification manager or fallback action policy.

## Evidence

- Independently reproduced on the base through two production UI builds, the production static HTTP handler, and synthetic Gateway RPC. Actual Activity and toast assets returned 404; dirty config and the current document survived. The only failing assertion was the absent explanation.
- Final built proof passes both clean and dirty cases. After owner-invoked explicit discard, one reload preserves the Activity route/query and connects to the current build; no config write occurs. Discard is invoked through the existing app owner, not a Settings Discard click.
- 39 focused unit/browser tests pass, including loaded ordinary toasts, original notice retention, fragment Retry, dismissal, and a second pending notice arriving during fallback. Two production E2E cases pass separately.
- UI production/test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, controller guard, i18n verification, test-line ratchet and diff checks pass. Fresh independent parent source/visual review completed on `94d45c8d514..7ac8a2785ad`; no local autoreview or ClawSweeper run is claimed.
- Test cost: touched unit 1.32s Vitest/2.16s command wall; browser 0.707s/2.51s; production E2E 106.60s Vitest for two cases including four fixture builds. CI seconds unavailable. Allocation 83 exactly funds net regression growth.
- Printed raw startup shared chunk increases approximately 0.60kB; rich toast chunks remain lazy and unchanged. No latency benchmark claim.

Inspected real before/after screenshots use synthetic data at 1440×900. The immutable anonymous PNG URLs below return 200 image/png and match the captured SHA256 digests. This is Chromium with service workers disabled, synthetic RPC and real built asset retirement, not a live Gateway upgrade. WebKit/Firefox and broad remote CI were not run here.


### Before

![Before: reload explanation hidden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indra622/openclaw/2683cab9a65108829f238e2318dabb6eeec50702/before.png)

### After

![After: retained save-or-discard explanation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indra622/openclaw/2683cab9a65108829f238e2318dabb6eeec50702/after.png)

prs.title: fix(ui): enable heading navigation between chat turns
prs.body:
Related to #154524. Keep the issue open until the remaining review and acceptance work is complete.

## What Problem This Solves

Screen-reader users cannot quickly return from the chat input to a user or assistant turn using heading navigation.

## User Impact

Users can navigate between rendered conversation turns through level-two sender headings, including assistant replies while they stream. The visible chat layout is unchanged. Long histories remain virtualized: only mounted turns are available to heading navigation until more history is scrolled into view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing sender name as a screen-reader-only heading before each user or assistant message group. Keep a single heading for a grouped assistant turn and preserve it as a reply streams and settles. Headings inside Markdown message content remain independent navigable headings.

## Evidence

### Main conflict resolution — October 31, 2026

Merged upstream `7232a8de67eff527b3f5764987312f2424beda94` into the PR branch in `ea07f0d783be5aee34dbe5915ae659980a1792c2`, preserving the existing commits and main's native Solid renderer and reply-connector changes. Migrated the heading test to the current transcript fixture and lifecycle, retained upstream's intentional deletion of the external-pending-input E2E test, and regenerated the raw-copy baseline. Identical message-group prop declarations now share a type to remain within the file-size lint limit.

- Focused heading and transcript invalidation tests: **30 passed**, 9.71 seconds Vitest wall time, one worker (`pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-headings.test.tsx src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-invalidation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`). Hosted CI timings are pending. Solid reactivity diagnostics were emitted; the tests passed.
- Production UI build, UI typecheck, scoped oxlint, changed TypeScript formatting, i18n verification, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh canonical Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The subsequent lint repair only consolidated identical prop types and shortened an equivalent assertion; UI typecheck and lint passed afterward.
- This merge does not claim a new Safari/VoiceOver or browser-flow retest. The October 29 browser evidence below remains evidence for its named earlier head. The requested full inspectable composer-to-heading/streaming evidence and maintainer approval of default heading semantics remain outstanding. New-head CI is pending; prior-head CI is not current-head proof.

### Safari / VoiceOver verification — October 29, 2026

The contributor manually tested the current Solid implementation in Safari with VoiceOver and confirmed:

- Heading navigation works between mounted user and assistant turns.
- Sender headings render correctly.
- The assistant reply streams and completes as expected.
- The agent heading is available during streaming and remains after completion.

This exercised the UI renderers at `30155f0056bffb365238afb3dc44670bfd5af17b` using synthetic Gateway data. Local, uncommitted mock-harness adjustments supplied the normal input acknowledgment and a roughly 12-second incremental reply; the heading/rendering implementation was unchanged. This is mocked Control UI evidence, not a live Gateway/provider test.

A separate automated Chromium browser check also passed: partial text appeared before the final reply, exactly one agent heading was present during streaming and after completion, the working indicator disappeared, and the composer accepted another draft. The completed assistant turn's accessibility snapshot included:

```yaml
- heading "Molty" [level=2]
- paragraph: "Mock reply: Streaming verification"
```

This excerpt omits unchanged surrounding metadata. No Safari recording was captured. Maintainer approval of the default heading semantics remains pending.

### Earlier Solid port (historical)

Ported onto upstream `48d96b4e3b6f2bd79583e0fac438ab91a3cd57c7`. The old TypeScript modules remain upstream's delegation adapters; the sender headings now live in the native Solid turn and stream containers. The merge preserves both original PR commits.

- One level-two sender heading per mounted turn, outside the message-body child structure; existing `sr-only` styling is reused. Working-only rows, inner narration/tool blocks, and continuation parts do not add duplicate sender headings. Markdown content headings remain independent.
- Adapted the heading tests to `mountSolid` and reactive updates. Eight focused tests pass, covering hidden own names, streaming/settlement/name changes, grouped messages plus a continuation, Markdown headings, and actual virtual-window scrolling. The initial five positive regression cases failed against the unmodified Solid renderers because sender headings were absent.
- The existing transcript invalidation suite passes all 24 tests, including the ported sender-visibility and settled/active-run heading assertions.
- Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: heading test file, 6.01 s Vitest / 7.95 s runner; transcript invalidation, 21.95 s Vitest / 24.69 s runner (includes transform/import overhead; test bodies remained under 5 s per file). Hosted CI timings are pending.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passes after regenerating the raw-copy baseline for the shared stream sender name. The baseline only removes the former inline fallback entry.
- Fresh independent in-session source review found no actionable defects. The canonical autoreview CLI could not run because the Codex executable is unavailable; it is not claimed as passed.
- `git diff --check` passes. UI typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:ui`), scoped oxlint, and changed-file formatting pass. The aggregate changed-check run passed its initial guards, then stopped at the raw-copy drift fixed above; it was not rerun in full. An initial parallel lint attempt hit the shared generated-artifact lock; serialized lint passed after typechecking completed.
- Validation limits: current Safari/VoiceOver and automated Chromium browser evidence is recorded above; manual Chrome/VoiceOver testing has not been repeated for this Solid port. Full build, full `pnpm check`, full suite, and the footer-selector E2E have not been rerun. The full suite is **not claimed green**; the earlier unresolved failures below remain historical evidence, not a conclusion that they are fixed or unrelated.

### Earlier Lit implementation evidence (historical)

The following results and manual observations apply to the previous implementation, not a retest of the Solid port:

- Manual testing reported by the contributor: VoiceOver on macOS 27, using the mocked Control UI in both Safari and Chrome; heading navigation looked good. This was mock testing, not a live Gateway/provider session.
- Chromium boundary check using the real message renderer and production styles: the accessibility tree exposes `heading "You" [level=2]`, followed by user content, then `heading "OpenClaw" [level=2]`, followed by assistant content. This is a semantic-only change with no visual appearance change.
- Regression proof: the new heading tests and added transcript assertions failed on the original implementation, then passed with the fix. Focused coverage: 263 tests across message rendering, message headings, and transcript invalidation.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm check`: passed. The changed-scope check against `upstream/main` also passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent autoreview through P2: scoped-clean; no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm test`: completed all 776 scheduled shards in 9,207.48 seconds (about 2 hours 33 minutes), exit 1. The runner reported 31 failed shards. Available per-shard summaries total 261,172 passed, 235 failed, and 847 skipped tests, plus one worker error. These are reported test executions, not a claim of unique tests or successful completion of the crashed worker.
- Diagnostic follow-ups: staging the new test fixed the tracked-file inventory mismatch; the whole planner file then passed all 119 tests (55.98 seconds). Replaying the shared UI suite in its original observed file order reproduced the debug-overlay cleanup failure: 21,761 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped (465.11 seconds). All four new heading tests passed in that replay. The UI failure remains unresolved; a passing isolated test would not establish a fix.
- Test cost, measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `chat-message-headings.test.ts` passed 4 tests in 2.18 seconds wall time (1.28 seconds Vitest); `chat-transcript-invalidation.test.ts` passed 22 tests in 3.01 seconds wall time (2.10 seconds Vitest). Hosted CI timings are pending.

The full suite is **not green**. Confirmed host prerequisites, fixture/contract evidence, and unresolved failures are distinguished below; this PR does not claim that every failure is unrelated or repair them as part of the accessibility change.

<details>
<summary>Full-suite failure findings and complete failed-file inventory</summary>

### Findings

- Host prerequisite failures include tests explicitly requiring Bash 5+, missing GNU `timeout`, and script preflight cases whose login shell selects Node 18.15.0 instead of the test runner's Node 24.18.0. The SSH-upload fixture also references unavailable `gstat`; that attribution remains a strong prerequisite hypothesis.
- macOS probes reproduced rejection of 105-byte Unix socket paths and invalid UTF-8 filenames before the behavior under test. Telegram thread assertions also differ on `/tmp` versus canonical `/private/tmp` paths. Shell completion output contains Apple Terminal session-saving text.
- Managed triage/continuation failures report `managed handoff lease database path changed`; canonicalization is a hypothesis, not a proven fix.
- Source inspection found several fixture/contract mismatches: an obsolete static JSZip mock, missing plugin install metadata, changed native-session retirement timing, an absent launchd mock export, a host-only admission guard reached from worker fixtures, and a startup fixture rejecting the supported Node fallback when `timeout` is unavailable. No unrelated product/test changes are included here.
- PTY evidence shows reused acknowledgement lookup and command coalescing concerns; timing and cancellation cases remain partly unexplained. Local HTTP Git fixtures, Python artifact-server startup, update handoff/migration timeouts, provider compaction, node-worker recovery, plugin lifecycle/admission, sandbox transport, and Mattermost failures also retain uncertainty.
- The shared UI failure is `debug-overlay-layout.test.ts`, expecting zero queued animation frames after cleanup but observing 45. It reproduced in the original observed file order, before the new heading test runs. The exact leaking owner is not established.
- The gateway-methods shard additionally reported a worker `SIGABRT` error.
- The planner failure was caused by the new test being untracked: the planner uses `git ls-files`, while its expected inventory uses filesystem discovery. Staging the file resolved it; all 119 planner tests passed afterward.

### Files reporting failed tests in the original run

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-stdio.sandbox.test.ts`
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.boundary.test.ts`

The repair supplies the localized title to the existing shared search filter without changing stored session metadata. Both sidebar shortcuts track the same selection; other conversations and pages clear it. The optional selection-color redesign is excluded. ## Verified result **Current-head binding:** the PR now publishes `84d5c5b2701fa17be445d53192791a95f4cbe714`, tree `585da1799fdaa3e69b5e1303aaaa1b0342cf5653`, after the necessary target-base conflict reconciliation described below. prs.title: fix(apple): Gateway connections fail behind hostname-routed HTTPS proxies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iOS users adding a Gateway through a QR setup code would fail to connect when an HTTPS reverse proxy routes requests using an exact hostname match. The same endpoint worked through a dedicated proxy port.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway WebSocket URLs now omit port 443 for WSS, preventing URLSession from adding an explicit default port to the HTTP Host header. Stored endpoint ports, Gateway identity, cleartext WS ports (including explicit port 80), non-default TLS ports, encoded context paths, and TLS pinning are unchanged. Cleartext ports remain explicit because existing macOS URL canonicalization treats an omitted WS port as 18789.

This replaces the original SNI diagnosis and custom Network.framework WebSocket transport. Live investigation established that HTTP Host matching, not missing SNI, caused this deployment's routing failure. The original URLSession transport and fingerprint probe are restored, retaining their existing authority checks, authentication, cookie, redirect, and WebSocket behavior; the reviewed transport regressions are removed rather than reimplemented.

## User Impact

Users can onboard and reconnect to Gateway endpoints behind hostname-matched HTTPS proxies without requiring a separate frontend port or another TLS setting.

## Evidence

- Physical iPhone on iOS 26.6.1: the author tested the revised local app and confirmed QR onboarding and reconnect after relaunch, against the existing proxy configuration.
- Native before/after proof on macOS and an iOS 26.5 simulator, using the original URLSession pinning session against the same live endpoint (hostname redacted):

  | Input | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | Explicit `wss://gateway.example:443/` | HTTP 404; no TLS validation failure |
  | Synthetic setup code decoded through the revised URL builder | Stored port remains 443; URL omits the port; HTTP 101 and first WebSocket message received |
  | Reconnect through the same session using the revised URL | HTTP 101 and first WebSocket message received |

  The diagnostic sent no Gateway authentication payload and did not log server message contents.
- Independent IPv4 curl matrix: `Host: gateway.example` returned HTTP 200 with or without DNS-name SNI; `Host: gateway.example:443` returned HTTP 404 with or without DNS-name SNI. Certificate verification was disabled only for the unauthenticated IP-URL/no-SNI diagnostic cases.
- Regression tests demonstrated default-port failures against the original URL builder. After the fix, 73 tests across `DeepLinksSecurityTests`, `GatewayTLSPinningTests`, and `GatewayCustomHeadersTests` passed, including default/non-default ports, IPv6, retained endpoint ports, and encoded paths.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: passed, with no inventory changes needed after removing the custom transport.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repository `check:changed` for the two-file candidate passed, including app SwiftLint, macOS tooling/process suites, and native schema guards; focused Swift suites and production SwiftLint were rerun after retaining explicit cleartext port 80.
- Follow-up macOS CI repair updates the primary Gateway replacement test to distinguish a default-port setup link from a profile's supplied explicit port, retaining all credential retirement assertions. Changed-file checks and fresh isolated autoreview, including secret scanning, passed with no P0/P1 findings.
- Required `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on 7dec4a7aa5b6c44e17af7bd8b1f0c7fa73b8930d, including successful `macos-swift (tests)`, `ios-build (smoke)`, and `android-test-third-party` checks ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34441657776)). The earlier macOS URL assertions are repaired. The earlier Android failure did not reproduce: its exact test and all eight tests in `SettingsScreensContrastTest` passed locally, and fresh CI passed without Android changes.

The native diagnostic proves handshake and reconnect, not a full authenticated app session; physical-device onboarding and relaunch reconnect were separately confirmed by the author. Earlier custom-transport test counts and build evidence have been superseded by this narrower implementation.

prs.title: fix: missing final answer after tool calls when reasoning is visible
prs.body:
Closes #194891

## What Problem This Solves

When reasoning is visible, OpenClaw can show a warning after tools finish instead of giving the user a final answer.

## User Impact

The agent can summarize completed work without running the tools again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reasoning text alone does not count as a delivered answer. Media and other delivery evidence still count.

## Evidence

In the regression case, the agent writes two files and stops after reasoning. Before the fix, the run ends there. With the fix, the agent writes each file once and makes one request with tools disabled to give the summary.

Three fixture lines enable the reasoning case in the existing test. The file ran in 54.28 seconds locally. CI time is pending.

prs.title: fix(cli): expose manualSelectionAllowed in models list inventory
prs.body:
## Summary
- Build the policy-candidate set from `registry.models` prior to `applyModelInventoryPolicyFilter` in `loadModelInventory`, and look up `policyBlocked: true` entries in `buildModelListRow` (`src/commands/models/list.list-command.ts`).
- When a policy-blocked model is still present in the raw registry (`registryKeys.has(key)`), append the `policy-blocked` tag (`toPolicyBlockedModelRow`), preserving `missing: false` while surfacing the manual-selection policy block in `openclaw models list --all` and `--json`.
- Add a focused regression test in `src/commands/models/list.list-command.configured-Order.test.ts` verifying that `models list --all --json` marks available policy-blocked models with `policy-blocked` (`missing: false`) instead of hiding the restriction.

## What Problem This Solves
When `agents.defaults.models` (or an explicit model inventory policy filter) restricts which models can be selected automatically, `openclaw models list --all` (and `--all --json`) still enumerates every model from `registry.models`, but previously dropped the `policyBlocked` metadata from `applyModelInventoryPolicyFilter`. As a result, available models that are blocked by policy appeared identical to unrestricted catalog models in the full inventory output, giving operators no indication why manual selection or routing was blocked by policy (#194738).

## Evidence
- Verified with focused Vitest unit test in `src/commands/models/list.list-command.configured-Order.test.ts` (`marks available models blocked by policy in --all output while keeping missing false`):
  - Input: `registry.models` contains both `openai/gpt-4.1` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, while policy filter blocks `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514` (`policyBlocked: true`).
  - Output of `modelsListCommand({ all: true, json: true }, runtime)`: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514` row includes `tags: ["policy-blocked"]` and `missing: false`.
- All 108 CI build, lint (`oxlint` + `oxfmt`), typecheck (`tsgo`), and test checks on PR #194760 passed (`check-lint-core-1`, `checks-node-core-test`, `checks-fast-core`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, `build-artifacts`, `check-docs`).

Fixes #194738

prs.title: fix(firecrawl): unresolvable baseUrl reported as private-endpoint policy
prs.body:
Closes #135333.
Related: #137783.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a self-hosted Firecrawl `baseUrl` would see a private-endpoint / SSRF policy error when the hostname simply failed DNS (for example `http://raspberrypi:3002` or `http://firecrawl.lan:3002`). The message pointed them at HTTPS or privateness policy when the real cause was resolution failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

`firecrawlEndpointTargetsPrivateNetwork` was swallowing every resolver failure with `catch { return false }`, so DNS misses took the same path as “resolved to a public host.” Resolution failures (empty answers and lookup rejects such as `ENOTFOUND`) now throw a host-specific DNS error; `SsrFBlockedError` still falls through to the existing private-endpoint policy messages. Successful public resolves keep those policy errors. The same classification was previously attempted in #137783 and self-closed over live channel proof this error-path change does not need. The searxng client still has the same swallow-all catch and is left as a follow-up.

## User Impact

Operators and plugin authors who mistype or cannot resolve a Firecrawl `baseUrl` host now see:

`Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: <host>. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.`

instead of the HTTP/HTTPS “must target a private or internal self-hosted endpoint” messages. Hosted `api.firecrawl.dev` and correctly resolving private self-hosted endpoints behave as before.

## Evidence

### Real behavior (system DNS, no mocked lookupFn)

Same plugin invocation path on current `main` vs this branch. `baseUrl=http://unresolvable.invalid:3002`, keyless `runFirecrawlSearch`, plus `testing.resolveEndpoint`. Host deliberately uses the reserved `.invalid` TLD so resolution fails via real DNS (`ENOTFOUND`).

**Before (origin/main @ cdda5825f8bb):**

```text
=== Before-fix real-DNS Firecrawl proof (current main) ===
ref: origin/main
sha: cdda5825f8bb50e4112f13a9405856cad87bfa79
baseUrl: http://unresolvable.invalid:3002
lookupFn: (none — system DNS)

--- 1) testing.resolveEndpoint ---
error.message: Firecrawl HTTP baseUrl must target a private or internal self-hosted endpoint. Use https:// for public hosts.

--- 2) runFirecrawlSearch (keyless) ---
error.message: Firecrawl HTTP baseUrl must target a private or internal self-hosted endpoint. Use https:// for public hosts.
```

**After (fix/firecrawl-unresolvable-baseurl @ c01c38b263a0):**

```text
=== After-fix real-DNS Firecrawl proof ===
branch: fix/firecrawl-unresolvable-baseurl
head: c01c38b263a071d15542606060c6017cac21cdec
baseUrl: http://unresolvable.invalid:3002
lookupFn: (none — system DNS)

--- 1) testing.resolveEndpoint (plugin validation path) ---
error.message: Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: unresolvable.invalid. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.

--- 2) runFirecrawlSearch (plugin invocation; fails at endpoint validation before HTTP) ---
error.message: Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: unresolvable.invalid. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.

--- 3) https sibling ---
error.message: Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: unresolvable.invalid. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.

--- 4) DNS sanity (system resolver) ---
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND unresolvable.invalid
```

### Regression tests (mocked DNS)

```text
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts
# 34 passed — including DNS vs privateness classification cases

pnpm test:extension firecrawl
# Test Files  3 passed (3)
# Tests       103 passed (103)
```

OpenClaw rejects `medium` for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, or sends `HIGH` when the setting reaches the Google request builder directly.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): classify prepared-model-runtime generation supersession as preemption, not agent-runner-failure
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring `heartbeat-main` false **`agent-runner-failure`** (job `7bf06607`), observed live on 2026-09-09 (e.g. run `18:17:12` → failed `18:23:44`, and repeated hourly).

**Root cause — a TOCTOU race in the runtime, not config or network.** The heartbeat run passes its point-in-time idle guards (`resolveHeartbeatWakeStage`), then `main` re-prepares its runtime and bumps the *published owner generation*. When the heartbeat's model turn goes to acquire that owner, `prepared-model-runtime` throws `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError` ("prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded"), which fast-fails **every** model-fallback candidate in a few ms and surfaces as `Embedded agent failed before reply`.

Because this arrives as a **thrown** error (carried on the model-fallback summary's `cause`), not an abort-signal supersession, `resolveReplyOperationAbortReason` did not recognise it, so the run was classified `failed` → a false `agent-runner-failure` alert. The **non-throwing** supersession path already maps to a benign `preempted` skip; this makes the thrown path consistent.

Live evidence (sanitized), run history, and the full write-up are attached to the ops report.

## Fix

Teach `resolveReplyOperationAbortReason(replyOperation, error)` to detect a prepared-model-runtime generation supersession carried by the **terminal error** — direct, `cause`-chained, or inside a model-fallback summary — via a new `isPreparedModelRuntimeSupersessionError` chain-walk (mirroring the existing `resolveRestartLifecycleError` walk). It then returns `"superseded"`, and the existing plumbing (`handleAgentExecutionError` → `resolveReplyOperationAbortReason(op, err)` → `{kind:"aborted", reason}` → heartbeat dispatch) maps it to a `preempted` skip.

Any other thrown error stays a real, visible failure — this **preserves error visibility** and only reclassifies the genuine race. A lower turn timeout or more retries would *not* fix this (verified in the prior diagnosis); the failure interleaves with healthy 260 ms `no-route` skips.

## Not a duplicate-delivery bug

The "duplicate log entries" are duplicate `applyJobResult` WARN emissions, not duplicate sends: the authoritative `cron runs` history has **one** finished run per failure while the raw log has two WARN lines, and all 50 runs report `deliveryStatus: not-requested`. Heartbeat sends nothing here, so there were zero duplicate chat messages.

## Tests

New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-operation-abort.superseded-classification.test.ts` (8 cases): the classifier (direct / fallback-summary-cause / cause-chained / genuine-negative) and the abort-reason resolution. The two integration cases go **RED** when the one wiring line is reverted, and the genuine-failure case stays classified as a real failure. `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p tsconfig.extensions.json` both exit 0; touched existing suites (`heartbeat-wake.preemption`, `heartbeat-runner.failure-delivery`, `heartbeat-runner.tool-response`) stay green (52 + 8 = 60 passed).

## DEPLOY
- target: none (merge only)
- service: agent-runtime
- depends-on: none
- supersedes: none
- frontend-touched: no
- migrations: no
- env-vars: none
- feature-flag: none
- verify: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-operation-abort.superseded-classification.test.ts` (8 passed); revert the `|| isPreparedModelRuntimeSupersessionError(error)` clause to see the 2 integration cases go RED. Live activation is a separate, gated step (install to `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist` + one detached Gateway restart) — NOT performed here because a campaign worker is active.
- rollback: revert this PR / restore the unpatched installed `dist` (previous snapshot); no state or config changes.
- urgency: normal

prs.title: fix: plugin tools disappear for agents with separate workspaces
prs.body:
Related: #194674 (merged; this is a separate workspace-recovery fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled plugin tools, including `x_search`, disappearing from effective tool inventory when an agent uses a workspace different from the Gateway's discovery workspace.

## User Impact

Agents with separate workspaces recover the Gateway's available plugin tools while retaining their existing tool and authentication policy. No configuration migration is needed. This PR covers inventory recovery; actual X invocation and citations remain pending on a separate Research execution failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery guard compared a fingerprint captured for Gateway plugin discovery with one computed using the agent's execution workspace. It now compares the Gateway's discovery workspace while continuing to use the caller's config; tool creation still receives the agent's actual workspace.

Current-owner, manifest-identity, discovery-fingerprint, plugin-policy, narrow selected-model scope and retain/release guards remain intact. No new credential source or global fallback is introduced. Temporary Research timeout diagnostics are excluded.

The integration tests use real selected-model acquisition, the admitting Gateway registry and bundled XAI tool construction. A schema-only mock would not cross the discovery-workspace fingerprint guard that caused the empty inventory. Shared provider/owner setup and a three-row XAI table remove 96 lines from the initial tests while preserving all four cases. The remaining net growth is 177 regression-test lines. The separate allocation record grants exactly those 177 lines under the documented test-line policy; the shared scalar and all other allocations remain unchanged. This preserves existing base slack rather than consuming a moving shared allowance.

## Evidence

- **Red:** on `60521f723188be7c91b768d424cafa1ef1e49453`, real selected-model acquisition passes with equal workspaces and fails with distinct workspaces: expected `['x_search']`, actual `[]`. Both affected baseline files match source base `963de16b208f24f398172db276fba482af98277c`.
- **Green code/test source:** all four cases pass at `5efaa44c7e70e9f1a5220a2c48b4a2735bc0b18b`: direct OpenAI/Codex preview metadata, real selected-model acquisition with equal and distinct workspaces, and full Gateway recovery without widening the selected-model generation. Synthetic inherited XAI OAuth is present; no provider inference or X fetch occurs.
- Negative and lifecycle coverage retains changed discovery precedence, mismatched manifest identity, disabled plugins, unavailable current owner, no cold plugin reload, execution-workspace delivery, and retained work during owner closure.
- **Measured cost:** the focused file passes 4/4 in 70.02 seconds of wall time including compilation/import; reported case times total 3.874 seconds. File-specific CI seconds are not separately available. The cold wall time is why this uses the real composition only at its owning boundary rather than duplicating it across layers.
- Core types, affected test types, type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass for the unchanged code/test bytes. The allocation-only follow-up reuses that runtime proof and validates the native ratchet against both source base `963de16` and CI's exact merge `a921c919268147d320de3976c6fa03840c6290ff` over base `4f84bfd25e78aa35f6eb5fb17c5332d271fdfb29`. The old CI failed by 51 lines because newer main reduced shared slack from 177 to 126; the allocation preserves both bases' existing slack.
- Supporting live evidence on combined candidate `c3d95bd2ece101a370c85d6ae79818214bc7237b` (base `60521f7`) changed the existing separate-workspace Research inventory from empty to exactly `['x_search']`. Its production repair is byte-identical, but that candidate also contains excluded diagnostics and is not exact-head PR proof. Its 59-test inventory suite is supporting evidence only.
- An exact P3 comprehensive review of code/test head `5efaa44` found zero actionable defects. Current-head CI/review remain required; the [native generation for that head](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42429428779) failed before publishing a verdict and does not clear native review. No merge or release is requested.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.gateway-plugin-tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mts --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.gateway-plugin-tools.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --threads 2 src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.ts src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.gateway-plugin-tools.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.ts src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.gateway-plugin-tools.test.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 963de16b208f24f398172db276fba482af98277c
git diff --check
```

The acquisition fixture uses a synthetic non-XAI dynamic model; it does not claim native OpenAI/Codex model discovery. Allocation checks also use task-owned index snapshots of the exact source and CI merge, with the real index and worktree untouched.

</details>

prs.title: fix(cron): agent-less automations cannot be added or edited on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a Gateway with several agents and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, `openclaw automations add` without `--agent` and `openclaw automations edit <job-id> --model ...` on an agent-less job fail with `invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. Select an agent explicitly; CLI callers can pass --agent <id>, ...` (`cron.add` likewise). The scheduler itself runs that same job on the configured system agent, so the job works but cannot be created or have its model changed without repeating `--agent` on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: agent-less automations now add and edit on the agent the scheduler runs them on. The inference-account capture for `cron.add` and `cron.update` resolves the owner the documented way (`docs/cli/cron.md`: explicit `--agent`, then an agent-qualified session key, then `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` or the legacy/sole-agent fallback). When no owner is resolvable at all, the request now fails with the cron-specific hint (`Agent-less cron job has no resolvable owner. Pass --agent <id> when creating or editing the job, or set agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.`) instead of the generic selection error. Jobs with an explicit `agentId` are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.ts` resolved the account owner with `resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg)` in three places (create capture, scheduled operator source, update capture). That helper is marked `@deprecated` in `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts` because it only honors a raw legacy default marker or a sole agent and throws `AgentSelectionRequiredError` otherwise; it ignores `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`. The run path (`src/gateway/server-cron-targets.ts`, `src/cron/local-service.ts`) uses `resolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId(job, tryResolveAmbientOwnerAgentId(cfg))`. The three sites now share one small helper that applies that same resolution, so validation and execution agree on the owner.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.owner.test.ts` (two cases: an agent-less edit on an explicit two-agent fleet with `systemAgent.agentId: "main"` resolves; the same fleet without a system agent rejects with the cron ownership hint): without the change `2 failed (2)` (both reject with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, `agentIds: ['main', 'worker']`), with it `2 passed (2)`.
- Consumers unchanged: `cron.validation.test.ts`, `server-cron.test.ts`, `server-cron.session-target.test.ts`, `cron.list-scoped.test.ts`, `server-cron-completion.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts` (the existing test of the update capture): 160 + 120 + 40 = 320 passed across their three shards, 0 failed.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the two TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt` clean, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` clean (exit 0), line-cap ratchet OK (2 changed source files, no over-cap growth) and max-lines ratchet OK.
- Field data from one Gateway on 2026.11.1 (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`, two agents, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`): `2026-11-07T16:15:08 [ws] res ✗ cron.update 1ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. ...` for `automations edit <id> --model ...` on an agent-less job, and `2026-11-07T18:52:36 [ws] res ✗ cron.add 2ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are configured, ...` for `automations add` without `--agent`; the same job runs on `main` from the scheduler, and the same edit succeeds with `--agent main`.
