prs.title: fix(auto-reply): exec completions keep the requester's current sender and DM tool policy
prs.body:
Closes #177510

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a background command's completion turn loses `exec` and `process` when the sender who started it is allowed only by their own `toolsBySender` entry and the `"*"` entry denies those tools.

## User Impact

User impact: with a `toolsBySender` wildcard deny, a sender allowed by their own entry can let a background command finish its task on the completion turn, without sending another message. Guests stay denied, and changing that sender's entry, or denying the tool for the conversation they wrote in (a Telegram DM entry under `channels.telegram.direct.<chat>`, including `toolsBySender` keyed on their id, username or name, or a Discord guild or channel entry under `channels.discord.guilds.<guild>`), before the completion runs takes the tool away.

## Why This Change Was Made

A completion turn is built without a sender, so requester policy fell to the `"*"` entry. #185476 restored the sender only for command owners (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`); a sender allowed only through `toolsBySender` was never restored.

My first revisions restored too little. Review found four real gaps, all fixed:

- Without the conversation id, `resolveRequesterConversationToolPolicy` skips the channel's `security.resolveDirectToolPolicy`, so an unchanged sender entry escaped a DM-level deny. #185476's owner completions had the same gap.
- Without the sender's username and name, Telegram's `resolveTelegramDirectToolPolicy` missed a DM `toolsBySender` entry keyed `username:` or `name:`, fell back to the DM's unrestricted tools, and the requester's global id entry then allowed exec.
- Without the requester's group space and channel name, a completion in a Discord guild channel resolved group policy with no guild, so `resolveDiscordGuildKey` found no guild entry, a guild or channel deny added after launch was missed, and the requester's global id entry allowed exec.
- `combineSessionEventTargetsForHost` compared only command-owner requesters, so targets from two `toolsBySender`-only requesters could share a batch that restores only the first one.

What the PR does now:

- The session-event target keeps the requester's channel, account, sender id, E164, username, display name, group space (a Discord guild), group channel name, chat type and conversation id, taken from the host-owned tool caller. The group id comes from the completion's own route, which is the requester's conversation.
- The completion turn restores `SenderId`, `SenderE164`, `SenderUsername`, `SenderName`, `GroupSpace`, `GroupChannel` and `ChatId`, but only on the requester's own channel account and only when the turn has the requester's conversation type. A completion routed to another chat stays senderless and gets the `"*"` policy.
- The restore grants nothing by itself: a non-owner's `senderIsOwner` stays `false`, and owner-only effects still recheck at use.
- A batch refuses targets whose retained requester differs in any of those fields.
- Only exec completions and node `system.run` events retain a requester. Subagent announces, cron, heartbeats, session-state notices and adopted durable processes do not, so their authority is unchanged.
- Behavior change for #185476: an owner's sender is restored only when the chat types match; before, a matching channel and account was enough. Where they differ, the owner-effect check now fails closed.

## Evidence

Head `6fbcf9eae1e` (main `586f576` merged in), macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1.

Real Gateway (QA Lab flow `exec-completion-requester-sender-policy`: Gateway child, qa-channel, real `exec` and `config.patch`; only the model is scripted). `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario exec-completion-requester-sender-policy --concurrency 1 --fast`, run at `58bf6c5`:

- This branch: pass. The allowed sender's completion runs `exec` and writes its marker. The guest gets `exec is not available in this turn. Do not retry exec.` at launch. Revoking the third sender's entry after launch (same Gateway pid) leaves its completion with `Unknown tool id: exec` and no marker.
- Same flow with main's `session-event-target.ts` and `session-event-context.ts`: fail, `allowed requester's completion did not run exec: {"launched":true,"ran":false,..."completionOutput":"exec is not available in this turn. Do not retry exec."}`.
- #185476's `exec-completion-owner-authority` still passes in the same run.

Completion-side exec through the real Telegram and Discord plugins (`session-event-completion-reauthorize.test.ts`): the managed tool host has shell tools; DM policy resolves through `telegramPlugin.security` (`resolveTelegramDirectToolPolicy`) and guild policy through `discordPlugin.groups.resolveToolPolicy` (`resolveDiscordGroupToolPolicy`). The completion runs `printf ran > <marker>` through `exec`. 13/13 pass.
- Telegram DM rows: allowed; guest; sender revoked before admission; DM `.tools` revoked; DM `toolsBySender["username:alice"]` revoked; DM `toolsBySender["name:Alice"]` revoked; command owner with DM revoked; DM revoked with the completion routed to another chat; sender or DM revoked after admission (the tool host is retired before the call: `agent harness host capability is no longer active`).

prs.title: fix(subagents): private child results no longer show as delivered in the parent's context
prs.body:
Related: #173650

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the parent agent's runtime context and the `subagents` tool report `delivery=delivered` for a `completionTarget: "parent"` child when the result was only processed in a private turn and nothing was sent to the user.

## User Impact

User impact: after a private subagent completion, the parent's own facts no longer claim the result was delivered. It sees `delivery=consumed_privately`, so it has no runtime fact telling it the user already has the result. When the turn that processed the result did reach the user (a private turn that sent its final with `message`, or a yielded parent's resumed answer), the label stays `delivered`. Settlement outcomes, retries and channel delivery are unchanged, and nothing new is sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main settles a private completion as `delivered` once the private requester turn processes it (`resolvePrivateCompletionDeliveryResult`: "no external receipt is owed"), and `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md` says later parent turns own any outstanding answer (#185388). This PR keeps that contract. The problem is the projection: `buildSubagentList` copied `delivery.status` into the list view and `buildActiveSubagentRuntimeContext` printed it as `delivery=delivered` under "Recently Completed Subagents" for 30 minutes, the same label an announced child gets. The `subagents` wait view copied it too. In #173650 (2026.10.3, `1ecf113bef64`, same rendering code) the registry recorded `delivered` with 0 messaging-tool outcomes and no channel send, and 13 minutes later, inside that block's 30-minute window, the parent told the user the result was already "in the thread above". That turn's request was not captured, so the label is the likely source of the claim, not a proven one.

- Settlement records the fact. Both settlement writers, `recordAnnounceDeliveryResult` (direct private turn) and the requester batch in `subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts` (settle wakes, including a yielded parent's resumed turn), call `recordPrivateConsumption`. It sets `delivery.consumedPrivately` for a `completionTarget: "parent"` result only when the host did not confirm a visible final (`requesterVisibleFinalDelivered`).
- `resolveSubagentDeliveryStatus` in `subagent-list.ts` reads that fact. The list view (runtime context and `subagents` list) and the `subagents` wait view both call it.
- My first revision inferred private-only consumption from a missing `requesterVisibleFinal`. That was wrong: it is a per-requester-turn dedupe receipt that the requester release deletes, that is bound only while `requesterTurnRunId` is set, and that the batch settlement never writes, so a yielded parent's answer that reached the user was labeled `consumed_privately`. The projection no longer reads it.
- Rows settled before this change have no `consumedPrivately` and keep reporting `delivered`. No migration: it is an optional field in `subagent_runs.payload_json`.
- Docs: the private parent completion section and the `subagents` tool reference.

Not changed:
- Settlement outcomes. The existing case "preserves private parent consumption and final evidence: private text" still pins `delivered: true` with no visible final and no send, and the QA scenario still waits for `delivery.status=delivered` on both private runs.
- No tracking of an update the model promised in prose. That is the open product question in #173650.
- "Child results awaiting delivery" keeps the raw status: rows there are outstanding, and the one way a `delivered` row lands there (a retained settle marker) is what #166270 removes.
- The private final text stays in the parent's model transcript as hidden assistant text. That can also feed an "already sent" claim; this PR does not touch it.

pr-simplify: one helper decides private consumption and both settlement writers call it; one helper projects it for both readers. No schema version and no change to settlement outcomes. Removed in the review round: the projection's reads of `requesterVisibleFinal` and `completionTarget`, and the seeded-receipt test. Deltas vs main: production +31/-4 in 6 files, tests +54 (allocation 54), QA scenario +50/-1, docs +9/-2.

## Evidence

Base `f5f27c3ef6e`, head `519a4826f87`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1.

**QA lab** `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` (mock-openai, qa-channel, real Gateway child). After both private children settle, the scenario sends one more DM in the private conversation, reads that turn's model request from the mock, and checks the `delivery=` label for the two private runs and the announced `visible` run.

| Source | Result | Labels (private-first, private-second, visible) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | pass, 1/1 | `consumed_privately`, `consumed_privately`, `delivered` |
| main's 6 production files | fail at `[private-follow-up]` | `delivered`, `delivered`, `delivered` |

On this branch the same labels appear on the session's turns after `gateway.restart`, so the recorded fact survives the SQLite round trip. Both private runs still settle `delivery.status=delivered`. In the private conversation qa-channel saw only "Worker started." and the follow-up reply; 0 of 20 captured outbound events carried private child text or media.

**Settlement**, through the real writers instead of a seeded receipt:
- Lifecycle receipt cases (`recordAnnounceDeliveryResult` via announce cleanup): parent without a visible final -> `consumed_privately`; parent with `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered` -> `delivered`; non-private -> `delivered`.
- Persisted requester batch (`mutateRequesterBatch` on SQLite): private batch with a confirmed visible final -> `delivered`; without -> `consumed_privately`.
- On the first revision `2a25638df1e` the visible-final case fails in both: `expected 'consumed_privately' to be 'delivered'`.
- Removing the visible-final check, the `completionTarget` check, the kernel call or the lifecycle call each fails exactly one of these cases.

**Projection**: `subagent-active-context.test.ts` and `subagents-tool.test.ts` render a settled `consumedPrivately` row as `delivery=consumed_privately` and `deliveryStatus: "consumed_privately"`.

**Focused suites**: 33 files, 668 tests passed (completion admission and kernel, registry lifecycle, delivery state, list, active context, requester yield, maintenance, SQLite store, catch-up integration, announce delivery and requester-settle cases, `subagents` tool, runtime facts, prefix stability, gateway prompt cache, recent-subagents prompt, silent-completion and announce-owner product tests).

**Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:all` exit 0; oxlint and oxfmt clean; line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets OK. Test-lines: +54 with a matching allocation; at `f5f27c3ef6e` main itself is 10 lines over its ceiling (6421662 vs 6421652), so the ratchet reports "over by: 10" until main is back under.

Not covered: a live model. The mock answers the follow-up from a fixed directive, so this proves what the parent reads, not how a real model acts on it. No Telegram or Discord run; qa-channel stands in for the channel. The yielded-parent visible-final case is proven at the settlement owner on SQLite, not through a Gateway run.

prs.title: fix(agents): refresh provider catalogs only for the published owners
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #194911. A scoped config publication (one agent's `agents.entries.` changed) and an auth-triggered publication rebuild only the affected agents. Both still end with `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs(owners.values())`. That walks **every** configured owner on the Gateway and starts `loadFullModelCatalog({ changedOnly: true })` on each, which opens every agent database. On the reporter's ~470-agent Gateways, one agent's config change produced 132 slow agent-database opens, 155 main-thread stalls of up to 4.5 s, and 30–60 minute stalls of unrelated agents' turns. ## User Impact Adding, removing or editing one agent, or changing one agent's credentials, now refreshes only that agent's provider catalog. Unrelated agents on a large Gateway keep answering. ## Why This Change Was Made `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs` now takes the publication's agent scope and skips owners outside it, using the existing `isPreparedModelRuntimeOwnerInRefreshScope` rule: - **Config publication:** passes `publicationAgentIds`, the same scope `refreshPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshotsNow` rebuilt. A full publication passes `undefined` and still refreshes every owner, so cold starts and full reloads keep all-owner discovery. - **Auth publication:** passes the `invalidatedConfiguredAgentIds` it rebuilt. - Standalone, read-only and non-configured owners keep their existing handling. ## Evidence **Regression test.** `refreshes only the published owners of a scoped publication (#194911)` in `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.test.ts`: - With the scope `{changed}`, only `changed` starts `loadFullModelCatalog({ changedOnly: true })`. - Without a scope (a full publication), the unrelated owner refreshes too. | Rev | Result | | --- | --- | | `main` | ❌ `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (the unrelated owner refreshed) | | this PR | ✅ 3/3 | `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts` passes 19/19 with this change. **Live Gateway run.** Windows 11, Node v26.12.1. Setup: - Source Gateway on loopback, with isolated state. - 9 configured agents: `main` and `a1`..`a8`, created with `openclaw agents add`. - A stub model. Each agent's owner is published at startup. - Then `config set agents.entries.a3.model "stub/n"`, which logs `[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.entries.a3.model)`. - A local-only diagnostic, identical in both builds, records every `loadFullModelCatalog({ changedOnly: true })` started by `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs`. | Phase | `main` c61a7c0 | this PR 3de58ec | | --- | --- | --- | | startup publication (full) | main, a1..a8 (9) | main, a1..a8 (9). A full publication still refreshes every owner | | after changing only `a3` (scoped) | ❌ main, a1..a8: **9 agents** | ✅ **a3 only** | On the reporter's ~470-agent Gateway, the same fan-out means each single-agent change opened every agent database. With this change, only the changed agent's catalog is refreshed. **Gates:** - `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean.

prs.title: fix(crabbox): recognize Boat in cloud worker OS discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Boat cloud-worker profiles show no operating-system choices because Crabbox advertises `boat` as an alias of its canonical `ascii-box` provider. OpenClaw also lacked a Boat-specific setup guide.

Requested in https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2119233044204929269.

## User Impact

Operators can discover Boat's advertised Linux target and follow documented setup paths for either hosting a Gateway on Boat or using a cold Crabbox cloud-worker profile. The hosting guide uses private port forwarding rather than public Gateway exposure.

**Draft / qualification gap:** live Boat allocation, node enrollment, an agent turn, workspace reconciliation, and teardown have not been tested. That requires Boat account credentials and authorization for a short-lived billed VM. No Boat resource was created. Full build and PR CI remain pending.

Boat's SSH/fixed-lease support is not proof of support for the Crabbox tool-sandbox backend, OpenClaw desktop, or warm images; the guide distinguishes these capabilities and keeps snapshots/reserves disabled in the example.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume canonical IDs and aliases from the existing Crabbox catalog, pointing them at the same cached metadata. Crabbox remains the owner of native Boat API access, authentication, VM lifecycle, and durable lease identity. There is no new vendor plugin, SDK surface, credential store, configuration option, or lifecycle manager.

The guide was checked against Boat's official documentation at https://docs.boat.dev/ and the upstream Crabbox Boat provider guide. It documents the adapter's legacy authentication/configuration names rather than assuming `boat login` configures Crabbox.

Simplification pass: reuse the existing catalog owner and cache; no parallel provider implementation. Net production growth is 6 lines. Net test growth is 28 lines, covered by the exact, separate test-line allocation for alias discovery and mapped-catalog coverage; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the real installed Crabbox catalog: before the fix `boat` returned no operating systems while `ascii-box` returned Linux; after the fix both return Linux. This is an offline catalog check, not a live VM test.
- New Boat regression failed on the original production code and passed with the fix. It covers aliases/canonical IDs sharing one catalog request, unmapped sizes remaining absent, and unknown providers remaining absent. Existing mapped-catalog coverage now exercises an advertised alias too.
- 95 focused tests passed across the worker provider, platform filtering, binary discovery, and profile suggestion suites (172.37 seconds wall time, including 125.39 seconds of worker compilation). After reducing the regression fixture for lint, the touched provider suite passed again: 67 tests, 60.89 seconds wall time. The final subsequent edit only renamed a shadowing fixture parameter.
- Targeted `tsgo` for the changed production module and repository ambient declarations: passed. Scoped repository lint: no problems in both changed TypeScript files.
- Docs MDX, config examples, and internal-link checks passed; 16,485 internal links checked, zero broken. Docs formatting clean across 1,421 files. Staged `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, complete staged change against base `a606a90b4bf57c143ad51677dd56a4c2426304e2`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Production and documentation are unchanged since that review; subsequent changes only made the test fixture minimal/lint-clean and adjusted its exact line allocation.
- CI seconds are not yet available; this PR remains a draft pending qualification.

prs.title: feat(research): show a quiet research card in the chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194780 removed the Deep research chat card so the side panel was the only entry point, with a redesigned card to follow. Without it, a `deep_research` call in the chat shows only a text summary, which never updates as the research progresses.

This brings the card back as one quiet row that matches the other cards in the chat. It builds on Josh Lehman's (@jalehman) original card from #194780 and credits him as co-author. The design was picked by Vyctor from three prototypes rendered in the real chat.

## User Impact

When the agent starts or resumes research, a card appears in the conversation at that tool call:

- **Title:** the research question, two lines at most.
- **Detail line:** the current step while running ("Gathering evidence (round 1)"); otherwise the outcome ("Report ready", "Partial report", "Paused", "Cancelling", "Failed"…). After that come the counts: sources, findings and open gaps.
- **Actions:** **Read report** (or **View progress** before a report exists), plus a quiet Cancel or Resume when allowed.

Only failures add color. The search icon pulses gently while research runs, but not when the user has reduced motion turned on. The line above the card now says "Started deep research" (or "Resumed…"). Before, it repeated the state at call time, so it could say "running" next to a finished card. On narrow screens the actions and counts wrap whole; no count is ever split. The side panel still works on its own, from Explore panels.

## Changes

- Restore the `research-job` inline view, version 1: the backend descriptor, the `api.inlineView` result on start/resume, and the browser registration. The whole result stays under the existing 24 KB limit.
- Fixes for the three findings ClawSweeper raised on Josh's original card:
  - **Errors show on the card.** A rejected Cancel/Resume, or a failed first read, appears as a line on the card instead of failing silently.
  - **Import through the API barrel.** The view contract now comes from the plugin's `api.ts`, not `src/`, which fixes the boundary check.
  - **Read report opens the report.** It opens the panel on the **Report** tab, and View progress opens **Progress**. A one-time tab request is handed from the card to the panel.
- Card views use the research client in a mode that never touches the panel's saved pending-start state, so a card can't clear a start the panel is recovering.
- Header controls and the session-menu action stay removed.

## Evidence

**Before:** Josh's original card from #194780, which was removed before landing.

prs.title: feat: add optional Phoneuse iPhone plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users need an opt-in way to operate a locally paired iPhone through [lxe/phoneuse](https://github.com/lxe/phoneuse), as requested in [this thread](https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2119248363761889625).

## User Impact

Adds the disabled-by-default `phoneuse` plugin, upstream stdio MCP connection, and an operating skill. Operators must set up Phoneuse on the phone-connected Linux/Hyprland desktop; nothing is installed or enabled on the running Gateway by this change. Existing MCP overrides and tool permissions remain authoritative.

MIT code does not mean zero total cost: the phone, compatible host, local OCR/grounding compute, agent model usage, hosting/electricity, and maintenance remain operator responsibilities. The inspected upstream does not deliver Mac, Windows, Android/ADB, USB control, a managed phone fleet, or an SLA.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses existing manifest-owned MCP and skill contracts rather than introducing another device runtime, transport, credential store, or retry owner. Upstream was inspected at [`6bce214`](https://github.com/lxe/phoneuse/tree/6bce214f3dba4a79c2a273c63d6bab4789493d05); no upstream source is vendored. Setup, dependencies, license/cost/platform limits, privacy, takeover, and hardware qualification are documented in `extensions/phoneuse/README.md`.

**Safety limits:** upstream can acknowledge an action and then fail to observe its result. It exposes no frame-age token, transaction receipt, or idempotency key. The skill says to stop mutations, obtain a fresh observation, and reconcile an uncertain effect before considering another attempt. This is agent guidance, not an enforced freshness interlock or exactly-once guarantee.

**Comparison gap:** the earlier requested YC company could not be identified from accessible context. Its name/link has been requested; this PR makes no commercial feature-parity claim.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/phoneuse.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **2 passed**. Exercises the production manifest/config/MCP owners for opt-in, operator/session disablement, command override, a received action whose stdio response is lost, and explicit observation after reconnect without action replay.
- Isolated real CLI `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect phoneuse --json`: discovers the built bundled plugin and stdio server, with `enabled: false`, `imported: false`, and no diagnostics.
- Targeted repository TypeScript check for the changed entry/test: passed.
- Repository lint for both changed TypeScript files: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed, including runtime/package builds and declarations. The build also reports non-fatal Control UI size-budget overruns (document, JS, and CSS); their attribution was not established, and this change does not edit UI source or relax budgets.
- Formatting, `git diff --check`, generated plugin inventory, config-example validation, MDX checks for the new docs/skill, and internal-link audit: passed (0 broken links).
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete 10-file candidate against base `e64215c411f1addeeb765568c5d82e6a99f9652d`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings.
- Simplification pass: 9 runtime TypeScript lines; all lifecycle/reconnect/authorization remains with existing owners. The whole change adds 367 lines and removes 2, including 112 test lines and operator/safety documentation. No parallel phone manager was added.

The MCP peer in tests is synthetic. Upstream Python, physical iPhone, Bluetooth, AirPlay, OCR freshness, and real-agent compliance with the skill were **not** verified. The README gives the required benign-tap/AirPlay-interruption reconciliation procedure for an operator with hardware.

prs.title: perf(ui): shorten reconnect after an announced setup restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nine fresh isolated first-run journeys found the Gateway available for 1.35–1.88 seconds before the browser accepted its new hello after setup. The Gateway itself was unavailable for 3.47–3.79 seconds.

## User Impact

An authenticated expected-restart announcement starts the existing reconnect backoff at 700 ms instead of 800 ms. The transport continues to own exponential growth, jitter, cancellation, server retry floors, authentication and pairing. Ordinary outages keep the existing seed. The UI already presents Restarting followed by Reconnecting.

A successful hello or stop restores 800 ms. Accepted edge case: a canceled announced restart leaves the smaller seed until the next accepted hello; no extra timer or state is added for that recoverable case. No dependency or protocol is added.

## Acceptance recorded before measurement

Real isolated Gateway, fresh synthetic provider setup, immutable compiled base/head bundles; desktop localhost and 100 ms RTT; 20 serial rotated base/control/head triplets in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. A/A is identical base versus control. Target: shutdown announcement to accepted new hello and usable composer, at least 5% lower median with p95 no worse. The hello metric uses browser-native RPC-observer timestamps, including WebKit; host timing is reported separately. Other first-run steps and established Chat must stay within 5% median with p95 no worse. Noisy A/A is disclosed. No per-frame layout diagnostics during timing. Missing event pairs remain unavailable.

Timing acceptance is pending; this draft is not ready to land. The post-flow CLI accepted-but-not-clean shutdown watchdog is recorded and outside this change.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression | Existing boot suite extended for announced 700 ms / ordinary 800 ms; base fails the announced case; head passes 15 tests |
| Types | UI typecheck passes |
| Strict base/head performance | Zero violations; startup 90,858 → 90,913 B gzip (+55); Chat 1,296,642 → 1,296,697 B (+55); New 804,039 → 804,094 B (+55); CSS unchanged, one startup request |
| Size policy | +55 B is within the checker’s 64 B variance allowance; no caps or baselines raised |
| Test-line ratchet | Net zero; repeated synchronous hello envelope consolidated without changing scheduling |
| Independent review | Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Timing | Pending 20 rotated pairs plus A/A per engine/profile |

Production: +9/−1 (net +8 lines); test source: 357 → 357 lines. The implementation uses the existing backoff owner and adds no state, timer or wrapper. Larger temporary-retry-window candidates were discarded before timing because they exceeded the size allowance.

Related activation layout fix: #194914. This PR makes no visual change.

prs.title: fix: keep filesystem fixtures valid across fs-safe upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The fs-safe upgrade exposed filesystem fixtures that assumed synchronous reads and direct exclusive creation at the final lock name. These fixtures missed their intended fault or contention boundary after asynchronous admission and crash-safe staged publication, contributing to the full scheduled CI failure behind #194589.

Related: #194560, #194589.

## User Impact

Prepares the regression suite for the coordinator's fs-safe patch upgrade. This draft contains fixture changes only; dependency pins, lockfile, and runtime behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep fault injection attached to the actual operation: recognize exclusive sibling stages, observe an existing lock for contention, model both metadata paths consistently, and inject read/cache conditions at the owning boundary. Synthetic volume statistics now preserve real bigint identities. Existing confinement, ownership, cleanup, FIFO, and error assertions remain intact.

The investigation also found two upstream regressions, fixed in openclaw/fs-safe#1079 and openclaw/fs-safe#1081. The non-9p preparation optimization is openclaw/fs-safe#1080. Those corrections are tested together here without landing the dependency bump.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the relevant failures with published fs-safe 0.27.1, 0.27.2, and 0.28.0. Async-read fixture differences begin at 0.27.2; staged-publication differences begin at 0.28.0. Adapted read cases also pass on 0.27.1.
- A local packed library containing all three upstream fixes, plus its matching native addon, passes all 16 originally failing test files: 280 tests passed, one Windows-only test skipped. This includes full lifecycle, migration, state-owner, build-ownership, capacity, workspace, sandbox, memory-read, prewarm, and affected tooling files.
- The real async FIFO swap still rejects. The explicit nonblocking flag contract is additionally covered upstream by `test/path-stress-regression.test.ts` and `test/pinned-open.test.ts`; both async and sync opens consume the shared flags in `src/pinned-open.ts`.
- Formatting, targeted typechecks/lint, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass. Net test growth is 40 lines, with an exact allocation; no new test cases were added.

Release-note context: test-only upgrade compatibility preparation; user-facing fs-safe fixes belong to the linked upstream changes.

Changed-scope PR CI is insufficient. The real manifest generator produces the same main matrices for a same-revision manual main-tier run and the schedule: 75 Node jobs, five Windows jobs, two macOS Node jobs, four Android jobs, plus the same UI/contracts/QA matrices, using the repository's configured hybrid backend.

```sh
head=$(gh pr view <rebump-pr> -R openclaw/openclaw --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)

  -f target_ref="$head" -f validation_tier=main \

```

prs.title: perf(ui): load Settings search schema alongside config
prs.body:
> **Draft: current performance candidate is blocked by the unchanged byte ceiling.** The published head is preserved for review; the refreshed candidate `1845912eaafcc5bb338f5f939cd48502b254e6bd` is local and unpushed. Against `3930e4fa90810b273a4345673052507fcaccdf84`, its New Session normalized gzip is 803,304 B versus the 803,250 B cap (54 B over; base 803,133 B). Three structural reductions were tried: folding schema dispatch, moving pre-hello schema demand into the existing lazy editor, and moving Settings-only search initiation into the existing lazy sidebar. None raised an asset ceiling. The final candidate passes the affected owner/host/sidebar tests, UI types, and scoped lint; no refreshed timing matrix or screenshot claim is made because strict size failed. Immediate schema-loading publication remains required by Channels. Normal same-origin Settings navigation already receives bootstrap config; the remaining proposed benefit is independent search/schema readiness.

## What Problem This Solves

A Settings search waits for the entire config snapshot before requesting its search schema, even though schema labels do not depend on current config values. A slow `config.get` therefore delays schema-only matches, and ordinary remote reads pay an unnecessary round trip.

Start config and schema loading together through the captured runtime-config capability. Preserve a schema request made before hello until the existing editor owner can admit it. A request is cleared on connection replacement or disconnect, and authentication and policy checks stay at their existing owner. Settings navigation itself already renders independently; this change improves schema-only search.

Keep known navigation matches usable while schema is pending. Show an explicit loading status until schema readiness, retain a schema failure even if config succeeds afterward, and make Retry refresh the failed schema receipt. A viewer without operator-read access completes static-only search without issuing schema requests. Unknown or failed schema no longer appears as a completed empty result.

## Evidence

Acceptance is defined before measurement: a 3-second `config.get` delay must improve schema-only search readiness by at least 5%; measure 20 rotated base/head pairs plus A/A in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, with separate no-delay and 100 ms RTT conditions. Weigh delayed benefit against normal-use cost; a small tail movement with a flat median is not an automatic rejection, while a real normal-use median regression still rejects the candidate.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Host tests | 27 passed; schema is admitted before config resolves and neither read moves to a replacement capability |
| Config owner / schema admission tests | Existing capability 48 passed before focused split; dedicated schema-admission 7 passed, including two first-hello regressions reproduced before the fix |
| Settings sidebar integration tests | 5 passed, including pending, persistent failure, held retry, cached-schema retry and denied-read states; new loading assertion fails on the original candidate |
| UI and scripts typechecks; targeted lint/format | Passed on final correction |
| Full-context independent review, P0–P2 | Clean on final correction; includes complete owner, capability/editor, sidebar/search and benchmark runner |
| Base build provenance | Shared same-Mac bundle identifies clean `c9e4fdfa3a50de6c7e06d2fe1756506ecfb4e9b4`; full artifact hashes pinned |
| Head build and strict size comparison | Passed on final merged head `2b1963cfd405`; zero violations against current-main base. Old candidate CI had +163 B Chat/New; the final current-main comparison decreases both routes |
| Startup JavaScript/CSS gzip and CSS request count | 90,853 B / 39,090 B / 1, unchanged. Chat 1,295,525→1,295,440 B and New 802,972→802,887 B (−85 B each); requests unchanged; no cap raised |
| Test-line ratchet | Passed; exact 199-line allocation, existing 21 lines of slack unchanged |
| WebKit RTT admission diagnostic | 6/6 observations passed on the final merged head, two rotated base/head/A-A triplets; not a statistical acceptance claim |
| 3-second delay, no-delay and 100 ms RTT matrices | Pending: 20 rotated pairs plus A/A in all three engines |
| Forever-held/released visual proof | Pending: synthetic-only captures will be inspected and embedded before landing |
| Production Knip | Pending |

The committed `page-settings-search-visit` workload searches for a synthetic schema-only label and records browser-local `searchReadyMs`, config/schema request counts, retained input and whether config is still pending at publication. The original candidate completed delay and no-delay matrices but failed its WebKit RTT reproduction because pre-hello schema demand could be forgotten. Those measurements are historical only; the corrected owner and visible status boundary require a fresh matrix.

Production LOC in touched owners/views: 1,873→1,947 (+74). Touched tests: 2,205→2,404 (+199). Workload/runner files: 2,122→2,224 (+102). Added production code owns pending-schema presentation and first-hello admission; no new Solid effect, subscription, DOM query or cleanup is introduced. Review base: `83f7614cc70d`; final corrected runtime: `c893b803fe2`; final merged build `2b1963cfd405` against current-main base `c9e4fdfa3a5`. The scoped runtime and workload are unchanged by the merge.

prs.title: fix: avoid slow follow-ups from native rollout size rotation
prs.body:
Related: #175256

## Summary

Avoid needless history rebuilding on ordinary Codex follow-ups when the saved native rollout is large but its active context is safe.

## What Problem This Solves

A long-running conversation waited about 91 seconds before accepting a follow-up. OpenClaw rotated the existing native thread because its append-only rollout exceeded `maxActiveTranscriptBytes`, then rebuilt history and synchronously compacted the host mirror. Saved rollout size includes old and compacted records; it is not the current model input size.

## User Impact

Ordinary follow-ups retain the reusable native thread when saved-log bytes are the only pressure. This avoids that replacement's history import and seed preparation. Native token-pressure recovery and legitimate fresh-thread bounded seeding remain in place.

No new setting, schema, retention policy, deletion, or deployment. No measured latency, cache-hit, or cost improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the competing saved-byte rotation decision rather than add another threshold or cache. Preserve safe-path/file-descriptor checks, the token snapshot reader, projected-turn and reserve calculations, authority checks, and the supervised-thread exception.

The regression coverage exercises a native-compacted rollout above 2 MB through the production startup caller, both with and without a context engine. Connection-policy and abort-listener tests now trigger real token pressure rather than the removed saved-byte trigger. The 98-line test allocation is the exact net regression growth; the shared baseline is unchanged.

A separate, explicitly approved 43-line allocation reconciles inherited test-budget debt. Upstream `dd2e7c34b037e052ae181634a7fb19c67e46f9be` already contained 6,571,220 test lines against a 6,571,177 ceiling. This is not additional test growth, a disabled check, or a production change.

Original implementation: @VACInc. Follow-up review and regression coverage: @roboclaw-bot, with @VACInc credited on the commits.

## Evidence

Final head: `e887efe6262fbc204e965f4b9ae7d63828ff6e51`.

- **Exact-head applicable CI is green:** [run 42438851049](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42438851049), including the test-line ratchet, bundled-extension tests, production/test types, lint, security-fast, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Unselected/skipped platform lanes are not claimed as executed.
- **102 focused tests passed:** startup 18, history lifecycle 19, overflow recovery 7, bounded host seed 18, and connection 40. Covers token/projected-input pressure, authority, supervised threads, custom home, safe-path discovery, bounded reads, genuine overflow recovery, and connection-policy/abort-listener cleanup.
- The saved-rollout regression fails against the parent implementation. The image-heavy lifecycle regression fails in both engine modes on the parent by creating `thread-selected-2` instead of retaining `thread-selected-1`; all 19 lifecycle cases pass with the candidate.
- Obsolete startup and connection expectations were reproduced before repair. Assertions were retained and moved to real token-pressure fixtures, not deleted to make CI pass.
- Focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed in **4m 37.3s** on unchanged production code. Advisory UI bundle-size warnings were not build failures. Final reconciliation changes allocation metadata only; it does not invalidate the build or runtime proof.
- Independent Codex review of the complete candidate, followed by fresh reviews of the image-regression and connection-repair deltas, found **no actionable P0–P3 concerns**. The final metadata-only reconciliation was checked against upstream counts and passed CI. Reviewers did not independently execute tests.
- Hosted ClawSweeper is **not claimed as approved**: its [exact-head generation run 42439032304](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42439032304) failed with `codex_or_content_failure` and produced no published review artifact. The independent reviews above provide substitute review.

Tests ran in non-hydrated AWS leases with no instance-role credentials and temporary HOME directories. Initial runtime/test bytes were the original draft plus the reviewed test patch (SHA-256 `cf645f75fd37660ce0db9ba29e5e04dfbb06b4439f1ae463758e12e0dea4bdfe`). The final lifecycle file was separately hash-verified (`e600f9ba60fecf8dad1b08930634fe47b4b6f086c6d5f4fe14375624a57f724c`) and revalidated. The final connection patch was applied to exact head `ba3ca53`, tested in run `run_6d1762382e12756fbbd24cc586841f8e`, then committed as `88a166b7`; subsequent changes are allocation metadata only. No operator Gateway or private conversation was used as a fixture.

Measured file wall times including compilation/setup: startup 65.80 s, final history lifecycle 28.44 s, overflow 14.25 s, host seed 52.04 s, connection 81.49 s. In the preceding hosted run, the bundled-extension job took 173 s, production types 32 s, test types 100 s, and lint 203 s. Hosted values are whole-job elapsed time, not per-file runtime or billed compute. The lifecycle and connection suites exercise the production ownership boundary; compilation/setup dominates the connection wall time (individual cases complete in milliseconds to 3.4 s), so helper-only tests would miss the caller regressions.

### Image-heavy repeated compaction regression (#175256)

The earlier fix moved host byte-bound compaction to genuine fresh-thread seed consumption. This change preserves that owner and removes another route that unnecessarily forced the same seed work. With a compacted native rollout and host history containing over 2 MB of opaque image bytes, two ordinary follow-ups and a cold client resume keep the same native thread in both engine modes. They cause **zero additional bounded-seed preparations, zero selected-history injections, zero native compaction requests, and zero historical-media preparation calls**. The original fresh start still prepares one seed.

Existing bounded-seed media accounting and token-overflow tests remain passing; large *active* token pressure is not ignored. This is production-caller boundary proof with synthetic protocol I/O and opaque image data, not live decoder/provider or full Gateway restart proof. It cannot guarantee arbitrary image request sizes or eliminate legitimate native compaction.

### Remaining limitations

No live-provider/channel end-to-end run, full Gateway restart/plugin-refresh experiment, or interleaved before/after latency and token/cache benchmark was performed. The passing lifecycle tests are deterministic boundary proof, not those live experiments.

Native token pressure can still pause a turn. Large saved files still consume disk; this change does not reclaim logs. Missing or malformed token snapshots can require scanning older data; no new scan-time bound is introduced. Request-size protection is separate from active context: existing WebSocket/node transport bounds remain unchanged, and no new guarantee for arbitrary image-heavy requests is claimed. Retaining useful history may retain more active input tokens than a smaller replacement summary.

**No merge is authorized by this review task.**

<details>
<summary>Original incident and source investigation</summary>

Sanitized measurements from one real Codex app-server conversation:

| Event or measurement | Observed baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Message received | t=0 |
| Existing native rollout | 7,169,386 bytes (6.84 MiB) |
| Configured `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` | `2mb` (2,097,152 bytes) |
| Rotation diagnostic | `codex app-server native transcript exceeded active byte limit; starting a fresh thread` |
| Context-engine input | 559 messages |
| Native thread creation RPC | 29 ms |
| Total thread lifecycle preparation | 88,204 ms |
| History injection RPC within that lifecycle | 272 ms |
| Host compaction completed during preparation | 107,775 tokens before compaction |
| Turn accepted | approximately t=91 s |
| First assistant output | approximately t=94 s |
| Final answer / full dispatch completion | approximately t=110 s |

The 272 ms history injection must not be mistaken for the entire history-preparation cost: the asynchronous bootstrap callback runs before that measured RPC. Most of the approximately 88-second lifecycle gap surrounds bounded-seed preparation and host compaction. There is no finer profile proving how every millisecond inside that interval was spent.

The source chain is:

1. `extensions/codex/src/app-server/startup-binding.ts`: `rotateOversizedCodexAppServerStartupBinding` compares the full native rollout's filesystem size with `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` and clears the binding when it crosses the threshold. It runs before normal turn execution. The observed route did not meet the context-engine thread-bootstrap exemption.
2. `extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-history.ts`: a replacement invokes the asynchronous `historyBootstrapItems` callback; only the subsequent `thread/inject_items` RPC has the `thread-start-seed-history` duration span.
3. `src/agents/harness/host-seed.ts`: `bindBoundedSeed` bounds imported history and attempts host compaction before omitting unsummarized history that does not fit. This path awaits `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` before handing the prepared history to Codex.
4. Codex owns the existing native thread's working history and native compaction. Its persisted rollout also contains older records and compaction records; total saved-file bytes are not the active model input. The inspected Codex dependency routes `thread/inject_items` through `request_processors/turn_processor.rs` to `inject_response_items`; rollout records are maintained by `codex-rs/rollout`. Recheck the actual installed Codex revision during live validation.

The incident runtime was OpenClaw 2026.11.1 at base `27ea834825c92c2f4a1de833bceb1a3b21a8de23`, with overlays #193550, #193775, and #193899. The byte-trigger owner and fresh-seed owner were unmodified by those overlays, and the same byte trigger was present on current upstream when this draft was prepared. #193550 also gates host compaction model requests, so its contribution to time *inside* the compaction interval is not independently isolated. #193775 changes access-program selection; #193899 changes model output-budget defaults. The proposal targets the evidenced unnecessary rotation, not every possible contributor to summarization latency. Private transcript identifiers, paths, message content, and screenshots are deliberately excluded.

</details>

prs.title: test(qa-lab): replayed plugin media paths stay text in the next provider request
prs.body:
Closes #168610
Related: #101866

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: nothing fails when a media path from a plugin tool registered under a core tool name, replayed from Telegram history, reaches the next provider request as an image or file input or with its text rewritten.

## User Impact

User impact: no runtime change. QA Lab gains a Crabline Telegram regression on the final provider request for replayed media references, and a mock-provider directive that scripts exact tool calls.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR used to expect replay to rewrite the plugin's path to `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/...`, the behavior #101866 proposed. That expectation was wrong. #101866 was closed unmerged on October 31, and the [closing comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101866#issuecomment-6541917131) found that on main replayed references stay literal text, produce no `input_image` or `input_file` payloads, and leave stored rows unchanged. It asks that a follow-up preserve stable conversation bytes and start from a final-provider-request regression. This PR is that regression.

`telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history` installs a run-owned, non-bundled plugin that registers `music_generate` and returns a PNG under the state media directory. No music provider is configured, so the plugin's tool is the one that runs. The state media directory is a local media root, so the prompt image loader would accept that file. Turn 1 calls the tool and replies with the path through the real Telegram plugin. The last provider request on turn 2 must have:

- no `input_image` or `input_file` part anywhere in `input`, and `imageInputCount` 0;
- the turn 1 reply, byte for byte, in the replayed channel history of the current turn, and separately in the earlier assistant message.

`QA tool plan:` works as before: the mock calls each listed tool in order with the given arguments, then replies, and `{{media:N}}` becomes the first media path the Nth result carried. It now sits at the end of main's scripted automation chain, so `server.ts` is identical to main.

pr-simplify, against merge base `f5f27c3ef6e`:

- Removed: the placeholder expectation and its `path.sep` suffix; the unmanaged control path, which only made sense for selective redaction; the `server.ts` hunk, which after merging main grew it from 2251 to 2253 counted lines against the line-cap ratchet; and the `exec_command` ordering case with its cron argument checks, which test the cron planner rather than this change.
- Still protected: a plan never preempts a scripted cron turn, plan order and media substitution, undeclared tools, drive-rooted Windows paths, and Code Mode `wait`.
- Delta: no production code. qa-lab mock +119/-2, tests +92 (allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/qa-tool-plan-directive-168610.txt`), scenario +217.

## Evidence

Main `f5f27c3ef6e` merged in, on an M4 Pro, with `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history --concurrency 1 --fast`:

- This head passes: 1/1, 22.4 s for the scenario, 105 s for the whole command including the build. The second request has 0 media parts, `imageInputCount` 0, and 2 replayed copies of the reply, both with the path unchanged.
- With a local patch that makes prompt image preparation also scan the replayed inbound history, it fails: `the replayed plugin path became provider media: {"mediaParts":["\"type\":\"input_image\""],"imageInputCount":1}`.
- With a local patch that rewrites the replayed channel-history text the way #101866 did, it fails: `second request did not replay the first reply with the plugin path unchanged`. The assistant-message copy kept the path; the channel-history copy read `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/qa-core-named-<id>.png`.
- With channel-history replay disabled locally (history limit 0), it fails: `the current turn's channel history did not replay the first reply unchanged`. The previous head `e57316ac0fa` passed that same run on the assistant-message copy alone, which is the gap ClawSweeper found.
- None of these patches is on the branch.

Unit and gates on this head:

- The `server.tool-routing.test.ts` and qa-lab catalog tests (scenario catalog and channels, coverage report, CI smoke plan, profile selection, tool coverage report) pass: 7 files, 102 tests. All 13 mock-openai test files pass: 200 tests.
- Removing the plan from the chain fails the four plan cases. Putting it first fails the ordering case (`Expected message tool call`).
- oxfmt, type-aware oxlint (a planted error is reported), `tsgo:all`, and the line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race and max-lines ratchets pass.
- The test-lines ratchet reports `over by: 10` with this change's +92 allocated. Those 10 lines are already over on main.

Cost: the scenario is crabline-only and its primary coverage ID, `plugins.plugin-tools`, is not in `smoke-ci`, so nothing per-PR runs it unless selected.

Not covered:
- A trusted core tool's managed path; I did not look for a synchronous core tool in QA that returns one.
- Windows; the path comparison handles JSON-escaped separators, but I have not run it there.
- Crabline refuses to start from a checkout with a group-writable ancestor directory, so I ran from a checkout of the same commit on a separate volume.

prs.title: fix: show multi-question reply format
prs.body:
Closes #173760

AI-assisted. Substantially follows the shared-guidance and regression shape from #173845 by @D41910; the commit credits Winoren as co-author.

## Summary

- Show one bounded, copyable multiline example in the initial multi-question prompt and invalid-answer recovery notice.
- Document the same accepted reply format.
- Derive the regression's successful reply from the displayed example so guidance and parser behavior cannot drift.

## Issue

Closes #173760.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messaging-channel users can be told to answer every `ask_user` question by number or id without being shown that each answer needs its own keyed line.

## User Impact

User impact: after an incomplete grouped answer is rejected, the user sees a concrete two-line reply template and can fill it in while the same question remains open.

## Root cause

The multi-question parser already accepts one keyed answer per line, but the shared prompt owner and rejection notice exposed only abstract wording. A normal one-line prose reply fills question 1 and leaves later required questions empty, so the recovery path repeated guidance that did not demonstrate the required shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt guidance is the canonical owner for this format. Reusing one bounded constant in the initial prompt and rejection notice fixes both user-visible paths without changing parsing, validation, authorization, custody, or question lifecycle. #190513 remains complementary parser/numbering work; #193400 remains complementary correction-delivery work.

## Verification

- Exact upstream base: `c61a7c0cf6b72f9c35ad8acdc432e132f4d86a50`; the five touched files were unchanged from the reproduced `95363ce54afd893d89cc6bd6645578dba52888d0` snapshot.
- Before source oracle: exit 1. A one-line two-question answer populated `where`, left `game` empty, and found no copyable example in prompt, rejection, or docs.
- After the same oracle: exit 0. It extracted `1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>`, filled it as `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000`, and mapped both keyed answers while confirming the rejection notice and docs use the same format.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --check` passed for all four touched TypeScript files.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Production delta: `+6/-2` (net +4); tests `+13/-6`; docs `+10/-3`.

## Before/after

Before:

```json
{"answers":{"where":"either is fine, and lets do X","game":""},"hasExample":false,"docsExplain":false,"reproduced":true}
```

After:

```json
{"example":"1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>","completeAnswer":"1: Lisbon\n2: 2000","answers":{"destination":"Lisbon","budget":"2000"},"correctionUsesShared":true,"docsExplain":true,"fixed":true}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Multi-question text prompts and invalid-answer recovery now show the keyed multiline reply shape the existing parser accepts.
- **Real environment tested:** Exact current OpenClaw source snapshot on macOS with Node 22.22.3; source-level behavior oracle plus syntax/docs/diff checks.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Node source oracle reading the production prompt, rejection, parser contract, and docs; `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on the four TypeScript files; `node scripts/docs-list.js`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The oracle derived `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000` from the displayed example, resolved both keyed answers, confirmed both runtime messages share the guidance, and exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** The user-visible recovery text now contains a copyable answer that satisfies both questions without changing parser or lifecycle semantics.
- **What was not tested:** No live Telegram account, deployed Gateway, external model/API, or focused Vitest run.

## Risk and scope

Low. This changes shared bounded guidance, one recovery string, one documentation paragraph, and assertions around the existing custody flow. No config, schema, protocol, persistence, parser, validation, authorization, or delivery lifecycle changes.

## Not tested

Focused Vitest did not start. Blacksmith Testbox failed before allocation because the local `blacksmith` executable is unavailable. Local dependency installation failed first because the configured npm mirror lacks `@pnpm/macos-arm64@12.15.0`, then because Corepack's pnpm 12.15.0 cache was incomplete. The repository formatter and autoreview also could not bootstrap through the same blocked network path; no passing claim is made for them.

prs.title: fix(release): isolate Plugin SDK predecessor fetch
prs.body:
## Summary

- run the early Plugin SDK API comparison in a disposable Git repository
- copy only the exact candidate and trusted-tooling commits locally at depth 1
- fetch only the selected predecessor tag from the canonical origin at depth 1 with blob filtering
- resolve the renderer's TypeScript loader from the trusted tooling module, including bundled CI workers
- leave the release checkout's shallow boundary, tags, history, and dependencies unchanged

## Cause

Fetching an exact predecessor tag with `--depth=1` inside the release checkout can rewrite that checkout's shallow boundary. Removing `--depth` avoids that mutation for a full clone but can download broad history for a shallow release checkout. The comparison now owns an isolated repository instead, so neither tradeoff reaches the release checkout. Renderer children resolve `tsx` from the trusted tooling module rather than the disposable repository or a presumed sibling source file.

## Verification

- real-Git regression proves the release checkout stays shallow and receives no tag
- isolated repository contains only the candidate and exact predecessor commits and retains lazy blob fetching
- bundled-worker renderer suite succeeds with no `node_modules` in the child cwd: 11 passed
- focused release-candidate checklist suite: 149 passed
- scripts typecheck
- touched lint, format, diff, and exact test-lines ratchet checks pass
- allocation matches current `main` with zero excess headroom
- exact-head hosted review requested for `95625de42ff3`

## Worked on by

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

The old repeated traversal/context path is removed. Executable production code grows by 11 lines because full coverage requires batch collection and ancestor pruning. The separate 183-line test allocation exactly covers the two DOM regressions; the shared scalar is unchanged.

No CPU profiler, screencast or geometry sampler in scored captures. Main advanced during the experiment; all numerical comparisons retain the same application build, and the probe source remains identical after rebase.

prs.title: fix: prevent missing exports in large standalone builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large standalone builds can fail during native export capture, or silently omit valid entries when earlier bundling has exhausted Bun's process-wide filename store.

## User Impact

Standalone builds capture package exports with fresh resolver state and stop on unexpected resolution failures before publishing an incomplete executable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native adapter sends one explicit export-resolution batch to a fresh process using the same executable, preserving Bun's conditional exports and built-ins. Resource retention and ownership stay in the existing adapter. A separate filesystem resolver checks caught missing-entry errors so a false `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` cannot silently remove a valid export.

Upstream resolver fix: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/36675. Compiler pins, dependency pins and the plugin contract are unchanged.

## Evidence

- A compiler-only reproduction fills pinned production Bun's filename store at exactly 8,396,800 entries and reaches the same resolver panic as the failing OpenClaw build.
- The mitigated pinned-JIT build now succeeds and is signed. Its parent peaks at 8,284,710 filename slots; isolated export capture uses 151,505. The old failed build reached 8,396,656 slots immediately before its final read buffer and panic.
- Stock Bun 2596ac5d AOT builds and signs successfully in 601.8 seconds; the frozen fork AOT build also passes and signs in 692.7 seconds. All three use the same source, plugin selection and build recipe.
- Both new regressions fail on the old implementation: a poisoned parent loses a valid export, and a false missing-module result is swallowed. Both pass with the change. All 30 native/export tests and 20 related module-resolution, WASM and plugin-loader tests pass.
- Existing native-test fixture setup is consolidated without removing any of its 28 cases or 258 assertion calls. Including the new regression file, test lines decrease by five. No test-line allocation is added.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, native line-budget checks and independent autoreview pass. Core build passes in 321.6 seconds.

Runtime builds use the same frozen source and plugin selection. Follow-up commits only consolidate test setup and remove obsolete allocation metadata; the builder and application source are identical to the build candidate. Full application qualification continues separately from this builder fix.

prs.title: fix(models): avoid repeated module probes for absent build stamps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog checks repeatedly probe missing build-info modules before finding the packaged stamp, or all three candidates in a source checkout. Failed native module resolutions can retain directory filenames in Bun, and are unnecessary for reading three known JSON paths.

## User Impact

Catalog stamp reads keep the loaded build's timestamp, or its absence, for the process lifetime. Packaged timestamp precedence and invalid-stamp fallback remain unchanged. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the known files directly and retain the result at the build-metadata owner, including a missing stamp. This avoids native module resolution on every runtime and removes repeated filesystem work after the first read.

## Evidence

- On the pinned macOS arm64 Bun, 100 source-layout calls previously caused 300 failed module loads and 1,100 additional FilenameStore slots. The same instrumented workload now causes zero module loads and zero additional slots. Measured loop time changed from 65.36 ms to 0.158 ms; this is a focused instrumented comparison, not a Gateway throughput claim.
- For the root-level packaged chunk used by the Gateway, 100 warm calls caused 200 failed module loads and 600 additional slots before the fix, versus zero of both afterward (26.05 ms versus 0.016 ms instrumented).
- The regression fails on the original implementation in all five absent/invalid-stamp cases and passes after the change. The successful-stamp case verifies candidate fallback and consistency after the original file is removed.
- Focused suite: 6 tests passed, 0.97 s Vitest / 2.36 s wrapper. Formatting and diff checks passed. Independent review found no actionable P2-or-higher issue.
- Targeted type-aware lint and strict typecheck pass using task-local physical dependencies. Initial linked-dependency preflight was correctly rejected and was not bypassed.
- The 45-line regression allocation is scoped to the previously untested build-stamp owner.

Exact-head CI run [42438204528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42438204528) completed on `460b192501a1b1c3b2fe9a704c51723f9d1975a6`. All selected jobs passed except the baseline test-line ratchet and its aggregate gate. The tested baseline already has a 46-line effective-budget deficit; this PR adds 45 test lines with a matching 45-line allocation, preserving that deficit. Landing uses the native inherited-failure exception and does not claim green CI. The checker and shared ceiling are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ios): Claude CLI tool rows show no result despite returned output
prs.body:
Related: #171975

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Claude CLI chats on iOS see “No result” on tool rows even though the tool returned output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude CLI can embed a result beside its call in an assistant message, with `tool_use_id` and nested `content: [{type: "text", text: "…"}]` but no top-level `text`. Normalize that output through the existing decoder without splitting or duplicating the assistant message. A separate ended activity with no status still means the execution outcome is unknown, not that output is absent.

Native collapsed outcome cues are preserved, including desktop status badges and the mobile uncertainty cue. When output exists but the execution outcome is unclassified, the label is “Outcome unknown.” Rows without output retain “No result” and their existing disclosure behavior. Expanded rows show output and outcome separately. Unknown does not become success.

The merged iOS fix #171976 handled user-role result carriers; this covers results embedded in assistant rows. #191658 is Android-only. Web references: `ui/src/lib/chat/tool-cards.ts` (`extractToolText`), `chat-tool-card-row.solid.tsx`, and `chat-tool-expanded.solid.tsx`.

Users can expand Claude CLI tool steps and read their actual output without a misleading missing-result label. Unknown execution outcomes remain explicitly unknown.

prs.title: feat(ai): record bounded prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations
prs.body:
# Prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations

Implements the approved PRI-1119 minimal design v1.2 (Tier B): bounded, fact-only presence checks that verify whether a frozen injection expectation's full body text appears inside the **pre-submission request object**, on both the `openai-responses` and `openai-completions` paths.

## What this does

- **Pure bounded checker** (`packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.ts`): three mutually exclusive outcomes — `full_hit` / `checked_missing` / `unknown` with explicit reasons (`assembly_truncated`, `body_over_limit`, `expectations_over_limit`, `scan_region_over_limit`, `cumulative_scan_over_limit`, `unparseable_content`, `check_failed`). Caps: per-body 64 KiB, per-message region 8 MiB, expectation count 64, message count 512, and a **cumulative UTF-8 scan cap (32 MiB) covering legal AND wrong-role regions — exceeding it never outputs `checked_missing`** (owner condition 1).
- **responses path**: the existing egress observer frame computes `presenceCheck` (with per-attempt index) when the request carries a frozen expectation set (options-keyed carrier). The `provider.prompt.observed` event gains `presenceCheck` (+ `requestIndex` stamped by the runner wrapper).
- **completions path** (previously zero observation): a checkpoint after `onPayload` replacement and before `encodeBody` emits the same event channel with `egress: "completions"`, `attemptIndex: 0`.
- **runner**: per-run `requestCount` on the run-scoped prompt state (incremented once per attempt assembly), expectation set frozen by the prompt-build phase **after the size guard**, carrier bound per request, `requestIndex` stamped on emitted events.
- **plugins**: optional structured `injectedExpectations` field on the before_prompt_build result (validated passthrough; merged by concatenation across plugins).

No request mutation. No body persistence. Requests without frozen expectations are unaffected: no carrier → no `presenceCheck` field → no measurable added cost.

## Owner acceptance conditions — where implemented

1. Cumulative scan cap (32 MiB default) over legal AND wrong-role regions; exceeding yields `unknown:cumulative_scan_over_limit`, never `checked_missing`.
2. Expectations carry `bodyComplete`; truncated-assembly fragments force `unknown:assembly_truncated` and can never yield `full_hit`. The injecting plugin freezes expectations after its size guard and marks completeness by containment.
3. Event identity reuses existing fields: envelope `runId`, wrapper-stamped `requestIndex` (run-scoped ordinal, incremented per attempt assembly), egress-closure `attemptIndex` + `payloadVariant`. Tests cover same-run multi-request, concurrency isolation, and retry attempt indexing.
4. Event size measured in UTF-8 bytes (table below).

## Measured on the implementing machine (script: `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-measure.mts`)

| fixture | runs | median | p95 | event bytes (UTF-8) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| representative: 18 expectations × ~2.2 KiB bodies, 58k-char system region | 30 | 0.111 ms | 0.192 ms | 2,994 |
| representative: 1 expectation, same region | 30 | 0.008 ms | 0.010 ms | 249 |
| boundary: 64 expectations × 64 KiB bodies (under limits) | 10 | 128.620 ms | 129.286 ms | 10,702 |

## Tests

- `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.test.ts` — 20 fixtures (containment, roles, parts, no-concatenation, prefix-not-hit, limits, cumulative cap, truncated-assembly rule, exception fail-open, completions roles).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-state.presence.test.ts` — 6 tests (carrier binding + event stamping, same-run multi-request ordinals, concurrency isolation, absent-expectation untouched events, truncated-assembly rule through the real transport chain, retry attempt indexing).
- Regressions green: existing observer/transport suites 36/36; runner-side scoped tsc clean for touched files.

## Trust boundary

The check runs inside the host process (host-recorded, not third-party). It observes the pre-submission request object — the exact object `encodeBody` serializes into the wire body via body-override. It does not prove network-peer bytes or model-context inclusion.

prs.title: fix(ci): assert effective selected shard deadlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The selected serial-shard test requires an explicit `timeoutMinutes: 60`, but the planner can omit that optional field when all contributing jobs use the same default. The existing workflow applies 60 minutes in that case.

## User Impact

Test-only repair. No runner size, concurrency, selected test scope, or timeout budget changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the selected-job, runner, concurrency, and exact-target assertions. Check the effective deadline using the same 60-minute fallback as the planner and workflow, instead of requiring one representation. Allocate the two added test lines.

## Evidence

- [Failing exact-head CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42435863274/job/128594867971): the selected serial job has the expected runner and concurrency but omits the optional timeout field.
- A dependency-free Node 26.13.0 probe through `createSelectedNodeTestShardBundles` reproduces the original assertion failure and passes the effective-deadline assertion and exact-target checks.
- Independent exact-head source review completed with no actionable findings.
- Targeted oxfmt, normal signed commit hooks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [Exact-head CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42437385181/job/128599607546): both selection-capacity cases pass on Node and Bun (four executions). The job later fails a separate `runtime-plugins.ingress-load.integration.test.ts` case on Bun; that failure is not claimed resolved.
- [Exact-head build-artifacts job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42437385181/job/128599603638) passed.
- [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42439059270) reports a test-budget failure: 6,571,186 lines against a 6,571,131 ceiling. This PR's two added lines already have a two-line allocation; the remaining 55 lines are inherited debt. No extra allocation has been added. Other observed non-ratchet checks passed.
- The manual full run also reports UI and dependency failures, which are tracked separately; no unrelated failure is represented as fixed.

- Full exact-head diagnostic validation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42437385181.

Main subsequently merged [#194970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194970), which reconciled 22 lines of inherited test debt at that main revision. The failed runs above remain the exact-head CI evidence for this PR; they are not relabeled green. No further inherited-debt allocation is included in this change.

prs.title: fix(ui): own chat bubble ignores the accent color when the viewer's profile is unknown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the viewer's own (right-side) chat bubble shows an identity color instead of the accent when the Control UI doesn't know the viewer's profile. Examples are Tailscale or trusted-proxy sign-in without a profile, or a connection without self-profile access. Two gateways with the same appearance settings then paint your own messages differently.

## User Impact

User impact: your own bubble always uses the accent, either the theme accent or the accent you picked in Appearance, on every access path. Other participants' bubbles on the left keep their identity colors, and placement is unchanged from `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185821 made own messages use the accent, but it decided "own" only by matching the sender's profile to the viewer's profile id. Placement uses a different rule: a user turn goes on the left only when the viewer's profile is known and the sender is someone else. Everything else is on the right and is the viewer's.

When the viewer's profile isn't known, turns that carry a sender stamp stayed on the right but got that sender's identity hue. Identity tint now follows the same peer decision as placement. The viewer fill itself is unchanged: the accent-derived soft fill and the stronger dark-theme tones from #188114.

## Evidence

- Regression unit test `paints every right-side user turn with the viewer accent and only peers with identity hues` (`chat-message-group.solid.test.tsx`): red on current `main` (`expected false to be true`), green with the fix.
- On the head with current `main` merged in, the touched suites pass: `chat-message-group.solid`, `chat-message.forwarded-attribution`, `chat-message`, `chat-avatar`, `chat-view` (247 tests). `tsgo:ui` and the `ui-chat` test typecheck lane pass, and oxfmt/oxlint are clean.
- Test-line budget: the regression test adds 15 net lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/control-ui-viewer-bubble-accent.txt`. The test is the only proof of the right-side accent invariant, and the shared scalar is unchanged. The local ratchet against current `main` passes (slack 64).
- Browser proof: source Control UI against the mocked Gateway in the dark Claw theme. Each gateway has one viewer; the team case adds a teammate. Sender and presence data match `gatewayClientSenderFields` and `buildAuthenticatedPresenceUser`. Each case ran once with the theme accent and once with the Blue accent picked in Settings → Appearance. Values are the right-side bubble's `--chat-participant-surface`.

| Access | Theme accent `#ff5c5c`, before → after | Picked Blue `#5b9cf6`, before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Team, profile (teammate on the left) | accent → accent; teammate keeps its hue | accent → accent; teammate keeps its hue |
| Gateway token | accent → accent | accent → accent |
| Tailscale, no profile | identity green `h 157` → **accent `h 23.9`** | identity green → **accent `h 256.9`** |
| Profile-stamped turns, no self-profile access | identity olive `h 103` → **accent `h 23.9`** | identity olive → **accent `h 256.9`** |

Tailscale with the theme accent, before and after:

![Before: Tailscale, theme accent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13f96f46-f09e-4237-afa3-20d977a7d7ea)
![After: Tailscale, theme accent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c9f07e2-71a2-4f7f-b538-9f8e3ecbddbe)

No self-profile access with the picked Blue accent, before and after:

![Before: picked Blue accent ignored](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05c7da00-e170-4243-9467-279f4bd03a7c)
![After: picked Blue accent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eca4f84c-a346-4cc5-8520-0ac33efbe7a9)

Unchanged references, token with the theme accent and team profile with the picked Blue accent (teammate on the left):

![Token, theme accent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1a8627a-50fe-448d-8b3b-66f839f0ce3c)
![Team, picked Blue accent, teammate on the left](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50a094f0-71b4-445d-ab54-3a3ba85fa24b)

Gap: these captures use the mocked Gateway, not a live Tailscale gateway. A real-gateway trusted-proxy run on this host hit the readiness timeout under load.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

Fixes #194330

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android shows an unexplained total-refresh warning when model discovery fails but a populated model catalog remains available.

<!--

"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."

-->

## User Impact

User impact: users keep their model choices and see a bounded provider or native-discovery warning when that scope is known, with an honest partial-catalog fallback when it is not. Genuine refresh failures remain visible.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog attempt owner records provider/native failures, including an unknown scope, but previously published only an aggregate flag. This draft derives live `refreshFailures` from that owner, carries the facts through the decision adapter and RPC projection, and updates Android to consume them without changing authentication outcomes or model eligibility. Partial recovery now publishes a status change even while another acquisition remains failed.

The public projection omits raw errors, credentials, endpoint/profile-shaped labels, and provider identities outside the requested view. Android honors these sanitized scopes rather than recovering hidden labels from legacy outcomes; legacy fallback labels must be present in the returned catalog.

**Related work:** #194338 overlaps the same producer and proposes synthesizing `providerOutcomes`. This is an alternative, not a parallel auth-state fix: it retains ready/auth outcomes, distinguishes native and unknown acquisition scopes, and includes Android handling. Reconcile the two approaches before either is merged. #159670 was also inspected; its catalog-auth retention change is not copied here.
