prs.title: fix: keep agent identity and saved personal instructions in worktree sessions
prs.body:
Builds on and supersedes #193739 by @PollyBot13, who worked on this first. His commit is included unchanged as the base of the personal-instructions part, and he is credited as co-author (`Co-authored-by` on the follow-up commits).

## What Problem This Solves

Worktree sessions get the wrong instructions, in two ways:

1. **Agent identity is lost in project worktrees.** When a session runs in a managed worktree of a **separate project repository**, OpenClaw loads every bootstrap file from the worktree. The agent's own `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md` and `IDENTITY.md` are dropped (shown as `[MISSING]` at the worktree path), and the project's `AGENTS.md` becomes the agent's only instructions. On the team server, Roboclaw sessions in worktrees of the openclaw repo never see the team workspace rules, such as "check for existing PRs first". One of them started duplicating #194780.
2. **Saved personal instructions are missing (#193739).** Personal instructions saved in **Settings → Profile** (the selected person's `USER.md`) are read from the worktree instead of the agent workspace where the editor saves them. Worktree sessions therefore get no saved instructions, or a stale or committed copy from the checkout.

Both come from #188970. Its selector, `resolveRunBootstrapWorkspaceDir`, returns any recorded `sessionRoot` (or `workspaceOnly` execution workspace) as the **sole** bootstrap root. That was right for #129411, where the worktree is a checkout of a Git-backed *agent workspace*. It is wrong for unrelated projects, and it is wrong for the Profile file in every case.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Bootstrap root (`workspace-run.ts`).** The execution root owns bootstrap files only when it is a checkout of the agent workspace's own Git repository (same Git common dir) or is the agent workspace itself. Otherwise the agent workspace owns them, and the root's `AGENTS.md` is layered after them as `execution-project` context. The loader already supported this layering, and both callers already pass the execution root.
- **Personal instructions (`bootstrap-files.ts`, @PollyBot13's commit).** The selected personal `USER.md` is always loaded and provenance-checked in the configured agent workspace, independently of the bootstrap root.
- **Integration fixes on top of his commit:**
  - The personal workspace now also resolves when the config has only `agents.defaults.workspace` and no agent roster, as in some CLI runs. The autoreview flagged that case, and the original fell back to the worktree.
  - The `AGENTS.md`-only project-layering pass no longer reads the personal file.
  - His Gateway test now expects the agent's `SOUL.md` in project worktrees.
- **Docs:** `docs/concepts/system-prompt.md` "Workspace bootstrap injection" describes both rules, and `docs/concepts/user-model.md` notes that worktrees use the saved Profile file.

## User Impact

- Project worktree sessions get the agent's persona and team rules, the person's saved Profile instructions, and the repository's `AGENTS.md` as project rules.
- Worktrees of a Git-backed agent workspace still load that checkout's bootstrap files, with no fallback to the shared checkout. The one exception is the saved Profile `USER.md`, which always comes from the agent workspace, so a branch can't replace someone's personal instructions.
- Accepted edge case: in `workspaceOnly` project sessions, the injected agent files sit outside the tool root, so file tools can't edit them. This matches behavior before #188970. Session privacy filters and memory provenance apply as for sessions on the canonical workspace.

## Evidence

- Real TLS Gateway flow (`server.personal-instructions-worktree.test.ts`, from #193739): a Profile save and update reach the agent's request, along with the project's `AGENTS.md` and the agent's `SOUL.md`, while a worktree `USER.md` decoy is excluded. It runs against a local replay provider, not a paid model. With the bootstrap selector reverted to base it fails at the agent-`SOUL.md` assertion. It passes with this change.
- Regressions red on base `867ed52` and green with this change:
  - embedded "layers execution project instructions" for project worktree and `workspaceOnly`;
  - CLI "keeps agent bootstrap and adds only project instructions from a project worktree";
  - "roster-less worktree" personal-instructions provenance case (red without the roster fix).
- The existing #188970 cases ("rooted checkout of the agent workspace": present, missing, symlink) still pass, now with a real linked-checkout layout.
- Related test runs:
  - bootstrap-files (core, personal, remote, memory-core), CLI preparation and the Gateway flow: 167 passed;
  - `attempt-bootstrap-prepare`, `workspace-run`, `skill-runtime.workspace`, `run-attempt-dispatch.owner`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability` and `run.session-permissions`: all passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap and test-lines ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, branch vs `867ed52`): the first run found the roster-less gap, now fixed. The final run is **scoped-clean**.
- **Not run:** a live production Gateway check. Hosted CI is pending.

## Related

- Supersedes #193739 (and #191734). Narrows #188970; keeps #129411/#129404 fixed for agent-workspace worktrees.

prs.title: fix(gateway): release old session rows after metadata updates
prs.body:
Related: #194880

## What Problem This Solves

Session metadata updates retain superseded resident entries and displayed rows until another reader arrives. This repairs the deterministic large-10 retention failure in [scheduled main run 42434232909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42434232909/job/128589770580).

## User Impact

Updated sessions can release old row graphs without waiting for another list request. Current row caching, wire values, and recipient authorization remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`aba709b7bc12` (#194880) moved strong publication caches from materializations to an identity shared across materializations. Its cached facts and audience revisions therefore kept the previous materialization and entry alive after replacement.

Restore materialization ownership of strong publication caches. Keep only weak references to preceding audience maps for optional structural reuse, and remove the redundant materialization witness and per-view revision arrays. Common nested producer fields still use the existing sharing owner. Reusing preceding audience variants is best effort across garbage collection; a collected comparison map causes recomputation with the same values.

The existing integration regression also checks collection of each old common display row. No assertions are weakened, and test-line growth is zero. Simplification removed the retained revision/filtering machinery; the small production growth connects weak comparison witnesses to the existing owner.

## Evidence

- Named failing file only: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-projection.retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, under `timeout` and the coordinator's local-run lock.
- Unmodified base: **1 failed, 2 passed**, reproducing the superseded-row collection assertion (60.61 seconds including preparation).
- Final candidate: **3 passed** (49.49 seconds including preparation; 6.23 seconds across the three test bodies).
- Touched-file oxlint with `--type-check`, targeted oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent requested autoreview of the complete candidate and owning source: **scoped-clean, P0–P3**, no actionable findings.
- Only these three source/test files changed: two production owners and the existing retention regression. Production delta: +11 lines; test delta: 0 lines.
- Broad proof is delegated to PR CI. No workflow dispatch, rerun, remote-box warmup, container, broad suite, or merge was performed. The sibling actor failure is owned separately by #194940.

prs.title: fix(agents): terminate background CLI tasks on cron timeout
prs.body:
Closes #138499

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where cron jobs running automated agent turns that launch background CLI tasks via the `exec` tool leave orphaned processes running on the host when the cron job times out, causing the Gateway restart drain loop to block and eventually force-shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a cron job hits its execution deadline, `cleanupTimedOutAgentRun` triggers an abort with reason `"cron_timeout"`. We ensure this timeout reason propagates through `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` and `EmbeddedAgentQueueHandle.abort` to `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`, where the abort is classified as a timeout with `TimeoutError`.

Key design decisions:
1. **Timeout reason ordering & re-entrancy**: In `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`, `input.abortRun(true, createTimeoutAbortReason())` and `attempt.onDeferredLifecycleAbort?.(reason)` are invoked before `attempt.onAttemptAbort?.()`, preventing re-entrant generic cancellation callbacks from the lane controller from latching first and discarding the `TimeoutError`.
2. **Selective background process termination**: In `bash-tools.exec-run.ts`, backgrounded execution retains its abort signal listener until process settlement (`settlement.onSettled = detachAbortListener;`), allowing `isSignalTimeoutReason(signal?.reason)` to terminate background processes on `TimeoutError` while preserving them across ordinary turn cancellations and restarts.
3. **Task settlement & restart unblocking**: Process settlement triggers `finalizeBackgroundExecTask`, recording the task's terminal state and clearing the `background-exec` active work restart blocker in `gateway-active-work.ts`.

## User Impact

Scheduled cron jobs that launch background CLI commands will no longer leak orphaned processes when the cron job reaches its execution deadline, preventing host resource exhaustion and enabling graceful Gateway restarts.

## Evidence

### 1. Real Behavior Runtime Verification
Executed an end-to-end integration test against the real process supervisor, real exec tool, real process registry, and real gateway active work monitor (`verify-cron-timeout-real.ts`):

```text

=== STEP 2: Spawning Real Background CLI Task via Exec Tool ===
Exec tool result status: running
Background Session ID: plaid-tidepool
Child PID: 321092
Active background exec session count: 1
Gateway restart blocked before timeout? true
Active blocker before: 1 active background exec session(s)
Child process alive in OS before timeout: true

=== STEP 3: Triggering Cron Timeout Abort ===
Simulating cron scheduler: queueHandle.abort('cron_timeout')
[Attempt] External abort marked
Run abort signal aborted? true
Run abort signal reason: TimeoutError
Abort state terminal outcome: {"kind":"timeout","phase":"prompt","source":"runtime","aborted":true}

=== STEP 4: Waiting for Process Settlement & Task Finalization ===
Finished session found: true
Finished session terminal status: failed
Finished session exit signal/code: SIGTERM
Child process alive in OS after timeout: false
Active background exec session count after timeout: 0
Gateway restart blocked after timeout? false

=== VERIFICATION SUMMARY ===
Real cron timeout process cleanup verified: SUCCESS
```

### 2. Targeted Vitest Test Suites
All targeted suites pass cleanly (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file>`):

- **`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.background-abort.test.ts`** (9/9 passed):
  - `background exec is not killed when tool signal aborts`
  - `pty background exec is not killed when tool signal aborts`
  - `background exec still times out after tool signal abort`
  - `background exec without explicit timeout applies default timeout`
  - `background exec with timeout zero bypasses default timeout`
  - `yielded background exec still times out`
  - `yieldMs exec without explicit timeout applies default timeout`
  - `background exec is killed when tool signal aborts with TimeoutError`
  - `yielded background exec is killed when tool signal aborts with TimeoutError`
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`** (30/30 passed):
  - `processes cron_timeout abort through external-abort sequence as a timeout`
  - `preserves timeout classification when onAttemptAbort synchronously triggers re-entrant generic abort`
- **`src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts`** (33/33 passed):
  - `removes the abort listener when an exec process is backgrounded and exits`
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.lifecycle.test.ts`** (23/23 passed):
  - `forwards cron_timeout reason to abortEmbeddedAgentRun`
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/deferred-lifecycle-owner.test.ts`** (2/2 passed):

### 3. Static Checks & Ratchets (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged`)

prs.title: fix(ui): keep transcript content steady while scrolling upward
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scrolling upward into newly measured transcript rows could move messages already on screen. The anchor covered rows above the viewport but missed newly revealed predecessors inside it. Applying the correction with `scrollTo` also discarded native WebKit wheel input.

The existing reader anchor now compensates those predecessors and holds corrections in the existing row column during qualified native input. At native zero, the first row owns the position; a lower retained row must not pull the reader away from the top. Programmatic startup/composer motion retains its existing positioning behavior. Retention, row estimates, history admission, and Markdown reconciliation remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Current replacement head: `59f18f98840`, after merging main `4af0013a2c5` (runtime bundle built at `0cbf0105b80`; subsequent commits change only the test allocation and cap/comment). The coordinator accepted the byte tradeoff. Native replacement-head recovery landed this exact head as `d59f00281eb02167a86b57c42f04b2b59ed203fe` and completed managed checkout cleanup. The full timing and frame evidence below is reused because main did not change either transcript owner.

The first CI run exposed history-loading and composer-rail regressions from treating all virtualizer motion as native input. The second exposed three short-transcript top-boundary regressions. All were reproduced through the existing E2E tests against frozen production bundles and repaired without weakening assertions. The final repair also adds a native ResizeObserver case for a positive height correction at zero, and shares a stateless test fixture to stay within the existing test-line allowance.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| History loading, composer rail, native-wheel pagination, archive flow | Passed after qualifying reader input; exact-head full CI also passes |
| Narrow subagent report, content copy, image lightbox | All three fail on previous candidate, pass on merge base, pass on current production bundle |
| Native anchor cases | 5 pass; new positive-height-at-zero case fails before its fix |
| Transcript geometry consumers | 28 pass |
| Page observer identity | 3 pass |
| UI typecheck; targeted lint/format; production Knip | Pass |
| Current-main merge checks | UI typecheck and 30 focused tests pass; the archive conflict regression passes; Chromium/WebKit desktop/mobile scroll smoke passes with zero browser/resize errors. The installed Firefox executable is missing, so its completed full-matrix proof is reused. |
| Test-line ratchet | Own allocation corrected 140→158, exactly net added test/helper lines; inherited 22-line debt also fails on current main |
| Independent P0–P2 review | No actionable findings in full change, subsequent repairs, or final cap-only change |
| Prior integration CI | [Run 42437623374](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42437623374) failed on a read-coalescing case and test-line ratchet; repairs and baseline attribution below |
| Full CI before current-main merge | [Run 42409879991](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42409879991) succeeded, including full UI E2E and real-Gateway shards |
| Final scroll qualification | 360/360 pass, plus 30/30 extra Firefox mobile observations; desktop task CPU −6.57% median / −7.79% p95 |
| Final streaming qualification | 780/780 pass: 20 rotated triplets per engine/viewport/flow, plus 10 additional Chromium typing triplets per viewport |
| Retention | Mounted DOM unchanged; existing forced-GC lifecycle contracts pass in full CI. No browser heap-neutrality claim |

The completed scroll timing comparison uses merge base `fe2b1a51b41` and the corrected production bundle, with 20 rotated base/head/base triplets in Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox. Separate cells cover desktop native wheel traversal, mobile instant jump, steady streaming, and streaming while typing. The stopped previous-head run had 140 passing observations; it is incomplete and unqualified. Current-head desktop traversal wall median/p95 changes are Chromium −4.60%/−5.52%, WebKit −9.57%/−14.08%, Firefox −7.32%/−18.17%. Mobile is neutral. Firefox mobile received 10 extra triplets: combined 30-pair head +1.02%/+2.27%, unchanged-base control −0.01%/+12.56%; the extra batch reversed the head tail while control spread exceeded the effect.

The streaming comparison completes all 720 observations, then 60 targeted observations resolve small typing-timing uncertainties. Every observation retains all 645 deltas, 400 messages, native input, and tail follow, with zero browser/resize errors. Chromium renderer task CPU median/p95 changes are:

| Streaming flow | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Steady, no input (20 triplets) | −0.69% / +0.03% | +0.17% / −2.01% |
| While typing (30 triplets) | +0.44% / +0.07% | +0.26% / +0.76% |

These are neutral streaming results. The desktop typing input-to-frame median moves by 0.505 ms (+3.31%); its tail is +1.69% versus A/A +2.77%, with unchanged frame cadence. The mobile typing CPU tail contracts from the initial +3.15% to +0.76% after the extra triplets. Firefox mobile steady-frame p95 is noisy: 33.337→49.993 ms, with the unchanged-base control also at 50.000 ms. Host load ranges from 8.254 to 89.053 on 32 CPUs. That shared tail is not a head-specific regression, and these measurements do not claim universal frame neutrality. WebKit/Firefox CPU and CLS counters remain unavailable.

## Bytes and scope

Complete production builds on the same machine against current main `4af0013a2c5`:

| Surface | Current main | Merged head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup normalized gzip | 90,858 B | 90,858 B |
| Startup served gzip / raw | 91,489 / 285,508 B | 91,539 / 285,508 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |
| Chat normalized gzip | 1,296,175 B | 1,296,315 B |
| Chat served gzip / raw | 1,303,625 / 4,177,326 B | 1,303,654 / 4,177,754 B |

**Coordinator-accepted tradeoff:** the earlier paired result added **384 B** normalized gzip on a roughly 1.3 MB Chat boot; it fixes visible retained-row drift **27/44 px → 0/0**, restores WebKit wheel gestures, and reduces desktop scroll task CPU **6.57% median / 7.79% p95**. After merging current main, the measured growth is **140 B**. The sole cap change is Chat: **1,296,187 → 1,296,379 B**, exactly current-main measured bytes + 140 B growth + the existing 64 B allowance. No other cap changes. Identifier mangling moves gzip by hundreds of bytes; raw and served values are retained above. Document, largest ordinary JS, aggregate CSS, and New Session overages remain inherited and do not grow beyond the checker's allowance.

Whole change: **15 files, +655/−75**. Runtime anchor: **339→360 lines**. Most growth is optional benchmark diagnostics and regression proof. Solid audit of the touched plain TypeScript owners: rendering controllers, effects, render effects, `untrack`, direct `addEventListener` calls, DOM query calls, Solid owner calls, and dynamic imports each remain **0→0**. No new cache, state owner, or async mechanism.

## Motion evidence

Raw CLS alone is misleading here. Earlier compositor diagnostics captured intermediate layout rectangles that were corrected before paint; a −71 px retained-row shift was balanced by +71 px compensation. The earlier candidate retained 234 matched rows without residual movement even while raw CLS rose. The final exact-base capture now shows drift in 259/259 retained-row comparisons (median −27 px), versus zero residual movement in all 234 final-head comparisons in each of Chromium and WebKit. Final desktop CLS is 0.4582→0.5679; this change does not claim CLS zero. Final-head Chromium and WebKit diagnostics each show zero residual displacement across 234 retained-row comparisons spanning 104 complete non-clamped gesture intervals. Both reach message 0 at y72 and native offset 0 across all six endpoint samples; the final clamped input is classified separately. Selected Chromium compositor frames corroborate the completed-gesture result. Some intermediate rAF rectangles remain nonzero: the first −88 px sample is absent from the captured compositor frames and is followed by an equal correction; another −17 px entry changes native coordinates while screen positions remain fixed. This does not establish that every possible paint is shift-free. WebKit evidence is geometry-only.

Streaming diagnostics found ordinary text wrapping, table growth, code-control reveal, and mobile composer growth, with retained Markdown nodes rather than unexplained block replacement. Recent typing can exclude the same movement from CLS; zero CLS during typing is not proof that nothing moved. The benchmark now snapshots shift-source identity before virtualization removes nodes and separates no-input streaming from typing.

Final streaming all-shift sums are identical across every base/head/control sample within each flow: desktop 0.0946406336, mobile steady 0.2426243711, and mobile typing 0.2469974155. Steady CLS is likewise identical (desktop 0.0268001699; mobile 0.0623932548). Typing changes recent-input exclusion, not those movement totals. The original 0.0098 desktop typing maximum appears on the base in this comparison, not the head. No Markdown behavior change is warranted by this evidence.

Before (synthetic data):

![Before: retained transcript content shifts between frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f23814e-0075-49ef-9028-439e56b059f4)

Current corrected head: retained messages remain aligned as preceding rows appear.

![After: retained messages stay aligned while preceding rows appear](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/015c45fe-fa49-4ad3-bd5f-bdceec026e71)

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and bundle identity</summary>

Build each side completely with `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 pnpm ui:build`, then preserve its `dist/control-ui` directory after the process exits. The full timing matrix used the pre-merge head bundle, built before committing; its embedded build ID names the preceding commit. That pre-merge evidence uses complete-bundle SHA256 over the manifest's 4,844 files:

- Base: `5a1f7379dc498a5c649163a2c733c2a0d5ebb0bb5e48c4d77480f61944c6a68c`
- Head: `bc178b16f6c3c3fcfc58aebe45652dd53877fbdebf9a5c826dd30412398820ff`

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir "$BASE" --compare-bundle-dir "$HEAD" --control-bundle-dir "$BASE" \
  --steps transcript-scroll-top --viewport both --engines chromium,webkit,firefox \
  --pairs 20 --output .artifacts/transcript-scroll

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir "$BASE" --compare-bundle-dir "$HEAD" --control-bundle-dir "$BASE" \
  --steps streaming-645-deltas,streaming-645-deltas-no-input \
  --viewport both --engines chromium,webkit,firefox --pairs 20 \
  --output .artifacts/transcript-streaming

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir "$BASE" --compare-bundle-dir "$HEAD" --control-bundle-dir "$BASE" \
  --steps streaming-645-deltas --viewport both --engines chromium --pairs 10 \
  --output .artifacts/transcript-streaming-typing-extra10
```

Add `--transcript-layout-audit` only to a separate bounded diagnostic run. Its layout reads and Chromium filmstrip invalidate timing comparisons. All browser runs are headless, with synthetic Gateway fixtures; no live Gateway, cloud lease, or Docker is involved.

</details>

## Final integration repair

Run 42437623374 had two failing jobs. `paces incomplete ancestry and validates metadata against the pending catalog` also fails on the exact size baseline e64215c411f, with the same duplicate `sessions.describe` assertion. Current main contains bd1fc681705 (#194892), which starts recording at the settled boundary; after merging it, that test passes on the replacement head. This is an inherited failure repaired by main, not a transcript regression.

The test-line allocation previously counted only 140 of the 158 net added regression-test/helper lines. It now counts exactly 158; assertions are unchanged. The remaining 22-line deficit is reproduced on both the replacement head (6,571,391 lines / 6,571,369 ceiling) and current-main base (6,571,233 / 6,571,211); both checker commands fail by exactly 22. No allowance is granted for that inherited debt. The scalar baseline remains untouched.

After this merge, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, five anchor cases, the read-coalescing E2E, and all four Chromium/WebKit desktop/mobile scroll smoke observations pass. The complete paired size comparison also passes (even under the preceding, 38 B tighter cap). Final exact-head [CI42439200419](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42439200419) completed with **43 successful jobs,23 intentional skips**, and only the test-line ratchet plus its aggregate gate failing. All UI and real-Gateway jobs passed. The exact CI main baseline f6abc882 also fails by22 (6,571,202 /6,571,180); the actual tested merge fails by22 (6,571,360 /6,571,338). Native inherited-failure recovery uses this matching deficit; the failed check is not labelled green.

Native landing completed with the inherited-failure evidence above; [required Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42439271320) passed. Separate Security High run 42439200427 (six jobs) and precise scan run 42439200447 stopped during SARIF publication because GitHub installation API quota was exhausted. Their failed logs contain publication errors, not source findings; no security gate was waived. The merged commit is verified on `origin/main`.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep Apple Event permission probes off the cooperative thread pool
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On 2026.9.3 the macOS app periodically goes dead while still running: the paired node shows **offline** in the Gateway dashboard although the Mac is on and the TCP session to the Gateway is still ESTABLISHED (32 KB of unread bytes sitting in the receive queue), the menu bar item stops opening its menu, and the process ignores SIGTERM (needs SIGKILL). It "fixes itself" only when the app is relaunched.

## Root cause

`AppleEventPermissionProbe.state` runs the blocking `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget` in `Task.detached`, which schedules onto the Swift cooperative thread pool. The call blocks until Terminal answers the Apple Event handshake (and, when `askUserIfNeeded`, until the user answers tccd). `MacNodeModeCoordinator` re-probes permissions on every refresh trigger (`UserDefaults.didChangeNotification`, config change, permissions change, app activation, reconnect probe), so a slow Terminal under system load lets probes stack up.

A 3 s `sample` of the wedged process showed **all 16 cooperative threads** parked here, main thread idle:

```
DispatchQueue_18: com.apple.root.user-initiated-qos.cooperative
  closure #1 in AppleEventPermissionProbe.state(askUserIfNeeded:)
    AppleEventPermissionProbe.determineTerminalPermission(askUserIfNeeded:)
      AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget
        _dispatch_semaphore_wait_slow
          semaphore_wait_trap
```

Terminal automation was already **granted** in TCC (`kTCCServiceAppleEvents ai.openclaw.mac → com.apple.Terminal = 2`), so this was not a pending prompt. Once the pool is exhausted nothing async in the app can run, including the gateway websocket receive and the status item, and any continuation the AE reply needs can never be scheduled.

## Fix

- Run the blocking probe on a dedicated `DispatchQueue` (concurrent, so a prompt is never queued behind a hung passive check), bridged with a `CheckedContinuation`, so it never pins a cooperative thread.
- Single-flight concurrent callers per `askUserIfNeeded` value through a small actor (`AppleEventPermissionProbeCoordinator`), so at most one probe blocks at a time regardless of how many refreshes fire.
- Bound passive (non-prompting) probes with a 10 s timeout that surfaces as `.failed(errAETimeout)` → capability `.unknown`, instead of hanging the caller. Prompting probes keep waiting on the user.

No change to call sites; `AppleEventPermissionProbe.live` and `TerminalAutomationPermission` keep their API.

## Evidence

- `concurrent passive checks share one blocking probe`: 32 concurrent passive `state` calls → exactly one `determine` call, all callers get the result.
- `a hung passive probe times out instead of blocking callers`: a `determine` that never returns yields `.failed(errAETimeout)` in ~200 ms with a 200 ms timeout.
- `interactive prompts are never timed out`.
- Existing suite unchanged and green (12/12).
- Live observation, 2026-09-09: reproduced twice on the same Mac (2026.9.3 release build). Both times `netstat -anv -p tcp` showed the OpenClaw-owned socket to the Gateway ESTABLISHED with 32,778 and 52,617 bytes in Recv-Q, and `sample <pid> 2` showed 16 and 17 frames in `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget`. The second occurrence started within 60 s of a Gateway restart, i.e. on the reconnect refresh path. `pkill -9` + relaunch cleared it each time.

`swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` ✅, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` ✅, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` ✅ (Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3.3).

## Review follow-up (revision 3)

Both P2 findings are addressed:

- **Retain the in-flight operation after a caller times out.** The coordinator now keeps the operation in `inFlight` until the native call actually returns. Caller deadlines are measured from the operation's start, so once the deadline has passed later passive callers answer `errAETimeout` immediately and never enqueue a second native call. When the target replies, the tracked operation drains and the next probe runs fresh. Covered by the new test `timed-out callers never enqueue a second native call behind the hung one` (second caller answers in < 150 ms with `callCount == 1`, operation still in flight; after release the next probe runs and `callCount == 2`).
- **Synchronize overlapping callers before releasing the test probe.** The concurrency test now waits until all 32 callers are parked on the coordinator (`waiterCount == 32`) before releasing, and `BlockingProbeGate.release()` opens the gate permanently so every native call a test started completes during cleanup.

The probe queue is concurrent so an interactive prompt is never queued behind a hung passive check.

## After-fix native proof

Debug build of this branch on a second Mac (macOS 26.4.1, Xcode 26.6), run in a throwaway app profile pointed at a remote Gateway URL that refuses connections (so every reconnect attempt builds a manifest and evaluates permissions). Terminal.app, the Apple Event target, was frozen with `SIGSTOP` so the probe could not get a reply, then resumed with `SIGCONT`. The passive probe returned `noErr` on this host: its TCC database already holds an allowed `kTCCServiceAppleEvents` row for bundle id `ai.openclaw.mac` → `com.apple.Terminal`, which the debug build shares, so recovery shows as a normal `returned 0`.

| Phase | `sample` probe frames | Cooperative-pool frames in the probe | `openclaw-mac status` (control socket) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | 0 | ok |
| Terminal frozen, 55 s | 1, on `DispatchQueue: ai.openclaw.apple-event-permission (concurrent)` | 0 | ok |
| Terminal resumed, 50 s later | 0 | 0 | ok |

Unified log (`ai.openclaw`/`AppleEventPermissionProbe`), timestamps relative to the freeze:

```
-27 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.172922083 seconds
-19 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.033881875 seconds
-10 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.208797417 seconds
  0 s     Terminal.app frozen (SIGSTOP)
+17 s  E  probe ask=false timed out after 10.0 seconds; operation retained
+58 s     Terminal.app resumed (SIGCONT)
+58 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 50.992712958 seconds
+66 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.032903625 seconds
+97 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.137408166 seconds
```

No second native call started while the first was hung (the only lines between the freeze and the resume are the single timeout), the retained call returned as soon as Terminal answered, and the probes after it ran fresh.

The app answered its control socket throughout, kept exactly one blocked thread (on the private queue, never the cooperative pool), released it when Terminal answered, and quit within 1 s of `SIGTERM` afterwards. On the release build the same condition ends with 13 to 17 cooperative threads blocked, a dead status menu, and `SIGTERM` ignored (openclaw/openclaw#146030).

Filtered test run (`swift test --filter AppleEventPermissionTests`, private HOME, throwaway profile, `--skip-build`): 13 tests, 0 failures. Full native suite left to the `macos-swift` CI job per `apps/macos/AGENTS.md`.

### Signed-bundle run (signing provenance)

The run above used the bare SwiftPM debug binary (ad-hoc signed). Repeated on the same Mac with a full `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` bundle of head `621a4a4d8`, signed through `scripts/codesign-mac-app.sh` with a real Apple Development certificate and kept at the fixed path the permissions guide asks for (`<checkout>/dist/OpenClaw.app`). Provenance, identity details redacted:

```
Identifier=ai.openclaw.mac.debug
Format=app bundle with Mach-O thin (arm64)
CodeDirectory v=20500 flags=0x10000(runtime)
Authority=Apple Development: <redacted>
Authority=Apple Worldwide Developer Relations Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
TeamIdentifier=<redacted, set>
Sealed Resources version=2 rules=13 files=42384
codesign --verify --deep --strict: OK
```

`ai.openclaw.mac.debug` has no Automation grant on this Mac, so the passive probe's real answer is `-1744` (`errAEEventWouldRequireUserConsent`), returned without a prompt once Terminal answers. Same procedure (throwaway profile, refusing Gateway URL, Terminal `SIGSTOP` for 55 s, then `SIGCONT`):

| Phase | `sample` probe frames | Cooperative-pool frames in the probe | `openclaw-mac status` (control socket) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | 0 | ok |
| Terminal frozen, 55 s | 1, on the private queue | 0 | ok |
| Terminal resumed, 50 s later | 0 | 0 | ok |

```
-28 s  I  probe ask=false returned -1744 after 0.207445334 seconds
  0 s     Terminal.app frozen (SIGSTOP)
+14 s  E  probe ask=false timed out after 10.0 seconds; operation retained
+58 s     Terminal.app resumed (SIGCONT)
+58 s  I  probe ask=false returned -1744 after 54.768811875 seconds
```

One blocked native call, no second call queued behind it, bounded caller wait, control socket answering throughout, the retained call returning the moment Terminal resumed, and the app quitting within 1 s of `SIGTERM` afterwards.

## Release note

Fix the macOS app wedging (node offline while TCP alive, menu bar item unresponsive, ignores SIGTERM) when concurrent Terminal Automation permission probes exhausted the Swift cooperative thread pool.

Diagnosed and written with Claude Code: https://claude.ai/code/session_014TmTvgdhcL7bPCwg3f8B6G
Review follow-up, after-fix proof, and this revision: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RW45HgmUaFSiM4DSZGrVSp

prs.title: fix(workers): desktop observe and launch skip stale-build admission
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Closes #143100

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an inconsistency in worker-environment admission where an environment whose stored `bootstrapReceipt` no longer matches the current Gateway bundle was refused for `startTunnel` and session attach but was still granted `worker.desktop.observe` tickets (including `control: true`) and `worker.desktop.launch` app launches. Operators with the `cloudWorkers.desktop` lab enabled could thus drive a worker that the Gateway had already decided is not current enough to talk to, during the window before background reconciliation retires the stale environment.
- **Related:** #121081 (merged tunnel-admission repair) and #140400 (shared eligibility refactor) established the sibling invariant but left the desktop paths unchecked; #141336 bound observer tickets to the Gateway connection on an orthogonal axis. ClawSweeper advisory on this issue confirms the desktop gap remains and recommends applying the canonical build validator at desktop admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `observeDesktop` and `launchDesktopApp` now enforce the same build-identity admission as `startTunnel` and `attachSession`: the current bundle is prepared outside the environment lock, and the freshly read durable record's `bootstrapReceipt` is validated with the canonical `verifyWorkerAdmissionHandshake` before any desktop transport or launcher side effect. A stale worker is refused with the existing `StaleWorkerBuildError` ("Worker build does not match the current Gateway build; redispatch the session..."), surfaced to the client as `invalid_state` with the same redispatch guidance tunnels already return.
- **Out of scope:** no change to reconciliation timing, lifecycle-state gates, transport fencing, or `startTunnel`'s existing admission path; missing `bootstrapReceipt` on a desktop record is treated as an admission failure rather than a distinct lifecycle error.
- **Highest-risk area:** the node-backed desktop carrier branch — mitigated by an explicit regression test asserting a stale node-backed environment is refused before the durable carrier's `observe`/`launchApp` is reached.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** with `cloudWorkers.desktop` enabled, an otherwise-eligible desktop worker whose bootstrap receipt no longer matches the current Gateway bundle is refused for desktop observe and app launch with the same stale-build error tunnels and attach produce; a current-build desktop worker keeps working (existing observe/launch tests unchanged).
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/worker-environments/environment-access.ts` (`prepareCurrentBuild` / `requireAdmittedBuild` helpers and their call sites in `observeDesktop` / `launchDesktopApp`), plus the new `environment-access.test.ts` fixtures: "rejects desktop observe with stale receipt / unavailable current bundle", "rejects desktop app launch with ...", and "rejects a stale node-backed desktop before reaching the durable carrier".

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** three real layers, in increasing fidelity. (1) Unit admission fixtures drive the real `createWorkerEnvironmentAccess` factory over the real durable store and the real `admission.ts` validator, fencing only the desktop tunnel/launcher managers with `vi.fn()` so rejection is provable by "transport never called". (2) The full-runtime composition suite uses the real node desktop carrier, the real pairing store, the real provider lifecycle/reconciliation and a real in-process supervisor-protocol transport. (3) **New on heads `da307e3`→`79db02c`** — a committed wire proof (`test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/paired-node-worker-desktop-admission-wire.e2e.test.ts`) runs a real packaged Gateway child process against a real paired node host (real `handleInvoke` → real `NodeWorkerBundleInstaller`, real supervisor, real workspace runtime) and a real headless TigerVNC `Xvnc` with `VncAuth`, splicing real RFB bytes node → Gateway → observer WebSocket. Install and launch acknowledgements are not synthesised there: the install extracts real bundle bytes into the node host's bundle store and the launch executes a real executable through the real launcher.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Committed wire proof on a real worker desktop (real Gateway child + real node host +
  # real TigerVNC/RFB): access → stale refusal → real reconciliation recovery → restored access
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/paired-node-worker-desktop-admission-wire.e2e.test.ts
  # Regression suite (RED first: stale/unavailable cases failed before the fix, GREEN after):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/worker-environments/environment-access.test.ts
  # Full gateway-server runtime composition (real store + real node carrier + real transport):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-worker-environment-startup.test.ts
  # Adjacent desktop/tunnel/desktop-RPC suites (no regressions):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/worker-environments/desktop-tunnel.test.ts \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/node-desktop-carrier.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/environments.desktop.test.ts
  # Format + lint + tests + tsgo:core gate (validate.sh on the changed files): all green
  # Import-boundary source contract (startup module lazy loads): pass
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  Committed wire proof, head `79db02c` — eight consecutive green runs (test body 170.4–185.8s),
  the last two on the corrected harness described below. Captured phase trail of the last run, plus
  the real Gateway's own log lines for the same window:
  ```text
  phase: pairing the worker node
  phase: dispatching the worker session onto the paired node
    gateway: ⇄ res ✓ sessions.dispatch 6701ms
  phase: attesting the worker desktop onto the durable environment record
  phase: observing the current worker's real desktop
    observe resolved wsPath on the first bounded request  (state-gated readiness, no retry loop)
    observed real RFB ServerInit 1024x768 name="x11"      (real RFB 3.8 handshake, real geometry/name)
    gateway: ⇄ res ✓ worker.desktop.observe 96ms
    gateway: desktop observer closed  sourceKey=worker:32104533cbb533c11f009275079c2911
    gateway: node stream closed       streamKind=desktop nodeId=326e39deacec83…
  phase: launching the advertised desktop app on the real worker
    -> {app: "terminal", status: "ready"}
  phase: updating the Gateway build to supersede the worker's bundle
    (real rebuild of the owned fixture -> a genuinely different content-addressed worker bundle)
    gateway: Worker disk-space probe failed: Worker build does not match the current Gateway build…
  phase: refusing the stale worker at desktop admission
    stale observe refused: GatewayClientRequestError: Worker build does not match the current
      Gateway build; redispatch the session so its worker can bootstrap the current build before retrying.
    stale launch refused:  GatewayClientRequestError: Worker build does not match the current
      Gateway build; redispatch the session so its worker can bootstrap the current build before retrying.
    gateway: ⇄ res ✗ worker.desktop.observe 9ms  errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Worker build does not match…
    gateway: ⇄ res ✗ worker.desktop.launch  11ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Worker build does not match…
    (asserted: no desktop stream/launch frame reached the node host)
  phase: recovering the retained worker through real reconciliation
    reconciliation installed refreshed bundle
      7fff06dc50c1719db0b16e0b1ab4e44330a61a020770a77384aeb95f120f23d2
      (superseded 8cfa905f038461047478dbc1d49a576bc89f099cf0dac9de169dd15186564ac5)
    durable receipt refreshed on the same environment record worker:32104533cbb533c11f009275079c2911
  phase: restoring desktop observe and launch on the recovered worker
    launch -> {app: "terminal", status: "ready"}
    recovered observe served real RFB ServerInit 1024x768 name="x11"
    gateway: desktop observer closed sourceKey=worker:32104533cbb533c11f009275079c2911 (same record)
    gateway: node stream closed      streamKind=desktop nodeId=326e39deacec83… (same node, new connId)

  ✓ serves desktop observe and launch from a real worker, refuses a stale build after a Gateway
    update, and restores access through real reconciliation   179632ms
  Test Files 1 passed (1)   Tests 1 passed (1)
  ```
  The same `sourceKey` is refused after the build change and serves real RFB frames again after the real
  reconciliation refresh — recovery on the same durable record, no reseed and no extra record.
  The test is `skipIf` no local VNC server exists, so it stays opt-in on hosts without a headless desktop.

  Unit and composition suites (unchanged):
  ```text/json
  environment-access.test.ts: 24 passed (24)   # includes 5 new admission assertions
    - rejects desktop observe with stale receipt          -> code: invalid_state,
        message: "Worker build does not match the current Gateway build;
                  redispatch the session so its worker can bootstrap the current
                  build before retrying."                 (desktop.acquire NOT called)
    - rejects desktop observe with unavailable current bundle -> invalid_state
        "Current worker build identity is unavailable"    (desktop.acquire NOT called)
    - rejects desktop app launch with stale receipt / unavailable bundle (launchApp NOT called)
    - rejects a stale node-backed desktop before reaching the durable carrier
        (nodeDesktopCarrier.observe / launchApp NOT called)
  server-worker-environment-startup.test.ts: 4 passed (4)  # full runtime composition:
    - current-build node desktop launch resolves {app: terminal, status: ready} over the
      real carrier + in-process supervisor transport
    - a sibling record bootstrapped against a superseded bundle (hash "c"*64) is refused
      with the canonical stale-build message and the carrier's launchApp is never reached
      (carrier invocation count unchanged)
  validate.sh (oxfmt + oxlint + vitest + tsgo:core): all green on the 5 changed files
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** a mismatched-bundle desktop worker is refused at admission time for observe and launch, before any transport acquisition, token minting, or app-launch side effect — now demonstrated on a real worker desktop over the real Gateway wire, where the refused record and the recovered record are the *same* durable environment (`worker:32104533cbb533c11f009275079c2911`), and recovery is the real reconciliation refresh (real bundle install of `7fff06dc50c1719db0b16e0b1ab4e44330a61a020770a77384aeb95f120f23d2`, canonical receipt verification, `refreshBootstrapReceipt`) rather than a reseeded record. Current-build desktop observe/launch keep serving real RFB frames (1024x768, desktop name `x11`) before and after the upgrade window.
- **CI regression found and fixed while this PR was open:** the gateway-server shard (`checks-node-compact-small-16`, head `9eeda8ed`) failed in `server-worker-environment-startup.test.ts > composes node desktop control into the worker environment runtime` — the new desktop admission resolves the current worker bundle through the runtime's bundle producer, and an unpackaged source checkout has no built worker deploy artifact, so packaging throws and desktop launch is refused as "Current worker build identity is unavailable". Fixed by letting `createGatewayWorkerEnvironmentRuntime` accept an optional bundle producer (default unchanged: package the running tree on first use) and adapting the composition test to seed the current-build identity its record bootstrapped with. Rebased onto latest `main` and re-verified (validate.sh green).
- **Unrelated CI flake on the previous head (resolved by rebase):** head `12194ab9` failed `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-27` / `openclaw/ci-gate` in `extensions/telegram/src/model-callback.loopback.integration.test.ts` ("Network request for 'editMessageText' failed") — an extension this PR does not touch. Main already fixed that flake upstream in #143197 (`4d475f153ae`, merged 2026-09-09); this branch was rebased onto that main, and the PR's own checks are green on the new head.
- **Recovery through real reconciliation (committed regression, head `b1c124ab`, replacing the earlier seeded-record version):** the full-runtime composition now drives the actual recovery machinery instead of seeding a replacement record: after the stale refusal (stable on repeated attempts), `service.reconcileOnce()` runs the real provider-lifecycle refresh for the same node-backed desktop environment — the paired device is resolved through the real durable pairing store, the real device worker provider inspects its lease, the owner is stopped and its credential revoked, the current bundle is installed through the real gateway bundle installer + transfer service, the returned receipt is verified by the canonical `verifyWorkerAdmissionHandshake`, and the refreshed receipt is committed on the **same durable record** via `store.refreshBootstrapReceipt`. Desktop launch on the recovered record then succeeds (+1 carrier invocation) with no new record seeded:
  ```text/json
  composes node desktop control into the worker environment runtime: PASS
    stale launch -> code "invalid_state", STALE_WORKER_BUILD_REASON (stable on retry)
    reconcileOnce(staleEnv) -> device provider refresh path:
      paired device from real pairing store; provider.inspect -> {status: "active", sharedHost: true}
      stopOwner -> credential revoked; bundle install invoked exactly once (exact current bundleHash)
      store.refreshBootstrapReceipt -> same record now ready with current-bundle receipt
    recovered launch -> {app: "terminal", status: "ready"}; carrier invocations = before + 1
  server-worker-environment-startup.test.ts: 14 passed (14)
  environment-access/desktop-tunnel/node-desktop-carrier/environments.desktop: 72 passed (72)
  tsgo:core + gateway-root test type shard: green
  ```
- **Real-artifact upgrade evidence (heads `64c9beb`→`93f422f`):** an additional run of the same composition drove the **real** `createWorkerBundleProducer` over two genuinely different real worker deploy artifact sets (no injected identity): an older real build as the environment's bootstrapped bundle (`H_old` = `7675acc4…`, 10 953 078-byte tarball) and this branch's freshly built artifacts as the current Gateway bundle (`H_new` = `1bd8f978…`, 11 357 321-byte tarball), with the real durable store, real `createGatewayWorkerEnvironmentRuntime`, and real node desktop carrier:
  ```text/json
  [phase A] current-build launch (receipt == H_old) -> {app: "terminal", status: "ready"}; carrier=1
  [phase B] after upgrade to H_new, same record refused:
            code = "invalid_state"
            message = "Worker build does not match the current Gateway build; redispatch the
                       session so its worker can bootstrap the current build before retrying."
            carrier invocations before=0 after=0 (carrier NOT reached); stable on retry
  [phase C] redelivered record (receipt == H_new) -> {app: "terminal", status: "ready"}; carrier=+1
  ```
  The two content-addressed bundle hashes are distinct, so the refusal is driven by a real manifest mismatch of real packaged worker artifacts, and the redispatch recovery happens on the same runtime/store without a gateway restart.
- **The previously reported “observe stalls” were a proof-harness deadlock, not Gateway behaviour:** the earlier attempt cleaned its observer socket up with `await failure.catch(…)` *before* `ws.close(…)`, where `failure` only settles on socket error/close — so the harness hung on its own success path whenever the Gateway (correctly) kept the observer stream open. No product code was changed for it, and none was needed: after reordering, `worker.desktop.observe` resolved on the first attempt in all six runs (~35–100 ms). Three further harness races found while chasing it are also fixed in the test: the operator-hello baseline was captured *after* the Gateway restart (so the wait could never advance), the “no transport side effect” assertion counted *all* node frames while a restart legitimately re-publishes `worker.workspace.retain.v1`, and the refreshed-bundle directory was checked when the install *frame* arrived rather than after extraction. This is the answer to the merge-risk question: the desktop observe path does not hang — refusal returns in ~10 ms and the real recovery completes in ~62 s including the real bundle install.
- **Harness corrections after review (head `79db02c`):** two findings on the committed proof were fixed rather than argued. (1) *Readiness* — the fixed 10 s settle plus three-attempt observe retry is gone; the test now waits on the state the restart produces (`environments.list` reporting the record `available` with `desktop: true` and `desktopApps: ["terminal"]`) and then issues **one** bounded observe request, per `test/AGENTS.md` ("synchronize on the state an action produces … do not substitute longer timeouts, sleeps, retry-wrapped downstream assertions"). A retry loop could otherwise let a current-worker request that genuinely fails before dispatch pass on a later attempt. (2) *Cleanup* — `withCleanupLog` converted every rejection to `"done"`, resolved its own timeout, and callers discarded the result, so teardown failures could never reach the failure list and the proof could pass with a node host, Gateway, provider or Xvnc still running; it now returns a per-step `done|failed|timeout` outcome that is aggregated into the proof's failures and reported through the trail. Both corrections are validated by two further full green runs (170.4 s / 178.7 s test body).
- **CI note (resolved, no action needed):** on head `da307e3` the only red checks were `checks-node-compact-small-51` and the `openclaw/ci-gate` aggregating it, failing in `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts > keeps hosted tooling within the GitHub job cap when its inventory grows` with `compact github node test plan exceeds 80 jobs (81 planned)`. That guard inventories git-tracked test files, and `main` had gained `test/plugins/fireworks-model-alias.test.ts` in `4e32fcc1687` (#144913), taking the pull-request compact plan from 80 to 81 jobs; I reproduced the identical failure on a clean `origin/main` checkout (`90e44fe1b00`) with this branch's changes absent, and this branch adds only an `.e2e.test.ts` file, which that tooling inventory excludes by pattern. On the current head `79db02c` the shard passes and no check is failing.
- **What was not tested:** no remote/SSH worker host, and no GUI application drawn inside the desktop. In the wire proof the node host runs in-process in the test worker rather than as a separate OS process on another machine, and the advertised app is a real non-GUI executable (`/usr/bin/true`) started by the real launcher; the desktop itself is a real headless TigerVNC X server on loopback. Everything across that boundary is real: Gateway WebSocket wire frames, one-time stream tickets, the RFB handshake and frame bytes, bundle install bytes on disk, durable-store transitions, reconciliation and receipt refresh.
- **Proof tier:** L2+ (wire-real). Real packaged Gateway, real node-host stack, real content-addressed bundle artifacts, real VNC/RFB stream, real durable record and real reconciliation on one machine; the node host's separate-OS-process boundary and a GUI app inside the desktop are the only edges this environment cannot provide.

prs.title: fix: only label scheduled heartbeat alerts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving an event-driven completion through the heartbeat dispatcher could see it mislabeled as their “First heartbeat alert.” The same event delivery could also consume the state marker, preventing the next genuine scheduled heartbeat alert from receiving the onboarding context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first-alert preamble and its persisted delivery markers now apply only to scheduled heartbeat runs: explicit `interval` wakes and the existing source-less scheduled compatibility path. Explicit event, manual, hook, and other non-scheduled wakes keep their original text and do not advance scheduled-heartbeat onboarding or dedupe state.

A regression test covers the user-visible sequence: an exec completion is delivered unchanged and leaves heartbeat state unset; the following scheduled heartbeat receives the first-alert preamble and persists its state.

## User Impact

Background task and event completion messages are no longer presented as heartbeat onboarding alerts. Users still receive the onboarding explanation on their first genuine scheduled heartbeat alert.

## Evidence

- Regression demonstrated red on unmodified main: the event-driven delivery included the first-heartbeat preamble.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.structured-delivery.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-session-mirror.test.ts` — 83 passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/heartbeat-dispatch.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/heartbeat-dispatch.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent P0/P1 targeted review — clean after two identified state-ownership edge cases were fixed.

Full local core/test typecheck did not produce a terminal result: one attempt encountered a stale artifact lock left by an interrupted check, and a subsequent run exceeded the local tool timeout. Exact-head CI remains the source of truth for the complete typecheck lanes.


## Production reproduction (2026-09-10)

A real Telegram DM on the contributor's OpenClaw `2026.9.3` runtime reproduced the reported pre-fix behavior at `2026-09-10 15:16:08 GMT+8`.

A background `openclaw doctor` completion was delivered through the heartbeat path and incorrectly received the scheduled-heartbeat onboarding prefix:

```text
First heartbeat alert: your bot runs periodic background checks and messages you only when something needs attention. Set agents.defaults.heartbeat.target: "none" to keep these internal.
补充检查结果：`openclaw doctor` 未成功跑完（退出码 1）……
```

This is user-visible production evidence for the bug mechanism: a background/event completion can be mislabeled as the first scheduled heartbeat alert. It supplements the red-on-main regression test. It is intentionally not claimed as exact-head after-fix proof; the remaining acceptance proof is the bounded Telegram Test Server sequence on `8bc954f7c103b8fa5512e3449acb09c58e1ed42a`: event delivery without onboarding or marker consumption, followed by the first scheduled alert with onboarding, then a later scheduled alert without repeated onboarding.

prs.title: fix(macos): recognize installed asdf Node and pnpm CLI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS app users could not start their local Gateway with an asdf-managed Node runtime and a pnpm-installed CLI, even though both worked in Terminal. Supported Node 26.1.0 was reported as `(unreadable)`, followed by `Command "openclaw" not found`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the Node version probe and the downstream Gateway CLI version probe now preserve the app's inherited environment and override only PATH with the discovered search paths. Previously, passing a PATH-only environment removed HOME and caused asdf to fail. CLI discovery also searches `~/Library/pnpm/bin`, retaining the existing parent-directory layout and path precedence.

## User Impact

Users can reuse supported asdf Node and pnpm CLI installations without adding manual symlinks. The change stays in macOS app discovery and includes updated installation documentation.

## Evidence

### Actual asdf/pnpm installations

Following ClawSweeper's review, I tested the compiled native app's `GatewayEnvironment.check()` (used by Connection Recheck) and `CLIInstaller.status()` (used by onboarding) with **actual installed asdf 0.18.0, Node 26.1.0, pnpm 12.2.1, and OpenClaw CLI 2026.9.3**.

Each run had a fresh isolated Foundation HOME/defaults store and no remembered CLI path. Symlinks exposed the actual installed asdf shim and pnpm CLI at `~/.asdf/shims/node` and `~/Library/pnpm/bin/openclaw`; `ASDF_DATA_DIR` pointed to the existing Node installation. The initial PATH contained system/Homebrew directories. Assertions checked the selected shim, discovered CLI, exact versions, and final native statuses. Actual installed executables and package contents were readable, while operator configuration, Gateway state, Keychain services, and network access remained blocked by an OS sandbox.

**Before this follow-up**, on the initial PR head `19d53cd0`, the real installation run confirmed ClawSweeper's downstream concern:

```text
Node: ~/.asdf/shims/node -> 26.1.0
CLI: ~/Library/pnpm/bin/openclaw
GatewayEnvironment.check: kind=error, node=26.1.0, gateway=nil
CLIInstaller.status: ready=true
```

**After preserving the downstream probe environment** (follow-up commit `a97eb115`), a separate fresh HOME/defaults run passed:

```text
Foundation HOME matches isolated HOME; no cached CLI preference
Node: ~/.asdf/shims/node -> 26.1.0
CLI: ~/Library/pnpm/bin/openclaw
GatewayEnvironment.check: kind=ok, node=26.1.0, gateway=2026.9.3
CLIInstaller.status: ready=true
CLI validated: 2026.9.3; compatible with app 2026.9.3
Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed (exit 0)
```

The temporary proof harness called the actual compiled app methods and was removed from the submitted sources. This proves native discovery and downstream validation with actual installations; signed-app GUI interaction and starting an operator Gateway were outside this run.

### Regression and repository checks

- The initial HOME-dependent Node and pnpm-layout regression cases failed before their respective fixes. The new downstream CLI-to-Node-shim regression failed on `19d53cd0` and passed after the follow-up.
- All 24 selected Swift tests passed, including runtime compatibility, both pnpm layouts, downstream CLI validation, path precedence, profile isolation, and inherited SSH environment behavior.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed with only the submitted test sources after removing the temporary proof harness.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base d9216e894e89cec406d42607c175aeecf4a13ee9` passed, including 1,141 macOS-related Vitest tests, SwiftLint, formatting, dependency guards, and the native state schema guard.
- Independent autoreview confirmed that the working-tree follow-up repairs the downstream defect. Its sole INDEX-only finding referred to the previous PR revision; the reviewed repair is included unchanged in this update.
- Native i18n verification, the changed document's MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver
- core tests use a fixture channel; they no longer import `extensions/qa-channel`

Sabotage: switching decision injection back to unguarded `resolveFollowupCurrentMessageId` turns the foreign-channel and inter-session tests red.

Runtime observation on `ba68eaeb` used the real Gateway + Telegram transport after restart and recorded the queued answer referencing message 11. That remains the dispatcher-less recovery proof. Telegram Test Server E2E for ordinary overlap was **not** rerun (no Convex QA broker credentials on this fork).

## Maintainer refresh — September 14, 2026

Refreshed onto `82a9bef596011a6145d7f639d9773ff5e7267f7d`, preserving the original patch and contributor authorship. Current candidate: `6d592e236f8d40d33c911391ad795ed59062b439`.

Fresh review exposed an empty-target regression on channels without a transport resolver. The shared threading owner now distinguishes an absent reply target from `replyToId: ""`; the latter remains an explicit opt-out. Inline explicit-reply directives still override that implicit-threading opt-out. This is an owner-level condition change, not a follow-up-specific workaround.

Verification:
- Added regressions failed on the pre-repair candidate: **3 failed, 46 passed**.
- Repaired candidate: **183 passed across 7 suites**, covering queued delivery, channel boundaries, admission/provenance, resolver delegation, shared threading, empty/false opt-outs, inline override, first-reply slot accounting, and deduplication.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.channel.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-threading.test.ts`
- `git diff --check` passed. The repair adds one net production line (an explanatory comment) and 61 test lines. Full changed-surface static checks and hosted CI are tracked separately; this section does not claim they have completed.
- This is deterministic owner/channel-boundary proof, not new authenticated live-channel proof.

Review adjudication: the fresh autoreview returned four reports, not a scoped-clean result. The index-only empty-target finding is resolved in the committed candidate. Two resolver-owned issues were verified as unchanged baseline behavior and recorded as follow-ups: **resolver-owned empty/false opt-out consistency** and **separating explicit inline current-message resolution from implicit correlation policy**. The reported QA dedupe mismatch was not established: that resolver returns a native message reference without `threadId: null`, while the dedupe owner treats `replyToId` as a conversation thread only for the explicit-null transport contract. No new unresolved P0–P2 regression was independently confirmed in this candidate.

prs.title: fix: adopt controllers across completed historical incident gates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Allows explicit controller adoption for a new retained V1 `ROLLBACK_FAILED` incident when the canonical adoption gate completed for an older incident, including when a later reviewed installation changed the actual incumbent closure. Related: #194605. Rebased onto landed retirement #194949 (`34bb0cfb5103adabdda48d75c92626a24a2e5969`).

## User Impact

The operator can authorize `historical-successor` through the existing four-file adoption owner. A strict request binds historical gate/completion descriptors, the current retained source, four actual reviewed incumbent files and four approved replacements. Historical completion is immutable evidence only (`current=false`); current FD9/lock, source, closure, safe metadata and audited hooks are validated independently. Existing gate handoff, backups, apply and exact replay remain the sole installer.

Adoption performs no restart and introduces no schema/config/lifecycle change or cache. Retirement is a separate action. The complete reviewed controller closure must be adopted; publication alone does not install it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old owner required the historical completion to match the current installed closure and incident source, so it could not express this new-incident authorization. Ordinary same-incident/bootstrap checks remain strict. Production delta is **+10 lines** (25 added, 15 deleted): explicit historical binding replaces a redundant current-completion validation at handoff. The allocation record covers exactly 212 new regression-test lines; shared scalar unchanged.

## Evidence

Both source-only and source-plus-later-incumbent cases fail on exact `e4f99f3372683bba7a2241c51e63c305ba7fdf1e` at the unsupported action after valid historical completion setup. Both actual-shell cases fail there too. Candidate proof covers incomplete/tampered history, stale source/closure, unsafe metadata, ungated incumbents, mixed publication, stale shell/library readers, replaced lock, config change without native audit, interrupted gate handoff, and before/after interruption at each of four file renames with exact replay.

The adopted shell reaches `--prepare-retained-repair`: `PREPARED ... restart=0 activation=0 original-journal=retained`. External service/build IO is synthetic; Linux FD9/flock and controller execution are real. No deployment host was accessed.

Full controller suite against exact main parent `34bb0cfb5103adabdda48d75c92626a24a2e5969`:

| Snapshot | Total | Pass | Fail | Skip | Duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact main parent | 795 | 406 | 388 | 1 | 639.076 s |
| Candidate `0116a12bad9bf6dd560852a2116298f4b12c9917` | 827 | 438 | 388 | 1 | 654.945 s |

**Zero new failures**; all 32 additions pass, no tests removed or renamed, identical failure-name multisets. Same-incident, bootstrap and retirement integration pass. Both snapshots pass Python health (5/5), qualified non-root maintenance launcher (5/5), and Prometheus. The native systemd test retains its explicit opt-in skip.

The 388 inherited failures remain attributed to #193647 (`3efe1deca653`: canonical lock/FD9 fixtures, duplicate lock setup, extracted-shell mode and maintenance order), #169752 (`aee12b63234c`: removed migration stop contract still called), and #187090 (`a968dc19900d`: missing rollback process instance). They remain main defects. Original pre-rebase comparison was 392→424 passes, 388 unchanged failures, 1 unchanged skip; all 32 additions pass there too.

Fresh **Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean**, two complete passes against the exact rebased parent, no accepted/actionable findings. `pnpm check:changed` passes every selected check except 20 inherited changelog-attribution errors from #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`); exact-parent script/changelog blobs are identical to the independently reproduced failure. No waiver or baseline masking was applied.

Exact-head [CI run 42439866996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42439866996) has only the test-line ratchet and its aggregate gate red. CI merged this head into exact main parent `34bb0cfb5103adabdda48d75c92626a24a2e5969`. The parent independently counts **6,571,304 / 6,571,282 ceiling = 22 inherited debt**; CI counts **6,571,516 / 6,571,494 = the same 22**, after this change adds +212/+212. All other selected jobs pass. This is inherited-only red, not a green CI claim.

The inherited test-budget regression first crossed the ceiling in #194899 (`5e1a27a9bcc4`), grew in #194856 (`4f539a5ec07f`) and #194882 (`c61a7c0cf6b7`), and was reduced by subsequent cleanups. This PR covers its own growth only; the remaining debt needs a main fix.

## Measurements

Fresh synthetic fixtures use a 35.04 GiB SQLite DB, 6,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.1 GB inside the runtime, on btrfs. Serial A1/B1/A2/B2 controls have five fresh stable-depth samples per block. Owner wall time excludes setup. CPU is instrumented Node-child CPU only; allocations are 64 KiB V8 sampling estimates including collected objects. No production data was copied.

Final exact-parent/candidate same-incident comparison (10 samples per version):

| Owner | Wall median / p95 ms before → after | Node CPU median ms before → after | Allocation median MiB before → after | Node processes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Adoption | 483.82 / 1443.71 → 419.06 / 734.36 | 160.23 → 150.24 | 9.96 → 8.82 | 2 → 2 |
| Prepare | 6650.26 / 6958.82 → 6500.27 / 7053.20 | 6794.79 → 6707.57 | 723.25 → 726.94 | 39 → 39 |

Final preparation p95 rises 1.36%. The final baseline has a 1.44 s adoption wall outlier with 194 ms Node CPU; the apparent wall-time improvement does not establish a performance win. Both distributions are retained, with no sample removed.

Final control medians (ms):

| Block | Adoption | Preparation |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 532.82 | 6921.49 |
| B1 | 461.55 | 6573.57 |
| A2 | 428.16 | 6326.17 |
| B2 | 316.17 | 6489.26 |

The final historical baseline refuses all five attempts (adoption/preparation medians 44.19/61.68 ms). All five candidate historical flows succeed: adoption median/p95 **457.19/2953.78 ms**, preparation **6859.53/16273.52 ms**. Median Node CPU is 153.26/6797.42 ms and allocation 9.26/721.15 MiB. The 16.27 s preparation tail includes 11.30 s Node CPU; its cause remains unproven. These capability-tail observations are retained, not hidden by the median. Baseline refusal and candidate success are different outcomes, so no latency-ratio claim is valid.


Prior-head measurements retain an unresolved **+23.67% preparation p95** observation (7.04→8.70s), with +2.75% median wall and roughly unchanged allocation. The outlier slowed multiple unchanged helpers; its exact cause remains unproven. It is preserved in the report, and refreshed measurements do not erase it. No speedup or p95 non-regression claim is made.

This PR is ready for review and intentionally **unmerged**.
