prs.title: fix: keep Send now available after a steering timeout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: **Send now** disappears when a steer waiting behind a long tool reaches the 120-second delivery deadline and becomes a queued follow-up.

## User Impact

The waiting message keeps its normal user bubble and **Send now** link while the original run has supported interruptible tools. Clicking it stops those calls through their existing cleanup path and delivers the correction once at the next model decision, or as the next turn if the original run ends. Unsupported tools retain the existing explanation. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The captured capability belonged to the injection receipt that timeout withdrawal retires. It now belongs to the input itself. An explicit fallback request reuses the Gateway starter for fresh writer authority and delivery preparation, re-admits that exact input, then interrupts the captured run’s tool calls. Completing queued custody as consumed prevents replay. The UI projects that server capability instead of hiding every queued follow-up.

Related: #193665, #194907. Rebased after #194907; its initial-only browser case is extended through fallback. This does not duplicate #194805’s quiet pending-state labels.

## Evidence

The native 120-second withdrawal regression fails on exact main parent `b97bc15cd7af` because history loses `steerNow`. It passes with the fix, including concurrent clicks, writer revocation during preparation, replacement-backend protection, cleanup ordering, and exactly-once delivery.

- 97 focused core tests; the final four-case Gateway suite also passes after its fixture type repair.
- 104 affected UI/unit/browser tests; 12 mocked-Gateway follow-up cases on the rebased head.
- Real Gateway + foreground exec + scripted local provider: actual 120-second fallback, link retained, physical process cleanup before inference, correction and recorded interruption in request **2**, exactly **2** requests total.
- Steering documentation updated; MDX, formatting, focused lint/typechecks, and Codex P0–P2 autoreview pass.

`pnpm check:changed --base b97bc15cd7af` completed. Its fixture callback type error was fixed and the failed shard, lint, and four tests passed on the correction. Remaining changelog/export failures reproduce on the exact parent: archived thanks (#194364), `OpenClawShell` (#194815), `CommandPaletteOpenDetail` (`9151ac22e005`), `isSessionUnreadAckOnlyPatch` (#194839), and `readReleaseChangelogFiles` (#194899). These are main regressions, not ignored findings.

The separate test-budget check retains main’s **65-line debt**, introduced by #194899 and subsequently increased by #194856/#194882. This change’s **+237 test lines / +237 allocation** adds no debt. Production code is **+77 lines**: retaining the captured capability, fresh authority preparation, consuming queued custody, and sharing concurrent requests account for the growth.

Measured a fresh synthetic **35 GiB / 5,000-session / 62,000-file** fixture through the real Gateway, public RPC, and foreground exec. Two A/A controls and two interleaved parent/fix pairs passed (10 timed inputs per arm), each after the actual 120-second fallback. The baseline tool has a controlled 1,000 ms remaining hold; cold samples stay included.

| Full Gateway metric | Parent | Fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Model-visible delivery median | 1,205.84 ms | 64.24 ms |
| Delivery p95 (maximum with 10 samples) | 2,497.12 ms | 228.84 ms |
| Action CPU mean per input | 790.14 ms | 222.09 ms |
| Total model requests | 30 | 20 |

A/A medians varied 1.22%, and mean CPU 5.35%. All fixed inputs interrupted physical exec and delivered the correction once in request two. The successful RPC itself takes 13.60 ms versus the old no-op’s 1.14 ms. Separate source-run profiles measured 133.86→91.64 MB sampled main-isolate allocation per input; these include cold module compilation and do not predict production memory savings. Startup/integrity checks, the deadline wait, and profiler timings are excluded from the latency table.

The 4,096-resident controller-only series independently passed 500 inputs per arm: with a 50 ms synthetic tool hold, delivery median 50.79→0.149 ms, full-iteration CPU mean 2.717→1.540 ms/input, and separate sampled allocation 695.9→635.1 KB/input. The no-click control remained within A/A spread. Exact source hashes were checked before and after every cohort.

Scope: APFS, five short active conversations beside the large stored history/workspace, scripted local inference, whole-process Gateway CPU (excluding exec child CPU), and main-V8-only sampled allocation. No production data or btrfs/long-context inference claims.

Exact-head CI run [42437773076](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42437773076) completed **49 successful / 24 skipped / 2 failed**. Only test-budget debt and the aggregate gate failed. CI’s newer main parent `bd1fc681705b` independently reproduces **48** lines of debt from #194882; intervening main deletions removed 17 of the pinned parent’s 65. Functional/UI checks passed. No rerun or merge was requested.

The first two images compare the same mocked-Gateway fallback. The third shows the real Gateway after the actual timeout.

![Before: the fallback hides the user bubble and Send now](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdbee9d5-372e-45b3-8c46-32b1509e4e07)

![After: the queued fallback keeps its bubble and Send now](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e221f583-a2b4-4daa-8b0e-e1ea7c365ca1)

![Real Gateway: Send now remains after the actual 120-second fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d59e41b-47fd-45c8-a422-0ee03525e2a5)

prs.title: improve(ui): stop showing "Loading mentions…" above loaded Inbox rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

While mentions were loading, the Inbox put a "Loading mentions…" text row at the top of the list, including on the **All** tab when other rows were already showing. On the **Mentions** tab the same row sat where the list starts, so "still loading" and "nothing here" looked almost the same.

## User Impact

- **Tabs that already have rows** (for example, All with system items): rows stay in place. No status row is added above them, and mentions join the list when they arrive.
- **Empty tab while mentions load** (Mentions, or All with nothing else): a quiet centered spinner that only appears after 300 ms, so fast loads never show it. Screen readers still hear "Loading mentions…".
- **"No mentions yet"** only appears after loading finishes with nothing to show.
- **Errors and "unavailable"** keep the existing note and **Refresh** button.

## Why This Change Was Made

Loading and empty are separate states, and a loading indicator should never sit on top of content that has already loaded. The spinner uses the empty state's layout, so going from loading to "No mentions yet" doesn't shift anything.

Context from the investigation: on a live team Gateway, `mentions.list` and `users.self` respond as fast as `health`. `mentions.changed` only fires when the viewer's own mentions change. So the row mostly showed up during connect and reconnect, not because of a slow request.

Accepted edge case: mentions that arrive after other rows can still be inserted into the All list. New content appearing there is expected.

Not in this PR: if `users.self` fails with a non-FORBIDDEN error, mentions can stay in loading until a presence update supplies the identity. That needs a separate fix.

## Evidence

- **Regression test:** `shows mention loading only after a delay and only while the list has nothing to show` in `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-layout.browser.test.ts`. It asserts nothing renders before the delay, the spinner after it, no status row on All, and "No mentions yet" once loaded. It fails on the base (the All-tab status note is present). The file passes 14/14 in Chromium.
- **E2E on the bundled build:** `sidebar-inbox-latency.e2e.test.ts` and `mobile-inbox-sheet.e2e.test.ts` pass.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop auto-highlighting unlabeled code fences
prs.body:
## TLDR

Code blocks without a language label (```` ``` ````) were colored as if they were Python, so plain English prompts showed random red and blue words. Those blocks now render as plain text. Unlabeled blocks that parse as JSON keep JSON coloring, and labeled blocks (```` ```ts ````, ```` ```bash ````, …) are unchanged.

## Problem

When a fence had no language, `highlightCodeHtml` in `ui/src/components/markdown-highlight-runtime.ts` fell back to `hljs.highlightAuto()` and kept the guess if the confidence score (`relevance`) was at least 2. English prose matches Python keywords (`from`, `with`, `not`, `for`, `or`). On the prompt in the screenshot below, auto-detection picked **Python with relevance 16**, while a real Python snippet scored 3. Raising the threshold can't fix this, because prose scores higher than actual code.

## Solution

Replace the guess with one deterministic check: an unlabeled fence that starts with `{`/`[` and parses as JSON is highlighted as JSON; everything else stays escaped plain text, the same way GitHub renders it. Labeled fences are unchanged.

## Impact

- Prompts, notes, logs and other unlabeled blocks no longer get misleading syntax colors.
- Unlabeled JSON keeps its colors.
- Trade-off: other real code sent without a language label (including indented code blocks) is now uncolored. Model replies usually label their code.

## Evidence

- `markdown-transcript-corpus.json` (byte-for-byte rendering corpus) gains an "unlabeled prose fence" entry, and the indented-code entry now expects plain text. On `main`'s runtime both entries fail; with the fix all 14 corpus/highlight tests pass. The existing unlabeled-JSON entry is unchanged, proving JSON stays colored.
- The regression lives in the JSON corpus, so the test-lines ratchet sees net delta 0.
- Markdown, chat-component, cron, app-host and sidebar tests pass locally on the merged head (1,753 + 149 + 53 + 4 tests), plus `markdown-code-blocks` and `markdown-streaming-security` (72 + 37).
- Earlier CI on the old base had inherited reds (a `src/gateway` Madge cycle and `app-host`/sidebar test failures) unrelated to this diff; `main` has since fixed the cycle (Madge reports 0 cycles locally), and those UI tests pass locally. `origin/main` was merged in for that reason.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Before/after: same message rendered through the Control UI browser e2e runner with a mock gateway (2× scale, wrap enabled):

![Before/after: unlabeled fence colored as Python vs plain text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8f0bc6d-74b8-48e8-accf-20ff16e8d2fd)

prs.title: fix(ios): Auto-connect on launch turns itself back on after a reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: "Auto-connect on launch" in Gateway settings turns itself back on when the app reconnects (socket drop, Gateway restart, returning from background, push wake), so a user who turned it off gets auto-connected on the next launch anyway.

## User Impact

Turning off "Auto-connect on launch" now sticks. Pairing or an explicit connect still turns it on, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`NodeAppModel.handleNodeGatewayConnected` stored `gateway.autoconnect = true` on every node connect (added in #99572). Reconnects inside an existing connect attempt (channel reconnects, the foreground stale-socket restart, push-wake reconnects, settings refreshes) also reach that handler, so they overwrote the user's choice.

The handler now enables the preference once per connect attempt (`gatewayConnectGeneration`). Explicit connects, auto-connect at launch and target-review resumes start a new attempt and still enable it; reconnects keep their attempt's generation and leave the preference alone. Nothing else reads or writes the preference differently.

## Evidence

iPhone 17 simulator, isolated Gateway profile: pair with a setup code (toggle On), turn "Auto-connect on launch" off in Settings → Gateway, restart the Gateway so the app drops and reconnects on its own, then read the toggle and the stored preference.

- Before (`main`): after the reconnect the toggle is On and `gateway.autoconnect` is `true`.
- After: the app reconnects (sidebar Online), the toggle stays Off and `gateway.autoconnect` stays `false`.

| Before (`main`) | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: Auto-connect on launch is back on after a reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64d51e87-2a4c-41fe-bc05-3139730f7ec0) | ![After: Auto-connect on launch stays off after a reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4b12ace-b082-4572-b41e-36f04d766e4d) |

- New `GatewayConnectionControllerTests` "reconnects keep the user's auto-connect choice" drives a real connection against the native loopback Gateway fixture: connect (preference on), user turns it off, foreground stale-socket restart reconnects (preference stays off), new explicit connect (preference on). It fails on `main` at the reconnect step and passes with the fix.
- `pnpm ios:test GatewayConnectionControllerTests GatewayConnectionSecurityTests NodeAppModelInvokeTests SettingsHubVisualProofTests GatewayAccessDeviceAuthBindingTests`: 403 passed. `GatewayIngressControllerTests` (includes the ingress activation tests that set this preference): 94 passed on a fresh simulator.
- SwiftFormat lint clean.
- Review: hosted ClawSweeper on this PR.

Merge danger: two-way door. One preference write becomes conditional; no schema, protocol or reconnect timing changes.

prs.title: fix(memory): use portable glob semantics for extra paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes hidden files being indexed or authorized by extra-memory globs such as `*.md` on stock Bun.

## User Impact

Configured memory patterns preserve Node's hidden-file semantics on every supported runtime. Hidden files need an explicit dot pattern. Globstar prefixes also keep hidden directories out of traversal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing minimatch 10.2.6 dependency for discovery and read authorization, declared by its consuming package. Cache the parsed file matcher and existing directory-prefix matchers per normalized entry. This removes the memory path's dependency on https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/45038 without runtime detection. Complex patterns retain the existing conservative traversal policy; file admission always uses the full pattern.

The first version used minimatch's partial matching for directories. Review identified that `**/team/*.md` could enter `.hidden`, despite rejecting its files. The owning enumeration regression reproduced that extra read; full prefix matching fixes it.

Consolidated three directory-scan error cases and replaced duplicate non-null assertion helpers with the already imported assertion. All cases remain covered, and the test file has **15 fewer lines** overall. No test-line allocation or ceiling increase. The one-off benchmark script is kept out of the repository rather than adding a permanent command solely for this proof.

## Evidence

Isolated macOS arm64 proof through `listMemoryFiles` and `readMemoryFile`:

| Runtime | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock Bun 2596ac5d | Hidden-file regression fails, including unauthorized hidden read | 45/45 owning tests pass |
| Pinned Bun 191755ec | Pass | 45/45 owning tests pass |
| Node 26.12.1 | Pass | 45/45 owning tests pass |

The test expectations explicitly state Node semantics. The review-discovered traversal case also fails on the first candidate (11 directories read instead of 10), then passes after the prefix correction. Final owning-file times: 490/459/800 ms on stock/fork/Node; full commands 1.37/1.38/2.23 seconds.

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` and `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` selecting each Bun binary; `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` for Node.

Five paired warm samples of 50,000 matcher calls under Node 26.12.1 have identical match counts and overlapping ranges. Baseline median/p95: 88.30/89.21 ms; final candidate: 89.18/89.86 ms. No per-entry filesystem calls. Targeted oxlint, formatting, diff checks, and the test-line ratchet pass. Fresh Codex autoreview of the final complete candidate is scoped-clean at P0–P2.

An earlier manual CI run exposed the now-removed benchmark's script-type/deadcode issues and an old command-help expectation; current main was integrated for that expectation. The [manual run for this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42436145731) passes type checks. Its dependency scan reports four unchanged exports outside this diff: `isSessionUnreadAckOnlyPatch`, `readReleaseChangelogFiles`, `OpenClawShell`, and `CommandPaletteOpenDetail`. No CI exception is requested. The [required build and artifact verification passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42436145731/job/128595709986) for this exact head. Normal PR CI is still required before landing; these unrelated dependency failures remain visible and are not waived.

prs.title: perf(ui): keep Skills settings usable during inventory reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills Settings waited for `skills.status` before adopting the page. A slow inventory read therefore also held the filter and left the content area blank.

## User Impact

Users can type into the Settings filter while inventory loads. Unknown inventory shows Loading without fabricated zero counts; a failed first read shows its error without an empty-result claim. The eventual inventory preserves the typed query. Agent scope, read access, installation destination and write authority keep their existing gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The route now prepares the inventory read without awaiting it. The existing `loadSkills` owner accepts or retires the result, so the page can use its already-known state without introducing another request or publication owner. The completed-report path and redundant route flag are removed.

This addresses Skills Settings only. Main already decoupled Discovery in #194869; no Discovery timing gain is claimed here.

## Evidence

### Timing

Final branch head `88d83ed56dc6546b7bdd5f36e30bfe52df476f53`; build, timing and browser-behavior candidate `64d73eeffada99eb5241719a271a783670fe36cf`; base `3930e4fa90810b273a4345673052507fcaccdf84`. Synthetic screenshots below show the same held request before and after, followed by the released inventory.

The page still waits for the roster to identify the scoped agent. Inventory status/rows and toggles need `skills.status`; installation requires inventory plus `skills.library.list` destination and current write authority. Security verdicts remain pending/unknown until their read completes. Already-sent route prefetches can finish after navigation; the existing owner prevents retired results from publishing.

Existing effects 1→1 and `onSettled` 2→2; no new render effects, listeners, DOM queries, flush calls or Solid owner escape APIs in production. The extra proof code measures early input and complete inventory in a single visit; the production change removes the completed-report path and redundant route flag.

Probe SHA256: `e6cb575e028462e723685fa11f1f4df3697cb8b02962a219fdfa6a977d9cd3e5`. Its tightened Settings assertions type during the hold and require 1,000 real rows after release. Rejection is covered by the actual route/page regression tests; console-error collection is not presented as RPC-rejection proof.

The canonical checker on an isolated index of that parent reports 6,571,233 lines / 6,571,211 ceiling; the corrected merge reports 6,571,311 / 6,571,311. ## Status: superseded — do not merge

[PR #194807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194807) already fixed this Systems dependency on main, merged at **2026-11-07 22:13:28 UTC** as `16f02454a7f8bb4e95e1a733d04303ecac193632`. That canonical implementation independently loads measurements through the existing page owner.

This draft was prepared against the older pinned baseline `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`. Current-main inspection caught the overlap. The committed early-content regression also passes when run with the Systems owning modules from inspected main `adca0b0844c71362be6da780008c642d17b2e350`. There is therefore **no additional validated performance opportunity here**, and this alternative must not replace or duplicate the current owner. The branch remains preserved as historical experiment/proof, not a proposed second cutover.

## What Problem This Solves

Historical problem: Systems inventory was hidden until optional node/host telemetry settled. The current canonical main implementation already removes that dependency.

## User Impact

The desired first-content behavior is already on main through #194807. **This superseded draft adds no required user-facing fix.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The original experiment published the canonical inventory early while retaining full-request settlement, selection, cancellation, and live scope/access guards. After reconciling current main, no further production change is proposed from this branch. **Systems only; no unrelated page changes.**

## Evidence

### Historical comparison only

Five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, fresh Node/jsdom process per sample, fixed 250 ms optional host-response delay:

| Component-harness inventory readiness | Old baseline | This experiment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 204.1 ms | 74.7 ms |
| p95, nearest rank (n=5: maximum) | 204.5 ms | 76.8 ms |
| Min–max | 193.2–204.5 ms | 72.8–76.8 ms |
| Optional telemetry gates before inventory | 1 | 0 |

Baseline `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`; experimental head `0f26ff48829754a5715f340c782f91b55aac712b`. **This table does not compare against today's main and is not evidence of an incremental win over #194807.** It replaces the earlier non-interleaved preliminary table. No deployed/browser latency, CPU, or RSS improvement is claimed.

Committed workload:

```sh
OPENCLAW_PAGE_PERF=0 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/systems/systems-page.test.ts \
  -t 'first content' --maxWorkers=1
```

The old baseline fails the early-readiness assertion; the experimental head passes. Crucially, the same regression passes with current main's Systems owning modules as well, confirming that the opportunity is already covered. No attempt was made to resolve this draft's merge conflict by restoring obsolete machinery.

Historical branch checks: 33 focused tests, production UI typing, UI test type shards, scoped type-aware lint/format/diff checks, test-line and UI ownership ratchets passed. Fresh independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reported no actionable findings on the experimental local snapshot against the old baseline; it did not establish necessity against newer main. Author simplification retained one request owner (production LOC +31; exact 33-line scoped regression allocation, shared scalar unchanged).

Routed Chromium/source-renderer behavior proof used a synthetic Gateway with host statistics held from boot: inventory appeared before any statistics response, with one Systems-navigation statistics request and one separately counted bootstrap request. This is not production timing evidence.

**Superseded draft. Do not merge. No landing is authorized.**

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): edit the bot's own messages
prs.body:
Related: #189815

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp is missing the `edit` message action that Telegram and Discord have, so an agent cannot correct a message it already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can edit their own WhatsApp messages. Turn it off with `channels.whatsapp.actions.editMessage: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `edit` the same way `react` works, behind the host's exact-current chat gate. Editing another user's message is refused when the cache knows the sender. On a cache miss the edit goes out under the bot's own key (`fromMe: true`); WhatsApp applies an edit only when it comes from the original sender, so such an edit has no effect on the other phone. That is provider behaviour, not something this PR enforces. Baileys resolves on the socket write, so the result says `submitted: true, confirmed: false`.

The edit key's chat is pinned to the chat the caller named. The message-cache lookup that quoting uses also matches a message through its sender. Only an entry whose stored peer number is the target's own number counts as this one-to-one chat under its other JID (phone number or LID) and may supply the key's `remoteJid`; anything else (a status update keyed by its poster, a broadcast list, a match through a bare participant JID) is another chat, and the edit is rejected with `message belongs to another chat`.

Caller authority: `edit` is declared in `writeAuthorityActions`, and the host's `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` is passed down the edit chain as a plain parameter. It is checked at the action handler and again inside the queued socket task, right after the socket-identity check and right before the native `sendMessage`. An edit whose originating run lost authority while it waited in the per-socket queue is dropped before any I/O. A revocation is never retried: the caller guard runs at the start of every send attempt, also while the socket is away, so a revoked caller never waits for a reconnect backoff, and the retry path re-checks the caller before classifying an error as a disconnect, so the caller gets the original guard error. Edits now use the ordinary send path, so the separate single-attempt path is gone.

Provider ownership (`fromMe`, the message cache) only scopes which messages are eligible; it does not stand in for caller authority. Both are required.

Scheduled edits stay out on purpose: `edit` is not in `providerOwnedReadGates`, so the host keeps its exact-current chat check and rejects a scheduled edit. A contract test locks that.

Known limitation: for an external install the host compares targets literally (it applies `normalizeTarget` only to bundled plugins), so a delegated edit must name a DM as `+E164`, the spelling the agent's prompt shows, or omit the target; a `...@s.whatsapp.net` spelling is rejected, fail-closed. Changing that is host policy and out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Live proof on 2026.11.1 (latest stable)

**Upgrade.** A real linked WhatsApp install was upgraded from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 with the normal npm install, `plugins update` and `doctor --fix`. Before and after the upgrade, the full config (sorted JSON), the WhatsApp auth creds and the number of files in the WhatsApp auth dir hashed identically, and the cron list count was unchanged. The channel came back `linked, connected, health:healthy` and the agent answered on its primary model. The config has no `actions.editMessage` key.

**Edit.** Then this PR's commit was cherry-picked onto `v2026.11.1`, `extensions/whatsapp` was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, and only the plugin's `dist` + manifest were swapped in (same dependency versions; all 94 `plugin-sdk/*` imports exist in the installed 11.1 core). Afterwards the stock 2026.11.1 plugin was put back. The cherry-pick differs from this branch only where 11.1's file layout differs from main (the action list lives in `channel-actions.ts` there, plus import lines); the edit, authority and socket code is the same as the pushed head, including the final same-chat guard and the no-socket caller check.

Phone number redacted; the message id is a random WhatsApp id.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

$ openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 3"
"action": "send", "handledBy": "core", "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8"
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 4"
"action": "edit", "handledBy": "plugin",
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8" }
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +15555550100 --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "must not arrive"
ToolAuthorizationError: WhatsApp edit blocked: chatJid "+15555550100" is not in the
configured allowFrom list for account "default".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message ""
Error: WhatsApp edit rejected: text is empty.
[exit 1]

# a message the other phone sent earlier; after the restart the cache does not know it
$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A --json \
    --message "must not arrive (not this account's message)"
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A" }
[exit 0]
```

**Receiving side.** On the receiving account's WhatsApp Web (read-only IndexedDB lookup by message id), the received message `3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8` carries `latestEditMsgKey`, with the edit's sender timestamp 4.4 s after the original. So the edit reached the other phone; it is not only a socket write. The last command above targets a message the other phone itself sent: the socket accepted the write (`submitted: true`), but on the receiving side that message has no `latestEditMsgKey`. WhatsApp dropped the edit because it did not come from the message's sender, which is the provider behaviour the Why section relies on for a cache miss.


### Delegated edit from a real inbound turn (2026.11.1)

Same install and plugin port, plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/extensions` (origin `global`, so the host treats it as an external plugin, the same trust class as the integration test below). The owner's phone sent the bot a WhatsApp DM asking it to call the `message` tool twice. The group is configured and allowed (`groups` + `groupAllowFrom`, the bot is a member), so the plugin itself would accept it. Gateway log plus the session trajectory from `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`; numbers redacted, times UTC:

```text
14:19:11  CLI (direct operator)  message send -> +<owner>  messageId 3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19  "...: meet at 3"
14:19:43  web-inbound            Inbound message +<owner> -> <bot> (direct, 494 chars)
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"+<owner>",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"...: meet at 4"}
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"<allowed-group>@g.us",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"must not arrive"}
14:19:49.762  tool.result (group)  error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.
14:19:49.789  tool.result (DM)     {"ok":true,"submitted":true,"confirmed":false,"messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19"}
14:19:52      web-outbound         the bot's text reply with both raw tool results
```

Receiving side (read-only WhatsApp Web IndexedDB lookup by message id): before the turn the received message had no `latestEditMsgKey`; after it, `latestEditMsgKey` is set with edit sender timestamp 14:19:49.783, the moment of the DM tool result. The group call was stopped in `message-action-dispatch` before the plugin ran (gateway log: `[tools] message failed: Error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.`); the only outbound socket traffic in that window is the edit and the bot's text reply.

The earlier `openclaw agent --to ...` attempts were rejected for a different reason: a CLI-started run has no host-minted turn capability, so the gateway receives no tool context or requester account and fails closed before comparing targets. That is the host's design, not this PR.

Not covered live: a second linked account and revocation while queued (one linked account; revocation cannot be timed from outside). Both are covered by the host-issued-guard integration test below.

### Tests on this branch, rebased on current main

- Host-issued caller guard, end to end (`test/whatsapp-message-edit.integration.test.ts`, on the shared `createMessageReadAuthority` harness, reaching the plugin only through `api.js` and a new `extensions/whatsapp/test-api.ts`, the same public test surface the Discord and Slack suites use): a really minted turn capability and run claim, the message tool under the gateway caller identity, the in-process `message.action` handler (which builds `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` itself), the plugin registered as an external install, the real WhatsApp handler and the real socket session; only Baileys' `sendMessage` is a mock. The test never supplies a guard. The config allows both the other chat and the other account, so only the host can refuse them. Cases:
  1. the current chat's edit reaches the socket with the edit key and returns `submitted: true, confirmed: false`;
  2. the same run naming another allowed chat is rejected before the socket;
  3. the same run's identity sent straight to the gateway's `message.action` with another allowed account is rejected by the host before the socket;
  4. `revokeMessageActionTurnCapability` (what the reply run calls when it ends), called after the edit's preflight while it waits behind a busy send, drops it with `agent runtime authority is no longer active`; the socket only ever sees the busy send.

  Red checks: with the in-queue re-check removed, case 4 fails (the edit reaches the socket); with the host's account comparison disabled, case 3 fails. The old vertical test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` is removed; this test replaces it.
- Socket session (unit level, with a test guard): the queued caller check runs after the socket-identity check and before native I/O; a revoked caller is not retried and gets the guard's own error, also when the error text looks like a disconnect; a revoked caller with no current socket is rejected at once, without a backoff wait; a guard rejection leaves no send-ready proof behind for the next send.
- Message cache: ids containing `:` are never cached or found, so the colon-joined cache key cannot collide.
- Contract: a scheduled `whatsapp:edit` is rejected with "requires provider-owned target authorization".
- Through the plugin handler: a target outside `allowFrom`, another account's `allowFrom`, a message cached as foreign, a message cached in another chat (a status update, or another person's chat matched only through a participant JID), and `actions.editMessage: false` all stop before the socket; a message cached under the other spelling of the same chat, with the target's number as its stored peer, keeps its cached `remoteJid` in the edit key.
- Through the host dispatcher: a direct operator's edit reaches the listener, a delegated caller naming another chat stops at the gate, and a chat removed from `allowFrom` stops the next edit.
- Upgrade compatibility: a config without `actions.editMessage` parses and enables edit; the message cache is in memory and its shape is unchanged.

WhatsApp extension: 101 files, 1107 tests passing; the new integration file 4/4; the extension test-boundary suite 13/13. Contract, dispatcher (`message-action-dispatch.registry`) and schema tests pass; `tsgo` (core, extensions, extension tests, root tests), oxlint, format, `config:docs:check` and `check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` are clean.

### Test-line allocation

Duplicated cases were removed (the vertical queued-revocation test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` and its helpers, now replaced by the host-issued-guard test; the duplicate queued-revocation case in `monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts`; the per-dispatch allowFrom case in `channel-actions.test.ts`; the cached-foreign case in `send.test.ts`); each contract is still proven at an equal or stronger boundary. The attached-listener setup that `channel-actions.test.ts` and the new test both need lives once in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/attached-listener.test-support.ts`, and the shared harness only gained an optional gateway-context resolver. The remaining net growth of 1161 lines (ratchet slack 0) is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/whatsapp-edit-own-messages.txt`, shared scalar unchanged. It is needed because this adds a new write action whose authority has to hold across the host gate, the plugin's account/`allowFrom` checks and the queued socket write, and each of those boundaries has its own test.

prs.title: feat(openai): add GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Flare models
prs.body:
Related: #193523 (open; adds GIF output and also registers the 2.6 models)

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI released `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.6-flare` on 2026-11-04, but OpenClaw's OpenAI image provider doesn't list them. `image_generate action=list` stops at GPT Image 2.5.

Requests with an explicit `openai/gpt-image-2.6-*` model already reached OpenAI: a 1024x1024 low-quality generation worked on the current release. The gap is the advertised catalog and the per-model capabilities. Without them, OpenClaw silently drops `xhigh`/`max` quality and snaps `auto` or custom sizes such as `1536x864` to a fixed size for these models.

## User Impact

`image_generate` and `openclaw infer image` now list both 2.6 models. They accept the same options as GPT Image 2.5 for generation and edits:

- `low` through `max` quality
- `auto` or custom `WIDTHxHEIGHT` sizes
- transparent PNG/WebP backgrounds
- up to 5 reference images

The default stays `openai/gpt-image-2`. Images from the direct Images API now report the quality OpenAI actually applied, where the tool used to report it as unknown.

These options apply to the direct API-key route. The catalog doesn't distinguish sign-in methods, so on ChatGPT/Codex sign-in, 2.6 may not behave as listed (see Gaps).

## Why This Change Was Made

- The 2.6 IDs join the existing 2.5 model family list, so both versions share one set of capabilities. The capability table didn't need a new mechanism.
- OpenAI's guide and API reference list both 2.6 models for `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`. But the reference's text on quality, sizes and backgrounds still names only 2.5. Live API validation checks show 2.6 responding the same way as 2.5 (Evidence below), and a source comment cites them.
- The catalog constants and capabilities moved, unchanged, into `extensions/openai/image-generation-models.ts`. The line-cap ratchet rejected any growth in `image-generation-provider.ts` (853 lines, cap 700).
- On the "quality unknown" report: `quality` was already in the request body. The direct Images API echoes the applied `quality` at the top level of the response, but OpenClaw only read per-image quality from the Codex Responses route. The response reader now copies it onto each image.
- Pricing: the OpenAI image provider has no model-specific price or usage-cost tables, only token counts, so there's no 2.6 pricing to add. OpenAI lists 2.6 at $5/$1.25 per 1M text input/cached tokens, $8/$2 per 1M image input/cached tokens and $30 per 1M image output tokens, the same for both models ([pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Sunburst](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst), [Flare](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2.6-flare)).
- Test-line budget: the new regression file adds 98 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/openai-gpt-image-26-catalog.txt`. The existing OpenAI image provider suite sits exactly at its 1000-line cap, so the 2.6 regressions need a sibling file with its own HTTP and auth mocks. Nothing nearby was a duplicate worth deleting to offset the growth.
- Catalog v3: obviyus is working on catalog v3 so that new models like these won't need an OpenClaw release. When it lands, this hardcoded image list can move into catalog data. Until then, this PR is the stopgap.

Deferred: these need new `image_generate` parameters or output formats, which means maintainer approval and prompt-prefix review (`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`):

- `complexity` (`low`/`medium`/`high`; OpenAI defaults to `high` when it's omitted)
- markup-guided edits (`markup` on `/v1/images/edits`)
- SVG output (`output_format: "svg"`, generations only, `n=1`)
- animated GIF output (`output_format: "gif"`, `frame_count` 2–16, `frame_duration_ms` 20–2000). #193523 covers this. Its body says `frameCount` allows 2–64, but OpenAI's guide and API reference currently say 2–16.

None of these fits an existing provider option without a schema change, so none is included. The docs say they aren't exposed yet. Docs: [GPT Image 2.6 guide section](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation#gpt-image-26).

Overlap: #193523 also registers the 2.6 models, as part of its GIF work. This PR is the catalog-only part, so it can land without the tool-schema change. Whichever lands second will need a small rebase in the OpenAI image catalog.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests:** `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.models.test.ts` runs the real `generateImage` runtime against the provider with mocked HTTP. It checks both 2.6 models for catalog listing, `1536x864`, `xhigh`, transparent PNG, no ignored overrides, and applied quality reported on the image. It also checks a 2.6 edit with `size: "auto"` and `quality: "max"`. All 3 tests failed on the base with only the test file applied, and pass with the fix.
- **Test cost:** `pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.models.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 39.1s wall time from a cold transform cache. Transform was 96% of that; the tests themselves were about 1%. CI seconds for this file weren't broken out.
- **CI:** all required checks pass on head `f926737`: 39 succeeded and 65 were skipped, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and the baseline ratchets.
- **Focused suites:** all OpenAI image provider suites (models, provider, usage, direct-errors, url, auth, tls, codex-response), plus `src/image-generation` and `image-generate-tool` tests, pass.
- **`pnpm check:changed`:** all lanes pass (extensions lint, tsgo extensions/test, format, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, docs) except `changelog attributions`. That one fails on existing `CHANGELOG/*` lines this PR doesn't touch. With the allocation, `check:test-lines-ratchet` also passes locally (slack 41).
- **Docs anchors:** `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports no problems in the changed pages. Its 2 failures are in pages this PR doesn't touch (`/tools/acp-agents-setup` and `releases/2026.10.1.md`). The kept `#gpt-image-2.5` anchor still resolves.
- **Full `pnpm test extensions/openai/`:** 87/90 files pass. The 3 failures are realtime/GPT-Live transport and token-sharing OAuth tests, which don't import image code. They fail the same way when run alone in this sandbox.
- **Live API capability checks** (2026-11-07, API key, direct `/v1/images/generations`):
  - `size: "1536x864"` and `16x16` get the same pixel-budget validation as `gpt-image-2.5-flare`. `gpt-image-1` rejects custom sizes.
  - `background: "transparent"` with JPEG gets "not supported for JPEG output format", the same as 2.5. `gpt-image-2` gets "Transparent background is not supported for this model".
  - OpenAI accepted `quality: "xhigh"` and `"max"` for both 2.6 models without a validation error, like 2.5: each request was still running when cut off after 6s. `gpt-image-1` returns 400 immediately: "does not support quality 'xhigh'". This shows the API doesn't reject these values; no full `xhigh`/`max` generation was run. The completed live runs below used `low`.
  - A raw 2.6 Flare response includes top-level `"quality": "low"`, `"size": "1024x1024"` and token usage.
- **Live OpenClaw runs (this branch)**, using an isolated profile/state, an explicit API-key route and `openclaw infer image` (same runtime + provider path `image_generate` uses):
  - `infer image providers`: OpenAI `defaultModel: gpt-image-2`; models include `gpt-image-2.6-flare` and `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`.
  - `generate --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst --quality low --size 1024x1024`: PNG 1024x1024, `ignoredOverrides: []` (quality sent).
  - `generate --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare --quality low --size 1024x1024`: PNG 1024x1024, `ignoredOverrides: []`.
  - `edit --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst --quality low --size auto` (recolor the generated lemon): PNG 1254x1254, with `auto` sent as-is rather than snapped; the visual edit was correct.
- **Local review:** autoreview (codex engine) on the committed branch range, run twice with `--mode branch --base origin/main`:
  - At `--max-priority P2` before publishing: "patch is correct (0.91)".
  - At `--max-priority P3` on the final head before landing, with the runtime, tool and image-asset sources as context: "patch is correct (0.88)".
  - Neither run had accepted/actionable findings.
- **Hosted review:** every ClawSweeper review run for this PR (rev 1 to 5, including the explicit re-review) failed in its own source preparation (`review_blob_metadata_unavailable`) and used up its retry budget. It never posted findings, and the failure is in ClawSweeper's pipeline, not this PR.

Gaps:

- The agent-turn `image_generate` proof through an isolated Gateway was refused by the CLI's inter-session attribution guard when run from an agent exec. The live proof uses the capability CLI on the same runtime/provider path, and the tool-level quality reporting is covered by the runtime test.
- **ChatGPT/Codex sign-in is untested with 2.6, and the catalog doesn't distinguish sign-in methods.**
  - That route snaps every request to a fixed size (`applyNativeLimits: true`). This is existing behavior, already true for 2.5 and `gpt-image-2`; the image result records the requested and snapped size.
  - It also sends requests through the Responses API, which OpenAI lists as not supported for 2.6. Users with only OAuth may see 2.6 requests fail outright, not just get snapped sizes.
  - The docs point 2.6 users to the API-key route, as for 2.5. Advertising capabilities per sign-in method would need a core capability-contract change. A clear "use an API key" error on that route is worth adding only once someone with Codex OAuth confirms the rejection.
- ClawRouter and fal have their own GPT Image catalogs and aren't changed here.
- Production code: +134/−96 lines, about 100 of them moved without changes. Tests: +98 lines, covered by the test-line allocation above.

prs.title: fix(tts): speak an answer that carries a picture instead of dropping its voice
prs.body:
Closes #142188

> **Rebased onto current `main` again (2026-11-02, `796b1471345`).** The branch was
> ~4,800 commits behind. One conflict, in `dispatch-from-config.tts.test-support.ts`:
> kept the media guard in the mocked synthesizer, because the supplement tests depend on
> it. Two rebase adaptations beyond the mechanical ones:
> - `main` replaced `resolveStatusTtsSnapshot` with `resolveTtsSettingsSnapshot`, which
>   changed the captioned-final deferral: with `tts.auto` unset it now reads `off`, so the
>   streamed-answer test sets `tts.auto: "always"` explicitly. Behaviour is unchanged.
> - Upstream growth pushed `dispatch-from-config.finalize.ts` over the 700-line cap, so
>   `withInheritedSupplementMetadata` and `resolveMediaFinalTtsText` moved to the sibling
>   `dispatch-from-config.media-tts-supplement.ts`.
>
> Local on this head: targeted suites 407/407, core and core-test typechecks, line-cap
> ratchet and lint green.

### Current status (2026-11-02)

ClawSweeper re-review: **0 code findings**, `proof: sufficient`, patch 4/6.

CI on `89672c0`: 64 pass. The only red lanes are `main` regressions, not this diff:
- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7` — the lease fixture in
  `deliver-queue.lease-integration.test.ts` (`preserves lost ownership during provider`),
  already being fixed upstream in #190934;
- `checks-node-changed-boundary` — the boundary scan flags
  `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts` (main commit `91f4975` imports
  `extensions/baseten/decision-provider.runtime.js`); this PR changes neither file.

This branch's own lanes pass. Waiting on the owner decision below. The branch already
carries the live-only behaviour; on approval of option 2 I will add the restart test
that proves a recovered queue never replays the audio (and name the signal if the review
wants it separate from `ttsSupplement.liveOnly`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with auto-TTS enabled would receive no voice message at all
when the assistant's answer carried an attachment. A reply that says something *and*
shows a chart arrives silent: no audio, no error, nothing in `doctor`. The same text
without an attachment is spoken normally, so the feature disappears exactly when the
assistant illustrates its answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`maybeApplyTtsToPayloadCore` skips synthesis whenever the payload already carries media.
That guard is correct and stays: on success the same function writes the audio into
`mediaUrl`, so removing it would overwrite the picture. One message carries one media
set — `ttsSupplement` holds only `spokenText` and a flag, not a second set.

So the answer is spoken by a **second message** instead. A final that carries non-audio
media is delivered untouched; afterwards its text is synthesized separately and sent as
an audio-only payload marked
`markReplyPayloadAsTtsSupplement(…, { visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true })`. This is the
mechanism `dispatch-from-config.finalize.ts` already uses for deferred final text; only
the entry condition is new.

Audio versus non-audio is decided by `hasNonAudioMediaReference`, built on the shared
media table (`isAudioFileName`), so a reply that already carries a voice note gets no
second one. Legacy `MEDIA:` directives participate in that classification and are
stripped from the spoken copy while staying in the visible message. Only speech-related
metadata (`tts`, `ttsExplicit`, `commandReply`) is inherited by the synthesized payload,
so command replies stay silent and delivery ownership is not transferred.

Boundaries: the ACP delivery coordinator has its own synthesis application and is not
touched here; the same branch can be added there if maintainers want it.

**Note for channel authors:** this makes a case reachable that previously only appeared
on channels with captioned-final delivery — a final that carries media and no text.
Such a payload is marked `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` and must not be read as "no answer
was produced". Our own VK channel plugin did read it that way and deleted the message
holding the answer; the flag is what tells them apart.

## Supplement lifetime: live-only

The supplement is optional audio that repeats an answer already delivered, and its writer
fence is the in-memory `sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority` it inherits. Durable recovery
cannot rebuild that fence — the supplement owns no pending-final completion of its own —
so a persisted row could replay the audio after the writer was replaced.

It therefore carries `ttsSupplement.liveOnly`, and the queue boundary in
`deliver-queue.ts` refuses to persist such a payload, next to where `skipQueue` is
consumed. That placement is layer-independent: both the routed and the channel-local lane
reach it, as does any caller of `deliverOutboundPayloads`. The normalizer
`getReplyPayloadTtsSupplement` preserves the flag, since delivery reads the lifetime from
the normalized supplement.

What this costs: a Gateway restart between the picture and its voice loses the audio. The
answer it repeats has already been delivered and recorded, so nothing the user needs
disappears. The alternative — an independently fenced durable completion — would need a
second owner of the session's pending final, which is a change to session delivery
ownership for the sake of optional audio; that decision is the maintainer's.

## User Impact

An answer that comes with a picture is now also spoken: the picture arrives in its own
message, the voice follows in the next one. Answers that already carry audio, command
replies, and replies without attachments behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**The guard is unconditional — real synthesis path, no channel, no TTS mocks**
(`src/tts/tts-entry-delivery.test.ts`, synthetic speech provider):

| payload | synthesis called |
|---|---|
| text + PNG / JPEG / PDF / MP4 / Opus | no |
| text + several attachments | no |
| text + legacy `MEDIA:` line | no |
| **same text, no attachment** | **yes** — control |

**Delivery, through `dispatchReplyFromConfig`** — 19 attachment formats plus edge cases:
mixed attachments, audio-only sets, a caption-less picture, `isError` payloads, non-final
TTS modes, two finals in one turn, a streamed answer ending in a picture, command replies
with and without an explicit speech request, and synthesis failure. Every case first
asserts the visible message survives untouched.

**The regression test fails without the fix:** stashing only `finalize.ts` turns
"speaks a picture answer as a separate voice message" red while the rest stay green.

**Writer authority is preserved and enforced.** A settled final can carry
`sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`, and an absent authority reads as authorized at every
check, so the supplement inherits it — while transcript and completion ownership stay
with the visible message. Three dispatch tests pin the boundary:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| writer still holds the turn | picture, then its voice supplement |
| writer replaced while the supplement is being synthesized | picture only — the audio is rejected before transport |
| replaced writer, ordinary settled final (pre-existing test) | not dispatched, unchanged |

The middle case is the one this PR had to earn: the first attempt attached the authority
to the synthesis input instead of the delivered payload, and since that metadata lives by
object identity it never reached the send path. The test failed until the authority moved
onto the payload that is actually sent.

**Speech comes from the prepared text.** `sendFinalPayload` now reports the text it
prepared for delivery — normalization applied and deferred block text merged, TTS not yet
run — and the supplement synthesizes that, reading it after the media pass so a rewritten
or cleared caption is what gets spoken. A recording cannot be normalized after the fact.

**A supplement follows only a message the recipient can see.** Eligibility is decided by
the outcome of preparation and delivery, not by the raw reply:

| situation | supplement |
|---|---|
| final delivered (queued or routed, settled) | yes |
| final deduped against a block that was delivered | yes |
| block vetoed by the channel (`channel-transform`) | no |
| visible answer failed to route | no |
| preparation cleared the caption (media pass, channel transform) | no — an empty prepared text says "say nothing" |
| queued answer cancelled in `beforeDeliver` | no |
| queued answer suppressed as a channel transform | no |
| answer delivered but not visibly (`visibleReplySent: false`) | no |
| settlement could not complete within its bound | no |

Admission is not visibility, so eligibility is decided after `turnLedger.settleQueued`,
the same bounded wait the no-visible-reply gate uses — but this gate fails closed. The
neighbouring gate treats admission as the strongest fact because uncertainty there must
not produce a duplicate message; here uncertainty must not produce a voice note that
arrives alone. Both answer "stay quiet"; only the reasoning differs, and the code says so.

**Runs** (Node 24.20.0):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` | pass |
| `auto-reply-reply` shard | 223 files, 5474 tests, 0 failures |
| `src/tts/tts-entry-delivery.test.ts` | 11 tests, 0 failures |
| `src/media/audio.test.ts` | 13 tests, 0 failures |
| `pnpm build`, `pnpm check` | pass |
| `autoreview` (claude, P2) | no accepted findings |

**Live traffic**, one install, before and after (redacted, hashed peer ids):

```
before   11:36:01  deliver kind=final len=758 media=true
         11:36:02  vk upload ok kind=photo
         11:36:03  vk upload ok kind=photo          ← no synthesis in the turn

after    15:43:54  deliver kind=final len=621 media=true
         15:43:55  vk upload ok kind=photo
         15:43:57  tts synthesize: format=ogg, size=385395
         15:43:57  deliver kind=final len=0 media=true
         15:43:59  vk upload ok kind=audio          ← voice as its own message
```

Docs updated: `docs/tools/tts.md` described the old behavior in both the rule list and
the decision tree.

## Plugin compatibility

Channel plugins see a new message shape: a final that carries media and no text. It is
marked `ttsSupplement.visibleTextAlreadyDelivered`, which is exactly the signal that tells
it apart from "no answer was produced".

Our own VK plugin got this wrong at first and deleted the message holding the answer,
because its progress-draft finalizer read an empty final as "no answer came". The repair
was to check the flag — not to work around the core — and it is a five-line guard plus
seven regression tests in that plugin. We report it because it is the upgrade risk a
reviewer should weigh: plugins that infer "no answer" from empty final text need that
one check. Plugins that only deliver what they are given need nothing.

## Open question for maintainers: durable recovery of the supplement

This is the one finding we have not implemented, because both ways to close it change a
contract that is yours to set. Everything below is what we traced; we are happy to build
whichever you choose.

**The gap.** `buildRecoveryDeliverParams` installs the writer fence
(`assertDirectAdapterHandoff` / `onPlatformSendDispatch`) only when the queued entry has a
`pending-final` `deliveryCompletion`, and reads the authority from that record alone. The
supplement carries its authority in payload metadata, which is process-local, and has no
completion of its own. If the process stops after the supplement is enqueued and the
session writer is replaced before recovery runs, the recovered audio sends unfenced.

**Why the supplement has no completion.** Reusing the visible answer's receipt would give
a second message the first one's delivery ownership — the mistake this PR was already
corrected for in an earlier round. So the choice is a new receipt or no recovery at all.

**Option 1 — give the supplement its own `pending-final` completion.** This is more than a
field: a completion is a durable record with a lifecycle (`prepared` → `queued` →
`delivered` / `suppressed` / `unknown`, settled through `settlePendingFinalDelivery`).
Minting one per supplement means new rows in that store and a new owner obligation to
settle them on every path, including failure. `AGENTS.md` asks contributors to agree
material persistent-store changes before implementing them, which is why we stopped here
rather than guessing at the shape.

**Option 2 — keep the supplement out of durable recovery.** Our preference, and the one
ClawSweeper now recommends ("Approve live-only supplements: add a narrowly scoped
non-recoverable delivery path"). A voice note lost to a restart is a small loss, while one
that outlives its writer is exactly what the fence exists to prevent.

We re-checked whether an existing signal already expresses it, so the ask is not for
something already there. `OutboundDeliveryQueuePolicy` is `required | best_effort`, and
`best_effort` is about how a failure is treated, not about persistence: recovery carries
the policy forward (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts` reads `entry.queuePolicy ?? "best_effort"`)
and replays such entries like any other. There is no admission bypass for an optional
send. So live-only needs a new signal, however small, and that is a contract addition.

**What is already fenced.** The live path: the supplement inherits
`sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`, it is attached to the delivered payload rather than the
synthesis input, and a replacement during synthesis is covered by a regression test. Only
the recovered path is open.

Tell us which option you want — or a third we have not seen — and we will implement it in
this PR. If you approve option 2, we will add the narrowest signal that expresses "do not
recover this send", thread it from the supplement through admission, and cover it with a
restart test that asserts the recovered queue never replays the audio.

## Related

- #42539 asks for text and voice as separate messages as a general Telegram delivery
  option. Different problem — there the answer is spoken and the split is a preference;
  here synthesis never runs. The mechanism is the same one, so that option could be
  built on this branch.
- #132736 (closed) covers auto-TTS supplement messages on Signal — separate voice
  messages are an existing shape in the core, not a new one.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep commentary line breaks in preamble progress text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a very visible rendering glitch in the Control UI WebChat during tool-calling turns. The assistant's text streams in correctly formatted (paragraphs, bullet lists, tables), and then at the moment a tool call begins it snaps into one long paragraph. Bold text and links survive, but every line break, list marker, and table row is flattened into a single line.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the provider resolves commentary at the tool boundary, `createReplyDelivery` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.reply-delivery.ts` emits the commentary-phase text as a keyed `preamble` item whose `progressText` had all whitespace collapsed to single spaces (`text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()`). The WebChat's `handlePreambleProgress` then takes that item as the owner of the text it had already streamed and renders `progressText` as Markdown in its place. Markdown without newlines has no paragraphs, list items, or table rows, so the block structure disappears exactly when the item replaces the stream.

The collapse was introduced with the native commentary progress work (#128793). No consumer needs it: the CLI runner path already emits multi-line commentary as `progressText`, the channel progress compositors (`pushPreambleHeadline`, `pushCommentaryProgress`) and the session-observer digest normalize their own single-line headlines, and the WebChat and history snapshot store the text verbatim. This change sends the trimmed text with its line breaks intact.

Non-goal: this does not change how commentary is phased, deduplicated, or persisted; the commentary signature used to suppress duplicate emissions still keys on the (now uncollapsed) text.

## User Impact

Pre-tool commentary in the WebChat keeps its paragraphs, lists, and tables through the tool boundary instead of collapsing to a single line. Other channels are unchanged because they already normalize the text themselves.

## Evidence

The existing "preserves aggregate commentary for providers without Responses item boundaries" expectation encoded the collapse (`"First. Second."`) and now expects the actual `\n` join. A new test streams multi-line Markdown commentary (paragraphs and a bullet list) through an Anthropic-style tool handoff and asserts both the update and end preamble events carry the text unchanged. Both fail without the fix.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe
  Test Files  34 passed   Tests  866 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-chat src/gateway/session-observer src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-progress.test.ts
  Test Files  8 passed    Tests  348 passed
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>   # clean
oxfmt --check <changed files>                 # clean
```

Observed on the 2026.9.2 release with an `openai-completions` transport driving tool-calling turns in the WebChat.

prs.title: fix(code-mode): publish canonical tool inputs
prs.body:
Closes #194865

## What Problem This Solves

- Code Mode advertises string boolean literals for Gemini-routed tools, causing calls that follow its generated types to fail validation.

## User Impact

- Gemini optional-read declarations use boolean `true`, so calls following them reach the read tool.
- Collector declarations follow surviving native readers.
- Deep tool descriptions retain the existing schema-depth bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep provider projections on native definitions, raw validation contracts, and bounded canonical catalog inputs. Prepare collector availability before normalization and preserve execution-only overrides.

## Evidence

- Built CLI → loopback SSE model fixture → Code Mode → real read handler, before and after.
- Google OAuth → model-generated Code Mode call → real read result → completed Google reply; no fallback.
- Complete native tool definitions are equal across both fixture captures.
- `tool_describe` schema depth drops from 5,000 at `c9b02dccebe` to at most 128.
- Full build and 112 runtime, availability, finalization, schema, and prefix tests passed; production/test types, lint, format, assertion-safety, and test-line checks passed.
- Regressions cover generated types, missing-file reads, collector policy filtering and fresh assembly, and hidden exec options.

### Before (model fixture)

```text
HEAD d4ae77eae296fd8eb1f90f7a4ebb5d77fa2e6ad9
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (d4ae77e) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.
Error: Invalid arguments for tool "read": optional: expected boolean; received "true" (string); optional: must be equal to constant (allowed: true); received "true" (string). Expected input: { path: string; cursor?: number /* integer, >= 0 */; limit?: number; offset?: number /* integer, >= 1 */; optional?: true }.
    at openclaw-code-mode:user.js:5:22
```

### After (model fixture)

Closes #141472 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Workboard users who paste URLs or markdown links into card notes or operator comments would see dead plaintext in the Control UI, even though the notes placeholder already says "Notes, acceptance criteria, links." The same text is shown on compact cards, in the detail drawer, and in the edit-card comment list. Operators currently have to copy the URL out by hand during triage. ## Why This Change Was Made Workboard now linkifies two conservative patterns in notes and comments: - Markdown links: `[Anrop](https://anrop.no/)` - Bare `http://` and `https://` URLs Links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Other text, including newlines, stays unchanged. This is not full markdown: no bold, lists, headings, images, or HTML, and no `innerHTML`. `javascript:` / `data:` URLs stay plaintext. Balanced parentheses inside a destination are kept, so Wikipedia-style paths such as `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)` stay intact in both the markdown and bare-URL forms. Trailing `.,;:!?` on a bare URL stays outside the href. A wrapping `(https://example.com)` still leaves the surrounding parentheses as text. Clicking a link on a compact card does not open the detail drawer (the existing `a` action-target guard). Native `` links remain keyboard-activatable. The edit-card comment list uses the same linker as the drawer, so the three surfaces stay consistent. ## User Impact Operators can click research, docs, PR, and competitor URLs directly from Workboard cards instead of copying them out of notes. ## Evidence **Before** (current Control UI): notes interpolate as escaped plaintext. ![Workboard notes before, with markdown and a raw URL shown as text](https://github.com/schjonhaug/openclaw/releases/download/workboard-pr-141481-proof/workboard-notes-before.png) **After, production compact card:** markdown labels and bare https URLs become anchors on the real Workboard card renderer. Clicking `Example` opened `https://example.com/` in a new tab and did not open the detail drawer. Dummy fixture only (`example.com` / `example.org`). ![Workboard compact card after, with Example and example.org as clickable links](https://github.com/schjonhaug/openclaw/releases/download/workboard-pr-141481-proof/workboard-compact-card-after.png) Focused Control UI unit tests passed on this revision: - `vitest --project unit` on `linkify-text.test.ts` and `view.test.ts`, including: - markdown + bare https become `` - balanced parentheses in bare and markdown destinations (`Function_(mathematics)`) - wrapping parentheses around a bare URL stay outside the href - trailing punctuation stays outside autolinked URLs - `javascript:` / `data:` markdown is not turned into anchors - compact-card link click / Enter / Space do not open the detail drawer - edit-modal comments use the same linker This revision also formats the Workboard view files (`oxfmt`) and regenerates `extensions/workboard/openclaw.plugin.json` so the bundled control-ui asset hash matches the source. Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.2 before this change: card detail notes render as `

${card.notes}

`, so a note such as `[Anrop](https://anrop.no/)` is escaped text. After this renderer, that note is a real anchor.

prs.title: feat(prometheus): expose provider usage windows
prs.body:
Closes #139188

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can monitor OpenClaw request and tool behavior through the authenticated Prometheus exporter, but cannot monitor provider subscription allowance windows or refresh health without maintaining a separate Gateway RPC collector.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing provider-usage cache with a sanitized, selection-bound metrics snapshot and gives only the official Prometheus exporter a lifecycle-scoped observer capability. The cache owns periodic refreshes and last-good retention; Prometheus scrapes remain synchronous, render-only, and network-free.

Credential-backed provider polling is explicit opt-in through `providerUsage.enabled`, which defaults to `false`. The selection contract follows the same default/legacy-agent credential selection as unscoped `usage.status`. Selection changes withdraw prior allowance series until the new selection produces an observation. Exported labels are bounded to provider, window, and refresh outcome; account emails, profile IDs, credential fingerprints, prompts, responses, and other identifiers are excluded.

## User Impact

When operators explicitly enable provider-usage polling, they can graph and alert on:

- provider allowance used ratios;
- allowance-window reset timestamps;
- last refresh attempt and success timestamps;
- refresh success and bounded failure outcomes.

Upgrades and fresh installs do not begin credential-backed provider polling unless `providerUsage.enabled` is explicitly set to `true`. No provider API call is triggered by a Prometheus scrape.

## Review Fixes

- Makes provider-usage polling explicit opt-in and default-off for upgrades and fresh installations.
- Supports lifecycle-safe hot enable/disable without changing ordinary diagnostics or Prometheus metrics.
- Releases the observer and withdraws provider metrics when diagnostics are disabled, and reacquires exactly once when re-enabled.
- Rejects callbacks from retired exporter generations and revoked service leases.
- Cancels future provider refresh scheduling after observer release.
- Reads lifecycle-managed runtime configuration instead of ambient configuration.
- Preserves bounded Z.AI window identities so allowance and reset series cannot overwrite one another.
- Integrates the restricted observer with current plugin-service ownership, reload, rollback, cleanup, retirement, pending-owner, and current-claim lifecycle fencing.
- Preserves explicit runtime-config overrides in capable-client cache tests after the latest upstream rebase.
- Updates the generated plugin config baseline for the intentional two-entry surface increase (`4623` to `4625`).

## Evidence

The exact published head `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295` passed both the isolated Portainer candidate validator and the published-release upgrade proof before the PR branch was updated.

### Candidate validation

- Validation ref: `validate/pr-141276-5bcdf1a3d6`
- Verified target: `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295`
- Validation base: `3150853d9dee8ad161011682c130ea5731faa365`
- Merge base: `2f228582f354803021c3d217d3a2fd79b54b0305`
- Candidate runtime handoff SHA-256: `924213e6e6d7dae92d5f038666360275f31423173fa3e87363b0a11db1235dee`
- Runtime build cache: rebuilt

Passed gates: locked dependency installation; changed-file diff hygiene, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and type-aware lint; core, extension, owning test-graph, and extension-test types; plugin contracts; focused provider-usage tests; exact-SHA runtime build; isolated managed-install lifecycle proof including auth-suspended revocation; and the final temporary-ref identity fence.

Managed-install evidence recorded an authenticated scrape, one initial provider request after explicit enablement, provider metrics observed, and zero requests caused by scraping, disabled startup, hot-disable release, plugin revocation, or authority revocation during authentication. The restricted observer capability remained unavailable to a non-official plugin.

### Published-release upgrade compatibility

- Integrity-pinned baseline: `openclaw@2026.9.4` and `@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus@2026.9.4`
- Baseline/default-off provider requests: `0` / `0` over 65-second observations
- Database schema migration: `19` to `27`
- Operator intent and runtime invariants preserved: `true`
- Diagnostics, provider-plugin, Gateway configuration, and managed exporter installation preserved: `true`
- Initial/scheduled requests after explicit opt-in: `1` / `1`
- Observed cadence: `59852 ms`
- Scrape-triggered requests: `0`
- Requests after exporter disable: `0`
- Candidate exporter tarball SHA-256: `7fcd9712b575c84b346b6a50834f31a4f7e77a91948ec524d847b87bfbe58587`
- Final temporary-ref identity fence: passed

### Current upstream conflict check

Canonical `main` was refreshed to `2f2c09d1c12d93408692e950a82d01fd04fa5af1` after validation. An isolated real merge completed with zero conflicts.
## Maintainer Gate Still Required

The compatibility concern is addressed by making credential-backed polling explicit opt-in. The security-sensitive capability boundary still requires authorized maintainer review and approval for the exact published head.

prs.title: fix: chat links return 404 with unknown query parameters
prs.body:
Fixes #194859

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI chat links return 404 when an outside source adds an unknown query parameter, such as `homescreen=1` on a Home Screen shortcut.

## User Impact

User impact: Chat links with extra query parameters redirect to the same chat path with only recognized parameters kept. Recognized parameters still undergo validation, and session authorization remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A 302 redirect removes unknown parameters before the return path or app receives them, including `token` and `gatewayUrl`. This lets otherwise valid chat links open without passing unintended settings to the app.

## Evidence

Checked at `ea459ad` before pushing:

- The new regression test fails without the fix (`expected 404 to be 302`) and passes with it.
- `control-ui-public-chat.http.test.ts`: 15/15 passing.
- Session-entry neighbor tests: 86/86 passing.
- Core typecheck and oxfmt: clean.
- An isolated local gateway running the fix commit:
  - `?homescreen=1` returns 302 to `/chat/main` and lands on the same page as the plain link.
  - `?draft=hi&homescreen=1` redirects to `/chat/main?draft=hi`.
  - `?token=x&gatewayUrl=…` redirects to `/chat/main`.
  - `?dashboard=bogus` still returns 404.

Not checked: lint (the UI eslint plugin was missing locally) and a real iPhone.
