prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled CI and release live-test coverage after the stalled-turn recovery test was added outside the existing shard directory routes.

## User Impact

Release validation now includes the auto-reply recovery live test. This changes test routing only.

## Why This Change Was Made

[7db090f5f614 / #194707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194707) added `src/auto-reply/reply/stalled-turn-recovery.live.test.ts`. Discovery found 162 live files, but the release shard union selected only 161 because no shard included `src/auto-reply/`.

Route that directory through the existing agents shard and update its documented coverage. The existing partition assertion and live test remain intact. Simplification pass: one routing line, one documentation update, zero new test lines or machinery.

## Evidence

- [Failed scheduled job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42431148894/job/128580463996) at `f6a8ce9a6f22`: the check annotation identifies this exact missing file in `test/scripts/test-live-shard.test.ts:68`. prs.title: fix: keep sandboxes running during file and media reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

File/media previews used to checkpoint and reconcile the entire local sandbox workspace, pausing running guest commands for every read. The pause ended before opening the file; its invariant was coherent reconciliation, while the existing descriptor boundary protected file containment.

## User Impact

Reads now select live sandbox backing through a bounded existing-worker metadata lookup and preserve canonical public paths, live authority, mount visibility, and descriptor containment. Capture/publication/lifecycle operations still quiesce. No new config, cache, or schema.

**Required follow-up: #194957 fixes save→reload consistency and host-only sessions with retained old sandbox backing.** The final audit found these regressions after this original head was published. That PR keeps canonical CAS writes and projection import under one custody, restricts live backing to sandbox sessions, and removes the retired read checkpoint adapter. The complete lane documents that direct host edits enter retained sandbox previews at the next preparation; UI saves synchronize immediately.

## Evidence

Original exact-parent regression: nine reads caused nine pauses; this head causes zero. Existing alias/shadowed-mount and descriptor containment tests plus new symlink-swap, partial-write and authority-revocation proof passed. Initial focused suites: 136 passed, one existing filesystem skip. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42429341781) passed at `9f44964f8b79bc5b17ca89d65dca8a5c03f62808`. Later corrective tests/review/CI are recorded in #194957.

Production-shaped synthetic campaign: 62,000 files (1,181,100,000 bytes), 40.28 GiB synthetic agent DB, 10,001 metadata sessions, 3,006 populated transcript sessions. Real isolated Gateway WebSocket `sessions.files.get`; continuous Docker guest writes with 20 ms heartbeat; 30 serial reads offered at 2-second intervals. Five AB/BA pairs plus A/A controls, no production data or Team access.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Read-induced pauses / 150 reads | 150 | 0 |
| Manifest scans / 150 reads | 150 | 0 |
| Pooled read p50 / p95 | 2,740 / 3,221 ms | 129 / 176 ms |
| Median process CPU per read | 3,281 ms | 136 ms |
| Median main V8 allocation per read | 30.33 MB | 10.55 MB |
| Median maximum guest heartbeat gap | 3,040 ms | 31.4 ms |
| Total excess guest gaps above 40 ms | 382,299 ms | 24.2 ms |

A/A median read latency differed 2.95%; p95 differed 79.92%, process CPU 25.34%, allocation 12.39%. The noisy first control is retained. All five paired median latency reductions were 94.89–95.42%, CPU reductions 95.36–96.45%, allocation reductions 61.46–65.44%. The baseline overran the offered cadence (median batch 82.77 s); candidate finished in 58.14 s. Excess heartbeat gaps include unrelated scheduling/storage noise, not only pause time.

The five timing pairs used this original head and parent owner/caller source replay in common runtime/dependencies, not separately built full releases. The follow-up read scenario is source-equivalent; its separate 30-read confirmation returned zero pauses/scans and p50/p95 142.85/197.62 ms. Local platform is OrbStack Docker with macOS/APFS backing, not native Podman/btrfs; no btrfs causal claim. No Team access or production data.

`check:changed` exposed two exact-parent main regressions: changelog attribution introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364), and Knip `OpenClawShell` export failure introduced by `adca0b0844c7` (#194815). Affected type/lint/format/ratchet checks and Codex autoreview pass; no overall `check:changed` green claim. Complete lane production delta after follow-up is +72 lines; follow-up alone removes ten production lines. Related prior work: #185554. Reader/projection overlap: #194430, whose conflict algorithm is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: treat Anthropic-compatible sensitive stop as provider refusal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #182654

Anthropic-compatible endpoints such as Z.AI report content-safety stops as `stop_reason: "sensitive"` without an error payload. `mapAnthropicStopReason` already maps `"sensitive"` to `"error"` (historical crash fix for #43607), but the Messages transport lifecycle only called `applyAnthropicRefusal` for `"refusal"`. That left `errorMessage` empty, so the stream threw `"An unknown error occurred"` and never attached a `provider_refusal` diagnostic.

This PR routes `"sensitive"` through the same refusal path:

```ts
// Z.AI and other compatible endpoints use "sensitive" for content-safety stops.
if (delta.stop_reason === "refusal" || delta.stop_reason === "sensitive") {
  applyAnthropicRefusal(output, delta.stop_details, model.provider);
}
```

No recovery/failover/overflow logic changes. `mapAnthropicStopReason` is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on Z.AI / GLM (and other Anthropic-compatible proxies that emit `sensitive`) now see a provider-refusal outcome with a readable message and diagnostic, instead of a generic unknown stream error after a content-safety stop.

## Evidence

**Unit tests.** With `anthropic-stream-lifecycle.ts` reverted to `main`, the new case fails:

```
 × packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.sensitive-stop.test.ts > Anthropic-compatible sensitive stops > treats a Z.AI sensitive stop as a provider refusal
   → expected 'An unknown error occurred' not to be 'An unknown error occurred'
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

With the fix (Node 24.22.1):

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.sensitive-stop.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  58 passed (58)
```

`oxfmt --check` on the touched files passes.

## Scope

- `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-stream-lifecycle.ts` (one condition + comment)
- `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.sensitive-stop.test.ts` (regression)

## Relation to #43607

#43607 / #56639 fixed the hard crash from an *unhandled* stop reason. This PR fixes the remaining incomplete cutover where `"sensitive"` is mapped to `"error"` but not recorded as a provider refusal.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): keep file I/O failures inside the documented CLI error envelope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path` documents that JSON mode reports path/file errors as one object — `{ ok: false, error: { type: "cli_error", code, message } }` — and that file errors exit `2` (`docs/cli/path.md`, exit-code table). Only the domain checks honoured that contract. Two file-system calls sat outside any error boundary:

- `loadOcPathFile` awaited `fs.open(...)` **before** its `try`, so `ENOENT` / `EACCES` / `EISDIR` / `EMFILE` escaped from every verb that loads a file (`resolve`, `find`, `set`, `emit`).
- `set` awaited `fs.writeFile(...)` with no guard, so `ENOSPC` / `EACCES` escaped there.

Users got the generic failure envelope instead: exit `1`, no domain `code`, and in human mode only a bare `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…'` line with no `OC_PATH_` identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both boundaries now report through the module's existing `emitError` owner, which already produced the documented envelope for the domain errors, and set `process.exitCode = 2`:

- read side → `OC_PATH_FILE_UNREADABLE`
- write side → `OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED`

The parse calls (`parseJsonc` / `parseJsonl` / `parseYaml` / `parseMd`) stay outside the new `catch`, so parse errors keep their current propagation and are never relabelled as I/O failures. The existing domain codes (`OC_PATH_FILE_NOT_REGULAR`, `OC_PATH_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` / `OC_JSONC_INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `OC_PATH_INPUT_NOT_UTF8`) are untouched. No new abstraction, no new option, no change to the write mechanism.

Docs: the exit-2 row, the JSON-envelope paragraph, and the `set` exit note now name both codes. Tests: four cases folded into the existing `resolve` and `set` suites. To stay under the 1000-line `max-lines` cap, the quoted-literal `it.each` case moved verbatim into `cli.quoted-literals.test-support.ts` and is registered from the same suite; `config/test-lines-allocations/oc-path-cli-fs-error-envelope.txt` carries the test budget.

## User Impact

A missing or unreadable file, or an unwritable target, now fails exactly like every other `openclaw path` error: one JSON object carrying `error.code` in JSON mode, `CODE: reason` on stderr in human mode, and exit `2`. Scripts that branch on `error.code` can finally tell an I/O failure apart from a parse error or a refused pattern, and human-mode output names the file and the cause instead of only the raw `errno` string.

## Evidence

Real CLI, current head `1ff62b1a`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with `oc-path` enabled (disabled by default). "before" is `origin/main` with the same command and workspace.

| # | Command | before (`origin/main`) | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `path resolve oc://does-not-exist.md/heading --human` | exit `1`; stderr `ENOENT …` (no code) | exit `2`; `OC_PATH_FILE_UNREADABLE: failed to read …: ENOENT …` |
| 2 | same, `--json` | exit `1`; no `code` | exit `2`; `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"OC_PATH_FILE_UNREADABLE",…}}` |
| 3 | `path set oc://note.md/[frontmatter]/name changed --json` on a `chmod 444` file | exit `1`; no `code` | exit `2`; `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED","message":"… The file was left unchanged. Check that you can write it, then retry."}}`; sha256 unchanged |
| 4 | control: `path resolve oc://x/../y --json` | exit `2` + domain `code` | exit `2` + same domain `code` (no regression) |

### Raw terminal output (inline, current head `1ff62b1a`, paths redacted to `<work>/`)

```
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (1ff62b1)
$ openclaw path set oc://note.md/[frontmatter]/name changed --json
{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","code":"OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED","message":"failed to write <work>/note.md: EACCES: permission denied, open '<work>/note.md'. The file was left unchanged. Check that you can write it, then retry."}}
EXIT=2
$ openclaw path set oc://note.md/[frontmatter]/name changed --human
OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED: failed to write <work>/note.md: EACCES: permission denied, open '<work>/note.md'. The file was left unchanged. Check that you can write it, then retry.
EXIT=2
$ sha256sum note.md
d952fb302e81cd623597a39f3823b4bf694b19afee594c218f7ad26d7dee5392  note.md
```

Regression, same shipped handler: pre-fix (production file reverted) `2 failed` — `AssertionError: expected '…' to contain 'The file was left unchanged'`; post-fix `2 passed`. Full suite `81 passed | 4 failed (85)`; the 4 are pre-existing `spawnSync patch ENOENT` failures on `origin/main` in this environment.

```
check-test-lines-ratchet: Test lines OK: 6556089; ceiling: 6556094; slack: 5.
check-line-cap-ratchet:   OK (3 changed source files; no new violations or growth)
oxfmt / oxlint:            correct format; 0 warnings, 0 errors
```

Review follow-up: `fs.writeFile` truncates only after `open` succeeds, so `OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED` now states "The file was left unchanged" when `err.syscall === "open"` and reserves backup-restore advice for failures after a successful open. CLI-S11 pins the unchanged bytes and both message branches (RED/GREEN above). The `set` doc line now separates an unparseable file (exit `1`) from an invalid `oc://` address or file I/O error (exit `2`); the exit-code table is left for #193166, which rewrites it. The `win32` guard stays: `chmod 444` sets a read-only attribute there, and releasing it for the auto-cleanup fixture is a separate cross-platform concern.

Collision check: #172164 edits `cli.test.ts` in a different region; #193166 rewrites the same `docs/cli/path.md` paragraph, so one PR needs a trivial rebase. No open PR touches `cli.ts`.

prs.title: fix(skill-workshop): show what whole-file SKILL.md writes and drafts drop
prs.body:
Closes #194826

_Prepared for Cosmin Toma (RUF agentic team)._

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent silently wipes most of a live skill when it sends a short change note as the content of a whole-file `SKILL.md` write or draft.

## User Impact

User impact: when a `SKILL.md` rewrite or draft would drop most of a live skill, the agent (and the user reviewing drafts) now sees how much is removed and which sections disappear, before anyone relies on it. Nothing is blocked; writes still land and can be undone with `restore`.

## Why This Change Was Made

In #194826 (on 2026.7.1-2) an 87-line change note replaced a 387-line skill through the old proposal flow, and nothing showed the loss. On `main` that flow is gone, but `write_file` of `SKILL.md` and `draft` still replace the file whole, and the tool contract never says so.

This PR:

- adds `skillReplacementReport(before, after)` in `skill-lint.ts`: body line count before/after (`SKILL.md body: 387 → 87 lines (-78%).`), up to 8 removed `##` sections (code blocks ignored), and a non-blocking advisory when the new body is under 60% of the old one;
- shows that report on `patch`/`write_file` of an existing `SKILL.md`, on `draft` for a live skill, and on `view draft`;
- adds a `change-note` lint advisory when the title starts with Fix / Proposal / Change(s) / Changelog (only when the write introduces it, like the other rules);
- states in the tool description, the `/learn drafts` prompt and `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` that `write_file`/`draft` content is the complete file and replaces it whole.

Advisory rather than blocking: writes are versioned with `restore`, and the codebase has no override-flag pattern for this. The Control UI already shows a diff before applying a draft.

Known nits: a legitimate title such as `# Change management` gets the change-note advisory; every `SKILL.md` patch now carries a one-line size summary; with the shrink advisory a write can end with four advisory lines instead of the documented three.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: `skill_library` `update` with `proposal_content` also replaces `SKILL.md` whole.

## Evidence

On `main` at d44c9ad92 with this commit applied:

- `pnpm test extensions/skill-workshop`: 16 files, 140 tests passed.
- New tests: `skill-lint.test.ts` (report and `change-note` rule) and `tool.test.ts` ("shows what a whole-file SKILL.md rewrite or draft drops from the live skill"), which reproduces the incident: a 65-line skill rewritten with a `# Fix: …` note via `draft`, `view draft`, and `write_file`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `oxlint extensions/skill-workshop`, and `git diff --check` pass. (On the original base 1ad3ec3d2 also oxfmt, `lint:docs` and the pre-commit hooks.)
- Gap: no end-to-end run against a live Gateway with a real agent; the change only adds text to tool results.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).
- Workflow validation passed, including pinned tooling fallback and zizmor.
- Changed-surface checks passed: formatting, root-test typechecks, dependency/coercion/dead-export guards, and script/test lint. `git diff --check` passed.
- Repair delta: 12 insertions / 37 deletions across workflow and guard test; removed the separate preflight input, scheduling branch, and branch-dispatch route.
- Local autoreview of this repair against `7bf16b8fd47f07612777b4957b1a14bbc66eba42`: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

prs.title: fix: compaction skips configured fallback after quota errors
prs.body:
Closes #194803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes compaction skipping a configured fallback when a summarization provider returns an HTTP 429 quota error without a separately recognizable rate-limit phrase.

## User Impact

Compaction can try its existing configured fallback instead of stopping at the failed primary summary. This does not replenish quota, add fallback providers, or guarantee that a backup succeeds. No configuration or public API changes are included.

**Review readiness:** focused regression tests and isolated-Gateway checks cover the quota-429 fallback path, including automatic and manual compaction and saved fallback summaries. A subsequent external report also exercises manual compaction with a real fallback model and a replayed primary 429; see below. The exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42426200469) and its applicable CI gate passed. @vyctorbrzezowski approved landing in the linked work session on 2026-11-08; the exact head remains `30ff6a55d5b755cf4f677b9a579e684c72f7282e`. A quota 429 originating from the real primary provider remains untested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compaction wrappers preserve the original SummaryProviderError and assistant response, but classification used the wrappers’ prefixed display text. Wrapping `Provider API error (429): daily token quota exhausted` can hide the status from the existing text-based fallback adapter.

Use the retained provider response with the existing assistant failure classifier and carry its normalized failure metadata through the existing compaction result. Other failures retain the existing classifier. Reuse the same cause-chain lookup for summary timeout detection.

This is separate from diagnostic-label misclassification in #194759 and the configurable summary cap in #194719. It does not establish what happened in the original historical incident.

## Evidence

Tested from base `f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1`; final candidate tree `9e4ac34dfb899aaf5a27158ac327bea2927f1401`.

- **Red before the fix:** the added `provider quota 429` row failed: only the primary model was requested instead of primary followed by backup; result was `ok: false, compacted: false`.
- **Green after the fix:** `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed both shards: **10 + 88 tests**. Existing assertions check fallback request order and the persisted summary; timeout and terminal-error cases remain covered.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- Repository formatter and file-scoped lint passed for all three changed TypeScript files: **No problems in 3 files**.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base HEAD` and `git diff --cached --check` passed. The one-line test allocation adds quota wording to an existing regression matrix instead of duplicating its fixture.
- Native local Auto Review returned **scoped-clean at P0-only**, with no findings. It did not execute tests. A subsequent lint-only change replaced parameter reassignment with an equivalent local cause-chain cursor; final tests/typecheck/lint were rerun.
- Final independent native code review of commit `30ff6a55d5b755cf4f677b9a579e684c72f7282e` returned **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no actionable findings. This reviewed the four-file patch and supplied frozen source context; it did not rerun tests and noted incomplete visibility into unchanged classifier/harness internals. The existing boundary tests and external runtime evidence remain the execution proof.
- Simplification review retained canonical assistant-error classification as the policy owner; no broad new text matcher or separate fallback policy was added.

An initial incorrectly scoped lint run timed out after visiting unrelated files; the corrected file-scoped run above passed. The external Gateway/stub-provider report below adds separate evidence; hosted CI is tracked in this PR’s Checks tab.


## External verification and handoff

@wr-web [reported an isolated Gateway reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194813#issuecomment-6713323856) on 2026-11-07, with a [linked result summary image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/194803/proof-194803.png). The requester confirmed that this is their agent continuing from their fork, rather than a report personally authored by the requester.

Reported setup: Windows 11, Node v26.12.1, a source Gateway on loopback with isolated state, and `chat.send "/compact"`. The primary HTTP stub returns `429 {"error":{"message":"daily token quota exhausted"}}` on summarization, without an error code or the phrase "too many requests"; the configured fallback stub returns a summary.

| Reported source | Fallback requests | Observed outcome |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `main` at `fc9749f` | 0 | Compaction fails without trying the fallback |
| This PR at `30ff6a5` | 4 | Primary classified as `rate_limit`; fallback candidate succeeds |

The comment and image agree on this result. This session inspected those supplied materials but did not rerun the Windows environment; the image is a result summary, not an independently captured execution trace. This adds reported real-Gateway/HTTP-provider-boundary coverage, not live-model-provider proof.

### macOS raw-artifact verification

The fork-agent follow-up [posted under @saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194813#issuecomment-6714147421) supplies a [public, commit-pinned evidence bundle](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/tree/019194c82300859866452b3c809762a3d8410db7/pr-194813-gateway-validation) with harness source, redacted Gateway records, per-request stub logs, decoded persisted state, and test logs. It compares this exact PR head with `main` at `1ad3ec3d2081f3c7228b5bed8ae95e3821cd609f`. Environment reported: macOS 26.5.2 arm64; **Bun 1.4.4 runs the Gateway**, while Node v24.22.1 runs the launcher, driver, and tests.

| Case | Base fallback requests / saved compaction | PR fallback requests / saved compaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Budget-triggered, turn 6 | 0 / no | 2 / yes |
| Manual `/compact` | 0 / no | 2 / yes |
| Manual, unstructured fallback summary control | not part of this control | 4 / yes, quality-guard degraded summary |

This session fetched the public files without GitHub authentication, inspected the harness without executing it, independently counted the supplied request records, and compared them with the Gateway decision excerpts and decoded transcript entries. They agree: the primary produces three HTTP 429 attempts; the PR classifies it as `rate_limit`, requests the fallback, and saves a summary containing the fallback marker. The checked unchanged fallback-owner files are byte-identical between the two referenced source commits. These are reviewed external execution artifacts, not a new local rerun.

The unstructured-summary control records four fallback requests plus `quality_guard_degraded_fallback`, supporting the explanation for the Windows report’s four versus the structured-summary runs’ two. The recorded counts are fixture-dependent, not a promise of exactly one or two requests.

**Artifact reading note:** successful runs also have `fallbackSummaryInHistory: false` and `sessionsCompactionCount: null` in `summary.json`. Those are convenience probes of public history/session responses, not the persistence verdict. The separate `state-inspection.json` files decode stored `compaction` entries and show `hasFallbackMarker: true`; the base files have no compaction entries.

The supplied test logs confirm **10 + 88 passing PR tests**, **79 adjacent tests across four files**, a passing core typecheck, and the quota-429 row as the only failing row among six fallback cases on the red base. External full-core lint exits nonzero on unrelated diagnostics, and its attempted direct file-scoped invocation reports no files; neither is presented as a passing external lint gate. The locally passing file-scoped check in the earlier Evidence section used the repository wrapper, not that direct invocation:

```sh
pnpm lint --base HEAD --files-json '["src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.ts","src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/direct-compaction-preparation.ts","src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.safeguard.test-support.ts"]'
```

The runtime checks in the macOS subsection above use loopback HTTP stub providers. The later real-fallback report below adds separate evidence. Errors carrying only a type/body signal without an HTTP status remain outside this proof.

### Reported live-fallback validation (manual compaction)

A [follow-up posted under @saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194813#issuecomment-6715639469) reports an isolated macOS Gateway run on this exact PR head, using Bun 1.4.4 for the Gateway and Node v24.22.1 for the driver. The [commit-pinned evidence bundle](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/tree/5b8707883e2c7e38accb59455e146a178a78162f/pr-194813-gateway-validation/live-fallback) includes the harness, sanitized excerpts, and dry-run request logs.

- **Real:** the Gateway and a Google Gemini fallback model accessed through an authenticated provider plugin.
- **Replayed:** the primary quota failure, using a loopback Google Generative Language API stub through OpenClaw’s Google transport, returning HTTP 429 with a `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` body.
- **Reported outcome:** manual `/compact` classifies the primary as `rate_limit`, reaches the real fallback, and saves one compaction entry with a 2,388-character summary (`tokensBefore: 26,322`). The report records one real model completion.
- **Controlled configuration:** quality guard and memory flush disabled, `keepRecentTokens: 1000`, and `contextInjection: "never"`; `compaction.model` unset. A prior stub-only dry run established one fallback summary request for this setup. Disabling context injection avoids the separately reported false split-turn defect in #194915; it is not part of this PR’s fix.

This session read the public report; it did not execute this live run or independently recount real provider calls. This adds reported live-fallback execution, not a live-primary quota-exhaustion test or a default-configuration live test. It supplements rather than replaces the earlier automatic/manual Gateway stub checks.



The `guard_blocked` diagnostic label remains unchanged, as expected for the separate #194759 diagnosis issue. This recovery PR does not claim to fix it.

Fork-based follow-up belongs to the requester’s agent. This session is preserving the upstream source branch and using PR metadata for coordination rather than pushing competing implementation changes.


Reported and coordinated by @saariuslystoned.

## Worked on by

- @saariuslystoned

## Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/016a6fd3-51e2-4037-9d73-09b75696bf5e)

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): report full CPU capture duration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A five-second diagnostic CPU capture can report a sub-millisecond `actualDurationMs` when the runtime supplies an incorrect native profile interval.

## User Impact

CPU capture results report the elapsed capture duration on every runtime. The native profile graph and timestamps remain unchanged; Bun's profile timeline still needs the upstream fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared capture owner already measures elapsed time with a monotonic clock, and heap captures already use that measurement. CPU results now use it too, from requesting native startup through completed stop, including startup blocking. This removes a second duration calculation without adding a runtime check or compatibility path.

The existing deterministic timing test covers startup, the requested wait, and stop completion. The existing real-runtime test now rejects a near-zero duration after its five-second capture. The graph-redaction test retains its graph and cleanup assertions without duplicating the timing assertion or its clock fixture. Scope: production +4/-3 lines, tests +3/-4, documentation +5/-0. No test allocation or ceiling increase is needed.

## Evidence

Removes the reported-duration dependency on https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/45035. It does **not** repair the native CPU-profile timeline addressed by that upstream PR.

Isolated macOS arm64 captures, each requesting 5,000 ms, used stock Bun `2596ac5d3`, the pinned Bun fork `191755ec1`, and Node `26.12.1`:

| Runtime | Before: reported duration | After: reported duration | After: native interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Stock Bun | 0.267 ms (fail) | 5004.412 ms (pass) | 0.766 ms |
| Pinned Bun fork | 5002.566 ms (pass) | 5002.770 ms (pass) | 5002.662 ms |
| Node | 5020.694 ms (pass) | 5025.140 ms (pass) | 5023.744 ms |

Before proof used the unchanged owner at `94d45c8`; the candidate is based on `e4f99f3`, whose intervening changes are outside this owner and its consumers. Each proof called the real `captureDiagnosticCpuProfile` with synthetic home, state, config, and temporary paths.

Formatting and targeted lint pass. Codex autoreview of the complete change from `e4f99f33726` to the tree committed as `5fd89a9d5f7` is scoped-clean through P2. The test-only simplification in `27b064c1fc8` is independently scoped-clean through P2. The reconstructed failed CI tree reproduced the test-line overage; repaired merge trees pass the unchanged guard against both the actual CI base and current main, with net test delta -1 and existing baseline debt still visible.

The original implementation passed all 39 CPU/worker-GC tests on each runtime; total wrapper times were 39.90 s on stock (28.03 s cold worker compilation), 12.44 s on the pinned fork, and 12.75 s on Node. The current-head timing and graph-cleanup tests pass two cases each on stock, the pinned fork, and Node, with wrapper times of 8.01 s, 35.65 s (cold worker compilation), and 6.57 s respectively. No new sampling wait was added.

One earlier narrowed invocation passed its assertions but exited with SIGTERM during final artifact verification. The cause of that interruption is unestablished and retained in local review evidence; subsequent focused invocations completed normally. Exact-head CI [42436049036](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42436049036) passed for `27b064c1fc8c3bd9f15130ccb8adac51e0176e85` (839 s wall time).

prs.body:
Depends on [#194814](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194814), including its [#194755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194755) dependency. [Changes after the reviewed dependency](https://github.com/dubr1k/openclaw/compare/c82b75dc1197a5fc43a97aea3d5f1b749afd9ca6...41995f7efadbf439ffae9bbd81399bb7a0e7ef81).

**Proposed budget exception, requiring upstream performance-owner acceptance before merge:** Chat boot gzip cap +64 B, 1,295,248 → 1,295,312 B. The [CI merge on upstream `636fc28d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42420001679/job/128546493664) measured 1,295,252 B at 20 requests, 4 B above the old cap, against a 1,295,153 B baseline. The proposal leaves 60 B headroom; other budgets stay unchanged. The [performance workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/636fc28d8bbd11a3ba91569b2bb250339fa21a45/.agents/skills/openclaw-performance/SKILL.md) requires the owner's explicit acceptance. This proposal does not claim that approval.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing first-folder creation and conversations appearing to disappear after moving them into a collapsed chat folder.

## User Impact

Users can create their first project folder from the agent chat toolbar and immediately see accepted menu, drag, or batch moves in the destination. Successful empty-folder creation also makes its grouped view visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep creation and moves with the organizer's existing scoped operations and lazy dialog loading. The toolbar uses the authoritative access check. Reveal a collapsed destination only after a current accepted move; a batch reveals it when at least one member succeeds. Rejected members retain their error feedback, and a fully rejected batch leaves the destination collapsed. Browser tests use the accessible button name; the existing 22px geometry, labels and permission checks remain intact.

## Evidence

- Functional UI head `f9b66066`: 14/14 bundled browser cases (5 creation, 5 physical-session menu/DnD/batch, 3 agent/owner scope, 1 retained-folder reload) and 184/184 tests across 11 affected owner/layout suites. Coverage includes pending admission, read-only denial, failed-save recovery, main/new agents, captured physical session identities, rejected/partial batches, and persistence after reload.
- UI and strict E2E types, lint, formatting, allocation and fresh independent integration review passed. All functional CI jobs also passed on the newer `636fc28d` merge graph; the 4 B size overage and its aggregate gates were its only failures.
- Proposal-only head `41995f7e` changes no UI/runtime source. Existing budget contracts pass 50/50 (21.45 s). Exact CI candidate/base replay reproduces the old 4 B violation and no violations with the proposed cap, asserting that Chat gzip is the sole changed budget. Targeted lint/format and fresh review pass.
- Current-head CI passed for `41995f7e` (57 successful checks; 41 intentionally skipped checks); performance-owner acceptance remains pending. Captures use synthetic sidebar data and a mocked Gateway. The retained creation captures originate from ancestor `de74d3ad`; final creation behavior is covered by the five final browser cases.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(slack): accept thread follow-ups before the first reply
prs.body:
Closes #139152.

## What Problem This Solves

A human adds an unmentioned clarification to an accepted Slack request while its first response is still running. The clarification is skipped because delivered-reply participation does not yet exist.

## User Impact

With thread participation enabled, accepted human work temporarily makes the same thread eligible for human follow-ups before the first visible reply. Eligibility ends with the existing publisher/queued-work lifetime; delivered participation is still persisted only after actual delivery.

This expands the documented activation contract for installations already using thread participation. **Maintainer acceptance of that policy remains required; no previously working release is claimed.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing active Slack publisher registry. Current main's extracted thread-mention owner resolves eligibility, preserving its bot-owned-thread policy, explicit mention settings, sender restrictions, and thread/account/monitor boundaries. Bot/control/abort inputs cannot open temporary human participation. No new store, scheduler, timeout, retry, or production runtime patch is introduced.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner. Existing in-flight human eligibility is carried into its inline conversation shape; retired context/authorization helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing thread-mention sibling. The shrink-only line-cap contract passes without an exception.

Removed the duplicate in-process scripted-agent pipeline and its helper (436 lines). The actual Gateway proves model/final delivery, focused prepare tests own policy/isolation, and existing dispatch tests now verify human eligibility through first-mode and queued settlement. Failure and cleanup coverage remains in the existing dispatch owner.

## Evidence

Candidate: `d8c6f0427d056988a288c34f63839db6c4e0aa02`; ordinary merge parents are the previous accepted head `637a18c3417d663940f2dda43f808adc1786f743` and fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa`.

- 106 focused preparation/dispatch owner tests pass on the integrated source.
- Canonical extension production types, changed-source and E2E lint/format, shrink-only line-cap, conflict/diff checks, and outgoing-diff secret scan pass.
- Fresh P0-P2 reviews cover the conflict integration and the subsequent cohesive mention-owner move; no actionable findings. The only later adjustment selects the existing exported nested SDK input type, validated by production types and typed lint.
- Exact-head [CI 39897146815](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39897146815) and `openclaw/ci-gate` pass. All 103 current checks are terminal with zero failures or pending checks. The corrected Evidence-heading check [39897416741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39897416741) passes; its earlier failed run remains historical. Previous-head CI below is historical evidence. No later-main freshness rebase is planned. No employee runtime or package distribution occurs.

## Earlier accepted evidence (previous head)

Candidate: 637a18c3417d663940f2dda43f808adc1786f743. Current-head hosted CI completed **SUCCESS**, with no nonpassing jobs: [run 39422440900](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39422440900).

- **100 focused owner tests pass** across existing dispatch and in-flight preparation suites. Coverage includes overlapping publishers, explicit opt-out, bot/control input, sender restrictions, thread/channel/account/monitor isolation, and the current `requireMentionInBotThreads: true` policy.
- **Actual isolated Gateway E2E passes:** signed HTTP Slack ingress; real Slack plugin, core/session processing and provider HTTP requests; the first model response held with zero visible posts; unmentioned human follow-up reaches the post-mention Slack thread-context HTTP read before that response is released; then two real model requests, two same-thread replies, and independent `conversations.replies` stored readback. All owned processes/services stop. The final rebuilt-head scenario body took about 19s (Vitest 46.14s); only this opt-in product E2E needs a complete Gateway. The ordinary owner suites take under five seconds of test time per file.
- The prior log-based preparation observation no longer exists on main. The updated proof uses current public Gateway sessions APIs and the external thread-context read. Focused before/after admission regression remains the defect-isolating proof; a baseline Gateway run is not claimed.
- Extension production/test types, focused E2E types/lint, scoped source lint/format, build, shrink-only line-cap gate, and fresh independent P0-P2 review pass. No accepted findings remain. Public diff secret scan is clean.

```sh
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/slack-inflight-gateway.e2e.test.ts
```

Inspectable value-free runtime verdict from this candidate:

```json
{
  "sourceHead": "637a18c3417d663940f2dda43f808adc1786f743",
  "actualChildGateway": true,
  "coreDispatchMocked": false,
  "rootHeldBeforeFollowup": true,
  "visiblePostsBeforeRelease": 0,
  "followupObservation": "post-mention thread-context HTTP read",
  "modelRequests": 2,
  "sameThreadReplies": 2,
  "storedReplyReadback": true,
  "cleanupComplete": true,
  "passed": true
}
```

Slack and model services are controlled HTTP simulations. This is an actual child Gateway test, not a live Slack workspace/provider run. No employee runtime, settings, credentials, or jobs were changed. The remaining decision is acceptance of the expanded in-flight human admission policy and normal maintainer adoption.

Closes #194842

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `swabble serve` replaces the user's config with defaults when the existing file fails to load (e.g. a JSON typo).

## User Impact

User impact: a broken config makes `serve` exit with the load error and leaves the file unchanged. A missing config still gets defaults written, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`serve` caught every load error and saved defaults over the file. It now only does that for `ConfigError.missingConfig`, and other errors propagate.

## Evidence

- New `CLIProcessTests.testServeLeavesUnreadableConfigUntouched` runs the real binary against a config missing its closing brace.
  - Without the fix it fails: the file is rewritten with `"command":""` (was `/usr/bin/say`).
  - With the fix: exit 1, file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `swift test --package-path apps/swabble`: 13 passed, 0 failed (macOS 26, Swift 6.4.2).
- `apps/swabble/scripts/lint.sh` (SwiftLint strict): 0 violations. SwiftFormat lint: clean.
