prs.title: fix(buzz): agents answer without the message a room reply points at
prs.body:
Closes #137651

<sub>Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the production proof below was run and verified by hand.</sub>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who reply to a message in a Buzz room and mention an
agent would get an answer with no referent. The agent receives the reply text
alone — "@bot what do you think?" — and then asks what you mean, or answers from
unrelated room chatter. The only workaround is to restate the quoted message by
hand inside every reply.

It is worst when the reply targets a message the agent never received: an older
message, or one posted before the agent joined the room. `historyLimit` does not
cover that case — that window holds recent messages the agent saw, not the
specific event a reply names.

## Why This Change Was Made

Buzz already parsed the NIP-10 `reply` marker into `replyToId`, and OpenClaw's
shared inbound context has carried the slot for this since before the Buzz
plugin existed: `supplemental.quote` becomes `ReplyToBody`/`ReplyToSender`, and
telegram, feishu, googlechat and signal all fill it. Buzz passed no
`supplemental` at all. This resolves the parent event through the bus and
projects it through that same shared quote context, so there is no new config
surface and no Buzz-specific prompt shape.

The issue asked for a maintainer decision first, because filling the quote for a
parent the bot never received needs a per-turn relay lookup, and Buzz
deliberately avoids per-message queries. The review's recommendation was to
extend the Buzz relay lifecycle owner with validated bounded cancellation, then
retrieve only the reply target and project it through shared quote context. That
is what this implements:

- The lookup reuses `queryBuzzRelaySnapshot` with a new
  `closeSubscriptionOnTimeout` option, so a silent relay drops only this
  subscription and never the account relay every room shares. The existing
  default — recycle the relay on timeout — is untouched for background paging.
- That close keeps the existing lifecycle invariant. `relay.send` is deliberately
  unawaited, so a CLOSE could otherwise overtake an asynchronously registered REQ
  and orphan it server-side; the subscription handle now carries the send promise
  and the timeout path waits for the REQ frame to leave the client first.
- `Subscription.close()` decrements `ongoingOperations`, so the helper now closes
  each subscription exactly once; a late EOSE after a timeout cannot
  double-decrement.
- Bounded to 2s and fail-soft. A missing, unreachable, or cross-room parent
  degrades the turn to a quote-less prompt rather than dropping the message.
- Quote context follows `contextVisibility`. Under `allowlist` a quoted message
  is withheld unless its author passes the room's `groupAllowFrom`;
  `allowlist_quote` keeps it. The judgment is on the quoted author alone, as the
  shared policy defines it — neither the bot nor the current sender is exempt,
  so `allowlist` means the same thing on Buzz as on every other channel.
- Every transient relay query — profile, room-directory, membership, history
  paging and reply targets — takes one slot from a single per-relay lease, sized
  to the same reserve the room budget already sets aside, so the configured-room
  limit stays where it is and the two numbers cannot drift. Callers in front of
  an agent turn take the slot without waiting and degrade to a quote-less turn;
  background queries queue for the next free slot. A timed-out query keeps its
  slot until its deferred close has actually run, so a replacement can never
  overlap a subscription that is still open. A freed slot is transferred to the
  head of the queue rather than released and re-acquired, so the count never
  dips while a hand-off is in flight; and a queued caller whose signal aborts is
  dropped from the queue and rejected without ever reaching the relay.
- A reply marker is attacker-controlled free text, so it is only looked up when
  it is shaped like an event id. The room-scope guard normalizes both sides
  before comparing, so a parent whose `h` tag differs only in hex case is still
  recognized as the same room.
- `ReplyToId` now names the parent rather than the incoming message, matching
  telegram. The prompt renders it beside the quote's sender and body, so the two
  must agree; Buzz delivery anchors replies through its own `replyTarget`.
- The quoted author must still be a current room member, matching
  `snapshotBuzzPendingHistory`.
- Cancellation surfaces through the caller's `assertCurrent()` after the await,
  so a shutdown mid-lookup releases the dedupe claim instead of committing a
  message that was never answered.

Non-goals: where the agent's own answer is posted does not change — delivery
keeps using the `replyTarget` Buzz already built from the incoming message; no
media or attachment context is carried from the parent; the history window is
unchanged; Buzz DMs are unaffected, since they cannot be wired to a bot.

The decision on whether Buzz should do a per-turn lookup at all is still yours.
This PR is the implementation of the recommended option with the relay-lifecycle
contract resolved, not a claim that the decision is settled.

## User Impact

Reply to any message in a Buzz room and mention an agent: the agent now sees the
message you replied to and answers about it, including a parent it never received
and one posted before it joined the room.

Operators who restrict rooms with `groupPolicy: allowlist` can gate quoted
context with `channels.buzz.contextVisibility` (`all`, `allowlist`,
`allowlist_quote`) — the same knob telegram uses, resolvable per account or from
`channels.defaults.contextVisibility`. Existing installs see no change beyond the
quote arriving: the default stays `all`, matching every other channel.

## Evidence

### Real-behavior proof (self-hosted relay, live agent)

Built this branch, installed it over a running gateway, and ran a test shaped so
the agent could not know the answer any other way.

1. Room with `requireMention: true` and `historyLimit` unset. A message with no
   mention therefore never reaches the agent — no turn, no history entry.
2. Posted **without a mention**: `창고 점검 메모. 봉인 번호는 ZEBRA-4471-QUARTZ 이다.`
   ("Storage check memo. Seal number is ZEBRA-4471-QUARTZ.")
3. Confirmed the agent had not received it: 0 replies in the room, 0 transcript
   rows matching the token.
4. Replied to that message **with a mention**: quote the seal number from the
   message I replied to; if it is not in your context, say so and do not guess.
5. The agent answered:

```
ZEBRA-4471-QUARTZ
답글 대상 메시지가 컨텍스트에 들어와 있다 —
「창고 점검 메모. 봉인 번호는 ZEBRA-4471-QUARTZ 이다. 회신 필요 없음.」
```

("the replied-to message is in my context —") quoting the parent verbatim. The
token had no other path into the prompt.

A second, independent signal — the same question in the same room, before and
after, measured by the gateway's tool-call audit log:

| | agent tool calls | answer |
|---|---|---|
| before the fix | `Bash` ×2 (queried the relay's Postgres by hand) | correct |
| after the fix | 0 | correct, and reported the quote was present |

Before the fix the agent had to go dig for the parent; after it answered from the
prompt.

### Focused tests

`pnpm test:extension buzz` — 36 files, 355 tests, all pass. New tests cover
quote delivery, top-level messages, cross-room reply tags, hex-case room tags,
malformed reply markers, unreachable parents, cancellation, non-member authors,
all three `contextVisibility` modes, the reply-target id, the shared query lease
(allowance, atomic hand-off against a racing no-wait caller, double release,
per-relay isolation, an aborted waiter dropped from the queue, a slot returned
when its waiter was cancelled in the same turn, and a reply lookup refused while
background queries hold the reserve), the delayed-registration close ordering,
the slot being held through a deferred close under saturation, a queued query
rejected on cancellation before any relay I/O, and the config schema.

Red/green — reverting only
`supplemental: replyQuote ? { quote: replyQuote } : undefined` fails every
assertion that expects a quote and leaves all nine guard tests green
(5 failed | 9 passed):

```
× passes the replied-to message to the agent as quote context
    -   "ReplyToBody": "The deploy script takes 12 minutes.",
× points the reply-target id at the parent, not the incoming message
    -   "ReplyToBody": "parent body",
× keeps an allowlisted author's message as quote context under allowlist visibility
    AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'Deploy done.'
× keeps another member's message under allowlist_quote visibility
    AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'quoted anyway'
× accepts a parent whose room tag differs only in hex case
    AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'same room, different case'
✓ omits quote context for a top-level message
✓ keeps the anchor on the incoming message for a top-level message
✓ ignores a reply tag that names an event in another room
✓ never sends a malformed reply marker to the relay
✓ still dispatches when the reply target cannot be fetched
✓ surfaces cancellation from the lookup instead of dispatching
✓ omits quote context when the quoted author is no longer a room member
✓ withholds another member's message under allowlist visibility
✓ withholds the bot's own message under allowlist visibility when it is not allowlisted
```

Each of the other production lines was checked the same way and fails only its
own test: `contextVisibility` on the dispatch, the post-await `assertCurrent()`,
the `senderAllowed` field, the parent id on `reply.replyToId`, the marker shape
check, the normalized room comparison, the concurrency cap, and
`closeSubscription()` on timeout.

### Gates

`pnpm build`, `pnpm check` (typecheck, lint, format, generated-output ratchets)
and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all pass. `pnpm config:channels:gen` output is
committed, so the Control UI validates `channels.buzz.contextVisibility` against
the same schema the docs describe.

`pnpm test` has failures on this checkout that are unrelated to Buzz — control-ui
chromium suites, `src/gateway/client.test.ts`, tui scopes, and tooling-docker.
`src/gateway/client.test.ts` fails identically at `origin/main` (98 failed /
4 passed), so they do not come from this change. No Buzz test fails.

`.agents/skills/autoreview` could not run in this environment (`codex` and
TruffleHog are not installed); an independent local review was run instead. It
found two CI-red issues and four defects, all fixed before this PR was opened: a
mock bus missing the new `BuzzBus` member, the stale generated channel metadata,
`quote.id` being silently dropped so the reply-target record mixed the incoming
message's id with the parent's body, the raw `h`-tag room comparison, the
unvalidated marker reaching the relay, and a subscription-budget overflow.

### Review follow-up

The three findings on the first push are addressed in `a66fbdee`:

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| **P1** Preserve the real-EOSE close invariant | The timeout waits for the REQ frame to leave the client before closing, with a delayed-registration regression that holds `send` pending and asserts no CLOSE until it settles. |
| **P2** Coordinate reply lookups with all reserved relay queries | One per-relay lease now gates every transient query, sized to the room budget's reserve so they cannot drift. Covered by an interleaving test where background queries hold the reserve and a reply lookup is refused. |
| **P3** Add Buzz to the supplemental-context channel inventory | Buzz added to the exhaustive channel list in the shared groups guide. |

The CI failures came from the generated config doc baseline, which the channel
surface change grows from 3706 to 3708; `pnpm config:docs:gen` output is
committed and `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` pass.
Thanks to @kaxo-io for pinpointing that.

### Second review follow-up

The P1 from the second review is fixed in `446802a`, and the branch is rebased
onto current `main` so the conflict is gone.

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| **P1** Retain the lease until delayed timeout cleanup finishes | Correct, and it was a real gap between the two earlier fixes: a timeout rejected the snapshot, so the `finally` returned the slot while the subscription stayed open until its REQ frame landed. The deferred cleanup is now carried back to the lease holder, which releases only after the close has run. The saturation regression holds `send` pending, fills the remaining slots, and asserts the timed-out query keeps its slot until the frame lands. |
| Merge conflict | Rebased onto `main` (351 commits ahead of the previous base). The only conflicts were the two generated config baselines; both were regenerated on top of `main` and `pnpm config:docs:check` passes. |

On the note about verifying the deferred cleanup against nostr-tools: the
behavior this relies on is that `Subscription.close()` sends `CLOSE` and
decrements `ongoingOperations` unconditionally, and that `relay.send` is the only
path that registers the `REQ`. Both are in
`nostr-tools@2.25.0/lib/esm/abstract-relay.js` (`close()` at the subscription
class; `ongoingOperations` incremented on subscribe and decremented in
`close()`). The regression tests model the orderings that follow from it —
timeout before send settles, late EOSE after a timeout, and REQ send failure.

### Third review follow-up

All three P1s from the third review are fixed.

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| **P1** Reserve the slot before waking a queued query | Correct. `release()` decremented `active` and then woke the waiter, and the waiter incremented only after resuming — a no-wait caller could take the apparent vacancy in between, for four subscriptions against a three-slot reserve. The slot is now transferred: `release()` hands it to the head of the queue without touching `active`, and the waiter inherits it. The regression releases and, in the same tick, races a no-wait acquire, which must be refused. |
| **P1** Reject cancellation after waiting for a query lease | Correct. The lease wait is now abort-aware: an already-aborted caller is refused up front, a waiter whose signal aborts is removed from the queue and rejected with the reason, and a waiter woken and cancelled in the same turn returns the slot immediately. `queryBuzzRelaySnapshot` passes its signal through and surfaces the abort as its own, so a cancelled background query never reaches relay I/O. Covered at both the lease and the snapshot layer. |
| **P1 / security** Keep allowlist visibility tied to the quoted author | Correct, and I was wrong to add the exemption. Treating the bot's own and the current sender's own messages as allowed changed what `allowlist` means on one channel. The exemption is removed; the quoted author is judged by the shared policy alone. The former test that expected the bot's quote to survive `allowlist` now expects it to be withheld, and a new test covers an allowlisted author's quote surviving. Docs updated to match. |

The remaining blocker is the Buzz owner decision on the per-turn lookup and the
`contextVisibility` override, which is not mine to resolve.


### Fourth review follow-up

The one P1 from the fourth review is fixed.

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| **P1** Make timeout and send-failure closure share one owner | Correct, and reachable. A timeout that fired while `relay.send()` was still pending deferred its cleanup onto `requestSent`; a later send rejection closed the subscription from its own handler, and the deferred cleanup then closed it again because each path consulted only its own guard. The handle now owns closing: both paths go through `closeOnce()`, which closes at most once. The surviving `openSubs` check stays on the send-rejection path, where it answers a different question — see the contract notes below. New regression covers the missing sequence (timeout, then delayed send rejection); removing the idempotence guard fails that test alone, with two close calls where one is expected. |

### Fifth review follow-up — nostr-tools 2.25.0 contract

The fifth review could not inspect the package source and left two items open on
that basis. Here is what 2.25.0 actually does, from the installed package
(`nostr-tools/lib/cjs/relay.js`; the esm build is the same code).

**`Subscription.close()` is not idempotent.** Only the CLOSE frame is guarded:

```js
close(reason = "closed by caller") {
  if (!this.closed && this.relay.connected) { /* send CLOSE */ this.closed = true; }
  this.relay.openSubs.delete(this.id);
  if (!this.id.startsWith("<forced-ping>")) {
    this.relay.ongoingOperations--;
    if (this.relay.ongoingOperations === 0) { this.relay.idleSince = Date.now(); this.relay.scheduleIdleClose(); }
  }
  this.onclose?.(reason);
}
```

So a second call does decrement `ongoingOperations` again. That is the concrete
consequence the review flagged as unverified: the count then reports less work
in flight than the relay really has, and `scheduleIdleClose()` can tear down a
connection every room shares. This is why the fix routes both paths through one
closer rather than making each guard tighter.

**Why the send-rejection path still checks `openSubs`.** There are two teardown
orders, and only one of them sets `closed`:

| Path | Order | `sub.closed` after |
|---|---|---|
| `Relay.close()` | `closeAllSubscriptions()` runs, then `_connected = false` | `true` — the CLOSE frame was still sendable |
| socket drop | `_connected = false` runs, then `closeAllSubscriptions()` | `false` — but `openSubs` was cleared and the count already adjusted |

A send rejection arriving after a socket drop therefore cannot rely on `closed`;
the missing `openSubs` entry is the only evidence that teardown already ran. The
existing "sending fails after relay shutdown" test covers exactly that.

**Reply-target integrity is enforced before Buzz sees the event.** A relay
dispatches to a subscription only when both hold:

```js
if (matchFilters(so.filters, event) && this.verifyEvent(event, this.url)) { /* deliver */ }
```

and `verifyEvent` recomputes the event hash, compares it against `id`, then
schnorr-verifies `sig` against `pubkey` — returning false on any mismatch or
throw. The concrete `Relay` constructor installs that verifier, and Buzz builds
every relay through it (`new Relay(url, { enableReconnect: false })` in
`extensions/buzz/src/relay-auth.ts`), never overriding `verifyEvent`.

So the id comparison in `reply-context.ts` was never the integrity check — the
comment there said "the relay is untrusted", which is what made it read like
one. It is a relevance check: a relay may also answer with events it holds that
the reply tag never named, and only the named one may reach the model.

### Sixth review follow-up — local verification added

The sixth review kept the integrity item open on the same basis: it cannot read
the dependency, so the contract above stays a contributor claim. Rather than
argue it, the lookup now verifies locally. `queryBuzzEventById` accepts an event
only when the id matches **and** `verifyEvent(event)` holds, so the guarantee is
visible in the code that relies on it.

This is close to free. `verifyEvent` caches its verdict on the event object, so
an event the relay already admitted returns the cached result. That holds because
both `Relay` and `verifyEvent` come from the root `nostr-tools` entry — one
bundle, one cache symbol; importing them from split subpaths would defeat the
cache, and nothing in Buzz does.

The test fixture that fed the lookup unsigned events (`sig: ""`) now signs them
with `finalizeEvent`. A new regression hands the lookup an event with the right
id and the right signature but different content — the forgery only verification
can separate from the real parent — and expects `null`. Removing the
`verifyEvent` call fails that test alone.

One honest note on the fourth-round P1: in 2.25.0, `Relay.send()` settles within
a tick (it does not await the socket write), so the timeout-then-delayed-
rejection window is a contract matter rather than something that fires today.
The fix does not depend on that detail and is right either way.

### Seventh review follow-up — passive history ordering

The seventh review's finding is correct, and it was reachable. Fixed in `5ca1df6`.

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| **P2 / security** Build passive history after the reply lookup | Correct. `snapshotBuzzPendingHistory` rendered the history window before the lookup awaited the relay, freezing a roster the lookup then outlived. `assertCurrent()` re-checks this turn's sender alone, so an author removed while the lookup was pending kept contributing already-rendered text to the prompt, past the membership filter the snapshot itself applies. The snapshot now runs after the lookup and the liveness check; its inputs are unchanged, and only the roster it reads is current. |

Reproduced before fixing. Holding `fetchMessageById` open, removing a peer from
the room while it is pending, then resolving it puts the removed author's text
in `BodyForAgent`:

```
[Chat messages since your last reply - for context]
cccccccc...cccccc: said while still a member

[Current message - respond to this]
@bot what do you think?
```

Red/green — reverting only the ordering in `inbound.ts` and keeping the test
fails that assertion alone:

```
x drops a member removed while the reply lookup was pending from passive history
    AssertionError: expected '[Chat messages since your last reply ...' not to contain 'said while still a member'
```

Scope: the window is `historyLimit > 0` (unset by default, so installs that
never set it were not exposed), a reply that triggers the lookup, and a roster
change while that lookup is in flight.

A cancelled turn is better off too. `snapshotBuzzPendingHistory` mutates
`historyMap`, so before this change an `assertCurrent()` that threw left the
window already trimmed; on that path the snapshot no longer runs at all.

`pnpm test:extension buzz` — 36 files, 358 tests, all pass, plus `pnpm build`,
`pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm check:test-types`. The built
`dist/extensions/buzz` bundle carries the new ordering, so this is the code the
gateway actually loads.

`.agents/skills/autoreview` runs in this environment now (TruffleHog installed;
`--engine claude`, since `codex` still is not available). It reports no accepted
or actionable findings on this change.

### Eighth review follow-up — post-lease cancellation, and the rebase

Both actionable items are fixed. Head is `024eb99`, rebased onto current `main`.

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| **P2** Recheck cancellation after acquiring the query lease | Correct. `acquireBuzzQueryLease` finishes its abort checks synchronously when a slot is free, but awaiting its resolved promise still yields, and a caller that aborted in that gap reached `runBuzzRelaySnapshot` and opened a REQ anyway. Since `profile.ts` and `room-discovery.ts` pass no `checkAbortAfterSubscribe`, they then waited for EOSE or the timeout. The signal is now re-checked inside the `try`, before the snapshot starts, so `finally` still returns the slot. |
| Merge conflicts | Rebased onto `main` (291 commits ahead of the previous base). The only conflicts were the three generated config baselines; regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` and `pnpm config:channels:gen` (channel count back to 3708), and `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm plugins:inventory:check` pass. GitHub now reports the branch as mergeable. |

Two regressions, both requested and both red without the fix — each one times
out instead of aborting:

```
x rejects a query cancelled after a free slot was granted
x rejects a query cancelled between the slot hand-off and the subscription
    AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error including 'gateway shutting down' but got 'timed out'
```

The first also asserts the slot comes back, by re-acquiring the full allowance
afterwards; without that, the reserve would leak one slot per cancelled turn.
The second deliberately lets the lease's own post-wake abort check pass first,
so it lands in the caller's gap rather than in the path already covered by
"returns a slot handed to a waiter that was cancelled in the same turn".

One existing test needed a timing change: "defers query cleanup until the relay
confirms EOSE" cancelled before its subscription opened, which now aborts early
by design. It waits for the subscription first, so it still covers what it was
written for — cleanup deferred to EOSE for an already-open request.

`pnpm test:extension buzz` — 36 files, 360 tests, all pass on the new base, with
`pnpm build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm check:test-types`.
`.agents/skills/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` reports no accepted
or actionable findings across both review passes.

The remaining blocker is unchanged and is not mine to resolve: the Buzz owner
decision on the per-turn lookup and the `contextVisibility` override.

prs.title: feat(telegram): roll Telegram's native dice from the message tool
prs.body:
Closes #137110

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw bot cannot take part in a Telegram dice roll. Sending 🎲 as text posts a static
emoji: no animation, no roll, no value. Telegram's `sendDice` is the only way for a bot to
trigger the real thing, and it was unreachable — the message tool exposed no action for it.

The distinction matters because Telegram picks the outcome server-side. Nobody in the chat,
agent or operator, can influence or fake it, so a roll everyone watches land is credible in a
way a number the agent typed is not.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dice` joins the core action vocabulary with target mode `to` and no conversation read — it
is an outbound send to an explicit target. That vocabulary is closed by design ("Plugins add
names through a core PR; runtime registration is intentionally unsupported",
`src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), so a third-party plugin cannot add this and
the core entry is the intended path.

Scoped tool schemas prune parameters the selected actions do not use and merge the surviving
groups into one flat object. Dice therefore gets its own `diceEmoji` key rather than reusing
the reaction group's `emoji`: sharing that name would retitle the reaction parameter for
`react` whenever both actions are enabled. The group is also part of the full schema, so the
six faces are advertised in both scoped and unscoped tool surfaces.

The Telegram runtime wraps `sendDice` and returns `messageId`, `chatId`, `emoji` and the
rolled `value` in the same tool result, so the agent learns the outcome without a second
round-trip. Input is validated against Telegram's documented allowlist before the API call,
after stripping the emoji presentation selector (⚽️ vs ⚽) the same way the plugin's reaction
path does — that form is what most keyboards and models emit.

No new configuration key. Dice rides the existing `sendMessage` gate: permission to post in a
chat already governs it, and a roll is an ordinary outbound message to a chat the bot may
already post in, so a dedicated toggle would guard nothing. `sticker` is gated because it also
enables `sticker-search`, which reads external sticker packs; dice has no such surface, which
puts it with `edit`, `delete`, `reactions` and `topic-create` — all enabled without a toggle.
Disabling `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage` withdraws dice too, and a test asserts that.

Accepted tradeoff: the returned `emoji` echoes the validated request rather than
`result.dice.emoji`. Telegram's contract returns the requested face, and reading it back
would add a branch for a state the API does not produce; the rolled `value`, which the API
alone decides, is read from the response.

Inbound dice are a separate defect and ship in their own PR (#137112); this one is outbound
only.

Opened so the product decision on #137110 has a concrete diff to judge rather than a
description. The gate shape here follows the recommendation in that issue's review — dice under
the existing send gate, no new configuration key. If maintainers decide against the capability,
closing this costs nothing.
`sticker` and `poll` have `openclaw message` subcommands and `dice` does not; CLI parity
is a small follow-up rather than part of this change, since most action names have no
subcommand either.

## User Impact

Telegram operators can have their agent roll Telegram's native animated dice — 🎲 🎯 🏀 ⚽ 🎳 🎰 —
and act on the result in the same turn, with no configuration to discover or enable. Operators
who have disabled Telegram sending are unaffected: dice is withdrawn along with `send`.

## Evidence

- **Live**: run on a live gateway against a real Telegram bot.
  `{"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲"}` returned
  `{"ok":true,"messageId":"944","emoji":"🎲","value":6}`, a real animated roll landed in the
  chat, and the agent reported the value in the same turn with no chat re-read between the
  call and the reply. The model picked the `diceEmoji` key unprompted, from the schema
  description alone. That run predates the gate change below; the send-gate coupling is
  covered by a test rather than by that session.
- **Live**: ⚽ with the presentation selector (`U+26BD U+FE0F`) was accepted and reached
  `sendDice` as the bare face, returning `{"emoji":"⚽","value":1}`. That form was rejected
  before this change.
- **Live**: the stale-key case behaves as documented — `{"action":"dice","emoji":"🎯"}` with
  no `diceEmoji` rolls 🎲, since `emoji` remains a legal key belonging to reactions in the
  same flattened object. This is why the separate key is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
- **Live, earlier revision**: an earlier form of this action ran for a week on a live
  instance before the rename and the selector handling.
- `pnpm check:changed` — exit 0 (oxlint 0 errors, `tsgo:all`, assertion/max-lines ratchets,
  Knip dead-export scan, import cycles, plugin boundaries, generated-metadata check).
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — exit 0.
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels` — 13 files, 32 tests passed.
- Focused: dice send tests (default face, all six faces, presentation selector, rejection
  before the API call, missing dice payload) and schema-scoping tests, including a regression
  test that `emoji` keeps its reaction description when `react` and `dice` are both in scope.
- Gate coupling: `ties dice availability to the send gate` asserts dice is offered under an
  ordinary config and withdrawn when `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage` is `false`.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — exit 0 as its own job, confirming the generated bundled
  channel metadata matches the schemas now that no dice key exists.
- `autoreview` (skill) — `scoped-clean`, no accepted findings.

Note on the telegram lane: three cases in `bot/body-helpers.inbound.test.ts` (inline-code
whitespace normalization) fail on this branch, and they fail identically on a clean
`upstream/main` checkout with the file byte-identical to upstream. They are unrelated to dice —
not Node-version specific (same on 24.20.0 and 26.8.1) and not locale specific (same under
`C.UTF-8`). Nothing in this PR touches that file or its subject.




## v2

Rebased onto current `main` first: `annotateSourceDelivery` was refactored there after the
review, which absorbed part of the second repair and made the rest smaller.

- `dice` is declared `GUARDED_ACTION` in `CHANNEL_MESSAGE_ACTION_DEFINITIONS`
  (`src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), so a roll addressed by `to` clears the same
  cross-context check as every other recipient-visible send. As a plain targeted action it
  carried no `crossContext` fact, and the guard returns early for such actions, which is why the
  gap was silent rather than a build error. Deliberately not `"marker"`: that decoration writes
  into `params.message`, which dice never sends.
- A successful roll now sets `messageToolOnlySourceReplyDelivered`. The fact was neither
  produced nor trusted, so the repair has two halves:
  - Produced: `source-reply-mirror.ts` carried the "which actions address their conversation by
    target" rule twice — once inside `isCurrentSourceConversation`, once in the `default` arm of
    `isDeliveredCurrentSourceReply`, where it compared `params.action` raw while the switch head
    compared it normalized. Both now read one `TARGET_ADDRESSED_ACTION_NAMES` set that includes
    `dice`, since a roll addresses its conversation by target exactly like a send. Net zero
    production lines in that file (+11/-11), one duplicate policy gone. Transcript mirroring
    shares the predicate and needs no second gate: a roll carries no text or media, so it drops
    out on the existing empty-payload check.
  - Trusted: `isDeliveredMessageToolOnlySourceReplyResult`
    (`src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.ts`) re-derived eligibility from an
    action-name list (`["reply", "thread-reply", "poll"]` plus the send names) even when the
    producer had already recorded the route, so it still rejected dice after the marking landed.
    It now reads the recorded fact. This is more permissive in exactly one direction: a result
    the producer stamped `current-source` is trusted regardless of action name, and only results
    that passed the target comparison carry that stamp — nothing that did not deliver visible
    content to this conversation can reach it. The `allowExplicitSourceRoute` path, where no such
    stamp exists, still requires the name list.
- Mirrorable payload eligibility is now separate from current-source delivery classification.
  The message tool's argument object is flat, so `{action: "dice", message: "You rolled a six"}`
  passes validation; Telegram ignores `message`, but `mirrorDeliveredSourceReplyToTranscript`
  reads text and media straight out of `actionParams` and would have recorded assistant text no
  recipient ever saw. A `MIRRORABLE_SOURCE_ACTION_NAMES` set (currently `send` alone) gates the
  mirror, while `TARGET_ADDRESSED_ACTION_NAMES` keeps covering delivery classification. The same
  hole already existed for `poll` — its params can carry `message` too — so the regressions cover
  dice text, dice media and poll text; all three fail without the gate.
  Both halves are in core rather than in `extensions/telegram/src/channel-actions.ts` where the
  finding was reported: a channel plugin cannot classify itself into a core delivery decision,
  and the classification has to hold for any channel that grows an equivalent send.
- `silent` is read in the dice handler and forwarded to `sendDiceTelegram`, matching the schema
  the action already advertises.

Named follow-up, not changed here: `sticker` is likewise absent from `MESSAGE_TOOL_SEND_ACTIONS`
and the reply-name list, so it does not set `messageToolOnlySourceReplyDelivered` either. Whether
that is the same gap or deliberate — a sticker may not answer the question, so the fallback reply
is wanted — is a product call this PR does not make. Stickers behave exactly as before.

### Dependency contract

The review recorded that it could not inspect the `sendDice` contract (dependency sources absent,
DNS blocked). From the installed tree:

- `grammy@1.46.0`, `node_modules/grammy/out/core/api.d.ts:470` —
  `sendDice(chat_id: number | string, emoji: … | "🎲" | "🎯" | "🏀" | "⚽" | "🎳" | "🎰", other?, signal?): Promise<Message.DiceMessage>`.
- `@grammyjs/types@5.0.0`, `methods.d.ts:927-935` — payload is `chat_id`, `message_thread_id?`,
  `emoji?` restricted to the same six faces, and `disable_notification?`, which is what `silent`
  maps to. This is the upstream source of both the allowlist and the silent option.
- `@grammyjs/types@5.0.0`, `message.d.ts:878-883` — `Dice` is `{ emoji: string; value: number }`,
  with value ranges documented as 1-6 for 🎲 🎯 🎳, 1-5 for 🏀 ⚽ and 1-64 for 🎰. The roll is
  server-decided, which is why `value` is read from the response while `emoji` echoes the
  validated request.

### v2 evidence

- Regressions, each verified by reverting its own fix and rerunning:
  - cross-context denial for `dice` (`src/infra/outbound/outbound-policy.test.ts`) — without the
    policy entry: `expected [Function run] to throw an error`.
  - current-source marking for a target-addressed send
    (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.reply-action.test.ts`, plus the negative case
    for another conversation) — without the set entry:
    `expected { ok: true, …(2) } to match object { sourceReplyRoute: 'current-source' }`.
  - the classifier accepting a recorded route it does not enumerate by name
    (`src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts`, plus the unconfirmed negative)
    — without the fix: `expected false to be true`.
  - `silent` forwarded to `sendDiceTelegram` (`extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts`)
    — without the fix: `expected undefined to be true`.
- `pnpm check:changed` — exit 0.
- `pnpm tsgo` — exit 0.
- Vitest over `src/infra/outbound`, `src/agents/tools`, both source-reply suites,
  `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` and `extensions/telegram` — the only failures are
  the three pre-existing `body-helpers.inbound.test.ts` whitespace cases noted above. Both that
  test and the module it covers are byte-identical to `upstream/main` on this branch.
- `autoreview` (skill) — `scoped-clean`, no accepted findings.

Repair commit alone: production +20/-9 (net +11), tests and test support +114/-3. The
`source-reply-mirror.ts` half is net-neutral (+11/-7 replacing a duplicated action list with one
set). Whole branch versus `main`: production +285/-62, tests +185/-3, docs +16/-1.

Test-line budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-dice-action.txt` allocates the
branch's net +182 test lines. They hold the contracts no cheaper layer proves: the dice
authority gates, silent and topic delivery at the Telegram sender, cross-context and delivery
classification in outbound policy, and source-reply ownership in the agent.

The branch is a linear series of six commits on current `main`, with no merge commits.

### Live proof

Captured against a real Telegram bot on `dfa0fb6`, an earlier head of this branch. Later
revisions rebased and compressed it without changing the behaviour on the proven paths. The run used a gateway built from this
branch, agent model `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`. Chat identifiers are redacted as `<chat-a>` (the
conversation the run is bound to) and `<chat-b>` (a different configured chat).

**Cross-context egress.** With `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider: false`, a
direct message-tool call from the session bound to `<chat-a>`:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","target":"telegram:<chat-b>","diceEmoji":"🎲"}
toolResult Cross-context messaging denied: action=dice target="telegram:<chat-b>"
           while bound to "telegram:<chat-a>" (channel=telegram).
```

Nothing reached `<chat-b>`. Before this change `dice` carried no `crossContext` fact, so the
guard returned before it ever compared targets.

**Terminal delivery.** With `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, a roll in the bound
conversation:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲","final":true}
toolResult {"ok":true,"messageId":"…","emoji":"🎲","value":4,
            "sourceReplyRoute":"current-source"}
```

`sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"` is the marking this PR adds; the operator observed
exactly one message in the chat — the animated roll — with no fallback text after it.

**Silent.** The call carried the option and the roll was delivered:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲","silent":true}
```

The forwarding is covered by the sender-boundary regression above and by
`extensions/telegram/src/send-special.ts:183`, which maps `silent` to the
`disable_notification` field `@grammyjs/types` declares for `sendDice`.

**Forum-topic roll.** Captured on the current head `6b6731dd31c` with a Gateway built from
this branch in an isolated state directory, agent model `litellm/deepseek-v4-flash`, and
`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`. `<forum>` is a forum supergroup; the
request was a user message in its topic 14 that mentioned the bot and asked for a roll there.

```
session    agent:main:telegram:group:<forum>:topic:14
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲"}
toolResult {"ok":true,"messageId":"727","chatId":"<forum>","emoji":"🎲","value":5,
            "receipt":{"threadId":"14"},"sourceReplyRoute":"current-source"}
delivery   {"createdThreadIds":["14"],"status":"settled","sourceReplyDelivered":true}
```

The call named no target or thread: the roll landed in the topic the request came from, and
the receipt in the result reports that topic. The tool result ended the turn (`terminate: true`,
stop reason `toolUse`); the model was not called again, no assistant text was produced, and the
Gateway sent nothing after the roll. The operator observed the animated die, face 5, in topic 14
with no message after it.

Follow-up, not changed here: the trajectory recorder labels this turn
`non_deliverable_terminal_turn` (`status: error`). `finalizeEmbeddedAttempt` in
`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.ts` counts a tool-use turn as delivered
only through `messagingToolSent*` evidence, which neither `poll` nor `dice` records. The runtime
terminal check, `hasAttemptTerminalState` in `attempt-terminal-evidence.ts`, also accepts
`didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool`; delivery and fallback follow that check, so only the
trajectory label is affected. A turn that ends with `poll` takes the same path.

An earlier attempt at the cross-context case did not exercise the guard: the model routed
around it with `sessions_send`, asking the session already bound to `<chat-b>` to roll in its
own conversation, where no cross-context target exists. The proof above is the direct call.

prs.title: fix(exa): year freshness skips Feb 28 when searching on Feb 29
prs.body:
Closes #194844

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Exa `web_search` with `freshness: "year"` on Feb 29 starts the window at Mar 1 of the previous year, so Feb 28 results are dropped.

## User Impact

User impact: the year window now starts on Feb 28 of the previous year, matching how `freshness: "month"` already handles short months.

## Why This Change Was Made

The year branch used `setUTCFullYear(year - 1)`, which rolls Feb 29 forward. The existing month clamping moved into a small helper, and both month and year use it (1 and 12 months).

## Evidence

- New `it.each` test pins the clock with fake timers.
  - Year on 2028-02-29 expects 2027-02-28. It fails on main with `2027-03-01`.
  - Month on 2026-03-31 expects 2026-02-28. It already passes and guards the refactor.
- `pnpm test extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.test.ts`: 20 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed. oxfmt and oxlint on both changed files: clean.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare completed runs using captured conditions
prs.body:
Closes #138134.

## What Problem This Solves

QA runs with matching scenario names can still use different task contents, source revisions, or runner settings. Comparing their results without checking those conditions can be misleading.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `qa parity-report --cross-harness` using identities captured by the existing flow-suite runner and rechecked before summary publication. Missing, incomplete, or mismatched inputs return `not-comparable`; matching inputs show scenario outcomes, regressions, elapsed time, and separate harness/primary-model/alternate-model identities.

This stays inside QA Lab, adds no dependency, and leaves existing parity modes unchanged. No winner selection, token-cost ranking, or authenticated harness-version claims. Custom execution setups and unified/runtime-pair summaries are not eligible.

## User Impact

Developers can check recorded conditions before comparing completed runs. Older summaries remain readable but require a fresh supported run for this mode.

## Evidence

- 39 focused comparison/CLI tests plus 277 existing suite/parity tests covered. One existing Crabline test could not read process identity in the macOS sandbox; the unchanged owning suite passed 33/33 with host process access.
- `pnpm build`, changed-file gates, `pnpm docs:list`, and `git diff --check` passed. An initial concurrent build/lint lock collision was resolved by running the gates serially, without bypassing the lock.
- Independent code review through P2 found no actionable findings.
- Actual source-checkout CLI proof at `688a8b90703e79e6ac65838ce9d0a2ac149f81af`: three local `mock-openai` suites passed; two matching runs compared successfully, while a changed readiness timeout was rejected. This proves producer-to-report plumbing, not a live cross-harness benchmark or npm-install behavior.

<details>
<summary>CLI commands and captured results</summary>

Run from the clean source checkout with Node 24.19.0. The proof used an isolated config/state directory and no real provider credentials. Config: `{"plugins":{"allow":["qa-lab"],"entries":{"qa-lab":{"enabled":true}}}}`. `node scripts/run-node.mjs` is the source launcher behind `pnpm openclaw`.

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --scenario channel-chat-baseline --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/a
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --scenario channel-chat-baseline --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/b
OPENCLAW_QA_TRANSPORT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=240000 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --scenario channel-chat-baseline --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/changed-timeout
```

Each exited 0 and published `counts={"total":1,"passed":1,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`. Each captured the exact commit above. The first two captured the same task, check-profile, and run-profile digests; the third differed only in run-profile digest.

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa parity-report --cross-harness --candidate-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/b/qa-suite-summary.json --baseline-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/a/qa-suite-summary.json --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/matching
```

Exit 0. Captured report:

```json
{"status":"comparable","reasons":[],"candidate":{"harness":"openclaw","primaryModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna","primaryProvider":"mock-openai","alternateModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt","alternateProvider":"mock-openai","elapsedMs":8580},"baseline":{"harness":"openclaw","primaryModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna","primaryProvider":"mock-openai","alternateModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt","alternateProvider":"mock-openai","elapsedMs":8119},"checks":[{"name":"Channel baseline conversation","candidate":"pass","baseline":"pass"}],"regressions":[]}
```

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa parity-report --cross-harness --candidate-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/changed-timeout/qa-suite-summary.json --baseline-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/a/qa-suite-summary.json --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/mismatch
```

Exit 1. Captured report:

```json
{"status":"not-comparable","reasons":["runProfileDigest is missing or different."]}
```

`git status --porcelain` was empty before and after. Assertions checked completed summaries, successful scenarios, exact source identity, both comparison verdicts, and model-pair reporting. No identities were filled in by hand.

</details>

prs.title: fix(doctor): settle state migrations for plugins with disabled channels
prs.body:
Fixes #194875

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor leaves a required plugin state migration pending after update repair when the plugin is enabled, its channel is disabled, and every retired source is absent.

## User Impact

Update repair can now confirm readiness for that no-op migration while preserving the disabled channel and saved configuration. Present sources and failed detectors stay pending; enabled-owner migrations retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing activation owner to classify channel-disabled plugins as inactive, and admit required state-only obligations to Doctor’s existing read-only inspector. Both migration phases must report no work before Doctor records completion. No plugin runtime or repair execution is added. Production grows by 12 net lines; the existing fixture gains 34 net regression-test lines, covered only by this change’s separate allocation.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on base `f6a8ce9a6f22`: the real Doctor-preflight SQLite ledger remains `pending` instead of `completed`. It passes with this fix and confirms readiness.
- 78 tests passed across `doctor-config-preflight.plugin-deferral.test.ts`, `state-migrations.plugin-doctor.disabled.test.ts`, `state-migrations.plugin-doctor.test.ts`, and `doctor-contract-registry.state-migrations.test.ts` (306s total; Doctor file 231s). Existing re-enable/import, retained-settings, action-order, and replay controls pass.
- Final eight-case regression rerun passed (56s): absent sources, present sources in each phase, and detector failure, for plugin-disabled and enabled-plugin/channel-disabled configurations. Execution markers prove neither runtime nor repair was attempted; source bytes and disabled settings remain unchanged.
- Touched-file lint/type checking (`run-oxlint.mjs --type-check`), formatting, and diff checks passed. Broad [CI passed at this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42432098865), including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. The final Doctor file passed in CI in 204.47s (206.17s wrapper).
- Isolated shared autoreview, P0–P2, reviewed the complete final local candidate against `f6a8ce9a6f22`: scoped-clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper checkouts were dirty; hosted review follows the maintainer fallback route.
- **MISSING live proof:** Crabbox/Testbox rejected allocation with `invalid duration "0s"`; no box was granted. Shipped Doctor and latest-stable upgrade proof were not run. No containers, packaging, browser E2E, or broad local suites/checks were run for this task.

prs.title: fix(macos): stop local startup after choosing an existing Gateway during onboarding
prs.body:
Contributor: Jacob Tomlinson (@jacobtomlinson).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6c710642-fbbe-4496-bec2-ea00bb56618c)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/07636d54-877d-4c2c-9b57-cd989f2ca024)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a local Gateway continuing to start when first-run macOS onboarding chooses **Connect to an existing Gateway**.

## User Impact

Choosing an existing Gateway leaves this Mac connect-only instead of retaining automatic local hosting, including while the saved remote connection awaits device approval. Cancelling sign-in does not re-enable local hosting; explicitly choosing **On this Mac** still works. Ordinary **Add Gateway** coexistence and independently managed external Gateways are unchanged.

**Draft pending native proof:** the macOS build/rendered regression and real pending/rejected-approval, launchd, and Keychain end-to-end flow have not run. Do not mark ready until the required exact-head native CI passes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved Gateway profiles connect independently from the primary Gateway. The first-run button previously opened the profile editor without retiring a local primary already selected by automatic setup. It now uses the existing primary-deferral action before opening sign-in, reusing its app-local persistence and lifecycle handling without changing the Gateway configuration file. The saved profile and its approval/retry behavior keep their existing owner; no authentication or approval policy changes are introduced.

## Evidence

- **Independent review:** a separate read-only reviewer inspected the complete frozen two-file diff and native test compile contracts; no actionable findings.
- **Local autoreview:** the installed canonical autoreview helper reviewed the complete two-file delta, both changed files intact, and supporting owners at P0-P2; completed `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings. Both reviews cover the unchanged precommit candidate against `636fc28d8bbd11a3ba91569b2bb250339fa21a45`; its diff SHA-256 is `08793b40110433f219274d4de790c9b682a50db8d81910026e5b66f260b46ddc`. The committed tree matches that reviewed snapshot.
- **Supplemental actual-source Linux fixture:** unchanged base fails because existing-Gateway selection retains automatic local mode. The candidate passes fresh/automatic-local selection, cancellation, retiring a held older startup, saved-callback persistence across a separate process, and explicit local reselection. This compiles the production action/deferral/resolver/coordinator paths with fixed external-effect doubles; it is not native AppKit, launchd, Keychain, or device-approval E2E proof.
- **Focused checks passed:** SwiftFormat 0.63.1, SwiftLint 0.65.1 (zero violations), Swift 6.3.3 syntax parsing, `git diff --check`, and normal commit hooks, including native localization freshness.
- **Native regression added, not executed:** the rendered onboarding-button test covers fresh and automatic-local states, unchanged config/re-read, sign-in cancellation, and explicit local selection. Native wall time and CI seconds are pending. This Linux host has no AppKit SDK and no eligible connected macOS test host was available.
- **Draft build-capacity route:** dispatch `ci.yml` from `main` with `target_ref` set to the full published head and `validation_tier=main`. Verify that the resolved checkout is that head, the applicable runtime producer succeeds, and `macos-swift (tests)` completes both **Build Swift tests** and **Swift test** before readiness. The exposed managed publisher has no workflow-dispatch operation, so an authorized operator must start this CI run; no shared-credential fallback was used.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid unnecessary cold-start initialization
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## What Problem This Solves

Constrained ARM64 Gateways can pass health checks and still run out of memory before completing a model turn. This change removes optional runtime initialization from startup and request preparation.

## User Impact

Headless Gateways with `gateway.controlUi.enabled: false` defer browser-oriented prewarming and initial full provider discovery until needed. Default Control UI startup stays eager, and request-time handlers remain available. Scoped refreshes, native-first discovery, provider authentication, tool authority and the public synchronous SDK contract are preserved.

Headless remote catalog updates preserve deferred discovery until inventory is requested. Once requested, pending and completed discovery survives catalog replacement.

Ordinary provider-filtered model-picker reads keep their provider scope. Providers first requested after startup retain their source identity, so a repeated settled read reuses discovery; later unfiltered demand can still acquire the full inventory.

Workspace prewarming loads worktree/template code only for eligible sandboxes. Headless startup skips the optional first-page session display warm while retaining projection materialization and readiness; real sessions.list demand still serves rows. Lease-error formatting stays separate from runtime schema loading.

Strict ARM64 acceptance remains unresolved; this PR does not yet establish that the constrained model workload succeeds. This PR adds no migration or configuration option beyond the integrated main schema 41 changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep catalog discovery on captured inputs and lightweight provider/authentication metadata. Defer execution, OAuth, media and session-event delivery code until requested, preserving authority checks after asynchronous imports.
- Avoid ordinary tool construction and auxiliary MCP/LSP/client preparation under resolved global deny-all policy. Async preparation uses shared assembly without the synchronous SDK facade; host-owned tools, collectors and final policy enforcement remain intact.
- Reuse state/runtime snapshot owners, defer PostgreSQL migration construction in SQLite workers, and export the existing opaque session-event target type so plugin declarations can name it without changing its brand or redemption checks.
- Defer initial full catalog discovery only for explicit headless configuration. Picker demand uses the current owner and requested provider set. Native-only or scoped inventory cannot suppress the first complete acquisition, and later provider-local refreshes retain their scope.
- Preserve already-loaded provider and authentication registrations when composing lightweight discovery entries, without loading new plugins. Preserve pinned main's research client byte-for-byte, including its intentional accessory removal; no UI redesign or new authentication scheme is introduced.

## Evidence

Candidate: `d54d6955da197e9c0412f98a3ffbac8ab3b48c2d`, integrated with pinned main `af13a39e3718ffdab036ec879801c27d5981466e` through a signed merge. The full PR diff against that base is 218 files, +3077/-5239.

- Current selected tests passed 100: 85 across nine affected owner suites, 14 prompt-prefix cases, and the existing catalog in-flight sharing/cache/refresh case. Headless seeded real sessions.list, enabled/disabled sandbox behavior, provider scope/reuse and SQLite cold migration construction remain covered. Core types, targeted lint and formatting passed.
- Exact-candidate sourcePerformance build passed in 59.6 seconds with the commit stamp verified. Fresh full-PR review against pinned af13 found no actionable correctness or security findings.
- Current staged test-line ratchet passed: 6,570,334 LF / 6,570,455 effective ceiling, 121 lines spare. The merge adds no allocation or shared-baseline edit; the older frozen-base deficit is historical.
- Merge resolutions preserve main's browser client exactly and its npm override extraction. Main's unchanged schema 41 PostgreSQL migration chain remains inside the existing lazy factory. Real PostgreSQL 39-to-40 and 40-to-41 lanes were not run locally; their required hosted results remain pending.
- Historical db386/e496 local synthetic primary samples completed real replies and owned cleanup but showed no measured memory saving. They are not peak, ARM or constrained-service qualification, and were not rerun for this merge.
- Prior 34bad [CI run 42320379833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42320379833) completed 145 jobs: 116 passed, 24 skipped and 5 failed. Its four attributed roots and PostgreSQL passes remain prior-head evidence only.
- Current merged-head hosted CI is pending. **Exact-package ARM64 acceptance is pending; R1 remains unresolved.** No current ARM success is claimed.

The preceding `34bad692` canonical ARM64 package passed build/static gates and health, then its Gateway service was OOM-killed before a completed model reply or soak. Service counters recorded three OOM events and one kill; outer peak was 961,413,120 bytes. The conditional 512 MiB trial was skipped and owned resources were closed. The new source boundaries are proven; the final exact package still requires constrained runtime qualification.

R1 remains open until the final package produces the real `CARDPUTER_GATEWAY_OK` response, completes a 60-second soak, stays at or below 928 MiB peak and records zero OOM under unchanged 1 GiB outer / 768 MiB service limits. The conditional 512 MiB trial remains gated on primary PASS.

prs.title: docs(gateway): correct Gateway port precedence for named profiles
prs.body:
Related: #191428

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the documented Gateway port precedence points to `18789` when a named profile is selected and no port is set.

## User Impact

Operators who select a named profile with `--profile <name>` or `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` and set no port can find the port the Gateway actually uses: `19001` for `dev`, otherwise a port derived from the profile name. They can also see that `--profile dev` puts `19001` ahead of `gateway.port`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Port resolution checks the named-profile default after `gateway.port` and before `18789`. When `--profile dev` selects the profile and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` is unset, the CLI sets that variable to `19001`, so `19001` takes precedence over `gateway.port`. #191428 corrected the `dev` case of the named-profile default, but the precedence statements in the Gateway runbook, the Gateway configuration reference, and the ports FAQ still end at `gateway.port` → `18789`. This change adds the missing step and the `--profile dev` exception to all three, and states the default without documenting how the derived port is computed. Documentation only; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source at `90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a`: [`resolveGatewayPort`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/config/paths.ts#L358-L372) returns `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT`, then `gateway.port`, then the named-profile default for `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, then `18789`. [`resolveProfileGatewayPort`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/profile-utils.ts#L25-L36) returns `19001` for `dev` and otherwise derives a port from the name. [`--profile` sets `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/profile.ts#L126), and [for `dev` with no `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` it also sets that variable to `19001`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/profile.ts#L150-L152), which the resolver reads before `gateway.port`. [`openclaw gateway` applies `--port` before the resolver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/gateway-cli/run.ts#L490-L496).
- [Existing resolver cases in `src/config/paths.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/config/paths.test.ts#L151-L158) cover `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=dev` resolving to `19001`, `gateway.port` taking precedence over the profile default, and a non-`dev` profile resolving to a derived port. They call the resolver directly and do not exercise the `--profile dev` CLI step.
- On a Linux development host with this change applied to `90d24e9`, `pnpm format:check` (oxfmt), `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs`, and `pnpm lint:docs --no-globs` passed on the three changed files; markdownlint linted 3 files and reported 0 issues. In a review checkout of the same commit, `git diff --check` on the same patch exited 0 with no output.
- Local ClawSweeper review (`--local-range` from base `90d24e9`, covering this diff and description) ran three times and reported no findings, risks, or security concerns.
- Documentation only; runtime tests were not run.

prs.title: docs(gateway): add 120-port spacing to multi-gateway FAQ and config docs
prs.body:
Related: #184694

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway FAQ and the Gateway configuration reference tell operators who run several Gateways on one host to use unique ports, but omit the 120-port spacing between base ports that the multiple-gateways guide and the Gateway runbook require.

## User Impact

Operators reading either page now see that base ports must be at least 120 apart, so they do not pick nearby base ports whose derived sandbox, browser control, and CDP ports overlap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gateway derives additional ports from its base port: the sandbox host, when active, uses base + 1, browser control uses base + 2, and browser profile CDP ports by default run from base + 11 through base + 110. The multiple-gateways guide states the 120-port rule, and #184694 added the same wording to the Gateway runbook checklist. This change adds that wording to the multi-gateway answer in the FAQ and to the multi-instance isolation section of the configuration reference. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Port derivation at `90d24e9`: the sandbox host port is the Gateway port + 1 unless configured (`src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` L21, L253-267). Browser control is base + 2, and the default CDP range starts at control + 9 and spans 100 ports, through base + 110 (`extensions/browser/src/config/port-defaults.ts` L15-29); browser config applies these helpers to the resolved Gateway port (`extensions/browser/src/browser/config.ts` L260-263).
- `docs/gateway/multiple-gateways.md` L20 and `docs/gateway/index.md` L194 at the same commit already state the 120-port rule; this PR does not change them.
- On a Linux development host at `90d24e9` with this change, these checks passed: `pnpm format:check` (oxfmt) on the two changed files reported "All matched files use the correct format."; `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` reported "Docs MDX check passed (2 files)"; `pnpm lint:docs --no-globs` linted the 2 changed files and found 0 issues; and `git diff --check` on the same patch in a review checkout exited 0 with no output.
- Local ClawSweeper review (`--local-range`, base `90d24e9`, this diff and description) ran three times with no findings, risks, or security concerns.
- Not changed here: above base port 65425 the default CDP range falls back to `18800`-`18899`, and above 65533 browser control falls back to `18791` (`extensions/browser/src/config/port-defaults.ts` L3-8, L10-29), so 120-port spacing alone does not separate such a Gateway from one on the default port, `18789`.
- Documentation only (+2/-2); runtime tests were not run, and Gateways were not started side by side. The overlap is derived from the source, not observed.

prs.title: fix(hooks): reuse live gateway plugins for queued turns
prs.body:
## Summary
### High Level TLDR
Webhook turns can reload plugins instead of reusing the Gateway's live instances. Pass the owning transport's registry resolver into queued hook execution, matching scheduled jobs.

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes unnecessary cold plugin preparation on hook-driven agent turns when a prepared runtime must be built.

## User Impact
Hook-driven turns can borrow current Gateway-owned plugins. No configuration changes, migration, permission changes, or new cache.

## Root Cause
The HTTP transport already owns a live plugin-registry resolver. Hook dispatch passed only the Gateway-context resolver to `createScheduledGatewayRunner`, omitting its existing registry-resolver argument. Prepared plugin loading deliberately requires a current, request-scoped Gateway registry before borrowing instances; without it, preparation loads independent instances. The same omission exists on the base revision.

## Why This Change Was Made
Forward the existing live resolver through the lazy hook dispatcher and HTTP-handler fallback. Resolve it at execution time so queued turns see registry replacement rather than a captured generation.

## Verification
Verified candidate: `5841b26af7d861e72caa6dbbe6f094e3df978eaf`.
- Negative control: removing only the production fix makes both new regressions fail because the registry resolver is absent; queued execution observes `[undefined, undefined]`.
- Restored candidate: 52 tests pass across hook early-failure recovery, transport ownership, scheduled execution ownership, hook trust, and prepared-runtime registry borrowing. Repository runner wall time: 74.62s across two shards.
- Type-aware lint passes for both changed production files and both changed tests; all four files pass formatting.
- Fixed the original CI lint failure by removing a redundant `<void>` from `createDeferred()`; no runtime behavior changed in that correction.
- Full isolated `pnpm build` passes (3m 36.2s), including declarations and plugin assets. Build emitted advisory Control UI bundle-size warnings; no build failure.
- Exact-head CI passed: [run 42432183398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42432183398), attempt 1, completed successfully on `5841b26af7d861e72caa6dbbe6f094e3df978eaf`. All 70 workflow jobs were inspected: 40 passed and 30 were skipped by workflow selection; no failed, cancelled, or pending jobs. The native full-rollup watcher reports GREEN, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and applicable security checks.

## Real behavior proof
Closest feasible environment: isolated checkout, Node 26.12.1 host, repository Vitest runner.
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/hooks.early-failure.test.ts src/gateway/server-runtime-state.hook-broker.test.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.startup-registry.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
Result: 43 Gateway tests plus 9 prepared-runtime tests passed. The regression dispatches two queued turns, replaces the transport registry between them, and observes the correct registry in each execution scope. Existing real-loader tests prove current-owner borrowing and rejection of retired/unbound registries.

## Evidence
Independent canonical autoreview of the full candidate from `ade7c07d4c70a08ea0b294de27ddc519120e817e` through `5841b26af7d861e72caa6dbbe6f094e3df978eaf`, with relevant owner/caller/loader source context and explicit P0–P3 coverage: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Manual security and lifecycle review found no hostile changes or weakened ownership checks. The existing hosted ClawSweeper request has repeatedly failed without a publishable review artifact; no duplicate request was posted. It supplied no substantive finding. The completed independent P0–P3 review above provides the requested replacement review, not a claim of ClawSweeper approval.

## What was not tested
No patched live deployment or production cold-start before/after benchmark. Production hook replay would risk repeating device commands, and a controlled cold Gateway benchmark requires an isolated equivalent deployment. The tests prove the missing binding and registry-lifecycle behavior, not a guaranteed latency reduction or attribution of every second in a production stall. Exact-head broad PR CI and the isolated full build passed.

prs.title: feat(qa): replay confidence reports from portable evidence
prs.body:
## Status: draft — maintainer design decision requested

This is a proposed implementation for discussion, not an accepted product scope or a merge-ready change. It was prepared before upstream design agreement; it is now held in draft in response to the [issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138098#issuecomment-5538187135). Local validation and independent code review below do not constitute OpenClaw maintainer approval.

Before further implementation or merge review, could maintainers confirm:

1. **Ownership and CLI:** Should the existing QA Lab own portable evidence capture and offline confidence replay through these two commands?
2. **Bundle and sharing contract:** Is the proposed bounded, versioned, exact-byte format acceptable, including captured strictness settings, explicit missing inputs, content-integrity-only verification, and operator review before sharing rather than automatic redaction?
3. **Compatibility:** Is deterministic classification within the same OpenClaw build sufficient for an initial version? This proposal does not guarantee identical classifications across OpenClaw versions. If a stronger cross-version contract is required, please specify the expected behavior before the format is adopted.

The implementation and existing validation evidence remain intact. We are requesting design direction, not automatic repair or merge.

## What Problem This Solves

Related: #138098.

A QA Lab confidence report is difficult to reproduce once the producer's artifact directory changes or disappears. Sharing only a verdict does not preserve the inputs or the strictness policy used to classify them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two native QA Lab commands:

- `qa confidence-export`: capture the selected manifest, every declared lane input (including explicit missing entries), timestamp, and strict flags in a bounded evidence bundle.
- `qa confidence-replay`: verify the exact bundle bytes against a separately supplied SHA-256 digest, validate embedded artifact digests and the complete input set, then run the existing classifier entirely from captured bytes.

The implementation stays within the existing QA Lab plugin and public filesystem SDK. Tests construct their own synthetic fixtures. There is no external service, repository checkout, harness fork, added package dependency, configuration setting, or persistent-state migration. Export and replay are in one PR so reviewers can exercise a complete user-facing feature rather than a foundation without a consumer.

## User Impact

Reviewers can reproduce confidence classifications without the original filesystem or provider credentials. Reports keep integrity separate from confidence verdicts: an intact bundle can still fail. Captured policy cannot be loosened at replay, and omitted entries cannot silently become missing lanes.

Input paths are relative and bounded; symlinks/hardlinks and nonregular inputs are rejected. Export never overwrites an existing file. Replay does not execute artifact-provided commands or consult artifact paths.

This is content integrity and reproducible classification, **not producer authentication, independent code testing, model-run replay, or a Workboard completion attestation**. Individual captures are not an atomic suite snapshot. Exact contents are preserved, not automatically redacted; operators must review inputs before sharing. Replay classifications may differ across OpenClaw versions.

## Evidence

### Fresh CLI proof — September 4, 2026

Rebuilt unchanged head `85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b` on macOS with Node 24.19.0. `pnpm build` exited 0; the four focused files passed again (**139/139 tests**).

The actual QA CLI exported the synthetic inputs and replayed the same report after their original directory was moved. Assertions compared the complete before/after replay, including its timestamp. Replay also matched the existing `confidence-report` result except for the independently generated timestamp. Wrong digests and unsupported bundle versions exited 1; a valid bundle containing a failing lane also exited 1.

**Scope correction:** this is built **source-checkout CLI proof**, not an npm-install smoke. [QA Lab is intentionally omitted from the npm tarball](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/qa-e2e-automation#observability-smokes). A preliminary direct `node openclaw.mjs qa ...` invocation failed before classification on the private `sqlite-runtime-testing` SDK import. The successful run below uses the documented source launcher, which [enables and builds private QA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b/scripts/run-node.mts#L1599); no loader, dependency, or production-code workaround was added.

<details>
<summary>Exact CLI commands and captured output</summary>

From a built checkout at the PR head, create a fresh temporary proof directory with `inputs/profile.json` and `inputs/checks.json` containing the fixture JSON shown in the trace. Use this isolated config:


Set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` to that config and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` to a new directory under the proof directory. ### Earlier validation

- `pnpm test:extension qa-lab`: **238 files passed; 3302 tests passed, 3 skipped**.
- Focused capture/replay, evidence boundary, existing classifier and CLI tests: **139 passed**.
- Rebased onto main at `be967f4a514`; `git range-diff` confirms the feature patch is unchanged. The 139 focused tests passed again on final head `85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b`.

prs.title: fix(doctor): keep updater-retired plugin aliases removed during record reconciliation
prs.body:
Closes #136025

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor restores a retired official plugin alias immediately after the updater successfully replaces it with the canonical plugin: `repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls` counts only `updated`/`unchanged` updater outcome IDs and restores every original missing record absent from that set, so the retired alias (e.g. `qqbot`) comes back alongside the canonical record (e.g. `openclaw-qqbot`), losing the updater's committed install-owner migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair now consumes the committed owner migrations attached to the updater result (`resolvePluginInstallOwnerMigrations`): an alias whose canonical target was repaired in the same run stays retired — its original record is not restored, it is excluded from install candidacy, and a change note records the retirement. Migrations are honored only when the canonical target was repaired in the same result, so a failed canonical update without migration metadata keeps the previous preserve-everything behavior (including no persistence write). Plain `skipped` outcomes are still neither success nor failure, per the issue.

Note: this issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`; opening anyway because the fix shape is marked clear (`fix-shape-clear`), the regression is reproduced with exact steps, no open PR or assignee exists, and the change is confined to the owning repair boundary.

## User Impact

After a successful canonical plugin update, Doctor no longer resurrects the retired alias record or attempts to reinstall it; operators see one canonical record plus an explicit retirement note.

## Evidence

- New `keeps a retired duplicate alias removed when the updater commits an owner migration` regression test following the issue's exact repro shape (mocked updater returning only the canonical 2.0.3 record, `updated` + diagnostic `skipped` outcomes, committed `{qqbot: "openclaw-qqbot"}` migration metadata, real temp package files).
- New `preserves original records when a canonical update fails without an owner migration` negative control asserting unchanged records and no persistence write.
- Both edited files pass an esbuild transform check; existing doctor tests that mock the updater without migration metadata are behaviorally unaffected (the resolver returns `undefined` → no-op). Local vitest lane cannot run in this Windows checkout (rolldown native binding failure at config load), so CI runs the full suite on the exact head SHA.

## Why This Change Was Made
