prs.title: fix(imessage): check reply_to_guid in echo cache for paired mirror rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iMessage, when Messages.app writes a paired inbound mirror row for an outbound message, the mirror carries a distinct GUID (`GUID-B`) but references the original outbound GUID (`GUID-A`) via `reply_to_guid`. The echo cache stores `GUID-A`, but `resolveInboundEchoMessageIds()` only collects the row id and `guid` — not `reply_to_guid`. The cache treats `GUID-B` vs stored `GUID-A` as conflicting identities, the marker-based reflection guard does not match ordinary text, and the mirror is dispatched as fresh inbound input — causing duplicate replies, recursive turns, and extra model usage.

Related to #135704

## Why This Change Was Made

`reply_to_guid` is already parsed and used for reply context (`describeReplyContext`), but was not consulted for echo identity. The fix adds a `replyToGuid` probe in `hasIMessageEchoMatch` that checks the echo cache with `reply_to_guid` as the lookup ID, using a new `requireMessageIdTextMatch` cache option that prevents the cache from short-circuiting on messageId equality alone. This ensures text must also match the same cached outbound entry, so legitimate inline replies with different body text are not dropped.

Key design decisions addressing ClawSweeper review findings:

1. **`requireMessageIdTextMatch` cache option** — Added to both in-memory (`DefaultSentMessageCache`) and persisted (`hasPersistedIMessageEcho`) cache layers. When set, a matching messageId is only sufficient when text also matches the same outbound entry.

2. **`guidTextCache` (keyed by `scope:guid:text`)** — Binds text to a specific outbound GUID. Without this, two outbound sends (A="Hello", B="Okay") would let an inline reply "Okay" referencing GUID-A match A's ID timestamp and B's text marker, causing a false-positive echo drop.

3. **Early echo probe before access/pairing** — Placed after basic row validation but before the access resolver, so paired mirrors from unpaired or blocked senders are suppressed as echoes rather than triggering pairing.

4. **Authored self-chat exclusion** — Early probe skips `is_from_me=true` rows; main echo probe suppresses `replyToGuid` when `isSelfChat` is true. Prevents authored self-chat rows from being misclassified as echoes.

5. **Self-chat limiter exemption** — Early probe returns `"self-chat echo"` reason (not `"echo"`) when either `isSelfChat` is true or `selfChatCache.has()` confirms a duplicate. The loop rate limiter exempts `"self-chat echo"` drops, preventing benign mirror bursts from suppressing legitimate conversation.

Changes:
1. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts`** — `replyToGuid` parameter, early echo probe before access, `selfChatCache.has()` check for benign accounting, scoped cache probe with `requireMessageIdTextMatch`.
2. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/echo-cache.ts`** — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` option, `guidTextCache` for GUID-bound text matching.
3. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/persisted-echo-cache.ts`** — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` in persisted `has()`, text check on messageId match.
4. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.reply-to-guid.test.ts`** — 5 regression tests using real `createSentMessageCache`.
5. **`scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs`** — Real production-path proof exercising classifier + both cache layers.
6. **`scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs`** — Monitor boundary proof exercising limiter accounting contract.

## User Impact

iMessage deployments where Messages emits paired inbound mirror rows with `reply_to_guid` will no longer see duplicate agent replies or recursive turns from reflected outbound text. Legitimate inline replies (same parent GUID, different body text) remain unaffected and continue to dispatch normally. Mirror bursts do not trip the loop rate limiter.

## Evidence

### Changed files

- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` — `replyToGuid` parameter, early echo probe, self-chat limiter exemption, scoped cache probe
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/echo-cache.ts` — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` option, `guidTextCache`
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/persisted-echo-cache.ts` — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` in persisted `has()`
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.reply-to-guid.test.ts` — 5 regression tests
- `scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs` — classifier + cache proof
- `scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs` — monitor boundary limiter proof

### Real Behavior Proof 1: Classifier + Cache (7/7 PASS)

Production-path proof exercising the real `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` with real `createSentMessageCache` (no mocks) and the real persisted echo cache (with iMessage runtime initialization). Script: `scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs`.

```console
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.reply-to-guid.test.ts --run

      ✓ drops paired mirror with reply_to_guid matching outbound echo cache guid
```

### Lint

```console
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/echo-cache.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/persisted-echo-cache.ts scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

## Notes

- The early `replyToGuid` echo probe runs after basic row validation (group without chat_id check) but before the access resolver, ensuring paired mirrors from unpaired or blocked senders are suppressed as echoes.
- The `requireMessageIdTextMatch` option ensures the cache does not short-circuit on messageId alone; text must be proven to come from the same outbound entry (`guidTextCache` for in-memory, `entry.text === text` for persisted).
- Self-chat limiter exemption covers both `isSelfChat=true` (with `destination_caller_id`) and `selfChatCache.has()` (without `destination_caller_id`) cases.
- This is a partial fix for the `reply_to_guid` identity gap. The reporter also mentions remembering an observed `is_from_me=true` concrete GUID when a send path did not return one — that is not addressed here and may warrant a separate change.

## Proof Limitations

The `handleMessageNow` function in `monitor-provider.ts:734` is a closure (not exported), so it cannot be called directly from a proof script. The echo cache is seeded through `createIMessageEchoCachingSend` (in `deliver.ts:123`) during outbound delivery, which requires the full agent dispatch chain (`runChannelInboundEvent` + bindings + agent runtime).

The two proof scripts exercise the real production functions that `handleMessageNow` calls:
- `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` — the real classifier with real `createSentMessageCache` and persisted echo cache
- `createLoopRateLimiter` — the real limiter with `record()` and `isRateLimited()` (the exact API used at `monitor-provider.ts:803` and `:849`)

The limiter boundary proof script (`scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs`) replicates the monitor's accounting contract from `monitor-provider.ts:800-804`:
```typescript
// monitor-provider.ts:800-803
const isLoopDrop = decision.reason === "echo" || decision.reason === "reflected assistant content";
if (isLoopDrop) { loopRateLimiter.record(rateLimitKey); }
// monitor-provider.ts:849
if (decision.kind === "dispatch" && loopRateLimiter.isRateLimited(rateLimitKey)) { return; }
```

This covers the limiter accounting logic without requiring the full agent dispatch chain. An e2e monitor test that seeds the echo cache through actual outbound delivery would require mocking `sendMessageIMessage`, `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, `ensureConfiguredBindingRouteReady`, and the channel inbound debouncer — essentially the 1700-line fixture from `monitor.last-route.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(infra): decode OEM console code pages in Windows subprocess output
prs.body:
Related: #135856, #136203

Not a fix for #135856. That report is `doctor --fix` refusing maintenance, and this pull request no longer changes Doctor or Scheduled Task inventory.

The Spanish and German `schtasks /FO LIST` parser was dropped. Current main reads task inventory from typed COM (`Schedule.Service`) through `listScheduledTasks`, and #151608 superseded the localized LIST-parser part of this pull request.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows subprocess output on a Spanish or German console comes back with U+FFFD in place of accented characters. Those consoles default to OEM code page 850. `chcp` reports 850, the console encoding probe only consulted the ANSI code-page map, and Node's `TextDecoder` has no label for the OEM `cp###` pages, so the bytes were decoded as UTF-8.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `chcp` probe now falls back to the existing OEM code-page map that the `.cmd` launcher already uses. Legacy decoding goes through iconv-lite for the `cp###` labels ICU lacks. `decodeWindowsOutputBuffer` and `createWindowsOutputDecoder` share that decoder. Valid UTF-8 is still tried first, and UTF-16 BOM handling is unchanged. The system ANSI probe is unchanged. Main's locale-independent task inventory is left as it is.

`src/infra/windows-encoding.ts` is on the PR wrapper inventory, so iconv-lite is pinned in that extracted dependency context. Without the pin, wrapper boot could not load the module.

## User Impact

Windows command output on the OEM console pages in that map, including 850, decodes accented text instead of replacement characters. English and UTF-8 consoles are unchanged. Deep Scheduled Task scanning stays on main's COM inventory.

## Evidence

No native localized Windows run was done. The previous Linux stand-in exercised the `schtasks /FO LIST` parser, and that path has been removed, so it is not proof for this scope.

Focused tests on the decoder head (Node 24.21.0):


prs.title: fix(codex): normalize overlength Responses call_id in settled-turn projection
prs.body:
Fixes #130965

## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex-harness turn finishes its tool work without producing final text, OpenClaw runs *settled turn finalization*: it projects the transcript into raw OpenAI Responses items and injects them into the Codex thread via `thread/inject_items`.

On current `main`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.ts` never bounds the replayed `call_id` to the 64-character Responses contract:

- `requireCallId()` (`:51-57`) rejects only empty ids and ids longer than **256** characters — it never rewrites.
- The `function_call` emission (`:154-165`) and the `function_call_output` emission (`:181`/`:234`) embed that id verbatim.

So an 83-character historical `call_id` reaches OpenAI unchanged and the request is rejected:

```text
Invalid `input[3].call_id`: string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.
```

Finalization then fails closed, the channel surfaces a generic generation error, and the affected session has to be deleted to recover (`impact:session-state`, `impact:message-loss`).

**The upstream harness is not a viable fix site.** I checked `openai/codex` at tag `rust-v0.153.0` (`41e22fee981a63b3698df7ed36bad393cda24715`): `thread/inject_items` forwards `call_id` byte-identically.

- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:943-971` — `thread_inject_items_response_inner` deserializes each raw item into a `ResponseItem`, calls `validate_response_item_image_urls(&items)?` (its only validation), then `thread.inject_response_items(items)`. No `call_id` inspection.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:34-60` — that validator rejects only remote HTTP(S) `input_image` URLs; `ResponseItem::FunctionCall { .. }` is in the pass-through arm.
- `codex-rs/core/src/codex_thread.rs:617-652` → `codex-rs/core/src/session/inject.rs:72-107` — `inject_client_response_items` maps items through `annotate_client_response_item`, which only attaches `CodexHarnessMetadata { client_authored }` for developer messages and otherwise stores the `ResponseItem` unchanged.
- `codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/normalize.rs:21-80` — the only history-level `call_id` logic (`ensure_call_outputs_present`) *pairs* missing outputs by cloning `call_id` verbatim; it never shortens or rewrites.
- No `call_id` length bound exists anywhere under `codex-rs/`.

Whatever the projection emits is what OpenAI receives, so the contract has to be enforced here.

## Why This Change Was Made

A per-projection deterministic resolver rewrites overlength ids into the `call_` ≤64 Responses shape, and **both** emission sites resolve through it, so a `function_call` and its `function_call_output` can never diverge.

- Resolution happens where the id is read (`resolveCallId(requireCallId(...))`), so the emitted items *and* the duplicate / ambiguity / completeness bookkeeping in `projectSettledCodexMessages` operate on one id space.
- The map is created inside `projectSettledCodexMessages` — per invocation, not module-level.
- The rewritten tail is derived from a `sha256` prefix of the **full original id**, so the mapping is stable across calls and processes, and two distinct overlength ids cannot collide.
- Ids already within 64 characters pass through **byte-identical** — no gratuitous rewriting, so prompt caching and every currently-working id are unaffected.
- Empty ids and ids over the existing 256-character sanity bound still throw exactly as before. Only the (64, 256] band changes behavior, from "silently forwarded and rejected by OpenAI" to "deterministically rewritten".

Production change is ~30 lines in one file. **No new configuration option. No new plugin-SDK export. No change outside `extensions/codex/src/app-server/`.**

### Local implementation vs. exporting core's resolver

Core already owns an equivalent transform — `createOpenAIResponsesToolCallIdResolver` / `normalizeOpenAIResponsesToolCallIds` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.ts:95-190` — but it is **not exported through `plugin-sdk`** (`normalizeOpenAIResponses*` appears nowhere under `src/plugin-sdk/`), and extension production code may only cross into core via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` (root `AGENTS.md:94-95`).

I asked on the issue which shape you prefer and did not want to block on the answer, so this PR ships the **local** option and documents it in a comment at the resolver:

| | Local resolver (this PR) | Export core's resolver through plugin-sdk |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin-SDK surface | unchanged | widened (a new published API) |
| Duplication | one structurally similar resolver | none |
| Blast radius | `extensions/codex` only | every plugin-SDK consumer |
| Decision owner | contributor | maintainers |

If you would rather have the export, say so and I will swap the implementation — the tests are written against projected output, not the resolver, so they carry over unchanged.

Two deliberate differences from core's version, both narrowing scope rather than widening it:

- **Pass-through predicate is length-only** (`id.length <= 64`), where core additionally requires the `^call_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,59}$` shape. The reported failure is a length rejection, and a length-only predicate guarantees every id that works today keeps working byte-identically. A stricter predicate would rewrite currently-valid ids (including this file's own `"call-1"` fixtures) for no reported benefit.
- **No `callId|itemId` pairing split.** Core handles that because it also normalizes `function_call.id`; this projection emits only `call_id` and never an item `id`, so the pairing form does not arise here.

## User Impact

A Codex-harness turn that replays a historical tool call with an overlength `call_id` now finalizes normally instead of failing closed and stranding the session. Every id that already satisfied the Responses contract is untouched.

## Evidence

All of the following was actually run — no step is claimed from inspection alone.

**Pre-fix red (stash method), local, base `d2a616bdf373a5b3cac0add8e9b2f70cd0802f42`.** With the production file stashed and only the new tests present:

```text
× projectSettledCodexMessages > rewrites overlength call ids once per projection and keeps the pair deterministic
AssertionError: expected 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa…' to match /^call_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,59}$/
Tests  1 failed | 23 passed (24)
```

That is the defect case failing for the intended reason — the 83-character id arrives unrewritten. The other added cases (pair identity, collision-freedom, byte-identical short ids, and the duplicate / ambiguity / completeness guards under overlength ids) pass on base by construction: they are regression guards protecting behavior a careless fix would break, not additional proofs of the defect.

An earlier standalone reproduction against untouched `main` printed the projection directly and showed the failure end to end:

```text
"type": "function_call",       "call_id": "call_…MnQwE"   (83 chars)
"type": "function_call_output","call_id": "call_…MnQwE"   (83 chars)
call_id lengths: 83 83
```

**Post-fix green, local.** `settled-turn-projection.test.ts` → **30 passed (30)**, every pre-existing case included.

**Changed-file gate, local.** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts` → **exit 0**, all lanes green: conflict markers, max-lines ratchet, assertion SAFETY ratchet, changelog attributions, doctor deprecation registry, guarded extension wildcard re-exports, plugin-sdk wildcard re-exports, **extension test core imports**, duplicate scan coverage, dependency pin guard, format, doctor contract closure, **plugin boundaries**, package patch guard, **typecheck extensions**, **typecheck extension tests**, **coercion helper declaration guard**, deprecated API usage, **dead export scan (Knip: 0 entries, script/production/full-tree)**, lint, database-first legacy-store guard, media download helper guard, runtime sidecar loader guard, **runtime import cycles (0)**.

**Two-sided proof on an isolated Linux box** (Hetzner VPS, Docker `node:26`, fresh clone of base `d2a616bdf3`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`):

- **Side A** — base + *test file only*: `settled-turn-projection.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `side-a exit=1`, failing case `rewrites overlength call ids once per projection and keeps the pair deterministic`.
- **Side B** — base + *full patch*: same file → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `side-b exit=0`.

So the change is what turns that case from red to green, reproduced on a second OS and a clean dependency tree — not just on my machine.

**Adjacent suite.** On the pre-reservation head, `npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/` was exit 0 with **3430 passed, 0 failed**. Re-running it locally on the current head reached **3460 passed with 0 test failures** and then aborted on a vitest worker crash under local disk pressure, so I am not presenting that re-run as a clean green — CI on this head is the authoritative adjacent signal.

`pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` is not applicable to this change and was not run: the fix adds no plugin-SDK export, and the boundary is instead covered by the `plugin boundaries` and `extension test core imports` lanes above, both green.

Core is untouched — the diff is exactly two files, both under `extensions/codex/src/app-server/`.

### ClawSweeper review round 1 — P1 collision, fixed in `64929bd861`

ClawSweeper blocked this with a P1 I had missed, and it was right. The rewrite puts generated ids in the same `call_` space raw ids occupy, and nothing kept them apart. Since `projectSettledCodexMessages` keys its duplicate / ambiguity / completeness bookkeeping by the *resolved* id, a transcript carrying both an overlength id **and** a legitimate raw call whose id equals that id's rewrite was rejected as `duplicate tool call` — the exact fail-closed finalization this PR exists to remove.

I reproduced it before changing anything. Projecting the overlength pair alone yields `call_aaaa…aaaa_8ddbdef916`; feeding a transcript that holds that id *and* the overlength one threw `Codex settled-turn projection found a duplicate tool call`.

Worth being explicit: three independent model reviews all saw this overlap and waved it through as "~2^-40, fail-closed, not a practical hole". They were wrong — the colliding value is *derivable*, not merely improbable, and a history that mixes normalized and original ids (exactly the provider-switch origin the issue describes) can contain both. The bot caught what the reviewers rationalized.

Fix: collect every id the transcript replays verbatim before resolving, and skip those when generating. A clash re-derives from a salted hash of the original instead of colliding, and generated ids are reserved as they are produced so two rewrites cannot converge either. Salting is deterministic, so the mapping stays a pure function of the transcript. The mixed-collision regression the review asked for is added, and it fails with the reservation disabled, reporting exactly `duplicate tool call`.

Production delta for this round is **+57/−9**. That growth is the reservation invariant itself — the passthrough scan, the salted rebuild, and the taken set. I could not absorb it into the existing resolver: it cannot know which raw ids a transcript will replay until it has seen them, so the pre-pass is load-bearing rather than defensive.

### ClawSweeper review round 2 — boundedness regression, fixed in `1c24988fab`

Round 2 confirmed the collision fix was addressed, and caught a second defect — one my *own* round-1 fix introduced. Reserving replayed ids needed the whole id set up front, and the shortest way to get it was `[...messages]`. That defeats the caller: `settled-turn-context.ts:136` passes `verifiedSettledMessages()`, a **generator** that pulls message payloads lazily, precisely so the projection can reject at its item and byte limits *before* the rest of the history is read. Draining it first forces every later SQLite payload to load even for a transcript the projection was about to refuse.

I checked the caller this time rather than assuming: `function* verifiedSettledMessages` at `settled-turn-context.ts:55`. The finding is correct.

Fix: stream again, and defer the rewrite. Bookkeeping keys on the **original** ids, exactly as it did before this PR, so duplicate / ambiguity / completeness still hold on unmodified values and no rewrite can invent a duplicate. Once the transcript is proven complete, rewrite the collected items — already bounded by `MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS` and `MAX_PROJECTION_BYTES`. The resolver still reserves every verbatim-replayed id, so round 1's collision fix is preserved.

Added a laziness regression: a generator that throws if drained past the item limit. It fails with the materialization restored, reporting `history was drained past the projection limit`.

This round is **+49/−47** production, so close to net-neutral, and the deferred rewrite is simpler than the pre-scan it replaces. Cumulative production growth over the whole PR is now modest rather than the +57 round 1 carried.

### Injection-boundary proof — added in `c7ce0f4eee`

Round 3 was right that the assertions stopped one layer short: OpenAI rejects the *request*, and what reaches OpenAI is whatever `bounded-turn` hands to `thread/inject_items`. So I moved the assertion to that boundary.

`settled-turn-injection.test.ts` drives the **real** `runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn` against the repo's existing fake app-server client and asserts on the **recorded `thread/inject_items` params** — the outbound payload, not the projection's return value. Observed request sequence:

```text
model/list -> config/read -> configRequirements/read -> thread/start
  -> mcpServerStatus/list -> thread/inject_items -> turn/start
```

Two-sided at that boundary, from the same 83-character source id:

| | on-the-wire `call_id` lengths | result |
|---|---|---|
| base `d2a616bdf3` | `83, 83` | fails — `expected 83 to be less than or equal to 64` |
| this branch | `64, 64` | passes, both sides identical |

**What this is, precisely:** a harness-level boundary proof. The transport is faked and **no Responses call is billed**. It is not a live Codex session, and I am not presenting it as one.

**What was still missing at that point** — an after-fix trace from a real authenticated Codex app-server against the live Responses API — is now provided in the "Live proof" section below, run on my own subscription login rather than a maintainer budget.

**Independent pre-submission reviews.** Three independent models reviewed the diff read-only against the caller chain, core's equivalent transform, and the repo's extension-boundary and test-audit rules. All three returned **GO** with no CRITICAL or MAJOR production findings. Their MINOR/NOTE points are folded into this description rather than waved away:

Both of the review's test-coverage findings are now **fixed in `50f5ffb1e6`** (tests only, no production change):

- **The `<= 64` passthrough boundary was unpinned.** The gate is inclusive on purpose — the Responses `maxLength` is 64, so a 64-character id must stay byte-identical — but the suite only exercised lengths 83 and 6, so narrowing it to `< 64` would have silently begun rewriting ids that already replay correctly, with every test still passing. There is now a case asserting a 64-character id is projected unchanged on both sides while a 65-character id is rewritten into the `call_` ≤64 shape and stays identical across the pair. I confirmed it **fails under exactly that `< 64` mutation** (`Tests 1 failed | 27 passed`, the boundary case) and passes once restored — so it is pinning the bound, not just describing it.
- **The fail-closed table had lost its short-id coverage.** `missing result` / `duplicate call id` / `tool-name mismatch` had been retargeted from `"call-1"` onto the overlength id. Those three rows are now generated for *both* id shapes from a single helper rather than a duplicated table, so the pre-existing short-id paths stay covered alongside the overlength ones (`fails closed for 'duplicate call id (short id)'` and `… (overlength id)`, etc.).

- **The resolver comment overstated its fidelity to core.** It said it "keeps a local copy" of core's resolver, when the trigger is deliberately narrower (length-only vs core's shape regex and `call_id|fc_id` pairing split). Left as-is, someone could later swap in core's resolver assuming parity and silently change emitted ids for previously-passthrough transcripts. The comment now states the narrowing and why, in `1a65b3eee9` (comment only, no behavior change).

Suite after the deltas: **30 passed (30)**; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` → **exit 0** on both changed files.

- The collision-freedom test passes on base, so it is a companion invariant guarding against a plausible bad fix (deriving the tail from the truncated prefix alone — the two fixtures share an 82-character prefix and differ only in the last character, leaving the hash as the sole discriminator). It is not itself a bug-regression test, and I am not citing it as one.
- The 256-character bound is no longer the API-conformance bound; it survives as an absurd-input ceiling that preserves base fail-closed behavior. Worth a comment line so a later reader does not mistake it for dead code.
- If OpenAI ever enforces the `call_` *shape* rather than only the length on injected history, this projection would still fail closed; exporting core's resolver is the durable answer, and at that point this local copy should be deleted rather than aliased (`AGENTS.md:111`, one canonical path).
- Three of the four fail-closed guard cases now use the overlength id instead of `"call-1"`. That is a net widening — the duplicate case now also fails if the rewrite ever becomes non-deterministic — but the pure short-id variants are gone; `"call-1"` byte-identical pass-through keeps its own dedicated case.

*Disclosure: this contribution is by Sho (human, @shojikumaru) working with AI assistance — implementation by an AI agent under my direction, with the verification above run and read by me, plus independent model reviews before submission. Maintainer edits are welcome: "Allow edits by maintainers" is enabled.*

### Live proof — real managed Codex app-server against the live Responses API

The remaining gate was an after-fix trace from a real authenticated Codex app-server, not a fake transport. That trace now exists, and it is two-sided. It was produced on my own ChatGPT-authenticated Codex login (no maintainer budget involved, no API key), so the earlier "I will not spend a maintainer's API budget uninvited" objection no longer applies.

**Setup.** A `*.real-binary.live.test.ts` harness in the same style as `thread-lifecycle.restricted-mcp.real-binary.live.test.ts`: it calls the **real** `runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn` with the finalizer's exact parameters (`taskLabel: "settled-turn finalization"`, `requireNoExternalCapabilities: true`, `allowEmptyText: true`, `historyItems` from `projectSettledCodexMessages`) and a `clientFactory` that wraps the real `createIsolatedCodexAppServerClient` (managed `@openai/codex` 0.153.0 binary, `homeScope: "user"`, native ChatGPT auth) with a `request` spy so the literal `thread/inject_items` params are recorded as they go to the app-server. Nothing is faked between the projection and OpenAI. The source transcript is the same 83-character `call_` id used by the unit tests. The base side runs the projection file checked out at `d2a616bdf3` (the merge base) through the identical path.

**Result.** Same request sequence on both sides:

```text
model/list -> config/read -> configRequirements/read -> thread/start
  -> mcpServerStatus/list -> thread/inject_items -> turn/start
```

| | on-the-wire `call_id` (from the recorded `thread/inject_items` params) | live Responses outcome |
|---|---|---|
| base `d2a616bdf3` | `83, 83` — the raw id forwarded verbatim | **rejected, HTTP 400**: `[StringParam] [input[3].call_id] [string_above_max_length] Invalid 'input[3].call_id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.` |
| this branch `c7ce0f4eee` | `64, 64` — `call_aaaa…aaaa_d7395395db`, identical on `function_call` and `function_call_output` | **accepted, turn completed**: final assistant text `Done—the update has been sent.` (usage: 2795 input / 11 output tokens) |

The base-side 400 is byte-for-byte the error class from #130965, produced by the live API from the unmodified projection, so the reproduction and the fix were measured against the same provider on the same day.

<details>
<summary>Recorded <code>thread/inject_items</code> payload on this branch (verbatim, synthetic content, nothing redacted)</summary>

```json
[
  { "type": "message", "role": "user",
    "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "Send the update." }] },
  { "type": "function_call",
    "call_id": "call_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa_d7395395db",
    "name": "message", "arguments": "{\"action\":\"send\"}" },
  { "type": "function_call_output",
    "call_id": "call_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa_d7395395db",
    "output": "Message sent." }
]
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Base-side live error, as thrown by <code>runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn</code></summary>

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": null,
    "message": "[StringParam] [input[3].call_id] [string_above_max_length] Invalid 'input[3].call_id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.",
    "param": null
  },
  "status": 400
}
```

</details>

**Honest notes on the run.** (1) The first attempt failed on both sides with a `401 Missing bearer` because the repo's live-test harness stages `auth.json` under an isolated `HOME` while the user-scope home resolver consults the mocked `os.homedir()`; pinning `CODEX_HOME` to the staged home fixed the harness, and only the second run is reported above. (2) The model was the account's `live-default` selection; I have not hand-picked one. (3) The harness is not part of this PR's diff — it depends on a checked-out copy of the base projection and a harness-specific `CODEX_HOME` pin, neither of which belongs in the tree. I can commit an env-gated head-only version as a `*.live.test.ts` if maintainers want it in the suite; say the word.

### Rebase onto current `main` — head `7170120704`

Round 5 reported merge conflicts with main's newer typed history-rejection handling (#139933 replaced the projection's message-bearing `Error`s with `CodexHistoryRejection(reason)`). Rebased onto `aafe0878fd`. The production file merged cleanly — this PR adds no rejection sites, so no production line changed in the rebase. Only the test file conflicted: the fail-closed table and the laziness regression now assert on main's reason codes (`invalid_pairing` / `incomplete_pairing` / `item_limit`) instead of the retired message strings; assertions on the rewritten ids are unchanged. Mechanical, no behavior change, so no separate comment.

Proof on the rebased head: the five `settled-turn-*` suites **85 passed (85)**; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the three changed files **exit 0**; swapping in main's projection file makes **4 tests fail** (the injection-boundary test plus three projection regressions) and restoring this branch's file makes all 31 pass, so the regression coverage still bites on current `main`. `mergeable: MERGEABLE`.

### Re-port onto the `HistoryProjection` design — head `2c172601d2` (2026-09-13)

`main` rewrote this file after the last rebase: #143081 replaced the generator-based projection with a `HistoryProjection` class (`"reject"` mode for current-turn evidence, `"omit"` mode for prior turns) and now assembles the final injected array in `SettledTurnPriorContext.prependTo(current)`. A mechanical rebase was not possible, so this head is a re-implementation of the same reviewed semantics on the new structure (a second, test-only commit `2c172601d2` tightens three assertions after review; previous history is kept at the old head `7170120704` for comparison; the branch was rewritten on top of `4675c2b4d6`).

What is unchanged: the trigger (`length > 64` only; a 64-character id is byte-identical), the deterministic `call_` + clipped tail + sha256 rewrite, salting on clash, reservation of every verbatim id before any rewrite, laziness (the projection still rejects at `item_limit` / `byte_limit` before the caller's generator is drained), bookkeeping keyed on original ids, and the local-resolver rationale.

What moved: the rewrite now runs **once, in `prependTo`**, on the concatenated notice / prior-groups / current array, with the shared `seenCallIds` set as the reservation namespace. That is the one place ids leave the projection, and it means an overlength id in an earlier turn group is normalized the same way as one in the current turn — the old head only covered the current turn because prior context did not exist yet. `projectSettledCodexMessages` itself still returns original ids; `settled-turn-evidence.ts` is untouched.

Tests: the five ported regressions and the fail-closed table for both id shapes are back, plus two new cases for the new design — an overlength id inside a prior turn group, and a current raw id that equals what a prior overlength id would rewrite to (proving the salted re-derive works across the prior/current boundary). The injection-boundary test now assembles `historyItems` through `prependTo`, the same path production uses.

Proof on this head (local, macOS):
- Base-red: new tests against `main`'s projection file → **6 failed / 27 passed**, failing for the intended reasons (unrewritten 83-char id, `invalid_pairing` on the raw-id collision case, 65-char id passed through, prior-group id unrewritten, injection payload carries 83-char ids). Restoring this head → all green.
- Focused suites (`settled-turn-projection`, `settled-turn-injection`, `settled-turn-context`, `settled-turn-prior-context`, `settled-turn-finalizer`): **101 passed (101)**.
- Adjacent suite `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` under `test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex.config.ts`: **2907 passed; 8 failures, all in files this PR does not touch (`auth-refresh-authority.integration` fixture-manifest owner, `attempt-startup`, `managed-binary` host-shim detection: host-environment conditions, identical on base by construction since neither the tests nor their subjects are in this diff), then a vitest worker crash ended the run. CI is the authoritative adjacent signal**.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the three files: **exit 0, all 29 lanes green (plugin boundaries, extension test core imports, typecheck extensions + extension tests, lint, format, import cycles 0)**.
- Mutation checks: moving the trigger to `> 63` is killed by the 64-character passthrough test; skipping the clash retry loop is killed by both collision tests. Both reverted.
- Independent review before this push: three read-only reviewers on the commit (GLM 5.3, Opus 5, Kimi K3, all GO; their three MINOR findings, all test-side, are the follow-up commit).

The live authenticated trace above was taken on the old head and was not rerun; the wire shape it proved (`inject_items` carrying 64-character ids) is what the boundary test pins on this head.

### On the `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` label

I read that label as "does not recommend queueing a new **automated** fix PR", not as a moratorium on human contributions — and the ClawSweeper comment states plainly why the automation stopped: *"Reproducibility: no… the authoritative Codex behavior and a current finalization trace could not be inspected."* That is precisely the gap closed above: a reproduction on current `main`, and the authoritative Codex injection contract read at a pinned tag with file:line citations. If that reading is wrong, or if this belongs to someone already, close it and I will step aside without argument.

prs.title: fix(ui): renaming, pinning or changing settings moves sessions to the top of Last updated
prs.body:
Related: #194839

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with the sidebar sorted by **Last updated**, sessions jump to the top when you rename, pin, unpin, archive, restore, snooze or wake them, change their group, change chat settings (model, thinking, speed, context window, permissions), share them, or mark them read or unread, even though nothing new happened in the conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: the **Last updated** sort now moves a session only for conversation activity, like a message you send or an agent reply or run result. Organizing a session or changing its settings leaves it where it was. Sessions with no recorded activity keep their previous position, based on their last recorded change. The sort label is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar sorted this mode by `updatedAt`, which the Gateway advances on almost every write to a session, settings changes included. Agent turns already record real activity in `lastActivityAt`, and the user's message time in `lastInteractionAt`. The shared `sessionActivityTimestamp` helper already turns those into one "latest activity" time and falls back to `updatedAt`; the Activity page uses the same helper. The sidebar's Last updated comparator now uses that helper. Including `lastInteractionAt` means a session you just messaged moves up when you send, rather than only when the reply arrives.

The Gateway's list paging still uses `updatedAt`. Every activity write also advances `updatedAt`, so any session with recent activity is always inside the loaded 200-session window. The accepted edge case: past that window, the tail of a very large roster may miss a few sessions whose activity is older than the window's cutoff. The Created sort already pages this way.

## Landing order

1. **#194839 lands first**, unchanged. It stops mark read/unread from advancing `updatedAt`. That still matters after this PR: sessions without activity clocks fall back to `updatedAt`, and other consumers still read it (API callers' default order, the Sessions page Updated column).
2. **This PR lands second.** The two PRs touch separate files. I agreed this with the session that owns #194839: it owns `src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts`, its test, `session-unread-ack.ts` and its one-line docs addition; this PR owns the sidebar comparator, the sessions navigation helpers and the sort paragraph in `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md`. If this PR merges first, nothing conflicts or breaks. The order only keeps the history readable.

## Evidence

- **Regression test:** `orders Updated mode by conversation activity, not metadata writes` in `app-sidebar-session-navigation-logic.test.ts`. It fails on the base comparator (`metadata-touched` sorts first) and passes with the fix. The file passes 33/33.
- **Sibling suites:** `app-sidebar.sessions.test.ts`, `lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` and `app-sidebar-session-tree.test.ts` pass 132/132.
- **Browser check (mocked Gateway, not committed):** three synthetic sessions. *Renamed earlier chat* has the newest `updatedAt` and the oldest activity, *Latest reply* has the newest activity, and *Legacy without activity* has no activity clocks. With **Last updated** selected, the base build shows the renamed chat on top; the fix shows Latest reply → Legacy → Renamed.

Before (base):

![Before: Last updated puts the renamed session first](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c563f009-fdef-419d-b7e4-8fff9514485c)

After (this PR):

![After: Last updated follows conversation activity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f75c7285-a297-4b35-93f4-f97723881124)

- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` pass, oxlint finds no problems in the 3 changed files, format check and `git diff --check` are clean.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, merge-base → `3a76ae22b54d`, priority up to P2) was scoped-clean with no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't available on this host.
- **Gaps:** I didn't run a real Gateway and model end to end. That the Gateway advances `updatedAt` on metadata writes is already covered by the existing `sessions-patch.test.ts` assertions for pin and rename. I didn't audit whether every message source records `lastActivityAt`, for example channel messages that arrive without starting a turn, or messages added to a session from outside it. Sources that don't record it keep the current `updatedAt` behavior.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(discord): channel edits persist applied forum tags
prs.body:
Related: #36736

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord `channel-edit` reports success without changing forum or media thread tags when `appliedTags` is provided.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can replace or clear a Discord forum thread applied tags through `channel-edit`, so Kanban status changes persist instead of silently no-oping.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action schema already exposes `appliedTags`, but the Discord channel-edit parser, payload type, and REST adapter did not carry it to Discord `applied_tags` field. This change wires the value through and deliberately preserves an explicit empty array for both camelCase and snake_case input so callers can clear every tag.

## Evidence

- Focused shared-reader regressions pass: 34/34, including direct-key and snake_case empty arrays.
- Focused Discord parser regressions pass: 7/7, including `appliedTags`, `applied_tags`, replacement, and clearing.
- Full Discord extension lane passed 258 test files and 2,682 tests before the final review fix.
- Updated-head CI is green, including channel tests, type checks, lint, boundaries, CodeQL, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Live Discord behavior proof

Run at 2026-11-07T21:57:21Z against a completed forum card. The script imported this PR head `readDiscordChannelEditParams` and `editChannelDiscord`, used `applied_tags: []` to exercise the snake_case path, and independently read the channel from Discord after each PATCH. Credentials and raw tag IDs are omitted.

```text
exercised:
  - readDiscordChannelEditParams
  - editChannelDiscord
  - independent Discord GET /channels/:id

before:
  name: Neon Goals TODOs
  applied_tags: [Done, Automation]

clear:
  input: { applied_tags: [] }
  parsed: { appliedTags: [] }
  PATCH response applied_tags: []
  independent readback applied_tags: []

restore:
  input appliedTags: [Done, Automation]
  parsed appliedTags: [Done, Automation]
  PATCH response applied_tags: [Done, Automation]
  independent readback applied_tags: [Done, Automation]
  exact_original_restored: true
```

This proves both explicit clearing through the previously broken snake_case alias and non-empty replacement through the changed parser and REST adapter against live Discord.

prs.title: fix: active tool sessions report idle after steering
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes diagnostics reporting an idle session while its run is still executing a tool, after a steering message finishes dispatching or falls back to the follow-up queue.

## User Impact

Long-running-session logs and diagnostic events retain `processing` with `activeWorkKind=tool_call` during active execution. Queue accounting still consumes the completed dispatch without counting the active original input as backlog. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Message completion was unconditionally publishing session idle. The message-lifecycle producer now shares its existing controller lookup between arrival and completion, while the diagnostic writer can consume the completed input independently of the published state. Controller retirement remains authoritative. Production code grows by two lines to separate message accounting from run state, with no new cache or scan.

The Control UI uses a separate run projection and pending-input capability, so no UI production change is needed. A mocked-Gateway regression verifies a 215-second active exec with a 30-second pending steer shows Stop and Send now, and targets the exact input. The existing 120-second transcript-commit timeout can withdraw a steer and remove its Send now capability after follow-up fallback; this PR does not change that policy.

Related: #193665. Complements #194805 without changing its files or presentation.

## Evidence

The heartbeat regression fails on base `ec41ea83a44cf84f2cdc1cf4a7d7b0983523952c` with `state=idle activeTool=exec reason=tool_execution_wait`, then passes with correct processing state and backlog. Focused core tests: 46 passed (new regression 21 ms). UI E2E: 12 passed (18.294 s test time); the final fixture rerun passed in 996 ms. Component/access and Chromium sidebar tests: 40 passed (7.05 s). CI duration is pending.

Codex autoreview of the complete local change against that base: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings (fresh review after the gate-driven correction). The test-line allocation covers exactly 134 new lines for the distinct diagnostic-owner and browser contracts; the benchmark adds 185 proof-only lines.

`check:changed` completed red. It caught a patch-local import cycle and test lint pattern, both repaired; final targeted lint/types/format and cycle checks pass. Remaining main regressions: 20 historical attribution violations introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364), unused `OpenClawShell` reported after `adca0b0844c7` (#194815), and unused `CommandPaletteOpenDetail` introduced by `9151ac22e005`. All reproduce on the exact base; the two Knip reproductions reuse the existing same-base lane proof. No overall green or guard exception is claimed.

The committed `scripts/perf/diagnostic-state-measure.ts` uses 4,096 resident controller identities, 2,000 diagnostic entries, an outstanding exec and one queued input. Each measured steer constructs a fresh message lifecycle. Four A/A controls, five interleaved before/after pairs, separate allocation passes and CPU profiles cover two million dispatches. Every queue-count assertion passed; incorrect idle observations fell from every baseline sample to zero.

| Warm owner dispatch | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median / p95 | 833 / 1,083 ns | 1,250 / 1,458 ns |
| CPU per dispatch | 1,394 ns | 1,776 ns |
| Sampled allocation per dispatch | 2,789 B | 4,122 B |

This is a correctness cost, not a speedup: the additional indexed lookup and shared lifecycle helper add 417 ns median, approximately 0.38 microseconds CPU and 1.3 KB sampled allocation per steer. Median increases 50.06%, CPU 27.35%, allocation 47.82%; these exceed A/A variation and are retained as a small absolute per-message correctness cost. All five paired CPU changes were positive; A/A CPU ranged 139.161–146.594 ms per 100,000 actions. The benchmark excludes import/setup, diagnostic subscribers, database/workspace I/O, transport and real tool/provider execution. It makes no cold-start or full-Gateway performance claim. No live deployment was accessed.

prs.title: fix: exec refuses every command once lost launches fill the spawn broker
prs.body:
Related: #177656

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every exec fails with `Spawn broker request capacity exceeded` until the Gateway restarts, once enough commands have been lost between their launch grant and the broker's ownership receipt.

## User Impact

User impact: a command the Gateway loses after granting its launch no longer leaves a slot behind in the spawn broker, so a long-running Gateway keeps running exec instead of refusing every command after about 256 such losses.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the service-child relay fails a command after the host has granted its launch, but before the broker's `owned` receipt arrives, the host retires the request at `owned`. The broker then transfers that command's pipes. The host's branch for requests it no longer tracks answered each transfer with `pipe-received` only. The broker forgets an owned command only once every transferred fd is drained (`forget()` in `worker.ts`), so that entry stayed in its owned map for the life of the Gateway and counted toward the cap.

The untracked-pipe branch now also sends `output-drained` with an error for that fd. That is the same acknowledgement `BrokerChild.attachPipe` already sends for tracked requests. The helper is in `pipe.ts` because `host.ts` is at its 700-line cap.

This is the leak in [KarolAdamiec's heap readings on #177656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6629331547): one `owned` entry with `openPipes=1` left per post-launch identity loss, until the broker hit 256 and exec was dead for about 9 h. The host-side `nativeInitiated` path from [an earlier comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6546377246) does not leak on main: the worker answers `launch allowed:false` with an `error` frame, which clears it.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`host-transport-retirement.test.ts`): drives prepare -> launch -> relay loss -> `owned` -> `pipe` through the existing synthetic broker fixture. On main `24401ee0555d` it fails with `expected undefined to match object { type: 'output-drained', ... }`; with this change it passes. No timers: one `setImmediate` turn after `pipe-received`.
- **Suites**, macOS arm64, Node 26.13.0: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/spawn-broker/ src/process/supervisor/` gives 449 passed, 16 skipped (Linux-only cases), 0 failed. These ran under Node because the default Bun runtime skips the broker's real command transport.
- **`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 24401ee0555d`**: line cap, oxlint, format, core typecheck and the other ratchets pass. Three gates fail, and they fail identically on unmodified `24401ee0555d`:
  - the mock-export ratchet on two `ui/src` tests;
  - TS1117 in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-terminal.ts`;
  - two unused exports, `QUALIFIED_PACKAGE_SMOKE_LANES` and `sessionStopCopyKey`.
- **Test cost:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/spawn-broker/host-transport-retirement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 23.3 s wall for the whole file (18 tests, mostly startup). The new test runs in 1-2 ms.
- **Our two Mac mini Gateways** (logs, read-only):
  - Before #169584/#167739, cleanup identity loss was frequent. On a 10.5/10.6-based build, mac-mini logged 9-14 `[process/supervisor] spawn failed ... cleanup identity lost` a day (83 over 10-24..10-30, 458 agent turns).
  - That trigger is gone on 10.10 code: 0 spawn failures of any kind from 2026-10-31 07:30Z to now, over 405 agent turns, on 10.10-beta.4/beta.5-based builds.
  - Identity loss still happens there for other reasons: two `service child cleanup identity lost: anchor channel closed without a matching closing receipt` on 2026-11-02, on the beta.5-based build.
  - Neither host has reached the 256 cap, because both restart for deploys every few days, so they do not show the leak itself.

Not covered: I did not reproduce the full chain with a real relay losing identity inside that window, and I did not run on Linux. The test pins the host's half of the protocol, the half that was missing.

prs.title: perf(gateway): preserve nested row identities across publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming session updates repeatedly hash byte-identical nested row fields because actor transfers and row producers replace their object identities. The existing frozen-value fingerprint reuse cannot help when each publication supplies a new frozen object.

## User Impact

Reduces session-event and activity-summary publication CPU while preserving nested replacement detection and emitted row/delta values. No configuration, protocol, or database schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Turn results are already detached by the actor phase owner, so receipts can use the existing entry delta. Restore list metadata from the canonical entry with the existing snapshot-stripping helper. Retain common nested fields once during materialization/fact replacement, before audience fanout. Keep the preceding observed variants in the existing publication owner and retain recipient-dependent fields only after current source, clock, recipient, and permission checks. No consumer fingerprint cache is added.

Production LOC is +67 (144 added / 77 removed); the actor repair is net zero. The growth supplies bounded producer identity continuity and order-preserving structural sharing. Ordinary deep equality ignores property order, while serializing for equality would recreate encoding/allocation work. Profile projection moves unchanged to its existing identity owner to keep the row module within its size limit.

## Evidence

The benchmark uses real input-actor admission, SQLite transcript/tool writes, replica receipts, row projection, presentation, and event fanout: 2,000 synthetic sessions, 64 child links, 20 client sinks across three audiences, usage/model updates, people/sharing fields, and unchanged/replaced activity summaries. No handcrafted frozen row inputs. Separate real Gateway/socket integration covers transport and delta/legacy payloads.

Across 64 measured updates after 32 warmup updates, nested hashing falls from **685 calls / 2,932,257 input bytes** to **six calls / 3,530 bytes**. The remaining calls are two deliberate summary replacements across three audiences. **Unchanged nested values trigger zero hashes.** The dominant repeated input is toolOverrides: 62 × 43,978 bytes (93% of input bytes); people/profile/runtime fields repeat once per publication, while activitySummary repeats per audience. Inputs were deeply frozen but newly allocated, not mutable.

Five alternating AB/BA pairs plus A/A controls compare exact parent 28a5a66d0703003576563c95b0b492f94200a499 with head 98b271eb43f213d79fccd34404b6a664de8795c7. All 24 serial processes passed; CPU and allocation use separate runs. Node 24.22.1 on Apple M3 Ultra. Median columns are medians of arm means; paired percentages are medians of paired ratios.

| Per update | Before | After | Median paired change | A/A drift |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 6.290 ms | 5.473 ms | -13.00% | +0.32% |
| Row-consume CPU | 1.236 ms | 1.031 ms | -16.59% | -0.98% |
| Row-consume wall | 1.234 ms | 1.029 ms | -16.65% | -1.00% |
| Sampled allocation | 3,293,988 B | 3,222,655 B | -1.86% | +1.42% |

CPU paired changes: -11.15%, -12.79%, -14.38%, -18.98%, -13.00%. Consume CPU: -13.20%, -16.59%, -17.76%, -19.87%, -15.73%. Allocation: -2.24%, -1.96%, -1.71%, -1.80%, -1.86%. Allocation reduction is modest relative to control drift; this is not a large-allocation-improvement claim. Allocation uses V8 Inspector sampling at 4,096 bytes, including collected objects. Worker CPU/allocation is excluded. This resident-row fixture does not reproduce production database size or production stall magnitude.

The first implementation compared large common fields per audience and regressed consume CPU; it was replaced with producer sharing before fanout. Final regression coverage proves three redundant common-field traversals become zero.

A phase caveat: total CPU for the first measured summary replacement rises about 3 ms, while later replacement and summary-consume timings improve. A separate post-matrix CPU/GC profile attributes this to collection timing: baseline minor GC at update 63 (3.12 ms), candidate minor GC at update 64 (2.38 ms during the pump, outside consume). Selection/preparation and replacement work are comparable; neither arm collects at update 96. Profile totals are not used for performance claims because profiling adds overhead.

## Validation

- Before-fix regressions captured for native actor receipt identity, list metadata restoration, real-publication hash work, and redundant common-field audience traversal.
- Producer/delta, native receipt, owner, and real Gateway/socket coverage pass. After consolidation, all 20 tests in the two edited files pass (29.21 seconds total wrapper wall time). Coverage includes exact delta JSON, nested replacements, permission changes, nested property order, array length/holes, snapshot omission, and writable public-result independence.
- Across five pairs, 9,800 captured frames match as ordered JSON after removing only independent-worker updatedAt and scheduling-dependent snapshotAt fields. Controlled tests verify exact delta bytes without normalization.
- Three Control UI browser tests and 15 UI end-to-end tests pass; production UI bundle builds.
- Independent Codex autoreview, including the test consolidation, is scoped-clean through P2.
- Test-line budget: removed 13 redundant lines, reducing the PR delta from +298 to +285. The allocation grants exactly 285 for producer identity continuity, with no extra credit. The ratchet passes against CI base 3651abf03ad802976e1a9a6fd46967ef96ef2e38 using --no-merge-base on the original CI merge plus this follow-up: 6,569,109 lines / 6,569,235 ceiling; the base’s existing 126-line headroom is unchanged. Production code and measured performance are unchanged from 98b271eb43f213d79fccd34404b6a664de8795c7.
- pnpm check:changed completes with all selected checks passing except the changelog attribution gate. That failure reproduces on exact parent 28a5a66d0703003576563c95b0b492f94200a499; commit 266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957 (#194364) introduced the excluded handles while existing thanks lines remained. This is a main regression requiring repair, not a passing check.

No production data or server access was used. Do not merge as part of this task.

prs.title: fix: unblock retained repair after a reviewed config change
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained forward repair being blocked when an operator's native config replacement prevents rollback and the failed selected release cannot pass readiness.

Related: #194584.

## User Impact

Operators can append the reviewed `CONFIG_SHA256` to `--prepare-retained-repair OPERATION TARGET CURRENT PID START JOURNAL_SHA256`. Activation inherits that approval through its exact build receipt. Preparation needs no CPU-load flag; full target acceptance remains mandatory. The native audit row and separate config backup are still required: successful `agents.delete` alone does not prove that its best-effort audit persisted. Controller adoption and deployment remain separate operator actions; this PR performs neither.

## Why This Change Was Made

In the November 7 incident, a deleted-agent readiness refusal left a failed candidate serving in `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, while an atomic config replacement blocked rollback. Ordinary config reconciliation still waited for that broken candidate to become ready. Retained repair now reuses the existing reconciliation snapshot, audit and backup, with the original journal and live process bindings.

The prepared config descriptor owns config identity throughout preparation, activation-shell checks, resume, and the native start condition. Historical SQLite identity and all other guards remain. Original journal bytes are archived unchanged. No schema, cache, runtime configuration option, or verification bypass is added. Production delta is **+12 lines**: optional approval routing and a validated identity projection for the existing shell guard; redundant historical config checks are removed.

## Evidence

Rebased without conflicts onto exact main parent `f6a8ce9a6f2207121b7ffd5c6d65365fe1875d84`, which contains `fd83c2d5` and `16463ef4`.

- New config-binding regression fails on the exact main controller at the unsupported reviewed input; its preceding unreviewed assertion reproduces the original protected-identity refusal.
- Real systemd PID1 regression: **3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. It uses the installed root `ExecCondition`, private cgroup v2, real procfs/D-Bus/listener/flock, actual shell identity-loading functions, and real library lifecycle transitions. The reviewed config passes bind/resume/start; a later replacement blocks resume and native execution before claim publication. Original journal bytes remain unchanged.
- The same native proof fails on the original PR at `repair claim protected store changed`. Strengthening it with the actual shell consumer also exposed a pre-bind refusal, repaired by consuming the owner's prepared identity projection.
- The synthetic target deliberately returns readiness 503 and premature completion is refused. This proves native start admission and refusal, **not** successful real Gateway/model acceptance. Existing strict acceptance remains mandatory.
- Every controller test file is included in identical-command paired runs, using one pinned Linux image: Node 26.12.1, Bun 1.4.3, pnpm 12.15.0, Prometheus 3.2.1, `umask 022`. Node command: `/usr/bin/node --import ./test-environment.mjs --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-reporter=tap ./*.test.mjs`. Exact main: **384 passed / 388 failed / 0 skipped**. **Candidate: 392 passed / 388 failed / 1 skipped** (781 tests, 581.585 seconds versus main 772 tests, 687.553 seconds). The complete failing-name multisets match: **zero new failures and zero resolved failures**. Eight new passes cover reviewed binding, rejection guards, CLI contention, and shell preparation; one existing contention test was renamed without removing coverage. The service-mutating native test is deliberately opt-in and also run separately under real systemd.
- Both Python files and Prometheus run too. Health-check Python passes 5/5 on each arm; launcher Python passes 5/5 on each arm as required non-root `nobody`; Prometheus reports SUCCESS for all six scenario groups on both. The initial root-user launcher refusal was a setup error, not a main regression.
- `pnpm check:changed --staged --base f6a8ce9a6f2207121b7ffd5c6d65365fe1875d84`: every selected check passed except 20 changelog-attribution violations reproduced on the exact parent and introduced by #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`).
- Fresh full-owner Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2 on the final source. Current head: `93339d6d38d43b3121da2c04b226136788327ebf`; **[exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42433136469)**: 27 successful jobs, 30 scope skips, zero failed/cancelled jobs, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Earlier cancelled PR-context/auto-response runs have successful successor runs. The PR remains open and unmerged for lead landing.

<details>
<summary>All exact-parent controller failures are attributed</summary>

The 388 failures consist of 386 failing leaves and two failing parent tests. They are existing main regressions, not noise:

| Root cause | Failing leaves | Introducing commit / PR |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Library FD9/canonical-lock admission missing in old callers/fixtures | 290 | `3efe1deca653` / #193647 |
| Duplicate fixture lock creation | 47 | `3efe1deca653` / #193647 |
| Extracted drain shell leaves `mode` unset | 35 | `3efe1deca653` / #193647 |
| Stale maintenance-call ordering assertion | 1 | `3efe1deca653` / #193647 |
| Deleted `migration_stop_contract` still called | 11 | `aee12b63234c` / #169752 |
| Ordinary rollback lacks the required handoff instance | 2 | `a968dc19900d` / #187090 |

Each attribution has `git log -S` and raw introducing-parent patch evidence. A bounded unchanged-parent diagnostic replay captured actual failed-child stderr for the seven previously opaque journal/handoff assertions: two are lock refusals, five call the deleted helper. No baseline source or assertions were changed. Earlier container umask/pnpm setup gaps were corrected before the paired run. Prior-run-only process-census races are not claimed fixed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Preserved production-shaped synthetic measurement</summary>

Synthetic btrfs fixture: physically allocated 35.05-GiB agent SQLite file, 4,097 sessions, 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.10 GiB. No production data. Five alternating fresh-process samples per arm after contention cleared:

| Snapshot owner path | Median wall | Median CPU | Peak RSS | Sampled V8 allocations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base A/A control 1, unchanged config | 132.52 ms | 138.41 ms | 91.70 MiB | 18.87 MiB |
| Base A/A control 2, unchanged config | 136.48 ms | 138.55 ms | 91.15 MiB | 18.22 MiB |
| Fixed, unchanged config | 129.23 ms | 142.09 ms | 91.57 MiB | 18.78 MiB |
| Base incident, refused | 36.74 ms | 41.32 ms | 57.26 MiB | 2.57 MiB |
| Fixed incident, reviewed snapshot accepted | 135.24 ms | 145.12 ms | 92.28 MiB | 19.66 MiB |

No speedup claim: refusal and successful evidence capture perform different work. Allocation figures are inspector sampling estimates. The final shell/native-consumer corrections do not change this snapshot owner; prior measurements were preserved rather than repeated. Production grows by 12 lines, regression tests by 198, fixture support by 31. No default CI/Vitest workload is added.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep Last updated position when marking a session unread
prs.body:
## Problem

Choosing **Mark as unread** on a session bumped its `updatedAt`, so with the sidebar sorted by **Last updated** the row jumped to the top. Marking unread is a reminder, not session activity; the row should stay where it is.

Read acknowledgements (`unread: false`) and icon/color-only patches were already recency-neutral (#170405); `unread: true` was the remaining exception.

## Solution

`applySessionsPatchToStore` now treats any read-marker-only patch (`unread: true` or `unread: false`, plus only its identity/CAS preconditions) as recency-neutral via the existing `isReadMarkerOnly` owner in `session-unread-ack.ts`. Patches that combine unread with real changes (pin, rename, archive, …) still age the row as before.

`markedUnreadAt` still advances on every mark, so the conditional-ack revision is unchanged.

## Impact

- Single and batch **Mark as unread** keep the row's Last updated position.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` notes read/unread marks are not session activity.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` › "commits read and unread marks without ageing the session row": **red on base** (`expected 1794090536933 to be 1`), green with fix.
- `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts`: 99/99 pass.
- Related Gateway server suites (`server-methods.session-narrow-mutations`, `server.sessions.list-changed`, `server.sessions.store-rpc`, `server.sessions.patch-expected-identity`): 76/76 pass.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean.
- Gap: no live Control UI e2e run; the change is confined to the Gateway's `updatedAt` decision, which the sidebar's Updated sort reads directly.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(gateway): limit restricted roles to public repositories
prs.body:
## Problem

Roles without `operator.write` (on the team Gateway: `guest` with `operator.sessions.write`, and `contributor`) could discover and obtain the source of admin-registered private org repositories (for example `openclaw/openclaworg`). Every path read the shared project registry with no requester check:

- the New session picker (`projects.list`, `projects.checkoutOptions`)
- `sessions.create` with a registry `projectId`
- background (`visible: false`) agent spawns with `projectId`
- children that inherit their parent's checkout
- pasting the repository URL: `projectGitUrl` reused the registry row and refreshed it with the Gateway's GitHub token
- contributors only: project skills via `commands.list`, and `worktrees.list` (every session's paths, repo roots and branches)

## Solution

- New predicate owner `src/gateway/project-access.ts`. A caller without `operator.write` may use a project when it is an agent-workspace pseudo-project (still governed by `roles.agents`), or when its origin is `owner/repo` on the configured GitHub host and `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}` reports `visibility === "public"`. Private, Enterprise `internal`, non-GitHub, credential-bearing or non-default HTTPS-port origins, 404s, rate limits and failures all deny. It reuses `gitHubPublicApi.fetchGitHubJson`, with the server token when available.
- Discovery (`projects.list`, `checkoutOptions`, `commands.list` project skills) caches definitive answers (200, 404) for 10 minutes per API base + `owner/repo`. Every source handoff (`sessions.create`, background spawn, inherited checkout) starts its own GitHub request; it cannot join an earlier in-flight discovery lookup.
- Enforcement sits at requester-aware call sites, not in the registry readers; `projects.remove`, Doctor, clone de-duplication and scratch maintenance keep the raw registry.
  - `sessions.create`: connection scopes; client-less in-process dispatch stays internal. A hidden project returns the same `unknown project id` as a missing one.
  - background spawns: the admitted operator run's effective scopes (membership caps included), else the creator's live role. Owner, cron and unlinked runs stay internal.
  - inherited children (`prepareSessionWorktreeCreation`): the child's requester must reach the parent's project or repository URL; a cwd-based parent without a project is allowed only when it is an agent workspace.
- Scopes: `sessions.create` with `projectGitUrl`, `projects.searchRemote` and `worktrees.list` now need `operator.write`. `worktrees.list` lists host paths for every session, so it is raised rather than filtered; UI callers already tolerate a failed call. `projects.list` returns `defaultRepository` only to writers.
- Control UI: non-write callers get no GitHub search or URL entry. A saved or selected project the Gateway no longer lists falls back to the agent workspace, and a saved repository URL is not restored for non-write callers.
- Docs: `gateway/operator-scopes.md`, `web/control-ui.md`, `concepts/managed-worktrees.md`.

## Accepted edge cases

- Existing checkouts are kept; forking or resetting your own old session on a now-hidden repo re-copies it.
- A repo turning private can stay in the picker (and `commands.list`, `checkoutOptions`) for up to 10 minutes; handoffs are blocked right away.
- Non-GitHub and credential-bearing origins become write-only. Restricted roles lose clone-by-URL, even for public repos. GitHub Enterprise restricted users see public repos only.
- Without a server token, lookups are anonymous (60/h); a rate limit or a missing bundled `github` plugin hides even public repos (fails closed).
- A hidden saved project switches to the workspace without a notice; hidden and removed projects look the same.

## Screenshots

Guest (`operator.sessions.write`) with a saved selection of the private `openclaw/openclaworg` project, then pasting its URL. Same Control UI e2e scenario for both rows (mocked Gateway, synthetic data). **Before:** the UI from this PR's base on `main`, with the full `projects.list` that `main`'s Gateway returns to guests. **After:** this PR's head `98d7168e`, with the list this PR's Gateway returns (private repository filtered out).

| | Saved selection | Paste repository URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before (`main`) | ![before: private repo restored for the guest](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01f93a2e-036a-48a9-bf4b-7110c584126a) | ![before: clone offered for the private repo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ab78f99-a15b-458d-81c4-c043653fb953) |
| After (this PR) | ![after: falls back to the openclaw workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61806160-cf44-480a-adba-894ee1a72f43) | ![after: no clone option](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8cd9f2d4-2779-477d-b1e1-04d4fa31ed3e) |

## Evidence

Preparation evidence (`d3a377e107f`):
- Fixed two independently reviewed visibility defects: non-default HTTPS ports must not borrow another endpoint's public status, and fresh source admission must not reuse an older discovery request. Both red assertions were observed before the interrupted red run; the repaired tests pass.
- **134 focused tests pass** across project access (4), session/checkout admission (2), project handlers (30), project skill discovery (4), native spawn/inheritance (13), and method scopes (81). Each file ran via `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; measured walls respectively **18.05s, 20.25s, 30.86s, 22.68s, 31.75s, 14.80s**, including harness/compiler overhead. CI seconds for this revision are pending. Unchanged UI behavior reuses the author's rendered/e2e evidence; fixture-only internal-requester literal replacements were typechecked.
- Core types, all six affected test type graphs, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, the exact test-line allocation, and `git diff --check` pass. Unused-file scanning passes. Dependency/export scans remain red only in unchanged `src/process/command-reservation-census.ts` (`parseDarwinProcessBirths`) and `scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts` (gesture exports); this PR's unused exports were removed.
- Fresh independent autoreview completed. Its assertion defect was repaired and rechecked. Its proposal to deny all no-creator native runs was declined: this change explicitly preserves owner/cron/unlinked internal access; admitted operators carry effective scopes, including empty membership caps, and identified creator fallback uses the existing role-policy owner. Request/session/dispatch owners retain current authority checks after awaits and at effects.
- Already obtained on incoming `98d7168e`: an isolated real Gateway with synthetic role/device identities and signed WebSocket transport, using anonymous real GitHub REST public/404 responses. Guest and contributor identities listed/opened the public project, could not create the unavailable project, and were denied URL/search/worktree scope paths; admin retained visibility. No personal or Team Gateway was touched. This is real public/404 transport evidence, not real private/internal-repository proof.

Author validation before preparation (retained for unchanged inputs):
- Base run: the 18 changed production files reverted to the base (new `project-access.ts` kept so imports resolve), then every changed unit test file run. 12 tests in 7 files failed on assertions, none on setup, and pass with the fix; one of them (the `project-chip` unavailable label) was later removed with that label. Remaining: subagent-spawn-session-patch 2, method-scopes.own-session 3, commands.project-skills 1, projects 3, server.sessions.create.sandbox-project 1, session-method-access 1. `project-access.test.ts` tests the new helper directly; 4 other updated test files pass on both and are not regression proof.
  - `server.sessions.create.sandbox-project.test.ts`: a guest and a contributor through `handleGatewayRequest` with role config: the private repo is missing from `projects.list`, `checkoutOptions` is not current, `sessions.create` with its `projectId` returns `unknown project id`, and `projectGitUrl`, `projects.searchRemote` and `worktrees.list` are refused.

  - `commands.project-skills.test.ts`: a contributor sees only the public repo's skills; an admin sees both.
  - `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.project-access.e2e.test.ts`: writer vs guest picker; the guest's saved private project falls back to the workspace.
- Consumer suites pass, including `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn.test.ts` (39) and 13 New session UI unit files (167 tests).

Consolidated duplicate handler setup and removed a redundant UI scope mirror; all six independent access boundaries remain. The access module is 201 lines, down from 215, with test-only fetch/cache-reset hooks removed and implementation helpers kept private.

- No real private or Enterprise internal GitHub repository was queried; these visibility responses remain contract fixtures. No background spawn was driven by a real model. The isolated live observation below was obtained on the incoming head; the port and fresh-request repairs use focused regression/handler proof, with no new live campaign.
