prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/config/config-page.notifications.test.tsx src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts src/pages/config/notifications-section.test.tsx src/app/native-notifications.test.ts src/app/native-device-settings.test.ts src/app/web-push.test.ts --project unit --maxWorkers=1

prs.title: fix(signal): inbound message bursts pile up in memory and are lost on restart
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/127383

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a burst of inbound Signal messages piles up in Gateway memory, and is lost on restart or crash, because each message waits for its own database write and drain pass before the next one is stored.

This addresses part of the linked issue: the lasting pile-up and the loss. It adds no bound on memory (see the accepted edge cases below), so the bound that issue asks for stays open there.

## User Impact

User impact: a Signal account that receives a large burst (signal-cli pulling its backlog after a reconnect, or a busy group) moves the whole burst into the durable inbound queue within seconds. Nothing is dropped. A restart, shutdown or crash right after the burst loses none of the messages OpenClaw has read. The stored backlog is then delivered in order, at the same per-message speed as a small one.

This replaces the earlier revision of this PR, which paused the WebSocket while a message was stored. The signal-cli-rest-api container drops messages for a client that does not keep up (see Evidence), so the client must keep reading at full speed and the backlog has to go to the durable queue, not back to the container.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `main`, the Signal receive handler awaits `admit` for one event and then `waitForPumpIdle`, a full drain pass, before the client hands it the next frame. That is about 55 messages per second here. Everything the socket reads in the meantime stays in the client's promise chain, in memory, until its turn.

Now:
- The container client hands each decoded frame to the receive handler in arrival order without waiting for earlier ones. A shared promise still joins them for close and failure.
- The Signal ingress groups the events that arrive while one append runs into the next `admitBatch` transaction (up to 10,000 rows, about 0.4 s). Receive settles at the durable append; claiming and dispatch run on the drain as before. If a batch append fails, its events are appended one by one, so only the event that cannot be stored (or all of them, if the store is down) rejects.
- A graceful stop first appends every event the socket already read, then stops the monitor. If that takes longer than the client's 1.5 s shutdown wait, the client log now says the ingress stop still stores the events, instead of "messages may be lost".

The per-receive `waitForPumpIdle` came from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111449, so that messages accepted just before shutdown were not abandoned before their durable claim. `monitor.stop()` already awaits the admission tail and the pump before it returns, so that shutdown guarantee stays. A row appended just before stop is not claimed in that process, but it is durable and is claimed on the next start.

Storing the whole burst needs two changes in the shared ingress:

**Lane order in admission.** Pending rows drain by `(receivedAt, eventId)`, and one batch shares one `receivedAt`. In a group lane, event ids come from different senders, so a lane's arrival order need not be its id order. Shared admission now keeps each lane's last `(receivedAt, eventId)`:
- An event keeps its arrival time unless an earlier admission had a later one, or it would sort ahead of its lane's last row; then it steps 1 ms past that row. Other lanes keep their own time.
- Stepped rows can run ahead of wall time, so the lane tails are read from the queue once, before the first admission. A restart inside the step window cannot let a new event overtake older rows of its lane.
- Matrix seeded its own arrival time from the queue at start for the same reason. That copy is removed; Matrix now uses the shared admission.
- The SDK docs for `admitBatch` say so.

**Drain cost.** Each drain pass listed every unsettled row, so with 100,000 rows stored it took about 3.3 s per pass and delivered 66 rows in 120 s. The drain now reads the backlog in pages of 100 pending rows that skip lanes it already knows are blocked (claimed, retry-delayed, or started in this pass), with every claim in the same read snapshot. A lane stays blocked for the whole pass, so lane order and FIFO are unchanged. A pass ends when it has started its limit or the backlog ends. When only blocked lanes have pending rows, the read ends after one probe per blocked lane on the existing lane index instead of walking their rows. Channels that derive lanes, supersede pending work or prioritize (Telegram, Slack, Discord and others) still read one whole snapshot, as before.

### SDK addition

`ChannelIngressQueue.listUnsettled` takes three optional fields: `pendingLimit`, `after` (a `{ receivedAt, id }` cursor in `orderBy` order) and `excludeLaneKeys`. They bound one read's pending rows; every claim is still returned. A queue may ignore them and return every unsettled row, and the drain then behaves as before. The change is additive: no existing caller or queue changes, and no schema, index or migration changes. `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/state-and-system.md` names the fields.

Accepted edge cases, also named in the code:
- There is no bound on received events waiting in memory. While SQLite keeps up, the wait is short: the 100,000-frame burst below was durable in 7.6 s. If the state database stalls (full disk, broken database), later events wait in memory without limit, as they do on `main`. A bound would have to drop events or stop reading. Dropping recreates the loss this PR removes, and the container has no flow control: a client that stops reading makes the container drop instead (see Evidence). So the stall is made visible instead of bounded: past 50,000 waiting events (about 200 MiB of decoded messages) the ingress logs one error naming the state database, and logs again if the backlog drops and comes back. Nothing is dropped.
- Admission reads the whole unsettled queue once per monitor start, at the first admission, to seed the lane tails: about 3.3 s at 100,000 rows, nothing on an empty queue.
- While other lanes have pending rows, a page read still walks the index past the rows of a large blocked lane; only a read where nothing else is pending ends early.
- A page read excludes at most 1,000 blocked lanes, sent as one `NOT IN` list as `claimNext` already does, so it stays far below SQLite's bound-parameter limit. Past that limit the read returns rows of the other blocked lanes, and the drain skips them itself, so order is unchanged.

## Evidence

Tested at `c729be7e269` (base `upstream/main` `210d3df7f65`). The burst, crash and container measurements below were taken at `eda993f7f21`; the later changes are in admission ordering and the drain, outside the receive and store path they measure. Delivery was measured again at `2c9eb8f4977`, at the previous head `377edf16faf`, and on the base; the later commits change no drain path those runs take (the shared lane-tail read in admission, a bound on the excluded lanes that these one-lane runs stay far below, lint fixes, and a test-only change).

Harness: the plugin's real `streamContainerEvents` client and real `startSignalIngressMonitor`, writing to a real SQLite state database in an isolated state directory. Node 24, Linux x64. A local `ws` server in a worker thread stands in for the container's `/v1/receive` endpoint and sends synthetic receive frames of about 1 KB. The agent dispatch handler holds the first event, so the numbers measure receiving and storing. No Signal account.

100,000 frames, one direct-message lane: base stored 4,939 in 90 s; this PR stored all 100,000 in 7.6 s.

<details><summary>100,000-frame table</summary>

| | base | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| frames read by the client | 100,000 | 100,000 |
| durable in SQLite | 4,939 after 90 s | 100,000 after 7.6 s |
| heap growth | +129.4 MiB, still held at 90 s | peak +344 MiB during the first second, back to −1.3 MiB at 8 s |
| graceful stop | 93,207 receives failed with "Channel ingress monitor is stopped"; drain timed out, "messages may be lost" | nothing waiting |

</details>

The same run with 7 senders in one group lane: all 100,000 durable after 7.7 s, rows in arrival order, heap back to −1.3 MiB. The backlog warning fired once in both runs. The higher transient peak is the decoded burst plus the batch being written; on `main` the same burst stays in memory for as long as it takes to store at about 55 per second (about 30 minutes for 100,000). A smaller batch does not lower the peak: with 1,000 instead of 10,000 events per transaction it was +351 MiB instead of +356 MiB in a rerun at `c729be7e269`, and storing took 13% longer.

Crash (`kill -9` mid-burst, then reopen the state directory and count rows):
- This PR: killed at 1.35 s with 31,046 receives settled. After restart, SQLite has 31,046 rows, contiguous from the first frame. Every appended frame survived.
- Base: at 30.9 s only 3,000 were durable while all 100,000 had been read. After restart, 3,001 rows; the other 96,999 were only in memory.

Delivery after release (burst stored while dispatch is held for 30 s, then delivered for 120 s; every run delivered in order per lane):

| | base `210d3df7f65` | previous head `377edf16faf` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100,000 frames, one direct lane | 6,033 stored by the end; 3,250 delivered in 120 s, the rest of the burst still in memory | 100,000 stored; 66 delivered in 120 s | 100,000 stored; 49,709 delivered in 120 s |
| 2,000 frames, 7 senders in one group lane | 2,000 in 24.3 s | 2,000 in 24.4 s | 2,000 in 5.3 s |

Delivery no longer depends on how many rows are stored. The 2,000-row run is faster too, because base and the previous head also listed every unsettled row for each pass.

Real container: `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api:latest` (0.101) in json-rpc mode, with the signal-cli daemon inside it replaced by a synthetic JSON-RPC stand-in that sends receive notifications. The container itself drops messages. Its JSON-RPC reader hands each notification to the WebSocket handler with a non-blocking send, and drops it when the channel cannot take it:
- At 0.101, the image used here and the latest release, the receive channel is unbuffered ([`jsonrpc2.go` line 276](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/0.101/src/client/jsonrpc2.go#L276)), so a notification that arrives while the handler is still writing the previous one is dropped, however fast the client reads.
- At https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/commit/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1 on `master`, the channel holds 64 entries ([line 378](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1/src/client/jsonrpc2.go#L378)). The buffer came with https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/commit/ad0c2310325154b59b8bb5523e29a132a82326f8 (a manual receive mode) and is in no release yet. Once 64 are waiting behind the handler's write, the next one is dropped the same way.

In both versions, a client that pauses keeps the handler's write blocked, and every notification after that is dropped. That is why this PR keeps reading.

Measured through the container (0.101):
- 100,000 notifications at full speed: the container passed about 13,500 to OpenClaw on both sides. This PR stored all 13,594 it received, with +0.7 MiB heap. Base had stored 2,851 of 13,465 after 30 s, and its stop timed out with "messages may be lost".
- Paced at 20 notifications every 10 ms (20,000): the container still passed only 2,514; this PR stored all of them.
- One notification every 10 ms (2,000): this PR received, stored and delivered all 2,000 in order.

That loss is in the container and needs an upstream fix.

Regression tests (each fails on base and passes with this PR; the other tests in these files pass on both):
- `extensions/signal/src/signal-ingress.test.ts`, "appends a burst of received events in a few transactions, not one each": 50 concurrent receives, at most 2 appends. Base: `expected 50 to be less than or equal to 2`.
- `src/channels/message/ingress-monitor.admission.test.ts`, "keeps each lane in arrival order across a restart when event ids do not sort that way": a stepped batch, a new monitor on the same queue, then one event in the stepped lane and one in another lane. The previous head drains `sender-a:0` ahead of the older rows of its lane; base drains the lane out of order.
- `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts`, "starts a lane behind blocked busy lanes without reading their backlog": 5,000 rows behind a claimed head and 5,000 behind a retry-delayed head, then one row in a third lane. The pass starts only the third lane and reads fewer than 1,000 pending rows; base and the previous head read all 10,000 (`expected 10000 to be less than 1000`).
- `extensions/signal/src/client-container.websocket.test.ts`, "drains accepted and socket-buffered events before resolving shutdown", now also asserts that frame 2 reaches the receive handler while frame 1 is still held. Base: `expected [ 1 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 2 ]`.

Two guards pass on base and on this PR, and protect the new read: `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts`, "ends a pass when the queue ignores the page bounds" (a queue that returns every row for every read still ends the pass; without the check the pass never ends), and a `src/state/sqlite-query-plan.test.ts` case that keeps the lane probe on the covering lane index.

Checks:
- The touched test files pass.
- So do the other durable-ingress suites in `src/channels/message`, and the consumers of shared admission and the drain: Signal (`extensions/signal/src`), LINE `webhook-spool`, Matrix `monitor/ingress` and Telegram `polling-session`, plus the ingress tests of the other channels that use the shared drain.
- `pnpm check:changed` against `upstream/main`: typecheck, lint, the ratchets and the guards pass. Its two red lanes come from files outside this diff on `main`: changelog attributions in `CHANGELOG/records` and unused exports in `extensions/deep-research`.

<details><summary>Test cost</summary>

Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local; CI seconds come from this PR's run):

| Test file | local | new test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/signal/src/signal-ingress.test.ts` | 10.8 s (9 tests) | 501 ms |
| `src/channels/message/ingress-monitor.admission.test.ts` | 3.3 s (18 tests) | 38 ms |
| `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts` | 17.1 s (29 tests) | 518 ms (blocked lanes), 472 ms (page bounds) |
| `src/channels/message/ingress-monitor.test.ts` | 14.9 s (41 tests) | none new; one existing scan gate now waits for a read with pending rows |

</details>

Test-lines ratchet: these regressions and guards add 120 lines, so this PR adds `config/test-lines-allocations/signal-receive-batch-order.txt` for exactly those lines and leaves the shared baseline unchanged. `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 210d3df7f65` passes.

Simplification: shared admission now reads its lane tails through the same unsettled read as the drain, and Matrix's own arrival-time seeding is gone (-29 lines in Matrix). Against `main`: production +394/-176 (+325/-107 ignoring the re-indented drain loop), tests +127/-7 (the ratchet counts 120), docs +3/-1. Since the previous head `377edf16faf`: production +320/-180, tests +107/-38. The remaining growth is the paged read (new `ingress-drain-backlog.ts`, 61 lines, and the bounded branch and lane probe in the SQLite queue) and the lane tails in admission.

Not covered:
- A real Signal account or a real signal-cli daemon; the container run uses a synthetic daemon stand-in.
- A full Gateway with a real agent and model: dispatch is held during the burst and is a stand-in after release, because the change is in receiving, storing and selecting rows.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh, unpinned default-branch sessions can reuse a compatible completed snapshot only when its revision belongs to the admitted default-branch history. Explicit refs and existing pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests still prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages are reused through exact aliases; damaged or missing code falls back to verified archive installation. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification. Only negotiated peers defer content verification to first binding, with the full verification timeout; exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Status:** signed corrections are now published for **proof**, not landing. AUTH-2, UPGRADE-3 and dependency #193873 remain open. GitHub currently reports merge conflicts; the new head has not completed broad CI qualification. No server deployment, ready transition or merge was performed.

**Landing dependency:** older-snapshot behavior requires [managed publication recovery #193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873). Publication is not dependency acceptance. Capture normalization and diagnostics are separately covered by #193776.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve the flow. The correction preserves actual-base propagation, main's preparation callback, hash memoization, capture verification, diagnostics and timing coverage. Strict requests exclude receipt-only fields. A negotiated capability preserves old/new verification-stage compatibility without a protocol-version bump.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparison responses decline optional reuse only after repository/account revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

Original PR and contribution: @galiniliev. Automated actual-base repair and qualification: @roboclaw-bot.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/70153122-6ab4-4eea-96e9-a8b689da6467)
- [Implementation and verification — first-bind and seed-only regressions](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/649d3ef7-7e03-41fc-b728-f1e3cc134da1)
- [Implementation and verification — mixed peers and snapshot lineage](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/acd66058-9c68-4d20-bd3e-3bb4b94b466b)
- [Implementation and verification — comparison fallback boundaries](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b0bc6b4e-8b23-422c-85ab-e11a9c70d9f7)

## Evidence

### Published identity and scope

- **Head:** `60f2916cfa679b55b25313d55f0fc5b8e676496d`; **tree:** `413b4fa30707ba457f030cf94c0c32cff765c9f6`.
- Native `prepare-publish-for-proof` fast-forwarded `e45cfac4d439cec7ef2e75542fa5967fa9643849` to this exact candidate. Receipt: `PUSH_PURPOSE=proof`, `PUSH_REPLACED_HOSTED_ANCESTRY=false`, pending findings `AUTH-2,UPGRADE-3`.
- Remote readback matched the full tree and all **33 changed blobs**. All four new commit signatures, parent links and Galin co-author trailers were verified. Prior hosted ancestry and both earlier signed main merges remain intact.
- This publication contains the strict registration fix, unique receipt-helper export, measured per-PR test allowances, first-bind/memo/replay regressions, mixed-peer negotiation, seed-only handling and admitted snapshot-lineage checks. Global test baselines were not raised.

### Source-pinned local proof

These results belong to their stated executing sources; they are not summed into a fictitious final-head suite.

| Source | Completed proof |
| --- | --- |
| `32b13317…` | Original **93-test** correction proof retained with its immutable source bundle. |
| `adbf95d3…` | **175** owner/direct-consumer tests, including the original 93 and three new cases; **321** test-routing checks. Types, lint, formatting and safety/growth guards passed. |
| `50ae028d…` | **238** owner/direct-consumer cases plus **17** native transport/startup cases on supported Node 26: **255 distinct passes**. Legacy cross-process proof measured five cold registration reads, zero first-bind reads and zero private-edit replay reads. Types, native lint, formatting and ratchets passed. |
| **`60f2916c…`** | **119** owner/read-consumer cases plus **4** exact-revision fallback caller cases: **123 distinct passes**. Final **82-case** owner replay passed and is not double-counted. Core/scoped test types, six-file lint/formatting, max-lines, test-lines and diff checks passed. No new allowance was added for this final correction. |

Pre-fix runs reproduced the first-bind timeout and seed-only rejection, legacy verification-stage incompatibility, topic-only snapshot retention, and unavailable/oversized comparison failures. The fixes preserve fail-closed identity/repository changes and strict wire rejection of unknown fields.

**Recorded runtime limitation:** the `50ae028d…` pinned-Bun startup replay had one fixture `spawnSync sh ETIMEDOUT` before the fence assertion. That case and the complete 17-case suite passed on Node; this does **not** establish a Bun timeout repair.

### Independent source review

The whole incoming branch from `abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24` through `50ae028d…` completed **27/27** canonical P0–P3 review passes with **206 complete owner bodies in every pass** and six preserved composition datasets. Its complete **FINDINGS** report identified the two comparison fallback defects.

The exact final `60f2916c…` correction then received a focused independent canonical P0–P3 review: **scoped-clean, zero findings**. This is composite source-pinned review evidence, not a relabeling of the earlier whole-source report or a claim of installed production acceptance. Historical composition views are not combined execution proof. The reviewer model remained `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, high thinking, tools off.

### Hosted CI

The earlier [CI run 42233989169](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42233989169) failed for `e45cfac…` while executing merge `8ec803862669addf1279d0b98dda2d7a2c011b1c`: **103 pass, 43 skipped and 6 failed contexts**. Its owned export, allocation, memo/startup and strict-registration defects are addressed by this correction; that old run is not relabeled green.

Initial checks on `60f2916c…` showed **7 success and 4 skipped**, with no failing or pending checks in that observation. Only automation/context/security workflows were attached; **no broad CI workflow run was present for this head**, and GitHub reported a merge-conflicting state. These checks are not full qualification.

### Important proof gaps

- **AUTH-2 — IMPORTANT:** exercise the real registered `RepositoryIntegration.withIdentity` policy with an admitted isolated repository/account, including revocation and reassignment during provisioning and zero prepared-content execution afterward. Local identity-boundary fixtures and mocked integration drafts do not close this requirement; authorized access to the selected production policy/test environment remains missing.
- **UPGRADE-3 — IMPORTANT:** complete installed stable/mixed-peer/provider acceptance through actual owners, strict negotiation and actual-base binding. Current typed/parser/runtime fixtures remain bounded local proof. Earlier discovery found no Docker CLI for the supported survivor harness, and the stable package attempt was refused by the repository's release-age policy; neither safeguard was bypassed. #193873 remains an unsatisfied landing dependency.
- Resolve merge conflicts and obtain the required hosted CI/ordinary landing gates before any merge qualification.

The native correction assessment remains **NEEDS WORK** for proof-only publication. No external Platinum rating, live cloud latency result or landing readiness is claimed.

prs.title: fix(imessage): prevent reflected replies from triggering duplicate turns
prs.body:
Related: #135704 (verified self-chat reflection subset only).

## What Problem This Solves

An iMessage self-chat reflection with a new row GUID can trigger a duplicate agent turn; counting benign reflections toward the loop limiter can also mute a later legitimate message.

## User Impact

Verified incoming self-chat rows whose parent GUID and normalized body match one accepted send in the same account/conversation within four seconds are classified as `self-chat echo` without consuming the loop budget. Authored replies, ordinary DMs, groups, different-body replies and post-window replies keep their existing behavior.

**Maintainer decision required:** an incoming human self-chat reply with the same parent GUID and body inside four seconds is indistinguishable from a reflection using the available fields and is also suppressed. A native bridge discriminator would be preferable. This PR does not claim acceptance of that delivery tradeoff or close the broader ordinary-DM issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The strict parent probe uses the existing persisted echo owner's scoped GUID/body pair, excludes pending entries, and refuses independent ID/text memory maps as evidence of an exact pair. It reuses existing conversation scopes, normalization, state, retention and loop-accounting classification. The general matcher is relocated unchanged to respect the file's inherited line cap; the monitor regressions share the existing fixture lifecycle. No schema, configuration, public SDK, native bridge or retention change.

This CI repair integrates pinned main `91f796d79f906b234d024abde6bcb9410327060c` to resolve the inherited absolute test-line failure. The complete ten-path PR patch and all ten PR-owned file blobs remain byte-for-byte identical to the previous hosted head. There are no manual source, test, allocation, baseline, manifest or lockfile edits. The dedicated allocation remains exactly 246 net LF and the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

Reviewed and tested head: `8d1a76dd945ce8dbe552e4b5700ac908fab1768a`. Complete binary/full-index PR diff SHA256: `2654e9457b5da64f8a6e3a31d95069b5d71a21efcc1af2889ab969ee955e2be7`.

- Fresh frozen installation in this PR's independent worktree; manifest/lockfile hashes unchanged by installation or verification. Repository execution was serialized in a secretless container.
- `pnpm test:extension imessage --maxWorkers=1`: **60 files passed, 1 skipped; 841 tests passed, 1 skipped**.
- Targeted format and type-aware lint: passed, zero lint warnings/errors. Both extension production and test type graphs passed.
- Line-cap and submitted-diff whitespace passed. Canonical full-index test-line check passed: **6,484,513 total / 6,484,542 ceiling; 29 slack**.
- Clean-head public CLI bundle build passed in **348.269 seconds**, with networking disabled. The supported declaration-skip setting was used; this is not a full declaration/package/release build.
- The actual built Gateway exercised public seed-send RPC, durable iMessage ingress, the production persisted echo owner, agent/provider runtime, dispatcher and outbound send. Only external imsg JSON-RPC and Responses SSE were deterministic local protocol fixtures; no internal mocks or TTL/clock overrides.

Sanitized current-head runtime result:

```text
public seed send: exact chat_id=123, accepted GUID/body/scope persisted
five incoming reflections: each dropped with reason="self-chat echo"
maximum seed-response-to-drop: 425.847 ms (production window: 4000 ms)
reflection burst: model requests=0, additional transport sends=0
subsequent different-body input: model requests=1, transport replies=1
first reflection to legitimate model request: 11.404 s (limiter window: 60 s)
reply: exact deterministic provider output, originating chat
SIGTERM: exit=0, native clean shutdown, forced kill=false
remaining task-owned processes/groups=0; HTTP fixture owner joined
post-shutdown SQLite: accepted GUID/body/scope and six completed ingress rows confirmed
```

Independent local review inspected the complete committed diff, affected owners/consumers and final raw execution evidence: **PASS, no confirmed unresolved implementation finding**. All ten final log hashes and 25 independent evidence readback assertions passed. This does not grant the maintainer's policy decision.

Limitations: no native macOS Messages/imsg hardware, live account, real model inference, fresh pinned-main RED replay, stable-release upgrade, downtime replay or attachment proof. The isolated Gateway retained optional state page-cache warming (`Function not implemented`) and remote model-catalog refresh warnings under network isolation; message behavior, durable readback and clean shutdown passed. Historical native observations remain evidence only for their original heads.

<details>
<summary>Retained unsuccessful setup attempts</summary>

The first typed-lint preparation hit the default five-minute declaration-generation timeout before lint ran. With the repository-supported timeout/resource environment, declaration preparation and typed lint passed; the successful extension tests were reused against the exact unchanged source and log hashes. The initial offline build lacked the current lockfile's Darwin fs-safe archives. After integrity-checked preparation of the canonical ignored cache, the build passed again without networking. Failed logs are retained; no dependency, product setting or verification requirement was weakened.

</details>

## Current hosted CI

The previous hosted head `6b2e079afc27f30c2260c53325f1e0f96732ae7b` failed [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41710079586/job/126176964735) because its CI base was 359 test LF over the absolute ceiling; all other selected substantive lanes passed. This update integrates upstream budget reconciliation, with the local canonical check passing as shown above. Fresh [CI run 42004198386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42004198386) for head `8d1a76dd945ce8dbe552e4b5700ac908fab1768a` completed **successfully: 32 jobs passed, 31 skipped, zero failed**. Both `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and the `openclaw/ci-gate` job passed. Skipped jobs are not claimed as passing coverage. See the [Checks tab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137189/checks) for the current check and commit-status reconciliation. CI success does not decide the disclosed human-reply suppression tradeoff.

prs.title: fix(logbook): show historical timelines before capture status
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A pinned historical Logbook day waited for fresh capture status even when its timeline and the capture timezone were already available. Historical cards now appear when the selected timeline arrives; initial and Today loads still wait for capture-host day correctness.

The existing Logbook owner retains day/connection/generation guards, pending actions and queued refreshes. Maintainer review reproduced and repaired an early-rejection gap: `Promise.all` released load admission before a pending timeline could publish. `Promise.allSettled` now retains full request custody through both outcomes, then exposes current errors.

## Production-renderer qualification

Baseline `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`; final candidate/workload `f07fc91eda1d5fc81cc5e17725ade2dea1937b8a`. Production UI bytes were built from the identical candidate UI at `b41a89cc628827db594aac3ce42e1d2d444f32c5`; the later commit only repairs benchmark observation. Both bundles use the repository production builder and native Gateway HTTP delivery, with **synthetic WebSocket responses, not a live backend**.

Five serial baseline/candidate/baseline-control triples per scene, fresh owned Chromium 156.0.8078.4 per observation, macOS arm64 Tempbook, desktop 1440×1000/light/1× CPU/native clocks. One timeline card per day, UTC capture/browser timezone, only `logbook.status` delayed 250 ms. Historical navigation starts after initial settlement. The UTC CDP session stays attached for the owned observation, and both variants start observing fresh status before the action.

**30/30 primary observations and 30/30 separate RSS observations pass.** Every measured action settles with exactly one status and one timeline RPC, visible selected content, and the expected capture timezone. RSS polling (25 ms cadence) and traces are separate diagnostics; their latency/CPU numbers are excluded from primary comparisons.

Cells show **median / p95 (min–max)**; with n=5, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. Latencies are automation-to-observation, including locator/paint scheduling, not network latency or INP. Initial observation has substantial polling spread, so tiny differences are not precise user-latency claims.

Sampled RSS medians rise only 0.062/0.078 MiB (initial/historical), within overlapping ranges; neither is retained heap or a leak test. The evidence does not establish a repeatable material user-visible regression. **One subphase crosses the recorded 20% stop threshold:** initial `TaskOtherDuration` median rises 11.925 → 16.214 ms (+4.289 ms, +36.0%), with nonoverlapping ranges; p95 rises 12.167 → 17.100 ms. This is not dismissed as spread. It coincides with script time falling 5.100 ms and total thread task time falling 1.447 ms. A separate trace pair shows no long tasks, initial main-thread busy time 57.972 → 55.325 ms, task counts 400 → 397, and almost identical microtask-checkpoint time (11.101 → 11.169 ms); Logbook's sampled module-inclusive time is 7.503 → 7.487 ms. Those diagnostics suggest a shift among execution categories rather than added total work, but one instrumented pair does not prove the cause of the untraced subphase change. **PERF1 explicitly accepted by the human owner for this PR:** “landar e subir outras sessoes para hillclimb pra ver se consegue other task melhor”. This accepts the documented +36.0% other-task subphase trade-off; it does not relabel the counter as improved or within spread. The owner requested landing now and separate follow-up sessions to investigate improving other-task time. That hillclimb is outside this PR; its production bundles, raw primary/RSS/trace reports and source maps are retained. This scoped performance acceptance does not waive source review, security, or enforced merge requirements.

## Reproduce and inspect

The committed scenarios live in `scripts/lib/control-ui-logbook-readiness-scenarios.ts` and use the existing interaction harness. Build each exact UI with `NODE_ENV=production node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts --production-build <bundle-dir>`, then:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-interactions.ts \
  --bundle-dir <baseline> --compare-bundle-dir <candidate> --control-bundle-dir <baseline> \
  --steps data-logbook-first-content-250ms,data-logbook-previous-250ms \

Local raw campaign artifacts are retained for the maintainer handoff under `.artifacts/landing-readiness-194869-194871/logbook-primary/warm-ZG9UTM` and `logbook-rss/warm-GVkygL`. Four separate traced observations pass under `logbook-trace/warm-COK8rz`; their timing is diagnostic only.

The first smoke attempt caught a fixture error: detaching CDP reset UTC to the system timezone, so the product correctly fetched the capture host's day again. A direct Chromium probe reproduced the reset; the fixture was repaired and four smoke cells passed. Smoke values are excluded above.

## Correctness and fresh review

- Replaced the real 250 ms timer, performance logging, and environment-driven repeats in normal tests with a held response and real rendered outcomes. Added one regression for the reproduced status-rejection/late-timeline settlement defect.
- The deterministic historical-readiness test fails against the original baseline; the rejection regression fails against the original PR. Both pass after the repair.
- **39 focused tests pass** across Logbook view, readiness, actions, keyframes and PluginPage. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/plugin/logbook-view.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: **12 tests, 2.86 s wall**. No new CI run was requested; CI seconds are not available for the repair.
- UI types, all eight UI-test type shards, script types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, source/test-line and Control UI ownership ratchets pass. The per-change test allocation is exactly **72 added LF lines**; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Native Gateway HTTP/startup boundary proof (22 tests) and the benchmark HTTP delivery test are reused from the preceding Skills worker run: the test files and owning HTTP sources are byte-identical here. The production campaigns also use that native HTTP delivery boundary. This is isolated boundary proof, not a deployed Gateway claim.
- Fresh canonical installed autoreview, P0–P2: scoped-clean for the full repaired change and the final benchmark fixture delta. The earlier review independently confirmed the repaired early-rejection issue. No outstanding actionable code findings. PERF1 has the explicit human performance acceptance recorded above; all measured adverse values remain unchanged.
- Product growth is 33 net lines, preserving one owner; benchmark instrumentation is outside normal regression tests. Existing incoming visual proof is retained.

## Earlier component-harness evidence

The author previously reported five interleaved jsdom pairs at the original head `7ec8718ec9f679773d30a9d2e3df79d84d8fa13a`: historical readiness median 251.8 → 69.2 ms, p95 252.7 → 74.1 ms, ranges 251.1–252.7 → 66.6–74.1 ms, one status/timeline read per navigation. This remains lower-tier historical evidence, not production timing; the timer-based benchmark test has been retired in favor of the committed production workload above.

The execution worker publishes evidence and bounded fixes; final independent source review, exact-head CI/security admission, protected merge and human credit verification remain with the parent maintainer. prs.title: fix(catalog): recommend DeepSeek's canonical Flash id
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #194819. The hosted catalog derives each provider's `recommendedModels` by projecting the global seed `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json` onto that provider's served rows (`projectRecommendedModels` in `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts`). The seed only carried the versioned keys `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4-flash`. The DeepSeek provider's canonical `deepseek-flash` row therefore never matched, was never recommended, and stayed collapsed under "All models" in `/models`. After a refresh dropped `deepseek-v4-flash`, the reporter's picker recommended only `deepseek-v4-pro`. ## User Impact `/models` lists the working `deepseek/deepseek-flash` as a recommended DeepSeek model, so users no longer have to find it under "All models". ## Why This Change Was Made This is the seed repair the review recommends: - Add the canonical `deepseek-flash` key to the seed. - The versioned keys stay, because other providers (OpenCode Go) still declare `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Their removal, and the `deepseek-v4-pro` retirement question, need separate verification. - `deepseek-flash` is not hidden by the family-recency rule next to `deepseek-v4-flash`, as the live run below shows. ## Evidence **Live run.** Windows 11, Node v26.12.1. The real exported `projectRecommendedModels()` is fed each build's `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json` and the DeepSeek rows declared in `extensions/deepseek/openclaw.plugin.json` (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`, `deepseek-flash`). | DeepSeek rows served | `main` c044eee seed | this PR bd1876c seed | | --- | --- | --- | | all manifest rows | `["deepseek-v4-flash","deepseek-v4-pro"]` | `["deepseek-v4-flash","deepseek-flash","deepseek-v4-pro"]` | | after a refresh drops `deepseek-v4-flash` (the reporter's state) | `["deepseek-v4-pro"]` | `["deepseek-flash","deepseek-v4-pro"]` | A full `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts` run needs models.dev network access, which this host does not have (`models.dev catalog unavailable: TypeError: fetch failed`). The projection step above is the part this PR changes. **Regression test.** `recommends DeepSeek's served canonical Flash id from the repository seed (#194819)` in `test/scripts/publish-model-catalog-v2.test.ts` projects the real repository seed onto `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` rows. | Rev | Result | | --- | --- | | `main` | ❌ received `["deepseek-v4-pro"]` | | this PR | ✅ | On Windows, 4 symlink-based publication tests in that file fail with `EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink` on unmodified `main` as well. That failure is unrelated to this PR. **Gates:** - `oxfmt` and `oxlint`: clean. - `check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK.

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.1 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2638 -> 2642 on main `f6a8ce9`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `6d9ace7` (on main `cd20cf7`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.1` from npm (npm 11.20 skipped the package's install scripts by default; the CLI ran without them). The branch CLI on `6d9ace7` reported `2026.10.10` because main had not bumped its version string yet. An earlier run from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.1 and existing data:** 2026.11.1 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.1, v27 -> v40), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.1, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.1 OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.318 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.310 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.303 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.296 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.290 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.1): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.1): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (6d9ace7) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.1 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v40 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.1 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.318 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.310 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.303 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.296 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.290 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~2s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +145, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch now merges main `f6a8ce9` at `05585b7`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. The v2026.11.1 proof above ran on `6d9ace7`; the merge after it brought in main's changes and the regenerated baseline. Main's #139230 reworked dirty-index maintenance and the watcher's background sync in `manager-watch-ops.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge keeps this PR's one `excludePaths` line there, and `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts`, `watch-policy.test.ts` and `manager.watcher-config.test.ts` pass on `05585b7`. Main's #191749 bounded the realpath deduplication at the end of `listMemoryFiles`; it merges cleanly because `excludePaths` filters files as they are collected, before that step. Main's #192488 moved the search manager types into `search-manager.types.ts`; this PR does not import them. Main's #193952 added provider name and icon help to `schema.help.models.ts`, which this PR also edits; both sets of entries merge cleanly. On `1cc43f3`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `ci-gate`) failed because main `bf10667` was over its own test-line ceiling by 137 lines; main's own scheduled job logged the same overage and passed only because that run added no test lines. Main `d1ffc39` got back under the ceiling, and the ratchet passes locally on `05585b7` (6,569,373 test lines, ceiling 6,569,494, with this PR's +145 lines covered by its 145-line allocation). On `df4f9e6`, `check-prompt-snapshots` failed on three JSON prompt snapshots this PR does not touch: main's #192596 stopped formatting JSON snapshots without regenerating the committed ones (the content was identical, only the layout differed). Main fixed it in #192628, `5d93337` merged that fix, and `prompt:snapshots:check` passes locally on `05585b7`. On `0a3aa17`, 19 CI jobs failed in setup before running any check because downloading the pinned Bun runtime from the `openclaw/bun` release returned HTTP 504; `pnpm test:ci-failed 188294` found no test failures, and CI on `5858e44` passed. On `b0f8904`, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-6` failed in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file.test.ts` (`scopes extra-path EACCES/EPERM/EIO errors to the requested file`), a file this PR does not touch. prs.title: feat(pr): release dependency cache holds left behind by dead wrappers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/pr` dependency cache entries stay pinned forever when the wrapper that created their anchor dies without retiring it, because only the creator may release its holds.

## User Impact

User impact: maintainers can review leaked dependency holds with a read-only dry run, then release exactly the reviewed anchors with an explicit confirmation, so the existing collector can evict those entries. No release happens automatically, and ordinary `scripts/pr` runs are unchanged.

This changes a documented rule, so it is worth reading on its own: `docs/reference/scripts/pr-tooling.md` previously said a creator crash never authorizes releasing holds. Nothing releases them automatically now either, and PID death, age, and path disappearance still never authorize release on their own. The one new exception is an operator confirming a reviewed plan.

## Why This Change Was Made

Eviction already works, but it only considers settled, unheld entries. Holds from a dead creator can never release, so their entries are never considered. #194520 stopped one source of new leaks; this handles the holds that already exist and any future leak from a crash.

Holds exist because an inherited consumer can outlive its creator, so no signal alone proves an anchor finished. Authority follows `lock-recover`: an explicit operator confirmation, plus evidence checks that fail closed, plus exact identity rechecks by the owner.

```bash
scripts/pr dependency-hold-release --dry-run [--anchor <path>]... > plan.json
scripts/pr dependency-hold-release plan.json --plan-sha256 <SHA256> --confirmed-no-running-tools
```

Evidence is collected again immediately before each anchor and never trusted from the plan. Any of these blocks an anchor: a live same-uid creator, a live process in the creator's group, any process referencing the anchor or an entry it holds (by command line or open file), or a changed anchor or entry identity. A failed `ps` or `lsof` stops the command.

Decisions worth a reviewer's attention:

- **Present anchors are retired, not just released.** On the host that prompted this, 196 of 204 anchors still exist, at about 29 MiB of wrapper source each. Release follows the creator's order: remove the anchor, then release its holds, so a crash leaves a state a rerun of the same plan finishes. Holds are the only authority to remove a path: with no ledger rows for an anchor, the command reports `already-released` and never touches that path.
- **Process scans run outside the metadata mutex.** Other wrappers wait at most one second for it, and `lsof` alone takes about 0.3 s, so scanning under the lock would make live wrappers fail. The ledger recheck does run under the lock, inside the transaction. A hold a live wrapper takes during a batch is safe by accounting: its anchor is not in the sealed plan, and its row keeps the entry unsettled.
- **One settlement path.** `retireAnchorDependencies` and the new release share their snapshot and settlement code rather than forking it.

Accepted edges, deliberately not coded around:

- A PID reused by another uid cannot be the creator, so it is recorded but does not block. This happens today: one creator PID now belongs to a system service. A PID reused by the same uid delays release until that process exits.
- There is no correlation with retained operation locks. Across this host's clones, 0 of 204 anchors match one. Resolving them first is part of what the operator attests.
- The collector deletes evicted entries synchronously, so the next materializing wrapper run after a large release pays for those deletions before it continues. The docs say so.

Release-note context: new maintainer command `scripts/pr dependency-hold-release`.

## Evidence

**End to end on a real projection.** The existing live package reader test drives the real embedded materializer, leaving a real `node_modules` projection, an exited creator, and a live reader, which is exactly a leaked hold. It now continues:

1. while the reader lives, the anchor is `blocked` with `process-references`;
2. once the reader exits, the anchor is releasable;
3. a sealed release retires the anchor, leaves the entry's files readable (removal did not follow the symlinks), and settles the entry;
4. rerunning the plan reports `already-released`;
5. the next real materialization evicts the entry.

**Refusals leave the ledger byte-identical:** missing confirmation, wrong seal, a hold added after review, and an anchor replaced at the same path (the replacement survives).

**Live holds are never released,** even through a sealed, confirmed plan. Using real `ps` and `lsof` with no mocks, the cases are a live creator, an orphaned process group whose leader has exited, a process with its cwd in the anchor, and a process whose command line names the entry key. For the creator and group cases, the test deliberately promotes the blocked record into a sealed plan, because a dead PID cannot be made live; this proves evidence is recollected rather than read from the plan.

**Negative controls, each failing for the intended reason:** release blockers disabled (4 live-hold cases fail), reviewed-holds comparison removed (the added-hold case fails), anchor removal skipped (the end-to-end test fails). All were restored afterward.

**Live dry run on one maintainer host, read-only:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Ledger | 31 entries, 5 settled, 204 holds |
| Anchors | 204 releasable, 0 blocked |
| Anchor state | 196 present, 8 missing |
| Creators | 203 gone, 1 PID reused by another uid |
| Entries that would settle | 26 |

Ledger bytes were unchanged and no lock remained. Two runs produced the same seal. An independent raw `ps` and `lsof` check agreed: no references, and no same-uid process with a creator PID as its pid or pgid. **No live hold has been released;** that awaits the maintainer's decision on this output.

**Test cost.** Net test lines are -6 against the merge base (422 added, 428 removed), through consolidation that keeps every existing assertion. Measured with `--maxWorkers=1`: `pr-dependency-cache.test.ts` passes 62 tests in about 30 to 50 s depending on host load, of which the 10 new cases take about 11 s. The extended reader test takes about 8 s. CI seconds to follow.

**Local suites run:** `pr-dependency-cache`, the dependency-cache-recovery, closed-reader and live-reader cases of `pr-wrappers`, `pr-materialized-anchor`, `check-deadcode-exports`, and the wrapper inventory check. Autoreview reported no P0 to P2 findings, though one of its 9 chunks contained only file statistics, so it carries little weight there.

Known gaps:

- The macOS end-to-end run used a local install 54 packages behind the manifest, so I aligned the manifests temporarily for that run. Nothing from that is committed. PR CI covers a current install on Linux, which also proves `ps` and `lsof` behavior there.
- Production lint could not run locally against that borrowed install. It passed in a copied checkout before a small later change to the release loop, so CI's static gates are the proof for the final code.
- The per-anchor rescan has no dedicated test. Making liveness appear between two anchors deterministically would need a test-only hook.
- A real release against a real cache is unproven until the maintainer approves one.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact candidate head: `f1c66eb055618f0aa79505abd7bfacb1498445c8`; frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree: `de8299f6f3c4776fce1a0e00db9843f8289c8f7a`.
- Focused test command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.watch-subscribe-retry.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.session-patch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts` → 5 files, **43/43 passing** on the merged tree. Core and extension TypeScript gates and touched-file formatting pass under Node 26.7.0.
- Production path exercised by the mock-Gateway proof: `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` → `createIMessageGroupActivationResolver` in `group-activation.ts` → runtime `getSessionEntryInWorker` → SQLite worker-backed read; admission uses `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`. The test calls the production decision function with a routed group and real isolated SQLite store, not Apple's Messages transport.
- The proof harness writes persisted activation entries through `runtime.agent.session.upsertSessionEntry` (simulating the command's persistence), rather than issuing live `/activation` commands. Command owner-gating/persistence is separately covered by `commands-session.activation.test.ts`. This distinction matters: it is not a single end-to-end live Apple/command receipt.
- The exact frozen-base deterministic preflight is green after a lockfile-frozen dependency refresh. It passes extension production/test type graphs, touched-file formatting/lint, dead exports, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. The refresh exposed and the branch repaired a strict session-entry test fixture that lacked required identity/timestamp fields and literal activation typing.
- Earlier sanitized behavior receipt (the production behavior path is unchanged by the frozen-base replay):

```json
{ "verdict": "PASS", "base": "9bb171bf39b98a6965a47ab4f636e35a5701b409", "head": "68a07b52e5881bc9294ec1ddaa548a605ad7a433", "harness": "real SQLite session store + worker-backed read + mock Gateway iMessage admission", "sessionKey": "agent:main:imessage:group:99", "decisions": { "mention": "drop", "always": "dispatch", "restoredMention": "drop" } }
```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected private-QA tests repeatedly build the same runtime when their remaining test work can fit in fewer CI jobs. This is maintainer-requested CI cost work.

## User Impact

Fewer repeated setups and private-QA builds, with the same selected tests, subprocess isolation, runners and concurrency policies. Full validation and hourly reservations keep their existing layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a private-QA policy that already selects a slow target can exceed the ordinary 150-second test packing target. Its limit stays below that selected target and the existing 300-second serial envelope less the 104-second preparation estimate. The 12-target cap remains. First-fit packing is not monotone, so keep the original plan unless the candidate uses fewer jobs without increasing either private-QA policy's count.

## Evidence

Read-only replay of recorded completed CI cohorts, using the pinned base/candidate packing functions, actual source routing and committed timing weights:

| CI run | Selected targets | Original QA jobs | Candidate QA jobs | Maximum prediction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [42389135891](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42389135891) | 19 | 12 | 11 | 419s, unchanged |
| [42389055599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42389055599) | 19 | 12 | 11 | 419s, unchanged |

Historical input order is reconstructed from recorded rows and reproduces every baseline target partition. Target/config routing and per-target build/concurrency/runner policies are unchanged. The longest sum of recorded target wrapper times stays 210.61s / 206.95s. These are packing projections, not newly executed groups or measured billing savings. No additional tests are omitted.

The new planner regression fails on base (4 jobs instead of 3), passes with the change, and covers small-only selections plus a first-fit counterexample where wider packing would add a job. Its 62-line allocation covers those contracts. Root-tooling typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and test-line ratchet pass.

Final committed-head validation: all90 planner tests pass (82.12s suite,82.91s wrapper; existing broad planner suite). The preceding bounded draft passed163 affected tests across four files, including source ownership, fallbacks and hourly reservations; the final change adds only the tested baseline-packing safeguard.

Full local ClawSweeper review of3651abf03ad802976e1a9a6fd46967ef96ef2e38..6af2c01bf833729efecfcd440ff2356ef5ca704d completed with no actionable findings (0.91 confidence).
