## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an intermittent Android Play cancellation-test failure during the initial channel claim, before the cancellation scenario starts.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is a focused fixture repair for the maintainer-directed investigation of [main CI run 42425211259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42425211259/job/128562180421).

## Why This Change Was Made

Put pending-channel expiry on a virtual clock in this cancellation case while retaining the fixture's parent Job and real IO readers. The case still exercises actual registry claiming, cancellation, retirement, and retry. All assertions and numeric deadlines remain intact; the separate expiry test continues to cover expiration.

The failed case took 1.630 seconds and returned null on the first claim (line 757), before cancellation began. Its pending channel expires after 1,000ms. The same unchanged case passed in 0.112 seconds on [run 42420555752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42420555752). Premature expiry is inferred from the source and elapsed time; the failing run did not record its scheduling order.

The case originates in [#116593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/116593) (`88876f780b81`), with credit preserved. Both the registry and its test are unchanged between the green and failing heads. Neither recent Android candidate, [#194321](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194321) nor [#185978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185978), touches this path.

## Evidence

- Original failure: `WearRealtimeChannelRegistryTest.cancelled promotion retires its reserved channel before retry`, `IllegalStateException: Required value was null` at the initial claim; 3,652 tests, one failure. The class had 23 cases and took 4.498 seconds.

prs.title: fix(skills): show discovery before installed status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Skills discovery cannot show its independent library while installed-skill status is slow.

## User Impact

User impact: the library can appear before installed status finishes. In the controlled production-renderer workload below, first-visit readiness improves **308.0 → 118.1 ms (61.7%)**. This is not a deployed-page or real-Gateway throughput claim.

**The strict no-worse target is not fully clean:** first-visit layout time increases by 0.365 ms, and warm median readiness increases by 1.1 ms. Aggregate renderer CPU is unchanged in these samples. The current maintainer request authorizes review and landing. These adverse cells remain disclosed for the landing owner’s assessment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Start the installed-status prefetch at its existing route boundary and let the existing mounted Skills request owner adopt the same promise. Discovery renders independently; Settings still waits for its report. Preserve agent-selection revisions, connection ownership, visible errors, installation consent, and write settlement. No new cache or duplicate status request. **Skills only.**

## Evidence

### Production-bundle method and predeclared rule

Chromium **156.0.8078.4**, Linux x64, **1440×1000**, light theme, 1× CPU. Real production bundles are served through the existing Gateway HTTP delivery owner; WebSocket responses are synthetic. The page-specific fixture has **one library entry and one installed-status sentinel**, with only skills.status delayed **250 ms**. This tests the dependency mechanism, not large-catalog scaling.

For each first-visit and warm-revisit scene: **five serial baseline/candidate/baseline-control triples**, a fresh owned Chromium process per observation. First visit means opening Skills after a settled New Session, not document startup. Warm revisits do not force artificial reads; in this run every measured visit issued one status read. A newly returned status marker, followed by final frames, defines full settlement and the request-count assertion.

Latency/CPU use the **unpolled** pass. RSS comes from separate explicitly diagnostic scenes with 25 ms-paced polling of the owner-validated renderer processes; their latency and CPU values are excluded. RSS is the sampled peak sum of browser-owned renderers, not a true peak, whole-browser/Gateway memory, retained-heap, or leak measurement. Heap endpoints are unforced. Host load and raw samples are retained in the generated reports. Separate traces/profiles are excluded from timing distributions.

The rule was recorded here before production measurement: lower first-visit median/p95; no worse warm/full-settlement latency, counts, CPU or memory; any real worse metric needs explicit owner acceptance; a >=20% adverse cell stops qualification. A/A controls do not waive that rule. This is the page-specific five-sample rule, not a claim to meet the generic harness manifest's ten-pair stability budget.

### Production renderer results

Cells show **median / nearest-rank p95**. With n=5, p95 is the maximum. Times are milliseconds; RSS is MiB. Control is a fresh observation of the baseline bundle after the candidate.

| Phase / metric | Baseline | Candidate | Baseline control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First visit: visible library | 308.0 / 309.6 | **118.1 / 122.8** | 307.0 / 308.8 |
| First visit: full status settlement | 335.1 / 337.0 | 315.8 / 319.7 | 336.1 / 336.6 |
| First visit: renderer process CPU | 120 / 130 | 120 / 130 | 130 / 130 |
| First visit: sampled renderer RSS | 468.6 / 471.5 | 469.4 / 471.6 | 470.4 / 470.8 |
| Warm revisit: visible library | 19.0 / 21.6 | 20.1 / 21.3 | 18.9 / 23.3 |
| Warm revisit: full status settlement | 343.7 / 345.8 | 328.4 / 330.0 | 336.2 / 345.1 |
| Warm revisit: renderer process CPU | 50 / 130 | 50 / 110 | 40 / 50 |
| Warm revisit: sampled renderer RSS | 482.7 / 483.7 | 478.5 / 483.7 | 481.2 / 483.3 |

Readiness min–max: first visit **291.0–309.6 → 114.4–122.8 ms**; warm **18.5–21.6 → 19.1–21.3 ms**. RSS min–max: first visit **466.8–471.5 → 468.0–471.6 MiB**; warm **478.0–483.7 → 477.8–483.7 MiB**. RSS observations contain 6–8 samples each. These distributions do not establish an arbitrary-duration memory bound.

### Adverse cells are not hidden

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First-visit thread-clock task time | 68.499 / 71.289 | 69.441 / 75.920 |
| First-visit layout time | 2.813 / 2.992 | 3.178 / 3.250 |
| First-visit style time | 10.327 / 11.080 | 10.294 / 11.239 |
| Warm thread-clock task time | 26.617 / 40.138 | 27.025 / 41.188 |
| Warm style time | 4.053 / 4.224 | 4.070 / 4.212 |

The largest primary A/B adverse relative cell above is **+13.0% layout median**, an absolute **+0.365 ms**; first-visit task median is +0.942 ms (+1.4%) and p95 +6.5%. Warm readiness median is +1.1 ms (+5.8%). First-visit sampled RSS median is +0.79 MiB (+0.17%); control and unforced-GC variability are reported rather than used to claim a free memory win. Unforced heap-after medians move by +0.03% first visit / +0.66% warm. No listed primary median/p95 cell crosses the 20% stop, but **the all-metrics no-worse claim is not made**.

All **30 unpolled observations, 30 RSS observations, and two separately traced observations** pass their functional assertions. Renderer CPU counters are complete for all unpolled/RSS observations. Each measured visit ends with **one skills.status request and two cards**; library-list/search counts remain one each. First-visit measured CLS changes 0.00769→0; warm CLS remains 0.00769. Separate traces show no >50 ms task in either candidate scene; cold profile mapping reports 309 mapped / 116 unmapped frames.

### Reproduction and source custody

UI baseline: `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`. Candidate UI bundle: `3f75190f8bfcc325d8cb63a46d31a735bba6e38e`. The committed workload is on current head **`4f7d4d7c0b312837b18b1e4e7f314fdf24f4f503`**; its later commits change benchmark code only, not the measured UI modules.

Build each exact UI revision with `buildProductionControlUiE2e`, then run from the workload head:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-interactions.ts \
  --bundle-dir <baseline-bundle> --compare-bundle-dir <candidate-bundle> \
  --control-bundle-dir <baseline-bundle> --data-pages \
  --steps data-skills-first-content-250ms,data-skills-revisit-250ms \
  --viewport desktop --pairs 5 --cpu-throttle 1 --thread-cpu-time \
  --renderer-process-metrics --first-pair-screenshots --output <timing-artifacts>
```

For RSS, use the same command with the two step IDs suffixed `-rss` and a separate output directory. For attribution, use the candidate as the sole bundle, normal step IDs, `--pairs 1 --trace`, and another output directory. Never combine profiler/RSS-polling timing values with the unpolled table.

Retained artifact groups: `production-qualified-routed/warm-RPehNx`, `production-rss-routed/warm-m20dkA`, and `production-profile-routed/warm-XqRULN`, containing manifests, raw results, reports, captures and traces. Earlier combined-polling smoke and string-evaluation/CSP failures are retained and excluded. Production CSP was not relaxed; the repaired workload uses the existing route observer.

### Correctness and review

- **44 targeted UI tests pass**, including affected mutation/lifecycle/discovery siblings; the same early-readiness regression is red on the old production source.
- Production UI typing, UI test type shards, scoped lint/format/diff checks, test-line and UI ownership ratchets passed for the unchanged UI fix. New benchmark modules pass scripts typing, scoped lint/format and commit hooks.
- Independent local P0–P2 autoreview covered the UI fix and subsequent benchmark work. Its benchmark findings—synchronous RSS polling contaminating timing, and counting requests before final status publication—were repaired by separate diagnostic scenes and a final recount. Runtime production observations above exercise those repairs; no clean-review result is substituted for execution.
- Author simplification preserves one request owner. Production UI LOC **+11**; benchmark scenes are explicit-only and reuse the existing measurement harness. The initial **68-line** regression allocation is reduced to **57 lines** by the deterministic maintainer repair; the shared scalar remains unchanged.

### Maintainer review update

The first-visit improvement is well separated from both baseline observations. Warm readiness differs by 1.1 ms and overlaps baseline/control spread; sampled RSS differs by 0.17% with overlapping ranges. The layout median increases by 0.365 ms (+13.0%), a measured subphase cost that is retained rather than called a win. These five-sample data do not demonstrate a material user-visible regression, but do not prove every metric is unchanged. This assessment uses the published distributions; the original Linux report files were not available in this review checkout.

The normal regression now uses a held promise, forwards the actual route-loader result to the mounted page, verifies the eventual installed card, and checks one status request after settlement. Real timers, performance logging, and the environment-dependent repeat count were removed; the committed browser benchmark remains the timing owner. The regression fails against the old route and passes on the candidate. Its allocation shrinks from 68 to 57 lines with no shared-scalar change.

85 focused tests pass (Skills discovery, lifecycle, mutation, domain owner, and route provenance). The changed test file’s measured `pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1` wall time is 5.30 s, with 7 tests taking 121 ms; CI seconds are not yet available for the repair. Full-context independent P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issue. Production UI source and the measured bundle identity are unchanged by this test-only repair.

UI production types, all UI test type shards, scripts types, scoped lint, formatting, test/source-line ratchets, and UI ownership guard pass. The native Gateway HTTP/startup boundary suites pass 22 tests, and the benchmark HTTP-delivery boundary test passes. These exercise the real HTTP owner with synthetic fixtures; they are not deployed-Gateway latency evidence.

Final CI/security admission and merge remain with the landing owner.

### Maintainer assessment

The measured +0.365 ms first-visit layout cost and +1.1 ms warm-readiness median are accepted here as a bounded trade-off for the 189.9 ms first-visit improvement in this controlled workload. Warm-readiness distributions overlap, request counts remain unchanged, and aggregate renderer process CPU does not increase in the reported samples. This is not an all-metrics-no-worse or deployed-page latency claim. The reviewed repair changes only deterministic regression coverage and its allocation; the measured production code is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): provider setup fails when advancing to endpoint compatibility
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh provider setup can throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'variant')` when advancing from the API-key field to endpoint compatibility. A real fresh-Gateway baseline reproduced the render failure in **10/10** Chromium sessions.

## User Impact

Provider setup advances through its existing choices without the picker render failure. The existing benchmark can now measure a new user's setup, consent, restart, first two replies, and native plugin first visits against an isolated real Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep `SingleChoice`'s required picker parameters in one stable object with reactive getters instead of a whole-object memo. No fallback state, new product option, or consent change is added.

Extend the compiled-Gateway RPC benchmark with fresh state, a deterministic loopback provider, mobile assistant dismissal, optional empty plugin installation, and browser document/reconnect diagnostics. Each sample starts a new Gateway and browser context. First-run's 100 ms RTT preset retains localhost identity; the existing remote-client census behavior is unchanged.

The new workload exposed two bugs in the shared latency simulator. Independent packet timers reordered TCP bytes; one FIFO delivery timer preserves their order. Normal upstream close could also discard delayed response bytes; preserve the reverse delivery until it finishes. Both have regressions that fail their previous owners.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Real provider-setup reproduction | Base: render error in 10/10 Chromium journeys. Selected candidate journeys have no render or step errors. |
| Core first-run matrix | 16 conditions: Chromium/WebKit/Firefox, desktop/mobile, localhost/100 ms RTT, plus Chromium 4× CPU. |
| Optional native-plugin matrix | Same 16 conditions; Workboard, X, ClawRouter, Knowledge and MCP Relay, plus packaged Memory/Channels/Nostr/WhatsApp views. |
| First versus second reply | Three additional local desktop cases, one per engine. Together with the matrices: 35 complete selected cases, one sample each. |
| Wizard tests | 11 passed. The added transition case also passes on base; the real Gateway is the failing picker reproduction. Two duplicate assertions were removed. |
| Wire-link tests | 8 passed. Byte-order and HTTP connection-close regressions fail old owners. A real 8 MiB TCP transfer returns the exact checksum. |
| Types, lint, format, Knip | UI and scripts types, tooling test types, targeted lint/format and final-head production Knip passed. |
| Test-line ratchet | Passed with a scoped allocation of exactly 173 net regression-test lines (61 wizard, 112 wire); shared scalar unchanged. Concurrent main changes consumed the previous shared slack. |
| Build and strict asset check | Base/head UI builds pass. Both strict checks report the same six existing violations; no ceiling changed. |
| Independent review | Complete candidate and subsequent corrections reviewed; no actionable P0–P2 findings. |
| Final-head CI | `ci:full` run [42429586635](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42429586635) passed: 44 jobs passed, 24 skipped, including UI E2E and real-Gateway shards. Head `13b3e1e3c4f2bd6cc08bf58099271ea84147da23`. |

Startup JavaScript remains **90,853 B normalized gzip / 3 requests**; CSS remains **39,090 B / 1 request**. Total JavaScript normalized gzip decreases 19 B; document gzip differs by 1 B. Lazy boundaries are preserved.

These are **coverage measurements, not a claimed timing optimization or 20-pair acceptance result**. Browser readiness starts after Gateway startup. The loopback provider excludes external inference latency and OAuth. Per-step RPC counts are filtered to the observer window; resource totals are completed subresources and exclude initial navigation. Unsupported engine counters remain null.

One optional-plugin Chromium mobile RTT/4× trial reloaded during the first send. Its screenshot shows the delivered reply and enabled composer, but document replacement reset the readiness probe and invalidated the timing. That failed measurement is retained; a single repeat completed all 24 steps. It is not described as a 120-second user reply. Every selected run also retains the existing final CLI shutdown watchdog failure: the server closes, but the process self-terminates with two remaining message ports.

Remaining findings are visible rather than hidden: setup's deferred restart costs roughly 6–7 seconds; cold first replies exceed same-session second replies; provider activation records about 0.415 desktop CLS from the hidden navigation column's grid transition. The shell transition and optional mascot import recovery are unmeasured follow-up candidates. Host-installed AI binary discovery remains host-dependent despite isolated HOME/PATH.

Previous-head CI found the diagnostic `innerText` lint error and test-budget exhaustion; both are fixed and checked locally. The scoped 173-line allocation covers only the picker transition and TCP ordering/close regressions; no asset ceiling changes. Its E2E shard ended without a failed test name in its log/timeout artifact, so no inherited-failure claim is made. The final-head `ci:full` run passed, including the previously unidentified E2E shard; no inherited-failure exception is used.

## Visual Proof

Synthetic model selection before/after, inspected for private data. Choices and layout are unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: synthetic model selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19590638-a967-4901-a9ad-34b1390fee07) | ![After: synthetic model selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d79b8f65-bf53-48a8-b083-4a689759dfcd) |

## Scope and Size

9 files, **2,312 → 3,593 LOC** (+1,481/−200). Product UI is 661→671 LOC; memos 6→5, with no new effects, DOM queries, flush calls or owner APIs. Most growth is the requested real first-run driver and measurement. No dependencies, product config options, or changelog changes.

prs.title: test(perf): separate warm reload timing from visual proofs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm-reload paint gates currently include continuous geometry and compositor work, and the first measured warm return can produce V8 code cache. The campaign's measured 14-state timeline for a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link makes it important to distinguish application work from measurement work.

## User Impact

Internal tooling only; application behavior is unchanged. Ordinary unprofiled chat captures use a lightweight timing collector and exclude one warm prime. `--visual-proofs` retains geometry, backtracking, screencast and pixel proofs; `--prime-reloads 0` measures the first return. Reports identify the harness and ordinal and leave missing visual evidence unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

On one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge and one fixed application build (`636fc28d8bbd`), eight alternating pairs plus A/A give a **16 ms adjusted Team standard-probe rows tax**, versus a 14 ms A/A IQR spread. Standard rows were 472 [467, 484] ms; minimal rows 462 [456, 465] ms. Native's 8 ms adjusted tax sits within A/A noise. Reduced probes do not show a reproducible additional rows tax. Screencast rows have an order interaction, while LoAF blocking rises about 42–46 ms; those captures remain separate diagnostics.

Across eight contexts, warm #4 minus #1 rows are −76 [−84, −72] ms on Team and −158 [−171, −139] ms on native. Trace-only captures show substantial first-return module-cache production and a consume regime from #2. Natural native exit writers remain intact; snapshot bookkeeping changes and the avatar-cache key appears once, so this ordinal effect is not attributed solely to V8.

Twelve steady reloads (#5–16), median [IQR], milliseconds:

| Workload | Rows ET | FCP | Pane start |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Team active | 454 [448, 461] | 182 [164, 188] | 264.3 [261.7, 269.8] |
| Team archived | 408 [404, 427] | 184 [151, 188] | 260.3 [254.8, 273.2] |
| Native active | 558 [555, 576] | 48 [48, 49] | 271.6 [268.7, 282.8] |
| Native archived | 524 [516, 528] | 48 [48, 48] | 286.9 [280.5, 295.8] |

Team rows and visible Details co-frame below 480 ms in all 12 samples per workload. **This passes the timing prerequisite, not complete-frame visual qualification.** The requested `BeginLifecycleUpdates` event is absent from the trace categories; the report provides observed `CommitLoad` offsets, approximate translated ET and the explicit clock gap. No application change or visibility join is included.

An extra eight-pair plus A/A validation of the shipped shared collector against the calibration minimum found overlapping rows IQRs and no added tax beyond control noise (adjusted tax −17 ms Team against 84 ms A/A spread, −2 ms native against 70 ms spread). These are not additional improvement claims.

The full calibration report includes every per-pair delta, order-specific A/A subtraction and spreads, all five metrics, code-cache counts and clock references in [the committed calibration report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7a557422515c6134618a883bb2473aa3b18ef677/scripts/perf/warm-reload-harness-calibration.md). Preparation still qualifies real saved caches; timing reads happen after the window. The unconditional measured-page samplers/capture path is replaced by one explicit capture-mode decision. Growth is required to keep the requested full visual-proof contract available alongside timing-only capture, and to retain unmeasured priming separately.

## Evidence

- One lease: `cbx_95fb8436562f`, AWS c7a.4xlarge; repo-pinned full headless Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Synthetic data only. One application build, no CPU sampler in timed comparisons, no captures committed.
- Focused `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: CLI 3/3 (39.32 s), comparator 2/2 (3.00 s), paint audit 3/3 (2.50 s).
- New regression coverage protects absent pixel data and rejects timing reports as paint-audit evidence. The 37-line allocation covers only net test growth.
- Real-entry smoke: Team timing/visual and native timing on both chat/dashboard plus native visual passed; default primes and unavailable pixels checked. Two-bundle timing/visual comparisons passed, including bundle-switch navigation. Regressions fail on the pinned base. Autoreview is clean through P2. Script and all root test typechecks, ratchets, dead export scans, and targeted final lint/format passed. `check-changed` retains only the inherited changelog-attribution failure: the same 20 violations reproduce from current-main records (`ade7c07d4c70`, unchanged through rebased main `3651abf03ad8`). Lease released and no owned Gateway listeners remain.
- Required non-test diff scope: **+767/−155 = +612 lines** across 8 files (`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`). That includes 305 lines of performance documentation and the 2-line test allocation; executable tooling grows **305 lines** to preserve the full diagnostic capture contract while adding the timing path and separate priming.
- Exact-head CI: **green** on `7a557422515c6134618a883bb2473aa3b18ef677` — [run 42430169660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42430169660), including `openclaw/ci-gate`. PR is ready; no merge performed.

Release-note context: performance tooling now reports lightweight warm timings separately from geometry/visual diagnostics and primes the first warm return by default. Operators diagnosing first-return behavior can opt out of priming. No user-visible application or schema change.

prs.title: fix(agents): prevent false stall aborts after history compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

History compaction can detach the watchdog from an active foreground turn. The turn then loses its runtime-owned wait and may be aborted as stalled even while it is making progress.

Fixes #194715. The separate recovery-guidance change in #194707 addresses the aftermath of an abort; this fix does not depend on it.

## User Impact

Turns that compact history retain their foreground watchdog ownership. Compaction still has its own execution deadline and resource cleanup; it does not extend the foreground deadline or disable stall detection.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Direct compaction uses a nested attachment under the existing watchdog owner instead of replacing the foreground attempt.
- Parent retirement closes nested resources. Nested cleanup does not close the parent, clear its deadline, or revive an obsolete attempt. Standalone compaction keeps its existing behavior.
- Cleanup registration/removal uses the same bound closure. Type declarations move to a companion module while existing public type exports remain available.
- Regression tests cover nested lifetime, independent deadlines, resource cleanup, parent replacement/cancellation, and the actual direct-compaction success/failure boundary.

No new configuration, protocol changes, synthetic heartbeats, or persisted-state migration.

## Evidence

- **Failing before:** six watchdog regressions and both direct-compaction boundary tests reproduce the original lifetime/deadline defect on the old implementation.
- **Passing after:** 87 focused tests pass on `95bf30be5d9b1a3d01e1f515d81af074140a0deb`; changed-file format parity and production lint pass with zero warnings/errors.
- **Build and CI:** the full build and required hosted CI pass on the same head ([CI run, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42404336285)).
- **CI investigation:** the [first attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42404336285/job/128498974246) timed out after 180 seconds in the graceful-restart E2E fixture. A single same-head, same-shard replay passed without code changes. The original failure is retained; its root cause remains unproven, and no timeout fix or inherited-failure waiver is claimed.
- **Review:** fresh independent Codex autoreview covered the complete committed range `3c408499583cb6d584473f72aa0bb8087a45bafc..95bf30be5d9b1a3d01e1f515d81af074140a0deb` at P0–P3 and returned `scoped-clean`, with no findings. Follow-up owner/caller/deadline/cleanup and test-context inspection resolved its context limitation. Earlier staging and lint findings were fixed. No hostile behavior was identified in the reviewed changes. Hosted ClawSweeper stopped before code review because review-blob metadata was unavailable; the author requested the local independent review route instead. No hosted approval is claimed, and enforced review, security, and CI requirements remain in force.
- **Limits:** direct-compaction tests exercise the production entrypoint with fixture model I/O. No live-provider or instrumented reproduction of the specific reported incident was performed. The existing incident evidence remains in #194715.

Implementation by @VACInc.

## What Problem This Solves

Implements #150029 by adding the strict config option `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with values `always`, `errors`, and `never`. The default is `always`, preserving existing behavior.

This supersedes #175817, which was closed unmerged. The approach is rebased onto current `main` and additionally proves that the policy applies to isolated agent-run announcements through the shared delivery append path.

## Behavior

- `always`: include Control UI `Inspect` links on successful completion announcements and failure alerts (backward-compatible default).

- Gate link generation in `server-cron-completion.ts`, `server-cron-notifications.ts`, and isolated agent delivery dispatch.

prs.title: fix: interrupted tasks stop at an incomplete recovery summary
prs.body:
## Summary

Resume an interrupted task instead of steering its recovery toward an incomplete final summary.

## What Problem This Solves

The old recovery instruction says to answer from the existing transcript, minimize further tool use, and report what could not be verified. In the inspected incident, recovery made no tool calls and ended with unfinished work; a new user `continue` resumed the task.

## User Impact

Recovery is told to continue the outstanding request, honor newer instructions, reconcile pending actions before retrying, and finish and verify the work or explain a genuine blocker. Existing permissions, cancellation, routing, and one-recovery limits are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared instruction is reduced from 58 words to 36 rather than adding runtime guards, queues, or retry machinery. The same guidance serves standalone recovery and eligible queued follow-ups. Queue documentation is aligned with that behavior. This does not fix the separate watchdog/liveness issue.

## Evidence

- Added two real-model regression cases using the actual recovery builder and native embedded runner: pending-work completion and a newer corrective instruction. Both pass with `gpt-6.1-sol`; each verifies one operation start, completion before writing, the correct saved value, and readback.
- Canonical native whole-runner before/after checks with a genuine asynchronous comparison worker both passed: one start, no write before completion, saved value `21`, and readback. The fresh baseline did not reproduce the historical failure.
- Existing stalled-turn coverage: **10 passed**; steering: **13 passed**; follow-up and queue-custody coverage: **34 passed**.
- A scoped allocation covers exactly 216 net test lines for these real-model completion, single-start, newer-instruction and readback regressions. The shared test-line ceiling is unchanged.
- Exact candidate test types, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent review reports no findings.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and scope of the evidence</summary>

Run the maintained live cases with:

`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live -- src/auto-reply/reply/stalled-turn-recovery.live.test.ts`

The historical zero-tool recovery is an inspected real incident, not a newly reproduced deterministic test failure. Fresh synthetic baseline runs also completed successfully. The new tests exercise the desired completion contract; they do not establish a statistical reliability improvement or guarantee model behavior. An early experiment with a test-side completion timer was discarded because it could misrepresent a pending job as having no completion mechanism.

The prompt cannot by itself guarantee completion or exactly-once effects. Existing tool/authority owners remain responsible for outcome reconciliation. No permissions or required approvals are bypassed.

</details>

Credit: @VACInc.

## Work sessions

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes authorized local Codex `/goal` sessions stopping after an incomplete turn when optional Gateway operator roles are not configured.

## User Impact

Local goals can continue under the already-admitted source authority. Remote-worker execution still requires operator authority. No configuration migration or deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve Codex placement independently of the optional operator capability, then require that capability for remote workers at both enqueue and admission. Existing source, cancellation, goal-state, budget, and fresh-placement checks remain in place. This uses OpenClaw's existing continuation queue; it does not enable Codex's separate native goal engine.

## Evidence

- Three local-no-authority regression cases fail on the original implementation and pass with the fix.
- **175 tests passed:** 83 continuation-owner cases, 38 admission cases, and 54 Gateway goal/queue cases.
- Independent **P0–P3 review: clean**, with complete owner, test, and caller context. No hostile behavior identified in the reviewed changes.
- Formatting, core/core-test typechecks, core/scripts lint, dead-export checks, test-line budget, and the remaining focused authority guards passed. The PR-specific test-line allocation was removed as requested; the lower ceiling still passes with 36 lines of slack. Production code and regression tests are unchanged by that follow-up.
- The full `check:changed` run found an **inherited changelog-attribution failure** in archived release notes. It reproduces on main `055544b9fa35317f2cf19c0f74736edd0ba9e0ea` with identical checker/data inputs. Its overall time limit interrupted the final pairing guards; both passed when run separately. No unrelated release history was edited.
- Gateway proof uses test harnesses, not a live external channel/provider. The original incident's historical logs do not uniquely establish which gate rejected its continuation.
- Exact-head CI is green for `4e2e47efb82632c40e4dad8e042cd43d8eb065ff`: [CI run 42403841933](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42403841933), 49 passed and 61 non-applicable/skipped checks; native CI watcher returned GREEN. Security and dependency-review statuses pass.
- Final source/security and regression-coverage review found no actionable issues. Production code, tests, and their relevant main-branch context are unchanged from the completed independent P0–P3 review.
- Hosted ClawSweeper has not produced a review: its retries fail with `Could not obtain complete review blob size metadata.` This is not approval. Landing uses the completed independent review and native enforced gates, as explicitly requested by the PR author.

Test cost: the two focused files took 91.70s including compiler preparation; the Gateway suite took 276.33s. These reuse existing suites rather than adding another Gateway boot.

prs.title: fix(channels): unblock ingress after a transient shutdown release failure
prs.body:
Closes #193019

## Main compatibility refresh — 2026-11-06

Published merge head `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`, integrating main `b11b610d173cc6ff87eb026b6506c20fc7e5fd62` without rewriting PR history. The single `ingress-drain.ts` conflict is resolved preserving upstream failure callback extraction, queue-cap drops, selective custody retirement and test consolidation.

**Updated scope:** main #193423 already mitigates the old indefinite hold by retiring failed drains and permitting recovery of known never-adopted claims after disposal. This PR retains the bounded, token-fenced native cancellation-release retry before disposal; it does not claim current main remains indefinitely blocked. Pinned-main production overlay fails the focused retry regression (one release instead of two). Exhaustion coverage now follows upstream recovery after joined disposal; uncertain outcomes remain fenced.

**New-head verification:** 180 tests across 13 affected files passed; final worker handoff rerun 12 passed, coordinator independent rerun 12 passed. Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, source-line ratchet and scoped whitespace passed. Independent exact-head semantic review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install used target-identical manifests/lockfile. Test-line ratchet retains main's 25-line debt: pinned main is 25 over, candidate is 25 over, and the PR adds exactly its existing 182-line grant. No shared ceiling was changed. New-head CI is not claimed green.

**Proof provenance:** all Telegram/Claude live evidence below remains historical at `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. Writer bytes are equivalent, but upstream custody/disposal, dependencies and test contracts changed; no live-proof equivalence or new-head live run is claimed. No production restart or new Telegram traffic occurred.

Later observed main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e` also merge-probes cleanly; intervening changes are iOS tooling, so no additional merge was introduced.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued channel messages remain blocked when a pre-adoption cancellation release fails once during shutdown and the retained old drain continues holding its claim.

## User Impact

A transient known release failure can recover automatically so a replacement monitor can deliver the queued conversation. Cancellation preserves delivery retry history. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained cancellation after abort now joins at most three token-fenced release attempts, with 1s and 2s backoffs. The existing settlement owner holds custody throughout. Explicit disposal prevents another attempt; failed completion, ordinary abandonment, standalone drains, and uncertain write outcomes keep their existing safety behavior. Exhaustion or an uncertain cancellation write remains observable and retains custody. The bounded retry can add up to three seconds of backoff to shutdown, plus storage I/O.

## Evidence

- A real production ingress monitor stop/restart with an actual isolated SQLite-backed queue fails on the unchanged base and passes with the repair. One known failure is injected before the native release write; the lifecycle callback is invoked only once. The replacement processes same-lane events in order, rejects stale-token writes, and does not replay already-adopted unrelated work.
- Focused drain, monitor, handoff and claim-owner suites: 73 tests passed. Added checks cover exhausted retries, nested uncertain outcomes, explicit disposal during backoff, takeover during retry, standalone cancellation and ordinary abandonment. Existing failed-completion and retry-history controls pass.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, line-cap/test-line ratchets and whitespace checks are recorded in the local handoff.
- Independent shared autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, one pass over the complete uncommitted candidate against `06d4059a3d06` and supplied unchanged owner context; no actionable findings. This is evidence-based review, without a repository mount or test execution in the reviewer sandbox. Subsequent test edits only added required braces and an explicit already-completed return and removed a redundant default type argument. The coordinating parent independently inspected the final source and clean commit and reran all 10 boundary cases successfully.

**Initial test scope (historical; supplemented by the real Telegram/model run below):** proof here is the owning monitor/SQLite boundary with a synthetic pre-write failure. Actual SQLite locking, a complete Gateway process, a real agent/model, and Telegram transport were not exercised; no live outage reproduction is claimed. Exact live Gateway channel stop/restart under an actual storage lock remains a broader integration gap. No external API or transport contract changes here.

The dedicated allocation grants exactly 182 added test lines for this recovery regression and its distinct custody bounds; the shared baseline is unchanged. The change reuses existing owners and removes redundant release wrappers; production code grows by 12 lines. The four-suite run took 41.92s including worker preparation; the final boundary file took 4.63s in Vitest (50.61s wrapper including compiler preparation), and the parent independently measured 4.92s (53.90s wrapper). CI timing is unmeasured before publication.


## Additional shipped-entry-point evidence — 2026-11-05

The earlier Evidence section describes the initial monitor tests. This additional run used the real built CLI/Gateway, its plugin loader, and the public `channels.stop` / `channels.start` RPCs. It was **not another in-process monitor test**. The channel was a task-only local diagnostic plugin (`ingress-proof/default`), not Telegram. Its delivery callback deliberately calls synthetic `onDeferred` / `onAdopted`; **no real agent/model response or external transport was exercised, so this does not claim the root real-agent/model E2E gate is fully satisfied**.

**Isolation and provenance.** Separate task HOME, config, SQLite state, workspace and loopback ports; only the diagnostic plugin enabled; no provider credentials copied, no production Gateway restart/config/state change, no real-channel messages. The same fixture and one-shot fault wrapper ran against head `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2` and runtime inputs from base `06d4059a3d06e1a34a3cacfd3f635b93fe803a38`. For the base run, only the two owner files were temporarily restored byte-for-byte from the base and rebuilt through the CLI; all other runtime inputs matched base (only the new test/allocation differed). This was a documented base-runtime overlay in the head checkout, not a Git checkout whose HEAD changed. Original source was restored afterward.

The external plugin uses public SDK `createChannelIngressMonitor` and `api.runtime.state.openChannelIngressQueue`. It throws exactly once **before** calling the native release operation, logs refresh only after the real queue returns `true`, and reads the committed queue via the public API. There is no SQLite method mock, SQL reset, forced owner retirement, manual second cancellation callback, or claimed actual `SQLITE_BUSY`. The fixture SHA-256 is `d1d039654e952e53eff1e39baa8680360637a26f3e8cf0bad372773df0b7fcb3`.

**Base observation.** Real Gateway PID `95449`: the channel stop RPC reported `stopped: true`, but the internal joined monitor stop rejected the injected error. Starting the replacement channel did not drain its lane. Only `unrelated` was synthetically adopted; `task` remained claimed and `waiting` pending. Committed `claimedAt` values advanced at `2026-11-05T11:03:19.612+09:00`, `2026-11-05T11:03:21.614+09:00`, and `2026-11-05T11:03:58.706+09:00`; heartbeat commit counts were `[4, 6, 43]`. This is a bounded observation of continued old-owner renewal, not an empirical claim that it can never recover.

```text
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":95449,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-abort","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":95449,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-rejected","generation":1,"pid":95449,"message":"Error: Synthetic known cancellation release failure before native write","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback-returned","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:58 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
```

**Head observation.** Real Gateway PID `93148` remained the same across channel generation 1→2. One cancellation callback caused one known pre-write failure, then release attempt 2 committed about one second later and joined stop succeeded. The replacement synthetically adopted `task`, then `waiting`; the already-adopted `unrelated` was not replayed. The old token's release/complete/refresh all returned `false`, the successor token differed, and re-enqueue of `unrelated` returned `completed`. Final pending and claimed sets were empty.

```text
10:58:29 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:58:59 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"unrelated","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":2,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-result","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","committed":true,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"stale-token-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"release":false,"complete":false,"refresh":false,"changed":true}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"waiting","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:14 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"dedupe-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"kind":"completed"}
11:00:37 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
```

**Shipped command path.** Under each task-only environment: `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`; then `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call` with `--expect-url` pinned to that task's configured loopback Gateway, using `ingressProof.seed`, `ingressProof.arm`, `channels.stop`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, `channels.start`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, and `ingressProof.dedupe` (head). Public lifecycle params were `{"channel":"ingress-proof","accountId":"default"}`. All these RPC commands exited 0; the base's reported stop success is distinguished above from its monitor failure. Both task Gateways later handled SIGTERM and exited 0 with clean shutdown. No commit/push was required for this instrumentation.

**Interpretation and limits.** A generally slow model cannot explain this comparison because no model runs; identical fixture, queue, lane and fault behavior plus the advancing native timestamps distinguish a retained old-owner claim from a delayed initial read. However, the fixture deliberately supplies deferred/cancelled work and observes its own callback receipts. Its synthetic adoption is not evidence of agent execution, outbound send, Telegram acceptance, or user-visible response. It does not prove an actual database lock, indefinite blockage beyond the observed interval, every channel adapter, or a whole-Gateway process restart. It proves a real Gateway-hosted local channel stop/replacement through shipped entry points with actual SQLite persistence. Whether this layer satisfies the requested real-behavior gate remains for review; the broader real agent/model/transport gap is explicit.


## Real Telegram and real model recovery evidence — 2026-11-05

**Observed result:** recovery eventually succeeded through the production Telegram adapter, real Claude CLI agent/model, and Telegram Bot API. It did **not** succeed on the first replacement: the task relay refused two overlapping local polls and the adapter automatically restarted twice before both replies completed. The human operator confirmed in the Telegram client that the replies arrived in A → B order. Per-event counts below are backed by the queue, transcript and Bot API receipts; the human confirmation specifically establishes client-visible order.

Pinned PR head: `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. The requesting user confirmed their dedicated bot was unused elsewhere, then sent a fresh exact handshake and prescribed A/B prompts manually in the verified private DM. No automated user account or team QA pool was used. The isolated Gateway had task-owned config/state/workspace/ports. A parent-owned, destination-bound protected HTTPS relay consumed the stored token sentinel; no credential value was extracted or copied into the Gateway. The operator Gateway was untouched.

Temporary instrumentation held only A before real admission and injected one known error before the original claim's native cancellation release write. It never invoked synthetic adoption. Native cancellation, the PR's existing bounded writer retry, real Telegram replay, real agent/model execution and outbound delivery remained production paths. Setup `deleteWebhook` was a recorded local no-op after verified empty webhook; no upstream webhook deletion or queue flush occurred. Command-menu deletion attempts were refused locally.

Measured timeline, KST:

```text
13:31:16.764  A held before native adoption
13:31:58.907  bound B observed by real Telegram poller
13:32:36.938  read-only task SQLite: A claimed, B pending; same lane; attempts=0
13:32:38.283  one known pre-write release failure for original A token
13:32:39.285  second release attempt for that same token (+1002ms)
13:32:40      manual channel replacement starts
13:32:41      local concurrent-poll refusal; automatic restart scheduled
13:32:47–48   first automatic restart also hits local poll guard
13:32:58      second automatic restart starts
13:32:59.308  real A adoption/completion write commits with new claim token
13:33:03.954  Telegram accepts final A response
13:33:04.053  real B adoption/completion write commits
13:33:06.414  Telegram accepts final B response
```

The old long-poll request remained in the relay until its bounded upstream request returned after the downstream client was cancelled. The relay's single-poll guard refused the two successor attempts rather than starting another upstream poller. This was task relay lifecycle behavior, not a second bot consumer or a newly fixed PR behavior. No queue reset, forced retirement, manual second cancellation callback or failed-send retry was used to recover.

Final read-only SQLite inspection found exactly A and B, both `completed`, both attempts=0, with no pending/claimed work. The real agent transcript contains exactly two assistant records matching the prescribed A and B responses in order, both `provider=claude-cli`, `api=cli`, with actual usage: A input10/output181/cache-write11936; B input10/output81/cache-read11936/cache-write710. Telegram returned two distinct accepted message receipts, A then B; no duplicate-send refusal or uncertain-send event occurred. Native launch/probe/maintenance subprocess counts are not misrepresented as exactly two model requests. The separate one-shot provider setup qualification is excluded from this recovery proof.

The native Claude child used its existing login without copying credentials, with global home file writes denied by an OS policy, tools/customizations and native session persistence disabled. Gateway/OpenClaw state stayed task-owned. This was a real provider, not mock-openai or synthetic `onAdopted`. Source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte, Git was clean at the pinned head, and the uninstrumented head build completed successfully. The Gateway logged a clean shutdown in82ms; its launcher group received SIGTERM and reported-15, so that wrapper is not reported as exit0. Parent verified the protected relay ended code0 and both task ports closed. No live task processes remain; persistent review Remote is retained.

**Client observation:** on 2026-11-05 at 13:43 KST the human operator confirmed the replies arrived in order. This is a human client observation, not an inference from Bot API acceptance.

**Limits:** Actual SQLite locking, every transport/provider, and whole-Gateway restart were not tested or required for this known pre-write failure. The earlier base/head Gateway comparison and existing safety regressions are separate supporting evidence. This run establishes eventual real-channel/model/outbound recovery with the explicit transient relay failures above; it is not presented as a clean first-restart run or proof of all client-rendering behavior.

prs.title: fix: OpenClaw ID sign-out and sign-in asks to re-approve an already-approved browser
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: signing out of OpenClaw ID and back in on an already-approved browser asks the Gateway owner to re-approve that browser, under the title "Approve the new role", even though it asks for the same role and scopes as before.

## User Impact

User impact: an OpenClaw ID browser that signs out and back in reconnects with the access it was already approved for, without a prompt. A new role, added scopes, or a different device still needs owner approval. When a prompt is needed, the Control UI now says what is being requested instead of always saying "new role".

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw ID remote sign-out revokes the browser's Gateway tokens but intentionally keeps its device approved. Effective roles only count active tokens, so the next connect reported the approved `operator` role as a `role-upgrade`. No auto-approval lane accepts a repair with that reason, so it fell through to a manual prompt. This is the generic re-pair path, triggered by OpenClaw ID sign-out. It is not specific to the tunnel, and it is not caused by the `trusted-proxy` approval provenance.

- **Gateway:** on the OpenClaw ID lane only, a same-key reconnect for a role that the device row already approves gets that role's token back. The scopes are first capped by membership and connection, and the token is issued only when they fit inside the row's approved scopes. Anything broader stays a manual owner decision. Generic trusted-proxy `deviceAutoApprove`, remote-ingress, local and node lanes are unchanged.
- **Approval kernel:** a revoked token's old scopes no longer set the scopes of its replacement when the request names scopes. The new token gets what the request asked for, so a narrower reconnect after sign-out is not blocked by the old grant.
- **Connect error details:** these now describe the merged pending request that approval would grant. If the request carries an earlier role the device doesn't have, that role is reported.
- **Control UI:** the login gate titles the prompt by what approval adds. "Approve this browser again" means the same access as before. A scope prompt names the added scopes. "Approve the new role" names the role.

Accepted edge case: an owner's explicit `devices revoke` of an OpenClaw ID browser is also restored on that browser's next connect. A fresh key from the same admitted principal is already auto-paired on this lane, so revocation was never a lasting block there. Removing the OpenClaw ID membership still refuses admission.

## Evidence

- Reproduced first through the real WebSocket connect path over the OpenClaw ID tunnel test harness. The owner reconnected after token revocation and got `reason: "role-upgrade"`, the same role and the same six scopes. That test now passes.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts`: owner and operator-member restores; fewer scopes (only those are issued); more than approved still pending; a merged pending `node` role is named and stays pending. The last two cases from review fail without the repair.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts`: on the non-OpenClaw ID trusted-proxy lane, a revoked token's reconnect with the same access still waits for the owner (flag-off guard).
- `ui/src/components/login-gate.test.ts`: restore, added-scope and new-role titles.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything passes (core/UI typecheck, core lint, dead-export scan, ratchets, i18n catalog) except `changelog attributions`, which fails identically on main (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`, untouched here).
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: this PR adds 140 test lines with a matching allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-signout-restore.txt`). The tree stays 5 over the ceiling, which main already is on its own.
- UI oxlint on the changed UI files: clean. Scoped suites on HEAD: tunnel, trusted-proxy auto-approve, Control UI auth, device pairing, ingress approval, local/trusted-CIDR node pairing, remote sign-out, login gate, connect-error, gateway-store auth/retention. All pass.
- Independent security review (isolated, read-only) found two P2s: a narrower reconnect was refused by the revoked token's scopes, and "nothing new" copy could hide a merged role. Both are fixed and covered by tests. Re-review: clean, with no P0–P2 findings.

Login gate before and after, using the same `role-upgrade` request (same role and same six scopes as in the issue):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Same role, same six scopes (the OCF-495 case) | ![before: Approve the new role](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da1daa69-ea38-495b-9bea-15735b2e1bc5) | ![after: Approve this browser again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f939eb9-b0b4-4819-af8a-5aec6429833c) |
| Role not yet approved (a real new role) | ![before: Approve the new role](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f65aeb5-3781-4ba4-99da-c3e5dc59877c) | ![after: Approve the new role, naming operator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bad753c2-7703-4bcc-b185-275e7d890f4c) |

Captured from the production Control UI build with a mocked Gateway connect rejection (`role-upgrade`, request `7f6e33d0…`), on main `936f38793bab` and on this branch.

Not done: a live sign-out/sign-in cycle on staging gateway3. The tunnel tests use the canonical token revocation that sign-out performs.

prs.title: fix(crabbox): require the published 0.82.0 distribution
prs.body:
Related: #190941

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's managed Crabbox installer selects 0.81.0, which predates the runner-registration cancellation and portable cleanup fixes needed for the Boat cutover.

## User Impact

Managed worker, sandbox, and remote-proof commands use the published Crabbox 0.82.0 distribution. Older executables are preserved and the existing managed installer prepares a supported copy. Boat defaults and runner credentials are unchanged. Restricted hosts without release-download access must provision a supported executable before using these routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raise the existing shared minimum to 0.82.0 and align supported-version fixtures and minimum-version documentation. The installer, platform selection, checksums, cache, and fallback behavior continue to use the same owner. There is no new runtime machinery or net test-line growth.

The immutable [0.82.0 release](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.82.0) includes [registration cancellation settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3045) and [portable runner cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3046).

## Evidence

- Independent review of all 13 changed files: no actionable findings.
- Commit hooks, formatting, documentation inventory, syntax checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Published Darwin ARM64 archive: checksum, all six runtime hashes, Foundation signatures, hardened runtime, timestamps, and online notarization verified; CLI reports 0.82.0. No provider resources were allocated.

- Exact-head native proof: 43 managed-binary/provider tests passed (55.97s command), covering fresh installation, preservation of an old executable/distribution, offline reuse, and version admission. Ten selected wrapper cases passed (43.88s; 279 unrelated cases unselected).

prs.title: improve(knowledge): reduce redundant work during cold loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cold Knowledge catalog scan performs a history lookup for every record immediately after writing its observation, even though that new row already establishes non-agent provenance.

## User Impact

Cold scans do less database work without changing revisions, agent bylines, conversions, or lifecycle behavior. This is a small second hillclimb, not a claim that all cold loading is now fast.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip the redundant lookup only after the observation owner just inserted an observed/external-edit row. Unchanged records retain writer and conversion lookups; deletion handling and lifecycle guards remain unchanged.

Follows merged #194792. Vyctor authorized landing both at 20:38 UTC on November 7, superseding the earlier hold. This PR is being rebased onto main before its final required checks.

## Evidence

- Owning scan regression is red on the original code: two newly observed records cause two writer SELECTs; with this change they cause zero. Rename/deletion/restoration revisions remain correct.
- An 8,000-record synthetic cold catalog avoids 8,000 unnecessary history SELECTs. Initial single runs were 4,658 ms before / 4,495 ms after; this is not a statistically established speedup. The deterministic improvement is removed work.
- The initial combined stack passed 48 focused tests. After consolidating duplicate fixtures, the first layer passed 34 store/UI tests on Node. The SQL spy was repaired to preserve native statement overloads, and full extension test typing passed.
- Extension production typechecking, targeted formatting/lint, and git diff --check passed. Rebased-head required CI remains a landing gate.
- Independent local review with full affected-module context found no actionable defects.
- The real Gateway inventory timing improvement belongs to #194792, not this smaller observation optimization.

Limits: selected-store cold parsing and observation still take several seconds. Full browser paint was not measured. The pre-existing vocabulary lint finding is disclosed in #194792. Further profiling and a larger bounded-batching candidate are separate from this PR.

Related: #180298.

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing File can reopen a media-source chooser when the user wants to browse files and document providers directly.

## User Impact

On browsers exposing direct file browsing, **Files** opens that route with unrestricted file types and multiple selection. Unknown extensions and `.stl` files use the normal attachment pipeline. Selection stages a draft; sending stays explicit.

**Scope:** this is the supported-browser Files contribution, not final cross-platform separation. Browsers without the direct API retain their existing File/Attach… route. The iPhone experience and final unsupported-browser UX remain reserved to #180298; no overlapping chooser is newly accepted as the desired fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mounted composer invokes `showOpenFilePicker()` from the user gesture, then uses the existing attachment admission, preparation, draft and send owners. Cancellation preserves the draft; failures report errors without silently opening a different chooser. Late results cannot populate a replacement draft or unmounted composer.

Image-only composers, arbitrary documents, file-provider access, upload policy, size checks, lazy camera registration and permission documentation remain intact. No file-type allowlist, custom filesystem browser, persistent handles, permission changes or deployment is introduced.

Proposed and directed by **Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit)**.

prs.title: fix(subagents): parents miss results from independently resumed children
prs.body:
## Merge-Readiness Status

**Not merge-ready.** A subsequent qualified Crabbox run exposed a remaining real late-result failure on `94b08a2`: the child finishes successfully after the parent waiting turn ends, but completion retries because operator execution authority is inactive. A separate real admitted guest-parent regression also exposed loss of the requester's model ceiling on resume. Corrections are in progress; the earlier passing checks below do not establish either invariant. No merge or deployment is requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parent sessions missing successful child results when siblings were admitted under different operator invocations or the originating invocation ended.

## Intended User Impact

Accepted child results should return once to their recorded parent without retaining the spawning operator invocation. Parent execution and external effects must retain their normal policy and lifecycle checks. No new settings are intended; previously terminal non-delivery receipts are not automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete retained operator completion custody and the mixed-authority batch policy instead of adding authority-compatible batching. Internal settlement uses the existing registry, controller and receipt ownership. Preserve requester accounting, generation/incarnation checks, cancellation and idempotency.

The accepted agent turn keeps the Gateway instance lifetime as its execution fence, not the caller input-admission callback. Ordinary sender/communication contracts are unchanged. Detached typing owns its own existing effect authority. Committed registration recovery metadata survives a caller disappearing before acknowledgment.

## Evidence on the Published Candidate

- Two owning-boundary regressions are red on the original source (zero parent wakes) and green with the candidate: independent caller contexts, invocation retirement, both results exactly once, and duplicate terminal events. The wake does not borrow a sibling operator.
- Gateway authorization/lifecycle/transcript, pause, requester settlement, store replacement, registration/publication and worker ownership checks passed in the recorded local runs.
- Core and core-test TypeScript, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed before the subsequent repairs. These are not current proof for the in-progress corrections.
- An isolated real-provider completion-provenance probe passed, but it did not expose the later held-child boundary below.
- Local Codex autoreview through P2 completed scoped-clean on the earlier candidate. Retired-policy tests and the native-completion fixture correction received supplemental review.
- The native-completion fixture now owns ordinary input lifetimes explicitly. Both revocation cases and the nearby 36-test set passed; no production completion lease or authority comparison was restored.

## Real Crabbox Finding Requiring Repair

Configured provider: **Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox**, lease `tbx_01m6vs51qgakqhkfva54fnzpnr`, exact clean published head `94b08a2b4eccc0645203a646b954207b7c3fdb9c`. Prepared Node 24.22.1; observed 4 CPUs and approximately 16.6 GB RAM. CI-owned OpenAI credential, isolated test state/HOME, no source-loader injection.

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-late-reply.live.test.ts`.

The real Gateway/agent/subagent/native-exec flow reached the decisive boundary: the parent waiting turn finished before the held child was released. The child then ended `ok`, while recorded completion stayed pending/retryable with `operator execution authority is no longer active`; the parent-consumption assertion timed out. This is a product failure, not a setup failure. Verified synthetic evidence is retained locally with SHA-256 `d1d3208e0d36dc95409269fab07e86ed640f5ffaafd4ffb1fb8c77ee52c48793`. The owned Testbox was stopped after evidence collection.

The remaining completion boundary must shed ambient request-client/tool-caller authority while retaining its recorded Gateway/controller/task relationship and parent lifecycle checks. Separately, continuation must preserve the requester's own model restriction facts without borrowing a child's human grant. Guest ceiling assertions will not be removed to make CI green. Combined fresh review, focused checks, and a corrected real Crabbox replay remain required.

## CI Context

Guest spawn/yield cases expose the model-policy issue above. Stop/followup CI failures passed focused local reproduction but are not considered remotely cleared. The earlier update-canary synthetic-merge assertion expects `requester-revoked`, while upstream #194659 produces `UpdateInterruptedError("interrupted")`; no update/canary repair is bundled here. A selected Postgres job also ended by cancellation rather than a recorded test assertion. Final current-head CI and substantive hosted review still need reconciliation.

- @jalehman

## What Problem This Solves

The campaign's 14-state signed-in dashboard deep-link reload motivated this rig-only DOM replay experiment. On five synthetic real old-page reload workloads, first witnessed replay surfaces arrive at 199–264 ms, but four show a skeleton first. All workloads also delay live rows substantially.

## User Impact

Report-only stop: no product behavior change, product implementation or client HTML store. This experiment draft is closed without merging.

## Why This Change Was Made

An opt-in rig probe measures passive DOM replay, its actual first compositor surface, handoff fidelity and the live-app cost before proposing persistence. The requested complete first-frame experience is not qualified by this implementation.

## Evidence

One fixed AWS c7a.4xlarge lease (`cbx_3fe849c57427`), repository headless Chromium, 12 alternating-order A/B pairs plus 12 A/A pairs per workload. Application build pinned to `84b79b298a9a1a04b30fd2873ee83852ff3e1c9e`; L300 driver pinned to `3257c0d02ff644a7c8e06e33211e9a40f751234e`. Values below are rows Element Timing, median [IQR] in ms; the final column subtracts matching A/A medians within each order before averaging.

| Synthetic workload | Baseline | Replay | Adjusted delay |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native active | 620 [583, 652] | 1294 [1199, 1319] | +651 |
| Native archived | 558 [552, 599] | 992 [960, 1050] | +397 |
| Native dashboard | 618 [568, 645] | 922 [902, 950] | +300 |
| Team active | 530 [501, 553] | 838 [812, 856] | +340 |
| Team archived | 468 [455, 486] | 724 [709, 749] | +260 |

Every A/B rows pair is worse, with non-overlapping arm IQRs in all five workloads. The dashboard content-DOM marker is also +349 ms after control. These are costs of this implementation, not a lower bound on every possible passive representation.

Iframe content is absent from the replay. The native dashboard widget alone changes 34% of its region at handoff. An avoidable native font flash came from removing temporary loaded font declarations while the canonical faces were still unloaded. Separate retention-only visual attribution reduces native active's raw swap difference from 6.83% to 0.44%; this is not a proposed production font lifecycle or a new paired timing result. Images also require actual paint/decode evidence: a warm native community image initially leaves a reserved empty area.

Only three files under `scripts/perf/` change: the opt-in preload, its guide, and explicitly labeled endpoint-only post-capture analysis for timing repetitions. Production runtime LOC delta is **0**. The requested filtered diff stat is **674 insertions, 1 deletion (net +673)**, entirely experimental tooling/guide; no product path is added or superseded.

Proof: full remote build; 240 scored warm reloads with rows markers and 192 open-Details markers; all 144 native captures have one document request and no page errors; five complete visual audits; passive/nested custom-element and witness pixel controls. One invalid compositor-clock block was preserved and replaced as a whole; its guard was not relaxed. The changed-file gate passed types and broader guards, then exposed script lint issues; those were repaired and targeted checks rerun. Final-head lint, format, script typecheck and line-cap checks pass, with a clean isolated Codex review. The original exact-head selected code checks passed (7 successful, 58 skipped). A later metadata refresh rejected the report-body rewrite for missing template headings; this edit restores those headings and keeps the experiment closed. No UI source changed; no full UI-suite qualification is claimed.

No captured HTML or images were committed or uploaded. The detailed synthetic evidence, per-pair deltas, remaining fidelity gaps, and proposal-only storage/security/ownership sketch are retained in the lane report. No schema, stored server shape, product configuration option, publication, or release changes.

Closing this remote-clone experiment draft without merging. Recommendation: do not approve a persisted full-page HTML projection from this prototype; first resolve paint admission, canonical font ownership, live-app cost, and passive widget representation.

prs.title: fix(learn): allow explicitly sandbox-compatible plugin contributors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The /learn dispatcher rejects every sandboxed turn before it checks plugin contributions or tool policy. A plugin with a host-backed, scoped learning tool therefore cannot expose /learn in a sandbox, even when that tool is allowed and validates its requester at the write boundary. The bundled Skill Workshop remains host-backed and should continue to be rejected by default.

## Change

- Add an optional LearnContribution.sandboxCompatible flag, defaulting to false.
- Filter sandboxed contributions before building the capability profile. Eligible contributions still pass the existing model, harness, tool-surface and per-tool policy checks. The flag does not grant tool access or bypass a plugin tool's own authorization.
- Document the SDK contract and make the generic unavailable reply accurate for both ordinary and compatible contributors.

## Evidence

- Based on openclaw/openclaw main a6ee6a18a5d748a8ed8e395b63c4a5d2a6e02982.
- The new regression fails on the unmodified base at the sandbox admission assertion (14 passed, 1 failed), then passes with this change (15/15). It covers an opted-in skills contributor, a non-opted-in memory contributor and a denied skill tool. The existing sandbox/default-deny cases remain green.
- Windows focused test: 269.56 s wall time after the final refactor, including 244.96 s transform/setup; 15 tests pass. Core and commands test TypeScript graphs, changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, docs link audit (16,475 links, zero broken), git diff check and test-line ratchet pass.
- An independent Connector Gateway CI on the same pinned main applies the equivalent per-contribution host patch plus the separate unmerged sandbox-fact fix, then passes real fork and sandbox-mode fixtures: https://github.com/WangKangAandy/dingtalk-openclaw-connector-fix-Community/actions/runs/42388448260 . This is combination evidence, not an exact-head upstream Gateway run or a stock-main claim.
- Local autoreview was attempted on this final source but produced no report after a prolonged live process; it is not counted as a clean review.

## Scope

This change only governs which learning contributors may enter a sandboxed /learn turn. It does not change the bundled Skill Workshop contribution, CLI sandbox support, tool grants, or the prepared-sandbox fact issue in #191205.
