prs.title: fix(gateway): expose session model selection provenance
prs.body:
Closes #149341

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.list` reports the same model for a configured default and an explicit selection, without telling callers which source supplied it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSessionSelectedModelRef` labels its answer as `runtime`, `override`, or `configured`. The existing selection owner derives this result on reads; the row and `sessions_list` forward it.

## User Impact

The optional `modelSelectionSource` distinguishes identical values. It reports the existing resolution stage, not the model used by every execution path. Selected and active values retain their meanings. No UI display changes.

## Evidence

### Current head (2026-10-13)

The current head is `c121729b65eb6a9ee25a6f09c5f4904922161348`. It merges main
`e0bb91e1542957cbab98326753a38fa667ce4d5f` into `8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf`
without conflicts. The PR diff against main is unchanged (ten files, +156/-5); this
merge adds no PR code. [CI run 38352360624](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352360624)
completed successfully for this head on 2026-10-13 at 05:50 UTC. That includes `build-artifacts`
and the shard that runs `src/gateway/session-utils.metadata-perf.test.ts`, where both
thinking cases below pass.

**Attribution of the three red checks on `8396b904b78`.** [CI run 38348089309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348089309)
tested `8396b904b78` merged into main `78410c7b949614e158c1be8bd8d64f5a6a0ec7a2`.
Both failures were already present on that main commit, and main fixed both shortly after it:

- **`build-artifacts`** reported `extensions/workboard/openclaw.plugin.json` as stale.
  Main regenerated exactly that file in [`faa8ad8e598`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/faa8ad8e598)
  ("fix(workboard): regenerate browser asset manifest"), whose parent is `78410c7b949`.
  This PR does not touch `extensions/workboard/`. On `8396b904b78` (base `c86edb99b3d`),
  rebuilding the Workboard Control UI reproduced the committed manifest bytes. On the
  current head, `pnpm plugins:assets:check` reports "Generated bundled plugin assets
  match the committed bytes."
- **`checks-node-changed-compact-large-19`** failed the two cases
  "preserves a stored level with a missing/identity-only catalog after warming thinking
  facts" in `src/gateway/session-utils.metadata-perf.test.ts`. This PR does not touch
  that file or the thinking-facts code. Both cases failed locally the same way on main
  `c86edb99b3d` with this PR's ten files reverted to main: `thinkingOptions` fell back to
  the default ladder, and the policy call count was 2 instead of 1. Main fixed this in
  [`7b871cd72f2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b871cd72f2) (#170659,
  "retain thinking facts across partial catalog rows"), which also updates that test
  file. On the current head the file passes 7/7, and it passes 7/7 on main
  `e0bb91e1542` with this PR's files reverted.
- **`openclaw/ci-gate`** only aggregates the two jobs above.

No PR-caused failure was found, so this update contains no code change.

**Local validation on the current head:** all five PR test files passed (46 tests).
Lint, line ratchets, and the core typecheck were not rerun locally for this conflict-free
merge; the PR's ten files are byte-identical to `8396b904b78`, where they passed, and the
CI run above covers them on this head.

### Conflict resolution in `8396b904b78` (2026-10-13)

`8396b904b78` merged main `c86edb99b3d363c2b7e519289668f4fbab37a2c4`. Main had moved the
selection owner to prepared runtime ownership and reworked the row Golden test, so the
branch had become conflicting. These notes still describe the current code:

- **Conflict resolution keeps main's structure:** the [selection owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-model-selection.ts#L45)
  keeps main's prepared-ownership path and its new async wrapper. The sync
  resolver still labels the `runtime`, `override`, and `configured` branches,
  and the async wrapper inherits the field through its return type. The
  [row projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts#L586) keeps main's
  removal of the undefined active-model placeholders and copies
  `modelSelectionSource` as before.
- **Golden pins unchanged from main:** main now pins sorted wire values and
  asserts additive fields separately. This head follows that pattern: the
  [Golden hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts#L34)
  are main's values byte for byte, `modelSelectionSource` is excluded from the
  hashed wire fields, and a [separate assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts#L509)
  checks it for every fixture and timestamp: `override` for the three fixtures
  with a stored or inherited selection, `configured` for the other twelve
  (45 rows). The remaining wire fields still hash to main's unchanged pins, so
  the merge changes nothing else in those rows.
- **Moved test:** main removed `session-utils-model.identity.test.ts`. Its
  selection-ref case now lives in `session-utils-model.thinking-default.test.ts`,
  which expects `selectionSource: "override"` there. The registered
  `sessions.list` regression now prepares the runtime config snapshot before
  seeding entries, as main's session-store path resolution requires.
- **Local validation on this head:** all five PR test files passed (46 tests),
  plus 11 adjacent session row, projection, list, and chat-metadata suites
  (141 tests). Type-aware oxlint on the ten changed files, both line ratchets,
  the conflict-marker check, and the core typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`)
  passed. Swift generation was not rerun; the schema file merged without
  conflict.

### Previous head and compatibility evidence (2026-10-03)

The previous head was `67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d`, which merged main
`9c32426f5c19dbef12803c9a2952c14a658a29b3`. [CI run 37044752947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37044752947)
completed successfully for that head on 2026-10-02 at 18:17:30 UTC.

- **Read-time metadata, not stored state:** the [selection owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/src/gateway/session-utils-model-selection.ts#L30)
  labels the existing runtime, override, and configured branches. The [row projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts#L567)
  copies that result into `modelSelectionSource` on reads. This PR adds no field
  to stored `SessionEntry`, no storage writer, and no database migration.
- **Old/new response contract:** [SessionRowSchema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-row.ts#L273)
  makes the field optional and retains `additionalProperties: true`. Old rows
  may omit it; existing consumers can ignore the additive field. The earlier
  compatibility proof exercised actual new rows against the prior expected
  shape, old-shaped rows against the new schema, and old/new literals against
  packed public declarations with both optional-property modes. Those are
  retained earlier proofs, not new executions on this merge head.
- **Exact merge-head Golden evidence:** the 2026-10-02 merge validation compared
  17 fixtures at three timestamps, **51/51 exact matches** against main
  `9c32426f5c19dbef12803c9a2952c14a658a29b3` after removing only
  `modelSelectionSource`. `snapshotAt` was excluded by the existing test;
  all remaining JSON bytes and property order were preserved. Only then were
  the [Golden hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts#L33)
  updated. The temporary comparison instrumentation was removed and the regular
  test passed again.
- **Merge validation:** all five PR test files passed (35 tests); type-aware
  lint, both line ratchets, conflict-marker checks, Swift generation, and the
  Swift protocol check passed. Main's move of generated Swift output to
  `.build/protocol` was preserved; no generated native source remains in this
  PR's tracked diff.

The authenticated create/patch/list and three-row reopen observations below are
prior runtime evidence retained by the review. They are not a claim that the
full live scenario was rerun on either merge head. Source, Golden comparison,
targeted tests, and CI are the merge-head evidence.

### Earlier runtime and registered-handler evidence

Authenticated `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, and `sessions.list`: before, identical values had no source; after, configured and explicit selections have distinct markers. Reopening the same three stored session rows preserves every field and derives the markers again. No inference was requested.

The registered `sessions.list` regression also fails on main at `ece550b7c2df5a88c97ecc9a3d9938766ffdf83d` because the response omits the source. It passes with the fix, checking configured, explicit, inherited, and runtime selections with identical values, then runtime ownership removal. It calls the registered handler through `coreGatewayHandlers`; no row builder or list response is mocked.

## Compatibility

This additive response change was approved by the owner on 2026-09-16. The row schema already allows additional properties. Actual new rows pass the prior expected row shape, and old-shaped rows pass the new schema. Native protocol types were regenerated and checked. An external consumer compiled old and new row literals against packed public declarations with both optional-property modes. No storage migration, version bump, or new setting is needed.

## Consumers

Gateway clients and `sessions_list` receive the optional field. Search and placement retain their existing selection behavior.

## Invalidation

Each row derives the source from current ownership, overrides, and configuration; it is not stored independently.

## Change Size

Growth accepted under the owner's standing acceptance (2026-09-15).

At the current head, the diff against merged main is +27/-3 production lines across five files and +129/-2 test lines across five files. There is no tracked generated-native diff.

## Earlier test evidence

The earlier checked source includes main at `ece550b7c2df5a88c97ecc9a3d9938766ffdf83d`, merged in `7d385ec31b02c2e7af8b1d478529567e9e70cdce`. The earlier 310-test owner, schema, and tool result and unchanged generation/declaration proofs remain valid. Duplicate helper provenance checks were replaced with the registered handler case; identity, cache-order, context-window, and selected/active assertions remain.

Those earlier corrected suites passed 281 tests (not a new run on the current head):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-metadata.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-utils-model.identity.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts
```

The same-value regression command is:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-metadata.test.ts \
  -t 'sessions.list distinguishes selection sources'
```

prs.title: fix(research): keep deep research in the side panel and return findings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Idle Control UI sessions show both a "Deep research" header button and a full-width bar (reported by Ryan S. on Discord). Separately, portable research rejects otherwise usable detailed model replies when their lists exceed the schema limits, producing empty partial results.

## User Impact

Deep research is available through **side panel → New tab → Explore panels → Deep research**. The header controls, session-menu action, and transcript research card are removed. The panel retains the question, saved jobs, status, progress counts, sources, findings, report, gaps, and cancel/resume controls. The agent's `deep_research` tool remains available.

Start/resume tool results omit full source text and stay below 24 KB. They include a hint to call `action: "result"` with the job ID for the complete retained result; oversized compact results fall back to status plus that hint.

## Changes

- Keep Josh's research-quality fixes: state model list limits in the prompt and trim plan questions, extraction lists, and unanswered audit questions before validation. **Audit verdicts are not trimmed**; contradictory or repeated verdicts still reject the response. Exact quote checks and independent support audits remain intact.
- Keep bounded start/resume tool results and `reload.turnHandover: true` for the durable job service.
- Per Vyctor's direction, make the side panel the only plugin UI entry point. Delete the card, its inline descriptor, session-menu registration, unused styles, and alternate client mode rather than hiding them.
- Update the existing browser scenario to open research from Explore panels and assert the idle conversation has no research button.
- Reduce the test-line allocation from 110 to the final introduced **74** lines after removing card-specific coverage.

## Evidence

**Before:** idle session with the header button and full-width bar.

![Before: idle session with Deep research button and full-width bar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/038db128-d09b-4de8-ad67-d4a5b7be2117)

**After:** Deep research is listed under Explore panels, with no header controls or chat card.

![After: side panel launcher listing Deep research](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ebe0456-7368-4054-adc5-809c12443486)

![After: research panel with report](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dd1f272-3aeb-43e5-a63c-00b4e58240be)

![After: mobile panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9423e058-3614-4034-93e6-d7a6916ad350)

Captures use the actual native plugin bundle and a synthetic Gateway in `ui/src/e2e/deep-research-plugin.e2e.test.ts`. All four published images were decoded and visually inspected in the GitHub-rendered PR body HTML (scripts disabled).

### Validation and Review

- On `abcca6230ddf9145261c29e85904c1a9384e0523`: 104 plugin tests and both browser E2E scenarios passed; extension/UI-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and diff checks passed. The final `4c23b7def6a394b25c648f74faf924701036cd73` changes only the numeric test-line allocation; production and test sources are unchanged.
- Fresh independent source review of the complete change: no behavioral blocker. It identified the stale allocation now corrected, reran 59 focused tests successfully, and passed the extension import-boundary check. Read-only simplification review confirmed the removed UI paths have no remaining registrations.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): **scoped-clean**, base `11a9e5668b4aac5593cdc96227d689e6763e0533` to final head `4c23b7def6a394b25c648f74faf924701036cd73`. Coverage was the supplied complete diff; unchanged context and tests were not independently executed by that reviewer. Local ClawSweeper's available checkout was dirty, so the documented autoreview fallback was used.
- Earlier hosted review findings concerned card error rendering, the card descriptor import, and the card's report navigation. Those implementations are deleted by the requested side-panel-only change.
- CI run 42425777024 identified the oversized allocation (110 versus allowed growth 74); the final commit corrects it. The older-base local ratchet additionally reports one inherited line of baseline debt; current merge-ref CI is the landing gate, not a claimed green local replay.
- Josh's earlier live Gateway check reported seven exact-quote-backed findings for a question that previously ended partial with no findings. The research execution code is unchanged since that proof; the current UI proof is the synthetic browser scenario above.

Known gaps unchanged: source titles can expose `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` wrapper text, the 60 KB retained-corpus cap can starve later sources, and malformed JSON gets no repair attempt. In-chat card redesign is explicitly outside this PR.

Selecting a free-form slash command leaves no guidance about what to type next.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The original before/after images remain valid: preparation moved the hint derivation into the existing reactive composer frame without changing markup, styles, or behavior. The view consumes the prepared hint value. No new state owner or component was added.

## Validation

- Strict scoped lint and formatting pass for both changed source files, without exceptions. `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 7b205f0d5659b20834360c8f3867221a050b043c` passes. The view shrinks by 12 physical lines, the frame grows by 11, and one redundant view memo is removed.

The retained hint regression failed on the original implementation, and all 55 affected tests passed with the three slash changes combined. No broader suites were rerun solely for this extraction.

prs.title: feat(ui): ask about a selection in a new session
prs.body:
## Problem
The transcript selection toolbar can send a passage to the main composer or to Side chat, but you can't start a fresh session about it. Today that means copying the text and pasting it into Cmd+K.

## Solution
- The selection toolbar now shows three plain buttons: **Add to chat** (renamed from "Add to message"), **Ask in side chat**, and **New session**. There's no hover state, sub-menu or layout shift.
- The toolbar is 31px tall (3px panel padding, 24px rows) on every device, instead of 36–52px depending on the pointer type.
- **New session** creates the same selection annotation that **Add to chat** creates. The shell's palette owner receives it in memory through the open event. It is never saved in the lazy shell descriptor, and it reaches the launcher whether the palette is still loading or already loaded. The launcher draft then adopts it as an attachment.
- When you start the session, the passage is sent as quoted message text ahead of your prompt, the same way the chat composer sends comments, and mention offsets shift to match. It is not uploaded as a file.
- The launcher can't reopen the comment editor because the passage has no transcript anchor there. Its comment preview therefore hides **Edit** (`commentsEditable: false`). **Delete** and **Remove all** are handled by the palette draft.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md` and `docs/tools/btw.md`.

## Evidence
- New e2e in `chat-selection-to-main.e2e.test.ts`: select text → **New session** → the launcher shows the excerpt chip with no Edit button → Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. `sessions.create` receives `message: "> <passage>\n\nSummarize the risks."` with no `attachments`, and the chat draft is unchanged.
- These pass with the renamed button: `chat-selection-to-main`, `chat-comment-draft-recovery`, `chat-comment-lifecycle`, `chat-comment-pane-retirement`, `chat-session-companion-composer` (28 tests). `chat-selection-popup.test.ts` passes (20 tests), including the New session routing.
- A recorded lifecycle run (real mouse drag-selection, 1280×800) passed. It covers the toolbar at 31px with the three buttons in order, Escape dismissal, and each action through to its request: **Add to chat** → comment → `chat.send` with the quote, comment and prompt; **Ask in side chat** → comment → `sessions.companion.ask` with the selection context, answered in Side chat; **New session** → launcher → `sessions.create` with the quote and prompt. The video is in the requesting chat.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, `ui:i18n:sync`/`check`, docs format check, and `git diff --check` are all clean.

## Notes
- The launcher chip uses the existing comment chip copy ("1 comment").
- On touch the rows are 24px tall, below the shared 40–44px menu row height. This was chosen deliberately so the floating toolbar stays compact and looks the same everywhere.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(control-ui): drop the IP address parser from the chat boot bundle
prs.body:
Closes #193832

## What Problem This Solves

Every cold load of the Control UI chat route downloads and compiles `ipaddr.js` and `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` (about 15 KB minified) in the chat boot bundle, although first paint never uses them. They are only needed to check an assistant `MEDIA:` line whose https host is an IP literal.

## User Impact

The chat boot bundle is 4,329 B (gzip) smaller with the same 20 requests, and `MEDIA:` host decisions are unchanged. Cold-load timing did not change measurably.

Decision needed from the Control UI owner (see Risks): the first IP literal `MEDIA:` attachment in a page load now waits for one extra request, and the first link reader open downloads about 5 KB gzip more.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `MEDIA:` host guard is split at the point where the IP parser is needed:

- `src/media/remote-media-host.ts` normalizes the host and decides plain hostnames on its own. A host goes to the full guard if it has any character outside `[a-z0-9._-]`, or if every label is decimal or `0x` hex. That covers every input the canonical, loose or legacy IPv4 parsers can read. Until the full guard is installed, those hosts are rejected.
- The full guard is the existing IP literal check, unchanged, written as `createRemoteMediaIpHostnameGuard(ip)` over the `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` module. `src/media/parse-output.ts` stays the server entry point: it imports the full guard statically and installs it at import, so the Gateway's existing importers keep the same synchronous result.
- In the browser, the Control UI message normalizer installs the guard with one dynamic import of `@openclaw/net-policy/ip`, the first time a host is rejected only because the guard was missing.
- `ui/config/control-ui-chunking.ts` keeps `ipaddr.js` and `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` in the lazy `link-reader-response` chunk. The link reader panel and hovercard import the parser too and already preload that chunk, so readers need no extra request and the guard is one request.

<details><summary>Per-file details</summary>

- The parser body moves to `parse-output-core.ts`, which the browser imports. Apart from the guard import it is unchanged (`git diff -B -M` reports a 93% copy); it has to move because the existing server import path must keep the synchronous guard, while the browser needs the same body without a static import of the IP parser.
- `src/media/remote-media-host-ip.ts` binds the full guard to the static `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` import for `parse-output.ts`. The server graph has no dynamic import of the guard, so `pnpm build` reports no ineffective dynamic import for these modules.
- The Control UI normalizer calls `splitMediaOutput` from the core. Its previous `splitMediaFromOutput(text, { extractAudioDirectives: false })` call never enabled markdown image extraction, so the result is the same. A message whose media host was rejected only because the guard was still loading is not stored in the per-message normalized cache (`message-derivations.ts` on main), and the computation that built it subscribes to the guard's load.
- If the guard import fails, IP literal hosts stay rejected. When unsaved work (a private attachment draft or a memory-only outbox entry) blocks the automatic stale-chunk reload, the normalizer reports that once per page through `canReloadControlUiDocument(true)`, so the owner of that work shows its existing reload-blocked notice with Review, and reloads after the review.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.ts`: the transcript item cache treats guard readiness as part of its structural identity, so a message that had no visible content while the guard loaded (a captionless `MEDIA:` line) gets its row once the guard is installed. The first guard load in a page therefore rebuilds every cached session transcript once, including transcripts with no IP literal media; it happens at most once per page load.
- `src/media/remote-media-host.ts` keeps its hostname helpers module-private; only the guard entry points are exported.
- `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json`: the chat set drops `ipaddr.js`, `net-policy/src/ip.ts`, `media/parse.ts`, `media/parse-output.ts` and `markdown-core/src/image-spans.ts`, and adds `media/parse-output-core.ts` and `media/remote-media-host.ts`. `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` on this branch shows the same unrelated drift as on main (13 lines, none of these modules).
- `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` lists the three new modules that `parse-output.ts` now imports.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/control-ui-media-ip-guard.txt` allocates the 73 test lines this change adds (the host table rows in `src/media/parse.test.ts`, the transcript cases, the e2e case and two chunking rows).
- Without the chunk rule, the bundler emits the parser as a new `ip-*.js` chunk; at an earlier base that added +79 B gzip to the shared boot chunk's preload table. With the rule, `control-ui-boot-shared` is 11 B smaller raw and 41 B larger gzip as served: its preload list for the link reader panel drops the chat boot chunk and its chat dependencies (20 to 15 entries), because the parser is no longer there, and the shorter list compresses slightly worse. A side effect is that opening the link reader from a route that has not loaded chat no longer preloads the chat boot chunk.

</details>

The guard chunk is not preloaded. A speculative idle preload was measured at an earlier revision and rejected: on every cold chat load it fetched the guard code (16.2 KB transferred), which is more than the boot bundle saves.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before the timing runs: chat boot JS gzip drops with the same request count; no other boot budget grows beyond build variance; cold-chat JS transfer bytes drop in every pair; no timing metric moves beyond its A/A control.

All numbers below are on current main `fe2b1a51b41b80941fe93cfb0dfbdc0def2401d1`, this branch merged with it, one Mac (Node 24.22.2, Darwin arm64), checkouts without `dist/`, no budget changes.

```sh
pnpm ui:check-performance:base fe2b1a51b41b80941fe93cfb0dfbdc0def2401d1
```

The check exits 0.

| gzip bytes (asset hashes normalized) | Base | Head | Change | Limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat boot JavaScript (20 requests both) | 1,294,259 | 1,289,930 | -4,329 | 1,294,652 |
| New Session boot JavaScript (15 requests both) | 802,613 | 802,632 | +19 | 803,250 |
| Startup JavaScript (3 requests both) | 90,837 | 90,837 | 0 | 91,484 |
| CSS (startup, chat, new session, total) | unchanged | unchanged | 0 | |

The chat boot bundle is 393 B under its limit on the base and 4,722 B under with this change. New Session grows 19 B, inside the check's 64 B build-variance allowance. The largest ordinary chunk (`control-ui-boot-shared`) is 551.1 KiB gzip with this change, under its 551.3 KiB limit. The check's three warnings (document gzip, total CSS gzip and raw over their fixed ceilings) are the same on the base (+0 B).

Emitted chunks from `pnpm ui:build` on the same two trees:

| Chunk | Base raw | Head raw | Base gzip | Head gzip | Base br | Head br |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `control-ui-boot-chat` | 1,398,584 | 1,383,085 | 413,914 | 409,607 | 343,243 | 339,326 |
| `link-reader-response` (lazy) | 3,972 | 20,802 | 1,689 | 6,813 | | 6,224 |

`control-ui-boot-chat` no longer contains `ipaddr.js` (-15,499 B raw); `link-reader-response` now carries it (+16,830 B raw, +5,124 B gzip at level 9). The build writes no compressed copy of the base `link-reader-response`, so both of its gzip figures are level 9 on the emitted file.

Cold load with the committed bench, 20 interleaved base / base (A/A) / head triplets per profile, untraced, cold chat route, production Gateway HTTP handler, Playwright Chromium headless shell, same host and toolchain for all arms:

```sh
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --gateway-http --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --runs 60 \
  --first-load --cold-http-cache --untraced --thread-cpu-time --face chat \
  [--network-latency-ms 100 --download-kbps 10000]
```

| Cold chat, median (paired median vs preceding base, p95 of absolute paired change) | Base | A/A | Head | A/A paired | Head paired |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Local: JS transfer bytes | 1,362,109 | 1,362,109 | 1,358,089 | 0 B in 20/20 | -4,020 B in 20/20 |
| Local: first transcript ms | 394.1 | 381.7 | 379.4 | -1.9% (57.8%) | -4.4% (36.2%) |
| Local: first enabled composer ms | 235.0 | 211.4 | 204.0 | -6.2% (57.8%) | -12.7% (40.2%) |
| Local: main-thread task ms | 929.7 | 924.0 | 936.6 | +1.1% (35.7%) | -1.4% (21.2%) |
| Local: script ms | 490.7 | 487.5 | 499.2 | +2.4% (44.6%) | +2.5% (12.1%) |
| Remote (100 ms, 10 Mbps): JS transfer bytes | 1,362,109 | 1,362,109 | 1,358,089 | 0 B in 19/20 | -4,020 B in 18/20 |
| Remote: first transcript ms | 1,726.2 | 1,738.1 | 1,744.3 | +1.5% (9.0%) | +0.8% (12.1%) |
| Remote: first enabled composer ms | 1,599.4 | 1,606.2 | 1,595.2 | +1.9% (9.2%) | -0.3% (7.1%) |
| Remote: main-thread task ms | 1,151.6 | 1,158.1 | 1,110.5 | +0.9% (23.7%) | -1.9% (29.1%) |
| Remote: script ms | 594.9 | 595.6 | 570.9 | +1.4% (22.0%) | +0.2% (29.8%) |

Every run records 65 JS requests except two remote runs: the base run of pair 1 (64, without a 2,706 B lazy chunk, which also moves that pair's A/A cell) and the head run of pair 10 (62). The other 18 remote head pairs are exactly -4,020 B. The host was shared (1-minute load average median 34 local, 32 remote). Every timing difference is inside the A/A spread, so this change shows no cold-load timing gain and no regression beyond A/A. The claim is the byte reduction.

V8 parse and compile, from traced runs (10 interleaved base / head pairs, same command without `--untraced` and without a comparison bundle, one run per process): main-thread compile is 6.7 ms on the base and 6.6 ms with this change (median), paired median difference 0.0 ms, all renderer threads 97.3 ms and 94.3 ms with a paired range of -241 to +215 ms. The parser's compile cost is below what this host resolves.

Real Gateway run (built UI from `pnpm build`, isolated Gateway with a seeded transcript, Playwright Chromium headless shell, every https request answered locally, run before the merge with current main; the merge only changes where the normalizer stores its cached result, under the same condition): a captionless `MEDIA:https://8.8.8.8/a.png` message shows no image while the guard request (`link-reader-response-*.js`) is held, and its image is requested 26 ms after the chunk is released and renders. Eight blocked hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254`, `[::1]`, `0x7f.1`, the private-range fixture `192.168.1.10`, `100.64.0.1`, `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]`, `localhost`) are never requested and never appear in the transcript; `https://8.8.8.8/a.png` is the only https request among 57.

Transcript after the guard chunk is released (the image card above "History ends here."):

![Transcript after the guard chunk loads: the image card (a decoded 1x1 grey fixture) renders above the closing text](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/raw/5eebcfdac5aa4ce5844416927478bf45376dc8f7/real-gateway-guard-loaded.png)

While the chunk is held, the same transcript shows only the prompt and the closing text: [real-gateway-guard-held.png](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/5eebcfdac5aa4ce5844416927478bf45376dc8f7/real-gateway-guard-held.png). Full request log, Gateway origin redacted as `<gateway>`: [real-gateway-media-ip-host.json](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/5eebcfdac5aa4ce5844416927478bf45376dc8f7/real-gateway-media-ip-host.json).

<details><summary>Network summary from the request log</summary>

| ms after navigation | event |
| ---: | --- |
| 378 | `GET <gateway>/assets/link-reader-response-*.js` (held) |
| 560 | transcript shown |
| 2,071 | public IP images in the transcript while held: 0 |
| 2,384 | guard chunk released |
| 2,410 | `GET https://8.8.8.8/a.png`, the only https request of 57 |
| 2,495 | image rendered and decoded |

Requested: none of `https://127.0.0.1/loopback.png`, `https://169.254.169.254/metadata.png`, `https://[::1]/loopback-v6.png`, `https://0x7f.1/hex-loopback.png`, `https://192.168.1.10/private.png`, `https://100.64.0.1/shared.png`, `https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/mapped.png`, `https://localhost/name.png`. All other requests go to the Gateway origin.

</details>

### Guard load failure while unsent work blocks the reload

Run at `d09fe6c8ec8` with the same built UI, real Gateway and headless shell. An Incognito session holds an unsent attachment draft (`private-note.txt`), and from then on `link-reader-response-*.js` is route-aborted. In-app navigation then opens the transcript with the captionless `MEDIA:https://8.8.8.8/a.png`. The guard import fails, so there is no image and no reload. The draft's notice "An unsent Incognito draft is keeping this tab open" appears once with "Review private draft". The automatic stale-chunk path only checks without reporting, so this notice comes from the normalizer's `canReloadControlUiDocument(true)`. The chunk is then allowed again. Review opens the draft dialog, and "Discard this draft and refresh" reloads the page. The guard loads and the image renders. The eight blocked hosts are never requested. `https://8.8.8.8/a.png` is the only https request among 117 and is made only after the reload.

![Reload-blocked notice with Review private draft; the transcript shows no image while the guard chunk fails](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/raw/feee462d3ab6ce9deb92f9e11e070784f8f06f42/real-gateway-blocked-reload-notice.png)

![After the refresh the guard loads and the image card renders above the closing text](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/raw/feee462d3ab6ce9deb92f9e11e070784f8f06f42/real-gateway-blocked-reload-recovered.png)

Review dialog: [real-gateway-blocked-reload-review.png](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/feee462d3ab6ce9deb92f9e11e070784f8f06f42/real-gateway-blocked-reload-review.png). Request log and timeline, Gateway origin redacted as `<gateway>`: [real-gateway-blocked-reload.json](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/feee462d3ab6ce9deb92f9e11e070784f8f06f42/real-gateway-blocked-reload.json). Steps: [real-gateway-blocked-reload.md](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/feee462d3ab6ce9deb92f9e11e070784f8f06f42/real-gateway-blocked-reload.md).

At an earlier revision the real Gateway run also passed with the `chat-thread.ts` change reverted, because something else in that page rebuilds the transcript after the guard loads. The unit test below is the regression guard for that change.

Tests (all pass on this branch merged with `fe2b1a51b41`):

- The remote host tables in `src/media/parse.test.ts` pin the end-to-end decision for 85 hosts plus scheme, credential and quoting cases through `splitMediaFromOutput`: special-use dotted IPv4; shorthand, octal, hex and integer IPv4; IPv6 loopback, unspecified, link-local, ULA, multicast and documentation; IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 embeddings; localhost, `.local`, `.internal` and dotless names; public IPs and hostnames that look like IPs; non-https, credentials, and hosts the URL parser refuses. The same tables pass unchanged on the base.
  Because `parse.ts` imports `parse-output.ts`, the tables also show that the server entry installs the full guard at import: the public IP literals would be rejected otherwise.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-media-host.test.ts`: a captionless IP literal `MEDIA:` message has no row before the guard loads and gets one after, through the transcript stream source (which reads `buildCachedChatItems`) inside a computation, with no history change; this case fails without the `chat-thread.ts` change. A second case makes the guard import reject while a registered reload guard blocks reload: the guard's owner is notified once and the host stays rejected. It fails without the normalizer's report (the owner is never notified).
- `ui/src/app/control-ui-chunking.test.ts` pins `ipaddr.js` and `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` to the `link-reader-response` chunk.
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.media-files.e2e.test.ts` (Control UI e2e, shipped bundle, mocked Gateway): a public IP literal `MEDIA:` image renders and loads, and a `127.0.0.1` one is dropped (9 passed).
- `pnpm test src/media/` (414 passed, 9 skipped); the Control UI normalizer, chat thread, chunking, vite build, stale-chunk reload and document reload tests (22 files, 389 passed); `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`; oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files; `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` (0 cycles); `node scripts/check-control-ui-controllers.mts`; `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base fe2b1a51b41` (OK with the 73-line allocation); `pnpm build`; `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` (exit 0, above).
- Not rerun after this merge: the full Control UI test lane and `pnpm lint`. They are left to CI.

The screenshots above are behaviour proof for the delayed IP literal attachment. Rendered output does not change for any message once the guard has loaded.

Risks:

- Decision needed: is saving 4,329 gzip bytes on every cold chat load worth delaying the first IP literal attachment in a page load and adding about 5 KB gzip to the first link reader download?
  - Accept (recommended): every cold chat load is 4,329 B gzip smaller (15.5 KB raw less to parse), with the same request count and every boot budget held on current main. The cost lands only on pages that show an IP literal `MEDIA:` attachment or open the link reader, and only once per page load: one extra request (20,802 B raw, 6,686 B gzip as served) before the first IP literal attachment appears, or about 5 KB gzip more in the link reader's existing `link-reader-response` request. Hostname URLs are not affected, and forbidden hosts stay blocked while the guard loads or fails (shown above).
  - Reject: chat boot keeps the parser; IP literal attachments stay synchronous and the link reader chunk stays at 3,972 B raw.
  Recommendation: accept. IP literal `MEDIA:` hosts are rare next to hostname URLs, the deferral is bounded to one request per page, and the failure path keeps forbidden hosts blocked and offers the existing in-product recovery. Cold-load timing did not change measurably either way, so this is a bytes-on-the-wire decision.
- If `link-reader-response-*.js` cannot load (offline, deploy skew), IP literal hosts stay rejected and their attachments stay hidden. The existing stale-chunk listener reloads the page when it can. When a private attachment draft or a memory-only outbox entry blocks that reload, its owner shows its reload-blocked notice with Review once per page and reloads after the review; the attachment appears in the reloaded page. Until then the message has no IP literal attachment.
- A new server caller that imports `parse-output-core.ts` or `remote-media-host.ts` directly, without `parse-output.ts`, rejects IP literal hosts, because only `parse-output.ts` and the Control UI install the full guard. That is safe, but different. The module headers say so.

prs.title: fix: sent turns fail mid-reply when the sender's scheduled run ends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's reply fails mid-turn with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active" when another session's scheduled run sent it work with `sessions_send` and that run then ends.

## User Impact

A turn that another session hands off keeps running after the sender's scheduled run finishes, reschedules itself with `next_check`, deletes its one-shot job, or has its isolated run session cleaned up. Revoking the sender's device, changing their profile or role, or ending their access grant still stops it, and so does an explicit Stop. A job's own turn still ends when the job is disabled, removed or replaced.

## Why This Change Was Made

A turn admitted through `sessions_send` (and chat.send or Talk) inherits the sending run's operator authority. Since #176422 (`d74a4aeb7d62`), a scheduled continuation restores that authority bound to its single occurrence and to its exact session. #178693 moved only **child** targets onto the retained continuation authority, which keeps device, profile, role and grant checks but not the occurrence binding. Any other receiver, such as the sender's parent or a peer, kept the occurrence-bound authority and failed as soon as the occurrence ended. This shipped in `v2026.10.10-beta.3`; the last stable release `v2026.10.9` is unaffected.

This change:
- makes every accepted turn retained through `retainGatewayOperatorRun` use the continuation authority, and removes the child-only `spawnedBy` plumbing;
- separates the claimed sender session's lifecycle from the continuation. Previously, replacing or removing the sender's session (for example, cleanup of an isolated run's exact-run session) aborted the shared policy signal and still killed handed-off turns. Now that lifecycle ends only the sender's own run-bound authority.

### Deliberate revocations (ruled on by @jalehman)

1. Sender device revoked: kept.
2. Profile or role change, or access grant ended: kept.
3. Explicit user Stop: kept.
4. A job's own turn when the job is disabled, removed or replaced: kept. The job's own run does not go through this path.
5. Messages sent into a job's own `cron:<jobId>` session, which the next run takes over: unchanged for now.

### Known follow-up

Plugin subagent dispatch (`server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts`, `plugin_subagent`) still borrows its caller's authority without a retained continuation. It is out of scope here.

A related failure, also out of scope: a `sessions_yield` completion-delivery turn (`subagent_settle`) can fail mid-execution with "subagent source lifecycle changed before completion delivery". That turn is gated by the settle-wake's `isSourceSessionEffectsAllowed` (via `isExecutionAllowed`), which ties execution to the requester's yielded run, the settle batch and its custody (`subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts`). Operator authority is not involved, so this PR does not change it. Seen on 2026-11-07 at 12:16:34 PST: the yield was recorded at 12:16:34.021, the yielded run ended at 12:16:34.441, and delivery failed at 12:16:34.942.

## Evidence

- **Production incident:** on 2026-11-07, a session failed at 07:47:26 and again at 08:08:29, 1–3 seconds after each `sessions_send`-ing run of a scheduled CI follow-up job finished (07:47:23, 08:08:28). The same error also appears on 2026-10-23, 10-24 and 11-06, and never before 2026-10-23.
- **Regression tests** in `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`:
  - Ending the sender's occurrence: fails on base, passes with the fix.
  - Cleaning up the sender's session: fails at the first commit, passes with the second.
  - Revoking the device still stops the turn.
- **End-to-end:** isolated in-process Gateway with real cron scheduling, agent loop and tools, and a scripted model. A scheduled run sends to another session, ends and deletes itself while the receiver is held mid-turn; the receiver then calls a tool and finishes.
  - **Base** (`e60517b`): fails. The scheduled run finishes and its job is removed while the receiver is held. Once released, the receiver's turn ends with "Your request couldn't be completed.", the same banner seen in production.
  - **Fix:** passes. The receiver calls `sessions` patch and posts its final reply.
  - **Not committed:** the repo recently removed a similar 500-line real-Gateway test under the test cost budget. The e2e has a scripted model, so it isn't a live-model run; a live model can't reliably reproduce the timing.
- **Related suites:** 122 files and 1,522 tests pass (gateway authority, Talk, chat.send, agent-turn admission, `sessions_send`, restart recovery, cron operator source, subagent completion), plus a re-run of the recovery and cancellation suites after the second commit (78 tests).
- **Checks:** `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` pass; commit hooks ran.
- **Independent review:** found one P2, the sender-session cleanup gap. It is verified and fixed in the second commit. No scope or model widening was found.

prs.title: improve: measure interrupted Control UI navigation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Existing UI benchmarks wait for each action to settle before starting the next, which misses users changing destinations during loading. This adds 23 opt-in interruption scenarios to the existing cross-engine harness: five/twenty-session bursts, long transcripts, picker arrows, lazy route replacement, history, early overlay closure, and typing during boot/route arrival.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Developers can measure interrupted navigation and distinguish delivery, settlement and remaining work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scenarios record actual input delivery and deadline lateness, final-input-to-two-correct-frames readiness, late RPCs, retained panes, completed chunks, supported longest tasks and whole-interval CPU. Direct controls and rotated base/head/base runs expose unrelated host variation. The methodology explicitly distinguishes native input, programmatic route/history actions, synthetic Gateway replies, and unavailable counters.

**No production performance change or accepted speedup is included.** Two candidates were investigated and withdrawn. Devices still removed three superseded RPCs (6→3), but a change already on main removed its measured CPU benefit: ten rotated triplets in every engine/view/supported throttle cell found no ≥5% win. A Chat first-admission guard showed a provisional desktop CPU signal (−5.88%, A/A −2.62%, ten triplets) and prevented a hidden mount, but the full acceptance matrix was not established. Slow-mobile native selection kept the old pane legitimately presented while the new route loaded. The experimental cache probes and both runtime/test patches are excluded from this PR.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original 23-scenario matrix | 180 combined applicable observations passed: 136 historical unchanged cases plus 44 strengthened cases; four desktop-drawer cells are inapplicable; Chromium/WebKit/Firefox at 1× and Chromium at 4×, desktop/mobile |
| Historical repeated owner/session comparisons | 720 + 720 completed observations; recorded as historical, not a final-head performance claim |
| Current-base Devices candidate screen | 240/240 selected observations passed; no qualifying win; candidate withdrawn |
| Final scripts typecheck | Passed |
| Targeted lint/format and diff check | Passed on final source |
| Production Knip | Passed |
| Fresh independent P0–P2 review | Three P2 assertion findings fixed; final independent review scoped-clean |
| Negative assertion proof | All six ignored-input fixtures pass before the fix and fail after it; stuck-open native picker also rejected |
| Strengthened real-UI round-trip checks | 44/44 passed in the supported engine/view/throttle matrix |
| Same-machine final build/strict size comparison | Passed: startup JS 90,910 → 90,910 B gzip; startup CSS requests 1 → 1; no comparison violations. HTML +16 B gzip within 64 B build variance; no budgets changed. |

The six affected cases were rechecked with the final assertions against the production bundle at `23f2cd68e9d`: 44 passes in `strengthened-smoke-1x`, `final-assertion-smoke-1x`, `final-assertion-smoke-4x`, and `closed-overlay-smoke-{1x,4x}`. The selected cells exclude superseded visibility-only failures; those failed attempts remain recorded as observer-contract failures and were corrected to test native open state before first paint.

The arrow/overlay cases now also require observed intermediate selection/open states; draft-return must leave the original session; final-state equality alone is insufficient. The negative proof runs the actual scenario functions against a browser page that intentionally ignores inputs.

The original smoke used recorded pre-integration sources (`matrix-smoke-head/engines-aq8fU0`, `static-boot-smoke/engines-D3p51Q`, `matrix-smoke-4x/engines-C1VSBR`, `palette-4x-fixed/engines-Odm2nW`). It is collection/correctness evidence, not fresh final-head timing. Early offscreen-row and palette-readiness setup failures were corrected and affected cases passed. Later cache setup failures and an intentionally stopped comparison are retained locally and are not product verdicts.

<details>
<summary>Per-scenario observed correctness</summary>

P/P means desktop/mobile passed; —/P means desktop inapplicable.

| Scenario | C 1× D/M | W 1× D/M | F 1× D/M | C 4× D/M | Specific observed contract |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rapid-boot-typing` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | Typed text survives static-composer → connected-pane handoff; static input events observed. |
| `rapid-drawer-close-50ms` | —/P | —/P | —/P | —/P | Mobile drawer opened, then Escape at requested 50 ms; final drawer open/modal states cleared. |
| `rapid-history-back-forward-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | History back/back/forward ends on session 2 with its transcript and empty draft (programmatic History API). |
| `rapid-menu-close-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | Model picker opened then Escape; native picker closed and origin draft intact. |
| `rapid-model-arrows-20-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 20 down + 20 up native keys; original active-descendant restored. |
| `rapid-model-arrows-5-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 5 down + 5 up native keys; original active-descendant restored. |
| `rapid-route-clicks-cold-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | Native sidebar System status → Automations; final route and ≥50 automation rows. |
| `rapid-route-clicks-cold-direct` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | Native sidebar direct Automations; final route and ≥50 rows. |
| `rapid-routes-cold-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | API Devices → Automations before first destination settles; final route and ≥50 rows. |
| `rapid-routes-cold-direct` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | API direct Automations; final route and ≥50 rows. |
| `rapid-routes-warm-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | API Devices → Automations with modules primed; final route and ≥50 rows. |
| `rapid-routes-warm-direct` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | API direct Automations with modules primed; final route and ≥50 rows. |
| `rapid-session-palette-arrows-20-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 20 down + 20 up native keys; original active-descendant and typed search query intact. |
| `rapid-session-route-typing-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | Click session 5 then type; its 2,000-message tail visible and new text belongs to destination. |
| `rapid-sessions-20-150ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 20 native session choices at requested 150 ms; final 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; 19 nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-20-400ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 20 native session choices at requested 400 ms; final 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; 19 nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-20-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 20 native session choices at requested 50 ms; final 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; 19 nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-5-150ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 5 native session choices at requested 150 ms; final 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; 4 nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-5-400ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 5 native session choices at requested 400 ms; final 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; 4 nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-5-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | 5 native session choices at requested 50 ms; final 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; 4 nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-direct-20` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | One native click to session 20; 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; zero nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-direct-5` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | One native click to session 5; 2,000-message tail, empty draft, bottom gap <100 px; zero nonfinal history reads. |
| `rapid-sessions-draft-return-5-50ms` | P/P | P/P | P/P | P/P | Five native session choices then origin; original draft restored and scrollTop <2 px. |

</details>

## Limits and scope

This uses production bundles with synthetic Gateway data, not live server/provider latency. Rapid network profiles delay HTTP/lazy chunks by 100 ms while RPC replies stay immediate. WebKit/Firefox have no equivalent 4× throttle or thread CPU here. CPU is not attributed to individual abandoned owners, and completed ResourceTiming entries do not count still-in-flight requests. Readiness is not paint/INP; late correctness observation is bounded. Native pacing can miss its target because driver delivery, virtual-row scrolling and mobile drawer reopening are part of the workload. Boot typing covers same-context reload, not a first-ever visit or boot clicks. Session keyboard navigation uses command-palette results because the sidebar has no arrow-selection contract.

Production UI and tests: **unchanged**. Changed benchmark/methodology files: **2,122 → 3,153 LOC**. The new catalog is 933 lines for the requested matrix and one shared observer; it adds no production owner, cache, dependency, route, selector or budget exception. Experimental diagnostics were removed during simplification. No appearance change, so no before/after screenshot is claimed.

## Post-merge validation

Merged as `121aabda3ef98ef9696eff6a83126abb12a4e686`. The original PR run [42422771584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42422771584) passed its selected checks, but broad UI suites were skipped despite `ci:full`; the label was not reflected in the triggering event's selection.

Exact-merge follow-up [42424594612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42424594612) ran from the same workflow/source SHA. The temporary validation ref was deleted afterward; the tested commit remains on main. An earlier dispatch [42423679702](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42423679702) stopped in preflight because main-tier validation requires identical workflow/source revisions; no tests ran in that setup attempt.

| Exact-merge check | Result at 23:51 UTC |
|---|---|
| UI unit shards | 3/3 passed |
| Real-Gateway shards | 2/2 passed |
| Control UI performance | Passed |
| Selected UI E2E shards | 4 passed; 1 assertion failure; 1 timed out without a failed assertion |
| Full run | Not green: 126 jobs passed, 8 failed, 13 skipped, 10 other Node jobs still running at the recorded observation |

The assertion is `new-session-page.details-motion.e2e.test.ts > reveals Details after session creation: fresh reveal`: samples `[0,0,0,0,312.037,313]` missed the expected intermediate width. The other E2E shard hit its 20-minute action timeout. These are recorded gaps, not passing UI proof or established inherited failures.

Other failures: catalog fallback baseline drift in `control-ui-i18n` (the same command passed locally on both base and branch head); a 120-second timeout in `vitest-worker-artifacts.ci.test.ts > owns real CI group generations (parallelism=2, shared=true)`; a timestamp assertion in `service.publication-refresh.test.ts > service publication refresh scheduling > keeps refreshing after a same-second restart publication is refused as stale`; and a Chromium DevToolsSession crash under `control-ui-e2e-browser-lifetime.test.ts > shares Chromium across native projects while isolating clients and custom launches`. They are not labeled inherited without matching baseline failures.

Build/package and Docker seed failures have the same missing-lazy-chunk tarball-integrity signature as latest completed scheduled main run [42420555752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42420555752), jobs `128548125202` and `128548126118`.

The merged diff changes only benchmark code and its methodology; the listed product/fixture/CI/package owners are unchanged. No failure was hidden with retries, relaxed assertions, or baseline changes. The remaining unrelated Node jobs continue; this report makes no full-CI success claim.

## User Impact

The shared import scanner now resolves browser module aliases through the portable UI document's import map and checks every mapped JavaScript/CSS target. prs.title: fix(knowledge): avoid gateway stalls when opening large vaults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway main-thread stalls when the first Knowledge operation opens a large vault. Recursive `fs.watch` on Linux synchronously traverses the private partition and installs native watches, even though the plugin only requests two logical watchers.

## User Impact

Other Gateway work can continue while Knowledge sets up or recovers its watchers. External edits and renames still emit the same data-free, debounced notification; authorized queries still reconcile content. No configuration, schema, dependency, public API, or prompt changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing per-vault storage worker now owns `LiveState`, including setup, native callbacks, debounce and recovery. The existing worker protocol carries invalidation hints and observed watch health. Store retirement already joins worker termination, which now also releases the watches. There is still one runtime per physical store, shared by its agents; ordinary sessions and turns reuse it. A worker crash retires its watches, and the next normal query recreates both through existing recovery.

This deliberately relocates filesystem work instead of implementing a second recursive watcher or adding a polling scan. Node supports recursive watching on Linux since 19.1.0, but this is synchronous user-space traversal. Node 26.0.0 watches files as well as directories; 26.12.1 watches directories/symlinks on Linux while still enumerating files. See [Node's API history](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fswatchfilename-options-listener) and [26.0.0 implementation](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.0.0/lib/internal/fs/recursive_watch.js).

Production delta: **+26 lines**, needed for two small worker-message variants, watch-health propagation and worker activation. The former main-thread watcher owner is removed. No new thread, scanner or cache. Test delta: **+8 lines**, with a matching allocation for the thread-boundary assertion and native-event fixture isolation.

## Evidence

Acceptance fixed before measurement: zero main-thread native registrations; preserve real external change detection; five serial AB/BA blocks plus five A/A pairs; no material total CPU/allocation regression (20% is a stop).

Node 26.12.1, Linux container, 32 available CPUs, initial load averages 0/0/0. Synthetic single vault: **62,000 files / 1,116,000,000 bytes**, 15,500 attachment directories plus the vault/private/artifacts/claims/projects directories. The attachment layout follows the plugin's per-request artifact directory; the population is a stress assumption, not a census of any deployment. No database, session or production data is copied or required by this watcher owner.

Ten measured starts per arm, warmed filesystem and fresh watcher each sample; allocation uses a separate identical sequence:

| Metric | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Synchronous caller interval (ms) | 160.063 / 204.816 | 0.054 / 0.073 |
| Watcher `start()` elapsed, on its owning thread (ms) | 156.391 / 197.120 | 155.815 / 168.885 |
| Watcher `start()` CPU (ms) | 152.521 / 189.627 | 152.694 / 160.965 |
| Main-thread lifecycle CPU (ms) | 178.062 / 213.031 | 0.863 / 1.752 |
| Total lifecycle CPU (ms) | 216.289 / 260.529 | 216.111 / 234.546 |
| Owner sampled allocation (bytes) | 100,593,960 / 102,999,600 | 102,481,240 / 106,589,352 |
| Main-thread sampled allocation (bytes) | 100,593,960 / 102,999,600 | 0 / 32,832 |
| Native watcher registrations on main | 15,505 | 0 |
| Total native watcher registrations | 15,505 | 15,505 |

A/A arm medians: caller interval **156.476 / 152.868 ms**, owner CPU **150.447 / 145.278 ms**, total lifecycle CPU **202.478 / 198.149 ms**, sampled allocation **100,167,304 / 95,827,152 bytes**. The +1.9% allocation shift is smaller than this control spread. No claim of reduced total watcher work or faster first Knowledge response. Lifecycle CPU covers start, change detection and stop; the synchronous baseline caller interval also includes its pre-sample GC. Worker imports/bootstrap are excluded because production reuses its existing storage worker. Allocation is sampled JS allocation, not native allocation. This is not a btrfs or large-database benchmark.

Every benchmark sample writes an existing nested file and waits for the actual production notification. Separate CPU profiles show native watch `start`, `readdir` and `internal/fs/recursive_watch` dominate on both arms, relocated to the worker. Reproduce with:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import {build} from "esbuild"; await build({entryPoints:["extensions/knowledge/src/live-state.ts"],outfile:"/your/proof/live-state.mjs",format:"esm",platform:"node",bundle:true})'
node --expose-gc scripts/perf/knowledge-watch-start.mjs --module /your/proof/live-state.mjs --root /your/proof/new-fixture --output /your/proof/watch
```

The service regression fails on parent `fd83c2d59181b0021ba5b63423f5f0e05c80e483`: `LiveState.start` runs once on the caller thread. It passes after the move. The native-event test seeds the vault before restarting observation so the save's explicit hint cannot stand in for native creation delivery; edit/rename notification assertions and the original timeout remain intact. An initial candidate run exposed this fixture ambiguity; the baseline rename run passed, so it is not classified as inherited.

Focused proof: 47 tests across live-state, storage-worker, stores, maintenance and worker-entry. The final live-state file passed all six tests (10.3 seconds of test bodies, 71.75 seconds wrapper wall including compilation). Other four suites' passing proof is reused; their production inputs are unchanged apart from the equivalent one-line retirement simplification. No touched module is imported by `ui/src`.

`pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed (4m 19.7s). `pnpm check:changed` completed: all runtime/type/boundary/export/format checks and extension lint passed. Its benchmark-script lint errors were repaired; targeted script lint passed, and the final script smoke re-confirmed 15,505 main-thread registrations before versus zero after, with change detection in both arms. The test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` passed. The final edit/rename regression also passed under Node (10.1s test body, 76.35s wrapper wall).

The remaining `check:changed` failure is **20 historical changelog-attribution violations**, reproduced using the exact parent changelog tree and unchanged gate. This is a main regression introduced by [#194364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194364), commit `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957`, which added the rejected handles; its parent gate accepted those handles. It needs a separate owner fix and is not treated as noise. No exception or baseline was changed here.

Requested Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2; the final tooling repair also received a scoped-clean review (patch-correct confidence 0.88). Reviewed source was committed as `1c1d091f3df05dbbd72f0bbf45f6297f2b4666b3`. The review covers the complete local diff against `fd83c2d59181b0021ba5b63423f5f0e05c80e483`; reviewer tests were not independently executed. The PR is intentionally left unmerged.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): clarify slash-command descriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Some slash-menu descriptions contain command syntax, unclear wording, or claims that do not match their handlers.

## User Impact

Commands have short, direct descriptions. The Control UI correctly describes its local agent list and usage report; other channels keep descriptions suited to their handlers. Model scope flags and loop syntax remain in the existing argument descriptions and command help.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep action summaries separate from usage instructions. Reuse the existing UI description overrides and English catalog; leave other locales unchanged.

The slash menu shows descriptions without a trailing period.

This formatting happens only when rendering command rows in the chat slash menu. A single final `.` is removed; `…` and `...` are preserved. The 13 description rewrites below show the source text.

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| /learn (shared) | Learn from recent work or named sources into skills or memory. | Save lessons from recent work or named sources to skills or memory. |
| /loop (shared) | Loop a prompt: /loop [interval] <prompt> \| /loop status \| /loop stop [name] | Run and manage recurring prompts in this conversation. |
| /diagnostics (shared) | Explain Gateway diagnostics and Codex feedback upload options. | Request Gateway diagnostics and optional Codex feedback uploads. |
| /allowlist (shared) | List/add/remove allowlist entries. | List, add, or remove allowlist entries. |
| /approve (shared) | Approve or deny exec requests. | Approve or deny pending requests. |
| /agents (shared) | List thread-bound agents for this session. | List agents and conversation bindings for this session. |
| /usage (shared) | Usage footer or cost summary. | Set the usage footer or show a cost summary. |
| /send (shared) | Set send policy. | Control message delivery for this session. |
| /model (shared) | Show or set the model; use -s, -a, or -g to choose scope. | Show or set the model. |
| /models (shared) | List model providers/models. | List model providers and their models. |
| /bash (shared) | Run host shell commands (host-only). | Run shell commands on the host. |
| /agents (Control UI) | List thread-bound agents for this session. | List available agents |
| /usage (Control UI) | Usage footer or cost summary. | Show token and context usage for this session |

## Evidence

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce broadcast compression allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large WebSocket broadcasts already share compressed payloads, but each large deflate operation still allocates an input-sized temporary output buffer (up to 64 KiB), then copies its used bytes into retained storage.

## User Impact

Reduces allocation pressure during large broadcasts without changing negotiation, compressed wire bytes, client sequences, or payloads. The 1 KiB threshold and no-context-takeover policy remain intact. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing synchronous codec now owns one reusable 64 KiB output workspace per negotiated window for large deflation and returns exact owned copies. Queued writes never borrow scratch space. This deletes the downstream copy; one-shot fallback output keeps exact ownership. Small-envelope compression and inbound inflation retain their existing path. There is no new payload cache or per-connection workspace.

Production delta **−2 lines**. The regression adds 62 test lines (with a matching scoped allocation): 20 real peers, three audiences, seven native deflate operations per update, no repeated large temporary output allocation, and intact queued messages across consecutive updates. It fails on the base allocation assertion and passes with the fix. The existing benchmark gains streaming/cohort inputs and measurement instrumentation (+69 lines).

## Evidence

Acceptance recorded before the final comparison: 20 real sockets in 17/1/2 audiences, growing synthetic assistant messages up to 64 KiB, 3,000 updates per timing arm and 1,500 per allocation arm; five alternating AB/BA pairs plus A/A, run serially. Require lower output allocation without a reproducible CPU/latency regression and byte-identical decoded messages/wire volume. Base: `fd83c2d59181b0021ba5b63423f5f0e05c80e483`; Node 26.12.1, ws 8.22.0, macOS.

| Metric | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] | A/A change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Send CPU, µs/update | 206.2 [201.1–208.8] | 200.3 [193.1–202.4] | +8.33% |
| Process CPU, µs/update¹ | 3,046.6 [2,904.5–3,118.5] | 2,904.1 [2,803.7–2,939.1] | +7.13% |
| V8 sampled bytes/update¹ | 230,319 [228,617–231,202] | 229,868 [229,128–230,446] | -0.51% |
| Explicit Buffer bytes/update² | 88,845 [88,845–88,845] | 38,225 [38,225–38,225] | +0.00% |
| Delivery p95, ms | 2.136 [1.999–2.166] | 2.097 [2.056–2.155] | -9.47% |
| Delivery p99, ms | 3.365 [3.133–3.678] | 3.380 [3.170–3.708] | -13.02% |
| Wire bytes/update | 107,186.3 [107,186.3–107,186.3] | 107,186.3 [107,186.3–107,186.3] | +0.00% |

Explicit Buffer requests fall **56.98%** (50,620 bytes/update). All five timing pairs favor send CPU, but the 2.85% median reduction is smaller than A/A variation; treat CPU as neutral. V8 allocation is neutral. Every client's decoded SHA256 and total wire bytes match across all arms. Delivery p99 moves +0.45%, versus −13.02% A/A; end RSS +1.24%, versus −9.15% A/A. No GC improvement is claimed. One-minute host load ranged 16.2–25.8 on 32 CPUs; allocation counts are deterministic, but timings are not a quiet-host speedup claim.

¹ Process CPU and sampled V8 allocation include in-process clients. Send CPU isolates synchronous broadcaster work. ² Counts explicit `Buffer.allocUnsafe`/`allocUnsafeSlow` size requests during broadcast, not total native allocations or retained memory; V8 samples exclude Buffer backing storage. Warm workspace cost is 64 KiB per negotiated window, independent of peer count.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/ws-compression-measure.ts --clients 20 --audiences 17,1,2 --streaming --size 65536 --batches 3000 --port 42663`; use `--codec <base-module>` for base, `--allocations --batches 1500` separately, and `--cpu-profile <file>` for a separate profile pass.

Focused validation: 34 passed / one platform skip, including mixed windows, raw clients, worker-precompressed segments, and real-Gateway bidirectional compression. After test typing repairs, the touched suite passed again (9 passed / one skip, 37.78 s wrapper wall time; compilation dominates). Fresh sourcePerformance build passed. The built Gateway completed three 300-chunk turns with 20 compressed clients in 17/1/2 capability cohorts; each delivered the expected 240 session events. This integration smoke uses 1,000 synthetic sessions / 57.6 MB DB. No native apps were launched, and no new 35 GiB/btrfs whole-Gateway comparison is claimed; the transport byte checks establish unchanged wire output.

`pnpm check:changed` completed all gates. Its patch-related test typing and benchmark lint errors were fixed and their targeted checks passed. Remaining main regression: changelog attribution guard reports 20 historical entries on the exact base, identically reproduced at introducing commit `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364). That commit's parent reports a different set of 26 entries with zero overlap. This patch does not alter those files or suppress the gate.

Codex autoreview of the complete final local change against `fd83c2d59181b0021ba5b63423f5f0e05c80e483`: scoped-clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings. The author simplification pass leaves the existing codec as sole owner and removes the downstream copy. No merge requested.

prs.title: perf(ui): restore profile display independently of config
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When bootstrap display preferences are unavailable, a slow `config.get` prevents the current user's saved appearance and rail shortcuts from restoring, even though `users.prefs.get` can answer independently. Normal same-origin bootstrap already supplies display preferences; this change targets the missing-bootstrap path.

Start the profile read alongside the existing display-config read. Publish explicit profile values and profile-only navigation from their authoritative response, while fields requiring unknown operator defaults remain pending. Apply a late profile response against the current config, retaining the existing connection, hello, profile, invalidation and generation guards. Do not finish an identity switch until its deferred defaults can reconcile; this prevents a previous profile's theme from surviving a slow read.

Authentication, session identity, binding and policy authority stay in their existing owners. Locale application and inherited config-backed fields still wait for config. The Appearance editor retains its existing `ConfigReadBoundary`: while display config is unknown, its inherited-theme controls, provenance and reset targets remain behind visible loading, even if an explicit profile accent has restored elsewhere. No new cache, configuration setting or Solid effect is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance is defined before measurement: `config.get` delayed by 3 seconds must improve restored appearance time by at least 5%; measure 20 rotated base/head pairs plus A/A in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, with separate no-delay and 100 ms RTT conditions. Weigh delayed benefit against normal-use cost; a small tail movement with a flat median is not an automatic rejection, while a real normal-use median regression still rejects the candidate.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Gateway owner tests | 42 passed |
| Profile preference tests | 15 passed; two identity-switch cases failed before the completion fix and passed afterward |
| UI and scripts typechecks; targeted lint/format | Passed |
| Full-context independent review, P0–P2 | Clean after resolving the identity-switch finding |
| Test-line ratchet | Passed after the allocation-only correction; exact 49-line allocation, existing slack unchanged |
| Base build provenance | Shared same-Mac bundle identifies clean `83f7614cc70d136f5e32d6357c6b67f39e985187`; full artifact hashes pinned |
| Head build and strict size comparison | Passed on current-main base `c9e4fdfa3a5` and runtime build `9a5d4407750`; final head `c804a8fc9e8` retains the measured English runtime and reuses that proof; zero violations; no ceilings raised |
| Current-main startup JavaScript/CSS gzip and CSS request count | 90,853 B / 39,090 B / 1, unchanged. Chat 1,295,525→1,295,430 B and New 802,972→802,877 B (−95 B each); requests unchanged |
| 3-second delay, no-delay and 100 ms RTT matrices | 540/540 observations passed; 20 rotated base/head/A-A triplets per condition, Chromium/WebKit/Firefox |
| Forever-held/released visual proof | 9/9 diagnostic observations passed across all 3 engines; explicit profile restores with config held, Settings input/navigation remain usable, inherited Appearance controls retain visible Loading until release |
| Forwarded Chat browser tests | Corrected streaming case passed. Full file 7/8 locally: unchanged retained-width case also fails when replayed from its original source. This is a local proof gap, not an inherited-CI claim; corrected head CI must prove it |
| Migration E2E | Exact failing test reproduced request-count failure, then passed with a fixture scoped to unfiltered migration reads; independent filtered appearance read remains allowed |
| Production Knip | Passed again on exact current-main head `c804a8fc`; no ignores added |

CI's earlier merge context reported +240 B of Chat/New route growth. The final current-main comparison above has no added route bytes and passes strict checking. Existing absolute document/CSS/Chat warnings are already present on the same base; document and CSS do not grow, and Chat decreases. No budget was raised.
