prs.title: perf(ui): show model providers before catalog discovery settles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Models settings route waits for both `models.authStatus` and `models.list` before adopting any data. A slow model catalog therefore leaves the page waiting even after the Gateway has returned the authoritative provider and credential rows. Users cannot inspect or search those rows while an independent catalog read is pending.

Start the same reads concurrently and adopt the route after auth settles. Hand the pending catalog request to the existing catalog loader, which owns its loading/error feedback, cancellation and retry. Page retirement and agent/connection changes retire the result; a catalog invalidated between preload and mount is refreshed after the adopted read settles. Do not infer “no usable model” while discovery is still pending.

Forced refresh and credential completion retain auth-before-catalog ordering. Authentication, selected-agent identity, binding and config mutation authority are unchanged. Runtime imports remain behind the Models route's existing lazy boundary.

## Evidence

Base: `d44c9ad927d65e2b9587bb3a1764deba3134117e`. Candidate: `3f3416808d39152ca641a1209c48de67a12863a5`. Refreshed by merging current main; the Models owner, tests, relevant benchmark inputs and dependency manifests are byte-identical to the originally reviewed variant. The same-Mac base bundle is `c9e4fdfa3a50de6c7e06d2fe1756506ecfb4e9b4`; the only change from it to the merge base is `src/process/exec.test.ts`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Held catalog route + rendered credential input regressions on base | 3 failures as expected: auth rows remain unavailable until catalog completes |
| Three changed test files, final candidate | 26 passed; 5.74 s Vitest, 7.42 s wrapper |
| Invalidated preload recovery | First candidate failed; final candidate passes through real route navigation |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Targeted lint and formatting | Passed; existing-style reactive-props warnings remain in the tracked `needsModelSetup` helper |
| Independent full-owner P0–P2 review | Scoped-clean after the final owner extraction |
| `git diff --check` | Passed; final checkout clean |
| Full `ci:full` run 42423273180 | Passed on exact candidate head |
| Three-engine timing matrix | All 540 observations passed: 20 rotated base/head/base-control triplets × 3 engines × 3 conditions |
| `pnpm ui:build` and strict base/head performance check | Passed: startup JS 90,853 → 90,853 B gzip; startup CSS 39,090 → 39,090 B, 1 request; no violations |
| Chat and New route boot JS | Both decrease 239 B gzip; no request increase |
| Three-engine native held/released census | All 18 observations passed native Back/New navigation; all 6 forever-hold re-entry/release cases restored ready content with zero page or render errors |
| `pnpm deadcode:knip` (production Knip) | Passed on exact candidate head; no new ignores |
| Inspected synthetic pending/released before/after screenshots | Four Chromium images fully inspected; synthetic-only; native uploads byte-verified |

The strict checker reports the same existing document/CSS ceiling warnings on the shared base and head; total CSS is unchanged (325,566 B gzip / 1,676,608 B raw), and this change raises no cap.

The selected timing flow is the first Models visit from Chat at the desktop viewport. Its readiness predicate is the existing `.provider-row[data-provider-id]` selector with at least three rows. The fixture supplies three authoritative auth-backed providers, so the measurement asks whether useful provider content is available, rather than whether optional catalog discovery has finished. Ran 20 rotated base/head/base-control triplets in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox for `models.list` delayed by 3 seconds, no delay and 100 ms RTT. Report both wall time and browser-local application time, including A/A noise and available Chromium CPU metrics. A separate three-engine census holds `models.list` forever, tests native Back/New navigation, re-enters Models, releases the hold, and records synthetic screenshots. That proves re-entry/release recovery; late-result-in-place behavior is covered by the changed rendered owner tests rather than attributed to that navigation probe.

Acceptance weighs the delayed-read improvement against normal-use cost: require at least a 5% readiness improvement with the target method delayed and reject a real normal-use median regression. A near-band tail movement with a flat median is assessed against the size of the delayed-case win, with both sides and A/A noise reported. Acceptance decision under the revised tradeoff rule: the 93–97% delayed-read readiness gain outweighs small normal readiness movement (+1.5–4.1%) with flat or improved wall-time medians. Normal Chromium/WebKit readiness p95 improves. Firefox normal p95 rises 6.0%, inside its A/A tail movement (+7.5%); at 100 ms RTT its median improves 0.17% and p95 rises 2.83%. These are disclosed costs, not a zero-cost claim.


### Timing results

Readiness is browser-local application time; wall time is reported separately, not substituted for WebKit application time. Measurements ran serially on the same Mac, with the same production HTTP owner. One-minute host load across all 540 observations was 8.37–23.56; every cell includes A/A controls.

| Run | Engine | Metric | n base/head/control | Median base→head | Delta | p95 base→head | A/A median / p95 | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| delayed | chromium | readiness | 20/20/20 | 3057.00→97.95 | -96.80% | 3061.20→99.90 | -0.02% / -0.08% | 0 |
| delayed | webkit | readiness | 20/20/20 | 3078.00→213.00 | -93.08% | 3128.00→231.00 | -0.03% / -1.47% | 0 |
| delayed | firefox | readiness | 20/20/20 | 3062.00→122.00 | -96.02% | 3076.00→155.00 | -0.05% / -0.23% | 0 |
| normal | chromium | readiness | 20/20/20 | 91.75→95.50 | +4.09% | 104.60→103.50 | +1.25% / -3.06% | 0 |
| normal | webkit | readiness | 20/20/20 | 198.00→201.00 | +1.52% | 210.00→206.00 | -0.25% / +2.38% | 0 |
| normal | firefox | readiness | 20/20/20 | 121.00→123.50 | +2.07% | 133.00→141.00 | -0.41% / +7.52% | 0 |
| rtt100 | chromium | readiness | 20/20/20 | 775.15→777.45 | +0.30% | 794.80→794.10 | +0.15% / -0.31% | 0 |
| rtt100 | webkit | readiness | 20/20/20 | 969.00→971.00 | +0.21% | 990.00→980.00 | -0.10% / -1.01% | 0 |
| rtt100 | firefox | readiness | 20/20/20 | 908.00→906.50 | -0.17% | 920.00→946.00 | -0.11% / +0.33% | 0 |

With the three-second catalog delay, wall medians fall from 3,125.65 → 161.16 ms (Chromium), 3,144.77 → 275.44 ms (WebKit), and 3,130.11 → 195.25 ms (Firefox). Without delay they are 161.28 → 161.28, 262.57 → 262.64, and 198.71 → 195.52 ms. With 100 ms RTT they are 844.09 → 845.91, 1,037.12 → 1,039.01, and 984.28 → 983.56 ms.

Chromium no-delay script/task medians are 34.60 → 34.55 / 91.91 → 91.42 ms. At 100 ms RTT they are 32.79 → 33.36 / 81.72 → 81.96 ms. With the held catalog they are 53.07 → 34.44 / 165.55 → 94.59 ms; those delayed CPU values cover the readiness window, so they demonstrate work moved off the critical path, not eliminated full-refresh work. WebKit/Firefox CPU is unavailable.

Each of the 540 timing windows sends exactly one `models.list` and one `usage.status`. Auth is prepared/cached during boot, so zero `models.authStatus` calls in the navigation window does not mean auth work disappeared. The separate native census records full-document counts as well as post-navigation counts. All 18 base/head native observations contain exactly two full-document `models.list` calls and one `models.authStatus` call. The post-navigation slice contains one or two catalogs depending on whether the late boot read crossed the reset point; it does not demonstrate an added full-document request. A short Chromium diagnostic confirms the two request shapes are distinct and identical on both builds: Chat requests `{view: "configured", agentId: "main", sessionKey: "agent:main:interaction-a"}`, and Models requests `{view: "configured", agentId: "main"}`. They are separate cache projections, not a duplicate refresh.

The census initially failed before any RPC because its old preview wrapper did not serve the current import-map bundle correctly. It was rerun through the same canonical production HTTP owner as the timing harness; the failed setup contributes no product evidence.

The one canonical Testbox attempt queued and was stopped before source sync or workload execution. It supplies no build, behavior or timing evidence; the local matrix remains required.

Production LOC: **1,384 → 1,455 (+71)**. Test LOC: **526 → 618 (+92)**, with an exact test-line allocation. The added code transfers an already-started read into the existing catalog owner and preserves cancellation and stale-preload recovery. The main page controller remains the same total length. Solid audit: effects **2 → 2**; render effects, direct listeners, DOM queries, `untrack`, `flush`, component cleanup and owner APIs remain **0 → 0** in the touched production files.

Still required: provider rows wait for the selected agent and authoritative auth snapshot; native-agent provider filtering waits for installed-agent inventory; writes wait for current config/revision/permission authority. Explicit refresh and login completion retain ordered auth publication before refreshed catalog discovery. Saving a credential while the initial catalog is unknown does not infer that it should replace a missing default model.

Deferred to a separate core-owner follow-up: in-page selected-agent changes, reconnect/replacement, publication refresh and credential completion still publish auth and catalog together. Those presentation waits are residual couplings, not required authority ordering, and this route-only timing matrix does not prove them.



### Synthetic before/after screenshots

![Before: catalog held, provider rows still wait](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d41444ab-c923-4a21-83ab-c4dbce6b284a)

![After: known provider rows available while catalog discovery is pending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8107daa5-1fef-4144-a53f-4e976dd73d2d)

![Before after catalog release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94b21bc4-fa25-499d-8e01-7ba16abe48b5)

# W-PERF-BOOT-BLOCKING: split cold boot tasks

## Coordinator acceptance and repaired-head confirmation

The coordinator accepted the measured tradeoff on 2026-11-07: **coordinator-accepted** Chat normalized gzip growth **1,295,811 → 1,296,187 B (+376 B)**, which was **312 B** beyond the paired check's 64 B allowance. The measured cold longest-task improvements are 33–43% (desktop/mobile: 99→66 / 97→58.5 ms at 1×; 512→382 / 537→307.5 at 4×; 768.5→536 / 844→491.5 at 6×), large-open blocking improves 12–30%, readiness improves 3–8%, and CLS is zero. The coordinator also accepted Firefox mobile cold readiness median +5.005% with p95 −18.6%, and WebKit mobile warm p95 +4.7% with a flat median. This is coordinator acceptance, not an inherited-budget exception.

The repaired application head is `a4471c848cdb` against integration base `23f2cd68e9d`. Only the Chat cap moves, to exactly 1,296,187 B (measured base +376 B, no headroom); every other cap stays unchanged. The old fixed Chat cap was already below the measured base. Cheap shared-fallback/prop-forwarding changes removed 196 raw bytes but increased normalized gzip 120 B and were reverted; no redesign was made for compression.

| Startup JS | 90,910 → 90,910 B | +0 B | +6 B | 3 → 3 |
| Chat JS | 1,295,811 → 1,296,187 B | +507 B | +239 B | 20 → 20 |
| New Session JS | 803,029 → 803,129 B | +186 B | +102 B | 15 → 15 |

Startup CSS stays at 39,090 B gzip and one request. Chat and New Session CSS are unchanged. The original auto-merge request is confirmed cancelled (`e7f1587c3bb0cbf1dde0f341d6d55bccdf350cb0`); landing uses fresh native replacement-head recovery.

## Repaired-head confirmation: passed

Chromium covers cold/warm/2,000-message open at 1×/4× and both viewports; Firefox covers mobile cold. No WebKit or 6× rerun was needed. All Chromium samples have zero CLS and retain the expected cache admission (cold/large false; warm true).

Cold longest-task medians improve **31–40%**, large-open medians **7–30%**. Desktop large 1× is a smaller but still qualifying 7% gain (100→93 ms); its readiness improves 1.7%. All Chromium readiness medians/p95s hold or improve within 5%. Warm desktop 4× longest-task p95 is +5.95% (336→356 ms), alongside A/A +6.55% (336→358); its median is +0.47%, readiness +2.76%/+1.28%, and task CPU +0.69%/+4.48%. This shared tail movement does not reproduce a causal regression. Firefox mobile cold is **490/679→503/537 ms (+2.65%/−20.91%)**, within the band and better than the previously coordinator-accepted median edge.

Host one-minute load ranged from 11.2 to 23.5. The table retains raw distributions and identical-build controls. The complete strict paired byte check passes with **zero violations** on the unchanged complete builds and the new Chat cap; every other cap is unchanged.

| Stage / engine / viewport / flow | n base/head/A-A | Long task base → head (A-A) ms | Ready base → head (A-A) ms | Ready Δ median/p95 | A-A ready Δ | Task CPU Δ | Max head CLS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chromium-1x / chromium / desktop / cold-boot | 10/10/10 | 99.0/104.0 → 68.5/74.0 (101.0/103.0) | 442.6/716.0 → 432.6/455.1 (444.2/458.2) | -2.3%/-36.4% | +0.4%/-36.0% | -2.1%/-0.5% | 0 |

| chromium-4x / chromium / mobile / large-transcript-open | 10/10/10 | 574.5/637.0 → 401.5/437.0 (554.0/698.0) | 2201.3/2473.4 → 2071.1/2262.8 (2178.4/2494.9) | -5.9%/-8.5% | -1.0%/+0.9% | -5.0%/-8.1% | 0 |

Exact-head CI on `0f87ca49f3b` passed full UI units, real-Gateway, byte and security checks. Its unavailable-handshake pacing and persistent New Session render-recovery cases each passed one diagnosed-flake rerun. The New Session artifact showed a failed document HEAD probe (`net::ERR_ABORTED` after 413 ms), for which production correctly retains Retry; pacing mixed virtual time with real WebCrypto work. Neither failure was claimed inherited. A later rerun exposed `Knowledge first-install settings > shows omitted read/write gates as enabled and retains explicit opt-outs after saving and reloading`: request inspection could miss the two-second Saved notice. The test now arms notice/request observation before the click, retaining all payload and reload assertions. The single local case, E2E typecheck, lint, formatting and independent P0–P2 review pass. Full `ci:full` CI [run 42424537142](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42424537142), attempt 1, passed on exact head `b7cf7c8a324`. Application performance and complete-build byte evidence are unchanged.

Two CI E2E failures reproduced through the production bundle. `keeps the submitted preview and restores its thinking choice after a rejected edit` observed an empty loading frame during new-session handoff: the pane now yields only when the initial document still owns its boot composer. `keeps recovery visible and automatically enters a reachable Gateway after refused upgrades` froze RAF with its virtual clock: its recovery wait now advances the clock in 1 ms steps, matching the sibling test. Both targeted cases pass after repair; the transition passes with zero invalid frames. A verification started before build publication completed was discarded (unrelated disabled-picker setup failure) and rerun against the completed source-verified build.

The nine pane bridge tests pass, including held DOM completion/disposal and immediate non-boot handoff. UI and E2E test typechecks, targeted lint, and formatting pass. Earlier lineage/type repairs remain unchanged. Production Knip passes. Final staged independent review is scoped-clean through P2. The earlier unstaged review identified the old index's route-continuity bug; staging the tested repair removed that index-only defect.

**The original full timing/trace tables and images below belong to earlier head `512b6ada517` versus `ae0739da8acc9d2f2d8630533f19688da7e00a15`. They remain labeled as earlier-head evidence; the repaired-head confirmation is reported separately above.**

## What Problem This Solves

Opening Chat groups shell/sidebar construction, pane startup, composer/Details layout, and transcript work into long main-thread tasks. This change gives Chromium a render-frame and native-task boundary before cold shell construction and before uncached initial-document pane construction. Admitted warm shells, cached panes, and later route handoffs stay immediate.

## User Impact

The measured candidate reduces cold and large-open blocking without changing the visible layout. The repaired head confirms the cold and large-open gains while warm readiness remains within the band; the Chat byte tradeoff is coordinator-accepted.

The existing layout-frame scheduler owns the boundary. The pane's existing completion contract waits until its actual mount or disposal; the change adds no timer fallback, cache, or competing domain owner. The first cache-admission fact stays immutable inside the prepared pane. Existing lazy imports, loading geometry, composer adoption, and the string-valued cache marker's loading grace remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source-mapped baseline traces contain several accumulated owners, not one dominant algorithm. Earlier universal scheduling variants delayed Firefox readiness, so the optimization requires the Chromium marker, native `scheduler.yield`, and a visible document. A prior candidate also yielded warm shells; its 30-pair mobile 4× confirmation regressed longest-task median/p95 by 5.7%/12.1%, so that candidate was rejected. This version reads the existing `ApplicationRuntime.warmBoot` fact after the lazy import and skips the shell boundary for admitted warm boot.

The benchmark's warm fixture needed correction: persisting the transcript under token auth without a stored credential did not admit a cached boot record. The fixture now uses its existing trusted-proxy authentication and persists the snapshot's stored weight. Both comparison arms use that same corrected fixture, and the benchmark records actual cache admission.

## Evidence

The acceptance rule was written before measurement: 20 serial rotated base/head/identical-base-control triplets in each of 30 cells; cold/warm/2,000-message open, desktop/mobile, Chromium at 1×/4×/6×, and WebKit/Firefox application time at 1×. Affected Chromium longest tasks must improve at least 5%; readiness must hold within the campaign band, with no correctness/CLS regression. Traced runs are separate diagnostics. Both arms use the corrected warm fixture.

The committed workload command was repeated for the stated engines, throttle rates, and viewports, with both bundles built completely on the same host:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir <base-build> --compare-bundle-dir <head-build> \
  --control-bundle-dir <base-build> --pairs 20 --engines chromium \
  --cpu-throttle 4 --viewport both \
  --steps cold-boot,warm-boot,large-transcript-open
```

The affected cold/large flows qualify: longest-task medians improve 10–43%, with improved readiness. The complete matrix and fixed continuations total 2,250 observations with zero application failures. Initial matrix: 1,800 observations; first continuations: 330; final fixed 20-pair warm 4×/6× confirmations: 120. All earlier observations remain included. No repeated-until-green selection.

The warm-tail decision uses the campaign confirmation rule. The pooled 50-pair desktop warm 4× sample still has longest-task p95 +5.56% and script p95 +7.67%; readiness is +0.36%/+2.19% and total CPU +1.06%/+3.44%. Those initial tails did not reproduce in the predeclared final 20 pairs: longest-task 317.5/352 → 320.5/349 ms, readiness 1250.95/1326.6 → 1266.4/1312.6 ms, total CPU +0.79%/+0.53%, and script +0.89%/+0.16%. Host-load medians declined across stages, so this is confirmation-based acceptance, not proof that the original tail was noise. Desktop warm 6× final20 longest-task 554.5/624 → 543.5/611 ms and readiness 2068.65/2361.1 → 2109.55/2269.6 ms; CPU +2.49%/−4.24%. Its pooled50 readiness and CPU tails also hold.

Firefox mobile cold readiness median is +5.005% (489.5 → 514 ms), at the 5% band within the timer’s resolution; its p95 improves 18.6%. WebKit mobile warm confirmed p95 is +4.7%. These limits are retained rather than described as universal wins.

Values are median/p95 milliseconds; readiness is head versus base.

| Flow | CPU / target | Desktop longest task | Mobile longest task | Desktop readiness Δ | Mobile readiness Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cold-boot | 1× / 50 ms | 99/104 → 66/67 | 97/103 → 58.5/62 | -3.7%/-3.2% | -3.5%/-4.8% |
| cold-boot | 4× / 200 ms | 512/588 → 382/451 | 537/574 → 307.5/335 | -3.9%/-1.4% | -4.7%/-5.5% |
| cold-boot | 6× / 300 ms | 768.5/862 → 536/650 | 844/917 → 491.5/520 | -5.6%/-5.5% | -3.9%/-5.5% |
| warm-boot | 1× / 50 ms | 69/73 → 68.5/72 | 69.5/74 → 70/77 | +0.2%/-0.1% | +0.8%/-0.6% |
| warm-boot | 4× / 200 ms | 325.5/378 → 326/399 | 359/469 → 350.5/436 | +0.4%/+2.2% | +0.1%/-5.3% |
| warm-boot | 6× / 300 ms | 564/694 → 557.5/711 | 536.5/588 → 535/570 | -0.2%/-0.6% | +1.2%/-0.7% |
| large-transcript-open | 1× / 50 ms | 97.5/101 → 86/91 | 116.5/122 → 85.5/90 | -4.3%/-2.5% | -5.7%/-8.6% |
| large-transcript-open | 4× / 200 ms | 512.5/578 → 460.5/494 | 559.5/652 → 387/454 | -2.7%/-2.6% | -7.3%/-5.7% |
| large-transcript-open | 6× / 300 ms | 950.5/1091 → 803.5/906 | 903/972 → 628.5/655 | -7.6%/-5.3% | -6.3%/-5.7% |

No absolute target is reached. The structural split improves cold and large-open blocking, while warm boot retains its immediate path. ## Trace attribution

Separate native traces cover both viewports and all three flows at 1×/4×/6×. Every new continuation follows a main-document Paint (24/24, zero unmatched events). Warm base/head have no yield continuations. This proves renderer paint work occurred, not completed display presentation.

The original long tasks combine several owners: bootstrap/theme preparation → shell/sidebar construction; then pane startup/hydration → header/Details → composer → transcript preparation. After the split, transcript/Markdown/geometry becomes the longest task. At desktop 6× in the instrumented diagnostic, cold bootstrap+shell (~993 ms), pane (~1,073 ms), and transcript (~821 ms) become separate bootstrap (~475 ms), shell (~580 ms), pane (~620 ms), and transcript (~763 ms) tasks. Large-open leaves a ~961 ms transcript task. These diagnostic numbers are not substituted for the untraced table.

Prominent remaining owners are `chat-details.tsx` positioning, `chat-composer-dom.ts` anchor/textarea geometry, Markdown parsing/sanitization, transcript message indexing, and virtualizer geometry. No single giant algorithm accounts for the full freeze. Native warm profiles retain the same owner families and do not establish a new causal owner for the small tail movement.

Focused proof: UI typecheck; all 19 warm-root tests; all nine pane bridge tests; targeted lint; production Knip; full UI build; strict paired size check. The warm regression fails on the preceding shell implementation and passes with the bypass. Independent Codex review of the complete change found no actionable P0–P2 finding. Final lint retained warnings for intentional immutable first-admission decisions and an existing progress projection. CI: full `ci:full` run 42424537142 passed on exact final head `b7cf7c8a324`.

Touched UI production LOC after repair: 537 → 589 (+52). All ten touched files: 3,719 → 3,874 (+155); the cap-only file has no LOC growth. Solid audit is unchanged: one effect, one component cleanup, zero render effects, untrack, direct DOM queries/listeners, flush, or owner-restoration calls. The added code owns the two conditional boundaries and completion lifecycle; the pane indentation change keeps its immutable admission fact local instead of passing a one-use prop.

prs.title: fix: stop closed macOS dashboards reconnecting after native auth refusal
prs.body:
Related: #168743

## What Problem This Solves

Closing or replacing a natively authenticated macOS Dashboard can leave its committed page reconnecting after that window can no longer obtain native authorization, producing repeated pre-connect warnings.

## User Impact

Closing or replacing a native Dashboard now retires and unloads its document. A retained window reopens its trusted route using the same WebView storage; hiding or minimizing preserves its live document. Exact repeated native-refusal warnings retain the first diagnostic and periodic suppressed counts rather than one warning per attempt.

Real-WKWebView and Gateway evidence is now available, with the revision and host limits below. The reporter's installed-app trigger and cessation of its reconnect loop remain unconfirmed. No full native-suite green or exact-new-commit native rerun is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stopping WebKit navigation does not unload a committed page. The existing controller now retires that document and its identity at actual native close/replacement, retains its trusted reopen route, and keeps the inert retirement page non-deliverable. Browser identity, origin/account storage boundaries and transient native recovery remain intact; there is no refusal cap or retry-policy change.

The Gateway extends its existing bounded authentication-log limiter only for pre-connect code 4008 and the exact raw reason native authorization unavailable. Code 1006, near-matches and credential-mismatch warnings keep their previous behavior.

The supplied native run also exposed an obsolete notification-test oracle: after closing, it expected the outgoing page to remain at /. The follow-up test repair now requires about:blank while closed, explicitly reopens, then waits for the retained / route instead of the stale notification's completion route. Window identity, closed state and non-close navigation checks are preserved.

## Evidence

- The notification replay test is repaired without removing ownership checks. Supplied stock-host focused runs pass **9/9 only with that dirty test patch**; they are not executions of the new commit.
- Real WKWebView evidence denies stale credentials and permits a fresh document after close, replacement and immediate reopen. A selective base overlay actually fails the two immediate-reopen assertions.
- New supplied focused TypeScript proof is **65/65**, separate from the historical **67/5-file** run. The synthetic real-Gateway trace emits **2 native + 3 control** warnings versus **12 + 3** on the selective base overlay; it does not prove app reconnect cessation.
- **Lint is not green:** normal scope has one source-verified inherited file-length violation; a different explicit touched-test scope reports 60 serious diagnostics. Restricted sibling sweeps, crashes, timeouts and omissions are disclosed below—not counted passing.
- **Remaining validation:** exact-new-head native execution and reporter-side built-app close/reconnect correlation. Current-head ordinary CI passed; the hosted review is high-confidence ready for maintainer review with no Before-merge items, but rates overall readiness 3/6—not Platinum overall. No full native-suite green or current-main validation is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Audited receipts, sanitized excerpts, source equivalence and all negative results</summary>

### Revision, source equivalence and hosts

The [reporter's public evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6552265574) and independently audited supplied bundle concern head f56bd97a670203f386ff71e313f25e50d6562afc and admitted base 3a3246e7c1389c03e933e1f15805306945b1df1c. The audit inspected artifacts; it did not rerun supplied scripts or tests. All 70 declared bundle checksums matched; ZIP SHA-256: 3c684b5ed17f6304d842331974a271b140bfb86ee3a16b288d861b61d99b6bb2.

The [new repair commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4) changes only DashboardNotificationWindowTests.swift (+4/−1) from that recorded head. Its complete resulting file is byte-identical to the published f56 file plus the audited patch (patch SHA-256 3151270b79163551c9f5082ba0dc15a161bb855139191716f680dd6682235d64; resulting Git blob 7ab8659bf05356f99fddfef4e7a05b4db7236e31). All eleven earlier changed source files still match f56. This establishes tracked-source equivalence, not a new-commit test execution or complete generated/untracked/build-input attestation.

- Host A is reported as stock Xcode 27.1/Swift 6.4 on macOS 27.2 arm64 with a GUI. Library/platform/AppKit records partly corroborate that metadata; the bundle does not contain a complete pinned checkout/toolchain attestation.
- Host B directly records swift.org 6.3.3/SDK26.5 without GUI, substitute SwiftUI/Preview macro plugins, and two omitted XCTest files (SimpleTaskSupportTests.swift and MacNodeLocationServiceTests.swift). Its results are adapted, restricted coverage—not a stock/full native build. Supplied Studio scripts omit untracked files from dirty-state output.
- Head-plus-patch passes still record the old f56 HEAD and a modified test. Base-overlay runs retain the head checkout/tests and restore selected production files, not a clean full-base checkout. Exact overlaid bytes cannot be independently reconstructed from the bundle. No supplied scripts or macro stubs were executed during this audit/update.

### Real WKWebView outcomes — including the original red test

Unpatched f56 is not native-green: “older manager command replay does not cancel a newer notification click” fails refreshed-close and new-window-close, receiving an empty path where its old oracle expected /. The supplied base overlay and head-plus-patch each pass its four cases on both hosts. The source owner inspected the real retirement implementation and wait helper before applying the audited correction above.

| Supplied selection | Audited result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| A, recorded clean-state f56, focused 9 tests / 3 suites | 8 test functions pass; older-manager fails with 2 issues; EXIT=1. The WK ownership matrix (10 cases), forbidden frame/browser-identity cases (3), retained close/reopen (2), replacement unload, device-settings (9 cases) and 3 ControlUIDocument tests pass. |
| A, f56 plus dirty test patch, same selection | 9 tests / 3 suites pass in 31.181 seconds; EXIT=0. Separate older-manager rerun passes 4 cases. Not an exact-new-commit rerun. |
| B, adapted focused selections | Auth bridge 4 tests pass, including 3 + 10 + 2 parameter cases; device settings 1 test / 9 cases and isolated conversation factory pass. Socket-retirement and saved-profile selections crash with signal 5 on both head and base overlay; those are not passes. |
| B, adapted restricted sibling sweep | 252 test-pass records; 253 tests / 46 suites fail with 2 issues, EXIT=1. The completed sweep's failing test is older-manager. Other attempts abort or remain incomplete. No full-suite green. |

The important completed negative control uses the real WK reply boundary: A's selective native base overlay reaches immediate-reopen, delivers a grant to the retired document and fails two assertions. The recorded head denies that stale recipient and completes a fresh current recipient after close, replacement and immediate reopen. It also accepts current/current-password/current-device-only and rejects document/provider/socket/browser-identity stale replies.

Sanitized excerpts below are supplied-log evidence, not independent reruns. Anchors name bundle-relative files; they are not public download URLs. Credential payloads, local paths and endpoint/host values are omitted.

    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-base-native-WK_challenge_replies_are_owned_.log:20,23,41–48
      immediate-reopen: expected error != nil and result == nil; both fail
      transition=immediate-reopen result=true error=false
      ten cases failed with 2 issues; EXIT=1
    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-head-native-focused.log:26–32
      close and replacement: stale response denied; new current recipient completes
      transition=immediate-reopen result=false error=true
      current-recipient=new-document completed; ten cases passed
    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-patch-head-native-focused.log:45–49
      older-manager four cases passed
      Test run with 9 tests in 3 suites passed after 31.181 seconds. EXIT=0

Other negative results remain material: A's base unload/reopen and replacement attempts time out at planning with no test-start marker; these are noncompletion, not assertion-red. Its base forbidden-frame filter reports No matching test cases were run, not coverage. A's experience selection fails with Keychain -60006 (10 tests / 3 suites, EXIT=1). B sweep run2 aborts on an uncalled download completion handler (signal 6); run3 has a miniaturize wait failure and Keychain -61 failures without a completed summary. The saved sweep script has nine exclusion-regex alternatives; the completed log lacks exact argv and earlier filters evolved. Exclusions/crashes are not passes, and not every failure/exclusion is independently matched on base.

### Gateway and focused TypeScript proof

New supplied focused tests: 65/65 in 3 files pass, EXIT=0. The same head tests with selective base connection.ts and handshake-auth-log-limiter.ts yield 63 pass / 2 fail, EXIT=1; only the two native-refusal aggregation regressions fail. Both captures identify Vitest 5.0.5, test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts and:

    node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server/ws-connection.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-log-limiter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

A real isolated loopback Gateway and synthetic WebSocket client receive connect.challenge and send 12 native-refusal closes (10, wait 31 s, then 2), plus 3 connect-failed controls. The selective base overlay emits 12 native +3 control lines; recorded head emits 2 native +3 control lines, with suppressed=9 on the second native warning. This proves transport logging suppression, not authentication success or app reconnect cessation. The final suppressed attempt has no later emitted summary; 2+9 must not be presented as accounting for all 12 attempts.

    EVIDENCE/head-ts-focused.log:127–135: 3 files passed; 65 tests passed; EXIT=0
    EVIDENCE/base-overlay-ts-focused.log:185–195: 63 passed; 2 failed; EXIT=1
    EVIDENCE/live-gateway-head.log:3–15: 12 native closes +3 controls; 5 warning lines
    EVIDENCE/live-gateway-base-overlay.log:3–14: same plan; 15 warning lines

These captures do not establish complete dependency/configuration/source-state parity or a combined app-to-Gateway run.

### Formatting and lint — scopes are not interchangeable

Supplied SwiftFormat lint reports 0/416 files requiring formatting (6 skipped), then0/33, with one combined EXIT=0. It is not compilation or a blanket touched-test lint pass.

Both normal SwiftLint captures report 1 serious violation / 419 files, EXIT=2: DashboardManager.swift file_length 1505 >1500. Source comparison now independently establishes that DashboardManager.swift is byte-identical at admitted base 3a, recorded f56 and this candidate (SHA-256 896a2f6f9c430ab7cacde9f0345e43b26c809e4ce012e0965f713d0d51d5ec64). The PR does not introduce this failure. Current main has a separate provider addition, not identical bytes; it is not claimed lint-clean.

The additional explicit touched-file capture reports 60 serious violations / 5 files, EXIT=2, in the test-file inputs; DashboardWindowController.swift has no diagnostic there. This negative result is retained, not called green or silently attributed to base. Exact touched-command flags/effective config/version are absent from the bundle, so its 60 findings cannot be equated to the standard invocation.

The pinned standard owner is scripts/lint-swift.sh macos → run-swiftlint.mts --strict --config config/swiftlint.yml, plus the swabble config. Those wrappers/configs are unchanged across admitted base, f56, candidate and inspected current main. The standard config includes Sources roots, not the explicit test-file list. Its 1500 file-length warning becomes serious under local strict mode; the existing wrapper treats limit rules as advisory only in genuine GitHub Actions. This is source-policy inspection, not an executed CI/lint pass; no flags, baselines, exclusions or rules were weakened. The standard format wrapper also checks declared Sources roots, not every test file.

### Historical proof kept separate

Historical local October 27 validation leading to f69148d4cbef51ff1586c74a87637071b9ede57d: 67 tests /5 files passed (40.39s), targeted TypeScript lint/typecheck/format/diff checks passed. An isolated Gateway run observed 3 refused closes → 2 warnings including suppressed=1, another signed client remained connected, and a later signed reconnect received hello. Native-auth UI recovery 29 passed; draft-commit persistence 1 passed. The new 65-test bundle neither contains that historical terminal run nor independently reproduces it. Neither number is a new-head rerun.

The preconnect consolidation preserved 28 named tests and 38 transferred assertions; original/replacement overlap 36 passed and deliberate producer omissions failed the retained old/new guard families. Counted TypeScript test delta remains −24 with no baseline/counting-policy exception; these inputs are unchanged by the notification-test correction. prs.title: fix: preserve owner tool access after network reads
prs.body:
Regression introduced by #193098.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicitly authorized owner's setup request is rejected after the agent reads a network result, such as looking up a GitHub profile before assigning its role.

## User Impact

An explicit owner with current administrator authority can continue the same request after a network lookup, without avoiding the lookup or sending another prompt. Revoked authority, insufficient scopes, explicit tool policy, and taint restrictions on inherited non-owner authority remain enforced. Network content remains marked untrusted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained-operator continuation change added an unconditional taint veto to the general owner-tool guard. That also revoked ordinary explicit-owner eligibility, although the requester's identity and permissions had not changed. Confine the taint veto to callers without explicit owner attribution, while retaining the existing current-authority and administrator checks. Use the same condition in the error selection so taint no longer masks a different owner-authority failure.

This replaces the earlier guidance-only candidate: those description/documentation edits have been removed. No new setting, grant, approval flow, or alternate role-assignment mechanism is introduced.

## Evidence

- Incident evidence records `senderIsOwner: true` and `trigger: user` for both the network lookup and subsequent rejected setup call.
- The regression uses actual outer-tool construction and taint observation, mocking only final Gateway I/O. On the base: 3 failures / 14 passes. Explicit owners were rejected after lookup, pre-existing taint falsely reported a non-owner turn, and taint masked revocation. With the fix: all 31 retained-owner and prompt-stability checks pass, including those failures, owner policy denial/narrow authority, and retained non-owner controls. Taint remains set after successful delegation.
- Green test run: 199.76s Vitest / 205.22s wrapper, largely compilation. The changed regression file adds 52 lines, with a matching allocation; no duplicate fixture or production framework was added.
- Production core TypeScript check (`pnpm tsgo:core`), targeted type-aware core lint, formatting, line-growth checks, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks passed. Prior production-head CI run [42343084587](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42343084587) completed with three failures; attribution is recorded below. The gate is not passing.
- Independent native P0–P3 review of the complete runtime/regression candidate against `06a5df2659599e96ecfa184f84a22d48abfb89fb`: no actionable production/test findings. Reviewed patch SHA-256: `59ebcc60c7b3285dde26d1dd7bf609099b235e65cdfa91d3b456fb9bbefb364f`. This is a narrative independent assessment, not an autoreview-helper machine result; earlier helper attempts failed before review.
- Earlier live attempts (historical; superseded by the successful OAuth trace below): the corrected isolated Gateway test started, but the local test environment’s outbound proxy rejected the API destination before inference or any tool call (`status: error`, no tool calls, no saved mapping). Earlier attempts failed during isolated-auth staging/startup; an interim candidate was deliberately stopped to repair two proof-oracle defects. The experimental fixture also assumed API-key authentication; environment-variable presence did not establish a usable API credential, and at that time no supported OAuth-backed live run had been demonstrated. The proxy refusal is an observed failure, not evidence that changing network policy alone would make the fixture usable. None of those failed attempts is counted as success, and the experimental fixture is not included in the PR. The reproduced and repaired contract is the actual outer-tool authority/delegation boundary; those attempts did not verify a model-driven end-to-end role write. The successful native-OAuth run below now supplies that evidence.


### Prior-head CI attribution

Tested head: `bbe4e8c663d4031bfd162b60a0bac9faa1d67b4a`; frozen base: `f231ad6693d808e8da6008ca2643058072ebbb3a`; tested merge: `47325a26274641d55f12345ec01488c86e04ae8a`. The exact base-to-merge diff at that run contained only the original three changed files. The subsequent integration-test addition is not covered by this run.

- **Architecture:** `madge-import-cycles` reports `control-ui-static.ts` ↔ `server-control-ui-root.ts`. Neither file nor production import edges change here. Upstream [#194496](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194496) merged a repair after this run’s frozen base. The failed run is retained, not relabeled green.
- **UI E2E:** `gateway-fresh-visit.http.e2e.test.ts` expected the old app-bundle failure heading at line 204. The test and production UI are unchanged by this PR. Separate [#194504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194504) addresses the stale expectation; it is open, not a shipped fix.
- **Test-line ratchet:** the merge reported 6,558,578 lines, a 6,558,571 ceiling, and +52 lines. This PR adds exactly 52 test lines and 52 allocated lines. Thus its frozen base already has 6,558,526 lines against a 6,558,519 ceiling: seven inherited lines of debt. No extra budget or test deletion is being used to hide that deficit.

[ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194472#issuecomment-6702670509) reviewed production head `bbe4e8c663d4031bfd162b60a0bac9faa1d67b4a`. It found no discrete introduced correctness defect and recommends the explicit-owner exemption, subject to final-effect authority proof and current-head security approval. The subsequent test-only addition addresses the deterministic authority-chain gap described below. The real-model lookup → delegated assignment → persisted readback trace is now supplied below. Enforced current-head maintainer security approval remains outstanding.

### Joined delegated-write proof (synthetic inference)

The new integration regression exercises real outer-tool construction and the owner wrapper, in-process Gateway dispatch, `openclaw.chat`, delegated approval, the setup engine/proposal tool, config validation, and disk persistence. Inference/auth ownership uses the existing synthetic fixture and an explicitly admitted test source grant; no API key or live model request is used. A wrapper around real config validation pauses after its genuine result, before persistence, without substituting a validation result or a write.

- **Active explicit owner after a network observation:** the mapping for `fixture-contributor` is persisted and read back from the disposable config file. Taint remains set.
- **Original source grant revoked during delegation:** abort the admitted owner's grant after real config validation, release the paused handler, and join settlement. Original file bytes remain identical and the role mapping is absent.
- **Tainted non-owner:** rejected before Gateway dispatch or inference; original file bytes remain unchanged.

Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-owner-write.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **3 passed**, 100.56s wall / 93.78s Vitest / 11.639s case execution (cold compilation dominates). CI seconds are not yet available. The 231-line test uses existing fixtures and has a matching separate test-line allocation. This composition is needed because the previous outer-tool tests mock dispatch and the writer tests supply only a synthetic authority callback. No production API or test-only hook was added. The fixture starts with a source receipt for the same grant, so this proves composed source-chain revocation rather than independently proving that the outer guard is the sole supplier of that receipt. Gateway-methods test typecheck, targeted repository lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.

This is deterministic final-effect integration evidence, **not** a real-model recording, live GitHub lookup, or proof of a person's subsequent login. Earlier failed live attempts remain documented above. The final integration test was also replayed with only `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` restored to its pre-fix `ac0c596b119` bytes: **2 failed / 1 passed**, both explicit-owner cases failing with `Owner-level tools cannot run on a tainted turn.` Baseline wall time was 96.02s. The fixed guard was restored byte-for-byte afterward. This isolates the guard change; it is not a claim that a full old checkout or live model was exercised.

Independent native review of this addition found one P2 test-lifecycle issue: bind the deferred wait to test cancellation. Addressed with the existing `withinTest` helper and Vitest’s context-aware table API; no production behavior changed. After that repair, all three controls, the Gateway-methods test typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and the test-line budget pass. Final test-file SHA-256: `10f8c839d0a8030e2dd4e648bf4037593da8bc1cbfc137b2e0d76472b2f2c36d`.

Sanitized terminal summary:

```text
Fixed guard: active owner saved mapping and readback matched — PASS
Fixed guard: source owner revoked after real validation; unchanged config — PASS
Fixed guard: tainted non-owner; no Gateway dispatch — PASS
Tests: 3 passed
Original guard: active owner — Owner-level tools cannot run on a tainted turn.
Original guard: revoked-owner scenario — Owner-level tools cannot run on a tainted turn.
Original guard: tainted non-owner — PASS
Tests: 2 failed | 1 passed
```


### Real-agent OAuth proof — completed November 7, 2026

Tested unchanged published head `37b5e053951bd8e60f187ff508a93d9787d070b0`. The ordinary `pnpm dev` build and `pnpm dev gateway run` launched a separate loopback Gateway with disposable config, workspace, roles and sessions. Actual model inference used the Codex runtime and the existing native ChatGPT OAuth login (`appServer.transport: stdio`, `homeScope: user`); no API key, credential copy, synthetic inference, tool mock or production Gateway change was used. A new native thread was created, not a resumed live thread.

The shipped Gateway client's normal token handshake explicitly requested and received `operator.admin` (plus read/write/approvals). Through the public Gateway WebSocket API, `sessions.create` made a Full Access session and `chat.send` submitted the request: fetch GitHub's public `octocat` profile, then use `openclaw` to preassign that login to the existing contributor role. The model selected and executed the lookup and both setup calls. Tool and provenance evidence was retrieved using `chat.history`, not reconstructed from assistant prose.

Sanitized recorded sequence (UTC):

```text
2026-11-07T07:03:26.824Z web_fetch: HTTP 200; resultContentSource=network
2026-11-07T07:03:33.253Z openclaw call: turnTainted=true
2026-11-07T07:04:14.919Z openclaw result: done: config.set
2026-11-07T07:04:17.687Z openclaw call: turnTainted=true
2026-11-07T07:04:28.468Z openclaw result: readback confirms octocat = contributor
2026-11-07T07:04:31.121Z agent.wait: status=ok; rerouted=false
```

The first `openclaw` result reported:

```text
[openclaw] running: config.set
Updated gateway.roles.assignments.byGithubLogin.octocat. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
[openclaw] done: config.set
```

The model then requested a separate read-only setup-tool verification. Its result confirmed the saved `octocat = contributor` mapping and unchanged existing mapping, role definitions and default role. Independent disk readback found:

```json
{"existing-fixture":"contributor","octocat":"contributor"}
```

The complete post-write config equals the original config plus this mapping, passed through the existing `stampConfigWriteMetadata` function. This matters: the minimal fixture also acquired the normal selected-model allowlist and migration/version metadata on first write. Those automatic additions are disclosed, not hidden under a claim that only one JSON field changed. Every other authored setting is preserved. Both delegated calls retained `turnTainted: true`; the public lookup remained `resultContentSource: network`. The sole recorded `exec` item was native Code Mode wrapping `tools.web_fetch`, not a shell command or file mutation. There was no extra user prompt, auth fallback, live-account role assignment, external message, or production restart.

Post-run artifact checks:

```text
PASS: HTTP 200 lookup precedes both tainted OpenClaw delegations
PASS: delegated config.set, setup readback and independent disk readback agree
PASS: complete config matches requested change plus canonical write migrations
PASS: no shell/file mutation shortcut; terminal status ok and no reroute
PASS: isolated Gateway shutdown completed cleanly
```

Earlier failures remain part of the evidence: the API-only experiment never reached inference; the first OAuth run did reach real inference but generic `gateway call chat.send` requested only `operator.write` and correctly failed owner authorization. No mapping was saved by that run. The successful run used the same production candidate with properly admitted administrator scope, not a sender-flag override or an authorization bypass.

This closes the requested live lookup → delegated assignment → persisted readback evidence gap. It does not claim subsequent GitHub login, deployment, passing CI, or maintainer security approval. Current-head approval remains separate. No code changed in collecting this proof.

prs.title: fix(research): keep deep research in the side panel only
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every Control UI session showed a full-width "Deep research" bar and a second "Deep research" button under the header, even with no research. Reported by Ryan S. on Discord.

## Solution

This builds on Josh's #194780 (his commits are included) and narrows the UI to one entry point:

- **Kept from #194780:** the header button and full-width bar are removed; portable research no longer fails on detailed model replies (lists trimmed to their maxima, audit verdicts untouched); start/resume results drop retained source text and stay under 24 KB, with a hint to call `action: "result"` for the full result.
- **Removed on top:** the transcript research card (inline view, its descriptor and styles) and the session-menu "Deep research" action.
- **Result:** the Deep research panel (side panel → New tab → Explore panels → Deep research) is the plugin's only Control UI entry point. Everything the card showed — status, counts, findings, report, gaps, cancel/resume — is already in the panel.

A redesigned in-chat research card will come in a separate PR with visual QA.

## User Impact

- Sessions carry no deep-research chrome.
- Open research from the side panel's Explore panels list; on mobile, Panels restores an open research tab.
- Tool callers: start/resume results no longer include full source text (from #194780).

## Evidence

**Before (`main`):** idle session with the header button and full-width bar.

![Before: idle session with Deep research button and bar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/038db128-d09b-4de8-ad67-d4a5b7be2117)

**After:** Deep research listed under Explore panels; no header chrome.

![After: side panel launcher listing Deep research](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ebe0456-7368-4054-adc5-809c12443486)

![After: research panel with report](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dd1f272-3aeb-43e5-a63c-00b4e58240be)

![After: mobile panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9423e058-3614-4034-93e6-d7a6916ad350)

Screenshots come from the real native plugin bundle in `ui/src/e2e/deep-research-plugin.e2e.test.ts` against the mock Gateway.

- `ui/src/e2e/deep-research-plugin.e2e.test.ts`: 2/2 pass. Asserts no "Deep research" button outside the panel, opens the panel from Explore panels, and covers running, cancel, report, sources, mobile, offline and denied states.
- `pnpm test extensions/deep-research`: 104 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.

If this lands, #194780 can be closed in its favor.

prs.title: fix: keep ignored build outputs out of worker results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: worker builds can fill the result byte budget with ignored build/cache outputs, rejecting the user's actual source changes.

Related: #194475, #194642.

## User Impact

Local managed sandbox results omit new Git-ignored build output under checkout-root `dist/` and `.cache/openclaw-bun/`, while retaining tracked changes and other authored files, including ignored screenshots and reports. Remote Git workspaces retain their existing Git eligibility boundary and additionally capture ordinary `.artifacts/` outputs in results. The byte cap, over-limit handling, staged-input collision guards, and publication admission remain unchanged. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local capture owner asks trusted Git for standard excludes using the canonical index/config and guest worktree ignore files, then passes prepared facts to the manifest scanner. The scanner cannot depend back on the Git owner; this avoids the import cycle found in the first candidate. Tracked files and exact admitted or accepted paths remain protected; recovery shares this capture policy.

Native-node and SSH captures use the existing Git eligibility owner: tracked/nonignored paths, explicit `.worktreeinclude` inputs, marker-authenticated private inputs, and prior accepted paths. Results also traverse ordinary `.artifacts/` outputs, applying the existing disposable-cache exclusions. Preparation and completion verification explicitly request eligible capture. Prior receipts retain paths; they do not select capture mode.

The broad remote filesystem walk in the previous revision was a regression: it enrolled ignored private project files and hard-linked lookalike ownership markers. Portable manifests omit filesystem link counts, so reconciliation correctly refused the newly enrolled unowned directory. This correction restores admission at capture and removes the redundant remote ignored-output/retained-ancestor bookkeeping. Existing collision, private-file, preparation, and screenshot assertions remain intact.

Full PR LOC: **+71 handwritten production**, **+18 generated**, **+134 tests/test-support**, and a separate **+265-line benchmark**. Production growth supplies trusted Git exclusion facts across the existing worker boundary and explicit capture scope/artifact retention; duplicate local serialization and recovery capture were removed. This follow-up is **−1 handwritten / −70 generated production lines** relative to `86034a28`.

## Evidence

Exact main parent: `2e13c52c97bbe81228c4f45212c8ca8cd346dbf9`. The two reported regression files pass **18/18** on that parent; `86034a28c510` fails exactly the reported **five**, with **13 passing**. The original ignored-build-output regression also fails on the parent. Earlier import-cycle, screenshot, and prepared-project failures were candidate regressions and were corrected without weakening their assertions.

The complete requested comparison finished with **zero failures on either revision**:

| Revision | Passed tests | Skipped tests | Passed files | Skipped files |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact main parent `2e13c52c97bb` | 3,972 | 25 | 345 | 5 |
| Candidate `44014310182d` | 3,974 | 25 | 345 | 5 |

Both selected 350 files across three Vitest shards. The candidate has no failures absent on main. This includes the whole worker-environments directory, node-host workspace and transfer tests, and all response-authority tests.

The whole comparison command is run on isolated parent/candidate worktrees with the same installed Git and bounded concurrency:

```sh
PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1 \
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments src/node-host/*workspace*.test.ts \
  src/node-host/node-worker-transfer*.test.ts \
  src/gateway/control-ui.response-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

The bounded candidate run overlaps the latter part of the parent run (two workers each). The initial broader node-host selection stopped at unrelated plugin build prerequisites before any tests. An initial concurrent comparison suffered Git command timeouts; those interrupted runs are not the before/after proof. No test timeout, assertion, filesystem safety check, or ownership guard was weakened.

`pnpm check:changed --base 2e13c52c97bbe81228c4f45212c8ca8cd346dbf9` ran. Core/test/script types, format, line/test budgets, database guards, boundaries, and runtime cycles passed. Its generated unused-function lint finding was fixed by moving the local-only predicate out of remote script text; final affected lint passes. Both Madge and runtime import-cycle checks report zero cycles; generated assets are current.

Two documented baseline checks remain red: unused exports `parseDarwinProcessBirths` introduced by #194245 (`5577faefa9e1`) and six gesture-probe exports from #194676 (`055544b9fa35`); archived changelog entries rejected by the attribution policy introduced in #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`). Prior exact-parent reproductions and attribution are retained; these are main regressions requiring owner follow-up.

The broader macOS check also hit a native skills-watcher freshness failure (`Original` instead of `Final` after 10 seconds). The same unresolved area was reported by another lane. Focused replay passes on exact parent and candidate. The unchanged notification-based owner/test originated in #176905 (`be0c50ad03b6`), but the intermittent failure mechanism is unproven: **this is not claimed as a proven inherited exception or a clean aggregate check**. No unrelated watcher code or assertions changed.

Final staged-candidate Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. No live environment was accessed and no UI-imported modules changed.

Synthetic real-owner fixture: 22,001 tracked files plus 40,000 ignored build/cache files, about 1.144 GB. The parent rejects **880,000,012 bytes / 40,001 changes**; the fix successfully stages/reconciles **12 bytes / one tracked change**, preserving the complete tracked inventory. All 30 original runs verify those assertions. These measurements compare the exact parent with the original candidate `2d22e4a23999`; the follow-up policy selects the same paths in this fixture (only ignored `dist/` and Bun-runtime cache outputs), so the campaign was not rerun. They are not new-head timing measurements.

Five serial A/B pairs per measurement, with four identical-code A/A controls per phase; CPU profiles run separately:

| Metric | Parent median / p95 | Fix median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Owner wall time | 8.28 / 14.73 s | 2.46 / 10.29 s |
| Process CPU | 14.99 / 21.01 s | 4.51 / 10.41 s |
| Main-thread CPU | 60.42 / 63.99 ms | 47.78 / 69.11 ms |
| Sampled V8 allocation, main + retained workers | 3,660.70 / 3,686.58 MiB | 870.47 / 872.50 MiB |

Median wall/CPU improve about 70%; allocation improves 76%. A/A wall pairs were 7.690/7.529 s and 6.727/6.757 s; allocation controls differed by −0.12% and +0.36%. All paired wall measurements improved, but host load varied and the slow first candidate is retained. Main-thread CPU p95 rose 8%, within the observed 17% A/A variation. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum.

This is warm-owner checkpointing in fresh processes on local APFS, comparing baseline rejection with successful fixed reconciliation. It does not qualify btrfs or whole-Gateway latency. Process CPU excludes Git subprocesses; allocation samples V8 main/five retained workers, excluding native allocations and ephemeral heartbeat workers. No new retained worker escaped profiling. The committed benchmark reproduces the fixture; frozen sources and raw profiles are retained locally.

prs.title: fix(ios): Rewind overwrites text and attachments added while the request is pending
prs.body:
Closes #193817

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unsent text and attachments added to the iOS composer while a Rewind request is in flight are silently overwritten when the request completes.

## User Impact

User impact: people who edit the composer during a Rewind now keep their newer text and attachment selections, while the history rewind and branch reconciliation still complete. When the composer is untouched, Rewind restores the earlier prompt and images exactly as before. No migration or user action needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewindToMessage` restored the editor text and the full attachment array unconditionally once the request succeeded. The change captures the composer's text and attachment revisions when the request starts and restores the rewound prompt and images only when the composer stayed unchanged, treating the composer as one draft so rewound content is never mixed into newer edits. Attachment edits now advance their own per-session revision (the existing revision tracked text only), and programmatic restores are excluded so they are not mistaken for user edits.

## Evidence

Executed validation, in three parts with distinct sources and scope:

- **Package regression tests (GitHub-hosted macOS runner, my fork):** all three new Rewind tests in `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` pass on PR head `d25b7a9`; on merge-base `5825589` with the same tests added, all three fail with the expected draft-preservation assertion failures. Both versions built successfully. Run: https://github.com/marlonferreira1800-hue/openclaw/actions/runs/42151119310 (the run shows failed only because an extra log-counting check miscounted the expected baseline failures; the test logs show three passing on head, three failing on base). Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193867#issuecomment-6675717728
- **Native iOS Simulator proof (my fork, scratch branch; the PR branch is unchanged at `d25b7a9`):** attach a photo, start Rewind, hold the `sessions.rewind` response, type "Keep this newer note", then release. Baseline `58255890` overwrites the composer with the earlier prompt and loses the attachment; head `d25b7a9` preserves the newer text and attachment, the Rewind response completes before the app's 15-second timeout, and the app calls `chat.history` and `sessions.branches.list` after release. Run: https://github.com/marlonferreira1800-hue/openclaw/actions/runs/42205370495 (artifact `rewind-ios-demo-evidence`). Limits: the Branches menu did not render, so branch UI behavior remains unverified, and this run has no unchanged-draft control. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193867#issuecomment-6685873915
- **Independent native comparison by ellibbe** (iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 27.0): pre-change production `58255890ba9e` fails the draft-preservation assertion, head `d25b7a96575d` passes, and the untouched-composer control passes (restores the earlier prompt as intended), with unedited native captures. Scope: controlled Gateway responses, not a persisted rewind on a real Gateway. Review: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193867#pullrequestreview-5798815859

- New regressions in `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` cover text-only, attachment-only, and combined composer edits through the existing controlled-completion gate, and assert that history refresh still completes when restoration is skipped. Each fails against the pre-change code, where the restore was unconditional.
- Existing controls are preserved by construction of the guard: the unchanged-composer case (`rewind seeds editor and refreshes history`) still restores, and the different-session completion case in `ChatSessionCompletionOwnershipTests` is untouched.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed against current main (85c39026a90f).

prs.title: fix(postgres): chat history slows under concurrent reads
prs.body:
Related: #188956, #190001 (this PR removes the worker queueing in front of `chat.history` on PostgreSQL, a measured part of the #188956 latency; #190001 removes the repeated read snapshots inside each history page)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on PostgreSQL, `chat.history` requests queue behind two history workers when several clients load history at once, so tail latency grows with concurrency while the CPU sits mostly idle.

## User Impact

User impact: concurrent `chat.history` on PostgreSQL waits much less for a history worker. Re-measured on current `main` (medians of 8 interleaved runs per build): at 8 concurrent clients p50 drops from 19.6 to 12.02 ms, p99 from 54.31 to 31.76 ms, and throughput rises from 378.1 to 622.95 requests/s; at 32 clients p99 drops from 163.13 to 103.1 ms. Single-client p50 is unchanged; single-client p99 rose from 15.08 to 17.07 ms over all runs (14.87 to 15.13 ms in the quieter block). SQLite keeps its current lane size.

Cost, measured on the same runs (medians of 8 runs per build):

- Memory: during concurrent history reads the Gateway runs up to two more transcript isolates (about 57 MiB of heap each). Peak transcript-worker heap rose from 334.1 to 453.6 MiB and peak Gateway RSS from 2,764.9 to 3,153.1 MiB. The extra isolates retire after the pool's existing idle timeout: 45 s and 100 s after load both builds ran the same number of transcript isolates with about the same heap (45 s: 229.4 vs 242.8 MiB; 100 s: 223.8 vs 227.8 MiB). RSS at 100 s was 2,106.1 vs 2,324.7 MiB.
- PostgreSQL connections: backends for the runtime role peaked at 23 on base and 25 with the change; both were back to 13 after 100 idle seconds. Each extra history isolate can retain up to two idle transports for three minutes; the documented budget (`isolates × (active + 2)`) now notes up to four history isolates.

**Decision for review:** should PostgreSQL history use up to four workers, accepting the cost above? This revises the two-worker reader cap from #167295 and #169110 for one lane on one engine.

- (a) Accept four workers for PostgreSQL history (this PR). Cost: up to two more isolates (about 120 MiB of worker heap, about 390 MiB of peak RSS) and two more peak backends, only while history load is concurrent; single-client p99 from 15.08 to 17.07 ms over all runs (14.87 to 15.13 ms in the quieter block). On a host whose CPU is already saturated by other work, the extra workers did not help p99 (see Evidence, block 1).
- (b) Keep two workers. PostgreSQL history keeps queueing: 5.57 ms of queue wait per worker request at 8 clients, 13.34 ms at 16.
- (c) Make the larger lane opt-in with a setting. No default cost, but it adds a config surface for an internal pool size, and the default keeps the queueing.
- (d) A cap of eight. Measured on an older `main` (see Evidence): lower queue wait at 16 clients, at about two and a half times the extra memory and with more backends.

Recommended: (a). The extra workers exist only on PostgreSQL agent stores and only under concurrent history reads, they retire through the existing idle timeout and cleanup owners, and SQLite, transcript search and every other lane keep the current cap. The memory bound stays fixed (at most four history isolates on any host), and the latency it buys is the symptom #188956 reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

On PostgreSQL a history worker spends most of a request blocked in `Atomics.wait` on bridge replies, so sizing the lane like a CPU-bound reader leaves requests queued while CPU is free. The history lane on PostgreSQL agent stores now gets two workers per CPU above one, capped at four (two on a two-CPU host). Transcript search, the other transcript lanes, and every SQLite lane keep the existing reader size from #167295 and #169110. No new setting.

The database engine is installed during boot, after the lane module is imported, so the history pool now resolves its size on first use instead of at import. Production code: +48/-9 lines ignoring whitespace (the pool options block is re-indented inside the first-use constructor); tests +117; docs +9/-4.

Scope: this is a partial fix of #188956, so it keeps `Related:` instead of `Closes`. It addresses the queueing in front of the history workers; #190001 cuts the transaction round trips inside each page. The two touch different files and are measured separately. Whichever of this and #190001 lands second switches to `Closes #188956`.

## Evidence

Evidence files: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/pg-r2-l3d-history-reader-lane-evidence/current-main-2026-11-07 (paths below are relative to it; method, host and store in `README.md`). The earlier bench on `31866655fd6` stays at the root of the same branch.

Acceptance rule: through a running Gateway on PostgreSQL, at 8 or more concurrent clients, queue wait per worker request and p50 drop, throughput rises and p99 at 8 clients drops; single-client latency holds; the memory and backend cost is reported, and the extra isolates retire once history load stops.

- **Tests** on this head merged into current `main` `078033289a3`: a per-engine sizing table (`src/infra/worker-pool-sizing.test.ts`) and a lane test that installs the engine after importing the lane, as boot does (`src/config/sessions/session-history-lane-sizing.test.ts`: PostgreSQL 4, SQLite 2, search 2). Both pass, as do the consumer suites for the transcript lanes, the search worker, reconcile readiness, the chat history worker and worker-pool preparation: 12 files, 161 tests (`tests/unit-head.log`). On `main` the sizing table fails because the resolver does not exist, and the PostgreSQL lane case gets 2 instead of 4 while the SQLite case passes (`tests/unit-base-red.log`). `pnpm check:changed` on the merged head passes every check except two repo-wide audits that fail the same way on plain `main` `078033289a3`: changelog attributions (bot credits in `CHANGELOG/` files) and the dead export scan (`scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts`, `src/process/command-reservation-census.ts`) (`tests/check-changed.log`, `tests/base-changelog-attr.log`, `tests/base-deadcode.log`). CI on this head is green.
- **Closed-loop `chat.history` bench on current `main`**: base `main` `078033289a3` vs this head merged into it, both built with `pnpm build`. A fresh Gateway on PostgreSQL 17.11 per run, seeded through its own RPCs with 200 sessions (170 sessions across 6 agents with 2 to 4,675 messages each, plus 30 imported Claude CLI sessions with tool rows hidden between visible turns). Limit 100, 45 s per arm, 16 runs (8 per build) in two interleaved blocks (base head head base base head head base). No run was dropped. Medians over all 16 runs (`bench/block-all/medians.tsv`; every run in `bench/block-all/arms.tsv`; raw scrapes in `bench/runs/`):

| arm | p50 / p95 / p99 ms | p99 range | requests/s | queue wait per worker request | handler mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 client, base | 6.09 / 10.69 / 15.08 | 12.85 to 51.11 | 156.4 | 0.0 ms | 5.19 ms |
| 1 client, fix | 6.00 / 11.02 / 17.07 | 11.9 to 106.71 | 154.4 | 0.0 ms | 5.27 ms |
| 8 clients, base | 19.6 / 31.82 / 54.31 | 28.99 to 161.47 | 378.1 | 5.57 ms | 19.46 ms |
| 8 clients, fix | 12.02 / 19.64 / 31.76 | 20 to 230.82 | 622.95 | 1.23 ms | 10.1 ms |
| 16 clients, base | 37.66 / 54.15 / 88.16 | 58.52 to 200.55 | 411.8 | 13.34 ms | 37.21 ms |
| 16 clients, fix | 24.6 / 42.92 / 66.77 | 45.72 to 499.74 | 606.65 | 6.73 ms | 23.41 ms |
| 32 clients, base | 71.04 / 96.61 / 163.13 | 90.84 to 421.36 | 431.7 | 28.54 ms | 72.43 ms |
| 32 clients, fix | 48.48 / 84.22 / 103.1 | 66.74 to 578.74 | 634.25 | 17.02 ms | 47.23 ms |

Queue wait is `openclaw_worker_queue_wait_seconds{kind="sessionTranscript"}`; handler mean is `openclaw_gateway_rpc_handler_seconds{method="chat.history"}`. The host is shared, and the wide p99 ranges come from runs under other load, so the two blocks are also reported separately:

- Block 2 (`bench/block-b2/`, started only below a 1-minute load of 12; arms at load 4 to 25): p99 at 1, 8, 16 and 32 clients 14.87 / 30.47 / 68.2 / 115.94 ms base vs 15.13 / 25.1 / 64.69 / 88.53 ms fix; p50 at 8 clients 18.11 vs 11.73 ms, throughput 431.6 vs 651.05 requests/s. At 16 clients p99 is about even while p50 drops from 35.98 to 24.6 ms.
- Block 1 (`bench/block-b1/`, load 6 to 55): p50, throughput and queue wait improve at 8, 16 and 32 clients as above, but p99 does not improve consistently: 69.65 vs 73.11 ms at 8 clients, 147.19 vs 113.72 ms at 16, 198.87 vs 281.24 ms at 32. The worst fix tails are `pg-head-r1` (the highest 1-minute load in the bench, 37 to 55) and `pg-head-r2` (load 25 to 33, started with 25% of host memory free); the other two fix runs in the block have p99 21.7 and 36.16 ms at 8 clients. When the host's CPU is already saturated, extra workers add little.

- **Moved the wrong way**: memory and backends (see User Impact: +120 MiB peak transcript heap, +388 MiB peak RSS, +219 MiB RSS 100 s after load, +2 peak backends); single-client p99 15.08 to 17.07 ms over all runs (14.87 to 15.13 ms in block 2; p50 6.09 to 6.00 ms over all runs, 5.71 to 5.94 ms in block 2; single-client p95 10.69 to 11.02 ms over all runs) and 19.35 to 33.27 ms in block 1 (driven by `pg-head-r2`, single-client p99 106.71 ms); single-client throughput 156.4 to 154.4 requests/s over all runs (163.6 to 155.65 in block 2); and in block 1, under the heaviest host load, p99 at 8 clients 69.65 to 73.11 ms and at 32 clients 198.87 to 281.24 ms. These are part of the decision above.
- **Memory and connections** (`bench/block-all/memory-medians.tsv`, per run in `memory.tsv`): see User Impact. Heap and isolate counts come from the Gateway's worker metrics, sampled by the 30 s diagnostic heartbeat; RSS and backend counts are sampled every 2 s.
- **SQLite**: the lane size is unchanged by construction (the resolver returns the existing reader size for every non-PostgreSQL agent engine; covered by the sizing table and lane test). The earlier bench on `31866655fd6` measured SQLite p50, throughput and transcript isolates unchanged; not re-measured here.
- **Cap of four vs eight** (earlier bench on `31866655fd6`, 3 runs each, `bench/medians.tsv` and `bench/memory-medians.tsv` at the branch root, rows `base-a`, `fix4` and `fix8`): eight gave 0.07 ms queue wait at 8 clients and 1.66 ms at 16, at +325 MiB peak transcript heap, +974 MiB peak RSS and 27 peak backends over `base-a`, against +120 MiB heap, +382 MiB RSS and 25 peak backends for four (`fix4` over `base-a`).

### Gaps

- The bench store is synthetic, written through the Gateway's own RPCs, because `main` does not admit a `pg_restore` of a production store. Its shape follows the production bench in #188956.
- Shared host: the p99 tails in block 1 are dominated by other load (per-arm load in `arms.tsv`). Two fix runs (`pg-head-r2` in block 1, `pg-head-r8` in block 2) started while another job held most host memory; both are kept.
- At 16 clients and above the four-worker lane queues again (6.73 ms per worker request at 16, 17.02 ms at 32). A cap of eight removes most of that at a higher memory cost.
- Memory figures needed one measurement-only line, applied identically to both builds: the diagnostic heartbeat publishes its memory sample every 30 s instead of only after agent activity (`scripts/instrument-*.diff`). Isolate counts and heap cover every transcript lane, not only history, and 30 s sampling can miss the exact peak. RSS was watched for 100 s after load here; the earlier 300 s pair on `31866655fd6` (`bench/runs/pg-*-idle-r1` at the branch root) showed no lasting RSS difference with the same isolate count (1,676 vs 1,745 MiB at 300 s).
- Transcript search on PostgreSQL also blocks on bridge replies and keeps its two-worker cap; not measured here.
- Not benchmarked together with #190001.
