prs.title: fix(talk): stop voice claiming cancelled consult work finished
prs.body:
Closes #189070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime Talk keeps reporting a task as in progress, then as done, after Google Live cancels the `openclaw_agent_consult` call and OpenClaw aborts the run.

## User Impact

After a cancelled consult, the voice model is told the request was interrupted and its outcome is unknown. It stops claiming the work finished and checks what was done before running it again, since steps that ran before the cancellation are not undone.

## Why This Change Was Made

When Google Live sends `toolCallCancellation`, the relay already aborts the consult run (`cancelTalkRealtimeRelayProviderToolCall`). The Android client then submits `aborted` for that call, but the Google provider deliberately drops results for cancelled call IDs (`submitToolResult` early return, added in 5be95ad4bab). The model's last word on the call was "working" or nothing, and it never learns the work stopped.

The relay's `tool.call.cancelled` handler now sends one notice through the existing bridge `sendUserMessage` path, the same path forced consults use for their "checking" and result prompts. It fires only when the relay actually retired an uncompleted call, so replays and cancellations after an accepted result send nothing. The notice says the outcome is unknown rather than that nothing happened: cancellation aborts only the remaining steps, so an earlier file write may already have landed.

<details>
<summary>Why the default model is exposed</summary>

The default `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` gets no async function calling and no `willContinue` interim result (`supportsAsyncFunctionCalling`, `modelSupportsToolResultContinuation`), so the consult is declared blocking. Speech while it is pending is a likely cancellation trigger; the reporter did not confirm the trigger.

</details>

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/talk/relay/cancellation-recovery.test.ts`: 14 passed. With the one `sendUserMessage` line removed, the new notice test fails with "Number of calls: 0"; the control (cancellation after an accepted result sends nothing) passes both ways.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/talk/relay`: all relay tests passed.
- Live run: an isolated QA Gateway with real Google Live (`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`) and a real Gemini agent model. A client speaks generated audio through the same RPCs Android uses (`talk.session.create` on `gateway-relay`, `talk.session.appendAudio`, `talk.client.toolCall`, `talk.session.steer`, `talk.session.submitToolResult`). It asks for a 20-second wait plus a file write, interrupts after about 4 s, then asks for status. Main is `upstream/main`'s `session-create.ts` swapped in with `dist` rebuilt.
  - Google cancelled the running consult in all 13 trials that reached it. Each showed `chat.aborted`, then `toolCallCancelled`, then the dropped `{"error":"aborted"}` submit.
  - Main, 6 cancelled trials: in 1, the voice model claimed success right after the cancellation. It said "the greeting file has now been created in your workspace. Protocol complete!", and no file existed. The other 5 made no such claim.
  - This branch, first notice wording, 3 cancelled trials: none claimed the work finished, and the notice was not spoken over the user.
  - This branch, current wording (`c7299c7b70d`), 4 trials with a real agent and no rate limits: Google cancelled the consult in all 4, and none claimed the cancelled work finished. After the cancellation, the voice said "there isn't an active run" in 3 of 4. In the other trial it started a new consult, which wrote the note, and then it reported the save. The note file was read back from the workspace after each trial: absent in the 2 trials where nothing re-ran, and `hello\n` in the 2 where a new consult wrote it. In every trial the spoken status matched the file.
  - Gaps: the main sample is small because the bug is intermittent and free-tier quota rate-limited some main trials. Those trials were excluded (`reason=rate_limit` in the Gateway log). The notice's delivery to Gemini is not logged, so that is shown by the unit test.

<details>
<summary>Live trial transcript (this branch, current wording: cancel, check, accurate status, readback)</summary>

```
+192.1s talk.toolCall          openclaw_agent_consult  runId=talk-077ff5…
+197.4s user.speaks            "Actually, while you do that, what is two plus two?"
+201.7s chat.aborted           runId=talk-077ff5…
+201.7s talk.toolCallCancelled
+201.8s submitToolResult       {"error":"aborted"}   (dropped by the provider)
+206.3s openclaw_agent_control -> no_active_run
+223.7s assistant              "Oh, dear, there isn't an active run right now to add that to. But, 2 plus 2 is 4! ... are you asking me to look into what happened with that previous request and also save the file?"
+245.8s user                   "Is the note saved now? Did you finish writing proofnote.txt?"
+246.1s talk.toolCall          openclaw_agent_consult  runId=talk-965a70…
+256.5s chat.final             "The previous execution attempt to wait 20 seconds was interrupted before completing or writing to disk. Upon checking the workspace, proofnote.txt did not initially exist. proofnote.txt has now been created ..."
+261.1s assistant              "...the previous attempt to save that file was interrupted. However, I have now verified that proofnote.txt has been created and it contains the word "hello". So, yes, it is saved now!"
+262.0s readback               workspace/proofnote.txt = "hello\n"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Live trial transcript (main, the false-completion trial)</summary>

```
+66.3s talk.toolCall          openclaw_agent_consult
+66.5s toolCall.ack           runId=talk-c684…
+70.6s user.speaks            "Actually, while you do that, what is two plus two?"
+71.9s chat.aborted           runId=talk-c684…
+71.9s talk.toolCallCancelled
+72.0s submitToolResult       {"error":"aborted"}   (dropped by the provider)
+81.0s assistant              "...2 + 2 is 4. And one moment... the greeting file has now been created in your workspace. Protocol complete!"
+129.4s artifact              no note file in the workspace
```

</details>

Production delta +8/-0; test delta +38/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is relay Talk sessions whose provider emits `tool.call.cancelled` (Google Live today).

prs.title: fix: keep repository mentions out of file links
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repository mentions such as `openclaw/openclaw.ai` becoming workspace-file links in chat, which hides the owner portion and shows a misleading file preview affordance.

## User Impact

Repository mentions remain intact in prose and inline code. Familiar paths such as `src/index.ts` still open files; explicit paths such as `./assets/logo.ai` and authored Markdown links retain support for uncommon extensions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing file-extension allowlist for inferred, unprefixed paths at the shared Markdown file-link parser. Both prose and code-span consumers receive the same policy without adding filesystem lookups or repository-specific exceptions. Explicit prefixes and authored links keep their existing handling.

The heuristic is intentionally conservative, not a repository detector: a repository name ending in an allowlisted extension can still be inferred as a file. Uncommon-extension files remain addressable with `./`, another explicit path prefix, or an authored link.

Simplification: one existing parser and allowlist own the decision; no new state, services, or dependencies. Production delta: +14/-3 lines; tests: +17 lines; docs: +4/-1 lines.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced through the production Markdown renderer on the base: the repository mention became file links in prose and inline code. It passes with the fix.
- Initial implementation: `pnpm --dir ui test src/components/markdown` passed **572 tests across 29 files**.
- Final test-only consolidation reuses the existing parameterized table, retains all cases and assertions, and passes **46/46 file-link tests**, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. The local test-line ratchet passes with 104 lines of slack. Fresh PR CI is required for this head.
- [Before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194739#issuecomment-6711441727), captured with the unchanged production Markdown renderer and chat styles, show preserved repository text and working ordinary/explicit file links.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and scoped UI test-graph typecheck passed for the production change.
- Local autoreview and a separate fresh P0–P2 review found no actionable issues in the production change.

Scope: isolated renderer/browser proof, not a live Gateway E2E run. Landing requested; waiting for the final head's required CI gates.

prs.title: fix(codex): serialize native completion handoffs and accept yielded input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native subagent completions can collide on the parent thread or report failed delivery when a successful parent consumes the result and yields again.

## User Impact

Completion handoffs to the same parent run one at a time and wait while a sibling still owns native execution. A successful optional native handoff that yields again is acknowledged without requiring an immediate visible answer; visible-reply requirements, errors, and aborts remain failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Serialize the existing delivery attempts per physical parent and defer admission while a live child retains the native subscription. Keep retry and custody checks at their existing owners. When the last live sibling settles, immediately wake only handoffs that were waiting for a sibling; ordinary transport failure backoff is preserved. The direct-response classifier recognizes the narrow native completion family’s successful yielded input separately from delivery of a user-visible final answer.

## Evidence

- Separate regressions fail on the base for early admission while a sibling is running, concurrent terminal-child handoffs, and rejection of a successfully consumed native yielded input.
- 36 focused tests pass across completion contention, monitor delivery, parent retention, and direct-response classification, including all six native-follow-up custody scenarios and both deferred handoffs before advancing the retry clock. Negative cases cover another completion family, a required visible reply, aborted input, and an error.
- Core and Codex production and test TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, pre-commit hooks, and a justified test-line allocation pass. Independent scoped local review found no actionable P0–P2 defects; the root additionally inspected the full response classifier and retry/custody paths.

prs.title: test(perf): cover mobile viewports in rich boot comparisons
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The rich-boot benchmark could only measure a desktop viewport, leaving mobile warm reloads outside the same reproducible comparison.

## User Impact

No production UI change. The benchmark now accepts `--viewport desktop|mobile`, retains the 1440×1100 desktop default, and records the selected viewport. Mobile uses 390×844 with touch/mobile emulation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-up to #194740: investigate its previously reported warm localhost p95 increases (+10.42% Chromium, +17.57% WebKit). The fresh comparison does not reproduce those large tails, so this PR preserves the existing production loading behavior and update-cache win. No changes to #194730, security/build identity, budgets, or startup outputs.

## Evidence

Exact #194740 merge `80938071c75145b6e61a614f3d6c9c0974fdcb19` versus immediate parent `636fc28d8bbd11a3ba91569b2bb250339fa21a45`; fresh canonical builds with matching build metadata except source commit identity. Twenty rotated base/control/head triplets per cell, 480 warm reloads. Control uses the identical base bundle. Each sample primes a real `/new` page, settles for 3 seconds, then reloads that same page. HTTP cache enabled; service worker blocked. Headless Chromium/WebKit. Readiness is browser-local enabled composer plus fonts, not driver wall time or paint. The 100 ms profile is server-response delay, an RTT approximation without bandwidth or WebSocket delay.

| View | RTT | Engine | Base median / p95 ms | Head median / p95 ms | Head Δ median / p95 | A/A Δ median / p95 | A/A paired absolute p95 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| desktop | 0 | chromium | 131.15 / 135.90 | 131.35 / 140.00 | +0.15% / +3.02% | -2.17% / +5.59% | 11.16% |
| desktop | 0 | webkit | 198.00 / 206.00 | 195.00 / 208.00 | -1.52% / +0.97% | -1.52% / +3.40% | 8.06% |
| desktop | 100 | chromium | 232.90 / 238.60 | 229.45 / 232.50 | -1.48% / -2.56% | -0.28% / +0.13% | 3.55% |
| desktop | 100 | webkit | 292.50 / 305.00 | 292.50 / 304.00 | +0.00% / -0.33% | -0.17% / -0.33% | 5.63% |
| mobile | 0 | chromium | 123.55 / 132.90 | 125.10 / 137.80 | +1.25% / +3.69% | +1.54% / +0.45% | 11.48% |
| mobile | 0 | webkit | 191.00 / 205.00 | 189.50 / 199.00 | -0.79% / -2.93% | -2.62% / +5.85% | 14.15% |
| mobile | 100 | chromium | 231.30 / 244.00 | 229.65 / 237.50 | -0.71% / -2.66% | +0.97% / -0.94% | 6.23% |
| mobile | 100 | webkit | 287.50 / 297.00 | 289.00 / 298.00 | +0.52% / +0.34% | +0.52% / +1.35% | 5.24% |

Every cell's median and p95 change is within 5%. A/A paired absolute p95 is the p95 of absolute per-pair percent differences, not a confidence interval. The unchanged desktop-localhost controls included individual +26.58% Chromium / +17.28% WebKit tails. Chromium task-CPU median/p95 deltas: desktop local −0.75%/+1.83%, desktop 100 ms −2.42%/−1.99%, mobile local +2.22%/+0.41%, mobile 100 ms −0.42%/−4.23%. WebKit untraced CPU is unavailable. Host load ranged 7.97–22.32.

All 480 reloads: zero script/style/font requests at the server; zero application errors or recoveries. Native inspection confirms a small real WebKit request-initiation shift for mapped JavaScript, while cache reuse remains intact; this is not a claim of identical waterfalls or zero map cost. 

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | Passed |
| Scoped oxlint | Passed |
| oxfmt, two touched files | Passed |
| Independent local review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Warm comparison | 480/480 completed, all eight cells within 5% |
| Production diff | None; no build/budget or five-pair recensus needed |

LOC: 13 added / 1 removed across the harness and its README. No visual change; screenshots are not applicable. Full retained evidence is in the lane's `.artifacts/warm-tail-1107/`; reports are not committed.

### Direct request/cache/parse mechanism

60 separate diagnostic reloads (48 ordinary, 12 parser-bracket) completed with zero page/CSP errors. All 168 WebKit requests for the seven used map targets report memory cache; all 168 Chromium requests report unspecified browser cache. Chromium’s generic cache event does not establish memory versus disk. No asset/font requests reached the server through usability.

| WebKit profile | Connection native initiation Δ | Shared boot native initiation Δ |
|---|---:|---:|
| Desktop, localhost | +5.58 ms | +8.97 ms |
| Desktop, 100 ms | +5.42 ms | +8.69 ms |
| Mobile, localhost | +4.64 ms | +8.13 ms |
| Mobile, 100 ms | +5.37 ms | +8.70 ms |

The five used mapped JavaScript targets (connection, shared boot, shared styles loader, Solid runtime, English catalog) retain document modulepreloads in both builds. Both CSS targets retain preload-as-style plus stylesheet links. The sixth JavaScript target contains only `src/shared/dedupe-by-key.ts`; it is not requested or preloaded by `/new`.

The small WebKit shift is real native initiation, consistent with omitting HTTP JavaScript Link hints on mapped documents while preserving HTML modulepreloads and HTTP CSS hints. It is not evidence of a lost cache hit or a new network dependency. Chromium’s diagnostic deltas varied from earlier to later; no consistent initiation win is claimed.

In a separate diagnostic-only HTML/CSP variant, marks around map parse/registration measured 0–0.1 ms in Chromium and 0 ms at WebKit’s integer-ms precision (the empty base bracket measured 1 ms once). These include parser/sentinel overhead and do not establish zero parse cost. The first native JavaScript request preceded the bracket end by 2.58–3.01 ms in Chromium, but followed it by 1.59–2.34 ms in WebKit. Thus “map processed before every raw module fetch” is not uniformly true; speculative target fetch is distinct from import-map-dependent module resolution. No resolution/execution ordering claim is inferred from request timestamps.

**Verdict:** the old +10.42%/+17.57% readiness tails do not reproduce and are consistent with A/A host variation. Preserve the small real WebKit initiation cost in the evidence, but do not change production loading without a repeatable readiness regression. Existing five-pair update-cache results, strict budgets, and admission/stale-build boundaries remain unchanged.

### All mapped targets


Range of per-cell head-minus-base medians across the four viewport/delay profiles (three samples per variant/cell); milliseconds, diagnostic only.

| Target | Chromium range | WebKit range |
|---|---:|---:|
| chat-english.js | -4.05 to +3.43 | +6.02 to +6.87 |
| control-ui-boot-shared-styles.css | -4.67 to +1.43 | -2.00 to -1.20 |
| control-ui-boot-shared-styles.js | -4.02 to +3.46 | +8.23 to +9.02 |
| control-ui-boot-shared.js | -4.01 to +3.46 | +8.12 to +8.97 |
| control-ui-connection.css | -4.47 to +1.63 | -1.28 to -0.48 |
| control-ui-connection.js | -3.93 to +3.54 | +4.64 to +5.58 |
| solid-runtime.js | -4.02 to +3.46 | +8.20 to +8.96 |
| shared dedupe-by-key JS | unrequested | unrequested |

The two CSS targets show no consistent head-only initiation delay; all four WebKit CSS cell medians are earlier.

prs.title: improve(gateway): avoid archived scans in active session lists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session lists repeatedly scan archived rows when active sessions change, and archived-only metadata updates invalidate an otherwise unchanged active list.

## User Impact

Retained active and archived list refreshes visit only their requested population. Results, ordering, visibility, and sharing decisions remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Split the existing selection owner's hash partitions by archive membership, with separate revisions. Each row still belongs to one partition. Archive/unarchive moves invalidate both populations; readers consume the owner's membership instead of filtering every row again. Skip hashing keys before the partitions exist during initial selection setup. The overall production line count is unchanged, with no new cache.

## Evidence

Synthetic fixture: 60,000 sessions, 55,000 archived and 5,000 active, across 20 physical stores. The selection owner uses 64 hash buckets per population. Default list parameters, 20 committed row updates per logical second, one list per second. No live deployment data is used.

| 40-list work-count run | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Active timestamp updates: retained misses | 748 | 748 |
| Active timestamp updates: entries visited | 703,493 | 58,839 |
| Entries visited per miss | 940.50 | 78.66 |
| Archived timestamp updates: active retained misses | 799 | 0 |
| Archived timestamp updates: entries visited | 750,054 | 0 |

All per-call normalized response hashes match. Pure token-field updates already preserve partition revisions; timestamp or other selection-fact changes correctly invalidate them.

Five alternating AB/BA pairs plus A/A controls, separate timing and allocation passes, 200 measured lists per arm after 20 warmup lists. Both revisions use the same pinned-source loader. Values below are medians across five arms; changes are the median of paired changes.

| Measure | Before | After | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| List thread CPU/call | 8.433 ms | 5.394 ms | −35.07% |
| List p95 wall latency | 11.698 ms | 7.176 ms | −36.32% |
| Roster-batch attributed allocation/cycle | 634,256 B | 430,867 B | −32.06% |
| Total allocation/20-update-plus-list cycle | 11,356,104 B | 11,182,073 B | −1.53% |

A/A variation: list CPU +3.65%, roster allocation −3.75%, total cycle allocation +0.058%. Active timestamp updates still produce the same required invalidations: 2,924 misses / 12,800 bucket lookups (22.84%) in each 200-list arm. Update CPU is neutral (paired −1.67%, A/A −2.56%). Initial/final response hashes match across timing/allocation arms; the 40-list verification streams additionally hash every response.

First-capture CPU is neutral within the A/A spread (paired +1.44%, A/A −5.77%); one retained cold pair is +16.14% CPU / +34.31% wall time. First capture includes list capture and canonical hashing after projection materialization, not startup. Allocation sampling spans the whole update/list cycle; frame-attributed families overlap and are not additive.

Separate 100-list controls with active updates: archived=true CPU 19.259→2.486 ms/call, misses 1,873→0; archived=all CPU 16.054→3.811 ms/call, with unchanged 1,873 misses and reuse of archived partitions. Initial/final results match. These are single-pair controls, not five-pair headline estimates. Separate 200-list CPU profiles show inclusive `filterSessionEntries` time 615.528→191.202 ms and `selectPage` 721.558→304.247 ms. Archive-predicate self time falls from 17.977 ms to below sampling resolution. Final-head work-count replays confirm the table above and every response hash matches the baseline.

Validation: 48 focused tests passed, including sharing freshness, order, child archive filtering, rematerialization and deletion. The new handler regression fails on the base (four visited rows instead of two) and passes after the fix. Its original 74-line test allocation covers population work counts, viewer isolation and archive moves in one existing fixture. Combined test wrapper wall time was 97.98 seconds on a shared host; the new regression took 286 ms in that run. The 19 directly affected tests passed again after the cold setup follow-up (96.21 seconds including compiler preparation).

`pnpm check:changed` ran. Two instrumentation iterator typing errors were corrected; core/test/script typechecks and lint now pass. Dead-export scans and other guards pass. The remaining failure is 20 historical changelog-credit violations, reproduced on exact parent `a384228dd7b42a3c502c3e82e560d9fb99ddf7a2`, introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364). This is a main regression, not a passing check.

Codex autoreview through P2 found no actionable issues. The cold setup follow-up also passed Codex review; mechanical lint fixes and the final regression replay passed. No UI-imported module changed.

Scope: this measures the resident projection/list owner and real list-handler regression, not transport, filesystem scale, or large-transcript database startup. The synthetic databases total about 237 MiB and have no transcript payload.


## Archived-only profile reference follow-up

`selectSessionEntries` explicitly excludes truthy `involvingProfileId` from incremental partition selection (`src/gateway/session-utils-list.ts:80–87`), on both the main parent and this branch. Such queries keep the full-roster `entries` callback: `filterSessionEntries` reads `entries("all")` before archive filtering, so visible archived rows still contribute profile references and allowed IDs. The partition-local callback is reachable only by `entries(opts.archived)`; no current caller requests a different mode there. Search, catalog, project, and usage consumers retain the original archive-aware callback. No production repair is needed.

Added a 35-line real sessions.list handler regression, with `includePeople` omitted, covering exact/prefix references to visible and hidden archived-only profiles across `archived=false`, `true`, and `all`. It passes on the candidate and with both production owners restored to exact main parent `a384228dd7b42a3c502c3e82e560d9fb99ddf7a2`. Removing only the existing involvement gate makes it fail because the selected profile ID becomes undefined. Those temporary proof changes were restored byte-for-byte. The total test-line allocation is now 109.

Follow-up validation: 41 focused tests passed (47.11 s wrapper; three files); new case took 880 ms in its isolated candidate run. Core-test typecheck shards, targeted lint, formatting, line-budget ratchet, and Codex autoreview through P2 pass. Production code and benchmark workload are byte-identical to measured head `2662711ae37c`; benchmarks were not repeated. Production LOC remains net zero.


## Retained-partition CI repair

The three failures in `session-row-selection.retained.test.ts` were stale test assumptions introduced by this PR, not inherited failures or production defects. Retention sampled a key from empty archived buckets; the streaming assertion required the removed per-entry archive predicate; paging assumed every owner partition had a retained result. The revised tests exercise both populations, check membership and population-only traversal without an eager whole-roster copy, and proxy actual retained pages while preserving pruning, baseline retention, result ordering, and bounded read-work assertions. The earlier focused proof omitted this retained test file; the full comparison below closes that gap.

Production audit confirms archive updates use replacement snapshots, archive membership invalidates selection facts, and moves/deletion retire the previous partition before updating the destination. No production consumer assumes a total of 64 partitions. Production code and the measured hot path are unchanged.

Complete matching inventories: 46 session-row, 31 session-utils, and 15 session-list files, run through the repository wrapper with explicit `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and `bun`. Node v24.22.1; pinned Bun revision `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. Exact parent: `a384228dd7b42a3c502c3e82e560d9fb99ddf7a2`.

| Scope | Parent Node | Candidate Node | Parent Bun | Candidate Bun |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| session-row | 355 | 355 | 355 | 355 |
| session-utils | 303 | 303 | 303 | 303 |
| session-list | 48 | 50 | 48 | 50 |

All entries are passing tests. Each runtime also has the same two existing opt-in benchmark skips; no new skips or failures. The candidate's two extra tests are the handler regressions added earlier in this PR. Every selected file was observed in the logs, and parent/candidate inventories match. Initial isolated-baseline dependency setup failures were repaired without source changes and are excluded from test verdicts. Candidate wrapper times: Node 108.87/99.35/33.77 s and Bun 165.04/109.07/53.38 s for row/utils/list.

Codex autoreview through P2 is clean; gateway test typecheck, targeted lint, format, and line-budget checks pass. After lint-only binding-name cleanup, the affected seven-test file was replayed under both runtimes. Follow-up production delta: 0. Test delta: +42/−25 (net +17); total test-line allocation 126. Benchmarks remain valid because production and workload code are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported). The consolidated table preserves all 10 independent scenarios, including snapshot precedence, reset boundaries, retained-user-only windows and the structural anchor.
- Runtime proof on a real compacted session (regenerated after the earlier /tmp artifact expired): isolated Gateway plus embedded agent against the scripted provider; a real injected 400 `context_length_exceeded`, one committed auto-compaction, then one more turn. The committed marker carries a 464-char summary and names a retained 91-char user message as `firstKeptEntryId`, so the boundary leaves a summary-plus-retained-user window. The artifact is the session's real settled transcript events serialized back to legacy JSONL, with redacted variants that drop usage fields and the model-snapshot entry so the chars estimate is what gets measured. The after-fix reader reports `totalTokens: 139` on the redacted prefix ending at the boundary (ceil((464 + 91) / 4), the summary plus the retained user text) and `176` on the full redacted artifact (ceil((464 + 91 + 56 + 90) / 4), adding the post-boundary assistant and user text). On the usage-carrying artifact the reader still reports the real provider aggregates (input 105 / output 25, latest context snapshot 120 total and available), so the estimate path and the snapshot path stay separate.
- Current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, including upstream main `3f2e7078de23`: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-derived-readers.usage.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.transcript-usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 4 files and 50 tests. oxfmt and direct type-aware oxlint pass on the consolidated test; the net PR diff passes `git diff --check`.
- Shipped diagnostic builder proof on `591ef68b2e9`: the real settled Gateway compaction events drive the production `buildReplyDiagnosticsPayload` raw diagnostic path through `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptAsync`, not just a direct reader call. With usage fields removed, the boundary-terminal artifact emits `total=139` and the full artifact emits `total=176`. The measured control emits `input=105`, `output=25`, `cacheRead=0`, `cacheWrite=0`, `total=120`. The probe prints only the session usage block, with no transcript text, credentials or endpoints. This builder-level evidence does not satisfy Revision 17's separate shipped CLI/Gateway diagnostic request gate; that proof requirement remains open.
- Test budget: the four repeated retained-window fixtures now share one table helper, preserving all 10 scenarios while reducing the new test file from 157 to 145 lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-usage-active-window.txt` grants exactly those 145 added lines. The full-index ratchet on current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, using hosted CI's current main `3f2e7078de23` with `--no-merge-base`, reports `Test lines OK: 6561328; ceiling: 6561328; slack: 0.` An earlier sparse local run omitted 566 tracked test lines and produced a false slack result; materializing those files reproduced hosted CI's over-10 failure before this consolidation.

prs.title: fix: Android chat inputs do not capitalize sentence starts
prs.body:
Closes #194320

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native Android app's chat composer ignores Gboard's sentence auto-capitalization, so messages start lowercase even when the user has auto-capitalization enabled — unlike Signal/Telegram/WhatsApp and unlike the web Control UI.

## User Impact

Android users get automatic sentence-start capitalization in the chat composer and in the question free-text answer field, matching every mainstream messaging app. No behavior change for other fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both prose inputs set no `keyboardOptions` (or `KeyboardOptions.Default`), and Compose's default is `capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Unspecified` — the IME receives no `textCapSentences` hint, so Gboard never capitalizes. This adds `KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences)` to the two chat prose inputs. Intentionally untouched: the emoji custom-reaction field (capitalization would be noise), secret/URI question fields (already set deliberately), and the model-picker search box (not prose). Attribute-only change, no logic touched.

## Evidence

- Before recording + frame from the issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/194320#issuecomment (Gboard auto-capitalization ON; typing `why don't you auto capitalize?!` stays all-lowercase in the shipped 2026.10.90 app).
- Root cause verified against androidx source: `KeyboardOptions` default `capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Unspecified` (compose/foundation `KeyboardOptions.kt`).
- Maintainer verification: reproduced on native Android with Gboard and verified both fields on the unchanged PR head. Disabling auto-capitalization, existing lowercase drafts and the password field retain their behavior. Both builds and five existing focused tests passed. [Complete before/after recordings, controls and source revisions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194321#issuecomment-6702781219).

prs.title: fix(oc-path): preserve code examples when editing Markdown fields
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`path set` can overwrite a Markdown code example while leaving the resolved field unchanged. This happens when a list item's field paragraph follows a fenced code block containing the same key.

## User Impact

Editing the field now updates the paragraph returned by `path resolve`, preserving the preceding code block and neighboring items. A table-cell field without a source location is rejected as `not-writable` instead of guessing where to write.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser selected the field paragraph, but the editor searched from the list marker. Track the selected paragraph's source line and use it for replacement bounds. Existing edit/insertion logic keeps that position current; reported list-item line numbers remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Built clean base `10592dacdc6e` and final commit `b13c230efbfd` with `pnpm build qaRuntime`. Tested through the normal `pnpm openclaw` CLI on Windows with Node 24.22.1 and isolated configuration, using this file:

````md
## Tools
- ```
  name: decoy
  ```

  name: actual
- keep: unchanged
````

Commands (each with `--json --file <fixture>`):

```sh
pnpm openclaw path resolve 'oc://notes.md/tools/#0/name'
pnpm openclaw path set 'oc://notes.md/tools/#0/name' updated --dry-run
pnpm openclaw path set 'oc://notes.md/tools/#0/name' updated
pnpm openclaw path resolve 'oc://notes.md/tools/#0/name'
```

- Before: resolve returned `actual`; preview/write changed `decoy` to `updated`; resolve still returned `actual`.
- After: preview/write changed `actual` to `updated`, kept `decoy` and the neighboring item intact, and resolve returned `updated`. Dry-run left the file unchanged. A second CLI fixture verified CRLF preservation and a code block without a matching key. An unmapped table-cell write returned `not-writable` without changing bytes.
- Regression: `pnpm test extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/tests/edit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` had two failures on the old implementation; all 24 tests pass after the fix in 3.71 seconds wall time. CI seconds are pending. The chained-edit case also checks frontmatter shifts, multiline values, and insertion. The affected plugin suite passes 482 tests with 5 skipped; the required `pnpm test:extension oc-path --maxWorkers=1` lane also passes.
- Targeted production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and the test-line ratchet pass. Test source shrinks by two lines while retaining existing assertions. Independent P0–P3 local review completed with no findings; final file hashes match the reviewed snapshot. PR CI is pending.

prs.title: fix(plugins): follow the stable channel for official plugin selectors
prs.body:
Fixes #194804

## What Problem This Solves

After core moves from beta to stable, saved official-plugin `@beta` selectors can keep resolving the beta line and downgrade a matching stable plugin to an older compatible beta.

## User Impact

Trusted official plugins with saved prerelease channel tags now follow the effective stable channel. Updates prefer the core-matching release, use `latest` when that release is unavailable, and save `latest` with a warning after success. The saved selector keeps core preference and the stable version floor on every subsequent stable update. If no compatible stable replacement meets the core release floor, the installed plugin and selector are retained with a warning.

This channel-tag recovery preserves exact-version and range selector handling, third-party plugins, explicit command selectors, and the beta update channel. Existing managed release-pin recovery still applies. Historical records do not distinguish automatically saved channel tags from authored tags, so both follow the documented stable policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the channel decision in the shared npm/ClawHub update selector owner and enforce the stable floor on the staged artifact before publication, including compatibility fallback. The existing install transaction retains the old payload on refusal. The updater performing plugin convergence must contain this fix; it needs no new config option, schema, or update protocol.

## Evidence

- Production updater and npm installer regression fixtures fail five cases on `a384228dd7b4`, including an install-record downgrade from `2026.11.1` to `2026.10.10-beta.5`.
- Independent follow-up review found that normalized ClawHub `@latest` lost its policy on the second update. Both new two-pass regressions fail at `71924279b576` and pass with this repair: a published core target remains preferred, and a missing second core target cannot admit stale `latest` below core.
- `update.test.ts`, `install-channel-specs.test.ts`, `install.npm-spec.test.ts`, and `plugin-version-drift.test.ts`: **210 passed**, 70.81 seconds command wall time. The ClawHub regression exercises the real update owner and staged version callback with a fixture installer that publishes the on-disk package only after the callback accepts it. ClawHub installation is simulated.
- Touched-file lint and compiler diagnostics via `run-oxlint.mjs --type-check`, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) of the complete repair against `71924279b576`: **scoped clean**, no actionable findings. Hosted ClawSweeper previously acknowledged intake.
- The PR's isolated allocation is **257 lines**: the original 195 plus 62 for repeated-update alignment and fallback-floor regressions.
- **MISSING:** live registry/CLI and latest-stable upgrade proof. The earlier configured Crabbox/Testbox attempt queued and its task-owned lease was stopped; no remote proof command executed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42415155437)). PR CI supplies broad validation.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

prs.title: fix(config): stop auto-restoring hand-authored configs missing meta (#126806)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #126806.

A valid, schema-passing `openclaw.json` that an operator wrote by hand (or deployed via dotfiles/Ansible/Nix) — one without a `meta` block — was silently replaced by the previous `openclaw.json.bak` generation the next time any command loaded config, including read-only ones like `openclaw models list`. The operator's `update.channel` value and agent roster were dropped into a `openclaw.json.clobbered.<ts>` sidecar behind a single log line: recoverable, but not obvious.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadConfig` runs suspicious-read recovery *after* validation succeeds, so the restore only ever applies to configs that validate cleanly. `missing-meta-vs-last-good` was on the recoverable-reason list, and OpenClaw's own writer always stamps `meta.lastTouchedVersion` — so a valid config lacking `meta` was, by construction, hand-authored, the exact file a silent revert hurts most. The write path already treats the identical signal as benign (`missing-meta-before-write` is only logged; `resolveConfigWriteBlockingReasons` does not block), so the read path was stricter than the write path and reverted on it.

The fix removes `missing-meta-vs-last-good` from `isRecoverableConfigReadSuspiciousReason` (`src/config/io.observe-recovery.ts`). A valid config is now left untouched on read; the independent observe path (`observeConfigSnapshot`) still records the anomaly as a warning (`Config observe anomaly: … (missing-meta-vs-last-good)`) — the "at most, a warning" the issue asks for. `gateway-mode-missing-vs-last-good` and `update-channel-only-root` stay recoverable because they describe genuinely clobbered shapes.

Two follow-up commits close the residual windows that first fix left open:

- `9637d635e2b` — once a metadata-free config has been *accepted* and recorded as the last-known-good baseline, a later suspicious read could still auto-restore an older `.bak` generation over the operator's accepted file. The recovery source-eligibility check refuses a `.bak` whose bytes differ from a hand-authored accepted baseline, so a revert to *older* bytes is blocked while a `.bak` holding the accepted bytes itself still restores.
- `40bf9d02050` — that skip still left a *recognized valid clobber* active when Gateway had promoted the accepted bytes to `${configPath}.last-good`. The read recovery path now prefers that retained payload, accepting it only when its bytes hash to the recorded accepted-baseline hash (`prepareLastGoodRecoverySource`); a recognized clobber is then repaired from the operator's own accepted config instead of staying active. When no hash-verified copy exists (no `.last-good`, or its bytes diverged), the skip remains fail-closed with an explicit unavailable-baseline warning (`Config auto-restore from backup skipped: … accepted baseline is hand-authored and no verified last-good copy exists`) — divergent bytes are never restored. The last-known-good promote/recover owner moves to its own module (`src/config/io.last-known-good.ts`) so the read path stays under the file-size budget.
- `634bab43c8e` (`40fac9dcfc3` adds docs only) — closes the two findings from that review. **Acceptance bookkeeping (P1):** both observers (`observeConfigSnapshot`/`observeConfigSnapshotSync`) advanced `lastKnownGood` only on completely clean reads, so the *accepted* warning-only read itself — the hand-authored edit — left the stale product-written fingerprint in place; a later recognized clobber then compared against that stale baseline, bypassed the hand-authored guard, and restored the pre-edit `.bak` over the live settings. A valid read whose anomalies are not recoverable now advances the baseline while the warning stays, with the recoverable/acceptance predicates owned in one place (`isAcceptedConfigRead` in `src/config/io.observe-suspicious.ts`). **Source selection before backup preparation (P2):** the `.last-good` branch sat behind `.bak` read/parse/prepare/`gateway.mode` checks, so a missing, unparsable, rejected, or gateway-mode-less `.bak` short-circuited recovery before the verified promoted payload was ever consulted. Selection now needs only the retained baseline's hash and runs before any source-specific preparation; `.bak` preparation runs only when `.bak` is the selected source.

## User Impact

Operators who hand-author or config-manage a valid `openclaw.json` without a `meta` block no longer have it silently reverted to an older `.bak` generation by a read-only command — neither on the metadata-only read itself, nor later when a clobbered shape arrives (Scenario F). The accepted read itself becomes the recorded baseline, so later recovery compares against the operator's bytes rather than the pre-edit generation. When Gateway has promoted their accepted config, a later recognized clobber is repaired from that exact accepted payload even when the `.bak` is missing, unreadable, or rejected (Scenario D); otherwise the clobber is left in place with an explicit warning instead of being silently reverted or silently ignored (Scenarios C/E). Configs that genuinely lost their `gateway.mode` or collapsed to an `update.channel`-only root are still auto-restored as before whenever the accepted baseline is a product-written config (Scenario B).

## Evidence

## risks
- **Removed recovery fallback for `missing-meta-vs-last-good`**: configs that previously auto-restored on missing-meta alone no longer do. This is the intended fix — those were almost exclusively hand-authored valid files; a genuine clobber that lost *only* `meta` while keeping every other field valid is near-impossible (corruption truncates/damages, it does not surgically strip `meta`), and even then the file still validates and is left flagged. The observe path still records the anomaly; `.bak`/`.clobbered` backups remain for manual restore.
- **Skip is fail-closed only when no verified copy exists**: with a recognized clobber and a metadata-free accepted baseline whose `.bak` differs, recovery now repairs from the hash-verified `.last-good` payload (Scenario D). Only when that payload is missing or diverged does the read leave the recognized clobber active with the explicit unavailable-baseline warning — the operator compares against the retained `.bak`/`.last-good`/`.clobbered` artifacts and restores manually, or rewrites the file. This trades one automatic repair for never restoring unverified bytes; the skip warns with the exact reason and the observe anomaly is still audited.
- **`.last-good` payload trust is hash-scoped**: the promoted payload is accepted only when its bytes hash to the recorded accepted-baseline fingerprint hash; a diverged `.last-good` (partial write, operator edit, tampering) is never restored (Scenario E). The fingerprint itself is Gateway-promoted state in the shared SQLite health store, so the trust boundary matches the existing last-known-good promotion contract rather than widening it.
- **`size-drop-vs-last-good` sibling**: the issue traces the same read-stricter-than-write asymmetry for size drops but did not reproduce it; the write side blocks `size-drop:` unless `allowConfigSizeDrop` is set, so it is a weaker case. Intentionally out of scope here — flagged for a separate change with its own reproduction.

## bestSolution
Removing `missing-meta-vs-last-good` from the recoverable-reason list at its owner (`isRecoverableConfigReadSuspiciousReason`), plus source eligibility that prefers the hash-verified promoted `.last-good` payload and otherwise fails closed with an explicit warning, is the canonical fix set: the observe path provides the warning, recognized clobbers are repaired from the operator's own accepted bytes whenever a verified copy exists, and recovery for the unverifiable state stays explicit instead of silently reverting or silently ignoring.






## Main rebase (head 718ae1765c4)

Resolved the merge conflicts flagged in the review against current main (which now includes the config deslop in #157146):

- `src/config/io.observe-suspicious.ts`: main's deslop removed `isRecoverableConfigReadSuspiciousReason` and made any suspicious reason trigger recovery (`suspicious.length === 0`). The merge restores this branch's policy — `missing-meta-vs-last-good` is excluded from auto-restore and drives the accepted-baseline advance instead — because reverting a valid hand-authored config is exactly the bug this PR fixes.
- `src/config/io.observe.ts`: kept the `isAcceptedConfigRead` import alongside main's move of `NormalizedConfigIoDeps` to `io.read.types.js`.
- `src/config/io.observe-recovery-effects.ts` / `io.last-good-recovery-source.ts`: follow main's `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` and `io.read.types.js` import locations.

Verified on the merged head: `tsgo` clean; the recovery suites (`io.observe-recovery.test.ts`, `io.observe-recovery.accepted-baseline.test.ts`, `io.health-state.test.ts`, `io.load-env-restore.test.ts`, `io.observe-freshness.test.ts`) — 109/109 pass. The remaining before-merge items are the maintainer decisions on the accepted-baseline fallback behavior, which the Scenario G / real-CLI evidence above documents.

prs.title: fix(codex): avoid replaying consumed native results after cold resume
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A resumed native Codex parent can consume child results without emitting raw receipt notifications. Retiring that parent then loses the receipt owner and can admit the same completion again. Codex's resume listener explicitly disables raw events ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L4372)).

## User Impact

Cold-resumed parents can recognize a child result they already consumed, avoiding duplicate completion handoffs when native raw receipts are absent. Missing or ambiguous proof preserves normal completion delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before releasing a settled parent's existing custody, reconcile exact consumption facts from its canonical local rollout. A typed child-completion intent identifies the child turn; only a later consumed native `agent_message` with the exact owned parent turn, trusted alias and immutable result can acknowledge it. Complete child history must also prove that every other turn has a distinct known result. Intent alone, identical outputs and incomplete history preserve normal delivery.

The entire observation has one hard **30-second total** deadline covering lifecycle checks, RPCs and filesystem reads. It retains observation custody, grants no execution authority, and rechecks lifecycle/source/runtime/candidate ownership before acknowledgement. Timeout, cancellation, revocation and late async resolution fail closed. Remote transports and unsafe or unproven files retain normal delivery.

## Evidence

Validation on parent `eb4ebb59f` (receipt-ingress/alias fix) and head `73de4409e`:

- Actual monitor regression: with raw receipt events omitted, the base admits a consumed child result again; the fix does not.
- Monitor negatives cover intent-only history, duplicate child output, remote transport, yielded parent, revoked lifecycle and source, and total-budget timeout with late resolution.
- Registration guard regression proves closed execution remains closed while bounded observation retains only current lifecycle/connection checks.
- Canonical-reader cases cover wrong owner/turn/child/path, missing or ambiguous facts, complete-LF boundaries, invalid UTF-8, bounded tail windows, hardlinks, symlinks and path escapes; complete child-history cases cover ambiguous earlier and later turns.
- **74 focused monitor/receipt/input-scope tests passed**, as did production extension and extension test typechecks, formatting, lint and commit checks. Independent Codex source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the reviewer did not execute project code. Final guard-call/type refinements were checked by typechecks, focused tests and author review.

These are deterministic source-level checks using synthetic native records and notifications. They do not establish live-model or production acceptance for this source revision. Previously deployed runtime validation is separate evidence and is not presented as proof for this port.

Depends on #194748 (receipt ingress and trusted aliases). The additional source is necessary for canonical same-descriptor provenance, a complete bounded snapshot, exact child-history uniqueness and lifecycle-safe retirement; the existing generic live-receipt ambiguity rules remain unchanged. Existing receiver eligibility and registration execution guards are extracted unchanged to keep their original files within the source line-growth gates.

## What Problem This Solves

Preserve the actual, safe startup-failure explanation in desktop chat instead of replacing it with a generic error. Keep it concise: the failure statement only, without appended operator/recovery/retry advice or the generic “Check any completed work before trying again” banner.

## User Impact and Scope

- **Web Control UI and macOS:** show the first failure statement, including after reload. For example: “OpenClaw's storage worker ran out of memory.”
- **Channels, iOS, and Android:** existing shared message text and delivery behavior stay unchanged, including when a phone opens the same conversation.
- Unknown errors remain generic. No changes to permissions, retries, model selection, database behavior, or message delivery.

## Implementation

Capture explicitly public failure copy before startup errors are flattened, then carry its first sentence as desktop presentation metadata rather than replacing shared transcript content. Web consumers explicitly opt in; native decoding and rendering are gated with `#if os(macOS)`. Native preflight desktop copy remains separate from the default channel-facing renderer. The global storage-error wording remains unchanged. The Web UI no longer adds a blanket completed-work warning.

## Evidence

- After consolidating duplicate test scaffolding, 40 native-harness tests, 9 reader/preflight-helper tests, and 6 public `chat.send` startup tests passed locally. The unchanged dispatch coverage previously passed 23 tests. The concise-copy correction was initially red on three Gateway cases and two UI assertions.
- 46 UI tests and 3 browser E2E tests passed on the unchanged product code. Core, Web UI, and affected test-graph typechecks passed, including the corrected reader callback in the QA product proof. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The QA product proof itself was not replayed for its callback-only change.
- Earlier unchanged-layer proof: 14 history-paging tests, 118 display/lifecycle tests, and 9 failure-recorder tests passed.
- The wording and test-consolidation changes were reviewed directly, without subagents. Earlier full-branch independent review and committed-delta autoreview found no actionable issues; those reports precede these updates.
- **Scoped test allocation:** `config/test-lines-allocations/194741-desktop-startup-errors.txt` allocates the exact 317 net new test lines after removing 51 lines of duplicate scaffolding. These regressions are needed to distinguish desktop-only display from shared/mobile content, preserve startup causes across persistence, exercise native consent/binding guards, reject malformed metadata, and verify concise rendering/reload. The shared baseline is unchanged; the allocation follows the documented per-change mechanism and does not suppress a test or product failure.
- **Native verification limit:** this Linux host has no Swift toolchain or connected Mac. Native runtime tests and macOS visual execution are not claimed. Landing is now requested; required CI is being checked on the current head.
- Gateway proof injects preparation failures before model execution. Browser proof uses synthetic history and checks reload behavior; neither is a live replay of the production incident.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The window-resize benchmark claimed to retain session Details, but its `data-panel-slot="detail"` assertion only checked the Review panel. That left the actual Details inspector out of resize coverage.

## User Impact

Benchmark-only change; application behavior and styles are unchanged. Resize measurements can now distinguish Review from an explicitly opened session Details inspector.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing scenario ID, fixture and viewport trajectory for comparable results, and label its Review coverage correctly. Add `gesture-window-resize-details-{realistic,large}` using that same gesture, open Details before timing, and assert it remains open afterward alongside both split panes and Review.

The performance experiments from this investigation are excluded: none met the complete frame acceptance criteria. This PR makes no application speedup claim.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Exploratory large-fixture listener comparison: both window states, Chromium/WebKit/Firefox, baseline/candidate/A/A | 180/180 observations passed; zero ResizeObserver-loop errors; runtime candidate removed |
| Final benchmark scenario: realistic fixture and Chromium 4× coverage | 5/5 passed: realistic in all three engines, realistic/large at Chromium 4×; zero observer-loop errors |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | Passed |
| Scoped format and lint | Passed |
| `pnpm deadcode:knip` (production) | Passed |
| Independent autoreview, P0–P2, base `055544b9fa3` → staged candidate | Clean; no actionable findings (complete staged scope) |
| Startup | No UI build inputs changed; frozen base is 90,900 B gzip JS and one startup CSS request; no ceiling changed |
| LOC | Gesture scenarios 507 → 525; scripts README 1,065 → 1,068; production UI unchanged |

The observations use headless browsers and synthetic 100/2,000-message fixtures. Each window gesture makes 90 paced viewport updates; actual delivery cadence is recorded. Viewport calls serialize for driver correctness. Callback intervals are not display presentation timestamps or CPU time.

Before: the existing workload retains Review.

![Existing resize workload with Review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c630eedc-ae8e-43d3-acbb-f97292fc5905)

After: the added workload also opens the session Details inspector.

![Added resize workload with session Details open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8e0e992-eef7-4c11-8760-8c85af4eb1fa)

<details>
<summary>Why the runtime candidates were not included</summary>

A traced window-resize frame contained eight style passes and six layouts. Details width writes were followed by another instance's bounds read, then pane viewport writes/native clamp reads and column-width/end-anchor reads. Narrowing the inherited Details width reduced restyled elements, but the completed 20-triplet WebKit sidebar comparison regressed median frame interval by 61.35% against flat paired A/A and increased the >33 ms fraction by 3.095 percentage points, despite a lower p95. It was rejected.

Deleting only the duplicate window listener changed paired p95 by less than 1% across all six 10-triplet window cells. Deferring sidebar scroll publication left Chromium 4× wheel p95 at 50.1 ms. Those changes were also removed. A larger native-read candidate exceeded the unchanged Chat byte allowance. The remaining resize problem is explicitly unresolved.

</details>

prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an extra parent completion delivery when Codex already consumed a child result but the receipt races projection settlement or validated child restoration.

## User Impact

Parents keep the existing consumed-result acknowledgement across delayed projection writes and restoration of a known native child. The normal parent, turn, child and custody checks remain authoritative; raw author names do not create aliases.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the native current-turn consumption fact before awaiting projection writes. During validated reconstruction, replay only aliases already retained for that exact native parent and child through the existing live-alias conflict guard. The existing child reconstruction operation moves to a sibling module to keep the monitor within its line-growth limit; it remains one operation with the same caller.

## Evidence

Base: `2e13c52c97bbe81228c4f45212c8ca8cd346dbf9`. Head: `2c5461e4baf09476f5b539f479ad9471e54bd8b4`.

- A deterministic monitor regression delays projection settlement and retires the parent. The base issues one extra synthetic completion delivery; the fix issues none.
- A separate monitor regression prunes and restores the same child under its trusted path. It fails with one extra delivery before the alias repair and passes after it. This case was reproduced with the ingress repair already present, so it tests the distinct restoration defect.
- **26 tests passed** across the monitor completion-delivery and delivery-receipt suites on Node 24.22.1:

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve the parent tool catalog during completion delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A native child releases the parent's execution pin when its final turn settles, before its result has finished delivery. The detached completion then rebuilds the parent's dynamic tool catalog. Without a live pin it loses the original declarations, which can rotate the native thread or prevent the completion from being delivered.

## User Impact

Completed native subagents can deliver their result on the original parent thread after the execution pin has been released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the original catalog available only to the exact in-flight completion owner. The existing monitor verifies the physical parent/client, requester, child source, announcement, active delivery attempt, and current completion custody. Recheck that custody after the awaited metadata read and under the existing binding authority before consuming the fingerprinted catalog. Do not keep the execution pin or change the current executor/permission checks. The existing settled-child retention loop moves to its parent owner so the monitor can delegate without growing its oversized module.

This ports the completion-catalog portion of #188698 to current main. It depends on #194748 (the native completion receipt custody change); it does not include the broader stable-release continuation/schema compatibility patch.

## Evidence

- The new catalog regression fails on the base: a completed child's unprotected catalog resolves to `undefined`. With the fix, the original catalog is restored; a revoked read, changed runtime, ordinary turn, and missing custody remain rejected or unavailable.
- Catalog tests: 14 passed. SQLite-backed native completion contention tests: 7 passed, including actual pin release, exact/wrong request lookup, receipt handoff, retirement, and captured-custody invalidation.
- Two composed native-dispatch regressions recover declarations from the real native metadata file during actual completion custody, then invoke the native bridge. A missing current executor is denied; session reassignment during awaited execution admission revokes custody and the prepared native policy denies execution. No OS command is spawned. This is synthetic protocol evidence for the current-main head, not clearance of the historical PR head or a live-model claim.
- Current executor tests: 52 passed. Native follow-up custody and lifecycle sibling tests: 10 passed.
- Targeted core and full Codex production/test TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, diff whitespace check, and justified test-line allocation pass.
- Independent local review found no actionable P0–P2 defects in this delta. It was limited to the supplied change/evidence.

The native protocol is represented by the repository's app-server fixture in these checks. This exact source head has not been exercised against a live model; previous installed-release incidents and proof are background, not an exact-head production claim.

## Problem

prs.title: fix(codex): recover a fresh connection after terminal WebSocket relay failure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A settled native Codex turn can report the private inference relay's 502 error with a `ws://127.0.0.1` URL. The transport classifier currently recognizes the corresponding HTTP URL but misses WebSocket URLs, so the failed shared client remains available to later attempts.

## User Impact

After this specific terminal WebSocket relay failure, later attempts use a fresh connection and preserve completed work on the saved thread. Successful native transport fallback remains visible and does not retire the connection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the same exact relay error with a loopback WebSocket URL. Reuse the existing settled-transport recovery: keep completed work and its transcript, mark replay unsafe, retire the failed pooled client only after the native turn settles, and resume the existing thread on a fresh connection. Foreign-host URLs and unrelated 502 errors keep their existing behavior.

This does not suppress the native “Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS” warning. Codex emits that warning when it switches transport and may still finish successfully; the successful-warning regression keeps it visible and keeps the usable connection.

## Evidence

- The new owning attempt regression fails on the base because the terminal WebSocket failure leaves the shared client registered.
- The focused fixed cases cover HTTP and WebSocket relay failures, a foreign-host near miss, an unrelated 502, and a successful visible fallback warning. Completed tool work is preserved and is not replayed; recovery uses a new client and resumes the saved thread.
- Five focused owning attempt cases pass; production/test typechecks, lint, formatting, test-line budget, whitespace checks and an independent local review are recorded with this candidate.

The native protocol uses the repository's app-server fixture. No live network outage or model run is claimed. Native fallback semantics were checked against sibling Codex revision 6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9, `codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs:133` and `codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:2454`.
