prs.title: perf(ui): bound chunk hash cascades after updates
prs.body:
Related: #194718. Does not include #194730.

## What Problem This Solves

A CSS edit, Search edit, Chat edit, translation refresh and media dependency update all renamed the same 574 reference-only JavaScript chunks. A warm cache therefore lost roughly 5 MB after each update, even when almost none of that JavaScript payload changed.

## User Impact

Repeat visits after a Gateway update retain substantially more of the browser cache, especially for CSS, leaf-page and translation changes. Cold and warm behavior, admission identity and unsaved-draft recovery remain the acceptance boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root Cause

The emitted graph has a 574-node strongly connected component:

```mermaid
graph LR
  Connection -->|dynamic import| Shared[Boot shared]
  Shared -->|dynamic import| Search
  Search -->|static import| Shared
  Search -->|static import| Connection
  Shared -->|filename in preload tables| CSS[Shared CSS]
```

Cycle size and affected importer count are distinct: the historical CSS pair has a 573-node cycle plus affected outside importers; fresh main has the 574-node cycle shown above. The final CSS pair’s largest emitted filename-reference cycle is 160 nodes.

The payload roots differ by change: shared CSS changes session-header spacing; Search changes the field-hints memo; Chat changes highlight reuse; 22 Cron locale namespaces add translated schedule labels; the media worker and `pele.min` change with the dependency bump. The CSS filename appears in 63 JavaScript preload tables. These different roots all reach the same reference cycle. Production identity already comes from the document; there is no volatile bundled build ID to remove.


| Pair | Payload root chunks | Changed payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSS | `control-ui-boot-shared-styles-*.css` | Session-header spacing rules; no JavaScript payload root |
| Search leaf | `search-page-*.js` | Field-hints memo |
| Shared Chat | `control-ui-boot-chat-*.js` | Syntax-highlight reuse |
| i18n | 22 `locale-namespace-<locale>-cron-*.js` | Four translated Cron schedule labels |
| Dependency | `chat-attachment-video.worker-*.js`, `pele.min-*.js` | Media library update |

## Solution

An **eight-entry import map (six JavaScript, two CSS)** cuts incoming filename dependencies on Connection and Boot shared plus their static closure. Rolldown's runtime retains native hash dependencies. Vite still computes real preload lists; equal-width substitutions preserve source-map columns. A canonical graph/config/toolchain signature covers late preload rewrites, with build failures for unprotected substitutions or ambiguous identities.

The Gateway roots both map keys and targets before calculating CSP hashes. The map precedes inline preload producers and native document modulepreloads. Mapped documents omit JavaScript HTTP Link hints, because those run before the import map; CSS HTTP hints and unmapped-document behavior remain. Build identity, admission and stale-tab recovery owners are unchanged. No dependency or production-budget changes.

Graph/configuration/toolchain changes deliberately invalidate the affected set. Shared Chat and media changes still reach a substantial importer graph; the bounded map leaves a 160-node reference cycle. A narrower experiment extracting only the Vite preload helper reduced the original cycle from 574 to 570 while adding a request and violating Chat budgets, so it was discarded. These are accepted limits of the small map. Savings apply between builds using the fix; the first deployment of the new chunk scheme is a separate cache transition.

## Evidence

### Five Real Adjacent Pairs

Current source: `1aa35897d6abe8a162c387dae59e69d4b2b4932d`. The final correction only changes the managed-image test fixture; one exact-head canonical build confirms unchanged immutable assets and passing strict sizes. The five-pair census uses the final build transform from `826d4665df7f`; the last correction changes only offline-shell map/CSP preparation. All 3,074 immutable asset URLs and bytes match on the exact final head; the census therefore applies unchanged. The historical corpus was not relabeled as a fresh final-head run. All pairs use canonical `pnpm ui:build`, historical frozen locks, Node 26.12.1 and identical metadata. Both sides replay landed #194718 to isolate this follow-up. This is a fully populated immutable-cache census, not one route's traffic. Gzip/Brotli use served sidecars; public files use identity bytes. Revalidated HTML and worker traffic are measured separately.

| Change | Adjacent commits | Gzip before → after | Brotli before → after | Renamed JS before → after |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CSS | `b4fe3d2655c4` → `12026082dc86` | 5,313,016 → 59,322 B | 4,958,808 → 50,116 B | 574 → 1 |
| Search leaf | `fcdb89571453` → `9d13d1f09392` | 5,269,177 → 578,348 B | 4,923,664 → 480,669 B | 575 → 2 |
| Shared Chat | `c3b92c2597b3` → `1de61f3e587c` | 5,269,447 → 3,683,797 B | 4,924,485 → 3,405,541 B | 575 → 300 |
| Cron translations | `38b3a0d00ae8` → `4020bfd9d7be` | 5,447,829 → 665,036 B | 5,089,600 → 612,975 B | 596 → 45 |
| Media dependencies | `2e83d371655d` → `10bbb1ed2182` | 5,654,901 → 4,070,913 B | 5,247,242 → 3,730,082 B | 576 → 303 |

No immutable URL/content collisions occurred. Renamed-but-byte-identical JavaScript count is zero in every pair. The remaining JavaScript classifications are:

| Change | Unchanged URL/content before → after | Reference-only renames before → after | Payload-changed JS before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CSS | 2,115 → 2,688 | 574 → 1 | 0 → 0 |
| Search leaf | 2,115 → 2,688 | 574 → 1 | 1 → 1 |
| Shared Chat | 2,115 → 2,390 | 574 → 299 | 1 → 1 |
| Cron translations | 2,093 → 2,644 | 574 → 23 | 22 → 22 |
| Media dependencies | 2,113 → 2,386 | 574 → 301 | 2 → 2 |

Search still changes its genuine shared route-table importer (roughly 568 KB gzip), the Search payload and a small navigation-preload JSON. This is not a leaf-only transfer claim. The CLI now reports payload roots and reference cycles so this distinction is inspectable.

## Reproducibility

Identical source built in two checkout paths produces identical URLs and bytes for all **3,074 immutable assets**, including 2,690 JavaScript and 124 CSS assets. All 53 font-directory entries also match: 33 WOFF2, nine CSS, 11 documentation files; documentation is outside immutable totals. A different timestamp changes only `index.html` and `sw.js`. The final replay verifies an identical 44-file resolved Vite configuration closure before building. Stock production output and the final bounded map are both path-reproducible.

The experimental full native import map had path-dependent synthetic keys. Stock production output was already reproducible; the bounded implementation uses canonical source identities and remains reproducible. An earlier incomplete source replay was discarded and corrected before qualification.

## Sizes and Correctness

| Production size | Base | Head | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Document raw | 68,226 B | 68,817 B | +591 B |
| Document gzip | 15,988 B | 16,048 B | +60 B |
| Startup JS served gzip | 91,564 B | 91,512 B | -52 B |
| Startup JS served Brotli | 81,413 B | 81,449 B | +36 B |
| Startup JS normalized gzip | 90,900 B | 90,881 B | -19 B |
| Startup CSS normalized gzip | 39,090 B | 39,090 B | 0 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Chat boot JS normalized gzip | 1,294,914 B | 1,294,718 B | -196 B |
| New Session JS normalized gzip | 803,127 B | 803,080 B | -47 B |

Strict same-machine base/head comparison passes with no violations or raised production budgets. Document gzip grows 60 B, within the 64 B build-variance allowance. The base already exceeds fixed document, total-CSS and Chat boot ceilings; this is a strict no-growth comparison, not a claim that every absolute ceiling passes. Two inert HTML comments were removed to offset map cost. Native modulepreload, lazy boundaries and request counts remain.

Production smoke on the runtime-equivalent `26fdcb06ea0` passes eight pages: Chromium/WebKit/Firefox at root and `/dashboard`, plus Firefox French at both paths. No physical-alias requests, HTTP errors or page errors. Open-tab proof passes all three engines: actual missing old Activity chunks return 404, dirty raw config stays intact, reload stays blocked, and explicit discard allows exactly one reload into `/activity?view=live`.

A separate 30-second service-worker observation on `26fdcb06ea0` in Chromium and Firefox shows **4,690,526 → 135,030 B** of actual wire bodies (Brotli plus identity). Chromium requests are 561/559 for base/control → 8 for head; Firefox 558/558 → 7. At readiness, the old worker remains active and the replacement is installing in all six observations. After readiness, the baseline downloads another 3.5–3.9 MB over 535–541 requests; head downloads about 4 KB over three requests. By 30 seconds the replacement is active, all 117 boot assets and the offline shell are complete, and the predecessor is retained. No errors or recovery. These n=1 observations prove lifecycle and that head’s traffic, not timing acceptance. Timing was measured on `f67b416a072`; later build-transform corrections have zero normalized immutable payload changes. The final `1aa35897d6ab` build has the same 44-input configuration fingerprint as the completed `826d4665df7f` census: `ec5abc9a1554de1259971768faf1c869260f5f1ea8d6386437a920f3b67729b0`. The exact final-head cross-path/timestamp replay preserves all 3,074 immutable URLs and bytes, including all 2,690 JavaScript files; only index.html and sw.js differ. The offline correction is separately exercised on the final worker, as described below.

## Timing

The full initial matrix ran 19:56–20:49 UTC on 2026-11-07, with 20 rotated base/control/head triplets per state, engine and latency profile (1,080 measured visits). A single warm localhost extension added ten triplets in each engine (90 visits); a single Firefox cold 100 ms extension added ten triplets (30 visits). No errors, missing assets, interrupted navigations or recovery reloads occurred in these 1,200 measured visits.

The endpoint is recorded inside the page with `performance.now()`: an animation-frame observation of the visible, enabled New Session composer, followed by `document.fonts.ready`; the wait also verifies the route and expected build identity. It is application readiness, not paint or driver wall time. The separate updated transition starts before the build swap and includes driver/swap overhead through final build readiness. HTTP caches are enabled, service workers blocked, and warm/update primers dwell for three seconds. The 100 ms server-delay profile approximates remote request latency; it is not a full packet-level WAN emulation. All browsers are headless. Chromium CPU uses thread ticks; WebKit/Firefox CPU is unavailable.

### Interpretation and limits

The updated CSS visit improves about 30–32% in Chromium and WebKit, and 27% in Firefox at the remote-delay profile. Firefox localhost improves 2.44%, below the nominal 5% target. Cold and warm medians stay within the 5% band. All three warm-localhost confirmation segments have no worse p95; Firefox cold-remote confirmation and its combined thirty observations are also inside the band.

The pooled warm-localhost p95s remain worse: Chromium +10.42%, WebKit +17.57%, Firefox +4.19%. The single confirmation did not reproduce those tails, but it does not erase them. Chromium pooled warm task CPU is +1.63% median / +6.46% p95, while the confirmation alone is +0.76% / -0.10%. Thus this evidence supports a clear updated-visit win and non-reproduced warm tails; it does not establish an unconditional pooled-p95 no-regression claim.

The warm-tail audit retains each ordered triplet, host load, request count and available CPU in `boot-lint-final-warm-tail-audit.json`. Both largest Chromium warm values (153.8 and 152.6 ms) and both largest WebKit values (294 and 261 ms) occur with the rotated control/head/base order. The same order in the confirmation has no comparable tail. Initial Chromium high-tail rows also have higher measured script CPU, so scheduler noise alone is not a demonstrated explanation. No additional JavaScript or font download appears in those warm rows; the requests are the document and optional bootstrap configuration. One WebKit outlier includes that 395-byte configuration response, the other does not, so it is not a sufficient cause. There is no isolated, verified source-causal regression mechanism in this dataset, and no further retries were run.


**Acceptance:** accepted under the stated single-confirmation clause: each prescribed follow-up block meets the band. The original and pooled tails remain above, and intermittent warm-tail regression remains unresolved. This is the lane’s proof judgment, not maintainer approval. No claim that every pooled p95 is unchanged.


The first candidate used classic-script HTTP preloads to avoid Firefox's import-map ordering issue. It was rejected: Chromium cold readiness regressed 10.35% and task CPU 9.8% over 20 triplets. A trace showed disabled streaming compilation (`wrong script type`). Removing JavaScript HTTP hints restores native background streaming; the final matrix above qualifies that corrected implementation. The rejected measurements are not counted as final proof.

## Checks and Review

The graph CLI regression, Vite boundary regression, Gateway HTTP suite (20 tests), UI types, targeted lint/format, production Knip, test-line ratchet, and strict performance comparison passed. The final worker correction passes all 49 worker-cache tests; its new map/CSP assertions fail on the old worker across all three tested scope forms. Final test-line allocation is 6,566,358/6,566,367. Production Knip passed in 54.2 s. Independent P0–P2 implementation and correction reviews are scoped-clean.

CI run 42413539672 on `de7ac44690b7` exposed a real deep-link regression: 116/118 captured browser failures requested an unmapped alias and received 404s in absolute-base previews. This was PR-caused. Commit `826d4665df7f` makes the map honor Vite’s resolved base; the new regression is red before the fix and green after it, and the previously failing agent-identity browser scenario passes at desktop/mobile widths.

A review then identified the same rooting requirement in the worker-owned offline shell. Commit `f0b2f7da0bcc` roots that map and replaces only its exact CSP hash, leaving identity, admission and recovery unchanged. Hard-cut network proof passes in Chromium and Firefox at the root and `/dashboard` prefix: the offline deep link renders Appearance from the service worker, with no successful server response, alias failure or CSP violation. All four previous-worker cases fail in Chromium and Firefox with synthetic-filename errors and a persistent loading skeleton; all four fixed-worker cases pass. Final broad CI is tracked on exact head `1aa35897d6ab` in run [42418584040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42418584040). The prior auto-merge intent was retired before either correction push.

The next full run, [42416775456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42416775456), reported only the two failing `managed-image-actions` cases (`reuses full image bytes after 0/2 failed download attempts`). Both failed before roster readiness; the test overrode the page CSP without its new import-map hash. Both reproduce locally and pass after `1aa35897d6ab`, which replaces that duplicate fixture with the existing `fulfillWithControlUiCsp` helper. No image/download assertion or production code changed. The correction passes UI types, scoped lint/format and independent P0–P2 review; test-line count is 6,566,358 /6,566,367. Full CI [42418584040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42418584040) **passed** on the corrected exact head `1aa35897d6ab`. Its one canonical rebuild preserves all 3,074 immutable URLs and bytes; document gzip is 16,048 B (+60 B), with strict violations empty. No five-pair or timing rerun was needed.

Changed-scope LOC: **7,976 → 8,690** (+714; 744 insertions /30 deletions, 18 files). Production/build/tooling LOC: **5,809 → 6,252**. This includes the existing service-worker owner and its directly coupled fixtures. The growth is the bounded build transform, emitted-graph diagnostics and regressions for immutable hash safety, preload ordering and rooted online/offline CSP. The larger experimental map and classic-preload workaround are not retained. No runtime state owner or report was added to the repository.

### Open-tab recovery (synthetic data)

After an old lazy chunk disappears, the existing recovery owner keeps the dirty config in memory and blocks reload until explicit discard.

After explicit discard, exactly one reload reaches the requested Activity view.

prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid reclamation rollback during cold startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SQLite session reclamation rolling back during cold startup when the current owner takes more than five seconds to authorize the worker commit.

## User Impact

Cold startup can finish an authorized reclamation instead of failing its commit checkpoint. The decision remains bounded at 30 seconds. Current-owner checks, revocation, rollback and writer admission are unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker already waits on an owner-controlled shared gate. Allow 30 seconds for that existing authorization decision; do not change who can authorize it or what happens after revocation.

## Evidence

- A real Worker and SQLite transaction regression holds the owner for 6 seconds after the commit request and verifies the persisted value. With the original 5-second bound, the new case fails with a commit-checkpoint expiration while the other 5 cases pass. With this change, all 6 cases pass, including revocation and rollback/worker-exit settlement.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on Node 24.22.1. Final wall time 36.28 s, including a cold compiled-worker generation; test time approximately 7.4 s. The 6-second delay deliberately crosses the shipped 5-second boundary and proves real cross-thread behavior.
- Core typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`), targeted lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete two-file working change against `2e13c52c97bbe81228c4f45212c8ca8cd346dbf9`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no accepted findings. Reviewer assessed the supplied patch and worker fixture; it did not execute tests.
- This is the reclamation authorization window, separate from native child-completion observation budgets.

prs.title: perf(ui): show Systems inventory before telemetry settles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Systems waits for canonical inventory and unrelated telemetry together. A slow or permanently pending `node.list` or an uncached `system.info` hides known devices; one stuck telemetry source also suppresses healthy sibling polling.

## What Changes

Let canonical `environments.list` inventory render independently from node and Gateway telemetry. Each telemetry source owns its pending request, so either can finish and continue polling while the other is slow. Membership, availability and initial selection still come from canonical inventory; telemetry only enriches accepted rows in the matching connection scope. Pending measurements show Loading, failed measurements show their actual read error, and navigation and device selection remain usable.

Periodic failures preserve last-known values with their stale indication. An inventory refresh that fails to refresh a telemetry source clears only that source's previous enrichment; healthy sibling telemetry and canonical membership remain. This preserves the existing manual-refresh behavior, including fallback from a previously enriched macOS version to the canonical platform label. Initial samples survive selection changes; selected-host polls retire, and departure/reconnection cancels outstanding work.

Authentication, session identity, Desktop operations, binding and policy authority are unchanged. No dependencies, options, cache owners or size ceilings are added.

## Evidence

Base: `83f7614cc70d136f5e32d6357c6b67f39e985187`. The complete timing matrix measured frozen candidate `7bfccd666b13db141daa59f8dd23a393002d79ba`: 20 rotated base/head/identical-base triplets per engine and condition, **540/540 observations passed**. All browser runs were headless, on the same Mac, with host load recorded. Synthetic delay injection isolates UI coupling; it does not estimate current server latency.

| Condition | Engine | Application readiness median / p95, ms | Automation wall median / p95, ms | A/A readiness median / p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| node.list +3s | Chromium | 3058.50→75.30 / 3070.80→87.50 | 3127.40→143.10 / 3140.22→157.12 | -0.01% / -0.16% |
| node.list +3s | Webkit | 3115.50→131.00 / 3122.00→143.00 | 3191.80→195.06 / 3195.25→210.70 | +0.00% / +0.54% |
| node.list +3s | Firefox | 3095.00→106.00 / 3109.00→115.00 | 3164.31→179.22 / 3183.18→186.25 | +0.02% / -0.32% |
| No delay | Chromium | 74.90→74.50 / 77.60→76.40 | 143.60→143.41 / 145.54→145.92 | -0.53% / -0.77% |
| No delay | Webkit | 133.50→137.00 / 143.00→150.00 | 195.13→194.86 / 209.26→211.77 | -2.25% / +3.50% |
| No delay | Firefox | 107.50→108.50 / 117.00→117.00 | 178.47→179.65 / 186.63→185.72 | -6.05% / -0.85% |
| 100 ms RTT | Chromium | 574.95→575.75 / 577.40→578.00 | 643.75→643.91 / 645.63→646.88 | +0.11% / +0.09% |
| 100 ms RTT | Webkit | 713.50→715.50 / 721.00→725.00 | 790.30→791.95 / 795.21→794.73 | +0.14% / +0.42% |
| 100 ms RTT | Firefox | 695.00→694.00 / 704.00→706.00 | 764.72→761.78 / 776.61→780.80 | -0.22% / +0.28% |

With `node.list` delayed three seconds, application readiness improves **95.8–97.5%**. Normal-use application medians move −0.53%, +2.62%, +0.93% without delay and +0.14%, +0.28%, −0.14% at 100 ms RTT; automation wall medians remain effectively flat. The largest no-delay tail movement is WebKit 143→150 ms (+4.90%), with flat wall time and an A/A p95 movement of +3.50%.

Chromium script CPU median is 25.98→27.94 ms (+1.96 ms) without delay and 29.09→31.47 ms (+2.38 ms) at RTT100; task CPU is 57.46→60.42 ms and 63.66→66.51 ms. **Applying the coordinator’s tradeoff rule:** a bounded roughly 2 ms script cost and flat normal wall time do not outweigh recovering approximately three seconds of otherwise blank inventory. This is a readiness improvement, not a total-work or CPU saving. CPU counters end at readiness, so delayed-window CPU reductions are not presented as total-work savings. WebKit/Firefox script/task CPU is unavailable, not zero.

The original prototype's same-run no-delay evidence was 143.69→143.16 ms wall, 75.25→74.05 ms readiness, and 27.10→28.99 ms script CPU (+1.89 ms). Its delayed evidence came from another prototype and is not combined with those numbers; the table above supplies the complete current candidate comparison.

### Behavior and refresh correction

Standard held/release census: 42 observations across base/head and all three engines, zero harness failures. A held `node.list` leaves inventory blank on base and visible on head; programmatic and native navigation work, and releasing the request restores data. Held canonical `environments.list` correctly keeps inventory pending on both versions.

Immediate first visits can reuse the shared ten-second boot `system.info` cache. The first supplemental attempt therefore observed zero requests and is excluded as a setup failure. The corrected supplemental waits eleven seconds before first Systems entry, asserts a real `system.info` request, and exercises three-second and indefinitely held responses. 18/18 supplemental observations passed. Single-sample first-ready timings after cache expiry were Chromium 3111.5→113.3 ms, WebKit 3157→184 ms, and Firefox 3163→189 ms; these are behavior samples, not the statistical acceptance matrix. An indefinitely held response left base inventory pending while head inventory rendered in all three engines; navigation and release recovery passed.

CI exposed one real regression in the measured candidate: `Systems workspace mocked Gateway E2E > names Macs consistently and enables a discovered desktop without reconnecting`. Manual inventory refresh retained an old source's OS enrichment after that source failed. The final correction changes only the inventory-sample failure branch; the successful execution path remains unchanged. Timing evidence above remains pinned to `7bfccd6`; final committed head is `f1bfcc87c6236cb570a1425e55b684749f162e49`; the precommit rebuild and failure/release checks use the exact retained final production source, recorded with per-file SHA-256 hashes in `.artifacts/systems-final-build-provenance.json`. Its bundle metadata identifies `7bfccd6` plus the dirty working tree, not a clean final commit. Later changes only add test braces and the test-line allocation; no production source changed after that build. The existing E2E assertion remains unchanged, and a two-source regression proves periodic stale retention versus inventory-refresh clearing.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` and UI-page test typecheck | Passed; test-only fixture uses the existing readonly-context construction pattern |
| Systems data tests | 5 passed on unchanged data tests |
| Systems page tests | 28 existing cases passed; the temporary combined file passed 30/30 before its two new cases moved into the focused owner-state file |
| Failure regression | Both sources failed the intended rendered assertion on the pre-correction candidate and passed after the fix; relocated owner-state file passed 2/2 in 2.03 s wall / 0.241 s test time |
| Exact previously failing Mac E2E | Passed 1/1, 22 unrelated cases skipped (14.93 s wall / 1.063 s test time); exact test name above |
| Final corrected-source held/released proof | 9/9 observations passed across Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, including all six held-source recoveries; each delayed method was observed and its selected machine showed live measurements after release |
| Scoped lint/format and `git diff --check` | Passed; exact +137 test-line allocation passes the staged checker (21 lines remaining) |
| Independent P0–P2 autoreview | Scoped-clean P0–P2 on the final staged correction, with full owner/lifecycle context |
| Final production build / strict sizes | Passed; strict base/head comparison has zero violations |
| Final production Knip | Passed on the final retained source, 49.9 s |

The named Playwright E2E uses the canonical bundled setup with its automatically cleaned tool-owned system-temp build. `TMPDIR` stays unchanged for the secure-temp contract; durable logs and artifacts remain on the SSD.

### Visual evidence

Synthetic-only full captures were inspected. The before/held pair uses the frozen timing candidate; the release capture uses the corrected final source and a differently named synthetic Gateway, so it is separate recovery proof. 

Before, uncached `system.info` held forever:

![Before: Systems inventory waits for telemetry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62f9e5ba-8917-41d7-8210-9b920de51225)

After, same held response:

![After: known Systems inventory and explicit telemetry loading](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/faa9c37c-e50d-4f6f-bdec-bf503e5a2358)

Corrected final source, after releasing the selected Gateway telemetry:

![Final head: Gateway measurements visible after release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a51e8f9d-764a-483c-937c-2565da4d4fd7)

## Size and remaining dependencies

Final changed production files: 889→948 LOC (+59). Tests: 1,161→1,298 LOC (+137); docs: 1,004→1,011 (+7). An exact +137 test-line allocation retains the two-source regression and independent polling proof without widening shared test headroom. Diff is seven feature files plus the two-line allocation record; no report files are committed.

The original candidate's strict comparison passed with zero violations: startup JavaScript **90,900→90,900 B gzip**, startup CSS **39,090→39,090 B gzip**, **one startup CSS request**. The precommit rebuild of the corrected final source also measures exactly **90,900 B startup JavaScript gzip** and **39,090 B startup CSS gzip**, with **one CSS request** and zero strict base/head violations. Served JavaScript bytes are 91,595→91,583 (hash variation); normalized bytes are unchanged. No size ceilings were raised. Existing fixed-ceiling warnings remain visible in the checker report but add no violations against this base.

Canonical environments and authorization-dependent operations legitimately wait for their owner. Measurements still wait for their own source and never masquerade as ready data; periodic failures explicitly mark last-known readings. prs.title: fix(android): gateways behind Cloudflare Access can't connect because custom headers can't be set
prs.body:
Closes #122215 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the Android app cannot reach a gateway behind Cloudflare Access service tokens (or another authenticating reverse proxy) because no screen can set the per-gateway custom headers the app already stores and sends. ## User Impact User impact: Android users can add proxy headers such as `CF-Access-Client-Id` and `CF-Access-Client-Secret` when they set up a secure (TLS) gateway manually, in onboarding, in Settings > Manual Gateway, and in Add Gateway. The form explains which name and value go where, refuses a Client ID or secret typed as a header name, lists the header names saved for that address (never the values), and lets the user remove one after a confirmation. ## Why This Change Was Made The only header editor (#100765) was placed in the Connect tab after that tab had already been disconnected, so it never shipped, and it was later deleted as dead code; the release notes for v2026.7.1 still list the feature. This PR restores one shared editor in the three manual setup flows. Headers travel with the connect request and merge by name into that gateway's saved headers before the first upgrade, so rotating one header keeps the others. Requests that carry custom headers (the WebSocket upgrade, ticketed media downloads, and the client handed to Media3 for streamed video) no longer follow redirects: OkHttp keeps custom headers across hosts, so a rejected or revoked service token would otherwise be sent to the proxy's login host. The second commit comes from a real device test. The tester typed the Client ID into Header name and the Client Secret into Header value, Access answered with a login redirect, and the saved header could not be seen or removed without forgetting the gateway. So the form now: - names both service token headers and switches the name placeholder to `CF-Access-Client-Secret` once a Client ID header exists; - blocks Add and connect when the name looks like a Client ID (`<32 hex>.access`) or a secret (64 hex or `cfast_…`), with a warning and a "Fix the custom header above before connecting." message; - lists saved header names for the address in the form; a credential saved as a name is described ("Client ID saved as a header name"), never printed, including in accessibility text; removal asks first and takes effect on the next connection; - keeps typed rows when a connect to a wrong port is corrected, in onboarding and in Settings, so the credentials are not retyped; Settings clears them when another flow, such as a setup code, saves a different address; - hides the editor in Add Gateway for an address that is already saved, because adding a saved address only selects it; Manual Gateway in Settings changes its headers. Header values stay masked, out of saved instance state and logs, and are sent only on TLS routes.
Limits and related work - Settings > Manual Gateway is prefilled without the context path (existing behavior). - #162247 (proxy Basic login) edits the same Android files; whichever lands second needs a rebase. - iOS has its own header editor and is not changed here.
## Evidence Physical Android device (debug build of this branch) against a gateway behind Cloudflare Tunnel with an Access application that has a Service Auth policy: - Before this branch no screen could enter the headers, so the upgrade carried none and Access sent it to its login page. - First attempt with this branch, Client ID typed as the header name: the app failed with `Expected HTTP 101 response but was '302 Found'`, which is what exposed the confusion above. - With `CF-Access-Client-Id` and `CF-Access-Client-Secret` as names: the upgrade reached the gateway and pairing completed. Redacted gateway log: ``` closed before connect conn= peer=:->:18789 ... host=gateway.example ua=okhttp/5.5.0 code=1008 reason=pairing required: device is not approved yet (requestId: ) phase=auth_validated device pairing approved device= role=operator # openclaw nodes status (this device) {"clientId": "openclaw-android", "platform": "android", "version": "2026.8.2-debug-dev", "connected": true, "paired": true} ``` Redirect proof on the production session path (`GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest.proxyHeadersStopAtTheGatewayWhenItRedirects`: a real `GatewaySession` and OkHttp against a TLS gateway that answers the way a proxy answers a rejected token, with a second HTTPS server, trusted through the same pinned certificate, standing in for its login host): | Request to the gateway | Gateway answer | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | WebSocket upgrade | `302` to the login host | not followed; the session retries | | WebSocket upgrade | `101` | connected | | ticketed image download | `302` to the login host | not followed; the image loads as unavailable | | streamed video, sent with the client and headers Media3 receives | `302` to the login host | not followed | Every gateway request carried `CF-Access-Client-Secret`; the login host received 0 requests. With the protection removed, or reduced to `followSslRedirects(false)`, the same test fails because streamed video follows the redirect (`expected:<302> but was:<200>`). Access responses measured with curl against the same app, which match the app's behavior: no headers → `302` to login, malformed `CF-Access-*` values → `401`, a valid token before the Service Auth policy existed → `403`, non `CF-Access-*` names → `302`. Device screenshot after the fix (address redacted). The first row is the tester's earlier mistake, shown as a description instead of the Client ID: Before / after in Settings > Manual Gateway for `https://gateway.example` (Robolectric captures, synthetic values): | Before (main) | After: saved names | After: secret typed as a name | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | Checks on the final head (rebased on current `main`): - `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` 3594/3594 passed, `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` 3726/3726 passed, `ktlintCheck` passed. - `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm android:i18n:check`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check` passed. - New regression tests fail when their fix is removed: credential names wrapped in quotes or ending in a period, a header re-added after its saved copy was removed, typed headers hiding at the saved address and coming back for a corrected port (onboarding and Settings), Settings clearing them when another address is saved, and the redirect proof above. - Stored data: this PR changes no persisted format. `SecurePrefs.kt` and the gateway registry are unchanged; custom headers use the SecurePrefs entries that shipped with #100765. No released build could write those entries (current `main` has no production caller of `saveGatewayCustomHeaders`), so a device upgrading from the latest stable release reads no custom headers for any gateway and keeps its saved credentials and pairing, exactly as before, until the user adds headers. On the device, the build from the first commit was upgraded in place to the second: the saved header names were listed (the screenshot shows names saved by the first build), and `openclaw nodes status` reports the device `"connected": true, "paired": true` afterwards. Play builds are release-signed under another application id, so a contributor cannot upgrade one in place to a debug build. Size against the merge base: production +495/−36 (one new editor file of 278 lines, the rest wiring in the three hosts and `MainViewModel`), native string inventory +27, tests +518/−21, docs +11/−2. The third commit, which answers the first review, is production +28/−31: one no-redirect client now serves every request that carries custom headers and replaces the upgrade-only client. After the second review I cut the input unit test to the one case no form test reaches (rotating one header keeps the others saved); without the merge it guards, that test fails. Before opening the PR I removed one unit test that repeated what the Settings UI test proves and folded a punctuation case into the existing credential-shape test.

prs.title: test(perf): measure warm reload from the real old page
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm-cache measurements leave an empty reset document, so they cannot show the physical old application surface during a signed-in deep-link reload. The campaign's original dashboard reload exposed 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds; separating real application work from measurement overhead matters when judging that flow.

## User Impact

Application behavior is unchanged. Performance investigations gain an opt-in, calibrated capture of the actual previous page and the next document's surfaces. No configuration, database format, snapshot policy, presentation gate, or bundle-budget change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`--paint-holding` uses pinned full headless Chromium with PaintHolding enabled, checks synthetic early/late controls, and records compositor timestamps without CPU sampling. The existing warm-state owner restores repeatable inputs while retaining the real DOM. The capture caller owns one CDP session through restoration and capture; the helper no longer creates and detaches a second session. Old-document geometry samplers are stopped before navigation. Ordinary reset-document benchmarking is preserved.

The frozen mode deliberately dispatches synthetic pagehide before restoring inputs. It measures a real old surface with repeatable inputs; it does not reproduce natural exit behavior by itself. A separate page-triggered natural reload confirmed trusted exit handlers, empty pending snapshot queues, and no old transaction spanning navigation. There is no application exit-writer fix in this PR.

## Evidence

Measurements used one AWS c7a.4xlarge lease, 16 observed vCPUs, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, and the same application build throughout: `d5415411e970cb91d49be50159bd2a8836c0b98e`. The PR was subsequently rebased; these numbers do not benchmark the later application source.

| Team-active diagnostic | Imported capture mode | Corrected tooling |
|---|---:|---:|
| Real old-page rows + Details, median [Q1,Q3], n=4 | 558 [511,581] ms | 518 [511,535] ms |
| Reset-document control, n=4 | 486 [478,492] ms | 512 [483,516] ms |
| Descriptive real-minus-reset median gap | 72 ms | 6 ms |
| Independent natural reload, n=1 | 564 ms | 568 ms |

These are small grouped diagnostic samples, not an interleaved product improvement comparison. The application bundle did not change. The gap is insufficient evidence for deleting application exit work. Timeline-only attribution found no old transaction crossing navigation; wrapped exit handlers totaled about 2.3–3.5 ms including instrumentation, with individual application handlers below 1 ms. Team's later snapshot callbacks overlap new-document CPU work; callback latency is not a backend lock-wait measurement.

- Focused `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/control-ui-cold-load-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1/1 passed after rebase, wall time **13.37 s**.
- Baseline `corepack pnpm build`, required capture workloads, calibration, and natural-reload witness checks passed on AWS lease **cbx_206eb871c1fa**. Focused lint on the final three TypeScript files passed remotely in **6.38 s**. The lease is verified released; owned Gateway listeners were empty before release.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through **P2**.
- Initial CI identified four tooling lint errors; they were corrected. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42418576261) for `85b6fd8474197a8e4c6884cf85656161f7c58c31` is green (55 successful jobs, 3 successful external checks, 48 skipped jobs, 1 neutral check). No merge is requested.
- Non-test/non-doc diff: **+268/-80, net +188 LOC** across four tooling files. Application runtime delta: **0**. Growth implements the calibrated physical-surface measurement contract; session creation/teardown duplication is removed and no application owner or cache is added.
- Synthetic old/skeleton/rows frames were inspected. No private capture or private content was uploaded or quoted. There is no application appearance change.
- The application experiment stopped at attribution: no application candidate, twelve-pair/A/A product comparison, new freshness regression, or full UI suite was run. No `ui/` file is changed.

Release-note context: internal performance tooling distinguishes real old-page reload surfaces from empty-document warm-cache loads and excludes the old document's measurement samplers from navigation.

prs.title: fix(models): surface manual-selection permission in the full CLI inventory
prs.body:
Closes #194738

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models list --all --json` reports a policy-blocked but authenticated model as `available: true` with no field distinguishing manual-selection permission from runtime readiness. An agent selecting a reviewer from this inventory then hits the native `sessions_spawn` policy rejection. The policy rejection is correct; the missing policy visibility is the bug.

Plain language: the model catalog told the agent "this model is ready to use", but the permission layer separately forbids picking it — and the catalog never said so. Now the catalog row says it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection already exists: `models-list-result.ts` renders `manualSelectionAllowed` for clients that opt in, gated by the `model-selection-policy` client capability, and the protocol schema documents the field as "Scoped manual-choice permission; separate from runtime readiness". The CLI never opted in, so the full inventory omitted it. The CLI now advertises the capability on the gateway path, passes the internal `includeManualSelection` flag on the local-reader path, and carries the projected field through to each JSON row. Models are not removed from the full inventory and admission is unchanged.

## User Impact

`models list --all --json` rows for policy-blocked models now show `manualSelectionAllowed: false` (and `true` for allowed ones), so inventory consumers can filter before attempting `sessions_spawn`. When the projection is unavailable (older gateway, or the field is not projected), rows omit the field exactly as before.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main tree this change is based on (files byte-compared as `main` + exactly this delta):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `list.prepared-catalog.test.ts` new test: gateway result carrying `manualSelectionAllowed: false` surfaces on the `--all --json` row, and the CLI gateway call advertises the `model-selection-policy` cap | green (16/16) |
| Red check: reverting the capability advertisement and the row passthrough makes exactly the new test fail (caps missing, field absent) | confirmed |
| Adjacent suites `list.refresh-secrets.test.ts`, `load-config.test.ts` | 7/7 green |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json`: zero errors in changed files | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep to trace the existing `manualSelectionAllowed` projection through the gateway capability gate and the CLI row mapping, then wired the existing mechanism into the CLI. The implementer understands the code: no new policy logic is introduced; the CLI simply joins the existing opt-in projection. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(ui): Undo after archiving a session restores it instantly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after archiving a session, clicking **Undo** takes a noticeable moment to bring the row back, because the archive (including stopping its active work) has already been sent and Undo has to send a second unarchive request and wait for a roster refresh.

## User Impact

User impact: archiving still hides the session immediately, and **Undo** now brings it back instantly with nothing sent to the Gateway. The archive is only sent once the Undo notification closes (timeout, dismiss, or replaced by the next archive) or the page is left, so active work keeps running until the Undo window has actually passed.

Behavior change to note: archiving is now applied a few seconds later than before (the toast duration, paused while hovered or focused). Accepted edge cases, documented in code and docs: a Gateway reconnect during the window drops the pending archive and the row reappears; closing the tab sends the archive best-effort, so a lost final request also leaves the session unarchived and visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Undo was a compensating action (archive now, unarchive later). It is now a cancellation: the shared archive runtime holds the request behind the Undo toast and every toast ending other than Undo commits it, as does `pagehide`. Undo only releases the local pending-archive state.

All archive entry points with Undo — sidebar row and menu, chat header, ⌘⇧A, bulk/tree archive, and the Sessions page — go through this one path. The Sessions page previously had its own archive-then-restore flow; it now uses the shared owner and hides held rows the same way the sidebar does. The Undo machinery that re-sent unarchive and restored personal pins is removed, since nothing is pruned before the commit.

Production delta: +137 / −357 across 4 files.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`session-organizer-archive.test.ts` › *hides the session and lets Undo restore it without any Gateway write*): red on the base runtime, green with this change. Companion cases cover committing exactly once on timeout/dismiss/replace and on `pagehide`, and a held tree committing after navigation with partial failure reporting.
- **Browser e2e** (`ui-e2e` lane, mocked Gateway, real bundled UI): archive → row hidden, toast with Undo, zero `sessions.patch`; Undo → row back, still zero requests; close the toast → archive sent, "Archiving…" while pending, failure restores the row with an error, success keeps it hidden and the chat open. Also updated: Sessions page kebab archive, nested archive dialog, archive-history QA, observer-notice/Undo coexistence. All 4 e2e files pass.
- **Unit/DOM suites**: archive runtime, batch mutations, sidebar interactions/sessions, Sessions page archive outcomes (held page archive, navigation/reconnect/failure, held tree), plus surrounding Sessions page and session mutation suites. Re-ran the core suites and `pnpm tsgo:ui` after replaying onto current `main` (no upstream changes to these files).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and format on changed files: clean.
- **Local review**: autoreview (codex, gpt-6.1-sol, `--mode local`, max priority P1) on the complete change: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` archive paragraph updated.

Gap: no live-Gateway run; the browser proof uses the mocked Gateway e2e harness. No visual design change — the toast and rows render as before, only the timing of the Gateway write changes.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(a2a): retain accepted tasks after Gateway crashes
prs.body:
Related: #183490

## What Problem This Solves

An unexpected Gateway restart forgets an accepted A2A task before its terminal result is recorded, so polling loses the original task and retrying the same peer message can start another agent turn.

## User Impact

The original task remains queryable after a crash. Recovery reports `TASK_STATE_FAILED` with an explicit warning that external effects may have occurred, and the same peer message returns that task while its recovered terminal result is retained. The task-store recovery does not itself resume inference, but the full Gateway proof below found that core startup recovery still resumes the interrupted A2A session. The A2A wrapper reports terminal failure while the canonical core owner continues recovery; that ownership mismatch is **not yet resolved**. This does not guarantee exactly-once external effects or recover tasks already lost by an older Gateway.

This draft requests maintainer acceptance of the changed durability and admission-capacity semantics under the [storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes). Real Gateway/model E2E has now been run and exposed the remaining recovery-coordination gap below. Stable upgrade/downgrade qualification remains unrun; an older Gateway does not honor these pending records.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing A2A task owner records admission through the worker-owned plugin-state store before dispatch or a successful response. Pending records have no TTL, reject new admissions at 500 entries per account, and are deleted only after a terminal result commits. Terminal retention remains 24 hours/500 entries. Known terminal results and newer admissions win over stale cleanup records when a message ID is reused. Uncertain write acknowledgements stay fenced until restart reconciliation; definite admission refusals remove never-admitted memory records.

Cleanup failure preserves the known result and logs an error. A remaining pending record consumes capacity; if its terminal result expires before cleanup, later recovery conservatively reports uncertainty. No SQL schema migration, configuration option, background service, or new protocol is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Blocking real Gateway/model finding on this head:** a built isolated Gateway used a real cached Qwen2.5-3B MLX model, with no paid provider or model stub, output capped at 128 tokens, and tools disabled. A normal A2A task completed. A second real model response was held by a byte-preserving transport observer, then the actual Gateway PID received SIGKILL; all task-owned processes exited and the listener disappeared. A different Gateway process reopened the same state and preserved the original failed task, replay identity, peer isolation, and prior completed result. However, core `restart-recovery` automatically resumed the interrupted context and issued another real model request: count **2 → 3**. The strict no-new-model-request assertion failed. Generic root-session continuation is documented, intentional behavior; the extra inference is not proof of duplicate external side effects (tools were disabled). The proven mismatch is that the A2A wrapper publishes terminal failure while the canonical core owner continues recovery. This candidate is **not ready** until those owners are coordinated. The source path is `session-restart-resume.ts` orphaned-run recovery → `enqueueSessionEventForHost(... source: "restart")`; the generic skip predicate does not exclude A2A. No global recovery behavior has been changed.
- **Owner decision required:** either (1) the core owner settles the interrupted A2A run without enqueueing a restart input while normal chat recovery remains unchanged, or (2) core continuation retains durable task correlation and reattaches completion to the original Task ID/peer/message identity. The missing contract is who owns restart policy and terminal publication for task-owned channels, and how core resumed turns carry durable correlation back to that task owner. A blanket A2A skip is insufficient because the current skip predicate also bypasses orphan-run settlement; unrelated `modelSelectionLocked` settings and global recovery suppression are not suitable substitutes.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passed on this head (2m59.7s). The earlier process/storage and HTTP-handler proofs below remain valid at their stated boundaries; they do not establish this missing whole-Gateway behavior.
- **Red on base `99f4ff69c621e6cb67b10514502fb1922deee547`:** the owning HTTP-handler restart regression returned `-32001 Task not found` for the original task. It passes with this change and verifies peer isolation and no replay dispatch.
- **Actual process-crash red/green:** separate Node 24.22.1 processes used production `A2aTaskStore` and `PluginStateKeyedStoreV2` against synthetic SQLite state, with `SIGKILL` after acknowledged `start()`. The base lost the original ID and admitted a new task for the replay. This candidate preserved the ID, returned the explicit ambiguous failure, denied another peer, and returned no dispatch admission on replay. All four processes exited and their state was removed. This is process/storage proof, not a Gateway HTTP/agent/model E2E; no external effects ran. The copied base module changed only SDK import locations, preserving its logic.
- **79 focused tests pass** across `task-store`, `task-store.persistence`, `http`, `inbound`, and `gateway`, using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. Coverage includes durable admission before first/duplicate responses, shutdown during admission, real-store capacity refusal/retry, uncertain acknowledgements, and stale cleanup versus newer pending/completed tasks. The latter two recovery-priority cases were also observed failing before the repair.
- Scoped TypeScript proof covering all A2A sources/tests and ambient declarations passes through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`. Targeted repository lint, formatting, commit-hook docs/line checks, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet pass. The exact-head [product CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42398131930) was skipped for this draft; CI seconds are unmeasured.
- Per-file `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times: task store **81.87 s**, real storage **31.10 s**, inbound **64.92 s**, HTTP **18.57 s**. Cold transform/import preparation dominates these runs; test execution per file stays below 5 seconds. The real-storage test uses the existing database-worker lane because mock storage cannot prove admission capacity or durable recovery.
- Fresh independent Codex review of the complete change against the base: **no remaining actionable findings** after the recovery-priority repair. This is an independent agent review, not a ClawSweeper or autoreview CLI result.
- `pr-simplify`: one existing task owner and the existing keyed-state API serve admission, settlement, and recovery. Shared in-memory deletion logic was consolidated. Production delta **+123/-23 (net +100)**; test/support delta **+273/-34 (net +239)**. The separate 239-line allocation covers only this change's justified regressions; no shared baseline was raised.

prs.title: fix(ci): stabilize tooling duration regression across inventory changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the selected-tooling duration regression failing scheduled main CI as the repository's test inventory changes. Related: [failed main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42401234392/job/128489494460), introduced by the test in #194290.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. CI continues checking measured-subset pricing and unknown-file fallback costs without relying on the incidental size of a live tooling stripe.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test mocked measured timings but left fallback weights and stripe membership dependent on the checkout. Its hybrid unknown-timing case could legitimately cost 16 seconds, violating the test's assumption that the stripe always costs more than the 25-second measured-selection startup floor. Local reproduction likewise failed at `25 > 25`.

Pin unknown tooling-file weights to 60 seconds, retain the original `>25` assertion, and additionally require `>=60` so dropping an indivisible fallback cost still fails. Measured selection must still cost exactly 25 seconds. Production pricing, budgets, and thresholds are unchanged.

Simplification: no production machinery added; production delta 0, test delta +4. The separate four-line test allocation credits exactly this fixture repair and stronger fallback assertion; the shared scalar stays unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sessions): include archive metadata in JSON listings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users listing sessions with `openclaw sessions list --json` could not distinguish archived sessions from active sessions because the JSON omitted `archived` and `archivedAt`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing archive timestamp through the shared display row, using the same presence check as the Gateway, including timestamp zero. Remove the one-use JSON helper and reuse the prepared model reference; production code decreases by three lines. Recorded runtime provenance remains unchanged, so this addresses only the archive metadata portion of [#124524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124524).

## User Impact

Single-agent and all-agent JSON inventories expose archive status while preserving existing model, provider, token, count and pagination fields. Internal display fields remain omitted. Thanks [@wangyan2026](https://github.com/wangyan2026) for the original fix and regression.

Related: [#124524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124524)

## Evidence

The [baseline run](https://github.com/steipete/openclaw/actions/runs/34316928126) built successfully and captured five missing-field observations: three shared-row projections and two real single-agent CLI rows. The job failed afterward because its preservation assertion rejected newly created empty WAL and shared-memory files; the main database bytes were unchanged. The later all-agent listing and post-read checks did not run.

Full source autoreview and both fresh committed-head reviews completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Pending: the independently reviewed combined proof retains those five observations, completes the missing baseline coverage, and checks the candidate through shared-row and real single/all-agent CLI flows with full-entry readbacks and complete database-image preservation. Candidate runtime results, repository tests/changed checks, exact-head CI and native landing are not yet complete.

## Real Behavior Proof

This section completes the after-fix CLI proof that the `## Evidence` section above marked as pending. The candidate runtime results below were captured against head `92025ff2dde787febc1cf9ed878957b2e75bc95f` (the current PR head after rebase).

**Behavior addressed**: `openclaw sessions list --json` omitted `archived` and `archivedAt` from each session row, so archived sessions were indistinguishable from active sessions in the CLI JSON inventory. After this patch, the shared display projection carries both fields through to single-agent and all-agent JSON output.

**Real environment tested**: Local checkout of `openclaw/openclaw` at commit `92025ff2dde`, branch `fix/sessions-list-archive-runtime-124524`, running the CLI via `node --import tsx src/index.ts` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-proof` state directory. A SQLite session store was seeded with one archived session (`archivedAt` set to 1 hour ago) and one active session (no `archivedAt`), then read back through the real `sessions list` command path — not through unit-test mocks.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
# 1. Seed an isolated session store with one archived + one active session
#    (via the source SessionEntry writer, not a mock)
node --import tsx /tmp/create-archived-session-all.mts
# -> Store created at: /tmp/openclaw-proof/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/sessions.json

# 2. Single-agent JSON listing
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-proof node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions list --json

# 3. All-agent JSON listing
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-proof node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions list --json --all-agents
```

**Evidence after fix**: Single-agent listing (`sessions list --json`):

```json
{

  "count": 2,
  "totalCount": 2,
  "limitApplied": 100,
  "hasMore": false,

    {

    },

```

All-agent listing (`sessions list --json --all-agents`):

```json

  "path": null,
  "stores": [
    {
      "agentId": "main",
      "path": "/tmp/openclaw-proof/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite"
```

prs.title: fix: node approvals fail to save when the deletion journal is missing
prs.body:
Closes #192227

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: node approvals fail to save when the state database never received the agent deletion journal.

## User Impact

User impact: on a node whose state was created by native bootstrap before the journal backfill, `exec.approvals.node.set` now works instead of failing with a SQLite error, and the Control UI save persists. No action needed from users; the repair runs once at startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway only forwards `system.execApprovals.set` to the node, so the failing database is the node's. Its state was built by native bootstrap, which used to create the catalog without the `agent_deletion_journal` table, and later migrations never backfilled it for databases that already existed. The mutation fence queries that table on every approvals save, so every write threw before it could reach the fence.

This fixes the initialization path instead of bypassing the fence. At startup, after the native init, the node checks read-only whether the journal is missing, and if it is, creates the empty table and records a migration receipt. It refuses when a prior Doctor reconstruction or an earlier backfill is recorded and the table is missing again, so a second disappearance stays Doctor-owned. The check runs read-only first so startup never opens an unrecognized database for write. An empty journal is neutral for the fence: a mutation is allowed when no journal row exists for the agent, and a deletion can only begin when the journal exists, so nothing here weakens deletion authority.

## Evidence

Reproduced the production error on the September 25 codebase first: after native bootstrap init, saving an approvals allowlist threw `UNAVAILABLE: Error: no such table: agent_deletion_journal` from the mutation fence. After the fix the same save succeeds. On that codebase the recovery, startup, node-worker-bootstrap, and exec-approvals suites pass (119 tests) and oxlint is clean on the changed files.

Ported to current main with every import and signature checked against the current files, and the new tests use the existing harnesses in each file. The full suite on this exact head is for CI here, since the port targets a moving main.

prs.title: fix: reduce plugin preparation overhead in agent runs with fallbacks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated plugin auto-enable work during agent runs with configured fallback models, even when the primary model succeeds.

## User Impact

Agent runs reuse prepared plugin activation decisions across an unchanged runtime generation, reducing CPU and allocation without changing which plugins activate. Config reloads still take effect, including when the publisher reuses the same mutable config object. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fallback rate-limit preparation reaches the bundled-compatibility activation owner through provider model normalization. Its existing memo expires after one event-loop turn, so each run repeats candidate materialization and creates another plugin-policy normalization input.

The existing plugin metadata cache now owns generation-long reuse, keyed by captured config, metadata, environment publication, registry/discovery facts, and ambient-trigger policy. Rewritten runtime captures reuse the existing immutable normalization projection. Mutable setup inputs retain their same-turn behavior. The change adds 76 net production lines to preserve both publication and setup semantics; it adds no polling, independent cache lifecycle, config setting, or storage schema.

## Evidence

- Regression exercises real `runWithModelFallback` across event-loop turns: the exact parent materializes three times for three runs; the fix materializes once. Changed config and metadata generations trigger fresh decisions. Both published mutable and frozen inputs are covered.
- 113 focused tests pass, including plugin activation/lifecycle siblings and the prompt-prefix contract. Codex autoreview of the repaired complete candidate is clean through P2.
- Five alternating AB/BA pairs plus starting/ending A/A controls: direct activation sampled allocation 329,002 → 1,535 B/run (−99.53%); full `runWithModelFallback` preparation 2,353,152 → 1,592,047 B/run (−32.34%). Main-thread CPU medians are 201 → 9 µs and 2,063 → 1,634 µs respectively. Every paired CPU result improves, but ending runner CPU A/A differs by 24.6% under shared-host contention, so the runner CPU figure is not a precise portable speedup. Allocation controls are steadier (0.32% direct / 0.025% runner spread); all runner allocation pairs improve 31.9–32.6%. Heap sampling includes GC-collected objects. Independent V8 coverage over three runner calls confirms materializations 3 → 1 and plugin-entry normalizations 100 → 28.
- `pnpm check:changed` ran all 38 stages. A benchmark-only type error was fixed and its typecheck/lint replay passed. Remaining failures reproduce on exact parent `83f7614cc70d136f5e32d6357c6b67f39e985187`: dead exports introduced by #194245 (`5577faefa9e12`) and #194676 (`055544b9fa35`), and 20 historical changelog attribution entries rejected by the gate introduced in #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`). These are tracked main regressions; #194800 addresses the export owners. Both standalone-script unused-file scans pass.

The synthetic benchmark is committed at `scripts/perf/model-fallback-activation-inputs.ts`. It uses 40 plugin entries, six configured channels, two model candidates, and one auto-enable rewrite with published mutable config. It measures preparation with a no-op model callback; it does not measure inference or whole-Gateway throughput. This path does not read session databases or enumerate workspace files. Cold fixture captures include inherited catalog-label filesystem reads; an isolated cold outlier did not reproduce in A/A/B/B repeats, and no startup-speedup claim is made. No production data or live service access was used.


The initial PR head exposed a static/type import cycle that the runtime-only cycle check did not detect. The repair moves `AmbientEnvTriggerPolicy` into an import-free leaf contract and makes the plugin activation owner pass captured config, cache, metadata, and environment keys into config policy. `check-madge-import-cycles.ts` and `check-import-cycles.ts` both report zero cycles; the existing behavioral tests are unchanged. Core typecheck and targeted lint pass, and the independent three-run count remains one materialization / 28 normalizations. The five-pair timing/allocation matrix above was measured on the initial implementation; this ownership repair preserves its preparation algorithm and work counts.

Closes #180755. Related: #157466.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators with large model catalogues need a personal shortlist they can curate directly while choosing a model.

## User Impact

User impact: click the inline heart beside a model to add or remove a favourite without selecting the model or closing the picker. Favourites appear first and remain available in their provider groups. The Favourites heading uses the same heart icon; there is no separate Manage favourites editor.

Favourites retain this PR's personal, per-signed-in-profile and per-agent scope, persist across reloads and browsers through existing user preferences, and do not change model availability or selection policy. Shared-agent curation and hiding models remain outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

This updates the existing contribution rather than adding a competing implementation. It retains conditional user-preference writes and canonical model/runtime identities, while separating presentation keys so a favourite can safely appear in multiple groups. Inline hearts have accessible pressed state and do not trigger model selection. Keyboard navigation, large-catalogue virtualization and provider settings remain owned by the picker.

Original implementation by @Alix-007. Inline-heart interaction, duplicate provider listing and consistent heart icons requested by @jacobtomlinson; follow-up implementation by @roboclaw-bot. Original contributor commits and history are preserved.

## Work sessions

prs.title: improve(knowledge): open Browse without scanning unrelated stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Knowledge Recent or Browse waits for record counts from every running store, although those views do not display those counts. An unrelated populated store can hold the whole page in its loading skeleton.

## User Impact

Browsing no longer scans unrelated stores before loading the selected agent's view. Settings retain live counts. No configuration, permission, storage-format, or visual-design changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing inventory operation accepts optional `includeRecordCounts`, defaulting to the current behavior. Browse refresh requests metadata without counts; the same owner still constructs and authorizes the inventory. Unrequested counts remain `null`, not cached.

First layer of a measured performance stack; #194796 follows it. Vyctor authorized landing both on November 7 at 20:38 UTC, superseding the earlier hold.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway/WebSocket proof: two synthetic stores, 8,000 valid records each, changed before the request. Counting inventory: **1,528 ms**. Metadata-only inventory: **100 ms first request / 2 ms subsequent request**. These are directional inventory RPC timings, not full browser paint timings or a statistical qualification.
- Service regression: browse inventory makes **zero storage calls**; default settings retain live counts. Red on the original code.
- UI regression verifies the actual request opts out of counts.
- After consolidating duplicate fixtures, **34 store/UI tests passed on the supported Node lane**. Full extension test typing passed; the test-line ratchet has nine lines of slack. The initial Bun retry stalled during setup; it was not counted as a passing test run.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Required GitHub checks are green on head `5e7afcc0c1d2eff0d00efe2efa83f9199f7ee7bf`.
- Independent local autoreview: no actionable findings in the diff. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable in this checkout.
- Type-aware lint reports a pre-existing `no-redundant-type-constituents` error at `page-refresh.ts:21`; reproduced on the original file and not suppressed here.

Limits: selected-store cold catalog scans remain. Real Gateway API and DOM-mounted UI tests were exercised; full browser rendering was not measured. Further cold-load profiling is continuing separately.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(ui): reduce shared control requests on first page visits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

First visits acquired small shared-control requests that can occupy HTTP connection slots and delay the page's own CSS or JavaScript by another response interval. Current-main request timestamps reproduce the queueing; discovery itself is early.

## User Impact

This removes the standalone Switch request and lets Dashboard/Custodian use keyboard radio navigation without loading Radio's stylesheet. In the 20-pair desktop comparison at simulated 100 ms RTT, full-content medians improve by 10.5–22.2% in the affected engine/route cells. Other RTT cells remain within the timing band. Tags, markup, keyboard behavior, and lazy page boundaries are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch and `settings-ui` form a cross-chunk cycle through `liveChecked`; they now share the existing lazy `settings-controls-runtime`. The unchanged `nextRadio` helper moves to plain TypeScript in `navigation-helpers`, with all five internal consumers migrated. The existing emitted-graph regression now guards Switch/liveChecked co-location and the helper mapping.

Checkbox already belongs to neutral deferred support, and InlineAlert loads through a genuine shell dependency. Provider presentation stays in its intentional 651 B gzip chunk. Even the smallest alternative (`navigation-helpers`) would add about 1 KB to lightweight pickers and lazy Chat icons without removing their request; deferred support adds about 33 KB. A blanket controls group would mix eager and lazy owners.

Related: #194116, #194145, #194393.

## Evidence

Base: `fe2b1a51b41b80941fe93cfb0dfbdc0def2401d1`. Candidate source: `e14f5b1c2699492eacefb9d5ba6a4c973d1177d4`. Frozen bundles were built on this Mac; the candidate was captured immediately before committing identical source bytes. No size ceiling or baseline changes.

The current-main screen passed 48/48 observations. Main acceptance passed **2,880/2,880**: eight routes × three engines × localhost/100 ms RTT × 20 rotated base/head/independent-base-control pairs. Full content is browser-local application time to the complete synthetic fixture over two ready frames. Simulated RTT delays HTTP responses and incoming mock Gateway frames; there is no throughput cap or live-provider latency claim. Host: 32 logical CPUs, Darwin arm64; one-minute load ranged 9.72–29.68.

The statistical comparison is desktop (1440×1000). Mobile (390×844) receives a three-arm resource/visual screen. Native CPU counters are available only in Chromium here: median renderer task CPU deltas range −2.5% to +3.4% across the matrix. WebKit/Firefox results below are application elapsed time, not CPU.

| Mobile resource/visual screen | 72/72 passed; inspected captures, 22/24 pixel-identical pairs; two Lobsterdex pairs differ by less than 0.004% |
| CSS/request audit | No added CSS in any of 48 desktop groups; no standalone Switch; no Radio JS/CSS on Dashboard or Custodian |
| Channels requalification | 120/120 passed; details below |
| PR CI | [Run 42415173524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42415173524), exact reviewed head: success; 41 jobs successful, 26 skipped, no failures. Merged as `23f2cd68e9d38bbffe561bada8eab5a72b9af110`. |

| Built surface | Base | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup JavaScript gzip | 90,900 B | 90,910 B | +10 B (within 64 B build variance) |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Startup CSS gzip | 39,090 B | 39,090 B | 0 |
| New Session boot JavaScript gzip | 803,127 B | 803,034 B | −93 B |
| Chat boot JavaScript gzip | 1,294,914 B | 1,294,759 B | −155 B |

Both builds pass. Strict head-vs-base performance check passes with zero violations. The base alone exceeds existing document/CSS/Chat fixed caps; no cap is raised. All CSS build bytes are unchanged. The per-route table explicitly retains the small fetched-byte increases where Switch co-location trades bytes for fewer requests.

Touched production LOC: **2,602 → 2,605 (+3)**; test LOC +11 with an exact scoped allocation. Existing `untrack` 1→1; no new controller, effect, render effect, listener, DOM query, flush, or owner capture.

### Localhost tail qualification

The original 20-pair results and every follow-up remain separate in the evidence; slow observations were not removed.

| WebKit localhost, 30 samples per arm | Base median / p95 | Head median / p95 | A/A median / p95 | Assessment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Dashboard | 150.5 / 200 | 153 / 203 | 142 / 175 | +1.7% median, +1.5% p95; within band |
| Custodian | 192 / 214 | 196 / 224 | 195 / 206 | +2.1% median, +4.7% p95; within band |
| Debug | 131.5 / 145 | 132 / 153 | 133 / 165 | Flat median; +5.5% p95 is inside the worse +13.8% A/A tail |

Firefox Debug needed a causal check. Original 20 plus 10 extra samples had three slow head observations (347–424 ms), with p95 135 → 380 ms. Reversing only bundle assignments in the same committed workload reproduced the same delayed-first-request signature on **base bytes in server/arm 1**, while both candidate arms remained fast:

| Reversed roles, 20 samples per arm | Bytes | Median / p95 / max ms |
|---|---|---:|
| Server/arm 0 | Candidate | 85 / 97 / 98 |
| Server/arm 1 | Base | 90.5 / 101 / 343 |
| Server/arm 2 | Candidate control | 88.5 / 108 / 110 |

The slow reversed-base sample ran first in its rotated pair, so this is not simply a second-in-execution-order effect. This supports a measurement-slot cause rather than attributing those tails to candidate source. It does not identify the lower-level Firefox/server scheduling cause; one original base observation also stalled. Native Firefox CPU/long-task data remains unavailable. No production workaround or timing sample exclusion was added.

The primary workload was:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .artifacts/base-dist --compare-bundle-dir .artifacts/head-dist \
  --control-bundle-dir .artifacts/base-dist \
  --source-root . --compare-source-root . --control-source-root . \
  --steps page-debug-visit,page-custodian-visit,page-dashboards-visit,page-lobsterdex-visit,page-memory-import-visit,page-skills-visit,page-skill-settings-visit,page-talk-visit \
  --engines chromium,webkit,firefox --network-profiles localhost,rtt-100ms \
  --viewport desktop --pairs 20 --output .artifacts/acceptance
```

The mobile screen uses the same three bundles with `--viewport mobile --pairs 1 --network-profiles rtt-100ms`. Localhost extensions use ten pairs on the named WebKit/Firefox cases. The Firefox role check uses 20 pairs with head/base/head as the three bundle arguments. All browsers were headless. No remote lease was used.

### Channels

The old 214/204 px vertical content shift did not recur in 20 current-main observations per engine and viewport. Chromium mobile has 0/20 native CLS events; desktop has 2/20 tiny horizontal header shifts, maximum CLS 0.00318. That residual differs from the old failure and remains documented; no Channels code changed. WebKit and Firefox do not expose native CLS in this harness, so their values are unavailable, not zero.
