Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser tool reports a crashed tab as a generic 20 s timeout and tells the agent the whole browser is unavailable, even though the browser and its other tabs keep working. `navigate` on a crashed target waits the full request budget, and the tab list gives no hint that the target is dead.

## User Impact

User impact: a crashed tab now fails fast with tab-scoped guidance to open the page in a new tab (or retry once a busy page settles), instead of steering the agent into browser-wide troubleshooting. `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `navigate` all take that path; `tabs` marks targets observed as crashed in both the JSON payload and the CLI text output, and implicit tab selection prefers a healthy tab. Existing-session and extension-relay drivers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A crashed renderer leaves its Chrome target listed while every page-level CDP command stalls. Snapshots waited out the full action budget and then attached the browser-wide unavailability hint, and `navigate` timed out the same way. The fix adds one bounded `Page.getFrameTree` liveness probe before snapshot and navigate work, maps Playwright `Target crashed` errors to a 409 with tab-scoped recovery text, and keeps the observed crash on the tab record for listing, the CLI handle list, and implicit selection. A dead renderer and a long-blocked main thread look the same to that probe, so the wording names both and suggests a retry once the page settles. Snapshot media helpers moved to a sibling module to stay under the file line cap.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/target-crash.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.local-managed.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.selection.crash.test.ts` — 6 files, 93 tests passed.
- Real renderer crash (gated Chromium test, system Chrome): `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CRASH_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=... pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.chromium.test.ts` — `Page.crash` then probe rejects with `BrowserTargetCrashedError` inside the bounded probe window.
- Independent live check by @wr-web (`Page.crash` + CLI on Windows) confirmed snapshot/screenshot on `906d205`; their navigate and tab-list findings are wired in `76b7e18520f` and `905b07cae7b`.
- Base behavior reproduced locally: after `Page.crash`, the listed page's WebSocket accepts connections but `Page.getFrameTree`, `Runtime.evaluate`, and `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` never answer; a healthy page answers in milliseconds.
- `pnpm check:changed` — all checks pass except the repo-wide `changelog attributions` check, which already fails on `origin/main` from untouched `CHANGELOG/` files (no changelog changes in this PR). The test-line allocation is sized to the final diff so the baseline ratchet stays at its existing slack.
- Gap: no full Gateway + agent turn was run; request-boundary behavior is covered by the route tests and the real Chromium probe test.

prs.title: fix: worker turns fail before inference when web search is offered
prs.body:
Closes #182647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running an agent turn on a cloud worker or a paired device node would see the turn fail before any model request when `web_search` was offered. The gateway reported `Session capability metadata requires worker preparation` for the dashboard session, and the placement never reached inference. The same agent and model succeeded for a gateway-local session. Denying `web_search` made the worker turn succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Worker inference resolved native search policy synchronously without the session capability preparation the local runner already uses. The admitted tool surface is resolved first, then that synchronous policy call is prepared through the existing capability-read owner. Permission checks and live execution authority stay as they are.

Completion-announce delivery, restart-recovery classification, and transcript stale-base-leaf handling are out of scope. Those shapes on this issue, including the local completion-announce reports and #177477 / #192595, need their own repairs. Merged #186238 preserves prepared reads across model changes for completion announces and child follow-ups; it does not cover this first-turn worker policy path.

## User Impact

Worker-hosted and device-hosted dashboard turns can start inference when `web_search` is offered, including when durable dashboard metadata denies search. Search stays unavailable when the tool is not offered or stored policy denies it. Operators no longer need to deny `web_search` only to get a first turn.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

Original unit-test evidence was collected against `1f94418f19af0b83edd8698bd4d567b529da0167`. This branch is rebased onto `4cedec0f47a5fbd24046e9a3cfe73fe92bee116e`.

Before this change, `executePreparedWorkerInference` called `applyExtraParamsToAgent` at `src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-runtime.ts:217` with no capability-read preparation. A regression through that owner wrote a real SQLite dashboard row (`agent:main:dashboard:worker-search-policy`, spawn envelope, `inheritedToolDeny: ["web_search"]`) and offered `web_search`, with no ambient prepared read and no committed projection. The turn rejected before the provider stream:

```text
Error: Session capability metadata requires worker preparation
```

The stack entered from `inference-runtime.ts:217` through `applyExtraParamsToAgent` → `isNativeWebSearchAllowedByToolPolicy` → `resolveWebSearchToolPolicy` → `resolveRequesterToolPolicies` → `resolvePersistedSubagentToolPolicyEnvelope` → `resolveSessionCapabilityEntry`.

Command:

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-runtime.test.ts -t "durable dashboard capability" --maxWorkers=1
```

After the repair, that command passes on the final tree. The shipped executor returns a completed inference result, the real policy function is called with `webSearchEnabled: true` for that dashboard key, and it returns false from the durable deny. The provider stream runs once.

Stubbed: model catalog and auth admission, the provider stream, and the worker tool-surface owner (it returns one `web_search` tool definition). Not stubbed: `applyExtraParamsToAgent`, `isNativeWebSearchAllowedByToolPolicy`, requester and search policy resolution, and the session capability read of the SQLite row written with `replaceSessionEntry`.

This is the shipped entry point because the test calls `executeWorkerInference`, which the turn owner binds to `executePreparedWorkerInference`. It does not reimplement the policy call.

Also passed on this tree:

- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-runtime.test.ts src/agents/requester-tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-capabilities.store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (44, 28, and 20 passed)
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (14 passed)
- `pnpm run tsgo:core`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the two changed files
- `pnpm format` on those files, then `git diff --check`

### Live Gateway and paired session-host proof

Reproduced on 2026-11-07 on a disposable Linux host with a loopback Gateway and a paired session-host node. `settings.inference` was left unset, so default paired-device placement kept inference on the Gateway (`executePreparedWorkerInference`). Each turn used a fresh dashboard session after `sessions.dispatch` reported `placement.state: "active"` and `runner.kind: "device"`. The selected model was `openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`. `web_search` was offered through `tools.profile: "full"` and the bundled DuckDuckGo search provider. Node v24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0.

- Unpatched main `055544b9fa35317f2cf19c0f74736edd0ba9e0ea` (no `withPreparedSessionCapabilityRead` wrap in `src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-runtime.ts`), `web_search` offered: `agent.wait` failed, and the Gateway log contained `Session capability metadata requires worker preparation`.
- Same main commit, with `tools.deny: ["web_search"]`: `agent.wait` completed with visible reply `PONG`. The preparation error was absent.
- This change (live-tested at `c0f05cda9568aeffb7ec7ccecbff25039a54fb59`, rebased to `1243da476c5074899a3b7a95ace5164cb9bc1792`, wrap present at the `applyExtraParamsToAgent` call), `web_search` offered: `agent.wait` completed with visible reply `PONG`. The preparation error was absent.

This does not claim a live web search. It shows a first worker turn can reach inference when search is offered.

The change prepares the existing synchronous search-policy read and does not broaden tool access.

prs.title: fix(ui): People and session hovercards switch to other rows while moving to them
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the sidebar People list and the session list, moving the mouse diagonally from a row toward its hovercard crosses other rows, and each crossed row immediately replaces the card. Today you have to steer straight across your own row to reach the card. Session links share the session hovercard and had the same problem.

## User Impact

User impact: you can move straight toward a person's or a session's card, even across other rows, and the card stays. Moving straight down the list still switches cards right away, and stopping on a row switches to that row.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared portaled hovercard owner now has a safe-triangle hover-intent check, the same corridor Zag uses for the submenus we already ship (Zag's `isPointInPolygon` ray casting over the card's near edge). When a mouse leaves the trigger while its card is open:

- The corridor runs from the pointer's last point inside the trigger to the card's near edge, and includes the card. While the pointer stays inside it, the card stays open.
- Any trigger crossed on the way waits. It takes over only when the pointer rests on it for 150 ms or leaves the corridor while still over it.
- If the pointer leaves the corridor anywhere else, the card closes normally.

Gotchas from Floating UI `safePolygon`, Amazon's menu-aim, and our own testing:

- **Sparse samples:** fast moves can land the exit event well past the row edge and off the line toward the card. So the corridor apex is the last point *inside* the trigger, clamped to the trigger, not the exit point.
- **Boundary jitter:** the apex backs off 4 px from its edge so that jitter on the edge stays inside.
- **Adjacent triggers:** this is the case where Floating UI added `requireIntent`. We switch on rest instead of on cursor speed, so careful, slow movement toward the card still counts as intent.
- **No pointer-events blocking:** we don't block pointer events (Floating UI's `blockPointerEvents` side effects). Crossed rows still show hover styles; only the card handoff waits.
- **Touch and window exits:** touch input and leaving the window keep the existing 220 ms timed close. Only mouse and pen exits that the owner can observe use the corridor.

Two consumers use the corridor:

- **People rows** (first commit).
- **Session rows and session links**. The session hovercard provider passes pointer exits to `schedulePointerExit(event)`, and a target hovered while the pointer is still heading to the open card goes through `deferPointerSwitch`. Rows and links share one provider, so both get the behavior.

Other hovercard consumers keep the old `schedulePointerExit()` behavior.

## Evidence

People:

- New Control UI e2e `sidebar-users-filter.e2e.test.ts` › "keeps a person card while the pointer crosses other people toward it", driven by real Playwright mouse moves on a paused virtual clock. It covers three paths:
  1. A diagonal path to the card's lower half across Bob and Jacqueline keeps Ada's card.
  2. A straight sweep from Ada to Bob switches within the normal 80 ms.
  3. Resting on Bob inside the corridor hands the card to Bob after the rest delay.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs with new-tab recovery guidance
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

When a Chromium renderer crashes, browser requests can wait for a timeout and tell the agent that the entire browser is unavailable, even though healthy tabs and newly opened tabs still work

## User Impact

Crashed tabs now return prompt, consistent guidance to open the URL in a new tab, including a screenshot requested before the automation connection attaches

Known crashed targets remain visible and closable, and implicit selection preserves the selected tab identity instead of redirecting actions to another page

Tab crash markers reflect observations from persistent automation connections — a raw screenshot-only failure returns the crash error immediately but does not persist a list marker until normal automation observes the target

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native crash facts in the existing CDP connection lifecycle and carry them through the existing `ACT_OPERATION_FAILED` error contract

The raw screenshot adapter enables Inspector before sending page commands, while snapshot metadata fallbacks preserve terminal crash errors and cold-crashed targets can be closed through their browser owner

## Evidence

- Reproduced on unmodified `c25ff93b56723e0075a4c82a789ac3b1acd06aeb` with a real managed browser: crashed-tab snapshot timed out after 20,012 ms with browser-unavailable guidance, while a healthy sibling and a replacement tab remained usable
- Committed request and output regressions failed on the original behavior, with separate real-browser reproduction of the screenshot-first cold path
- Final real-browser cold screenshot-first validation returned the correct crash error in 7 ms, with later snapshot, screenshot and navigation errors in 3 ms each
- Complete persistent enumeration, healthy sibling access, replacement-tab recovery and crashed-target closure passed, with the target confirmed absent after close
- Browser package run: 3,151 passed and 108 skipped, with two fixture-isolation failures subsequently repaired — all seven affected connection suites then passed, 105 tests total
- Browser production types, extension test types, typed lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line checks passed

Live validation used headless Chrome 157 on macOS with Node 24.22.1 — Linux headed mode and live existing-session or extension-relay drivers were not exercised

## What Problem This Solves

Restoring a cached conversation can leave its URL on the previous agent after the Gateway resolves it to a moved session. Persisted sidebar admission could canonicalize the URL before authority settled and then ignore a moved identity.

## User Impact

Cached conversations still render immediately. URL replacement and message delivery wait for confirmed identity; deleted or moved results replace the cached view. Confirmed current-connection handoffs avoid duplicate discovery, including when their row still comes from storage. No configuration or storage changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing route loader confirms both persisted-roster and transcript-snapshot admission. The shell and pane consume the same provisional marker. The existing handoff owner supplies its current-connection fact so an authoritative canonical replacement is not mistaken for another unconfirmed cache load. URL-only hints retain verification.

The cache-verifier split originated in [8e639ee](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8e639ee1203408d55cd2449ddee3fe399f99cbc9), later exposed by live title synchronization. The fix does not alter #191795's operator Home privacy hunks.

Its artifact records the old agent's title URL and no moved-agent navigation.

prs.title: fix: reuse restored Anthropic history across tool turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restored Anthropic sessions repeatedly encode large historical tool results during tool loops because final history preparation seals assistant messages but leaves restored user/tool-result messages mutable.

## User Impact

Repeated requests reuse unchanged history fragments without changing prompt-cache bytes. In a synthetic ~200-message session, warm main-thread CPU falls **44%** and sampled JS allocation **85%**. The median paired one-time cold increase is **1.33 ms**, below the **3.52 ms saved per warm request**. No configuration or migration is needed.

**Tradeoff:** the median of each run's maximum warm latency rises from **8.66 to 12.56 ms**, with larger GC pauses. This meets the explicitly selected cold/warm payback criterion; it is not an across-the-board tail-latency improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing final-publication owner now seals user and tool-result history alongside assistants, after writable replay/context-engine edits. Hydration stays writable, custom messages stay unchanged, and later prompt edits continue to replace messages. Responses consumes the same source immutability contract; no separate Responses cache was added.

Cold fragment creation uses the already-proved-equal editable hook copy, synchronously before yielding, with the frozen source as the existing cache key. This avoids encoding frozen arrays on V8's slow JSON path without letting later mutations of a hook's retained copy poison cached bytes. Edited/replacement/opaque hooks still use full serialization. The byte-fragment cache remains a single existing WeakMap.

Production delta **+19 lines**: +3 for the explicit publication role boundary and +16 for early fragment creation with a shared cache-miss implementation. Keeping the equality check and byte creation in one synchronous section is necessary; encoding the mutable copy after an await would violate the cache-key contract. Tests add **127 net lines**, covered by the scoped allocation record for multi-turn byte/reuse and retained-hook-copy ownership regressions.

## Evidence

Acceptance fixed before the final run: identical bytes, at least N−2 historical fragments reused, lower warm CPU/allocation, and the one-time preparation+first-request CPU increase below one warm request's CPU saving (or within control noise). All five pairs individually meet that payback rule.

Real transcript append → writable restoration → attempt preparation → LLM boundary → Anthropic transport. Synthetic fetch consumes the actual Blob and returns SSE. Initial history: 199 messages, 99 tool results with 40 KiB text; each process appends 20 tool turns. Node **26.12.1**, V8 **14.6.202.34**, macOS arm64. Five serial AB/BA pairs plus A/A and B/B controls; CPU runs untraced, allocation sampled separately including collected objects. No live-provider or whole-Gateway latency claim.

| Metric (median of five processes) | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Frozen source messages | 99/199 | 199/199 |
| Stable source identities | 199/199 | 199/199 |
| Historical fragments reused on next request | 99/199 | **197/199** |
| Message encodes on next request | 102 | **4** |
| Full-body fallback encodes | 0 | 0 |
| Cold preparation CPU | 5.505 ms | 5.997 ms |
| Cold first-request CPU | 8.215 ms | 8.552 ms |
| Warm main-thread CPU/request | 7.985 ms | **4.455 ms** |
| Warm sampled JS allocation/request | 20.706 MB | **3.079 MB** |
| Warm wall/request | 8.024 ms | 4.475 ms |
| Maximum of 20 warm requests | 8.656 ms | 12.555 ms |
| Total GC over 20 warm requests | 5.474 ms | 10.546 ms |

The workload's `p95Ms` field uses `floor(n * .95)` and therefore reports the **maximum for 20 samples**. The cold request is excluded. This is not a population p95 estimate. Median paired cold delta is 1.327 ms versus 3.515 ms warm CPU saving; differences of independent column medians are a different statistic.

<details>
<summary>Pairs, controls, byte proof, and reproduction</summary>

| Pair/order | Cold CPU delta | Warm CPU saved/request |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 / AB | 3.084 ms | 3.515 ms |
| 2 / BA | 1.327 ms | 2.436 ms |
| 3 / AB | 0.626 ms | 3.467 ms |
| 4 / BA | 1.424 ms | 3.755 ms |
| 5 / AB | 0.607 ms | 3.685 ms |

A/A controls: cold total 14.590/13.948 ms, warm CPU 8.595/8.108 ms, warm allocation 20.718/20.779 MB. B/B controls: cold total 14.729/13.550 ms, warm CPU 3.958/3.951 ms, warm allocation 3.097/3.084 MB. Host 1-minute load ranged 10.27–31.66; all runs retain that metadata. The byte-proof fixture is released and zero retained source WeakRefs are asserted before measurement.

Initial, appended-turn, and final SHA-256 hashes match across all 28 processes; initial/final bodies are 4,239,745/5,096,221 bytes. The regression compares actual multi-turn transport bodies before/after publication and bounds second-turn encodes at four. On exact parent `f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1`, it fails with 101 > 4 encodes. Retained-hook-copy coverage ensures a later edit cannot change checked history bytes or poison a later request.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/anthropic-request-construction.ts --restored --iterations 20
```

Add `--allocation` separately. For baseline, add `--baseline-dir <baseline-overlay>` containing the exact parent's two production files at their repository-relative paths: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-history-prepare.ts` and `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-request-body.ts`. The committed workload supports both arms. Node CPU profiles confirm substantially fewer serializer/encoding samples; profiled timings are not used for acceptance.

V8 contract inspected at the [pinned Node source](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.12.1/deps/v8/src/json/json-stringifier.cc#L2789-L2819). A hydration-only brand was rejected because nested model views must remain writable; lazy freezing of fresh wire messages is too late to preserve the converted source identity. A split-comma Blob pilot did not improve cold cost and is excluded.

Reuse is within a prepared attempt. Separate hydrations still create private model views. No new cache, configuration, schema, or public API was added.

</details>

Validation: **144 focused tests**, **1 UI browser test**, and **10 UI E2E tests** passed locally. Final Codex P2 autoreview is scoped-clean. `pnpm check:changed --base f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1` completed with the inherited failures below plus two non-null assertion lint errors in this patch. Those assertions were removed; affected lint, 25 transport tests, core typechecking and formatting passed on the final source. The production assertion removal has no emitted-runtime effect. Package-test typechecking and the test-line ratchet also passed.

`check:changed` inherited failures were reproduced on the exact main parent and attributed: #194245 (`5577faefa9e1`, unused process-birth export), #194676 (`055544b9fa35`, unused gesture-probe exports/types), and #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`, attribution denylist rejects historical changelogs). These are recorded main regressions, not ignored test failures. No merge requested.

prs.title: fix(ui): remember the session Details rail collapse preference
prs.body:
Closes #194649

## What Problem This Solves

The right-hand session Details rail re-opens itself on every page load and window refocus: its mount state starts at an "auto" intent that re-docks whenever the window is wide enough, and any presentation reset (gateway reconnect scope identity changes on refocus) resets a manually collapsed rail back to that auto state. A collapsed rail cannot be kept collapsed, and it overlaps the chat column on every focus return.

Plain language: you close the side panel, switch to another window and come back, and the panel has popped open again by itself. Now the panel remembers being closed and stays closed until you open it again.

## Why This Change Was Made

A manual open/close is a durable preference; presentation-driven resets are not. The rail now persists a device-local `chatDetailsCollapsed` preference (same UI settings store as other browser-local preferences) on manual open/close, and both re-open paths — the mount initializer and the presentation-reset clause — restore that preference instead of forcing "auto". When no preference exists yet, behavior is exactly as before (auto-dock). Programmatic closes (outside click, Escape handling unchanged) do not write the preference.

## User Impact

Collapsing the Details rail survives page reloads, tab switches, and gateway reconnects; opening it manually likewise persists. Fresh profiles keep the current auto-dock behavior, so the discovery path is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main tree this change is based on (files byte-compared as `main` + exactly this delta; dependencies installed fresh because main added `@solidjs/vite-plugin`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `chat-details.browser.test.ts` new test (real browser, 1700×900 viewport where auto-dock would open): saved `chatDetailsCollapsed: true` → rail stays closed on mount AND after a gateway-scope presentation reset; manual open persists `false`; manual close persists `true` | green |
| Existing `chat-details.browser.test.ts` suite (auto-dock, revisions, mobile, Escape focus) | 20/20 green |
| `settings.chat-details.test.ts` new jsdom test: preference round-trips through `saveSettings`/`loadSettings` including unset | green |
| `chat-pane-header-details.test.tsx` (jsdom) | green |
| Red check: reverting the component wiring (initializer restore + manual persistence) makes exactly the new browser test fail | confirmed |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.ui.json`: zero errors in changed files | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep to trace the Details rail state machine (`chat-details.tsx` choice/intent signal), identify the two force-open paths, and implement the preference wiring. The implementer understands the code: the "auto" intent plus presentation resets are the only re-open sources, so restoring a saved preference in both spots is sufficient. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

Fixes asynchronous plugin discovery and Doctor's post-install repair step failing when their plugin setup sources are cold.

## User Impact

Configured plugins can participate in discovery and post-install repair without requiring an earlier operation to warm their setup modules. A successful Doctor config-repair preparation does not prepare the later setup-probe entry point.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both asynchronous callers now use the existing asynchronous auto-enable owner. Doctor keeps that work inside its current metadata scope after inventory repair. Setup preparation, source-custody checks, enablement policy, and repair ordering retain their existing owners; the full plugin runtime is not loaded.

The regressions use small synthetic plugins and the real main-thread preparation guard. One covers supplied and internally loaded metadata; the other calls Doctor's repair sequence with only the completed installer result mocked.

## Evidence

- The discovery regression fails on the base and passes with the repair in the normal plugins fork lane.
- The Doctor regression fails at the real post-install call site on the first repair revision and passes after this follow-up.

If this revised candidate has already been tested, link the existing evidence instead of repeating the run. Please post the results on this PR; no merge or release is requested for this validation.

prs.title: feat(compaction): make the summary character cap configurable
prs.body:
Closes #194408

## What Problem This Solves

`MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS` (16,000) is hard-coded: every persisted compaction summary — including preserved turns, split-turn context, tool failures, and workspace sections — must fit inside it, and no config key reaches it. The reporter's long-context production agent compacted 120k–241k-token sessions into ~4k-token summaries, with the `[Compaction summary truncated to fit budget]` marker on 66% of 117 compactions and 532 safeguard loss events over 22 days.

Plain language: the "keep a shorter version of the conversation" step writes its notes into a fixed-size notebook. On a big-window model the notes get cut off constantly, and there was no way to ask for a bigger notebook. Now there is one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cap is threaded from config instead of remaining a module constant: `agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryChars` (default 16000, schema-bounded 2000–200000) flows through `SettingsManager` → `CompactionSettings` → `CompactionPreparation.settings`, and now bounds the summary fitter (`fitCompactionSummary` gains an explicit bound parameter), the derived preserved-turns/split-turn budgets in the safeguard, the request-budget reserve probe, and the final persisted-summary cap. Explicitly setting `compaction.model` or unrelated behavior is unchanged; omission preserves the exact current behavior.

## User Impact

Operators on long-context models can raise the cap so compaction summaries stop losing summary tails, preserved-turn heads, and suffix content. Default behavior is byte-identical when the key is absent. Config docs and schema help text document the key.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main content this change is based on (every changed file verified as `main` + exactly this delta, byte-compared; config doc baselines regenerated from the same tree):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `settings-manager.test.ts` new test: `maxSummaryChars` override exposed via `getCompactionSummaryChars()` / `getCompactionSettings()` | green |
| `compaction-summary-cap.test.ts` new test: fitter honors a configured 4,000-char bound | green |
| `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` new test: preserved-turns section truncates with the configured bound and reports the `preserved-turn-head` loss | green |

prs.title: fix(signal): align autoStart daemon bind with local connection URL port
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A path-prefixed managed-native URL is a proxy, not the daemon bind. For a saved `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, autoStart reserves port 8080 for that proxy and binds the daemon on 8081. Readiness stays on the unchanged proxy URL. A URL on another port, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8082` with no `httpPort`, also stays the client endpoint. Set `httpPort` when the daemon should listen on a non-default port. Remote, HTTPS, and cross-family URLs stay independent.

Ref #116165

## Evidence

Head `1d08a5e9d41ee8a57dafde368361ada21a050ee8`. The production change from current main is the path check in `isSignalManagedNativeConnectionUrlForBind`.

Local `monitorSignalProvider` autoStart for `url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`:

```text
PROOF_SPAWN {"cliPath":"signal-cli","httpHost":"127.0.0.1","httpPort":8081,"sendReadReceipts":false}
PROOF_CHECK ["http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",1000]
```

The readiness check succeeded. The daemon bound 8081. The probe URL stayed `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`.

Saved config loaded through `normalizeCompatibilityConfig`, then `resolveSignalAccount`:

```text
PROOF_SAVED {"kind":"managed-native","url":"http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal"}
PROOF_RESOLVE {"kind":"managed-native","baseUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal","cliPath":"signal-cli","httpHost":"127.0.0.1","httpPort":8081,"startupTimeoutMs":30000}
```

The stored path URL is unchanged. Resolution keeps that base URL and allocates daemon port 8081.

`extensions/signal/src/accounts.test.ts` passed (23), including name, configured state, and account on the default-account case. Doctor cases "preserves an independent managed connection URL" and "ignores legacy native URL paths when the daemon bind matches" passed.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A same-port path-prefixed proxy stays the client endpoint while the daemon is allocated the next free port. A saved copy of that transport still loads and resolves the same way.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-116176` at `1d08a5e9d41ee8a57dafde368361ada21a050ee8`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `monitorSignalProvider` autoStart with `transport.url` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. Then `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` and `resolveSignalAccount` on that saved transport. Then the account test file and the two Doctor transport cases.
- **Evidence after fix:** spawn `httpPort` 8081. Readiness argument `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. Saved transport after normalize is still that URL. Resolved transport `httpPort` 8081 and `baseUrl` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The monitor readiness check returned success. The saved-config resolve returned the path URL and port 8081. Account tests passed (23). The two Doctor cases passed.
- **What was not tested:** A registered signal-cli with a real phone number, or two live signal-cli processes at the same time.

## Summary

- Treat a non-root connection URL path as an independent proxy
- When that proxy uses port 8080, allocate the daemon on 8081 and leave the proxy URL unchanged
- Leave a saved URL on another port as the client endpoint
- Restore the default-account name, configured-state, and account assertions

## Test plan

- [x] Same-port path `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` spawns daemon port 8081 and probes that proxy URL
- [x] `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` keeps that saved URL, and resolve allocates port 8081
- [x] Doctor preserves an independent managed connection URL
- [x] Default-account test checks name, configured state, and account

prs.title: feat(sandbox): allow named host roots for sandbox bind sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- External sandbox binds currently require disabling the source-root check. Named `allowedBindSources` grants permit specific host roots while preserving canonical-path and reserved-target checks.

## User Impact

- Configure permitted host roots globally or per agent. Global grants are additive for every agent; an empty per-agent list does not revoke inherited roots.
- Changed permissions are checked before agent or browser container reuse. Revocation refuses reuse while preserving existing containers and data.
- Restricted plugin dispatch rejects writable external binds, including affected browser and managed-worktree binds and read-only or absent workspace modes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep bind admission in the existing sandbox security and container-allocation owners, with one workspace-confinement contract for plugin callers.
- Existing configs retain their validation behavior. The new key requires this version; older versions reject it. No database schema or stored-state format changes are introduced.
- Upgrades using restricted plugin dispatch require removing external writable binds or using an appropriately confined workspace.
- Merge requires maintainer acceptance of additive grants and stricter plugin confinement, plus security approval for this head.

## Evidence

- Head: `e0a682c737568b839234360014352d79cbfb1f2e`.
- Three selected named-root regressions fail on main `3412694c1977a5e4d31757cb305c0c63a98c98fb`.

prs.title: fix: keep channel replies authorized through long-running attempts
prs.body:
Related: #145506

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channel replies losing delivery authority while a fallback candidate is still running beyond its original attempt timeout.

## User Impact

Long-running replies can still prepare delivery until their candidate finishes or is cancelled. Cancellation revokes authority immediately, even while the model promise is still settling. Scheduled automation keeps its existing admission owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel capabilities used a timeout-derived expiry although retries and approval waits can outlive one attempt. Use the existing run-owned lifetime and revoke it on the candidate's abort signal and in its existing finally block.

```diff
- expire authority at the attempt-derived deadline
+ retain authority while the candidate is active
+ revoke on cancellation, and always on settlement
```

This addresses one reproducible route to “plugin delivery capability is no longer active”; it does not claim to resolve every session-key or registry-replacement cause in the related reports. No timeout increase, new owner, or migration.

## Current real-model evidence — 7 November

[The exact-head compiled Gateway/channel flow now passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6713019903): 1/1, exit 0, on a7b13235d820. The existing dist/entry.js image ran the actual native model and registered qa-channel HTTP ingress/outbound path; one nonce reply reached the correct account/room. The exact inbound transport completion receipt confirmed deferred delivery/preview settlement before the 250 ms no-extra-message check and clean exit. Setup took 12.173 s and the real-model settled flow 8.077 s. No credential copy, build, install, source patch or extended deadline.

This closes the previously missing real-agent/model isolated compiled-Gateway registered-channel integration boundary. It does not turn the archived Telegram public:fallback or its CI result green, add a 41-minute real wait, or claim published-package installation/live Telegram proof. Existing simulated-clock/cancellation regressions keep their stated scope. The remaining inherited queue-context/CI disposition is separate; no empty push, manual CI retry or unqualified merge approval is inferred. Earlier dated statements that real-model proof was absent describe their then-current evidence, not this latest result.

## Evidence

### QA2 reproduced on the candidate and its exact CI main base — 7 November

The retained QA2 artifact 13046107768 from [run 41210635478/job124564973204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210635478/job/124564973204) was downloaded and inspected, not inferred from its job name. The historical synthetic merge 7c97777d is no longer served; no replacement is claimed to be that exact object.

Two separate private qaRuntime builds completed through the repository owner: candidate a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4 in 93.3s; actual historical CI main base 2d7376d2e6e111ae28bdf7d9e888cbb077139204 in 116s. Each build-info commit matched its checkout. Dependency declarations/lock/workspace files matched; dependencies were copied COW into an isolated baseline, not installed or reconciled. The first baseline setup missed workspace-local dependency links and stopped before runtime proof; those existing links were copied from the same declared dependency snapshot, then the qualified build succeeded. No source/config/timeout was changed to clear setup.

Both ran ONLY the original subagent-completion-direct-fallback scenario with mock-openai, crabline Telegram loopback, concurrency 1, fastMode:false and the unchanged 60s assertion. Both failed at public:fallback with the same event sequence and outcome: visible/silent controls delivered their exact markers; fallback child execution terminal/ok; fallback delivery suspended/permanent_failure; no expected fallback marker; loopback sendMessage aborted. The scenario and mock-provider source hashes match across both trees.

This establishes that the failed behavior already occurs on the CI main base without this PR delta. It is not evidence that the branch introduced the QA2 failure, and is not a passing QA verdict or proof that no other branch-specific defect can coexist. The A/B comparison alone did not identify the abort owner. [The subsequent first-abort observation and upstream source check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6711153646) narrowed it to the current consuming async-work scope in the shared Telegram queue, not the prepared reader’s captured requestSignal. Merged PR #189457 already restores the submitted caller context before admission and dispatch; duplicate #194701 is superseded. That separate fix is not present merely because this candidate’s original QA2 artifacts exist, and this PR’s acceptance remains incomplete. No timeout, assertion, revocation check or retry protection was weakened.

The log wording about potentially sent chunks is classification, not proof of an identified delivered chunk. Existing ambiguous/post-dispatch retry protection is retained. The isolated observation and producer source work are now recorded in the linked follow-up. Reuse the merged queue-boundary correction; do not weaken the ended-scope guard, extend deadlines, or claim that these source findings pass the original scenario.

Private qaRuntime is not a public package/release build, a live Telegram test, real-model acceptance or full PR qualification. Both isolated Gateway probes completed and exited; no operator Gateway, installed package, updater attempt or workflow retry was touched. No new source commit/empty push is justified by these A/B results alone. Candidate/CI-base reports, diagnostics, raw local Gateway logs and a hashed comparison are preserved for the remaining cause investigation.


- On base `32f9477bf46d`, the two regression cases fail: authority expires after 41 simulated minutes with a 30-minute attempt timeout, and cancellation leaves authority valid until model settlement.
- With this change, all 6 execution-authority cases and 10 adjacent runner-utils cases pass: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-message-authority.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Focused typecheck, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent read-only review found no blocking issue.
- A separate isolated backport probe against the published 2026.10.8 package uses its actual channel minting and plugin delivery preparation: the baseline refuses after 41 minutes; the candidate succeeds. Wrong session/run, explicit revocation and registry replacement still reject. Zero external deliveries.
- Scope of proof: source tests use the real execute/mint/resolve path with the model and fallback selection mocked; elapsed time is simulated. No live provider retry, real approval wait or external channel delivery was exercised. Broad integration remains for CI.

Reversible code-only change; affected scope is channel reply delivery authority.

## Current source-boundary proof — 29 October

[Qualified local final-transport evidence and repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6493700861) on head `d2c24b2642cd941ce3b4cb4c99141b64e40856c0`: three cases pass through production authority/delivery owners and actual loopback HTTP, including independent cancellation, normal settlement and candidate replacement while a started send is held before physical I/O. The existing final adapter-handoff hook now rechecks reply authority. Production core types, focused fixture types, canonical core/extension lint, formatting and native ratchet pass. The new fixture/source contains synthetic data only; raw private diagnostics remain withheld. No actual unresolved user decision prevented these local tests. This is explicit **source integration with model/fallback selection controlled by the fixture and a simulated clock jump**, not a shipped-package CLI, real-model/approval wait or live Telegram/Test Server claim. The original stronger shipped-flow request remains for fresh review to assess; no automated approval or merge acceptance is inferred.

## CI fixture repair — 29 October

Previous fixture-repair head: `8eb48f11b00270abf5635155f2a02c8b81071a4e` (fixture repair `be7378539e81` plus inventory-position-only conflict avoidance; all tested source/test blobs and lane membership unchanged). [CI diagnosis, repair and passing local checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6494309715): move the host authority integration test out of Telegram extension-private ownership; consume the existing public test facade and route through the existing host-SQLite fork inventory. All three original observable-behavior cases and assertions are preserved. The normal wrapper now passes 3/3 without a pool override; the unchanged extension boundary suite passes 11/11, with core-import guard, focused types/lint/format and native budget checks passing. No production behavior or boundary guard changes. The previous entry and proof remain pinned to `d2c24b2642cd`; the fixture path at that revision was `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-reply-authority.telegram-http.test.ts`. New-head hosted CI is separate and not claimed green. The accepted loopback final-effect coverage remains source integration with a controlled model and simulated clock: **the required real-agent/model isolated-Gateway channel proof remains missing**. No new review request or live proof is claimed.

## Sparse type-graph repair — 29 October

Previously published head: `992fc2ee9ee6d57ec33234cdaa98cfae7fe9f178`. [Fresh CI diagnosis and proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6494615934): the root integration owner is now `test/reply-authority.telegram-http.integration.test.ts`, still on the existing SQLite fork lane. The sparse core messaging graph drops from 264 Telegram source files to zero and the complete core tsgo boundary guard passes without any guard/config exception. The relocated three-case integration, focused root types/lint/format and native budget pass. Test bodies/assertions and production source are unchanged. Prior evidence retains its source identities. New-head hosted CI remains separate. The previous macOS job additionally invoked a tooling test absent from its PR checkout; that workflow/source-version mismatch is documented, not claimed repaired or attributed to queue capacity. **Real-agent/model isolated-Gateway proof remains outstanding**; this fresh result is still controlled-model/loopback/simulated-clock evidence.

## Current Darwin workflow/source integration — 31 October

Current published head: `a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4`, normal merge of pinned main `ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff`. [Qualification and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6544754752): the required `test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts` is now present; the entire seven-file PR patch has the same stable patch-ID before and after integration. Checkout-local frozen/prefer-offline dependencies were reconciled with lifecycle scripts disabled. **13 distinct targeted tests passed**, with 12 Windows-only tooling skips on macOS. Core and focused integration types/lint, seven-file format, whitespace and the core tsgo boundary guard pass. Native ratchet against prepared main: **6,342,969 / 6,368,719**; no author budget increase. The initial default comparison against the old parent rejected inherited main allocation credit; that failure and the supported prepared-base qualification are disclosed in the evidence. GitHub confirms MERGEABLE; exact-new-head CI remains separate. **Real-agent/model Gateway proof remains outstanding**: the HTTP regression still uses controlled model/fallback selection and a simulated clock. No production installation, restart, broad core build, new grant or live-model/channel run.

## Exact-head QA failure — 31 October

At `a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4`, [QA Smoke CI profile 2/6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210635478/job/124564973204) fails `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` at `[public:fallback]` after 60 seconds. The artifact records child execution `ok`, but delivery `suspended/permanent_failure`. Gateway logs show Telegram `sendMessage` aborting at 14:36:41.843Z, followed by an `OutboundDeliveryError` and the incomplete-send duplicate-prevention guard. Visible and silent control cases delivered.

This is the same observed failure sequence as the independently captured PR173026 run, not proof of a common root cause or an inherited-main classification. The announcement delivery owners, Telegram production sources and scenario are byte-identical to pinned main `ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff`; attribution still requires production-boundary reproduction. The CI gate also reports failure. No rerun or green-only push was requested.

The existing isolated reproduction attempt for this failure sequence stopped before Gateway startup at the runtime-artifact-publication guard; its checkout has no prepared `dist/entry.js`. That setup failure is not product proof, and no guard was bypassed. The source-pinned QA runtime must be qualified before identifying the abort owner and selecting a regression/fix. Previously passing focused tests are unchanged evidence, not a fix for this QA failure. **Exact-head CI and real-agent/model acceptance remain incomplete.**

prs.title: fix(ui): hide speed controls for standard-only models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the chat composer showing a Speed selector when Standard is the only available speed, including routed Anthropic models. Unsupported Ultrafast was also advertised as a disabled option.

## User Impact

Models without a nonstandard speed now show only their usable effort controls. Models with Fast or Ultrafast retain their speed selector. Saved speed preferences are preserved rather than rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared speed-state resolver previously treated standard-only routes and saved overrides as reasons to expose the control. It now exposes speed controls only when the selected route can actually offer a nonstandard speed. The picker advertises Ultrafast only when offered, or when showing an existing selection alongside an available alternative.

## Evidence

- Full composer regression reproduced the failure before the fix: one Speed panel rendered when zero were expected.
- Model-state, cached-composer, and picker suites: 66 tests passed for the unchanged production fix.
- Full model-controls browser E2E suite: all 9 tests passed after consolidating the new regression into the existing routed-model scenario.
- CI exposed a stale new-session consumer expectation. The failure was reproduced locally; the corrected full new-session model-control suite passed all 37 tests.
- Test consolidation fixed the CI test-line ratchet without changing its budget or adding an exception: 6,566,404 test lines; ceiling 6,566,407; slack 3.
- Core-test and UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed, including reruns for the two-file CI repair.
- Independent source review found one stale cached-composer test expectation; it is corrected and passing. No production-behavior findings.

prs.title: fix: resume replies after idle database worker recovery
prs.body:
Related: #169229

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an active reply failing on a retained session reader after an idle database worker has been lost and the same database has already recovered.

## User Impact

A reply can continue after a prepared native-worker replacement without replaying a failed operation. Cancelled, released or reset work stays invalid, and a read interrupted by another replacement is still rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Logical borrowers already survive idle native loss, but session admission retained the original native generation. Let that admission adopt an already-prepared successor for the same physical database. Freeze a separate native claim for each read, after FIFO acquisition where applicable, so recovery cannot validate a result obtained across retirement.

```text
retained admission -> already-prepared successor
each read -> fixed native claim -> validate -> consume
```

This does not reopen the database from the admission guard or change worker recovery, timeouts, schema or replay policy. The related issue has multiple reported causes; this PR addresses the retained-reader case only.

## Evidence

- On base `32f9477bf46d`, the extended existing idle-worker-loss regression fails at the first retained reader access after recovery: 1 failed, 9 passed.
- With the change, all 10 close-wedge cases pass. The regression exercises real worker termination, repeated retained reads through both APIs, replacement during an awaited read, successful subsequent access, and rejection after session reset.
- All 14 adjacent cohort lifecycle cases pass, covering queue/owner/caller boundaries.
- Commands: `pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.close-wedge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` and `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-entry-cohort-lifecycle.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Focused typecheck, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent read-only review found no blocking issue.
- The equivalent 2026.10.8 backport also passes an isolated package-level chat → child → yield → one final result → next turn flow, with a local synthetic model and zero external deliveries. Separate package probes retain reset, release, Stop, physical-file and read-consumption fences.

Limitations: this fixes continuation after recovery, not the original cause of a worker disappearing. The new test does not inject retirement during FIFO waiting or during the synchronous consume callback; those paths were code-reviewed and separately probed in the backport. Broad integration remains for CI. Reversible code-only change affecting retained session-read admission.

## Current-head Gateway proof and CI boundary — 29 October

[The existing source Gateway trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186854#issuecomment-6476315450) on exact head `af0d3f74b13466b16fd3ca17e0952dfac171f0f6` exited 0: the actual retained chat reply survived idle-worker termination and a same-physical-database successor prepared once; the retained reader adopted it, exactly one RETAINED_REPLY_OK final and one NEXT_TURN_OK final were observed, and shutdown was clean. This is an instrumented **source Gateway**, with synthetic HTTP provider transport and explicit harness-driven successor preparation/retained-reader invocation. The preparation source guard and explicit reader caller guard are no-ops; the retained reply admission uses production logic. It is **not** an unmodified shipped-package/real-model/real-channel qualification, and does not waive the requested shipped-entry-point gate. No rerun accompanies this update.

[The unresolved CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40715475300/job/122927297685) reports self-hosted runner communication loss, not a source diagnostic. Its log download returned BlobNotFound and the already attempted targeted rerun was denied with 403 Resource not accessible by integration. The aggregate CI statuses retain that failure. An Actions-write maintainer must rerun the affected job and check its aggregate; no duplicate retry or whole-workflow rerun is requested here. [Review revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186854#issuecomment-6473470512), reviewed 29 October at 09:13 UTC on this exact head, assessed this source trace and found it meaningful but not sufficient for the required isolated real-agent/model Gateway scenario through natural production callers with active source/caller guards. The natural-caller and active-guard portion of that gap is now covered by the new synthetic-provider source proof below. Real-model/shipped-entry-point acceptance and the maintainer-owned CI rerun remain open; no code findings were identified. No full acceptance or new review verdict is inferred.

## Natural public-caller recovery proof — 7 November

[The new exact-head source proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186854#issuecomment-6711413514) passes 1/1, exit 0. A public sessions.create establishes a distinct durable peer; after matched idle-worker loss, an authorized real label change through sessions.patch commits and prepares a same-physical-file native successor. The original reply operation/admission are unchanged, the retained reader adopts through production use, exactly one RETAINED_REPLY_OK final and one NEXT_TURN_OK final arrive from two provider requests, the original operation settles, and the 250 ms observation sees no extra final/request. Shutdown is clean and resources are joined. No direct harness preparation/reader call or no-op guard is used.

Setup/readiness completed separately in 49.293 s with no model calls; recovery completed in 32.528 s inside its unchanged 60 s limit. Startup 60 s, readiness 10 s and teardown 10 s remain bounded; whole-fixture 130 s supervises those distinct phases. Existing slot-observer instrumentation only; no production source change, build, installation or CI retry. The earlier fixture’s optional-path observation error and all failed history probes are preserved and are not product failures.

This is source Gateway/real-agent behavior with a synthetic local HTTP model, **not real-model, packaged Gateway/CLI or live-channel qualification**. Those explicitly requested acceptance limits and the maintainer-owned runner-contact issue remain separate.

---
[View the OpenClaw team session](https://openclaw.johaneilertsen.no/chat/openclaw-contributions)


## Real-model follow-up — runtime environment boundary

[The genuine-model attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186854#issuecomment-6712974068) stopped before inference because the candidate Codex owner plugin could not resolve its declared smol-toml 1.9.1 dependency. The public path reported owner-plugin-degraded; no worker fault or real-model recovery occurred. The fixture later reached its unchanged 60 s test deadline waiting for an impossible tool event. Cleanup joined owned resources. No credential copy, install, build, guard change, retry or deadline increase. The previously passing synthetic-provider natural recovery remains valid. The real-model/package prerequisite is a correctly prepared isolated candidate environment or exact-head artifact, not a new model-authentication grant.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): attribute native pane invalidations [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Attribution experiment for repeated style/layout work before painted rows on a signed-in warm reload of a chat deep link. **Stopped: both native primary gates failed. This experiment is closed and must not merge.**

## User Impact

No qualified performance improvement. The candidate preserves composer width behavior but did not consistently advance painted rows under the required within-order A/A rule. Dashboard/Team secondary campaigns, the full UI suite, and ready-PR CI were not run after the primary failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lazy composer-width module calls `CSS.registerProperty` for an inherited typed length. Chromium explicitly records `PropertyRegistration` on the HTML subtree. On the archived baseline, the subsequent style pass resolves 2,692 node identities, of which 2,685 were already styled (2,696 reported elements; 29.6 ms with invalidation instrumentation). Active registration instead joins the first large style pass. This is a registry mutation, rather than one of the initially suspected stylesheet/root-attribute/custom-property-value writes.

The candidate moves the identical property declaration into eager base CSS and deletes the JavaScript registration and duplicate-registration catch. Reads, cached content, reveal timing, transport and stored shapes stay unchanged. The ownership change is small and correct, but the painted-rows evidence does not qualify it for landing.

## Evidence

Qualification: main `72b51fb60890` versus candidate `e42cde4fb739`, one AWS c7a.4xlarge (`cbx_20520e6df2e1`, released), Chromium 156.0.8078.4, synthetic 3,000-session real Gateway, 1720×1180, 80 ms profile. Observed 16 CPUs/16-CPU affinity and 32,902,856,704 bytes MemTotal. Twelve alternating pairs plus A/A per native chat route. Profiled attribution is separate from all timings below.

| Route | A/B arm median rows, ms | Arm IQRs, ms | A/B raw paired Δ | A/B balanced Δ | A/A balanced Δ | Corrected AB-first / BA-first | Corrected mean | Gate |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Active | 629.5 → 625.5 | [595.5, 643.4] → [597.5, 648.4] | −4.1 | +4.0 | −0.0 | +16.0 / −8.0 | +4.0 | FAIL |

Neither route improves in both corrected orders; arm IQRs overlap. Raw better counts are 6/12 active and 7/12 archived, while A/A also reports 7/12 on each route. These counts are diagnostic, not the gate. Populated Details remains co-frame 12/12 in both arms on both routes; the native observed secondary metrics do not show a regression. No complete secondary pass is claimed.

### Ranked invalidation handoff

Attribution main `078033289a36`, diagnostic-only head `beba3ce2591f`, AWS c7a.4xlarge `cbx_75252e1696a7` (released). Three unprofiled warm reloads and one separate invalidation/CPU profile each for native active and archived chat. Baseline row ranges: active 627.5–739.5 ms; archived 575.6–683.5 ms. Details co-frame 3/3 each, zero measured Details movement. Source rebasing subsequently added a streaming-source change; qualification uses that newer main in both arms.

|---|---|---|
| Lazy typed-property registration, `chat-composer-width-ref.tsx:13` | HTML-subtree `PropertyRegistration`; archived 29.6 ms / 2,696 elements, 2,685 repeated resolved node identities | Tested candidate; failed painted-rows qualification. |
| Mono font admission, `typography.ts` / browser font selector | Font file starts on first glyph use; completion precedes `Fonts changed` on 2,307 active / 2,393 archived existing objects. Following layout 4.9 / 5.2 ms, alongside style-update work. | Separate font/first-shaping cost, retained. Lead may select its admission owner. |
| Transcript initial geometry, `chat-transcript-layout-owner.ts:260` | 32.9 / 28.3 profiled ms; 693 / 692 newly attached DOM node identities, despite only 47 / 37 dirty objects | Predominantly first layout; small dirty totals do not prove repeated shaping of the entire transcript. |
| Sidebar relational selectors | 680 / 717 elements, 671 / 710 already styled. `:has()` invalidation sets include sidebar focus/disclosure and Details SVG selectors. | Invalidation tracking inflates this pass drastically (164.6 ms active; older profile about 5.5 ms). Do not treat trace overhead as an available 164 ms win. |
| Virtualizer range and scroll callback | Range layout 14.0 / 10.8 ms; later scroll callback 14.7 / 11.6 ms, with container-dependent style resolution over existing transcript nodes | Retained; no read relocation attempted. |

The full local handoff enumerates every style/layout pass ≥2 ms through first rows, with invalidation records, node IDs/names, reasons, mapped stacks, object counts and repeated resolved-node counts. Raw traces and synthetic frames are retained in the lane worktree. No private captures or transcript content are included here.

### Proof and scope

- New early-inset regression: red with main's base stylesheet (unresolved calc/empty default), green with candidate (`26px` / `0px`). Canonical `pnpm test ui/src/styles/transcript-inset.node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: local 4.07 s wall; exact-head AWS 1/1, 7.55 s wall. The initial browser-mode setup attempt was corrected to the existing Node-driven Chromium style-test lane.
- Exact-head AWS composer-width browser tests: 13/13. Composer-layout e2e: 9/9. Both complete production builds passed.
- Independent autoreview scoped-clean through P2; formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full UI, dashboard/Team secondaries, candidate ledger-diff qualification, and byte gates remain unrun because primary failed. Draft CI at closeout: 11 success, 69 skipped, 2 cancelled; this is not a full CI pass. No cap changed.
- Application runtime: **−5 LOC** (12 JS removed, 7 CSS added). Requested filtered diff: **+3 LOC** (16 additions, 13 deletions). The remaining growth is the required invalidation trace (+4), its guide (+2), and exact 29-line regression-budget metadata (+2); tests are +29. The obsolete JavaScript registration/catch is deleted.

prs.body:
## Decision needed (Josh)

**Draft only — do not mark ready or merge.** Stacked on `openclaw-517/node-ffi`.

1. **Durable node enrollment:** approve the proposed `OpenClawNativeState` node-target table and migration. Neither is implemented here. Enrollment persistence is behind the `OpenClawIDNodeTrustStore` interface, exercised with an in-memory test store; durable enrollment and app/controller integration remain incomplete.
2. **iOS native support:** blocked upstream by `netdev` 0.46 (iroh/netwatch) using `libc::in6_ifreq`, which the pinned libc exposes only for macOS. This draft's native integration/proof is macOS-only. No dependency changes or `[patch]` workarounds are included.

## What Problem This Solves

Apple nodes need a node-role-only enrollment and tunnel foundation, plus a private macOS worker bridge, before they can connect through OpenClaw ID.

## User Impact

This is an incomplete, opt-in foundation, not a usable end-to-end enrollment feature. Native transport requires `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1` and a source-built XCFramework; default builds remain artifact-free and unchanged. Without native packaging, binding fails closed with a readable error. No database schema or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared Swift code owns local node identity, pinned/fresh trust validation, signed enrollment, tunnel framing and node-role WebSocket transport. Uncertain enrollment delivery retries the exact signed redemption bytes, preserving Discovery deduplication. The native adapter uses per-operation cancellation and one connection-lifetime close observer. The macOS bridge uses an owner-only Unix socket and restricts access to worker routes.

A separate path-filtered workflow checks the default build, builds a same-revision universal macOS XCFramework, and exercises native Swift and opted-in shared tests. iOS slices are deliberately excluded until the upstream issue is resolved.

Refs: openclaw-517.7, openclaw-517.8. Depends on the node-FFI branch; complements Android #194194.

## Evidence

- **Trust retirement correction (`ae4fc193d83e09f49bb74975f71394c88283b751`, protocol #194459):** signed four-attempt enrollment regression failed before the fix (binding retirement dropped 5 → 4 and replay returned a target), then all 10 enrollment tests passed in the same sandboxed exact-source macOS harness (0.023s); newest membership and maximum snapshot binding sequence now remain independent, with future-snapshot exclusion unchanged. The coordinator independently reviewed the staged delta and red/green logs with no verified P0–P2 findings; normal commit hooks passed. [Exact-head `swift` CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42387168644) **passed** (2026-11-07 16:02:21 UTC): artifact-free shared tests **22/22**, same-revision bindings and universal macOS XCFramework build, native loopback **1/1**, and opted-in shared tests **22/22**; the new trust-retirement regression passed in both shared configurations.

- **Foundation:** 36 focused tests passed: 19 shared enrollment/tunnel tests plus 17 macOS bridge tests. Bridge proof includes upload and response larger than 2 MiB each way under a sandbox denying operator state and non-loopback outbound networking. The proof caught and repaired CRLF header truncation; the golden signature test now verifies cryptographically rather than requiring byte-identical signatures.
- **Default/native opt-in:** default build passed with the XCFramework physically absent; native build passed with it restored. After adding immutable redemption retries, 21 focused shared tests passed. The retry regression failed on the original owner with a lost response and passed with identical POST bodies through lost-response/429/503/acceptance; cancellation stops retries.
- **Native linking:** source-locked Rust build, SwiftPM compile/link and macOS app product link passed on Studio. The app was not launched. Real Swift → Rust loopback proved stream bytes/FIN, typed close codes, cancellation preserving other streams, and endpoint reuse.
- **Current macOS-only follow-up:** fresh arm64 framework rebuild and Swift compile/link passed; sandboxed loopback passed again. Generated binding hashes match the source. Earlier Apple commits are patch-identical after rebase onto `fad580f3ef88`; only the CI platform-selection delta changed.
- Independent source reviews found no verified P0–P2 issues in the reviewed integration and follow-up deltas. Normal commit hooks and whitespace checks passed. These are scoped reviews, not proof of the unfinished app flow.
- **CI at `d95076cbaad161af54891a4882bae71a23486213`:** [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42247081573) passed, including actionlint and zizmor. [Apple node native transport — swift](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42247081566) **passed**: default artifact-free build, same-revision bindings and universal macOS XCFramework build, native Swift package tests, and opted-in shared adapter tests. Completed 2026-11-06 at 16:13:27 UTC. This establishes the scoped macOS CI gate, not Intel runtime, iOS, or end-to-end app enrollment. The inherited `iroh native binding` Apple job has the separately documented upstream iOS blocker; it is not this macOS gate.

<details>
<summary>Retained local evidence paths (not public artifact links)</summary>

Under `/home/josh/.openclaw/workspace/reports/`:

- `ocid-node-apple-studio-20261106/shared-after.log`, `bridge-after.log`, `bridge.sb`, `validated-foundation.patch`
- `ocid-node-apple-native-20261106/PROOF.md`, `native-retry-red-tests.log`, `native-retry-green-tests.log`, `native-default-tests.log`, `native-optin-tests.log`, `native-token-macos-link.log`, `final-studio-logs.tar.gz`

The fresh harness initially referenced an obsolete build layout and failed before test execution. Only the bundle path was corrected; isolation was unchanged, and the actual loopback test then passed.

</details>

### Unverified / before distribution

- iOS native integration, device/simulator execution and full multi-platform XCFramework: blocked upstream.
- Intel runtime; CI will cross-build Intel but executes tests only on its runner architecture.
- Full unfiltered suites, including Keychain/preferences tests; deliberately not run against the operator's desktop state.
- End-to-end enrollment, durable storage, app/controller lifecycle, background/network-change behavior, and screenshots.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 / Swift lint: unavailable, not installed. Local workflow lint tooling remains unavailable, but the hosted Workflow Sanity actionlint/zizmor checks passed (linked above).
- **Third-party license notices:** separate shared P2 before-distribution release gate across both native crates. The partial `generate-apple-notices.py` and `apps/ios/Resources/Licenses/iroh.txt` remain untracked and are not in this PR; inventory/source-obligation completeness is not claimed.

prs.title: feat(android): enroll OpenClaw ID nodes with opt-in native transport
prs.body:
## Decision needed (Josh)

**Draft only. Do not mark ready or merge until Josh approves the new durable storage contract.** These new entries may change after his decision.

`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/gateway/OpenClawIdNodeStore.kt` persists one encrypted record through the existing `SecurePrefs` owner, wired by `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/NodeRuntime.kt` via `prefs.getString` / `prefs.commitSecureStrings` (owner: `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/SecurePrefs.kt`).

- Preference key: `node.openclaw-id.$stableId`, where `stableId` is `openclaw-id|${clawId}|${rootFingerprint.substringAfter(':')}`.
- Target/pin fields: `claw`, `root`, `host`, `discovery`, `relay`, `admitted`.
- Node identity field: `seed` (W, stored only through the existing secure preference owner).
- Anti-rollback/high-water fields inside `trust`: `binding`, `seq`, `issued`, `snapshotBinding` (binding sequence, snapshot sequence, snapshot issued-at, and snapshot binding sequence).

Approval is requested for the target, pinned trust identity, and snapshot high-water persistence and these key names. A correctly signed newer snapshot that removes this node still advances the durable high-water state, preventing replay of an older admitting snapshot; a storage failure never exposes a dial target.

Related: #194174 (native crate base). Coordinated work: `openclaw-517`; Android lane `openclaw-517.9`.

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an explicit, owner-approved way to enroll as an OpenClaw ID node and reach its Gateway through the native tunnel without acquiring operator or chat credentials.

## User Impact

Opt-in builds provide an experimental paste-or-scan node invitation flow with a separate Discovery HTTPS origin, a six-digit verification code, and owner approval of the declared capabilities. This is node-only access, not an operator/chat login.

Native packaging is **opt-in with `-PopenclawIrohNative=true`**. Existing default build lanes remain unchanged: they do not require Rust/NDK or package this native transport. Generated Kotlin still compiles unconditionally; attempting an OpenClaw ID node connection without native packaging fails closed with a clear “native transport not packaged” error. Ordinary Gateway connections retain their existing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android adapter uses the OpenClaw-owned UniFFI crate from native commit `92c25067451b1a105b1e83615da641e352c51e7c`, with matching checked-in Kotlin bindings. Enrollment verifies pinned signed trust evidence before dialing the verified server key over `openclaw/tunnel/1`; no TCP proxy, default relay, hostname dial, or direct WebSocket fallback is added.

Native suspend calls drain under `NonCancellable`, explicit cancellation signals terminate the underlying work, and returned resources are disposed if cancellation wins the handoff. Cancelling admission may retire this node's single connection; reconnect recreates it. Endpoint initialization is lazy and seed buffers are erased.

The dedicated path-filtered `android-iroh-native.yml` owns its NDK/Rust provisioning and verifies a pinned rustup-init checksum before execution. Shared Android actions, CodeQL, and the native owner's `iroh-ffi.yml` are unchanged relative to the base.

Scope/simplification: this is the Android consumer stage stacked on the separately owned native crate, not a second transport owner. The earlier shared CI provisioning and obsolete guard allocation were removed in favor of one opt-in packaging lane. Necessary growth is enrollment/trust verification, framing, the transport adapter, explicit UI intent, and distinct replay/cancellation/EOF regressions; the checked-in protocol fixture accounts for 1,127 lines. Against the native base: 39 files, 4,737 insertions and 19 deletions. No native crate changes are included in this consumer diff.

## Evidence

Passed:

- **24 focused JVM tests**, compiling the production OpenClaw ID sources with the generated Kotlin bindings, covering enrollment, tunnel framing, WebSocket behavior, durable replay protection after refusal, and native cancellation/cleanup.
- **Real host JVM → generated Kotlin/JNA → Rust loopback at native commit `92c25067451b1a105b1e83615da641e352c51e7c`**: framed HEAD status 101, FIN, maximum 62-bit numeric application-close code, explicit connect cancellation token, and a typed pre-cancelled dial. Built from the exact archived source with locked Rust 1.99.0 inputs; Linux x86_64 only, not Android JNI proof. Native library SHA-256: `5075327bfbed3e3cf89ab261b24648917d2781c03b37cc09b28bdb7bb1d66a0b` (13,185,944 bytes).
- Kotlin formatting, native i18n inventory checks/regeneration, actionlint 1.7.12, and `git diff --check`.
- Default protocol checks, without a protocol-base override.
- Independent cancellation follow-up resolved both prior P1 findings; the opt-in correction review found no new verified P0–P2 issues. Coordinator also inspected the opt-in rework.

**Packaging passed** at head `b3959bc24da3d965326483351b68cdae9ba213b3`: [PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42246599743) and [push run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42246594975), verifying the default APK excludes iroh and the opt-in Android variants build and pass their tests; this is build/packaging evidence, not device-runtime proof.

The unmodified generated binding builds in `:openclaw-iroh` with compiler warnings allowed, while the app retains its unchanged `allWarningsAsErrors(true)` gate; no native-generator-owner action is required.

**Unverified / required before completion:**

- Full Gradle build and task graph; opt-in native APK packaging/loading for all four ABIs; release shrinking/R8, APK size and ZIP alignment.
- Device/emulator execution, including a 16 KiB-page device; real enrollment-to-Gateway connection.
- Before/after screenshots of the new UI (not yet captured).
- Android Keystore behavior and foreground-service/lifecycle behavior.
- **Distribution license-notice gate:** the `openclaw-517` P2 task remains open. The inventory covers 285 crates; 20 archives lack notices. Complete transitive notices and MPL source-availability obligations for **UniFFI and `attohttpc`** are not complete. The current iroh/Tailscale notice is partial, not clearance to distribute.

No host SDK/NDK installation or app distribution was performed. This draft does not waive storage approval, build proof, screenshots, or the distribution gate.
