prs.title: feat(iroh-ffi): add uniffi bindings for the OpenClaw ID tunnel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native OpenClaw ID node apps (macOS, iOS, Android) need an iroh transport that meets `openclaw/tunnel/1`. The official `iroh-ffi` bindings (v1.0–v1.2) can't: they report a closed connection only as reason text, with no numeric application close code, and they offer no QUIC keep-alive setting. Their macOS package is also Apple-silicon only.

## User Impact

None yet. This adds a standalone crate that generates Swift and Kotlin bindings. No app uses it until the macOS/iOS and Android node PRs stacked on this one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Josh chose an OpenClaw-owned UniFFI crate over waiting for an upstream patch or deferring native nodes. The crate pins the same iroh version as the Node addon (1.4.1) and adds UniFFI 0.31.2. It exposes only what the tunnel needs:
- bind with iroh's Minimal preset, only the selected relay and a required keep-alive;
- connect to an already-verified endpoint key;
- bidirectional streams;
- **full-range numeric close codes** (`i64`, so every legal QUIC code 0…2^62−1 round-trips);
- a home-relay watcher that ends on shutdown;
- a shutdown that interrupts pending reads, accepts and connects;
- an optional `CancelToken` on `connect`, `openBi` and `acceptBi`, so a caller can abandon one dial or one stream wait without shutting down the endpoint or closing the connection.

The native seed copy is zeroized on every bind path. There is no key getter, default relay, discovery service, pkarr, or TCP proxy. The existing Node/N-API crate is unchanged.

Two things apps must handle:
- **Swift `Task.cancel()` does not reach Rust** (UniFFI 0.31.2's generated Swift has no cancellation hook). Pass a `CancelToken` to `connect` and cancel it from the task's cancellation handler; use `stop`/`reset` for streams and `endpoint.shutdown()` for a whole route. **Kotlin must not cancel a coroutine around a native call either:** UniFFI 0.31.2 lowers the result when the Rust future becomes ready, so freeing a ready future before it's lifted leaks the handle (an open `Connection`, or an `Endpoint` still holding its key). Kotlin runs native calls under `NonCancellable` and uses the same explicit signals.
- **Android** must call `OpenClawIrohAndroid.install(applicationContext)` before `bind`. Without it, `bind` fails closed.

## Evidence

Run locally (Linux, Rust 1.99):
- `cargo test --locked`: 6 tests, all passing. Five are real loopback integration tests covering streams, the exact 2^62−1 close code, rejection of -1 and 2^62, keep-alive validation, the relay watcher ending, shutdown interrupting a blocked read, accept and connect, a `CancelToken` aborting one hanging dial while the endpoint stays usable, and a `CancelToken` abandoning a blocked `acceptBi` and a credit-starved `openBi` while the connection keeps working in both directions. The sixth is a unit test for seed erasure.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, fmt, actionlint and shellcheck all clean.
- Bindings regenerate deterministically. A temporary Python UniFFI smoke test ran the async transport.
- The release host library was 13,180,024 bytes before the `CancelToken` change.
- An independent read-only review of the first commit found no verified P0–P2 issues. A second review of the follow-ups through `3113717` (CI NDK setup, `CancelToken` on `connect`, the jni fix) checked the cancel race, handshake cleanup on drop, FFI `Send`/`Sync` and binding checksums, and found one P2. Its finding: calls typed as the generated `EndpointProtocol` must pass `cancel:` explicitly, because Swift protocol requirements carry no default arguments. That's left as is: this API is new, nothing outside this stack calls it, and callers are expected to pass a token for each dial. The later stream-wait tokens (`2dd6b82`) follow the same reviewed pattern and are covered by their own test.

Left to this PR's CI (the `iroh native binding` workflow, which runs on drafts). At `92c2506`, **Linux and Android pass**: all four Android ABIs (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64, x86) with 16 KiB alignment. Both macOS slices build. The iOS slices failed there: `netdev` 0.46.x (pulled in by iroh's `netwatch` 0.19.3) uses `libc::in6_ifreq` on every Apple target, and `libc` 0.2.190 limited that type to macOS.

`Cargo.lock` now pins `libc` at 0.2.189, the version n0's official iroh-ffi v1.2.0 ships its iOS builds with; nothing else in the lockfile moves. `libc` has no RustSec or OSV advisories, and the one memory-safety fix in 0.2.190–0.2.191 (`af_alg_iv` trait impls) isn't used by any locked crate. `scripts/check-pins.sh` fails if the pin drifts while `netdev` 0.46.0–0.46.3 is locked, and a new `iroh native binding audit` workflow runs it plus `cargo audit` (0.22.2) on lockfile changes and weekly. The pin comes off once a `netdev` that skips that code on iOS reaches the lockfile (0.47 already does; `netwatch` 0.20 still needs 0.46). Locally, all six Rust tests pass with the pin. **CI at `031aad5` passes:** [`iroh native binding`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42314731390): linux, android and **apple**. The apple job built all five Rust targets (macOS arm64 + x86_64, iOS device, iOS simulator arm64 + x86_64), wrote the three-slice XCFramework (`macos-arm64_x86_64`, `ios-arm64`, `ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator`) and typechecked the generated Swift. [`iroh native binding audit`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42314731430) passed: the pin check, and `cargo audit` over 412 locked crates found no vulnerabilities, only two unmaintained-crate warnings (`basic-toml` RUSTSEC-2026-0374, `paste` RUSTSEC-2024-0436). `OPENCLAW_IROH_APPLE_PLATFORMS=macos scripts/build-apple.sh` still builds a macOS-only XCFramework, and `PACKAGING.md` documents the pin and the opt-in contract for Swift consumers.

Consumer-lane evidence (not this PR's CI): the Android lane built a host `.so` from `92c2506` with locked, offline Rust 1.99 (13,185,944 bytes, sha256 `5075327bfbed3e3cf89ab261b24648917d2781c03b37cc09b28bdb7bb1d66a0b`; the ABI is unchanged at the current head). It loaded the library on the JVM through the matching generated Kotlin/JNA binding. A loopback smoke passed HEAD framing, FIN, the 62-bit close code, a `CancelToken` dial and a pre-cancelled dial. The generated Kotlin emits seven `UNUSED_EXPRESSION` warnings under Kotlin 2.4.21. The Android app compiles the binding in its own `:openclaw-iroh` module so the app's warnings-as-errors stays on. On the Studio (Apple silicon), the macOS lane built the arm64 macOS library from source, linked it through SwiftPM, and passed a Swift → Rust loopback (streams, FIN, 62-bit close, `CancelToken` with endpoint reuse). The Swift run used `2dd6b82`, which has the same ABI as the current head.

Not yet proved: on-device runs, iOS device and simulator runtime, and the apps actually using the bindings in shipped builds.

Related: stacked on #193993.

prs.title: feat(node): enroll with owner-approved OpenClaw ID invitations
prs.body:
Related: #193982 (transport base)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an owner-approved way to enroll with an OpenClaw ID claw without a user account or Gateway token.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw node join <openclaw-node-link>` and routes the same link through `openclaw connect`. The node shows a six-digit code and its signed command surface for owner approval, verifies admission, then connects in the foreground or installs a service with `--service`.

Discovery must be explicitly configured with `--discovery-url` or retained from the saved node target; there is no production default. Missing configuration fails before key generation. The origin is never inferred from the claw hostname or relay URL.

This is a draft stacked on the Unix/native-process transport preview. Live Gateway node-principal enrollment, real OS service installation, relay-path proof, packaging and broad CI remain unqualified. Bun: addon loads, pairing and worker WS pass; streaming transfer stalls and the tunnel child misses IPC health pings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node signs its actual prepared manifest with its locally held key, sends only the redemption proof to Discovery, and waits for a descriptor. Root/claw/hostname pins, the highest saved same-claw binding sequence, signed snapshot freshness and node membership are checked before the runner persists the target. The same prepared runtime is used for the first connection. Service installation requires an explicit successful first hello and successful cleanup, not merely a resolved runner promise.

Discovery currently returns the same refusal for pending, denied, removed and unavailable membership. The client cannot promptly distinguish these states; it uses bounded polling and an honest ambiguous denial/expiry timeout. No new status API or workaround is invented.

Simplification kept the runner as the sole target-persistence owner and reused existing command selection, key storage, guarded fetch and protocol verification. This PR is the enrollment stage only; it introduces no new state store or migration. The added production logic owns the signed enrollment transaction and its CLI handoff; 499 net regression lines protect distinct protocol, cancellation, CLI and service boundaries.

## Evidence

- Frozen Node-runtime run: **125 tests passed across seven files**, four shards, **124.93s wall time**, including worker compilation. Covers real signed requests against an in-process Discovery HTTP server, root/claw substitution, stale and missing membership, same-claw rollback, cancellation, first-hello outcome, service refusal, CLI dispatch and existing reconnect behavior.
- Core TypeScript check passed (`tsconfig.core.json`). Scoped lint passed on 12 files. Format and diff checks passed.
- CLI helper verified both docs with the MDX checker and repository docs links (16,448 links, no broken links).
- Independent Astra read-only review found two P2 issues (service installation after unsuccessful completion; resetting the saved rollback pin). prs.title: fix(node): reconnect after OpenClaw ID server rotation
prs.body:
Related: #193993, #193982

## What Problem This Solves

Saved OpenClaw ID nodes keep dialing the server key from enrollment, so an honest Gateway key rotation cannot be discovered on reconnect.

## User Impact

Nodes refresh and verify current signed server authority and membership before connecting, retire an active connection when its server key changes, and preserve learned trust across restart and refused re-enrollment. Verified node removal stops the host with a rejoin instruction.

Preview targets without an explicit Discovery origin must rejoin. Pairing assumes the invitation remains secret; the six-digit comparison does not protect against a stolen invitation combined with control of pairing delivery. Existing freshness/v1 bounded-replay limits remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and reconnect share one bounded, node-signed Discovery client and descriptor verifier. The canonical SQLite writer retains the strongest binding pin, membership order, and binding-retirement facts without overwriting unrelated node settings. Persistence completes before dialing; failed persistence stops further attempts. Periodic authority refresh continues during active traffic.

This is one repair commit on top of `openclaw-517/node-join`, not a replacement for the draft feature stack.

## Evidence

- Original source failed the real Unix bridge regressions (8 failed, 4 passed), the protocol retirement regression (1 failed, 8 passed), and the SQLite stale-startup regression. The repair passed all 106 focused tests, including 21 SQLite config tests and four native Gateway integration tests. All 18 affected connection/bridge/native Gateway tests passed again after final corrections.
- Isolated Linux arm64 execution used the real native addon, production Unix bridge, signed loopback Discovery, and a task-local relay. HTTP 200 moved from server A to B after signed rotation; active A closed; restart refused replayed or missing evidence; previously learned retirement evidence survived a newer-order snapshot. Native callback persistence and real SQLite durability were proved separately.
- Changed-file lint, core types, all selected changed-test type graphs, formatting, diff checks, and the test-line budget passed. The +668 LF allocation covers the new bridge, lifecycle, enrollment, protocol, and SQLite regression coverage; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- A qualified local ClawSweeper runtime was unavailable. Local autoreview (OpenAI/Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, high, P0–P2) completed against the change snapshot based on `b7abc8d1cb76e3a5ffba12c1a3f4dca6bf74b81f` with no actionable findings after three initial findings were repaired. Final head: `b697e1b192249307525a33970a8d3fc5df8b466a`.

prs.title: fix(tooling): attribute Control UI coverage at its capture cutoff
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI cold-load coverage had no source-module attribution or exact fetched-script inventory at its cutoff, so unused-code investigations could confuse later network requests with boot cost.

## User Impact

No application behavior or rendering changes. Developers can rank loaded, executed, unused, and fetched-only emitted bytes against an exact production bundle, and compare settled readiness with a later cutoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing source-map attribution and V8 execution-mask owners. The analyzer preserves nested execution overrides, UTF-16 source offsets, emitted UTF-8 byte counts, and explicitly unmapped ranges. It rejects mismatched captured byte lengths. The cold-load harness snapshots completed JavaScript resources immediately before coverage stops, instead of borrowing the full-run waterfall. Legacy captures retain an explicitly labeled whole-run fallback.

A focused first-custom-icon-input scenario also makes deferred validation cost observable without warming the input or applying the draft. This caught a false optimization during the investigation.

The boot investigation did not establish a qualifying application speedup. All experimental production changes were removed. Deferring emoji validation regressed first input; changing the regex to a literal merely moved cost into parsing; a separate IP-address chunk added a boot request; deferring a source-preview parser did not clear the screen. The printable-ASCII fast path was screened with ten rotated A/A/B pairs per engine and cold/warm flow, then removed for lack of a meaningful gain. No size ceiling changes.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused attribution tests | Passed: emitted-byte conservation, nested overrides, Unicode, fetched-only and unmapped assets, exact-build mismatch and invalid-range rejection |
| UI and tooling test typechecks | Passed, including the repair |
| Archived performance fixture tests | 50 passed after repair; missing-helper failure reproduced locally first |
| Targeted format / lint | Passed; final CLI replay exactly matches the captured report |
| Production Knip | Passed |
| Independent autoreview | Scoped-clean at P0–P2 on the initial snapshot and again on the isolated-fixture repair; no actionable findings |
| Application code | Unchanged; no visual change or screenshot requirement |
| Startup / Chat / New Session normalized JS gzip | 90,900 / 1,294,876 / 803,127 B; unchanged by the final tooling-only diff |
| Requests | Startup 3 JS + 1 CSS; Chat 20 JS; New Session 15 JS; unchanged |
| Absolute budget state | Base already exceeds document gzip, total CSS raw/gzip, and Chat gzip caps. The discarded ASCII candidate was within the 64 B comparison variance floor; final application bytes are unchanged. |

Initial CI run `42410269505` exposed an isolated-fixture dependency omission in the `Control UI performance budgets` suite and the archived comparison cases `compares archived source revisions` and `preserves comparison failure when candidate attribution is malformed`. The missing import was reproduced locally. The unchanged execution mask now has a dependency-free helper shared by the trace and attribution owners, and the archived fixture explicitly includes it. No assertions were weakened.

Coverage uses the existing synthetic cold-load fixture and a fresh context per cutoff. “Ready” means the harness's settled route and event queue (including its 750 ms quiet window), not first paint or the first enabled composer. Both cutoffs include idle preloads begun in that window. Coverage is range execution, not CPU attribution or permission to delete a module.

| new-0 | 2,751,924 | 1,310,477 | 1,441,447 | 52.38% | 0 |

The three-engine initializer diagnostic used three fresh passes per route (18 successful captures). It wraps Rolldown source initializers as well as chunk bodies, subtracting nested initializer time. Chromium's largest repeatable leaf costs were the emoji regex (~8.9 ms), grapheme Segmenter (~4.6 ms), and Markdown file grammar (~5.1 ms on Chat). Firefox's emoji regex was ~10–11 ms; WebKit did not show a comparable leaf cost. Instrumented elapsed time is diagnostic and does not establish the cause of WebKit's first-visit gap.

prs.title: feat(node-host): connect nodes over the OpenClaw ID tunnel
prs.body:
Related: #193980 (protocol base), #193993 (enrollment follow-up), #192345 (tunnel server)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need to reach a claw through OpenClaw ID without LAN reachability, Tailscale, SSH, or a Gateway bearer token.

## User Impact

Labs transport preview: a saved OpenClaw ID target can run or reinstall a Unix node host using its locally generated iroh key. Main and worker WebSockets, desktop/portal attachment streams, bundle downloads, and workspace transfers share the same private tunnel. Existing ws/wss targets are unchanged. Enrollment remains the separate #193993 follow-up.

This preview supports Unix hosts and native-process workers, not Windows or container-isolated workers. Node is the qualified runtime. Bun streaming, relayed operation, and live node-principal enrollment are not qualified by this PR. Native prebuilt packages must be rebuilt for the added optional `keepAliveMs` API through the existing platform packaging flow; no binaries are committed or published here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node verifies the saved ServerBinding against its claw/root/sequence pin and dials only its K_srv over `openclaw/tunnel/1`. IP transports remain enabled; the relay is a routing hint. The local key stays in a 0600 private node-state file, not config, logs, or worker descriptors. One owner-only Unix bridge (0600 socket in a fresh 0700 directory) shares that identity without distributing its secret or opening a TCP listener.

The connection owner supplies keep-alives, silent-connection probes, relay-denial backoff, and terminal membership-removal handling. Diagnostics show the logical claw target and observed route, not private socket paths. Service installation preserves the saved target and does not inherit unrelated Cloudflare/Gateway credentials. Optional Discovery routing is persisted independently, never inferred from the claw hostname or relay.

Review repairs keep desktop/portal attachment paths on that same bridge and drain queued WebSocket data before graceful close + FIN; abnormal closure still resets immediately. This fixes a reproduced finite-response truncation rather than adding another connection or buffering owner. Existing binding, framing, client, key-storage, and config owners are reused; enrollment and Gateway authorization remain separate stack stages.

## Evidence

Reviewed repair head: `5771dc00ae185442c456c6899c015cc31e6eb058`, based on protocol `d6f0b8f7c9b2d594a44c524adbe52aeec294071b`.

- Independent Astra/high read-only review of the full PR range, followed by scoped re-review of all repairs: **three verified P2 findings fixed; no remaining verified P0–P2 findings**. Findings were unsupported auxiliary-stream URLs, Cloudflare environment interference with saved-target installation, and premature tunnel reset on graceful EOF.
- All three defects reproduced red at their production boundaries before repair. Native finite-response reproduction received only **1,376,256 of 2,097,169 bytes**. The repaired native regression receives and verifies the entire payload after delaying the downstream reader until local completion.
- Final EOF repair: **33/33 tests pass across two files** — **7/7 real native/Gateway tunnel tests** and **26/26 existing direct-stream tests**. Native cases cover node-role pairing, worker WebSocket transport, desktop and portal attachments, finite-response EOF, both >2 MiB HTTP transfer routes, health, and private key permissions. Latest run wall time **110.76 s**; native file **97.86 s**, predominantly compiler/startup work (one shared Gateway/child fixture).
- Earlier frozen repair proof retained for unchanged inputs: **104/104 tests across five files**, including installer partial/full Cloudflare environment regressions and direct TLS/proxy stream siblings (**124.92 s** wall). Original full focused run: **187/187 tests across 11 files**, including all four then-existing native cases (**324.87 s** wall).
- Final core TypeScript check, touched-file lint, complete PR formatting, staged diff check, and test-line allocation pass. A dedicated **116-line regression allocation** preserves the shared scalar, with **27 lines slack** against the pinned protocol base.
- Native addon built with CI-pinned Rust 1.99; **11/11 binding tests**, `cargo fmt --check`, and release clippy with warnings denied pass. Full `pnpm build` passed before the review repair; it emitted UI-size budget warnings, not a failed build. The initial missing-plugin dependency setup was repaired with a frozen-lockfile install, without lockfile changes.
- The first ready-state CI at `c32fd63f27cb` completed with 80 passing checks and three PR-owned failures: the synthetic WebSocket fixture lacked an explicit payload bound; the worker-connect fixture lacked its canonical client identity/protocol range; two type assertions failed the safety-comment guard. All are repaired in `5771dc00ae18`, independently re-reviewed, and verified with the failed assertion guard, core and Gateway-server test typechecks, lint, and all 33 native/direct-stream cases. No inherited failure was identified. [Initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42410791592).
- **Final-head CI is green:** [run 42411845223](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42411845223) completed successfully on `5771dc00ae185442c456c6899c015cc31e6eb058`. The final PR check rollup has **79 passing, 54 skipped, zero failing, zero pending** checks, including precise security scanning and native build lanes. No inherited failures remain. CI wall time: **485 s**; sum of executed CI-job durations: **9,955 s** across **58 non-skipped jobs** (parallel job time, not wall time).

The native fixture uses owner-principal admission and a synthetic worker/attachment upstream to exercise transport; it is not proof of live node enrollment, node-principal authorization, or a full desktop UI session. Earlier Bun testing passed pairing/worker WebSocket but stalled streaming HTTP and missed child IPC health pings; no Bun workaround was added. Direct iroh dialing was used for native proof. Native tests skip when the separately built addon is unavailable, but none skipped in the local runs reported above.

prs.title: improve(gateway): reduce unnecessary session visibility work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session lists and session-event row publication eagerly read invitation membership even when the caller's visibility capability does not use it.

## User Impact

Less main-thread work when preparing session rows for callers whose visibility is not invitation-limited. Visible rows, sharing roles, draft handling, and invitation revocation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing visibility owner consumes membership only for the `invited` capability. Its list, linked-row, and event callers now skip preparing that unused input for other capabilities. Role projection still reads membership where it determines member versus viewer. Production LOC is net zero; there is no new cache, policy, configuration, or schema.

The freeze/copy audit found the retained operations protect newly composed display data or recipient-specific enrichment identity. Actor entries and owner identity facts already reuse their upstream ownership; deleting those remaining protections would change their contract.

## Evidence

The existing cold RPC list test fails on the parent with 390 unnecessary membership reads and passes with zero. Its viewer/draft assertions remain intact. The prepared-sharing capability table also fails on the parent for excess reads and passes with unchanged visibility and roles. All 27 focused tests pass across serialization, prepared sharing, event sharing, and row presentation, including invitation revocation at final delivery. The final deferred-target refinement was replayed through the cold RPC test. Independent Codex autoreview is clean through P2.

`pnpm check:changed --staged` completed. The initial line-cap failure was corrected and that guard passes on the final tree. Other type, lint, SQL, and boundary checks pass except these exact-parent failures, reproduced at `f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1`:

- Dead export `parseDarwinProcessBirths`: introduced by #194245 (`5577faefa9e1`).
- Six gesture-probe dead exports: introduced by #194676 (`055544b9fa35`).
- Historical changelog attribution: 20 rejected credits introduced by #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`). The affected four files pass at its parent and fail at that commit and this baseline. This is a newly identified main regression requiring separate owner repair.

No shared or UI-imported runtime module changed. No production environment or data was accessed.

### Synthetic measurement

3,000 synthetic sessions, four agents, mixed owners and sharing, an identified viewer, default `{}` list params, 100 returned rows. Five AB/BA pairs plus A/A, 100 warmups and 2,000 calls per arm; separate CPU/GC and inclusive allocation sampling. Both arms use the same Git-source loader, with runtime sources pinned to the parent and candidate. Every response digest matches.

| Consumer | CPU ms/call before → after | Median paired CPU change | Allocated kB/call before → after | GC/2,000 calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| plain | 1.585 → 1.209 | -10.73% | 1464.50 → 1461.88 | 87 → 87 |
| serialized | 0.486 → 0.488 | +1.69% | 661.95 → 660.86 | 39 → 39 |

Plain-response CPU improves in every pair (9.0–30.2%); its A/A CPU drift was −3.34%. Serialized CPU has no convincing change (A/A −3.39%). Allocation A/A drift was +0.25% / +0.16%; no meaningful allocation or GC-count reduction is demonstrated. Production LOC: **0 net**. Tests: **+5**, extending existing behavior cases; workload script: **+28**.

Median/p95 latency, ms: plain **1.570/2.169 → 1.174/1.690**; serialized **0.440/0.755 → 0.438/0.744**. One original serialized pair had +30.4% p95. A separately reported 10,000-call AB/BA follow-up did not reproduce that increase: p95 **0.480 → 0.473** and **0.517 → 0.551**; CPU **0.4048 → 0.4044** and **0.4163 → 0.4189**. All four diagnostic arms had 189 GCs and identical output. No original pair was discarded.

First-read wall-time medians: plain **195.3 → 206.6 ms**, serialized **199.0 → 188.0 ms**; mixed-sign cold pairs, with no cold-start improvement claimed. This is a resident owner workload on a shared Mac, not full Gateway transport, large-database, filesystem, or production stall proof. The pre-run rule required identical results and lower ordinary-consumer CPU/allocation without a reproducible >20% serialized regression. CPU/work removal is demonstrated; the allocation objective is not.

Reproduce on this head (first run seeds the fixture; add `--reuse-fixture` thereafter):

```sh

  --state-dir .local/session-visibility-bench --sessions 3000 --agents 4 \
  --iterations 2000 --warmup 100 --updates-per-list 0 --list-shape default \

```

Use `--mode allocation` for separate allocation sampling; omit `--plain-result` for serialized consumers. Orders: AA, AB, BA, AB, BA, AB. Separate `--cpu-profile` runs diagnose owners and are excluded from timing results.

Separate diagnostic CPU profiles show `session-membership-projection.membership` self time dropping from **0.101 to 0.007 ms/call**. Necessary role membership reads remain. Profiled total CPU is not used for the performance comparison. Candidate: `95082407850555f9e9f62c13f16bfb03d6135388` (its tree exactly matches the measured snapshot).

prs.title: fix(ui): keep Worked timing on earlier completed turns
prs.body:
## Problem

In Control UI chat, a completed turn's "Worked for 47m 11s" header drops back to plain "Worked" once a newer run starts in the same session. Only the session row (`lastRunId` / `runtimeMs`) could supply a duration, and that row only describes the latest run.

## Solution

`collapseCompletedTurnWork` still uses the session row while it describes the run. For earlier runs it now reads the transcript instead: it measures from the prompt that started the run (matched by its `<runId>:user` key) to the last `recordTimestampMs` write of that run's output. The duration is the write time of the output, not when the message was created, which avoids the original concern that creation timestamps miss the final model request. Output with no recorded write time, and work spanning several runs, still shows no duration.

Accepted edge case: right after a newer run starts, the earlier turn's duration may differ by about a second from the lifecycle value it had before. On live sessions, the transcript value was within 1–4 s of `runtimeMs`.

## Evidence

- Regression: `chat-transcript-duration.test.ts` (independent earlier run) fails on base (`["Worked", "Worked for 20s"]`) and passes with the fix (`["Worked for 8s", "Worked for 20s"]`).
- Real data: rendered the exact reported turn from a live session's `chat.history` (session row showing a newer running run). Base shows `Worked`; the fix shows `Worked for 47m 11s`. The temporary harness is not committed.
- Consumer unit tests: 9 files, 297 passed. UI e2e: `chat-run-lifecycle`, `chat-worked-for-visualization`, `chat-cold-load-anchor` all pass (21 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix(plugins): cancel interrupted marketplace list reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An acknowledged interrupt during the read-only `openclaw plugins marketplace list <source>` does not cancel the pending marketplace source read. When the source is a git/GitHub URL, the read is a `git clone` that stays open until the process is forced down, and an uncancelled late result can still reach the renderer. This is the invocation-interrupt class repaired for ClawHub package searches in #194076, and for inference in #192896 and #193893.

Precedent: #194076（同形状：read-only CLI 网络读 + invocation signal 转发；本 PR 换点位到 git-clone 泳道）

## Why This Change Was Made

#194076 forwarded the invocation signal through the ClawHub HTTP adapters (`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already declared `signal`). The marketplace list git-clone path was not covered: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` passed no signal into `listMarketplacePlugins` / `loadMarketplace` / `cloneMarketplaceRepo` / `acquireGitSource`, so the underlying `git clone` never saw cancellation even though `runCommandWithTimeout` already declares `signal`.

This PR preserves the established behavior: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` now checks the invocation signal before dispatch and before publishing a result, and forwards it through the existing chain into `acquireGitSource`, whose `run` closure passes it to `runCommandWithTimeout`. The parameter stays optional, so install callers (`installPluginFromMarketplace`, git-install, source-install) keep their existing behavior. No new validator, option, config, retry policy, lifetime owner, or schema.

Production LOC is `+17/-0`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Interrupting `openclaw plugins marketplace list <git-or-https-source>` inside a managed async-work scope now aborts the pending clone and suppresses the late result/output, instead of printing the marketplace after Ctrl+C. Uninterrupted listings, local path sources, and install flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `02e423602de`
- Current-main RED baseline: `8662f3bf78dc7d644d207c8afb6f2f8b8f5750b0`
- Production entry: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` in `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `listMarketplacePlugins` in `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`, `acquireGitSource` in `src/infra/git-source.ts`
- Decision surface: the interruption signal forwarded from the CLI into the git-clone read path
- Recorder/readback boundary: captured CLI output / JSON write for a late marketplace result after the signal fires
- Acceptance RED: on pristine current-main, the same `AsyncWorkScope` scenario prints the late marketplace result (`writeJson`) after `beginClose()`; both cancel cases fail.
- Acceptance GREEN: on this head, both cancel cases emit no output, no JSON, no error, no exit; all 16 marketplace suite tests pass.
- Legal controls: uninterrupted json/text listing still prints the marketplace; existing marketplace/git-source suites (39 tests) pass unchanged.
- Cleanup and limitations: every run used isolated temp state; no production Gateway, session, channel, token, or config was touched.
- Format and ratchet: the cancellation regressions live in a dedicated command test file (oxfmt-clean), and the justified test lines are offset by a scoped test-lines allocation.

### Real Git child-process cancellation (RED -> GREEN)

The signal-forwarding contract is proven against a **real `git clone` subprocess**, not a mock. A local TCP listener that accepts but never responds (`git://127.0.0.1:<port>/repo.git`) holds a real `git clone` open; `acquireGitSource` calls the real `runCommandWithTimeout` and the real `git` binary. The CLI-side `AsyncWorkScope` owns the forwarded signal.

| Build | Interrupt | Returned after | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| RED (no signal passed) | — | **8041 ms** (timeout 8000) | clone hangs until `runCommandWithTimeout` force-kills it |
| GREEN (signal forwarded) | `beginClose()` | **11 ms** | git child process cancelled immediately; no late output |

Timing is monotonic wall time from start; both runs share the identical hanging source, temp output dir, and `git` binary. The RED run proves the pre-fix behavior waits out the whole timeout; the GREEN run proves the forwarded signal reaches and cancels the live git child process. No external network, credentials, or non-local services are involved.

### Shipped CLI real-PTY proof (independent build)

A **shipped `openclaw.mjs`** was independently built from this head (Node 24.22.1, tsdown runtime build) and driven through a **real controlling PTY** with a **real `git clone`** against a local slow git source (`http://127.0.0.1:19428/repo.git`, a TCP listener that accepts but never responds, so the clone stays pending). SIGINT is delivered as the terminal VINTR byte; the same slow source, temp HOME/profile, and `git` binary are used for every run.

| Build | SIGINT | Settled after | Observable behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| RED (base, no signal) | VINTR | **1.6 s** | Bare `^C`; the process is hard-killed by the signal with **no cleanup notice and no cancellation of the in-flight clone**. Without SIGINT the clone stays pending past the `runCommandWithTimeout` window (>15 s, only the timeout force-kill settles it). |
| GREEN (this head, signal forwarded) | VINTR | **3.2 s** | `^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` then `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"Plugin CLI invocation is closed"}}`; the live `git clone` child process is cancelled (zero git processes remain) and no marketplace JSON is emitted. |

The RED run proves the interrupted in-flight Git read is not cancelled on the base (either hard-killed with no settlement, or left pending to the timeout), and the GREEN run proves the forwarded invocation signal reaches the real `git clone` subprocess and cancels it with a clean settlement. No mocks are imported into the CLI; the built binary, the child git process, and the terminal are all real.


### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace (command suite)

`vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

```text
RED (pristine main, production code without signal):
  × plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: before
  × plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: result
  Tests  2 failed (2)

GREEN (this head):
  ✓ plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: before
  ✓ plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: result
  Tests  2 passed (2)
```

### Test placement

The cancellation regressions live in a dedicated `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts` that mocks only `../runtime.js` and `../plugins/marketplace.js`, each with a `mock-isolation:` annotation accepted by the mock-exports guard:

- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` — passes (two annotated factories in the new file).
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` — passes; the added lines are offset by a scoped test-lines allocation.

The cancellation cases were deliberately kept out of `src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts`, which carries a pre-existing redaction fixture with credential-like literals; touching that file changes its head blob and trips the review input scanner's literal-mismatch heuristic as a false positive.

### Verification

- `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts` — 2 passed (head), 2 failed (pristine base)
- `src/plugins/marketplace.test.ts` + `src/plugins/marketplace.sources.test.ts` + `src/infra/git-source.test.ts` — 39 passed (no regression)
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` + `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` + `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` — pass
- `git diff --check`
- Not tested: a live `node openclaw.mjs` PTY run against a remote git URL on this host (network read; the terminal-recording form of this proof was supplied by the maintainer for the sibling #194076/#193893); the signal-forwarding contract is proven here at the live git-child boundary and at the CLI output-suppression boundary.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+17/-0`
- Test LOC: `+65/-18` (dedicated file; the entries suite is reverted to main)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `getAsyncWorkSignal` (already exported for CLI commands) and the already-declared `signal` on `runCommandWithTimeout`; no new abstraction.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Optional parameter; all existing callers unchanged.

Closes #194709

Requested by @GrahamMcBain: https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2119116272671785017

OpenClaw users looking for phone control lack a discoverable guide to Phone Harness's existing native OpenClaw integration.

## User Impact

Users can find the vendor plugin installation path, choose an appropriate Gateway/device setup, expose `phone_exec` deliberately, and understand privacy and consent implications before using a personal or cloud phone. This is documentation-only: it does not introduce a driver, messaging channel, cloud account, credential store, or new runtime behavior.

Phone Harness already maintains the plugin and bundled skill. Reusing that integration follows the existing capability ladder instead of creating a competing phone runtime in core. The guide covers Gateway-host requirements, local versus cloud devices, telemetry opt-out before first use, tool profiles, sandbox limitations, session-wide approval semantics, human takeover, and consequential-action consent. Runtime and device details remain owned upstream.

Installing the plugin does not authorize messages, calls, purchases, paid cloud provisioning, or access to private verification codes. The guide recommends synthetic test data and user takeover for passwords/PINs/2FA.

## Evidence

- Audited the official [OpenClaw plugin README and source](https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness/tree/4bebff105af853215fb74c958c2c5e78bc275be2/integrations/openclaw), device installation guide, and cloud MCP documentation.

Validation gap: no third-party plugin installation/execution, authenticated cloud session, or real-device end-to-end test was performed. No phones, private codes, calls/messages, purchases, or paid services were used. prs.title: fix(agents): reduce stalls from failed file tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Failed file edits calculate full string distances for diagnostic candidates that can never be shown. Missing-file reads also retain and sort every qualifying filename in large directories.

## User Impact

Failed file tool calls spend less time on the main thread while returning exactly the same candidates, ordering, scores, and messages. No configuration, data, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep only the best three suggestions at each existing owner and bound later distance calculations by the current third-best score/distance. Edit scoring also uses the existing 0.45 acceptance threshold. Round score-to-distance bounds outward, retain final score filtering, and preserve stable edit ties and filename locale ordering. The shared distance helper is unchanged. No first-character/extension heuristics or caches. Production code is net −3 lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: real `prepareFileEdit` and `createReadTool.execute` owners; synthetic 1,000 × 120-character files and 50,000 real directory entries; pinned parent `f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1` versus candidate with unchanged dependencies. Ten measured warm-ups per arm, five counterbalanced AB/BA pairs plus five A/A pairs. Separate main-thread CPU/wall timing and collected-object heap sampling. Require exact outputs, lower dominant CPU, and no material regression. This measures diagnostic owners, not model/Gateway latency. Ten failed calls are distinct from a ten-edit batch, which stops at its first mismatch.

| Workload | CPU median ms A → B | CPU p95 ms A → B | Wall median ms A → B | Heap median bytes A → B | Heap p95 bytes A → B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| read-50000-short | 3.296 → 3.245 | 4.209 → 3.704 | 37.160 → 37.614 | 7,673,784 → 7,665,576 | 7,760,312 → 8,009,008 |
| read-50000-long | 155.328 → 141.515 | 156.661 → 154.105 | 189.604 → 176.138 | 15,706,416 → 15,256,520 | 16,117,520 → 15,548,952 |
| edit-unrelated-10x1000x120 | 416.472 → 234.177 | 425.559 → 239.169 | 418.265 → 234.258 | 4,389,552 → 4,424,232 | 4,476,520 → 4,457,384 |
| edit-unrelated-batch10x1000x120 | 41.402 → 23.455 | 41.640 → 23.590 | 41.389 → 23.454 | 463,064 → 426,320 | 467,256 → 446,624 |
| edit-near-10x1000x120 | 427.023 → 327.682 | 430.640 → 328.578 | 427.097 → 327.739 | 6,911,440 → 4,914,504 | 6,938,504 → 4,947,632 |
| edit-near-batch10x1000x120 | 43.753 → 32.725 | 44.372 → 33.991 | 43.760 → 32.711 | 890,920 → 489,304 | 1,064,408 → 509,576 |

All 2,512 benchmark differential cases and 32 randomized read-message comparisons match the old implementation. All 95 focused edit/read tests pass. The read work-count regression fails the parent with 4,326 character-code reads against a 206 budget and passes the fix. Boundary tests preserve cutoff scores and earlier equal-score lines. Test growth of 93 lines has an exact allocation record. Cold-wrapper times: 61.43 s for the two edit suites; 13.74 s for the final read suite. Actual test bodies stay below five seconds per file.

`pnpm check:changed` completed. Core production/test and script typechecking and other guards passed. Task-local formatting/lint findings were fixed and focused checks rerun successfully. Remaining failures reproduce with the entire tracked working tree verified equal to the exact parent:

- #194245 (`5577faefa9e1`): dead export `parseDarwinProcessBirths`.
- #194676 (`055544b9fa35`): dead gesture-probe function and five types.
- Additional main regression #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`): newly forbidden attribution handles reject 20 unchanged historical release entries. This needs main repair; it is not noise.

Final Codex P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean. Focused lint/format, test-line budget, and affected typechecks pass. No changed module is imported by Control UI; the shared helper is unchanged. No deployment performed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, controls, and measurement limits</summary>

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/read-path-suggestions-measure.ts --baseline f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1 --sizes 50000 --pairs 5 --mode timing
# Repeat with --mode allocation.
```

A/A controls (both labels execute the parent); CPU medians and full min–max spread:

- read-50000-short: CPU 3.257/3.428 ms, range 2.857–4.088; sampled heap medians 7,603,848/7,628,728, range 7,285,384–7,814,624 bytes.
- read-50000-long: CPU 157.075/156.087 ms, range 155.303–162.297; sampled heap medians 15,917,696/15,646,096, range 15,525,472–16,197,664 bytes.
- edit-unrelated-10x1000x120: CPU 415.903/413.435 ms, range 412.235–422.046; sampled heap medians 4,299,368/4,319,640, range 4,194,728–4,528,664 bytes.
- edit-unrelated-batch10x1000x120: CPU 41.551/41.589 ms, range 41.411–41.896; sampled heap medians 438,048/430,184, range 397,192–483,776 bytes.
- edit-near-10x1000x120: CPU 428.473/429.916 ms, range 425.241–434.428; sampled heap medians 6,810,784/7,005,072, range 6,497,984–7,139,800 bytes.
- edit-near-batch10x1000x120: CPU 42.989/43.552 ms, range 42.080–44.278; sampled heap medians 860,768/903,776, range 782,920–958,040 bytes.

Allocation is sampled V8 heap including collected objects; ArrayBuffer backing stores are excluded. Both edit arms still allocate 10,000 rows × 121 × 4 = 4,840,000 backing-store bytes for ten 120-character failures. Unrelated-edit heap median moves +0.8%; near-edit heap falls 28.9%, long-read heap falls 2.9%, and short-read heap is neutral. Short-read wall median/p95 move +1.2%/+7.6%; long-read wall p95 moves +6.4% while its median improves 7.1%. No 20% acceptance regression remains. Five-sample p95 is the sample maximum; the JSON includes every sample, load, source hash, and min/max spread.

An intermediate `.entries()` loop increased allocation about 50% and was replaced with direct `forEach`. An earlier timing run had scheduling noise during review setup; final acceptance timing runs separately from task checks/reviews. The previous two-call warm-up biased allocation tails because A/A warmed only the parent. Both arms showed transient allocations during early profiled calls; ten paired measured warm-ups remove that bias without dropping samples. Final fully warmed long-read CPU improvement is 8.9%, smaller than the preliminary 17.6%.

A separate pinned-parent CPU profile attributes 98.3% of edit-subtree sampled time to Levenshtein self time. Profile timings are not acceptance evidence. Files and names are synthetic; session database size and unrelated workspace file contents are not traversed by these diagnostic owners.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

SQLite startup builds historical agent PostgreSQL schemas that it never uses, including in workers that import the agent database owner.

## User Impact

SQLite processes defer those allocations. PostgreSQL keeps the same migration plan and constructs it once on first use. No configuration, schema version, data migration, or operator action changes. RSS savings have not been measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing shared-state database pattern at the agent schema owner: lazily materialize and retain the historical migration plan. This removes eager historical-schema construction from SQLite imports without adding another cache or backend policy. The current schema remains available immediately.

## Evidence

- All 14 migration array entries are byte-identical to the base; historical builder expressions are unchanged apart from indentation.
- Targeted formatting, `git diff --check`, and native pre-commit checks passed. Independent source review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Extended the existing regression through a real in-memory SQLite agent opener, then requests both state and agent PostgreSQL plans and checks reuse. Runtime execution is pending.
- Local runtime dependencies are unqualified and the existing remote proof allocation was capacity-stalled and stopped. Exact-head [main-tier CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42395207004) is running; build and focused test results are required before marking ready. No baseline-red/candidate-green or RSS result is claimed yet.
- Production +14 net lines implement deferred ownership; tests +10 net lines extend the existing boundary regression, with an exact 10-line allocation.

Release note: avoid constructing historical agent PostgreSQL schemas during SQLite startup.

## What Problem This Solves

Qualifies whether a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link can preserve the old page until one complete cached frame.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The original campaign recorded fourteen visual states over roughly fifteen seconds. Current cached rows and Details co-frame, but their readiness must fit Chromium's compositor hold before a visibility join is admissible.

Frame inspection found that the Team benchmark's existing cache-input reset navigates through an empty document. That cannot prove old-app → complete behavior. The opt-in diagnostic now calibrates PaintHolding, retains the real old-page DOM while restoring the existing frozen inputs, and records untraced native compositor surfaces. There is no DOM/screenshot replay. Ordinary benchmark reset behavior remains intact. This diagnostic mode excludes profiling and multi-bundle comparison.

The corrected baseline misses the prerequisite on both Team workloads. No visibility hold, new Details wait, or sidebar-first yield deletion was implemented. Pane-cost work remains outside this lane.

Measured application build: `bdadf47c59c951941a9ec201da7dcef47b0f3e6e`, a documentation-only child of main `078033289a36539d966439be4f111cb52dcc1975`, including `fe2b1a51b41b`. The first new-document state is a skeleton in 20/20. prs.title: fix(agents): classify the explicit auth-order refusal as an auth failure
prs.body:
Closes #194689

## What Problem This Solves

When the compaction model's credentials become unusable, budget-triggered compaction fails after a single attempt (`attempt=1 maxAttempts=1`) and never walks the configured model fallback chain, so long sessions get stuck on "conversation is too long" for every message. Ordinary turns recover by rotating to the next fallback candidate; compaction did not, because the refusal was not recognized as a failover-eligible failure.

Plain language: the summarizer's login stopped working, so every cleanup attempt died instantly and the whole conversation got jammed, even though two healthy backup models were configured and ordinary chats were already using them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compaction already runs `runWithModelFallback`, but its `classifyResult` only falls back when the failure coerces to a failover error. The OpenClaw route preflight refusal — `Explicit auth order for <provider> has no usable profiles.` — matched none of the auth failure patterns, so `coerceToFailoverError` returned null and the fallback loop stopped before the first candidate. Adding that OpenClaw-authored refusal string to the auth patterns classifies it as `reason: "auth"`, which the fallback loop already treats as rotate-to-next-candidate (and ordinary turns gain the more accurate `auth` reason instead of `unknown` for the same message).

## User Impact

Compaction now rotates to the session's configured fallback models when the primary compaction route's credentials are unusable, matching ordinary turn behavior. Diagnostics for the same refusal report `auth` instead of `unknown`. Explicitly setting `agents.defaults.compaction.model` still pins compaction to that model without a fallback walk — that broader behavior change is left out of this focused fix.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on latest main content (worktree files verified byte-identical to `main` + this change before push):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `classify.test.ts` auth-evidence table, new row `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.` → `isAuthErrorMessage=true`, `classifyFailoverReason="auth"` | green (43/43) |
| `failover-error.test.ts`, new test: `coerceToFailoverError(new Error("Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles."))` → `{ reason: "auth" }` (the exact value compaction's `classifyResult` needs to fall back) | green (54/54) |
| Red check: pattern removed → exactly the new classify row fails (1 failed / 42 passed); restored → all green | confirmed |
| Adjacent failover suites (`classify.legacy-provider-predicates`, `failover-classification.corpus`, `retry-evidence`, `provider-structured-signals`) | all green, no new false positives |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #194689, trace the compaction fallback path through `compact.ts` classifyResult to the failover message patterns, and implement the one-pattern fix. The implementer understands the code: the refusal is an OpenClaw-authored preflight string, so pattern-classifying it as `auth` is the minimal seam that reuses the existing fallback loop. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): admit nodes over the tunnel with owner-approved pairing
prs.body:
Related: #193980

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need to reach a claw through OpenClaw ID without an account, a shared Gateway token, or Tailscale, while remaining separate from owner and member identities.

## User Impact

Labs-enabled claws can admit owner-approved node keys over the tunnel. The owner compares a six-digit code and reviews the node's signed, self-reported command/capability description. First pairing approves only that surface, once per key; removing the pairing keeps later requests manual. Removing or revoking the key disconnects it and retires its node-role pairing and surface without deleting unrelated roles.

This is the Gateway portion of the coordinated stack. The node-host, Discovery, and Control UI pieces are separate. It adds no Gateway-local invitation signing and has not been exercised against a live relay deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node principals accept only node-role/node-mode connections, with no operator scopes, operator HTTP access, or plugin cookies. Worker WebSocket and transfer routes keep their own credentials. Existing authority serialization owns invitations and membership; the pairing worker atomically records the one-time receipt, provenance, and reviewed surface. Startup reconciliation also cleans orphaned grants when Labs is off, without deleting still-current listings.

The owner view exposes pending descriptions/codes and admitted nodes through existing authority/People APIs. Documentation marks the flow as Labs. Invite operations and owner projections live in sibling modules rather than growing the authority/service lifecycle modules beyond their limits; no new database schema or parallel authority owner is introduced.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `4fc18ce33e9763b25f01c7ece2f1643c6de10634` (ready, not merged).

- Restacked on protocol #193980 at `d6f0b8f7c9b2d594a44c524adbe52aeec294071b`. On pre-repair head `e58742427a9cbc850107bdda0be797a526d8ddcb`, core typecheck passed and 313 tests passed across 52 files (10 skipped). This covers Gateway OpenClaw ID, node access/pairing, workspace transfer, and device pairing.
- Independent read-only review of the full `d6f0b8f..e587424` delta found one P2: manually paired first-time tunnel nodes could automatically re-pair after explicit removal. A Gateway WebSocket regression reproduced the defect (reconnect unexpectedly succeeded after database close/reopen). The existing pairing transaction now consumes automatic eligibility when it issues or reuses a node-bound token, including manual-first connections. The repair passed 54 tests across 6 files; the corrected migration fixture was separately rerun, 4/4 passing.
- Startup migration remains solely in the protocol parent's `upgradeNodeCollections()`/`readInitial()`, unchanged here. Node-authority fixtures now persist a pre-node Labs record without either collection before loading it; signed node invite registration, pending redemption, approval, removal and expired approval rejection all pass on migrated state.
- Core typecheck, 12-file scoped lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet, test-line budget, database-worker ratchet and Madge cycle check passed locally. Gateway/infra repair suites took 144.20 seconds wrapper wall time including 78.81 seconds compiled-worker preparation; the manual-first regression test body took 2.43 seconds. Migration fixture rerun took 33.92 seconds wrapper wall time.
- The complete repair received a second read-only review with no verified P0–P2 findings. The optional-signer fixture type correction was checked separately with tests/lint. The exact two-line credential-writer inventory registration also received independent review with no verified P0–P2 findings.
- Simplification reuses one suppression-receipt helper, the existing pairing transaction and canonical machine-state writer. Result types now live in a leaf contract rather than a circular import. Removed the mock-only removal call-shape test and its three incomplete mocks; actual pairing/removal lifecycle coverage remains. No schema or additional state owner was added.
- Narrow guard registration: only `consumeOpenClawIdNodePairingInWorker` may call the canonical machine-state writer. Its key is always `devicePairing.openclawIdNode.<peer>` and value is boolean `true`; it cannot select `authProfiles.store`. The source-verified exact caller registration follows existing fixed-prefix registrations and does not exempt a file or weaken generic writer checks.

### CI and proof limitations

The pre-repair [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42408712165) found PR-caused mock-export, machine-state writer and type-cycle guard failures; this repair addresses them. Its [archive-lifecycle shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42408712165/job/128512310122) also failed `identity changes fence archive before cancellation and force fresh authorization` during native-borrower teardown. The repository classifier reported **unknown** (no matching main job), not inherited. Bounded standalone replay passed all 17 archive-lifecycle tests, and all 103 credential-writer guard tests passed. This is not an original-order shard reproduction and does not prove the teardown defect fixed. Final-head [CI run 42409996878](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42409996878) completed **successfully** on `4fc18ce33e9763b25f01c7ece2f1643c6de10634`; the final archive shard also passed. The PR check watcher exited 0 with no pending or failed checks. Non-CI superseded automation entries include three canceled checks; these are not counted as passing tests.

No live relay deployment or latest-stable upgrade was exercised. The transport-boundary tests use attributed test ingress; they do not establish assembled node-host/Discovery/relay end-to-end proof. Final-head CI is green, not a claim that these proof gaps are closed. Josh performs the merge after the protocol parent lands; this session will not merge.

### Upstream tunnel ingress integration

The protocol base now includes #192345's synthetic-address ingress fix. Production ingress sets `reportedClientIpSource = "none"` for tunnel traffic, preventing trusted-CIDR and SSH network identity approval. The node-specific first-pairing path uses live authority, the owner-reviewed description and the once-per-peer receipt. Existing explicit local/SSH exclusions remain redundant and harmless; no second ingress implementation was added. The separate node-session guards remain necessary to prevent retained bootstrap/SSH provenance from approving a new tunnel capability surface.

### Handoff

The branch and PR head both equal `4fc18ce33e9763b25f01c7ece2f1643c6de10634`; the worktree is clean, the PR is open and ready, and GitHub reports mergeable. Protocol #193980 was still open at handoff, so no post-squash rebase has been performed. After that parent lands, restack onto its merged main and refresh affected/exact-head gates before Josh merges.

prs.title: test(ui): add per-method RPC hostage census
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A uniform mock Gateway delay cannot show which specific RPC holds unrelated UI work. A forever-held roster response also made the test navigation helper wait before the scenario could inspect the UI.

## What Changes

Add per-method response delays and explicit release to the existing mock Gateway, preserving the normal zero-delay path and suppressing replies to closed sockets. Navigation setup recognizes intentionally held roster methods. The new `bench-control-ui-rpc-hostage` command uses existing fixtures and the production bundle to discover each flow's calls, delay one method at a time, and record readiness, visible content/skeletons, composer input, navigation and recovery. The existing engine benchmark accepts the same method-specific injection for paired timing proof.

**No production UI behavior changes are included.** Devices and Systems experiments were removed after timing/CPU controls rejected them. Their production sources, tests and user-facing documentation match the merge base byte-for-byte.

## Coverage and Interpretation

The census covers 59 flows: 57 measured and two redirects, with 217 discovered method/flow cases and 493 included observations. Both delay cells were reached in 203 cases; six were one-sided and eight never issued the target during replay. Unreached cells are explicitly unexercised, not proof of independence. Activity, Dashboard, Portals and Profile setup corrections retain provenance in the local evidence. The complete table is below.

Ordinary browser UI RPCs have no general deadline. Separate handshake, explicit system-info and early selected-session bounds are not a universal request timeout. Holds were observed for four seconds and explicitly released; selected 35-second probes corroborated persistent waits. This is response-coupling evidence, not a blocked server event loop or a production-frequency census. Generic `native=no` can reflect the probe's pre-click restoration guard; a separate native-first Devices probe reached Chat at 669.1 ms and New conversation at 809.9 ms with config held.

## Experiments and Decisions

All timings below are application-document measurements in headless browsers, with rotated base/head/identical-base controls. A large injected-delay win did not qualify a change that regressed normal operation.

| Experiment | Deciding evidence | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Systems independent telemetry, then duplicate-notification and membership-work removal | Final 20 Chromium CPU triplets: script 27.10 → 28.99 ms (+7.0%), p95 29.22 → 32.54; A/A median −0.2%. Earlier variants were worse. | Removed. |
| Devices display-only refresh | 20 Chromium no-delay triplets: median +8.8%, A/A +0.7%. | Removed. |
| Devices editor-first refresh | Full three-engine matrix: WebKit 100 ms RTT median 715.5 → 754 ms (+5.4%), p95 730 → 807. Sending inventory first and awaiting existing preparation also failed ten-pair screens. | Removed. |
| Devices refresh at page adoption | Full 20-triplet matrix per engine/condition plus ten extra WebKit RTT triplets. Target delay improved 92–97%, but pooled WebKit RTT30 p95 remained 733 → 770 ms (+5.05%), A/A p95 −2.18%; median 704 → 703. All 570 behavior observations passed. | Removed. |
| Devices refresh after inventory, before loader return | Ten WebKit RTT triplets: median 699 → 758.5 ms (+8.5%), p95 725 → 839; A/A median +2.0%, p95 flat. | Removed. |

No measured production optimization qualified. These results do not establish that the remaining couplings are irreducible. In particular, skipping the page's editor-readiness guard was rejected by source review: it could enable binding controls before the lazy editor exists.

## Priority and Remaining Waits

Historical isolated-Gateway evidence makes `config.get` plausible: a warm Devices example was 158.9 ms RTT / 0.3 ms handler at 100 ms transport RTT; a cold example was 902.4 / 526.9 ms. Earlier catalog examples were 301–384 ms median. These are synthetic historical examples, not current production percentiles or frequency. Old model request counts predate later reductions. A 3.8-second historical `update.status` example did not hold input in this census.

Legitimate waits remain for authenticated current connections, unresolved session identity, a transcript's own subscription, roster membership, node/pairing inventory, canonical environments, binding/execution-policy authority and each page's own results. The composer remains editable with a held transcript subscription.

Avoidable couplings remain: Devices config and approvals joined with inventory; restored presentation readiness and Settings sidebar waiting for config; Systems initial aggregate/polling; model/auth aggregation; Skills/Plugins whole-page loading; Debug diagnostics. This PR supplies reproducible evidence and tooling for those follow-ups without changing their behavior.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused mock regressions | 10 passed: per-method delay, release, closed connection and preserved normal timing. |
| Suppression audit | 14 passed; census intentionally uses rendered text, excluding hidden parked panes. |
| Static checks | UI/scripts typechecks and targeted lint/format passed; production Knip and the exact final `pnpm ui:build` passed. |
| Test-line allocation | Exactly 131 net LF lines for mock delay/release/closed-connection and default roster-navigation regressions. Shared scalar unchanged; allocation check passes. |
| CI | Final head `6f1b3a17640` passed all 44 executed jobs in [run 42409226201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42409226201), including all seven UI E2E shards, both real-Gateway shards, all three UI-unit shards, lint and ratchets. Twenty-six inapplicable jobs were skipped. |
| Review | Independent P0–P2 reviews clean for retained mock/census and final scope restoration. Lead separately verified all restored Devices/Systems sources and tests match the merge base byte-for-byte. |
| Assets | Production source is identical to base. Exact final-head build and strict base comparison passed with no violations: 90,900 B startup JS gzip, 39,090 B CSS gzip and one CSS request, unchanged from base. Existing absolute document/CSS warnings remain unchanged; no ceiling was raised. |

Touched-file LOC: tests/mock 3,967 → 4,098 (+131), benchmark/configuration 6,369 → 7,451 (+1,082), documentation 0 → 100 (+100); production UI unchanged. The growth is the requested reusable census and its documentation; no new dependency, production owner, cache or configuration option is introduced. Reports, traces and measurements are not committed.

<details>
<summary>Complete baseline method-by-flow table</summary>

## BASE method-by-flow delay census

One diagnostic observation per method/flow/delay; this is coverage evidence, not the paired timing acceptance. A 3-second delay and a 4-second held-response window were configured for every discovered method. A zero-call cell did not exercise that method and is not evidence of independence. prs.title: fix(perf): retry stress setup while Gateway sidecars start
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes canonical Team-shaped stress setup aborting when `/readyz` passes before Gateway startup sidecars admit the first `sessions.create` request.

## User Impact

Benchmark operators can finish setup through this temporary refusal. There is no Gateway runtime behavior change. The first setup request gets a maximum 120-second total budget; transport errors, unrelated refusals, and measured RPC failures still fail immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway explicitly reports a pre-admission `UNAVAILABLE` error with `retryable: true`, `details.reason: "startup-sidecars"`, and `retryAfterMs`. The existing script WebSocket client now supports an opt-in retry for exactly that response, honoring the delay within one request-and-wait deadline and logging every wait. Only the first synthetic session creation opts in, before warmup or measurement.

The existing client owns the retry; there is no new module, product configuration, schema, or production runtime code. Added tooling is necessary to respect the existing startup response contract.

## Evidence

- Existing real-WebSocket suite: 10/10 pass, 1.96 seconds including wrapper startup. Cases cover success after the advertised delay, a stalled retry within the same deadline, an advertised delay beyond the deadline, an unrelated refusal, and unchanged default behavior.
- The recovery regression fails against unmodified `10bbb1ed21821aac4ab7409a5be75699a02fd671`: the request settles immediately with the startup refusal instead of waiting. It fails on behavior, not imports, type arity, or fixture setup.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`: all four strict root shards pass, including scripts and tooling. Changed-file format, lint, and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix(codex): complete explicit final messages without false interrupt markers
prs.body:
Related: #111019

## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server turns that deliver a confirmed final source reply were released through `turn/interrupt`. That persisted Codex's canonical false "user interrupted" marker into an otherwise clean thread rollout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful terminal delivery is not a user abort. The turn should finish through Codex's native `turn/completed` path when it wraps normally, while retaining a bounded escape hatch for runaway generation.

This deliberately does **not** change `sessions_yield`: yield retains OpenClaw's current parent-resumption contract and continues to interrupt/release the child turn immediately.

## Behavior

- A confirmed final source reply lets Codex finish through its native `turn/completed` event, avoiding a false "user interrupted" marker in the rollout.
- After the terminal tool batch settles, one absolute 10-second timer bounds the wait; later output cannot extend it.
- Existing steering rejection/queue fallback, sibling settlement, and response-admission ownership remain unchanged.
- If Codex does not finish inside the grace period, OpenClaw uses the existing interrupt fallback.
- `sessions_yield` remains exempt from this path and keeps its immediate interrupt/handoff behavior.

## User Impact

Long-lived Codex threads no longer accumulate false interruption context after ordinary explicit final-message delivery. A delivered reply remains successful if OpenClaw later needs the bounded fallback interrupt.

## Evidence

- Exact repaired head: `c4e776a1ad57cc8c4d1d2c08416d415f477d45f4`.
- Frozen base: `1e101d06645b30edfc0c686813de5c795acea2d4`; clean merge tree: `6d12a9cf45ddff5797f32ece2362fa76ceff41a5`.
- The canonical pre-PR gate passed on Node `26.12.1` with the frozen lockfile: formatting, extension and extension-test type graphs, type-aware lint, dead exports, SQLite ratchets, plugin boundaries, import cycles, Control UI i18n verification, and `git diff --check`.
- The two changed app-server suites pass `50/50`, including natural final-reply completion with no interrupt, the 10-second fallback, both failed-sibling orderings, steering preservation, durable-context history, and unchanged `sessions_yield` cleanup.
- Earlier real-client proof on `673460e4cabf` exercised the same native-completion mechanism against the pinned Codex app-server and observed native `turn/completed` with zero `turn/interrupt` requests. That evidence is historical; the current head's exact proof is deterministic rather than a new live channel/model run.
- No app-server protocol or configuration surface changes.

prs.title: fix(cli): expose the scoped manual-selection permission in the full model inventory
prs.body:
Closes #194738

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models list --all --json` reported an authenticated but policy-blocked model as `available: true` with no separate manual-choice permission field, so an agent using the inventory to pick a reviewer hit a local `sessions_spawn` rejection ("model not allowed") that the inventory could have predicted.

## User Impact

User impact: the full CLI inventory now carries `manualSelectionAllowed` beside `available`, so readiness (runtime/provider facts) and override permission (the agent's model policy) are separately visible, exactly as the gateway protocol documents the field. Models without a projected permission show `null` (unknown) instead of implying "allowed", and the rendered table is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already projects `manualSelectionAllowed` for clients that declare the `model-selection-policy` capability, and `ModelsListParams`/`BuildModelsListResultParams` already carry the opt-in — the CLI simply never requested or surfaced it. The CLI's `models.list` connection now declares the capability, the offline local-catalog read passes `includeManualSelection` directly (the operator's own policy computation), and the row projection keeps the field beside availability.

## Evidence

- New regression in `list.prepared-catalog.test.ts`: a gateway response where one model carries `manualSelectionAllowed: false` and another omits it renders rows with `false` and `null` respectively — and the test asserts the CLI's request advertises the `model-selection-policy` capability, which is the piece that makes the gateway project the field at all. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/models/list.prepared-catalog.test.ts` — 16/16 passing.
- Independent review round 1 found a P1: the capability was declared on the offline `runWithLocalStateOwner` path while the reported scenario (a running Gateway) goes through `readSelectedGatewayModelCatalog`, whose `callGateway` call had no caps — fixed by declaring the cap there; the dead `runWithLocalStateOwner` plumbing was removed, and the test now pins the request shape so the gap cannot reappear.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the pre-existing red lanes on current `main` untouched by this diff (`changelog attributions`, and the `dead export scan` flagging `extensions/google/provider-policy.ts`). The 21 net added test lines have a matching `config/test-lines-allocations/models-list-manual-selection.txt` record.
- Not exercised: a live Gateway with a real model policy over RPC; the mocked-response regression stands in.
