prs.title: fix: restore Git backups containing Unicode line separators
prs.body:
Closes #188519
Related: #145938

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Git backup restoration failing when saved text contains Unicode line or paragraph separators.

## User Impact

Operators can restore and verify existing Git backups containing U+2028/U+2029 without rewriting their backups. The backup format and SQLite publication checks remain unchanged; no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backup writer produces LF-delimited JSON, but `node:readline` also splits at Unicode separators on the tested runtime. Read records at LF boundaries with the existing streaming UTF-8 decoder instead. Keep hashing the original byte chunks and inserting rows in bounded batches.

### Published 2026.10.10: restoration gap remains

The published tag still [constructs a `node:readline` reader and parses each emitted record as JSON](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.ts#L490-L529). The Unicode-separator regression covered by this PR remains reproducible in the shipped 10.10 reader. The release's other backup improvements do not establish that this framing defect is fixed.

This PR changes record framing only. It preserves the existing backup format, raw-byte hashes, bounded inserts, integrity checks, and fresh-database publication. It remains separate from the Codex/WebChat fixes in #188698 and #188526; no Gateway preload or runtime-wide workaround is proposed here.

## Evidence

### Additional stable 2026.11.1 compatibility check — November 7, 2026

The source change applies cleanly to the stable 2026.11.1 codec and produces the same candidate used in the isolated package checks. The unchanged stable reader fails verify/restore on literal U+2028/U+2029 while its ASCII control passes. With LF-only framing, verify and fresh-target restore both pass on Node 24.22.1 and Bun 1.4.3 for ASCII, Unicode records larger than 1 MiB, and a record/chunk-boundary fixture. Hash mismatch, invalid UTF-8, incorrect row count, and an existing restore target are rejected without publishing a partial target. This is additional shipped-release compatibility evidence, separate from the exact PR-head CLI proof below; it does not claim a new execution of this PR head.

[Current main `2e13c52c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e13c52c97bbe81228c4f45212c8ca8cd346dbf9/src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.ts#L502) still constructs the `node:readline` reader, so this remains an outstanding source fix. The branch is mergeable at the time of this check; no unrelated rebase or runtime-wide preload is added.


### Additional published-release check — November 3, 2026

The official 10.10 reader failed on a synthetic backup containing literal U+2028/U+2029. An isolated, explicitly scoped verify/restore helper applying the same LF-framing correction in memory passed against the installed 10.10 packages on macOS and Linux. Fresh synthetic restores preserved the exact SQLite TEXT bytes, and integrity checks passed. Corrupted data or manifest hashes were rejected without publishing a target; an existing target was preserved.

This is compatibility evidence for the framing correction on shipped 10.10, not a new exact-head CLI run of this PR. The helper is external to the proposed patch and is not loaded into Gateway. No production database was restored. The exact-candidate CLI proof and CI evidence remain below.

- Extended the existing production SQLite dump/restore round trip with literal U+2028/U+2029 in TEXT keys and values. On the base, restoration fails with `Unterminated string in JSON`; with the fix, byte-level SQLite comparisons and manifest verification pass.
- Node 24.22.1: 28 tests pass across the codec, restore-failure cleanup, and Git backup integration suites; one existing test is skipped. The final command took 72.74 s including worker preparation and integration fixtures. The exact changed test file also passes separately with the repository’s default runtime selection (2 cases, 12.10 s wall time). Production core typechecking, targeted oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Shared autoreview of the production change and regression against `b195f61511f9310d9a4dd416e517fb9ec0755f4d`, P0–P2: no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected the diff and supplied UTF-8/cleanup context; test execution was performed separately.
- Added one test-line allocation for the single new fixture row; the shared baseline is untouched. No extra test fixture, process, or model call was added.

The shipped CLI was built at `ea07e82` (`pnpm build`, exit 0, 4m 16s). Both `backup git verify` and `backup git restore` exit 0 on the same unchanged, committed synthetic backup containing literal U+2028/U+2029. Independent SQLite reads preserve the exact TEXT bytes; integrity and foreign-key checks pass. A modified table with its original manifest is rejected by both commands (exit 1, hash mismatch), and restore publishes no target.

GitHub CI, dependency review, and security-sensitive review gates pass on this head. All databases and state used for CLI proof were disposable and isolated; no production restoration or release qualification is claimed.

<summary>Redacted CLI proof on the exact candidate</summary>

```text

Fixes the intermittent Details Outputs E2E timeout on cached chat reloads, including [scheduled main run 42396268435](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42396268435).

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

A cached wide Details pane intentionally waits for its Session module before painting the first chat frame. prs.title: fix(zalouser): sanitize outbound tool traces
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem / value:** Zalo Personal's custom monitor callback bypasses its standard adapter, so a `message_sending` hook can reintroduce internal tool traces immediately before transport. This patch keeps recipient text and captions clean while preserving configured Markdown-table rendering.
- **Relevance:** Independent P1/security report #90684 tracks this leakage class. Merged #112621 sanitizes the standard adapter only; current `main` still leaves this distinct callback seam open.
- **Smallest complete fix / review map:** Keep configured table conversion in `delivery.preparePayload`, where durable final delivery sees it, and sanitize only the effective post-hook payload in the custom callback. Scope is 4 files, `+76/-20`: two small helpers, two focused regressions, and the boundary wiring.
- **Risk / proof:** Risk is limited to ordering between two existing transforms. Exact head `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`; full Zalouser `221/221`; changed-file format/lint, extension production/test types, branch ratchets, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass. The exact deterministic wrapper has only untouched frozen-base Codex/dead-export debt.
- **External proof limit:** Authenticated recipient-visible transport is `blocked_external` because no safe configured account/recipient route exists. Exact-head tests reach both lifecycle boundaries; no live send is claimed.
- **Non-goals:** Standard adapter, sanitizer parser dialects, Zalo Bot, authentication, configuration schema, and protocol changes.
- **Maintainer ask:** Please apply `no-stale` while authenticated recipient proof is coordinated; the assigned-PR age clock otherwise ignores substantive updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo Personal's custom inbound-reply path in `monitor.ts` can deliver a post-hook payload without passing through the standard outbound adapter. That leaves one route for compact tool-failure lines or tool XML to reach recipients. The repair must also preserve `channels.zalouser.markdown.tables` for final replies handled by durable delivery. Related: #90684.

## User Impact

Recipients get intended assistant text and media without internal tool-trace scaffolding, while existing table preferences such as `markdown.tables: "bullets"` continue to apply to durable final replies. Ordinary prose, captions, chunking, and media delivery remain unchanged; users have no migration step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delivery.preparePayload` owns configured table conversion before the lifecycle can return through durable delivery.
- The private custom callback owns sanitization after `message_sending`, so a supported hook cannot reintroduce internal traces.
- Merged #112621 covers the standard adapter only; this remains a narrow, distinct callback repair.

## Evidence

- Exact signed candidate head: `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9` on frozen maintenance base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/zalouser`: `33` files and `317/317` tests passing, including configured bullet-table preparation before durable delivery and post-hook trace sanitization at custom delivery.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passing.
- Changed Zalouser scope passes type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Repository-wide extension lint's only failure is unchanged frozen-base debt in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (`max-lines`).
- Deterministic `openclaw-pre-pr.sh` gate: passed for frozen base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`, exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`, and merge tree `1d2e0ad6dc09fd07dfa21423c38602b80e92ae9d`.
- Current-`main` negative control: the custom monitor callback still resolves and delivers the post-hook payload directly. This head restores pre-durable table preparation and sanitizes immediately before custom text/caption resolution.
- Remaining proof state is `blocked_external`, not a claimed live pass: authenticated recipient-visible proof still requires a safe Zalo Personal account and recipient route.

AI-assisted change, manually reviewed and validated.
## Exact-head refresh (2026-10-26)

<!-- clawsean-head-refresh-2026-10-26 -->
The current signed PR head is `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`, rebuilt on frozen base `f4a0d4875912103be54dd672e32db17064d003db` with a four-file patch and clean merge tree `f44ddf096cf52e14aadcf50b892f2ea4b8765eee`.

- Disposable Linux/arm64 proof used Node 24.22.1 and a fresh frozen-lockfile install; the full Zalouser suite passed `221/221` across 30 files.
- Changed-file format/lint, production and test extension typechecks, conflict/line-cap/assertion/SQLite/plugin-boundary ratchets, doctor-contract tests, media/runtime guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- Independent exact-diff review found no P0-P2 findings. GitHub and the fork ref read back this exact head, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass with none pending or failed.
- Authenticated recipient-visible Zalo proof remains externally blocked: no consented safe recipient route is available, so no private recipient was used and no live-send claim is made. The deterministic negative path, exact-head full suite, and hosted execution are the strongest contributor-safe evidence currently possible.

prs.title: fix(macos): exec host returns empty output for invalid UTF-8
prs.body:
Closes #187601

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app exec host returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` when a command's output contains any invalid or incomplete UTF-8 sequence, while still reporting `success: true`. A command killed at its timeout right after printing half of a multibyte character (spinners, box drawing, emoji) comes back with `timedOut: true` and no output at all.

## User Impact

Agents running `host=node` commands on a Mac now get the valid part of the output, with `U+FFFD` in place of the bad bytes, instead of an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ShellExecutor`'s file-backed capture decoded each whole buffer with `String(bytes:encoding:) ?? ""`. That decode fails for the entire buffer when any one byte sequence is invalid. It now uses `String(decoding:as: UTF8.self)`, which `runStreamingDetailed` in the same file already uses through swift-subprocess. Process, timeout, and capture behavior are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and other readers</summary>

- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ShellExecutor.swift:45-46` is the only failable decode of captured command output. The pattern has been there since the file-backed capture in #104827, which kept the earlier pipe-based decode.
- `PortGuardian.swift:461` decodes `ShellExecutor.run`'s payload, which is now always valid UTF-8, so its fallback can no longer trigger.
- `GatewayProcessManager.swift:1403` reads the Gateway log file. That's a different owner, outside this bug.
- The issue's related note about signal-terminated children being reported as `exit N` is a separate behavior change and is not part of this PR.
</details>

## Evidence

I packaged main (`c32556b0cea`) and this branch as ad-hoc macOS apps. Each ran under a named profile in remote mode against an isolated Gateway (private state and config, loopback port) started from that app's bundled runtime. Each case is a Gateway `node.invoke` `system.run` call to the paired app, the node command that `exec host=node` forwards and that runs `ShellExecutor.runDetailed`.

Main:
```
## control-ascii: /bin/sh -c "printf 'plain-ascii'; printf 'err-ascii' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"plain-ascii","stderr":"err-ascii"}
## invalid-byte: /bin/sh -c "printf 'abc\377'; printf 'abc\377' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
## split-multibyte: /bin/sh -c "printf 'abc\342\234'; printf 'abc\342\234' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
## timeout-split: /bin/sh -c "printf 'building \342\234'; sleep 5" (timeoutMs=1000)
{"success":false,"exitCode":null,"timedOut":true,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
```

This branch:
```
## control-ascii
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"plain-ascii","stderr":"err-ascii"}
## invalid-byte

prs.title: fix(outbound): settle permanent unknown-send reconciliation failures terminally
prs.body:
Fixes #180582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a queued message whose delivery outcome is unknown after a crash keeps retrying up to 5 times with backoff when the channel's reconciliation fails with a permanent provider error (for example `chat not found` or `User … not in room`), instead of being marked failed right away.

## User Impact

User impact: deliveries that can never succeed are reported as failed on the first recovery pass, instead of using up the retry budget and delaying the failure report. Transient reconciliation errors are still retried, and nothing is ever resent without proof it wasn't delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a channel's reconciliation throws, the fallback now uses the same permanent-error check that direct-send recovery already uses (`isPermanentDeliveryError`), instead of always marking the failure retryable. The result stays `unresolved`, so recovery still never resends. Explicit verdicts from channels such as Slack and Matrix, and legacy queue migration, are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression test `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery-reconciliation.test.ts` runs durable recovery against the real SQLite queue with a reconciler that throws:
  - `chat not found`: the entry is removed after one reconciliation call, with no resend.
    - **Fails on base:** `expected [ { …(11) } ] to deeply equal []`, meaning the entry was still pending.
    - **Passes with the fix.**
  - `provider lookup timed out`: the entry stays pending with `retryCount: 1`, with no resend. This guards against treating transient errors as permanent.
- `pnpm test src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery-reconciliation.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`: 46/46 passed. `delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` passes.
- `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, import-cycle and boundary guards pass. Two failures I believe do not come from this change; I did not rerun them on `main`:
  - `core tsgo graph boundary`: advisory shard root budget (`infra` 735, `gateway-root` 726, limit 720).
  - `dead export scan`: about 136 existing unused exports, none in the files this PR touches.

<details>
<summary>Test output</summary>

Base (without the fix):

    FAIL  delivery-queue recovery unknown-send reconciliation failures > terminalizes an unknown send when reconciliation throws "chat not found"
    AssertionError: expected [ { …(11) } ] to deeply equal []
    ✓ retains an unknown send when reconciliation throws "provider lookup timed out"
    Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)

With the fix:

    Test Files  2 passed (2)
    Tests  46 passed (46)

</details>

**Gap:** there is no live provider reproduction. Bundled channels return explicit reconciliation verdicts rather than throwing, and reaching this path requires a crash between the platform send and the ack. The durable-recovery test is the production-path proof.

prs.title: feat(android): mute the Talk microphone without ending the conversation
prs.body:
Closes #187721

## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk users need to pause microphone input without ending the conversation or interrupting the assistant's work and response audio.

## User Impact

A separate, accessible microphone button beside End Talk lets users mute and unmute input while keeping the call, accepted work, and reply audio active. Mute remains set across Talk restarts in the app process until explicitly unmuted; standalone push-to-talk still works after ending Talk.

Realtime mute sends silence while the recording session stays open, so Android's microphone indicator may remain visible. Native Talk finishes already-recognized words before pausing recognition. No new permission, configuration, dependency, protocol, or release-version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending Talk and muting reply playback are different operations from muting input. Keep input mute owned by `TalkModeManager` and expose that state through the existing runtime/view model to the actual ChatScreen control. Reuse the capture ownership lock to retire native recognition and keep queued microphone audio from crossing a mute/unmute toggle at socket enqueue. Preserve upstream detach/abort behavior.

The patch excludes selected-chat routing, Health Connect, SMS, version bumps, and the unrelated chat-metadata warning repair. It adds no parallel capture manager: the necessary growth is one input state plus audio-frame invalidation and the control/proof. Production Kotlin delta: +132/-20; tests: +253/-1; README: +1.

## Evidence

- Built and tested against pinned main `6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`; Initial Kotlin test/review head `750c924b8ec5e95018239108fd9f85382d936a7c`; current head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc` adds only the generated source inventory entries described below.
- `:app:ktlintCheck` passed. `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **121 tests**, zero failures/errors/skips: all 118 `TalkModeManagerTest` cases and three targeted `ChatComposerLayoutTest` cases covering the real toggle, accessible state, and 320dp/French/large-font controls. Gradle build/check wall time: **4m 11s**; recorded suite times: **17.745s** and **12.297s**, respectively. These are Kotlin/Gradle suites, not `pnpm test` suites. The completed updated-head CI result is summarized below.
- Transport checks exercise microphone PCM replacement with silence, a read spanning a toggle, and queued audio waiting at the actual socket enqueue. Native/relay checks preserve admitted work and playback; push-to-talk checks cover muted admission and standalone use after Talk ends.
- The requester initially liked the feature during real voice use on the custom 2026.10.7 phone build, but subsequently reported that muting seemed to silence assistant playback as well. That observation is not yet reproduced or attributed; do not treat output preservation as accepted device proof. Source inspection confirms separate microphone and speaker controls, but does not establish what happened on that phone. This current-main port has not separately been installed on a device; do not treat the synthetic screenshots as live audio proof.
- Fresh independent Codex read-only review of the final mute-only snapshot against the pinned base found no actionable likely/high-impact findings. CLI AutoReview was attempted but unavailable because OpenAI returned HTTP 401; it is **not** counted as a passing AutoReview. `git diff --check` passed. Full Android framework/resource lint and broad hosted CI are not claimed passing.

### CI localization correction

The initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492) passed Android third-party, Play, Wear, both native-accessibility jobs, and Kotlin style. Its one underlying failure was `native-i18n`: the source extraction inventory omitted the five new mute strings. `openclaw/ci-gate` reflected that failure.

Reproduced the same inventory failure locally before the repair. Ran `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`, which added exactly five generator-owned entries to `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` now passes, including Android and Apple source safety checks; `pnpm android:i18n:gen` regenerates the Android lookup/resources with the new labels. Kotlin source and tests are unchanged, so the earlier focused test and independent review evidence remains scoped to that unchanged code. The [updated-head native-i18n job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538746357) now passes on GitHub for `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`; that run is now complete. Android third-party and Wear tests, ktlint, both native-accessibility jobs, and native-i18n passed. The [`android-test-play` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538748350) exceeded its 20-minute unit-test limit, which failed `openclaw/ci-gate`. No failing assertion was established in the inspected log, and the empty failure-classification table does not establish an inherited failure. The timeout remains under investigation; no blind CI rerun was requested.

Translated dictionaries and derived locale metadata remain owned by the serialized post-merge locale refresh ([publication policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/landing.md#open-or-update-the-pr)); this correction commits the source-owned inventory, not hand-edited translations. The new labels can use English fallback until that refresh.

### Current-head phone testing artifact and CI follow-up — October 30

An [unofficial contributor test APK](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/tag/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659) is available from the exact
clean head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`. The download page includes the APK SHA-256,
signature/build manifest, and [route-specific test instructions](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/download/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659/TESTING.md).
It is phone-only `thirdPartyDebug` (`ai.openclaw.app.debug`), not an official
release; no private Health/Samsung/selected-chat/lock-screen patches or version
source changes are included. No device installation was performed.
The unchanged upstream version label is `2026.8.2-debug`; identify
the artifact by commit and SHA-256, not the version label.

The new local build also passed **121 focused Play tests**, zero failures/errors/skips
(118 TalkModeManager cases and three ChatComposerLayout cases), with artifact
signature, CRC, manifest, compiled mute setters, and exact commit/timestamp
verified. This does not replace full hosted CI or physical audio proof.

**Physical acceptance remains pending.** The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6500004345)
found no actionable code findings but requires a device recording or redacted
runtime trace for **both native and realtime** mute/unmute during active answers,
showing suppressed new input, uninterrupted audio, and completed accepted work.
The testing packet includes that exact scope and a result template. The maintainer
decision on the feature's control, silence-based realtime behavior, and mute
lifetime also remains open. No new review was requested without that proof.

**CI investigation:** the [timed-out Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538748350)
left about **9m50s** after launching the app test JVM, whereas the
[previous passing Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492/job/123513827300)
needed **10m32s** and passed 3,658 tests. Those heads differ only in the five
localization inventory entries, not Android code/tests/Gradle/CI. Current-head
third-party CI passed 3,776 tests in about 9m19s after test JVM launch.
This strongly supports inadequate whole-job headroom; failed-only logging and
skipped timeout reports mean an individual stall is not ruled out. The
[full findings](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/download/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659/CI-NOTES.md) propose a **test-play-only 30-minute
budget** while preserving all other budgets, followed by one result on the changed
head. Current upstream main still uses 20 minutes for this job. **No workflow
edit, blind CI rerun, inherited-failure classification, or green-gate claim was made.**

### Remaining before merge

- Supply runtime evidence on this current-main Android port for native and realtime mute/unmute during an active answer, including input suppression and continued playback. The older custom-build user report and synthetic UI captures do not establish that evidence.
- Obtain the maintainer product decision on the separate input control, silence-based realtime mute, and mute lifetime across Talk restarts. The author's requested feature and phone acceptance are not represented as upstream maintainer approval.

### Synthetic ChatScreen captures

The images below come from the real ChatScreen Robolectric fixture at 320dp, not a mock-drawn control or a live provider call. They demonstrate the control/status and layout only.

**Before: pinned main, no input-only microphone control**

![Android Talk before the feature, with End Talk but no separate microphone mute](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f97c2d5-51c7-4f04-861e-ef117d1d4ea4)

The before capture used an isolated checkout of the exact pinned base, with a temporary UI-only proof asserting that the microphone toggle was absent (1 test passed; capture build wall time 3m 15s). No baseline proof code or generated images are included in the source branch.

**After: microphone enabled**

![Android Talk with the separate microphone toggle enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e8e6157-509b-4703-ae6d-e1018cdd7ce3)

**After: microphone muted**

prs.title: fix(ios): chat reconnects load the transcript before refreshing catalogs
prs.body:
Closes #194223 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: after a reconnect on a slow or flapping connection, iOS chat repeats its model and capability catalog requests on every reconnect, ahead of the conversation history, so the transcript has to share a slow link with them. ## User Impact User impact: when iOS chat reconnects, the conversation history now loads before the model and capability catalogs are refreshed. macOS keeps the same transcript and draft behavior; this change does not guarantee history-first ordering for all macOS traffic, and no latency improvement is claimed. ## Why This Change Was Made After a reconnect, native chat can compete with model and capability catalogs while recovering its transcript. This change delays the recovery-owned catalog refreshes until history settles and coalesces overlapping recoveries. Stale state is still invalidated immediately, and session metadata needed by queued sends remains immediate. The reviewed correction by @vyctorbrzezowski (`f211a4b6c1d`) fixes two defects in the deferred path: a catalog request could target the previous conversation, and catalogs could overtake an overlapping iOS bootstrap history read. It now waits for an overlapping iOS bootstrap to finish and verifies that the captured conversation is still current before refreshing catalogs. This prevents a request for the previous agent and addresses the persistent history timeout reproduced during review. First-connect setup, live question events, cancellation, and progress-card recovery are preserved. ## Evidence ### Verified behavior Real native apps, isolated Gateway, and persisted model-generated conversations: | Scenario | Before | Corrected PR | | --- | --- | --- | | iOS: repeated cuts, 8 KiB/s downstream | 7,091 model-response bytes before the first history response on all 4 observed history-bearing connections | 0 on both observed history-bearing connections in each of 2 repetitions | | iOS: overlapping bootstrap after reconnect | Earlier PR candidate reproduced a persistent timeout from a clean start | Both final repetitions recovered without Retry or dismissing the error | | macOS native Quick Chat: 2 cuts per build | Messages and editable draft preserved | Same messages and editable draft preserved; 2 successful history reloads | Interrupted connections are excluded from the history-bearing counts. These measurements establish ordering, not a normalized request-count or latency improvement. macOS has a separate catalog loader; this change does not guarantee history-first ordering for all macOS traffic. Four focused tests and 42 related lifecycle/outbox/reaction checks passed. Both new regression cases fail on their respective earlier code and pass with the correction. Normal iOS/Watch and macOS builds passed; independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. These controlled-transport tests support, but do not replace, the native recordings. ### Native recordings All videos retain their complete recorded timeline and original speed. Gray masks cover model labels and adjacent metadata. No application state, Gateway response, or rendering style was injected. #### Timeout found and fixed during review The left image is the earlier corrected candidate, not main. The right is the final repetition after the bootstrap fix. #### iOS: original behavior on main https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3d12b28-6227-47d5-b850-186355d9bccc #### iOS: final correction, repetition 1 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d4824ba-4591-401b-9cdc-568064a81204 #### iOS: final correction, repetition 2 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc1a207c-7e4f-4735-83cc-a14ad6d44544 #### macOS: preservation control These images are not a proposed visual change. The same saved reply and unsent draft remain usable after two network interruptions. Main: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f77dcca5-f494-4fbe-a63b-fbac021a4174 Corrected PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cf819af-f4eb-46cc-a6fe-3779d1791511
Build provenance and limits - Live baseline: `4f61482980507ec61c3436f32a37eac8adabfc2e`. - Corrected PR: `f211a4b6c1da60d50ba6e3dd0d3053c026c1af84`; tested tree `35e8417f8ff722f3d1e78dd9079e85e7357a3314`. - iOS 27.2 Simulator, Xcode 27.2; native macOS Quick Chat in an isolated macOS 26.6.2 VM. - Gateway `04cc8c1e4328b873a3a5791eeecf5d4d213c34db` held constant across each comparison. Later main `74dbd7cc` was source-compared, not rebuilt; relevant Apple source is unchanged. - Response order comes from Gateway logs; request-start estimates subtract server duration with millisecond precision, not packet capture. - First final iOS recording: 85.745 seconds of sparse simulator video during 120 seconds of observation. Repeat: 114.382 seconds plus a final still after the full interval. No padding or acceleration. - Mac recordings: about 57 seconds each, two three-second network interruptions, followed by draft editing. A new send after the interruptions and node-side tools were not covered. - GitHub's full checks are separate from these local results and may still be pending. No merge or auto-merge has been requested.
Earlier contributor evidence: original head 75b5fdd69e4 The evidence below concerns the original head, before the two review corrections. Its transport fixture is supporting evidence, not the real-Gateway recording above. Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple silicon Mac, 32 cores. Head `75b5fdd69e4` (tree `9abb6dd7fca`); the changed files on the test machine match the commit byte for byte. **Real iOS transport, wire order.** A proof-only harness (not part of this PR) runs in the OpenClaw iOS test host on an iOS 27.2 simulator (iPhone 18 Pro). It drives `OpenClawChatViewModel` through the app's `IOSGatewayChatTransport` and `IOSSourceResourceLoader`, over `GatewayNodeSession` and a real `URLSession` WebSocket, to a local Gateway fixture (`NativeGatewayWebSocketFixture` with a chat mode added). The fixture answers each `chat.history` after 1.5 s, drops the socket, sends `health` false then true, and drops the socket again; each reconnect raises the same `seqGap` the app sees on a flapping link. The harness and its driver are `rig/harness.diff` and `rig/ios-sim.sh` on the fork at [`a946eb71977`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/a946eb7197750d2d50a633939c4e27d4656e1ab1/rig). Loopback only; no credentials in the trace. | 3 runs per side, same counts each time | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Catalog reads during the burst | 20 | 8 | | Catalog reads before the first transcript answer | 20 | 1 | | Most times one catalog was read before that answer | 5 | 1 | | Harness test | fails | passes | Catalog reads here are `models.list`, `chat.metadata`, `question.list`, `config.get` (composer and source context), `skills.status` and `tools.effective`. The `sessions.list` read for session metadata still goes out immediately on each reconnect, on purpose, and is not counted.
Wire trace, this branch (run 1, condensed: request/response pairs on one line) ``` +521ms conn1 connected +523ms conn1 -> chat.history +523ms conn1 sessions.list +527ms conn1 event health {ok: false} +629ms conn1 event health {ok: true} +629ms conn1 sessions.list +1336ms conn2 connected +1337ms conn2 health +1337ms conn2 question.list +1337ms conn2 -> chat.history +1337ms conn2 sessions.list +2847ms conn2 <- chat.history +2848ms conn2 health +2850ms conn2 models.list, question.list, chat.metadata, config.get x2, tools.effective, skills.status ``` On main the same scenario sends these catalog reads with each reconnect and again with the health recovery: 20 catalog reads, all before the first `chat.history` answer.
**Focused tests.** `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests` uses a fake transport that records request order and holds history open. | Test | main | previous head `6afa276f229` | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `flapping reconnects recover history before one catalog refresh` | fails (10 issues) | passes | passes | | `health recovery during a failed transcript read still refetches the progress card` | passes | fails (card never refetched) | passes | ``` main: RECONNECT_BURST requests= source,models,composer,source,models,composer,source,models,composer,questions,history,questions,swarm,questions,history.done,health,history,history.done,health branch: RECONNECT_BURST requests= history,history.done,history,history.done,health,source,models,composer,swarm,questions ``` **Suites on this branch** (in apps/shared/OpenClawKit): - `swift test --filter 'ChatViewModel|ChatModelSignIn|ChatStreamReplay|ChatQuestionCard|ChatSwarm|ChatSource|ChatComposer|ChatSessionCompletion|ChatProgress'`: 727 tests in 32 suites pass; 18 XCTest cases pass. On main the only failure is the burst test. - `swift test --parallel`: 2491 tests in 222 suites pass; 40 tests in 4 suites and 61 XCTest cases pass. On main the only failure is the burst test. - Both runs skip two clipboard tests, `ChatComposerPasteSupportTests` and `file selection remains with the captured conversation`. The test machine had no logged-in desktop session, so `NSPasteboard.writeObjects` returns false and the paste test then crashes the test process. Run alone, both fail the same way on main and on this branch. Lint: SwiftFormat 0.63.1 `--lint` with `config/swiftformat` reports no files need formatting; SwiftLint 0.65.1 with `config/swiftlint.yml` reports 0 violations; `git diff --check` is clean.
Additional runs and gaps - Same focused results with the Swift 6.4.2 Command Line Tools (MacOSX26.5 SDK) on the first head. That lane rewrote `#Preview` blocks and `@Entry` properties at build time (none in the files this PR touches) and left the XCTest files out. - Pre-existing, unrelated: `stale fallback refresh keeps retrying while run remains pending` sometimes takes about 64 s under parallel load, on main and on this branch alike (this branch: 64.0 s in the suite run, 4.5 s in the full run). It takes 0.2 s when run alone. - The simulator harness build is unsigned and leaves out the Watch app target. - Not run: a physical device on a real flapping network.

Related: #194727, #194735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Full Release Validation stopping during source admission when an approved qualification exemption requires retained historical evidence. Observed in [FRV 42404191085/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42404191085/job/128498246664): `verified child rejected an uncached GitHub request`.

## User Impact

Release operators can qualify the selected candidate without replaying an explicitly exempted workload. No runtime, release policy, threshold, publication permission, or version changes. This does not publish a release or claim successful qualification.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential-free inventory verifier correctly refused historical evidence requests that its bootstrap had not collected. The verified admission owner now supplies authenticated evidence locators for bounded acquisition; the full verifier still validates the historical bytes, and both operators are rechecked after acquisition. Arbitrary requests remain rejected.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the observed error through the actual publication-admission workflow subprocess before production edits.
- Three subprocess controls pass: valid retained evidence, tampered historical ZIP refusal, and authority revoked after the historical download. Negative controls reach neither source admission nor registry/first-hop work. Lead independently reran all three successfully.
- 258 affected tests have passing evidence: initial 4-file run was 257 pass/1 fail due to a missing import in the extracted test fixture; repaired it and reran the complete 12-test exemption file successfully. No test disabled.
- Targeted script and tooling-test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, test-line ratchet, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent source review: no actionable correctness/security findings. Local ClawSweeper unavailable; canonical restricted OpenClaw autoreview of the entire 9-file local change against `fe2b1a51b41b80941fe93cfb0dfbdc0def2401d1` completed scoped-clean at P0/P1. It reviewed supplied patch/fixtures, not unchanged source or test execution; independent source review covered owners/callers.

prs.body:
Related: #166678

## What Problem This Solves

Internal worker agents must be configured as full `agents.entries` entries to stay spawnable as `sessions_spawn` targets, so every user-facing agent picker (sidebar roster, agent switcher, New Session target picker) lists agents that are never meant to be chatted with directly. The only way to remove one from the picker today is to delete its entry, which breaks spawning.

## User Impact

Operators can set `agents.entries.<id>.picker.hidden: true` to keep those agents out of chat-facing agent pickers and switchers. Hidden agents remain valid `sessions_spawn` targets and stay listed by `openclaw agents list`, marked `(hidden)`. Administrative and automation surfaces keep them selectable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the config flag proposed in #166678. The UI distinguishes the two roster predicates: `listSelectableAgents` and `findSelectableAgent` remain the administrative/automation projection (system rows only), while chat-facing surfaces use the new `listChatAgents`/`chatAgentsList` helpers (`kind === "system"` and `hidden` excluded). That fixes the first review's Settings finding: `SettingsAgentSelector` still offers picker-hidden agents for management. Docs explicitly state the initial scope is the Control UI; native apps (macOS, iOS) do not yet consume this flag.

## Evidence

**Visual proof** (mocked Control UI via `pnpm dev:ui:mock`, Chromium, agent switcher menu open, `scout` with `picker.hidden: true`):

- Before: switcher rows `[Show all, Molty, Forge, Scout, Bloom]`
- After: switcher rows `[Show all, Molty, Forge, Bloom]` — Scout gone, no other change

Captured locally at `/tmp/opencode/picker-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/picker-after.png` (GitHub API cannot attach images; uploads were posted in the issue thread).

**Focused tests**, all green on this head:

- `src/config/zod-schema.agents.test.ts` — accepts `picker.hidden`, rejects unknown picker keys / non-boolean values, and asserts the default stays visible when omitted
- `src/gateway/session-utils.picker-hidden.test.ts` — projection carries `hidden: true` for hidden agents, omits it for visible agents, and legacy rosters without `picker` still project
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.test.ts` — `AgentSummarySchema` accepts `hidden`, rejects a non-boolean flag
- `src/commands/agents.commands.list.test.ts` — text output marks `- worker (hidden)` while JSON keeps the row
- `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` — `listSelectableAgents` keeps picker-hidden rows for administration; `listChatAgents` excludes them; `findSelectableAgent` still resolves hidden agents so existing sessions stay reachable
- `ui/src/components/settings-sidebar.test.tsx` — Settings switcher still offers a picker-hidden agent and selects it
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-navigation-logic.test.ts` — the sidebar switcher excludes picker-hidden agents while a hidden agent's existing session stays resolvable by id

**Targeted gates** (`pnpm check:changed`, first run): typecheck all, typecheck core tests, typecheck UI, format, config docs baseline, mock-export ratchet, and all architecture/ratchet checks pass. `pnpm build` exits 0 locally.

The config surface deliberately grew by 2 (the new key), so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.{counts.json,sha256}` are regenerated in this PR per the config-surface bar. Test-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/194280-picker-hidden.txt` records exactly this change's net test growth; the shared scalar is unchanged.

Two `check:changed` checks fail, pre-existing on clean `origin/main` (`changelog attributions`, dead export scan in `extensions/codex`). PR CI job failures are in infra/generated paths: `pnpm build qaRuntime` fails resolving generated `extensions/deep-research/browser/index.tsx -> ./client.js` (only `client.ts` is tracked) and the Node-test shards fail in the same build step, while the local full build passes; `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` is the same inherited main debt (main alone reports `over by: 32; net delta: 0`). No failure in this run points at the changed contract.

prs.body:
## Maintainer verification — November 7

The separate Talk mute control, its accessibility state, repeated toggles, mute retention across Talk stop/start, and restoration of dictation after End Talk worked in the real iOS app. At accessibility3, the muted label remained readable and the action remained reachable.

**Audio acceptance is still incomplete.** The production app refuses native speech capture on Simulator. These recordings show actual UI/state behavior with that restriction intact; they do not prove acoustic cutoff, trailing-word recognition, audible playback, live realtime providers, or physical audio/background transitions. Earlier device evidence is retained below with its original scope.

Both iOS/Watch builds passed. The exact private integration passed **39 existing iOS tests in four suites**, **12 shared relay/control tests in the isolated macOS guest**, and native localization verification. No production or test changes were made.

One test issue remains: the fixture's `aborted` acknowledgement is classified as in-flight, so it waits for a missing terminal event. Its long runtime is not measured audio latency. A first-grant speech-permission crash also occurred on unchanged main in an identical source file and is recorded separately.

Source: main `c3b92c2597b3`, PR head `417349df1cf4`, clean private integration `eca5d552c9a44`. Both app versions connected normally to the same isolated real Gateway, held at `a6ee6a18a5d7`. Later inspected main changes did not affect the tested native inputs.

The four complete recordings retain their original speed. Their encoded frames/timestamps match the raw captures, and all four played completely at 1× in Chromium without media errors or backwards presented time. No transcript, recognizer events, styles, or application state were injected into the UI demonstrations.

## Before and after — actual app, simulator audio restriction intact

| ![Main at large accessibility text size](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90bc017c-8cde-40ae-8f5d-2cc7ce952414) | ![Readable muted label at large accessibility text size](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2757285-156b-4459-8623-f2f8d0739d09) |

<details>
<summary>Earlier proposal and evidence, preserved with their original scope</summary>

Related: #187722

## What Problem This Solves

iOS Talk has no microphone mute button separate from ending the conversation.

## User Impact

Adds a microphone toggle to the Talk activity strip. Works across native speech recognition, Gateway relay, and WebRTC, retaining mute across Talk restarts within the app run.

The UI follow-up uses the composer's scaled 17-point medium SF Symbol styling and retains a 44-point hit target. A crossed-out mic is gray when input is on and orange when muted. The collapsed strip is about 48 points tall at normal text size. Idle muted realtime Talk displays **Connected (Realtime)** above **Microphone muted**; thinking, speaking, connecting, and error statuses remain visible. VoiceOver continues to announce the action and microphone state. While Talk is active, the composer's dictation/voice-note microphone is hidden and returns after Talk ends. Mute stays exclusively in the Talk activity strip, not in the dictation button's position.

**Ready for review.** The requester has verified pre-mute word preservation on an iPhone. Returned kit v3 now verifies the Apple build, all 373 selected iOS tests, and all 21 selected shared-package tests for the repaired candidate matching `c22355b8f89a`. Actual normal-size UI screenshots and the requester’s lifecycle recording are now attached below. Remaining physical audio/lifecycle cases, large-text layout, and pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this recording. The confirmed conflict with `main` was resolved in `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`, integrating base `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`. GitHub now reports the branch mergeable. Current-head CI is green (38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures or pending checks at the November 6 check). The requester has also posted current-head targeted simulator red/green results and base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders, summarized below. Earlier Mac-kit results remain evidence for their explicitly identified candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the Android feature from @davelutztx in #187722, using the existing iOS Talk manager and transport owners. No new configuration, permissions, dependencies, or protocol changes. Shared control defaults leave existing macOS callers unchanged.

Android reference checked on November 5, 2026: still open at `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`.

**Native finalization repair:** [Android feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6547128842) and the [iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033) showed that immediate recognizer cancellation discards pre-mute trailing words. Native continuous Talk now closes the audio tap/engine immediately and calls `endAudio()`, retaining that recognition generation until a usable final result or a two-second fallback. Errors, empty finals, and the deadline use the latest nonempty partial; settlement submits once and retires old callbacks. Quick unmute/re-mute cannot replace the draining recognizer. End Talk/session teardown cancels it, and gateway replacement invalidates its transcript owner. Realtime mute and accepted reply playback paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Layout issue also observed without the mute button — November 6

**Requester comparison result:** the requester reproduced the intermittent issue with and without the mute button in **the same chats containing very long messages**, and reports **no apparent worsening with this PR**. This is the requester's comparative device observation; it was not independently executed in this session.

This supports treating the overlap as a pre-existing long-message layout problem, **not an observed mute-button regression or exacerbation**. It remains a separate investigation, not a blocker specific to this PR on the available evidence. The earlier blanket merge hold is withdrawn. No layout repair or root cause is claimed, and other review and validation requirements are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Original observation and related investigation</summary>

The supplied recording and four screenshots show lost reading position and newer user/assistant bubbles overlapping older assistant content. The overlap is visible even after the Talk card disappears. No message-role or persisted-transcript corruption has been established.

![Real iPhone screenshot: newer chat bubbles overlap an older assistant response](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b46564f-ae0c-403a-a419-ea7bc374dd7c)

This inspected crop removes model metadata and unrelated surrounding UI; originals are retained unchanged. Seven transcript layout/identity/rendering files are byte-identical to base `0499ce287bb8`. That source comparison alone did not prove baseline behavior; the requester’s subsequent device comparison is the additional evidence.

[PR #192232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192232) addresses related lazy-height instability causing blank transcripts. It remains an investigation lead, not a verified repair for this overlap. No code from it has been imported, no layout repair is claimed, and no broad device/provider test matrix is requested.

</details>

### Conflict-only integration — November 5

- Published head: `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`; verified ancestry includes main `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`.
- The sole manual conflict was the demo fixture helper extraction: main independently made the same extraction with different helper names. Kept main's names and verified the complete fixture file matches that main revision byte-for-byte. The fixture and shared initializer build repairs are now already upstream, reducing the PR-relative diff to 13 files.
- Native mute manager/regressions, WebRTC mute, relay mute, and Talk-strip UI are byte-identical to the earlier Apple-tested candidate. All 13 PR-relative files plus the two upstream build-repair files were verified against the published head.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,637 entries, no drift); base-relative staged whitespace check passed. Fresh full-candidate Auto Review against the integrated base: P0-only, scoped-clean, no findings. No Apple code was executed in this Linux session; these checks do not replace current-head Apple integration validation.
- [Latest completed ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6626345064) covers current head `417349df1cf4`: overall Gold, patch quality Diamond, no actionable findings, ready for maintainer review, and no before-merge items listed. It notes remaining declared device-proof gaps separately; this rating is advisory. The targeted source-hunk red/green report and requester device evidence are retained below.
- Current-head CI is green as observed November 6: 38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures/pending checks. This includes iOS screenshot/evidence and Periphery build jobs; the dedicated iOS build matrix is skipped, so this is not a claim that every Apple test suite ran in CI. No merge has been submitted.

- Native repair published at `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`; the three repair files were verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed workspace matching the locally supplied patch.
- **Requester device report, November 4:** tested the supplied native-finalization repair locally and confirmed that words spoken before mute are no longer cut off. This is a manual result for the supplied local patch. Kit v2 subsequently exposed build blockers; kit v3 confirms the build repairs and automated regressions pass, as detailed below.
- `git diff --check` and staged whitespace check: passed.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` added the source-owned UI wording entries; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,549 entries, no inventory drift).
- Fresh Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`: **P0-only**, scoped-clean, no findings. This does not certify Swift compilation or Apple runtime behavior.
- Separate source-only lifecycle review of the finalization changes and tests: no unresolved concrete issues after preserving the latest partial on empty finals and adding automatic-unmute-resume cases. This was an excerpt-based audit, not executed proof.
- Author simplification pass: finalization stays in the existing Talk manager, reuses its recognition and transcript-processing generations, and splits input shutdown from recognizer retirement. The added bounded pending state prevents pre-mute word loss without a second capture manager or configuration option.
- Added gateway-boundary regressions in `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: final results with/without an earlier partial; error/timeout/empty-final fallback; exactly-once send; quick unmute/re-mute, including no-word automatic resume; stale callbacks; End Talk/session replacement. They exercise actual `GatewayNodeSession` `chat.send` framing with synthetic recognition callbacks and a terminal-aborted acknowledgement to stop at the submission boundary. **Passed on the requester's Mac in kit v3:** all seven regression definitions, including their parameterized cases. This is fixed-candidate green execution; automated red-on-base execution was not performed.
- [Requester device results at `7e0def937e73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033): iOS app build passed; 27 tests in three iOS suites passed; xAI Gateway relay and OpenAI WebRTC mute/unmute worked on an iPhone. Native recognition lost a word spoken before mute. These are **prior-head results**, not proof of the native finalization repair or revised UI.
- The same report found the shared OpenClawKit test target blocked by a pre-existing `ChatViewModelTests.swift` initializer mismatch, so shared relay tests did not run on that host.
- Apple compilation and automated Swift tests were run on the requester's Mac, not in this Linux session. The returned xcresult summary/tree and Swift XML/logs were independently inspected here. Actual current UI screenshots from the requester's recording are now attached below. Remaining physical lifecycle/input/playback cases still need verification; the silent recording does not establish audio behavior. Chat mockups and render-smoke tests remain separate from runtime screenshot evidence.

### Additional requester evidence on integrated head — November 5–6

All reports below name head `417349df1cf4` and base `0499ce287bb8`.

- [Simulator red/green report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6667982238): on Xcode 27.2, the requester reports **red** after reverting only finalization, muted-recognition, and relay-silence source hunks while retaining the tests: 7 mute tests with 21 issues, and 10 relay tests with 3 issues. **Green** on unchanged PR head: 18 tests across `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests` and `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, plus 10 shared relay tests, all passing. Reported mute-suite time: 721 seconds. This is targeted regression sensitivity, **not a literal plain-base test run**. These are attributed results from the comment; raw xcresult/log bundles for this new run were not supplied to this session.
- [Base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669395455): publicly accessible immutable images were downloaded; normal and large-text active/muted examples and large-text connecting were inspected. They show real SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` output from a fixed 393-point test fixture at 3x, not full-app screenshots. Head adds the expected gray/orange crossed microphone and muted wording. At accessibility3 the muted text wraps mid-word (`Micropho / ne muted`); status/transcript text is also constrained. Treat the real chat's large-text layout as unverified, not accepted based on this fixture.
- [Requester's evidence mapping and remaining device checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669410988): simulator assertions cover finalization, fallback, exactly-once submission, Talk-session restart, quick toggles, and teardown. Audible playback and physical-device lifecycle/large-text verification are still pending. The earlier successful native trailing-word device report remains valid and should not be discarded.

**Restart contract clarification:** mute is retained across Talk stop/start and reconnect within the same app run. It is intentionally not persisted across quitting and relaunching the app. A full-app relaunch retaining mute is therefore **not** an acceptance requirement for this PR; the relevant retention check is restarting Talk without terminating the app.

### Requester real-device lifecycle recording — November 5

The requester supplied a 36-second iPhone recording and explicitly authorized use of the test-chat screen. These are **actual device screenshots, not mockups**. The recording does not display a build commit, so this is requester-supplied visual evidence, separate from the hash-verified kit v3 test run.

![iOS Talk lifecycle: active at 00:04, muted at 00:14, unmuted at 00:22, and ended at 00:34](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3f306d3-3bb9-48a0-84e0-4b23fce03bbc)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/271983e6-399c-4788-b066-920970c21f33

Observed in the recording:
- **00:04:** Listening (Realtime), gray crossed-out microphone in the Talk card, and no composer dictation microphone.
- **00:14:** Connected (Realtime), orange crossed-out microphone and Microphone muted label. The Talk controls remain present and the agent reply appears in chat.
- **00:22:** Unmuted; Listening (Realtime) and the gray mute action return.
- **00:34:** Talk ended; the Talk card is gone and the composer dictation microphone is visible again.
- A stop/restart segment is also present. It is not independently counted as proof of mute retention or capture exclusion because the recording does not expose touch events or microphone input.

Publication edits only: the composer model label is covered, the final iOS Control Center transition is omitted (published clip is 34.5 seconds), and the silent audio track and file metadata are removed. Test-chat text and Talk controls are unchanged. The original recording is retained locally unchanged. Its audio track contains no audible signal; this evidence does **not** prove TTS continuity or post-mute speech exclusion. Normal-size current UI is covered; large-text layout and a pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this clip.

### Returned Mac kit v3 results — November 5

**Apple build and both selected test groups passed. No rerun is needed for the collector's summary error.**

Returned archive: `talk-mute-results-20261105T034708Z-0712fe.zip`, SHA-256 `1fb79eeebf7d716ca593c263e4939da1230e34f6cd28980ba55a78909edf715e`. This was the pinned `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7` base plus bundled build-repair SHA-256 `f0c863e5a3c1ffa1b379908840c256d7ef54f77fb9febc1c5f41c21e813a8684`, not a bare-base run. The six manifest source hashes match the reviewed files published at `c22355b8f89a6abb0ebce72dd0eced45cecb0b93` and remained unchanged during the run.

Environment: Xcode 27.2, Apple Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 arm64, isolated iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5. Caller-selected Node 26.12.1 and repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 passed preflight. The created simulator was deleted successfully.

| Check | Result | Reported wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS `build-for-testing`, including strict lint | Passed, exit 0 | 568.084 s |
| iOS `test-without-building` | 373 tests passed; 0 failures, skips, or expected failures | 777.116 s |
| Shared `swift test` | 21 tests in 3 suites passed; 0 failures or skips | 174.464 s, including build |

iOS xcresult records 373 test definitions / 429 parameterized invocations. All eight requested suites and all seven required mute regression definitions are present and passed:

- `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: 7
- `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`: 11
- `TalkModeManagerTests`: 51
- `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests`: 7
- `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`: 258
- `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`: 13
- `OpenClawTypographyTests`: 22
- `LocalFixtureChatTransportTests`: 4

The shared XML and console output independently confirm `RealtimeTalkRelaySessionAudioInputTests`, `ChatTalkControlTests`, and `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests` all passed. This includes relay silence while muted, queued-audio retirement, and preservation of capture/reply playback in the test harness.

**Collector-only defect:** kit v3's top-level summary says `shared: results_unverified` / `attention_required` because it looked only for `shared-results.xml`; Swift emitted `shared-results-swift-testing.xml`. That actual report is present in the returned archive with 21 passing cases and no failures/skips, and the command exited 0. The local collector now reads framework-suffixed reports as well. Its regression reproduces the false warning on shipped v3 and passes after the fix; the original returned ZIP is preserved unchanged. This correction does not alter or rerun the app tests.

The native regression fixtures took approximately 2 minutes for final-result submission and 1 minute 20 seconds each for fallback and quick-toggle groups; these are measured automated harness times, not a physical speech-finalization latency claim. The two-second native finalization deadline remains unchanged. Apple tests are green, but this run does not establish red-on-base automation, physical speech exclusion/playback across every transport, or screenshot acceptance.

#### Earlier v2 blockers — repaired and superseded by v3

Kit v2 reached both builds but executed no tests: strict lint rejected two raw-orange uses in `ChatTalkActivityViews.swift` and the unchanged 210-line demo seed function; shared compilation rejected the old route-lease initializer in `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests`.

The follow-up at `c22355b8f89a` uses existing warning/muted theme tokens, extracts two demo branches unchanged, and updates the routing-test initializer/closure signatures. No lint gate or assertion was disabled; native microphone-finalization code and tests were unchanged. Kit v3's successful build and tests above now verify these repairs on Apple tools.

### Local device test

Check out this PR, follow `apps/ios/README.md` for signing/build setup, run `pnpm ios:gen`, and build/run `apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj` on an iPhone.

- Mute/unmute while an answer plays; verify playback and accepted work continue.
- Speak while muted, then unmute; verify muted speech is not replayed.
- Native regression: say **five four**, mute, then say **three two**. Exactly one request should contain **five four**, excluding speech after mute. Also try muting before the first partial appears, quick unmute/re-mute, and End Talk during finalization.
- Restart Talk while muted, then test standalone push-to-talk after ending Talk.
- Verify the composer mic disappears during Talk and returns after End Talk; mute stays in the Talk card.
- Check the control at normal and large text sizes; capture real before/after screenshots.

The selected automated iOS and shared suites have passed in kit v3; no repeat is requested for unchanged source. The checklist above remains the physical-device acceptance scope.

## Android maintainer handoff (#187722)

The same native lifecycle correction applies to Android: stop new input and ask `SpeechRecognizer.stopListening()` to finalize, rather than snapshotting the current partial and immediately canceling/destroying the recognizer. Preserve the original recognition/session identity until `onResults`, or a bounded `onError`/deadline fallback to the latest partial; settle once before retiring that identity. Muted/draining callbacks must not restart capture or interrupt playback. Quick toggles and End Talk/session replacement must not leak old speech into a new capture or conversation.

The **five four → mute → three two** regression should send only **five four**, once. Also cover a final with no earlier partial, error/timeout fallback, duplicate finals, quick toggles, and teardown. iOS's two-second deadline is an implementation choice to validate on-device, not a prescribed Android timeout. This note is retained here for the Android author/maintainers; no Android code or metadata was changed.

## Current preparation status — November 7, 2026

**Do not merge the currently published `83ac2b2d3763fb005304fc2e3eb32256f69b19b6`.** The repaired candidate is local commit `b03355cd9b4c6e6b9a532b0bcd3ec530585b8a58` (tree `240940bc87f8c791ab4076e020c81a67c7dcd154`), on `roboclaw/merge-ready-178405-20261107`. Source publication to this existing PR is blocked by an unbound managed-publisher workspace. No replacement PR, source push, merge, or closure was performed.

- Focused source/session documents regain the existing Gateway setup and Back action **without hiding other usable desktops**, including when config-write capability is absent. Existing admission, config authority, explicit enablement and same-host retry owners remain unchanged.
- Preserves main’s newer Desktop copy (#192092) and newer attachment producers/guards. Restores the original pending-HTTP-download/same-session-metadata regression in the existing navigation scenario rather than replacing main’s production attachment code.
- **Fresh proof on the candidate tree: 81 tests passed** — 34 Desktop/Systems owner cases, 40 browser cases, and 7 review-layout cases. The browser batch includes the restored attachment interleaving and both files implicated by published-head CI. Matched main controls fail at the missing setup, after capturing the same usable desktop.

- Fresh independent source review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 issues. These are bounded reviews, not whole-main approval. The hosted ClawSweeper fallback remains pending publication of the repaired head.
- Local prospective merge against main `41ad585aef56074200ba445669ba16d1da63ef4d` is conflict-free. Main was not integrated again merely because it advanced. Existing PR history and contributor credit are retained as ancestors.

**Remaining mechanical gates:** establish a supported publishing binding to this existing PR/branch, publish the repaired head, update/complete hosted review as applicable, and verify exact-head CI. The published CI failures remain bound to `83ac2b2`; passing focused candidate replays are not causal attribution of those older failures.

**Screenshot scope:** matched 1280×844 real Control UI/Chromium captures with synthetic Gateway responses: main `dd11a9c2da9850f7dc091b5f011b66071b98ed4d` versus local repair `b03355cd`. No physical macOS permission, actual Mac/VNC authentication, desktop pixels, real Gateway/model-inference qualification is claimed. The inspected before/after sheet is attached below.

Follow-up to #177888. Related: #174368 (already closed).

## What Problem This Solves

The quality follow-up adds only a small admission regression: an advertised Desktop method must still reject a non-admin connection, offer no Enable action, dispatch no config patch/desktop observation, and retain Back. Production code is unchanged by that follow-up.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep submitted text when chat switching interrupts delivery
prs.body:
## Current-main reproduction review **Keep in Draft:** interrupted-send recovery is reproduced on iOS 27.2, but the affected native macOS submission path and the previously reported iOS 27.0 Clear issue remain unqualified. Original head `b26d8a68`; tested private current-main integration `f5a8e82f` on `243e1c65`. No production changes or source push. The same-session, agent-switch and independent-Gateway cases preserve text that frozen main loses. Existing focused tests and native builds pass. The updated [maintainer review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191535#issuecomment-6701240977) records the scope, limitations and full videos. Gateway captures obscure only a nearby device name/hostname; presentation timing and full duration are retained. ### Session switch Main loses the interrupted submission. The candidate retains a Delivery unknown item; its full recording also shows Copy Message and relaunch. The later background history differs. | Main | Candidate | |---|---| | | | ### Agent switch The accepted original message is separate from the newer local draft. Main loses that draft; the candidate displays it in recovery and releases it on explicit Clear. | Main | Candidate | |---|---| | | | ### Independent Gateway switch Main loses the newer draft after returning; the candidate retains it across a completed second-Gateway connection. The target pauses differ: 30.90 s versus 9.32 s. The old SEND 01 row belongs to an earlier trial. | Main | Candidate | |---|---| | | |
Original proposal and historical evidence Related: #165515, #190416. This is ordinary live-text delivery recovery; the local slash-command repairs remain separate. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: submitted text can disappear when switching chats, agents, or Gateways interrupts native iOS message delivery. ## User Impact Keep the original submission recoverable without overwriting newer drafts or automatically resending a message whose delivery is uncertain. If recovery storage is full or unavailable during a handoff, the original presentation stays in copy-only recovery: copy any needed text before choosing **Clear recovered text and continue**. **Draft for the explicitly requested local Mac/iOS runner handoff—not ready for review or merge. Native behavior and the new recovery UI are not yet qualified.** ## Why This Change Was Made - Recover against the captured conversation/composer key and revision, rather than whichever chat is currently displayed. - Distinguish interrupted pre-live admission, successful durable capture, known-unsent failures, and ambiguous delivery. Ambiguous delivery retains its warning and manual-review path; reconnect does not blindly replay it. - Revoke a replaced presentation's transport immediately, while the existing owner retains any text that could not enter the outbox. The fallback pane is copy-only; its explicit Clear action releases local recovery without sending or cancelling Gateway work. - Retire only the matching captured draft after durable acceptance, including after detachment, and preserve newer original/destination drafts. Defer new-session actions while recovery owns the presentation. No new manager, storage backend, schema, configuration option, dependency, or universal replay mechanism. ## Evidence ### Current source and local validation - Published head: `b26d8a68b96682b5901bf443f99990ae8c0d0c36`; exact tree: `5c967e200fecd75b7fc9d78950bfb00250fcba45`. Reconciled against main snapshot `b72ee38923d26c562179b8f9db7d0fa979cc42de`: **13 source/inventory files, +568/-90**. Prior published head4c560af3 and the accepted base are preserved in ancestry. The upstream fixture is unchanged; no workflow, dependency-pin, translated-dictionary or generated-catalog feature delta. - Recovery stays under the captured Gateway/agent/session/branch and composer revision. Known-unsent work retains recoverable custody; uncertain delivery remains copy-only/manual review, without automatic ambiguous replay or overwriting newer drafts. Existing outbox FIFO, question-authority retirement, current active-config checks, attachment pinning and default-agent hydration are preserved. The responsive toolbar/settings behavior and current accessibility New Chat sheet are retained; only the local copy/Clear pane remains usable through handoff. - Own frozen install used declared **pnpm12.15.0 / Node24.20** without pin or policy changes. Fresh current-base tooling consumer tests: **3 files /68 tests passed** (native/Apple i18n and native changed-scope contracts). These are repository tooling tests, **not Swift execution**. - The actual CI scope owner accepts the source-only packet and selects `strict_native_i18n=false`. Required `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes with **4,639 unchanged inventory entries**. Six English keys and four fixed-text `String(localized:)` lookup wrappers preserve the original English meaning. Source PRs own source plus stable-ID inventory; the serialized locale workflow owns translated/platform outputs. Prepared translation values are private, absent from this PR, and not public language-coverage proof. No English fallback was committed as translated coverage. - All nine baseline ratchets passed locally against exact baseb72 with `--no-merge-base`, including file/test growth, assertion safety, mock exports and database-worker/dialect checks. Docs formatting/lint/discovery proof is reused for unchanged documentation; fresh exact-base whitespace checks pass. These results **do not claim hosted CI passed**. - Fresh independent **whole13-file LOCAL P0–P3 source review was scoped-clean, zero findings**, on this exact tree/base. Review was static; unchanged implementations and native behavior were not independently validated. No prior-head CI or review result is relabeled as current-composition execution. ### Formatter-only follow-up The previous headd358 native screenshot build [job127763174260](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42178558159/job/127763174260) failed its SwiftFormat phase; it is not current-head success evidence. The repair is exactly **two files, +3/-2**: recovery-comment indentation in ChatProTab and a line break in an existing localized warning call in Sending. Complete inverse-edit comparison proves all string literals, signatures, assertions, SQL, control flow and captured-authority behavior unchanged. The CI build-stamped merge2c76 has relevant source/config/tool-guard bytes identical to headd358; accepted-base versions pass the same formatter. Pinned **SwiftFormat0.63.1**, using its SHA-256-verified official Linux release and unchanged repository configuration, reproduced the introduced `indent`/`wrap` violations. After correction, canonical `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` passes: **0/514 files require formatting**. Fresh **3 tooling test files/68 tests**, source admission/verification and all nine exact-base local ratchets pass; fresh whole13-file LOCAL P0–P3 review is scoped-clean with zero findings. These results are not historical478 Swift executions, Xcode compilation, SwiftLint, screenshots, or a new native/runtime CI pass. Independent current-head native results are recorded below; they do not turn local formatter/tooling proof into broader runtime acceptance. ### Observed native CI on headb26 Bounded current-head observation at **2026-11-06 07:59:41Z**: **38 successful checks,44 skipped/neutral,0 failed/cancelled/pending**. The main-run reader exposed49 jobs (20 success/29 skipped); Periphery exposed8 jobs (7 success/1 skipped). These are **exposed counts, not asserted complete workflow totals**; public REST re-enumeration was rate-limited and not retried. Skips are not native passes. - [iOS Periphery build job127773956129](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42182058350/job/127773956129) succeeded with **TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED at07:51:19Z**. The observed native formatter/lint/compiler build phases now succeed. Same synthetic data and 1280×900 viewport; the before/after contact sheet is attached in the successor chat. Gateway responses are mocked, not live identity proof.

Authenticated-query proof remains unverified: the source harness stalled before assertions, and the supported packaged flow stopped at the native process-custody guard (`service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction`). Remaining gates: the source-publication context is not bound to this existing PR; the required managed AutoReview tool is unavailable in this session; exact-new-head CI and current GitHub mergeability are not yet verified; the new contact sheet still needs a supported PR-media upload. No replacement PR or authority bypass was attempted.

Product recommendation: retain this owner-preserving fix. The personal page remains bounded, so newer personal but welcome-ineligible entries can crowd out older eligible web chats; this is a discoverability limitation, not an ACL or hidden-session bypass. Do not add an unbounded scan or client-side membership policy to this repair.

The original published-head description, contributor credit, and historical design evidence below are retained for provenance; they are not new-candidate proof.

---

Fixes: the Recent chats list shows unrelated teammates’ chats, including personally hidden sessions, on New Session and in empty conversations on signed-in multi-user Gateways.
