prs.body:
## Native verification **Decision still needed on the reported latency tradeoff.** The author's prior iOS simulator benchmark reports context-refresh p95 per call increasing from 45.05 ms to 60.73 ms in one run, and from 32.58 ms to 35.50 ms in another, while medians improve and the third run improves. That benchmark used demo transport on a heavily loaded runner. The new real-Gateway proof establishes work reduction and output preservation; it does not remeasure or dismiss the reported tail cost. The native owner should accept this bounded tradeoff or request a representative latency measurement before merge. The PR remains Draft for that decision. Updated against main `1c848332c84f` at head `130cdea4d816`, preserving the original contributor commits and both changed files. No production or test changes were added. A genuine web-fetch conversation was opened in the native iOS app and macOS Quick Chat. Ordinary messages were sent through the isolated Gateway and real model. | Retained source-card calculations during an unrelated append | Main baseline | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | iOS: three observed transcript updates | 1 per update | 0 per update | | Native macOS Quick Chat: two observed updates | 1 per update | 0 per update | The existing card remained in the output. Cold loading and context changes still recalculated it; switching sessions cleared the old projection. A final baseline reload matched the candidate's input, context and card-output digests. These are individual observed invocations, not independent benchmark trials or a latency/FPS claim. All 35 unchanged source-preview/resource tests passed. Both native platforms built and ran with equivalent observation-only counters, which are excluded from the branch. Source review found no blocking correctness issue. One non-blocking test-quality note remains: the new test uses array backing-buffer identity as a proxy for avoided work. The screenshots below are **later supplemental stills** showing the same real card. The full-speed videos preserve the actual flows, including the first iOS baseline's temporary blank transcript after reconnect; that observation is not attributed to or claimed fixed by this PR. No frames were spliced and no application state or responses were injected. The short final baseline reload supplies matching-history log evidence; the projection occurred before that short recording started.
Source and validation details Native baseline: `020ec24568b12416bf4315732532bae8762101aa`, with relevant production inputs qualified against main. Tested private integration: `d3e73c0b8bb9d155ac1f2c4224937a27779bbf63`. The published tree is identical to the reviewed final integration `4d5d7cb5fc67f6dd4b1baf625cab6f0cc1e8ea4d`; subsequent main differences did not alter the native production/build inputs used here. Original head: `8f03742d5687abb9138da0967dc94fd2a8e1378f`. Xcode 27.2/iOS Simulator 27.2; isolated macOS 26.6.2 guest; genuine task Gateway and Ollama model. Focused command: `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatSource --no-parallel` with the lab's isolated caches/build path. Full macOS runtime tests and a large-history timing benchmark were not run. Broad CI is separate from this native proof.
### Same card, preserved presentation Later supplemental native macOS stills; captured separately after the full recordings. | Main baseline | This PR | | --- | --- | | | |
Complete native flow recordings, original speed **iOS — baseline, including the reconnect and blank interval** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b272f857-99cf-4c05-97b4-5511c7a3780e **iOS — candidate append and session return** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bb7a46b-4666-43a5-822d-4e483631e94e **Native macOS Quick Chat — baseline** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76ec2af2-2d01-4f74-9fad-9717b2c6eb08 **Native macOS Quick Chat — candidate** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d4d6cd2-63b8-46e4-8bec-fa2b969b7498 **iOS — final baseline reload of matching history** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06084352-6eb5-445e-a51f-f2a06570928c
Original proposal and earlier evidence Closes #193862 Related: #193741 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the iOS and macOS chat rebuilds the source cards of every cited reply in the session each time a message is added to the transcript or history reloads, so long researched sessions spend milliseconds of main-thread time per update. ## User Impact User impact: long chat sessions with cited answers do much less main-thread work while an agent turn runs and when history refreshes; the source cards shown are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made `ChatSourcePreviewProjector` already kept each message's parsed links and result fields, but still rebuilt cards for every cited reply on every call. It now keeps each reply's cards and rebuilds them only when one of their inputs changed: the reply itself, an earlier message of the same run, the ids of those earlier messages (a removal, insert or reorder), or the source context. Those are all the inputs of the card builder. Rendered titles and excerpts are still shared between replies in one cache, as before, and are kept only for the cited replies that remain. A first projection does the same dictionary work as before: each rendered value is looked up and stored once, and each reply also records the values it used in a plain array. The shared cache is only rebuilt when a reply that had cards is rebuilt or removed; otherwise new values are merged into it. Why a cache (rather than deleting the work): the cards are needed and the projection runs from `messages.didSet`, which sees the full transcript each time. The per-message cache this extends already exists; this adds the per-reply result to it, keyed on the same inputs. The change adds no API, no initializer parameter and no test-only hook; the test drives the existing `project(_:context:)`. ## Evidence The proof below comes from the shipped iOS app (`apps/ios`, built from source) on an iOS simulator, driven through its demo chat transport so that appends, history refreshes and source-context refreshes all go through the normal view model path. Base and head ran interleaved in one job, and three runs repeat it. A shorter macOS run follows it. The measured head is `98e6cbaee3d`; the final commit `8f03742d568` only rewraps one call in `ChatSourcePreviews.swift` for the pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 lint, so production source is unchanged from the measured tree except formatting. - **Projector work:** card builds per persisted message drop from 83 to 0 (84 to 1 for a cited reply), and per history refresh from 87 to 0. A context refresh drops from 174 builds to 87. The card output is identical on every sample. - **Cold load:** no regression detected. On iOS the call that builds all 80 replies is 0.5 to 2.1% slower on head across the three runs (medians of 6 samples), much smaller than the spread between samples (run 3: base 115.7 to 187.7 ms, head 131.7 to 208.4 ms). On macOS, 30 pooled interleaved rounds gave 55.2 ms on base and 55.1 ms on head (-0.2%, sign test p = 0.86). An earlier +20.3% macOS figure came from 7 single samples and does not reproduce. A cost of about 2 ms on a fresh view in an already warm process cannot be ruled out. - **Context refresh:** median per call is lower on head in all three iOS runs, but p95 per call is higher on head in two of them; head does half the card builds per refresh. Details under Gaps. - **Frames:** display-link hitches move in both directions between runs, so this PR claims less main-thread work per update, not a frame-rate change. ### Native runtime proof #### Shipped iOS app on an iOS simulator The shipped iOS app (`apps/ios`, built from source) ran on an iOS simulator. Base and head were measured interleaved on one simulator in one GitHub Actions job on a fork. The runs used no secrets. - **Runs:** three runs of the same steps and code, all green (in run 3, the base round 1 XCUITest exited 65 on a screenshot timeout; its script had finished and its counts and digests are included): - Run 3: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42196768586. This is the main run; its measurement job is https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42196768586/job/127827857051. - Run 1: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42179860919 - Run 2: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42187968212 - **Artifacts (per run):** - `chatui-perf-proof-p2-ios` holds `summary.md`, `counts.json`, per-sample probe logs and screenshots (`samples/-/`), XCUITest logs, `environment.txt` and `load.txt` (runner load average). Run 3 adds the redacted trace in `timeline/-.json` and the os_signpost stream. - `ios-build-base` and `ios-build-head` hold the built apps, the applied scratch diffs and the build logs. - **Toolchain:** - Xcode 26.6 (17F113) on GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runners: macOS 26.7.2 (runs 3 and 1) and 26.6.2 (run 2), Apple M1 (Virtual), 3 vCPU. - iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5. - Debug build of `ai.openclawfoundation.app.debug`, made with xcodegen and `xcodebuild build-for-testing`, then run with `test-without-building`. - **Code under test:** - Base is `6b959f4ca63`, fetched from openclaw/openclaw. - Head is base plus `git diff --full-index 6b959f4ca63..98e6cbaee3d`. The head build checks that the resulting tree equals the head tree `446f8700623` (log: `head tree 446f8700623a... (expected 446f8700623a...)`). - **Scripts:** fork branch `proof/chatui-perf-p2`. Run 3 used [`9dbd9aebf56`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/9dbd9aebf56f8180cf9461f4465cdc5da6217bd7) (`rig/ios/`, `rig/ChatPerfProbe.swift`, `rig/instrument.py`), run 1 used `7668b84d981` and run 2 used `5778d323150`. None of it is part of this PR. - **Xcode 26.6 compatibility:** - Hosted runners only have Xcode 26.6. At this base the app references iOS 27.1-only SDK symbols at four sites: three `if #available(iOS 27.1, *)` branches (`ChatProTab.swift` twice, `OpenClawProComponents.swift` once) and one `@available(iOS 27.1, *)` private view modifier, `ChatToolbarStatusPopover` (`ChatProTab.swift`). - The scratch build wraps exactly those four sites in `#if compiler(>=6.4)`. An Xcode 27 build sees unchanged source, and on the iOS 26.5 simulator none of the iOS 27.1 code runs either way. - The scratch build also drops the SwiftFormat/SwiftLint pre-build phases so they don't lint the scratch code. **Same scratch changes on both sides:** - **Probes:** a call counter and a monotonic timer around `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` and `project`, with an `os_signpost` interval around each. The counters cover card builds and title and excerpt renders. - After each `update`, the probe writes a SHA-256 of each cited reply's cards whenever they change, plus one digest of all cards. It also records the cards handed to each rendered `ChatView` row. - A `CADisplayLink` records frame times. - **Fixture:** a launch flag seeds the app's local demo chat store (`AppleReviewDemoChatTransport`, the store behind `--openclaw-screenshot-mode`) with 80 cited turns. Each turn is a question, a `web_search` result and a reply citing 4 sources on public example domains (`example0.com`, `example1.com`, ...). - **UI test:** a scratch XCUITest case only launches the app on the chat tab, waits and takes screenshots. It does not type. **Event script.** After the transcript loads, the demo store publishes these events through the app's normal chat transport path, so the work goes through the view model into `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` and `project`: 1. **Appends:** 21 `.sessionMessage` events, one persisted message each: 7 turns of question, `web_search` result and cited reply. 2. **History refreshes:** 10 `sessions.changed` events (phase `message`). Each makes the view model refresh history, which returns the same rows (same ids) plus one new row. 3. **Context refreshes:** 10 `.chatMetadataChanged` events. Each makes the view model reload the source context through `loadSourceContext`, alternating between a gateway context and none. Under the gateway context, one cited link per reply is a gateway chat route on a reserved `.invalid` host, so its card is hidden. **Rounds:** 6 rounds per run, ordered ABBA (base, head, head, base, ...). One app launch per sample. All 18 samples per side (36 in total) across the three runs finished the full script (21 / 10 / 10 steps). **Card builds per step** (median over all steps of all samples, base / head). These counts are the same in all three runs: | Step | Cited replies | `update` calls | Card builds, base | Card builds, head | Title / excerpt renders, base | Title / excerpt renders, head | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | transcript load | 80 | 5 / 5 | 160 | 80 | 320 / 320 | 320 / 320 | | append: user question | 80 to 86 | 1 / 1 | 83 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | | append: `web_search` result | 80 to 86 | 1 / 1 | 83 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | | append: cited reply | 80 to 87 | 1 / 1 | 84 | 1 | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 | | history refresh: first after the appends | 87 | 1 / 1 | 87 | 7 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | | history refresh: later ones | 87 | 1 / 1 | 87 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | | context refresh (2 `update` calls) | 87 | 2 / 2 | 174 | 87 | 43.5 / 43.5 | 43.5 / 43.5 | Run 3 totals over all 6 samples per side, base -> head: append 10500 -> 42 card builds, history refresh 5220 -> 42, context refresh 10440 -> 5220, load 960 -> 480. **Reading the counts:** - **Appends:** base rebuilds every cited reply's cards on each persisted message. Head builds only the new cited reply. - **First history refresh:** it replaces the 7 event-delivered replies with their history copies. The ids are the same, but the rows are not field-for-field equal, so head rebuilds those 7. - **Context refresh:** head rebuilds every reply once, which is the expected invalidation. Base rebuilds every reply on both `update` calls. - **Load:** both sides build all 80 replies in one call. Base builds them again when the source context loads at launch, which is the 160. - **Timing at step edges:** in a few samples an append's `update` landed just after the next step began (`update` calls 0 to 3 per step). The step totals are unaffected. **Time per `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` call** (in-process timer around the signposted interval, all calls of all 6 samples per side; median / p95, base -> head): | Phase | Calls per side, per run | Run 3 | Run 1 | Run 2 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | append one persisted message | 126 | 9.83 / 19.43 -> 2.82 / 9.11 ms | 7.58 / 13.36 -> 1.57 / 6.14 ms | 9.21 / 16.90 -> 2.14 / 6.53 ms | | history refresh, same ids + 1 row | 60 | 13.79 / 24.05 -> 4.74 / 12.85 ms | 9.62 / 15.83 -> 3.54 / 8.29 ms | 12.59 / 23.45 -> 4.10 / 8.44 ms | | context refresh, per call | 120 | 16.29 / 45.05 -> 11.29 / 60.73 ms | 12.95 / 32.58 -> 8.47 / 35.50 ms | 16.93 / 51.60 -> 9.25 / 46.13 ms | | cold load: the call that builds all 80 replies, median of 6 samples | 6 | 161.8 -> 165.2 ms | 126.4 -> 127.0 ms | 157.5 -> 159.9 ms | **Signpost check:** run 3 also streamed the app's own os_signpost intervals (subsystem `ai.openclaw.chatperfproof` only) from the simulator's unified log during one extra run per side. That gives 56 `sourceStateUpdate` intervals per side: median 9.44 ms and p95 28.46 ms on base, against 4.38 ms and 34.24 ms on head. - The `signposts-*.json` files and the last lines of `summary.md` show 0.23 and 0.11 ms. They subtract `machTimestamp` values as if they were nanoseconds, but one tick is 41.67 ns on this runner, which the events' wall-clock timestamps confirm. - The figures above are recomputed from `signpost-stream-.ndjson.gz` with that factor. **Output unchanged:** - **Card digests:** in all three runs, the all-cards digest at the end of each phase is the same on every base and head sample: load `fc84a30f3c849913`, then `fd28340aed816e45` after appends, history refreshes and context refreshes. - At the end, 87 of 87 cited replies have equal per-reply digests on all samples. - The cards handed to the rendered `ChatView` rows are the same on every sample. - **Run 3 trace:** all 12 samples pass through the same sequence of 18 card states, including the gateway-context state (261 visible cards, digest `5d7d2f534905b3c5`). - **Screenshots:** each sample takes three (`sources-loaded`, `sources-after-appends`, `sources-end`). - The cards are visible in `sources-loaded` and `sources-after-appends`. `sources-end` shows the end of the transcript (the follow-up rows and only the bottom edge of a card); it is byte-identical on every sample that took it: all 12 in runs 1 and 2, and 11 of 12 in run 3. - In run 3, base round 1 hit an XCUITest "Timed out while requesting screenshot" on that last screenshot after its script had finished. XCTest saved a screen recording of the failure in its place. - The earlier screenshots show cited replies with their Sources cards ("Result 0 for question 80", `example0.com`). Their timing depends on how far the script had run, so they are not compared byte for byte. **The trace** (run 3, artifact `chatui-perf-proof-p2-ios`, `timeline/-.json`, 12 files of 42 steps each): a per-step timeline of the event script. - Each step has its start and end time, every `update` call in it (time, ms, card builds, title and excerpt renders), every reply whose cards changed (reply id and card SHA-256), and the card count and all-cards digest after the step. - Excerpt, head round 1 and base round 1 (card change lists shortened): ``` head-1 append 20 update 4.687 ms, cardBuilds 1, titles 4, excerpts 4; changed perf-run-86; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45... base-1 append 20 update 13.174 ms, cardBuilds 87, titles 4, excerpts 4; changed perf-run-86; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45... head-1 refresh 0 update 9.939 ms, cardBuilds 7; no card changes; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45... base-1 refresh 0 update 22.789 ms, cardBuilds 87; no card changes; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45... head-1 refresh 9 update 3.376 ms, cardBuilds 0; cards 348 base-1 refresh 9 update 12.014 ms, cardBuilds 87; cards 348 head-1 context 0 update 5.769 ms (0 builds) + 13.090 ms (87 builds); 87 replies changed; cards 261, sha256 5d7d2f534905b3c5... base-1 context 0 update 15.626 ms (87 builds) + 16.404 ms (87 builds); 87 replies changed; cards 261, sha256 5d7d2f534905b3c5... ``` **Redaction:** - The timeline holds only step names, times, durations, counts, fixture reply ids (`perf-run-N`) and SHA-256 digests. It contains no message text, no URLs, no file paths and no device identifiers; a scan for paths, URLs and token patterns over all 12 files finds nothing. - The transcript is the fixture. Its links point to public example domains, and the gateway route uses a reserved `.invalid` host, so no real endpoint is involved. The app never connected to a gateway, and the job had no secrets. - The raw files in the same artifact (probe logs, the signpost stream and xcodebuild logs) also contain no credentials or endpoints. They do contain the hosted runner's simulator paths (`/Users/runner/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/...`) and simulator UUIDs. **Frames:** the display link recorded hitches in every phase on both sides. The differences between sides go in both directions from run to run (for example, append hitches in run 1 were 163 on base and 145 on head, and in run 2 were 112 and 143), so I make no frame-rate claim from these runs. #### Earlier native run (macOS) The same probes, the real `OpenClawChatView` and `OpenClawChatViewModel` in an `NSHostingView`, and a local chat transport ran on the same Xcode 26.6 image: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42165891108, 7 interleaved rounds. - **Measured head:** `41394d91dc1`, tree `3fd4b5ec20f`. Its production source is identical to `98e6cbaee3d`; the only difference is 8 lines in `ChatSourcePreviewTests.swift`. - **Counts:** card builds per step match the iOS table: per append 83 -> 0 (cited reply 84 -> 1), refresh 87 -> 0, context change 174 -> 87. `update` per append was 5.385 -> 1.390 ms median. - **Cold first projection:** pooled with https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42164742047 (same production source), 30 interleaved rounds gave a median of 55.2 ms on base and 55.1 ms on head (-0.2%, sign test p = 0.86). - **Full suite:** OpenClawKit passed on head (2533 tests in 226 suites) and on base (2532 in 226) in https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42168510931. #### Gaps - **Build and device:** this is a Debug build on a simulator, on a shared 3-vCPU hosted VM, not a Release build on an iPhone. - **Runner load:** the runner was heavily loaded, with load averages from 35 to 146 across the three runs, and absolute times differ noticeably between runs (head append median 1.57 to 2.82 ms). The counts are the claim; the times are supporting evidence and point the same way in every run. - **Cold load and context p95:** the cold-load call (both sides build all 80 replies) is 0.5 to 2.1% slower on head in all three runs, well inside the spread between samples. A cost of about 2 ms on a fresh view in an already warm process cannot be ruled out. Context-refresh p95 per call is higher on head in two of the three runs, while its median is lower in all three; head does half the card builds per refresh. - **Scratch code:** the fixture, probes and UI test are identical on both sides and not part of this PR. The Xcode 26.6 compatibility wrap above is the only change to app source outside the fixture. - **macOS context change, pooled:** over the two macOS runs (14 rounds), the change as a whole was cheaper on head (median 19.3 ms on base and 15.7 ms on head, p95 33.2 and 30.5 ms), but the rebuild call that also renders titles and excerpts was slower on head in 11 of 14 rounds, by a median of 1.5 ms (sign test p = 0.06). A context refresh happens only when the session's source context reloads. - **Unrelated test failures in earlier runs:** some earlier macOS runs of the same production source had one hosted-runner audio timing failure each (`RealtimeTalkRelaySessionReviewTests`, `TalkBufferedAudioPlayerTests`). These tests are not touched by this change, and the full suite run linked above is clean. #### Tests - New test `incremental projection matches a fresh projection and reuses unchanged replies` (in `ChatSourcePreviewTests`): 11 steps of appends, an edited search result, a removed fetch, a reordered run, context changes, a return to the original and a new cited run. At every step the incremental projection must equal a fresh one. It also checks which replies keep their recorded cards: both after an unrelated append; only the other run's reply after a search result in one run is edited; neither after a source-context change; both after a new cited run is appended. On base it fails 3 reuse checks; on head it passes. - Mutation check, one change at a time: always rebuilding cards fails 3 reuse checks. Dropping the context check fails the identical-output check at 2 steps and 2 reuse checks. Dropping the earlier-row id check leaves stale cards: the identical-output check fails at 4 steps, and two existing tests (`refresh invalidates only changed transcript inputs and removes deleted sources`, `inline results and JSON result text retain invocation and canonical run ownership`) fail too. Restoring the fix passes 17/17. - Three mutations of the shared rendered-text cache (skipping its rebuild, dropping reused replies' values, skipping the merge) never change a card, because a rendered value depends only on its source text. They only change how much text is kept. This is not observable through `project`, so no test asserts it. A temporary local count of the cache caught each of them (9, 4 and 1 steps). - `ChatSourcePreviewTests`: 17/17 pass on head. Acceptance rule (it applies to the Command Line Tools package benchmark in the collapsed section below, not to the native run above): median `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` after appending one message to a 500-message transcript with 100 cited replies, release, warm, 60 iterations per run, base and head interleaved over 5 rounds on one machine. A win needs head to be faster than base in every round with identical output; any bench row that gets slower counts as a regression. Head met it on the append row in every round with identical output. The cold first projection was unchanged within noise there too. That table was measured on the first commit; on the final head, 7 more interleaved rounds gave a cold projection of 143.0 ms on base and 142.1 ms on head, with the update rows unchanged from the first commit. The native run above reports its own counts and timings, and its weak spots are listed under Gaps. Related: #193741 caches citation parsing for split rows in `ChatSourcePreviewState.previews(for:)`; this PR changes the projector underneath it. The two touch neighbouring code, merge cleanly and compose.
Earlier package benchmark (Command Line Tools) Machine: Apple M3 Ultra (32 cores), macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2, shared host (load average recorded per round). Base is `6b959f4ca63` (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit` is identical to `9f3ed313782`, where base was first measured). Each cell is the median of 5 round medians; each round median is over 60 samples, and the range is the lowest and highest round median. The harness records medians only, so there is no p95 column. | 500 messages, median of 5 rounds (range) | base | head | | --- | --- | --- | | `update` after one appended message | 8.72 ms (8.46 to 14.00) | 2.39 ms (1.23 to 2.59) | | `project` after one appended message | 9.68 ms (8.19 to 10.19) | 2.57 ms (1.36 to 3.70) | | `project` with unchanged messages | 8.77 ms (8.10 to 11.58) | 1.22 ms (0.96 to 1.95) | | history reload, same ids | 14.31 ms (12.63 to 17.92) | 6.78 ms (5.22 to 12.02) | | cold projection (first load) | 296 ms (257 to 330) | 293 ms (239 to 369) | The host was busy during these rounds (load average 36 to 48, and the cold row ran about 2x slower than in earlier runs on the same machine). An earlier run (cold projection about 140 ms instead of about 296 ms) of the same harness measured 6.5 to 8.6 ms on base and 0.84 to 0.93 ms on head for the append row. Head was faster in every round on every row except the cold projection, which is unchanged within noise. What is left on head (about 1 to 2.5 ms) is mostly comparing each message with its cached copy and rebuilding the dictionary, which this change does not touch. Per agent turn: an agent turn with k tool calls updates `messages` about 2k + 3 times (streaming deltas do not). Using the medians above, that is 113 ms on base and 31 ms on head at k = 5, and 375 ms on base and 103 ms on head at k = 20. Observation: the `previews` reassignment is not a second source of work. With identical previews the harness sees 0 of 5 observer notifications on base, because the observable setter already skips equal values. #### Harness and command The harness is a Swift Testing suite run locally and not included in this PR. It builds 100 turns of 5 messages (user, assistant with `web_search` and `web_fetch` calls, a search result with 8 rows, a fetch result with about 6 KB of text, a final answer of about 1.5 KB citing 3 result URLs): 500 messages and 1.49 MB of JSON. It times `project` and `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` for an append, an unchanged array and a history reload with the same ids, 60 iterations each, and reports the median. ``` swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --filter ChatSourcePreviewProjectionBenchmarkTests ``` #### Local toolchain notes Measured with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode). To build OpenClawChatUI there, a scratch copy expanded `@Entry`, disabled `#Preview` blocks and used the macOS 26.5 SDK, because the CLT install lacks the SwiftUI macro plugins. The 7 XCTest-based files could not run under CLT and were moved aside for the full-suite run; the benchmark and mutation runs used a test target reduced to the source preview suites to save build time. None of these local changes are part of this diff. The Xcode run above is the authoritative full-suite result.

prs.body:
## Current native review: changes required

Two regressions were reproduced: status-bar scroll-to-top while following latest, and the iPad transcript losing its centered reading column. The original intermittent iOS blank transcript was not reproduced in this bounded current-main comparison.

Tested author head `d2e1e29e1ef081c32e6fa5ea7e2006ca5a83f14f` through private integration `46f2091b5b325097361b4358a2c13b2df7455a49` with main `164c0dba58183af1be4b4af3b431b1a4fed6b021`. Four UI-test hunks were mechanically placed in main's split test files; no production repair or source push. Later main `74a5cbf2` has no changed relevant native inputs.

Native iPhone/iPad simulators on 27.2 and native Mac Quick Chat in an isolated macOS guest used the same real Gateway/model. The phone forks share 24 authentic messages; newly generated replies differ. Both iOS/Watch and Mac builds, 593 shared tests and one native retention test passed. iOS-specific package tests could not run because of unchanged `Process` use on that platform. No merge recommendation.

Full iPad and Mac recordings are attached below at original speed. Full phone recordings are preserved in the personal per-PR report; at 178 MB and 236 MB they exceed this upload route's 100 MB limit. Re-encoded phone copies failed timestamp validation and are not used. Phone findings are shown in the original frames below. MP4s are stream-copy companions, not recaptured or retimed; the iPad candidate's container drops only a 0.78-second trailing hold, with all encoded frames and timestamps retained.

The Mac supplement includes an inconclusive Jump attempt: main ends blank, the candidate remains in older history, and swipe recovery was not checked before stopping. It must not be read as a successful Jump or as proof that the PR fixes that blank.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal and historical author evidence</summary>

Related: #191478

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long iOS conversations going blank after sends and reply completion, and losing the reader's place as transcript content changes.

## User Impact

Replies remain visible at the live edge. Manual scrolling releases automatic following; sending or choosing Jump to latest resumes it. Canceled queued messages stay absent when retained history is projected.

The linked issue's sidebar-opening trigger remains unverified. This does not claim to fix every trigger in that report.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native self-sizing iOS transcript cells and one synchronous live-edge follow owner. Preserve the visible history prefix while reading and correlate streaming content with its completed row. Deletion revisions invalidate retained snapshots so cancellation cannot resurrect removed messages.

Shared grouping and rendering also change. macOS retains the SwiftUI path, but its history/live-tail composition changes; no new macOS visual verification is claimed. The broader paging and session-restoration work in #163153 is not included here.

## Evidence

- Focused package regressions: **142 tests across 8 suites passed**.
- Native iOS cancellation/history-trim regression: **1 XCTest, 0 failures**.
- Native iOS UI test: **1 XCTest, 0 failures**, exercising keyboard typing, sends, manual reader departure and explicit Jump. The strengthened Jump check verifies viewport intersection and rendered pixels; its captured screenshot was inspected.
- Scoped pinned SwiftLint/SwiftFormat checks passed with no warnings. Native build jobs bypass their unpinned lint phases; those jobs are build/test proof, not lint proof.

| Archived problem | Cleaned-port post-Jump result |
|---|---|

Fixes #194654

## What Problem This Solves

Candidate Doctor blocks updates when retained session rows contain ISO-8601 `endedAt` strings such as `2026-06-11T17:50:58.538Z`.

## User Impact

Doctor now converts those timestamps losslessly to epoch milliseconds, preserves the session and its unrelated data, updates indexed timing, and reports only a repaired count in a warning. Repeating Doctor makes no further changes. Invalid dates, timezone-ambiguous values, and sub-millisecond values that cannot be preserved still retain the existing offline-repair guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer decision for this fix authorizes automatic repair of these retained June values. The existing Doctor migration owns conversion, verified backups, and projection updates; canonical runtime admission remains numeric-only. The candidate must contain the repair; no updater protocol or schema change is needed.

## Evidence

- Main checked at `9c0b599224e1ca6fd831c146ae5132a7d301e885`; affected repair/admission paths match the supplied base and still reject this shape.
- Regression with the reporter's exact timestamp failed before the production fix (`found: 1, repaired: 0`) and passes with it, checking the original backup, canonical reads, indexed timing, preserved plugin data, count-only warning, and idempotence.
- Named tests: Doctor entry state **25 passed** (62.77 s including cold worker preparation; the new positive regression took 0.681 s), session normalization **45 passed** (12.38 s), Doctor transcript SQLite **12 passed** (3.59 s). These are production SQLite maintenance contracts; cold compilation dominates file wall time. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42391325033) passed (702 s workflow wall time), including production types, build, all selected Node shards, lint, docs, and the test-line ratchet; `openclaw/ci-gate` is green.
- Touched-file lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass. The targeted typecheck of all four touched TypeScript files passed on Testbox at `8fa36b1b32852535db86e2d4810b728597e8b397` (18.67 s). The local checkout-isolation guard was preserved when it refused shared dependency links.
- Local autoreview of the final change snapshot against `7fde96db4f149290e63c28b777126300577f8b42`: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper unavailable; the hosted fallback acknowledged automatic intake for this PR, so no duplicate request was posted.
- [Testbox upgrade proof passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42390997189) (202.94 s): installed latest stable `2026.11.1`, ran stable Doctor, seeded six retained June ISO rows across two agents, then ran candidate Doctor and canonical session listing. All six rows and unrelated fields survived, original JSON remained in backups, indexed timing matched, and a second Doctor run changed no rows and emitted no repeat repair warning. prs.title: feat(gateway): add suspension preflight and plugin participants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A hosting controller that wants to snapshot, freeze, or roll out a gateway host needs to know when it is safe to stop the process. Cooperative host suspension already ships and covers most of that contract, but two gaps remain.

First, an operator with read-only credentials cannot inspect whether the gateway is busy. The only preflight available is `gateway.restart.preflight`, which is documented as deprecated and reports a restart-specific inventory: it hard-zeroes session admissions, session mutations, chat runs, queued turns, terminal persistence, and terminal sessions. A controller polling it can see an idle gateway while chat runs and queued session-lane work are in flight, and its only alternative is `gateway.suspend.prepare`, which requires admin scope and closes admission as a side effect.

Second, a plugin that owns its own background queue is invisible to suspension accounting. Core tracks its own queues, sessions, and runs, but a plugin timer loop is not one of them, so `prepare` can return `ready` while plugin work is still running and lose it when the host freezes the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

`gateway.suspend.preflight` adds the missing read-scope observation: full structured counts plus blockers, `operator.read`, outside control-plane write rate limiting, and callable while a lease is held. It observes only — it never closes admission or takes a lease — so `prepare` remains authoritative and can still return busy immediately after preflight reported idle. That limitation is documented rather than papered over, because a point-in-time read can always go stale.

Plugin participants are an optional registry rather than a new lifecycle. `prepare()` is synchronous by contract and runs inside the existing atomic fence; making it async would let new work slip in between closing admission and taking the authoritative snapshot. A busy or throwing participant rolls every participant back, so a refused attempt never leaves a queue fenced with no lease. Participant resume folds into the coordinator's existing `resumeScheduling` path, so rollback, explicit resume, lease expiry, and in-process restart all release participants through the one fail-closed state machine that already exists rather than a second one. Participants are registered through the normal `api.*` registrar and namespaced by plugin id.

Non-goals: no Kubernetes or rollout policy, no SIGTERM orchestration, no forced cancellation, and no checkpointing of in-flight LLM execution.

## User Impact

Operators can poll a gateway's busy state with read-only credentials and get an itemized answer — which chat runs, cron runs, queued turns, or plugin queues are holding it open — instead of inferring it from a deprecated restart-shaped view or taking an admin-scope lease just to look.

Plugin authors can join their own background queues to the suspension fence with `api.registerGatewaySuspensionParticipant(...)`, so a host snapshot no longer silently interrupts plugin-owned work.

The change is additive. No existing method, scope, result shape, or default behavior changes, and `gateway.restart.preflight` semantics are deliberately untouched. New surfaces: one method, one optional blocker kind (`plugin-participant`), one optional count field (`pluginParticipants`), and one registrar that defaults to a noop.

## Evidence

**Tests — all passing** (Node 24.19.0, `pnpm` 11.15.1):

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `src/infra/gateway-suspension-participants.test.ts` | 9 passed |
| `src/infra/gateway-suspend-coordinator.test.ts` | 22 passed |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/suspend.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `extensions/admin-http-rpc` | 20 passed |
| `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.suspension-admission.test.ts` + `src/infra/restart-suspension.test.ts` + `core-descriptors.since.test.ts` | 18 passed |
| `src/gateway/server-http.probe.test.ts` | 29 passed |
| `src/infra/update-campaign.test.ts` + `src/infra/update-startup.test.ts` | 91 passed |
| `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` | 58 passed |

**New coverage:** 9 participant-registry cases (idle, busy rollback, fail-closed prepare, unavailable status treated as busy, resume-once, retry-only-failed-participant, unregister, re-register replaces, empty id rejected) and 4 coordinator integration cases (participant busy refuses prepare and rolls back, idle participant held closed until resume, reopen at lease expiry without polling, fail-closed when a participant cannot reopen). Preflight adds 4 handler cases plus an Admin HTTP RPC dispatch case.

**Checks:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` | all lanes ok — see known-failure note below |
| `tsgo` core / extensions / core-test-shards / extension-test-types | exit 0 |
| `oxlint` (34 changed files) | exit 0 |
| `oxfmt --check` | clean |
| `docs-link-audit.mjs` | 6550 links, 0 broken |
| `check-docs-mdx.mjs` | 780 files passed |
| `check-docs-config-examples.mjs` | exit 0 |
| autoreview (`codex`, high) | clean — no accepted/actionable findings, `overall: patch is correct (0.98)` |
| TruffleHog | clean |

**Pre-existing unrelated failure:** `check:changed` reports `doctor contract declaration + closure guard tests` failing — `src/plugins/doctor-contract-declarations.test.ts` lists `feishu`, `googlechat`, `line`, `matrix`, `memory-wiki`, `msteams`, `nextcloud-talk`, `synology-chat`, `telegram`, `whatsapp`, `zalo`, `zalouser` as "missing doctorContract declaration". This reproduces identically on clean `main` with this branch stashed, touches no file in this diff, and belongs to bundled-plugin manifest parity rather than gateway suspension. Not addressed here.

**LOC:** production +340/−6, tests +365, docs +317.

**Follow-up left open:** the participant API is exposed through the `api.*` registrar rather than a dedicated `plugin-sdk/*` subpath, because a new subpath requires regenerating the SDK api-baseline, which `AGENTS.md` forbids hand-editing. The registrar path is fully functional for bundled and third-party plugins; promoting it to a standalone subpath is a clean follow-up.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep parents on the same thread after native child completion
prs.body:
### Current-main port (November 7, 2026)

The current-main completion-catalog port is now tracked in #194753, on top of #194748. It uses exact native completion custody and current executor ownership without copying the older release-specific schema/catalog overrides. The evidence below remains historical evidence for this PR head; it is not proof of the newer port or clearance of the earlier downstream native-dispatch review request.

Related: #153354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a native Codex parent switching threads and losing access to its existing child when the last child's completion resumes the parent.

## User Impact

A parent can receive its child's completion and send a follow-up to that same child without replacing the native parent thread or rebuilding its accepted tool catalog. No configuration or migration is required. This change does not address duplicate visible completion replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing catalog recovery path depends on live-child execution protection. That protection is correctly released before the last child's completion is delivered, leaving the automatic continuation exposed to a newly generated catalog.

Use the existing completion-delivery owner to identify an exact, currently in-flight completion for the same parent, child, requester session, run, and physical client. Only that delivery can recover the native thread's accepted catalog. Its authority is checked again after metadata is read. Runtime, home, transport, catalog fingerprints, and current tool-execution checks remain enforced; ordinary turns retain their existing behavior. No additional registry or SDK surface is introduced.

Codex's native contract was checked against `rust-v0.164.0` (`6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`): `thread/start` accepts dynamic tools, while `thread/resume` does not replace them. A small existing parent-release loop moves to the existing parent owner without changing its behavior, keeping the monitor within the repository's source-size gate.

### Published 2026.10.10: what is already fixed and what remains

The [release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/CHANGELOG/2026.10.10.md) credit #174900 for native catalog continuity. That is the upstream foundation this PR extends: protected parents can reuse their accepted declarations while current tool permissions remain enforced. It does not cover every completion lifetime. In the [published tag's catalog guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-tool-catalog.ts#L28-L70), recovery still requires live-thread protection. The last child's completion releases that protection before delivery, so this automatic continuation can still miss catalog recovery and replace its parent thread.

This PR addresses that remaining completion-delivery interval through the existing owner, without weakening runtime fingerprints or granting execution rights from retained declarations. #188526 carries the corresponding release-branch change together with its WebChat-origin repair. The release notes therefore do not make this PR redundant.

## Evidence

### Additional published-release check — November 3, 2026

A selective port of this catalog change, the release-specific WebChat fix, and the remaining retirement error-class fix was applied to official 10.10 packages. On both macOS and Linux, a real-model authenticated WebChat run completed parent → child → automatic completion → same parent → follow-up to the same child. The parent and physical client stayed the same; the child returned its remembered marker. Shipped CLI history confirmed settlement. On Linux, an actual `session_status` call also succeeded after completion. These were observations of the combined installed port, not a new exact-head run of this PR or proof of all fallback paths.

The port's 50 focused tests passed, including composed checks for wrong-requester catalog denial, custody revoked during an awaited metadata read, and current executor restrictions after catalog recovery. The downstream native-dispatch denial and custody-reassignment trace requested in review is still missing. These checks do not clear that security/proof request. Accepted native metadata was inspected after each live run; no independent before-run catalog snapshot was taken. The exact-candidate evidence and its limits remain below.

- Regression cases fail before the fix at the completion owner and catalog loader, then pass with it. The final changed suites pass 19 tests; related availability, execution-authority, and continuation suites pass 26 tests. The existing two parent-retention cases also pass after the owner extraction.
- Codex production and test typechecks, targeted lint/format, `git diff --check`, source-size and test-line gates pass. The separate allocation grants exactly the change's 126 net regression-test lines; no shared ceiling or source-size baseline is raised.
- Shared autoreview of the final range `f3009a56907e34a42d0d453dddff8adb13de4f20..417d7e2113f065fb147bd458584dc72d9538b43f`, including complete affected owners and authority context, found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Tests were executed separately, not by the reviewer.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passes on `417d7e2` (82.3 s). A real-model, authenticated WebChat run on that exact source/build completes parent → child → automatic completion → parent continuation → follow-up to the same child. All three parent-ready events identify the same native parent and physical client; the child's follow-up returns its remembered marker. All 48 originally accepted functions match the final retained binding. The shipped CLI confirms the visible result and settled session.
- Full local `pnpm test:extension codex --maxWorkers=6`: **5,368 passed, 3 failed, 17 skipped**, across 441 executed files (481.57 s). Two failures are macOS process-inspection permission errors in unchanged `transport-startup.test.ts`; the third is the validation-watcher assertion in unchanged `transcript-mirror-cleanup.test.ts`. For the watcher failure, temporarily reversing this entire patch, verifying the parent-tree source bytes, and running the exact file through the supported Node 24 wrapper reproduces the same assertion on base `f3009a5` (1 failed, 12.77 s). The patch was then restored and all changed-file hashes and clean HEAD verified. The process-permission signatures were also reproduced during the release baseline investigation; they have not been repaired here. Watcher root cause/order sensitivity remains undiagnosed. This full lane is not claimed as passing. No assertion, timeout, retry, skip, or expected-failure setting was weakened.

The live run used the pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4 and Codex 0.164.0, isolated synthetic state, internal routing, and disabled model fallbacks. It produced two identical visible final replies, one for each child completion. It qualifies thread/catalog/child continuity, not exactly-once delivery, stale external routing, or general fallback behavior. The original accepted metadata was inspected after the run; no independent before-run catalog snapshot was taken.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized exact-candidate runtime proof</summary>

```text
Exact-candidate main catalog-continuity proof
Source/build commit: 417d7e2113f065fb147bd458584dc72d9538b43f
Gateway runtime: pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4 (openclaw-v1.4.4-20261026-191755ec11-webkit-b82bc917e9); identified from the running Gateway executable. Native runtime: workspace-pinned Codex 0.164.0.
Environment: authenticated WebChat client, isolated synthetic session, internal route, no external channels. Model fallbacks were disabled to fail closed.

One chat.send request was accepted; no manual continuation or model retry was sent.
Parent: 01a18e92-c25a-7e02-939a-b7ae5127109f
Child: 01a18e92-ef88-75d2-b7e3-14ee747f42e4 (native agent target /root/catalog_child)
Parent thread_ready: started, resumed, resumed; same parent and physical client throughout.
Parent native transcript: exactly one spawn_agent and one followup_task to that same child.
Child terminal results: FIRST_READY; FOLLOWUP_OK CATALOG_MEMORY_110.
Original accepted native catalog: 10 top-level declarations / 48 functions.
Accepted catalog fingerprint: sha256:a41950488f43f4dca21fd13f8e67488f888f443e901a80e45b2502112c1e9661
The final retained binding identifies the same parent and client and matches that accepted catalog fingerprint. The accepted session_meta record was inspected after the run; no separate before-run snapshot exists, so this is not a before/after digest comparison.

Shipped CLI read after settlement:
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<isolated-config> pnpm openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:catalog-chain-proof","limit":100}' --json
Result: logical session catalog-chain-proof; visible CATALOG_CHAIN_OK 01a18e92-ef88-75d2-b7e3-14ee747f42e4; hasActiveRun=false; pendingInputs.total=0.

Observed limitation: two identical visible final replies, corresponding to the two child completion announcements. This run proves catalog/thread/child continuity; it does not prove exactly-once visible delivery, general fallback behavior, or stale external routing. The inherited spawn record in the child's rollout was not counted as a second spawn.

Cleanup: the proof client finished; the task-owned Gateway stopped cleanly after settlement and its listening port is closed. No production state or services were used. Private fixtures remain only until this sanitized evidence is published.
```

</details>

prs.title: feat(ios): browse and preview files shared in a conversation
prs.body:
## Current maintainer verification **The tested feature works; product approval remains pending.** The remaining decision is whether iOS should add this direct **Artifacts** toolbar entry and include canonical user uploads alongside assistant-delivered files. No PR-introduced correctness defect was confirmed. ### Confirmed proposal scope The proposed flow is **conversation → Artifacts → find a file → preview or share/save**. Keep the direct toolbar entry beside Chat actions and one collection containing both canonical user uploads and assistant-delivered files from that conversation. The direct entry avoids searching the transcript or opening a configuration menu; including both participants avoids requiring users to remember who sent a file before finding it. Search and type filters already apply to this shared collection. Both behaviors are already implemented in this PR. No separate sections by sender or additional navigation are proposed in this iteration. Workspace Files remains a separate view of the agent’s working directory. ### Real before / after - **Before:** four files were uploaded through the native Files picker. A real local model then created and delivered a second `Review notes.txt`. The main Gateway catalog returned only that assistant file; downloading it from the message preserved its 48 bytes. - **After:** the integrated Gateway started normally on the same unchanged test state. The catalog returned all five files, including the four pre-patch uploads. Their stored bytes and the existing assistant artifact identity were preserved. - Search and type filters worked, including the two distinct files named `Review notes.txt`. Text, image and PDF previews worked; PDF rotation and return remained usable. ZIP had no preview but could be exported. - Native **Share → Save to Files** preserved the text (124 bytes), JPEG (1809 bytes), PDF (665 bytes) and ZIP (177 bytes) exactly. The existing picker converted the input PNG to JPEG before upload; the image comparison uses those stored JPEG bytes. - Canceling Share and reopening it in the same PDF preview worked. Temporary export files were removed when the preview closed. A second conversation kept its own collection; returning restored the original five files and unsent draft. **192 existing tests passed:** 70 native iOS tests, 112 artifact/media tests, one real WSS/HTTPS fixture test, and nine shared-consumer tests in an isolated macOS guest. Both normal iOS + Watch builds passed. The fixture tests support permissions, revocation, membership and byte-integrity checks; they are distinct from the real picker/model/export recordings. **Existing limitation:** terminating and relaunching the app loses the unsent draft on both main and the candidate. Collection, sharing and session navigation preserve it while the process remains running. This was recorded separately; no repair was made.
Sources and proof boundaries Native iPhone 18 Pro Simulator, iOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2. Baseline `a6ee6a18a5d7`; original PR head `b6bea62cd79b`; private integration `3fcfd0286230`. The integration preserves the author's ancestry and resolves only two mechanical conflicts, retaining both main's and the PR's behavior. Later main `f8b1a6ba3d8d` changes only two unrelated tests; relevant production inputs are unchanged. An isolated real Gateway and local model were used. Input files are synthetic; application responses, transcript history and metadata were not injected. No product/test fixes, source push, merge or auto-merge were performed. Full macOS UI and precisely scheduled live races were not exercised; shared-consumer and boundary tests cover their stated contracts. All six recordings preserve the original timeline. Container-only MP4 remuxes have identical compressed frames and presentation/decode timestamps. The last video is a supporting comparison of the pre-existing draft limitation, not a feature demonstration.
Before and after — native iOS | Main: message download | PR: direct Artifacts entry | | --- | --- | | ![Main native chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/986d40da-bb22-4fbb-b346-5e7853fe8ba5) | ![PR native chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4dccb4f-e125-4108-9589-d5797bf7200f) | | Conversation collection | Uploaded text preview | | --- | --- | | ![Five actual files](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36ebc2a1-70ad-4f30-b3f1-8eec8832b87d) | ![Uploaded text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5dfc8e7-a08b-4112-afec-44cc0a1a9b3b) | | PDF preview | Unsupported preview remains exportable | | --- | --- | | ![PDF preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40088673-7cec-4f27-b282-c93490d70bae) | ![ZIP export fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4211780e-fc9e-412a-ac39-c27dbb3a3d7f) |
Complete native recordings — original speed Before: picker upload, workspace Files and message export — 149 s https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba2edda2-cbbd-4a41-8787-4526352440d7 After: collection, search, distinct same-name files, text/image preview and export — 95 s https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9236f9bf-3289-4a1e-b73d-8b35ef60f2bc After: PDF rotation, ZIP fallback/export and draft return — 67 s https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a470e2a6-4f50-4162-ba15-b1ce3f38df7d After: separate session upload, return and relaunch behavior — 141 s https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9f35f23-7559-4e71-999d-c9f1774af221 After: cancel Share, reopen it in the same PDF preview and save — 36 s https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2403def9-d137-49bb-847c-2f8e448337c0 Supporting control: the main client also loses the unsent draft on process relaunch — 26 s https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8089a777-87eb-4c47-92aa-988a40256058
Original proposal and historical evidence Closes #192890. ## What Problem This Solves Returning to files shared in an iOS conversation requires finding their original messages; Workspace Files lists the agent's working directory instead. ## User Impact Users can open **Artifacts** beside Chat actions, find files by name or type, preview text/images/PDFs, and save or share originals while keeping their conversation and draft intact. This includes cataloged assistant files and canonical user uploads. Recovering uploaded documents requires the Gateway change in this PR; older Gateways retain their existing catalog coverage. This is an online collection, not an offline archive or a browser of arbitrary paths mentioned in chat. ## Why This Change Was Made The native app can reuse the conversation catalog already used by the web client. The toolbar entry makes conversation content accessible separately from configuration and workspace browsing. The proposed entry point is the Artifacts tray button shown below; scope and use cases are described in #192890. The iOS collection uses existing list/download contracts, captured conversation/Gateway identity, and the existing temporary-file owner. Text is rendered literally; images use the existing decoder and PDFs use PDFKit. Unsupported previews remain exportable when downloading is supported. The preview retains its rendered content rather than the original download buffer; Share reacquires the file under current authorization. Preview limits are smaller than the existing 100 MiB document-download limit. A real picker upload revealed that the full catalog omitted canonical inbound media facts. The Gateway commit projects those facts through the existing artifact owner and media store, preserving current session authorization, transcript membership, grant expiry, and byte-integrity checks. It adds no RPC, filesystem index, dependency, schema migration, or model tool. Internal custody locations stay out of public summaries. Builds on the workspace browser (#100767), native attachment downloads (#155195), and web Files browsing (#176329). ## Evidence Original, unannotated Light-mode captures from iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.1. Synthetic files; working native Debug screens, not App Store screenshots. Before/after use the same conversation and assistant file.
Before: individual message downloadAfter: direct collection entry
Assistant files and actual uploadsUploaded file preview and Share
- **Baseline:** upstream `4a43644e7a7b` downloaded the original 197-byte assistant file from its message. Chat controls had no collection; Workspace Files showed its separate workspace scope. - **Real upload and export:** picker → send → app relaunch/history → collection → preview → Share → Save to Files passed against an isolated TLS Gateway. The saved file matched the input byte for byte, a nonempty draft stayed intact, the export survived dismissal, and the temporary file was removed. An upload created before the Gateway fix also became retrievable. Another conversation could not download it. - **Native proof:** 78 focused native tests, 9 shared tests, and the connected collection UI flow passed. The UI flow covers duplicate names, search, filters, text/PDF preview, system sharing, and draft preservation. Duplicate catalog IDs have a regression that fails before the repair. - **Gateway proof:** 78 tests passed, including `operator.sessions.read`, foreign-session denial, revocation, removed transcript membership, changed bytes, size limits, missing files, and isolated media roots. The original projection fails inbound discovery; the fix passes with the same dependency pins. Empty media slots also fail before the final guard and pass afterward. - **Local checks/review:** native and Gateway builds, focused typecheck/lint/format, native source-inventory verification, and the test-line budget passed. Independent local source reviews found duplicate identities, an internal-locator leak, empty-slot projection, and an offline-demo control with no action; each was corrected before submission. Final demo/connected UI results are recorded below. ### Follow-up to the first review — `113cb167272b` The ordinary-ID download defect is repaired: the native loader now selects the existing validated resolver from the returned grant route, rather than the catalog ID prefix. The new native regression failed with `invalidSource` before the repair; the corrected route preserves TLS pinning, byte limits, current-connection checks, and the artifact grant's MIME/disposition checks. Native results: 56/56 selected tests passed on iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.0 with Xcode 27.2 (27B52); the new regression failed with the original loader and passed with the repair. The CI failure in `artifacts.images.test.ts` was an obsolete expectation that the unfiltered catalog excluded inbound uploads. Its explicit eight-item expectation now matches this feature while preserving the Activity gallery's pagination, path preference, unsupported-path and bounded-read checks. The same failing test passed after the change: 15/15; 12.616 s test time (47.93 s runner time including preparation). **Inspectable authority proof:** the existing HTTPS test now starts the production Gateway with isolated state, temporary TLS identity, synthetic canonical inbound media, and separate authenticated WSS clients. No authorization function or HTTP handler is mocked. The inbound record is seeded through existing media/transcript owners; the earlier native picker/export run proves ingestion separately. | Operation | Observed final effect | | --- | --- | | Reader with `operator.read` requests the upload grant, then HTTPS GET | HTTP 200; 51 bytes; SHA-256 identical to the expected file | | Client without `operator.read` requests that artifact | RPC rejected: `missing scope: operator.read`; no grant issued | | HTTPS GET without a valid grant | HTTP 404; exactly `Not Found` (9 error bytes, zero upload bytes) | | Administrator calls `device.token.revoke` for the original reader; reuse the **same original URL** | HTTP 404; exactly `Not Found` (9 error bytes, zero upload bytes) | Expected and received SHA-256: `d7efd3d8685b1cafc7abea4f55450ba775f2d1655e458d17957edd3daa622830`. The HTTP route uses a capability URL, not an additional reader identity on each GET. The forbidden-client case proves denied grant issuance and denial without a valid grant; it does not claim that a second holder of a live bearer URL is independently authenticated. Revocation invalidates the original reader's previously issued capability before file delivery. Reproduce with `OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm test:e2e:gateway src/gateway/artifacts-download.https.e2e.test.ts`. Result: 1 test passed, 6.745 s test time / 16.76 s runner time, reusing the official prerequisite build. The original unchanged test also passed independently. The extension reuses its server, port claims and teardown; it adds no production hooks. Full sanitized trace: ```json { "proof": "inbound-artifact-authority", "transport": "real WSS/HTTPS", "fixture": "synthetic", "expectedBytes": 51, "expectedSha256": "d7efd3d8685b1cafc7abea4f55450ba775f2d1655e458d17957edd3daa622830", "allowed": { "status": 200, "bytes": 51, "sha256": "d7efd3d8685b1cafc7abea4f55450ba775f2d1655e458d17957edd3daa622830" }, "forbidden": { "rpc": "missing scope: operator.read", "httpWithoutGrant": 404, "response": "Not Found", "uploadBytesDelivered": 0 }, "revocation": { "method": "device.token.revoke", "originalGrantReused": true, "status": 404, "response": "Not Found", "uploadBytesDelivered": 0 } } ``` The repair received an independent local source review with no actionable findings. CI for `113cb167272`: **84 checks passed, 46 skipped, no failures; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed**. Preview-state cleanup (`b6bea62cd79`): the original download buffer is no longer retained just to enable Share. Independent source review found no issues; the same 56 native tests passed again. The existing collection/search/text/PDF/system-sharing/draft UI test also passed (64.907 s) on iOS 27.0 / Xcode 27.2, using the documented synthetic loopback Gateway. This repeat validates native behavior; the production Gateway authority evidence above remains separate. No new tests or infrastructure were added. CI on `b6bea62cd79` is complete: 84 checks passed, 45 skipped, one neutral, no failures; `openclaw/ci-gate` and the iOS Periphery report passed.
Reproduce the focused checks and understand the proof boundaries Gateway regressions: ```sh pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/artifacts.prepared.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/artifacts.test.ts src/media/store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 ``` Native suites: `IOSGatewayChatTransportTests`, `IOSMediaArtifactLoaderTests`, `IOSSessionArtifactsModelTests`, and `OpenClawTypographyTests`. Shared suites: `ChatMediaURLTests`, `ChatMediaArtifactLoaderTests`, and `ChatDownloadedFileTests`. The opt-in `SessionArtifactsUITests/testFindPreviewAndShareSessionArtifacts` uses `apps/ios/Tests/Fixtures/session-artifacts.json`. For deterministic UI reproduction, start `node scripts/test-ios-shell-gateway.mjs --session-artifacts`, pair an owned simulator as documented in that script, and forward `TEST_RUNNER_OPENCLAW_IOS_ARTIFACTS_PROOF=1` to the normal `OpenClawUITests` xcodebuild command. The fixture exercises native UI; it does not prove server authorization or ingestion. The executed UI run used those fixture bytes through a real isolated Gateway. This opt-in run is local evidence, not a claim that ordinary CI runs it. The separate picker/export run used a real Gateway and iOS Files. Only the model reply was provided by a local synthetic responder; no external inference was required. `Review notes.txt` was 116 bytes, SHA-256 `dafc437c432185c533cf2567126a5a1b5aef9b9cd722e61b3ffecdfa9dcffbae`, identical before upload and after Save to Files. Captures show the connected layout from the same patch series: baseline `4a43644e7a7b`, toolbar `0915dd90976`, and uploaded-file screens with native `e332493c3d2` / Gateway `dc6343f9327`. Subsequent repairs only exclude empty media slots and hide the nonfunctional entry in offline demo mode; they do not change the connected layout shown here. Historical physical-device screenshots remain in the issue. Current local qualification is on the simulator; actual VoiceOver navigation, App Store distribution, and other OS versions are not claimed. The test allocation reserves 217 net TypeScript regression lines for inbound custody/authorization, captured media roots, the existing gallery consumer, and real HTTPS grant revocation. The shared scalar budget is unchanged. The collection has no editing, deletion, reorganization, or revision-history scope; partial catalog loads are identified and search covers returned items. Final focused UI checks: offline-demo regression passed in 26.286 s; connected collection/search/preview/share/navigation/draft flow passed in 65.620 s. An earlier run failed by asserting that the system share controller vanished from the accessibility tree. Its recording showed dismissal; the final check performs actual return navigation and verifies the preserved collection and draft instead. No sharing-production change or retry was needed.

prs.title: fix(android): show retry instead of SHA-256 entry on TLS timeout
prs.body:
Closes #142528 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android asks for a SHA-256 certificate fingerprint when the first TLS probe to a Gateway times out, for example a Tailscale Serve endpoint whose handshake stalls. ## User Impact A timed-out first connection now shows the connection recovery screen with Retry (and the Tailscale hint on tailnet hosts). Manual pin entry stays available on that screen as "Enter fingerprint manually", so an operator can still pin a Gateway whose handshake is slower than the probe. ## Why This Change Was Made #142651 routed `ENDPOINT_UNREACHABLE` to the network recovery path; this does the same for `TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` in `decideGatewayTlsTrust` and reuses `gatewayNetworkConnectError(timedOut = true)` in `NodeRuntime`, keeping the existing timeout text. The problem carries reason `tls-handshake-timeout` so the recovery screen can tell a stalled TLS probe apart from a WebSocket connect timeout. The manual-pin escape hatch from #110976 is kept, as the issue asks: the recovery screen's "Enter fingerprint manually" goes through the same refresh path as Retry, skips the probe, and publishes the existing manual-entry `GatewayTrustPrompt` for the same endpoint. Accepting it saves and enforces the pin exactly like the existing `TLS_UNAVAILABLE` manual entry. Saved pins still take precedence over the probe, and `TLS_UNAVAILABLE` still opens manual entry directly. ## Evidence Android 16 emulator (`system-images;android-36;google_apis;arm64-v8a`, the repo's screenshot image), Play debug APKs. Onboarding → Set up manually → host `10.0.2.2`, Secure (TLS), placeholder token → Test connection. Host listeners on `127.0.0.1`: `18443` accepts TCP and never replies (stalled handshake), `18444` answers plain HTTP (`TLS_UNAVAILABLE`), and a TLS server on `18443` with self-signed test cert A or cert B. Same manual setup on every build: **Stalled handshake, fresh setup** | Main | This branch | This branch: Enter fingerprint manually | |---|---|---| | | | | - Main: "Trust this gateway?" asks for a SHA-256 fingerprint after the probe times out. - This branch: "Connection issue" with Retry and "Enter fingerprint manually". Retry re-probed the same endpoint without retyping (new connection in the listener log). - "Enter fingerprint manually" opened the manual dialog with no new connection to the listener (no second 13s probe). Pasting cert A's fingerprint and tapping Trust stored `gateway.tls.manual|10.0.2.2|18443 = 30d951aa…3e00`. - The pin is enforced: with `18443` serving cert A the app completed TLS handshakes without a prompt; serving cert B, it made no session handshake and showed the changed-certificate prompt (old = cert A, new = cert B). - Control: `18444` (plain HTTP) still opens manual entry directly. **Upgrade from latest stable** Built `v2026.11.1` as a Play debug APK from `git archive` (same debug key and version code as this branch, so `adb install -r` keeps app data). The tag's Mermaid asset build needs dependencies this checkout's install lacks, so that one Gradle task was skipped and the current Mermaid bundle reused; it only renders chat diagrams. - Stable: setup against `18443` with cert A → first-seen prompt → Trust → `gateway.tls.manual|10.0.2.2|18443 = 30d951aa…3e00`. - `adb install -r` this branch: the pin and saved manual host are unchanged. - This branch, cert A: TLS handshakes complete with no prompt. Cert B: no session handshake; changed-certificate prompt with old = cert A. **Tests** (Temurin 21.0.13, Gradle 9.7.1): `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` (87), `GatewayTlsTest` (15), `InitialOnboardingLayoutTest` (19), `FoldAwareDialogTest` (8), `OnboardingFlowLogicTest` (57): 186 tests, 0 failed. - Main (fix lines reverted): the two timeout tests fail. - New `tlsHandshakeTimeoutRecoveryCanEnterAManualPinThatIsEnforced`: probe times out → recovery → `refreshGatewayConnection(manualTlsTrust = true)` → manual prompt for the same endpoint with no second probe → accepted pin saved and used for the session. It fails with only the new branch in `beginConnect` removed. - `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck` and `pnpm native:i18n:verify` pass. The new "Enter fingerprint manually" string is in `native-source.json`; locale files follow the usual locale refresh.
Listener logs ``` # stalled handshake (main, then this branch, then Retry) stall listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 23:07:10 accepted 127.0.0.1:53751; holding without reply # main APK 23:10:25 accepted 127.0.0.1:54014; holding without reply # this branch 23:11:06 accepted 127.0.0.1:54056; holding without reply # this branch, Retry connection # this branch: Enter fingerprint manually (no new connection), then cert A / cert B stall listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 00:16:32 accepted 127.0.0.1:57444; holding without reply # probe times out -> recovery screen # Enter fingerprint manually: dialog, no new connection 00:22:06 accepted 127.0.0.1:57805; holding without reply # after Trust: session connects with the pin 00:22:06 accepted 127.0.0.1:57806; holding without reply tls listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 cert=a.pem 00:22:24 handshake ok from 57823 # pinned session handshakes, no prompt 00:22:36 handshake failed from 57846: SSLError # fingerprint probe aborts after reading the cert 00:22:37 handshake ok from 57847 tls listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 cert=b.pem 00:23:03 handshake failed from 57895: SSLError # probe only; changed-certificate prompt shown # upgrade from v2026.11.1 tls listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 cert=a.pem # stable: first-seen prompt, Trust; then install -r this branch 00:24:51 handshake ok from 58116 # this branch, pinned, no prompt tls listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 cert=b.pem 00:25:22 handshake failed from 58163: SSLError # probe only; changed-certificate prompt shown plain listener on 127.0.0.1:18444 23:12:13 answered 127.0.0.1:54186 with plain HTTP # control: manual entry opens directly ```
JVM test output ``` # main (fix reverted) GatewayBootstrapAuthTest > tlsHandshakeTimeoutShowsRetryableNetworkRecoveryWithoutCertificatePrompt FAILED kotlinx.coroutines.TimeoutCancellationException: Timed out waiting for 5000 ms GatewayTlsTest > unreachableOrTimedOutEndpointDoesNotAskForFingerprintButRetainsAnExistingPin FAILED java.lang.AssertionError: expected: but was: # manual-pin branch in beginConnect removed GatewayBootstrapAuthTest > tlsHandshakeTimeoutRecoveryCanEnterAManualPinThatIsEnforced FAILED java.lang.IllegalStateException: Expected pending gateway trust prompt 186 tests completed, 1 failed # this branch GatewayBootstrapAuthTest tests=87 failures=0 GatewayTlsTest tests=15 failures=0 FoldAwareDialogTest tests=8 failures=0 InitialOnboardingLayoutTest tests=19 failures=0 OnboardingFlowLogicTest tests=57 failures=0 BUILD SUCCESSFUL ./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck BUILD SUCCESSFUL ```
Production delta +49/-5 (including one i18n source line); test delta +66/-18. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior prompt with no state or config migration, and saved pins are untouched in both directions. Blast radius is first-time Android connections whose TLS probe times out.
