prs.title: fix(apple): dead Gateway sockets stay "connected" for up to two minutes when keepalive pongs stop
prs.body:
Closes #194219 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the iOS and macOS apps keep showing a dead Gateway connection as connected for up to two minutes when keepalive pongs stop but the TCP connection stays open. ## User Impact User impact: when the Gateway stops answering on an open connection, the apps now show Offline or Connecting about 38 to 49 seconds into the stall instead of 51 to 88 seconds, or not at all for shorter stalls, and requests stop waiting on a dead socket. Tradeoff that needs a maintainer decision: how fast the app reconnects after the network comes back now depends on how long the outage lasted. Earlier detection means the client starts the existing reconnect backoff (0.5 s doubling to 30 s) sooner. For a stall of about 125 s the PR reconnects later than main (iOS median 19.01 s vs 4.70 s). For a stall of about 175 s it reconnects sooner (iOS 8.26/2.34 s vs 29.80/25.05 s). The retry policy itself is unchanged. The PR stays Draft until that decision is made. ## Why This Change Was Made The keepalive ping already runs every 15 s with a 10 s pong deadline, but its failures were ignored, so only the 60 s tick watchdog or a later receive error retired a stalled socket. This change counts failed pings. After two failed pings with no complete incoming message in between, it retires the socket through the existing disconnect and reconnect owner. Any complete incoming message, including one that arrives between probes, resets the count, so a busy socket whose pong is queued behind data is kept. There is no new timer, connection owner or retry policy. Why the reconnect after the outage can be slower: during an outage every reconnect handshake times out after about 6 to 7 s, and each failure doubles the next wait of the existing `GatewayConnectFailureBackoff` (reset only by a successful connect, a satisfied network path change, or a local Gateway restart on Mac). Starting earlier (by 13 to 43 s in the runs below) puts the client further up that ladder when a given outage ends. For a 125 s stall that usually means the 16 s or 30 s wait. Main reaches the same wait once the outage is longer. Removing that effect means changing the shared retry policy for every disconnect reason (cap, escalation on handshake timeouts, or new reset triggers). That is outside this fix and would apply to main as it is today. Decision requested: accept the outage-length-dependent recovery time as it is (recommended), or hold this until a separate retry-policy change lands. ## Evidence All runs use a real loopback `openclaw gateway run` built from main `5577faefa9e1` (token auth, isolated state, channels, cron and Bonjour off). Each client goes through a TCP stall proxy: during a stall no bytes move in either direction and TCP stays open, and new connections are accepted and held. On restore, held bytes and connections flow again. Before is main `5577faefa9e1`; after is the same main with this PR's head `22097df51607` merged (clean merge). Each before/after pair ran at the same time on the same machine (Apple Silicon, macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2), Debug builds. **Native iOS app (Simulator, iOS 27.2):** unchanged app, onboarded with a real setup code from the Gateway. The shipped chat status label (`Gateway: ...`) was sampled about every 0.3 s. Times are from the stall start. | Stall | Build | Label leaves Connected | Back to Connected after restore | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 125 s | main | 57.92, 51.20, 61.11 s | 4.70, 0.41, 7.82 s (median 4.70) | | 125 s | PR | 42.66, 37.56, 46.73 s | 19.01, 13.08, 23.51 s (median 19.01) | | 175 s | main | 58.28, 52.00 s | 29.80, 25.05 s | | 175 s | PR | 44.48, 38.92 s | 8.26, 2.34 s | **Shipped `GatewayChannelActor` on macOS (URLSession WebSocket, production timers, no network path updates):** three stall phases per row (35, 41 and 47 s after hello). Actual stall lengths drift a few seconds under load (70.66 to 182.65 s). | Stall | Build | Socket retired after | Detector | Connected after restore | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ~70 s | main | not before restore (stayed connected) | none | 0.66, 0.63, 0.53 s | | ~70 s | PR | 47.00, 41.93, 48.67 s | keepalive | 0.02, 0.02, 4.26 s | | ~125 s | main | 88.01, 84.07, 74.24 s | tick watchdog | 2.16, 0.03, 6.36 s | | ~125 s | PR | 47.00, 41.93, 48.68 s | keepalive | 15.84, 11.09, 17.42 s | | ~175 s | main | 88.01, 84.08, 74.25 s | tick watchdog | 7.38, 7.37, 0.03 s | | ~175 s | PR | 45.97, 41.42, 48.67 s | keepalive | 7.60, 0.02, 7.15 s | These are the same effect as the native macOS comparison below (Connected after 17.23/17.28 s vs 1.43/1.62 s for 125 s stalls). With three runs per row, only individual values and medians are reported.
Example: PR, 125 s stall, reconnect ladder during the outage ``` STALL_PROOF t= 50.08s stall start STALL_PROOF t= 98.76s disconnect generation=1 reason=gateway socket unresponsive to keepalive pings STALL_PROOF t= 105.47s disconnect generation=2 reason=connect failed: ... (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.) STALL_PROOF t= 112.61s disconnect generation=3 reason=connect failed: ... (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.) STALL_PROOF t= 120.75s disconnect generation=4 reason=connect failed: ... (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.) STALL_PROOF t= 131.33s disconnect generation=5 reason=connect failed: ... (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.) STALL_PROOF t= 145.78s disconnect generation=6 reason=connect failed: ... (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.) STALL_PROOF t= 168.78s disconnect generation=7 reason=connect failed: ... (NSURLErrorDomain error -1001.) STALL_PROOF t= 183.32s restore STALL_PROOF t= 200.74s hello generation=8 ``` Example: main, 175 s stall, iOS status label ``` STALL_UI_PROOF t= 0.00s stall STALL_UI_PROOF t= 58.28s main, Voice off. Gateway: Offline STALL_UI_PROOF t= 59.58s main, Voice off. Gateway: Connecting STALL_UI_PROOF t= 65.31s main, Voice off. Gateway: Attention STALL_UI_PROOF t= 175.24s restore STALL_UI_PROOF t= 205.04s main, Voice off. Gateway: Connected ```
**Focused tests on the head merged with current main:** `swift test --filter GatewayNetworkPathRecoveryTests` passed 11/11. The extended existing test fails on the original production code and passes with the repair. SwiftFormat 0.63.1 (`config/swiftformat`, lint mode) reports 0/2 files needing changes, and SwiftLint 0.65.1 reports 0 violations in `GatewayChannel.swift`. **Native recordings (iOS and macOS, earlier comparison on main `020ec24568b1` and this head):** complete recordings at original speed, with no application-state, protocol-response or style injection. These MP4s retain every original compressed video packet and its presentation/decode timestamp; only the container and metadata changed. Synthetic task data, public model labels and local test addresses are visible. | Run | Main | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | iOS, two 70-second stalls | First replacement TCP at 60.77/42.13s; second run identified the tick watchdog | First replacement at 39.47/43.54s; first run used tick, second explicitly used keepalive at 43.02s | | macOS native Quick Chat, two 125-second stalls | Native tick retirement at 100.32/86.46s | Keepalive retirement at 42.32s, then tick retirement at 42.33s | | macOS after traffic resumed | Connected after 1.43/1.62s | Connected after 17.23/17.28s | | Short iOS interruption | Historical control retained | 28 seconds: original connections retained; ordinary message subsequently completed and returned READY | Both Mac runs retained the saved conversation and draft. Later ordinary typing confirmed the draft remained editable. Example at 50 seconds in the iOS recordings: main still shows Online; this PR shows Connecting. iOS, main: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af847cd8-3e51-4529-a730-ca8aca93cd4f iOS, this PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7aa1ceea-e0f2-4d8e-922d-cd458c4def81 iOS, short interruption and a normal message afterward: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a1ccc82-a46e-4d28-b378-ab825aeb5360 macOS, two full stall/recovery cycles, main: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ffcfa7b-b509-425b-baa4-b7b93578257d macOS, two full stall/recovery cycles, this PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f7b92d5-8267-45a7-a663-3007a18f90c1
Source identities and limits - Stall matrix: Gateway and before build at main `5577faefa9e12645f716f6c3971ecf57bae64b5f`; after build is that main with `22097df51607911d67cf51d9e89c1b72847f464a` merged. - Stall matrix iOS builds: the Watch companion app was left out of the proof builds of both trees the same way, because its voice library needs a Rust toolchain that was not available. The iPhone app and its Gateway connection are unchanged. - The stall proxy holds bytes rather than dropping them, so a handshake that is in flight when the network returns completes at once. A packet-dropping network can add TCP retransmit delay on top of the backoff wait. - The native macOS app was not rerun for the stall matrix; the macOS rows above come from the shipped channel library and from the earlier native Mac recordings. - Earlier native comparison: main `020ec24568b12416bf4315732532bae8762101aa`; this PR `22097df51607911d67cf51d9e89c1b72847f464a`, tested tree `d0275349671c199f2ca69916de9ef76a143ea723`; iOS 27.2 Simulator; native macOS 26.6.2 guest; Xcode 27.2. The Gateway stayed pinned at `04cc8c1e4328b873a3a5791eeecf5d4d213c34db`. The corrected Mac startup also preloaded a hidden dashboard socket, excluded from detector attribution. One Mac recording failed to finalize and an iOS repeat had timestamp irregularities; their raw evidence is retained, not presented as clean proof. - Complete incoming messages are covered. Arbitrarily slow partial-frame or upload safety is not proven; an older matched upload control failed on both main and this PR, so it does not establish a new regression. - Focused tests use fake transports and a controlled clock. Physical weak-cellular conditions were not tested.

prs.title: fix: honor the approved 2026.9.37 performance exemption
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the frozen 2026.9.37 qualification workflow cannot honor the approved performance exception before launching another CPU workload.

Related: #194727 (merged on main first).

## User Impact

Release preparation can perform fresh qualification with performance explicitly recorded as **waived-not-run**. Every other selected check and stable soak remains mandatory. No runtime code, dependencies, version, runner routing, or published artifacts change. This does not authorize publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dallin Romney approved the performance exception and new candidate/harness on November 7, 2026. The original failed run `42361846301/1`, its source parent, archive and receipt digests remain authenticated historical support only—not measurements of the new candidate. Wrong or missing evidence fails closed.

## Evidence

- Initial backport: 737 tests passed across 11 suites, including producer/source-acquisition closure consumers; final CLI suite replay: 13 passed.

prs.title: fix(macos): use recognition language for Talk pause timing
prs.body:
Closes #190154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS Talk submitting Japanese speech too soon, or delaying English turns, when Talk's recognition language differs from Voice Wake's language.

## User Impact

Native Talk applies its existing two-second CJK minimum pause to the language actually selected by Apple Speech, including fallback from an unsupported language. Longer configured pauses remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native recognition startup owns both the selected recognizer and its pause window. Configuration no longer infers recognition timing from Voice Wake. Realtime-to-native fallback uses the same configuration and recognition path.

## Evidence

### Full signed-app turns through a real Gateway, agent, and model

On November 2, 2026, the signed production macOS app completed real microphone turns on a Mac Studio through a separate real Gateway, isolated agent/workspace, and existing local model via the vLLM-compatible provider. These were actual `OpenClaw` main-executable launches, not XCTest entry points. Recognition, native lifecycle, Gateway submission, model inference, and system playback were live. The launcher only selected test configuration and started/stopped the app; it supplied no recognition, transport, model, or playback mocks.

The app and its genuinely staged matching runtime were built from `aaecc05b7d9375eeccf6f4e91c14b72ac833a25b`, version 2026.10.9, and signed through the normal macOS signing script. Strict bundle verification passed. Current head `88f4d2b2f57` changes only the tests from that production build; the production source is identical. The separate Gateway was release 2026.10.9, commit `8b18b55`.

| Apple recognition | Voice Wake | Actual startup path | Gateway/model outcome | Playback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en-US | ko-KR | Native | Recognized `Hello`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |
| ja-JP | en-US | Native | Recognized `こんにちは`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |
| ja-JP | en-US | Realtime opted in, incompatible Gateway bootstrap configuration, native fallback | Recognized `こんにちは`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |

Sanitized log excerpts below use ET. Request/device identifiers, model identity, endpoints, and credentials are omitted. Transcript checks used only the requested synthetic greeting and its associated assistant reply.

```text
English, native:
15:34:37.967 talk.runtime speechLocale=en-US silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=false
15:34:44.654 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:34:49.714 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:34:50.132 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:34:50.448 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=46
15:34:54.879 talk.tts talk system voice done

Japanese recognition, native:
15:40:40.230 talk.runtime speechLocale=ja-JP silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=false
15:40:50.438 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:40:53.541 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:40:54.158 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:40:54.461 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=51
15:40:58.894 talk.tts talk system voice done

Japanese recognition after actual fallback:
15:51:16.229 talk.runtime speechLocale=ja-JP silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=true
15:51:16.229 talk macOS realtime relay opted in but Gateway tuple is incompatible:
                 mode=missing transport=missing brain=missing; using native fallback
15:51:16.238 talk realtime unavailable; using native fallback:
                 Gateway realtime Talk configuration changed before startup
15:51:28.107 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:51:31.820 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:51:32.244 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:51:32.666 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=46
15:51:37.103 talk.tts talk system voice done
```

The fallback is a real app transition after the real Gateway's native-only configuration lacks a compatible realtime tuple. No exception or bootstrap dependency was injected in this full-app run. This does not claim a live realtime-provider outage or reconnection test. The complete full-app turns establish product flow; exact silence duration was not instrumented in these runs. These captures establish turn completion, not normal application shutdown; the fallback fixture was forcibly stopped after its audible reply and TTS completion.

For audible Japanese-recognition checks, the isolated agent was instructed to answer in English while recognition stayed ja-JP and Voice Wake stayed en-US. An earlier run produced a Japanese model reply and logged system playback completion, but the user heard no speech. That result is not counted as audible proof. The unchanged macOS system-playback path uses Voice Wake's language when the response has no explicit language directive; Japanese-language playback remains outside this timing repair. Realtime opt-in in the final fallback run is confirmed by the actual app log.

The Gateway used isolated state, synthetic conversations, disabled tools/discovery, and a separate loopback port. Only the existing local-model provider credential was used with explicit permission. No normal operator Gateway or normal app profile was modified. Raw microphone audio, private configuration, credentials, device identifiers, non-public endpoints, and unrelated captured input are not published.

### Runtime regression replacing the helper table

The helper-composition table is removed. `TalkModeRuntimeNativeLocaleProofTests` applies real configuration, enters actual `startRecognition`, and observes the selected Apple recognizer and applied pause window. Identical test source was compiled against base `c8f87b2e5163870671510659745f4167239ff50e` and the fix.

| Runtime startup | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ja-JP recognition, en-US Voice Wake, 700 ms configured | Fails: 0.7 s, expected 2.0 s | Pass: 2.0 s |
| en-US recognition, ko-KR Voice Wake, 700 ms configured | Fails: 2.0 s, expected 0.7 s | Pass: 0.7 s |

The fixed run passes both argument cases in 0.035 seconds with no issues. The base run reports exactly the two expected window assertion failures. Separately, 50 current tests in `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests`, `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, and `TalkModeRuntimeReplyTests` pass in 1.816 seconds.

The opt-in startup regression requires `OPENCLAW_TALK_NATIVE_SETUP_PROOF=1`, available Apple Speech services, and no usable input device. It ran in the disposable macOS guest with a process-only audio-service denial. It reads the runtime's private recognizer and applied window through reflection, so private field renames require updating the test. Unused playback cleanup is stubbed; recognition startup and cleanup are real. This tests the applied startup state before missing-input rejection, not microphone timing or full-app completion. The real microphone runs above cover the latter boundary separately.

### Earlier isolated microphone timing measurements

At the same production source `aaecc05b7d93`, signed native-capture test-app runs exercised real Apple recognition, silence monitoring, finalization, and submission to an in-memory Gateway. These measurements exclude agent/model execution and playback; they are supplementary timing evidence, not the full-product proof above.

| Recognition | Voice Wake | Startup | Configured effective pause | Observed last-activity-to-submission |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| en-US | ko-KR | Native | 0.7 s | 1.298 s |
| ja-JP | en-US | Native | 2.0 s | 2.483 s |
| ja-JP | en-US | Injected realtime-startup failure to native | 2.0 s | 2.508 s |

Observed submission time includes recognition shutdown and dispatch overhead. Each measured run captured real speech, received a nonempty Apple transcription, submitted it, exited 0, and completed its Swift Testing event stream without issues or skips. The injected failure applies only to this earlier harness row.

### Other checks and review

- The native app and test bundle compile with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --disable-automatic-resolution`.
- The unchanged shared `OpenClawKitTests/TalkConfigParsingTests.swift` also passed: 11 tests in 0.002 seconds in the guest. Its exact source was temporarily compiled into the native test bundle and filtered by suite name; this was not a separate shared-package `swift test` invocation.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 pass for the changed test files. `git diff --check` passes. The earlier full lint found two inherited file-length violations in unchanged DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; no claim is made that those were repaired.
- A fresh independent Codex source review of the runtime regression replacement found no actionable likely or high-impact findings. The opt-in environment and reflection limitations above remain explicit. This is source review, not maintainer approval or proof of a ClawSweeper rating.

AI-assisted. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the mismatch.

prs.title: fix(mac): avoid duplicate Codex sessions with a local Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #130113

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users connected to their own local Gateway would see the same Codex sessions twice: once under the Gateway-local catalog and once under the paired Mac app node.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native manifest already omits session catalogs in local mode, but the node-host worker manifest added them back during capability union. This change applies the same local-mode boundary to the worker manifest while leaving remote-mode catalogs and unrelated worker capabilities unchanged.

## User Impact

The Codex picker presents one catalog for the local Mac instead of duplicating every session under two same-host entries. Remote Gateways can still discover and invoke the Mac's Codex and Claude catalogs through the app node.

## Evidence

Current public head is `3bfccab8247524aaddf1476482ffb11b62fd8027` (tree `aeb770de0f224d8dd00eee4ec46e69846192d0dd`). This merge preserves `68875e5adb581891922e5e15ad62bfe1ed3e8673` and integrates main `0c4cf7fea1d4b31c0c79ab10bbd794b4f224123f`. GitHub blob identities confirm that all three PR-owned Swift files are unchanged from `68875e5`. This body refresh changes no source.

**Current-head automation:** [canonical CI run 40200395021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40200395021) and its CI gate succeeded for head `3bfccab8247524aaddf1476482ffb11b62fd8027`. This run contains 5 successful and 39 skipped jobs. Both macOS Swift phases and the iOS build phase were skipped. [macOS and shared Periphery run 40200394886](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40200394886) completed all six selected jobs successfully, including both shared-kit producers and the intersection. These results establish automation at this head, not complete-app catalog behavior or focused native test execution. Historical native observations and prior-head reviews below retain their original revision boundaries.

**Historical integration at `68875e5`:** The then-current public head was `68875e5adb581891922e5e15ad62bfe1ed3e8673` (tree `8e936aa88e1c58ddfaac0b193a9ed21e5b59a474`). The contributor's merge preserves prior head `0048c0b6abab56334a0ea0591c6f4a4bd41ec870` and integrates `main` at `de55ea305cbd77d431ff99063e779876c1e3f4d1`. The three PR-owned Swift files are unchanged by that merge; this evidence update does not push source changes.

**Historical automation at `68875e5`:** [canonical CI run 40172973914](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40172973914) and its CI gate succeeded. The macOS Swift test lanes and iOS build/test lanes in that run were skipped, not executed passes. The [shared Periphery run 40172973893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40172973893) is not green: the macOS shared-kit scan passed, but the [iOS producer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40172973893/job/121107716759) failed uploading its artifact with `ENOTFOUND` after logging `TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED`; the [intersection job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40172973893/job/121110643664) then failed because `shared-periphery-ios-40172973893-1` was absent. This is an artifact-transport failure, not a demonstrated catalog regression. It does not establish a passing iOS scan or intersection. The observed check rollup was 24 passed, 2 failed, and 43 skipped/neutral, with no pending checks. No rerun or replacement dispatch was made.

**Resolved stale finding:** the [ClawSweeper comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130115#issuecomment-5426086316) now marks its review of `68875e5adb581891922e5e15ad62bfe1ed3e8673` stale against current head `3bfccab8247524aaddf1476482ffb11b62fd8027`. Its earlier missing-member allegation was against obsolete head `a1f0422b670f9149000ef66f439f76b26e9aa11a`. Contributor commit [c6ceb5b726b1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c6ceb5b726b1f5a5935ad6ddff9bb677089807d6) removed both references to the retired `MacNodeClaudeSessionCatalogContract.capability` member, using the maintained Anthropic capability literal `claude-sessions` in the filter and fixture. Current source retains that correction; restoring the retired member is unnecessary. This resolves that specific source allegation, not the remaining runtime-proof requirement.

The [October 22 source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130115#pullrequestreview-5613597785) at `0048c0b6abab56334a0ea0591c6f4a4bd41ec870` found no actionable issue and requested no further author changes. It is prior-head source-review evidence, not a current-head native test result or final maintainer product/design approval.

**Remaining proof gap:** no inspectable current-head complete-app Local/Remote manifest and `sessions.catalog.list` output is supplied. Still needed: one same-machine catalog per provider in Local mode, distinct remote hosts/source homes preserved, and usable remote-mode list/read operations for Codex and Claude. Focused native tests and a meaningful red control also remain unrun on this head. Source inspection and Periphery do not replace those checks.

The earlier QA dispatch for commit `98ae2529a1293116d71e3b3664fd8d73353deee2` was rejected with HTTP 422 (Actions disabled), creating no run. That refusal was not retried, and no workflow or permission change is claimed.

Prior-head automation only: [CI 38773755445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38773755445), [shared Periphery 38773755306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38773755306), and [macOS Periphery 38773755463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38773755463) succeeded at `0048c0b6abab56334a0ea0591c6f4a4bd41ec870`; their native test lanes were skipped. They are not validation of the new integrated head.

Historical evidence, not proof of this integrated head:

- [Signed-app/local-Gateway observation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130115#issuecomment-5428429164) used PR-owned blobs matching `601c10b058a7478d9981c01ca7b4d3ba5418ed48`.
- [28/28 worker tests and source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130115#issuecomment-5460405469) were reported at `74ef79564b12599e460b7ef9c1f33881140649a4`.
- The previously listed 39/39 coordinator tests, failed-first regression and formatting checks lack a verified revision in this evidence update. They are not claimed as current-candidate validation.
- [Colton-Harris's independent reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130115#issuecomment-5549185535) found 19 Claude and 33 Codex duplicates and verified a separate Gateway-side workaround. As the contributor stated, this does not validate this PR's Swift patch.

prs.title: fix: keep sent media visible in native chat history
prs.body:
Closes #154075

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sent photos, videos, and voice notes disappearing from native chat when canonical Gateway history replaces the local outgoing message. Canonical document/file attachments also remain visible as filename rows.

## User Impact

Sent images remain visible and open in image preview; sent videos/audio remain playable and survive reloading the same chat. Image frames also respect the decoded aspect ratio, removing oversized side margins around portrait and square photos without cropping. This is independent of the composer-freeze repair in #154082.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the Gateway’s persisted inbound-media references and load playable media through the existing authenticated, bounded resource route, including the Gateway playback-conversion/preparing contract. Reuse native image rendering and retain references—not image bytes—in transcript cache. Both iOS and macOS transport adapters are covered; no Gateway storage change.

## Evidence

### Video and other formats — September 21 follow-up

**Before — Photos MOV → Send → canonical reply, video disappears (119.3 seconds, real speed):**

[Watch before recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media/before.mp4)

**After — Photos MOV → Send → canonical reply → actual playback → relaunch/reopen the exact same chat (76.1 seconds, real speed):**

[Watch after recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media/after.mp4)

![Before: native chat loses the sent video after the reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media/before.png)

![After: native chat retains the sent video and playable preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media/after.png)

[Playback screenshot: fixture timecode advances to 1.333 seconds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media/playing.png) · [Same conversation after relaunch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media/reloaded.png)

- **Native MOV test passed: 63.166 seconds. Native MP4 test passed: 65.718 seconds.** Both use the real Photos picker, send to a real isolated Gateway, await the canonical reply, activate the actual native player, capture the selected session’s stable identifier, relaunch, reopen that exact session, and verify exactly one playable video. Inspected playback screenshots show the test clip’s timecode advancing, not merely a play icon disappearing. Gateway inbound files independently confirm MOV and MP4 containers.
- **61 focused tests pass:** 20 attachment staging/send/rejection XCTest tests plus 41 Swift Testing tests across media/history, source resources, URL validation, and playback retries. Final Swift Testing execution: 0.007 seconds; attachment XCTest execution under one second. Added format matrix covers MOV, MP4, M4A, MP3, WAV, JPEG, PNG, HEIC, GIF, PDF, text, and opaque files through canonical decode/cache round-trip. New metadata regression failed on the prior implementation before the fix. This matrix is not a claim of native playback for every codec.
- **Format scope:** native import remains image/video plus recorded voice notes; unsupported imported audio/documents still reject explicitly. Canonical documents retain filename rows, not a new document viewer. Non-native audio/video requests existing Gateway playback conversion; HTTP 202 feeds the existing bounded preparing/retry UI. Media-family/size validation, authenticated requests, route-retirement checks, duplicate prevention, and reference-only caching remain enforced.
- **Build/review:** iOS native test build and signed physical-device Debug build pass, pinned SwiftFormat/SwiftLint pass, macOS product build passes (130.65 seconds), diff check passes. Codex review against `origin/main` is clean after addressing its playback-conversion finding. The first native after-run failed on a test selector: iOS exposes the play button identifier as `play.circle.fill` and labels it with the filename; the test now uses the observed identifier. That failed run is not counted as a product regression or a passing proof.
- **Environment/provenance:** Xcode 27 beta; task-only iPhone 16 simulator on iOS 27. Before app embedded SHA `f62c407778746f4654c3320842faa9e9ead7dd12`; after source `0c9cfe0229060f1047e8b79df0e4e38a6463ae68`. Both use the retained real isolated Gateway build `df3fccbf6662705524abb76616b8bc42fc912d5f`, with synthetic H264/AAC clips and a local synthetic model endpoint. No production conversation traffic or paid model calls. Recordings are full-speed screen captures, re-encoded at 720px for delivery with no time compression; original recordings retained. Screenshots are unmodified product captures, personally inspected and attached in the originating chat.
- **Phone:** installed main `758ac0b6a143` plus the complete updated PR in the existing Debug bundle, preserving app data and the separate App Store app. Signature/get-task-allow verified. Physical-phone launch was blocked by its locked screen; native send/play/relaunch validation above ran on the simulator, not the phone.
- [Download proof files](https://github.com/Solvely-Colin/openclaw/tree/9e9d4d1994ed24565e90eab6dd83204495a2b68a/proof/pr-154094/media). Proof-only branch; no binary evidence added to the PR code diff. CI for the new push remains separate from the completed local validation.

### Original photo proof

**Before — add photo, send, image disappears after reply (71.6s, real speed):**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e461932a-73e3-4d36-9e51-d7d120e39ec9

**After — add photo, send, image remains, open native preview (59.1s, real speed):**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77ff9a8e-67b5-441f-875e-7543a8a26695

![Before: sent image missing after canonical reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7b8c4e3-099e-49ce-8a71-7df02ce490aa)

![After: sent image remains visible after canonical reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57554275-62f7-4148-a682-25526401bd20)


- Before: real isolated Gateway receives the photo, but the native user bubble loses it after the reply; canonical-history decoding regression fails.
- After: 28 focused media/cache/resource tests pass.
- Native connected test after review fix: **1 passed, exit 0, 78.260s** (105.577s test-operation wall time). Real photo picker, Send, canonical reply, visible image, and native preview verified. The test captures the selected conversation’s stable session-key accessibility identifier, relaunches, explicitly reopens that exact conversation, and verifies its expected reply and exactly one photo. The earlier video predates this correction; same-session reload is now covered by the updated native test and inspected result-bundle screenshot. This remains an opt-in isolated-Gateway test, not a default per-PR live test.
- Codex review after lint repairs: **scoped-clean through P3**. Native build, pinned SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, and diff check pass.

Test traffic uses a task-owned simulator, an isolated real Gateway, and a local synthetic model endpoint. No production conversations or paid model calls.

Environment: Xcode 27 (27A5209h), iPhone 16 simulator, iOS 27.0 (24A5370g), local synthetic 640×480 PNG staged as JPEG. Before: composer-repaired base480fa421af8 / build97405, without this image fix. After: basef62c4077787 / build97423 plus this patch. Raw native videos, logs, and xcresult retained locally. macOS transport is implemented and covered by shared tests; native macOS proportional-frame visual proof is included below. Both fixes were subsequently installed together in place on a physical iPhone (Debug build 97427), preserving app data; the photo-width follow-up was rebuilt, installed, and launched successfully.

## Physical-phone sizing follow-up

- The existing 320-point height cap could leave a portrait image inside a wider frame. Cap width by the decoded image aspect ratio as well, preserving the full photo and the available chat width.
- Native SwiftUI rendering check: portrait container **360×320 → 240×320**. Portrait, landscape, and square images passed at both 360- and 180-point available widths (six cases); no overflow or aspect-ratio distortion. This is an isolated layout check, not product screenshot proof.
- Fresh Codex review against refreshed `origin/main` (`5a2b1233186`) found no actionable defects.
- Native iOS build, signature verification, pinned formatter, and diff check passed. The changed source file matches the version installed on the phone.
- Colin validated the updated layout on his physical iPhone and confirmed: “looks good on phone.”
- The original videos/stills above predate this sizing follow-up. Fresh native product screenshots below now cover the proportional-frame change.


### Proportional-frame product screenshots

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent stale native dashboard builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native macOS Control UI can retain an older build in persistent WebKit service-worker and HTTP caches. After the gateway updates, the page sends an old `clientBuild` and the healthy gateway rejects the handshake with `control-ui-build-mismatch`, leaving the desktop app disconnected.

## User Impact

macOS dashboard recovery preserves normal desktop navigation and unrelated service workers; this follow-up changes only the regression-test setup, with no new user-visible behavior or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistent native caches can keep the dashboard disconnected after a Gateway update. The dedicated cache-policy capability repairs that path without enabling embed layout. The integrated-head test repair follows the current asset-helper contract rather than restoring a removed production API.

## Summary

- advertise a dedicated document-start macOS Control UI cache-policy capability without enabling native-embed layout
- unregister only an owned Control UI worker, preserving unrelated same-origin registrations
- report worker lookup, unregister rejection, and unsuccessful retirement diagnostics
- make macOS dashboard loads bypass WebKit local HTTP cache
- preserve service-worker-backed Web Push behavior for non-macOS native hosts

## Evidence

### Current-head test repair — 2026-10-22

Tested/published head: `6b70c22f1a00d3998068c5814e2d002c0eb633e6` (parent: `2be78e6fc5214edc1d51f3c5b334b9e6db19fcd5`). Addresses [the current-head custom-base finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148435#issuecomment-5668643704).

The only source change in this follow-up is the existing custom-base worker test. It establishes `/apps/openclaw/chat` through browser history, temporarily removes both window and document base-path fixtures so the real helper infers the mount, and restores the original URL, history state, property descriptor, and document attribute in `finally`. It calls the current one-argument API and retains the `true` ownership assertion for `/apps/openclaw/sw.js?v=old-build`. No production API, cache behavior, assertion baseline, or mocks were changed.

Validation used Node `24.22.1`, pinned pnpm `12.15.0` through Corepack, and an isolated worktree with its own `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; the lockfile passed all supply-chain policies. Global runtime defaults and shared dependency installs were not changed.

- **Before editing**, the unchanged parent reproduced the reported failure: `pnpm --dir ui test --run src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts src/app/public-assets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **23 passed, 1 failed**, with `expected false to be true` in the custom-base ownership test.
- The test-inclusive UI-app typecheck also reproduced **TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2** at the parent. The production UI typecheck passed at that parent because it excludes test files.
- **After the fix**, the same two-suite command — **24 passed, 0 failed** across 2 files; Vitest duration **1.43 seconds**. Hosted CI timing is not yet available for this head.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/ui.tsbuildinfo` — **passed** (production UI scope, equivalent to `pnpm tsgo:ui`).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-app.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/ui-app-tests.tsbuildinfo` — **passed**, including the affected test callers.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.ui.json ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `node node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts --base 2be78e6fc5214edc1d51f3c5b334b9e6db19fcd5` — **passed** (2,470 files, 5,652 grandfathered assertions; no baseline change).
- `git diff --check 2be78e6fc5214edc1d51f3c5b334b9e6db19fcd5..HEAD` — **passed**.

**Review / proof gaps:** Fresh local AutoReview was attempted through its restricted OpenClaw engine because Codex CLI is unavailable. It returned `reviewer_unavailable`, `engine_failed`, reviewer exit `1`, with no report or verdict. This is not a clean independent-review result. Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper re-review remain pending; this repair does not claim green hosted UI/macOS CI. No new native-app build, retained-profile recovery run, screenshot, production-bundle E2E, or dead-export scan was performed for this test-only follow-up.

### Historical validation — fdd88b27 (not current-head proof)

The results below are retained from the earlier candidate and have not been rerun or relabeled as proof of the integrated/repaired head.

Reviewed head: `fdd88b27e4c9be692a36bcb791e1238c58c92901`

- `pnpm --dir ui test --run src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts src/app/public-assets.test.ts src/app/app-host-refresh-control-ui.test.ts src/app/service-worker-refresh.runtime.test.ts` — 44 passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/native-nav-sidebar-toggle.e2e.test.ts -t 'preserves the desktop shell|retires an owned worker'` — 2 passed, 19 skipped by filter; a fresh production Control UI bundle was built from the reviewed head.
  - The shell scenario confirms the document-start macOS capabilities preserve `.shell-nav`, `openclaw-app-topbar`, and `openclaw-macos-titlebar-controls`.
  - The persisted-worker scenario serves the production bundle's real `sw.js?v=stale-profile`, retains that registration across the initial document, injects the native capability at document start for the reloaded document, confirms the capability survived reload, and observes zero owned Control UI registrations afterward.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` — passed.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` — passed; all three Knip export scans reported zero entries.
- `pnpm check:assertion-safety --base origin/main` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/main.ts ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.ts ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts ui/src/e2e/native-nav.test-support.ts ui/src/e2e/native-nav-sidebar-toggle.e2e.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/main.ts ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.ts ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts ui/src/e2e/native-nav.test-support.ts ui/src/e2e/native-nav-sidebar-toggle.e2e.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Exact-head CI: `macos-swift (tests)` passed; all 13 UI E2E shards passed; all 3 UI test shards passed. The aggregate gate is red only because five unrelated compact Node shards failed.

### Historical candidate-built macOS retained-profile proof — fdd88b27

The reviewed `fdd88b27e4c9be692a36bcb791e1238c58c92901` checkout was compiled into the `OpenClaw` SwiftPM product (`Build complete! (83.97 sec)`) and assembled with the same exact-head Control UI assets into an ad-hoc-signed proof app. `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed. The proof used bundle id `local.openclaw.native-proof`, an isolated state directory, an isolated config, and an isolated Gateway on `127.0.0.1:19943`; it did not read or mutate the operator Gateway profile.

The same persistent WebKit profile was first loaded with the pre-fix production Control UI from `e0b182236cd4dc394c5f3b77152fa94b29e7c809`. Immediately before launching the candidate app, WebKit's service-worker registration database reported:

```text
scopeURL = /
scriptURL = http://127.0.0.1:19943/sw.js?v=2026.9.4-e0b182236cd4-2026-09-14T21-25-13.000Z
```

The exact-head Gateway rejected that retained page as expected:

```text
clientBuild=2026.9.4-e0b182236cd4-2026-09-14T21-25-13.000Z
gatewayBuild=2026.9.4-fdd88b27e4c9-2026-09-16T05-02-45.000Z
reason=protocol mismatch: Control UI updated; reload this page to continue
```

Without deleting or moving any WebKit profile data, the candidate app then opened the dashboard through `DashboardWindowController`. Unified WebKit logging recorded the changed cleanup path executing:

```text
ServiceWorkerContainer::unregisterRegistration: Unregistering service worker.
```

The isolated Gateway then accepted the recovered page from the same native window:

```text
client=openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.4
build=2026.9.4-fdd88b27e4c9-2026-09-16T05-02-45.000Z
```

The screenshot below is that candidate-built macOS window. The native titlebar controls and `THIS MAC` settings section establish that this is the macOS host path; the About page visibly reports the reviewed commit and a connected Gateway.

![Exact-head candidate app recovered the retained stale WebKit profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/fc2356740f0df4d1deae3c4006a5dbe39b285587/.github/pr-evidence/148435/exact-head-retained-profile-recovery.png)

## Original incident evidence

- Live gateway health was `200 {"ok":true,"status":"live"}` while the app log repeatedly recorded `clientBuild=2026.9.4-cd1a208089ef` versus `gatewayBuild=2026.9.4-b0638604941d-2026-09-14T02-14-29.000Z` and `cause:"control-ui-build-mismatch"`.
- The native WebKit profile contained persisted `CacheStorage` and `ServiceWorkers` data for the local gateway origin.
- Moving only the app's Control UI/network cache directories to timestamped backups and restarting recovered the desktop UI; the gateway then served normal requests and the UI showed the connected Local Gateway state.

## Review follow-up

- The macOS document-start script sets `__OPENCLAW_NATIVE_CONTROL_UI_CACHE_POLICY__ = 'reload'` and leaves `__OPENCLAW_NATIVE_EMBED__` unset, preserving the normal desktop shell.
- Worker cleanup is restricted to the inferred Control UI base path and reports registration lookup failures, unregister rejections, and `unregister() === false` results.
- The retirement E2E skips null worker slots before parsing `scriptURL`.
- Native capabilities are installed with `addInitScript`, survive the tested reload boundary, and are asserted before worker-retirement success is accepted.
- The cache-policy helper is internal rather than an unused production export; underscored host globals use lint-safe typed bracket access; the reduced assertion baseline is recorded.

prs.title: fix: saved Gateway opens can fail when the Gateways menu closes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses a source-identified race where closing the Gateways menu can disconnect a saved Gateway while its first window is still opening.

## User Impact and Solution

The existing connection fleet owns consumer lifetime. Dashboard configuration acquires demand before native preflight and transfers it to the window; native chat retains demand while opening and in its window record. Hidden windows remain consumers. Close/replacement releases demand. Menu-private opening-task bookkeeping is removed. Explicit credential retirement, profile removal, and fleet shutdown remain unconditional; authentication, TLS, origin, and account-storage policy are unchanged.

## Readiness — November 7

**Product/design recommendation: retain this focused fleet-demand repair.** Fresh independent source review found no proven P0–P2 defect, and no unresolved product-direction decision was identified within this scope.

**Engineering validation, CI, and source publication are not complete.** The existing PR remains open at `fbb30e598cdad1e284058798bc6c6b5eaf80f2e5`. A successor task recovered candidate `e5c39a3b798cb557a779672909006592e6def968`, preserving the PR head and its previously integrated main parent `8e8d5b052457c221a973a2fe66b25f9f08e7302b`. The candidate includes the prior one-line test-formatting correction, not a new behavioral repair. It is preserved locally and has not been pushed to this PR. No additional main integration was performed merely because main advanced.

## Evidence

- **Fresh candidate source review:** local OpenClaw Auto Review, Codex engine, completed the range `8e8d5b052457c221a973a2fe66b25f9f08e7302b..e5c39a3b798cb557a779672909006592e6def968`, through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. Full affected owners and selected sibling lifetime tests were supplied as committed source context. A separate independent lifecycle pass reached the same result and inspected interaction with main snapshot `dd11a9c2da9850f7dc091b5f011b66071b98ed4d`. These are source reviews, not native behavior proof; project code was not executed.
- **Candidate integrity:** contributor ancestry is preserved; `git diff --check` passes. The review checkout and designated task branch have identical candidate commit and tree. Simplification retains one fleet owner and removes menu-private pending-open tracking; production delta remains +86/-54 lines, with 165 regression-test lines.
- **Reusable native evidence on the existing remote head:** the [disposable macOS job](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39361552642/job/118428661548) succeeded. Its [immutable workflow](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/commit/0df832829e6ed9569fe3d9fdbe0d0c95df418135) independently checks out and asserts upstream `fbb30e598cdad1e284058798bc6c6b5eaf80f2e5`, without persisted checkout credentials. The [validation report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177970#issuecomment-6282432918) records the native app/test build and **80 tests in seven suites**. The retained job log confirms that test result and the lifecycle suite. This evidence does not cover the merged local candidate or establish a pristine-base failure.
- Historical pinned SwiftFormat passed. SwiftLint's wrapper exited zero with one DashboardManager file-length advisory; this was not zero-violation lint. Syntax parsing is not behavior proof.
- **Outstanding exact-remote-head CI findings:** the [macOS producer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39366649706/job/118445104579) reported `stricter(_:_:)`; the [shared intersection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39366649706/job/118449364907) reported `replaceSocketCredentials(_:expectedToken:)` and `bindNull(at:)`. The local candidate no longer declares `stricter` or `bindNull`, but retains the credential-store API. Neither failed gate is claimed green without a new scan.

## Remaining Validation and Publication Gaps

- Qualify a regression red on the pristine base and green on the candidate. Existing harness tests depend on the new constructor seams; baseline compilation failure is not red proof.

prs.title: fix(ios): discard stale wake commands after chat or Gateway changes
prs.body:
Related: #165515 (focused-chat routing; intentionally unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

Buffered Voice Wake recognition can outlive a chat, agent, or Gateway change and create another command after the previous command was canceled.

## User Impact

Destination changes discard pending commands and buffered results from the old capture; fresh listening resumes through existing admission gates. **Ready for review and CI; current native validation remains outstanding—not merge-ready. This does not fix main-versus-focused-chat routing**, which remains separate in #165515.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing VoiceWakeManager owns recognition retirement: destination invalidation tears down the old pipeline/generation and cancels its command; internal start/teardown use cancellation-only bookkeeping to avoid recursive invalidation. Phone-focus and selected-agent changes invalidate before assignment independently of Talk's session-key shortcut. Watch-started Talk can already hold the next phone destination or next agent's main key, so that shortcut alone cannot retire the old capture. Current main's focus persistence, selected-agent cleanup, configured-route authority, and restoration ordering are preserved. No new routing owner, generations, configuration, automatic resend, or basic focused-routing callback changes.

## Evidence

The maintained upstream fixture supersedes the earlier extraction repair.

The production recognition-callback regression includes focus, Gateway, Watch-target coincidence, and agent coincidence; its `@MainActor` throwing receive helper and existing cancellation/stale/fresh assertions remain. **These current native cases are authored, not executed.**
- Owned frozen install passed on supported Node 24.20.0 with exact pnpm 12.15.0, without age-policy waivers or declaration changes. Canonical offline localization sync, verify, and strict local check passed: 4,633 entries, no inventory/catalog/InfoPlist changes, zero contradictions. prs.title: fix(macos): keep attach-only save failures visible
prs.body:
Closes #190153

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS Debug "Attach only" toggle silently failing when it cannot save the setting.

## User Impact

The toggle reports a failed save and returns to its saved value. A permission problem can be corrected and retried without the rollback erasing the error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The marker write now throws on failure. A user-action binding owns persistence, so updating the displayed value after a failed save cannot trigger another write that clears the error. There are no new settings or storage formats.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main `c8f87b2e516`, a non-root disposable macOS 27.0 guest exercised the real marker setter against a task-owned read-only directory. The new creation regression failed because the setter returned nil even though the marker did not exist. The complete owner suite finished with 24 tests and this one expected failure, 0.062 seconds.
- With the repair, all 111 tests in GatewayLaunchAgentManagerTests, GatewayProcessManagerTests, and GatewayAutostartPolicyTests pass in the guest, 17.267 seconds. The new table covers both write directions, unchanged saved state after failure, successful retry, and idempotency.
- The native app and test bundle compile with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --disable-automatic-resolution`, 101.86 seconds.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1, SwiftLint 0.65.1, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P1/P2 findings.

The full macOS formatting check passes. The full lint script reports two inherited file-length violations in unchanged DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; both files are byte-identical to the base. The local sandbox also prevented SwiftLint cache writes. Lint of every changed file passes without a cache.

Actual-app before/after proof was captured in the disposable guest on November 2. With the task-owned state directory at mode 0500, the baseline app's failed removal returned the toggle to on and erased the error. The fixed app kept the saved on state and displayed the permission error. Restoring mode 0700 and retrying turned the control off, removed the marker, and cleared the error. Failed creation likewise kept the control off and showed an error; a writable retry recreated the marker. The test directory is back at mode 0700. This was a new offline profile with no running Gateway, operator credentials, or live account data.

![Before: failed-removal rollback silently clears the save error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e1dabea-74b4-4fbd-ac50-8d2a48392281)

![After: failed removal retains the saved state and permission error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e917158-e598-4700-bfd2-df8d0d93211a)

![After: failed creation reports the save error and stays off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70a7209b-cdb0-4005-a941-2a93b63bc54f)

![After: restoring write access lets the retry succeed and clears the error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d38548c9-6e09-4350-9228-ed8fedbf563a)

The production change removes one net line; the regression adds 23 Swift test lines. Release-note context: macOS attach-only preference save failures remain visible and can be retried.

AI-assisted. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting both failure paths.

## Native Android verification: inconclusive The new action opens the native recorder, but returned MP4s did not stage in two offline attempts. Chrome 133 also could not complete current Gateway identity setup. The recordings below are partial evidence, not a successful capture-to-send proof.
Original proposal and earlier evidence Related: #180298. Continues #181083. ## What Problem This Solves The native Camera route only requests photos, and a late capture return can attach to a replacement draft. ## User Impact Recognized Android browser routes offer **Record video** alongside photo capture in Chat and New Session. A returned clip becomes a draft attachment and is sent only after an explicit send. Image-only restrictions, existing-media selection, Safari behavior, desktop photo capture, and upload safeguards are preserved. The opening-draft guard rejects stale camera returns. The handoff regression fix connects the test fixture before selection and preserves production rejection of disconnected inputs. This continues the RoboClaw contribution from my personal fork because publication and operator-access problems prevented the managed publisher from updating the original branch. Further updates and review should use this PR. The existing commit history and contributor attribution are preserved. Proposed and directed by Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit). AI-assisted implementation and publication. The Android exposure remains a proposal for human product review. ## Evidence - The [ClawSweeper follow-up](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/commit/bea551eb7710179e699d3835d2edc9ddf2696a97) keeps attachment-group construction in the shared root-menu owner, removes the single-caller module, and removes only the duplicate positive-return unit case. prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

## Evidence

The exact prepared-base test-line ratchet and whitespace checks pass. Resolved output passes the publication secret gate; unchanged authored inputs retain prior reviewed proof. This mechanical integration does not require a new behavioral review.

The first native [CI 42374591897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42374591897), attempt 1, completed **SUCCESS** on this exact head: **48 successful jobs, 27 skipped**, no failed or pending job. All three required statuses (CI gate, dependency review and security-sensitive review) are **SUCCESS** on this head. Earlier successful runs remain prior-head evidence. No workflow rerun, duplicate review request or adoption ping was submitted. Maintainer product adoption, official distribution and employee acceptance remain separate.

Earlier validated author head: `02db206611aaf040ab37ea819889b8264483914b`. It normally merges CI-green head `1c771bb8` with official main `0372963434f6a0b79394dbe330abde2ae34f2a89` to resolve one new generated Discord-delta conflict that arose while the prior CI was running.

The following is the captured stdout from the existing successful Gateway run, copied with ANSI escapes and duplicate reporter lines removed. It is not a newly generated result summary. prs.title: fix(ios): refuse an invalid custom header name before it looks saved
prs.body:
## Native verification The invalid-name defect and fix were reproduced in the real iPhone simulator app. Full recordings below preserve their original speed; the candidate includes waits for shared UI access. No transport or physical-device proof is claimed.
Original proposal and earlier evidence ## What Problem This Solves On iOS, Gateway Settings, Custom Headers, a name such as `X Client ID` can be added with no warning. The new row appears and the fields clear. After leaving the screen and opening it again, the row is gone. A name such as `X-Client-ID` stays. Storage already drops a name that is not one HTTP token. The editor treated that drop as a successful add. ## Evidence The Custom Headers editor uses `GatewayCustomHeaders.isValidName`. Add Header stays disabled for a bad name, the footer explains the token rule, and the draft stays on screen. A valid name is stored by the Add Header button and is still listed after leaving the screen and opening it again. The shots below are from that walk on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.2), head `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604`. The test opens Gateway settings, types `headers.example.com` into Host, opens Custom Headers, types `X Client ID` and a value, then replaces the name with `X-Client-ID` and taps Add Header. Invalid name, draft kept, Add Header disabled: ![Invalid header name stays in the field with the token explanation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SebTardif/openclaw/proof/193595-header-shots/proof/invalid-name-kept.png) Valid name after leaving the editor and opening it again: ![Saved X-Client-ID is still listed after the editor is opened again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SebTardif/openclaw/proof/193595-header-shots/proof/valid-name-reopened.png) ```console $ xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests \ -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=9CFD7CAB-3B71-45D1-90F9-EF3B770C0ABE' \ -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen Test Case '-[OpenClawUITests.OpenClawSnapshotUITests testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen]' passed (53.147 seconds). ** TEST SUCCEEDED ** ``` The same interaction and assertion sequence was run again on the base and on this head. That run used an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Light mode, and a separate XCTest runner bound to the laboratory Debug bundle. Base `1bf13d4df5c1` fails `XCTAssertFalse(add.isEnabled)` after `X Client ID` is entered. Add Header stays enabled. The run took 40.064 seconds. Before, the invalid name still enables Add Header: ![Before: invalid name still enables Add Header](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ab4b498-4222-4b85-816b-e96f006489c9) Head `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604` passes. The invalid name stays in the draft, Add Header is disabled with the explanation, and `X-Client-ID` is still listed after leaving the editor and opening it again. The run took 52.153 seconds. After, the invalid name is rejected and kept: ![After: invalid name is rejected and retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/746c7131-d694-44a9-b863-74018bebef00) Valid header after leaving and reopening: ![Valid header after leaving and reopening](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09c03a8a-f399-42d9-a44e-580ccb1fa2d4) The four existing `GatewayCustomHeadersTests` passed in a dependency-free Swift package, using the unchanged test file and the shared production file. Both app builds passed. The synthetic header was removed through the UI, and it was absent after the editor was opened again. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior or issue addressed:** An invalid custom header name is refused in the editor instead of appearing as a saved row that disappears on the next visit. A valid name remains after the editor is opened again. - **Real environment tested:** iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.2, Xcode 27, macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-193490` at `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604`. The base comparison used an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Light mode, base `1bf13d4df5c1`, and the same head. - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=9CFD7CAB-3B71-45D1-90F9-EF3B770C0ABE' -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen`. The base comparison used that same native sequence on base `1bf13d4df5c1` and on this head. - **Evidence after fix:** The invalid shot shows `X Client ID` still in the name field and the footer "Header names cannot include spaces or other characters outside a single HTTP token." There is no saved Headers section. The second shot, after Add Header and reopening the screen, shows `X-Client-ID` under Headers and an empty draft. The base shot shows Add Header still enabled for `X Client ID`. The later head shots show that name kept with Add Header disabled, then `X-Client-ID` still listed after reopen. - **Observed result after fix:** Typing the invalid name left Add Header disabled and kept the draft. Tapping Add Header for `X-Client-ID` stored that header, and it was still listed after leaving the editor and opening it again. On the base build, the same invalid name left Add Header enabled. - **What was not tested:** A physical iPhone, and the next gateway connection sending the stored header. The value is a secure field, so the shots do not show it. ## Summary Closes #193490
## Native before / after | Main: invalid header appears saved | Candidate: invalid draft retained | | --- | --- | | | |
Control: valid header survives reopening
Main complete recording https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31b60b1d-66a6-4bc8-bbcb-0a4dcc9da13e
Candidate complete recording https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71f1ebb8-eac9-46f2-b16b-5e810b708987

## Problem and change

The running-session idle fixtures were desktop-only, so selecting them in a mobile census skipped every observation. A mobile page with its navigation drawer open therefore had no measured running-clock path.

Add the explicit-only `idle-sidebar-clock-mobile-open-1` scenario, reusing the existing one-running-session fixture, drawer preparation, and post-window clock recovery. Before measurement it verifies the selected touch viewport, visible document, open non-inert modal drawer, one running clock, and visible clock text. Range geometry handles the elapsed-time host's `display: contents`; CSS visibility and opacity are checked separately. Native Chromium mobile observations now enable touch emulation, matching the existing Talk runner. Existing desktop scenarios retain their IDs and behavior.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing running-session idle selected on mobile | 9/9 observations skipped (three engines, reference/head/A-A) |
| Final mobile guard, Chromium/WebKit/Firefox 1× | 9/9 passed across frozen reference/head/A-A; one running clock and two post-window recovery entries per observation, no app errors |
| Chromium mobile 6× | 3/3 passed before the visibility-only guard correction |
| WebKit traced mobile | 3/3 passed before the visibility-only guard correction; Inspector wall-time collection retained, CPU/heap fields unavailable |
| Scripts typecheck | Passed on final source |
| Targeted scripts lint and formatting | Passed |
| Independent review | Final full-context P0–P2 review scoped-clean after fixing CSS visibility admission |

The browser runs are bounded setup/collector/recovery proof: one pair, 1 s warmup and 1 s measured window, not performance improvement evidence. Frozen app bundles are `cf80b26f093d` and `ce4260e0a5e8`; their bytes were not rebuilt or changed. Firefox emulates viewport and touch only. No application rendering, startup graph, dependency or public option changed, so no product screenshot or UI build is needed.

Simplification: the existing fixture and clock recovery remain the single owners; no parallel mobile fixture or inventory-mirroring unit test was added. Touched-file LOC: 2,154 → 2,223 (+73/−4). The added lines are scenario admission and native touch setup. Reports and captures remain uncommitted.
