prs.title: fix(cli): try requested audio and video inference models first
prs.body:
Related: #176246. Earlier strict-pin proposal: #172409 by @yetval.

## What Problem This Solves

`infer audio transcribe --model provider/model` and `infer video describe --model provider/model` can silently use a configured media model instead of the requested model.

## User Impact

The requested model is tried first, and the result reports the model that succeeded. Configured media models remain fallbacks: a failed attempt can send the file to another configured provider or CLI backend. This is a draft proposal while the strict-pinning versus configured-failover contract in the linked issue remains undecided.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flag was used as a conversation-model hint, which does not override configured media entries. A separate optional file-request override now reaches the existing media selector. Matching entries retain their original transport settings and credential-owner indices; a different model does not lend its model-specific settings. The configuration remains the source for fallbacks.

Reported and discussed by @yetval; this implementation was written independently of the earlier strict-pin proposal.

## Evidence

November 8 maintenance normally merges official main `71ec4d25a0a879a4fa223d28729ab73a838eccb7` into the prior draft `b06ac543c934962b32785a9b9f0b6693990446b5`. Current head is `b0908db8813de03305b51aec8828be7d11fd3c15`, tree `13d61f31d3988386ff19c06eec3fad42b60801cd`.

The two conflicted files now retain main's CLI cancellation signal and shared file-runtime authority owner while forwarding this proposal's `modelOverride`. Audio and video both use the existing guarded-fetch/command-process scope in `runFile`; the superseded audio-only wrapper is removed. Main's symlink-parent resolution, local-root checks, cleanup, disabled/scope decisions and per-attempt authority checks remain.

- Fresh canonical independent P0–P2 review of the complete ten-file proposal found no actionable defects. The committed tree and all ten file digests match the reviewed candidate.
- Eight focused files passed 60 distinct cases: 46 selector/runtime/automatic-audio/video/local-input, 10 audio authority/disposition, and four registered CLI controls for pending-audio cancellation, actual-result attribution and audio/video symlink-parent paths. The CLI file has 114 cases; its other 110 cases were unselected. Wrappers took 201.92s, 47.19s, 26.90s and 99.23s; these include compiler preparation and are not pure test time. The first CLI selection matched only two cases; an exact follow-up selected the two path cases without changing source or assertions.
- Core production types, affected test-consumer types, typed lint, source/docs format, MDX, whitespace, line caps and max-lines checks passed. The existing separate 91-LF test allocation is unchanged, matching the five selector/descriptor ownership/region regressions. Against pinned main71ec, the native test-line check reports 6,565,161 / 6,565,202, with 41 LF spare; the shared baseline and other allocations are unchanged.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passed at this committed head in 231.63s. Package/build-info both identify 2026.11.1 and b090. Validation used Node24.22.1 / pnpm12.15.0 and the repository-pinned Bun fork. This runtime build is not a new full UI/release validation.

Nine fresh real `pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <owned> ...` inference commands plus two configuration preflights pass on b090 in 128.63s. This is normal Node24.22.1/pnpm12.15.0 orchestration with the exact repository-pinned Bun fork executing the CLI. Fresh network/PID/mount views expose only loopback and private HOME/profile/state/cache; source, dependencies, build output and Bun are read-only. Every data POST asserts endpoint, requested model, synthetic-auth equality, configured-row header, response status, exact order/count and parsed CLI winner. All 11 CLI invocations, both HTTP servers/handlers and both namespace groups joined, with no forced kill. Source HEAD/tree/index/build/dependency manifests remain unchanged.

| b090 case | CLI winner | Ordered HTTP data requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| audio-control | `openai/gpt-4o-transcribe` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `gpt-4o-transcribe` / 200 |
| audio-explicit | `openai/whisper-1` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `whisper-1` / 200 |
| video-control | `moonshot/kimi-k2.5` | `/v1/chat/completions` / `kimi-k2.5` / 200 |
| video-explicit | `moonshot/kimi-k2.6` | `/v1/chat/completions` / `kimi-k2.6` / 200 |
| audio-no-configured-models | `openai/whisper-1` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `whisper-1` / 200 |
| audio-exact-owned-index-1 | `openai/whisper-1` | `/owned/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `whisper-1` / 200 |
| audio-provider-wide-row | `openai/whisper-1` | `/provider-wide/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `whisper-1` / 200 |
| audio-explicit-400-configured-fallback | `openai/gpt-4o-transcribe` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `whisper-1` / 400 → `/fallback/v1/audio/transcriptions` / `gpt-4o-transcribe` / 200 |
| video-explicit-400-configured-fallback | `moonshot/kimi-k2.5` | `/v1/chat/completions` / `kimi-k2.6` / 400 → `/fallback/v1/chat/completions` / `kimi-k2.5` / 200 |

The exact configured entry retains its `/owned/v1` endpoint and `owned-slot-1` header; the provider-wide entry retains `/provider-wide/v1` and `provider-wide`. In both injected HTTP400 cases, the explicit model is attempted first and the configured model wins second; only that second request carries `configured-only`. The header/endpoint observation is transport provenance, not a SecretRef-degradation test. Inputs are the historical synthetic WAV and repository MP4 below.

The first isolated attempt was intentionally stopped after the new launcher tried to download Bun without external network access. That attempt is UNQUALIFIED and is not counted as a product failure or successful wire proof. The rerun mounts the already verified, identical checkout-pinned fork through the launcher's supported environment contract; network isolation, source guards and all nine case assertions remain. prs.body:
Closes #182410 ## What Problem This Solves The chat attachment workflow has no built-in way to draw a quick sketch before sending it. ## User Impact Users can draw and stage an ordinary PNG attachment; sending remains a separate action. ## Why This Change Was Made Loads the existing annotation painter on demand and uses the current modal, conversation presentation and attachment-admission owners. ## Evidence ### Technical follow-up — 2026-11-07 UTC Current product head `9ba12e6d8d96599bb7c4c8339a34a4f9c4a79de4`, tree `94a8f00026d9031585eca69335ea79d8eaee0a09`. Preserved the maintainer's live attachment/lifetime repairs. The rendering-only memo now samples upload availability and image-only mode within its existing equality fence; unrelated publications retain the same menu DOM. Selection and sketch admission still read current controls. Accepted upstream `90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a` was normally merged to include its Sessions fractional-focus CI correction; strict geometry assertions remain. Observed regression: unchanged incoming code produces12 child-list mutations where the existing root-menu test requires0 (1 failed/4 passed). Not tested in this follow-up: Chromium/synthetic transport only; no newly claimed live authenticated Gateway, real model inference, physical touch/camera or Safari certification. Incoming PR:77252b7504819608e528d0fa43ca75457e921e4d. Published correction:d399707b5881665a25e9710b861decf84b00ff85 (tree a82d7e9ae70c8cc2ef9515ee78b77835c9f9d78a). No app state, model response, WebSocket event, style or canvas drawing handler was injected. Inputs are normal UI actions; only the real editor-download transfer was delayed for the navigation check. Videos retain their full duration and original speed. Explicit privacy masks cover the test computer's name in navigation/new-session recordings; originals are retained. Image crops below are taken from those recordings, with full context in the videos. ## Selected frames Main has the existing attachment sources; the tested PR can send a hand-drawn image through the ordinary conversation. | Main | Repaired PR: real vision response | | --- | --- | | | | | Incoming PR: click leaves no dot | Repair: the dot remains after release | | --- | --- | | | | | Incoming PR: rejected drawing is lost | Repair: drawing stays available for retry | | --- | --- | | | | | Before lifecycle repair: old dialog over next conversation | After: next conversation has no stale dialog | | --- | --- | | | | Mobile WebKit drawing control (viewport390px; video canvas retains room for rotation): ## Full recordings ### Main: existing sources https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a688991a-62d7-4802-825f-0d76cdd010bc ### Click and rejection: incoming PR, then repaired V1 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/228c86c2-931a-4bde-816b-b5c002669475 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f87aafbe-d749-45f2-9dac-982a5af64add ### Conversation change: before lifetime repair, then V2 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba037f9d-729c-4657-9085-73073ebd4845 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dedb2663-d38c-4559-a6ee-0b42152bf907 ### Side chat: V2 retained-menu failure, then final V3 repair https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f15d6568-65ef-4a0c-80be-29b4f2a2f12e https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0521920-af1e-4e5d-9fb1-62bf950aa675 ### Final V3: drawing, real vision response, reload https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/500cbbc2-ae25-491d-aa3a-ced3af27aadb ### WebKit: main File baseline, then final PR drawing and rotation; local-storage limitation remains https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/935126c5-4128-4838-bcb3-ddf52cbd8822 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d002dcc-350a-4b18-8cc5-f93198403aaf

prs.title: improve(worktrees): skip the default-branch fetch when origin has not moved
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Default-branch worktree creation unnecessarily fetches when origin still advertises the commit already tracked locally. The redundant fetch also enters the repository's Git ref mutation queue.

## User Impact

Worktree creation skips that fetch for an unchanged default tip. Changed or unavailable advertisements retain fetching and the existing warning/fallback behavior. Hydration, local fast-forward rules, cancellation, and the 30-second preparation reuse window remain owned by the existing preparation flow. To bypass the reuse window, fetch and choose an explicit base ref. No new configuration or cache is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the commit already returned by `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` and compare it with the local remote-tracking ref. This avoids an additional network request. The takeover rebases the original work onto main including `75694cca` and repairs the affected service fixture: creating the new commit directly in the bare remote keeps the local clone stale, so the test still exercises a real fetch and its timeout.

Related: #191130 (refresh deadline; separate change), #194712 (hydration output; separate change).

## Evidence

Rebased onto `7c0d3ab5a28774d2efefee24d535970539b27a1d`, which includes `75694cca`. The original implementation and verified contributor credit are retained.

The original two CI failures reproduce: the service fixture's push updates its own `origin/main`, so fetching correctly disappears and the expected 60-second fetch timeout is absent. Creating the commit directly in the bare remote fixes the fixture while retaining the timeout assertion. The unchanged-tip regression fails on the exact main parent because it performs an extra fetch. Real-Git coverage also checks default-branch switches, force-pushed rewinds, explicit refresh during the reuse window, and cancellation recovery.

Focused validation: 168 passed, 2 existing skips across `base-ref`, `service`, `service-branches`, `git-fetch`, and `git` suites. The repaired two consumer cases pass in 5.24 seconds; the three owner/Git files pass in 100.04 seconds (including transform time). `pnpm build sourcePerformance` passed. An isolated built Gateway's actual `worktrees.create` RPC produced the expected checkout SHA with one advertisement and zero fetches for a matching tip, and one advertisement plus one fetch for an independently advanced tip. No external services or production data were used.

Codex autoreview against the pinned base, including staged repairs and the benchmark, was scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings. The original and rebased production module bytes are identical.

### Measurement

Acceptance was fixed in this PR before measured runs: use the real default-base owner, five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs and five A/A pairs with fresh clone paths/processes; require identical selected commits, unchanged-tip fetch count 1 → 0, improved phase wall time/CPU/allocation, and investigate regressions above 20%.

Synthetic local-origin partial clone: 62,000 logical files, 1,142,784,000 target bytes, 600,000 unrelated historical blobs and 1,239 packs. Darwin/APFS, warm/unspecified filesystem cache; no agent/session database populated because this phase reads Git state rather than sessions or transcripts. This measures local owner work, not btrfs, network latency, mutation-queue contention, or complete send latency. Five-sample p95 is the maximum, not a production tail estimate.

| Metric | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseRefresh, ms | 211.93 / 345.15 | 136.02 / 153.03 |
| Main-thread CPU, ms | 17.798 / 19.338 | 12.464 / 13.222 |
| Native Git CPU, ms | 80 / 100 | 30 / 40 |
| Native Git peak RSS, MB | 30.097 / 30.163 | 24.609 / 27.361 |
| Main-isolate allocation, MB | 17.032 / 23.747 | 19.221 / 21.507 |
| Git commands / fetches | 7 / 1 | 6 / 0 |

Every paired wall-time and JS-CPU sample improved. A/A wall medians were 197.97 / 196.00 ms (−1.0%), supporting the 35.8% AB latency improvement. **Allocation improvement was not demonstrated:** its median increased 12.9%, its mean decreased 1.75%, and same-source A/A allocation had substantial spread (median −6.5%, p95 +14.8%). Do not treat the allocation acceptance criterion as passed or claim allocation neutrality. The counts, wall time, and CPU support retaining the optimization.

Reproduce using `scripts/perf/worktree-base-refresh-measure.ts --seed <fixture/seed> --base-file <saved-main-base-ref.ts> --output <new-directory>` through `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`. Save the baseline from the pinned main above. The fragmented fixture generator is committed in #194712 at `b23a43c1008996159cfa04e6e72e1f6ec34c5ac8:scripts/perf/worktree-hydration-fixture.py`; run it with `<new-fixture-directory> --extra-packs 1237`. This lane does not edit that peer-owned script. Separate baseline/candidate phase CPU profiles were also captured.

Production delta is **+10 lines** for parsing the already available tip, comparing the local ref and conditionally retaining the existing fetch path. No competing owner, new cache, configuration, schema, or state store is added. Tests grow by 85 lines, covered by a dedicated allocation for real-Git regressions and affected recovery/reuse contracts; the reproducible benchmark adds 268 tooling lines.

### Inherited main regression

`pnpm check:changed --base 7c0d3ab5a28774d2efefee24d535970539b27a1d --staged` completed: all checks passed except 20 historical changelog-attribution violations. All 20 reproduce identically in a clean sparse checkout of exact parent `7c0d3ab5a28774d2efefee24d535970539b27a1d`. The rejection rules were introduced by #194364 / `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957`, which newly forbids handles still present in historical changelogs. This is an inherited main regression requiring separate repair, not a passing check or noise. The original PR's worktree test failures are repaired separately above.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski (original implementation)
- @steipete (takeover and verification)

prs.title: fix(worktrees): stop waiting for stale template deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

New workspace requests wait for physical deletion of an unusable template before building its replacement, adding recursive tree removal and possible builder retirement to first-turn preparation.

## User Impact

Replacement requests stop waiting for old-template deletion. Existing housekeeping or `openclaw worktrees gc` removes the old generation later; it continues occupying disk until cleanup runs. Reader custody, dirty-template rejection, and recovery records remain enforced. No configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing atomic unpublication transaction moves the stale generation to a retirement key while retaining its path and existing preparing status. This frees the selection key without adding a background queue or another cleanup owner. GC also drops a duplicate reader scan; atomic unpublication retains the authoritative no-readers check before deletion.

Production delta is **+6 lines**, for the persisted handoff in the existing registry. Regression tests grow by 12 lines; the standalone benchmark is tooling. This complements the validation diagnostics in #193214 without changing their contract.

## Evidence

Synthetic Linux arm64 btrfs loopback: 62,000 payload files / 1.1 GB, 2,025 sibling snapshots, 1,239 Git packs. Frozen production template/registry/GC owners and native filesystem helpers, with input hashes checked against the base and final sources. Two A/A controls, **25 interleaved pairs**, plus five separate allocation pairs and CPU profiles. All timing samples, including outliers, are retained in these statistics.

| Owner operation | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm template preparation | 363 / 384 ms | 339 / 459 ms |
| Replacement preparation | 740 / 1,751 ms | 268 / 949 ms |
| Native template apply | 48.7 / 346 ms | 48.9 / 325 ms |
| Subsequent template GC | 171 / 481 ms | 803 / 2,414 ms |
| Replacement preparation + GC | 913 / 2,154 ms | 1,065 / 3,037 ms |

The emitted request-path `templateRetire` phase falls from **484 ms median to absent (zero physical deletion)**. Replacement preparation CPU falls **826 → 336 ms**, and sampled main-isolate allocation **3.83 → 1.60 MiB**. Across warm selection, replacement, apply and GC together, median CPU is **3,884 → 3,789 ms** and sampled allocation **6.31 → 6.52 MiB**.

**Tradeoff / unmet criterion:** combined prepare-plus-GC p95 grows **41%**, exceeding the pre-run total-work tail budget. The full four-operation sequence p95 grows **2.88 → 4.68 s**. This is a request-latency improvement with deferred cleanup cost, not a claim that every performance metric improved. Stop before merge for review of that tradeoff.

Long warm preparation delays did not reproduce. This is owner-boundary evidence, not a full Gateway/model send, registered Git worktree retirement, or dependency-builder benchmark. No 35 GiB agent database, live deployment data, loaded-production btrfs commit simulation, or cold OS-cache claim is included. Runtime code is host-mounted; fixture data is on native btrfs. The first two A/A replacement calls were 779 and 890 ms. One-minute load ranged 0.62–4.14.

Reproduction driver: `node scripts/perf/worktree-template-prepare-measure.mts --runtime <frozen-compiled-runtime> --root <disposable-btrfs-root> --label <arm-sample>`. Run with Node, preserve compiler-recorded external runtime paths, alternate frozen base/candidate runtimes, and repeat separately with `--allocation` / `--profile <path>`. Baseline: `19446cf417c68c8ba3aab80ede3f65a819f392e3`.

Validation:

CI follow-up: the source-only reuse/refresh test read the oldest registry row after a policy change. Deferred retirement keeps that old generation visible to GC, so list order no longer identifies the active template. The test now reads the stable selection key and requires the replacement to be ready. Independent checkout contents, CRLF policy replacement, same-generation commit refresh, template/clone counts, and host-filter suppression remain asserted. No production ordering or custody change was needed for this correction. The additional test line checks readiness.

- Follow-up proof: source-only filters file passes separately on Node (11 tests, 37.70 s wrapper wall time) and Bun (11 tests, 24.96 s). All 70 worktree test files were selected on both runtimes: each reports 67 passing files, 3 skipped files, 788 passing tests and 9 skipped cases; Node 664.77 s, Bun 597.00 s. Skips retain existing platform/filesystem/PostgreSQL conditions. The reported CI failure reproduced locally at the old identity assertion before this correction. Fresh Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2; focused formatting, lint, test typechecking and the test-line ratchet pass. Follow-up production LOC delta: zero.

- 80 affected tests passed across template custody, registry, service acceleration/restart, sandbox templates, btrfs selection, and provisioned-state consumers. The new custody regression fails on the exact base because the old files were already deleted; it passes after the fix. Six existing immediate-deletion expectations were updated and replayed successfully. Expanded run: 206 s including initial expectation failures; focused corrected cases: 48 s including worker compilation; btrfs replay: 24 s. CI seconds are pending.
- Final formatting, targeted lint, typechecks, line-cap/test-line ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2 with full owner/custody context. No UI-imported production module changed.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed; every gate passed except **20 inherited changelog-attribution violations**. The exact main parent reproduces all 20. Commit `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364) introduced these signatures; its exact parent `ca4affe5ac39` reports 26 different earlier violations with zero overlap. These are newly introduced main regressions for the release-tooling owner, not ignored noise. No changelog or gate exception is included here.

prs.title: fix(agents): prevent unknown models after creating secondary agents
prs.body:
Closes #58289

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a secondary agent created through `agents.create` can fail with `Unknown model` when its selected custom model exists only in the configured system agent's `models.json`.

## User Impact

User impact: secondary agents without a local catalog can use the system agent's custom model inventory while retaining their own authentication; existing secondary catalogs remain authoritative, and no secondary `models.json` is created, copied, or overwritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared model runtimes now use the configured system agent's catalog as a read-only fallback only when the secondary agent has no local `models.json`. The fallback participates in runtime identity and worker serialization so startup and on-demand discovery agree.

The inherited catalog is inventory, not credential authority. It is parsed with the same JSONC-compatible parser as `ModelRegistry`; provider API keys plus authorization, cookie, and token-like provider/model headers are removed. Safe route headers are preserved only for the matching provider/model/transport route, and current runtime configuration still wins. Embedded transport now forwards the sanitized headers returned by model resolution, while authentication remains request-scoped to the secondary agent.

## Evidence (October 28 update)

Merge commit `7a0c2366de1fa6cf4bd7924d6158a4a4077c3bd2` integrated upstream main `228596060e33dfcddbb6740416f381daac6f84fe` without rewriting the PR branch. Follow-up commit `b37ba82e91e6fbbc380df339185f905aeeca4bf1` fixes compatibility failures from that merge. Commit `98c5af5729e5839e99a0ecc68289294b9e12cedb` updates the E2E Gateway test harness to supply a recovery owner; the test throws if a real recovery restart is requested. The missing-secondary-catalog issue remained present in upstream source before this merge: prepared runtime capture and scoped catalog loading still read only the secondary agent directory.

The PR preserves a read-only catalog fallback only when the secondary catalog is absent. The secondary agent keeps its own credential authority; inherited provider/model authorization, cookie, token-like headers and API keys remain filtered. The ClawSweeper P2 finding is addressed: request-scoped headers reach the generic custom API stream fallback, while nullable header deletion sentinels are preserved.

Local verification on Node 24.20.0:
- Core production typecheck passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`.
- `embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts`: 27/27 passed.
- `attempt-native-provider-authority.test.ts`: 3/3 passed.
- `prepared-model-catalog-worker.test.ts`: 3/3 passed.
- `stream-resolution.request-headers.test.ts`: 2/2 passed, including custom API fallback.
- Three targeted fallback, local precedence, and credential/header isolation tests in `prepared-model-runtime.sources.test.ts` passed.
- `oxlint` on the six follow-up files, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passed without increasing the baseline.
- The SQLite offline-maintenance lock failure was reproduced on both the PR candidate and clean upstream main `228596060` under the same Node and test command.
- Full Gateway E2E passed locally on the final candidate: 1/1 using `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1` with loopback access. It verifies successful `agents.create`, two secondary-credential requests, and zero further provider requests after both credential stores are cleared. The in-process test Gateway now has a recovery owner that throws if an actual recovery restart is requested. The exact CI base `5437018` has the same relevant Gateway reload and test-helper code; this was a test harness compatibility issue. Root test typecheck was blocked locally by missing Discord workspace dependencies, while hosted checks on the previous head passed.

## Remaining gates

- Evaluate hosted checks on the current head `98c5af5729e5839e99a0ecc68289294b9e12cedb`; previous-head failures are not current-head results.
- Maintainer design and security approval remain required. This contributor update does not supply that approval.

prs.title: test(ui): measure continuous gesture frame costs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Click-to-ready benchmarks miss stalls during pointer movement, selection, wheel scrolling, and live resizing.

## User Impact

No application behavior or appearance changes. The engine benchmark can now exercise continuous gestures and report per-frame cost across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an opt-in `--steps gestures` catalog with realistic/large fixtures, native pointer/wheel input targeting 60 Hz, live divider/window resizing, cross-window text selection, selection-popup behavior, and mobile viewport changes. Record actual input cadence, rAF interval distributions and 16.7/33 ms budget counts, and ResizeObserver deliveries/entries per frame. Native diagnostics report style/layout passes, available restyle counts and forced-layout stacks; missing engine fields stay unknown. Geometry-read instrumentation is a separate diagnostic mode.

The census found obvious resize stalls in WebKit and Firefox. A small duplicate slot-observer receipt candidate was screened for ten rotated base/head/base triplets per engine, then removed: it did not improve the over-budget frame rate by 5%. This PR includes only the reusable measurement tools. Immediate/deferred row scans remain intact because they can see different virtual ranges and protect scroll compensation.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Untraced 1× census | 84/84 applicable cells pass: 14 gestures × two fixture sizes × three engines |
| Candidate screen | 90/90 behavior checks pass; ten rotated triplets per engine; runtime candidate rejected |
| Trace-parser contracts | 5 tests pass, including Chromium completion counts, WebKit callFrames stacks and unavailable metrics |
| Type/lint | UI and scripts typechecks, tooling test typecheck and scoped lint pass |
| Independent review | No actionable findings through P2, including the getter repair and both main conflict resolutions; the rejected runtime change is absent |
| CI repair | Run 42389960757 caught one new lint-suppression allowlist violation. Removed the suppression by retaining the getter receiver; 14 suppression-policy tests, scoped lint/type/format and a native-getter browser smoke pass |
| CI interaction flake | Run 42390947572 passed 41 jobs; one question-footer landscape tap assertion failed (543 sibling assertions passed). The exact named test passes on merge base f4c6c331e06. Application and fixture inputs are unchanged; one targeted shard rerun passed. Attempt 2 is green (42 successful jobs, 26 skipped). The intermittent failure is retained and is not claimed fixed or inherited. |
| Chromium 4× census | 28/28 applicable cells pass; all 112 untraced census cells complete |
| Native diagnostic census | 84/84 applicable cases pass (Chromium 1×/4× and WebKit); zero dropped samples |
| Production/full-tree Knip | Both pass with zero unused files |
| Main conflict repair | Merged 74a5cbf2fb9c into replacement head 4a9cb92312f. Both gesture tracing and new accessibility/live-region finalization remain; script typecheck, scoped lint/format and fresh independent review pass. The merged head exposed two additional CI repairs and an inherited Outputs reload failure; details below. |

The candidate screen's median per-gesture p95 / >33 ms frame fraction:

| Engine | Base | Candidate | Identical-base control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chromium | 16.80 ms / 0.52% | 16.75 ms / 0.52% | 16.80 ms / 0.00% |
| WebKit | 61.50 ms / 49.51% | 58.00 ms / 48.60% | 60.00 ms / 49.04% |
| Firefox | 50.00 ms / 56.59% | 49.99 ms / 57.14% | 50.00 ms / 58.24% |

Limits: rAF callbacks are not presentation or CPU timestamps; WebKit's integer-ms timestamps inflate strict >16.7 ms counts. Viewport reconfiguration serializes and cannot sustain 60 Hz in Firefox/WebKit. Mobile rotation is a viewport/touch emulation, not a native orientation event (Firefox lacks full isMobile emulation). Sessions displays its existing 100-row page within 100/1,000-session inventories; Advanced Settings has 303 rows in both size variants. Native trace ratios include gesture assertions and settling and are amortized per delivered input, not causal per-handler counts. Synthetic Gateway fixtures measure rendering, not transport latency.

Application LOC and startup assets are unchanged. Changed files: 3,220 → 4,483 LOC (+1,272/-9), including 121 new test lines. Startup from the same-machine baseline build: 90,890 B gzip, one startup CSS request. No size ceilings changed. The baseline's existing document/CSS budget violations remain unchanged; the discarded runtime candidate's +115 B chat increase is not included.

<details>
<summary>Complete gesture and native-work tables</summary>


Worst p95 across the realistic and large fixtures. Each cell is `p95 ms (>33 ms frames %)`, using the same selected observation. Full median/p95, >16.7 and >33 counts, RO/frame, input cadence and available native counters are in coverage.md/coverage.json. This is descriptive census evidence, not a paired performance acceptance claim.

| Gesture | Chromium 1× | Chromium 4× | WebKit | Firefox |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| sidebar-sweep | 16.70 (0.0%) | 16.80 (2.2%) | 19.00 (0.0%) | 17.20 (0.0%) |

| mobile-rotation | 16.80 (1.4%) | 133.40 (22.8%) | 46.00 (17.6%) | 17.60 (4.9%) |

The 16.7 ms budget is visibly missed in live resizing, especially WebKit/Firefox and Chromium 4×. Pointer sweeps and one-message selection remain near refresh cadence in these samples. Wheel scrolling and cross-window selection lose that cadence at 4×. WebKit viewport rotation stalls. Strict 16.7 ms counts are quantization-sensitive; none of these one-pair census cells certifies every frame on real hardware.


84 applicable diagnostic cells: Chromium 1×, WebKit 1×, Chromium 4× each have 28 passing cells. Zero failures, zero dropped probe samples, zero geometry-read instrumentation. The same 28 viewport/gesture combinations are covered in every group; 84 unsupported viewport combinations were explicitly skipped.

The following compact table takes each metric’s maximum across realistic and large fixtures for its gesture. A cell reads **style passes/input / layout passes/input; active RO mean/max per frame**. Maxima may come from different fixture sizes. Style/layout ratios include the whole native capture (setup bounds, actual gesture, assertions and settle); RO means/maxima use active rAF callback intervals. These are diagnostic counts, not a speedup comparison.

| Gesture | Chromium 1× | WebKit 1× | Chromium 4× |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mobile-rotation | 12.58 / 5.50; 1.24 / 13 | 11.58 / 13.50; 1.60 / 13 | 12.58 / 5.50; 3.13 / 13 |
| sessions-sweep | 1.38 / 0.26; 0.00 / 0 | 1.69 / 0.10; 0.00 / 0 | 1.14 / 0.01; 0.00 / 0 |
| sessions-wheel | 2.12 / 0.97; 0.91 / 1 | 1.55 / 3.64; 0.87 / 2 | 1.01 / 0.40; 0.70 / 1 |

| window-resize | 7.98 / 6.36; 13.20 / 24 | 8.38 / 7.29; 14.34 / 43 | 7.33 / 5.72; 12.64 / 24 |

## Main native-stack findings

Counts below are stack-backed native Layout events aggregated over each diagnostic matrix. Elapsed sums include tracing overhead, may include nested slices, and are not CPU time. Exact representative full stacks and per-cell counts remain in the compact `native-census-audit.json` stack registry.

| Mapped owner | Chromium 1× | WebKit 1× | Chromium 4× |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-scroll-events.ts:5` | 373 | 345 | 364 |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details.tsx:215` | 183 | 323 | 171 |

`readTranscriptViewport` is reached by layout-owner viewport publication; Details docking reads its bounds; marquee measures overflow; Sessions measures the visible window; sidebar scrolling repositions context UI; the position rail measures its layout. These are location evidence and follow-up candidates. Counts across throttles are not comparable wins because actual delivered/coalesced input differs.

- Chromium restyled-element visits are complete across 4,650 (1×) and 3,571 (4×) native style passes. WebKit supplies no element-count payload across 4,443 passes; this remains unavailable.
- Native stack coverage is partial: absence of a stack-bearing Layout field is reported as unknown, never zero. Script nesting remains separate from stack-backed forced layouts.

- Mobile rotation is a viewport portrait/landscape cycle, not a native device orientation event. Desktop wheel/hover/selection/handles are intentionally unavailable in the mobile matrix.
- Source maps are from the measured base bundle. All 116 unique preserved full stacks map successfully; original generated asset locations are no longer needed for the preserved source-level evidence.
- One native observation per cell is attribution evidence only. Acceptance/smoothness comes from the separately recorded untraced matrix; no runtime fix was accepted from these diagnostic counts.

</details>

## CI repair and inherited failure

The 121-line native trace-parser regression suite now has a matching PR-specific test-line allocation. The shared scalar and application byte ceilings are unchanged. The theme-branding E2E now waits for the existing zero-count “Lobster visits” condition after asynchronous plugin theme hydration; it keeps the same assertion and timeout. Its focused native browser run passes (20.48 seconds reported wall), as do the test-line ratchet, targeted typecheck, lint, format and independent review.

Run 42394853130 also failed both `Details module loading > reads Outputs after startup settles and releases hidden demand (history error=false/true)` cases at `chat-details-pr-loading.e2e.test.ts:408`. Both exact names fail at the same transcript-after-reload wait on the isolated merge base 74a5cbf2fb9c (40.90 seconds reported wall). That reproduction uses unchanged application/test source; only its temporary build output was redirected to the SSD. This failure is inherited and remains visible; it is not waived by a differently failing shard. Head f121b086064 retains the evidence and fixes the two PR-owned CI issues together. CI run 42396703688 completed:41 successful jobs,25 skipped, and only the two inherited Outputs cases plus the aggregate failed. The native exception retains that failure. Eighteen relevant source objects match across the reproduced baseline, actual CI main parent71ec4d25, and tested merge64a9f4c34.

Landed as `055544b9fa35317f2cf19c0f74736edd0ba9e0ea` through native inherited-failure recovery. Final run `42396703688` had 41 successful jobs and 25 skips; only the two reproduced Outputs failures and their aggregate remained red. The native source/checkout and landing-parent audits passed. The intermittent question-footer failure received one isolated shard rerun earlier; the test-line and theme-readiness defects were repaired in this PR.

prs.title: fix(models): keep generated catalogs credential-free
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated plugin model catalogs still persist provider/model API keys and headers, and refresh can discard a legacy-only credential before recovery. This revision replaces the original broader runtime-auth cutover with the remaining **storage and explicit migration** repair:

- Strip keys/headers from newly planned and published generated catalogs, including direct publisher calls.
- Stop copying a plaintext auth-profile key into a missing root catalog field.
- Preserve unresolved legacy generated rows during ordinary refresh without blocking unrelated providers.
- Have Doctor import and verify recoverable keys, then remove generated copies accounted for by canonical auth or current authored configuration—including already-canonical copies.

## User Impact

Authored root `models.json` bytes and existing SDK/registry authentication behavior are preserved. **No runtime-auth selection change is introduced.** This does not promise universal Gateway root-only auth: an actual root-only Gateway attempt exposed an unchanged embedded-auth prerequisite, documented in the proof.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair retained generated copies. Doctor includes configured agents with generated SQLite catalogs but no root catalog. Unverified fields stay recoverable with warnings. Pending sidecar migration bytes remain intact until retry convergence.

Doctor rereads source/auth after confirmation, checks the current config revision and included files, and validates source state at persistence/cleanup boundaries. Concurrent logout/source changes do not authorize stale recovery or deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

[#143664](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143664) already blocks generated credentials at request time; [#143647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143647) provides logout cleanup. This PR builds on their existing owners. It adds no dependency, config option, schema migration, or broader credential-precedence policy.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `cae19faf537bb04cbd39301d8a0a82f1b4ca5ac6`. Integrated current main; conflict resolved; final independent AutoReview clean. Exact-head build and added stable-2026.10.5/fresh-publication proofs are in progress. Historical linked receipts below remain attributed to their original heads.

[Immutable evidence bundle](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/README.md) · [file manifest](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/MANIFEST.sha256) · [final runtime boundaries](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/runtime/final-stage-summary.json) · [independent AutoReview](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/review/autoreview-current-cli.md).

- **167/167 focused tests**, 12 files, pass. Includes pre-fix reproductions and repairs for confirmation-time config/include data loss, pending-sidecar recovery, and logout races.
- Targeted lint/core types, formatting, MDX and standard docs routes pass. A hosted test-type error was fixed with a non-null assertion; emitted test JavaScript is identical. Extra anchor auditing found five pre-existing broken anchors in untouched files, disclosed separately.
- AutoReview: **scoped-clean; no actionable P0–P2 findings** on the implementation diff. Final follow-up is test-type-only. The final exact-head build passes; [source/artifact binding](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/runtime/final-source-binding.json) proves all 19 previously bound launchers/changed-owner bundles are byte-identical.
- **Actual published 2026.10.3 → built candidate:** real launcher Doctor migration, canonical/recovered-key Gateway requests, retained conversation and final-head restart/recall pass against an actual CPU local model. Supported logout removes profiles; the protected receiver rejects the subsequent credential-free localhost request, with no revoked-key reuse or upstream inference.
- **Authored compatibility:** built registry/LLM SDK inference with empty canonical auth returns `ROOT-AUTH-OK`, preserving exact authored bytes. The failed root-only Gateway attempt and the invalid initial zero-HTTP-I/O expectation for localhost are retained and explained—not mislabeled passes. Reproduction sources distinguish executed receipts from adapted, unexecuted recipes.

**Current-head CI and final proof refresh are in progress.** Previous-head CI passed; it is not claimed for this integrated commit. Fresh ClawSweeper review will be requested once the new evidence is published. No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix: preserve gateway administrator permissions across native UI clients
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An authenticated native-app administrator could receive caller-scoped automation inventory and “not found” for another conversation’s job, despite holding Gateway admin authority. The invariant is **same authenticated administrator, same effective scopes and policy, same Gateway permissions**, regardless of Control UI or native UI client. Rendering features remain separate.

## User Impact

User impact: native UI administrators can inspect and repair existing automations across conversations with the same effective scopes and policy as browser administrators. Caller-only caps, requester isolation, and live revocation remain enforced. Maintainer approval of this permission extension and the current-head sensitive-security change remains required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse shared authenticated UI-admin classification for fresh-turn automation admission and durable recovery, without labeling native clients as Control UI or granting direct-local execution.
- Retain recorded automation-admin delegation across scheduled recovery and repair/notice continuations. Legacy browser grants remain compatible; historical native snapshots without recorded delegation are not upgraded.
- Preserve scope intersections, principal-only snapshot contracts, exact-device reconnect custody, requester identity, and the existing authorization gates for provider-review acknowledgment, dashboard reads, task suggestions, and signed-in mentions.
- Retain deployment caller caps, tool policy, fresh/direct-turn and exact-run binding, and live authority/revocation checks through the final effect. Browser origin checks and transport-specific rendering remain separate.

## Evidence

Review repair head: `1d59863f8e6155adb544bb806acf134706c91c0e`.

### Review repairs and expanded proof — November 7, 2026

- **Architecture finding fixed:** replaced the scope module's import from the Gateway handler-type barrel with its minimal structural input contract. `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` now reports **0 cycles**, versus **1 cycle** on the reviewed head. Runtime authorization logic is unchanged.
- **All four current-head CI test-type failures repaired:** narrow the recovery snapshot discriminant, retain browser classification separately in the restored-source fixture, supply the native transport fixture's authenticated profile, and strip native-only delegation when building a principal snapshot. Core typecheck and the four affected canonical test-type graphs pass.
- **Recovered native owner continuation:** `operator-run-recovery.effects.test.ts` now takes a serialized native snapshot through a persisted CronService row, the production job target and failure-repair event owners, admitted child authority, and a host-bound file write. An allowed write persists; device revocation, email reassignment, and reassignment-then-restoration during the next held write reject it, with the file unchanged. This extends and relocates existing final-effect cases rather than duplicating them.
- **Native provider-review final effect:** `sessions-provider-review.integration.test.ts` exercises the real Gateway router, scope/session authorization, acknowledgment owner, and worker SQLite compare/commit. An authorized native writer clears the exact pause. Read-only, foreign-owner, and non-UI callers never reach runtime handoff; device revocation at commit leaves the entire session entry unchanged. External model acceptance is a fixed fixture: this is production-boundary proof, not a live native-app/provider E2E claim.
- **Latest-stable upgrade:** an actual released `openclaw@2026.11.1` store writer created a disabled synthetic automation. Supported backed-up Doctor migration and current-source `loadCronStore`/`CronService.list/update` preserve its authored prompt, disabled state, creator, owner, delivery, interval, and unrelated fields. Exact whole-store comparison permits only verified canonical metadata additions: every-schedule anchor, owner profile from stored creator, and versioned account tool policy from stored owner. Subsequent service update persists without changing unrelated fields. This proves the released-store → Doctor → current-service boundary, not a full native-package upgrade. No jobs or Gateway ran. Existing dependencies were reused without installing packages or overriding install policy.

Focused validation: **154 tests pass across separate runs**, not one all-green monolithic suite: recovery 43, recovered final effects 3, provider-review final effects 5, automation transports 15, scheduled-session custody 15, cron-context replay 13, and CI source-owner routing 60. Recovery effects took 43.69 s including compilation (3.97 s summed cases); the new provider-review cases initially took 45.81 s including compilation. Scheduled-session custody took 10.79 s (12.44 s wrapper). CI execution seconds for these new files are pending.

The first combined replay exposed the extracted recovery file running in an incompatible thread pool (host database broker unavailable). Registering it in the existing database-worker lane resolves that setup failure; the corrected effects shard and routing suite both pass. The repaired files pass focused lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the affected type graphs. Regression check: substituting the pre-generalization job target (`a43f5e814047`) and original provider-review handler (`d482d7616512`) produces four intended failures: missing recovered native owner authority and native continuation denial. Restoring the reviewed repair makes **8/8 pass**, Vitest 41.34 s / wrapper 45.61 s. No setup failure is counted as negative authority proof.

Fresh independent **autoreview, Codex, P0–P2**, covers reviewed head `697096f44c77820f7fde61cc005bd425a8227513` → the complete local repair snapshot, including untracked test files and the database-lane registration: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. It inspected supplied source/context and did not execute project tests. The helper's first preflight refused a shared temporary directory; the completed run used the OS-reported private macOS temporary directory without disabling isolation.

Test growth is allocated explicitly: **463 net LF lines** across the complete PR for distinct admission, recovery/continuation, forbidden-caller, revocation, and final-effect contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged. Existing authority and persistence owners are reused; the handler-type dependency is removed and no parallel policy registry is introduced.

**Upgrade-proof side effect:** Doctor also cleaned 3,387 recognized obsolete files in its shared temporary archive-read cache. Source inspection confirms it targets that cache, not original archives; no live Gateway or configuration changed. No further Doctor runs were performed.



**Inherited test-line ratchet failure (not waived or masked):** the clean merge base `d482d7616512` independently reports `6,552,043` LF lines against ceiling `6,551,994` (**49 over**, delta 0). This head reports `6,552,506` against `6,552,457` (**49 over**, delta +463). The PR adds exactly 463 lines and 463 allocation credits; it does not increase the inherited debt. The ratchet command still exits nonzero on this positive-delta branch. No unrelated tests, scalar baseline, or extra debt credit were changed. Broad exact-head CI remains to be assessed.

## Updated real-app proof — November 6, 2026

**Main proof uses the normal, web-backed Mac app interface, not the experimental native SwiftUI chat.** Experimental-native results from earlier preparation are supplemental only and are not substituted for the normal-interface results below.

### Provenance and signing

- Gateway and served Control UI built from proof head `697096f44c77820f7fde61cc005bd425a8227513`.
- Real macOS client: installed version `2026.10.4`, source metadata `3561a19c06ec0294c022b7b0ca3829a073f52ef5`, copied into a separate proof bundle and explicitly ad-hoc re-signed. Its client revision is older than the Gateway; this is not an exact-head native-package build claim.
- Proof bundle identifier: `local.openclaw.pr194443-installed-proof`. `codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2` reported **valid on disk** and **satisfies its Designated Requirement**.
- The normal embedded UI authenticated through the native bridge as `client=openclaw-macos`, `mode=ui`, `role=operator`; it was not replaced by a script claiming that client name. The real model invoked the production OpenClaw automation tool through a normal `chat.send` turn.
- Separate loopback Gateway, state, workspace, app profile, and disabled synthetic job. No LinkedIn or other external automation ran. The existing operator Gateway and installed `/Applications/OpenClaw.app` bundle were not modified or restarted.

**Signing constraint:** Ad-hoc signing is the signing path available to this contributor. This evidence does not claim Developer ID/distribution signing, notarization, or TCC permission persistence. Please assess the observed native authentication/authorization chain on that basis; if distribution signing itself is a material dependency, identify it and route that additional verification to a maintainer with distribution-build access.

### Normal-interface observations

| Scenario | Actual observed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Native admin manages another conversation’s job | The real model listed disabled jobs, updated the foreign-conversation fixture through the automation tool, and read it back. Independent persisted-state read showed `STANDARD-MAC-ADMIN-PR194443-VERIFIED`; the job remained disabled. |
| Explicit `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` | Through the same normal Mac app interface, the real model attempted the foreign-job update and received `cron job not found`. Persisted job state was unchanged and disabled. |
| Native device revoked during an in-flight delayed update | The model’s tool-orchestration call awaited a 60-second timer before attempting its write. The supported `devices revoke` CLI revoked the proof device’s operator authority while that run was active. The Gateway terminated the original run with `operator source authority is no longer active` and stopped model fallback because the caller signal was aborted. After the timer deadline, independent persisted-state comparison showed the entire job unchanged; the attempted new marker was absent. |

Sanitized Gateway receipt for the passing revocation run:

```text
21:21:47 [gateway] device token revoked device=<proof-device> role=operator
21:21:47 [agents/harness] error="operator source authority is no longer active"
21:21:47 [diagnostic] runId=9e343352-93e6-4fa3-8a2b-6230ba6378d9 durationMs=39586
21:21:47 [model-fallback/decision] stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted
post-deadline persisted job comparison: unchanged=true; enabled=false
```

The shared-bootstrap-token app subsequently reconnected/re-paired. That did **not** restore the original run’s authority or persist its attempted update. This live case proves in-flight revocation before the delayed tool call; it is not represented as a write already held inside Cron’s commit guard.

Earlier revocation setup attempts used an insufficiently scoped generic RPC client or omitted the explicit credential required by a URL override. Those attempts are **not** counted as negative proof; an earlier timer completed without a successful revocation. The passing case above used the supported device-management CLI with explicit, disposable proof-Gateway credentials. No credential values or private endpoints are included here.

### Additional live scope-demotion proof — November 6, 2026

A second disposable loopback fixture used the same PR-head Gateway and the identified installed `2026.10.4` client, copied to bundle `local.openclaw.pr194443-demotion`, ad-hoc signed and strictly signature-verified. The **normal web-backed Mac app interface** was used; experimental native experience remained disabled.

1. Through a real model turn and the production automation tool, the native admin read a disabled foreign-conversation job, updated its message to `DEMOTION-ADMIN-CONFIRMED`, and read it back.
2. The same turn entered a tool-orchestration call awaiting a **90-second Promise timer** before attempting a second update to `DEMOTED-MUST-NOT-PERSIST`.
3. While that run was active, the supported `devices rotate` CLI narrowed the proof device’s operator token to **`operator.read,operator.write`**, removing `operator.admin`, approvals, questions, and pairing. This was scope demotion, not device removal or token revocation.
4. At **21:43:43 PST**, the Gateway recorded the narrowed scopes and immediately terminated the original run with `operator source authority is no longer active`; fallback stopped with `caller_signal_aborted`. The app subsequently reconnected, but that did not restore the original run.
5. After the original 90-second deadline, an independent Gateway read verified every persisted job field against the pre-demotion tool readback: unchanged, disabled, and no forbidden marker. The CLI list adds only derived `effectiveAgentId` and `status` fields; those are not treated as stored mutations.

This proves **live scope-demotion propagation to an in-flight native-app model run before its delayed tool write**. It does not claim a fresh non-admin model turn, a write already paused inside the Cron commit guard, persistent denial after a new bootstrap-authenticated reconnect, or distribution signing. No live operator Gateway, installed app bundle, or real automation was changed.

## Earlier-head automation final-write boundary proof

Re-executed on `697096f44c77820f7fde61cc005bd425a8227513`:

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

**15/15 passed**; Vitest wall time 66.86 s, wrapper 70.65 s. This in-process suite uses fixture-authenticated connection facts and production admission, automation tools, and Cron handlers. It independently covers admin success, explicit caller-cap denial, native `operator.write` without admin denial, and device revocation while the update is held in Cron validation: resumed final write rejects and stored state is unchanged. It complements, rather than substitutes for, the real-app evidence above.

Earlier same-head focused validation: all **68 recovery/reconnect/session-run checks passed** after correcting a fixture to publish production revocation rather than merely rotate a token. Seven other focused files passed in the preceding broader run. This is combined focused evidence, not one all-green monolithic suite. Core typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Current proof also built the Gateway runtime and Control UI successfully.

Base reproduction and earlier narrow proof remain at `d482d7616512`, `c13ab576c5059102aa143ec3355540bdf2d12422`, and `a43f5e81404718b2e15dd1379bbf885513c967c0`; those are prior-head evidence, not substitutes for the current-head runs above. Independent local read-only review previously found no remaining P0–P2 defects; this is not an autoreview-helper-certified result.

## Remaining boundaries and gates

- A normal-app **non-admin real-model run** remains uncompleted. Non-admin final-write denial is covered by the 15-case production-boundary suite, not claimed as native-app E2E evidence. Live in-flight scope-demotion proof is recorded above.
- No distribution-signed/shipped-package or TCC-persistence proof. The current-head cold Swift build was stopped during dependency download; the app proof used the explicitly identified existing client instead. Broad CI is pending; no exact-head native package build is claimed. The latest ClawSweeper review accepts ad-hoc signing for the demonstrated authentication path and does not require distribution signing from this contributor.
- Maintainer product judgment on native administrator parity and fresh current-head `/allow-security-sensitive-change` approval remain required. This evidence does not grant or bypass them. No merge or live deployment was performed.

Simplification: existing classification, run-authority, and recovery owners are reused; browser identity is not widened and no competing authorization registry is introduced. The previously recorded test allocation covers admission plus restoration/revocation, reconnect, provider review, and native mention boundaries.

prs.title: fix(update): a killed Doctor's command reservation fences update repair forever
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a signal that kills Doctor while it is about to start a command leaves the Gateway stopped, and `openclaw update repair` refuses forever with `Another update executor owns this installation`.

## User Impact

The Gateway comes back on its own after an interrupted update in this state; when the updater died too, `openclaw update repair` restores it. Nothing else clears this state today: not repair, not a reboot, and the update's own message said repeating repair cannot help.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Problem

Doctor records a durable command reservation, starts the command, then binds the command's PID to the reservation. A kill between those steps leaves a `reserved` lease with no process identity. `managedCommandUnsettled` treated every unbound reservation as unsettled forever, so it fenced the installation permanently, including after a reboot. The update then stayed `doctor-processes-unsettled`, data-at-risk.

Reproduced natively on base `2a2cd293145` with Doctor held inside `reserve()`:

```
Doctor processes remain unsettled, data-at-risk. PIDs/process groups: 35532; 1 spawn reservations lack a process identity.
unit=inactive; no OpenClaw process left
openclaw update repair (twice): Another update executor owns this installation.
```

### Fix

One rule at the owner of the fence (`managedCommandUnsettled`): a reservation closes when its spawner is proven dead and no same-account process born within 15 s after reservation remains, other than the settling process's own ancestors and workers. The command can only have started in that window, and a dead spawner starts nothing new, so an empty census stays true. Unreadable start times and any inspection error other than disappearance keep custody.

- Reclamation, release and Doctor settlement all use that rule.
- Doctor settlement retries past that window, about 20 s and only in this state, so a poller's next short-lived child cannot refuse it.
- Darwin uses `ps`, because the sealed update helper has no native addon.
- `command-reservation-census.ts` joins the PR wrapper inventory, which bundles this custody code.
- A live Doctor, a bound command still running and a process born in the window still refuse, and the refusal now names the next step.

### Rejected alternatives

An environment marker on spawned commands (the first version, also native-proven). Reservations from shipped releases carry no marker, so a new reader needs a discriminator, and the lease schema is strict: a new field would make older published drivers reject the shared lease database. Unreadable environments (hardened macOS binaries, non-dumpable Linux processes) also leave it unable to prove absence. Birth time needs neither.

### Accepted edge cases

- A command that outlives the 15 s window, forks a worker and then exits leaves a worker born outside the window, which the census does not see. It takes a kill in the instant between spawn and bind plus a Doctor command that daemonizes that late; Doctor's commands are short-lived tools.
- A long-lived unrelated process started within seconds of the reservation holds custody until it exits or the machine reboots. The refusal is explicit and the safe direction.

## Evidence

Native, Crabbox AWS Linux, systemd, published-shape install -> relabelled build, Doctor stalled inside `reserve()`:

| Scenario | Base `2a2cd293145` | `80bcf95827f` (later commits only add the PID 1 guard and Darwin uid parsing) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SIGTERM, Doctor SIGKILLed with a reservation unbound, updater alive | exit 143, unit inactive, `doctor-processes-unsettled`, repair refused twice | exit 143 after 39 s, unit active and ready, no leases left; output names `openclaw update repair` for deferred maintenance |
| Doctor SIGKILLed alone, updater alive | not run | exit 1 after 41 s, unit active and ready |
| Updater tree and Doctor SIGKILLed | not run separately | repair first refused while a process born in the window existed, second try `Managed Gateway started and verified` (on `6dbf4a680be`) |

Regression lanes on `6dbf4a680be`; the production changes after it are the Darwin census, retry typing, refusal wording, wrapper inventory and a PID 1 guard, none changing the Linux settlement path these lanes exercise: SIGTERM at Doctor rolled back healthy in 146 s; SIGTERM at finishing healthy in 54 s; #191201 managed kill points healthy at +130 s, +185 s and +180 s with no recovery rows.

Doctor was instrumented only to stall inside `reserve()` so the kill lands deterministically. These lanes are Linux. On Darwin, `command-reservation-census.test.ts` runs against the real `ps` on a Mac and caught a defect this PR now fixes (below), but no native update ran on macOS.

Regression tests: `src/infra/update-managed-command-custody.test.ts` (helper death with a live candidate stays busy and the reservation closes once none remain; red on base, because it stays busy), `src/infra/update-doctor-process-custody.test.ts` (a slot whose reservation already retired settles; red on base), `src/process/command-reservation-census.test.ts` (a real child is a candidate only within its window; other accounts' and earlier processes are not).

Review: `$autoreview` scoped-clean. Independent Codex review raised and this head fixes: inspection errors treated as absence, Linux zombie leaders with live threads, too short a window against lease admission waits, the sealed helper lacking the native census, retries missing reservations with no pending slot, and a settling process running as PID 1, where every process descends from it and the census would come back empty. Running the census on a real Mac also caught rows for accounts printed with a negative uid (`nobody` is `-2`), which made every Darwin census fail closed; Codex then caught that such rows must compare unsigned when the updater itself runs as `nobody`. It also raised spawns delayed past the window and workers forked after it would escape the census; declined as the accepted edge above, because the spawn is in the same tick as the last reservation write and the window already covers lease admission waits.

Refs #164800
