issues.title: Custom image-generation provider: reference_images silently ignored (no /images/edits path)
issues.body:
## Summary

`generate_image` accepts `reference_images`, but the `custom` OpenAI-Images provider (nanobot-ai) drops them unilaterally and still returns a fresh, unrelated image. A user asking for an edit gets the wrong result, with no error signal.

## Where

`providers/image_generation.py`, `CustomImageGenerationClient.generate`:

```python
if reference_images:
    logger.warning(
        "Custom image generation does not support reference images; "
        "ignoring {} reference image(s) for {}",
        len(reference_images),
        model,
    )
```

Generation then proceeds without the references.

## Why it matters

Dynamic connections exist precisely so any OpenAI-Images-compatible endpoint can serve image generation, including self-hosted/local backends (in my case a thin OpenAI-Images shim in front of ComfyUI). The Images API has a standard edit surface for this exact shape: multipart `POST {api_base}/images/edits` (image file(s) + prompt, `response_format=b64_json`, `size`, `n`). As implemented, a custom connection can generate but cannot edit, even when the backend supports editing.

UX consistency note: the sibling Ollama client raises `ImageGenerationError` when given references (explicit refusal), while the custom client logs a warning and silently produces an unrelated image, which is the worse of the two behaviors.

## Suggested direction (design question)

1. Implement: when `reference_images` is non-empty, call multipart `POST {api_base}/images/edits` instead of `/generations`; backends without edit support surface their 404/405 cleanly.
2. Fail explicitly first: raise when references are passed (consistent with the Ollama client), then implement the edits path as a follow-up.

Either is an improvement over silently returning an unrelated image.

## Tested scope (single use case)

One setup validated end to end: a local shim exposing OpenAI-Images-style endpoints in front of ComfyUI 0.44.0 running Qwen-Image-2.1 Turbo.

- Text-to-image generation through the custom client works today.
- A one-reference edit (instruction-style img2img, about 12 s/image) works when driven manually against the shim edit endpoint (`{prompt, image: b64}`), but is unreachable through the tool because of the gap above.

Not tested: other custom providers, real-OpenAI multipart subtleties, size/aspect mapping differences. There may be complications I am unaware of, hence an issue-first discussion rather than a PR.

## Version

nanobot-ai 0.4.1 (deployed via [orrinwitt/nanobot-docker](https://github.com/orrinwitt/nanobot-docker))

issues.title: bug(feishu): file attachments sent together with text (post message "files" array) are silently dropped

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When a user sends text and one or more files together in a p2p chat, the Feishu client delivers them as a **single `post` (rich text) message** whose attachments ride in a top-level `files` array. The Feishu channel parses only the `content` rows of that payload — `_extract_post_content()` handles `text / a / at / code_block / img` tags — and never reads `files`. The attachment's `file_key` is therefore **silently discarded**: the agent only ever receives the caption text, and there is no log line, no placeholder, and no warning. As far as nanobot is concerned, the file never existed.

The standalone `msg_type="file"` path already has download logic (`_download_and_save_media`), and the resource API itself works for regular files — only the combined text+file (`post`) form is unhandled. This is the form Feishu produces whenever a caption accompanies the file.

**Actual behavior**

Silently dropped. (Observed in production on three separate occasions, 2026-10-28 / 11-02 / 11-05.)

**Evidence** (real payload, identifiers redacted)

Caption + PDF sent as one message:

```json
{"title": "",
 "content": [[{"tag": "text", "text": "see attached PDF"}]],
 "content_v2": [[{"tag": "text", "text": "see attached PDF"}]],
 "files": [{"file_key": "file_v3_00175_********",
            "file_name": "notice.pdf", "is_folder": false}]}
```

Calling the resource API directly with our app's `tenant_access_token`:

```
200 OK | 149,387 bytes | Content-Type: application/pdf
```

So permissions and the download path are fine — only the parsing is missing.

A ready-to-review patch with tests is on my fork: [`zhang-li-cs/nanobot@fix/feishu-post-files`](https://github.com/zhang-li-cs/nanobot/tree/fix/feishu-post-files) (commit `5c0c550`, based on `main` @ `12c7d11`).

Folder case (`is_folder: true`): the same call fails with HTTP 500 `{"code": 40009}` — folders are not downloadable via the API, which is why the fix must degrade gracefully rather than attempt the download.

**Root cause**

`nanobot/channels/feishu/runtime.py`:

- `_extract_post_content()` extracts text/images from `content` rows only; it never looks at the top-level `files` array.
- the `msg_type == "post"` branch of `_on_message()` therefore never sees the attachments.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a p2p chat with the bot (Feishu desktop client).
2. Type a caption (e.g. `see attached`) **and** attach a file (e.g. a PDF); send as one message. (Same for a folder.)
3. Observe: the agent receives only the caption; nothing lands in `~/.nanobot/media/feishu/`; no download attempt appears in the logs.

### Expected Behavior

The attachment is downloaded through the same API the channel already uses for `msg_type="file"`:

```
GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/{message_id}/resources/{file_key}?type=file
```

saved to the channel media dir, and passed to the agent as media with a path placeholder. For folders — which the resource API rejects — a visible fallback placeholder instead of silence.


### Relevant Logs

```shell
No log output at all — the attachment is dropped silently with no log line, which is part of the reported behavior.
```

### nanobot Version

0.3.5 (PyPI) — also reproduced on main @ 12c7d11 (2026-11-07)

### Python Version

3.14.4

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (self-hosted, no container)

### Channel / Platform

Feishu (Lark) — WebSocket long-connection mode, p2p chat, streaming enabled

### LLM Provider

xiaomi_mimo

### Model

mimo-v2.6-flash

### Browser

_No response_

### Connection

_No response_

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml
Default feishu channel config (streaming: true). Bug is config-independent.
```

### Additional Context

**Proposed fix** (patch available, 78 lines, single file)

1. Add a module-level `_extract_post_attachments(content_json) -> (files, folders)` that mirrors `_extract_post_content()`'s three payload shapes (direct / localized / `post` envelope), skips entries without a usable `file_key`, and separates regular files from folders (`is_folder: true`).
2. In the `post` branch of `_on_message()`:
   - download each regular file via the existing `_download_and_save_media("file", ...)` path (reuses current naming/sanitizing/error handling);
   - for folders, append a visible placeholder such as
     `[folder: <name> — folders cannot be downloaded via the Feishu API; ask the user to send a zip archive]`.

No signatures of existing functions change; the reply-context extraction path is untouched.

**Tests**

New `tests/channels/test_feishu_post_files.py` — 8 cases: direct / localized / envelope payload shapes, folder fallback, entries missing `file_key`, folder without `file_name`, empty payload, and a regression guard that caption extraction still works alongside files. `ruff check` clean; full `tests/channels` run shows zero new failures vs. the clean-`main` baseline in the same environment.

**Related issues / PRs** (checked — none of them cover this path)

- #1361 (merged) only added the `{"post": {...}}` wrapper shapes to `_extract_post_content()`; it never reads the top-level `files` array.
- #1137 (open) extracts `img` tags *inside* the post `content` rows — also not the `files` array.
- #909 / #986 and #486 (merged) implemented the standalone `msg_type="file"` download path — the one this fix reuses.
- No open issue or PR handles attachments riding in a `post` message's `files` array.

I have a working patch (78 lines, single file) plus the test suite ready. Per CONTRIBUTING.md PRs are accepted from collaborators only — I'd be glad to open the PR if invited, or to hand over the patch/adjust the approach to maintainer preference. Happy to provide redacted raw payloads or traces if that helps triage.

issues.title: DeepSeek Chat Completions: image tool results are sent in an unsupported message role
issues.body:
Checked main at `3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033`.

## Contract and mismatch

DeepSeek's [vision guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/vision#使用限制) states that images are supported **only in `user` messages** for Chat Completions. In contrast, its [Responses guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/responses_api#image-input) explicitly supports images in `function_call_output.output`.

With `deepseek-flash` and an explicit Chat Completions preset, reading an image through `read_file` produces this next-request shape:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "tool_call_id": "call_image",
  "name": "read_file",
  "content": [
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}},
    {"type": "text", "text": "(Image file: ...)"}
  ]
}
```

The image remains in the unsupported `tool` role rather than being adapted to the Chat contract. This also reaches the same request builder after a Responses-to-Chat fallback; it is not a claim that the default Responses path is broken.

## Verification and impact

Offline reproduction used the actual `AgentRunner`, `ReadFileTool`, OpenAI SDK and `httpx.MockTransport`, with a locally generated 1×1 PNG and `ModelAPICapabilities(("chat_completions",), "chat_completions")`:

1. The first mocked model response calls `read_file`.
2. The captured second HTTP request contains the image under `role="tool"`, as above.
3. When the mock rejects that request with HTTP 400 according to the documented role restriction, nanobot retries with **no images** and can finish normally without the requested visual input.

As a control, converting the same history through the Responses builder retains the image as `function_call_output.output[input_image]`.

No live DeepSeek request was made. The unsupported request shape and local fallback behavior are verified; the actual service's response/error wording was not tested.

## Source

- [nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py:319–325](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py#L319-L325): image reads return native image blocks.
- [nanobot/agent/runner.py:543–565](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/agent/runner.py#L543-L565): tool results are appended with the `tool` role.
- [nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py:589–682](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py#L589-L682): the Flash image-capable path preserves that content without moving images to a supported role.
- [nanobot/providers/base.py:1750–1794](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/providers/base.py#L1750-L1794): error recovery retries after removing image input.

Could you adapt image tool results to the selected API's supported shape rather than relying on image-stripping recovery?

issues.title: Bug: /goal message produces dozens of repeated replies when waiting for user's answer

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ### Bug Description ### Summary A single /goal message produced dozens of near-identical replies, all sent while the agent was waiting for an answer from the user. It ended only when the user intervened, or when the model finally recognised as a system loop and marked the goal cancel. The trigger is a goal in active state plus a final response that waits on the user, which is typically a question back to them. nanobot then re-prompts the model to "continue working toward the objective and loops. The model has no substantial work to do (it needs the answer) and cannot mark the goal complete (the objective is unmet), so it rephrases the same message. Every rephrase is a visible reply. That re-prompt is exempt from the brake that limits ordinary mid-turn injections: `_MAX_INJECTION_CYCLES` is only advanced for real user injections, so the goal continuation never advances it (`nanobot/agent/runner.py`, `_try_drain_injections`). What is left is max_iterations within a turn, and `_MAX_GOAL_CONTINUATION_ROUNDS` across turns. ### Impact - A single user message can burn the whole per-turn iteration budget (`max_iterations`), and `maybe_continue_turn` then schedules further turns until `_MAX_GOAL_CONTINUATION_ROUNDS` is spent, so one message can maximally cost roughly `max_iterations × 13` requests. - Every reply and re-prompt is appended to session history, so context and cost keep growing. - This is agent-loop behavior, so it is channel-independent. ### Steps to Reproduce **On a real channel.** The goal needs several rounds of tool work, and something the model will want clarified afterwards. 1. Send `/goal plan a two-week Rust study schedule, write it to workspace/rust-plan.md, then follow up on my progress daily` 2. Let it finish its first round of work. It then asks a question ("which day do you want to start?") — the loop begins there, with no further input from user. e.g. ### Expected Behavior A turn that has stopped making substantial progress should be bounded, rather than re-prompting the model and replying to the user until the budget is gone. The goal itself can stay active when the objective is genuinely unfinished - but it should not stand in the way of the user's next message, whether that message continues the goal or changes the subject. ### Relevant Logs ```shell ``` ### nanobot Version 0.3.0 ### Python Version 3.11 ### Operating System Linux ### Channel / Platform Telegram ### LLM Provider DeepSeek ### Configuration (Optional) ```yaml ``` ### Additional Context _No response_

prs.title: feat(settings): check sandboxes and configure trusted launchers
prs.body:
## Summary

Make sandbox setup easier to inspect without weakening command isolation.

- Add an explicit, gateway-owned sandbox check. It uses temporary files and the production launcher resolver and wrapper. It does not call a model or edit existing workspace files.
- Add `tools.exec.sandboxLauncher` for protected, nonstandard installations. Overrides must be absolute executable files with root-owned, non-writable ancestors, outside agent-writable roots. The gateway resolves symlinks and rechecks each command. Empty values retain the existing system lookup.
- Reuse the settings controls and CSS for isolation selection, saved-configuration status, translated errors, path editing and restart feedback. Confirm before turning isolation off. Do not run checks when opening settings.
- Show a dismissible chat notice for known launcher failures. The notice keeps input focus and drafts, and links to the relevant sandbox setting. It does not install a package, retry a command or reduce isolation. Repeated instances of the same issue stay dismissed for the turn. Opening history does not replay warnings.
- Add three interactive production-component examples: missing launcher, protected-installation rejection and startup failure. Include all ten interface languages.
- Preserve configuration defaults, aliases and the protocol-1 baseline. The optional `webui.sandbox-settings.v1` capability gates new controls. Older compatible hosts retain their existing editor. Windows remains unsupported for these Unix sandbox backends.
- Resolve saved `${VAR}` references with runtime rules while preserving their original text on disk. Missing references remain unavailable. Unrelated provider secrets do not block sandbox editing.

Missing or rejected Unix launchers still fail closed. This change does not change host permissions, trust arbitrary PATH entries, or modify model prompts and tool parameter schemas. The new error code is optional display-event metadata; the model-facing tool result retains its existing text.

## Verification

Current head: `2074a77165f0528c5a0af2836266bba2888694ae`, containing main at `5888791dc`. Its [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42396114622) is running. Earlier green checks do not establish this head's CI result.

- Focused Python tests passed for launcher rejection, normal command exits, registry hints and AgentRunner progress. The runner test checks that the model receives the same tool result while the display event retains its error code.
- Additional sandbox, shell, saved-settings and wire regression tests passed locally. Native macOS Seatbelt execution and temporary-file isolation checks passed. Timeout/cancellation cleanup and unchanged files after rejected patches remain covered.
- Frontend tests passed for live-only notices, dismissal, fresh-turn failures, stale host/turn events, old-host fallback, retained drafts, translated errors and deep-link focus. Restart-state changes do not reclaim focus.
- Browser tests passed at 390px and 1440px, with light/dark and reduced-motion cases. Notices share the composer's rendered edges and have no horizontal overflow.
- A real isolated gateway and WebUI exercised actual tool failure, notice display, settings navigation, return with an unsent draft, rejected path, save, manual check, restart/reconnect, retained history and successful command execution. The model endpoint was a loopback fixture; no user data or external provider credentials were used.
- Python Ruff/BasedPyright, import boundaries, frontend lint/typecheck, localization checks and production build passed locally.

The previous head's first Windows CI attempt hit an existing settings-service timeout while reading usage SQLite (`database is locked`). Its focused tests and one failed-job rerun passed without source, assertion or timeout changes. That result is historical, not evidence for the current head.

## Limits

The sandbox check is a basic test in a disposable workspace, not a full security audit or a guarantee that every application works with the configured mounts. The fnOS package and kernel restrictions still need native acceptance. A writable app-data installation needs a protected launcher from the package maintainer; the reported NAS path is not assumed safe.

The notice requires a known live launcher error and follows existing progress delivery settings. Ordinary stderr and nonzero command exits do not prove a sandbox failure and do not trigger this guidance. Use the explicit sandbox check for other failures. Native package and Windows installer jobs are not selected by this change's CI matrix.

Keep this PR draft. Do not merge or publish a release.

prs.title: feat(provider): support OpenRouter native image generation API
prs.body:
## Reason for the Change

OpenRouter now provides image generation through its native Images API. Nanobot needs to use this API so OpenRouter image generation remains compatible with the current service and can expose more image-generation providers and models through the existing `generate_image` workflow.

## Summary

Update the OpenRouter image-generation client to use OpenRouter's native image API instead of the previous chat-completions image flow.

The implementation:

- Sends generation requests to `POST /api/v1/images`.
- Looks up model capabilities through `GET /api/v1/images/models`.
- Sends `aspect_ratio` and `resolution` only when the selected model advertises the requested values.
- Sends reference images using OpenRouter's native `input_references` format.
- Decodes `data[].b64_json` responses into nanobot image data URLs.
- Preserves a valid response `media_type` when one is returned.
- Keeps provider configuration and the existing `generate_image` tool interface unchanged.

The implementation was tested with these OpenRouter models:

- `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`
- `meta/muse-image`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-lite`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-4.5`
- `black-forest-labs/flux.2-pro`
- `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality`

## Testing

- `pytest tests/providers/test_image_generation.py -q`
  - Result: 99 passed in 0.82s

The suite covers:
- Native `POST /api/v1/images` requests.
- `GET /api/v1/images/models` capability discovery.
- Supported and unsupported aspect-ratio and resolution values.
- `extraBody` overrides.
- Native reference-image inputs.
- Base64 response decoding and returned media types.
- Capability-lookup failures and responses without images.
- Missing OpenRouter API keys.

## Compatibility and Rollout

Existing OpenRouter provider credentials, image-generation settings, and the `generate_image` tool remain unchanged. Models that do not advertise a requested aspect ratio or resolution receive a request without that optional field, allowing the model to use its default behavior.

prs.title: fix(agent): bound sustained-goal continuation when the turn goes idle
prs.body:
## Summary

Bound repeated text-only continuation of an active sustained goal. Previously, each final answer could trigger another automatic "continue" nudge even when the model was waiting for user input, repeating replies until the iteration budget was exhausted.

- Allow at most two consecutive automatic nudges without tool execution, carrying the count across internal runner slices.
- Reset the idle budget when new user input is consumed or tools execute. Pending user input still takes priority over the idle guard.
- End the idle turn without marking its goal complete; the active goal remains available for a later user message.
- Document the behavior and cover slice boundaries, counter transport, malformed metadata, and isolation from ordinary user and recovery turns.

Fixes #5256.

## Scope and compatibility

This is a runner liveness guard, not semantic progress detection. Tool executions reset the count even when they return errors, and existing iteration and goal-continuation limits still apply. The initial answer plus two nudges can produce up to three text-only answers before the turn ends.

Goal admission, tool argument schemas, recurring-task routing, and saved goal records are unchanged. Ambiguous goals should still be clarified before admission, and recurring work belongs in cron/reminders. No data migration or configuration change is required.

## Validation

- Synced with current `main` while retaining the contributor's commits.
- 205 focused tests passed across runner continuation, loop integration, session continuation, user injections, recovery, runner core, turn persistence, and cancellation context.
- Ruff on all changed Python files and `git diff --check` passed.
- No live model calls or private session data were used. No WebUI changes.

prs.title: feat(providers): add Standard Compute as an OpenAI-compatible gateway provider
prs.body:
## What changed

Adds Standard Compute as a built-in OpenAI-compatible gateway provider. I work on Standard Compute.

Standard Compute is an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible gateway; monthly plans with a fixed compute budget.

- `nanobot/providers/registry.py`: `standardcompute` `ProviderSpec` after `edenai`, set up the same way: `backend="openai_compat"`, `is_gateway=True`, `env_key="STANDARDCOMPUTE_API_KEY"`, `detect_by_base_keyword="stdcmpt"`, `default_api_base="https://api.stdcmpt.com/v1"`. There is no `detect_by_key_prefix` because keys use the generic `sk_live_` prefix.
- `request_apis=("chat_completions",)` only. The gateway also serves `/v1/responses`, but it is stateless and rejects `previous_response_id`, so this PR doesn't advertise it.
- Model IDs are sent unchanged. `standardcompute` routes each request to one of the models enabled in the account. Exact IDs such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` pin a single model.

issues.title: Desktop: AuthError invalid_provider ('Unknown provider') is rendered as 'API key rejected' with an Update API key button
issues.body:
## Summary

When a session's pinned model references a provider name that is no longer registered in config, the Desktop chat shows the red **"AI 服务 拒绝了你的 API 密钥"** panel (title in the user's locale; English equivalent: "The AI service rejected your API key — saved key is invalid or revoked") with an **"Update API key"** button. The embedded terminal block correctly shows the real cause:

```
Unknown provider 'sohuplus'. Check 'hermes model' for available providers,
or run 'hermes doctor' to diagnose config issues.
Your request was not processed.
```

So the user is told to fix their API key when the API key is perfectly fine — the failure is provider-name resolution (here: a custom relay that had been re-registered under a different name; stale per-session model pins in `state.db` kept the old provider name).

## Repro

1. Register a custom provider (e.g. `providers.newapi`) and pin a session's model to it via the Desktop picker.
2. Rename / remove that provider registration while keeping the session's pinned `model_config` (`sessions.model_config` retains `"provider": "<old name>"`).
3. Send a message in that Desktop session.

## Actual

Red auth-error panel: "AI 服务 拒绝了你的 API 密钥 / 已保存的密钥无效或已被撤销" + **Update API key** + 重试 buttons. Gateway log shows:

```
2026-11-07 19:53:14 WARNING gateway.run: Model resolution failed for session agent:main:local:dm:local-9fdcaa2e...: Unknown provider 'sohuplus'. Check 'hermes model' for available providers, or run 'hermes doctor' to diagnose config issues.
```

## Expected

`AuthError(code="invalid_provider")` should render a distinct "model/provider configuration" error (suggest `hermes model` / `hermes doctor`, or re-picking the model in the picker), not the key-rejected panel. The "Update API key" action is a dead end for this error class.

## Environment

- macOS 27.2, Desktop app (Electron), gateway session key `agent:main:local:dm:...`
- Hermes config with custom OpenAI-compatible relay provider; per-session model pin survives a provider rename.

## Suggested fix

Branch the error UI on the error code: `invalid_provider` (and generally non-401 auth errors) → config-guidance panel; only real upstream 401/403 key rejections → the "Update API key" panel.

issues.body:
### Pre-flight
- [x] Searched open and closed issues/PRs (`model_aliases key_env`, "alias credential", "credential refresh wrong key", "model_override key_env", `_try_refresh_anthropic_client_credentials`, `direct_alias_api_key`, +18 more). Nothing covers this case. Closest:
  - #144960 / #144961: same refresh function, for `fallback_providers` entries
  - #118379: same function, credential-pool sessions
  - #133882: an alias without `base_url` ignores its key at switch time
  - #126533: `--global` persistence
  - Same class as #111267.
- [x] Confirmed on current `main` (`c305aedf`)
- [ ] `hermes debug share`: N/A. Reproduced with the real code paths against a temp `HERMES_HOME`, placeholder keys, no network.

### Bug Description
A `model_aliases` entry can select a second Anthropic account with `key_env`:

    model_aliases:
      alt:
        model: claude-opus-5-5
        provider: anthropic
        base_url: https://api.anthropic.com/v1
        key_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_ALT

`/model alt` resolves the right key (`direct_alias_api_key`). After that, two paths look the credential up again by provider and silently replace it with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`:

1. **Per-request refresh.** `_try_refresh_anthropic_client_credentials` (`agent/client_lifecycle.py:831`) runs before every native Anthropic request and calls `resolve_anthropic_token(model=...)` (line 851). That returns `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or an OAuth token). It differs from the alias key, so the client is rebuilt on the default key. From the first request on, the session runs on the alias's model but the default account.
2. **Gateway restart.** `PERSISTABLE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_KEYS = ("model", "provider", "base_url")` (`gateway/session.py:474`), so nothing records which credential the session chose. `_rehydrate_session_model_override` (`gateway/run_agent_cache.py:149`) then re-resolves credentials for `provider`, which gives the default key.

Same root cause, by code reading (not reproduced on their own):
- `_apply_session_model_override` attaches the provider's credential pool to an override that carries an `api_key` (`run_agent_cache.py:217-222`). A 429 on the alias key can then rotate onto a pool entry (`recover_with_credential_pool`).
- `delegate_task` children and CLI agent rebuilds receive the key value but not where it came from, so their next refresh hits path 1.

Nothing errors. With prompt caching on, cache reads are most of the traffic. In our deployment, the alias key's Anthropic usage report showed only uncached input, while the session's cache reads were billed to the default key's org.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Two Anthropic API keys from different orgs: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_ALT`. Alias config as above.
2. In a gateway chat: `/model alt`, then send a few messages.
3. Anthropic Console → Usage, grouped by API key: the session's usage (including cache reads) is on the default key, not the alias key.
4. Restart the gateway and send another message in the same chat: still the default key.

Code-level, no network (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` = a placeholder ending `ZZZZ`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_ALT` = `ALIAS_KEY`, a placeholder ending `AAAA`):

    agent = AIAgent(model="claude-opus-5-5", provider="anthropic", api_mode="anthropic_messages",
                    base_url="https://api.anthropic.com/v1", api_key=ALIAS_KEY,
                    quiet_mode=True, skip_context_files=True, skip_memory=True)
    agent._try_refresh_anthropic_client_credentials()
    assert agent._anthropic_api_key == ALIAS_KEY   # main: ...ZZZZ

    sanitize_model_override({"model": "claude-opus-5-5", "provider": "anthropic",
                             "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1", "key_env": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_ALT"})
    # main: {'model': ..., 'provider': ..., 'base_url': ...}  (no credential pointer)

### Expected Behavior
A session switched to a `key_env` alias sends that variable's key on every request, through refresh, restart, retries and subagents, until the user switches away. If that key fails (401/429/billing), the error is shown. It must not quietly continue on another account's key.

### Actual Behavior
From the first request after `/model alt`, and again after a restart, requests are sent with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

Not affected on `main`: auxiliary-call retries (compression, titles). `bdf45abd` already ties the aux refresh to the failing key; I checked 401 and 429 against `main`.

### Affected Component
Agent core, Gateway (CLI rebuild path too)

### Root Cause Analysis
The session keeps the key's value but not its source. Every place that rebuilds credentials asks "what is the key for provider `anthropic`?" and gets the default answer.

### Proposed Fix
Tie the session to the env var name:
- Carry `key_env` from the alias through `ModelSwitchResult`, then the persisted session override, then `AIAgent` (`_api_key_env`).
- While a session is tied to it:
  - refresh re-reads only that variable, so a rotated key in `.env` is picked up but the default chain never is
  - no credential pool
  - subagents inherit it only when they run on the parent's key
- `/model` to a non-alias model clears it.

Overlaps #144961: both are early returns in the same refresh function. #144961 remembers the key value; this remembers the variable, which also follows key rotation in `.env`. The two can coexist.

Running this fix in production on a multi-profile gateway: the Anthropic usage report for the alias key matches Hermes' own per-call cache-read counts to within 0.1%.

### Versions
`main` c305aedf · Python 3.14.7 · Linux

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: skills_guard: redirected named-variable existence check falsely flagged as dump_all_env
issues.body:
## Summary

`scan_skill` reports a named-variable existence check with all output redirected to `/dev/null` as `dump_all_env` / high-severity exfiltration. For a community source, that caution verdict makes `should_allow_install` return false.

This is a narrow likely false positive, not a request to trust Superpowers wholesale or weaken installation gates.

## Environment and affected upstream

- Reproduced with installed Hermes Agent v0.23.0, git revision `2bd378ed1b8d6bf2192cb26e0a55ff3091e6bd19`, Linux, Python 3.14.9.
- Actual example: [obra/superpowers systematic-debugging/SKILL.md at reviewed revision](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/22f0b463e7a5e579904dd6211a520321035526f7/skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md#L95).
- This report does not establish behavior on a newer Hermes main revision.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from a Hermes checkout with its Python environment. This writes and scans a Markdown fixture; it does not execute the shell example or read environment values.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from tools.skills_guard import scan_skill, should_allow_install

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    root = Path(directory)
    (root / "SKILL.md").write_text(
        "---\nname: named-env-check-repro\n"
        "description: Minimal named environment existence check.\n---\n"
        "```sh\n"
        'printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" '
        '|| echo "IDENTITY not in environment"\n'
        "```\n"
    )
    result = scan_skill(root, source="https://github.com/obra/superpowers")
    print(result.verdict)
    for finding in result.findings:
        print(finding.pattern_id, finding.severity,
              finding.category, finding.description)
    print(should_allow_install(result))
```

Observed in this minimal fixture:

```text
caution
dump_all_env high exfiltration dumps all environment variables
(False, 'Blocked (community source + caution verdict, 1 findings). Use --force to override.')
```

The same finding occurs at line 95 in the reviewed upstream skill.

## Expected behavior and regression scope

`printenv IDENTITY` requests one named variable, not the entire environment. Both stdout and stderr are discarded, and the subsequent `echo` statements reveal only existence. This example does not dump environment values into the transcript or send them elsewhere.

Please distinguish this specific existence-check form from actual environment disclosure. A fix should retain detection for bare `printenv`, unredirected value exposure where relevant, piping/uploading values to an external destination, and redirection combinations that do **not** actually suppress output. Blanket allowlisting `printenv`, a repository, or all shell redirections would not be appropriate.

## Impact and limits

The finding blocks admission of this community skill under the normal policy. No scanner bypass or default-profile installation was performed. This report is not a full plugin security assessment, compatibility claim, or demonstrated runtime benefit.

Related but different mechanisms:
- #143864: plugin scan scope includes repository files a client does not load.
- #132155: credential-pattern collision inside base64 data.

Opened by Daksh with Hermes assistance, based on a local synthetic reproduction and the pinned upstream source.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a multiplexed `hermes serve` whose launch profile uses the local terminal, opening the Bot Screen of a **Docker-backed** profile from Hermes Desktop fails with "Screen stream ended". The dashboard's display bridge resolves the sandbox with the launch profile's terminal scope instead of the routed profile's, so it looks up the wrong `_active_environments` key and gets a `LocalEnvironment`.

### Steps to Reproduce

Setup: Hermes Agent installed natively, `hermes serve` running as a system service for the `default` profile with `terminal.backend: local`. A second profile `assistant` has `terminal.backend: docker`, `terminal.docker_image: nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:v0.21.7-desktop`, `terminal.container_persistent: true` (default) and `bot_desktop.auto_start: true`.

1. Run `hermes serve` for the `default` profile (local terminal).
2. From Hermes Desktop connected to that server, chat with the `assistant` profile so its Docker sandbox starts, and start its Bot Screen (it comes up inside the container: `Bot Desktop for profile assistant up inside DockerEnvironment on :20`).
3. Open the `assistant` Screen pane in Desktop.

### Expected Behavior

The Screen pane streams the sandboxed Xvnc display.

### Actual Behavior

The pane shows "Screen stream ended". The server logs:

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.) — Bot Screen / display bridge in `hermes serve`, seen from Hermes Desktop.

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A: Hermes Desktop connected to `hermes serve`.

### Debug Report

Not attached: `hermes debug share` would publish this install's config and logs, and the bug reproduces in isolation from the steps above and the snippet under Root Cause Analysis, which shows the wrong task key directly. Happy to share specific log excerpts if useful.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (arm64)

### Python Version

3.14.7 (Hermes-managed)

### Hermes Version

v0.22.2 (stable, d923a5eb487a). `main` still has the same resolution logic (`return _routed_home_task_key(scope.docker_profile_scoped) or "default"` in `tools/terminal_tool.py`).

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```
File "hermes_cli/web_routers/display.py", line 101, in _open_rfb
    relay = _bd_runtime.open_rfb_stream()
File "tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py", line 550, in open_rfb_stream
    return sandbox_host.open_rfb_stream(env, _profile_name())
File "tools/bot_desktop/sandbox_host.py", line 304, in open_rfb_stream
    return streams.open_stream(env, ["python3", "-c", _RELAY, f"{rdir}/rfb.sock"], user=_user_for(env))
File "tools/bot_desktop/sandbox_host.py", line 183, in _user_for
    probe = streams.run_in(env, ["id", "-u", DESKTOP_USER], timeout=15)
File "tools/environments/streams.py", line 104, in run_in
    raise RuntimeError(f"{type(env).__name__} cannot exec argv")
RuntimeError: LocalEnvironment cannot exec argv
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`display._open_rfb()` sets the HERMES_HOME override to the routed profile home and calls `runtime.open_rfb_stream()` → `placement.terminal_environment(create=False)` → `terminal_tool._resolve_container_task_id(None)`. With no session key this goes to `_routed_home_task_key(scope.docker_profile_scoped)`, but `_session_scope()` reads the process-wide bridged `TERMINAL_*` values, which belong to the **launch** profile (local). So `docker_profile_scoped` is `False` and the key becomes `home:<profile home>`, while the sandbox was registered as `profile:assistant` (container label `hermes-task-id=profile_assistant`).

Reproduced in isolation in the same install:

```python
set_hermes_home_override(Path("~/.hermes/profiles/assistant").expanduser())
_is_routed_home(home)                  # True
_session_scope().docker_profile_scoped # False  (launch profile is local)
_resolve_container_task_id(None)       # "home:/root/.hermes/profiles/assistant"
# sandbox container label: hermes-task-id=profile_assistant
```

Host-placed screens (profiles with a local terminal) are unaffected, since they stream from `<home>/bot-desktop/rfb.sock` directly.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

- Resolve the terminal scope from the routed profile's config when a home override is active, so `docker_profile_scoped` matches how the sandbox was keyed; or
- Have the display bridge use the `bot-desktop/sandbox.json` marker it already writes (`backend`, `container`, `docker`) to exec the RFB relay in that container, instead of looking up the live environment by task key.

Related: #128410 and #138044 (same `LocalEnvironment` mis-resolution in other paths).

As a stopgap we wrap `tools.bot_desktop.runtime._sandbox_env` from a local plugin: when the lookup returns a non-Docker environment while `bot-desktop/sandbox.json` names a live Docker container, it returns a `DockerEnvironment` attached to that container (`_container_id` and `_docker_exe` from the marker). With it the stream opens and Xvnc answers `RFB 003.008`.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

## Bug description

`hermes doctor` reports the current active source install's channel record as stale:

```text
⚠ Stale channel record: 4a48d92e3f36e3f8
  (no live install claims 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 — safe to remove update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8)
```

However, `4a48d92e3f36e3f8` is the current install ID, and the active Hermes runtime is using state under that exact install directory.

This appears to be a false positive in `stale_channel_records()`.

## Environment

- macOS
- Hermes update channel: `main`
- Hermes version after reproduction: `v0.21.5+5778.g0a374d1`
- Commit: `0a374d16742`
- Python reported by `hermes doctor`: `3.14.7`
- Install ID: `4a48d92e3f36e3f8`

## Reproduction

Verify the current install ID:

```console
$ hermes update --install-id
4a48d92e3f36e3f8
```

Verify that Hermes is current:

```console
$ hermes update --check
→ Update channel: main
→ Fetching from origin...
✓ Already up to date.
```

Run `hermes doctor`:

```text
◆ Configuration Files
  ✓ ~/.hermes/.env file exists
  ✓ API key or custom endpoint configured
  ✓ ~/.hermes/config.yaml exists
  ✓ Config version up to date (v49)
  ✓ No deprecated config keys or env vars
  ⚠ Stale channel record: 4a48d92e3f36e3f8
    (no live install claims 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 — safe to remove update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8)
```

However, the same `hermes doctor` invocation reports an active runtime staged inside that install ID:

```text
✓ Runtime venv staged
  (~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/environments/<generation>/venv)
  (active in this process)
```

The gateway is also running successfully from the updated installation.

## Install-state directory

The corresponding install-state directory exists and contains `facts.json`:

```text
~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/

.install.lock
.recovery.lock
bootstrap/
environments/
facts.json
pm-runtime/
```

But `install.json` does not exist:

```console
$ test -f ~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/install.json \
    && echo "install.json EXISTS" \
    || echo "install.json MISSING"

install.json MISSING
```

`facts.json` is populated and contains the current staged venv information.

## Suspected root cause

`hermes_cli/update_channel.py::stale_channel_records()` currently determines whether an install ID is `unclaimed` by checking for:

```python
if not (installs_root() / sha16 / "install.json").is_file():
    stale.append((sha16, record, "unclaimed"))
```

The function's comments/docstring also describe `install.json` as the live install-state record.

However, the current source-install/package-management code maintains per-install state in:

```text
~/.hermes/installs/<install-id>/facts.json
```

A repository search shows extensive production use of per-install `facts.json`, while the `install.json` liveness check appears in `stale_channel_records()`.

This means a healthy source installation that has `facts.json` but no `install.json` can be classified as `unclaimed`.

## Local validation

As a diagnostic experiment, I changed only the liveness check from:

```python
if not (installs_root() / sha16 / "install.json").is_file():
```

to:

```python
if not (installs_root() / sha16 / "facts.json").is_file():
```

I also updated the corresponding healthy unit-test fixture from `install.json` to `facts.json`.

With those changes:

1. The false `Stale channel record` warning disappeared from `hermes doctor`.
2. `hermes update --install-id` continued to return `4a48d92e3f36e3f8`.
3. The targeted channel-record tests all passed:

```text
tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel.py::test_doctor_channel_records_are_read_only[missing-missing] PASSED
tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel.py::test_doctor_channel_records_are_read_only[replaced-replaced] PASSED
tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel.py::test_doctor_channel_records_are_read_only[unclaimed-unclaimed] PASSED
tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel.py::test_doctor_channel_records_are_read_only[healthy-None] PASSED

4 passed
```

I then reverted both modified files and removed the temporary test `.venv`, returning the checkout to a clean state.

I subsequently performed a normal `hermes update`, which updated Hermes from:

```text
v0.21.5+5726.g569fd58
```

to:

```text
v0.21.5+5778.g0a374d1 [main @ 0a374d16742]
```

The update completed successfully and created/selected a new runtime generation under the same install ID.

After the update:

```console
$ git status --short
```

returned clean, and:

```console
$ hermes update --check
→ Update channel: main
→ Fetching from origin...
✓ Already up to date.
```

Nevertheless, `hermes doctor` still reports:

```text
⚠ Stale channel record: 4a48d92e3f36e3f8
  (no live install claims 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 — safe to remove update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8)
```

while simultaneously using a runtime under:

```text
~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/environments/<generation>/venv
```

## Expected behavior

An active source install whose install ID matches the channel record and which has valid current install state should not be reported as stale/unclaimed.

In particular, `hermes doctor` should not recommend removing:

```text
update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8
```

when the same ID is returned by:

```console
hermes update --install-id
```

and is actively being used for the current runtime.

## Actual behavior

`hermes doctor` reports the active install ID as stale because:

```text
~/.hermes/installs/<install-id>/install.json
```

does not exist, even though the install has an active `facts.json` and runtime environment.

## Proposed fix

If `facts.json` is now the canonical live-install state marker for source installs, `stale_channel_records()` could use:

```python
(installs_root() / sha16 / "facts.json").is_file()
```

instead of requiring `install.json`.

The associated comments/docstring and healthy test fixture would also need to be updated accordingly.

If `install.json` is still intended to be the canonical liveness marker, then there appears to be a separate lifecycle issue: current source installs/updates are not creating it even though `doctor` requires it to establish liveness.

Either way, the current behavior produces a false-positive stale-channel warning and gives potentially incorrect cleanup advice for the active install.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start from a clean Hermes source checkout on the `main` update channel.
2. Run `hermes update` to update to the latest `origin/main`.
3. Confirm the update completes successfully and the default profile/service is running the new revision.
4. Run:
   `hermes update --install-id`
5. Observe that it returns:
   `4a48d92e3f36e3f8`
6. Run:
   `hermes doctor`
7. Observe that Doctor reports:
   `Stale channel record: 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 (no live install claims 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 — safe to remove update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8)`
8. In the same Doctor output, observe that the active runtime is actually staged under:
   `~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/environments/<generation>/venv`

The warning persists across Hermes updates. After the latest update in this reproduction, Hermes reported itself up to date, but `hermes doctor` still produced the stale-channel warning.

### Expected Behavior

`hermes doctor` should recognize the current install ID `4a48d92e3f36e3f8` as a live install and should not report its update-channel record as stale or recommend removing `update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8`.

### Actual Behavior

`hermes doctor` reports the active install ID as stale:

⚠ Stale channel record: 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 (no live install claims 4a48d92e3f36e3f8 — safe to remove update.installs.4a48d92e3f36e3f8)

However, the same Doctor run reports an active staged runtime under that exact install ID:

~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/environments/dfed288f3ceb4a6992491facc1de51a9/venv

`hermes update --install-id` also returns:

4a48d92e3f36e3f8

The warning therefore appears to be a false positive and, more importantly, recommends deleting the channel record belonging to the currently active install.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
hermes debug share --nous
⚠️  --nous: This uploads your debug bundle to Nous-INTERNAL storage (AWS S3),
    NOT a public paste service. The following is included:
  • System info (OS, Python/Hermes version, provider, which API keys are
    configured — NOT the actual keys)
  • Full agent.log, gateway.log, and desktop.log (up to 512 KB each — likely
    contains conversation content, tool outputs, and file paths), plus
    update.log and desktop-update-handoff.log when present (update/hand-off
    output — the root cause of update failures)

  • The bundle is viewable only by Nous staff (and allowlisted Discord mods)
    via a Google-login-gated viewer.
  • It is NOT a public paste — there is no public URL to the contents.
  • It auto-deletes after 14 days.

Upload debug report? [y/N] y
Collecting debug report...
Uploading to Nous diagnostics storage...

Debug bundle uploaded to Nous (private):
  View URL  https://support.nousresearch.com/diagnostics/0d52676f-2cf1-4c94-aac4-4d24d7c794be

⏱  Auto-deletes after 14 days.

Share this private link with the Nous team — only Nous staff (via Google login) can open it.

Pick up the discussion in:
  GitHub Issues        https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues
  Nous Portal Support  https://portal.nousresearch.com/help
  Discord              https://discord.gg/NousResearch
```

### Operating System

macOS 27.0.1 (Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

Environment note:  `python3 --version`: Python 3.14.8  `hermes --version` reports its runtime as: Python: 3.14.7  `hermes doctor` also reports: Python 3.14.7  Hermes is therefore running with its managed Python 3.14.7 runtime, while the shell's Homebrew `python3` is 3.14.8.

### Hermes Version

v0.21.5+5778.g0a374d1 (2026.9.24) · upstream 0a374d16

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The apparent false positive is in `hermes_cli/update_channel.py`, in `stale_channel_records()`.

The current implementation determines whether an install ID is claimed by checking for:

`installs/<sha16>/install.json`

Specifically, the check is equivalent to:

`(installs_root() / sha16 / "install.json").is_file()`

However, the current package/install-state implementation uses `facts.json` under the install-state directory. The active install can therefore have a valid `facts.json` and active environment while lacking the legacy/expected `install.json`, causing `stale_channel_records()` to classify the active channel record as `"unclaimed"`.

This is consistent with the observed contradiction: Doctor identifies an active runtime under `~/.hermes/installs/4a48d92e3f36e3f8/...` while simultaneously saying no live install claims that same ID.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Update the liveness check in `hermes_cli/update_channel.py::stale_channel_records()` so that it uses the current canonical install-state marker rather than `installs/<sha16>/install.json`.

In the current source layout, `installs/<sha16>/facts.json` appears to be the appropriate marker.

I locally tested replacing the `install.json` check with `facts.json` and updated the corresponding healthy fixture in `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel.py`.

The directly relevant parameterized test then passed all four cases:

- missing -> missing
- replaced -> replaced
- unclaimed -> unclaimed
- healthy -> no stale record

Result: 4 passed.

I restored the checkout afterward and reproduced the original warning again on pristine, fully updated `main`, so the report is based on unmodified upstream code.

issues.title: Public owner-configured plugin outbound delivery API
issues.body:
## Use case and current public-API gap

This follows [teknium1's review of Email Steward on PR150057](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/150057#issuecomment-6714987588). A standalone plugin needs to deliver scheduled private briefs/reminders to a destination explicitly configured by its owner, without importing private send-message helpers or inspecting live adapters.

Returning text from `register_command` and session-bound `ctx.post_message` cover replies to a current conversation. They do not establish authority for a background producer to address an owner-configured private destination after that turn ends.

Could Hermes provide a supported, owner-configured outbound-delivery capability for this case? This is a request for a generic extension seam, not Email Steward logic in core or an unrestricted plugin send API.

## Requested contract

Names and API shape are for maintainers to decide. The useful properties would be:

- The operator explicitly grants a plugin one private destination, transport account, profile and optional thread/scope. The plugin receives an opaque capability, not a gateway, adapter, SDK client or credentials. Runtime model arguments cannot grant an owner, change a destination or select another profile.
- Hermes owns routing and revalidates the grant at the transport-effect boundary, including after queueing, restart, retries, profile changes, unload and revocation. A stale grant must not fall back to another profile, account, parent thread, home channel or destination. Please define the revocation/commit point and any unavoidable in-flight limit.
- Bounded text/media input, backpressure, expiry and cancellation have documented outcomes. Durable plugin obligations are separate from permission to send. Stable occurrence/attempt IDs permit bounded idempotent retries without collapsing distinct identical messages.
- Structured outcomes distinguish blocked-before-attempt, queued, provider-accepted, failed, partial and unknown. A timeout or missing receipt must not become success or an unlimited automatic retry. Provider acceptance is not human delivery/read confirmation. Exact per-attempt status should be observable without parsing console output or inferring a payload receipt from the latest cron-job status.
- Secrets and raw transport state stay host-owned. Diagnostics are bounded and redacted. Concurrent profiles and isolated plugin hosts retain the same ownership semantics; unsupported topologies fail closed explicitly.

## Supported workaround today

The maintainer-approved workaround is a cron job with an explicit `deliver` target. Email Steward's repair uses an owner-created `HERMES_HOME/scripts` wrapper, the public Hermes CLI entrypoint and a registered production operation, with `no_agent` cron delivery of bounded stdout. The plugin records a handoff rather than a send receipt and preserves obligations and uncertain outcomes.

An isolated v0.23.0 source-install qualification has exercised actual scheduler → script → registered CLI → synthetic Gmail grant/HTTP → capture-adapter delivery for a brief, alert and due reminder, plus repeat suppression and delivery failure. This is synthetic production-wiring evidence, not live Gmail/provider acceptance or completed release qualification. No future API implementation is assumed, promised by maintainers, or required to use the cron route.

## Related discussions / deduplication

- #102131 is a non-persistent deferred reply bound to the initiating inbound source; this request covers an explicitly owner-configured private destination for durable background obligations.
- #125448 requests source-backed proactive follow-ups. Its ownership, revocation and outcome requirements overlap and could share a host contract; the configured-destination brief/reminder use case should compose with that work.
- #134330 and #151084 concern outbound policy interception and required-policy lifecycle. They complement, rather than themselves expose, a plugin-originated delivery capability.

Please point this request to an equivalent existing proposal if one was missed. A qualification fixture should cover two profiles with colliding destination/job IDs, regrant/revocation during queued work, restart/unload, thread/account changes, partial sends, cancellation and ambiguous receipts, with no private-helper workaround or real mail activity.

issues.title: Webapp (v0.23.0): Bot Screen pane always shows "Screen packages missing" — webapp host bridge lacks requestProfile
issues.body:
# Upstream bug report draft — v0.23.0 Webapp: Bot Screen pane broken (host bridge missing requestProfile)

> 由呀彪執筆（2026-11-08 12:15 HKT），證據齊料，Eric 掂出 GitHub 用。唔對外發佈前屬內部文件。

## Title
Webapp (v0.23.0): Bot Screen pane always shows "Screen packages missing" — webapp host bridge lacks `requestProfile`

## Environment
- Hermes gateway v0.23.0 (stable, git `2bd378ed1b8`), Linux
- Webapp served by gateway (`webapp.enabled: true`), accessed at `webapp.public_url` via Tailscale
- Browser: iOS Safari / Chrome desktop — same result
- Bot Desktop runtime: running, all binaries present (`installed: true, missing: []`)

## Symptoms
Bots → any bot → Screen pane renders "Screen packages missing / No supported package manager (apt, dnf, pacman) was found on the gateway host" — for EVERY bot (launch profile + named profiles), even though:
- `display.status` answered server-side returns `installed: true, missing: [], running: true` (verified via `tui_gateway.methods_display._display_snapshot()` in the gateway process scope)
- `tools.bot_desktop.runtime.status()` is healthy in the webapp listener's own environment
- apt-get/Xvnc/xfwm4 etc. are all at /usr/bin, PATH of the webapp listener includes /usr/bin

## Root cause (verified in-page)
In the webapp renderer, `window.hermesDesktop` implements ~70 methods but is **missing the entire profile-routing RPC surface**:
```
missing: ["requestProfile", "retainProfile", "retainProfileSocket", "request", "requestForBot"]
implemented includes: getProfileRoutes, getConnectionFor, getGatewayWsUrlFor, api, getAgentRoster, ...
```
`hermes-bots`'s `screen-connection.ts` `displayRequest()` calls `host.requestProfile(route, 'display.status', ...)`
→ `TypeError: host.requestProfile is not a function`
→ pane catch → status store stays at initial `{installed: false, install_command: null}`
→ ScreenNotInstalled renders with the misleading "No supported package manager" line (that line only means `install_command` was null on an EMPTY status object, not that the host lacks a package manager).

## Repro
1. Gateway v0.23.0, `webapp.enabled: true`, sign into the webapp
2. Bots → any bot (launch profile "default" displayed as "Hermes", or any named profile e.g. "researcher") → Screen pane
3. Pane shows "Screen packages missing" despite a healthy Bot Desktop

## Suggested fix direction
Wire `requestProfile`/`retainProfile` (profile-routing RPC) into the webapp host bridge (`window.hermesDesktop`), same contract as the Electron host. The Bots page UI renders fully in the webapp — it's only the routing RPC surface that's absent.

## Extra notes
- Same pane worked in the Desktop app before (Electron host implements requestProfile)
- Misleading error text suggestion: when the status object is the empty/default one (no RPC round-trip happened), show "screen unavailable" instead of the packages-missing install screen — that would have made this diagnosable in seconds

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `complete.path` raises `ValueError` inside `ntpath.relpath` and the whole WS request is dropped — the client gets no completion response at all. It fires whenever the completion candidate set contains an entry literally named `nul` (a reserved Windows device name), because `os.path.join(root, 'nul')` resolves to the device mount `\.\nul`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.7 (`b200f5bc60e3`), Windows 11 (10.0.22631), Python 3.14.9
- 12 occurrences since 2026-10-23, most recent 2026-11-03 08:36 — still live

## Traceback

```
2026-10-23 23:20:12,025 ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws dispatch crash peer=127.0.0.1:51650 id=1670 method=complete.path
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "...\hermes-agent\tui_gateway\ws.py", line 449, in _dispatch_one
  File "...\hermes-agent\gateway\session_controls.py", line 314, in dispatch
  File "...\hermes-agent\gateway\session_complete_path.py", line 39, in complete_path
    return {'items': await asyncio.to_thread(listing)}
  ...
  File "<frozen ntpath>", line 782, in relpath
ValueError: path is on mount '\\.\nul', start on mount 'C:'
```

## Where

`tui_gateway/methods_complete.py`, `_dir_listing_items`:

```python
full = pth.join(search_dir, entry)
rel = pth.relpath(full, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
```

## Repro (no Hermes needed)

```python
import ntpath, os
root = r'C:\Users\Admin'
ntpath.relpath(os.path.join(root, 'nul'), root)
# ValueError: path is on mount '\\.\nul', start on mount 'C:'
```

Any directory holding a file or folder named `nul` triggers it; `con`/`aux`/`com1` do not (they relpath normally).

## Impact

The exception escapes the handler and `_dispatch_one` logs `ws dispatch crash`, so the completion request is lost rather than degraded — typing a word that would complete to `nul` kills completions for that request.

## Suggested fix

Treat an un-relatable path as non-completable (skip the entry), or fall back to the absolute path:

```python
try:
    rel = pth.relpath(full, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
except ValueError:  # Windows device paths (\.\nul) share no mount with the root
    continue
```

A regression test on `@pytest.mark.platforms('win32')` with a `nul` entry in the search dir would pin it.

prs.title: feat(delegation): add delegate_tool_reply explicit delivery channel f…
prs.body:
## Summary

When a subagent produces its result on the same turn it calls a tool (e.g. writing a file then calling `terminal` to clean up a temporary script), the deliverable is silently lost. The conversation loop treats content emitted alongside tool calls as **mid-task narration** (`_last_content_with_tools`, `conversation_loop.py:4613`) rather than a final answer, so it never becomes `final_response`. A later turn where the subagent says something short — like "done, cleaned up, no files changed" — becomes `final_response` and the parent agent only receives that closing comment. The actual work product never reaches the caller.

A concrete example: you delegate an audit task to a subagent. The subagent runs its analysis, writes the full findings as its reply text, then calls `terminal` to delete the throwaway script it used. On the next turn it adds "the task is complete, nothing else to report." The parent agent's summary ends up being just that one-line closer — the entire audit is gone.

This is the failure reported in **#28326** (Lark + streaming) and is the class of bug that **#28453** attempted to address by adding a `content_segments` metadata field to the result dict.

## Why heuristics can't fix this

The existing fallback in `conversation_loop.py:4827-4851` only promotes prior content when **all** tool calls in the turn are housekeeping tools (`memory`, `todo`, `skill_manage`, `session_search`) **and** the follow-up is empty. Two counterexamples prove no content-feature heuristic is sound:

1. **Deliverable + cleanup via a substantive tool:** the subagent writes its result and then calls `terminal` (rm). `terminal` is substantive (not in `_HOUSEKEEPING_TOOLS`), so the fallback never fires even if we relaxed the "empty follow-up" gate.
2. **Short answer + long cleanup:** a subagent whose deliverable is a single bit ("yes/no") followed by a verbose multi-step cleanup sequence. Any length-based heuristic picks the cleanup narration over the answer.

The root cause is an **implicit delivery channel** — `final_response` is a trailing-prose proxy, and the agent loop cannot distinguish "this is the deliverable" from "this is narration before I go clean up." The fix is to give the subagent an **explicit** delivery channel.

## The fix: `delegate_tool_reply`

A leaf-subagent-only tool that hands the deliverable back through a structured tool call. The parent's extraction reads the tool-call args (authoritative) instead of guessing from `final_response`. Falls back to `final_response` when the child never calls the tool — **strictly not-worse-than-status-quo**.

### Extraction priority (`_extract_reply_deliverable`, `delegate_tool.py:1599`)

1. **Spill file** — handler writes `content` to `cache/delegation/delegate_reply-*.txt` and returns the path; extraction reads the file (complete, compression-immune).
2. **Tool-call args** — the in-memory `content` (intact for calls in the protected tail; may be truncated for older calls).
3. **Multi-call concat** — all calls' content joined in order (supports chunking a large deliverable across calls, exceeding single-response `max_tokens`).
4. **No call** → `final_response` unchanged.

When any `delegate_tool_reply` content is assembled, it **replaces** `final_response` as the summary.

## Why this approach over #28453's `content_segments`

**#28453** proposed adding a `content_segments` list to the result dict so callers could access every assistant content block. It was rejected (stale branch, wrong premise) and the approach has a fundamental problem: **no consumer reads it.** The result dict is assembled in `turn_finalizer.py`, not `conversation_loop.py`, and no gateway/platform caller reads `content_segments`. Adding a metadata field with no extraction path doesn't fix the bug — the parent still gets `final_response`.

`delegate_tool_reply` solves this by making the deliverable a **tool call** that the existing extraction layer (`delegate_tool.py:2037`) already scans (the tool-trace builder at `delegate_tool.py:2068-2075` iterates every assistant tool_call). The fix is wired into the real return path, not an unplumbed metadata field.

## Visibility — zero core footprint

`delegation_reply` is a separate toolset, **not** in `CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS` (`tools_config.py:60-86`) so it never appears in `hermes tools` / `/tools`. Unlike the `kanban` toolset (whose tool names *are* in `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` at `toolsets.py:70-77` and are gated by `check_fn` via `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`), `delegation_reply` is **also excluded from `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS`** — no platform bundle ever auto-includes it. `_build_child_agent` (`delegate_tool.py:1166`) appends it to every spawned child's toolset, so the schema only appears on subagents. Ordinary conversations never see the name; users never see a toggle.

This is Footprint Ladder rung 3 (service-gated tool) — narrower than kanban's env-gated rung, since it needs no `check_fn` and no env var. Visibility is purely toolset membership driven per-agent by `enabled_toolsets`.

## Compression resilience

If a long-running subagent triggers context compression, the compressor truncates `tool_call` args > 500 chars for assistant messages outside the protected tail (`context_compressor.py:1411-1429`, `_truncate_tool_call_args_json` at `:435`). This would destroy a large deliverable stored only in args.

The handler spills every call to `cache/delegation/` (mirroring the existing `_spill_summary_to_file` at `delegate_tool.py:1568`), returning the abs path. Extraction prefers the file over possibly-truncated args. The spill dir is mounted read-only into remote backends (Docker/Modal/SSH) via `credential_files._CACHE_DIRS`, so the parent's `read_file` can page through on any backend.

The handler runs **in the agent's Python process** (like `todo`/`memory`), not in the terminal sandbox — so the spill lands on the agent host regardless of whether the child's `terminal` points at a remote Docker/SSH/Modal backend. There is no separate "subagent host"; the child runs in a `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` worker thread inside the parent process.

## System prompt discipline

`_build_child_system_prompt` (`delegate_tool.py:705`) injects a Delivery Discipline block into every child's system prompt, instructing the subagent to call `delegate_tool_reply` with its result and not rely on trailing prose. This is auto-injected — not reliant on the parent hand-writing it in `context`.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tools/delegate_tool_reply.py` (new) | Handler, spill function, schema, `registry.register` under `delegation_reply` toolset |
| `toolsets.py` | `delegation_reply` toolset entry (`:251`); not in `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` |
| `tools/delegate_tool.py` | `_build_child_agent` injects toolset (`:1166`); system prompt discipline (`:705`); `_extract_reply_deliverable` (`:1599`) + extraction wiring (`:2167`) |
| `tests/tools/test_delegate_tool_reply.py` (new) | 17 tests: handler, extraction (no-call/single/multi/truncation/spill), visibility, system prompt |
| `tests/tools/test_delegate.py` | 2 assertions updated for new `delegation_reply` toolset member |

## Scope — what this does NOT fix (intentional)

- **#14894** (persistence precedes transforms in `turn_finalizer.py`) — separate bug, separate PR. The extraction change here is in `delegate_tool.py`, upstream of finalizer persistence.
- **Ordinary-conversation `_last_content_with_tools`** — the general heuristic unsoundness (narration vs. deliverable in normal chats) is a larger design question. This PR scopes to `delegate_task` where the deliverable contract is unambiguous.
- **#6067 / #7968** — pre-tool-call text delivery on non-streaming platforms and premature fallback with substantive tools. These are partially mitigated on streaming/interim-message platforms; this PR doesn't touch the general loop heuristics.

## Test plan

- [x] 17 unit tests pass (`tests/tools/test_delegate_tool_reply.py`)
- [x] 199 existing delegate tests pass (no regressions)
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all changed files
- [x] E2E: spawn a real subagent via `delegate_task` whose goal ends with "clean up tmp files, then reply" — assert parent summary contains the deliverable, not a cleanup comment

prs.title: Plugins and shell hooks can react after each curator run (salvage #43780)
prs.body:
Plugins and shell hooks can now run code right after the skill curator finishes a pass. Before, the only way to notice a curator run was to keep polling `logs/curator/` for new folders.

`post_curator_run` is a new observer hook that fires once per curator pass, after `run.json` and `REPORT.md` are written, with the paths to both.

Salvage of #43780 by @Sahil-SS9 (his commit, authorship kept). This is the scoped-down follow-up we asked for when closing #43113.

## Changes
- `agent/curator.py` fires `post_curator_run(run_dir, run_json_path, report_md_path)` at the end of each pass (after its state is saved, so `hermes curator status` is final when plugins run) through `hermes_cli.lifecycle.invoke_hook` (first-party observers, then plugins and shell hooks; each callback is isolated there, so no extra wrapper).
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py`: added to `VALID_HOOKS`, so `hooks:` shell-script config and `register_hook` accept it.
- Docs: hooks reference (table row + section), plugin guide hook table, observer list.
- `hermes curator run` now registers `hooks:` shell hooks and plugins at startup like `cron run` / `gateway run` (`hermes_cli/main.py::_AGENT_SUBCOMMANDS`); before, a manual pass reached neither.
- The hook fires only when both report files were written; a failed write removes its partial file and fires nothing.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py::_delivery_manager` always joins an in-flight background plugin scan before dispatching. It used to skip the join once the scan had *started*, so a hook fired during startup missed user plugins.

prs.title: X search answers no longer start with the model's 'I'll search for that' narration
prs.body:
When Hermes searched X through xAI, every answer started with the model's own narration ("I'll search X for posts about that.") before the actual result. Now the tool returns only the answer, and the xAI web-search backend no longer turns links cited in that narration into search results.

Ported from https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/11308.

## What changes

- Both xAI readers now take the `message` items of a Responses `output` minus `phase == "commentary"` items, unless commentary is all there is (`tools/x_search_tool.py::_answer_messages`, inline in the plugin since plugins may not import new core helpers per the boundary lint).
- `tools/x_search_tool.py::_extract_response_text` reads the answer from those filtered message items first and uses the top-level `output_text` only when no message text exists. xAI's aggregate `output_text` concatenates the commentary too, so preferring it (as main did) can never drop the narration.
- `plugins/web/xai/provider.py::_collect_output_text` applies the same filter, so commentary text and its `url_citation` annotations stay out of the annotation-paired fallback.
- `x_search`'s `inline_citations` extraction is unchanged.

Root cause: both readers took every `message` item (or the aggregate) without looking at `phase`.

## Before / after (real output)

Live leg: the real `x_search_tool()` and `XAIWebSearchProvider().search()` code paths in a fresh process per tree, making real HTTPS calls to `api.x.ai/v1/responses` with no base-URL override. The repo's `TLSInterceptProxy` (throwaway CA via `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`) routes them to a loopback stub that answers like xAI: a `phase: commentary` message (with one narration citation), a `phase: final_answer` message, and the aggregate `output_text`. 3 stub hits per leg, all on `/v1/responses`.

| surface | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `x_search` `answer` | `"I'll search X for posts about that.\n\nxAI announced Grok 5 on X today."` | `"xAI announced Grok 5 on X today."` |
| xAI web search, final = JSON block | `[("Grok 5", "https://x.ai/news/grok-5")]` | same (JSON path unaffected) |
| xAI web search, final = prose + citation | rows `["https://narration.example/", "https://x.ai/news/grok-5"]` | rows `["https://x.ai/news/grok-5"]` |

## Ours vs theirs

- omp filtered by phase AND added a heuristic for unphased messages (keep the last one plus any earlier one with citations or ≥300 chars), and normalized untyped/null-typed items. That heuristic is their own flagged trade-off ("can still drop short, uncited earlier answer segments").
- This port takes only the explicit-phase rule. Unphased and `final_answer` items are all kept as before, so no answer text is ever dropped on a guess. The rule is two lines, repeated in each reader because the plugin can't import a new core helper.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_x_search_tool.py::test_x_search_answer_excludes_commentary_narration` and `tests/tools/test_web_providers_xai.py::TestXAIProviderSearchJSONPath::test_commentary_message_is_not_parsed_as_results`: red on main, green here.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_x_search_tool.py tests/tools/test_web_providers_xai.py tests/plugins/web/test_web_search_provider_plugins.py tests/scripts/test_boundary_lint.py`: 49 passed, 0 failed. `scripts/check --only health`: ok. ruff: clean.

prs.title: feat(i18n): language packs for the web dashboard (web surface)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Language packs (#126296) let a plugin translate the Python core, the TUI and Desktop with no core change — but not the **web dashboard**: `web/src/i18n/context.tsx` compiles a fixed `TRANSLATIONS` map into the bundle, so every dashboard language needs a core PR that edits `web/src/i18n` and a rebuild. That is why dashboard translations queue up as competing per-language PRs (Vietnamese alone: #38269, #41424, #74538, #76141, #78626; also Polish #148855, Czech #105503, Korean #131043, …).

This PR adds **`web` as a fourth pack surface** and serves it exactly the way Desktop already gets its layer (`apps/desktop/src/i18n/backend-packs.ts` over `i18n.catalog`), so a dashboard translation can ship as a language-pack plugin (`locales/<lang>.web.yaml`) or a user overlay. It adds no bundled language.

## Related Issue

No single issue; it generalizes the per-language dashboard PRs listed above into the pluggable path #126296 introduced (related: #128928, #131450).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `agent/i18n_layers.py` — `SURFACES` gains `web`; packs and the user overlay may ship `<lang>.web.yaml` (the loader/validator pick it up unchanged).
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/i18n.py` (+ mount in `web_server.py`) — `GET /api/i18n/languages` and `GET /api/i18n/catalog?lang=&surface=web`, the HTTP twin of the `i18n.languages` / `i18n.catalog` JSON-RPC pair (`agent.i18n.language_options` / `surface_catalog`), behind the normal `/api/` session gate. No `profile` param on purpose: the dashboard language is a per-browser choice, and scoping a request to another profile's home flips the process to multi-profile hosting.
- `web/src/i18n/backend-packs.ts` + `context.tsx` — fetch the language list once and the current language's web layer on each switch; merge it over the bundled catalog with the existing shared helpers (`unflattenMessages`, `adaptStringOverrides`, `mergeTranslations`), so positional `{0}` strings work over function-valued entries like on Desktop. `Locale` widens to `BundledLocale | (string & {})`; the context exposes `locales` (bundled + pack languages that have web strings) and the RTL flag. An older backend without the routes (404) or any fetch failure keeps the bundle — never a blank UI.
- `web/src/components/LanguageSwitcher.tsx` — lists `locales` from the context instead of the static `LOCALE_META`.
- `locales/_keys.web.json` + `web/scripts/i18n-keys.mjs` (`pnpm run i18n:keys`, pinned by `web/src/i18n/keys.test.ts`) and `_KEY_EXPORTS["web"]`, so `hermes plugins validate` checks `<lang>.web.yaml` keys like the TUI/Desktop ones.
- `tui_gateway/contracts/i18n.py` — `LocaleSurface.web`; regenerated `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.*` with `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py`.
- Docs: `language-packs.md`, developer guide § language packs, `agent/AGENTS.md`.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_web_i18n_routes.py tests/agent/test_i18n*.py tests/tui_gateway/test_i18n_methods.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_locales.py -q` — all pass (two existing tests used `"web"` as their example of an *invalid* surface; they now use `"webz"` and also assert `web` is accepted).
2. `cd web && pnpm exec tsc -b . --noEmit && pnpm exec vitest run` — typecheck clean, 485/485 tests (new: `backend-packs.test.ts`, `keys.test.ts`); `node scripts/i18n-keys.mjs --check` verified; eslint on the touched files: same 3 pre-existing warnings as `main`, 0 errors.
3. Manually: drop `~/.hermes/locales/vi.web.yaml` with `common.save: "Lưu"` (or install a pack whose manifest declares `provides_locales: [{id: vi, endonym: Tiếng Việt}]` with `locales/vi.web.yaml`), restart the dashboard → "Tiếng Việt" appears in the picker and the translated strings render; keys missing from the pack stay English.
