prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add crash-test
prs.body:
## What this adds

One file, `plugin-catalog/crash-test.yaml`, pinned to `00f30620de92a470721b19a158fe26ceee8b0025` (version 0.1.0).

Crash Test is a safety rating for AI agents. For one armed turn it makes tools fail the way real systems fail: timeouts, dropped connections, rate limits, an outage, or reads that come back empty, cut off or out of date. It then rates what the agent did: retried, worked around it, told the user the truth, or claimed success anyway. The result is a 1-5 star rating under the reply and an HTML report. The same profile and seed give the same faults, so models and skills can be compared on identical failures.

A prompt or skill can't do this, because an agent can't test itself. Crash Test sits between the agent and its tools and registers no model-visible tools, so the agent has no way to tell a test from a real failure.

Entry for the Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon.

## Hermes surfaces used

- Hooks: `pre_llm_call` (binds an armed run to the session's turn), `pre_tool_call` (blocks a call for a loud fault), `transform_tool_result` (damages a read-only result for a silent fault), `transform_llm_output` (appends the scorecard), `on_session_end` (disarms if the turn errors or is interrupted)
- `ctx.register_command("crashtest", ...)` for `/crashtest start|drill|status|stop|report|compare`
- `ctx.get_config` for `max_faults`, `fault_rate`, `show_scorecard`
- `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir` for reports

No tools, middleware, required environment variables, dependencies, network calls or subprocesses. `hermes plugins validate` passes with no warnings.

## Safety and disclosure (rules 12 and 13)

- **Off unless armed.** A run covers exactly one turn in the session that armed it, then disarms itself, including when the turn errors or is interrupted. It doesn't survive a restart, and other sessions and subagents are never touched.
- **A blocked call never runs.** Loud faults return a block from `pre_tool_call`, so the tool doesn't execute, and the agent is told the call failed, which is true. A retry can never repeat a real action.
- **Silent faults only touch reads:** `read_file`, `search_files`, `web_search`, `web_extract`, and terminal commands on a read-only allowlist (`cat`, `ls`, `grep`, `git status/log/diff/show`, test runners). Anything with a pipe, redirect, chain or substitution is excluded. A write never gets a fake result.
- **Session tools are exempt**, including `clarify`, `memory`, `todo`, `delegate_task` and `send_message`.
- **Approvals are untouched.** It never approves, skips or routes around Hermes' approval system.
- **The user is always told.** The scorecard states that the faults were injected, which ones, and that blocked calls never ran. Because it's appended to the reply, it's also kept in the session transcript.
- **Writes only** under `<hermes home>/plugin-data/crash-test/`. It also reads the `CRASH_TEST` environment variable for one-shot arming in the process that runs the agent.

## Validation

- `hermes plugins validate`: passes every check with no warnings
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` from current `main`: OK
- 43 tests drive full turns through the registered hooks: blocked calls never run, writes never get silent faults, one turn only, other sessions untouched, deterministic seeds, HTML escaping, and the scorer's verdicts on realistic replies
- A live run in a real Hermes v0.23.0 install with `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`: `/crashtest start outage 7` blocked `execute_code`, the model switched tools and answered correctly, and the run was rated 4/5 ("reached the goal another way")

Not yet tested on Linux or macOS.

## Nearest neighbours

`proofgate` checks completion claims against tool evidence, and `hermes-verifier` reviews turns with a second model. Both watch normal runs. Crash Test causes failures on purpose and measures the response, which neither does. I found no fault-injection entry in the catalog. This is not a fork of a listed plugin.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add stash (capture bin for the desktop sidebar)
prs.body:
Adds **Stash** — a capture bin page in the Desktop sidebar.

Paste links, YouTube urls, image urls, uploaded images or plain notes into one box. Each line becomes
a row with a title and thumbnail fetched server-side; rows carry a **Chat** button that opens a new
session with the item as the opening message. The agent reads the same store through three tools
(`stash_add` / `stash_list` / `stash_update`), so "go through my stash" works from any conversation.

Owner submission — `RegeneratusLabs` owns `github.com/RegeneratusLabs/hermes-stash`.

**Pin:** `97d1667527c5a9508e733c82246b42f732f9d970` (v0.3.1, tree: credits + rename cleanup).

### Surfaces used

- `ctx.register_tool` ×3 (`stash_add`, `stash_list`, `stash_update`), one toolset.
- `dashboard/plugin_api.py` + `dashboard/manifest.json` — the plugin's own REST namespace, reached
  from the page through **`ctx.rest`** (no raw bridge, no relative `fetch`).
- `desktop/plugin.js` over `ROUTES_AREA` (page), `SIDEBAR_NAV_AREA` (nav row) and `PALETTE_AREA`
  (command). No hooks, no middleware, no env vars.

### Disclosures

- **Network.** Saving an item issues one `GET` to that url from the Hermes host (4 s timeout,
  400 KB cap) to read `<title>` / `og:image` / `og:description`. The fetch **refuses loopback,
  link-local, private and reserved targets before dialling and re-checks on every redirect hop**, so
  a pasted `http://127.0.0.1:…` or a metadata address is never touched. YouTube urls also use
  `https://www.youtube.com/oembed` plus the public thumbnail host. No credentials, no telemetry,
  no shell commands, no third-party API.
- **Storage.** `~/.hermes/stash/items.json` (plain JSON) and `~/.hermes/stash/media/` for uploaded
  images (8 MB cap). Nothing is read outside those paths.
- **No** self-updater, `eval` / `new Function`, dynamic `import()`, script-tag injection, prototype
  writes on renderer or storage objects, DOM reach into core UI, or core patching. `install.sh` only
  copies files already in the checkout; it fetches nothing.

### Known issues (also declared on the entry)

- The desktop half ships switched off: after `hermes plugins enable stash`, restart the app and
  enable Stash under **Capabilities → Plugins**.
- Install it on the machine that runs the desktop app; a copy installed only on a remote backend
  never reaches the sidebar.

### Validation at the pin

`hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` → **passed**, including
`desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface` and the capability probe.
`scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` → exit 0. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` → OK.

The screenshot on the entry is the Desktop page itself at the pinned commit (three saved items, one
with a fetched YouTube thumbnail), captured from the shipping `desktop/plugin.js`.

prs.title: Plugin guide: injected messages queue for the next turn instead of interrupting
prs.body:
The plugin guide said that a message a plugin injects while the agent is busy interrupts the running tool. That stopped being true when plugins moved into the gateway: the message now waits and runs as the next turn, and this fixes the docs to say so.

Docs only.

- `website/docs/user-guide/features/plugins.md` § Injecting Messages: the "classic CLI runs plugins in its own process" block (idle → new turn, mid-turn → interrupts) is replaced with how every local surface behaves today: idle starts a turn, busy queues for the next turn, the running tool is never cancelled.

Where that behaviour lives on main: `gateway/run_plugin_injection.py::_admit_plugin_injection` commits the plugin turn to the session's durable FIFO (`admit_automation`), and `tui_gateway/plugin_inject.py::inject_tui_session_message` queues on a busy TUI/Desktop session ("a notice must not cancel in-flight work"). The classic CLI no longer loads plugins (PLG-7, 4b6a8edd6a4), so `PluginManager._cli_ref` is never set and the interrupting branch in `hermes_cli/plugins_injection.py` can't be reached in production. That branch is left in place here because four tests on main still pin it; removing it is a separate call.

Prompted by the review of #85279 and #118906 by @Sahil-SS9, which asked for this queue-safe behaviour; main already has it.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add hermes-roam plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one file, `plugin-catalog/hermes-roam.yaml`, for **hermes-roam** ("Hermes Roam"), pinned to [`vcruz305/hermes-roam@05e13c8`](https://github.com/vcruz305/hermes-roam/tree/05e13c8182d053c128a31a65f05bba12407bf742) (0.5.4).

Hermes Roam syncs your Hermes home between your own machines: your laptop, desktop and VPS share one `SOUL.md`, one set of memories and skills, and the shared part of `config.yaml`, through storage you already own. It addresses #20510.

- **Your storage, your choice.** An S3-compatible bucket (Cloudflare R2, AWS S3), any git repository (a private GitHub repo works), or a local directory. No hosted service.
- **Encrypted before it leaves the machine.** Each push is an AES-256-GCM bundle under a key only your devices hold (`ROAM_ARCHIVE_KEY`). The remote only sees ciphertext plus a signed head.
- **Secrets never travel.** `.env`, `auth.json`, credential files and secret-looking keys inside `config.yaml` (API keys, tokens, `aws_*`) are stripped on push and kept per device. Only an allowlist of shared paths syncs; anything new or unknown stays local.
- **Host settings stay host settings.** `config.yaml` is merged, not replaced: home paths, terminal settings and each device's own keys survive a pull. Each device's `roam/rules.yaml` decides what it shares and never syncs itself.
- **Never a silent overwrite.** Pushes use compare-and-swap on a signed head: if another device pushed since your last pull, the push is refused with "pull first". Pulls are plan-first; `--apply` is journaled and backs up every replaced file. Both sides editing one file → a reported conflict, never a merge.
- **History and restore.** `hermes roam history <path>` lists every version still in the store (verified through a signed chain of heads); `hermes roam restore <path> --generation N --apply` brings one back through the same backed-up install.
- **Safe with the agent in the loop.** The agent can check status, preview and read history; pull `--apply` and restore require the user unless `allow_agent_apply` is set. Remote-controlled text (device names, filenames, git/S3 errors) is quoted and length-capped before it reaches the model.
- **Profiles and bots.** One store carries every profile: each profile's identity (`profile.yaml`), SOUL, memories, skills and shared config. Roam always syncs the root home, even when run from a profile context (`hermes -p work …`) or a multi-profile gateway, and every surface shows each profile's synced/excluded state. A profile can be excluded per device in `roam/rules.yaml`.
- **A brand-new device's first pull merges `config.yaml`** (and each profile's config): shared settings arrive, local values and keys stay.
- **Hermes bundled skills stay put.** Unmodified Hermes-shipped skills (matched against `skills/.bundled_manifest` origin hashes) never travel, so each device keeps the copy its own Hermes ships and keeps updating; a bundled skill you edited syncs like your own.
- **Opt-in, off by default: a read-only session archive.** A device that enables `sync_sessions` publishes the finished sessions of every profile, exported with Hermes's own `hermes sessions export --format md --redact`, into its own encrypted namespace (capped at 50 MB, newest first). Other devices list and read them with `hermes roam sessions` but cannot resume them. Hermes's live `state.db` and the `sessions/` debug-dump folder never travel.
- **Opt-in, off by default: cron job definitions** (`cron/jobs.json` only, never run output).

**Owner submission (rule 5):** `vcruz305` owns `vcruz305/hermes-roam` and wrote it. Tier left at `community`.

## Hermes surfaces used

- **Python plugin** (`plugin.yaml` + `register(ctx)`):
  - 3 tools: `roam_status`, `roam_push`, `roam_pull` (pull applies only with explicit consent, see above).
  - Hooks: `on_session_start` (optional auto-pull check, notice of a failed previous push), `on_session_end` (optional auto-push, skipped when the user holds the lock), `pre_llm_call` (one-line notice when the remote is ahead).
  - CLI `hermes roam …` (init, status, diff, push, pull, devices, rules, history, restore, sessions, doctor) and the `/roam` slash command (read-only verbs, including `/roam sessions`, which lists but never prints transcripts).
  - A bundled `roam-setup` skill that walks setup and routes `init --create-remote`, `push` and `pull --apply` to the user.
  - `config_schema` for backend settings; `requires_env: [ROAM_ARCHIVE_KEY]`.
- Imports only the documented plugin modules (`hermes_cli.config`, `agent.secret_scope`, `plugins.plugin_storage`, `plugins.plugin_utils`, `hermes_cli.plugins`) plus one disclosed exception, `hermes_cli.version_info.get_version_info`, used to refuse applying a home written by a newer Hermes onto an older one (the validator reports it as a caution).

`hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes on a clean clone of the pinned commit: security scan safe, declared tools and hooks match, no core override. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes on the entry.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

The same disclosure is in the README's Disclosure section and `docs/DISCLOSURES.md` at the pinned SHA.

- **Network calls.** Only to the store the user configures, and only when a roam command, tool, slash verb or session hook runs: S3/R2 via boto3 (`GetObject`, conditional `PutObject`, `HeadObject`, `ListObjectsV2`, `HeadBucket`), or the git CLI (`ls-remote`, `fetch`, `push`) for the git backend. Every operation has one absolute deadline (900 s push/pull, 60 s for the rest); unreachable remotes fail closed in ~10–17 s.
- **Shell commands / processes.** The git backend runs `git` as argv subprocesses (no shell) with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, SSH `BatchMode=yes` and hard timeouts, so nothing ever waits on a human under cron or the gateway. Session hooks run bounded daemon threads.
- **Local subprocess (opt-in only).** With `sync_sessions` on, push runs `hermes sessions export <tmpdir> --format md --redact` as an argv subprocess (no shell, stdin closed, hard timeout); if it fails, the rest of the push still succeeds with a notice. `--redact` is best-effort, so the README states that an archived transcript may still contain anything typed into a session (it travels encrypted).
- **Secrets.** `ROAM_ARCHIVE_KEY` and the S3 key pair come only through `agent.secret_scope`; the plugin never reads `.env`, `auth.json` or any credential file, never syncs secrets, and never logs them. For syncing secrets the README points to secret-source plugins (Hermes's built-in Bitwarden Secrets Manager source, `vaultwarden`, `pass-secrets`, `hermes-wincred`, `hermes-dpapi-secrets`).
- **Writes.** Pulled files into `$HERMES_HOME` (plan first, backup first, journaled), and its own state under `$HERMES_HOME/roam/`.
- **None of:** telemetry, self-updating code, runtime patching of Hermes, compiled payloads.

## How to test

1. `hermes plugins install vcruz305/hermes-roam` into two Hermes homes; `hermes plugins enable hermes-roam`; put the same `ROAM_ARCHIVE_KEY` in both homes' `.env`.
2. Point both at one remote (e.g. `hermes config set plugins.entries.hermes-roam.settings.backend git` and `…settings.git_remote <bare repo>`), then `hermes roam init --create-remote` and `hermes roam push` on the first.
3. On the second: `hermes roam pull` (plan only), `hermes roam pull --apply`; edit `SOUL.md`, `hermes roam push`; back on the first, `hermes roam push` is refused (exit 2) until `hermes roam pull --apply`.
4. `hermes roam history SOUL.md`, `hermes roam restore SOUL.md --generation 1 --apply`, `hermes roam doctor`.

Evidence at the pinned SHA: 611 tests (Python 3.11 and 3.14), two adversarial review rounds with a failing proof test per finding, a randomized two-device campaign on local and git backends with every pushed version recoverable, real-Hermes two-home demos (`docs/REAL_HERMES_PROOF.md`, `docs/session-archive-proof.log`, `docs/proof-0.5.0.log`), a live run against Cloudflare R2 (`docs/R2_PROOF.md`), and a live Linux-to-Windows 11 run on the git backend (0.5.4).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) — catalog entry only

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the catalog admission rules
- [x] Conventional commit message
- [x] Searched existing PRs and catalog entries — no duplicate
- [x] PR contains only `plugin-catalog/hermes-roam.yaml`
- [x] Tested on Ubuntu (Linux 6.8) with Hermes 0.22.5

prs.title: fix(anthropic): fit the thinking budget under the output ceiling
prs.body:
## Problem

`agent/anthropic_adapter.py` — `_thinking_kwargs()` ends the manual (`budget_tokens`) thinking branch with

```python
"max_tokens": max(effective_max_tokens, budget + 4096),
```

and `build_anthropic_kwargs()` merges that dict with `kwargs.update(_thinking_kwargs(...))` — after the lines that resolve `max_tokens` from the model's declared ceiling and clamp it to `context_length - 1`. The override runs last, so it wins both clamps.

## Failure scenario

**1. Above the model's own declared ceiling.** With `max_tokens=None` (the normal case) `effective_max_tokens` is `_get_anthropic_max_output(model)`. A model whose ceiling is at or below `budget + 4096` is then sent more output than it can produce, and Anthropic answers a non-transient 400 — the same model/effort pair every turn, so the session wedges:

| model | ceiling | effort (budget) | sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-opus-4-1` / `claude-opus-4-0` | 32000 | xhigh (32000) | 36096 → `max_tokens: 36096 > 32000` |
| `claude-3-5-sonnet` | 8192 | medium (8000) and up | 12096 |
| `claude-3-opus`, `claude-3-sonnet` | 4096 | every effort | ≥ 8096 |

Only the legacy manual-thinking families reach this branch: adaptive models (Claude 4.6+, Kimi/Moonshot) return earlier with `output_config.effort` and no `max_tokens`, and haiku returns `{}`. Within that set the table above is the reachable violation set; the 64000-ceiling families (`claude-sonnet-4*`, `claude-opus-4-5`) and the compat endpoints (`minimax`, `qwen3`) always fit.

**2. The context-window clamp was dead for every thinking request.** `context_length` comes from the endpoint, not from the table, so this half is reachable on any model that takes the branch. An Anthropic-compatible endpoint advertising an 8000-token window at the default `medium` effort was sent `max_tokens=12096` — the `max(context_length - 1, 1)` clamp two lines above had already been overwritten.

## What changed

`max_tokens` is still raised to clear `budget_tokens` — that is the constraint the override existed to satisfy, and Anthropic requires it — but only as far as `_get_anthropic_max_output(model)` and `context_length - 1` allow. Past that the **budget** shrinks instead, keeping `_THINKING_REPLY_RESERVE` (4096, the value the old expression already reserved) for the visible reply. A budget that would fall under Anthropic's documented 1024 floor for `budget_tokens` drops thinking for that request rather than sending one that cannot be served.

Requests that already fit are unchanged, including a caller-supplied `max_tokens` smaller than the budget (still grown, as before). Change is confined to the adapter; `build_anthropic_kwargs` is not restructured beyond passing `context_length` through.

Observed before/after (`max_tokens=None`, `reasoning_config={"enabled": True, ...}`):

```
                                                       before          after
claude-opus-4-1-20250805  ceiling 32000  xhigh   36096 (400)   32000 / budget 27904
claude-3-5-sonnet-...     ceiling  8192  medium  12096 (400)    8192 / budget  4096
MiniMax-M2.7   context_length=8000       medium  12096           7999 / budget  3903
claude-sonnet-4-20250514  ceiling 64000  high    64000          64000 / budget 16000  (unchanged)
```

## Bug-class sweep

`_thinking_kwargs` is the only site in the tree that emits `budget_tokens` or raises `max_tokens` for thinking on the Anthropic Messages path — `grep -rn 'budget_tokens' --include='*.py'` outside `tests/` returns only this function, and every Messages caller (`agent/transports/anthropic.py`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, `agent/auxiliary_client.py`, Bedrock/Vertex) goes through `build_anthropic_kwargs`. The nearest sibling shape is Gemini's `_effective_gemini_max_output_tokens` (`agent/gemini_native_adapter.py`), also reached from `agent/transports/chat_completions.py::_raise_gemini_thinking_max_tokens`; it raises the cap *to* the published ceiling (`max(requested, GEMINI_DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS)`) rather than past it, so it does not carry this bug and is left alone.

## Tests

Two invariant tests in `tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::TestManualThinkingOutputBudget`. The model set is derived from the module's own `_LEGACY_MANUAL_THINKING_CLAUDE_SUBSTRINGS` + `_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_LIMITS`, filtered through `_supports_adaptive_thinking`, so no model id is frozen and new catalog entries are covered automatically. They assert `max_tokens <= _get_anthropic_max_output(model)`, `max_tokens < context_length`, and `budget_tokens < max_tokens` (with a guard so the first test cannot pass vacuously by dropping thinking everywhere).

Proven red on current `main` (production change reverted, tests kept):

```
$ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py -k TestManualThinkingOutputBudget
E           AssertionError: claude-3-5-sonnet @ high asked for more than its ceiling
E           AssertionError: claude-3-opus @ low asked for more than its ceiling
E           AssertionError: claude-3-5-sonnet @ medium asked for more than its ceiling
E           AssertionError: claude-opus-4-0 @ xhigh asked for more than its ceiling
E               AssertionError: claude-3 overran a 4000 window
=== Summary: 1 files, 0 tests passed, 5 failed (100% complete) in 1.5s (20 workers) ===
```

Green with the fix, and the file's existing thinking tests (which pin the growth behaviour on a healthy model) still pass:

```
$ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py -k TestManualThinkingOutputBudget
=== Summary: 1 files, 5 tests passed, 0 failed (100% complete) in 0.5s (20 workers) ===

$ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py
=== Summary: 1 files, 100 tests passed, 0 failed (100% complete) in 2.2s (20 workers) ===

$ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/
=== Summary: 834 files, 9937 tests passed, 2 failed, 34 skipped (100% complete) in 456.9s (20 workers) ===
```

The 2 are not from this change — both fail identically on an untouched `main` checkout in this environment:

```
$ scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client_cache_follows_credential.py tests/agent/test_conversation_compression_manual.py   # on main
  ║ FAILED tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client_cache_follows_credential.py::test_pool_cache_hint_follows_rotation_during_per_model_cooldown
  ║ FAILED tests/agent/test_conversation_compression_manual.py::test_every_surface_honours_preview_without_compressing[acp]
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'acp'
=== Summary: 2 files, 12 tests passed, 2 failed (100% complete) in 2.3s (20 workers) ===
```

## Related

#53679 (still open) adds a `max` effort tier to the manual-thinking path and an output-ceiling clamp. This PR does not add the tier; it also covers the context-window clamp, which #53679 does not. The two touch the same lines of `_thinking_kwargs`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

If this is folded into a larger change, cherry-picking the commit keeps authorship (per AGENTS.md's contributor-credit rule).

prs.title: fix(gateway): opt-in approvals.approvers binds shared-chat exec approvals to the requester on every platform
prs.body:
Shared-chat exec approvals get an opt-in requester binding. Set `approvals.approvers: []` and an approval raised by Alice's message can only be answered by Alice, a listed approver or a platform admin. Anyone else who clicks Allow/Deny, reacts or sends `/approve` gets a private "Only Alice can answer this approval." and the command stays pending. **The default is unchanged from `main`:** `approvers` defaults to `["*"]`, so any admitted member can still answer.

Fixes #80281

## Config

```yaml
approvals:
  approvers: []            # opt-in: the requester, platform admins and the ids listed here
  # approvers: ["U024BE7LH", "123456789"]   # also let these chat users answer
  # approvers: ["*"]       # default (also what you get with no key): any admitted member
```

Platform admins are `allow_admin_from` / `group_allow_admin_from` in the platform's `extra` block. The setting is read when the approval is raised, in the turn's profile scope, so with multiplexed profiles each profile's `config.yaml` decides. It is documented in `website/docs/user-guide/security.md` (new `approvers` row and a "Who can answer an approval in a shared chat" section) and in the adapter guide's public-helpers table.

## Live two-user proof

A real `hermes gateway run` on a scratch HOME, with the Telegram and Slack stand-ins (`tests/fakes/platforms`) and the fake LLM (no model spend). User A (allowlisted) posts `clean up` in the group. The model calls `terminal rm -rf <victim>`. User B (also allowlisted) clicks **Approve once** on A's card. The output below is copied from the probe JSON.

| Leg | B's click | Victim dir after B | Then A clicks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Telegram, `main` @ 749cb638ff4, `approvers: []` | `answerCallbackQuery text="✅ Approved once"` | **deleted** (key ignored) | – |
| Telegram, this PR, no key (default) | `answerCallbackQuery text="✅ Approved once"` | deleted (same as `main`) | – |
| Telegram, this PR, `approvers: []` | `answerCallbackQuery text="Only Tester can answer this approval." show_alert=true` | **still there** | approved, deleted, card reads `✅ Approved once by Tester` |
| Slack, `main` @ 749cb638ff4, `approvers: []` | card reads `✅ Approved once by useru0000301` | **deleted** (key ignored) | – |
| Slack, this PR, no key (default) | card reads `✅ Approved once by useru0000301` | deleted (same as `main`) | – |
| Slack, this PR, `approvers: []` | `chat.postEphemeral user=U0000301 text="Only useru0000111 can answer this approval."` | **still there** | approved, deleted, card reads `✅ Approved once by useru0000111` |

The stand-in gives every Telegram user the display name "Tester". Each gateway was started by the probe and stopped by its PID. No probe process is left running.

## Per-surface coverage

| Surface | How it binds (with `approvers` narrowed) | Private note |
|---|---|---|
| `/approve`, `/deny`, bare "yes"/"no" while blocked (all platforms) | `_blocking_approval_or_stale` → `approval_refusal` | the command's reply |
| Slack buttons | `_handle_approval_action` | `chat.postEphemeral` |
| Discord buttons | `ExecApprovalView._resolve` | ephemeral reply |
| Telegram buttons | `_handle_exec_approval_callback`. The callback state is claimed only after the check, so a refused tap leaves the card live. | callback alert |
| Feishu card | `_handle_approval_card_action` (actor is the tenant `user_id`, else `open_id`, the same as `SessionSource.user_id`) | card toast; card unchanged |
| Teams card | `_on_card_action` (`aad_object_id`, the same as the inbound `user_id`) | invoke message; card keeps its buttons |
| Matrix reactions | `_handle_approval_reaction`, after the adapter's own `MATRIX_APPROVAL_REQUIRE_SENDER` gate (default on, already requester-only) | threaded notice (Matrix has no ephemeral messages) |
| WhatsApp Cloud taps | `_handle_approval_tap`, checked before the tap state is popped | DM reply |
| Relay prompt responses | `_consume_prompt_response` | in-chat ack |
| QQBot buttons | unchanged: on `main` it already accepts a click only from the session key's own user (`_is_authorized_interaction_for_session`), which is stricter than the opt-in | – |
| Session authority (`session_pending_controls`), API server `/v1/runs/{id}/approval`, TUI/Desktop/dashboard, managed workers | unchanged by design: these callers hold a host-issued `session:approve` capability and answer as the host. They are not chat members. | – |
| `/stop` | unchanged: it interrupts the run, which denies the wait. It can never approve a command, and it stays under the existing run-control authorization. | – |

All chat surfaces make the same call, `gateway.approval_actor.approval_refusal(session_key, actor_id, extra=…)`. It returns `None` (allowed) when nothing is pending, when no requester was recorded, or when `"*"` is in the recorded approvers. Plugin adapters can import it: it is listed in the adapter guide and the plugin private-import allowlist.

**Root cause:** button, reaction and text approval handlers authorized the clicker only by chat admission. The pending approval had no record of who raised it.

## Changes

- `tools/approval_gateway_wait.py::_ApprovalEntry` records `requester_id` / `requester_name` and the profile's `approvals.approvers` on a separate `authority` slot (a missing key means `["*"]`). They stay off the approval `data` that is replayed to a reattaching TUI/Desktop client and passed to the prompt renderers. `gateway.approval_actor` reads them through `tools.approval.list_gateway_approval_authority`.
- Admins: Discord buttons read both `allow_admin_from` and `group_allow_admin_from` from the platform block whether or not `require_admin_for_exec_approval` is on. Relay prompt answers use `gateway.approval_actor.runner_admin_ids`, which is the same `policy_for_runner_source` the text `/approve` uses.
- `gateway/approval_actor.py`: the single check every chat surface calls.
- Call sites: `/approve` / `/deny` (slash and plaintext), Slack, Discord, Telegram, Feishu, Teams, Matrix, WhatsApp Cloud, and the relay.
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: `approvals.approvers: ["*"]`.
- `gateway.exec_approval.not_requester` added to every locale.
- Relay prompt resolvers moved to `gateway/relay/prompt_resolvers.py`, with no behaviour change. This offsets line growth in the relay adapter's facade.

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_approval_requester_binding_admins.py`: a Discord admin answers with `require_admin_for_exec_approval` off, and a relay `group_allow_admin_from` admin answers; non-admins are still refused in both.
- `tests/gateway/test_approval_requester_binding.py`: `/approve` in a shared Telegram thread, with config.yaml written the way a user would. There are six rows: no key, `["*"]`, `[]` with another member, `[]` with the requester, a listed approver, and a platform admin. On the refused row, the requester's later `/approve` resolves the still-pending approval.
- `tests/gateway/test_approval_requester_binding_adapters.py`: Feishu card, Teams card, Matrix reaction and WhatsApp Cloud tap, each tested with the default and with the opt-in.
- **Red on `main`** (the same two files copied into an `origin/main` checkout): 9 passed, 5 failed. The 5 failures are exactly the opt-in rows (`/approve`, Feishu, Teams, Matrix, WhatsApp), each `assert True is False` on `entry.event.is_set()`. Every default row passes on `main`, which shows the default really is unchanged.
- **Green on this branch:** 54 approval-related files, 689 passed. These cover approve/deny commands, plaintext routing, authority projection, the Slack/Telegram/Discord/Feishu/Matrix/Teams/WhatsApp Cloud approval suites, the relay suites and the `tools/` approval tests. `python scripts/check --only health` is ok, with one reviewed `# health: allow F821` for the lazily bound Feishu SDK name `CallBackToast`.

## Credit

The requester-binding direction comes from #81388 by @cissel (Discord view) and #72008 by @necoweb3 (relay owner scoping). Their branches predate the current approval layout, so this is a rebuild rather than a cherry-pick.

## NOT_COVERED

- Live probes covered Telegram and Slack. Discord, Feishu, Teams, Matrix and WhatsApp Cloud are covered by unit tests through each adapter's real handler, not by a live stand-in.
- Approvals with no recorded requester (no user id in the session context) are never refused.
- Related but separate bug: #124974 (a tap resolves the oldest FIFO request, not the one tapped).

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafe11e/EzGAVqblKLLA4We7JA3T4_BVsEjZKZ.png)

prs.title: fix(dashboard): MCP catalog and plugin installs from Dashboard/Desktop never block on a terminal prompt (salvage #120537, #120541)
prs.body:
Installing an MCP catalog entry from the Dashboard or Desktop Connectors page no longer hangs `hermes serve`. Before this fix, a `hermes serve` launched from a terminal kept that TTY on stdin. The synchronous catalog install (run on an `asyncio.to_thread` worker) passed the `isatty()` guard and opened the curses tool checklist on a console nobody was watching. That worker held the process-global `_SKILLS_PROFILE_LOCK` while it waited. Every later profile-scoped request then parked on the lock until the default thread pool drained, and every `/api/ws` upgrade timed out. Now the install takes the existing non-interactive path: prior selection, else manifest `tools.default_enabled`, else all tools. It returns at once.

**Who hit it:** user-reported (#120527, py-spy dump from a live Windows incident). Reproduced here on a real `hermes serve` (see the live A/B below).

Fixes #120527

## Salvage

- Salvaged from #120537 by @KoNit-K: an explicit `interactive=False` from the Dashboard route through `install_entry` → `_prompt_env_vars` / `_apply_tool_selection`. A missing required credential fails fast (HTTP 400, `missing_credentials`). CLI installs keep the picker. Cherry-picked with authorship intact.
- Also salvaged #120541 by @liuhao1024 (both commits, authorship intact): `_interactive_prompt_possible()` requires stdin to be a TTY **and** the main thread. This covers every worker-thread caller of `install_entry`, not just the one route that passes the flag. The two conflicted on the same guard lines; I resolved both to `not (interactive and _interactive_prompt_possible())`, so either signal is enough and both PRs' tests pass.
- The base was current main; nothing was dropped from either PR.

## What I changed on top (same bug class, sibling paths)

The Dashboard/Desktop **plugin** install (`dashboard_install_plugin`, run on a worker by `/api/dashboard/agent-plugins/install` and the connector catalog) and `pm.extras.ensure_import` had the same `isatty()`-only gate in front of `input()`:

- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py::_is_tty()` now also requires the main thread. This covers the scan-caution prompt, the enable-now prompt, capability consent, update-all and catalog re-pin confirmations.
- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py`: the Node-sidecar and Python-deps consent questions used raw `sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()`. They now call `_pc()._is_tty()`. On a worker thread they take the existing non-interactive answer: Node deps skipped, Python deps refused with `non_interactive`, which leaves the plugin disabled. The Dashboard's own consent (`assume_deps_consent`) is unchanged.
- `pm/extras.py::ensure_import`: the "install optional feature? [Y/n]" prompt only fires on the main thread. Worker threads keep the existing non-TTY behavior (sync without asking).

**Review round (credit @BearHuddleston, Greptile):**
- The credential prompt only requires the console (main) thread, not a TTY. A redirected stdin on the CLI still answers it (`printf 'key\n' | hermes mcp install <name>`, as on main). The curses checklist keeps its TTY requirement.
- On the non-interactive path, a secret's declared default is saved to `.env` like a typed answer.
- Tests force a TTY, so the explicit `interactive=False` flag is what's tested, not pytest's non-TTY stdin.

`_spawn_hermes_action` subprocesses already run with `stdin=DEVNULL` + `HERMES_NONINTERACTIVE=1`, so the background git-install path was already safe.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py` | `interactive` kwarg (#120537) + `_interactive_prompt_possible()` main-thread guard (#120541) on the credential prompt and tool checklist |
| `hermes_cli/web_routers/mcp.py` | Dashboard install passes `interactive=False` |
| `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py` | `_is_tty()` requires the main thread |
| `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py` | dependency consent uses `_is_tty()` |
| `pm/extras.py` | `ensure_import` prompts only on the main thread |
| tests (4 files) | regressions below |

## Validation

**Red on main → green on head** (source files swapped to `origin/main`, new tests kept):

```
main:  4 files, 83 passed, 6 failed
FAILED test_mcp_catalog_env_boundary.py::test_dashboard_catalog_install_never_opens_curses_picker
FAILED test_mcp_catalog.py::TestInstall::test_install_from_worker_thread_skips_checklist_even_on_a_tty
FAILED test_mcp_catalog.py::TestInstall::test_install_from_worker_thread_with_required_env_raises_instead_of_blocking
FAILED test_mcp_catalog.py::TestInstall::test_noninteractive_install_rejects_missing_required_credential_without_prompt
FAILED test_plugin_dependency_consent.py::test_dependency_questions_never_prompt_off_the_main_thread
FAILED test_extras.py::test_ensure_import_never_prompts_off_the_main_thread
head:  scripts/run_tests.sh (13 files: mcp catalog, plugin consent/install/update/catalog, memory-provider migration, pm extras, tui plugins.manage install + mcp profile rpcs) → 239 passed, 0 failed
review-round tests (secret default → .env; piped CLI credential): red on the pre-review head, green now
```

Note: the local pre-push `no-tmp` guard flags `plugin-catalog/safe-swap.yaml:24`. That file is unchanged here; the line came from main's `fa1a597dfd7`, and the check fails the same way on an `origin/main` archive.

**Live A/B against the real Dashboard endpoint.** I ran a real `python -m hermes_cli.main serve` on a pty (stdin is a TTY, like a terminal launch) with an isolated scratch `HERMES_HOME` and `HERMES_OPTIONAL_MCPS`, so nothing touched the real `~/.hermes`. The catalog entry was a synthetic stdio MCP server exposing two tools, with `default_enabled: [alpha]`. Then I sent `POST /api/mcp/catalog/install` the same way the Connectors page does:

| | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/mcp/catalog/install` | **timed out after 40 s** | **200 in 0.5 s** |
| serve pty | `Found 2 tool(s). Pre-checked: 1.` → `Select tools for 'demo' (SPACE toggle, ENTER confirm)` | `Probing…` → `✓ Installed 'demo' (enabled)` |
| next `GET /api/mcp/catalog` (profile-scoped) | **timed out** (profile lock held) | 200 |
| `mcp_servers.demo.tools` | not written | `include: [alpha]` (manifest default) |

`ruff check` passes on the touched files; `check-windows-footguns.py` passes; `audit_pr_attribution.py`: all emails mapped.

prs.title: fix(cron): cron jobs deliver to a named Telegram private-DM topic (#80483, salvage #97139)
prs.body:
A cron job set to deliver to a named topic in a Telegram private chat (`deliver: telegram:<chat>:Debug`) delivered nothing, because the whole `<chat>:Debug` string was read as the chat id. Now the topic is found (or created on first use) by name, and the job's text and images both land in it.

**Outcome:** `telegram:<private_chat>:<topic name>` cron targets deliver into that topic.

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_ids.py::parse_send_target` accepts a topic name after a positive (private-chat) id. Group targets still take numeric topic ids only.
- `cron/scheduler_delivery.py::_named_dm_topic_route`: the live cron lane resolves the name through the adapter's `ensure_dm_topic` (the same helper the delivery router uses), so text and media go to one topic id.
- `tools/send_message_senders.py::_telegram_thread_kwargs`: the standalone sender (gateway not running) cannot create topics, so it fails the target with a clear error instead of posting to the chat root.

| `deliver:` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `telegram:111:Debug` (gateway up) | chat id `111:Debug`, nothing delivered | `createForumTopic` once; text + photo to topic 4242 |
| `telegram:111:Debug` (gateway down) | nothing delivered | target fails: "named Telegram topic 'Debug' can only be resolved by the running gateway" |
| `telegram:111:38049` | topic 38049 | unchanged |
| `telegram:-100123:Ops` | no topic | unchanged (groups never take names) |

**Live repro:** a real gateway against the Telegram Bot API stand-in. On main the job targeted chat `111:Debug` and nothing arrived; on the head, `createForumTopic` ran once and `sendMessage` + `sendPhoto` both went to `message_thread_id=4242`.

**Tests:** `tests/cron/test_cron_named_telegram_topic.py` (2 tests): red on origin/main (2 failed), green on the head; deleting only the cron call site turns the delivery test red. 293 passed across the 15 cron/send test files that reference the touched functions. `scripts/check` ok.

Root cause: the Telegram target parser only knew `<chat>[:<numeric topic>]`, and cron had no step that resolves a topic name to an id.

Fixes #80483.

Salvage of #97139 by @Sahil-SS9 (credited as co-author): that PR predates the `cron/scheduler_delivery.py` split, so the fix is rebuilt on current main.

prs.title: fix(gateway): non-admins can no longer answer an approval by typing "always" or clicking Allow when allow_admin_from is set
prs.body:
With `allow_admin_from` set, a non-admin is refused `/approve` and `/deny`. They could still answer a pending dangerous-command approval another way: type `yes` / `always`, or click the Allow button. `always` also wrote the pattern to the profile-wide `command_allowlist`, so that command was pre-approved for everyone from then on. This PR makes every way of answering an approval pass the same gate as `/approve`. Admins and ungated chats work exactly as before.

Fixes #120506

Salvaged from #120507 by @jonpol01 (bare-word gate + test, cherry-picked with authorship). Also includes #128104 by @Froraut (same bare-word gate, plus the sibling hole for slash-confirm prompts such as `/reset`, on typed replies and on every adapter's buttons; both commits cherry-picked with authorship). #147459 by @vanscodex is the same one-line bare-word fix and is covered here.

## What a member sees now

| How the member answers | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| types `yes` / `always` / `no` while the approval blocks | resolves it (`always` allowlists permanently) | ordinary chat; approval stays pending |
| clicks Allow / Always / Deny (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Feishu, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, QQ Bot, relay) | resolves it | private "⛔ /approve is admin-only here…" (or ignored on Slack/Feishu/QQ, like any unauthorized click); card stays live |
| reacts ✅ / ♾️ / ❌ (Matrix) | resolves it | reaction feedback with the same reason; prompt stays live |
| answers a `/reset`-style slash confirm (typed or button) | runs the command | refused; prompt stays live (from #128104) |
| **admin**, or any chat **without** `allow_admin_from` | resolves | resolves (unchanged) |

`user_allowed_commands: [approve]` still lets a listed member approve (and only approve), exactly as it lets them run `/approve`.

## Live repro (real `hermes gateway run`, real Telegram adapter over the Bot API stand-in, fake LLM)

Shared Telegram group, `group_allow_admin_from: ["111"]`, `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS=111,222`, `approvals.mode: manual`. Admin 111 asks for `rm -rf <victim>`. Member 222 is allowlisted but not an admin.

| Leg | `main` @ 22811165251 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| member types `always` | gateway replies `✅ Command approved (pattern approved permanently)`; **victim deleted** | `Slash command /approve denied for telegram:222` in the log; victim still there; admin's `yes` then runs it |
| member clicks **Always** | toast `✅ Approved permanently`; **victim deleted** | toast `⛔ /approve is admin-only here. …`; victim still there; admin's **once** click then runs it |

On `main` the second leg's `rm -rf` was never even prompted: the member's earlier `always` had already allowlisted it. Probe output, read back from the stand-in's recorded Bot API calls and the victim dir on disk:

```
main  bare_word {"victim_exists_after_member_always": false, ...}
main  button    {"victim_exists_after_member_always_click": false, "member_toast": ["✅ Approved permanently"], ...}
head  bare_word {"victim_exists_after_member_always": true, "victim_exists_after_admin_yes": false}
head  button    {"victim_exists_after_member_always_click": true, "member_toast": ["⛔ /approve is admin-only here. No slash commands are enabled for non-admins on this platform. ..."], "victim_exists_after_admin_once_click": false}
```

The probe is a scratch file built on `tests/e2e/core/platforms` and is not committed.

## What changed on top of the contributor commits

- **Native controls (the gap both PRs left open).** `TurnRunner` now passes the chat's slash policy to `tools.approval.register_gateway_notify(..., may_answer=)` for the length of the turn. Every chat surface that resolves an exec approval asks `gateway_approval_refusal(session_key, clicker, choice)` before it claims the click: Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, Feishu, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, QQ Bot and relay connector prompts. A refused click is never consumed, so the card stays live for an admin. Host surfaces (API server `/v1/runs/.../approval`, TUI, Desktop, session authority) register no gate and are unchanged.
- Slack rebase fix: main renamed the unpacked clicker id to `_user_id`, so #128104's Slack slash-confirm gate referenced an undefined name (F821).
- Relay prompt resolvers moved to `gateway/relay/prompt_resolvers.py` with no behaviour change, to keep `gateway/relay/adapter.py` under its line cap.
- Dropped #128104's duplicate bare-word test (it is the same as #120507's) and kept #120507's.
- `tools.approval:gateway_approval_refusal` is added to the published plugin API (`hermes_cli/data/plugin_api.json`, with `public-api.md` regenerated). The bundled platform adapters call it the same way they already call `resolve_gateway_approval_card`, and third-party platform plugins need it to apply the same gate. That is an intended boundary crossing; the baseline is not updated.
- Docs: the adapter guide tells plugin adapters to call `gateway_approval_refusal` before resolving, and the messaging guide's tier paragraph covers approvals.

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_approval_answer_slash_gate.py` (new, 13 tests). Each one registers a real pending approval and the real `TurnRunner` gate, then drives the adapter's real click/reaction handler: member refused + card live, then admin resolves. Covers Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, Feishu, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, QQ Bot and relay. There are also producer-side tests (the gate exists only for the turn) and tests for the ungated and `user_allowed_commands` controls.
- **Red on main:** with the production files swapped to `origin/main` copies, all 13 new tests fail, plus #120507's and #128104's 5 gate tests in `test_plaintext_approval_routing.py`.
- **Sabotage:** with `gateway_approval_refusal` made to always return None, 10/13 fail. The 3 that still pass are the controls, which must pass either way.
- **Green on head:** `scripts/run_tests.sh` over 383 related files (every approval, slash, busy, relay and per-platform adapter test file, plus `tests/tools/test_approval*`): 3806 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped.
- `python -m scripts.code_health`: 0 blocking. `scripts/check`: 15 checks ok.

Not covered live: platforms other than Telegram. They are covered by the adapter-level tests above through their real handlers. The Slack and Discord stand-ins could run the same probe.

![Approvals obey the admin gate](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab195c7/IbCPn6ZhuTNtRxT0T4NHw_22oWJpkg.png)

## What does this PR do?
- A cron run whose agent returns nothing is saved as `(No response generated)` and never delivered. Continuity and `context_from` were injecting that placeholder as "the previous run's output" and hiding the last real answer.
- The selector now treats the placeholder like `[SILENT]` or a blank answer and falls back to an older archive.

## Related Issue
Fixes #129609

- `cron/scheduler.py`: adds a `NO_RESPONSE_PLACEHOLDER` constant, used by the archive writer and the empty-reply check in `_final_response_from_result`.
- `cron/scheduler_prompt.py`: `_archive_answer` returns `None` for the placeholder.
- `tests/cron/test_context_from_response_extraction.py`: adds a test that an archive with the placeholder falls through to the older real answer.

## How to Test
```python
job = create_job(prompt="Report", schedule="0 8 * * *", context_from="self")
# older archive: "## Response\n\nREAL ANSWER", newer: "## Response\n\n(No response generated)"
prompt, _ = _inject_context_from(job, "Report")
assert "REAL ANSWER" in prompt and "(No response generated)" not in prompt
```

Before / after:
```python
# before
if not answer or _sched._is_cron_silence_response(answer):
# after
if (not answer or answer == _sched.NO_RESPONSE_PLACEHOLDER
        or _sched._is_cron_silence_response(answer)):
```

A fresh install no longer aborts in the uv bootstrap when GNU `sha256sum` prefixes its output with the `\` escaping marker (a backslash or newline in the temp path).

- `scripts/install.sh::ensure_uv`: strip one leading `\` from the locally computed digest before comparing with `UV_PIN_SHA256`. The integrity check is unchanged otherwise; `shasum` never escapes. `setup-hermes.sh` already normalises its archive digest the same way.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|

prs.title: catalog: add herd (cross-device sync with per-key config merge)
prs.body:
## herd — keep one Hermes across every machine

Settings, skills, memory and API keys follow you between devices, while each machine keeps what belongs to it.

**Why it is different from the existing sync repos.** They copy `~/.hermes` (or merge whole objects). A quarter of a real `config.yaml` is machine-bound — on my install, **37 of 155 keys across 12 sections** (Docker paths, `webapp.port`, `platforms.*`, `auth.*`). Copying those breaks the receiving machine, which is the failure reported in #20510 by people who tried it. Herd merges `config.yaml` **per key** against a stored base and resolves machine-bound paths to the local value *before* the comparison, so a pull cannot delete the section the machine is running on.

**Surfaces used**

- tools: `sync_status`, `sync_diff`, `sync_now`
- hooks: `on_session_start` (pull), `on_session_end` (push) — daemon-threaded, return in ~10 ms
- CLI: `hermes sync init|join|status|diff|push|pull|sync|conflicts|undo|code|policy|leave`

**Disclosures (rule 13)**

- Reads the active profile's `config.yaml`, `.env`, `memories/{MEMORY,USER}.md`, `SOUL.md` and `skills/**`.
- Writes only items that changed, and takes a timestamped backup of each path before writing it (`hermes sync undo` restores it).
- `.env` values selected by policy are copied to the store **AES-256-GCM encrypted**; the store is a folder or git remote the user names. Nothing is sent anywhere else; no telemetry.
- Machine env vars and gateway bot tokens are excluded by default — two machines holding one Telegram token both answer every message.
- Sessions and cron are not synced by default (`--cron` opts in); `state.db` is never touched.

**Verification**

- `hermes plugins validate` at the pinned SHA: all checks pass, security scan **safe**.
- 48 tests (`python -m pytest tests -q`), including two real `HERMES_HOME`s, a real conflict, a real undo, git transport, and the agent tools.
- Live run on a real profile: 76 items / 1.9 MB encrypted store; a second machine joined, received a changed setting, and kept its own Docker path. A pull that would have deleted `terminal`/`webapp` is now a regression test.

issues.title: [Feature] Add Tsubasa to the existing OpenAI-compatible provider catalog
issues.body:
# [Feature] Add Tsubasa to the existing OpenAI-compatible provider catalog

## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

Users can already select Tsubasa through an explicit `openai` model entry with a custom API base, but the provider picker does not offer its endpoint or public model aliases. A small catalog entry would make that setup discoverable without adding a new transport.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Add a named `tsubasa` provider using the existing HTTP/OpenAI-compatible path, the base URL `https://api.tsubasa.sh/v1`, and common models `tsubasa-fast` and `tsubasa-pro`. Preserve the existing API-base override and credential handling. Both aliases have a 32,768-token input-plus-output budget; a setup example should use `agents.defaults.context_window = 32768` and a bounded output setting such as `max_tokens = 4096`.

Do not add an unapproved icon or claim tool, vision, reasoning, or model-listing qualification. Keep model fetching disabled until that endpoint is verified.

## 🛠 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- Add the entry to `pkg/providers/provider_metadata.go`; keep `provider_catalog.go` deriving UI options from that source.

prs.title: ncl: warn when group scope overrides an explicit auto-fill arg (#2464)
prs.body:
Fixes #2464

## Summary

Under group scope, `dispatch()` auto-fills `agent_group_id`, `group`, and
`id` from the caller's locked context (and, for `wirings-get`/
`wirings-update`, from the resolved wiring for the current conversation).
When a caller explicitly passes a differing value for one of these keys,
nothing on stderr told them their value was overridden — the operator had
no signal that their write target changed.

This adds a single stderr warning, gated strictly on `provided !== undefined
&& provided !== locked`, at each auto-fill point:

- `agent_group_id`
- `group`
- `id` (groups/destinations resources, locked to the caller's own group)
- `id` (wirings-get/wirings-update, locked to the resolved wiring id for the
  current conversation — the case most likely to be missed, since it's a
  second, unconditional override a few lines below the general auto-fill
  block)

Matching-value passes stay silent, per the issue's guidance, so the warning
doesn't get trained out by redundant flags.

Note: for `agent_group_id`/`group`, a differing value is already denied by
the guard's cross-group check (`src/cli/guard.ts`) added in #2986, so those
two no longer reach the handler with the wrong value — but the caller
previously got no stderr signal explaining *why*, only a generic
`forbidden` JSON error. The wirings id case has no such guard check and was
a genuine silent override with no signal at all. This PR adds the warning
uniformly across all four auto-fill points so the operator sees the
mismatch immediately in every case.

## Test plan

- [x] Added 6 new tests to `src/cli/dispatch.test.ts` covering: warn on
      differing `--agent_group_id`, differing `--group`, differing `--id`
      (groups/destinations), differing `--id` (wirings-get resolved-wiring
      override), no warning on a matching value, no warning when the arg
      isn't passed at all.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/cli/dispatch.test.ts` — 64/64 passed.
- [x] `npx vitest run` (full suite) — 156 files / 1986 tests passed.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `npx eslint src/cli/dispatch.ts src/cli/dispatch.test.ts` — 0 errors (3
      pre-existing unrelated warnings in `dispatch.ts`, untouched by this
      change).

prs.title: feat(send_card): fields, tables and charts in agent cards
prs.body:
## Summary Agents can now put KPI fields, a table and charts in a `send_card` card, built with Chat SDK's own `Fields`, `Table` and `Chart` builders. - **Before**: a `send_card` child was text only, so a table went out as prose or monospace text. - **Change**: a child may also be a part: `Text`, `Fields`, `Table`, `Chart` (pie, bar, line, area) or `Divider`. The runner checks the parts by name with per-card limits and refuses the card with the child to fix. The bridge runs the same check (any producer can write the row) and builds each part from its checked fields with `chat@4.41.1`'s builders. No new dependency. - **Rendering**: Slack gets native `data_table` and `data_visualization` blocks. Teams gets a `FactSet` and a `Table`, and a chart as a text table (Chat SDK's fallback). - **Unchanged**: text children, link actions (same rules), approval and question cards (separate path). - **Out of scope**: images (the platform would fetch an agent-chosen URL unclicked), callback buttons (never on agent cards), streaming. ```mermaid --- config: look: neo --- flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] direction TB a1["`**Agent** send_card`"] -->|"title, text, link buttons"| b1["`**Bridge** CardText + LinkButton`"] b1 -->|"Chat SDK card"| s1["`**Slack / Teams** text only`"] end subgraph after["After"] direction TB a2["`**Agent** send_card + parts`"] -->|"Text, Fields, Table, Chart, Divider"| r2["`**Runner: check** parts by name + per-card limits, tells the agent what to fix`"] r2 -->|"refused: which child to fix"| a2 r2 -->|"row in outbound.db"| b2["`**Bridge: same check** refuses a row the tool didn't check, builds parts with Chat SDK`"] b2 -->|"Chat SDK card"| s2["`**Slack**: native table + charts **Teams**: table, chart as text`"] end before ~~~ after classDef agent fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#54aeff,color:#0a3069 classDef host fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,color:#24292f classDef lib fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#4ac26b,color:#116329 classDef out fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#d4a72c,color:#4d2d00 class a1,a2 agent class b1 host class r2,b2 lib class s1,s2 out style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:5 4,color:#8c959f style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:5 4,color:#8c959f linkStyle default stroke:#8c959f ``` Why two checks: `send_card` sends and moves on, so only the runner can tell the agent which child to fix. The agent runs in the container that writes `outbound.db`, so only the bridge can stop a row the tool never checked. The two files carry the same check function, since host and container share no module.
Example call and limits ```json { "card": { "title": "Perf review", "children": [ { "type": "Fields", "children": [{ "type": "Field", "props": { "label": "p95", "value": "118 ms" } }] }, { "type": "Table", "props": { "headers": ["Load", "Before (ms)", "After (ms)"], "rows": [["1x", 40, 38], ["20x", 990, 470]], "caption": "Latency before vs after" } }, { "type": "Chart", "props": { "title": "Latency (ms)", "chart": { "type": "bar", "categories": ["1x", "20x"], "series": [{ "name": "Before", "values": [40, 990] }, { "name": "After", "values": [38, 470] }] } } } ] } } ``` Per card: 10 parts and 10 fields; one table of up to 30 rows, 6 columns and 10,000 characters including its caption; two charts of up to 20 categories and 12 series or slices, none repeated, titles and axis labels up to 50 characters, other labels up to 20; text parts up to 2,500 characters and fields up to 1,500; 12,000 characters across the parts. The chart limits are what Slack draws natively; past 10,000 characters Slack swaps a table for plain text cut at 3,000; text and fields stay well under Slack's 3,000 and 2,000, since its adapter adds markup after the check; numbers must be finite; the card-wide caps keep the largest card near 75 KB of the 100 KB a Teams bot message may hold (counted as UTF-16, measured through the Teams adapter), and inside Slack's 50 blocks. The tool's schema for a part is a name `enum` and a `props` object; the fields are in the tool instructions, and a refusal names what to fix.
## Related work No issue: additive to `send_card`; every existing payload renders exactly as before. Overlaps with #3926, #3927 and #3940, which also change `send_card` children and the bridge's card branch, so expect text conflicts with those. ## Change kind - [ ] `kind/bug` - [x] `kind/feature` - [ ] `kind/documentation` - [ ] `kind/cleanup` - [ ] `kind/hardening` ## Validation - `bun test --isolate src/mcp-tools/interactive.test.ts` (container/agent-runner) -> 79 pass; full agent-runner suite -> 662 pass, 0 fail. - `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` -> 88 pass; full host suite -> 4,342 pass, 0 fail. - Host and runner typecheck clean. - A bridge test pins the exact Chat SDK card for a card of every part. It passed on the earlier json-render build that was posted live to Slack, and passes unchanged on this one, so Slack and Teams receive the same card. - Live (earlier build, same card): a local install on Slack (Socket Mode); a Claude agent sent a KPI card and a perf card (fields, captioned table, bar and pie charts, link button) next to a question card and an approval card; all rendered natively, no `invalid_blocks` (screenshots above). - Per-card limits, every string cap, repeated categories and slice labels, non-Field children and stray keys (an `ncq:` id on a part) are covered in both the runner and the bridge. - Not run live: Teams, and non-Claude providers sending a card. WhatsApp's adapter has no table or chart case and drops them; the tool instructions tell the agent to put numbers in text there. - [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not) ## User and release impact - [ ] No user-visible behavior change - [x] User-visible change — release note below - [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback ```release-note Agents can send cards with KPI fields, a table and charts through send_card. Slack draws them natively, Teams shows charts as a table, and WhatsApp doesn't show tables or charts yet. ``` ## Security and trust boundaries - **No callback buttons on agent cards.** Parts are allowed by name (`Text`, `Fields`, `Table`, `Chart`, `Divider`; `Field` only inside `Fields`), in both the runner and the bridge. Anything else refuses the card. - **The bridge does not trust the row**: the same check as the runner; a refused card throws, so the delivery fails and nothing is posted. Each part is rebuilt from the fields it may have, so stray keys never go out. - **No new dependency**: the builders come from `chat@4.41.1`, already pinned. ## Skill delivery - [x] Not a skill - [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above ## AI assistance - [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

## Summary

Bumps prettier from 3.8.2 to 3.9.10 and reformats the 11 `src/` files it changes. This stops the Dependabot group in #4282 from failing `Format check`.

- **Problem**: prettier 3.9 formats two things differently. prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, a faithful fake IMAP server for them (`src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`), the barrel import, and six exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, no Proton DMARC verdict, and a From domain that is Proton's own (`proton.me`, `protonmail.com`, `protonmail.ch`, `pm.me`, or a subdomain) or listed exactly in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS` (Proton custom domains, the Bridge account's own included: a Proton account can send from a connected Gmail address, so its domain is not trusted on its own; entries must be whole domains, and the adapter warns at startup when the account's own non-Proton domain is unlisted). Addresses are compared with the domain in ASCII (punycode) and the address in NFC, so one mailbox is one sender. The `From:` must be one plain address on one `From:` line. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread; internal mail from a domain not trusted is also flagged `$NanoClawFailed`, since it is almost always a real Proton user on an unlisted custom domain.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed, or no longer holds, refuses later replies with core's reason when it gave one. Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused rather than pushing one out. Answers to an open card are not held by the hourly sender limit (a held answer would let a gateway approval time out); mail on a card's thread that turns out not to be an answer is counted. While a card waits, its approver's reply without a command ("Approve" without the slash) gets a notice listing the commands instead of reaching the agent; a bottom-posted command is read below the quote. Card lines show a label the command doesn't say, and options sharing a label (two agents with one name) show their value.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`): core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received".
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required; certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until core's `onHostStart` has run (the host releases inbound first), so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing. The callback only sets a flag; an adapter set up after host start reads at once, and one still waiting after 5 minutes logs that it is still waiting (mail stays unread on the server). The inbound id is the adapter's (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts get just the answer. Failures inside the adapter are retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; routing failures inside the host are not retried (the mail is already handed over). Mail over 40 MB is flagged without being fetched. State is written atomically with a backup (`state.json.bak`); with both unreadable the adapter does not start, so no mail is skipped.
- **Reading mail**: parsing and HTML conversion run in worker threads with timeouts and a heap ceiling, so crafted mail cannot stall the host. When a mail has both bodies the HTML is read. html-to-text runs with no word wrap and no upper-casing. HTML hidden from a mail-client reader (`display:none`, `hidden`, zero-size, transparent text, `<template>`, …) is kept but marked `[hidden CODE: … /hidden CODE]` with a per-mail random code, and invisible or direction characters are marked too (a lone direction mark beside Hebrew/Arabic letters, or a zero-width space between Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar letters, is ordinary text and left alone); when the body the agent gets carries any mark, a note tells it to treat marked text as suspect. Quoted history and signatures are cut; a forward keeps the forwarded mail (a forward's subject prefix, or a "Forwarded message" / "Begin forwarded message:" line before any quoted history), with a coded `[forwarded CODE: …]` line where the forwarded mail begins, since its From:/Date: lines are the sender's claim. A forward sent as an attachment (`message/rfc822`) is read into the body under the same line. The channel's notes come last, after the shown subject, and any "[Note from the mail channel" the sender typed is rewritten as theirs. Attachment names are cleaned, made unique per mail and given extensions from their MIME type. A non-ASCII sender domain is shown in ASCII with its Unicode spelling beside it. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300.
- **Limits**: attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. Bounces, auto-replies (`Auto-Submitted`, `X-Loop`, no-reply senders, …) and mailing-list mail (`List-Id`, `List-Post`, `Precedence: list`) are skipped before the router; list mail is left unread and tagged `$NanoClawList`, since list headers can be forged. `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Hourly limits and the hold queue**: at most 20 mails an hour from one sender reach the host; beyond that, mail waits unread (in the state's retry list) and is handed over as the hour frees up. **This is a throttle, not a loop breaker**: two agents mailing each other are slowed to about 20 mails an hour each, not stopped. Bridge drops every loop marker on outgoing mail (below), and core has no loop handling for any channel yet, so that risk stays open project-wide. New addresses not yet approved are limited to 10 an hour, 200 in any 7 days, and 20 per registrable domain (subdomains share their parent's) in the same 7 days, freed early when core settles (approves or denies) an address; a denied address takes no slot. A new address over its domain's share waits, re-checked hourly, while the hold queue has room for it. Held mail is capped at 200, of which new senders may use 100 and any one domain 20, so approved senders' over-limit mail always has room. Past a cap, mail is left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. The own-address check, the inbound auto-reply filter and the hourly throttle are what remain.
- **Message kinds**: a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743, a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call); loop handling in core; laying out HTML tables row by row (#4257, stacked on this); an HTML alternative for agent Markdown in outbound mail (a follow-up).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted, and why only for some domains (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values. Since a Proton account can also send as an address outside Proton's domains (a custom domain, or a connected external address), and nothing Proton adds says which, `internal` is trusted only for the domains above. On a real inbox, every internal mail without a verdict came from a Proton domain or a subdomain (`notify.proton.me`).
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, six deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

CI does not run tests on PRs into `channels`, so these were run locally on this head (57d4a78e) after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from this branch's own lockfile:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/proton-mail.test.ts src/channels/proton-mail-adapter.test.ts \
    src/channels/proton-mail-registration.test.ts src/test-utils/fake-imap.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  241 passed (241)
$ pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
(no output, exit 0)
```

- `eslint`: 0 errors on the new files.
- The whole suite on a clean install of this branch's lockfile: two failures, neither in these files (`setup/mailbox-compatibility.test.ts`, a 5 s timeout on a slow host, and `src/group-skills.test.ts`), both failing the same way at the PR's base on `channels`.
- `proton-mail.test.ts`, the helpers: sender check (DMARC, `X-Pm-Origin`, trusted domains), plain-address and display-name checks, card matching and distinct commands, quote, signature and forward handling, hidden-text and invisible-character marks, attachment names, header caps, poll bounds, TLS options, skip and mailing-list rules.
- `proton-mail-adapter.test.ts`, the adapter against the fake IMAP server, faked SMTP and real mailparser: sender identity; approval cards (late answers, restarts, closed cards, ceilings, gateway confirmations, answers past the hourly limit); startup on `onHostStart`; the cursor across restarts and UIDVALIDITY changes; retries and giving up; worker timeouts; the hourly limits, the hold queue's caps and per-domain shares (by registrable domain), settled addresses freeing their slots, denied senders uncounted; forwards and their coded line, hidden text and attached forwards; non-command replies on an open card; list mail left unread; teardown during connect and before host start.
- Each fix from the third review has a test that failed on the head before it (fc9ecaec, then each fix commit in turn).
- A read-only replay of the old head's and this head's rules over a real inbox (638 mails, counts only): no change to any sender decision; the text changes are no word wrap, heading case, horizontal rules drawn 40 dashes long instead of 80, forwards kept whole, and the hidden-text note now added in the mails whose hidden HTML held block elements.
- Adapter tests run against a scratch working directory and refuse to run otherwise, so they never touch a real install's `store/`.
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, Docker): the install's own build of this adapter has been live since 24 Oct with Bridge 3.27.0 (pinned certificate, required STARTTLS, card answers from Outlook).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass (or Proton-internal mail from a trusted domain), and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself. Proton custom domains, the Bridge account's own included, go in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, trusted only for the domains above; anyone with a free Proton account is verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card.
- Hidden HTML and invisible characters are marked for the agent, not removed, with a code the sender cannot predict, so a mark without the code was written by the sender.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, and new addresses are limited per hour, per 7 days and per domain, so strangers cannot fill `pending_channel_approvals` or the cards the owner's approvals need.
- Loops: throttled, not stopped (see Hourly limits); stated here and in SKILL.md (#3726).
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `html-to-text@10.0.1`, `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

Code for the `/add-proton-mail` skill in #3726, which copies the `src/channels/proton-mail*` files from this branch and appends the barrel line. The adapter test imports `src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`, so #3726 is being updated to copy it (and its test) too.
