prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The `channels` side of #4168: text-command answers and the web chat wait for the host too.

- **Problem**: WhatsApp (Baileys), iMessage and the local web chat answered a pending question themselves before the host decided. They closed the question and posted "✅ Approved by <name>" even when the host refused, so the approver could no longer answer.
- **Fix**: they wait for the host's outcome. Accepted: confirmed, question closed. Refused: question stays open, nothing posted (no private reply on these channels; the web chat shows the refusal only to the person who clicked). Closed: "No longer available". Ignored: the question stays open, since it may still be pending. The host decides once, so WhatsApp needs no answer queue. The web chat draws the resolution the server returns, and none for a card the host updates itself; when two tabs answer at once, the losing tab keeps the winner's answer.
- **Discord**: a card edited into its resolved form also sends `components: []`, so it loses its buttons (moved here from #4156).
- **Any core**: on an older core `onAction` returns nothing, which counts as answered as before. The adapters type-check on `v2026.10.0` and `v2026.10.1-rc.2`.
- **Known gaps**: an expired approval answers "ignored", so a WhatsApp or iMessage question stays open after it; fixing that needs a core change. On a core from before #4168, two WhatsApp answers sent at the same instant are both confirmed (the old answer queue stopped that; a current host decides once).

**How to review**: review #4168 first. This PR's own change is the adapter files (`whatsapp.ts`, `imessage.ts`, `local-web.ts`, `local-web-page.js`, `discord.ts`, about +110/-40 lines, plus tests); the core files are byte copies of #4168. Squash on merge.

## Related work

Stacked on #4156 (base `fix/approval-card-length-channels`); merges with #4168, after #4156.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 4,923 passed. 3 git-heavy `scripts/` tests timed out under load; those files pass 98/98 alone.
- New tests per adapter: a refused answer keeps the question and posts nothing; an accepted one is confirmed once; "ignored" keeps the question open; two WhatsApp answers at once reach the host, and only the accepted one is confirmed; the web chat returns the resolution to draw (none for a gateway card, "No longer available" when closed); an older core's empty return counts as answered; a resolved Discord card loses its buttons. The web chat's guard for a second tab is checked by the page's asset test.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` clean. Codex adversarial review on the branch and each fix; real findings fixed. Left: the older-core gap above, and a web chat display race that needs a failed row delete first.

```release-note
WhatsApp, iMessage and the local web chat confirm an answer only after it is accepted; a refused answer leaves the question open. Discord: a resolved card no longer keeps its buttons.
```

prs.title: fix(approvals): resolve a clicked card only after the host accepts the click
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A clicked approval card now changes only after the host accepts the click, and each request is decided once.

- **Problem**: the channel edited the card (buttons removed, "✅ Approved by <name>") before the host checked who clicked. When the host refused the click, the request stayed pending, but the card showed it as decided and had no buttons left.
- **Fix**: response handlers return what a click did (`accepted`, `refused`, `closed` or `ignored`), and `onAction` passes it back. Both click paths (Chat SDK and Discord's forwarded events) decode the option, hand it to the host, then show only what the host did. Refused: the card keeps its buttons, and the clicker gets a private note where the channel has one. Closed: "No longer available". A late or repeated click leaves a resolved card alone.
- **Decided once**: sender approvals, channel connect and channel Reject claim their row in one transaction, so two racing clicks decide once, and report acceptance before the agent is woken. A question answer is claimed once its row is found (an approval card's click passes on to its own handler) and the row deleted only after the answer is written, under one id per question: a busy mailbox leaves the question open for the next click, and no question gets two answers (a click that finds an answer already stored closes the card and wakes the agent). A plain Reject acts only on a pending card, so a reason being typed isn't lost; a Reject whose reason prompt can't be sent is reported at once. Buttons are decoded by position, and the first card now keeps its buttons until the host accepts, so "Choose existing agent" sends the agent card before storing its options (on the request it read), and in memory no card click counts while it is sent and the clicked card is ignored once it is out: a double tap can't connect an agent nobody picked. A card that can't be sent leaves the first card as it was.
- **Discord**: the click is acked at once (type 6) and not awaited; each Discord call is bounded at 10 s; the buttons go only after acceptance. A click in a thread (types 10, 11, 12) is addressed by its parent channel, so durable gateway clicks match their card.
- **Out of scope**: the text-command channels (#4171). The card-message check, and the registration, reason-capture and replay races, move to a later PR.

## Related work

Stacked on #4147 (base `fix/approval-card-full-action`); merge after it. The bug is older than #4147 and affects every channel. No public issue.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 3,880 passed. 6 git-heavy `scripts/update` and `setup/lib` tests timed out under load; those files pass 62/62 alone.
- Tests: a refused click leaves the row pending and the buttons in place; an approver's click resolves the card; `closed` shows "No longer available"; racing clicks decide once (sender, question, connect, Reject); a failed answer write leaves the question open, and a second click answers it; a repeat answer the mailbox refuses closes the card; a click that read the question before an earlier answer finished doesn't answer again; a plain Reject while a reason is awaited is ignored; acceptance is reported before a slow wake; a handler returning `true` shows nothing; a stalled Discord ack holds neither the click nor the next event, and ends at 10 s; thread types 10, 11, 12; a second click on an approval card isn't held by a question's claim; a Reject whose reason prompt fails is accepted before the wake; the agent card: options stored only after it is sent and only on the same request, a double tap or a tap on either card while it is sent is ignored, the first card's buttons can't connect an agent after it, a failed send or store leaves a usable card, a Reject meanwhile keeps its resolution.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint 0 errors, prettier clean. Codex adversarial review on the branch and each fix, until a pass found nothing; real findings fixed. Left: the two breaking changes above; an older `main` issue this PR doesn't touch (an agent-to-agent message retried after a failed activity stamp is stored twice); and, until the durable card check, the agent-card guard is in memory (a restart in the moment after the options are stored and before the first card loses its buttons isn't covered).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Approval cards change only after the host accepts the click; a click from someone who can't answer the card leaves its buttons in place. Discord: clicks on cards from a durable approval gateway are now recorded (they were ignored), and a stalled click acknowledgement no longer holds later events in its channel.
Breaking for skill authors. Detect: a response handler that returns `true` still compiles, but its card no longer changes and the host logs `legacy_true`; a `finalizeReject` call with a 4th string argument no longer compiles. Why: a card may show only what the host decided. Fix: return `'accepted'`, `'refused'`, `'closed'` or `'ignored'` (or `false` to pass the click on), and pass a reject reason as `finalizeReject(approval, session, userId, { reason })`. Rollback: revert this change; handlers that return `true` then redraw as before.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Who may decide is unchanged (host checks only). The card's display now follows the host's decision. Gateway approvals still fail closed.

- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-log-rotation for host logs
prs.body:
Refs #3916 (the rotation half, on Linux with systemd).

**Problem**

The service appends to `logs/nanoclaw.log` and `logs/nanoclaw.error.log` (`StandardOutput=append:` in `setup/service.ts`) and nothing ever rotates them. They grow for the life of the install: #1088 reached 27 GB in five days, and #3916 found months of history in one file. Old restart loops in that history then look like a current incident.

**Solution**

A new skill, `/add-log-rotation`. It adds no core code: one script, one test, `SKILL.md`, `REMOVE.md`.

- An hourly systemd timer runs `logrotate`, which rotates a file daily or as soon as it passes 50 MB and keeps 14 gzipped archives per file. Archives get a timestamp suffix, so a busy day can rotate more than once.
- `copytruncate`, with no restart and no signal. The unit opens both files in append mode, so after the truncate the writer carries on at the new end of file with no sparse gap. The test checks this against a real `logrotate` run.
- Units, config and state are named after the install's service unit (`nanoclaw-v2-<slug>-logrotate`, from `setup/lib/install-slug.sh`), so several copies on one machine each get their own timer.
- A user install needs no root: a user timer, plus a logrotate state file under `~/.local/state`. Root installs get system units, matching what `setup/service.ts` does.
- The generated config is dry-run with `logrotate --debug` before anything is enabled. Re-running `install` is idempotent.

The test guards the two things the skill depends on in core:
- the unit's append-mode log paths, through `renderSystemdUnit`;
- the unit name, through `install-slug.sh` compared against `getSystemdUnit`.

**Install**

```bash
bash .claude/skills/add-log-rotation/scripts/log-rotation.sh install
bash .claude/skills/add-log-rotation/scripts/log-rotation.sh status
```

**Uninstall**

```bash
bash .claude/skills/add-log-rotation/scripts/log-rotation.sh uninstall
```

This removes the timer, the service, the config and the state file. Rotated `.gz` archives in `logs/` are left for the user to delete.

**Not covered**

- macOS/launchd. It would need a `newsyslog.d` entry, which requires root.
- The nohup fallback.
- Dates in log lines, the other half of #3916.

**Tested**

- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-log-rotation`, plus `skill-conformance`, `repo-hygiene` and `skill-pins` suites: 293 passing.
- `skill-directives` lint and prettier: clean.
- On Debian 13 (systemd 257, logrotate 3.22): install, re-run, manual trigger (`Result=success`), status and uninstall. Nothing was left behind.
- The same logrotate settings (in a hand-installed form) run hourly on a production install.

The main agent's global memory is broken in two ways:

prs.title: fix(channels): escape approval card text, and refuse a card a channel can't show
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Card text shows as typed on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud refuse a card they can't show whole, instead of cutting it.

- **Problem**: card text could turn into links or mentions on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud show a card as one message with a length cap, and cut or reject text past it.
- **Fix**: Slack, Google Chat and Discord escape card text (`escapeCardText`); Slack card titles keep link syntax inert. Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud set a fixed `maxCardTextLength` of 2,000, 4,000 and 1,024. A longer card is refused and nothing posts, so a gateway approval fails closed, as today.
- **Limits**: Discord 4,000 keeps an embed under its 4,096. Telegram 2,000: MarkdownV2 escaping at most doubles plain text, and 2,000 is the agent's own question cap. WhatsApp Cloud 1,024 is the platform's cap.
- **Telegram tables**: the adapter draws a Markdown table padded to its widest cell (a 1,100-character table grew to 50,000). Gateway card text gets a look-alike for one hyphen in each line shaped like a table delimiter row (after any line break), so no table is drawn; such a line in a code block, or a `---` rule, shows the look-alike too.
- **Known gaps** (Telegram): text that is mostly links or email addresses grows up to about 3.5 times, so a card under 2,000 can still be cut past 4,096. Agent questions keep their Markdown, so a wide table in one can still be cut, as today.
- **Any core**: the options go in through spreads, so the adapters still build on a core without them.

**MERGE HOLD**: lands together with #4147. This branch carries #4147's card text change until the next `main` -> `channels` sync. prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Names `@types/node` in the root `tsconfig.json`, so the TypeScript 6 bump in #4284 stops failing the add-opencode check.

- **Problem**: TypeScript 6 makes `types` default to `[]`, so it stops loading `@types/node` on its own. The root build keeps Node globals only by luck: `src/` imports better-sqlite3, and its types reference node. add-opencode's `scripts/tsconfig.opencode-auth.json` extends the root but has no such import. On TS 6 it loses `process`, `fs` and `console`, which gives 197 errors in `test (add-opencode, true)` on #4284.
- **Fix**: add `"types": ["node"]` to the root `tsconfig.json`. On TypeScript 5.9 nothing changes: `@types/node` and `@types/better-sqlite3` are the only `@types` packages, and better-sqlite3's types still load through its import.
- **Out of scope**: the TypeScript bump itself. Once this merges, #4284 needs `@dependabot recreate`.

## Summary

On Linux, a new local OneCLI gateway now publishes its admin API and Postgres on `127.0.0.1`; only the gateway proxy stays on the Docker bridge.

- **Before**: on bare-metal Linux the OneCLI installer publishes the gateway, admin API and Postgres on the `docker0` address. Agent containers only need the gateway (`host.docker.internal:10255`).

A bind the user chose (`ONECLI_BIND_HOST` exported, or anything but `docker0`), a compose file without the stock lines, and non-Linux installs are left as installed.

## Related work

Supersedes #2434 (closes #2433), which targeted `setup/onecli.ts` before OneCLI setup moved into `/add-onecli` (d5c7cccc). Related: #3302 (thanks @wakqasahmed) saves the bridge bind for the gateway (#2903); main already does that, and this keeps it for `:10255`.

prs.title: fix(docker-driver): wait out in-flight --rm auto-removal on stop
prs.body:
## Summary

Stops `DockerHandle.stop()` from reporting a failed teardown when Docker's own `--rm` auto-removal is still finishing.

- **Problem**: agent containers are created with `--rm`. `stop()` runs `docker stop`, which starts Docker's auto-removal, then `docker rm --force`, which the daemon rejects while that removal is in flight. `#confirmRemoved` probes `docker ps` once, still sees the container, and throws `session realization failed: unknown`. The container is gone a few milliseconds later.
- **Evidence**: on one Docker Desktop install, 60 of 164 absolute-ceiling kills over several days logged `Failed to stop session`. In one incident the daemon log shows the `ps` probe at `21:31:59.861` and "A container has been removed" at `.876`. A second `stop()` from `finishAndResolve` succeeds, so nothing leaks; the cost is a false error and a teardown marked incomplete. Two reviewers reported the same race on plain Linux Docker, one with containerd taking 10 to 20s to delete on a loaded Pi.
- **Fix**: only Docker's `removal of container ... is already in progress` error is waited out. The wait probes with `docker inspect` on the exact container name, backs off from 200ms to 1s, and gives up after 15s. If the container ends up `dead` or anything other than `removing`, it runs `rm --force` again. Any other `rm` error gets one probe and throws right away, and a failing probe (daemon down) still throws as `runtime-unavailable`.
- **Concurrency**: the wait makes `stop()` yield, so concurrent `stop()` calls on one handle share one in-flight teardown. The handle remembers which steps finished (main container, each auxiliary, private network), so a later `stop()` never re-runs a finished step but still retries what's left. Once the main container is gone, a later `stop()` also kills a `docker start --attach` process that hasn't exited, and every caller's reason is logged. This state is per handle: handles built independently by `listSessions` don't share it.
- **Network cleanup**: a `docker network rm` failure other than "not found" now rejects `stop()`. Before, it was swallowed, so the claim was released and the next session with the same name could fail on `network create`. Now the runner keeps the claim and lease, and the deferred finish retries only the network step.
- **Out of scope**: a name-keyed in-flight teardown shared across handles, running every cleanup step and rethrowing at the end, async probes (needs an async `Cli.run`), and logging Docker's raw error next to `opaqueRef`. The first one has an `it.todo` in `docker-driver.test.ts`.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `confirmRemoved`, "removal in progress", "session realization failed"). The change is limited to the Docker driver's stop path, its fake CLI, and a runner claims test.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/drivers/ src/container-runner` -> 10 files, 231 tests passed, 1 todo
- `pnpm test` -> 314 files passed, 2 skipped; 4329 tests passed, 15 skipped, 1 todo
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` -> clean
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the four changed files -> 0 errors, 18 warnings
- `src/drivers/docker-driver.test.ts` (`removal racing Docker auto-removal`) covers: in-flight removal resolving, a removal still pending at 8s that then finishes, giving up at exactly 15s, one last probe at 15s catching a removal that finished during the final sleep, an `rm` retry once the container is `dead`, other `rm` errors failing after one probe, the exact-name `inspect` argv, daemon outage, concurrent stops sharing one `stop` and one `rm`, a leaked network rejecting and then retried alone, "no such network" counting as removed, the attach process killed on a later stop, and every reason logged.
- `src/container-runner.claims.test.ts` adds a test that `killContainer` reaches `finish()` and its second `stop()` when supervision doesn't fire the terminal callback. The existing claim-retention test covers a rejected `stop()` keeping the claim and lease.
- Necessity checks: removing the 15s cap, the final probe, the finished-step skip, the network-removed flag, the attach kill, or `killContainer`'s fallback each fails the matching test.
- `FakeCli` gains an optional `once` flag on a scripted response, used by the new tests.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Stopping an agent container no longer logs a spurious "session realization failed: unknown" when Docker is still finishing its own auto-removal. A per-session network that can't be removed now keeps the session's claim and is retried, instead of leaking silently.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now installs jq, so Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup work on a stock Ubuntu or WSL install. It builds on #4200's sudo pre-flight, now merged.

- **Problem**: these skills pipe `curl` into `jq`, and nothing installs it. On WSL, Slack setup died at "Resolve your DM channel" with `jq: command not found`.   - An older install without jq: a step that fails because the shell can't find jq now says how to install it, instead of a bare exit 127.
- **macOS**: macOS 26 ships `/usr/bin/jq` (checked on 26.6.1); reports say 15 does too. The repo states no macOS minimum, so a Mac without jq gets it from Homebrew, which `nanoclaw.sh` already requires.

prs.title: fix(cli): named pipe for the ncl socket on Windows
prs.body:
## What

Node's AF_UNIX support on NTFS hits `EACCES` under the Windows service account (NSSM): the daemon binds but cannot `chmod data/ncl.sock`, then the next start re-binds and fails — the host circuit-breaker-loops on every restart. This is the same failure class the chat-style CLI adapter socket already had; the newer `ncl` host-side socket repeats the pattern.

## Fix

- Add `getNclSocketPath()` — `\.\pipe\nanoclaw-ncl` on win32, `data/ncl.sock` elsewhere (mirrors the existing `getCliSocketPath()`).
- `socket-server.ts`: skip the stale-unlink and `chmod` steps on win32 — the OS auto-cleans named pipes when the owning process exits, and `chmod` is meaningless on `\.\pipe\`.

The container-side `ncl` uses a DB transport, not this socket, so a host-only named pipe is sufficient.

## Production provenance

Observed on jsboige/nanoclaw (myia-ai-01, Windows host under NSSM): every service restart after the v2.0.30→v2.0.46 sync circuit-breaker-looped until this landed. Live in the fork's overlay as PATCHES.md#17 since 2026-05.

prs.title: fix(router): filesystem-safe separator in messageIdForAgent
prs.body:
## What

`messageIdForAgent` joins `${id}:${agentGroupId}` with a colon. Telegram's inbound `message.id` is already `${chatId}:${msgId}`, and the fanned-out id is later used as a filesystem directory name (attachment extraction under the session inbox). On Windows NTFS `:` is reserved (drive prefix / alternate data streams), so `mkdirSync` fails with `ENOENT` and inbound routing crashes for every voice/attachment message. POSIX accepts `:` in filenames, which is why this doesn't surface on Linux/macOS hosts.

## Fix

Use `_` as the separator and strip any remaining `:` from the base id. One expression change + comment explaining the constraint, plus an end-to-end router test asserting routed ids contain no `:`.

## Production provenance

Observed and patched on the jsboige/nanoclaw fork (myia-ai-01, Windows host): inbound routing died per attachment until this landed. Live in the fork's overlay as PATCHES.md#13 since 2026-05.

# Add a Tsubasa registry entry with an explicit 32K context-budget path

## Problem

IronClaw already has an OpenAI-compatible backend, but users configuring Tsubasa must enter the endpoint and model manually. A named provider could make credential setup and model selection clearer. Before exposing it as a normal agent choice, the 32,768-token combined input/output limit needs an explicit route through the existing context-budget configuration.

This is a feature proposal before implementation, following CONTRIBUTING.md. No provider feature code has been changed.

## Proposed scope

Reuse `ProviderProtocol::OpenAiCompletions` and the existing Rig adapter. Add one declarative entry to `crates/domains/ironclaw_llm/assets/providers.json` with:

- ID and display name `tsubasa` / Tsubasa.
- Default base URL `https://api.tsubasa.sh/v1`, optional `TSUBASA_BASE_URL`, and required `TSUBASA_API_KEY`.
- Default public alias `tsubasa-pro`, with `tsubasa-fast` also selectable as an explicit model.
- The existing API-key setup hint. Keep model listing disabled until it is qualified.
- The existing `unsupported_params` opt-out for `prompt_cache_key`: the shared adapter can otherwise attach this OpenAI-specific field when conversation metadata is present, while Tsubasa's request schema does not accept it.

Use the current registry/resolution owners rather than a new Rust provider module. Keep model facts separate from provider identity, as specified by the LLM module's CONTRACT.md. No tools, vision, reasoning, pricing, or privacy properties should be inferred from an OpenAI-compatible protocol.

## Context-budget decision

The inspected `PromptContextTokenBudget` default is 128,000 tokens, while its fields can represent a smaller context ceiling and a reserved output budget. The declarative provider record itself has no context-window field, and `LlmSlotSelection` currently contains provider/model/key-env/base-URL selection only. Adding a provider label alone would not prove that an ordinary selected agent route stays inside Tsubasa's 32,768-token total.

Please confirm the intended owner/configuration path for a per-selected-model context limit before implementation. A qualification test should capture the complete native prompt, reserve a bounded output allowance such as 4,096 tokens, and check the actual admission budget. Long-history truncation and oversized single tasks must be covered; a short client greeting would not establish those properties.

## Existing alternative

`[llm.default]` can select `provider_id = "openai_compatible"`, a public alias, `api_key_env = "TSUBASA_API_KEY"`, and `base_url = "https://api.tsubasa.sh/v1"`. This uses the existing explicit credential and endpoint override path. It is a source-inspected configuration route, not a qualified full-agent preset.

## Validation plan

Test registry parsing/selectability, explicit credential/endpoint precedence, the actual Rig JSON/SSE/401 path for both aliases, and complete prompt/output admission at 32,768 tokens. Run the owning crate's tests and module-charter checks plus the repository's required format, Clippy, build, and test commands. Reuse existing provider-chain assembly and shared hardened HTTP clients.

Inspected commit `b0b999d96781516ee05e6ba961d6f3ead900da96`, its registry, resolver, LLM module contract, config selection types, and prompt-budget contract. The unchanged budget module's three tests passed in an isolated Rust harness. No live Tsubasa inference or IronClaw request fixture is claimed. A Tsubasa issue/PR search found no existing contribution during this investigation.

Maintainer scope approval is pending.

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): make Windows text selection more reliable
prs.body:
## Summary

Windows selection toolbar fixes, found while testing in Edge and WPS on a 200%-scaled display.

### Large text produced no toolbar on scaled displays
selection-hook accepts a UIA selection only when one of its line rectangles is under 100 **physical** pixels tall. At 200% scaling any line over ~50 CSS px fails, so the whole selection is dropped (no event at all), e.g. the hero heading on lobsterai.youdao.com.

- `patches/selection-hook+2.1.2.patch` (Windows `engine.cc` only):
  - keep the text with `posLevel = None` when no rectangle passes; the hook then fills pointer positions and the toolbar is placed by the mouse;
  - the height limit is now 100 px × the monitor's DPI scale (`GetDpiForMonitor`, loaded at run time; 1.0 when unavailable).
- `scripts/build-selection-hook.cjs` / `npm run build:selection-hook`, run by `dist:win`: compiles the patched addon with node-gyp (x64), replaces `prebuilds/win32-x64/selection-hook.node`, removes `build/`, load-checks the result, and skips when already built from the current patch. Fails the build if the C++ build tools are missing.

Measured in Edge at 200% (UIA-selected, read with `getCurrentSelection()`):

| Text | Line rect height | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 110 px | 292 | no selection | text, pointer-placed |
| 66 px | 175 | no selection | text, own line position |
| 40 px | 107 | text, next line's position | own line position |
| 30 / 17 px | 81 / 47 | ok | ok |

### WPS Office selections were never read
UIA/IAccessible return no text in WPS (verified: every WPS selection came through the clipboard path). Enable selection-hook's clipboard fallback on Windows only for `wps.exe`, `wpp.exe`, `wpspdf.exe`; it saves/restores every clipboard format and only copies over the text I-beam. `et.exe` is left out because the hook matches names by substring (it would also match e.g. `telnet.exe`); WPS's combined window runs spreadsheets in `wps.exe`.

### Selection analytics
- The toolbar `shown` event now carries app category, well-known app id (others dropped), read method, position level, text length and the wait from gesture to toolbar.
- New Windows-only `miss` event: a drag/double-click over text (I-beam or app-drawn cursor at either end, via `GetCursorInfo`) that no readable selection followed within 2 s. Excludes LobsterAI, password managers, excluded apps, screenshot tools and drags on the toolbar.
- `msedgewebview2.exe` and `wpspdf.exe` added to the known app list.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/desktopCompanion src/shared/desktopCompanion` (514 passed)
- [x] Electron and renderer `tsc --noEmit`; ESLint on touched TS files
- [x] `npm run build:selection-hook` on Windows: compiles, replaces the prebuild, removes `build/`, second run skips
- [x] Hook still receives injected key/pointer input with the patched addon
- [x] Edge and WPS checks above
- [ ] Full `dist:win` on CI and a manual drag-select of large headings in the packaged app

Upstream fix for selection-hook to be proposed separately; the local patch and build step can be removed once a fixed version ships.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): snapshot Chrome MCP process trees natively on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary
On Windows the browser tool could become permanently unavailable. The in-app browser (the default display mode) attaches through OpenClaw's `existing-session` Chrome MCP driver. Before trusting a session, OpenClaw proves which processes it owns by listing every process with `powershell.exe Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` under a **2 s timeout**. That list runs twice per attach and at least three times per close.

On ordinary Windows machines the list takes 1.65–2.3 s, and up to 3.1 s under load (measured: bare PowerShell startup is only ~0.33 s, the cost is the CIM module plus enumerating ~420 processes). So most attaches failed with `Chrome MCP process inspection failed`. Our `openclaw-chrome-mcp-process-recovery.patch` then kept the session as `uncertain`, and every later browser command re-ran the same list first and failed the same way. Only a gateway restart recovered it.

This PR replaces the PowerShell list with a native Windows process snapshot (12–19 ms) and keeps PowerShell only as a fallback with a 10 s timeout.

## Related Issue
User feedback: browser tool permanently unavailable on Windows; the precheck enumerates `Win32_Process` through PowerShell with a hard 2000 ms timeout.

Upstream status: still unfixed on OpenClaw `main` and v2026.11.1 (same PowerShell list, same 2 s timeout), and no upstream issue or PR covers it. Upstream fixed the same class of bug in update repair (openclaw/openclaw#183238) via `@openclaw/proc-safe` (openclaw/openclaw#168942), which also removed koffi. When we upgrade past v2026.10.10, this patch should be rewritten on `proc-safe`'s `listProcesses()`.

## Changes Made
- New version-scoped patch `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/openclaw-chrome-mcp-windows-native-snapshot.patch`, applied after `openclaw-chrome-mcp-process-recovery.patch`:
  - New `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp-windows-processes.ts` reads the process table through koffi (`CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`, `OpenProcess`, `GetProcessTimes`, `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`). Each row's identity is `win32:<creation FILETIME ticks>|<image path>`. Exited and unreadable rows are dropped. A child is detached from a parent pid that now belongs to a younger process, so a recycled pid cannot pull an unrelated tree into `taskkill /t`.
  - The identity source is fixed per gateway run. PowerShell is used only if koffi cannot load or the first native read fails. A native failure after native rows were issued throws instead of switching sources, because mixing identity formats would make live owned processes look exited and skip their cleanup.
  - `chrome-mcp-process.ts` tries the native reader first on Windows; the PowerShell fallback timeout goes from 2 s to 10 s (two attach-time lists still fit the 30 s handshake). macOS `ps` keeps 2 s.
  - Unit tests, a Windows-only real-kernel32 test, and a Windows e2e (`chrome-mcp-windows-processes.e2e.test.ts`).
- `scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`: strong validator for the new patch.
- `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/README.md`: cause, measurements, design, verification, and removal condition.
- `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`: adds the patch to the reviewed set and checks its key lines.

koffi is already kept (real loader, not stubbed) in Windows runtimes for `openclaw-windows-private-directory-native.patch`; the bundled browser chunk resolves it through `createRequire`, the same way it loads `playwright-core`.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

**OpenClaw checkout (Windows 11):**
- 125 tests pass across `chrome-mcp-windows-processes.test.ts`, `chrome-mcp.test.ts`, `server-context.tab-ownership.test.ts`, `server-context.list-profiles.test.ts`. The Windows-only test reads this process, a spawned child, and the child's exit through real kernel32.
- E2E (`--config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`) with a real `.cmd` launcher → stdio MCP server → long-lived grandchild, and 2.5 s injected into every PowerShell list:
  - Native path: 5 attach/list/close rounds, attach 0.40–0.52 s, close 1.0–1.8 s, **zero PowerShell**, one `taskkill` per root, whole tree gone after each close.
  - Forced PowerShell fallback: every list took 4.7–5.2 s (all over the old 2 s limit) and attach and cleanup still succeeded.
  - Mutation check: with the fallback timeout set back to 2 s, the e2e fails with exactly the reported `Command timed out after 2000 milliseconds … Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`.
- oxlint clean on changed files; tsgo reports no errors in the browser extension or its tests (the remaining tsgo errors pre-exist in files changed by other patches).
- All 92 v2026.8.1 patches apply cleanly to a fresh v2026.8.1 worktree, and the result matches the tested files byte for byte.

**LobsterAI:**
- `npm test -- src/main/libs/openclawPatches`: 29 files / 108 tests pass; ESLint clean on the changed test file.

**Full app (rebuilt runtime, isolated user data, driven over CDP):**
- `window.electron.openclaw.browser.test({ profile: 'lobster-in-app' })` 5 times through the real gateway and LobsterAI's `.cmd` bridge launcher: **5/5 succeeded** (first run 18.6 s cold start, then 1.2–3.2 s).
- A native process watcher saw **no PowerShell started by the gateway**; the gateway log has no `process inspection failed`, cleanup failures, or 2 s timeouts.
- 10 bridge launchers started, ephemeral ones reaped by `taskkill`; only the cached session remained. After app shutdown the app, gateway, and every bridge process exited.

N/A

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [ ] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [ ] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [x] None

## Additional Notes
- Reviewers need to rebuild the OpenClaw runtime (`npm run openclaw:runtime:host` or `npm run electron:dev:openclaw`) to pick up the patch.
- Re-run the e2e from the OpenClaw checkout: `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts --silent=false extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp-windows-processes.e2e.test.ts` (drop the env var if `dist` is stale).
- Upgrade note: upstream removed koffi in v2026.10.10+ (openclaw/openclaw#168942). On upgrade, port this patch to `@openclaw/proc-safe/inspect` `listProcesses()` or drop it if upstream switches the browser extension itself.

prs.title: fix(auth): keep browser login visible and recoverable
prs.body:
## Summary
Users reported that clicking the login button in the bottom-left corner "does nothing". There were two causes:
1. Before opening the browser, the app looks up the login URL from overmind with no timeout. On a flaky network this took 7–9 s (seen in local logs), and the button showed no feedback in the meantime.
2. When the browser launch failed or stalled (`shell.openExternal` / ShellExecute, e.g. blocked by security software), the renderer ignored `success: false`. The user saw nothing and analytics still reported `success`.

Separately, once the browser *did* open, the app looked idle: the spinner disappeared after about a second while the user was still signing in.

This PR treats a login as a visible, recoverable **session** instead of a fire-and-forget click.

## Related Issue
User feedback: the login button does nothing on Windows (browser not opening).

## Changes Made
- **Login URL lookup timeout** (`auth.ts`): capped at 3 s. On timeout it falls back to the last resolved URL, or to the portal login page.
- **Browser open moved out of `main.ts`** into `src/main/libs/authBrowserLogin.ts`:
  - 10 s timeout on `shell.openExternal`; a stuck request is not retried.
  - A failed result now carries the login URL plus a `reason` (`open_failed` / `open_timed_out`, new `AuthLoginFailureReason` constants).
- **Shared browser login session** (`browserLoginSession.ts`): states `opening → waiting | open_failed`. It clears on sign-in, on cancel, or after 4.5 min (before the 5-min loopback callback server closes). It is not cleared by `authService.init()` / `destroy()`.
- **Sidebar account button**:
  - Shows "登录中 / Signing in" for the whole wait.
  - A non-modal status card anchored above it offers "重新打开 · 复制链接" as quiet text actions.
  - When the browser could not be opened, the card switches to a warning state with "复制登录链接" as the primary action.
  - Same-tick double clicks are ignored.
- **Login intro modal** (`ChatLoginExperienceModal`): on success it closes and the sidebar card takes over. On open failure it shows an inline "浏览器没能自动打开，复制登录链接" line instead of a generic failure toast. The duplicate toasts in `App.tsx` / `CoworkPromptInput.tsx` are skipped when a link is offered.
- **Analytics**: the account menu `login` action reports the real result, with `errorCode` set to the failure reason.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

Automated:
- New tests: `authBrowserLogin.test.ts` (timeouts, fallback order, manual URL) and `browserLoginSession.test.ts` (state transitions, expiry).
- Extended `auth.test.ts`: lookup timeout and cache, failure offers the link, the session clears on sign-in.
- The 68 login-related tests pass.
- ESLint passes (CI rules) on all touched files; `tsc` passes for both the renderer and `compile:electron`.
- The full `npm test` on Windows has 24 failures in unrelated suites: file modes, tab characters in filenames, POSIX paths, git timeouts, qqbot packaging. They are environmental and don't touch auth code.

Manual (`electron:dev`, Windows 11, isolated profile):
- From the login intro, a real browser handoff closes the modal; the sidebar shows "登录中" and the status card, and no modal appears.
- The sidebar button stays "登录中" through the wait.
- Copy link writes the correct URL to the clipboard; the × cancels and restores "立即登录".
- The open-failed card and the inline intro line were checked by driving the session state, since a real ShellExecute failure can't be reproduced locally.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
Screenshots of the waiting card, the open-failed card, and the intro inline line were captured during manual testing and can be attached on request.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (the related tests pass; the full suite has pre-existing Windows-only failures, see Testing)

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [ ] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

## Additional Notes
- **IPC contract**: the `auth:login` result is extended, not broken. On failure it now also includes `redirectUrl` and `reason`. Existing callers only check `success`. `StartupCreditCampaign` checks `success && redirectUrl`, which is unaffected.
- **Login path**: the login flow never used PowerShell. On Windows, `shell.openExternal` is ShellExecuteW. The PowerShell blocking users mention is most likely security software flagging the gateway process probe in `openclawWindowsProcess.ts` (`Add-Type` P/Invoke). That aggressive interception can also block the browser launch, which this PR now surfaces with a copyable link.

prs.body:
## Summary

Add Tsubasa to the existing provider setup and OpenAI-compatible registry. The
provider uses `TSUBASA_API_KEY`, defaults to `https://api.tsubasa.sh/v1`, and lists
`tsubasa-fast` and `tsubasa-pro` with 32,768-token context windows. Config-name
validation, the generated template, the README feature list, and the existing
provider guide are updated together.

This reuses the existing chat-completions transport and discovery path. Tools,
vision, and reasoning remain disabled in model metadata; the provider also
omits message names and unsupported reasoning controls. No dependency or new
transport is added. Static aliases remain available with `fetch_models=false`,
and conservative capability defaults are scoped to this provider, including
custom discovery aliases.

## Validation

### Completed

- [x] Follow-up regressions: all five targeted tests pass, including three new
  red/green checks for disabled discovery and provider-scoped capabilities.

- [x] `cargo test --locked -p moltis-providers tsubasa -- --nocapture`: two tests
  pass. Both aliases register with the correct context and capability defaults;
  controlled HTTP requests exercise JSON, authenticated SSE, usage, and 401
  propagation.
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p moltis-provider-setup new_api_key_providers_have_correct_env_keys`:
  one test passes.
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p moltis-config all_canonical_providers_accepted_without_warning`:
  one test passes.
- [x] `just build-web-assets`: passes. These generated assets were required by
  the broad Rust build and are not included in the diff.
- [x] `just release-preflight`: passes, including the required workspace and
  macOS Metal Clippy checks and pinned-nightly formatting. No gates were skipped.
- [x] `bash scripts/check-file-size.sh`: passes.
- [x] A separate native `ProviderRegistry::from_config_with_static_catalogs`
  fixture sent eight JSON/SSE requests with valid and invalid synthetic keys.
  Every serialized request passed Tsubasa’s actual schema and admission-budget
  helper. Unrelated OpenAI settings did not change routing or credentials.
- [x] `git diff --check`: passes.

Validation uses the pinned Rust nightly and a macOS 15.2 SDK. The machine’s
default macOS 27 SDK failed with an unsupported linker architecture; selecting
the installed older SDK resolves that toolchain failure. Native config/data and
XDG directories are isolated, real HOME is preserved, and no private credential
variables are inherited.

### Remaining

- [ ] `./scripts/local-validate.sh 1288`: executed, exits 1. Twelve local
  status contexts pass, including formatting, lint, native build, and selected
  Rust tests. The optimized Swift bridge and XcodeGen pass. SwiftLint 0.65.1
  fails `legacy_swiftui_aspect_ratio` at unchanged
  `apps/macos/Sources/MessageBubbleView.swift:244:26`. The same binary, config,
  and unmodified base source reproduce the same failure. The macOS app is not
  fully validated; iOS and later stages are not reached. No gate or upstream
  test was altered. No changed Playwright specs were selected by the script.
- [ ] Live inference and the settings UI against the live endpoint. The checked
  public `/v1/models` request from the original validation returned HTTP 404.
  A fresh curl request on October 17 returns HTTP 200 with both aliases; no
  fresh authenticated inference or native settings-UI success is claimed.

## Manual QA

The controlled transport exercise covers both public aliases, normal response
text, streamed text and usage, rejection of an invalid key, and isolation from
an unrelated OpenAI endpoint. It does not qualify long conversations, an entire
agent workflow, or live model tool behavior.

For live follow-up, set `TSUBASA_API_KEY`, select Tsubasa in Settings → Providers,
and check each alias with a short chat, a streamed response, and an invalid key.
Confirm the model context is 32,768 and the optional capability controls remain
disabled. Keep the PR as a draft until the outstanding checks are complete.

No private model identities, credential context, or actual keys are
included here.

issues.title: [Feature]: Expose row-only search on the structured recall_history tool

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

The Python REPL helper supports `ms.search(..., include_turn=False)`, and `MemorySpace.search` honors it, but the structured `recall_history` tool never accepts or forwards the flag.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Problem / Motivation

`include_turn=False` is the cheapest way to answer "which seqs match" without paying for full turn attachment. It is documented for the REPL (`repl.py:49-56`) and implemented in the search path (`memoryspace.py:883`), but the tool layer drops it:

- `recall_history` has no `include_turn` parameter (`recall_tool.py:979-996`).
- The call into `ms.search(...)` does not forward one (`recall_tool.py:819-829`).

So every tool caller always pays the attachment cost, even when the request only needs matching rows.

## Proposed Solution

Add `include_turn: bool = True` to the `recall_history` signature, forward it to `ms.search`, and document it alongside the existing `k` / date filters. Keeping the default `True` preserves current behavior.

## Alternatives Considered

- Make date-only searches row-only by default: changes existing output for current callers, so not proposed.
- Leave it REPL-only: keeps the capability unavailable to the main tool surface.

## Additional Context

A related cost factor, which can be split into its own issue if you prefer: the first hit page is fixed at `_SEARCH_HIT_PAGE_SIZE + 1 = 65` rows regardless of `k` (`memoryspace.py:28`, `memoryspace.py:1027`), so a `k=1` request still scans 65 rows.

Line numbers are from 2.2.2.post1.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

issues.title: [Bug]: Preserve SQLite errors when a search deadline has elapsed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1 (pip install), Python 3.12, Linux x86_64.

## Description

`MemorySpace.search` converts `sqlite3.OperationalError` into `TimeoutError` whenever the deadline has already passed (`memoryspace.py:777-782`):

```python
except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
    if budget.timed_out or time.monotonic() >= budget.deadline:
        raise TimeoutError("history search exceeded its execution timeout") from exc
    raise
```

The condition is temporal, not causal. A lock or busy error that surfaces after the deadline is therefore reported as "exceeded its execution timeout", which makes contention indistinguishable from a genuinely slow query. The original exception stays chained as `__cause__`, but the top-level type and message point at the wrong cause.

**Related PR(s):** none.

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Linux x86_64
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

Fault injection, no history database required. Same SQLite error, two deadlines:

```python
import sqlite3, time
from qwenpaw.agents.context.scroll.memoryspace import MemorySpace

class Conn:
    def set_progress_handler(self, *args): pass

for delay in (0.0, 0.03):
    m = object.__new__(MemorySpace)
    m._conn = Conn()
    m._search_turn_max_rows = 100
    m._search_turn_max_bytes = 10000
    m._search_max_seconds = 0.02
    def fail(*args, **kwargs):
        time.sleep(delay)
        raise sqlite3.OperationalError("database is locked")
    m._search_impl = fail
    try:
        m.search("example")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(delay, type(exc).__name__, "cause:", type(exc.__cause__).__name__)
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** before the deadline the error is re-raised as `OperationalError`; after the deadline it becomes `TimeoutError`.
- **Expected:** a lock/busy error stays distinguishable from an interrupted long-running query, either by type or by a structured error code.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
0.0   OperationalError cause: NoneType
0.03  TimeoutError cause: OperationalError
```

## Additional Notes

The reproducer injects a lock-shaped exception; it does not measure real SQLite lock timing. On a large `history.db` with concurrent readers, a real lock wait crossing the deadline would follow the same code path.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1 (pip install), Python 3.12, Linux x86_64, 2 vCPU.

## Description

`MemorySpace.search` resolves turn start seqs twice for the same hit rows:

1. `_collect_distinct_hits` resolves boundaries per fetched page (`memoryspace.py:1034`).
2. `_attach_search_turns` resolves boundaries again for the collected rows (`memoryspace.py:1275`).

Both call `_turn_start_seqs` over the same seqs, so the same boundary queries run twice inside a single search deadline budget.

**Related PR(s):** none yet; I can open one.

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (2 vCPU)
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

Run this isolated synthetic test; it needs no history database.

```python
import time
from qwenpaw.agents.context.scroll.memoryspace import MemorySpace, _SearchBudget

m = object.__new__(MemorySpace)
m._row_cap = 1000
calls = []

def boundaries(rows, budget):
    calls.append([r["seq"] for r in rows])
    return {r["seq"]: r["seq"] for r in rows}

m._turn_start_seqs = boundaries
m._load_turn = lambda hit, start, budget: (start, start, start, True, [hit])

budget = _SearchBudget(100, 100000, time.monotonic() + 60, 100, 100000)
rows, partial, _ = m._collect_distinct_hits(lambda offset, limit: [{"seq": 1}], 1, budget)
m._attach_search_turns(rows, 1, budget, raw_hits_partial=partial)
print(calls)
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `[[1], [1]]` — the same seq is resolved by two separate boundary passes.
- **Expected:** the boundary mapping computed during collection is reused where safe, so each seq is resolved once.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
$ python repro.py
[[1], [1]]
```

## Additional Notes

The second pass also has to cover rows appended by the saved-tool-output scan, so a fix should fill missing entries rather than replace the mapping — otherwise newly appended rows end up with `turn_start=None` and degrade to row-only output.

prs.title: fix(desktop): open workspace HTML via the decoded local path
prs.body:
## Description

The legacy desktop bridge (`WebViewAPI`, pywebview shell) opened workspace HTML previews by handing the percent-encoded `file://` URI from `GET /api/workspace/html-file-uri` (`Path.as_uri()`, UTF-8 percent-encoded) straight to `webbrowser.open`.

On Windows, `webbrowser`→`os.startfile`→ShellExecute percent-decodes with the **ANSI code page** — GBK on Chinese systems — so the UTF-8 encoding of a Chinese workspace path is decoded to garbage and Windows reports `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (issue #8502 复现 A; the same failure mode was verified with `ShellExecuteW` in the issue).

This change decodes the URI host-agnostically with `urllib.request.url2pathname` (UTF-8 aware, converts URI separators to native ones) and passes the **native local path** to `webbrowser.open` instead of the `file://` URL.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8502 (复现 A — the pywebview legacy bridge layer)

**Security Considerations:** None — the resolved URI already passed the loopback + `/api/workspace/html-file-uri` gate; this only changes how the resolved `file` URI is handed to the OS opener (same file the endpoint validated — suffix recheck unchanged).

## Testing

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py -q
..ss...                       [100%]
5 passed, 2 skipped in 0.43s
```

New regression case: `test_open_workspace_html_opens_the_decoded_local_path` builds a real workspace file at `workspace_dir/工作区/report.html`, feeds its `as_uri()` (percent-encoded) through the endpoint payload the same way the bridge consumes it, and asserts `webbrowser.open` receives the decoded native path. The test fails against `main` (assertion showed the encoded \'/C:/Users/.../%E5%B7%A5...\' arriving at the opener).

## Evidence

```
$ uv run pytest tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py -q
......ss                       [100%]
5 passed, 2 skipped in 0.43s

$ uv run pytest "tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py::test_open_workspace_html_opens_the_decoded_local_path" -q   # with the fix reverted
F                                                                                                                 [100%]
1 failed in 1.45s
```

FAIL output (fix reverted) — the opener received the encoded URI instead of the decoded native path:

```
E       AssertionError: assert [\'/C:/Users/T...imn6jmm_e7/工作区/report.html\'] == [\'C:\Users\...\report.html\']
E         At index 0 diff: \'/C:/Users/Tony/AppData/Local/Temp/tmpn6jmm_e7/工作区/report.html\' != \'C:\Users\Tony\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpn6jmm_e7\工作区\report.html\'
```

(The diff shows the pre-fix `unquote`-only form retaining the URI-leading \'/\'; with `url2pathname` the opener gets exactly the native path. The issue's复现 A error dialog — `file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/... Windows 找不到文件` — corresponds to that same encoded form reaching ShellExecute.)

Note: 复现 B (workspace-root-external file with pure-ASCII path, no reaction) involves a different layer (the Tauri shell invoke of `open_workspace_html` when the file sits outside the workspace root); that path resolves through the backend resolver and is not addressed by this bridge change.

prs.title: fix(scroll): keep sqlite lock errors out of search timeouts
prs.body:
Fixes #8620

## Description

`MemorySpace.search` turned any `sqlite3.OperationalError` into `TimeoutError: history search exceeded its execution timeout` once the clock was past the deadline. The progress handler is what actually aborts a long query, and it is the only thing that sets `timed_out`. SQLite does not call that handler while it waits out `busy_timeout`, so a lock that surfaces after the deadline was reported as a slow query. The original error stayed on `__cause__`, but the type and message pointed at the wrong failure.

The handler path is unchanged: when it aborts the statement, the search still raises that timeout. A lock, busy, or other `OperationalError` that the handler did not interrupt is re-raised as itself, whether or not the deadline has already passed. A deadline that has already expired before the search starts still fails in `ensure_time` with the same timeout, before any SQL runs.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8620

**Security Considerations:** None. This only changes which exception type is raised for a history-search lock. It does not read or log history contents.

prs.title: feat(tools): add SpecStream as a web_search provider
prs.body:
SpecStream's search API is the most accurate web search API in the world. It leads WideSearch at 60.9 and SimpleQA Verified at 99, ahead of Parallel, Exa, Tavily and Perplexity: https://specstream.ai/benchmarks

I work on SpecStream.

## Description

Adds SpecStream as a `web_search` provider, laid out like the Firecrawl provider from #8200.

1. `SpecStreamProvider` sends `GET https://api.specstream.ai/v1/web-search?q=<query>` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and maps the reply to the `title` / `url` / `snippet` / `content` shape the other providers return. `data.sources[]` become results (`title`, `url`, `snippet`). When `data.answer` is set, its `value` and `page` become the first result, titled "Answer".
2. The API has no result-count parameter, so the list is trimmed locally to `max_results`.
3. The key is required. It is read with the shared `read_optional_api_key()` from `tool/web_search/specstream`, and a missing key raises a readable error before any request goes out. Errors 401 (missing or invalid key), 402 (empty balance) and 503 (with `Retry-After`) come back as readable messages. Nothing is retried.
4. A small `_get` helper next to `_post` in `websearch/base.py` (same timeout, certificate validation on).
5. The Console modal and the tool config options get the `specstream` option. The default provider stays `anysearch`.

Price: $5 per 1,000 searches. Docs: https://specstream.ai/docs/search-api

No new dependency. No change to `web_fetch`, the MCP templates or the credential store.

**Related Issue:** None (provider integration, same shape as #8200)

**Security Considerations:** The key is read from the existing per-agent credential store and sent only as a Bearer header to `api.specstream.ai`. It is not logged. Tests use fake keys and mock all HTTP.

prs.title: fix(agents): sanitize malformed file content parts lacking file_id or file_data (#8280)
prs.body:
## Description

When a conversation history contains a file reference whose backing data is missing (e.g. from an unavailable file or an incomplete message block), OpenAI-compatible providers reject the request with HTTP 400:

```text
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'file must have a file_id or file_data'}}
```

This blocks the entire session from continuing until the corrupted reference is evicted from context.

This PR adds a post-formatting sanitization step in `FileBlockSupportFormatter.format()` via `_sanitize_malformed_file_parts()` in `src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`. Any `{"type": "file"}` content part lacking both `file_id` and `file_data` (either top-level or inside a nested `file` dict) is safely replaced with a descriptive text placeholder (e.g. `[File 'report.pdf' unavailable — data lost from conversation history]`) prior to wire transmission, while logging a warning. Valid file parts with `file_id` or `file_data` remain intact.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8280

**Security Considerations:** None. Malformed file parts are replaced with non-executable text indicators.

prs.title: fix(providers): recognize gateway context-overflow 400s
prs.body:
## Description

Strata (and other OpenAI-compatible gateways) rejects a request whose prompt plus `max_tokens` exceeds the window with:

```
prompt (83000 tokens) + max tokens (32768) exceeds the context (131072); requests are never truncated
```

Neither `QwenPawAgent._is_context_overflow_error()` nor the shared `classify_model_error()` matched that wording, so the 400 fell through as a generic bad request: Scroll's overflow recovery never ran and the turn failed even though eviction could have freed enough room.

Add the gateway's markers to both classifiers, and align the shared policy with the agent by also accepting `too many input tokens` (the agent's list already had it).

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** None. Only widens error classification for 400 responses that already match agent-specific wording.

prs.title: fix(token-usage): calibrate prompt estimates with provider-reported usage
prs.body:
## Description

AgentScope's default `count_tokens` estimates `utf-8 bytes / 4`. Prompts dominated by digits, UUIDs, timestamps and identifiers need 1.2-4x more tokens (Qwen-family tokenizers emit roughly one token per digit). Scroll compares that estimate with the compaction trigger, so a prompt can already be at the provider's limit while the local count still says it fits; compaction then starts too late or never runs.

This change pairs each local estimate with the prompt size the provider reports for the same request, keyed by `provider:model`, and scales later counts up by the observed factor. Calibration is advisory and one-sided (1.0-3.0x, never down): requests below 4K tokens are ignored, and a stored pair is not applied once the live prompt is far smaller than the prompt that produced it (after compaction), so it can never shrink the safety margin.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** None. In-memory, per-process factor keyed by model identity; no persistence and no external input.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Evidence

New unit suite `tests/unit/token_usage/test_calibration.py`:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/token_usage/test_calibration.py -q
10 passed in 1.41s
```

Existing token-usage and AgentScope-internals suites still pass:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/token_usage/ tests/unit/agents/context/test_as_internals_signatures.py -q
110 passed in 3.43s
```

Behavior covered by the new tests:

- `record("local:qwen", 10000, 14200)` makes the next 9K estimate count as 1.42x (digit-heavy prompt).
- A provider count below the estimate never scales it down (ratio floor 1.0); the ratio is clamped to 3.0.
- Estimates below 4K are ignored, and an unknown model is identity.
- A stale pair is ignored once the live prompt is far smaller than the measured one.
- `count_model_input_tokens()` applies the factor, and the model wrapper pairs `usage.input_tokens` from the response with the estimate taken for that exact request.

`black --check --line-length=79` passes on all four changed files.

prs.title: fix(context): reserve the configured output limit when planning compaction
prs.body:
## Description

Scroll reserved a flat 4K (or 5% of the window) for the model's output and compared the local prompt estimate against `min(trigger_ratio * window, window - 4K)`. Providers reject `prompt + max_tokens`, not the prompt alone. When the configured `max_tokens` is larger than that reserve, the trigger lands exactly on the rejection boundary: a 128K window with `max_tokens=32768` has a real prompt budget of 98304, which is also `0.75 * 131072`, so compaction never starts before the request is refused.

The prompt budget is now derived from the model's configured `max_tokens` (capped at half the window so a pathological value cannot starve the prompt), with a 15% margin below it so one step of growth still fits before the next check. `recover_from_context_overflow()` uses the same target when deciding whether a retry can succeed.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** None. Local token-budget arithmetic only.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Evidence

Reproduced against the current `main` with a 128K-window model configured with `max_tokens=32768`:

- Old trigger: `0.75 * 131072 = 98304`.
- Prompt budget the provider accepts: `131072 - 32768 = 98304`.
- The local estimate has to reach the trigger before compaction starts; at that point `prompt + max_tokens` already exceeds the window, so the provider rejects the request first and compaction never runs.

After the change the same model compacts at `(131072 - 32768) * 0.85 = 83558`.

Full Scroll unit suite:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py -q
92 passed in 10.66s
```

New regression tests:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py -q -k "input_token_limits or configured_output_limit"
3 passed, 89 deselected
```

- `test_input_token_limits_reserve_configured_output`: 100K window + `max_tokens=30000` -> 70K prompt budget.
- `test_input_token_limits_cap_pathological_output`: `max_tokens=90000` -> capped at 50K.
- `test_configured_output_limit_triggers_compaction_earlier`: a 70K live prompt (below the old 80K trigger, above the new 59.5K budget-derived one) now compacts.

issues.body:
## Summary

Make peer-agent turns durable, attributable runtime tasks instead of detached `process_message` calls with no sender or parent lifecycle.

## Problem statement

`send_message_to_peer` validates peer-group membership and channel binding, then launches the recipient turn as a detached `process_message` call. The recipient correctly rebuilds its own model, tools, workspace, memory, risk policy, and budget context, but the runtime loses important lifecycle facts at the dispatch boundary:

- sender agent identity and principal;
- parent turn or task relationship;
- durable queued/running/completed/failed status;
- cancellation linkage;
- result ownership and delivery status.

This makes peer work harder to cancel, resume, inspect, and attribute during incident reconstruction. `TaskKind::PeerInbox` already exists, but the peer delivery path does not use it as the production lifecycle owner.

This is adjacent to, but not fully covered by, #8844 and #9487. #8844 owns the `process_message` observability span lifecycle. #9487 owns the broader runtime-owned session architecture. This issue tracks the narrower peer-dispatch lifecycle needed regardless of the longer migration.

## Proposed solution

Route peer-agent delivery through one runtime-owned task lifecycle:

- create a durable `PeerInbox` task before dispatch;
- record sender, recipient, channel, parent turn/task, and delivery identity;
- transition one canonical record through queued, running, terminal, and cancelled states;
- propagate cancellation through that record;
- preserve the recipient agent's existing policy, memory, workspace, tools, provider, and budget ownership;
- make response ownership explicit, including whether a result is returned, stored for later retrieval, or intentionally fire-and-forget.

The implementation should reuse the runtime task/session direction in #9487 rather than introducing another peer-only task registry.

## Non-goals / out of scope

- Do not change peer-group authorization semantics.
- Do not transfer the sender's tool or risk-policy privileges to the recipient.
- Do not make peer responses public or transport-visible by default.
- Do not fold the full runtime-owned conversation-session migration into this issue.

## Alternatives considered

- Add logging fields to the detached spawn: improves diagnostics but does not provide durable status, cancellation, restart behavior, or result ownership.
- Leave this entirely to #9487: that RFC gives the long-term owner, but a concrete peer lifecycle acceptance target is still useful and independently testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every peer-agent delivery has one durable lifecycle record with sender, recipient, parent, and channel identity.
- The record reaches exactly one terminal state and survives the initiating request returning.
- Cancellation targets the recipient task without cancelling unrelated sender or recipient work.
- The recipient continues to use its own security policy, tools, workspace, memory, provider, and budget context.
- Restart and failure behavior are explicit and covered by regression tests.
- Observability events and cost records correlate to the same peer task identity.
- The implementation reuses or evolves the runtime task/session owner rather than adding a second lifecycle source of truth.

## Architecture impact

Likely surfaces:

- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/send_message_to_peer.rs`
- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/control_plane/task_registry.rs`
- runtime agent/session dispatch and cancellation paths
- peer lifecycle and observability tests

## Risk and rollback

Risk is medium because this changes asynchronous task ownership and cancellation. The main risks are double execution, orphaned records, cancellation leaking across tasks, or accidentally changing recipient policy resolution. Rollback is returning peer dispatch to the existing detached path while retaining no new durable state as authoritative.

## Expected routing

Should attach to an existing roadmap/tracker issue.

## Next decision surface

Align scope with #9487 and #8844, then decide whether this should land as an early runtime-task slice or remain an explicit acceptance target for the session migration.

## Breaking change?

No.

## Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.title: [Feature]: Bound peer-relay chains across recipient turns (A -> B -> A)
issues.body:
### Summary

Give `send_message_to_peer` a runtime-owned, finite chain limit that survives the recipient turn boundary, so an A -> B -> A relay chain stops at a configured hop count instead of relying on global cost.

### Problem statement

Follow-up requested by a maintainer in #9597 ("Enforcing a finite peer chain should be tracked separately and linked here"). Observed on `origin/master` at `641b76603`; read-only, nothing compiled or run.

- `max_delegation_depth` bounds nesting inside one turn. The check is `if self.depth >= max_depth {` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/delegate.rs:3244` and `:3574`); the increment I found is `depth: self.depth + 1,` (`delegate.rs:5488`).
- A peer turn does not inherit that depth. The recipient's tool registry is built from its own config, and its root `DelegateTool` is created at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs:3806` (`let delegate_tool = DelegateTool::new_with_options(`). `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md:71` documents that peer turns "mint a new root".
- The relay records its task without lineage: `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/send_message_to_peer.rs:475` (`kind: TaskKind::PeerInbox,`) writes `depth: 0` (`:481`), `parent_id: None` (`:482`) and `originator_chain: Vec::new()` (`:484`).
- Searching `\.parent_id\b` over every `*.rs` file at this SHA, the hits in `zeroclaw-runtime` are the SQLite write (`control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs:622`) and two test assertions (`control_plane/task_registry.rs:370`, `send_message_to_peer.rs:991`); the other hits are an unrelated Reddit field (`zeroclaw-channels/src/reddit.rs:270-289`). For `.depth` I searched only `control_plane/` and `send_message_to_peer.rs`: SQLite write (`task_store_sqlite.rs:621`) and one assertion (`task_registry.rs:367`). I did not read every `depth` match in the workspace. `originator_chain` is consumed for task visibility (`delegate.rs:2798`, `:2804`).
- `PeerGroupConfig` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/multi_agent.rs:158`) lists `channel`, `agents`, `external_peers`, `ignore`, `output_modality`, `admin_for_agent_scope`; none is a hop or cycle limit. `should_drop_self_loop` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/peers.rs:52`) takes a sender and an own handle, so it only compares A with A.
- `send_message_to_peer` is registered bare (`tools/mod.rs:2544-2553`, `Arc::new(tool)` with no `RateLimitedTool`).
- What does limit a chain today: each hop back needs the recipient's model to call the tool again (the relay does not auto-reply), and spend is recorded against a cost context built for the recipient (`send_message_to_peer.rs`, comment above `tool_loop_cost_tracking_context_for_agent(&cfg, &recipient_alias)`). As clarified in #9597, `CostTracker::check_budget` returns `Exceeded` above the daily/monthly limits (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/cost/tracker.rs:431`, `if projected_daily > shared_daily_limit`), which stops further provider calls. That cap cannot guarantee a finite chain: it depends on cost tracking being enabled and available, and on calls having recorded prices.

### Proposed solution

Per the maintainer guidance in #9597, and not as a new registry:

- The runtime derives the causal relationship at send time from the sending turn/task and records it on the `PeerInbox` row, reusing the existing `TaskRecord` fields (`depth`, `parent_id`, `originator_chain`). The linkage itself is #9597's "parent" requirement; this issue is the finite-chain enforcement that builds on it.
- The limit is enforced on the recipient side before another recipient turn starts, i.e. before the `registry.create(...)` / dispatch at `send_message_to_peer.rs:472-492`, with a clear refusal returned to the sending model.
- The count is authoritative and runtime-owned: not a tool argument, not model-suppliable, and not reset when a new recipient turn builds its tools from its own config (`tools/mod.rs:3806`).
- The recipient keeps applying its own permissions and risk profile; the chain carries a number and a parent link, not privileges.
- Open design question for maintainers: how the sending turn learns the id of the `PeerInbox` task it is running under (I did not trace this), and whether to reuse `max_delegation_depth` or add a peer-specific key.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Transferring the sender's tool or risk-policy privileges to the recipient (#9597 non-goal; #11667 is the separate policy question).
- Sender-side action checks on the single hop (#12167 / #12168).
- Exchange budgets for same-alias native Code sessions (#11119 / #11027); this issue is the cross-alias relay.
- Not audited, so not claimed either way: A2A and `send_via` entry points, daemon channel paths, a global concurrency cap on peer turns, and models with no price.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep global cost as the only cap (status quo): not a finite-chain guarantee, see above.
- Rely on #11119's finite exchange budgets: its first slice is same-alias native Code sessions and lists cross-alias delivery as out of scope, so it does not cover this relay unless reused.
- Populate `parent_id` only: per the #9597 reply, this alone would not make a depth limit apply across peer turns.

### Acceptance criteria

- With two agents and a fake provider whose turns call `send_message_to_peer` in a loop (A -> B -> A -> ...), the chain stops at the configured limit, and the count is not reset when the recipient starts a new turn (template: `tests/system/multi_agent_e2e.rs`).

issues.body:
### Summary

Extend the CI Quality Gate test job to a platform matrix (ubuntu / macos / windows) instead of running `cargo nextest run` only on `ubuntu-latest`.

### Problem statement

The Lint and Build jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already run on a three-OS matrix (`ubuntu-latest` / `macos-14` / `windows-latest`), but the Test job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` on `ubuntu-latest` only.

This means platform-specific regressions — path semantics, shell invocation, console encoding, platform-gated features — are never caught by CI. Concrete consequence: running the workspace test suite locally on Windows currently yields **74 failing tests** (tracked separately in the companion bug issue) while master CI stays green.

### Proposed solution

- Convert the Test job to the same `strategy.matrix` used by Lint/Build (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-14`, `windows-latest`).
- Skip or replace the mold-linker install step on non-Linux runners.
- Since Windows currently has a large number of known failures, roll out in two stages:
  1. Introduce the Windows test job as non-blocking (`continue-on-error: true` or a separate non-required check) to establish visibility.
  2. Flip it to required once the companion bug issue (Windows test failures) is resolved.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Fixing the existing Windows test failures themselves (tracked in the companion bug issue).
- Running tests on additional targets (Android, 32-bit, musl, etc.).

### Alternatives considered

- Keep status quo and rely on contributors testing locally — already proven insufficient (74 failures on Windows on current master went unnoticed).
- Add macOS only — macOS shares Unix semantics with Linux, so the incremental coverage is much smaller than Windows.

### Acceptance criteria

- `cargo nextest run` executes on ubuntu, macos, and windows in the Quality Gate workflow
- Windows failures are visible in CI (non-blocking at first, required once green)
- Workflow README/docs reflect the new matrix

### Architecture impact

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (tooling/ci) only; no runtime code changes.

### Risk and rollback

Risk: longer CI wall-clock time and possible flakiness on Windows runners. Rollback: remove the matrix entries / revert the workflow change.

### Breaking change?

No
