milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded agent owned-state retirement exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the agent owned-state retirement and knowledge-graph scoping in #9745 (which fixes #9647). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #9745 (`src/agent_owned_state.rs:741-745`, 2026-10-25), which found that the knowledge export-and-purge flow has no covering exception.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #9745 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `123b8396f3`, eighteen files: `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local,types,wss}.rs`, `src/tools/{mod,delegate}.rs`, `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`, `src/i18n.rs`, `locales/en/{cli,tools}.ftl` and `locales/{es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`. Most of it is continued work on a subsystem the crate already holds. On `master`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` carries `live_acp_session_count`, `archive_agent_workspace`, `OwnedStateReport`, `cascade_owned_state`, `RenameStateReport` and `cascade_rename_agent`, and the gateway reaches them through a three-line `pub use` shim; #9745 moves them into the new `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, re-exports the four functions from `agent_lifecycle` for compatibility, deletes the gateway shim, and extends them. The additions the row names are: the `PathPresence` classifier `inspect_lifecycle_path`, which re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe so an uninspectable path is residue on Windows as on Unix; the committed delete and rename residue contracts `committed_delete_residue_exists` and `committed_rename_residue_exists`, which probe the workspace, cron, control-plane (through the new read-only `SqliteTaskStore::count_existing_by_agent`), ACP, memory, knowledge and session stores; the shared resolvers that both contracts and both cascades use to reopen the configured memory or session backend when the live handle is absent, or for memory is the `none` placeholder, while config still expects persistence, so a delete or rename cleans or re-points that store instead of skipping it (on `master` the RPC delete substituted `NoneMemory` and warned, and the cascades returned zero for an absent backend); `AgentDeletionArchive`, which replaces `WorkspaceArchiveReport`, with an exclusively created leaf, `create_new` artifact writes and directory syncs up to the data directory, so a successful export gates the memory, knowledge, cron and ACP purges and a failure is reported in `warnings`; `prepare_knowledge_retirement` and `cascade_owned_state_with_retirement`, which export the agent's knowledge rows before the config commit, archive them as `knowledge.json` and purge through `KnowledgeGraph::purge_archived_owner` only while the store still matches the archived snapshot, plus the knowledge rename follower and the knowledge counts on both reports and the manifest; `plan_agent_delete_recovery_with_acp_count`, the recovery-mode preflight for a committed delete; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `run_agent_delete` behind `agents/delete` and `config/map-key-delete` (alias-grammar validation before any probe, so a reserved or malformed alias is now an `INVALID_PARAMS` error on `agents/delete` where `master` returned a `deleted: false` result; config-write authority for `agents.<alias>`, which `agents/delete` did not require before, and for every scrubbed path rechecked inside the commit, which neither method required before; a committed-delete retry that resumes the cascade without a config publication; and, on the map-key adapter only, refusing an agent with active RPC sessions as rename already does and answering `deleted: false` rather than an error for an unblocked alias with neither a config entry nor residue), the rename adapter validating both aliases and probing the old workspace through the classifier, `alias_create_refusal_message` for `config/set`, `config/set-many` and `config/map-key-create` when the alias they would create still owns knowledge or its store cannot be inspected, and the optional `owned_state` field on `ConfigMapKeyDeleteResult`; in `src/tools/mod.rs`, `knowledge_scope_for_agent` and the knowledge tool registration that binds a `KnowledgeScope` from the trusted agent alias, resolved per graph operation through the existing read-only live config handle (it registers no live-config consumer and acknowledges nothing) or from the configured `read_knowledge_from`, assigns unattributed legacy rows to `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` or the sole enabled agent, and withholds the tool when ownership is ambiguous; in `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `knowledge_tool_for_target`, rebinding the knowledge tool to the delegation target as the memory tools already are; the seven Fluent keys (five in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, two in `locales/en/tools.ftl`), of which `cli-alias-create-knowledge-{retained,uninspectable}` and `delegate-knowledge-init-failed` are translated in `es`, `fr`, `ja` and `zh-CN` with every-locale tests in `src/i18n.rs`; and the tests, including the test-only `pause_knowledge_archive_under` and negative-probe hooks and the `memory` parameter on the test-only `RpcContext::for_persistence_tests` with its call sites in `src/rpc/{dispatch,local,wss}.rs`. The row leaves out, as an implementation detail, the boxed `handle_config_map_key_delete` future that keeps `process_line` inside its stack budget. Everything else #9745 does lives in its owning crate and needs no runtime permission: `KnowledgeScope`, grant resolution, legacy assignment, `export_existing_owner`, the generation-checked `purge_archived_owner` and `rename_owner` in `zeroclaw-memory`; the scoped `KnowledgeTool` and the `model_routing_config` retirement check in `zeroclaw-tools`; the alias admission rule (`create_map_key_checked`, `ensure_knowledge_owner_retired`, `Config::ensure_map_key_for_path`) and the `read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` settings in `zeroclaw-config`; the HTTP adapters in `zeroclaw-gateway`; and the CLI paths in the `zeroclaw` binary. The row excludes per-principal ownership, the unwired Postgres graph (`knowledge_graph_pg.rs` is untouched), any new RPC method (the `Method` enum gains no variant), grant source, config key, store or persisted schema in the runtime (the existing archive bundle gains the `knowledge.json` artifact and its manifest counts), the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` (which still removes an agent without the cascade), the environment-override creation path (applied at config load without the retirement check), and any non-English locale beyond the three keys named. The `remove_agent` and environment-override items are pre-existing gaps #9745's body lists as out of scope. The row also says that it does not ratify the cascade's own landing in the crate (see below).
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge, so merging this pull request is what records the vote.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9647 and #9745 (head `123b8396f3`). Precedent: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062, the four row proposals open at the same table position.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #9745 gives every knowledge-graph row an owning agent and makes an agent's delete and rename carry that ownership with the alias: deletion exports the agent's knowledge, archives it next to the memory, cron and ACP exports the cascade already wrote, and purges it only when the archive is durable and still matches the store; rename moves ownership to the new alias; a committed delete or rename whose cleanup failed, or whose stores cannot be inspected, stays retryable on the RPC and gateway surfaces instead of reading as finished (the CLI's committed-rename retry is #10373); and no explicit config write can recreate an alias while its knowledge remains (an environment override that names a new agent is still applied at load, a pre-existing gap #9745 documents). The runtime half of that is the cascade itself, the RPC adapters that run it, and the knowledge tool's binding to the calling agent. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

### Why a row rather than relocation

Every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. The owned-state cascade sits in `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` on `master`, next to the delete preflight, and the RPC delete and rename adapters in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` already call it; the gateway and CLI call the same functions. It landed there on 2026-09-30 through #10621, after this table existed, and has no row of its own; this row covers #9745's changes to it and says so, and does not ratify that landing, which is a separate Core decision if one is wanted. The cascade reaches the cron store (`crate::cron`), the control-plane task store (`crate::control_plane`) and the runtime's Fluent catalogue (`crate::i18n`), all of which the holding crate still contains, so a crate of its own today would either pull those along or invert the dependency the kernel extraction is meant to settle. ADR-016 describes that case: extraction would establish a crate boundary the roadmap does not intend. #11701's proposed row (open, approved) names the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction as this subsystem's destination, and this row uses the same destination. The knowledge-specific logic that can live elsewhere already does: scope, grants, export and purge are in `zeroclaw-memory`, the tool in `zeroclaw-tools`, the admission rule in `zeroclaw-config`. What remains in the runtime is the lifecycle wiring between them.

### Coverage analysis

No row on `master` covers this work. All 47 active rows were read for the paths #9745 touches:

- `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`: no row names it. #11701 (open, approved) is the first row to touch the file, for #11301's rename recovery, and its scope cell excludes exactly this work: "No delete recovery, knowledge-graph follower, new follower store, new lifecycle operation, or non-English locale".
- `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`: named by the #10905, #10407, #11466/#11506, #10911, #11181, #10513/#10522, #11607, #9872/#10391, #11692, #11622, #11513, #11698, #11730, #11221, #11463 and #11286 rows. Each is limited to its own pull request and behavior (compaction, session prompts, config receipts, live-config publication, steering provenance, `sops.run`, the refresh pre-filter, the delegation ceiling call, budget warnings, message times, the profile projection, personality reload, delegate activity, tool selection, diff capture, one WSS regression). None covers the agent delete or rename adapters, alias admission, or the map-key delete response's `owned_state` field and `deleted: false` answer (the #11466/#11506 row covers only that response's `revision` receipt).
- `src/tools/mod.rs` and `src/tools/delegate.rs`: the #9872/#10391 bounded-delegation row covers rebuilding "a bounded delegate's context-sensitive tools for the target workspace", but is limited to #9872/#10391 and the caller ceiling; the #11221 row covers built-in tool selection and name reservation; the #11462 row covers delegate operator approvals; the #11465, #11473, #10331/#11450, #11292, #11730, #11456, #9579, #9447, #11698, #10911 and #10407 rows cover cancellation context, schema deferral, worker-loss recovery, progress, activity forwarding, resident-memory supervision, the docs skill, terminal handling, personality reload, live-config publication and session prompts. None covers binding the knowledge tool to a `KnowledgeScope` or rebinding it for a delegate. The #10911 row excludes a "new live consumer" of the live-config authority; the knowledge scope only reads the existing read-only handle per graph operation and registers nothing, which the row states.
- `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`: the #9597 row (task registration and settlement) and the #11292 row (progress persistence) do not cover a read-only residue count.
- `src/i18n.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,types,local,wss}.rs` and the locale files: each row naming them is limited to its own keys, fields, exports and tests.

The row therefore records the moved cascade and its additions together, so the holding crate's debt for this subsystem is legible in one place.

### Rebase note

Four other row proposals are open and append at the same table position: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062. Whichever lands later takes a one-line conflict fix. #11701 (for #11301) is adjacent in subject: it adds the rename recovery contract in `src/agent_rename_recovery.rs` and the path classifier and directory sync helper in `src/lifecycle_path.rs`, and removes the rename follower cascade from `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`, while #9745 adds `inspect_lifecycle_path` and the archive sync chain inside `src/agent_owned_state.rs` and moves and extends `cascade_rename_agent`. The two feature pull requests reconcile that duplication at rebase, whichever lands second, and the row for the one landing second is refreshed to the paths it then uses. This row describes #9745 at its current head.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; documentation-only change to a Markdown table. Please review the row's scope against the #9745 head (`123b8396f3`): `git diff --numstat 5d4b18d335 123b8396f32c0458707d37eebf7fe9c54027baa0 -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime` lists the eighteen files it names.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Docs Style` job's added-links gate (`docs_links_gate.sh`), which reads every changed Markdown file. That job's all-internal-links gate (`check_internal_docs_links.py`, default root `docs/book/src`) and its markdown-lint and em-dash step read only `docs/book/src`, so both were run by hand below, the link check with `--root crates/zeroclaw-runtime`. The comment-hygiene gate scans only Rust, TOML, shell, Python and Nix sources, so a Markdown change cannot trip it; it was run anyway, with a working ripgrep placed on `PATH` because the Homebrew one on this machine cannot load `libpcre2`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no CI markdown lint or full internal-link check for `crates/*/AGENTS.md` (both run by hand below). No check can confirm that a row matches the code it covers or that a Core decision exists; that is this review.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(acp): show the shell command as the tool-call title
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - ACP clients render a tool call's `title`. Both the pending `tool_call` and the completing `tool_call_update` set that field to the tool name, so a shell call was displayed as the literal word `shell`.
  - Shell titles now use the `command` argument (whitespace collapsed, truncated to 160 characters). The completion update restates that title, because the result event does not carry the original arguments and a client that replaces the title would otherwise fall back to the tool name.
  - Session-load replay uses the same title, including on the replayed completion update.
  - The ACP book example that showed `"title": "shell"` now shows the command.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change shell execution, approval, `rawInput`, `rawOutput`, or titles for tools other than `shell`. `name` remains the tool name. `deliver_file` still prefers its artifact title.
- **Blast radius:** ACP session updates emitted by `AcpServer`, including the gateway WebSocket ACP bridge and `session/load` replay. Clients that displayed `title` see the command instead of `shell`. Clients that key off `name` are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

When an ACP client shows a shell tool call, the label it renders is the protocol `title`. ZeroClaw was filling that label with the tool's name, so the card said `shell` instead of the command being run. The completion update sent `shell` again, which replaced a better title if a client does not merge updates.

This PR puts the command in that label, and repeats the same label when the call completes and when a saved session is replayed. The command text was already in `rawInput`; this only changes what the client is told to display.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` `acp` (stdio ACP and the gateway WebSocket ACP bridge both use `AcpServer`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A running daemon built from this branch, an ACP client connected through `zeroclaw acp` or `zeroclaw-acp-bridge`, and an agent allowed to use the `shell` tool.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On `master`, ask the agent to run a shell command such as `git status --short`.
  2. Note the tool-call label in the ACP client while the call is pending and after it completes.
  3. Repeat on this branch with the same prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The tool-call title is the command (for example `git status --short`), both while pending and after completion. Stdout still appears as the tool result body.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same card is labeled `shell`.

### How I tested

Focused library tests cover the notification boundary this PR changes. Full workspace `cargo test` and the docs gates were not run locally; see the skip note.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet. Required CI has not run on this head, so it is not evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local checks did not include the full workspace test suite, cross-platform lint, or the docs style/link gates. The Markdown edit is one string inside an existing JSON example and adds no links.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text

rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)

$ cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-channels -- --check
(no diff; exit 0)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features default-channels -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 24s

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features default-channels shell_tool_title
test orchestrator::acp_server::tests::shell_tool_title_is_the_command_not_the_tool_name ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2057 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features default-channels turn_tool_events_include_client_visible_tool_fields
test orchestrator::acp_server::tests::turn_tool_events_include_client_visible_tool_fields ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2057 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features default-channels deliver_file_tool_call_update_title
test orchestrator::acp_server::tests::deliver_file_tool_call_update_title_uses_artifact_title ... ok
test orchestrator::acp_server::tests::deliver_file_tool_call_update_title_falls_back_to_name_without_artifact_title ... ok
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2056 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features default-channels history_replay_restates_shell_command_as_title

```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The unit tests assert the exact `session/update` title for a pending shell call (`ls -la`), the completion update (`ls -la`, not `shell`), whitespace collapsing, truncation, the missing-command fallback, `deliver_file` title precedence, and session-load replay. I did not rebuild or restart the running daemon, and I did not watch a live ACP client render the new title.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact protocol output
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `3c6382115e65ff94bdd925a3a45e4f20713e4152`. The observed interface is the ACP `session/update` JSON produced by `notification_for_turn_event` and `history_notifications_for_message`, not a rendered client frame. No locale or terminal-width dependence.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Pending shell call title is `ls -la` (`turn_tool_events_include_client_visible_tool_fields`). Completion update title is `ls -la` when the call's title is remembered. Replay title is `git status --short` on both the call and the completion update (`history_replay_restates_shell_command_as_title`).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A shell `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` pair no longer publishes `title: "shell"` when the command is known.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. Shell tool-call `title` values change from the tool name to the command. `name`, `kind`, and `rawInput` are unchanged. No config migration.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk display fix. `git revert 3c6382115e65ff94bdd925a3a45e4f20713e4152` restores the previous titles.

prs.title: feat(session): implement append-only session event history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replace separate transcript writers with a shared, append-only session history. Record accepted inputs, model attempts and reasoning, tool execution, approvals, failures, model changes, context compression, and child-agent activity so recovery can reconstruct what actually happened.
  - Separate typed contracts and replay (`zeroclaw-api`), storage and migration (`zeroclaw-infra`), execution and authorization (`zeroclaw-kernel`), and application wiring (`zeroclaw-session-host`). CLI, RPC, ACP, channels, gateway, Web, and ZeroCode consume the standard session model.
  - Use one canonical `session_id`, with protocol source recorded only as creation metadata. Add a rebuildable session index, persistent titles and workspace metadata, same-session branches, copied sessions with shared frozen history, child sessions, and disposable temporary sessions.
  - Support SQLite and JSONL, resumable migration from master's stores, source-file backups, backend switching, and interrupted-execution recovery. Keep message, reasoning, tool, and multimodal content typed through the internal pipeline; convert protocols at provider/channel boundaries and parse legacy attachment markers only during import.
  - Store the cost ledger in the selected backend, attributed to actual session IDs where available. Preserve reported input/output tokens, cache reads and cache creation separately, and pricing evidence. Historical provider references remain unchanged when configuration aliases are renamed or deleted.
- **Scope boundary:** Full attachment/blob lifecycle work remains under #9488. This does not add history-content credential filtering, new at-rest encryption, a tamper-detection hash chain, automatic replay of external effects, a dashboard redesign, or a complete runtime extraction. Existing config-reference, authorization, and ownership rules still apply to provider edits.
- **Blast radius:** Session creation, listing, history queries, persistence, resume and TTL handling; provider/tool dispatch and approvals; compression and delegation; CLI/RPC/ACP/channel/gateway adapters; Web/ZeroCode session consumers; cost persistence and legacy migration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10526. Related #9600. Related #9487. Related #9488. These broader contracts and coordination issues are not automatically closed.

### Crate boundary changes

- **`zeroclaw-runtime → zeroclaw-kernel`:** The runtime calls the extracted session execution, recovery, authorization, approval, context-maintenance, and model-selection code through the kernel's ports. This dependency keeps those decisions in one owner instead of copying them into each entrance or back into the runtime holding crate. Kernel has no production dependency on runtime, providers, or channels, so this does not create a dependency cycle or move concrete model adapters into the kernel.
- **`zeroclaw-runtime → zeroclaw-session-host`:** The shared host wires the configured SQLite/JSONL backend, installation migration, repository, and kernel coordinator for all entrances. Retaining this dependency replaces the old direct ACP/transcript-store construction with one standard session implementation. Its runtime use is transitional: application composition already injects a session source, but daemon startup retains a native fallback and some lifecycle operations still open the repository directly. Those calls can later move behind narrow injected session-management ports; the boundary is not a new independent persistence owner or a claim that runtime extraction is complete. The runtime dependency ratchet also needs these new edges and their owners to be reconciled; adding manifest entries alone does not establish the architectural justification.

### What this does, simply

A transcript records messages, but does not reliably explain which model ran, what a tool did before an interruption, or which context survived compression. This PR records those observations as ordered events and rebuilds conversation views and working context from them.

With persistence enabled, reopening after a restart or TTL expiration restores the same logical session and its retained context. Recovery preserves partial execution and diagnostics; an unproven tool outcome stays unknown rather than being reported as successful or silently executed again. Historical permissions and approvals never grant current access.

SQLite and JSONL share the same logical format. Existing histories are imported into the configured backend and the old files are renamed as backups. ACP no longer owns a separate execution-history database. A session index provides discovery metadata; the event history remains authoritative. A copy gets a new session ID and references a frozen source prefix, while a fork creates a branch inside the same session. Temporary sessions are hidden and removed on close or cleanup after restart.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Use separate disposable installations for `master` and this branch; migration changes the on-disk writer format.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; automated coverage also exercises RPC, ACP and messaging-channel boundaries.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an agent named `fixture` with a working provider and a harmless permitted tool. Stop other writers. Repeat with `channels.session_backend` set to `sqlite` and `jsonl`.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a fixture --session-state-file /tmp/session-events-review.json`, exchange messages and request a harmless tool action, exit, then reopen with the same command. Repeat against a disposable copy of an installation containing legacy session/ACP history. Inspect `<data-dir>/sessions/` and its backups after import.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The standard event store and installation manifest contain execution observations and retained context. Reopening retains the conversation; imported source files become backups. Reading history does not repeat the tool. Renaming a provider alias does not rewrite its old historical references; select an available model manually if an old reference no longer resolves.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Separate transcript stores retain conversation messages, but do not provide this common execution-event history, shared session index, or installation-wide cutover.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No claim that required CI is fully green. The latest pushed revision is `2fac551de5`; its [CI run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41801200397) reports failures, including default-stack tests, the CLI cost fixtures, and the runtime dependency boundary check. These are not claimed as resolved on that pushed revision. Local evidence below covers the latest functional change and the subsequent master merge.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full workspace/all-features, platform/MSRV, million-event performance, and VM power-loss matrices were not repeated locally for the latest revision. Runtime tests below used a 16 MiB test-thread stack; they do not prove the default-stack gateway issue is resolved. Search currently builds a disposable authorized FTS view per query; no persistent full-text-index performance claim is made.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux, Rust 1.99.0, locked dependencies. Provider-edit checks ran on `ad2c3060d0`'s source; the subsequent `2fac551de5` merge only added master's desktop release workflow, smoke script, documentation and architecture tests.

```sh
TMPDIR=/tmp RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib provider_alias_ -- --test-threads=4
# gateway: test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
# runtime: test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test component provider_rename_cli -- --test-threads=1
# test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test architecture desktop_release -- --test-threads=4
# test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test architecture release_workflow -- --test-threads=4
# test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash -n scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh
# exit 0
git diff --check
# exit 0

DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md BASE_SHA=HEAD \
  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# Linting: 1 file(s); Summary: 0 error(s)
```

Earlier validation before the last provider-policy change included the config suite (1,958 unit tests plus 131 integration tests), gateway library suite (774 tests), CLI config suite (30 tests), and all-targets Clippy with warnings denied across API, infra, kernel, host, providers, runtime, channels, gateway and the root package. These are earlier evidence, not a fresh whole-PR run. Earlier session-specific suites covered migration/recovery, capture, authorization, compression, branches, copies and temporary cleanup.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed master's newly merged desktop packaging change against native daemon initialization; it required no storage adaptation. Automated SQLite/JSONL tests compare the original historical event prefix before and after provider configuration edits, verify manual model selection and reopening, and exercise CLI renames during native and incomplete migration states. Config-upgrade regressions preserve backend choice, persistence/TTL settings, history paths and the old config backup. No fresh Windows/macOS installer or VM power-loss smoke is claimed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot evidence remains outstanding for the Web/ZeroCode session-consumer changes. This PR does not redesign their layout, but no fresh final-interface capture is supplied.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ad2c3060d0` for provider-edit behavior; `2fac551de5` for the merge and architecture checks. Test boundaries: `tests/component/config_patch_cli.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_config.rs`, and `tests/architecture/{desktop_release,release_workflow}.rs`. Storage contract: `docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Automated output tails are included above. They cover storage/protocol behavior and do not replace final-interface evidence for Web/ZeroCode.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Native history no longer blocks provider alias edits; historical selections remain unchanged, manual selection persists, and configuration ownership checks still reject an unauthorized offline writer. The merged release workflow preserves the embedded dashboard dependency and smoke-test ordering.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Platform release builds and VM crash/power-loss tests require their respective environments. The actual packaged-desktop smoke was not run locally. The imported `apps/tauri/TESTING.md` has existing Markdown issues outside the changed lines; its full-file docs gate is not claimed as passing.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Adds session execution/query capabilities and durable files under the configured data directory. Current owner, policy, and reasoning-read authorization are checked at use; stored evidence cannot mint grants.
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing providers, tools and delivery transports remain responsible for network effects; reading/replaying events does not dispatch them.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No for configured credentials.** Existing credential encryption and provider error/log handling remain unchanged. History preserves observed content in plaintext, including credential-shaped text; it is neither filtered nor newly encrypted.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Tests use synthetic fixtures.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Context reconstruction now consumes event-backed content. Unknown provider fields remain evidence rather than instructions or authority, and replay cannot authorize tools or other effects.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: More execution detail, including reasoning and diagnostics, is retained. Authorized reads and explicit payload erasure protect the supported local access boundary; erasure does not certify removal from backups, snapshots or exports. Operators remain responsible for those copies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for old writers after storage cutover; master's supported stores are imported.** Migration targets the new format directly, without an intermediate per-session locator or a second ACP store. Unknown event types/codecs retain their raw type and fields while readers skip unsupported semantics.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Reuses existing backend, persistence and TTL settings; CLI persistence, session IDs and downstream session consumers are wired to native storage. Protocol source is metadata, not part of session identity. Provider aliases may be renamed/deleted under existing configuration rules without rewriting history. No new storage-selection environment variable is required.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The declared Rust 1.96.0 floor is unchanged; local commands used 1.99.0.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Stop old writers and take a consistent backup of config and the complete data directory, including SQLite WAL state where applicable. Select `sqlite` or `jsonl`, then start the new binary. Import resumes after interruption and publishes Ready only after successful import and source archival. Legacy session and ACP files are renamed as backups. Existing configuration schema upgrades retain their own backup. Do not run an old binary against the migrated installation. If an old provider reference becomes unresolved after a configuration edit, manually select an available model.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before storage migration, revert the PR's changes or deploy the prior binary. After migration, stop all writers, preserve the new installation separately, restore the complete pre-upgrade config/data backup, then deploy the prior binary. Code rollback alone does not reverse the format cutover; preserve post-upgrade writes separately for recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No switch restores legacy writers. `channels.session_backend` selects SQLite or JSONL; native backend switching is not a downgrade. Persistence-disabled channels retain their existing in-memory mode.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Session initialization or migration refuses an incomplete/conflicting import; capture failures stop execution; interrupted effects retain unknown outcomes and diagnostics. Inspect initialization/migration/capture errors and `sessions/session-format.json`. Do not delete the manifest or bypass writer fencing to force an older writer.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(runtime): degrade text-only follow-ups instead of pinning to the …
prs.body:
**Fixes #11706**

### Summary

- Fixes the "sticky vision route": with `[multimodal] vision_model_provider` configured and a text-only primary, a single image sent on any turn pinned every subsequent turn — including pure-text follow-ups ("now summarize that doc") — to the vision provider for the life of the conversation.
- Root cause: the vision router keyed the configured-fallback branch on `count_image_markers(history)`, a whole-history count of loadable image markers. The `[IMAGE:]` marker from an earlier turn never leaves the conversation history, so `image_marker_count > 0` was true forever and the fallback was always selected. `max_image_turns` only trims the provider request payload; routing never sees the trim (reported in #11706).
- Fix: the fallback branch now gates on whether the CURRENT turn carries an image, via a new `count_current_turn_image_markers()` helper (markers in the latest user message + declared attachments of current-turn tool-result carriers). A turn whose only markers are carried over degrades to the primary text provider with the stale markers stripped (`degrade_strip_images = true`), exactly like the existing no-fallback degrade path.
- Current-turn images still route to the configured fallback — including tool-produced screenshots, which stay "live for the user turn that produced them" per the existing `current_turn_tool_result_indices` contract.
- Two regression tests added: `configured_fallback_with_text_follow_up_degrades_instead_of_pinning` (the #11706 repro) and `configured_fallback_keeps_current_turn_tool_attachment_on_vision_route` (guards the current-turn tool-image case).

**Scope boundary:** no change to the no-fallback resolvability branch (its degrade-vs-error behavior is untouched); no change to `max_image_turns`/`max_images` semantics; no config, CLI, or provider surface changes; no edits outside `vision_route.rs` and `multimodal.rs`.

**Blast radius:** conversations with a text-only primary + configured `vision_model_provider`. After this change, pure-text turns in those conversations are served by the primary text model with carried-over markers stripped, instead of the vision fallback — the intended behavior change per #11706. Unaffected: vision-capable primaries, no-fallback configs, and any turn that actually carries an image.

**Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11706 (this PR fully resolves the pinned-provider behavior).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw routes image-bearing turns to a vision-capable provider and normally handles text with a cheaper, faster text model. The bug: once any message in a conversation contained an image marker, the router based its decision on "any image marker anywhere in the conversation's history" — and the marker lives there forever — so the conversation got stuck on the vision provider for every later text-only message. That cost image tokens on every turn (the image kept being re-sent) and locked the thread into the configured vision model.

This PR changes the decision basis from "did this conversation ever have an image?" to "does THIS turn have an image?" — the latest user message, or an image returned by a tool in this turn. If neither exists, the turn is served by the primary text model and stale markers from earlier turns are replaced with a text placeholder. One screenshot no longer condemns the rest of the conversation to the vision provider.

### Testing

**Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the behavior is user-visible and the A/B below is quick with a text-only primary + a cheap vision fallback configured.

- **Interface(s) exercised:** cli (agent session surface; multimodal routing is provider-agnostic).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with a non-vision primary (e.g. `openrouter.default`) and `[multimodal] vision_model_provider = "openrouter.vision"` (any vision-capable alias); a second separate instance/data dir so an operator install is untouched.
- **Steps to run:** 1) send a message with an image; 2) confirm the response comes from the vision provider; 3) send a pure-text follow-up ("ok, now summarize the doc"); 4) observe which provider/model serves the follow-up in the request logs.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the image turn is served by the vision fallback; the text follow-up is served by the primary text model with no re-sent image payload.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** both turns — and every subsequent turn — are served by the vision fallback, with the image re-encoded/re-uploaded each time.

**How I tested**

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Quality Gate `Test` job (`cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`) runs the new `vision_route` regression tests; `Format`, `Lint` (clippy `-D warnings`), and the `Check` jobs cover compile/fmt. CI on PR #11716 is the compile+test evidence — no local Rust toolchain is available in the authoring environment.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for this surface beyond the manual A/B step above.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Current-head Quality Gate Test, Format, Lint, and compile checks pass. Local `cargo fmt/clippy/test` was not run in the authoring environment.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?:** The author [reported an OpenRouter roundtrip](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11716#issuecomment-6237596481): an image request used the vision provider and subsequent text turns used the text-only provider. The routing logic was also traced against the pre-existing `vision_route` tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no visual/UI surface changed (routing + message preparation only).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated CI covers `94077b1092e733c0153bcf7d443d0dd6621b7389`. The live OpenRouter report is linked above; its binary revision was not stated.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the screenshot in the linked author report.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The author reports that the text-only provider was invoked after the image request.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** local `cargo fmt/clippy/test` — no Rust toolchain in the authoring environment (disk-constrained VM); CI covers all three.

### Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — the degrade path reuses the existing `strip_message_media` placeholder behavior; no new text reaches the provider.

### Compatibility

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — the routing behavior change is the intended fix; the config surface is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

### Rollback

- **Medium-risk PR:** revert the merge commit to restore the previous vision routing behavior.

### Supersede Attribution

- Not applicable — no `Supersedes #` used.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11076 adds the `agy_cli` coding-CLI tool. Its implementation lives in `zeroclaw-tools`, but registering it touches three files in this holding crate. Review on #11076 found no exception row covering that wiring, and the maintainer review there [recommended this separate proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11076#discussion_r4463798491) with the scope used here.
  - This adds one pending row at the end of the active-exception table. It covers the `tool-agy-cli` feature forwarding in `Cargo.toml`; the `AgyCliTool` re-export, the `tool-agy-cli` feature in the existing coding-CLI `cfg` gates, its `any_coding_cli_tool_enabled` term, the compiled-out warning, the `select_tool!`/`register_tool!` block and the `agy_cli` cases in the existing coding-CLI registration tests in `src/tools/mod.rs`; and the `tool-agy-cli` and `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in `locales/en/tools.ftl`.
  - Destination: the tool-composition owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction; the implementation stays in `zeroclaw-tools`. Review condition: when application wiring takes over native tool construction (#11187), or before the scope expands.
  - The approval cell says **Pending Core Team review**. If the row is approved, I'll record the approving handle and review link in a follow-up commit on this branch before merge, as #11980 did.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. Every existing row is unchanged. It covers no other coding-CLI tool, and grants no new executor, tool grant, approval or sandbox authority.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of #11076's runtime wiring under ADR-016.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11076, Related #11187

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core Team decision, and a feature PR can't grant itself one. This row is that record for #11076's registration of `agy_cli`, so reviewers can approve or narrow it here before #11076 merges.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for scope: compare the row's paths with `git diff --name-only master...pull/11076/head -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A, documentation only.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None specific. The docs quality and link gates cover `docs/book/src`, not this file.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `git diff --stat master` shows `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md | 1 +` with no line removed. `git diff --name-only master...388ee8df0 -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime` (the current #11076 head) lists exactly `Cargo.toml`, `locales/en/tools.ftl` and `src/tools/mod.rs`, the three paths the row names.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No build or tests: no code changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, if Core approves: the row permits the named additions in the holding crate. It grants no runtime authority.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the commit. If #11076 has merged by then, its code stays; reverting withdraws the permission for further additions under this row.

prs.title: feat(tools): route Discord external peers to an explicit destination
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #12116: the first commit is #12116's head (`5cf13a6aa`, patch-identical), and this PR's change is the second commit. Review the second commit, or the diff after #12116 merges.
- **What changed and why:**
  - On Discord, an `external_peers` entry is a user ID, but messages are posted to channels and threads. `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via` used that user ID (for `send_via`, the group's *first* entry) as the destination, so sends to a Discord external peer failed with Discord's 404 `Unknown Channel`, and which peer `send_via` picked depended on list order.
  - This adds an operator-chosen per-peer route, `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer ID>"]`, with `destination` (the channel or thread ID to post in) and an optional `mention`, following the decisions in #10926 (comment of 2026-11-06).
  - `external_peers` stays admission data: a route key must already be one of the group's `external_peers` (a Discord user ID), a wildcard cannot be routed, and a peer covered by an `ignore` list is not routable.
  - Routed messages always carry an explicit `allowed_mentions` policy on every chunk and attachment payload: nobody is pinged, or with `mention = true` the peer's mention is prefixed and only that user may be pinged.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Discord only. A route on any other channel type is a config error; Matrix and Signal behavior is unchanged and left to separate slices.
  - No peer selector and no group default for `send_via`: a group or channel target posts only when exactly one eligible routed peer exists. Explicit per-peer sends stay with `send_message_to_peer`.
  - The route is not checked against the Discord channel's `channel_ids`, which keeps its meaning as the listening filter. No `thread` field: `destination` is the ID the sender posts to.
  - Unrouted Discord sends and all non-Discord sends keep their payloads; `allowed_mentions` is omitted unless a policy is set.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `SendMessage` gains `allowed_mentions: Option<Vec<String>>` (default `None`, set by both constructors), so struct-literal sites get one more field. Open #11997 also edits `SendMessage`; whichever lands second adds the other's field at those sites.
  - The cron/announcement `DeliveryFn` gains a final `Option<Vec<String>>` mention-policy argument. `deliver_announcement` keeps its signature and passes `None`; the new `deliver_announcement_with_mentions` carries a policy.
  - The Discord sender builds every chunk through one helper, `chunk_payload`. For plain chunks it produces the same request body as the previous `DiscordOutgoing::text` path (tested).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926. Depends on #12116.

### What this does, simply

A peer group lists who an agent may talk to on a channel. On Discord, an outside participant (another bot or a person) is listed by user ID, but a bot can't post to a user ID: it posts into a channel or thread, and bots can't DM other bots. So asking an agent to message such a peer failed with a confusing "Unknown Channel" error.

With this change, the operator says where messages for that peer should go:

```toml
[peer_groups.discord_peers]
channel = "discord.main"
agents = ["assistant"]
external_peers = ["111111111111111111"]

[peer_groups.discord_peers.routes."111111111111111111"]
destination = "333333333333333333"   # channel or thread ID to post in
mention = true                       # optional: start with a ping of the peer
```

`send_message_to_peer` to that peer, or `send_via` to that group, then posts in the configured channel or thread. The result names the destination, so the agent knows it posted in a shared place rather than a private message. The route never lets anyone new in, can't be used for an ignored peer, and only applies through groups the sending agent is in. If two of the agent's groups route the same peer to different places, the send fails and names both groups. A routed message can only ping the routed peer, and only when `mention = true`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional; unit coverage is focused, and a live Discord check shows the end-to-end effect.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord` (agent tool calls `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Discord bot in a server with a test channel or thread. An agent on `discord.<alias>`, and a peer group containing that agent with another bot or user ID in `external_peers`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Without a route, ask the agent to `send_message_to_peer` the external peer on the Discord channel ref.
  2. Add the `routes."<peer ID>"` block above with your channel or thread ID, reload, and repeat.
  3. Optionally set `mention = true`, and include `@everyone` or another user's mention in the message text.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 1 fails with an error explaining how to add a route. Step 2 posts in the destination, and the tool result names it. In step 3 the message starts with the peer's mention, and only the peer is pinged.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 1 fails with Discord's `404 Unknown Channel`, because the user ID is used as a channel ID (#12116 replaces this with an actionable error). There is no way to route.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust lint and test jobs cover the config, tools, runtime, channels, API, and gateway changes; Docs Style and the links gate cover the two Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord API call in CI; the payload shape is covered by unit tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 Linux, on this head `8d3a951c2` before opening; the base was master `2341ab56c`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> clean
cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -> clean
  (run on the first revision; the review follow-ups touch only crates the clippy run below rechecked)
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings -> clean
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- route peer_group
  test result: ok. 63 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- send_via
  test result: ok. 30 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- send_message_to_peer cron::scheduler
  test result: ok. 108 passed; 0 failed   (plus the isolated child-process delivery test: ok)
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord:: announcement compiled_channel
  test result: ok. 327 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api --lib
  test result: ok. 321 passed; 0 failed
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh -> Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh   -> Checked 1 local docs link target(s)
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh -> passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - I ran a mutation check: each new guard was removed in turn, and a named test had to fail. All 15 were caught:
    - ignored-peer exclusion in route lookup, and in `send_via` across the agent's groups;
    - conflict detection across bare-type and dotted-alias groups;
    - sender-scoped lookup (a route in a group the sender is not in is not used);
    - route keys outside `external_peers`, and non-numeric keys, rejected by validation;
    - `send_via` refusing to fall back to the first peer on Discord;
    - the mention policy on later chunks, on routing instructions, on immediate sends, on announcement delivery, and on the routed `send_message_to_peer` call;
    - agent-only groups keeping their existing rejection.
  - Not verified: a live Discord post from this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (tool results and Discord message payloads only; no UI change).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `8d3a951c2`, unit tests listed above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded locally because its GTK system libraries are not on this host (CI excludes it too). The full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally; the focused suites above cover the changed modules.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** A configured route can post outside the Discord channel's `channel_ids` listening filter. It is operator-configured only. It applies only to a peer the sending agent's own groups already admit and do not ignore, and conflicting routes fail closed. The docs state that everyone with access to the destination can read routed messages.
- New external network calls? No. Same Discord message endpoint, to a different operator-chosen channel.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. IDs are synthetic, e.g. `111111111111111111`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new untrusted input. Routed message text comes from the agent as before, and the explicit `allowed_mentions` policy stops it from pinging anyone except the routed peer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, with one Discord behavior change.** `send_via` to a Discord peer group, or to a Discord channel one group covers, that has external peers but no single routed peer now fails with guidance instead of posting to the first external peer's user ID. That post already failed with `404 Unknown Channel`. Groups with no external peers keep their existing rejection, and non-Discord channels are unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer ID>"]` with `destination` and `mention`. Existing configs load unchanged; an invalid route is a load-time validation error.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: none needed. To deliver to a Discord external peer, add a route as shown above.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of this PR's commit. Routes are opt-in config; without them, the only change is the clearer `send_via` rejection described above.

prs.title: feat(gateway): scoped dashboard chat through the core, on a shared RPC client
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. It depends on #11964 (the daemon retires orphaned remote sessions) and #12232 (tools that can't act as the caller are withheld from non-administrators), and both merge first. Until #11964 does, this branch carries #11964's head as one merge commit (22504bcd73). That merge is replaced by a master merge once #11964 lands. After #12232 lands, the branch is refreshed onto master again, so the remaining review covers the combined behaviour.
- **One PR in place of three.** This replaces #11165 (the RPC wire contract), #11186 (the RPC client and the in-process transport) and #11986 (scoped dashboard chat). It is cut fresh from master, with every review point on the three answered (listed below). The RPC pieces exist for the chat and are only used by it, so they land together. A runtime placement row approved in #11963 asks for exactly that: the in-process adapter must not merge ahead of its use.
- **Commits:**
  - **The RPC foundation (11):**
    - f25e96ea39 refactor(rpc): extract the wire contract into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` with an OpenRPC drift check (from #11165);
    - 492ef50e4b feat(rpc): add `zeroclaw-rpc-client` and the in-process gateway transport (from #11186);
    - 44ac94d165 test(rpc): strengthen connector retirement regressions (by @Aarlington);
    - f67fa1c8fb fix(rpc): bound a request by its encoded frame before it is queued (by @IftekharUddin);
    - bc8818d167, f19359c8ed, 12966a5143, 0caf0cc94b, b3a4cf7a91, f284c7cc39 and 331d3abf0b: review follow-ups (a message, a doc, tests and their formatting).
  - **The chat (11):**
    - 28258e7010 feat(rpc): bind in-process connections to the provider their bearer came from;
    - 37ba342c46 feat(gateway): scoped dashboard chat through the core;
    - 195834a5ad feat(web): one conversation per chat socket for accounts chatting through the core;
    - a0e10317de docs(security): describe scoped dashboard chat and its limits;
    - then the review fixes: a2edf767bf, 654832760d, 1bb86b50a7, 32f33446df (by @IftekharUddin), 0bd93712ba, 63918008f7 and ed3d47bc79 (by @IftekharUddin).
  - **After opening (CI and review):**
    - cd0a6f1fa5 names the runtime's `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` edge in the composition consumer's retained-dependency policy;
    - 0919b0fe1a keeps a first message pending until it is sent (from the automated review);
    - da97348acd marks the generated OpenRPC document `linguist-generated`;
    - 6533ac3742 pins the stuck-write test's socket buffers to 64 KiB, because host TCP autotuning could hold the 7 MiB turn end.
  - **After #12232 landed:**
    - 762e37391a merges master, bringing in #12253 and #12232, with no conflicts;
    - 5c1753601a adds a gateway test: a member chat whose profile has `tools:execute` with wildcard tool and agent selectors is not offered `sessions_list`, `sessions_history` or `sessions_send`.
- **Limit to know first: a scoped account's conversation ends with its socket.** Reloading the page, leaving the chat or signing out ends it, and the dashboard can't reopen it. This is deliberate for this release (details under the scope boundary below).
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The RPC wire contract has one home.** Its method table, params and result types, notifications and frame limit move from the runtime into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, a crate with no async I/O. The runtime re-exports them, so the wire is unchanged.
    - `cargo generate openrpc` writes `docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json` from it.
    - The drift check fails when the document and the code disagree.
  - **A client for the daemon's RPC, and an in-process way to reach it.**
    - `zeroclaw-rpc-client` does the handshake, calls, notifications and reconnects, over the local socket or over a duplex inside the daemon.
    - The daemon's `InprocConnector` hands the supervised gateway such a duplex. Each connection authenticates as a socket client does, with no authority from being in-process, and is treated as remote for every local-only check.
    - A daemon reload seals the connector, drains its connections and releases the generation's context.
  - **Non-administrator accounts can now chat in the dashboard.** The daemon runs the chat as that account, under its grants, and keeps the conversation as that account's own. Administrators keep today's in-process chat and its history.
  - **Each chat socket is one conversation.**
    - The socket opens a daemon connection of its own through the in-process connector, presenting the token the account signed in with.
    - It creates one conversation there.
    - The conversation is closed (never deleted) when the socket closes, when the account signs out, shortly before its token expires, when it loses access, and at a daemon reload.
    - No other socket reopens it. So nothing about a conversation is shared between sockets: not its connection, not the identity the daemon holds it under, not its approvals.
  - **The daemon treats that connection as remote**, so it assigns the conversation's id, and only the connection that created a conversation can use it.
  - **At most four chats per sign-in, and 32 per account across its sign-ins.**
    - A conversation still being created, or not yet closed after its chat ended, counts. Signing out and in again therefore frees nothing until it is closed.
    - The chat holds its place from the start of its daemon handshake until it is done, including while the daemon is still verifying the token after the gateway stopped waiting.
    - A creation the chat stopped waiting for (after 10 minutes) stays counted until the daemon answers it. A conversation created after all is closed when the answer lands and then no longer counts.
    - A conversation whose close failed, or whose creation lost its connection before the answer, stays counted until the next reload, since its fate is unknown.
    - A chat past either limit is accepted, told `CONVERSATION_LIMIT` and closed with `4409`; no other tab's conversation is closed.
  - **The chat follows the account's current grants.** Every chat frame, and a periodic check while the socket is idle, requires the session grants a chat needs and its agent under the current policy. A policy that narrows either closes the socket with `4403` before anything else is acted on.
  - **A conversation the daemon finishes creating after its socket left is still closed.** The creation runs in a task of its own and waits as long as the daemon takes (MCP servers can make that longer than a request's usual deadline). Whatever it creates that nobody took, or creates after sign-out, is closed.
  - **The token goes only to the provider that issued it.**
    - Every connection a chat opens is bound to the sign-in's provider, as it was configured at sign-in: `InprocConnector::connect_bound`, verified with `authenticate_bound` in the daemon.
    - If the provider is repointed at another issuer or client, the chat is refused and the token is not sent there.
  - **Messages are bounded before they are read.** The chat socket refuses a frame, or a fragmented message as it is assembled, over the RPC frame limit (8 MiB). A prompt that fits the socket but not the encoded frame (escapes count) is refused by the client before it is queued, so the turn ends with `CORE_REFUSED` and the conversation carries on.
  - **A chat that ends stops its reply.** The browser leaving, sign-out or a reload closes the conversation at once, which cancels a turn under way. A turn end the socket can't deliver ends the chat the same way.
  - **The identity provider is asked once per chat.** Each chat's connection verifies the token once. The agent list is kept per sign-in for 30 s, under one policy generation only, and the account's current read grant decides on every request.
  - **Writes to the browser never hold up the end.** Every write gives up at sign-out or a reload, or after 10 s on a browser that stopped reading.
  - **A close survives a lost connection, a lapsed binding, or a send the client refused locally.** It is tried again on a new connection, with the chat's own identity and the token the chat kept.
  - **The chat is offered only to accounts that can use, read and close a conversation** (`sessions` create, read, execute and update). Its agent uses only the tools the account is granted.
  - **Dashboard chat for scoped accounts (web).** This applies to an account without the operator dashboard, or any session with `features.core_sessions`.
    - Opening the chat opens no socket. The first message does.
    - The composer stays disabled until the socket's `session_start` says the conversation exists, and only then does the first message go out. So nothing can be sent ahead of it, and a refusal at the conversation limit keeps the message for Retry.
    - If the socket closes before `session_start` for any other reason, the message goes back to the composer, ahead of anything typed since, and the send error is shown.
    - At the limit, the banner with its Retry is the only notice.
    - There is no history to load, no conversation list and no resume. The stop button aborts by the id from `session_start`.
    - Any close ends the conversation. The socket never reconnects, and the transcript stays on the page followed by a notice. The next message starts a new conversation on a new socket.
    - New conversation (`/new`, `/clear`) closes the current one and deletes nothing.
    - Administrators and paired browsers keep stored conversations as before.

### What this does, simply

**Someone who signs in to the dashboard without administrator rights can now chat** with the agents they're allowed to use. The agent runs as them: it uses their permissions, and nobody else's dashboard sees their conversations. If their permissions are narrowed while a chat is open, the chat closes.

**A conversation lasts as long as its chat.** Each chat window is one conversation. Closing or reloading the page, signing out, or a daemon restart ends it. The transcript is kept, but the dashboard can't reopen it.

**Each sign-in can have four chats open at once.** A fifth waits until one closes.

**Underneath, the dashboard now talks to the daemon the way other clients do,** through a shared RPC client, over a connection inside the process. The description of that protocol moves into its own small crate, from which a machine-readable document is generated and checked.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** Yes. Non-admin dashboard accounts can chat through the daemon, under their own grants.
- **New external network calls?** No.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** Yes. The session's access token is presented to the in-process daemon connection.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No. Test identities are synthetic.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** No.
- **Risk and mitigation:**
  - **The token** stays in memory only. Each chat keeps a copy until its conversation is closed, and the copies are wiped when dropped. No code in this PR logs or formats it, and `ConnectOptions` and `RpcClient` redact it in `Debug`. The handshake still copies it into `ConnectOptions` and the `initialize` frame as plain strings for the length of the handshake; wiping those is a follow-up (#12246).
  - **Bound to its provider.** The token is presented only on connections bound to the provider that issued it, checked by the daemon against the policy it would send the token under. A repointed provider never receives it.
  - **Remote, not local.** In-process connections get no authority from being in-process. They authenticate as socket clients do and are classed as remote for every local-only check: path attachments and chunked upload are refused.
  - **Grants at every step.** The gateway checks the chat's grants and agent before the socket opens and on every frame. The daemon re-checks grants at the current policy on every call.
  - **Size.** Chat input is bounded at the socket and again at the encoded frame, so a browser can't make the gateway buffer more than one frame or end the daemon connection with an oversized request.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** Yes. Dashboard sign-in is off by default, administrators and paired browsers are unchanged, and the RPC wire is unchanged.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No.
  - **HTTP:** `GET /api/agents/available` and `features.core_sessions` are new.
  - For a scoped dashboard session, `GET /api/sessions` answers with its open chats instead of `403`, `POST /api/sessions/{id}/abort` stops an open chat's turn, and messages, rename and delete answer `404`.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <landed-commit>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** without a revert, remove the providers from `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]`. Turning sign-in off ends every dashboard session and closes their conversations. The RPC client and the in-process transport are then idle; the wire is unchanged either way.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - the log line `dashboard chat opened through the core` without a reply;
  - `a dashboard conversation could not be closed; the core retires it once its client has stayed away`;
  - `a dashboard call to the core lost its connection`;
  - the daemon refusing new sessions with `Session limit reached`;
  - for the RPC crates: the OpenRPC drift check failing in CI.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- **Superseded PRs + authors:**
  - #11165 by @JordanTheJet
  - #11186 by @JordanTheJet
  - #11986 by @JordanTheJet
- **Scope materially carried forward:**
  - all of #11165, ported onto master;
  - #11186's client and in-process transport slice, unchanged apart from its context;
  - all of #11986 with its review fixes.
  - **Contributors whose work is incorporated:**
    - @IftekharUddin: the connector fix on #11186; the frame bound, the composer fix and the idle-socket test on #11986;
    - @Aarlington: the connector retirement regressions on #11186.
  - **Reviewers whose points are answered above:** @tidux and @Audacity88.
- **`Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors?** Yes.

  - @Aarlington is the author of 44ac94d165.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
