prs.title: feat(cli): zeroclaw user commands for roster password lifecycle
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11264 and #11313. This branch carries both until they merge: merge commit `5f679fe103` joins them, and `9707c30981` reconciles them (`is_auth_input_path` names `security.password_auth`, which #11264 made an authorization input, and the publication tests' roster literals spell out `password_hash`; whichever of the two lands second takes that commit). This PR's own change is the `zeroclaw user` commit as reviewed (`29fb0e0272`), the rework that addresses the review (`54cabe9ec8`), and `eede22bce7`, which checks the daemon's roster again just before a commit (from tidux's approval). The remaining commits merge #11264's updates and `master`; the latest, `ef5dcf3a61`, merges #11313's current head (`78ccdc1478`, its own merge of `master`) and leaves the tree unchanged.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #8076 requires a documented way to create the first admin and to rotate or disable a password (`zeroclaw user …`), and a way to repair a forgotten password on the daemon host. Hand-writing scrypt PHC strings is not that.
  - `zeroclaw user list | add | passwd | disable-password | remove | hash-password`. Every edit is checked as a complete authorization policy (`validate_accepted_auth_config`) before a password prompt and again before it is committed. A refused edit writes nothing.
  - **Edits go through the running daemon.** While a daemon serves the configuration, each edit is committed through #11313's verified daemon client, the same path `config set` uses for an authorization edit: `add` and `passwd` as `config/set-many`, `disable-password` as `config/delete` (the daemon's way to clear a secret, which `config/set` refuses to overwrite with an empty value), and `remove` as `config/map-key-delete`. The daemon validates, saves, and publishes the edit as one step, so `user remove` ends the entry's uid binding for established and new connections, and `user add --uid` grants it, with no restart.
  - With no daemon running, the command saves `config.toml` itself, as before. When the daemon refuses the caller at the handshake (a uid outside the roster, or the deny-all state), or cannot be asked (the reasons #11313 lists, such as a Windows named pipe), the command saves the file and reports the edit pending until the next reload or restart, which keeps it a lockout repair path. When the daemon identifies the caller and refuses the edit (`add` and `passwd` need `update` on config, `disable-password` and `remove` need `delete`), or rejects it, nothing is saved. The closing notice says which of these happened.
  - **The file and the daemon's roster can differ** while a hand edit or an edit reported pending waits for a reload, and the command decides from the file whether an entry exists. So before a password is typed, it reads the daemon's roster (`config/map-keys`, a config read) and refuses an `add` of a name the daemon still holds, which would merge into that entry and keep its other credentials live, and a `passwd` or `disable-password` of an entry the daemon has not loaded. It reads the roster again just before the commit and refuses, to be run again, an edit whose entry another writer added or removed through the daemon while the prompt was open. A `remove` of an entry the daemon never loaded gets `deleted: false` back (`Publication::DaemonUnchanged`), and the command removes it from the file itself, so a later reload cannot bring it back.
  - When the command saves the file itself, it refuses if `config.toml` changed since the edit began (a password prompt can take a while). That comparison and the write are separate steps, and the docs say so. It also refuses when the roster, profile, or OIDC section failed to load, or when an environment override sets a value the check reads but the file does not hold.
  - `passwd` checks the policy as it will be after the edit, so it also repairs an entry the policy refuses (no credential yet, or a hash outside the bounds).
  - Passwords come from a hidden prompt (typed twice) or one line of standard input (refused on a terminal), never from arguments, and are scrubbed from memory once hashed. A new password needs at least 15 characters (NIST SP 800-63B-4's minimum for a single-factor password) and at most 1024 bytes, with no composition rules.
  - **Hash policy decisions before the first stored hash** (from the #11264 review): passwords are hashed and checked as their NFKC normalization, as NIST SP 800-63B-4 recommends, so the same characters typed on another keyboard or input method still match. A new password needs 15 characters both as typed and once normalized (one typed ligature can normalize to 18), and may not contain a code point Unicode leaves unassigned, as UAX #15's process for stabilized strings requires, since a later Unicode version could change how it normalizes. scrypt work is capped at the top of OWASP's table, N times p at most 131072, which also bounds p (the separate `p <= 16` ceiling is gone).
  - Help text for `zeroclaw user` and its six subcommands is in all five CLI catalogs.
  - `hash-password` needs no config and prints only the hash, so it is dispatched before any config is loaded. The two dispatch arms that can never run now fail with an error, like the other pre-runtime commands.
- **Scope boundary:** No daemon, RPC, or gateway change: the commands use the daemon's existing config methods through #11313's client. Nothing presents a password to the provider yet (the session and gateway work that follows). Translating the shared validators' English refusals is #11570. The two-process lost-update window Audacity88 described stays a follow-up: an edit the daemon commits is validated and saved under its write lock, but two commands that both save the file themselves are only narrowed by the byte comparison.
- **Blast radius:** `src/main.rs` (the command, two early dispatch points), `src/config_publication.rs` (`commit_delete`, `commit_map_key_delete`, `live_map_keys`, and `Publication::DaemonUnchanged` for a delete that finds nothing; `config set` and `config patch` never produce it), `zeroclaw-config` (`check_new_password`, NFKC, the work cap, `Decoy::as_phc`; `unicode-normalization` and `zeroize` become direct dependencies, both already in the lockfile), five CLI catalogs, the authentication docs, and `zeroize` as a direct dependency of the root crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8076, Depends on #11264, Depends on #11313

### What this does, simply

The previous PR taught ZeroClaw to check a password against a stored hash. This one gives operators the tool that writes those hashes: `zeroclaw user add` creates a user, `passwd` changes a password, `disable-password` and `remove` take access away, and `list` shows who has what without printing a hash. When the daemon is running, each change takes effect immediately, so removing a user cuts off their access right away. When it is not running, or refuses the person running the command, the change is written to the config file and applies at the next restart, which is also how a lockout gets fixed. A user added this way cannot sign in with a password yet: the sign-in surfaces come in the next PRs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a scratch config dir: `mkdir /tmp/zc-user && printf 'schema_version = 4\n\n[permission_profiles.operator]\ngrants = { sessions = ["read"] }\n' > /tmp/zc-user/config.toml`
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user user add zeroclaw_user --profile operator --uid 4101 --password`, then `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user user list`; then start `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user daemon` and run `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user user remove zeroclaw_user`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the add succeeds after two masked prompts; `list` shows `password set`; with the daemon running, `remove` prints `Authorization change applied to the running daemon.`
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `zeroclaw user` does not exist.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the workspace test run executes `tests/component/user_cli.rs` and the new `zeroclaw user` cases in `tests/component/config_auth_publication_cli.rs` (a real `zeroclaw daemon` on a private config dir, the CLI in a separate process, and a raw JSON-RPC client), plus the unit tests in `src/main.rs`, `src/config_publication.rs` and `zeroclaw-config`; Rust lint; `Docs Style`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the live-daemon tests are Unix-only, like the rest of that suite; on Windows the CLI never sends an edit over the named pipe and reports it pending. The interactive prompt needs a terminal; see the evidence below.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0, head `4954238bbc`; head `ef5dcf3a61` has the identical tree, `git diff 4954238bbc ef5dcf3a61` is empty, so these results and the terminal evidence below hold for it unchanged):

```text
$ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                                                  # clean
$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings   # exit 0
$ RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo +1.98.0 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features   # exit 0
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --no-run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop          # exit 0
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw --test component -- config_auth_publication_cli user_cli
test result: ok. 42 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw -- user_add roster_edit only_overrides config_publication
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw --test architecture                          # ok. 55 passed
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo +1.98.0 nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-api
     Summary [  52.841s] 7918 tests run: 7918 passed (2 leaky), 8 skipped
$ cargo +1.98.0 deny check                                                             # advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh / docs_links_gate.sh / comment_hygiene_gate.sh        # clean
```

- **Re-run on `ef5dcf3a61`** (the restack onto #11313's `78ccdc1478`; its only conflict was the `config-lifecycle.md` CLI row, resolved to this branch's row naming `zeroclaw user`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo check -p zeroclaw --no-default-features` exit 0; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw` ok. 555 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component config_auth_publication -- --test-threads=1` ok. 30 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component user_cli -- --test-threads=1` ok. 12 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component config_patch_cli` ok. 25 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test architecture` ok. 55 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::auth:: daemon:: rpc::local::` ok. 183 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo doc` clean; docs, links and comment hygiene gates clean; `Cargo.lock` unchanged.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4954238bbc` (same tree as head `ef5dcf3a61`), `zeroclaw user passwd` at a pseudo-terminal (80x24, `LC_ALL=C`), driven by a script that types a freshly generated password and records every byte the terminal received; disposable config dirs under `/tmp`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**

```text
revision: 4954238bbc
binary: target/debug/zeroclaw, built at that revision
os: Darwin 25.5.0 arm64
--- case 1-no-daemon-match: exit=0 password_in_terminal_output=False
  screen, first entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | ••••••••••••••••••••••••

  config changed: True
--- case 2-no-daemon-mismatch: exit=1 password_in_terminal_output=False
  screen, first entry typed, before Enter:

    | New password

  config unchanged: True
--- case 3-daemon-running-match: exit=0 password_in_terminal_output=False
  screen, first entry typed, before Enter:

  saved hash line: password_hash = "enc2:44...
  daemon pid: 83528

```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The pseudo-terminal runs above: both entries stay masked (the transcript never contains the password), matching entries save the hash `enc2:`-encrypted, a mismatch writes nothing, and with a daemon running the edit is applied by the daemon. Not verified: Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact terminal output above (locale `C`, 80x24; the prompt draws a masked placeholder, no styling).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None. The tests nextest flags as leaky (`rpc::dispatch::tests::operator_lists_any_directory` and `uses_memory_true_cron_run_keeps_memory_tools`) are unrelated to this change; the flag marks a test that left a handle open, and which tests trip it varies between runs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (writes the same `config.toml` that `config set` writes, or asks the daemon to, through the existing config methods)
- New external network calls? No (the local daemon socket only, through #11313's verified client)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the CLI reads a password and writes its hash. The password is never an argument (no shell history or process-list exposure), is read masked or from a pipe, the buffers the command holds (including the normalized copy) are scrubbed once hashed, and the hash is stored as an encrypted secret, by the daemon or by the CLI. Only the hash crosses the local socket, to a daemon whose identity #11313's client verifies first. `list` never prints a hash.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: new `zeroclaw user` command. The hash policy narrows from N times p up to 16 times 2^17 to at most 131072; no shipped release wrote hashes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: none.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Hashes this command wrote remain valid config for #11264, but a revert also takes NFKC out of `verify_password`, so a password whose typed form is not already NFKC (an accent typed as a combining mark, a full-width letter) stops matching its stored hash until a new one is set.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `security.password_auth.enabled` governs whether stored hashes are used at all.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `zeroclaw user` exits non-zero with a reason, and nothing is saved; or it reports the edit pending, with the reason, when a running daemon did not take it.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

prs.title: fix(channels): honor Telegram 429 retry_after via shared per-token flood gate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram Bot API 429 responses were treated like formatting failures: `sendMessage` retried immediately as plain text (a markdown→plain double-hit), draft edits kept their cadence, and the typing loop never noticed — so a rate-limited token got hammered, its penalty escalated, and finalized replies were lost (issue #11615).
  - This adds a flood-control gate (`TelegramRateLimiter`) shared **by the clones of one channel instance** (channel fields, spawned typing loop, approval paths) — it is *not* a registry keyed by bot token: separately constructed channels on the same token, including repeated one-off announcement factories, keep independent windows. Gated surface: the channel's text traffic — `sendMessage` (final answers, draft creation, approval prompts), `editMessageText` (draft updates, finalize), and `sendChatAction` for the initial inbound hint and recurring typing loop. Model-picker sends and text/markup edits, approval-resolution text edits, acknowledgement reactions, media uploads, `deleteMessage`, and `answerCallbackQuery` still post directly and are not covered by this gate.
  - Droppable calls (typing, draft edits) skip silently while the window is open. Deliver calls wait the window out bounded by a caller-side budget (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs`), **re-check the shared gate after sleeping**, and stop with a distinguishable budget-exhausted outcome if the window is still active — the budget bounds how long the caller waits, never the server deadline, so nothing is sent into an active window. On a fresh 429 the generic Deliver helper retries once; final `sendMessage` retains the two-retry policy integrated from #11650. Every 429 contributes its own (possibly longer) `retry_after` to the shared window, and terminal flood-control outcomes stop the formatting/resume/resend fallbacks — a 429 is not a formatting failure.
  - The recorded deadline keeps the later of the active and new values, so out-of-order concurrent 429 responses cannot shorten the window; an unrepresentable delay is rejected rather than clamped into permission to send sooner.
  - Honors `retry_after` from the JSON envelope (`parameters.retry_after`), with a `retry after <N>` description fallback and a 5s fallback when nothing is parseable.
  - Partial deliveries still suppress the orchestrator's full-answer resend via `FinalizePartialDelivery`, and flood-control exhaustion now stops the chunk-resume path as well instead of burning the wait budget twice. The pending-narration loop in multi-message finalization also stops on the terminal gate outcome: instead of burning three narration retries plus a final-answer wait on fresh budgets, it propagates the gate error, so the outer resend is suppressed without reporting an undelivered final answer as delivered.
  - Two new optional telegram channel config keys: `rate_limit_max_wait_secs` (default 60; `0` restores the default — it is not a disable switch) and `typing_refresh_interval_secs` (default 4, previously hardcoded). Configured values are clamped to 300 seconds and 5 seconds respectively; zero restores the default for either setting. Both resolve from the live config authority at each use, including per-tick in the typing loop, so a published change applies to a running channel without a rebuild.
- **Scope boundary:** adaptive draft throttling and listener parsing/recovery changes are explicitly out of scope; the initial inbound typing hint is now gated without changing message delivery (per maintainer triage on #11615); no behavior change when no 429 occurs — the pre-send gate is a no-op on `Clear`.
- **Blast radius:** Outbound paths of the Telegram channel only (`send_text_chunks`, `send_draft`, `update_draft`, `finalize_draft`, `start_typing`, approval send) plus one guard in the orchestrator's finalize-fallback arm. Inbound parsing and delivery are unchanged; only their initial typing hint joins the gate. Other channels and the agent loop are unchanged. Defaults keep today's behavior for well-behaved tokens.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. Related #11608.

### What this does, simply

Telegram tells throttled bots exactly when to come back (`retry_after` in the 429 body), but the channel ignored that and fired again immediately — markdown attempt, then plain attempt, then more draft edits and typing ticks. Each ignored window made the next one longer, and when the final reply finally hit the limit it was dropped: users saw drafts vanish mid-sentence. Now the channel records "blocked until N seconds" per channel instance (shared by its clones) the moment a gated call sees a 429, keeping the longest active deadline. Gated cosmetic traffic (initial and recurring typing indicators, live draft edits) stays silent during the window; user-visible sends wait out the server-directed window up to one bounded caller budget. The generic helper retries once, while final `sendMessage` retains its integrated two retries. When the window clears within budget, the reply is late instead of dropped. When the window outlasts the budget, nothing is sent into it: the answer is held and an error is returned — this slice has no durable delivery queue or automatic later redelivery, so such a reply can go undelivered (WARN-logged) until the sender retries; the gated callers stop retrying inside the recorded window and suppress blind resends of accepted chunks. The direct-call exclusions listed above still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the rate-limit interaction is fully covered by mock-server tests (429-then-success, repeated limiting with escalating deadlines, blocked-window skipping, budget expiry without resend, mid-wait window extension, cancelled waiter, cross-chat window sharing, gated draft creation, live-config resolution, pending-narration finalize stop with zero and nonzero accepted prefixes); a live 429 cannot be induced reliably without flooding a real bot token.

### How I tested

Current-head hosted evidence at `d63d0026616490532636b3a255cd4b939b760ebc`: the [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41495762404/job/125450161211) passes the initial-typing dispatch, atomic deadline publication, shared wait allowance, exact-budget and orchestrator no-fallback regressions. Security currently fails on inherited `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.5 (`RUSTSEC-2026-0433`), which also fails CI Required Gate; this PR changes no dependency or lockfile. The local commands and live observation below remain historical evidence for their named revisions.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** channels/config unit and integration tests cover the changed surface (telegram channel + config schema).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` at workspace level shows pre-existing warnings in platform-conditional code outside this diff (unix-gated code on a Windows host, Windows-only service code); none originate from this change, and the channels crate itself is `-D warnings` clean. Two pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` test failures reproduce on unpatched master (`agent_bundle::…outside_shared_is_dropped_with_its_content`, `platform::native::…powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`).
- **Commands run and tail output (head `fe42c5d30`):** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram` → `test result: ok. 429 passed; 0 failed`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize` → `test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed` (including the two new `finalize_stops_on_flood_gate_with_{zero,nonzero}_accepted_narration_prefix` regressions and the retained transient-retry controls).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Author-reported live observation (distinct from CI signals): ran an earlier revision of this change as a production Windows service against live Telegram for 24h — 3 real 429s observed (previously 7+ per incident), zero `failed to reply` events, every post-429 turn delivered after the gate window. This predates the review-round semantics tightening; the current head's budget/no-resend and pending-narration-stop behavior is covered by the mock-server regressions above, not by live observation.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fe42c5d30` on branch `fix/telegram-429-retry-after`; terminal test output above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` run from the previous round was not repeated at this head; the changed surface (pending-narration finalization, flood gate) is covered by the `telegram` (429 tests) and `finalize` (23 tests) filters above. `cargo test --test integration telegram_` remains un-run locally (link step needs more free disk than this host currently has); the equivalent behavior is covered by the in-crate wiremock tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- Upgrade steps: none required. The two new telegram channel keys are optional with defaults matching prior behavior (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 60`, `typing_refresh_interval_secs = 4`). Existing configs load unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>` of this PR's merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none — `rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 0` restores the default 60s wait budget; it is not a disable/rollback switch. Rollback is reverting the PR.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep runtime trace for `failed to reply` or `Telegram sendMessage failed` reappearing, or users reporting vanished drafts/answers again.

prs.title: fix(rpc): guard SOP and session effects with current authority
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master. Depends on #11220 and #11234. Prerequisite contributor commits are retained. Review this PR's supplemental changes separately from its cumulative stack. Current head: c9a193ceba32224187e79fbfd8d3ffc16a19d848.
- **What changed and why:** Require administrator authority for SOP RPC start and decisions, including wildcard non-admins. Hold canonical current authority through synchronous effects and use a shared-data store view that immediately refuses connection or SQLite writer contention. Preserve configured operator execution and the existing SOP tool markers.
- **Additional boundary repairs:** Hold current authority before SOP decision lookup, broker outcomes, and final overlay disclosure. Capture the real selection with a recursive read so a queued config writer cannot deadlock an already-held SOP effect lease.
- **Session effect repairs:** Guard append and rename at the durable storage effect, retain live Agent/generation/TUI ownership through publication, and authorize `session/abort` after the real cancellation lock. Revoke queued remote steering when its TUI binding changes, including an A-to-B-to-A transfer. Keep create-only run-once admission distinct from resume and preserve its published generation; preflight the existing close permission and report a late cleanup failure after a completed turn.
- **Scope boundary:** OIDC security hardening and regression coverage. Two-provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, and milestone closure remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** SOP RPC dispatch, run-store contention, session storage and live publication, `session/abort`, remote steering, and transient run-once lifecycle.
- **Linked issues:** Related #11127, #11239, and #8289. No milestone closure is claimed.

### What this does, simply

Non-admin SOP RPC execution is now refused. Retry an administrator request when the SOP store is busy; ordinary background store timeouts are unchanged. Model-visible wildcard containment also depends on #11410. Session writes, `session/abort` and queued steering now refuse stale authority or transport ownership at their final effects. Run-once reports a late close failure instead of silently returning success.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, review this exact head and the combined #11423 integration; rerun validation after any subsequent dependency or conflict-resolution change.
- **Interface exercised:** Real RPC handlers and factory-built tool registries with synthetic principals, temporary databases, refusal assertions, and successful owner/operator controls. Storage tests use actual SQLite contention.
- **Setup:** A permitted Rust build environment with the repository's pinned toolchain and locked dependencies.
- **Expected:** Unauthorized requests have no new run, provider, mutation, transcript, or cross-owner audit effect; unchanged authorized controls succeed.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib session_
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
```

### How I tested

- **Current integration:** Head `c9a193ceba32224187e79fbfd8d3ffc16a19d848` retains its previous published head `2e6c2b7835abe169fb0cbaf6ecceafb0e21faefc`, pinned master `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293`, and refreshed adjacent prerequisite `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293` as ancestors. The six draft refreshes were pushed atomically by ordinary fast-forward; contributor histories are retained. The old-to-new changes are six upstream files, with only independent Fluent additions requiring resolution. The separate #11234 author-adoption candidate is not imported into these drafts.
- **Current focused validation:** The [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on exact source `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`: formatting; `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests`; config 7, storage 209, RPC 878, authority 26, principal 92, and steering 15 tests, all with zero failures/ignored; and Clippy for runtime/infra/config with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`. Fourteen selected RPC regressions each have exactly one passing record. Filters overlap; these are per-command results, not a unique-test total or full-workspace run. The separate superseded canonical-admission job in that workflow failed compilation; its failure is not hidden by this successful combined-stack job.
- **Current upstream CI:** Fresh required checks run on the published head above. Their exact status and the landing decision are recorded in the [coordination handoff](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408#issuecomment-6023921255). A passed fork job is not a substitute for those checks or independent Core review.
- **Adversarial review:** The independent refresh review verified all six old heads and canonical `d5df4214` ancestry, every refreshed stack link, byte identity with master for the five non-Fluent upstream files, and exactly one occurrence of each retained SOP/timeout Fluent key. No actionable finding remained in this bounded refresh review. The broader prior security review remains recorded on its earlier source, not represented as a new full sweep.
- **Historical sensitivity evidence:** [Earlier validation](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) on `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231` passed enrollment 46/46 and demonstrated intended failures when append guarding or steering revocation was removed. These tests were not rerun as mutation tests in the current six-draft refresh; the relevant OIDC implementation is unchanged by this upstream-only refresh.
- **Limits:** Local Rust execution remains blocked by Windows Application Control (OS 4551), without a bypass. No production deployment, provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, or milestone closure occurred. The earlier Keycloak 20/20 and Authentik 10/18 result does not certify this integration. Required CI, Core review, and a safe prerequisite landing decision remain distinct gates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem scope? No. The changed boundaries reduce access and retain existing operator controls.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets or credential formats changed? No. Authority is resolved from the existing canonical accepted policy.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No; principals, payloads, and workspaces are synthetic.
- New prompt-injection source? No. Private run output and captured tools are treated as protected data/effects.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Session compatibility:** This PR requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.
- **Backward compatible?** No for callers relying on the previously unsafe access described above. Non-admin SOP RPC execution is now refused. Retry an administrator request when the SOP store is busy; ordinary background store timeouts are unchanged. Model-visible wildcard containment also depends on #11410.
- **Config/env/CLI surface changed?** No new settings, flags, or schema migration.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade:** Review the restrictions before rollout; keep this stack together and use existing operator workflows for refused administrative operations.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback path:** Revert the supplemental session/SOP repair commits on an integration branch in reverse dependency order, preserving contributor prerequisites and upstream #11576. Re-run the denied/permitted authority tests before any rollback deployment; reverting these repairs reopens the corresponding boundaries. This refresh does not claim a completed rollback rehearsal.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable symptoms:** Unexpected permission refusals, SOP store-busy errors, missing owner audit records, or failed targeted/parallel runtime tests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not a replacement. Depends on the PRs above; original contributor commits are retained. Overlapping session authorization resolves to #11234's implementation.

prs.title: feat(rpc): stable denial reason identifiers and localized selector denials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every RPC authorization denial now carries an `RpcDenialReason`, a stable identifier set by the typed constructor that builds it. The constructor also derives the JSON-RPC code from the reason and renders the message from the reason's Fluent key. `AuthDenied`'s `reason` field is private, so a denial cannot be built without one; the free-text `auth_required(message)` and `forbidden(message)` constructors are gone.
  - The denial audit record (`RPC authorization denied`) emits the identifier as `reason` and the localized text as a separate `denial_message` attribute, so operators can group and alert on refusals without depending on wording or the daemon's locale. The attribute is not named `message` because log exporters copy attributes out flat and log backends reserve that name.
  - The coarse grant denial and every selector refusal (config path, agent, cron, session workspace, `fs/list_dir`, attachment source, session environment, global streams, SOP) resolve through 12 new `rpc-auth-*` Fluent keys with arguments instead of inline English literals. Request values are quoted and escaped exactly as the old `{:?}` literals quoted them, so the English text is byte-identical. The one exception is the global-stream refusal, whose key carries the wording #11326 gives it, naming the persisted log.
  - A denial after failed revalidation now records the principal id and auth provider of the binding it drops. Before, the dispatcher cleared the binding first and the record carried nulls. The same change removes a production `expect()`.
  - The branch merges current master, so the denial sites #11171 added (the authority lease, the expiry helper, and the chunked-upload recheck) use the typed constructors too. The upload recheck's session-ownership refusal gets its own `session_not_owned` reason. The later merge converts #11132's sites the same way: `require_additional_grant` refuses with `grant_missing`, and steering admission records its ownership refusal as `session_not_owned` and its remote local-capability refusal as a new `session_local_capabilities` reason instead of rebuilding denials from message text, while the binding checks it calls record their own refusals once rather than twice. The latest merge converts #12232's two sites the same way: the admin-only procedure execution refusal becomes `sop_principal_ceiling_required` and the agent cron-job trigger refusal becomes `cron_agent_principal_required`, each rendering the Fluent key #12232 introduced; the `sop_tool_selector_constrained` reason, which #12232's rework left without a site, is removed before it ships. The merge after that keeps #12239's steering admission, which decides under one authority lease and from one config view, and gives its new refusal for a remote session owner whose transport ownership moved a `session_transport_ownership_changed` reason with the same English text; #11149's cron write recheck uses the shared first-call key for an unbound dispatcher.
- **Scope boundary:** The JSON-RPC wire shape is unchanged: codes and English message bytes are identical (apart from the global-stream refusal's #11326 wording), and the identifier is not sent to clients. Gateway HTTP denial bodies, handshake (`initialize`) auditing, the refusals that bypass `AuthDenied` (session ownership outside chunked uploads, shared memory plane, SOP decision authorization, TUI signature, remote-WSS SOP methods), and translated catalogues are unchanged. The cron refusal's client text ("Cron job not found: ...") stays an inline English literal on purpose: it must match the genuinely-missing-job answer, which comes from the cron store, so the refusal does not confirm that a job exists. The `cron/patch` writer-transaction rechecks that #12232 added keep their plain `rpc_err` refusals, which master does not audit; only their unbound-dispatcher literal moves to the shared first-call key. Likewise, the post-admission lease rechecks that #12239 added for session effects return errors without audit records, as the docs section now states.
- **Blast radius:** The audit record's `reason` attribute changes from prose to an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`. The record merged in #10259 on 2026-09-24 and shipped in v0.8.6 and v0.8.7 with the prose in `reason`, so a consumer written against those releases must display `denial_message` and group or alert on the identifier, as the docs section says. Open PRs that build denials with `AuthDenied::auth_required`/`forbidden` or struct literals will stop compiling at rebase; the fix is a variant, a key, and a typed constructor per new site.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11005. Depends on #12062, the holding-crate exception row for this change, which must be recorded before this merges. Related #11326 (merged; this PR's denial-records docs and the global-stream refusal describe the `logs/query` and `logs/get` scoping it implements), #8289, #10259.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

When the daemon refuses an RPC request because the caller lacks permission, it writes a warning to its log. Until now the "reason" in that warning was the English sentence the client saw, so it changed whenever the wording changed and would change with the daemon's language, which makes it a poor thing to alert on. It is now a short fixed code such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, and the sentence moves to its own field. Several refusal sentences were written directly in the code instead of in the translation catalogue; they now live in the catalogue like the rest. Finally, one kind of refusal, when a policy change invalidates an existing connection, forgot who the connection belonged to before logging; it now records that. Clients see the same error codes and English messages as before, apart from the refusal for daemon-wide logs, which now also names the persisted log.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the changed output is a structured log record, and the new tests drive real refused requests through the dispatcher and assert the record each one writes.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Parallel Runtime Test` run the new unit and dispatcher tests; `Lint` covers the Rust changes; `Docs Style` and the links gate cover the documentation section.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Head 8b3ee1e18d** (merges master 641b766030, which includes #12239 and #11149): the merge's conflicts were in steering admission, which #12239 restructured around one authority lease; the lease structure is kept and each refusal is recorded once with its typed reason, with #12239's new transport-ownership refusal recorded as `session_transport_ownership_changed`. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `6177 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`; `-- rpc::`: `957 passed; 0 failed`; `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: `801 passed; 0 failed`. `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, clippy (no findings), the comment hygiene scanner on the touched files and the docs quality gate on `authentication.md` pass. Earlier heads: 23703b20b0 merged #12232 (`sop_principal_ceiling_required`, `cron_agent_principal_required`), 3ab104bdac merged #11326, 0a386d6cce converted #11132's two denial sites, da62caf7e1 dropped c94abbf93e's configure-race synchronization in favor of #11330's fence.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1, head 2e3f2e5101, which merges master a0f70b7925, unless noted):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `5455 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored`. The two failures are `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` and `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`. Master a0f70b7925 itself fails the same way under the same command (the configure test in 2 of 2 runs, the cost test in 1 of 2), each passes alone 3 of 3 times on this branch, and neither touches code this PR changes. Before merging master (2d96dfa52d, on 2443af29ea) the same command passed clean: `5313 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: `637 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `ws::tests::websocket_handler_projects_anthropic_empty_terminal_stream_as_user_error` hitting its response deadline under load; it passes alone 3 of 3 times, and `ws.rs` changes only in master's commits.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`: no findings in changed files. Under `-D warnings` it stops on four findings in files this PR does not touch, byte-identical to master: `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, macOS test builds) and three `clippy::drop_non_drop` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, which appear only when `-p zeroclaw-gateway` builds channels without `channel-telegram`.
  - `cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps`: 0 warnings.
  - `cargo fluent check`: all FTL files ok. `cargo fluent scan`: no `rpc-auth-*` key reported stale.
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (markdownlint 0 errors), `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each restored afterwards:
  - Emitting the message text as `reason` again fails all six dispatcher capture tests.
  - Auditing after the binding is cleared (the old order) fails `denial_after_failed_revalidation_keeps_the_principal_it_dropped` with a null principal.
  - Renaming one identifier fails the identifier-pinning test and the matching dispatcher test.
  - Deleting one new key from `cli.ftl` fails three tests that render the `{rpc-auth-agent-not-entitled}` missing-key marker.
  - Not verified: a live daemon under a translated locale; Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface changes; the changed output is a log record whose attributes the tests assert.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No `--no-default-features` check: nothing in `rpc/` is feature-gated, so no constructor can lose its only caller in that build.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The record carries the principal id and provider label it already carried, never bearer material; the attribution fix stops dropping data the dispatcher already held.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test principals are synthetic roster names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Request values that appear in denial messages (agent aliases, paths, job ids, procedure names) are quoted and escaped, so control characters cannot break a message or its log line.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for clients: codes and English messages are unchanged, apart from the global-stream refusal's wording. The audit record's `reason` attribute now holds an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`; the prose form shipped in v0.8.6 and v0.8.7, so log consumers written against those releases need that one-field change.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records whose `reason` is not one of the identifiers documented in `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md`, or a `denial_message` or client error message that is a `{rpc-auth-...}` missing-key marker.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Refusal cost:** argumented Fluent lookups parse the catalogue on each call. On an Apple Silicon Mac that measured about 180 µs per refusal for an English daemon and about 530 µs for a translated locale that lacks the new keys (every translated locale until a translation pass). This affects only refused requests. Caching parsed bundles would remove it, but it changes every argumented call site, so it is left for a separate PR. The same cost makes a cron refusal for another agent's job slightly slower than one for a missing job; the answers themselves are identical.
- **Unbound selectors:** the five selector helpers that refused an unbound dispatcher with a bare literal now use the existing first-call key and write a record. They are unreachable once the gate has run.
- **`code` stays a public field** derived once from the reason at construction, so the gateway's readers are untouched.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Expose `reason` on the wire and in gateway HTTP denial bodies.
- Audit handshake denials and the refusals listed as unrecorded in the new docs section.
- Translation fill for the `rpc-auth-*` keys, and parse each Fluent catalogue once.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(oidc): bind enrollment callbacks to the initiating browser
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. The branch carries @IftekharUddin's integration merge 5dbef39172 (onto master with merged #11965) and @JordanTheJet's master merge 703bbbe6c4 (empty remerge diff).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bind gateway OIDC enrollment to the browser that started it. A copied callback URL can no longer reveal a token in a different browser.
  - Generate a separate 32-byte random secret for each flow. Keep only its hash in the existing `PendingPkce` record. Check the cookie before code exchange; refuse and consume mismatched flows.
  - Preserve concurrent tabs, one-time consumption, issuer/provider checks, and the original deadline for a valid capacity retry. The cookie grants no session or API access.
  - Add four endpoint regressions, update existing callback tests to carry their actual issued cookie, and document cookie scope and recovery.
- **Scope boundary:** Enrollment start/callback, their documentation, and the integration (5dbef39172) that keeps the enrollment and dashboard sign-in bindings separate on the shared callback. Configured origin (#12048), same-host HTTP ports (#12088), broader availability (#12049), and response zeroization (#12090) remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Clients that complete `/oidc/login/<alias>` through `/oidc/callback` must keep the issued browser cookie. Device flow and bearer-authenticated API routes retain their current behavior. No manifest or lockfile change (master already carries `rand` as a normal dependency since #11965).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12050. Related #11965 and #8289.

### What this does, simply

The browser login page returns a token that a user can copy into a client. Before this change, someone could start a login under their own account, then send its final URL to another person. That person could receive and use the wrong account's token.

The gateway now gives the starting browser a short-lived cookie. The final page requires that cookie. A different browser gets the existing refusal page, and no code is exchanged. Start a new login in the intended browser after a refusal; do not forward callback URLs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: independent review of the callback boundary and an A/B browser check are useful for this security change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, gateway enrollment HTTP routes and the callback page. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a test OIDC alias and two isolated browser profiles. Use dedicated test accounts. Keep the gateway scheme/host consistent. The captured mock-provider recipe and source hashes are in [the evidence bundle](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/README.md).
- **Steps to run:** Start a login in browser A. Capture the final callback URL before following it. Open that URL in browser B. Then retry it in A. Start two fresh flows in separate tabs of A and finish both normally.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** B receives `Sign-in not completed`, with no token exchange. A cannot replay that consumed flow. Both fresh tab flows succeed, each once. A normal same-browser return succeeds and clears only its flow cookie.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The callback lacks this browser check. The guard-removal negative control reproduces acceptance of a missing-cookie callback (200 instead of 400). A live provider or a full unpatched-daemon A/B run was not performed.

### How I tested

### Current head 703bbbe6c4 — 2026-11-07 (maintainer update)

`CI Required Gate` passes on 703bbbe6c4. [Test job 127741357073](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42171878997/job/127741357073) passes all four `enrollment_binding_*` tests and `enrollment_and_dashboard_callbacks_preserve_each_others_cookies`. The combined Keycloak/Chromium HTTP and HTTPS exercise of enrollment plus dashboard sign-in is in [@JordanTheJet's comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6678201268). The sections below are historical and describe earlier heads.

### Earlier integration after #12200 - 2026-11-02 (historical)

Then-current head: a0b660c198c9a8aef8f00b3a2c2096af671ce127. Both original commits were true-rebased onto master 6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e, which includes merged #12200 and #11174. Both range-diff entries are unchanged; no manual conflict resolution or extra feature work was added. Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml and deny.toml match this master, including pulldown-cmark 0.13.6. The own scope remains 5 files.

The enrollment source, gateway manifest, locale loader and enrollment client are byte-identical to the previous head. The new master catalog keys are retained alongside the single enrollment error key, with no duplicate message keys. Focused rustfmt and whitespace checks pass. The callbacks, cookie parsing, consume-before-refusal and original-TTL capacity retry were traced again. Local Rust execution remains unavailable under Windows Application Control; the current-head upstream compilation and test results are recorded below. Earlier mock-provider/browser evidence remains historical and is not live-provider or combined dashboard evidence.

Two adversarial self-review passes and a final source review found no new supported defect. These are not independent Core approvals. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125581473661) passes on this exact head, including Security, Lint and Test. The [Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125571496498) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four browser-binding regressions. Parallel Runtime Test also passes. No new private workflow or live-provider run was used.

### Earlier Fluent follow-up — 2026-11-02

Earlier head: `1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a`. Both new enrollment-start errors now use `get_required_cli_string("cli-oidc-browser-start-failed")`. The canonical English catalog keeps the exact existing text, `could not start sign-in`. Other locales inherit that English fallback until translated. This uses the existing runtime locale; it does not add per-request language negotiation.

Local `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` and `git diff --check` pass. An exact inverse source comparison confirms that only the import, these two lookups and one English catalog entry changed. Status 500, the generic JSON error shape and early-return behavior remain. I traced the existing helper, catalog fallback and immediate JSON serialization; this was source validation, not a fresh gateway execution.

Historical CI on 1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a failed Security on inherited pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0433), with the aggregate gate also red. The merged #12200 repair is now inherited by the current head above. Historical results do not replace new-head checks.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical evidence: a bounded Ubuntu 24.04 job applied the exact patch to base `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`, checked all four source hashes, and ran Rust 1.98.0 tests, strict Clippy and the native browser fixture. Fresh upstream CI on the rebased head is recorded below. Independent Core/CODEOWNER security approvals remain required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The native browser check uses production enrollment routes, prefix and security headers over loopback HTTP, with a mock IdP. It is not the complete daemon, native TLS, dashboard popup integration, or real-provider acceptance. HTTPS cookie attributes and rejection of an unprefixed cookie have router assertions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
git diff --check
exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_oidc::tests:: -- --nocapture
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.95s
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0

# Temporary guard removal; require the selected regression to fail:
enrollment_binding_refuses_other_browsers_before_exchange_and_consumes_the_flow ... FAILED
left: 200
right: 400
# Exact bytes restored; repeat the OIDC suite:
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.89s

# Native browser fixture, then exact restoration and final suite:
5 browser assertions passed; same browser, isolated context, consumed replay and concurrent tabs
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 6.96s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes checked missing/wrong/duplicate cookies, consume-before-refusal, cookie-only API denial, concurrent flows, provider changes, issuer checks, original TTL and capacity retry. Source and dependency hashes were checked again. Both changed Markdown files passed pinned lint. No added documentation links need a new link target check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the existing success and refusal pages after the changed browser interaction; no layout redesign.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical source head `759ae4a5f1e4dffaa5d995503b222fc863e863d8`, exact four-file patch hash `945c228cff4dd8bf0a046630f7df1a22d3a14b34e6981eb64290d1e3fc9d55a9`; native Chrome `Chrome/156.0.8078.47`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway `localhost`, mock IdP `127.0.0.1`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Same-browser success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-same-context.png), [other-browser refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-other-context.png), and [machine receipt](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/receipt.json). All data is synthetic.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Follow the mock IdP page's link back to the prefixed callback: success with one exchange. Open a copied callback in another browser context: refusal with zero extra exchanges. Replay in the original context: refusal. Complete two fresh tab flows: both succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust execution was blocked by Application Control, so this source was validated on Linux. No full workspace suite or live IdP run is claimed. The first Linux attempt passed the Rust checks but failed because the mock page had a plain-text MIME type. That fixture was corrected; the complete successful run above uses the corrected harness. No browser assertion was relaxed.

### Earlier rebase and dashboard integration — 2026-11-02

Earlier rebased head: `4ef9abef542eb90153587669f2650cefc1abcb1d`. This is a true rebase onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. All four enrollment files and the exact patch are byte-for-byte unchanged from the historical tested revision above; range-diff reports the same single commit. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125043937233) passes, including Security, Lint and Test. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125040616464) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four new browser-binding regressions. Its checkout `0b80216b67e102089eebff5e2f6b7ff598a1e2bb` was verified to include this exact head. The earlier browser captures retain their named revision; no new native-TLS or real-provider acceptance run is claimed.

I also compared #11965 at `13486a064d2be1c05086e4ceaf6b08e94f2bc8b5`. At that historical snapshot, its delayed-start browser-family finding was open. It is now repaired at 02314854b32eb45a55d9d9c004f0bd73bb7b51e8, as recorded in [the repair review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11965#pullrequestreview-5731811340). That dashboard repair is separate from this per-flow enrollment binding. The branches overlap in `api_oidc.rs`; integration must keep one canonical binding in `PendingPkce`, checked before either exchange mode, with shared cookie parsing/cleanup and the original retry deadline. Preserve the dashboard's required ID token, provider pin, return/popup behavior and separate session-family/sign-out repair. Binding cleanup must coexist with the dashboard session cookie. (Historical: that combined integration has since been added in 5dbef39172; see the current-head section above.)

@IftekharUddin's [dependency and native-TLS proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6553383007) remains useful, separately attributed candidate evidence. The dependency repair is now inherited from master; no proposal commit was cherry-picked and no contributor source was replaced.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the existing discovery and token endpoints remain the only provider calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A new per-flow secret is sent only in an HttpOnly binding cookie; its hash is stored with the pending flow and compared in constant time. Cookies use SameSite=Lax and root Path with no Domain; HTTPS adds Secure and the __Host- prefix. A terminal consumed-flow response clears its cookie. The recorded transport scope preserves the cookie attributes chosen at issuance. A valid 503 retry keeps its original expiry. Remote deployments should use HTTPS; plain HTTP does not isolate applications on different ports of the same host.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for callers that complete an enrollment callback without the starting browser's cookie; this is the intentional security correction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Finish enrollment in the same browser that starts it and permit its cookie. If a callback was copied, the gateway restarted, or the cookie expired/was blocked, start a new login. Existing bearer clients and the device flow require no migration. The new field creates the browser-binding fact in the existing pending-flow store; it does not copy live policy.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the resulting squash commit through a reviewed PR, then restart the gateway. This restores the login-CSRF exposure, so use only as an incident response with an explicit exposure decision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Device flow is the alternative if browser cookies cannot be used.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A fresh same-browser login reaches `Sign-in not completed`; investigate cookie blocking, scheme/host changes and callback provenance. Do not log cookie secrets or token-bearing callback URLs.

The refreshed head now passes its required upstream CI; earlier results remain attached to their named revisions. This remains open for independent Core/CODEOWNER security review, with Jordan for the manifest and Audacity for the gateway and documentation. I have not approved my own change. After adoption, #11965 should use one binding fact in `PendingPkce` for both modes while preserving its dashboard-specific return, popup and ID-token behavior.

prs.title: fix(rpc): hold current authority through session effects
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** #11234 made queued session operations recheck the caller's authority after they wait. Several session effects still committed after another await, or never rechecked at all, so a revocation, demotion or ownership change that landed in between still let them through. This finishes those effects:
  - `session/configure` commits its overrides and provider in one step, under the caller's authority lease, rather than in two awaited writes after the recheck.
  - `session/append` and `session/rename` decide under the store's write lock, by the row's current owner and the caller's current authority. Append seeds the live Agent and sends its event inside the same commit.
  - For a remote client, configure, append, rename, abort and steering also check that the caller's TUI still owns the session when they commit. A same-generation resume by another TUI used to leave the old TUI able to reconfigure, write, cancel and steer. Steering it had already queued is now revoked when the session changes hands.
  - `session/abort` decides under the incarnation and cancellation locks with the caller's authority lease.
  - `session/run-once` looks up its id under current authority and requires `sessions:update`, since it closes the session it creates. If the close is refused after the turn, the call returns that error instead of reporting success. A remote caller can now name its own id, and the call keeps the generation it published even if that session is removed before it returns.
- **Scope boundary:** No new RPC method, config key or persisted schema. The SOP read repairs from #11411 are a separate follow-up after #12232 (which replaced #11220). Principal-owned Chat restore after a restart is #11737. Prompt admission, `session/new` resume and the destructive operations #11234 already covers are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** RPC session handlers in `zeroclaw-runtime` (`rpc/dispatch.rs`, `rpc/session.rs`, the run-once doc in `rpc/types.rs`) and two new default methods on `SessionBackend` in `zeroclaw-infra`, implemented for SQLite and for JSONL append. Gateway and channel sessions are not touched, since append still refuses any session that RPC does not write.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11126. Related #11234, #11408, #11411.

### What this does, simply

When an RPC client asks to change a session, the daemon checks the caller is allowed and then makes the change. Between those two steps it often has to wait: for the session's queue, a lock or the database. #11234 added a second check after those waits. A few changes still did more waiting after that second check, or skipped it. So a caller whose access was taken away at the wrong moment could still add a message, rename a session, change its model, cancel its turn or steer it.

This PR moves the final check to the moment the change is written, and holds it there until the write is done. It also covers a remote case: the TUI that loses a session to another TUI can no longer act on it, and any steering it had already queued is dropped.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: each case is a timing window that the focused tests open with test pauses. A manual run cannot hit them reliably.

### How I tested

**Current head f855688236 (maintainer update, 2026-11-07):** ffcfe904b3 + master merge 3d548e5cad + the two-line `SessionStore::owned` accessor fix. [Quality Gate run 42411111769](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42411111769) on the merge with master a0c90482ee passed every required job, including Check and Test (20,180 tests). The focused runs below were at ffcfe904b3; the code they cover is unchanged since.

On Linux x86_64 (Rust 1.98.0), at ffcfe904b3 (tree 3650786e3e), on master 72167d12e2:

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust lint and test jobs build and run `zeroclaw-infra` and `zeroclaw-runtime`, where all the changes are.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for this change; the windows are covered by the focused tests below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fetch --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, the comment-hygiene gate and `git diff --check` against master: clean.
  - `cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib`: `test result: ok. 329 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `test result: ok. 6084 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`.
  - The ported tests three runs in a row at 4ad6aebb42: runtime `12 passed; 0 failed` and infra `2 passed; 0 failed`, each time. At ffcfe904b3, the configure and remote session tests three runs in a row: `165 passed; 0 failed` each time.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I undid one functional line at a time (19 changes) and ran the session tests for each. Fifteen failed the tests written for them:
  - the configure commit without its authority check;
  - the SQLite append, SQLite rename or JSONL append without theirs;
  - configure, append, rename or abort without the TUI fence;
  - abort without its authority lease;
  - a create-only `session/new` capturing access, or re-reading its generation;
  - steering ignoring a revoked TUI binding, or a rebind that keeps the old binding;
  - run-once without the `sessions:update` check, or hiding a refused close.

  Four fail nothing, and I couldn't make them observable:
  - **Configure leaving automatic routing on after an explicit model choice:** the flag has no accessor outside the agent, the same gap master has.
  - **Run-once looking up its id by the connection's stamped scope:** the ownership check and the create-only `session/new` that follow refuse the same cases.
  - **Steering's TUI fence at enqueue:** steering admission fences the same TUI just before, and the revoked binding drops the steer when the turn consumes it.
  - **Steering resolving its grants without holding the lease:** only a publication racing that one read would show it.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** ffcfe904b3, RPC handlers through their unit-test dispatchers.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live daemon, macOS or Windows run, and no full workspace test suite. The infra and runtime libraries cover the changed code.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. `session/run-once` now requires `sessions:update` as well, which only narrows who can call it.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Steering that a TUI queued before it lost the session is now dropped before the model sees it.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No, in three narrow cases:
  - A principal granted `sessions:create` and `sessions:execute` but not `sessions:update` can no longer use `session/run-once`.
  - On a JSONL session backend, `session/rename` now returns an error instead of succeeding without storing the name. Guarded appends work on both backends.
  - A remote TUI that lost a session to another TUI now gets `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` for append, rename, abort and steer on that session.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: grant `sessions:update` to any permission profile that uses `session/run-once`. Nothing else needs to change.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the merge commit. The guarded writes add no state, so nothing needs migrating back.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** RPC clients getting `FORBIDDEN`, `AUTH_REQUIRED` or `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` on append, rename, abort, steer or configure without any policy or ownership change; run-once returning "Turn completed, but could not close transient session".

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

Not used. #11408 and #11411 stay open for their SOP parts. The session-effect commits here are Aarlington's work, kept as cherry-picks where they applied and otherwise ported with a `Co-authored-by` trailer:

- **Configure:**
  - f455ba115b and aaa681d085 (#11411), cherry-picked.
  - A follow-up keeps master's explicit-model routing step from #11516 in the atomic commit and removes the setter it replaced.
  - 3a833e4cdd and 561ece3f0e, ported onto master's version of their test.
- **Run-once lookup:** 85567e108c, cherry-picked.
- **Operator abort test:** 75a72e84a4, cherry-picked.
- **Append and rename:** the guarded writes from #11408's master merge 90a5978dbb, with the tests from 874b4e43bc and f00fe86148.
- **Remote ownership:** b86d4536bb, ported. Abort now uses `signal_cancellation_authorized`, and `abort_session_for_generation` is removed because nothing calls it anymore.
- **Steering:** 9c7cfd9823, and the steering part of 874b4e43bc.
- **Create-only generation:** the rest of 874b4e43bc.
- **Run-once cleanup:** 569e6fc11d, with the test changes from 08033c25a4 and 2e6c2b7835.
- **Abort test:** one new test of my own. Abort no longer rechecks before cancelling, so nothing else covered the handler passing its authority lease into `signal_cancellation_authorized`.
- **Not carried:**
  - 70a39b766f and ebfa6a1874: master's tests already publish config through the commit API.
  - The `sop_principal.rs` part of 70a39b766f goes with the SOP-reads follow-up.

IftekharUddin found that configure still committed without checking the current TUI owner and wrote the fix and its test: 66a93d5446, cherry-picked as ffcfe904b3 with IftekharUddin as author.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
